This difference is argued to derive from a non-linear relationship between SIC and momentum transfer into the ocean, as previously found in the Arctic. Due to this apparent importance of wind mixing, the following chapter investigates further the role of wind in setting the MLD by testing the model’s sensitivity to the wind forcing. This shows that the main influence of wind on MLD lies in increasing the depth of autumn/winter mixing, and in shortening the duration of shallow mixed layers in spring/summer. However, the experimental set-up used in this chapter could not fully disentangle the effects of wind on MLD from those of sea ice: adjusting the wind forcing does not only impact MLD, but also sea ice formation, melt, and transport. This consideration led to the construction of two one-dimensional column model set-ups, representing different sea ice regimes. Using this computationally faster modelling approach, a range of model experiments were conducted assessing the individual impacts of wind and sea ice-related freshwater fluxes on MLD. Prescr

title: ANN-assisted analysis of Hall-MHD Casson blood–gold nanofluid flow over a stretching sheet
summary: This study develops a validated numerical-neural framework for the steady boundary-layer flow of a Casson blood-gold (Au) nanofluid over a linearly stretching sheet. The model includes a transverse magnetic field with Hall current, Rosselan
content: This study develops a validated numerical-neural framework for the steady boundary-layer flow of a Casson blood-gold (Au) nanofluid over a linearly stretching sheet. The model includes a transverse magnetic field with Hall current, Rosseland thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, internal heat generation and an Arrhenius-type chemical reaction. The mixture properties are computed with the Tiwari-Das model, while Buongiorno's slip mechanisms govern the local nanoparticle concentration. Similarity variables reduce the equations to a coupled nonlinear boundary-value problem, which is solved by fourth-order Lobatto IIIA collocation with residual control (the bvp4c algorithm). The solver reproduces the benchmark data of Khan and Pop to four decimal places and an exact Casson-MHD-nanofluid solution to within [Formula: see text]. The numerical solutions (17 710 samples in ten scenarios) are used to train single-hidden-layer (2-12-1) networks with the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm. The networks reach test mean-squared errors of [Formula: see text]-[Formula: see text], regression coefficients [Formula: see text] and maximum absolute errors below [Formula: see text] at unseen parameter values; for the same network, LM gives errors two to five orders of magnitude lower than Adam or stochastic gradient descent. Adding 4% gold to blood raises the heat-transfer rate by 8.0% and lowers the streamwise wall shear by 17.9%, because the gold loading strengthens the thermal buoyancy. Increasing the magnetic parameter from 0.5 to 3 raises the streamwise wall shear by 86.5%, thermal radiation (R: 0.1→1.5) doubles the wall heat flux (+112%), and the chemical reaction (K: 0.5→2) raises the Sherwood number by 133%. The work is a fundamental transport model and a fast surrogate for the parametric screening of magnetically controlled blood-nanoparticle heat transfer.

title: Spatial Tailoring of Pt Clusters and Co Single Atoms Over TiO 2 Nanosheets Achieves Directed Charge Separation for Boosted Methanol Photoreforming
summary: ABSTRACT Efficient methanol photoreforming requires the coupling of methanol oxidative dehydrogenation and proton reduction, yet these half‐reactions demand distinct active‐site configurations. Here, acid‐etching‐assisted dual‐site engineer
content: ABSTRACT Efficient methanol photoreforming requires the coupling of methanol oxidative dehydrogenation and proton reduction, yet these half‐reactions demand distinct active‐site configurations. Here, acid‐etching‐assisted dual‐site engineering enables the synergistic integration of Pt clusters (Pt C ) and Co single atoms (Co SA ) on TiO 2 nanosheets (TNS). Experimental results and theoretical calculations reveal that the electronic interaction between Pt C and Co SA upshifts the d‐band center of Co SA to enhance the adsorption and activation of methanol‐derived intermediates, while downshifting the d‐band center of Pt C to weaken proton adsorption and facilitate H 2 desorption. Furthermore, compared with isolated Pt single atoms (Pt SA ), Pt C reduces the proton migration energy barrier and apparent activation energy, thereby facilitating efficient H 2 evolution. More importantly, the nanosheet structure of TNS accelerates the migration of holes toward Co SA and electrons toward Pt C , effectively suppressing charge recombination and establishing a directional redox pathway. Consequently, spatial tailoring of the reactive active sites enables Pt C Co SA /TNS to deliver an H 2 evolution rate of 117.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , approximately 2 times that of Pt SA Co SA /TNS, together with an apparent quantum yield of 66.4% at 365 nm. This work provides a novel strategy for the controlled fabrication of active sites on photocatalysts and efficient methanol photoreforming.

title: Doping engineering in piezocatalysis: Mechanisms, strategies, and perspectives
summary: Abstract Piezocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy for harvesting mechanical energy and driving chemical reactions toward sustainable energy conversion, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications. However, the practical
content: Abstract Piezocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy for harvesting mechanical energy and driving chemical reactions toward sustainable energy conversion, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications. However, the practical implementation of piezocatalytic systems remains constrained by insufficient piezoelectric polarization, inefficient charge separation, and limited interfacial reaction kinetics. Doping engineering provides an effective atomic-scale approach to overcome these limitations by simultaneously regulating crystal structures, defect chemistry, electronic configurations, and piezoelectric properties. In this review, we establish a comprehensive framework encompassing crystal-structure regulation (lattice distortion, bond-length variation, and symmetry breaking), defect chemistry and carrier behavior (band-structure modulation, defect evolution, carrier concentration, and density-of-states regulation), and piezoelectric properties (polarization regulation and piezoelectric response enhancement) to elucidate the fundamental roles of dopants in piezocatalysis. The applications of doped piezocatalysts in environmental remediation, energy conversion, and biomedical fields are further reviewed. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are proposed, focusing on rational dopant design, dynamic structure evolution, long-term stability, and scalable applications. This review provides mechanistic insights into doping-enabled piezocatalysis and offers guidance for the development of high-performance piezocatalytic materials for sustainable technologies.

title: The integrated aerosol–climate model CIESM-PAMT: Part 1. Model description and aerosol evaluation
summary: Abstract. Aerosols play a critical role in regulating the Earth’s climate system by influencing the radiative balance and cloud processes. Climate models with online-coupled aerosol modules are essential tools for studying such effects. To
content: Abstract. Aerosols play a critical role in regulating the Earth’s climate system by influencing the radiative balance and cloud processes. Climate models with online-coupled aerosol modules are essential tools for studying such effects. To enhance the representation of aerosol processes in the Community Integrated Earth System Model (CIESM), this study couples a new aerosol module, the Piecewise lognormal approximation Aerosol Model for Tsinghua University (PAMT), creating the integrated aerosol–climate model CIESM-PAMT. This work is presented in two parts. The current paper (Part 1) focuses on the model description and the evaluation of aerosol simulations, whereas Part 2 focuses on clouds, precipitation, and aerosol radiative forcing (paper in preparation). Compared with the original seven-mode aerosol module (MAM7) in CIESM (CIESM-MAM7), CIESM-PAMT updates nearly all aerosol processes, reduces the number of tracers from 31 to 24, and allows for more flexible adjustments of aerosol size-distribution resolution before compilation, thereby improving computational efficiency while maintaining simulation accuracy, albeit at the expense of representing some aerosol processes. Evaluation results show that CIESM-PAMT reproduces global aerosol spatial distributions, optical properties, and number and mass concentrations with varying degrees of agreement with observations. Compared with AERONET measurements, the relative biases in aerosol optical depth (AOD), fine-mode AOD, coarse-mode AOD, and Ångström exponent are 11 %, 30 %, −25 %, and −8.6 %, respectively. Comparisons with ground-based and shipborne observations yield relative biases of −6.7 % for black carbon (BC), −21 % for organic carbon (OC), 2.2 % for land sulfate (SO4), and 65 % for marine SO4 mass concentrations. The relative biases in PM2.5 and PM10 are −31 % and −58 %, respectively, while the bias in aerosol number concentration is −48 %. In the Arctic region (>60°N), CIESM-PAMT can also capture the observed aerosol optical properties and concentration variations, although discrepancies remain for some aerosol components and sites. Overall, the comparison indicates that CIESM-PAMT generally achieves better agreement with observations than CIESM-MAM7 for aerosol optical properties, BC and OC mass concentrations, and aerosol number concentrations. The two configurations show comparable results for land SO4 and PM2.5, whereas CIESM-PAMT exhibits larger biases in PM10 and marine SO4. In the Arctic, CIESM-PAMT reduces the systematic biases in most evaluated aerosol properties. Overall, CIESM-PAMT provides a more realistic representation of global aerosol distributions, optical properties, and concentrations by adopting a flexible piecewise lognormal aerosol representation, thereby improving the capability of CIESM for aerosol–climate simulations. These improvements establish a robust basis for future investigations of aerosol–climate interactions and their climate impacts.

title: Monitoring peatland dynamics in the Baltic region using EGMS products
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
summary: Climate change and the increasing regulatory requirements to preserve natural carbon sinks have intensified interest in the large-scale monitoring of peatland ecosystems, which are among the most effective terrestrial environments for long-
content: Climate change and the increasing regulatory requirements to preserve natural carbon sinks have intensified interest in the large-scale monitoring of peatland ecosystems, which are among the most effective terrestrial environments for long-term carbon storage and hydrological regulation. In this context, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides an opportunity to investigate peatland dynamics over extensive areas that are difficult to survey systematically on the ground, through repeated and cost-effective observations. This study tests the transferability of an open-source and reproducible methodology for the identification and monitoring of Peat-like Behaviour Areas (PBAs), based on Advanced Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (A-DInSAR) time series provided by the European Ground Motion Service (EGMS), under the demanding observational conditions of the Boreal region, where snow cover, freeze–thaw processes and coherence loss produce sparse and discontinuous displacement series. The workflow combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering and Density-Based Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN) to identify coherent areas characterised by peat-like displacement patterns and to distinguish sectors affected by subsidence from those exhibiting uplift behaviour. Applied across the Baltic countries within the Boreal biogeographical region, the methodology identified 576 PBAs (424 in Estonia, 125 in Latvia and 27 in Lithuania). A comparison with the CORINE Land Cover 2018 (CLC) inventory showed that approximately 43% of the identified PBAs occurred outside existing peatland inventories, highlighting the potential of the approach to identify areas exhibiting peat-like displacement patterns. Validation based on Sentinel-2 Total Productivity and Sentinel-3 OLCI Terrestrial Chlorophyll Index products revealed a strong spatial correspondence between the detected PBAs and areas characterised by reduced vegetation productivity and chlorophyll content. By distinguishing peatland sectors that are subsiding from those that are stable or rising, the approach provides a spatially continuous indicator of ecohydrological condition that complements static inventories, enabling degradation to be located within individual peatland systems and supporting the targeting and subsequent assessment of restoration interventions across different biogeographical regions.

title: Evaluating the added value of physical information for deep-learning estimates of global phytoplankton size classes from satellite
summary: Abstract. Phytoplankton size structure shapes marine food webs and carbon export, yet satellite ocean-colour retrievals remain subject to substantial uncertainties, since spectrally similar reflectance signals can arise from distinct commun
content: Abstract. Phytoplankton size structure shapes marine food webs and carbon export, yet satellite ocean-colour retrievals remain subject to substantial uncertainties, since spectrally similar reflectance signals can arise from distinct communities. Here, we assess whether satellite-derived physical variables can complement remote-sensing reflectance (Rrs) to improve global retrievals of total chlorophyll a (total-Chla) and of the micro-, nano-, and pico-Chla size classes. Using a global high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) dataset, we trained multilayer perceptrons (MLP) within a controlled framework that combines a spatio-temporal data split to limit leakage, explicit predictor selection without geographical coordinates, and delta-method uncertainty estimates. Compared with the operational OC-CCI product, a MLP using Rrs alone increased R2 by 0.04 for total-Chla, 0.09 for nano-Chla, and 0.33 for pico-Chla, all exceeding the evaluation uncertainty. Among the physical predictors tested, only sea surface temperature (SST) and absolute dynamic topography (ADT) provided consistent additional information; including them further increased R2 for pico-Chla by 0.15. Physical predictors mainly modified biomass partitioning among size classes rather than total-Chla, with the largest effects at high latitudes, where they reproduced the shift from pico- to larger phytoplankton observed by independent flow cytometry in the Southern Ocean. In warm equatorial waters, by contrast, they tended to overestimate pico-Chla. These results show that physical context helps resolve community shifts that are weakly expressed in the optical signal.

title: Continuous high-frequency monitoring reveals pronounced diel variability in greenhouse gas dynamics during pond drainage in hard clam aquaculture
summary: Abstract Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from aquaculture have attracted increasing attention in recent years; however, GHG dynamics during the pond drainage period remain poorly understood because previous studies have relied largely on sho
content: Abstract Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from aquaculture have attracted increasing attention in recent years; however, GHG dynamics during the pond drainage period remain poorly understood because previous studies have relied largely on short-term observations. In this study, continuous high-frequency monitoring was conducted over six consecutive days following pond drainage in hard clam ( Meretrix lusoria ) ponds to characterize the temporal dynamics of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), methane (CH 4 ), and nitrous oxide (N 2 O). Compared with the culture period, the drainage period exhibited substantially lower mean CO₂ fluxes (0.55 ± 1.17 µg m − 2 day − 1 vs. 1,126.88 ± 5,735.56 mg m − 2 day − 1 ), reduced CH 4 uptake (− 0.86 ± 9.84 µg m − 2 day − 1 vs. −0.52 ± 1.06 mg m − 2 day − 1 ), and higher mean N 2 O emissions (68.98 ± 393.54 mg m − 2 day − 1 vs. 0.88 ± 0.90 mg m − 2 day − 1 ). These results indicate that the drainage period was characterized by lower mean CO 2 emissions, weaker CH 4 uptake, and higher mean N 2 O emissions relative to the culture period, highlighting distinct responses among the three GHGs. Continuous monitoring further revealed pronounced diel variations in GHG concentrations during the early drainage stage. CO 2 concentrations fluctuated markedly during the first three days after drainage, CH 4 concentrations progressively declined as sediment aeration increased, and N 2 O concentrations exhibited a delayed diel pattern despite the absence of significant diel differences in fluxes, suggesting a potential temporal lag between microbial production and atmospheric emission. These findings demonstrate that GHG dynamics during pond drainage are highly variable and sensitive to sampling time. Measurements conducted at a single time of day may therefore overestimate or underestimate daily emissions. To our knowledge, this is the first study to characterize GHG dynamics during pond drainage using continuous high-frequency monitoring.

title: Large seed size accompanying GmSDP1 suppression is linked to cellular remodeling and phytohormone regulation
summary: Soybean (Glycine max) seeds contain approximately 20% oil and 40% protein and are important for food, feed, and biofuel. Improving soybean productivity and seed quality requires optimizing carbon partitioning during seed development. Previo
content: Soybean (Glycine max) seeds contain approximately 20% oil and 40% protein and are important for food, feed, and biofuel. Improving soybean productivity and seed quality requires optimizing carbon partitioning during seed development. Previously, seed-specific suppression of the lipase-encoding gene Sugar-Dependent 1 (SDP1) increased seed oil content by approximately 5% while slightly reducing raffinose family oligosaccharides without compromising protein content. Seed-specific SDP1 suppression also increased seed size by 18-25% without affecting seed number, resulting in greater seed biomass per plant. To determine the developmental basis of the increased seed size, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying this phenotype. Microscopy and biochemical analyses showed that larger seeds were associated with increased seed cell size and enhanced lignocellulosic cell wall accumulation. Temporal biochemical and transcriptomic analyses further revealed coordinated changes in hormone homeostasis, including altered levels of abscisic acid, 12-oxo-phytodienoic acid, and jasmonoyl-isoleucine, together with differential expression of F-box and RING/U-box family genes. The results indicate that the enhanced seed size resulting from SDP1 suppression is associated with coordinated changes in cellular development, cell wall accumulation, hormone homeostasis, and regulation of gene expression during seed development. Developmental and metabolic changes associated with the increased seed size phenotype support SDP1 manipulation as a potential strategy for improving soybean seed yield and quality.

title: The excavation, analysis and restoration of the pavement of the audience hall of Hammam as-Sarah (Jordan)
summary: The purpose of this article is to present the results of the excavation and analysis of the remains of the pavement and related features of the audience hall (and related rooms) of the Umayyad bath-house of Hammam as-Sarah (part of the Comp
content: The purpose of this article is to present the results of the excavation and analysis of the remains of the pavement and related features of the audience hall (and related rooms) of the Umayyad bath-house of Hammam as-Sarah (part of the Complex of Qasr al-Hallabat), which has led and guided the implementation of the conservation project of these remains, and their proper presentation to the visitor. After a systematic looting, the building had undergone a salvage excavation in 1974, which was not exhaustive, especially in regard to the pavements, the vaulting system and its building techniques. The amount of information regarding these building techniques, retrieved from the research conducted, is remarkable and has been essential not only to understand the original construction processes but also to guide the restoration. This research and the related intervention here presented have been conceived as a key component of a long-lasting project of excavation, restoration and musealization of this unique complex, but also as a training workshop for the students of the Master Program in Architectural Conservation of the School of Architecture of the German-Jordanian University. In this paper we focus on the paving and cladding systems of the audience hall area. Other components part of this phase of our research and intervention project, namely, the analysis and anastylosis of its singular entrance gate and the remains of the vaulted infrastructure will be the subject of separate papers devoted specifically to them. The outstanding results of the research and interventions here presented have allowed the recovery of a unique monument (which was at the verge of its total obliteration) as well as its effective interpretation and presentation to the public.

title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
summary: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dis
content: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. Molecular and structural properties of SPE-DOM remain unchanged during dense-water formation. Shelf processes minimally affect exported organics into the deep-sea, likely due to remineralization to inorganic carbon enhanced by long residence times on the shelf. Consequently, the dominant SPE-DOM signature in Weddell Sea Deep Water (WSDW) is established before dense shelf waters mix with warmer off-shelf waters. We estimate that 0.155 ± 0.03 PgC are transferred annually from the Weddell Sea to AABW, and that its molecular composition is expected to remain conserved despite ongoing climate-driven weakening of AABW.

title: Two-dimensional indium selenide (InSe): fundamentals, synthesis strategies, and next- generation optoelectronic device architecture
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) layered semiconductors have garnered significant interest as promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic applications, owing to their tunable electronic band structures, high surface-to-volume ratios, and pr
content: Two-dimensional (2D) layered semiconductors have garnered significant interest as promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic applications, owing to their tunable electronic band structures, high surface-to-volume ratios, and pronounced light-matter interactions. Among this growing family of materials, van der Waals indium selenide (InSe) has emerged as a particularly attractive candidate for future high-mobility optoelectronic devices, such as high-performance photodetectors, polarisation-sensitive devices, and chemical sensors. This is primarily due to its thickness-dependent bandgap, high intrinsic carrier mobility, and strong optical absorption. Compared with other extensively investigated 2D materials, InSe combines a comparatively high electron mobility with a layer-tunable band gap and spectral response extending from the visible to near-infrared region, whereas graphene lacks a band gap and MoS 2 shows weak near-infrared absorption. Its practical advantage, however, depends on encapsulation, contact quality, and phase control. This review provides a comprehensive and critical assessment of recent advances in InSe-based photodetectors, with particular emphasis on their crystal structure, electronic properties, synthesis methodologies, and device engineering strategies. Various fabrication techniques, including mechanical exfoliation, liquid-phase exfoliation, chemical vapor deposition, and physical vapor deposition routes (physical vapor transport, pulsed laser deposition, molecular beam epitaxy, and thermal evaporation) are systematically discussed in relation to their impact on material quality and device performance, together with the transfer and device fabrication steps that link the material to the photodetector. Furthermore, the fundamental photodetection mechanisms, including photoconductive, photovoltaic, and photogating effects, are analyzed in detail to elucidate charge generation and transport processes. Recent developments in device architectures, particularly heterostructure-based photodetectors, are also highlighted to demonstrate performance-enhancement strategies. Moreover, key challenges, such as environmental instability and the need for scalable synthesis approaches, are critically examined. Future research directions aimed at achieving high-performance, stable, and commercially viable InSe-based optoelectronic devices are also outlined.

title: Silane modified hemp shives and cellulose nanocrystals improve the strength and thermal insulation of alkali activated fly ash composites
summary: Abstract Hempcrete combines low thermal conductivity with biogenic carbon storage, but its compressive strength is typically 1 MPa or lower, whereas alkali-activated fly ash binders are strong but dense and carry an activator-related carbon
content: Abstract Hempcrete combines low thermal conductivity with biogenic carbon storage, but its compressive strength is typically 1 MPa or lower, whereas alkali-activated fly ash binders are strong but dense and carry an activator-related carbon burden. This study develops an alkali-activated fly ash–hemp–nanocellulose composite (AAFHN) in which hemp shives are alkali-washed and modified with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES), and cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) are dispersed in the activator solution. Five mixes were compared: an OPC control, a hemp–lime reference and three fly ash–hemp mixes with 0, 0.50 and 0.75 wt% CNC (relative to fly ash). The best-performing mix (M4; bulk density 780 kg/m 3 ) reached a 28-day compressive strength of 24.6 ± 1.3 MPa, a flexural strength of 3.5 MPa and a thermal conductivity of 0.142 W/(m·K), which is 89% lower than that of the OPC control, with a specific strength 2.3 times that of OPC. Total porosity fell from 78.2% (hemp–lime) to 54.1% and water absorption from 45.2% to 17.6%. After 50 freeze–thaw cycles M4 retained 89.4% of its compressive strength. The net cradle-to-gate (A1–A3) embodied carbon was + 32.4 kg CO 2 e/m 3 , 92.1% below OPC concrete; activators and CNC accounted for 93.5% of the gross emissions, and without the biogenic credit the reduction was 47%. Material cost was 2.6 times that of the control (US$213.75 vs US$82.50 per m 3 ). The strength–insulation compromise of bio-concretes can therefore be eased considerably, but the activator burden, CNC dosage and CNC price hinder deployment.

title: TERMINALIA ARJUNA (ROXB. ex DC.) WIGHT & ARN. A CULTIVATED SHADE-PLANT WITH GREAT CHEMICAL AND THERAPEUTIC ATTRIBUTES
source: International Journal of Applied and Experimental Biology
summary: A methanolic extract of Terminalia arjuna was subjected to GC-MS analysis, elemental and proximate analysis, antibacterial and antifungal testing, and SEM examination of the stem, bark, and leaves. GC-MS analysis identified approximately 10
content: A methanolic extract of Terminalia arjuna was subjected to GC-MS analysis, elemental and proximate analysis, antibacterial and antifungal testing, and SEM examination of the stem, bark, and leaves. GC-MS analysis identified approximately 100 notable compounds across different retention times. Elemental analysis revealed the presence of C, N, O, Mg, Si, Cl, K, and Ca. Proximate analysis determined high levels of dry matter, crude ash, protein, lipids, fiber, moisture, and nitrogen-free extract in the tested plant parts. The extracts exhibited antibacterial activity against Bacillus subtilis, Salmonella typhi, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus, and antifungal activity against Aspergillus niger, A. terreus, A. solani, and Alternaria alternata. The stem extract demonstrated stronger antibacterial activity than the bark and leaf extracts, though it was less effective than standard drugs (ampicillin and voriconazole). SEM studies revealed diverse microscopic structures, including fiber bundles, pitted vessels, stomata, and calcium oxalate crystals. Overall, these findings provide valuable insights into the elemental, nutritional, and antimicrobial properties of Terminalia arjuna, highlighting its potential therapeutic applications.

title: End-to-End Learning from Experimental Data: Integrating the PC-SAFT Equation of State into Neural Networks Training for Improved Polymer Parameter Estimation
summary: Accurate and computationally efficient thermodynamic models are essential for the design, optimization, and operation of many (bio)chemical processes involving polymer solutions, blends, and membranes. In this work, we combine machine learn
content: Accurate and computationally efficient thermodynamic models are essential for the design, optimization, and operation of many (bio)chemical processes involving polymer solutions, blends, and membranes. In this work, we combine machine learning (ML) with the PC-SAFT equation of state (EoS) to predict the non-associating pure component parameters for polymers, enabling the rapid evaluation of the pressure–volume–temperature (PVT) behavior of polymer melts and rubbers. Using a dataset of more than 5,400 PVT measurements for 78 chemically diverse polymers, we systematically evaluate the effects of EoS integration in the training process, the molecular representation, neural network architecture, and transfer learning. A baseline approach trained on pre-fitted PC-SAFT parameters is compared with a physics-informed approach that embeds the EoS in the training loop, enabling end-to-end training directly on experimental PVT data. Performance is assessed using 6-fold cross-validation. For a feed-forward neural network (FNN) using extended-connectivity fingerprints (ECFPs), embedding the EoS reduces the average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 8.67% to 5.57%. Replacing the FNN and ECFP representation with a graph neural network (GNN) using cyclic polymer graphs further reduces the average MAPE to 2.58%. Pre-training the models on PC-SAFT parameters for small molecules, followed by fine-tuning on polymer PVT data, yields additional improvements, reducing the average MAPE to 5.06% for the FNN and 2.15% for the GNN. These results demonstrate the benefits of combining an embedded EoS with geometric deep learning, and transfer learning for accurate polymer PVT predictions.

title: Sustainable tetracycline transportation using greener PIM: nanoindentation, prolonged stability, and process kinetics modelling studies
summary: The industrial application of Polymer Inclusion Membranes (PIMs) for pharmaceutical wastewater remediation is often limited by the extraction–stripping trade-off and carrier-mediated transport kinetics. To bypass these limitations, this stu
content: The industrial application of Polymer Inclusion Membranes (PIMs) for pharmaceutical wastewater remediation is often limited by the extraction–stripping trade-off and carrier-mediated transport kinetics. To bypass these limitations, this study introduces a highly efficient, liquid-plasticizer-free, self-plasticizing bi-continuous network PIM system and employs a 1 M NaCl strip phase. This transition provides mobile chloride (Cl⁻) counter-ions that trigger an accelerated, continuous ion-exchange “hopping” mechanism, breaking the low transport efficiency ceilings typical of traditional receiving chemistries. Scanning electron microscopy and nanoindentation modeling confirm that this optimized engineered PIM created a vertically aligned finger-like matrix channel, induced a ~92% reduction in nanomechanical stiffness, and a ~39% increase in elastic recovery. Process kinetics modeling demonstrates a well-balanced mass transport regime, splitting the kinetic diffusion share ( D m = 48%) and thermodynamic sorption share ( S = 52%) to drive a synchronized surge in the kinetic rate constant ( k = 0.09169 h⁻ 1 ) and effective diffusivity (8.48 × 10⁻ 10 m 2 s⁻ 1 ). As a result, the membrane exhibits 100% quantitative tetracycline extraction and an exceptional transport efficiency of ~99.5% at a peak initial flux ( J 0 ) of 3.98 × 10⁻ 10 mol · m⁻ 2 · s⁻ 1 . Long-term process stability trials confirm matrix integrity and a sustained high-flux transport environment across the initial four phases, maintaining membrane structural integrity across 10 consecutive cycles totaling 450 h of continuous runtime without chemical regeneration. This offers a robust, eco-friendly framework that aligns with Global Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6).

title: Transitional ecosystem states in coastal waters undergoing changing oxygen conditions revealed by coupled geochemical and microbial dynamics
summary: Background Coastal oxygen depletion is a major driver of changes in sediment biogeochemistry and microbial functioning. However, oxygen states vary over space and time, which results in temporal dynamics that are so far under explored. This
content: Background Coastal oxygen depletion is a major driver of changes in sediment biogeochemistry and microbial functioning. However, oxygen states vary over space and time, which results in temporal dynamics that are so far under explored. This study examined three sites with differing oxygen regimes across a year to investigate how temporal oxygen variability shapes surface sediment microbial communities and activity. Methods Coastal Baltic Sea surface sediments were sampled over one year at three sites with differing long-term oxygen regimes—one site that was predominantly oxic, one with predominantly low-oxygen conditions, and one intermediate site with fluctuating oxygen availability. Sediment biogeochemistry, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, and metatranscriptomic analyses were combined to assess temporal changes in microbial community composition and transcriptional activity. Results The results showed that long-term oxygen history was the primary factor structuring both microbial community composition and transcriptional profiles. The shallow site was characterized by mostly oxygenated conditions and exhibited relatively stable communities and transcriptional activity over time. The deep site was predominantly characterized by long-term low-oxygen conditions and was dominated by anaerobic metabolic patterns. In contrast, the intermediate site, that was exposed to more pronounced fluctuating oxygen conditions, showed the highest temporal variability in both community composition and RNA transcripts. This site also displayed stronger shifts in transcriptional activity over time, indicating a higher sensitivity of microbial processes to environmental variability compared to the other sites. Conclusion These results suggested that transitional oxygen habitats represented dynamic ecological states where microbial communities and functions rapidly responded to changing environmental conditions. Overall, oxygen availability strongly structured both microbial composition and activity in coastal sediments, with transitional habitats exhibiting enhanced temporal variability. These findings further indicated that environments experiencing fluctuating oxygen conditions may be particularly responsive to ongoing environmental change in coastal systems.

title: Northern palsa and peat ecosystem microbiomes are potentially supported by hydrogen and carbon monoxide metabolism
summary: Northern peatland and permafrost ecosystems are facing rapid changes, with increasing temperatures, permafrost thaw and shifts in hydrology. Characterizing microbial communities and metabolic potential from the soils and associated water bo
content: Northern peatland and permafrost ecosystems are facing rapid changes, with increasing temperatures, permafrost thaw and shifts in hydrology. Characterizing microbial communities and metabolic potential from the soils and associated water bodies is crucial to understanding the changes in biogeochemical cycling in these ecosystems. For this, samples were collected and sequenced from subarctic palsa and peat soils, along with samples from associated thaw ponds and streams. Metagenomics was utilized in describing the microbiome and its metabolic potential in these environments. Palsa soils hosted microbial communities that were distinct from the peatland soils, ponds and stream waters. Soils and their adjacent ponds shared taxa, and peat soils and ponds also shared taxa with the streams, unlike palsa soils which were likely more hydrologically isolated. Based on metabolic marker gene ratio for denitrification [(nirS+nirK)/nosZ], palsa soils had the strongest potential to be a source of nitrous oxide (N2O) out of all the sample types. Marker genes for hydrogen gas (H2) and carbon monoxide (CO) utilization were abundant across soil environments and metagenome assembled genomes, suggesting that trace gas oxidation is likely one of the key energy sources for microbiomes. In the palsa ponds and peat soils pmoA, marker gene for methanotrophy, was the most abundant compared to the other sample types.

title: LIVING AT THE FOREST FRONTIERS: LIVELIHOOD DYNAMICS, RESOURCE DEPENDENCE, AND HUMAN-ENVIRONMENT INTERACTIONS IN THE MOUNT CAMEROON FOREST LANDSCAPE, SOUTHWEST CAMEROON
source: GPH-International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research
summary: Abstract Forests and trees have an important role to play in poverty reduction. Man exploits forests for timber and other non-timber products. The forest has thus for the past years been the main source of subsistence for communities living
content: Abstract Forests and trees have an important role to play in poverty reduction. Man exploits forests for timber and other non-timber products. The forest has thus for the past years been the main source of subsistence for communities living in or near it. They have depended on the forest for livelihood needs such as food, shelter, healthcare, clothing, energy and source of income. This has led to his continuous exploitation of nature for food and other livelihood options, a practice which continues to have an unintended but damaging effect on the environment. The study suggests mechanisms and strategies for integrating community participation in sustainable forest resource management in the Mt. Cameroon forest reserve area in Buea Sub-Division. This research is qualitative ethnographic research that made use of qualitative techniques like; in-depth-interviews, observations and the focused group discussion as tools for data collection. Both primary and secondary sources of data collection were employed, the convenient sampling technique was used to choose the sampling population and a purposive sampling approach was adopted as the main sampling method for the study. Content analysis was the main technique used in analyzing data. Data analysis was based on the research questions and objectives of the work. Findings shows that actors concerned with management of forest resource have failed in their policies and activities with their target communities in forest conservation making them ineffective in the introduction and follow-up of other income-generating activities. Community Participation should be globally recognised as an effective strategy in the management and conservation of forest resource in the Mt. Cameroon forest reserve area in Buea Sub-Division. It is therefore recommended that participation should be taken as a 2-way learning process of dialogue, negotiation and decision-making between government and local communities concerning activities of forest management. Any participatory approach should therefore aim at local empowerment and accountability of individuals within the community. Keywords: Livelihood Strategies, Human-Environment Interactions, Political Ecology, Forest-Adjacent Communities, Indigenous Knowledge, Conservation and Livelihoods, Mount Cameroon, Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Two Years of the Journal of Geo-Energy and Environment: Progress and Future Directions
summary: Founded in 2025, the Journal of Geo-Energy and Environment (JGEE) provides a forum for research on geo-energy and the environmental issues associated with its development. In its first two publication years, 2025 and 2026, the journal publi
content: Founded in 2025, the Journal of Geo-Energy and Environment (JGEE) provides a forum for research on geo-energy and the environmental issues associated with its development. In its first two publication years, 2025 and 2026, the journal published six issues containing 30 articles. It is now indexed by Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) and has become a Partner Journal of the International Mine Safety and Emergency Rescue Association. Two Honorary Editors-in-Chief have been appointed, and the editorial board has been restructured. This editorial reviews the journal's progress over this period and summarizes the main findings reported in its published articles. It then outlines future research directions in geothermal energy, hydrogen energy, subsurface energy storage, and geological carbon storage. Academic quality, open scholarly exchange, and international collaboration remain the priorities that will guide the journal's development and its contribution to geo-energy and environmental research.

title: Spatial proteomics on repurposed sequencers reveals early astrocytic remodeling in an ALS mouse model
summary: Spatial proteomics can reveal how disease reshapes cells and their local environments, but extending these measurements across replicated tissue cohorts requires validated antibodies, consistent sample processing and integrated analysis. Th
content: Spatial proteomics can reveal how disease reshapes cells and their local environments, but extending these measurements across replicated tissue cohorts requires validated antibodies, consistent sample processing and integrated analysis. These requirements are particularly pressing in studies of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), where pathology evolves unevenly across spinal-cord regions and disease stages. Here, we established an end-to-end spatial proteomics workflow linking a validated 28-antibody panel to automated fluorescence decoding and imaging on repurposed high-throughput sequencers, followed by multicycle image processing, cellular profiling and probabilistic spatial-neighborhood analysis. We applied it to 70 lumbar spinal-cord sections from nine SOD1-G93A and nine wild-type mice at presymptomatic, disease-onset and symptomatic stages. Spatial neighborhood analysis revealed that the environments surrounding motor neurons were already remodeled at disease onset. GFAP-high neighborhoods expanded in the ventral gray matter, with 43% of motor neurons embedded in these environments in SOD1-G93A mice, compared with 15% in wild-type mice. This early expansion preceded the later decline of non-reactive gray matter and detectable motor-neuron loss. The regional organization of the protein-defined changes shared features with neuronal and astrocytic patterns mapped by spatial transcriptomics in mouse and human ALS. This work enables spatial proteomics across replicated tissue cohorts and identifies localized remodeling of the environments around surviving motor neurons as an early feature of disease in the SOD1-G93A model.

title: Effects of implant microstructure on drug release of ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) based long-acting implants
summary: The development of long-acting implants with a core-shell reservoir design is challenging because of their complex structure and prolonged testing requirements. While the polymeric shell has been investigated in a previous study, the presen
content: The development of long-acting implants with a core-shell reservoir design is challenging because of their complex structure and prolonged testing requirements. While the polymeric shell has been investigated in a previous study, the present study focuses on the implant core, characterizing its microstructural evolution during in vitro drug release in an aqueous medium using in situ micro-computed tomography. Results revealed progressive water uptake into porous depletion layers that developed during drug release. The mechanisms of water transport and drug diffusion were investigated using depletion layer model films fabricated from the implant core and evaluated using diffusion cells experiments. Permeation of a hydrophilic dye, Allura Red, demonstrated interconnected aqueous transport pathways in the water-filled model films. Separately, drug permeability was directly measured using etonogestrel as the permeant. Etonogestrel permeability in water-filled films was approximately 2.7 times that in dried films, primarily attributed to higher drug diffusivity through the interconnected aqueous pore network. Implant microstructure before and after drug depletion was characterized using high-resolution mosaic field-of-view scanning electron microscopy combined with artificial intelligence-based phase identification, supporting a mechanism in which drug particle dissolution generates pores that subsequently undergo structural evolution. The results support two drug transport pathways: (1) diffusion through the polymer phase and (2) diffusion through an interconnected, water-filled pore network. The effects of pore formation, water infiltration, pore connectivity, and pore shrinkage on drug transport were considered in relation to product development, including raw material properties, manufacturing processes, implant microstructure, and dissolution media. This work provides insights into the drug release mechanisms of EVA-based long-acting implants, material and microstructural attributes influencing diffusion kinetics, and analytical approaches that may support the development of generic Nexplanon ® products.

title: Improving Thermal Transport in Carbon Nanotube Films Through Interface and Structural Optimization
summary: ABSTRACT Carbon nanotube (CNT) films have significant potential for thermal management applications; however, their effective thermal conductivity remains substantially lower than that of individual CNTs because of microstructural effects a
content: ABSTRACT Carbon nanotube (CNT) films have significant potential for thermal management applications; however, their effective thermal conductivity remains substantially lower than that of individual CNTs because of microstructural effects and interfacial thermal resistance (ITR). This study investigates the influence of CNT alignment, film density, tube length, temperature, and interfacial thermal resistance on heat transport in CNT films using nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations. Approximately 400 independent molecular dynamics simulations were performed using LAMMPS with the AIREBO potential. CNT lengths ranging from 50 to 2000 nm and film densities from 0.6 to 1.3 g/cm 3 were investigated, together with three distinct alignment states: random, partially aligned, and fully aligned. The results indicate that interfacial thermal resistance is a major factor governing the thermal performance of CNT films. Films with interfacial thermal resistance below 3–5 × 10 −8 m 2 K/W exhibited thermal conductivity values of approximately 200–300 W/m K, whereas films with higher interfacial thermal resistance showed substantially lower thermal conductivity of approximately 50–100 W/m K. Increasing CNT alignment enhanced thermal conductivity by approximately 50%–70% compared with randomly oriented films, whereas the optimum density range was approximately 1.0–1.3 g/cm 3 . Further increases in density resulted in additional tube‐to‐tube junctions and associated thermal resistance, limiting the improvement in thermal conductivity. CNT length showed a secondary influence, with relatively modest improvements beyond approximately 300 nm, while temperature variations between 250 and 500 K produced no statistically significant effect on thermal conductivity. Overall, the findings identify interfacial thermal resistance and CNT alignment as key factors for improving thermal transport in CNT films and provide quantitative design guidance for optimizing CNT‐film microstructures for thermal management applications.

title: Microbial safety and shelf‐life dynamics of sprouted wheat: technological interventions and quality management
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Abstract Sprouted wheat is valued for its enhanced nutritional profile; however, the high moisture and moderate temperatures required for germination can promote foodborne pathogens, including Salmonella , Escherichia coli O157 and Listeria
content: Abstract Sprouted wheat is valued for its enhanced nutritional profile; however, the high moisture and moderate temperatures required for germination can promote foodborne pathogens, including Salmonella , Escherichia coli O157 and Listeria monocytogenes , as well as toxigenic fungi such as Aspergillus and Fusarium . Concurrently, germination activates endogenous hydrolytic enzymes, particularly α ‐amylase and proteases, which modify starch and protein structures and can contribute to quality deterioration and reduced shelf life. This review synthesizes current evidence on microbial hazards, enzymatic cascades and preservation strategies throughout the sprouted wheat processing chain. Particular attention is given to pathogen internalization and viable but non‐culturable (VBNC) states, which can compromise the effectiveness of conventional surface decontamination. Chlorine treatments have been reported to achieve reductions of 0.5–6.9 log colony‐forming units (CFU) g −1 , organic acids 2.4–3.0 log CFU g −1 and UV‐C and cold plasma approximately 3–5 log CFU g −1 , whereas biological agents such as phages and endolysins offer more targeted microbial control. Evidence further indicates that multi‐hurdle strategies combining mild organic acid tempering, low‐temperature drying and modified atmosphere packaging can provide more consistent microbial control and shelf‐life extension than individual interventions. An integrated framework that simultaneously manages enzymatic activity, moisture, temperature, and microbial contamination is therefore critical for improving the safety and stability of sprouted wheat products. Key research gaps include standardized approaches for VBNC detection, long‐term storage stability data, regulatory considerations for nanotechnology‐based packaging, and scalable and cost‐effective preservation technologies. Addressing these challenges could facilitate the safe and sustainable commercialization of sprouted wheat products. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Optimization, fuel characterization, and variable compression ratio diesel engine performance and emission of biodiesel from three different nonedible seed oils
summary: Abstract The present study investigates the engine compatibility of biodiesel derived from three non‐edible second‐generation feedstocks, Gossypium hirsutum (GHO), Hevea brasiliensis (HBO), and Pongamia pinnata (PPO), under identical operat
content: Abstract The present study investigates the engine compatibility of biodiesel derived from three non‐edible second‐generation feedstocks, Gossypium hirsutum (GHO), Hevea brasiliensis (HBO), and Pongamia pinnata (PPO), under identical operating conditions. The biodiesels were evaluated in a single‐cylinder variable compression ratio diesel engine at compression ratios of 16–20 using B20, B30, B40, B60, and B100 blends, with conventional diesel (B0) as the reference fuel. Engine performance, combustion characteristics, and exhaust emissions were systematically examined to identify suitable blend‐compression ratio combinations. The results showed that the optimum operating condition depended on the feedstock. GHO and HBO achieved their highest brake thermal efficiencies of 35.17% and 32.17%, respectively, at B30‐CR19, accompanied by minimum specific fuel consumptions of 0.217 and 0.253 kg/kWh. In contrast, PPO exhibited its highest brake thermal efficiency of 30.97% and a specific fuel consumption of 0.244 kg/kWh at B20‐CR18. These results indicate that moderate biodiesel blending combined with an appropriate compression ratio provides a more favorable balance between thermal efficiency and fuel consumption than either increasing the biodiesel fraction or the compression ratio alone. Increasing the biodiesel fraction and compression ratio generally reduced CO, HC, CO 2 , and smoke emissions, while NOx increased because of the oxygenated nature of biodiesel and higher in‐cylinder temperatures. This study demonstrates that the suitable operating condition varies with feedstock properties and that GHO‐B30/CR19, HBO‐B30/CR19, and PPO‐B20/CR18 provide favorable performance‐emission combinations under full‐load operation.

title: Dissolved oxygen gradients regulate microbial community assembly, metabolic function, and biogeochemical cycling in the southern Indian Ocean
summary: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a fundamental determinant in assessing the integrity and resilience of marine ecosystems. However, the influence of DO fluctuations on microbial community assembly, metabolic potentials, and interactions remain unre
content: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a fundamental determinant in assessing the integrity and resilience of marine ecosystems. However, the influence of DO fluctuations on microbial community assembly, metabolic potentials, and interactions remain unresolved from the open ocean surface to the seafloor, especially in the Ninety East Ridge (NER) region of the southern Indian Ocean. Here, DO profiles from 30 to 1000 m water depths at six stations proximate to the NER were characterized. Three stations exhibited significantly lower DO concentrations at mesopelagic-to-bathypelagic depths, which was potentially modulated by the local topography. Comparative analyses of microbial taxonomic diversity and metabolic potential between lower DO and normal DO stations were conducted by integrating 16S rRNA gene sequencing and metagenomic profiling. Our results show distinct DO-driven shifts, with reduced metabolic diversity and enhanced heterotrophic pathways under lower DO. Co-occurrence network topology found prevalent positive interactions in normal DO communities versus more negative relationships under lower DO. Notably, sulfur oxidation and denitrification were tightly coupled, especially at depths with lower DO, with sulfur-oxidizing denitrifiers identified as key players mediating nitrogen and sulfur transformations. This study found that the NER’s topography shapes oxygen availability, which in turn structures microbial ecological strategies and biogeochemical transformations in the deep ocean.

title: Silicon enhances photosynthetic pigment accumulation and antioxidant defence in nasturtium under shade and semi-shade conditions
summary: Silicon (Si) is recognized for enhancing plant stress tolerance, its physiological role in alleviating low-light stress in ornamental species remains poorly understood.This study evaluated the effects of foliar-applied Si (0, 50, and 100 μM
content: Silicon (Si) is recognized for enhancing plant stress tolerance, its physiological role in alleviating low-light stress in ornamental species remains poorly understood.This study evaluated the effects of foliar-applied Si (0, 50, and 100 μM) on growth, photosynthetic pigments, antioxidant metabolism, osmolyte accumulation, and flowering of nasturtium grown under shade and semi-shade conditions.Silicon application significantly increased plant biomass, leaf production, flower size, flower fresh weight, and floral yield, particularly at 100 μM.These improvements were associated with enhanced chlorophyll accumulation, increased activities of superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, and catalase, elevated ascorbic acid and total phenolic contents, and greater accumulation of proline and glycine betaine.Hence, Si enhances low-light tolerance by improving photosynthetic capacity, antioxidant defense, and osmotic adjustment, thereby promoting vegetative growth and floral productivity.

title: Spatiotemporal differentiation and driving mechanism of vegetation phenology in a high-latitude region of China
summary: Photosynthetic phenology describes the seasonal timing of vegetation photosynthetic activity. Using solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) data from 2001 to 2023, we extracted the start of the growing season (SOS), end of the growing
content: Photosynthetic phenology describes the seasonal timing of vegetation photosynthetic activity. Using solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) data from 2001 to 2023, we extracted the start of the growing season (SOS), end of the growing season (EOS), and length of the growing season (LOS) in Hulunbuir, China, and compared forestland, grassland, and cropland. The results showed that SOS and EOS mainly occurred at 120–144 and 244–256 days of year (DOY), respectively, while LOS was mainly 100–130 d. Forestland SOS was earlier than that of grassland and cropland. Under the original thresholds, forestland LOS was slightly longer than grassland LOS, although their ranking was sensitive to threshold choice. Across the region, SOS advanced by 0.07 d yr -1 , EOS was delayed by 0.04 d yr -1 , and LOS lengthened by 0.10 d yr -1 . Earlier SOS occurred in central and northern Hulunbuir, whereas later SOS and shorter LOS characterized the southwestern forest–grassland transition zone. EOS advanced in the central Greater Khingan Mountains but was delayed to the east and west; LOS lengthened in the eastern and southeastern grassland but shortened in the mountains. Forestland SOS and LOS showed less interannual variation than those of grassland and cropland, and most valid pixels had Hurst estimates below 0.5. Land use type had the highest single-factor explanatory power for spatial SOS variation, whereas annual mean maximum temperature ranked highest for EOS and LOS. After detrending, positive correlations of EOS and LOS with temperature and negative correlations with precipitation remained predominant. The direction of SOS-temperature correlations depended on the temperature metric, while the dominant SOS-precipitation correlation differed between forestland and grassland. These findings inform vegetation monitoring, carbon-sink assessment, and ecological restoration in high-latitude cold temperate regions.

title: Seasonally decoupled dynamics of dissolved organic carbon and fluorescent dissolved organic matter in continental shelf waters
summary: Abstract. We investigated seasonal variations in dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and humic-like fluorescent dissolved organic matter (FDOMH) in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea to better understand the factors shaping dissolved organic matt
content: Abstract. We investigated seasonal variations in dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and humic-like fluorescent dissolved organic matter (FDOMH) in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea to better understand the factors shaping dissolved organic matter (DOM) dynamics in continental shelf waters. Multi-year observations revealed that DOC concentrations increased with Radium based water residence time, whereas FDOMH showed no corresponding accumulation across seasons. This contrasting behavior was particularly evident during summer, when strong solar radiation may promote preferential degradation of photo-labile FDOMH, while a relatively more photo-resistant DOC remains in shelf waters, indicating a seasonal decoupling between DOC and FDOMH. The persistent increase in DOC with water residence time suggests that a fraction of DOC can accumulate in shelf waters despite ongoing degradation processes. Based on the observed relationship between DOC and water residence time, we estimated a net DOC accumulation flux of 1.1±0.2 Tg C yr-1, comparable in magnitude to annual riverine DOC inputs in this region. Our findings highlight the contrasting dynamics of DOC and FDOMH and suggest that prolonged water residence and selective DOM transformation may contribute to DOC persistence in continental shelf waters, potentially supporting the export of persistent DOC to the open ocean.

title: Nano-fertilizer formulations differentially affect growth, nutrient uptake, yield, and grain quality of rice
summary: Introduction In this study, five nano-fertilizer formulations (Nano-P, Nano-Zn, Nano-NPK, Nano Micro Mix, and Agrosatva) were evaluated for their effects on growth, physiology, grain quality, and elemental composition of the salinity-tolera
content: Introduction In this study, five nano-fertilizer formulations (Nano-P, Nano-Zn, Nano-NPK, Nano Micro Mix, and Agrosatva) were evaluated for their effects on growth, physiology, grain quality, and elemental composition of the salinity-tolerant rice cultivar Panvel 1 under the System of Rice Intensification. Methods A randomized complete block design with three (lab analysis) and five replications (field analysis) was implemented. Foliar applications were administered at tillering and panicle stages and compared with an unfertilized control. Results and discussion Data were analyzed using ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test (p ≤ 0.05). Nano-NPK significantly increased vegetative growth at tillering, resulting in the tallest plants (94.3 ± 1.6 cm) and longest roots (37.7 ± 2.3 cm) compared with the control. Nano-Zn produced the highest early biomass (fresh weight 137.1 ± 2.1 g; dry weight 67.5 ± 1.5 g) and markedly enhanced guaiacol and syringaldazine peroxidase activities, indicating improved oxidative defense. Nano-P consistently maintained the highest net photosynthetic rate across both stages and reduced the accumulation of FTIR spectra associated with stress-responsive functional groups. At the panicle stage, Agrosatva resulted in the greatest plant height (125.2 ± 2.4 cm) and supported superior grain nutritional quality, increasing crude protein from 1.63% ± 0.12% in the control to 5.05% ± 0.43% and starch from 77.83% ± 0.08% to 79.91% ± 0.48% (both p ≤ 0.05). ICP-MS profiling demonstrated that all nano-treatments reduced leaf arsenic by 15%–35% and sodium by 71%–83%, with Agrosatva providing the most balanced enrichment of macro- and micronutrients. Nano micro Mix (N-MM) maximized reproductive branching, increased chlorophyll a and enzyme activity at key stages, and elevated grain fat and protein content. Nano-NPK produced the highest levels of photosynthetic pigments, including total chlorophyll, and balanced vegetative growth. Agrosatva exhibited the most balanced elemental composition, accompanied by N-MM, Nano-P, and Nano-Zn, in the stage-dependent regulation of the thylakoid protein complexes (PSI, PSII, and LHCII), thereby optimizing light-harvesting apparatus assembly across growth phases. These findings indicate that nano-fertilizers represent a feasible and sustainable option for rice cultivation, offering enhanced nutritional value, improved stress tolerance, and reduced heavy-metal uptake under the tested conditions using the Panvel 1 variety.

title: Microplastic exposure reduces plant biomass and chlorophyll content with no detectable safety advantage for biodegradable polymers
summary: Abstract Biodegradable plastics are increasingly promoted as environmentally preferable substitutes for conventional polyethylene, yet whether the microplastics they release are less harmful to plants remains unresolved. We systematically r
content: Abstract Biodegradable plastics are increasingly promoted as environmentally preferable substitutes for conventional polyethylene, yet whether the microplastics they release are less harmful to plants remains unresolved. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed 31 studies (323 effect sizes) comparing biodegradable and conventional microplastics for effects on terrestrial plant growth, chlorophyll content and genotoxicity, using random-effects models with robust variance estimation. Microplastic exposure significantly reduced plant biomass and growth (− 19.2%, 95% CI [− 29.5, − 7.3]) and chlorophyll content (− 19.5%, 95% CI [− 30.4, − 6.8]). Reductions were numerically larger for biodegradable than for conventional microplastics (biomass − 22.1% vs. − 13.3%; chlorophyll − 26.8% vs. − 10.1%), but the between-class difference was not statistically significant. Co-exposure with heavy metals or other stressors more than doubled the biomass reduction (− 40.1% vs. − 16.2%). Aged biodegradable microplastics showed a non-significant trend towards genotoxic and cytotoxic responses, based on only two to three studies. Heterogeneity was extreme (I 2 ≈ 96–100%), but effects were robust in sensitivity analyses. These results provide no evidence that biodegradable microplastics are safer for plants than conventional ones, although a non-significant difference is not evidence of equivalence; co-occurring stressors intensify phytotoxicity, and ageing may introduce genotoxic potential, pending confirmation. These findings bear directly on environmental evaluation of biodegradable mulch films.

title: The ecological debt
summary: Researchers on “ecologically unequal exchange” have documented that energy and materials disproportionately flow from the Global South to the Global North. It is also obvious that sinks (the oceans and the growing vegetation) and the atmosp
content: Researchers on “ecologically unequal exchange” have documented that energy and materials disproportionately flow from the Global South to the Global North. It is also obvious that sinks (the oceans and the growing vegetation) and the atmosphere are disproportionately used to deposit excessive amounts of carbon dioxide. These two facts have allegedly given rise to an ecological debt, a notion that was introduced around 1990 in complaints from environmental activists from the South. This chapter elucidates the physical and economic calculations of the ecological debt, their persistent deployment by academic researchers and civil society organizations, and the negative reception of such claims in international agreements.

title: From Setpoints to System Dynamics: Integrating Light, CO2 and Fertigation in Controlled-Environment Agriculture
summary: Controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) allows growers to regulate temperature, humidity, light, nutrients and root-zone parameters with high precision. However, precision alone does not guarantee improved performance when each control var
content: Controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) allows growers to regulate temperature, humidity, light, nutrients and root-zone parameters with high precision. However, precision alone does not guarantee improved performance when each control variable is interpreted in isolation, because plants respond to these inputs as an integrated system. Light controls both photosynthetic activity and photomorphogenic signalling. CO2 changes carbon assimilation, stomatal behaviour, water use and source-sink relations. Fertigation variables such as individual macro- and microelement concentrations, electrical conductivity (EC), pH, and nutrient solution flow rate determine nutrient availability, plant development, osmotic status, oxygen delivery and root-zone signalling. In plants, these inputs converge on shared physiological and molecular processes, including carbon–nitrogen balance, transpiration-driven nutrient delivery, nitrate and phosphate uptake, H+-ATPase activity, hormone signalling, root architecture, and sink development. This narrative review proposes a qualitative, conceptual systems-dynamics framework; it does not present a calibrated simulation or validated control model. The central proposition is that plant growth, yield and fruit quality emerge from feedback loops among carbon capture, nutrient acquisition, hydraulic function and developmental sink strength. In crops such as cucumber, tomato, lettuce, strawberry, pepper and basil, the same environmental input can improve one trait whilst weakening another, depending on developmental stage, cultivar, sink demand, and root-zone conditions. A system-dynamics framework is therefore essential for designing production strategies that synchronise light settings, CO2 schedules and fertigation regimes with plant physiological stages. For compact cucurbits and other commercial CEA crops, this approach can help optimise productivity per unit volume whilst maintaining nutrient status, water-use efficiency and fruit quality. These insights also apply to CEA for long-term space, Moon and Mars missions.

title: Sótartalom hatása növelt hatékonyságú kőolajkitermelésben használt polimerek szerkezetére, töltésére és reológiai tulajdonságaira
source: SZTE Repository of Dissertations (University of Szeged)
summary: A múlt és a jövő energiahordozói között nagy ellentétek feszülnek nagyipari, környezetvédelmi és politikai érdekek mentén.Az emberiség ősidők óta ismeri a kőolajat, amely a XIX.század második felétől a világ vezető energiahordozójává vált.F
content: A múlt és a jövő energiahordozói között nagy ellentétek feszülnek nagyipari, környezetvédelmi és politikai érdekek mentén.Az emberiség ősidők óta ismeri a kőolajat, amely a XIX.század második felétől a világ vezető energiahordozójává vált.Fontossága a társadalmak számára megkérdőjelezhetetlen, ugyanakkor abból a tényből fakadóan, hogy a Föld gazdaságosan kitermelhető kőolajtartaléka véges, megjelent az igény a megújuló energiaforrásokra való áttérésre.A váltás azonban lassú, és nem mentes a kihívásoktól.Folytatni érdemes tehát azokat a közel 100 éve folyó kutatásokat, amelyek a nehezen elérhető olajkészletek felszínre hozásának technológiai fejlesztését segítik.A növelt hatékonyságú kőolajkinyerési technológiák (EOR) egyik zászlóshajója a polimeres elárasztás ("polymer flooding").Ennek során a magas viszkozitású polimeroldatnak a kőolajtelep tárólókőzetébe történő besajtolásával érik el a többletolaj termelést.A tárolóréteg (rezervoár) hőmérsékletén kívül kritikus tényezőnek számít az olajmezőben hozzáférhető víz minősége.Tekintettel arra, hogy az EOR technológiák vízigényét elsősorban a kitermelt rétegvíz biztosítja, a hozzáférhető víz kémiai összetétele mezőről mezőre változó, sőt, időben sem állandó.A rétegvizek összsótartalma (TDS) és az egy-, illetve kétértékű ionok aránya (ionspecifikus kölcsönhatások kialakításával) az elárasztásra használt vízben, meghatározza a polimerek oldatbeli jellemzőit.Extrém magas (≥50 g/l) sókoncentrációnál a legtöbb szintetikus EOR-célú polimer esetében az oldat elveszíti koherens, géles jellegét és makromolekulás oldat (szol) alakul ki.A szol-gél átalakulás döntően befolyásolja az oldat viszkozitását, ezáltal a polimer hatékonyságát és végső lépésben az alkalmazott technológia gazdasági mutatóit.Magasabb TDS-értékű oldatokban a polimerek teljesítménye adalékanyagokkal (pl.tenzidekkel) növelhető.Alternatív irányként megjelent az igény temészetes eredetű polimerek használatára a kőolajiparban, elsősorban magas sótűrő képességük miatt, ugyanakkor használatuk előnyös a kisebb környezeti terhelés szempontjából is.Ezek közül az egyik ipari méretekben is gyártásra került biopolimer a szkleroglukán.Szakirodalmi adatok támasztják alá, hogy magas toleranciát mutat az emelkedő sótartalom koherens szerkezetre gyakorolt negatív hatásával szemben.

title: Monthly Clean Electricity Generation Forecasting in Thailand via STL, Holt, and SVR-GA
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: Due to the demand for electricity to drive Thailand’s economy and the awareness of environmental impacts, Thailand mainly uses natural gas and renewable energy sources for electricity generation. However, the amount of production from clean
content: Due to the demand for electricity to drive Thailand’s economy and the awareness of environmental impacts, Thailand mainly uses natural gas and renewable energy sources for electricity generation. However, the amount of production from clean energy sources at each period is uncertain, which affects electricity production planning and policies. This research presents a hybrid model of STL decomposition, Holt, support vector regression, and genetic algorithm that emphasizes improving the quality of time series data before building a forecasting model to accurately predict electricity generation from clean energy sources. In addition, the proposed model is compared with conventional statistical forecasting models and other hybrid models to evaluate the forecasting performance using three performance criteria. The results indicate that the proposed hybrid model performs superior to other forecasting models. Furthermore, the proposed hybrid model can provide reliable and accurate forecasting results even when applied to new additional data. Therefore, the proposed hybrid model can be applied as a reliable tool for supporting strategic electricity planning and policy formulation in Thailand.

title: Optimalisatie van nettopologie voor de planning en exploitatie van hubs voor elektrische energie
summary: Transmission grids have become one of the major bottlenecks for the energy transition. The European transmission network was built decades ago to connect fossil fuel-based power plants with major demand centres. Renewable energy sources (RE
content: Transmission grids have become one of the major bottlenecks for the energy transition. The European transmission network was built decades ago to connect fossil fuel-based power plants with major demand centres. Renewable energy sources (RES), which are the preferred generation source in the European decarbonisation plans, are instead distributed, located according to the availability of natural resources, and cannot yet be forecast perfectly. Combined with the accelerating electrification of society, this shift alters the location, magnitude and uncertainty of power transmission through the grid. This results, to some extent, in unexpected power flows, fundamentally different from the expected ones that the existing transmission system was designed to host. These unexpected power flows can violate the thermal, voltage and angle stability limits, creating physical congestion in the grid. Congestion makes power transmission less efficient and leads to the curtailment of RES generation, which is replaced by expensive conventional generation and costly redispatch, resulting in higher overall costs. New transmission projects could resolve this problem, but due to permitting, construction, and public opposition, their construction time often exceeds ten years. Therefore, ongoing initiatives aim to maximise the power transmission capacity and integrate RES in the grid. In this sense, topological actions are used to redistribute power flows to solve congestion at low investment costs, yet in practice they are drawn from expert knowledge-based measures inherited from decades of predictable expected power flows. In addition, the infrastructure proposed to aggregate large RES capacity and transmit it to different countries raises technical challenges itself. Such multi-GW projects are being planned across Europe under interchangeable labels such as energy hub, offshore hub and energy island, without a technical definition and a common transparent methodology for their planning. This thesis develops the definitions, technical constraints, grid topology optimisation models and realistic test cases to try to address the aforementioned challenges. First, the term electrical energy hub (EEH) is defined to refer to projects involving a multifunctional node in a power system, managed separately from existing control areas, aggregating local GW-size generation capacity and holding multiple interconnections to other control areas. The definition is used to derive a hierarchy of seven areas of interest for technical design constraints related to EEH planning. These constraints are sorted by criticality into hard constraints, main drivers and key considerations, with their dependencies mapped explicitly. This contribution is a first step to aid system developers, operators and planners with the planning of EEHs by identifying and discussing the challenges related to them.
