title: A supercapacitor-assisted cyclic battery recharging method for solar and wind power systems
summary: The efficient use of solar and wind electricity in stand-alone power systems for remote facilities is limited during periods of reduced generation, when the source voltage may fall below the activation threshold of the charge controller. Un
content: The efficient use of solar and wind electricity in stand-alone power systems for remote facilities is limited during periods of reduced generation, when the source voltage may fall below the activation threshold of the charge controller. Under such conditions, direct battery recharging becomes impossible despite the availability of residual energy from the renewable source. This paper investigates a cyclic battery recharging method based on preliminary energy accumulation in supercapacitor modules and their subsequent discharge into the battery. The proposed approach was evaluated using a MATLAB/Simulink simulation model and a physical experimental setup with 166 F and 500 F supercapacitor modules and lead-acid batteries. The results show that preliminary energy storage in supercapacitor modules followed by controlled discharge enables additional battery recharging when the source voltage is insufficient for direct charging through the controller. For the 166 F modules, the duration of the complete first cycle was approximately 8.3 min, while for the 500 F modules it was approximately 28.5 min. Repeated cycles started from the residual voltage of the supercapacitor modules, which reduced the duration of the subsequent charging stages. The deviation between the simulated and experimental voltage characteristics did not exceed 3.5% in the most important operating regions and remained below 7.4% in the other regions. The proposed method is based on voltage-threshold switching logic; in the physical setup, switching was performed manually, while automated implementation is considered as a direction for future research.

title: Energy and power density of centralized renewable power plants in Brazil
summary: The global energy transition is driving the progressive replacement of fossil fuels with renewable energy sources (RES) in national power systems. With a predominantly renewable electricity system, Brazil constitutes a strategically relevan
content: The global energy transition is driving the progressive replacement of fossil fuels with renewable energy sources (RES) in national power systems. With a predominantly renewable electricity system, Brazil constitutes a strategically relevant case study for analyzing land-use efficiency across different renewable generation technologies, with direct implications for the country's remaining potential to expand renewable capacity, for the associated CO 2 emissions avoided relative to fossil-based alternatives, and for the energy policies needed to accommodate this growth. This study examines the set of large centralized renewable power plants operating in Brazil between 2015 and 2024, encompassing hydropower (large, small, and micro), wind, and solar photovoltaic plants, based on official data. For each plant, annual data were compiled on occupied area (km 2 ), installed nominal capacity (MW), and actual generation (MWmed), from which power density (MW/km 2 ) and energy density (MWmed/km 2 ) were calculated, with a temporal analysis of trends over ten years. The results show that centralized solar photovoltaic plants achieve the highest average power and energy densities, at 49.07 MW/km 2 and 5.85 MWmed/km 2 , while wind farms reach 6.85 MW/km 2 and 2.30 MWmed/km 2 , and small hydropower plants 4.50 MW/km 2 and 1.93 MWmed/km 2 , with temporal regressions indicating strongly increasing trends for solar in both indicators while large hydropower plants remain virtually stable. Because solar and wind achieve markedly higher densities than hydropower, the same territorial base can support substantially greater renewable capacity than current deployment levels suggest, expanding Brazil's potential to displace fossil generation and avoid a correspondingly larger volume of CO 2 emissions as the system continues to decarbonize.

title: Risk-aware hybrid reinforcement learning and robust optimization for reliable PV-battery scheduling under uncertainty
summary: Abstract The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) has intensified the need for intelligent scheduling strategies that can simultaneously reduce operating cost, preserve battery he
content: Abstract The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) has intensified the need for intelligent scheduling strategies that can simultaneously reduce operating cost, preserve battery health, and ensure operational reliability under significant uncertainty. In practical grid-connected PV–battery systems, the stochastic nature of solar power, load demand, and electricity prices often leads to constraint violations and high tail-risk costs when conventional optimization or purely data-driven methods are used. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a risk-sensitive hybrid framework that integrates Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), conformal uncertainty estimation (CUE), and robust optimization (RO) in a unified energy management architecture. The SAC agent learns a stochastic dispatch policy, while CVaR explicitly penalizes unfavorable cost outcomes and CUE provides distribution-free uncertainty bounds for uncertain inputs. These bounds are then embedded into a robust optimization layer to guarantee feasibility under adverse operating conditions. In addition, an adaptive fusion mechanism combines the outputs of the learning-based and robust controllers to balance economic performance and reliability. Simulation results for a typical residential PV–battery system demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best trade-off among cost, risk, and constraint satisfaction. Compared with a rule-based baseline, the full model reduces the SOC violation rate from 4.8% to below 1%, while also lowering the total operating cost and CVaR. Moreover, the proposed framework outperforms the RO-only variant by achieving a lower average cost without sacrificing robustness, and it consistently provides the highest reliability across independent runs. These results confirm that the proposed hybrid approach offers a practical and scalable solution for secure and economical PV–battery scheduling under uncertainty.

title: Design Blueprint: Geothermal Greenhouse and Aquaculture Cascade: Heating-Load, Pond Heat-Loss and Cascaded Flow Budgets
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Design blueprint derived from the source paper (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24235036): This paper presents a computed design study of a geothermal energy system on a single stated operating principle: geothermal water at a temperature too low for po
content: Design blueprint derived from the source paper (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24235036): This paper presents a computed design study of a geothermal energy system on a single stated operating principle: geothermal water at a temperature too low for power serves two food-production loads in cascade — greenhouse air and soil heating first, then warm-water aquaculture — because plants and fish are loads that want exactly the 20 to 40 degree heat that every other process in the energy system is trying to reject. The system is a supply at 68 degrees Celsius serving 22,000 square metres of greenhouse with a fabric-and-ventilation heat demand computed at a design temperature difference of 23 kelvin, soil heating at 25 watts per square metre, and a 1,800 cubic metre aquaculture installation exchanging a quarter of its volume daily into ponds held at 27 degrees Celsius, with reinjection at 30 degrees Celsius. The design target is the geothermal flow the combined loads require, built up load by load from the greenhouse envelope loss, the soil heating rate and the pond make-up heating duty, so each load's share of the well is visible. The combined loads require a geothermal flow of 28.4 kilograms per second delivering 4.53 megawatts of heat — 3.63 megawatts to greenhouse air, 550 kilowatts to soil heating and 349 kilowatts to aquaculture — and an annual delivery of 19.0 gigawatt-hours at the stated capacity factor. This work is a computed design study for civilian energy supply, with no targeting or weapon application. Its subject is the delivery of electricity or useful heat from geothermal resources, and its numbers are simulated from stated assumptions rather than measured on operating hardware. Status: DESIGN BLUEPRINT — SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED — NOT BUILT. All numbers are simulated values from the source paper's computation, deposited with this blueprint as compute.py and results.json. The design is a civilian geothermal energy system and has no targeting or weapon application. AI-use disclosure: Dave, an AI research system, assisted with the computation and drafting under the author's direction; author of record William Alexander Aldred.

title: Integrating Power and Connectivity: Feasibility Assessment and Digital Platform Design for EV Charging Infrastructure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Reliable electric-vehicle charging requires reservations to reflect deliverable power and energy, not only vacant connectors. This study develops a planning framework for a hub comprising two 120 kW DC chargers, two 22 kW AC chargers, 25 kW
content: Reliable electric-vehicle charging requires reservations to reflect deliverable power and energy, not only vacant connectors. This study develops a planning framework for a hub comprising two 120 kW DC chargers, two 22 kW AC chargers, 25 kWp photovoltaics, 50 kWh storage and a 250 kVA transformer. A descriptive survey of 100 respondents is combined with transparent, illustrative operating-envelope calculations. Station scarcity and waiting times accounted for 38% and 29% of reported hesitations; 55% definitely favoured pre-booking. Under assumed power factor and DC efficiency of 0.95, 44 kW AC demand and 5 kW auxiliary load, full charging requires 301.6 kW against a 237.5 kW grid ceiling. Without solar or storage support, combined DC output is limited to 179.1 kW. At 20 kW solar output, full charging requires 44.1 kW battery discharge; an assumed 38 kWh deliverable storage budget supports approximately 51.7 minutes. The analysis motivates reservation admission checks for equipment status, power allocation and cumulative energy. These are conditional planning results, not field validation. Unverified survey provenance, missing load profiles and absent cost data preclude claims of queue reduction, renewable-energy share or investment payback.

title: Energy-Efficient In-Memory Computing with Non-Volatile N-ary Spintronic Crossbar Arrays for Sustainable AI
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The electricity consumed by artificial-intelligence (AI) workloads is becoming a major sustainability concern, and a large share of it is wasted not on computation itself but on the constant shuttling of data between the physically separate
content: The electricity consumed by artificial-intelligence (AI) workloads is becoming a major sustainability concern, and a large share of it is wasted not on computation itself but on the constant shuttling of data between the physically separated processing and memory units of conventional von Neumann computers, the so-called memory wall. In-memory computing (IMC), which performs the computation directly inside an analog memory array where the data already reside, removes this energy bottleneck and is one of the most promising routes to sustainable AI hardware. Its energy efficiency, however, hinges critically on the memory device. The ideal cell would be non-volatile, so that the stored neural-network weights consume zero static power and survive power-down with no need for refresh, while also being CMOS-compatible for cheap integration and offering many evenly spaced conductance levels for dense, high-precision analog encoding. Here we show that spintronics, the branch of electronics that exploits the electron’s intrinsic magnetic moment (its spin) rather than only its charge, supplies exactly such a device. Our cell is a multi-state magnetic tunnel junction (M2TJ): two ferromagnetic layers shaped as crossing ellipses are separated by a thin insulating barrier, and the relative orientation of their magnetizations sets the quantum-mechanical tunneling resistance. Because magnetic shape anisotropy pins each ellipse’s magnetization along its long axis, the junction settles into several discrete, well-defined, and naturally equidistant resistance states that persist without power. This combination of non-volatility, CMOS compatibility, and intrinsically equidistant levels makes M2TJs ideal n-ary (multi-level) building blocks for neuromorphic IMC, in which each cell stores a multibit synaptic weight, complementing other emerging multilevel routes such as ferroelectric-FET crossbars. We present a simulation framework for multibit neural-network inference on n-ary crossbar arrays, developed for spintronic M2TJs but generalizable to any multistate memristive device. The framework retrieves the matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) result from the measured analog output with minimal assumptions, letting the crossbar act as a standalone AI co-processor placed where the data are generated: analog data from a camera or sensor enter the array directly as row voltages, cell currents sum along the columns by Ohm’s law, and threshold-sensing circuitry reads the outputs and feeds the next inference layer. Using simulated 4×4 arrays of 4-state M2TJs, we demonstrate successful inference on the XOR task and on MNIST handwritten-digit classification, reaching 94.48% accuracy against a 97.56% software baseline; principal-component-analysis (PCA) dimensionality reduction narrows this gap to 2.79%. A systematic error analysis identifies weight quantization as the dominant error source. We further study systematic nonidealities shared by all cells and cell-specific random nois

title: Wind-Solar Hybrid System with Battery Energy Storage (BESS) for Data Centre Power Supply in India: A SAM Simulation-Based Techno-Economic Analysis
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Data centres in India operate under constant 24×7 power demand while facing mounting pressure to reduce carbon footprints and cut electricity costs. This paper presents a SAM-based techno-economic analysis of a 20 MW Solar PV + 12 MW Wind (
content: Data centres in India operate under constant 24×7 power demand while facing mounting pressure to reduce carbon footprints and cut electricity costs. This paper presents a SAM-based techno-economic analysis of a 20 MW Solar PV + 12 MW Wind (4×3 MW) + 70 MWh BESS hybrid system designed to power a 5 MW constant data centre load, evaluated across three South Indian sites: Kurnool and Anantapur in Andhra Pradesh, and Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu. Using NSRDB solar and ERA5 wind resource data within NREL’s System Advisor Model (SAM), 25-year hourly simulations were run for each site. Four wind turbine configurations were tested — 2×6 MW, 3×4 MW, 4×3 MW, and 1×12 MW — with the 4×3 MW arrangement selected as optimal on grounds of lowest LCOE (₹1.96/kWh), highest reliability (97% availability), and lowest wake loss (6%). Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, emerges as the best site with a nominal LCOE of 8.64 cents/kWh, minimum DSCR of 0.71, and Year-1 generation of 83,435 MWh — approximately 90% above the annual data centre load — driven by its exceptional coastal wind capacity factor exceeding 40%. All three sites achieve 85%+ renewable penetration, confirming technical feasibility of the hybrid design. However, all sites show negative NPV under current PPA prices of 6.42–6.60 cents/kWh, indicating that policy support — through Viability Gap Funding, higher PPA tariffs, or declining BESS costs — is necessary for financial viability. This study demonstrates that Wind-Solar-BESS hybrid systems are technically ready for data centre applications in South India, with economic optimisation as the remaining frontier.

title: Multi-horizon wind speed prediction with physics-embedded state space neural operator learning
summary: Accurate and repeatable long-range wind-speed prediction is required for the integration of renewable energy into power grids, and these models will need to reconcile a number of contradictory requirements: high accuracy, low computational
content: Accurate and repeatable long-range wind-speed prediction is required for the integration of renewable energy into power grids, and these models will need to reconcile a number of contradictory requirements: high accuracy, low computational effort, physical plausibility, and quantified prediction uncertainty. In this paper, Physics-Embedded State-Space Operator Learning (PESO-Net) is proposed for multi-site, multi-horizon forecasting. The framework comprises a selective state-space encoder, gated cross-site mixing, a validation-controlled vertical shear regularizer, direct quantile decoding, and chronological conformal calibration. Observations from five years of 1-h synchronization at four anonymous sites were split chronologically into training, validation, calibration, and test sets, and one 168-h forecast trajectory was assessed over the 1–24 h, 1–72 h, and 1–168 h prefixes. The primary validation-weighted PESO-Net achieved MAE 2.080 m/s, RMSE 2.622 m/s, R² 0.176, 95.56% empirical coverage, 10.489 m/s mean interval width, and interval score 12.048. The primary validation-weighted PESO-Net had lower observed point errors and interval scores than the compared baselines. Among the four added model variants, PatchTST was closest by RMSE (2.727 m/s), with an interval score of 12.513. Mean predicted shear exponents ranged from 0.229 to 0.235, compared with observed means near 0.222; correlations of 0.287–0.302 support only limited physical agreement. The primary paired block-bootstrap RMSE contrast with Transformer was − 0.0185 m/s (95% CI − 0.0390 to 0.0042; p = 0.096), so statistical superiority was not established. The test period was used in earlier experiments, which limits the validity of claims of independent generalization. Thus, PESO-Net is not necessarily state-of-the-art for the four sites studied, but according to the data, it is competitive.

title: Leveraging Industry 5.0 for Sustainable Waste Valorization Planning: A Novel Decision‐Support Framework for Barrier‐Strategy Prioritization
summary: ABSTRACT Accelerating urbanization and increasing waste generation pose significant challenges to sustainable development and underscore the need to effectively implement waste valorization systems. This study addresses critical gaps in tho
content: ABSTRACT Accelerating urbanization and increasing waste generation pose significant challenges to sustainable development and underscore the need to effectively implement waste valorization systems. This study addresses critical gaps in thorough barrier and Industry 5.0‐integrated strategy identification for implementing sustainable waste valorization systems. This study develops an innovative decision‐making barrier‐strategy analysis tool, which extends Step‐wise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA) and Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to COmpromise Solution (MARCOS) within an Interval Type‐2 Trapezoidal Fuzzy Set (IT2TrFS) environment to capture a wider range of uncertainty for more accurate analysis. IT2TrFS‐SWARA facilitates holistic evaluations of implementation barriers, while IT2TrFS‐MARCOS prioritizes Industry 5.0‐oriented strategies. To validate this model, a case study of implementing advanced incineration‐based medical waste valorization was conducted. The results indicated “Inefficient process design for energy recovery mechanism” as the most significant barrier and “Integrate renewable energy as an energy source” and “Provide wearable safety‐monitoring IoT devices for workers” as most pivotal mitigation strategies. This tool can be extended to other urban sustainability domains, which support Industry 5.0‐enabled policy interventions for sustainable cities.

title: Optimization and Reusability of coal fly ash-Silica Composite Catalyst for sustainable Green Diesel Production from Used Cooking Oil
source: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
summary: The world energy demand has witness steady increase in recent time, this is driven by rapid growth in population, commercialization, industrialization, and advancement in technology. Researchers across the globe have intensified the search
content: The world energy demand has witness steady increase in recent time, this is driven by rapid growth in population, commercialization, industrialization, and advancement in technology. Researchers across the globe have intensified the search for alternatives energy to transportation fuels. Green diesel, otherwise known as Hydrogenation-derived renewable diesel (HDRD) is a potentials substitute for conventional diesel due to its paraffinic hydrocarbon composition which is compatible with compression-ignition (CI) engines without modification. This research investigates the potential of a coal fly ash (FA) admixture with silica oxide (SiO₂) composite for converting used cooking oil (UCO) into green diesel through hydrogenation process. A fine grained, powdery by product produced from burning pulverized coal in thermal power plant also refer to as coal fly ash collected from Eskom Holdings SOC Limited, South Africa, was sieved, and calcined before being mixed with SiO₂ at a 70:30 wt.% ratio. The composite was characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and thermal analysis to evaluate its functional groups, textural properties, crystalline phases, and thermal behaviour. The outcome shows a significant improvement in the textural characteristics of the composite compared to the unmodified bio- base Thermal power plant fly ash (BBTPPFS). The measured surface area increased from 0.8321 to 40.2332 m²/g, while the reported pore volume increased from 0.0040 to 0.1504 cm³/g. The corresponding pore-volume calibration changed from −0.0001 to 0.0015 cm³/g, The negative value requires confirmation against the original analytical results. These different confirmed that SiO₂ inclusion substantially modified the catalyst's accessible surface and pore structure, potentially improving reactant–catalyst potential interactions during hydro processing. The FA+SO2 also revealed physicochemical characteristics consistent with its potential to facilitate hydrogenation, deoxygenation, and controlled cracking of UCO. The combination of silica oxides and fly ash was established to be a technical potential of vaporizing fly ash and used cooking oil through an integrated waste to catalyst pathway.

title: Green Economic Opportunities and Energy Dependence in BRICS-T Countries: A Balanced Panel Dataset (2010–2024)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset provides a balanced panel of six BRICS-T economies (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, and Türkiye) covering the period 2010–2024, comprising 90 country-year observations. The dataset includes green economic opportunit
content: This dataset provides a balanced panel of six BRICS-T economies (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, and Türkiye) covering the period 2010–2024, comprising 90 country-year observations. The dataset includes green economic opportunities (GEO), energy import dependence, renewable energy share, real GDP per capita, industrial value added, and selected green growth indicators. The data were compiled from publicly available international databases, including the Green Growth Index, World Development Indicators (World Bank), and Our World in Data. Renewable energy share values for 2024 were estimated using linear trends based on 2021–2023 observations and are explicitly identified in the dataset. The dataset supports empirical research on the relationships between energy dependence, renewable energy transition, and green economic opportunities in BRICS-T countries.

title: Impact of Government-Funded Irrigation Project on National Development in Rwanda: Case Study of Kagitumba Irrigation Scheme in Nyagatare District
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study, entitled "The Impact of Government-Funded Irrigation Project on National Development: A Case Study of Kagitumba Irrigation scheme in Nyagatare District, Eastern Province of Rwanda," assessed the contribution of government irriga
content: This study, entitled "The Impact of Government-Funded Irrigation Project on National Development: A Case Study of Kagitumba Irrigation scheme in Nyagatare District, Eastern Province of Rwanda," assessed the contribution of government irrigation investment to agricultural development, farmers' livelihoods, food security, and value chain integration.The study was motivated by rainfall dependence, climate variability, and limited access to reliable irrigation systems.Its objective was to assess the impact of the Kagitumba Government-Funded Irrigation Project on national development.It assessed irrigation infrastructure development, examined RAB extension services and agricultural technology adoption, evaluated income generation and socio-economic improvement, and determined contributions to food security and agricultural value chain integration.A mixed-methods research design was adopted.Quantitative findings were obtained from questionnaires completed by 329 farmers and cooperative leaders, supplemented by document review.Findings showed effects of irrigation infrastructure on agricultural performance (mean = 4.01), extension services and technology adoption on crop productivity (mean = 4.03), income generation and socio-economic improvement (mean = 3.97), and food security and value chain integration (mean = 4.00).The study recommends strengthening irrigation maintenance, extension services, market linkages, financing, technology adoption, and cooperative development.It concluded that the project contributes to national development through improved agricultural productivity, livelihoods, employment creation, and food security in Nyagatare District.

title: Dijital Dünyada Yeşil Tüketici: Sosyal Medyadan Satın Alma Niyetine
summary: Çevre konusunda duyarlı olduğunu ifade eden tüketicilerin bu duyarlılığı her zaman satın alma tercihlerine yansıtmadığı bilinmektedir. Dijital Dünyada Yeşil Tüketici, bu bilgi–davranış açığını sosyal medyanın tüketici kararlarındaki artan r
content: Çevre konusunda duyarlı olduğunu ifade eden tüketicilerin bu duyarlılığı her zaman satın alma tercihlerine yansıtmadığı bilinmektedir. Dijital Dünyada Yeşil Tüketici, bu bilgi–davranış açığını sosyal medyanın tüketici kararlarındaki artan rolü üzerinden ele almaktadır. Eser, İnönü Üniversitesi’nde tamamlanan bir doktora tezinin kuramsal çerçevesine dayanan anlatısal bir literatür değerlendirmesidir; yeni ampirik veri sunmak yerine sosyal medya, sürdürülebilir pazarlama, çevre bilinci ve yeşil ürün satın alma niyeti üzerine yürütülmüş çalışmaları kavramsal bir bütünlük içinde tartışmaktadır. Kitap beş bölümden oluşmaktadır. Birinci bölümde sosyal medyanın temel özellikleri, başlıca platformlar ve sosyal medya pazarlaması incelenmektedir. İkinci bölüm sürdürülebilir pazarlama ve yeşil düşünme kavramlarını, üçüncü bölüm ise yeşil ürün satın alma davranışını ve bu davranışın belirleyicilerini ele almaktadır. Dördüncü bölümde Planlı Davranış Teorisi’nin tutum, öznel norm ve algılanan davranışsal kontrol bileşenleri ile yeşil tüketim ve sosyal medya bağlamındaki uygulamaları değerlendirilmektedir. Son bölümde ise dijital ortam, tüketicinin değerleri ve ürün bilgisi, niyetin kuramsal belirleyicileri ve somut satın alma koşulları arasındaki ilişkiler bütünleştirilmektedir. Kitap, sosyal medyada içeriğe yalnızca maruz kalma ile etkileşimli katılım arasındaki ayrımı vurgulamakta; yeşil aklama, eko-etiket güvenilirliği ve satın alma engelleri gibi konularda pazarlama yöneticilerine yönelik çıkarımlar sunmaktadır. Pazarlama, tüketici davranışı ve sürdürülebilirlik alanlarında çalışan araştırmacılar, lisansüstü öğrenciler ve uygulayıcılar için kapsamlı bir başvuru kaynağı niteliğindedir.

title: Integrated National Energy Management for Strengthening Indonesia’s Energy Self Reliance and Defense Resilience
summary: Energy self reliance and defense resilience are vital for Indonesia’s national sovereignty amid global geopolitical volatility and supply chain disruptions. This study formulates an Integrated National Energy Management framework using a mi
content: Energy self reliance and defense resilience are vital for Indonesia’s national sovereignty amid global geopolitical volatility and supply chain disruptions. This study formulates an Integrated National Energy Management framework using a mixed methods design that combines qualitative comparative policy analysis and systematic literature review with a quantitative recalculation of figures drawn from primary and secondary data. It addresses structural vulnerabilities, including high liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) import dependency (80.58% to 83.97%), a US$20.4 billion oil and gas trade deficit, low operational crude reserves (20 to 25 days), and heavy energy subsidies (Akbar et al., 2026). Drawing lessons from Japan, Brazil, India, and Germany, the paper introduces the Conceptual Framework for National Energy Supply Chain Resilience (KR RPEN). Evidence reported for Indonesian Army (TNI AD) border outposts indicates that hybrid solar microgrids can reduce fuel consumption by 70% to 85% and raise operational availability by 13% to 15% (Komara & Mahardika, 2026). Five strategic recommendations are proposed: establishing 90 day petroleum reserves (Anshori, 2025; Bai & Dahl, 2018), incentivizing domestic renewable manufacturing, conducting annual supply chain stress tests, maintaining baseload stability, and integrating critical energy infrastructure protection into national maritime defense.

title: Multilayer feed-forward neural network-based mobile app for photovoltaic module parameter estimation
summary: Abstract Accurate parameter estimation of photovoltaic (PV) cells and modules is essential for the modeling, simulation, and optimization of PV systems. However, this task involves solving a complex nonlinear optimization problem, which oft
content: Abstract Accurate parameter estimation of photovoltaic (PV) cells and modules is essential for the modeling, simulation, and optimization of PV systems. However, this task involves solving a complex nonlinear optimization problem, which often suffers from slow convergence and entrapment in local minima. The objective of this research is to contribute finding an efficient and software-independent approach to predict the parameters of the single diode model for polycrystalline and monocrystalline PV cells and modules from only the datasheet parameters at Standard Test Conditions (STC). To accomplish this task, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) approach is used, which resulted in the ability to estimate instantly without the need of commercial software. The developed model is additionally implemented in an Android application, which offers a user friendly and accessible instrument for PV system designers. The model was further evaluated through comparisons of reconstructed I–V and P–V characteristics with available reference characteristics, Simulink library modules, manufacturer datasheet values, and recently published algorithms. The results demonstrate high reliability, with RMSE, MAE and U95 values of 1.3610e−04, 6.8160e−05 and 2.659820e−04 respectively. Furthermore, the model reliably reproduced P–V and I–V characteristics under varying environmental conditions, closely aligning with the datasheet specifications of the four modules.

title: Input data and results for mission-constrained EV fleet support of a data center after an earthquake
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This record contains the input data and the result data of the article "Mission-constrained electric vehicle fleet support for data center resilience under staged post-earthquake grid return" (submitted to Applied Energy). Contents of Datas
content: This record contains the input data and the result data of the article "Mission-constrained electric vehicle fleet support for data center resilience under staged post-earthquake grid return" (submitted to Applied Energy). Contents of Dataset.zip- input/profiles: five days at 15-min resolution (480 steps): purchase and day-ahead price, outdoor temperature, PUE, available PV and wind power, critical and flexible data-center load per phase; wind turbine power curve.- input/fleet: 30 vehicle types, the 280 vehicles of the fleet and the 767 sessions of the representative sample.- input/scenarios: case definitions (C1-C5), grid-access profiles, islanding-duration scenarios and probabilities, renewable and load levels, probability vectors of the sensitivity analysis, and the 30 Monte Carlo samples.- input/parameters and input/network: model, penalty and network parameters and the 12-bus campus network.- input/model_input: the workbook read by the model; it holds the same data as the CSV files.- output: result files behind the tables and figures of the article (summary files and time series of all cases, benchmarks, diesel, stochastic and network runs).Column names of the workbook and of the output files are in Turkish; monetary inputs are in Turkish lira (49.7747 TRY/USD). Vehicle session generation (Monte Carlo sampling)- Random seed 2026; 30 samples. The representative sample is the one closest to the mean of the 30 samples (Euclidean distance of the standardized EV energy need, PV energy, wind energy, data-center energy and mean purchase price).- Buses, trucks, cars and light commercial vehicles: each vehicle takes the arrival and departure habit and the arrival SoE ratio of a randomly drawn vehicle of the same class from an existing fleet charging dataset (bootstrap). That dataset is not redistributed here for licensing reasons. Nightly return probability 0.55; time noise on arrival and departure normal with mean 0 h and standard deviation 0.33 h; arrival SoE multiplied by a log-normal factor LogN(0, 0.15^2), clipped to [0.02, 0.80].- Emergency vehicles: sessions per vehicle in five days Poisson with mean 2.5, truncated to 1-4; arrival day uniform over the five days, clock time normal with mean 12 h and standard deviation 6 h; dwell time log-normal with a median of 4 h; arrival SoE Beta(2, 4), clipped to [0.08, 0.70].- Representative sample: 280 vehicles in five classes, 767 sessions, at most 153 simultaneously connected vehicles.- The renewable and load levels of the stochastic model are derived from the same 30 samples. Software used for the results: Python 3.12, Pyomo 6.10, CPLEX 22.2 (primary) and Gurobi 13.0 (cross-check) with a 0.01% relative gap per stage, pandapower 3.5. The model code is available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.

title: Powering Independence: Energy Policy Evolution Under the Scottish National Party (2007–2023)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Master's thesis (Master 1, projet de mémoire) submitted in June 2024 for the Master 1 in International Studies – English-speaking World (Études internationales – Aire anglophone), Institut du monde anglophone, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle (
content: Master's thesis (Master 1, projet de mémoire) submitted in June 2024 for the Master 1 in International Studies – English-speaking World (Études internationales – Aire anglophone), Institut du monde anglophone, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle (Paris 3). Since the late 2000s, debates over Scottish independence have increasingly focused on energy policy. Energy governance in Scotland, historically shaped by the broader United Kingdom framework, has evolved in the context of accelerating global climate change and of pressure to move towards renewable sources. Between 2007 and 2023, the Scottish National Party (SNP) adopted a pro-environmental energy policy resting on investment in renewable generation and on denuclearisation. This approach contributed to shaping both energy policy and energy governance in Scotland. Governance theories suggest that the instrumentalisation and politicisation of energy policy are closely related to national identity and sovereignty. Energy policy became a strategic instrument through which successive SNP governments sought to assert Scotland's autonomy and to advance the case for independence. This research analyses the evolution of the instrumentalisation and politicisation of SNP energy policy between 2007 and 2023, considering the role of sub-national and national governments, policy instruments, and the institutional dynamics involved. Adopting a historical and systemic perspective, it examines the factors driving that instrumentalisation and politicisation, together with the interplay between political aspirations, economic considerations and environmental imperatives in shaping energy policy. Between 2007 and 2023, SNP energy policy combined political aspirations with practical energy solutions, which indicates the interconnectedness of energy and politics in a period characterised by more autonomous energy governance within a restrictive devolution settlement.

title: Human vs. AI: Comparing Student-Written and ChatGPT-Generated Essays in Terms of Thematic Progression and Rhetorical Organization
source: International Journal of Language and Literary Studies
summary: This qualitative study compares 27 argumentative essays written by Grade 12 students at Pualas National High School in the Philippines with a ChatGPT-generated essay in response to the same prompt. Drawing on thematic progression and genre-
content: This qualitative study compares 27 argumentative essays written by Grade 12 students at Pualas National High School in the Philippines with a ChatGPT-generated essay in response to the same prompt. Drawing on thematic progression and genre-based analysis, it examines textual organization, Theme–Rheme development, engagement and stance, contextualization, and the development of arguments and counterarguments. The analysis identifies both shared conventions and differences across the texts. Both student and AI-generated writing generally follow a recognizable argumentative structure and develop related themes concerning the potential effects of artificial intelligence on future employment. The student essays, however, display greater variation in paragraph development, more frequent personal positioning, and examples grounded in familiar contexts. The ChatGPT-generated essay presents a more consistently organized and generalized discussion, with explicit transitions and a comparatively impersonal tone. These observations describe the texts in this corpus and should not be interpreted as evidence of differences in students’ cognitive abilities or as defining characteristics of AI-generated writing more broadly. The study contributes a context-specific qualitative comparison of thematic and rhetorical features in secondary-level writing and highlights the value of assessing argument development and contextual relevance alongside linguistic accuracy. The findings support the use of AI-generated texts as materials for critical evaluation, provided that students remain responsible for developing and defending their own arguments.

title: WAR AND BLOOD TRANSFUSION CRISES: ADDRESSING BLOOD SHORTAGES, COLD-CHAIN DISRUPTIONS AND TRANSFUSION RISKS THROUGH CONFLICT-RESILIENT BLOOD SYSTEMS
summary: Armed conflict results in a complicated situation for blood transfusion services by halting blood collection, decreasing donor availability, harming healthcare infrastructure, disrupting cold-chain processes, and raising the demand for vita
content: Armed conflict results in a complicated situation for blood transfusion services by halting blood collection, decreasing donor availability, harming healthcare infrastructure, disrupting cold-chain processes, and raising the demand for vital transfusions. These problems affect trauma victims, women dealing with obstetric hemorrhage, children suffering from severe anemia, and those requiring ongoing transfusion support. This narrative review examines the impact of conflict on blood supply, the quality of components, transfusion safety, and continuous care. It analyzes shortages caused by conflicts, failures in refrigeration, delays in transportation, disruptions in compatibility testing, emergency blood transfusion releases, and lack of hemovigilance. Focus is on methods to improve resilience in blood services, including decentralized collection and distribution, strategic inventory management, solar-powered refrigeration, authorized alternative transport, digital traceability, and patient blood management. The evaluation also includes fair distribution, safeguarding the healthcare workforce, regulatory supervision, and humanitarian partnership. Advanced technologies like drones and renewable energy systems can enhance operational continuity but need validation, ongoing funding, and context-specific assessment. Future studies ought to evaluate cold-chain efficiency, compare logistics, enhance hemovigilance, and analyze cost-effectiveness and equitable access. Ultimately, successful blood transfusion services must integrate reliable infrastructure, trained personnel, evidence-based clinical protocols, structured supply networks, and continuous quality evaluation to reduce preventable transfusion-related harm and uphold life-saving assistance before, during, and after military conflicts. title: An Integrated Trend Analysis and Grey Relational Analysis of the Macroeconomic and Environmental Determinants of Sustainable Sanitation Infrastructure in Türkiye
source: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science
summary: Sustainable sanitation infrastructure, a critical component of the Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) nexus, possesses a multidimensional structure shaped by the complex interactions of macroeconomic and environmental dynamics, including
content: Sustainable sanitation infrastructure, a critical component of the Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) nexus, possesses a multidimensional structure shaped by the complex interactions of macroeconomic and environmental dynamics, including economic growth, rapid urbanization, increasing energy demand, and the filtration capacity of natural ecosystems. High multicollinearity and limited sample sizes in environmental time series often compromise the reliability of traditional regression models. While existing studies in the literature are generally limited to single rankings, this research aims to fill a methodological gap by integrating ranking reliability with dynamic temporal changes. In this study, the socioeconomic and environmental factors associated with safely managed sanitation services, used as a proxy indicator for water and environmental infrastructure sustainability in Türkiye, were examined. Grey Relational Analysis (GRA), which is robust against multicollinearity and effective for small samples, was utilized to determine the relative importance of the variables. The statistical stability of the obtained ranking was tested using the Moving Block Bootstrap resampling method, while temporal trends were analyzed via the Mann-Kendall trend test and Sen’s slope estimator. GRA and Bootstrap results indicated that forest area (representing the natural filtration and assimilation capacity of basins) and GDP per capita have the highest and most statistically stable relational levels with sanitation sustainability. Trend analyses indicated significant increasing trends in sanitation infrastructure, economic growth, energy use, and urban population, whereas a statistically significant decreasing trend was detected in the proportional share of renewable energy consumption within total energy demand. The findings indicate that sustainable infrastructure policies must simultaneously incorporate environmental strategies that enhance natural assimilation capacity, such as forest conservation, alongside economic investments. By validating classical GRA results with Bootstrap and integrating them with temporal trends, this study offers a reliable, holistic, and reproducible analytical framework for policymakers in the WASH infrastructure and environmental engineering literature.

title: Effect of scour on dynamic response within the fine sand seabed around a monopile foundation under wave action
summary: Offshore wind power, a renewable energy, effectively alleviates global energy pressure. Monopile foundation, known for its technical maturity, low cost, and rapid construction, is the predominant foundation type for offshore wind turbines.
content: Offshore wind power, a renewable energy, effectively alleviates global energy pressure. Monopile foundation, known for its technical maturity, low cost, and rapid construction, is the predominant foundation type for offshore wind turbines. Seabed response and scour evolution around monopile foundations are critical factors affecting their operational safety. Therefore, this study investigates the local scour evolution and its influence on wave-induced dynamic response within a fine-sand seabed around a monopile through physical model tests. Effects of wave height, wave period, and water depth on the spatial-temporal distribution of scour topography and pore pressure response around the pile are investigated. Results indicate that the development of scour pit modifies the local flow field and soil stress state, leading to a non-monotonic trend in the pore pressure response within seabed, which initially increases then decreases and finally recovers gradually. Increasing wave height and wave period enhances both the scour and pore pressure response, while greater water depth reduces the blockage effect of pile, mitigating scour and decreasing pore pressure amplitude. This study reveals the dynamic mechanism of scour evolution on seabed response, providing important theoretical and technical support for the design and safety assessment of monopile foundations in offshore wind power engineering.

title: Forecasting volatile electricity prices in the Australian National Electricity market using machine learning
summary: Abstract The growing integration of variable renewable energy Sources have intensified price volatility in the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM), creating operational challenges for market operators, traders, and battery energy s
content: Abstract The growing integration of variable renewable energy Sources have intensified price volatility in the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM), creating operational challenges for market operators, traders, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). Short-term electricity price forecasting is important for arbitrage, market operation, and participation in ancillary services such as Frequency Control Ancillary Services (FCAS). The evaluation presents a Comparative evaluation of eight forecasting models: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors (SARIMAX), linear regression, exponential smoothing, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Prophet with and without an exogenous demand regressor, using historical price data from New South Wales (NSW). Five-minute-ahead forecasting performance is assessed across selected stable, volatile, and rapidly fluctuating periods. XGBoost achieves the lowest mean validation MAE (0.040) and highest mean validation $$R^2$$ (0.949) among the evaluated models, and retains the best performance on the held-out test set. The findings support the use of market information in the evaluated forecasting models.

title: Mapping Aluminum Flows in the United States Using Advanced Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
summary: Abstract This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics
content: Abstract This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics. Results show continued U.S. reliance on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products. The posterior median end-of-life (EOL) collection rate was 66.8% [57.2%, 79.9%] in 2017 and 67.6% [62.3%, 73.9%] in 2022. Median domestic retention of collected EOL scrap was lower in 2022 (52.7% [49.6%, 55.6%]) than in 2017 (56.4% [51.7%, 60.5%]), although the credible interval for the change spanned zero. Across robustness cases varying source weighting, pedigree-to-uncertainty mappings, and prior strength, domestic retention remained below 60%. Spatial analysis identified mismatches between EOL scrap generation and domestic remelting capacity. These findings show that improved collection alone may not increase domestic recycling when processing constraints persist. We observe a continued import dependence, efficient circulation of prompt fabrication scrap, and limited domestic retention of collected EOL scrap.

title: When the grid overflows: a novel probabilistic framework to assess the success of storing excess electricity as heat in high-temperature ATES (HT-ATES) systems
summary: Abstract Increasing shares of variable renewable electricity (VRE) are creating more frequent periods of surplus electricity, increasing the need for flexible options that can absorb and use this excess generation. One option is to convert
content: Abstract Increasing shares of variable renewable electricity (VRE) are creating more frequent periods of surplus electricity, increasing the need for flexible options that can absorb and use this excess generation. One option is to convert surplus electricity into heat, but its effective use requires storage when heat production and demand do not coincide. Because heat demand remains concentrated in the colder months, long-duration seasonal thermal storage is needed to bridge this temporal gap. High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (HT-ATES) is one technology capable of providing this seasonal storage function. This study develops a demand-oriented operational probability of success (PoS) framework for evaluating whether HT-ATES can convert historically observed surplus electricity into useful seasonal heat. The Neubrandenburg system in Germany was used as a physically grounded reference case. Historical German electricity data from 2015 to 2022 were represented through empirical four-week surplus distributions and coupled to a chronological Monte Carlo inventory model accounting for charging availability, well thermal throughput, adopted storage limit, and thermal recovery. The model first generated a distribution of achievable seasonal heat delivery, which was then evaluated against alternative heat-demand targets. PoS is therefore expressed as the probability that delivered heat meets or exceeds a specified thermal requirement, rather than as a fixed property of the aquifer. For the base configuration, with a thermal power of approximately 3.72 MW, an adopted storage limit of 12 GWh, and a recovery factor of 0.72, the 20,000 retained Monte Carlo cycles produced a mean seasonal delivery of 8.551 GWh. The upper modeled heat delivery of 8.640 GWh was reached in 94.63% of the cycles. Constraint diagnostics showed that well throughput was the unique limiting condition in 57.06% of injection decisions, remaining storage space in 28.82%, and zero-surplus charging windows in 10.90%, while positive-surplus magnitude alone did not limit any base-case injection decision. Sensitivity analyses further showed that increasing thermal power shifts the range of heat-demand targets that can be met with high probability, but the benefit diminishes as the modeled upper delivery limit is approached. Equivalent non-interacting doublet configurations exhibit the same throughput-storage-limit trade-off. The results demonstrate that nominal storage capacity alone is insufficient for assessing HT-ATES performance. Operational success depends jointly on charging opportunities, thermal power, storage capacity, thermal recovery, system configuration, and the thermal target used to define success. The proposed framework provides a transferable screening method for linking historical energy-system variability with subsurface storage constraints and explicit heat-delivery requirements.

title: Owning What Can Quit
summary: Academic journals are part of the infrastructure of science, yet most journal titles are owned by commercial publishers while their standing rests on editors and boards who can leave. This paper asks what that separation means for the gover
content: Academic journals are part of the infrastructure of science, yet most journal titles are owned by commercial publishers while their standing rests on editors and boards who can leave. This paper asks what that separation means for the governance of science. Using a coded dataset of all 57 editorial mass resignations recorded by Retraction Watch from 2015 to 2026, data on editor tenure at 110 economics, finance and accounting journals, and journal-level publication and revenue data, I document three patterns. First, resignation does not reverse an owner’s decision: in none of the 19 episodes involving an editor’s replacement did the owner back down after the board resigned, so editorial communities have influence only before they leave. Second, whether a departing board can take a journal’s standing with it depends on institutions outside the board: successor journals follow most often where a scholarly society backs the board and rarely in medicine, where non-profit hosts are scarce, while journal ranking lists, which rate titles rather than the people who edit them, keep reputation with the owner. Third, a stated limit on editor tenure was applied at the publisher’s discretion; where it was applied, output grew almost fourfold, a short-run gain whose long-run effect on the journal’s standing is not yet known. I draw implications for scholarly societies, funders, publishers, and the bodies that compile journal rankings.
