title: Stage-Gated Biomaterial Strategies for Peri-Implantitis Management
summary: Abstract Peri-implant biomaterials are commonly compared as isolated antimicrobial technologies, although their clinical relevance depends on linked requirements spanning prevention and treatment. Preventive approaches must preserve tissue
content: Abstract Peri-implant biomaterials are commonly compared as isolated antimicrobial technologies, although their clinical relevance depends on linked requirements spanning prevention and treatment. Preventive approaches must preserve tissue integration and future cleanability; once disease develops, treatment must provide access to and disruption of mature biofilm, preserve or recover implant-surface competence, control destructive inflammation, support defect-specific regeneration, and enable durable maintenance. This structured critical review proposes a six-gate framework that evaluates preventive surfaces, decontamination methods, local delivery systems, host-directed materials, and regenerative adjuncts against those downstream requirements. Human peri-implant evidence was prioritized for treatment claims. Animal studies, clinically representative in vitro models, simplified implant models, and indirect oral-biofilm or general materials evidence were considered separately. The synthesis shows that mechanical and surgical strategies have the most direct clinical evidence, but no decontamination protocol has shown consistent, durable superiority across clinical settings. Reconstructive biomaterials can improve radiographic defect fill in selected defects, but their additional benefit for composite disease resolution remains uncertain. Meanwhile, antimicrobial coatings, plasma electrolytic oxidation platforms, smart hydrogels, and immunomodulatory materials remain supported mainly by preclinical models. Across different technologies, the same bottlenecks recur restricted access to threaded and protein-conditioned surfaces, reliance on immature or simplified biofilms, unmeasured surface damage or chemical residues, incomplete host-cell assessment, short follow-up, and little evidence on recurrence. Mechanics are considered separately as device biomechanics, interfacial transport, microbial contact cues, and host mechanobiology, which function through different mechanisms and levels of evidence, rather than as a unified cause of disease. The proposed framework links antimicrobial findings with surface integrity, host compatibility, regeneration and maintenance to identify gaps in translational evidence. Its generalizability and ability to predict clinical outcomes remain untested.

title: Contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems predominantly operate under an execution-oriented paradigm in which computational requests are processed as soon as possible after submission. Although immediate computation is essential for latency-sensitive applications, it is not necessarily the most economically efficient strategy for every computational task. Electricity prices fluctuate, GPU rental costs vary, cloud computing resources experience changing supply and demand, and different AI requests exhibit different degrees of tolerance for delayed execution. These conditions suggest that computational efficiency should not be understood exclusively in terms of execution speed. This paper proposes Postponed Computation (PC) as a central temporal computing paradigm in which an AI system deliberately postpones eligible computational operations until a more favorable future execution opportunity becomes available. Unlike conventional post-hoc computation, which analyzes or processes information after an event has occurred, Postponed Computation concerns the intentional scheduling of computation itself for a later time. The paper develops an Economic-Aware Postponed Computation framework for generative AI services, in which the decision to compute is separated from the decision of when to compute. Four principal mechanisms are introduced: User-Adaptive Postponement, Predictive Economic Timing, Deadline-Constrained Postponement, and Cross-Task Aggregation. The framework considers electricity prices, GPU and cloud resource costs, computational availability, waiting costs, service-level commitments, and user-selected execution preferences. A particularly relevant application is an economy-oriented AI service in which eligible user requests, including voluntarily deferred requests from free-tier users, can be retained and executed during periods of lower computational expenditure. The framework further investigates whether compatible requests from multiple users can be aggregated into larger execution batches to improve resource utilization. Existing research has established important foundations in deferred workload scheduling, electricity-aware computing, cloud resource optimization, and inference batching. Accordingly, the contribution of this paper is the formalization and proposed integration of Postponed Computation as a broader temporal decision principle for generative AI services, rather than a claim that workload deferral itself has never been studied. A conceptual architecture, mathematical formulation, operational mechanisms, research hypotheses, and evaluation methodology are presented. No experimental results or empirical performance improvements are claimed.
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has intensified the demand for computational resources, particularly high-performance graphics processing units (GPUs), electricity, memory, and large-scale data-center infra
content: The rapid expansion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has intensified the demand for computational resources, particularly high-performance graphics processing units (GPUs), electricity, memory, and large-scale data-center infrastructure. Contemporary AI services are predominantly designed around immediate or near-immediate inference, whereby computational requests are processed shortly after submission regardless of whether the current economic and infrastructural conditions represent an optimal opportunity for execution. Although existing research has investigated deferred cloud computing, deadline-aware scheduling, dynamic electricity pricing, carbon-aware workload shifting, and opportunistic utilization of low-cost computing resources, the broader possibility of treating AI computation as a long-horizon economic decision that may be postponed for months, reassessed, reorganized, and subsequently executed remains an important research direction. This paper introduces Ultra-Deferred Computation (UDC) as a proposed computational paradigm that extends conventional immediate inference and short-horizon deferred scheduling toward long-horizon, economically adaptive AI computation. The proposed framework distinguishes request submission, computational commitment, resource acquisition, execution, and result delivery as separate events that need not occur within the same operational period. It integrates future GPU availability, electricity prices, computing-resource rental costs, renewable-energy conditions, workload characteristics, computational opportunity, user service tiers, task utility, and acceptable waiting periods into a unified decision-making architecture. A particularly important application concerns generative AI services in which users of free or lower-priority service tiers may voluntarily authorize computationally intensive requests to remain in a persistent deferred queue for several weeks or months in exchange for reduced service costs or free execution. Rather than merely delaying an existing queue, UDC introduces the possibility of periodically reassessing task value, predicting future computational opportunities, reallocating execution priorities, and reorganizing compatible workloads before activation. A formal optimization model, task-lifecycle architecture, scheduling procedure, and research propositions are developed to establish the theoretical foundations of this paradigm. This study is conceptual and methodological; it does not claim experimental validation or measured cost reductions. To the best of our knowledge, this paper proposes one of the first unified conceptual frameworks specifically positioning long-horizon, user-tier-adaptive, economically conditioned deferral of generative AI computation as a distinct computational-service paradigm. The framework opens a research direction beyond immediate AI inference in which the timing of computation becomes an explicit dimension of intelligent resource allocat

title: REGULATORY QUALITY AS A SHORT-RUN CATALYST IN CHINA'S RENEWABLE ELECTRICITY TRANSITION: EVIDENCE FROM AN ARDL-BAYESIAN-MACHINE LEARNING FRAMEWORK
summary: This study examines whether regulatory quality conditions the translation of economic capacity into renewable-electricity integration in China, 2000-2024. Using ARDL bounds testing on a logit-transformed renewable-electricity share and a fi
content: This study examines whether regulatory quality conditions the translation of economic capacity into renewable-electricity integration in China, 2000-2024. Using ARDL bounds testing on a logit-transformed renewable-electricity share and a five-variable specification selected after diagnosing severe multicollinearity in a broader candidate set, we find a valid error-correction relationship (adjustment coefficient -0.372, p=0.005; bounds F-statistic 15.29, exceeding the 1% critical bound). Digital readiness is the only variable with a significant long-run association with renewable integration (0.771, p=0.048). Economic capacity has no significant direct long-run or short-run association. Regulatory quality's role is concentrated in the short run and is conditional on economic capacity: a regulatory-quality shock is associated with a significant negative short-run effect on renewable integration at low economic capacity (-1.61, 95% CI [-2.18,-1.04]), a null effect at mean capacity (-0.08, 95% CI [-0.58,0.42]), and a significant positive effect at high capacity (1.09, 95% CI [0.18,2.01]). Granger-causality tests indicate a significant bidirectional relationship between regulatory quality and renewable integration, consistent with a feedback dynamic rather than one-directional causation. Bayesian Model Averaging and blocked time-series cross-validated XGBoost-SHAP are used as robustness and exploratory tools respectively; the latter shows limited out-of-sample generalizability at this sample size and is reported descriptively. Rule of law and control of corruption, tested as alternative moderators, show materially weaker evidence of a cointegrating relationship than regulatory quality, supporting discriminant validity of the regulatory-quality construct specifically. We interpret the results as evidence that regulatory quality's association with renewable-electricity integration operates through short-run adjustment dynamics conditional on prior economic development, rather than as an independent long-run driver. Keywords: Renewable energy integration; regulatory quality; institutional moderation; ARDL bounds testing; Bayesian Model Averaging; China JEL Codes: O13, Q42, Q48, C51

title: Rural collective property rights reform, land reallocation, and e-commerce adoption: evidence from rural China
summary: Rural e-commerce has become an important channel for expanding rural households’ market participation, yet adoption remains limited and uneven. Using data from the 2020 China Rural Revitalization Survey and a conditional mixed-process frame
content: Rural e-commerce has become an important channel for expanding rural households’ market participation, yet adoption remains limited and uneven. Using data from the 2020 China Rural Revitalization Survey and a conditional mixed-process framework with a village-level instrument for reform completion, this study examines the relationship between rural collective property rights reform and household e-commerce adoption and explores land reallocation as a potential mechanism. The results show that rural collective property rights reform is positively associated with household e-commerce adoption. Land transfer is measured by both binary participation indicators and transfer ratios. Although results vary between these measures, the ratio specifications provide the clearest mechanism-consistent evidence: reform completion is associated with greater land transfer-in and transfer-out intensities, while transfer-in intensity is positively associated with adoption and transfer-out intensity is negatively associated with it. These relationships are evident for online sales of agricultural products but not non-agricultural products, consistent with production-expansion and agricultural-exit channels. Heterogeneity analyses suggest stronger reform associations among higher-income households and larger-scale land operators, but no significant variation by human capital. The findings highlight the potential role of collective asset governance in rural e-commerce adoption and the relevance of land reallocation and household production capacity.

title: Data for Participation Guarantees and Participant Selection for Renewable Electricity Trading Platforms
summary: This dataset accompanies the study “Participation Guarantees and Participant Selection for Renewable Electricity Trading Platforms.” It contains 52,608 hourly observations for the Danish electricity price areas DK1 and DK2 over 2023–2025. T
content: This dataset accompanies the study “Participation Guarantees and Participant Selection for Renewable Electricity Trading Platforms.” It contains 52,608 hourly observations for the Danish electricity price areas DK1 and DK2 over 2023–2025. The market variables include day-ahead electricity prices, wind generation, grid-injected solar generation, and gross electricity consumption, together with UTC timestamps and local-calendar attributes. The package includes archived source files, harmonized hourly inputs, parameters for constructed generator and buyer portfolios, seven deterministic design scenarios, and numerical result tables. The results cover recoverable service budgets, fixed annual service fees, participant gain guarantees, participant selection, sensitivity analyses, and retrospective evaluations across years. Contract portfolios are constructed from regional market profiles, with normalization constants established in 2023 and retained for subsequent years. The data preserve negative electricity prices, the 2024 leap day, and daylight-saving transitions. The 2025 physical series are supplied as a frozen aggregate snapshot. Supporting documentation describes variable definitions, units, portfolio construction, source attribution, and validation checks. The underlying market observations originate from the Energinet Energy Data Service.

title: Toward Gigawatt-Scale Alkaline Water Electrolysis: Durability-Driven Materials and System Optimization
summary: Alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) is a technologically mature and commercially deployed hydrogen production technology, offering advantages in materials availability, manufacturing scalability, and capital cost. However, scaling established
content: Alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) is a technologically mature and commercially deployed hydrogen production technology, offering advantages in materials availability, manufacturing scalability, and capital cost. However, scaling established systems to multi-gigawatt deployment requires more than incremental laboratory performance improvements. In this Perspective, we argue that the goal is to expand AWE's operating range while preserving its advantages in durability, safety, manufacturability, and cost. We identify six research priorities for the next 5-10 years: durability under combined stress, separator integrity and gas crossover, dynamic operation, stack-balance-of-plant integration, scale-relevant validation and manufacturing reproducibility, and system-level techno-economic optimization. We discuss how current density, temperature, pressure, electrode design, manufacturing, and electricity prices influence these priorities and propose quantitative benchmarks for performance, durability, and operating flexibility. We emphasize that laboratory advances must be validated under realistic operating conditions and assessed at system level to demonstrate durable, reproducible, and economically competitive AWE systems.

title: A SMART CUISINE FRAMEWORK: IOT-BASED PRESSURE COOKER DESIGN WITH MULTI-SENSOR CONTROL AND ELECTROMAGNETIC ACTUATION
summary: Traditional pressure cookers can result in safety issues. This study aims to explain why this may happen and how IoT can be used through a software solution. Using pressure, weight and temperature sensors the cooker can be monitored. An emb
content: Traditional pressure cookers can result in safety issues. This study aims to explain why this may happen and how IoT can be used through a software solution. Using pressure, weight and temperature sensors the cooker can be monitored. An embedded controller manages the electromagnetic coil to provide safe and optimal conditions. Through automation and thermal control, the Smart Pressure Cooker provides increased energy efficiency, consistency and safety/ease for the user

title: Machine and deep learning assessments for multi-scale wind power prediction: evidence from real-world SCADA datasets
summary: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for improving grid stability, optimizing energy management, and facilitating the large-scale integration of renewable energy. However, forecasting based on real-world SCADA measurements remains c
content: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for improving grid stability, optimizing energy management, and facilitating the large-scale integration of renewable energy. However, forecasting based on real-world SCADA measurements remains challenging because of the stochastic and nonlinear nature of wind generation. This study presents a comprehensive and reproducible benchmarking framework for short-term wind power forecasting by comparing fifteen forecasting approaches spanning statistical baselines, machine learning, and deep learning paradigms. The evaluated models include Persistence, Linear Regression, ARIMA, SARIMA, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, ExtraTrees, ANN, DNN, RNN, LSTM, GRU, CNN, and Informer. The comparison is conducted using a 24-month industrial SCADA dataset (2024–2025) collected at 10-min intervals from an operational wind farm in northern Morocco. All models are evaluated under a common chronological protocol with the same forecasting target, horizon, test period, and evaluation criteria, while model-specific input representations and optimization procedures are adopted according to the requirements of each forecasting paradigm. All models perform one-step-ahead forecasting at the native 10-min SCADA resolution. The resulting power predictions are subsequently aggregated into daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly accumulated energy quantities for multi-scale evaluation, rather than being generated as independent direct forecasts at these horizons. Performance is then assessed using multiple statistical metrics, a MeanRankScore framework, and formal statistical significance tests (Diebold–Mariano and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests). The results show that the Persistence model provides the highest forecasting accuracy under the investigated conditions, while XGBoost is the best-performing learning-based model, consistently outperforming the remaining machine learning and deep learning approaches. In contrast, complex recurrent and Transformer-based architectures, including GRU and Informer, exhibit substantially larger prediction errors, particularly during low-power operating periods. These findings demonstrate that increasing model complexity does not necessarily improve forecasting accuracy for structured industrial SCADA datasets and highlight the value of rigorous benchmarking for selecting reliable forecasting models in practical wind energy applications.

title: Segmented maximum power point tracking for photovoltaic systems using variable-step perturb-and-observe and predictive fuzzy PID control
summary: Photovoltaic maximum power point tracking (MPPT) faces a trade-off between rapid dynamic response and accurate steady-state regulation. This study proposes a segmented MPPT framework that uses large-step perturb-and-observe (P&O) control fo
content: Photovoltaic maximum power point tracking (MPPT) faces a trade-off between rapid dynamic response and accurate steady-state regulation. This study proposes a segmented MPPT framework that uses large-step perturb-and-observe (P&O) control for coarse tracking outside a normalized voltage range of 0.75Uoc-0.90Uoc and prediction-assisted fuzzy PID control for fine regulation within this range. The framework was evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations, threshold-sensitivity and hysteresis analyses, partial-shading tests, and outdoor hardware experiments. Under irradiance and temperature variations, the proposed method reduced tracking time by up to 79.9 % and dynamic power overshoot by more than 98 %, while maintaining tracking errors below 0.18 %. Threshold-sensitivity analysis confirmed the 0.75/0.90 range as an effective operating interval, achieving 100 % relative tracking efficiency, while hysteresis reduced switching events by 70.27 %. Under partial-shading conditions, tracking efficiencies of 99.23 % and 98.80 % were achieved. Outdoor experiments further verified real-time mode switching and demonstrated improved energy harvesting. Overall, the proposed segmented control framework enhances both dynamic and steady-state MPPT performance with low computational complexity, making it suitable for embedded photovoltaic applications.

title: Evaluasi Kinerja dan Keandalan Operasional Rectifier pada Catu Daya Telekomunikasi (Performance Evaluation and Operational Reliability of Rectifiers in Telecommunication Power Supply Systems)
source: JURNAL EDUNITRO Jurnal Pendidikan Teknik Elektro
summary: This study aims to evaluate the electrical performance of a rectifier system in a telecommunication power supply and analyse power supply continuity during module failures. Voltage, current, and output power were measured over seven days at
content: This study aims to evaluate the electrical performance of a rectifier system in a telecommunication power supply and analyse power supply continuity during module failures. Voltage, current, and output power were measured over seven days at four load points, while failure records were reviewed based on six months of operational history. The results show that the output voltage ranged from 54.04 to 55.13 V, with total output power ranging from 28.03 to 29.62 kW and averaging 28.91 kW. The summed current across the four load points ranged from 510.04 to 542.93 A. Compared with the reference rating of 3,600 A, this represents 14.17–15.08%; however, interpretation of the loading level requires verification of the actual system configuration. Operational records show one rectifier module failure with a reported handling time of 72 hours, without interruption of the power supply because the other modules continued supporting the load. These findings indicate relatively stable electrical output and power supply continuity during the recorded module failure. However, quantitative reliability assessment requires additional data on the number of active modules, operating hours, and total system downtime.

title: Numerical design and optimization of bifacial CIGS solar cell with Cu2O transparent back contact using SCAPS-1D
summary: Abstract Bifacial solar cells must operate efficiently under both front and rear illumination, yet their performance is often constrained by the low conductivity of p-type transparent conductive oxides used for rear contacts. Cu 2 O offers
tags: Copper indium gallium selenide solar cells
content: Abstract Bifacial solar cells must operate efficiently under both front and rear illumination, yet their performance is often constrained by the low conductivity of p-type transparent conductive oxides used for rear contacts. Cu 2 O offers a promising alternative due to its favorable electrical and optical characteristics. CIGS-based bifacial devices are strong candidates for high-efficiency photovoltaic operation, and this work presents a theoretical evaluation of their dual-sided performance. A device structure consisting of Al-doped ZnO/i-ZnO/n-ZnSe/CIGS/Cu 2 O was designed and simulated using SCAPS-1D, with the CIGS absorber layer thickness optimized for balanced operation. At an absorber thickness of 1 µm, ratio of rear-illumination performance to front-illumination performance parameters J SC , V OC , FF and PCE reach 96%, 100%, 97% and 94%, respectively. The optimized front-side performance yields a PCE of 23.25%, with J SC of 25.78 mA cm −2 , V OC of 1.06 V and FF of 84.35%. Rear-side illumination results in a PCE of 21.93% with J SC of 24.89 mA cm −2 , V OC of 1.06 V and FF of 82.54%. Analysis across multiple albedo levels highlights the strong influence of reflected light on bifacial output. A transparent Cu 2 O back-contact layer, a Cd-free ZnSe buffer layer, and a thorough optimization of bifacial functioning under both front and rear illumination are the innovative aspects of this study.

title: Sistem Monitoring Jalur DC dan Suhu PLTS 1.650 Wp Berbasis IoT dengan Dashboard Web (IoT-Based Monitoring of the DC Side and Temperature of a 1,650 Wp Solar PV System Using a Web Dashboard)
source: JURNAL EDUNITRO Jurnal Pendidikan Teknik Elektro
summary: This study developed and evaluated an Internet of Things (IoT) prototype for monitoring electrical and temperature parameters of a 1,650 Wp nominal-capacity photovoltaic (PV) power plant, with a web-based dashboard. The system combines a PZ
content: This study developed and evaluated an Internet of Things (IoT) prototype for monitoring electrical and temperature parameters of a 1,650 Wp nominal-capacity photovoltaic (PV) power plant, with a web-based dashboard. The system combines a PZEM-017 sensor for DC parameters, an MLX90614 infrared sensor for panel surface and ambient-area temperature, an ESP32 microcontroller, an LCD, and MQTT communication to the IoTKita dashboard. Readings are shown locally on the LCD and can be accessed remotely through the dashboard. The system was tested over five days by comparing its readings against a reference instrument. Because time-resolved data were not included in the test documentation, the comparison was made on average values. The relative differences from the reference instrument were 0.00% for voltage, 2.65% for current, 2.21% for power, 1.55% for panel surface temperature, and 0.51% for ambient-area temperature. The system recorded a cumulative energy of 14.67 kWh during the test period. The 0.00% voltage difference arises because both averages round to 120.9 V, so it should not be read as a measure of precision. These results indicate only a preliminary agreement at the level of averages. Sample-by-sample accuracy and long-term reliability cannot be concluded until the DC measurement point, data collection dates, and communication logs have been verified.

title: SMART GRID-BASED SOLUTIONS TO PROTECTION SYSTEM CHALLENGES ARISING FROM PV INTEGRATION IN POWER NETWORKS
summary: The presence of photovoltaic (PV) in the distribution network leads to inefficient protection devices that cannot detect the fault correctly because it changes the radial system to a bidirectional system; therefore, the need for an active p
content: The presence of photovoltaic (PV) in the distribution network leads to inefficient protection devices that cannot detect the fault correctly because it changes the radial system to a bidirectional system; therefore, the need for an active protection scheme is necessary. This paper suggests an adaptive protection scheme that updates its settings automatically based on a communication link between PV units and the protection relays. The proposed scheme used ETAP software to simulate an 11 kV radial system with PV installation. The results show an important improvement where the scheme is able to detect and isolate the fault within 200 milliseconds. The miscoordination decreased by 35 % in comparison to conventional protection schemes, in addition to reliability enhancement without complex computation

title: Activating Oxygen Radical Coupling via Ru–Mn Dual‐Site Electronic Regulation for Durable Acidic Oxygen Evolution
summary: ABSTRACT Realizing direct O–O coupling offers an effective strategy to reconcile activity and durability in Ru‐based anode catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet tuning active‐site distances for activation ca
content: ABSTRACT Realizing direct O–O coupling offers an effective strategy to reconcile activity and durability in Ru‐based anode catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet tuning active‐site distances for activation can compromise structural stability. Here, we synchronize the reactivity of paired Ru/Mn sites in an ingenious Ru@Mn‐RuO 2 core–shell catalyst composed of a metallic Ru core and a Mn‐doped RuO 2 shell, thereby enabling direct heteronuclear O–O coupling. Fermi‐level equilibration at the metal/oxide Schottky interface induces interfacial charge redistribution, narrowing the electronic and bonding disparities between Ru and Mn sites. The resulting electronic and bonding alignment modulates the evolution of oxygen intermediates on adjacent Ru/Mn sites, driving the transition from the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) to a synchronized oxygen coupling mechanism (SOCM). Ru@Mn‐RuO 2 requires only 172 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 , operates stably for over 4000 h in acidic electrolyte, and further sustains PEMWE operation for 1200 h at 1 A cm −2 . This work provides a mechanistic strategy to address the stability limitations of Ru‐based catalysts, advancing their practical application in PEMWE.

title: Use of Geothermal Energy as a Renewable Source of Energy with the Help of Heat Pumps
summary: Geothermal heat pumps are widely used for heating and cooling buildings. This technology is based on the principle of heat transfer between the ground and the building, significantly reducing electricity or fossil fuel consumption. In winte
content: Geothermal heat pumps are widely used for heating and cooling buildings. This technology is based on the principle of heat transfer between the ground and the building, significantly reducing electricity or fossil fuel consumption. In winter, heat from the ground is transferred to the building, and in summer, excess heat is returned to the ground. This closed-loop system not only provides a comfortable microclimate but also saves up to 50-70% of energy compared to traditional heating methods. This article discusses the operating principles, key technological solutions, as well as the environmental and economic aspects of using such systems. The focus is on heat transfer system types: vertical ground probes, horizontal collectors, and groundwater-based systems. Factors influencing configuration selection are analyzed, including geological conditions, available space, and the facility's heat load. It is emphasized that proper circuit calculation and design are key to long-term and efficient system operation. In conclusion, it is argued that integrating geothermal heat pumps into the energy systems of buildings and residential areas is a promising approach to decarbonizing heat supply, increasing energy independence, and achieving sustainable development goals. The widespread adoption of this technology will be facilitated by the development of a regulatory framework, government support, and increased awareness of its benefits.

title: Layered Bi‐Pt 3 Ni Dilute Nanoalloy Boosting Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer
summary: ABSTRACT Engineering nanoalloys can enable advanced low‐Pt electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet a challenge remains in terms of the arrangement of multimetallic active sites to simultaneously achieve high cat
content: ABSTRACT Engineering nanoalloys can enable advanced low‐Pt electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet a challenge remains in terms of the arrangement of multimetallic active sites to simultaneously achieve high catalytic activity and stability. In this work, a layer‐engineered dilute Pt 74 Ni 23 Bi 3 nanoalloy is developed as a highly active and stable composition toward alkaline HER, which is achieved via forming atomic‐layered PtNiBi shell on intermetallic PtBi nanoplates followed by a facile acid treatment. The hollow Pt 74 Ni 23 Bi 3 shell exhibits an ultralow overpotential of 7.0 mV at ‐10 mA cm −2 in 1.0 M KOH, owing to its faster Volmer‐Tafel mechanism. The assembled anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) achieves a low cell voltage of 1.656 V at 1.0 A cm −2 and remains steady at industrial current density. Density functional theory calculations further reveal a complementary Pt‐Ni functionality that Ni preferentially anchors H 2 O and stabilizes OH*, whereas neighboring Pt sites provide a slightly more favorable pathway for H 2 O dissociation and a weaker H* binding environment favorable for H 2 formation. This work provides a general strategy to engineer sophisticated nanoalloys at atomic‐scale, and advances the development of high‐performance electrocatalysts in particular.

title: Social and Behavioral Modeling of Community Adoption of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
summary: Hybrid renewable energy systems support decarbonization at the community scale, yet adoption remains uneven and slower than projected by techno-economic models. This paper develops an integrative socio-technical synthesis of the social, beh
content: Hybrid renewable energy systems support decarbonization at the community scale, yet adoption remains uneven and slower than projected by techno-economic models. This paper develops an integrative socio-technical synthesis of the social, behavioral, and institutional drivers of community adoption and links them to formal modeling approaches. A systematic review of peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025 is conducted using a PRISMA-guided protocol. The analysis identifies subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, trust, and governance equity as primary determinants of adoption, while financial incentives act as necessary but insufficient conditions for sustained uptake. The study shows that models grounded only in cost optimization fail to reproduce observed diffusion patterns, whereas approaches that embed behavioral theory capture heterogeneous decision processes and social influence effects. Agent-based modeling emerges as the most suitable framework for representing these dynamics, especially when integrated with constructs from the Theory of Planned Behavior, Technology Acceptance Model, and Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology. Evidence also indicates growing relevance of behavioral economics and digital infrastructures, including peer-to-peer energy trading, in shaping prosumer participation. Geographic imbalance in the literature and limited use of adaptive, data-driven modeling remain key gaps. The paper advances a unified framework that connects behavioral theory, governance design, and computational modeling to improve explanatory power and policy relevance. This framework supports the design of interventions that align incentives, strengthen social acceptance, and enable equitable energy transitions.

title: HIGH-EFFICIENCY TRIPLE-INPUT DC–DC CONVERTER WITH OPTIMIZED DESIGN FOR RENEWABLE POWER SYSTEMS
summary: Small renewable sources such as photovoltaic strings, fuel cells and batteries rarely share a common voltage, and none of these sources comes close to the 120 V bus expected by many auxiliary loads. A triple-input high step-up direct curren
content: Small renewable sources such as photovoltaic strings, fuel cells and batteries rarely share a common voltage, and none of these sources comes close to the 120 V bus expected by many auxiliary loads. A triple-input high step-up direct current to direct current (DC–DC) converter is reported here for exactly that situation. The circuit uses one switched-capacitor branch and three inductor–switch cells fed from 12 V, 24 V and 18 V, and was sized for 120 V at 2 A into a 60 Ω load, roughly the rating of an electric vehicle auxiliary rail. Duty ratios of 0.90, 0.80 and 0.85 set the three gains at 10, 5 and about 6.7. Each inductor (0.27 mH, 0.48 mH and 0.3825 mH) was chosen for the same 0.4 A current ripple, and a 22 µF capacitor holds the output ripple under 1 V at 100 kHz. Losses were estimated term by term: conduction and switching in every metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET), forward drop and reverse recovery in the diodes, copper and core loss in the inductors, equivalent series resistance (ESR) loss in the capacitor, and gate-drive power. The simulated total loss was 3.5 W with V1 alone and 5.75 W with all three inputs, i.e. 98.56% and 97.66% efficiency at 240 W, and the change of output voltage between no load and full load was 1.67%. In the triple-input case, 3.4 W of the 5.75 W was lost in the MOSFETs and diodes, so the switching devices, and not the inductors or the capacitor, limit further improvement. The converter is aimed at renewable source integration, electric vehicle auxiliary supplies and small distributed generation units

title: Entropy-based evaluation of empirical daily global solar radiation models for Mogadishu, Somalia
summary: Accurate estimation of global solar radiation (H) is critical for solar energy system design, building energy simulation, and renewable energy planning, sparticularly in data-scarce regions. This study evaluates four empirical models namely
content: Accurate estimation of global solar radiation (H) is critical for solar energy system design, building energy simulation, and renewable energy planning, sparticularly in data-scarce regions. This study evaluates four empirical models namely the Angström–Prescott (A–P) model, Local Polynomial Regression (LPR), quadratic spline regression, and cubic spline regression for estimating daily H in Mogadishu, Somalia. Models were assessed using conventional statistical metrics ( \(R^2\) , RMSE, MAE, MAPE) and entropy-based indicators (Shannon entropy of residuals, Kullback–Leibler divergence). Results demonstrate that the LPR model achieved superior performance ( \(R^2 = 0.907\) , RMSE = 0.156 kWhm \(^{-2}\) d \(^{-1}\) , 95% CI [0.132, 0.178]; Shannon entropy = 1.679, 95% CI [1.577, 1.917]), compared to the A–P formulation ( \(R^2 = 0.797\) , RMSE = 0.231 kWhm \(^{-2}\) d \(^{-1}\) , 95% CI [0.215, 0.262]). Entropy-based metrics indicated that non-parametric models preserved the statistical structure of observed radiation series, thereby minimizing information loss. The validated LPR estimator offers a deployable baseline for solar resource assessment in regions lacking ground-based meteorological infrastructure, while the locally calibrated A–P coefficients provide a parsimonious, site-adapted formula when sunshine duration data are available.

title: Kinerja Energi PLTS 1.650 Wp untuk Penerangan Parkir dengan ATS (Energy Performance of a 1,650 Wp Solar PV System for Parking Lighting with an Automatic Transfer Switch)
source: JURNAL EDUNITRO Jurnal Pendidikan Teknik Elektro
summary: This study evaluates the energy performance of a nominal 1,650 Wp solar photovoltaic (PV) system installed to support lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang parking building and connected to the PLN grid through an Automa
content: This study evaluates the energy performance of a nominal 1,650 Wp solar photovoltaic (PV) system installed to support lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang parking building and connected to the PLN grid through an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS). Measurements were recorded every 30 minutes from 09:00 to 20:00 Western Indonesian Time over seven days, covering voltage, current, power, energy, and battery state of charge. The summary data report an average PV output power of 351.714 W, while average PLN power on days with an active lighting load was approximately 1,508.990 W. The daily PV energy values listed in the tables range from 0.237 to 0.460 kWh, averaging 0.342 kWh. However, these energy summaries cannot be consistently reconstructed from the full interval data and are therefore not used to quantify PLN energy reduction. A single comparison between the KWS-302 monitor and an AVO meter gives relative differences of approximately 0.88% for voltage and 17.89% for current; current-measurement accuracy is consequently not considered validated. Design calculations indicate a 1,350 W lighting load requiring 5.4 kWh for four hours of operation, whereas the 48 V, 50 Ah battery at an 80% depth of discharge provides a theoretical 1.92 kWh DC, or about 1.82 kWh AC assuming 95% inverter efficiency. The system has been implemented, but further measurements are required to establish a validated energy balance and quantify the reduction in PLN electricity consumption.

title: EFFECT OF VENTILATED FAÇADE ON THERMAL COMFORT IN UNIVERSITY LABORATORIES
summary: The most effective technique for achieving sustainable building is the use of ventilated façades. Achieving thermal comfort in university laboratories and other facilities requires ensuring that building occupants feel comfortable and satis
content: The most effective technique for achieving sustainable building is the use of ventilated façades. Achieving thermal comfort in university laboratories and other facilities requires ensuring that building occupants feel comfortable and satisfied, as this has a direct impact on students' performance. The research aims to investigate the effect of applying ventilated façades, with variable distances from the main façade, on thermal comfort in a laboratory at the University of Mosul, Iraq, under the hot dry climate with hot summers and cold winters, to maximize the ventilated façade's performance. The research uses a simulation method with IES-VE, comparing opaque and perforated ventilated façades. The study evaluates (Predicted Mean Vote) PMV, (Predicted Percentage of Dissatisfied) PPD, Comfort Index, and the number of uncomfortable people for each façade. The results show that using a ventilated façade enhances thermal comfort in Summer, Autumn, and Spring. The study demonstrates that a perforated ventilated façade with a 0.10m air cavity significantly optimizes thermal comfort, offering a sustainable design strategy for educational facilities in arid regions

title: From Shale Independence to Strategic Competition: U.S. and Chinese Energy Policies in the Middle East
summary: The Middle East is at the heart of the energy security of the United States and China, which are the world's two biggest energy consumers. This research compares their energy policies toward the region, and considers the implications of the
content: The Middle East is at the heart of the energy security of the United States and China, which are the world's two biggest energy consumers. This research compares their energy policies toward the region, and considers the implications of the differences for regional stability, economic development and U.S. energy policy. The research design adopted is qualitative, comparative research, which uses secondary data that consists of descriptive trend analysis of IEA and EIA statistics (1960-2022), and comparative policy analysis and thematic review of government documents, think-tank report, and academic articles. The findings illustrate that shale oil and gas production reduced petroleum imports from OPEC and the Persian Gulf States for the U.S. after 2005, heightened the U.S. dependence on Canada, and turned the country into a net petroleum exporter around 2019–2020. However, it is clear that the Middle East is nonetheless of strategic interest to Washington in terms of global price stability and political leverage. The U.S. strategy is primarily military, security and bilateral, while China's strategy is economic, infrastructural (Belt & Road) and renewable energy. While Chinese investment incentivizes diversification, U.S. interventions have at times disrupted regional oil production, while a security order is largely being provided by the United States. The paper suggests that Washington has three options: competition, selective cooperation and disengagement and that the best way to postpone the choice is to give Beijing the upper hand.

title: Implementasi PLTS–PLN dengan Automatic Transfer Switch pada Penerangan Gedung Parkir (Implementation of a Solar PV–Grid System with an Automatic Transfer Switch for Parking Garage Lighting)
source: JURNAL EDUNITRO Jurnal Pendidikan Teknik Elektro
summary: Parking garage lighting needs an uninterrupted power supply, but solar PV output varies with irradiance and weather. This study implements a solar PV–PLN system with an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) for lighting on the seventh floor of th
content: Parking garage lighting needs an uninterrupted power supply, but solar PV output varies with irradiance and weather. This study implements a solar PV–PLN system with an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) for lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang Viktor parking building, and examines how far the field test records support conclusions about battery backup and energy contribution. The system consists of three 550 Wp PV panels, a 60 A MPPT controller, a 48 V 50 Ah battery, an inverter with a 1,500 W continuous rating, and a 63 A two-pole ATS, serving 75 LED lamps of 18 W each (1,350 W). Observations ran for seven days, 09:00–21:00 WIB, with readings every 30 minutes on the PV, battery, and PLN sides. The load was activated in three scenarios (12, 40, and 75 lamps) without controlled repetition. The system was assembled and supplied the lighting load. The design requirement of four hours at full load is 5.4 kWh, while the battery’s usable AC energy is only about 1.82 kWh (80% DoD, 95% inverter efficiency), equivalent to roughly 81 minutes. Transfer to PLN was observed at around 18:30, when battery voltage approached 45 V. Daily PV output was recorded at 275–446 W. On the first day, battery current differed substantially between instruments (11.86 A and 22.12 A), and ATS transfer time and actual irradiance were not recorded. The 50 Ah battery is adequate only for short-term backup. The 45.83% reduction in PLN energy use is a scenario-based estimate. Battery capacity should be matched to the required backup duration, and further work needs controlled loads, calibrated instruments, and per-source energy logging.

title: Meating protein requirements in a more sustainable future: cultivated, plant-based, or hybrid meat?
source: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
summary: Consumption of sufficient protein is fundamental to human growth and overall health. Historically, meat has had a distinct position as the key dietary protein source within the human diet. Meat is considered a high-quality protein source be
content: Consumption of sufficient protein is fundamental to human growth and overall health. Historically, meat has had a distinct position as the key dietary protein source within the human diet. Meat is considered a high-quality protein source because it is easily digested and absorbed and meets all the current indispensable amino-acid requirements. However, the production of sufficient amounts of conventional animal-based protein to meet future global food demands represents a challenge. This has resulted in the development of cultivated meat, plant-based meat, and hybrid analogues offering the potential for greater resource efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare compared with conventional meat. Yet, to date, little is known on the bioavailability and biofunctionality of these meat analogues in humans. Research studies are warranted to assess the in vivo bioavailability and biofunctionality of meat analogues in humans and to identify the factors that may or may not compromise their capacity to stimulate post-prandial muscle protein synthesis rates and, as such, support bodily growth and anabolism. Such research is required to determine whether the transition toward the consumption of more sustainable alternative meat products allows us to meet the increasing global dietary protein demands.

title: Anticipatory Computation: A General Framework for Long-Horizon Computational Demand Forecasting, Future-Condition-Aware Preparation, and Opportunity-Optimized Execution in Artificial Intelligence Systems
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly depend on computational resources whose availability, operational costs, energy requirements, and execution conditions vary across time, locations, and technological environments. Convention
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly depend on computational resources whose availability, operational costs, energy requirements, and execution conditions vary across time, locations, and technological environments. Conventional computing systems predominantly execute tasks when they are requested or become operationally available, while predictive resource management and deferred-computation approaches primarily optimize workloads that are already known or observable within relatively limited planning horizons. This paper introduces Anticipatory Computation (AC), a general computational paradigm that extends beyond immediate execution, conventional predictive computing, and short-horizon workload scheduling. The central principle is to anticipate future computational demand, prepare computational tasks and their associated dependencies in advance, and strategically determine when, where, and under which future conditions those computations should be performed. Rather than treating computational execution as an event that must occur immediately after a task becomes available, AC considers computation as a temporally allocatable process whose preparation, execution, and completion can be strategically distributed across future time horizons. Its optimization objectives are not restricted to economic efficiency. They may include electricity and computing costs, renewable-energy availability, accelerator accessibility, infrastructure capacity, environmental conditions, network availability, data readiness, technological compatibility, computational reliability, and other future operational opportunities. The paper develops a conceptual architecture consisting of long-horizon demand anticipation, computational preparation, future-condition forecasting, opportunity assessment, temporal and spatial execution allocation, and adaptive feedback. A mathematical formulation is introduced to represent the joint optimization of task preparation, execution timing, resource allocation, and multidimensional future conditions. The framework also establishes distinctions between anticipatory computation, predictive computing, precomputation, deferred computation, proactive resource provisioning, and conventional workload shifting. To the best of our knowledge, this paper introduces the first unified conceptual framework specifically centered on long-horizon anticipation, advance preparation, and future-opportunity-dependent execution of computational workloads as a general AI computing paradigm, rather than limiting the problem to energy-aware scheduling or economic resource optimization. The proposed framework is theoretical and methodological; it does not claim experimental validation or demonstrated performance improvements. Its purpose is to establish a research foundation for AI systems capable of strategically organizing computation across extended future horizons.

title: Optimized droop control-based load flow analysis for islanded AC microgrids with electric vehicle integration
summary: Abstract Microgrids have become a crucial element of modern power systems with increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and require an accurate load flow analysis (LFA) to determine the steady state operating conditions of Mic
content: Abstract Microgrids have become a crucial element of modern power systems with increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and require an accurate load flow analysis (LFA) to determine the steady state operating conditions of Microgrid. In islanded configurations, traditional LFA methods are less effective due to the absence of a reference bus. In this type of network, the bus voltage, network frequency, and coupling between droop-controlled distributed generator (DG) introduce additional nonlinear characteristics that are not addressed by conventional LFA formulations. This paper presents an optimized droop control-based Modified Gauss–Seidel (MGS) method for LFA in AC islanded microgrids (IMGs) with integration of static electric vehicle (EV) load models in which voltage and frequency are treated as operating variables due to IMG operation. A bio-inspired optimization is employed to obtain suitable DG droop coefficients with the objective of network loss minimization and maintaining voltage and frequency in an acceptable range with improved DG power sharing. The proposed approach is evaluated on 6-bus and 33-bus AC IMG test networks under diverse static EV load scenarios and is compared with alternative optimization approaches. The optimized droop coefficient achieves active power loss reduction of 23.35%, 10.57%, and 18.97% for EV-1, EV-2, and EV-3 load models, respectively, for inductive DG output impedance mode in 6-bus network. For 33-bus network the loss reductions are 42.38%, 46.18%, and 47.39% correspondingly. In addition an average 2.28% and 1.80% voltage profile improvement are achieved for EV-1 load model for 6-bus and 33-bus test network with corresponding unoptimized scenarios. The results confirm that the proposed technique provides an efficient and flexible framework for adaptive steady state LFA and optimized operation of AC IMG with DG droop control and static EV load model integration.

title: Preselected voltage vector strategy integrated with virtual flux-based predictive direct power control for AC/DC rectifier
summary: Aiming at reducing aging mismatch between phase leg of AC/DC rectifier and increasing lifetime of the leg with the highest aging state, a preselected voltage vector strategy integrated with model predictive virtual-flux-based direct power c
content: Aiming at reducing aging mismatch between phase leg of AC/DC rectifier and increasing lifetime of the leg with the highest aging state, a preselected voltage vector strategy integrated with model predictive virtual-flux-based direct power control is proposed in this paper. Starting from the principle of discontinuous pulse-width modulation technique, the preselected voltage vector strategy determines the clamping regions in the leg with the highest aging state and corresponding voltage vectors that maintain the current status of power switches. Thus, it leads to a reduction of switching loss, resulting in decreased thermal stress and an increase in lifetime of AC/DC rectifier. Different from other approaches, the proposed per-phase technique focuses on relieving the thermal stress of the leg with the highest aging state instead of both three-phase legs to achieve minimum switching loss and thermal stress in the leg. The proposed approach can guarantee the performance of line current harmonic distortion under harmonically distorted supply voltage due to the use of virtual flux vector. Additionally, the proposed technique does not require any extra hardware and is straightforward to implement in practical applications. In this study, besides the proposed technique, conventional model predictive direct power control and conventional model predictive virtual-flux-based direct power control methods are implemented in both simulations and experiments. The obtained performance from three control schemes is evaluated and compared to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of proposed method.

title: The Economics of Technology Leapfrogging
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Economics of Technology Leapfrogging examines how emerging economies can accelerate development by adopting advanced technologies and infrastructure without necessarily reproducing every stage of technological development experienced by
content: The Economics of Technology Leapfrogging examines how emerging economies can accelerate development by adopting advanced technologies and infrastructure without necessarily reproducing every stage of technological development experienced by industrialized countries. The report explores how innovations in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, renewable energy, digital finance, and decentralized manufacturing allow lower-income nations to bypass legacy systems, compress modernization timelines, and achieve sustainable productivity growth. Through empirical analysis of mobile leapfrogging, off-grid solar deployment, and digital public infrastructure, the study evaluates the institutional, human capital, and regulatory preconditions that enable successful technological bypassing while identifying persistent structural barriers that hinder widespread adoption.

title: Το ελληνικό σύστημα χωρίς λιγνίτη: σύγχρονη παραγωγή, αδράνεια και έλεγχος τάσης
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Η μελέτη μετρά, από τα ωριαία αρχεία SCADA του ΑΔΜΗΕ, πόση σύγχρονη παραγωγή (λιγνίτης, φυσικό αέριο, υδροηλεκτρικά) είχε το ελληνικό σύστημα κάθε ώρα το 2024 και το 2025 και πόσες ώρες λειτούργησε χωρίς λιγνιτική παραγωγή: 2.010 ώρες το 20
content: Η μελέτη μετρά, από τα ωριαία αρχεία SCADA του ΑΔΜΗΕ, πόση σύγχρονη παραγωγή (λιγνίτης, φυσικό αέριο, υδροηλεκτρικά) είχε το ελληνικό σύστημα κάθε ώρα το 2024 και το 2025 και πόσες ώρες λειτούργησε χωρίς λιγνιτική παραγωγή: 2.010 ώρες το 2024 και 1.548 το 2025. Εκτιμά την κινητική ενέργεια των σύγχρονων μονάδων μόνο ως εύρος τεσσάρων περιπτώσεων με δηλωμένες παραδοχές, επειδή οι σταθερές αδράνειας και η φαινόμενη ισχύς των ελληνικών μονάδων δεν εντοπίστηκαν στα δημόσια έγγραφα που εξετάστηκαν, και την παραθέτει δίπλα στην πρόταση της ENTSO-E για ελάχιστη σταθερά αδράνειας 2 sMW/MVA, χωρίς να κρίνει αν η Ελλάδα την πληροί. Καταγράφει ό,τι γράφουν ο ΑΔΜΗΕ, η ΡΑΑΕΥ, η ENTSO-E και οι εκθέσεις για τη γενική διακοπή της Ιβηρικής (28/04/2025) για την αδράνεια, τη στάθμη βραχυκύκλωσης και τον έλεγχο τάσης. Δεν είναι μελέτη ευστάθειας, δεν απαντά αν η Ελλάδα πρέπει να αποκτήσει πυρηνική ενέργεια και δεν προτείνει τεχνολογία, προμηθευτή ή θέση. Κάθε αριθμός παραπέμπει σε πηγή με αυτολεξεί απόσπασμα ή σε υπολογισμό με τον τύπο και τις παραδοχές του. Using the hourly SCADA files of IPTO (ADMIE), the study measures how much synchronous generation (lignite, natural gas, hydro) the Greek power system had in every hour of 2024 and 2025, and how many hours it ran without lignite generation: 2,010 hours in 2024 and 1,548 in 2025. It estimates the kinetic energy of the synchronous units only as a range of four cases with stated assumptions, because the inertia constants and apparent power ratings of Greek units were not found in the public documents examined, and sets it beside ENTSO-E's proposal of a minimum inertia constant of 2 sMW/MVA without judging whether Greece meets it. It records what IPTO, the Greek regulator RAAEY, ENTSO-E and the reports on the Iberian blackout of 28 April 2025 write about inertia, short-circuit level and voltage control. It is not a stability study, does not answer whether Greece should adopt nuclear power and does not propose a technology, supplier or site. Every figure cites a source with a verbatim quote or a calculation with its formula and assumptions. The full text is in Greek.

title: ELEPHANT SWARM WATER SEARCH AS A NOVEL METHOD FOR DISSEMINATING DATA ON TRAFFIC IN VEHICULAR AD HOC NETWORKS (VANETS)
summary: This paper focuses on the main agenda of ITS and VANET in solving the major issues related to road & traffic safety. A novel clustering algorithm, Elephant Swarm Water Search Algorithm (ESWSA) combined with Deep Q-Learning (DQL) algorithm f
content: This paper focuses on the main agenda of ITS and VANET in solving the major issues related to road & traffic safety. A novel clustering algorithm, Elephant Swarm Water Search Algorithm (ESWSA) combined with Deep Q-Learning (DQL) algorithm for data dissemination in VANETs is proposed in this study. The proposed method is a new hybrid method which improves significantly compared to conventional clustering methods such as SAMNET, CACONET, ROAONC and CAMONET. The simulation results demonstrate that ESWSA-DQL achieves a 21.3% reduction in the number of clusters, an increase in packet delivery ratio to ≈ 99% from < 90% in other protocols, a decrease in packet drop ratio to < 0.8% from 7–12% in other protocols, and a decrease in average latency to 7 ms from 18–32 ms. Besides, it improves the energy efficiency by almost 20–40% compared to the reference algorithms. The enhancements show that ESWSA-DQL could serve a scalable, energy-efficient and highly reliable communication system for large-scale urban VANETs and real-time ITS applications

title: A spectral-domain multi-strategy Fourier transform optimizer for numerical optimization and robot path planning
summary: Abstract The Fourier Transform Optimizer (FTO) provides a frequency-domain search framework for metaheuristic optimization, but its original spectral operations do not explicitly consider spectral-energy distribution, amplitude–phase-aware
content: Abstract The Fourier Transform Optimizer (FTO) provides a frequency-domain search framework for metaheuristic optimization, but its original spectral operations do not explicitly consider spectral-energy distribution, amplitude–phase-aware information exchange, or multi-resolution spectral manipulation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Spectral-Domain Multi-Strategy Fourier Transform Optimizer, termed MIFTO. Three complementary mechanisms are introduced. First, Spectral Energy Redistribution (SER) adaptively regulates the relative contribution of spectral components through normalized spectral energy and bounded energy redistribution. Second, Cross-Spectral Alignment (CSA) performs phase-reference-preserving cross-individual spectral recombination while maintaining the conjugate symmetry required for real-valued reconstruction. Third, Multi-Resolution Spectral Search (MRSS) partitions the spectrum into low-, middle-, and high-order subspaces and applies differentiated update mechanisms at different spectral resolutions. The proposed method is evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark suite at 30 and 50 dimensions and the CEC2022 suite at 10 and 20 dimensions against eleven representative optimization algorithms. Convergence analysis, statistical distributions, population diversity, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Friedman mean-rank analysis, ablation experiments, and computational-cost analysis are conducted. The results show that MIFTO achieves favorable optimization accuracy and robustness on the majority of the investigated benchmark functions. MIFTO is further applied to robot path planning in 20 × 20, 40 × 40, and 60 × 60 static grid environments. The corresponding mean path lengths are 28.4494, 60.2801, and 107.5165, respectively, and MIFTO obtains the first Friedman rank in all three scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of restructuring the internal spectral search process of FTO and indicate the potential of MIFTO for numerical and constrained path-planning problems.

title: Kinetic investigation of bio-based plasticized AP/HTPB/TDI propellants
source: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
summary: Abstract This study examines how castor oil (CST), palm olein (PLM) and dioctyl adipate (DOA) affect the cure kinetics, processing window and network properties of a highly filled (79.87 wt% solids) AP/Al/HTPB/TDI propellant (NCO/OH = 0.94)
content: Abstract This study examines how castor oil (CST), palm olein (PLM) and dioctyl adipate (DOA) affect the cure kinetics, processing window and network properties of a highly filled (79.87 wt% solids) AP/Al/HTPB/TDI propellant (NCO/OH = 0.94) relative to an unplasticized (UNP) baseline. Cure (ATR-FTIR) and slurry viscosity were followed at 50, 60 and 70 °C for two independent batches per system. Seven kinetic models were ranked by AICc and screened for parameter identifiability by residual bootstrap. The Kamal–Sourour autocatalytic constant was not identifiable; all parameters of a two-step second-order model were. The C = C band at 1620–1660 cm⁻¹, a common internal reference for HTPB, grew about 1.5-fold during cure relative to two independent bands, so results were checked with all three. Castor oil was the only plasticizer that accelerated the cure with every reference (k₁(60 °C) 16.1–17.7 versus 9.1–10.0 × 10⁻³ min⁻¹; t₅₀ 57–62 versus 100–110 min), consistent with its hydroxyl groups acting as co-curative. DOA and PLM cured no faster than UNP, and the late-stage cure of DOA slowed. All plasticizers lengthened the time to the 10⁴ P casting limit at 50 °C (UNP 68 min; CST 119, DOA 127, PLM 138 min), PLM giving the widest and least temperature-sensitive window. Diffusion control at high conversion remained unresolved. With network data for the same formulations (crosslink density 40–54% of UNP), the results show that cure rate, processing window and network structure respond differently to the plasticizer and must be characterized separately.

title: Forecasting-enabled microgrid optimization for adaptive renewable energy planning in remote coastal communities
summary: Remote coastal communities in the Sundarbans of Bangladesh depend on an unreliable distribution grid, yet microgrid planning studies for such sites usually treat demand and renewable generation as fixed inputs and rarely show what forecast
content: Remote coastal communities in the Sundarbans of Bangladesh depend on an unreliable distribution grid, yet microgrid planning studies for such sites usually treat demand and renewable generation as fixed inputs and rarely show what forecast quality means for operation. This study examines whether a grid-connected hybrid microgrid can be both least-cost and resilient for 150 households and three community buildings in Dhangmari, and what operational value hourly forecasting adds to such a design. Long-term NASA POWER resource data and a survey-based demand of 355.3 kWh/day were used in HOMER Pro to compare four configurations, followed by sensitivity analyses of resource, economic, grid-outage and battery-cost parameters and a screening of multi-day outages. Seven machine learning and deep learning models were then benchmarked for hourly load and renewable power forecasting under a chronological, leakage-free protocol, and their errors were converted into battery reserve requirements. The optimal system, combining 102 kW of photovoltaics, 45 kW of wind turbines and 150 kWh of battery storage with the grid, achieved a net present cost of $71,559, an energy cost of $0.0254/kWh and a renewable fraction of 73.4%. Unmet load stayed below 0.08% for 240–560 grid failures per year, and critical loads were fully served during 72-hour outages unless wind and solar generation were both lost. Renewable power was predicted with a coefficient of determination of 0.998 when weather at the forecast hour was known, falling to about 0.94 with 20% weather errors, whereas load accuracy (about 0.81) was bounded by the random variability of the demand profile; the best model, a stacking ensemble, reduced the hourly battery reserve by about one third relative to linear regression. The framework provides a reproducible basis for planning resilient, forecast-aware microgrids in climate-exposed coastal settlements.

title: Causal reliability-gated GRU sensor reconstruction for a reduced-order floating offshore wind turbine under false-data injection
summary: Sensor reconstruction under false-data injection (FDI) is investigated on a control-oriented, reduced-order nonlinear floating offshore wind turbine inspired by the NREL 5-MW rated scale. The model combines empirical aerodynamic maps, surge
content: Sensor reconstruction under false-data injection (FDI) is investigated on a control-oriented, reduced-order nonlinear floating offshore wind turbine inspired by the NREL 5-MW rated scale. The model combines empirical aerodynamic maps, surge–pitch platform dynamics, a single-mass drivetrain and constrained actuators. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) predicts six sensor outputs causally from trusted environmental inputs and previously applied commands. Distinct trajectories are used for training, validation, detector calibration and testing. Offline prediction-confidence weights blend received measurements and predictions after channel-wise residual detection; global detection and full-replacement variants are compared. Across 27 held-out attack/noise scenarios, channel-gated compensation reduces the dimensionless sensor-error metric by 19.02% with a mean paired rotor-speed RMSE reduction of -0.15% relative to the unprotected benchmark. Scenario reductions range from -4.04% to +6.46%, with improvement in 11 of 27 cases; near-zero mean change does not imply scenario-wise performance preservation. Channel improvements range from -3.28% for power to 78.65% for generator torque in the base condition. Reliability gating yields lower rotor-speed RMSE than full replacement in 22 of 27 matched comparisons, but superiority over fixed partial replacement or independent predictors is not established. Single-channel tests reveal limited rotor-speed attack detection: recall is 4.42% for a rotor-speed-only attack, and the clean rotor-speed false-alarm rate is 12.48%. Reliable feedback-channel protection and guaranteed post-attack recovery are not established. Vector error identities, a conditional mean-square benchmark, controller-command sensitivity, and a finite-horizon perturbation bound explain the relationship between reconstruction and regulation. The study establishes a reproducible evaluation framework for reconstruction and controller-aware assessment; its internal ablations do not separately establish advantages of the GRU architecture and the confidence-weighting rule.

title: A novel dual-switched inductor and switched capacitor converter with low ripple current and high voltage gain for a low-voltage fuel cell stack
summary: In this paper a non-isolated dual switched inductor-switched capacitor (DSI-SC) converter is proposed. This converter is designed for high-efficiency power conversion in applications using a low-voltage fuel cell stack. The topology is deve
content: In this paper a non-isolated dual switched inductor-switched capacitor (DSI-SC) converter is proposed. This converter is designed for high-efficiency power conversion in applications using a low-voltage fuel cell stack. The topology is developed to reduce the input current ripple, component voltage stress, enhance the voltage gain and thereby improve the performance of the system. The proposed DSI-SC converter is specifically designed to boost the output voltage of a fuel cell electric vehicle. Fuel cell technology is an important energy source for electric vehicles. The fuel cell stacks are the fundamental components of this technology. A high-voltage fuel cell stack requires additional fuel cells to produce enough power for an electric vehicle. But the heavier you make the electric vehicles, the more fuel cells you put in the stack. Moreover, fuel cells have a problem with loads with abrupt changes. The impact of the input ripple current is noticeable at high load currents. The proposed DSI-SC converter is therefore well suited for a low-voltage fuel cell stack, as it can provide high voltage gain with low current ripple at the input. The DSI-SC converter has been verified by hardware testing and modelling at a 400 V/400 W load.

title: The Economics of Distributed Renewable Energy
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Economics of Distributed Renewable Energy: Expanding Electricity Access, Productive Capacity and Energy Security Through Decentralized Systems. Examines how decentralized solar-plus-LFP mini-grids, productive agro-processing loads, smar
content: The Economics of Distributed Renewable Energy: Expanding Electricity Access, Productive Capacity and Energy Security Through Decentralized Systems. Examines how decentralized solar-plus-LFP mini-grids, productive agro-processing loads, smart PAYG telemetry, under-the-grid franchises, and FX-hedged blended finance accelerate electricity access and rural productive transformation (31 pages, 16 data visuals, Series #14, HH-2026-45).

title: ENHANCEMENT METHODS OF COOLING PHOTOVOLTAIC PANELS (PVS): A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
summary: Photovoltaic systems have contributed greatly to converting solar energy into electrical energy, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and lessening pollution. However, there are problems with the systems that make their efficiency low or li
content: Photovoltaic systems have contributed greatly to converting solar energy into electrical energy, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and lessening pollution. However, there are problems with the systems that make their efficiency low or limited. One of the most important issues is that their efficiency decreases as their temperature rises. This study aims to give a general and comprehensive review of photovoltaic system cooling techniques while showing the developments that have taken place in this area. The cooling methods are classified into two: passive cooling which does not need any external energy and active cooling which needs external energy plus hybrid cooling involving different technologies. If you clean the modules on a regular basis, they can work up to 35% better. If you don't clean them, they can work up to 80% worse. The paper shows that indeed there has been progress in so far as photovoltaic system cooling methods are concerned. Further research, accompanied by other materials as well as geometrical shapes, can even make the systems more efficient, hence attaining optimum performance and making them survive longer

title: Multi-stage optimal allocation of power system resources using a combination of deep reinforcement learning and chance-constrained programming
summary: Abstract With a high proportion of renewable energy integration, power system resource allocation faces the challenge of co-optimizing long-term dynamic uncertainties and probabilistic security constraints. Traditional deterministic program
content: Abstract With a high proportion of renewable energy integration, power system resource allocation faces the challenge of co-optimizing long-term dynamic uncertainties and probabilistic security constraints. Traditional deterministic programming and stochastic optimization methods struggle to balance economy, flexibility, and security. This paper constructs a multi-stage resource optimization allocation method that combines Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Chance Constrained Programming (CCP). To address the problem that resource allocation is difficult to adapt to the evolution of system state during long-term planning, a dynamic decision-making environment including new energy, energy storage, demand response, and network regulation resources is constructed. The Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm is used to learn the nonlinear mapping between state and configuration actions to achieve multi-stage in-distribution adaptability during rolling stages. For the problem of insufficient safety constraints in the configuration strategy, the CCP mechanism is applied to convert the new energy output error and load fluctuation into probabilistic safety constraints. Economic optimization and safety control coordination are achieved through risk feedback and Lagrange multiplier updates, and combined with the rolling deduction mechanism, the subsequent resource allocation path is continuously revised based on stage status feedback. The experiment constructs an equivalent test scenario based on the characteristics of new energy development in Jiangsu Province. The results show that, under the condition of high proportion of new energy access, the method in this paper reduces the total cost of the planning cycle by 8.5% compared with the second-best Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) method, increases the flexibility margin to 0.84, and keeps the frequency of constraint violations stably within 5%. Research shows that the method presented in this paper achieves comprehensive optimization of the economy, flexibility and security of resource allocation in uncertain new energy environments, providing an intelligent dynamic allocation decision-making method for long-term resource planning of power systems.

title: Digital green nudges and energy-saving behaviour among university students: a Stimulus-Organism-Response approach
summary: This study examines associations among university sustainability support, digital green nudges, peer energy-saving norms, and self-reported energy-saving behaviour using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework. A cross-sectional offl
content: This study examines associations among university sustainability support, digital green nudges, peer energy-saving norms, and self-reported energy-saving behaviour using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework. A cross-sectional offline questionnaire survey conducted in India yielded 691 usable responses from a purposively selected sample. Covariance-based structural equation modelling was used to evaluate seven hypothesised relationships among eight constructs. University sustainability support and digital green nudges were positively associated with energy-saving awareness; awareness was positively associated with green self-efficacy, which, in turn, was positively associated with energy-saving attitude. Attitude and peer energy-saving norms were positively associated with energy-saving intention, and intention, in turn, was positively associated with self-reported energy-saving behaviour. The contribution is an integrative application of SOR to institutional, digital, and social cues in a university context, rather than establishing a new causal mechanism. The findings identify relationships relevant to the design and evaluation of campus sustainability initiatives.

title: An Analysis Of Legal And Regulatory Framework On Renewable Energy In India With Special Refernce To SDG 7
source: HPNLU Journal of Environment & Disaster Management
summary: India has actively promoted renewable energy through various policies and legal frameworks, aligning with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7. Its objective focuses on ensuring universal access to affordable, reliable, s
content: India has actively promoted renewable energy through various policies and legal frameworks, aligning with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7.
