content: Εθνικό Μετσόβιο Πολυτεχνείο Σχολή Χημικών Μηχανικών Τομέας Σύνθεσης και Ανάπτυξης Βιομηχανικών Διαδικασιών Διπλωματική Εργασία Μελέτη της ποιότητας ανάφλεξης των φυτικών ελαίων και των μεθυλεστέρων των λιπαρών οξέων ως υποκατάστατων των συμβατικών καυσίμων.Αντωνίου Γ. Ελένη Επιβλέπων Καθηγητής: Δημήτριος Καρώνης Αθήνα, Ιούνιος 2026 Πρόλογος Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εκπονήθηκε κατά το ακαδημαϊκό έτος 2025-2026 στο Εργαστήριο Τεχνολογίας Καυσίμων και Λιπαντικών της Σχολής Χημικών Μηχανικών ΕΜΠ, υπό την επίβλεψη του Καθηγητή κ.Δημήτριου Καρώνη.Θα ήθελα να εκφράσω τις θερμές μου ευχαριστίες στον επιβλέποντα καθηγητή, κύριο Δημήτριο Καρώνη, για την πολύτιμη επιστημονική καθοδήγηση, την άριστη συνεργασία και την ουσιαστική συμβολή του.Η εμπειρία και οι γνώσεις του συνέβαλαν καθοριστικά στην ολοκλήρωση της παρούσας μελέτης.Επίσης θέλω να ευχαριστήσω τα μέλη του Εργαστηρίου Τεχνολογίας Καυσίμων και Λιπαντικών για τη προθυμία και τη βοήθειά τους σε όλη τη διάρκεια της διεξαγωγής των πειραμάτων.Οι χρήσιμες υποδείξεις, καθώς και η τεχνική τους κατάρτιση συνέβαλαν στην ευκολότερη προσαρμογή μου στο εργαστήριο, όπως επίσης και στην επιτυχή ολοκλήρωση των πειραματικών διαδικασιών.Τέλος, ευχαριστώ τους γονείς μου για την στήριξη, την εμπιστοσύνη και την υπομονή τους, καθώς και τους φίλους μου για τη συμπαράσταση και την ενθάρρυνση που μου έδειξαν καθ΄ όλη τη διάρκεια των σπουδών μου.των βιοκαυσίμων και στην αξιολόγηση της δυνατότητας αξιοποίησής τους ως υποκατάστατα συμβατικών καυσίμων στον τομέα των χερσαίων και θαλάσσιων μεταφορών.

title: Hydrocarbon Production of Botryococcus braunii in a Photobioreactor: Optimization of Irradiance and Mixing Regimes
summary: The slow growth of Botryococcus braunii impedes its large-scale cultivation as a feedstock for biofuel production despite its high hydrocarbon content. This study investigates how light and mixing regimes affect the growth performance of th
content: The slow growth of Botryococcus braunii impedes its large-scale cultivation as a feedstock for biofuel production despite its high hydrocarbon content. This study investigates how light and mixing regimes affect the growth performance of this green alga in a newly designed flat-plate photobioreactor. Three light intensities (75, 150 and 300 μmol s−1 m−2) and three mixing rates (0.95, 1.10 and 1.25 L L−1 min−1) were used to evaluate algal biomass and hydrocarbon production. The algal performance was then compared with a static culture under the same light and mixing conditions as in the photobioreactor. The results showed that light and mixing regimes significantly affected both biomass and hydrocarbon production in B. braunii. The best algal performance was obtained under high irradiance (300 μmol s−1 m−2) and medium mixing (1.10 L L−1 min−1). Mixing had no significant effect on biomass and hydrocarbon production under low light intensity (75 μmol s−1 m−2), while the high mixing rate (1.25 L L−1 min−1) reduced algal biomass at all light intensities. We again compared algal performance between the photobioreactor and the static culture system under the same light and mixing conditions to evaluate system efficacy. The photobioreactor produced 4.04- and 1.97-fold higher algal biomass and hydrocarbon yields, respectively, than the static culture. An independent study validated these results, showing that biomass growth and hydrocarbon production of B. braunii in the photobioreactor were 3.97-fold and 1.91-fold higher than in static culture, respectively. Therefore, a photobioreactor can increase biomass and hydrocarbon production in this slow-growing B. braunii under laboratory conditions, offering a promising strategy for future exploration of oil-producing algal species towards commercial production.

title: Wind–Solar Climate-Resource Adequacy in Semi-Arid Iraq: Reconstructed ERA5 Diagnostics and Conditional CMIP6 Models
summary: Mean-resource assessments miss days when wind and PV potential are simultaneously weak. Wind–solar resource indicators were reconstructed for the Al-Shahabi region in southeastern Iraq using 227,928 hourly ERA5 time steps across 12 grid cel
content: Mean-resource assessments miss days when wind and PV potential are simultaneously weak. Wind–solar resource indicators were reconstructed for the Al-Shahabi region in southeastern Iraq using 227,928 hourly ERA5 time steps across 12 grid cells during 1995–2020. Conditional resource responses were subsequently assessed using five CMIP6 models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5.WPD is calculated from hourly 100 m wind vectors and air density; a temperature-adjusted PV proxy is derived from hourly horizontal irradiation. Historical 20th-percentile (P20) thresholdsdefine comparable low resource days. The mean wind power density was 296.74 W m⁻², while the mean daily temperature-adjusted PV resource indicator was 0.7508 kWh m⁻² d⁻¹. Simultaneous deficiencies occur on 643/9497 (6.77%) days, mostly in boreal winter. For four future scenario–horizon combinations, the equal-weight five-model mean WPD changes −3.19% to −6.98% (all five models are reduced under transfer assumptions), while concurrent low-resource frequency changes range from −0.20 to +0.63 percentage points (pp) in the ensemble mean and are not signed consistently among individual models. Sensitivity analyses show strong seasonality dependence of thresholds and wind change amplitude transferred. These results separate a relatively coherent mean wind-resource response from much less robust compound-deficitbehaviour. Because monthly change signals are imposed on historical sequences, the adjusted daily episodes are conditional threshold outcomes but not predictions for weather persistence or operational electricity system reliability.

title: RESPONSIBLE TOURISM AS THE MAIN MECHANISM FOR ACHIEVING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN GEORGIA
summary: This study examines the role of sustainable tourism development in a country’s socio-economic progress and the effective utilization of its natural resource potential. The paper explores the prospects for developing "green" tourism in Georg
content: This study examines the role of sustainable tourism development in a country’s socio-economic progress and the effective utilization of its natural resource potential. The paper explores the prospects for developing "green" tourism in Georgia, current trends, and the primary challenges hindering the sector's sustainable growth. Georgia possesses significant potential to become a hub for sustainable tourism within the region. However, the sector's development is accompanied by complex issues, such as: ecological pressure on popular tourist destinations caused by mass tourism; a lack of "green" infrastructure in the regions; the absence of national standards for eco-certification; and the risk of losing authenticity due to chaotic urban development. Based on a qualitative methodology and content analysis of the data, the study analyzes the necessity of maintaining a balance between economic growth and environmental interests. It has been shown that transitioning to a sustainable model of tourism requires promoting community-based tourism (CBT), strengthening state regulations, and raising awareness among the local population.

title: Beyond IMEC: Stratified Resilience and the Limits of Flagship Connectivity in EU-India Geoeconomic Strategy
summary: Abstract The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), launched in September 2023, was framed as the most ambitious EU-India geoeconomic initiative in two decades and a counter-architecture to China’s Belt and Road Initiative. With
content: Abstract The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), launched in September 2023, was framed as the most ambitious EU-India geoeconomic initiative in two decades and a counter-architecture to China’s Belt and Road Initiative. Within weeks, the October 2023 Gaza conflict paralysed its western corridor, exposing a dependence on the political consent and transit access of third-party states that neither partner commanded. Yet EU-India cooperation did not collapse. This paper asks why cooperation persisted unevenly across sectors. The paper identifies stratified resilience as the observed pattern of uneven cooperation persistence, and explains it through institutionalisation depth: the density of bilateral frameworks in place before the disruption. Digital cooperation continued through three post-disruption Trade and Technology Council (TTC) milestones, a stock-taking meeting in November 2023 and ministerial meetings in February 2025 and July 2026, while negotiations on the EU-India FTA (Free Trade Agreement), including its Digital Trade chapter, concluded in January 2026 on a separate track. Energy cooperation persists through the Clean Energy and Climate Partnership (CECP), with EU-side commitment but no Indian central government commitment established in the sources examined. Transport, lacking any standing bilateral framework, shows IMEC persisting only declaratorily. Theoretically, the paper distinguishes announcement capacity from implementation capacity in geoeconomic statecraft, arguing that institutional density accumulated through iterative negotiation sustains cooperation under geopolitical stress. The argument is developed through process-tracing of official EU and Indian documents from October 2023 to July 2026, with falsification conditions specified.

title: Simultaneous Reduction of Silver and Indium in Silicon Heterojunction Solar Cells via Contact Transport Engineering
summary: ABSTRACT Silver (Ag) and indium (In) represent the two major material cost drivers in silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells, yet their reduction strategies are typically developed independently. Whether Ag‐lean metallization remains comp
content: ABSTRACT Silver (Ag) and indium (In) represent the two major material cost drivers in silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells, yet their reduction strategies are typically developed independently. Whether Ag‐lean metallization remains compatible with In‐lean transparent conductive oxides (TCOs) is still unclear. This work presents a systematic study integrating screen‐printed Ag‐lean pastes, including silver‐coated copper (Cu@Ag) and silver‐coated nickel (Ni@Ag), with three TCO configurations: indium tin oxide (ITO), an ITO/tin oxide (SnO X ) bilayer, and SnO X . The compatibility between Ag‐lean metallization and In‐lean TCOs is governed by the interplay between metallization properties and TCO‐dependent transport characteristics. The contact transport behavior of Ag‐lean metallization exhibits strong dependence on the carrier concentration of the underlying TCO. As carrier concentration decreases, thermally activated transport becomes increasingly important, consistent with the increased contact losses observed for lower‐carrier‐density TCOs. Combined with Cu@Ag paste, the ITO/SnO X bilayer achieves 25.62% efficiency with material cost reduction exceeding 65% relative to a conventional Ag‐ITO reference. Ni@Ag paste is demonstrated in high‐efficiency SHJ solar cells, achieving 25.02%. Device simulations further identify pathways for improving efficiency and reducing material consumption. These results provide a practical pathway toward combining Ag‐lean metallization with In‐lean TCO architectures in high‐efficiency SHJ solar cells.

title: Human rights due diligence and investment governance: Evidence of an emerging economy
summary: This article examines Presidential Regulation No. 60 of 2023 on the National Strategy for Business and Human Rights as an emerging yet incomplete instrument of corporate and investment governance in Indonesia. Drawing on normative legal res
content: This article examines Presidential Regulation No. 60 of 2023 on the National Strategy for Business and Human Rights as an emerging yet incomplete instrument of corporate and investment governance in Indonesia. Drawing on normative legal research and statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches, it analyses the Regulation alongside Indonesia’s Investment Law, Company Law, and the Financial Services Authority’s (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, OJK) sustainable finance framework. It also compares Indonesia’s approach with the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) and the approaches adopted by Japan, Germany, France, and the European Union. The article argues that the central challenge is not simply the absence of mandatory Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD), but also regulatory fragmentation across investment licensing, corporate governance, sustainable finance, ESG reporting, supply chains, and accountability mechanisms. It proposes reframing Presidential Regulation No. 60 of 2023 as a bridge regulation and develops a five-layer, ESG-based HRDD investment governance model encompassing investment licensing; corporate governance; sustainable finance and ESG reporting; supply-chain due diligence; and remedy and accountability. Indonesia should progressively integrate HRDD into existing regulatory instruments rather than immediately adopt a comprehensive, European-style mandatory due diligence statute.

title: From the CNR to the Birth of the National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology: a Virtuous Pathway
summary: Due to the severe damages caused by earthquakes in Italy, Guglielmo Marconi decided to activate the National Institute of Geophysics (ING) as a branch of the National Research Council (CNR) in 1936. The ING eventually became an independent
content: Due to the severe damages caused by earthquakes in Italy, Guglielmo Marconi decided to activate the National Institute of Geophysics (ING) as a branch of the National Research Council (CNR) in 1936. The ING eventually became an independent institute in 1945. The present Italian Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia, INGV) was created in 1999 merging together the ING, three institutes of the CNR (the “Istituto di Geochimica dei Fluidi” in Palermo, the “Istituto del Rischio Sismico” in Milan, the “Istituto Vulcanologico Internazionale” in Catania), plus the independent historical Vesuvius Observatory in Naples, established in 1841. This merger created one of the major geoscience institutions in Europe with more than 1100 people and 26 locations, handling a vast number of infrastructures distributed all over the country, monitoring the Earth. Therefore, the CNR was the primary incubator of INGV, which has now three departments focused on Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Environment, focusing on the natural risks and resources. The seismic, geodetic, magnetic, geochemical networks and laboratory facilities provide powerful tools to investigate the planet. The seismic, geodetic, magnetic, geochemical networks and laboratory facilities provide powerful tools to investigate the planet and are the natural connection with the universities. Research institutes and the academic world have the common goal of advancing the scientific knowledge; they contribute with scientists, the research institutes with expensive and distributed infrastructures, the universities with scientists and students, which can be guided both by university professors and scientists of the institutes. The two sides of the coin are the fundamental ecosystem for the scientific development. The European Union should have a continental federated geoscience institute, like the United States Geological Survey (USGS), fostering the studies on the Earth and supporting the political guidance by a strong scientific advice for the research, monitoring and surveillance of the seismic, volcanic, climatic, and hydrogeological risks, but also providing useful tools for discovering new resources and raw materials.

title: Breaking the Thermal Limits: Solvation Chemistry of Hydrogel Electrolytes for Extreme‐Temperature Stable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for safe and cost‐effective energy storage, yet their practical deployment across a wide temperature range is severely constrained by temperature‐dependent ion‐transport
content: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for safe and cost‐effective energy storage, yet their practical deployment across a wide temperature range is severely constrained by temperature‐dependent ion‐transport limitations and electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability. At low temperatures, sluggish Zn 2+ transport and desolvation promote concentration polarization and nonuniform Zn deposition, while elevated temperatures accelerate water‐induced parasitic reactions, corrosion, and interfacial degradation. Hydrogel electrolytes offer opportunities to address these challenges by regulating water activity, Zn 2+ solvation, ion transport, and interfacial mechanics within an integrated polymer network. This review systematically elucidates five representative design strategies: high‐entropy environments, water‐deficient hydrogels, deep eutectic solvent‐mediated regulation, zwitterionic networks, and nanofiller reinforcement, with particular emphasis on their effects on Zn 2+ coordination, water organization, transport kinetics, and interfacial stability. Quantitative solvation and kinetic descriptors, including coordination numbers, ion‐pair populations, diffusion coefficients, transference numbers, interaction energies, and activation energies, are compared to clarify how electrolyte structure influences performance at different temperatures. The advantages and limitations of the five strategies are further compared in relation to their applicable temperature‐dependent challenges. Finally, key priorities are discussed for temperature‐resolved solvation characterization, operando analysis, practical cell evaluation, and standardized thermal testing, providing guidance for the development of hydrogel electrolytes toward reliable wide‐temperature AZMBs.

title: Batas Kewenangan Host State Control dalam Hilirisasi dan Divestasi Saham: Menyeimbangkan Kepentingan Nasional dan Perlindungan Investor Asingdi Sektor Pertambangan Mineral Indonesia
summary: Kebijakan hilirisasi dan kewajiban divestasi saham merupakan instrumen host state control yang diterapkan Indonesia di sektor pertambangan mineral untuk memperkuat pengendalian negara atas kekayaan alam berdasarkan Pasal 33 UUD 1945. Namun,
content: Kebijakan hilirisasi dan kewajiban divestasi saham merupakan instrumen host state control yang diterapkan Indonesia di sektor pertambangan mineral untuk memperkuat pengendalian negara atas kekayaan alam berdasarkan Pasal 33 UUD 1945. Namun, kebijakan tersebut berpotensi menimbulkan sengketa dengan investor asing, khususnya klaim indirect expropriation dan pelanggaran standar fair and equitable treatment (FET). Penelitian hukum normatif ini menggunakan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan kasus melalui analisis deskriptif kualitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kewenangan negara dalam mengatur hilirisasi dan divestasi saham perlu dinilai melalui doktrin police powers, prinsip proporsionalitas, serta panduan UNCTAD mengenai ekspropriasi dan FET. Regulasi yang bertujuan publik yang sah, nondiskriminatif, proporsional, dan melalui prosedur yang layak cenderung berada dalam ruang police powers negara. Sebaliknya, regulasi yang menimbulkan interferensi berlebihan terhadap hak investor dan menghilangkan nilai investasi secara substansial dapat dikualifikasikan sebagai indirect expropriation, yang sah hanya jika disertai kompensasi dan, bila tidak, menimbulkan tanggung jawab negara. Perlindungan investor asing juga dapat ditempuh melalui penyelesaian sengketa investor-negara berdasarkan perjanjian investasi bilateral Indonesia yang berlaku. Selain itu, perubahan norma yang meniadakan ekspektasi sah investor yang dibentuk oleh jaminan spesifik negara tanpa justifikasi kepentingan publik yang memadai dapat melanggar standar FET. Oleh karena itu, kebijakan tersebut perlu diterapkan secara proporsional dan nondiskriminatif.

title: A context-token transformer framework for multi-resident smart home human activity recognition with comparative evaluation against recurrent architectures
summary: Human Activity Recognition has emerged as a key enabling technology for context-centric intelligent home environments, facilitating applications such as ambient intelligence, healthcare monitoring, assisted living, and elderly residents mon
content: Human Activity Recognition has emerged as a key enabling technology for context-centric intelligent home environments, facilitating applications such as ambient intelligence, healthcare monitoring, assisted living, and elderly residents monitoring. Despite substantial advancements in conventional Human Activity Recognition strategies as well as intelligent learning-based Human Activity Recognition mechanisms, reliable and robust activity recognition in real-world intelligent home environments remains challenging due to contextual ambiguity, overlapping activity patterns, and significant inter- and intra-subject variability, typically in multi-resident situations. In this paper, we present a comprehensive investigation of a unified context-aware Human Activity Recognition architecture for intelligent smart home environments, explicitly evaluated both single-resident and multi-resident activity recognition. In this work, four representative Deep Learning architectures, specifically Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention, Cascading Long Short-Term Memory, TransformerHAR, and the Patch and Context-Token-Transformer-based framework, were comprehensively investigated across single-resident and multi-resident smart home environments to measure their effectiveness under varying levels of activity complexity and resident interactions. The extensive experiments, validated through cross-validation and repeated-trial robustness analysis, are conducted using MARBLE and CASAS-Kyoto datasets to investigate performance under both single-resident and multi-resident smart home environments. These experimental results indicate that the Patch and Context Based Token Transformer framework accomplishes competitive performance in single-resident multiple activity recognition settings while significantly enhancing activity recognition performance in multi-resident settings, attaining an average accuracy of 69.38% compared with 58.66% (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention), 58.96% (TransformerHAR), and 60.41% (Cascading Long Short-Term Memory with Attention) for these competing baselines. Further, comprehensive class/activity-wise, confusion-matrix, and convergence investigations validate that the context-token conditioning competently assists in improving activity disambiguation, learning/training stability, and generalization, typically in multi-resident scenarios characterized by overlapping sensor patterns, concurrent activities, and complex contextual interactions.

title: Topology-Aware Federated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Dual-Level Voltage Regulation in PV-Rich Distribution Grids
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: Photovoltaic (PV) generation with high penetration in the distribution networks causes voltage rise, voltage deviation and three-phase imbalance between connected Medium-Voltage (MV) and Low-Voltage (LV) feeders. In this paper, a topology-c
content: Photovoltaic (PV) generation with high penetration in the distribution networks causes voltage rise, voltage deviation and three-phase imbalance between connected Medium-Voltage (MV) and Low-Voltage (LV) feeders. In this paper, a topology-conscious federated multi-agent reinforcement learning is introduced to subordinated dual-level voltage regulation in PV-rich distribution grids. The given approach represents the network as a graph and implements the state encoding with the help of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to ensure that every agent is able to represent local electrical state and local topology. Both LV control nodes are considered independent reinforcement learning agents, and the federated aggregation provides the means of updating shared parameters of the model without sharing the raw local measurements. The structure is aimed at minimizing MV voltage violations and LV phase unbalance collaboratively when there are different conditions of PV penetration and communication. The technique is tested on a stochastic load and PV test system on the IEEE 33-bus distribution test system. The findings show that voltage regulation and phase-balancing performance are enhanced when using the centralized RL strategy instead of baseline centralized RL and traditional MARL strategies. The research identifies the promise of topology-conscious learning and federated coordination in the provision of scalable voltage control in privacy-sensitive smart grid systems.

title: What do large language model panels add to multi-criteria decisions? Order-invariant q-rung dual hesitant preference aggregation and a hybrid supercapacitor case study
summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) increasingly replace human experts in multi-criteria decision analysis, but their contribution to decisions computable from published data is rarely examined. This is studied with q-rung dual hesitant f
content: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) increasingly replace human experts in multi-criteria decision analysis, but their contribution to decisions computable from published data is rarely examined. This is studied with q-rung dual hesitant fuzzy preference relations elicited from five LLMs of five developers. The standard group relation, built with the weighted geometric operator and a reciprocity rebuild, depends on the order of the criteria; a q-power-mean aggregation with row-sum priority weights is proved to be order invariant, to preserve the q-rung constraint and to keep every weight positive, and without consensus adjustments the results depend on each hesitant set only through the means of the q-th powers of its degrees. In a hybrid supercapacitor selection problem built from verified full-cell data, the standard construction yields up to 26 rankings over the criterion orderings, the proposed construction one; the elicited judgments, however, shift with the order of the prompt (four permutation tests, p ≤ 0.009). Single central judgments per entry reproduce the hesitant-set rankings. With the decision table in the prompt, all 18 direct-data configurations reproduce the LLM-pipeline ranking; without it, the LLM performance judgments diverge from the evidence and change the ranking. Under ranking by multi-objective optimization by ratio analysis plus the full multiplicative form, resampling of models and sessions places the lithium-ion capacitor first in 0.748 (standard) and 1.000 (fixed-bound variant) of the draws; with literature source rows also resampled and the rebuilt table as performance matrix, the shares are 0.533 and 0.504. The LLM judgments are not validated against human experts.

title: High condition index and distinct biochemical profiles in triploid Crassostrea gigas cultured at a high-energy open-water site
summary: High-energy open-water (HEO) sites are increasingly being explored as alternatives to conventional coastal oyster farms, yet their suitability for triploid Pacific oysters remains poorly documented. This study compared the physiological con
content: High-energy open-water (HEO) sites are increasingly being explored as alternatives to conventional coastal oyster farms, yet their suitability for triploid Pacific oysters remains poorly documented. This study compared the physiological condition and tissue biochemical composition of a single cohort of triploid Crassostrea gigas cultured for 7 months at three Korean grow-out environments: an independently moored HEO site located approximately 1.3 km from an operating offshore wind farm, a sheltered subtidal bay, and an intertidal flat exposed to regular emersion. Biometric observations were made on 30 oysters from three culture units per site and are reported descriptively. Biochemical analyses were based on three pooled composites per site, one from each culture unit. Oysters sampled from the HEO site showed smaller mean shell size and whole weight but greater mean soft tissue mass and the highest mean condition index (29.2%), compared with 13.9–15.0% at the coastal sites. Proximate composition differed among the three sites, with HEO oysters showing higher mean crude fat, ash, and carbohydrate fractions but a lower mean crude protein concentration. Within the diethyl ether extract, oleic acid and DHA showed their highest mean relative proportions at HEO, whereas EPA and ARA showed their highest mean relative proportions at the intertidal Gochang site. These findings provide initial site-specific evidence that independently moored HEO culture is compatible with high tissue condition in triploid oysters, and that tissue biochemical composition at this site differed from that of the two coastal sites. However, because site, culture system, and environmental conditions varied simultaneously, the findings should not be interpreted as an isolated test of hydrodynamic exposure or proximity to the offshore wind farm.

title: Climate-Adaptive Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems: An R-Based Digital Twin for Optimizing Energy Reliability and Environmental Health Resilience in Coastal Bangladesh
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: An R-based digital twin research framework for exploring climate conditions, hybrid renewable energy generation, battery storage, electricity reliability, and healthcare-critical energy resilience in coastal Bangladesh.
content: An R-based digital twin research framework for exploring climate conditions, hybrid renewable energy generation, battery storage, electricity reliability, and healthcare-critical energy resilience in coastal Bangladesh.

title: A Low-Cost Embedded System for Non-Technical Loss Detection in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: A low-cost wireless embedded system was developed and evaluated for the local and real-time detection of non-technical losses caused by electrical bypasses in low-voltage service drops. The architecture consists of two ESP32-based measureme
content: A low-cost wireless embedded system was developed and evaluated for the local and real-time detection of non-technical losses caused by electrical bypasses in low-voltage service drops. The architecture consists of two ESP32-based measurement nodes equipped with PZEM-004T V3 modules and interconnected through ESP-NOW. Node A measures the electrical variables at the service connection point, whereas Node B acquires the billing-point variables, processes the received telemetry, and displays the operating status through a local web dashboard. The detection model incorporates the estimated resistive loss of the service drop and applies a current-dependent dynamic threshold to distinguish technical losses from unexplained power discrepancies. Measurement pairs are validated through sequence identification, timestamp-based synchronization, and wireless-link quality criteria before classification. The experimental campaign comprised 40 scenarios, including 20 controlled tests and 20 different residential service drops with conductor cross-sectional areas of 6 and 10 mm², lengths from 4 to 25 m, and different load profiles. Thirty-eight acquisitions satisfied the established quality criteria. The system obtained 9 true positives, 28 true negatives, 0 false positives, and 1 false negative, corresponding to an accuracy of 97.37%, sensitivity of 90.00%, specificity of 100.00%, and precision of 100.00%. The ESP-NOW link achieved an overall packet error rate of 0.79% and a mean transmission latency of 4.36 ms. The results show that technical-loss compensation and acquisition-quality control reduce false alerts under the evaluated high-load, transient, and nonlinear operating conditions.

title: Green Mobile Computing: A Review of Energy-Aware Smartphones, Cellular Radio Access, Edge Intelligence and Smart Grid Analytics
source: International Journal Of Scientific Research In Engineering & Technology
summary: Mobile devices, cellular networks and the computing services behind them now form a large and growing source of electricity demand in the information and communication sector. A smartphone drains its battery through the screen, the radio an
content: Mobile devices, cellular networks and the computing services behind them now form a large and growing source of electricity demand in the information and communication sector. A smartphone drains its battery through the screen, the radio and background applications, while the network that serves it spends most of its energy in base stations that stay powered even when traffic is light. Research on these problems is split across mobile software, wireless networking, edge computing and power-system communities, each optimizing its own layer. The objective of this review is to bring these strands into one picture that follows energy from the handset, through the radio access network and the edge or cloud, to the buildings and grids that supply the power. The review organizes 41 studies into a five-layer taxonomy and compares their aims, methods and reported outcomes. Device-level studies point to screen state, radio signalling, application wake-ups and user behaviour as the main drivers of handset energy use, and a mapping study found user behaviour to be the factor most often linked to battery drain. Network studies show that sleep modes and lean carrier designs can cut a large share of radio access energy, and that one set of architectural measures could reduce total mobile network energy by roughly a third. Edge studies report that energy-aware offloading and federated training can reduce system energy, with one study reporting savings of up to 59.5%. Grid studies show that machine learning now supports load forecasting, smart metering and the control of hybrid renewable plants. Few studies measure energy across more than one layer, and the energy cost of the learning models themselves is rarely reported. Future work should develop cross-layer energy accounting, shared benchmarks and lightweight models that remain efficient on constrained devices.

title: CARMA report WP4: Scalability to the international level
summary: The transition towards climate-neutral energy systems will require both sustainable carbon resources and large quantities of renewable electricity. This report summarizes results from the CARMA-Green Fuels project concerning three interconn
content: The transition towards climate-neutral energy systems will require both sustainable carbon resources and large quantities of renewable electricity. This report summarizes results from the CARMA-Green Fuels project concerning three interconnected questions: the future global availability of biomass for fuels and its geographical implications; the role of biomass within the global carbon balance; and the techno-economic implications of locating green fuel production in different regions across the world. A critical review of global biomass assessments shows an exceptionally wide range of estimated biomass availability towards 2050, from approximately 40 to 1,500 EJ/year. The divergence is driven mainly by assumptions regarding agricultural yields, technological development, the use of marginal and degraded land, dietary change, and the treatment of competing demands for food, feed, materials and ecosystem services. From a carbon perspective, biomass cannot be regarded simply as an additional carbon-neutral resource: soil carbon, land-use change, alternative material uses, biodiversity restoration and the potential role of BECCS all affect its climate value. Finally, techno-economic assessments of green ammonia and e-methanol show that geographical location can strongly influence production costs. Regions with high-quality wind and solar resources can compensate for long transport distances, making imported green fuels competitive with or cheaper than domestic Danish production. However, self-sufficiency and security of supply are not considered. The combined results therefore point towards a future in which sustainable biomass is treated as a constrained carbon resource, while electricity-intensive green-fuel production is increasingly influenced by geographical differences in renewable-resource quality.

title: METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL TERMINOLOGICAL COMPETENCE IN ARCHITECTURE STUDENTS THROUGH PROJECT-BASED LEARNING (PBL)
summary: This article examines a methodology for developing the professional terminological competence of architecture students through Project-Based Learning (PBL). The study emphasizes that effective architectural education requires students not o
content: This article examines a methodology for developing the professional terminological competence of architecture students through Project-Based Learning (PBL). The study emphasizes that effective architectural education requires students not only to memorize specialized terms but also to understand, interpret, and apply them accurately in authentic professional communication. The research analyzes the content of professional terminological competence, the pedagogical potential of PBL, and mechanisms for integrating terminology acquisition with architectural project activities. The proposed methodology consists of five interconnected stages: diagnostic preparation, terminological preparation, project implementation, professional presentation, and reflection. The findings indicate that project-based instruction facilitates contextual acquisition of architectural terminology, productive vocabulary use, professional communication, collaborative learning, and greater terminological accuracy.

title: A Photo‐Assisted Calcium−Oxygen Battery Based on Dipole Heterogeneity Regulation
summary: ABSTRACT Calcium–oxygen (Ca–O 2 ) batteries represent an attractive energy‐storage technology that offers the potential for high energy density through reversible CaO 2 /O 2 chemistry. However, practical Ca−O 2 batteries are largely limited
content: ABSTRACT Calcium–oxygen (Ca–O 2 ) batteries represent an attractive energy‐storage technology that offers the potential for high energy density through reversible CaO 2 /O 2 chemistry. However, practical Ca−O 2 batteries are largely limited by the formation of an inert discharge product and intrinsically sluggish reaction kinetics, which lead to large polarization. Here, we report a rechargeable Ca–O 2 battery with an ultralow overpotential of 1.11 V via a photo‐assisted strategy based on dipole heterogeneity regulation. Dynamic light‐driven charge transport within the cell establishes favorable oxygen diffusion pathways and electrochemical reaction routes, significantly improving the transport efficiency of O 2 and charge carriers. Theoretical simulations elucidate the kinetic origin of this light‐enhanced process, revealing that regulating the reaction routes for CaO 2 formation and decomposition is effective in lowering the product‐decomposition energy barrier. The resulting photo‐assisted Ca−O 2 battery system achieves a round‐trip efficiency of 66.12% under illumination, revealing the effectiveness of the dipole‐heterogeneity‐enabled photo‐assisted strategy for Ca−O 2 electrochemistry. This work not only provides a strategy to mitigate the inherent kinetic limitations of traditional Ca–O 2 batteries but also provides insights for the development of new photo‐assisted energy storage systems.

title: Biogenic Fabrication of ZnO‐Ag Nanocomposites Using Chia Seed Extract for Enhanced Photocatalytic Degradation of Textile Dyes in Wastewater
source: Journal of the Chinese Chemical Society
summary: ABSTRACT The rising leakage of synthetic dyes into water bodies has increased the demand for effective and eco‐friendly remedial technology. In this study, zinc oxide (ZnO), silver (Ag), and ZnO‐Ag nanocomposites were produced by traditiona
content: ABSTRACT The rising leakage of synthetic dyes into water bodies has increased the demand for effective and eco‐friendly remedial technology. In this study, zinc oxide (ZnO), silver (Ag), and ZnO‐Ag nanocomposites were produced by traditional chemical and green synthesis procedures employing Salvia hispanica L. (chia seed) extract as a natural reducing and capping agent. UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, GC–MS, XRD, DLS, zeta potential, and SEM–EDX analysis confirmed the effective development of crystalline nanostructures of the produced nanoparticles. The biogenic nanomaterials showed lower particle size, better dispersion, and less aggregation than chemically synthesized nanomaterials. The photocatalytic activity of individual ZnO, Ag, and ZnO‐Ag nanocomposites was tested for the degradation of Congo Red and Methylene Blue under UV and visible irradiation. The green ZnO‐Ag nanocomposites exhibited the best photocatalytic effectiveness among all synthesized materials, with degradation efficiencies of 97.75% and 95.89% for Congo Red and Methylene Blue, respectively, within 60 min. The enhancement in performance was due to the synergistic interaction between ZnO and Ag, better charge separation, and the good shape of the biogenic nanocomposites. The degradation followed pseudo‐first‐order kinetics with the greatest rate constant value of 0.06235 min −1 . These results indicate that the chia seed‐based green synthesis is an eco‐friendly route for producing efficient ZnO‐Ag nanocomposites with great promise for photocatalytic wastewater treatment.

title: A semi-empirical closed-form healthy-state baseline model for online junction temperature monitoring of high-power IGBTs across a wide current operating range
source: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
summary: Abstract IGBTs are core devices in high-power electronic equipment, and online monitoring of their junction temperature is of great significance for ensuring safe device operation and condition assessment. Junction-temperature monitoring ba
content: Abstract IGBTs are core devices in high-power electronic equipment, and online monitoring of their junction temperature is of great significance for ensuring safe device operation and condition assessment. Junction-temperature monitoring based on static current–voltage characteristics measured at different temperatures is one of the key technical approaches. Existing data-based or polynomial-fitting models for describing IGBT current–voltage characteristics rely heavily on experimental data and exhibit limited applicability or insufficient accuracy over a wide current operating range. Moreover, a unified closed-form healthy-state baseline model capable of characterizing device behavior under multiple operating conditions is still lacking. Based on the fundamental semiconductor physics of IGBTs, this paper proposes a three-dimensional semi-empirical closed-form healthy-state baseline model that correlates the on-state voltage drop, collector–emitter current, and junction temperature, and validates the proposed model experimentally using three different IGBTs. The results show that the proposed three-dimensional mapping model can characterize the on-state current–voltage characteristics under different operating conditions using a unified set of characteristic parameters. Good predictive capability is achieved over a temperature range of 25–105 °C, a current range extending to approximately 4.5 times the rated current, and a gate-drive voltage range of 15–24 V. The maximum absolute junction-temperature estimation errors at gate-drive voltages of 15, 20, and 24 V are 1.50, 2.91, and 1.05 °C, respectively. While maintaining applicability over a wide current operating range, the proposed model reduces its dependence on experimental data and demonstrates good practical applicability, providing an effective healthy-state baseline for subsequent aging-condition assessment of IGBTs.

title: Disaggregating Green Growth: GGGI Sub-Indicators and Undernourishment in 107 Economies
summary: Composite indices of green growth summarize environmental and development performance in a single number and can hide sub-indicators that move with food security in opposite directions. Using data for 107 economies over 2010–2024, we ask wh
content: Composite indices of green growth summarize environmental and development performance in a single number and can hide sub-indicators that move with food security in opposite directions. Using data for 107 economies over 2010–2024, we ask which components of the Green Growth Index of the Global Green Growth Institute remain associated with the prevalence of undernourishment once each country’s level of development is accounted for. Each sub-indicator is tested against undernourishment before and after controlling for income and human development; p-values are adjusted for multiple testing, and the remaining associations are re-estimated in a five-year panel that separates between-country and within-country variation. Between 92% and 94% of the variation in undernourishment is between countries. A composite built from all components except undernourishment loses its association once income is controlled for, while six components survive in at least 20 of 22 specifications. Water and sanitation, clean fuels, and universal health coverage go with less undernourishment; the disease burden from unsafe water, the urban population in slums, and the renewable energy share go with more. The last two are the most stable under continuous development controls and in a Tobit model for 163 countries. Aggregate green growth scores, we conclude, largely reflect development.

title: Analysis of Attitude Toward Green Financing in Support Net Zero Emission by 2060 Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB): A Perspective from MSMEs
summary: Net Zero Emission (NZE) 2060 has become Indonesia’s national aspiration to achieve a carbon-neutral economy by 2060 that the banking sector has reinforced its role as a key catalyst in promoting environmentally sustainable economic activiti
content: Net Zero Emission (NZE) 2060 has become Indonesia’s national aspiration to achieve a carbon-neutral economy by 2060 that the banking sector has reinforced its role as a key catalyst in promoting environmentally sustainable economic activities, particularly through the provision of green credit, financing, and investment. This study examines the behavior of green MSMEs toward Green Financing in supporting NZE 2060 based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). The research focuses on green MSMEs located in four districts/cities in the Special Region of Yogyakarta (DIY), aiming to analyze the determinants of their behavioral intention to access Green Financing. The study applies the 10-times rule sampling technique and collects primary data from 62 respondents using a Likert scale (1–5) questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS 4.0. The findings reveal that Attitude does not significantly influence Behavioral Intention among green MSMEs actors in accessing Green Financing.

title: Removal of Total Petroleum Hydrocarbons from Simulated Crude Oil Contaminated Seawater Using Plantain Stem Derived Biosorbent
summary: Abstract This study investigated the application of plantain stem biosorbent for the removal of total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) from simulated crude-oil-polluted seawater. The prepared contaminated seawater exhibited a slightly acidic co
content: Abstract This study investigated the application of plantain stem biosorbent for the removal of total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) from simulated crude-oil-polluted seawater. The prepared contaminated seawater exhibited a slightly acidic condition (pH 6.47), salinity of 8.51 ppt, and an initial TPH concentration of 213.48 mg L⁻¹. The biosorbent was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis to evaluate its surface properties and adsorption potential. The results confirmed the presence of oxygen-containing functional groups, porous morphology, and carbon-rich composition suitable for hydrocarbon adsorption. A three-factor Box–Behnken design was employed to optimize the effects of adsorbent dosage, adsorption time, and particle size on TPH removal. The quadratic model was statistically significant (F-value = 109.02, p < 0.0001) with a high coefficient of determination (R² = 0.9929), indicating good agreement between predicted and experimental values. The optimum conditions were obtained at an adsorbent dosage of 2 g L⁻¹, contact time of 20 min, and particle size of 70 µm, achieving a predicted TPH removal efficiency of 95.63%. Adsorption equilibrium analysis showed that the Langmuir model provided a better fit than the Freundlich model, suggesting monolayer adsorption on the biosorbent surface. The study demonstrates that plantain stem, an abundant agricultural residue, is a promising low-cost and sustainable biosorbent for petroleum hydrocarbon remediation in contaminated seawater.

title: Real-Time Energy Management System for Optimal Scheduling of EV Charging in Renewable Microgrids
source: International Journal for Modern Trends in Science and Technology
summary: Coordinating electric-vehicle (EV) charging with renewable generation can reduce diesel dispatch, but the added value of predictive optimization depends on the comparator, forecast error, and economic assumptions. This paper evaluates a lin
content: Coordinating electric-vehicle (EV) charging with renewable generation can reduce diesel dispatch, but the added value of predictive optimization depends on the comparator, forecast error, and economic assumptions. This paper evaluates a linear-programming receding-horizon energy management system (EMS) for an islanded photovoltaic–wind–diesel microgrid with optional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation. A reproducible synthetic benchmark includes eight deterministic cases, 100 uncertainty realizations shared by four controllers, renewable profile sensitivity, reoptimized peak-penalty sensitivity, and offline optimization references. Under nominal inputs, the EMS reduces total diesel energy by 1.52% and EV-attributable diesel energy by 70.09% relative to uncontrolled charging. Its additional benefit over renewable-aware charging is 11.18 kWh of diesel and 61.48 USD in the daily surrogate operating cost. Under uncertainty, the EMS meets all EV targets in every run and reduces diesel energy by a mean 1009.94 kWh relative to uncontrolled charging. Relative to renewable-aware charging, however, it uses 219.85 kWh more diesel on average while reducing peak dispatch by 52.42 kW and the surrogate cost by 91.29 USD. V2G reduces the deterministic event peak by 385 kW; its economic valuation depends strongly on the assumed peak penalty. The results establish an energy–peak–service tradeoff for the evaluated model rather than universal controller superiority or hardware realtime validation.

title: GLOBAL ECONOMIC UNCERTAINTY AND GEORGIA
summary: Global economic uncertainty is a major challenge facing the contemporary world economy. Geopolitical tensions, shifts in international trade, inflationary pressures, and financial market volatility have particularly significant implications
content: Global economic uncertainty is a major challenge facing the contemporary world economy. Geopolitical tensions, shifts in international trade, inflationary pressures, and financial market volatility have particularly significant implications for small and open economies. This study examines the key drivers of global economic uncertainty and analyses their impact on Georgia’s economic development, with particular emphasis on foreign trade, foreign investment, tourism, and macroeconomic sustainability. The research draws on secondary data and academic literature using qualitative, descriptive, and comparative methods. The findings identify risks associated with the Georgian economy’s dependence on external factors, as well as opportunities to strengthen its economic resilience. The study emphasizes economic diversification, developing domestic production and exports, improving the investment climate, and preserving macroeconomic stability.

title: Hybrid stacking and logistic regression meta-model for credit card fraud detection using SMOTE and multiple machine learning algorithms
summary: Abstract This study presents a stacking ensemble framework for credit card fraud detection on the imbalanced Kaggle dataset, using SMOTE to address class imbalance. Base classifiers (RF, SVM, KNN, NB, GB, LR) are evaluated with accuracy, pr
content: Abstract This study presents a stacking ensemble framework for credit card fraud detection on the imbalanced Kaggle dataset, using SMOTE to address class imbalance. Base classifiers (RF, SVM, KNN, NB, GB, LR) are evaluated with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with RF and KNN emerging as the strongest learners, reaching 97% recall and 0.98 F1-score after SMOTE. The final ensemble employs RF and KNN as base learners with Logistic Regression as the meta-classifier, and pairwise prediction correlations (r ≈ 0.34 for RF–KNN vs. r ≈ 0.81 for RF–GB) confirm that RF and KNN form a more diverse and complementary pair. A refined stacked hybrid using RF–KNN–GB with meta-features and original data achieves the best trade-off for fraud and intrusion detection, obtaining 0.975 recall with only one false positive, 0.9968 precision, 0.986 F1-score, and accuracy of 0.9997, outperforming existing hybrid methods. These findings demonstrate that carefully designed ensembles and feature engineering can deliver robust fraud detection on highly imbalanced data, surpassing individual models and reported

title: Land-use input choice and policy-relevant environmental and sustainability indicators: a sensitivity assessment for Brazil
summary: Abstract Global assessments of climate, biodiversity, and ecosystem services rely on projections of land-use change (LUC), typically from integrated assessment models (IAMs) at coarse resolution (25 to 50 km) and downscaled to the 30 to 300
content: Abstract Global assessments of climate, biodiversity, and ecosystem services rely on projections of land-use change (LUC), typically from integrated assessment models (IAMs) at coarse resolution (25 to 50 km) and downscaled to the 30 to 300 m required by biophysical models. The choice of LUC projection introduces large variation in results, but this variation is rarely assessed. For Brazil, we systematically compare two LUC projections, a regionally calibrated model (Land Use and Cover Change Modelling Environment, LuccME) and a global product (Land-Use Harmonization 2, LUH2), downscaling both to 300 m with the Spatial Economic Allocation Landscape Simulator (SEALS) and computing five sustainability indicators (biomass carbon, biodiversity intactness, water yield, Forest Code compliance, and a diffuse-nitrogen index). The differences are large, from −37 to +45 % for biomass carbon, −20 to +23 % for water yield, −76 to +12 % for the diffuse-nitrogen index, and −0.27 to +0.17 in mean species abundance. The choice between the two projections also flips the Forest Code compliance call on 9 to 26 % of Brazil's land grid cells, and several biome-level shifts reverse sign under an alternative class correspondence, a sensitivity we quantify. Differences of this size could materially affect sustainability analyses, including REDD+ accounting, where a shifted carbon baseline could change results-based payments, as well as biodiversity assessment and nature-related financial-risk analysis.

title: Improving technical training for the mining sector in West Africa through digital learning: a case study
summary: The economy of Burkina Faso heavily relies on mining, which requires qualified technicians for production asset maintenance. However, higher education institutions face challenges in practical engineering training due to insufficient modern
content: The economy of Burkina Faso heavily relies on mining, which requires qualified technicians for production asset maintenance. However, higher education institutions face challenges in practical engineering training due to insufficient modern equipment, resulting from constrained financial resources in developing countries. The existing literature highlights this problem in southern African countries and other parts of the world, and explores the implementation of simulators, virtual reality, and augmented reality in student training. Yet little has been paid to the specific context of technical higher education institutions in Burkina Faso and francophone West African countries. This exploratory qualitative case study assesses the state of practical training equipment and the potential of virtual learning tools to improve student readiness for key sectors such as mining. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews ( N = 7 participants: 6 academic staff and 1 mining industry representative), workshop observations, and a structured survey of former students ( N = 8) with experience in the mining sector. Given the single-institution focus and the limited sample size, the findings are contextual and not broadly applicable. Yet they provide the first detailed assessment in this context and offer insights that can inform future multi-site research. Findings reveal high student-to-machine ratios (ranging from 6:1 to 42:1), absence of simulators and modern training benches, and equipment that is outdated compared to that used by local mining companies. These findings suggest that the phased adoption of a training model that integrates low-cost digital tools could improve access to quality practical training and better prepare students for the increasing demands of the mining sector. This research provides the first detailed assessment of mechanical engineering training equipment in Burkina Faso and offers practical recommendations for similar contexts across francophone West Africa.

title: Alkali-catalyzed transesterification of coconut and sunflower oils for biodiesel production
summary: Introduction: Biodiesel represents a promising renewable energy source because it is biodegradable, environmentally friendly, and can reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Coconut and sunflower oils, with their relatively high oil content and
content: Introduction: Biodiesel represents a promising renewable energy source because it is biodegradable, environmentally friendly, and can reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Coconut and sunflower oils, with their relatively high oil content and availability, are potential renewable feedstocks for biodiesel production. Materials and methods: Coconut and sunflower oils were converted into biodiesel through alkali-catalyzed transesterification using NaOH as the catalyst and methanol as the transesterifying agent at an oil-to-methanol volume ratio of 5:1. The reaction was conducted at 60 °C and atmospheric pressure for 60 min. The produced biodiesel was purified by water washing and drying, followed by evaluation of density, kinematic viscosity, and calorific value. Results: Distinct biodiesel- and glycerol-rich phases were observed after transesterification, providing qualitative evidence of product formation and phase separation. Coconut biodiesel exhibited a density of 723 kg/m 3 , kinematic viscosity of 5.59 mm 2 /s, and calorific value of 34.58 MJ/kg, whereas sunflower biodiesel showed 812 kg/m 3 , 3.61 mm 2 /s, and 39.32 MJ/kg, respectively. Both biodiesels showed kinematic viscosities within the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D6751-02 range of 1.9–6.0 mm 2 /s. Sunflower biodiesel exhibited fuel properties closer to conventional diesel. Conclusions: Coconut and sunflower oils are potential renewable feedstocks for biodiesel production. Sunflower biodiesel showed comparatively more favorable physicochemical properties and better fuel quality. These findings provide useful information for developing alternative renewable fuels and reducing fossil diesel use.

title: EvEMTBench, a simulation based dataset of faults and events for machine learning in power systems: Code for Data Generation
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Overview The integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources into electric grids challenges conventional power system protection. Machine learning-based solutions can address these challenges by utilizing available data in modern sma
content: Overview The integration of inverter-based renewable energy sources into electric grids challenges conventional power system protection. Machine learning-based solutions can address these challenges by utilizing available data in modern smart grids. However, the lack of open datasets prevents reproducibility and fair comparisons between different approaches and their results, which hinders further progress. Therefore, we propose EvEMTBench, a synthetic dataset of faults and events generated using electromagnetic transient simulations. The physical plausibility of the power system simulation is ensured by validating the simulation parameters against established literature and providing a comprehensive documentation of the simulation procedure. The dataset is designed for training, fine-tuning, and benchmarking machine learning models by providing synchronized point-on-wave voltage and current measurements at 9600 Hz across a diverse set of topologies and voltage levels. The inclusion of a wide range of fault and operating events allows the utilization of EvEMTBench for different tasks like incipient fault detection, fault localization or event detection. The dataset is available on FAUDataCloud and the generation code is available on GitHub as well as this repository on Zenodo. Usage Guide This repository contains the code to generate the dataset. It was tested with Python 3.9 and PowerFactory 2025. The main entry point is "main_datagen.py" - this script orchestrates the dataset generation pipeline. "create_datasets.py" provides higher-level dataset creation functionality. Please refer to the readme.md file for further instructions on how to execute the code to generate custom versions of the dataset. Use Cases The dataset can be used for a wide range of power system protection related tasks, including fault detection, fault classification, fault line indentification, fault localization and fault area classification. Additionally, the dataset can be used for broader tasks like event classification and localization or incipient fault detection.

title: Lattice‐Defined sp ‐ d ‐ p Orbital Hybridization in Ordered InNCo 3 Antiperovskite Enables Efficient Oxygen Reduction for Zn‐Air Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Regulating orbital hybridization provides a direct means to balance oxygen‐intermediate adsorption and desorption during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Yet translating this principle into uniform and controllable orbital coup
content: ABSTRACT Regulating orbital hybridization provides a direct means to balance oxygen‐intermediate adsorption and desorption during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Yet translating this principle into uniform and controllable orbital coupling within a structurally well‐defined catalyst remains challenging. Here we construct atomically ordered antiperovskite InNCo 3 nanoparticles, whose periodic lattice defines a sp ‐ d ‐ p hybridization motif for efficient ORR. Relative to Co 4 N, ordered occupation of corner sites by In expands the lattice and promotes N sp ‐Co d ‐In p hybridization, shifting the Co d ‐band center from −1.45 to −1.07 eV. This shift strengthens *O 2 /*OOH binding and lowers the potential‐limiting free‐energy change from 1.02 eV in Co 4 N to 0.47 eV in InNCo 3 . In situ Raman spectroscopy shows a larger fraction of four‐hydrogen‐bonded water in the electric double layer, consistent with greater hydrogen‐bond connectivity that may facilitate intermediate protonation. InNCo 3 delivers a half‐wave potential of 0.85 V and retains 98% of its initial current after 14 h at 0.6 V, exceeding Pt/C in both activity and stability. An InNCo 3 ‐based Zn‐air battery reaches a peak power density of 220 mW cm −2 , far surpassing that of the Pt/C (128 mW cm −2 ). These results link crystallographic ordering to controlled multi‐orbital hybridization in alkaline ORR catalysts.

title: MAPEAMENTO ENERGOAMBIENTAL DO MEIO ANTRÓPICO PARA USINAS FOTOVOLTAICAS NA REGIÃO DE PRESIDENTE PRUDENTE/SP
summary: A expansão da geração fotovoltaica centralizada representa uma das principais estratégias para a diversificação da matriz elétrica e a promoção da transição energética, exigindo metodologias capazes de identificar áreas tecnicamente viáveis
content: A expansão da geração fotovoltaica centralizada representa uma das principais estratégias para a diversificação da matriz elétrica e a promoção da transição energética, exigindo metodologias capazes de identificar áreas tecnicamente viáveis, ambientalmente sustentáveis e socialmente compatíveis para empreendimentos de grande porte. Este trabalho desenvolve um estudo de mapeamento energoambiental aplicado a usinas fotovoltaicas centralizadas com potência entre 50 MW e 300 MW, com ênfase nos condicionantes do meio antrópico. A metodologia proposta, denominada Metodologia de Mapeamento Energoambiental para Usinas Fotovoltaicas Centralizadas (MMEA-FV), fundamenta-se em revisão bibliográfica, análise documental e integração de critérios energéticos, ambientais e antrópicos, contemplando variáveis como irradiação solar, declividade do terreno, proximidade da infraestrutura elétrica, uso e ocupação do solo, distância de áreas urbanizadas, comunidades tradicionais e áreas ambientalmente protegidas, ponderadas pelo método Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), que atribuiu pesos de 0,40 ao grupo energético, 0,20 ao ambiental e 0,40 ao do meio antrópico, e integradas no Índice de Aptidão Energoambiental Fotovoltaica (IAEF). A metodologia foi aplicada em um estudo de caso na Região Administrativa de Presidente Prudente (SP), identificando áreas prioritárias com potencial de aproximadamente 405 MW e geração anual estimada de 850 GWh. Os resultados demonstram que a integração sistemática de variáveis técnicas, ambientais e do meio antrópico aumenta a eficiência do processo de seleção de áreas, reduz impactos territoriais e subsidia o planejamento energético sustentável, constituindo instrumento de apoio a órgãos de planejamento, investidores e agentes do setor elétrico.
