title: Skill power as soft power? China’s Luban workshops and the transformation of Sino-African relations
summary: Skill power as soft power? This article introduces “skill power” as a novel mechanism of state influence grounded not in cultural appeal but in the strategic provision of technical and vocational competencies that generate attraction throug
content: Skill power as soft power? This article introduces “skill power” as a novel mechanism of state influence grounded not in cultural appeal but in the strategic provision of technical and vocational competencies that generate attraction through demonstrable outcomes. Drawing on comparative discourse and document analysis of China’s Luban Workshops in Kenya and Ethiopia, we identify two divergent of skill power: Kenya’s model emphasizes rapid digital skills acquisition, vendor-linked certification and entrepreneurship aligned with the national digital economy agenda, whereas Ethiopia’s approach prioritizes industrial automation capabilities and trainer-of-trainers diffusion across national vocational systems. Across both cases, influence operates through three mechanisms: human capital formation linked to employability outcomes, institutional embedding of pedagogical practices and technical standards, and ecosystem entrenchment through vendor-associated technologies and certifications. However, these gains entail technological path dependencies because vendor-specific training and equipment ecosystems may constrain host-country technological choice. The study therefore conceptualizes skill power as a relational and conditional form of influence, whose durability depends on local ownership, institutional capacity, technological diversification, and alignment with national development priorities. We conclude with policy recommendations for national skills compacts, technology-neutral curricula and joint lifecycle financing to maximize developmental benefits while safeguarding technological pluralism and long-term institutional sustainability.

title: Optical Nanosensors
summary: Nanosensors based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), including colorimetric devices, are described. Among fiber-optic nanosensors, Fabry–Perot reflectometric optochemical nanosensors employing
content: Nanosensors based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), including colorimetric devices, are described. Among fiber-optic nanosensors, Fabry–Perot reflectometric optochemical nanosensors employing single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNTs) and optical fibers, in-fiber nanocavity sensors, and fiber-optic nanosensors for probing living cells stand out prominently. A nanograting-based optical accelerometer is discussed. Examples of fluorescent pH-sensitive nanosensors are a renewable glass nanopipette with fluorescent dye molecules, a ratiometric pH nanosensor, and pH-sensitive microcapsules with nanoparticle incorporation in the walls. Disadvantages of optical fibers and fluorescent nanosensors for live-cell studies are outlined. Photonic explorer or probe for bioanalysis with biologically localized embedding (PEBBLE) nanosensors are useful for exploring the intracellular environment. Quantum dots serve as fluorescent labels. Several quantum dot Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based probes have been developed, namely, probes for the determination of protein, protease, and maltose, as well as the dissociation constant between Rev (Regulator of Virion Expression) and Rev response element (RRE). Electrochemiluminescent nanosensors enable remote detection, while crossed zinc oxide nanorods serve as resistive ultraviolet (UV) nanosensors.

title: Designing A Sustainable Cloud Efficiency Model for Reducing Carbon Footprint in Large-Scale IT Operations
source: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: The exponential growth of cloud computing has transformed global IT infrastructure, but it has also led to escalating energy consumption and carbon emissions. This review explores the development of a sustainable cloud efficiency model aime
content: The exponential growth of cloud computing has transformed global IT infrastructure, but it has also led to escalating energy consumption and carbon emissions. This review explores the development of a sustainable cloud efficiency model aimed at minimizing the carbon footprint of large-scale IT operations while maintaining computational performance and reliability. It examines the intersection of cloud architecture, data center optimization, renewable energy integration, and intelligent workload management. Key focus areas include energy-efficient virtualization, dynamic resource provisioning, AI-driven predictive analytics for power usage optimization, and carbon-aware scheduling strategies. The study also evaluates the role of sustainability metrics such as Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) in assessing environmental performance. Furthermore, emerging green computing paradigms, including edge-cloud synergy and circular hardware lifecycle management, are reviewed as integral components of sustainable digital transformation. By synthesizing recent advancements in carbon-efficient data center design and policy frameworks supporting green ICT, this paper proposes a comprehensive model that aligns operational efficiency with environmental responsibility. The findings underscore the potential of intelligent sustainability-driven architectures to achieve net-zero carbon objectives and promote responsible cloud innovation for the digital economy.

title: Urban metabolic performance and spatiotemporal evolution in central Beijing: a community-scale emergy accounting study
summary: Introduction Urban areas are central to resource consumption and carbon emissions, yet community-scale metabolic mechanisms remain underexplored, particularly when green-space ecosystem services are incorporated into emergy accounting. Meth
content: Introduction Urban areas are central to resource consumption and carbon emissions, yet community-scale metabolic mechanisms remain underexplored, particularly when green-space ecosystem services are incorporated into emergy accounting. Methods Taking the 305.8 km 2 central area of Beijing as a case and communities as analytical units, this study develops a community-scale emergy accounting framework for 2011, 2014, 2017, and 2020. Green-space carbon sequestration and oxygen release are included as explicit output emergy. Results Emergy per area (EPA) was high and spatially uneven. Emergy per capita (EPP) was higher in 2020 than in 2011 in most communities, and its spatial disparities narrowed. The emergy yield ratio (EYR) remained below 1. The environmental loading ratio (ELR) rose from mostly 3-10 in 2011 to above 10 in many communities by 2020, and the environmental sustainability index (ESI) remained below 1. Within this accounting framework, expanding green space within community boundaries can only marginally improve the direct accounted output emergy and cannot raise ESI above 1; the limiting factor is the renewable fraction of external supporting flows. With only four observation years, these temporal changes cannot be attributed to specific policies as opposed to interannual fluctuations. Discussion Differentiated community governance should prioritize energy-efficiency retrofits and circular economy pilots in low-EYR areas, functional green infrastructure in high-ELR areas, and, more fundamentally, an increase in the renewable fraction of external supporting flows. The study advances community-scale urban metabolism accounting for SDG 11 while highlighting boundary, data, and methodological limitations.

title: Nonlinear optimal control of a four-wheel autonomous electric vehicle driven by a VSI-fed BLDC motor
source: Journal of Electrical Systems and Information Technology
summary: Abstract The article proposes a nonlinear optimal control method for a four-wheel autonomous vehicle driven by a VSI-fed BLDC motor. The dynamic model of the autonomous EV is formulated by integrating the state-space descriptions of the fou
content: Abstract The article proposes a nonlinear optimal control method for a four-wheel autonomous vehicle driven by a VSI-fed BLDC motor. The dynamic model of the autonomous EV is formulated by integrating the state-space descriptions of the four-wheel autonomous ground vehicle, of the three-phase permanent magnet brushless DC motor, and of the three-phase DC/AC inverter which is connected to batteries. It is proven that the dynamic model of the autonomous EV is differentially flat. Next, the state-space description of the autonomous EV undergoes approximate linearization with the use of first-order Taylor series expansion and through the computation of the system’s Jacobian matrices. The linearization takes place at each sampling instance around a temporary operating point which is defined by the present value of the EV’s state vector and by the last sampled value of the EV’s control inputs vector. For the approximately linearized model of the system an H-infinity feedback controller is designed. To select the feedback gains of the H-infinity controller an algebraic Riccati equation is solved at each time-step of the control algorithm. The global stability properties of the control scheme are proven through Lyapunov analysis. The nonlinear optimal control method ensures precise following of reference paths in the XY plane by the autonomous EV, as well as convergence of all state variables of the EV to the targeted setpoints. The variations of the control inputs are kept moderate. The proposed nonlinear optimal control method is a simple yet efficient solution for the design of low-cost autonomous electric vehicles.

title: Nonreductive Catalytic Cyclizations of Carbon Dioxide into Synthons for Fine-Chemical, Pharmaceutical, and Polymer Applications
summary: Conspectus Nature enables the transformation of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen via photosynthesis representing a crucial chemical process for life on earth. This carbon fixation process also helps to balance the global car
content: Conspectus Nature enables the transformation of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen via photosynthesis representing a crucial chemical process for life on earth. This carbon fixation process also helps to balance the global carbon cycle controlling the uptake of carbon from the atmosphere. Ever since the industrial revolution, anthropogenic carbon emissions have increased at such a pace resulting in an imbalance of the carbon cycle and, as a consequence, effects known as global warming and the occurrence of more extreme weather patterns. The “excess” of carbon dioxide is commonly perceived as waste, with little to no value to humanity. Thus, ideally technologies able to transform this waste carbon into value-added compounds and materials would be economically of interest to various communities. The principal technology to complement the chemical diversification that Nature can provide for carbon dioxide conversion is catalysis. Catalysis offers an approach to activate substrates in different ways building on diverse reactivity principles and contemplating on the possibility to activate CO2 directly or the coreactant. This includes the use of Brønsted or Lewis bases, transition metals, photo- and organo-catalysis, offering us a wide variety of activation modes. In this Account, we feature our extensive efforts in the area of catalytic carbon dioxide conversion with a particular emphasis on the activation of cyclic ethers and epoxy alcohols/amines used as partnering reagents. These two substrate classes require different chemical environments and thus the selection of the catalyst, additive and the reaction conditions (solvent, temperature, pressure) are crucial to control the process outcomes in terms of chemo- and stereoselectivity, and activity. The modular character of these coreagents will be highlighted together with the specific design features of the catalytic process, as to offer not only an overall good performance but also using cheap, attractive and easy-to-construct catalysts that mediate the straightforward activation of epoxides/oxetanes, and/or epoxy alcohols/amines. The latter category of precursors embeds two distinct functional groups (an oxirane flanked by either an alcohol or amine) and thus provides more ample opportunities for catalytic activation. Besides the different substrate categories, our focus was initially on improving the catalytic activity under metal and metal-free catalysis, delineating the relationship between the structure, functionality and substitution degree of cyclic ethers and how these features affect the catalytic coupling with carbon dioxide. As soon as we realized the limiting nature of these coupling reactions, especially in terms of the steric requirements, we turned our attention to epoxy alcohols/amines as alternative precursors. These complementary precursors provided new entries to otherwise difficult or impossible to prepare heterocycles with high (stereochemical) control. Moreover,

title: Hybrid intelligent modeling for calibrated business and financial risk classification: a decision-support perspective
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop a calibration-aware hybrid framework for large-scale business and financial risk classification, addressing heterogeneous features, nonlinear relationships, temporal distribution shifts, class imbalance an
content: Purpose This study aims to develop a calibration-aware hybrid framework for large-scale business and financial risk classification, addressing heterogeneous features, nonlinear relationships, temporal distribution shifts, class imbalance and unreliable probability estimates. Design/methodology/approach The hybrid multi-agent quantum neural transformer (H–MAQNT) combines a tabular transformer, domain-specialized variational quantum neural network (VQNN) agents and adaptive attention-based fusion. It uses leakage-controlled preprocessing, domain-informed features, imbalance-aware training, validation-only model selection and calibration and quantum-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (QMFBO) for cost-aware tuning. Findings On temporally held-out LendingClub and IEEE–CIS future test periods, H–MAQNT outperforms strong gradient-boosted, neural and transformer-based baselines in discrimination and probability quality. It improves the receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC–AUC) by approximately 1.1–1.3 percentage points over the strongest Transformer-based baselines, lowers expected calibration error (ECE) on both data sets and reduces high-fidelity optimization evaluations by 35% relative to single-fidelity Bayesian optimization. Research limitations/implications The evidence is based on two public data sets and classically simulated quantum circuits. Future work should test additional institutions, rolling time windows, physical hardware and prospective drift and recalibration policies. Practical implications Calibrated risk probabilities may support fraud-alert prioritization, risk ranking, threshold setting, and secondary review, helping institutions weigh predictive gains against computational cost. For LendingClub, the inclusion of loan grade and interest rate makes the framework more appropriate for post-pricing monitoring than for independent pre-pricing approval. Operational use would require institution-specific validation, monitoring for drift and subgroup performance, documented decision thresholds, and human oversight. Social implications The study integrates tabular attention, domain-specialized simulated quantum representations, calibration analysis and cost-aware optimization in one decision-support framework, while evaluating incremental value without claiming inherent quantum advantage. Originality/value The contribution is the theoretically motivated integration of tabular attention, domain-specialized simulated quantum representations, calibration analysis and cost-aware optimization in a unified financial decision-support framework. The study does not claim inherent quantum advantage; instead, it tests the incremental value of simulated quantum modules through temporal evaluation, strong nonhybrid comparisons and component-level ablations.

title: Beyond the burden of perception: misinformation and media discourse in the Abuja–Kaduna railway (China–Nigeria relations)
summary: Introduction This paper examines the evolving nature of China–Nigeria relations in diplomatic, economic and socio-political terms, with particular attention to how public-facing narratives, including misinformation, disinformation and other
content: Introduction This paper examines the evolving nature of China–Nigeria relations in diplomatic, economic and socio-political terms, with particular attention to how public-facing narratives, including misinformation, disinformation and other contested claims, frame interpretations of the bilateral partnership. Guided primarily by constructivist discourse analysis and supported by postcolonial media theory, the paper argues that the material benefits of Chinese engagement in Nigeria are mediated through contested narratives of development, debt, sovereignty, security and trust. Methods The study uses a qualitative literature review and discourse analysis of selected Nigerian and Chinese media reports, policy documents and academic studies, with the Abuja–Kaduna railway treated as a central illustrative case. Rather than claiming to measure Nigerian public opinion statistically, the study analyses how selected public texts construct and circulate competing meanings about China’s role in Nigeria. Results The analysis reveals that interpretations of China–Nigeria relations are shaped not only by material engagements but also by competing narratives that construct differing understandings of development, debt, sovereignty, security and trust. These narratives influence how China’s role in Nigeria is perceived and debated within public discourse. Discussion and conclusion The study concludes that transparency reforms, media literacy investment, stronger fact-checking ecosystems and culturally attuned public diplomacy are plausible responses to the burden of perception and could support a more credible bilateral partnership. In doing so, it contributes to debates on soft power, information disorder, postcolonial agency and the governance of South–South cooperation.

title: AI-Based Hybrid Solar Power Generation with Smart Energy Management Using IOT
source: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
summary: This paper presents an AI-based hybrid solar-wind power generation system with smart energy management and IoT monitoring. Solar panels and a wind turbine work together to generate electricity from available renewable sources. A battery sto
content: This paper presents an AI-based hybrid solar-wind power generation system with smart energy management and IoT monitoring. Solar panels and a wind turbine work together to generate electricity from available renewable sources. A battery stores excess energy and supplies power when generation is insufficient. The intelligent energy management system considers power load demand to control energy distribution effectively. IoT technology enables real-time monitoring of generation, storage, consumption, and system status. The AI-based approach helps the system respond to changing environmental and load conditions. The proposed system aims to improve renewable energy utilization, reduce power wastage, and decrease dependence on conventional energy sources, providing a practical solution for sustainable small-scale power applications.

title: Optimal Development of Hydropower Storage Potential for Enhancing Flexibility of Cascade Hydro–Wind–Solar Systems
summary: Developing cascade water energy storage potential is an effective way to enhance hydro–wind–solar flexibility and promote the accommodation of variable renewable energy. This study proposes an optimization method for developing cascade wate
content: Developing cascade water energy storage potential is an effective way to enhance hydro–wind–solar flexibility and promote the accommodation of variable renewable energy. This study proposes an optimization method for developing cascade water energy storage potential that considers reservoir dredging, energy storage pump station, and reversible pumped-storage unit. Firstly, the characteristics of various measures for developing water energy storage potential are analyzed, and the operating boundaries and constraints of the cascade water energy storage system are determined. Secondly, considering the volatility of grid-connected large-scale green energy, a short-term multi-objective cascade water energy storage system optimization scheduling model is established with the goal of renewable energy generation and peak-shaving benefits. Finally, a multi-objective fuzzy evaluation method is adopted to quantitatively analyze the impact of different measures on the green energy generation and peak-shaving of the cascade water energy storage system. The cascade hydropower system of Gansu section of the Yellow River basin is selected as a case study, and the results indicate that (1) at matched average daily cascade hydropower output, reservoir 2 dredging reduces the residual-load standard deviation by 27.8% on average, whereas the composite evaluation of generation and peak shaving improves it by 18.0%; (2) deployment of energy storage pump station and reversible pumped-storage unit can improve the overall operational performance of the cascade water energy storage system by 11.3% and 41.0%, respectively; (3) Among the schemes evaluated at the specified capacities, reservoir dredging combined with reversible-unit expansion performs best for the modeled generation and peak-shaving objectives.
