title: A STUDY ON GREEN FINANCING AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF SELECTED LISTED RENEWABLE ENERGY COMPANIES IN INDIA
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Abstract Green financing plays an important role in supporting renewable energy investments and the transition towards environmentally sustainable economic development. This study examines the relationship between green financing and the fi
content: Abstract Green financing plays an important role in supporting renewable energy investments and the transition towards environmentally sustainable economic development. This study examines the relationship between green financing and the financial performance of selected listed renewable energy companies in India. It focuses on how access to environmentally oriented funding, including green bonds and green loans, relates to profitability, liquidity, solvency, and operational efficiency. The study uses secondary data from annual reports, financial statements, sustainability disclosures, and other relevant published sources. Financial ratio analysis and comparative assessment provide a basis for examining financing patterns and financial performance across the selected companies. The analysis considers potential benefits, such as access to long-term capital and improved funding diversification, alongside challenges involving financing costs, regulatory requirements, and project implementation risks. The study seeks to clarify the role of green financing in strengthening financial resilience while supporting renewable energy expansion. It aims to provide useful insights for investors, financial institutions, corporate managers, and policymakers concerned with sustainable finance and the development of India’s renewable energy sector.

title: Data center facilities and city-level hosting conditions in China
summary: This dataset provides a facility-level registry of existing data centers and city-level hosting-condition indicators in China. It includes 322 existing data center facilities, 74 cities with existing data centers, and complete hosting-condi
content: This dataset provides a facility-level registry of existing data centers and city-level hosting-condition indicators in China. It includes 322 existing data center facilities, 74 cities with existing data centers, and complete hosting-condition indicators for 372 city spatial units.The dataset contains five files: dc_facility_registry.csv, city_dc_hosting_indicators.csv, city_hosting_conditions_ensemble.csv, metadata_codebook.csv, and README.md. Facility records include city assignment, rack capacity, standardized cooling type, evaporative-cooling assumptions, and matching information. City-level indicators include data center counts, total racks, cooling-type shares, water-resource conditions, wind and solar potential, climate-driven power usage effectiveness, and per-rack resource indicators.The complete city-level hosting-condition table provides ensemble statistics under three climate pathways, ssp126, ssp245, and ssp585, derived from ERA5 meteorology and CMIP6-based perturbations. The dataset can support analyses of data center spatial distribution, cooling structure, renewable-energy compatibility, water constraints, and urban hosting capacity for digital infrastructure planning.

title: Modeling the Brand Strength Component in Monetary Brand Valuation Using Fuzzy Logic: Evidence From a Place Brand
summary: Abstract Purpose : Monetary brand valuation remains a persistent challenge in brand management, due to the absence of transparent approaches for operationalizing brand strength. While financial-based valuation methods are well established,
content: Abstract Purpose : Monetary brand valuation remains a persistent challenge in brand management, due to the absence of transparent approaches for operationalizing brand strength. While financial-based valuation methods are well established, the integration of perceptual and behavioral dimensions into monetary frameworks remains limited. The purpose of this study is to develop and test a methodological approach for modeling the Brand Strength component within monetary brand valuation. The approach is operationalized as an interpretable fuzzy inference model that integrates perceptual data, objective indicators, and expert knowledge. The case of Ülemiste City in Tallinn, Estonia, is used as an empirical example to demonstrate and test the approach’s practical applicability. Design/methodology/approach : The study proposes a fuzzy framework for estimating brand strength in monetary brand valuation. The approach integrates heterogeneous data sources, including survey-based perceptions, objective indicators, and expert knowledge, within a rule-based, interpretable model. The model is empirically demonstrated through an application to the Ülemiste City place brand. Findings : The results show that this model produces consistent, interpretable brand-strength coefficients and supports two complementary use cases: internal, target-based brand management and cross-brand comparability. The findings demonstrate that fuzzy logic provides a practical mechanism for combining diverse sources of brand-related information into a coherent monetary valuation framework. Originality/value : This study advances brand management by offering a transparent method for integrating brand strength into monetary valuation, linking financial metrics with perception-based assessments. Given the lack of a widely accepted, publicly available method for calculating the monetary value of brands, the proposed framework offers both theoretical and practical value. It provides managers with a diagnostically useful and adaptable tool for brand valuation while enhancing the interpretability of monetary brand assessment.

title: Defect‐Conditioned Machine Learning for Molecular Passivator Design in Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
summary: ABSTRACT Dynamic defects, mobile ions, and evolving interfaces remain major obstacles to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics. Molecular passivation can mitigate these losses, but its efficacy is a conditional response rather than
content: ABSTRACT Dynamic defects, mobile ions, and evolving interfaces remain major obstacles to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics. Molecular passivation can mitigate these losses, but its efficacy is a conditional response rather than an intrinsic molecular property. It depends on defect identity and charge state, molecular conformation, adsorption geometry, interfacial composition, processing history, and operating conditions. This review therefore defines a defect‐molecule‐interface configuration as the learning object for machine‐learning‐assisted passivator design. We show how molecular, defect, interface, process, and device variables can be encoded without conflating passivation with platform‐dependent changes in film quality or architecture. Representative studies are compared by dataset size and scope, representation, prediction target, internal data split, external validation, and prospective experimental evidence. We further establish practical requirements for group‐aware validation, uncertainty calibration, applicability‐domain testing, and physics‐constrained learning. This framework positions machine learning as a decision tool for defect‐selective and experimentally verifiable interface design rather than as a ranking engine for isolated molecules.

title: Estimation‐Driven Model Predictive Control Architecture for Active Suspension Systems Under Road Disturbances
summary: ABSTRACT This research work presents an optimal control architecture for a quarter‐car active suspension system, which integrates a discrete‐time Kalman filter (KF) with a model predictive control (MPC) scheme. The proposed framework aims t
content: ABSTRACT This research work presents an optimal control architecture for a quarter‐car active suspension system, which integrates a discrete‐time Kalman filter (KF) with a model predictive control (MPC) scheme. The proposed framework aims to enhance ride comfort and vehicle stability by effectively suppressing the impacts of road disturbances, that is, road bumps and pathholes, through a feasible control input. The proposed framework is based on an estimation‐based control architecture, where a KF provides an optimal reconstruction of the unmeasurable states. The estimated states information is then fed as input to the MPC scheme, which minimizes a cost function by solving a finite‐horizon constrained quadratic optimization problem to compute an optimal control input. The stability of the proposed control architecture is thoroughly investigated via a Lyapunov‐based analysis, with the MPC cost function serving as a Lyapunov candidate function. Computer simulations are carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, where the results for both real and estimated states confirm the minimum‐variance property of the KF. Furthermore, the results corresponding to the open‐loop and closed‐loop configurations demonstrate the efficiency of the closed‐loop optimal control strategy in state regulation, disturbance rejection, and control effort. In perturb scenarios, the performance parameters, such as oscillation suppression, settling time, and overshoot, are comparatively analyzed. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed control framework in damping undesired oscillations, with minimum overshoot and reduced settling times, thus improving ride comfort and vehicle stability.

title: Boiling Heat Transfer on the Surface Made with Electro-Spark Deposition Technology
summary: The paper experimentally analyses heat transfer during water and ethanol boiling on an electro–spark deposited aluminum coating. The performance of this surface is compared with results for other microstructural coatings: laser-treated and
content: The paper experimentally analyses heat transfer during water and ethanol boiling on an electro–spark deposited aluminum coating. The performance of this surface is compared with results for other microstructural coatings: laser-treated and meshed surfaces, as well as an electro-spark-deposited copper coating. The results indicate worse performance of the analysed electro-spark-deposited aluminum layer. However, electro-spark deposition could be a more durable option, because the microstructure-coated surfaces (laser–made and meshed heaters) may be prone to fouling, and their performance could deteriorate over time. Additionally, the accuracy of the selected boiling heat transfer model was considered concerning the analysed aluminum surface. Acceptable agreement between the calculated and experimental data is observed only at low heat flux values.

title: Geometry-Aware Depth Anomaly Detection and Adaptive Decision Modeling for Automated Robotic Quality Sorting
summary: Abstract Industrial 3D anomaly detection remains challenging when defective surface structures must be distinguished from normal geometric variations across different industrial components. This study presents a geometry-aware anomaly detec
content: Abstract Industrial 3D anomaly detection remains challenging when defective surface structures must be distinguished from normal geometric variations across different industrial components. This study presents a geometry-aware anomaly detection framework that integrates local surface characteristics with global object-shape descriptors for industrial defect identification and localization. The proposed framework is evaluated using the MVTec 3D-AD benchmark, comprising 4,147 industrial 3D scans across ten object categories. Local geometric characteristics, including surface normals, curvature, depth variation, and neighborhood consistency, are combined with global descriptors, including convexity, solidity, and void ratio, to construct a complementary geometric representation. The experimental evaluation examines conventional geometric thresholding, an unsupervised 3D anomaly detection baseline, and the proposed local–global feature-fusion approach. Image-level anomaly detection and pixel-level defect localization are assessed using AUROC, average precision, Intersection over Union, and Dice similarity. Feature-ablation analysis investigates the respective contributions of local and global geometric representations. Furthermore, anomaly severity and prediction uncertainty are incorporated into a three-action quality-inspection strategy comprising acceptance, rejection, and additional inspection. The sorting component is evaluated through a cost-sensitive simulation that considers false acceptance, false rejection, and additional-inspection requirements. The study connects geometric anomaly detection with uncertainty-aware quality control decision modeling and investigates the contribution of complementary geometric information to automated industrial inspection. Physical robotic deployment and validation under actual manufacturing conditions remain outside the scope of this experimental evaluation.

title: Synthesis and Study of Molybdenum-Doped Layered Double Hydroxide for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
summary: Hydrogen is a clean and sustainable energy carrier that produces only water as a by-product when utilized in fuel cells. Electrochemical water splitting is considered one of the most promising and environmentally friendly approaches. The ef
content: Hydrogen is a clean and sustainable energy carrier that produces only water as a by-product when utilized in fuel cells. Electrochemical water splitting is considered one of the most promising and environmentally friendly approaches. The efficiency of this process largely depends on the activity and stability of the electrocatalyst. Therefore, this study focuses on the synthesis of Mo-doped Ni layered double hydroxide (Mo-Ni-LDH) via a simple coprecipitation method. The incorporation of Mo is expected to enhance the catalytic activity of Ni-LDH by improving charge-transfer kinetics and reducing the overpotential required for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Additionally, the Mo-Ni-LDH nanocomposite is anticipated to exhibit electrochemical stability under alkaline conditions. The synthesized Mo-Ni-LDH electrocatalyst demonstrated low overpotentials of 155 mV at 10 mA cm-2 and 267 mV at 50 mA cm-2, outperforming pristine Ni-LDH in alkaline media. The enhanced HER activity can be attributed to the synergistic interaction between Mo and Ni species, as well as the multiple oxidation states of the transition metals, which facilitate efficient electron transfer and increase the number of active sites. These findings demonstrate that Mo doping is an effective strategy for improving the electrocatalytic performance of Ni-LDHs and provide valuable insights for the rational design of high-performance LDH-based electrocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Tuning the Molecular Electronic Structure of Polysaccharides: A Comparative DFT Study of Chemically Modified Chitosan and Cellulose Derivatives
summary: Abstract The rational molecular design of functionalized polysaccharides for advanced electronic and sensing applications necessitates a comprehensive mapping of their electronic chemical space. In this study, we report a high-throughput co
content: Abstract The rational molecular design of functionalized polysaccharides for advanced electronic and sensing applications necessitates a comprehensive mapping of their electronic chemical space. In this study, we report a high-throughput computational screening of 115 chemically modified chitosan and cellulose derivatives. Frontier molecular orbital (FMO) energies, HOMO–LUMO energy gaps (ΔE gap ), and a comprehensive suite of global conceptual density functional theory (DFT) descriptors were computed for isolated oligomeric models at the B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) level with SMD implicit solvation. Our quantum chemical analysis reveals that while native polysaccharide backbones exhibit wide ΔE gap values (5.8–6.1 eV), characteristic of electronically rigid systems, targeted functionalization with π-conjugated aromatics, highly polarizable chalcogens (S, Se), and transition-metal coordination centers systematically narrows the gap to 2.6–4.5 eV, significantly enhancing intramolecular charge-transfer capabilities. Furthermore, chitosan derivatives demonstrate superior electronic tunability compared to cellulose due to the reactive C-2 amino group. To navigate the resulting high-dimensional descriptor space, we implemented an unsupervised machine-learning pipeline integrating Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-Means clustering, and Isolation Forest anomaly detection. This chemoinformatics approach successfully delineated distinct electronic clusters and identified transition-metal complexes and specific dye conjugates as statistical outliers with exceptionally narrow energy gaps. Ultimately, the generated molecular electronic-property map provides a robust, data-driven framework for the rational computer-aided design of next-generation functional polysaccharide materials.

title: Smart Building Asset Management Frameworks for Reducing Equipment Downtime, Maintenance Costs and Operational Risks in Saudi Arabia
summary: Smart building investment in Saudi Arabia is expanding the installed base of digitally connected mechanical, electrical and plumbing assets, yet connected equipment does not automatically deliver reliable operations. This critical integrati
content: Smart building investment in Saudi Arabia is expanding the installed base of digitally connected mechanical, electrical and plumbing assets, yet connected equipment does not automatically deliver reliable operations. This critical integrative review examines how asset management frameworks can reduce unplanned downtime, control whole-life maintenance expenditure and contain operational risk across complex building portfolios. Thirty DOI-identified articles published during 2020–2025 provide a bounded interpretive evidence base, complemented by two supplied technical examples. Evidence is compared across information continuity, sensing and fault diagnosis, maintenance prioritisation, decision accountability and performance verification. The resulting framework joins an authoritative asset register to condition intelligence, failure consequence analysis, executable work orders and post-intervention learning. Its distinctive proposition is that economic and reliability gains arise from disciplined decisions, not predictive models alone. Saudi implementation requires special attention to cooling dependency, climatic exposure, heterogeneous building maturity, contractor interfaces and data governance. The review offers measurable indicators, a phased adoption pathway and falsifiable research propositions. It does not claim that the proposed architecture has been field tested or that disparate case study savings can be generalised to Saudi portfolios.

title: Attribution analysis of runoff evolution during flood and non-flood seasons in arid inland rivers of Northwest China
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: ObjectiveThis study aims to clarify the temporal evolution characteristics and driving mechanisms of runoff time series in the upper and middle reaches of the Heihe River during flood and non-flood seasons， providing a scientific basis for
content: ObjectiveThis study aims to clarify the temporal evolution characteristics and driving mechanisms of runoff time series in the upper and middle reaches of the Heihe River during flood and non-flood seasons， providing a scientific basis for water resources management under climate change and underlying surface changes.MethodsFocusing on the upper and middle reaches of the Heihe River Basin， this study employed innovative trend analysis， the Pettitt abrupt change test， wavelet coherence analysis， and the Budyko hypothesis to quantitatively examine runoff variation characteristics during the flood and non-flood seasons and to assess the relative contributions of climate change and underlying surface change.Results（1） During the flood season， runoff in both the upper and middle reaches increased significantly （p<0.05）. During the non-flood season， runoff increased in the upper reach but decreased significantly in the middle reach. The abrupt change analysis showed that change-point years during the flood season all occurred after 2000 （2005 in the upper reach and 2002 in the middle reach）， whereas change-point years in the non-flood season were more dispersed （1998 in the upper reach and 1980 in the middle reach）， exhibiting clear spatial differences. （2） Under the background of inland arid regions， underlying surface factors exerted a significant regulatory effect on runoff. Sensitivity analysis indicated that runoff was most sensitive to underlying surface changes， followed by precipitation， while the sensitivity to potential evapotranspiration （PET） was relatively weak. （3） Contribution analysis further showed that runoff variations during the study period were mainly driven by the combined effects of precipitation and underlying surface changes. In the upper reach， precipitation played a more prominent role （76% during the flood season and 60% during the non-flood season）， whereas underlying surface changes contributed more in the middle reach （71% during the non-flood season）. In terms of seasonal differences， precipitation is the primary factor influencing runoff changes during the flood season （76% in the upper reach and 78% in the middle reach）， while the influence of underlying surface conditions increases during the non-flood season （36% in the upper reach and 71% in the middle reach）.ConclusionRunoff in the upper and middle reaches of the Heihe River Basin exhibits an overall increasing trend， primarily driven by climate change in the upper reaches. In the middle reaches， it increases during the flood season due to climate change but decreases during the non-flood season mainly under the influence of underlying surface changes.

title: Extreme rainfall intensification in the Mexico Valley, a warming and expanding tropical megalopolis
summary: Increasing atmospheric temperature is expected to lead to higher moisture-holding capacity and the potential for stronger storms. Urban regions are heating both due to global climate change and the urban heat island effect, particularly in
content: Increasing atmospheric temperature is expected to lead to higher moisture-holding capacity and the potential for stronger storms. Urban regions are heating both due to global climate change and the urban heat island effect, particularly in the understudied tropics with growing populations and where deforestation and urbanization rates remain high. Models and observations have concluded that sub-daily extreme rainfall is highly sensitive to temperature increases. However, little is known about the compounding effects of climate change and urbanization in urban rainfall intensification. In this paper, we analyze extreme precipitation intensification in the Mexico Valley megalopolis, an expanding tropical megalopolis and one of the largest in the world. We use a Regional Convection Permitting Model under a high greenhouse gas emissions and rapid urban growth scenario. We found that urbanization would be responsible for 67.5% of the increase in mean precipitation by midcentury, and for up to 34.3% of the increase in rainfall intensity. The median increase in rainfall intensity, due to the overall temperature increase, all over the megalopolis would be 16%/°C, more than twice the Clausius-Clapeyron rate, with stronger intensification occurring in shorter duration and longer return period storms. Conversely, higher-elevation regions might see a reduction in extreme rainfall intensity, particularly for longer return period events. Finally, we derive spatially explicit, grid-cell-level relationships to understand the spatial structure in changes in extreme rainfall intensity and for them to be estimated as a function of local temperature anomalies, where the largest increases happen in newly urbanized areas.

title: An Arctic Evaluation of the Polar Radiant Energy in the Far Infrared Experiment (PREFIRE) Release 1 Neural Network Cloud Mask
summary: Abstract The Polar Radiant Energy in the Far Infrared Experiment (PREFIRE) operational Release 1 (R01) neural network cloud mask (2B‐MSK) is described. We use Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS), Cross‐track Infrared Microwave Sounder Suite
content: Abstract The Polar Radiant Energy in the Far Infrared Experiment (PREFIRE) operational Release 1 (R01) neural network cloud mask (2B‐MSK) is described. We use Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS), Cross‐track Infrared Microwave Sounder Suite (CrIMSS), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), and CloudSat/CALIPSO cloud products to evaluate 2B‐MSK for Arctic data. Climatological comparisons against yearly CloudSat/CALIPSO climatologies suggest that PREFIRE is more sensitive to cloud occurrence than estimated from pre‐launch simulations. Average footprint‐scale cloud detection hit rates ( H ) are nearly identical for SAT1 and SAT2, ranging between 72% and 75% against AIRS and CrIMSS and 80%–82% against VIIRS. Higher (lower) H is found over ocean and land (snow and ice) surfaces. A decrease of H by a few percent is found for the largest temporal and spatial offsets between coincidences, while a decrease of 5%–8% is found for the highest AIRS, CrIMSS, and VIIRS satellite viewing angles. Thus, H is highest for the tightest subset of temporal and spatial collocations closest to nadir. A prototype ensemble‐based version of 2B‐MSK more fully captures uncertainties arising from limited sampling in R01 training sets. Ensemble mean values lead to higher H , particularly over snow and ice surfaces, and reduced cross‐track discrepancies in PREFIRE‐detected clouds. Consistent with previous climatological studies, PREFIRE observes larger cloud amounts with stronger surface winds, increased vertical wind shear, and ascending air. This study documents the first known cloud climatology derived from spaceborne measurements of emission spectra that include far‐infrared wavelengths longer than 15 μm.

title: Halomonas as a biological platform for climate change mitigation and ecosystem restoration
summary: Halomonas spp. are a diverse group of halophilic bacteria characterized by exceptional genetic and physiological adaptability, enabling survival in highly saline, alkaline, and other extreme environments. Owing to their metabolic versatilit
content: Halomonas spp. are a diverse group of halophilic bacteria characterized by exceptional genetic and physiological adaptability, enabling survival in highly saline, alkaline, and other extreme environments. Owing to their metabolic versatility and strong stress tolerance, they have emerged as promising microbial platforms for sustainable biotechnology and environmental applications. This review synthesizes current knowledge on Halomonas , spanning molecular mechanisms to ecosystem-scale functions, with emphasis on their role as next-generation industrial microbial chassis. Genomic and systems biology studies have identified key determinants of halotolerance, osmotic regulation, carbon utilization, and biosynthesis of high-value bioproducts, including polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), exopolysaccharides (EPS), ectoine, amino acids, and industrial enzymes. These traits support efficient metabolic performance under extreme conditions and enable sustainable biomanufacturing. Recent advances in metabolic engineering and synthetic biology, particularly CRISPR-based genome editing, optimized promoters, and improved expression systems, have expanded their industrial utility. Engineered Halomonas strains exhibit enhanced substrate flexibility, stress resilience, and higher product yields under non-sterile, seawater-based fermentation, thereby reducing energy demand, freshwater consumption, and contamination risks. A critical emerging aspect is lifecycle assessment (LCA), essential for evaluating environmental performance. Although preliminary evidence indicates reduced global warming potential, energy input, and operational costs compared to conventional systems, comprehensive cradle-to-grave LCA studies remain limited, constraining robust sustainability and techno-economic benchmarking. Beyond industrial applications, Halomonas contributes to environmental sustainability through CO 2 fixation, N 2 O reduction, hydrocarbon degradation, and remediation of saline and contaminated ecosystems. These functions enhance ecosystem resilience and align with circular bioeconomy principles by enabling waste valorisation, carbon recycling, and resource-efficient production systems. This review highlights recent advances, techno-environmental implications, and key research gaps, positioning Halomonas as a versatile platform for climate-resilient and sustainable biotechnology.

title: Interconnections of climate change, water scarcity, and conflict in shaping food security in the twenty-first century: a systematic review
summary: Food security in the twenty-first century is a complex challenge shaped by environmental, economic, social, and political factors beyond mere caloric availability. These challenges are particularly critical during political conflicts and em
content: Food security in the twenty-first century is a complex challenge shaped by environmental, economic, social, and political factors beyond mere caloric availability. These challenges are particularly critical during political conflicts and emergencies, where disruptions to agricultural production, water systems, and food supply chains can intensify food insecurity. This systematic review aims to examine the interconnected effects of climate change, water scarcity, and conflict on food security and to provide a scientific framework for policymaking in emergency and conflict contexts. The novelty of this review lies in examining food security during political conflicts within an integrated Climate–Water–Conflict Nexus framework. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between 2000 and 2025. Following duplicate removal, 392 records were screened, and 70 studies met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the final qualitative synthesis. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using appropriate Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) appraisal tools. The synthesis demonstrates that food-system resilience is undermined by the interacting effects of climate change, water scarcity, conflict, and socio-economic inequalities. Climate change and water scarcity reduce agricultural productivity and resource availability, while geopolitical instability further exacerbates food insecurity through infrastructure destruction, population displacement, and supply-chain disruptions. The findings highlight the need to address these drivers as interconnected rather than isolated challenges and identify persistent gaps concerning food sovereignty, food loss and waste, and marginalized communities. Sustainable food security, particularly in conflict-affected settings, requires an integrated, multisectoral, and resilience-oriented approach. Key strategies include climate-resilient agriculture, sustainable water governance, resilient storage and distribution systems, early-warning technologies, international cooperation, and community empowerment. Strengthening local self-reliance, diversifying food sources, and enhancing institutional capacity can improve the ability of food systems and affected populations to withstand, adapt to, and recover from interconnected environmental and political shocks.

title: Southern Ocean Control on the Relationship Between AMOC Slowdown and ITCZ Shift in CMIP6 Models
summary: Abstract Changes in the latitudinal position of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) are governed by changes in the temperature gradient between the northern and southern hemispheres. This raises the concern that a cooling of the north
content: Abstract Changes in the latitudinal position of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) are governed by changes in the temperature gradient between the northern and southern hemispheres. This raises the concern that a cooling of the northern hemisphere caused by a weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) may shift the ITCZ southwards and cause severe alterations of tropical precipitation. Here we show that there is only a weak relationship between AMOC decline and ITCZ shift in CMIP6 Earth system models, and that even models with a strong weakening of AMOC can show either a southward or a northward shift of the ITCZ, depending on the warming rate of the Southern Ocean. Our findings highlight the role of the Southern Ocean in future changes of tropical precipitation.

title: Climate Change In Indigenous Perspective: An Analysis
source: HPNLU Journal of Environment & Disaster Management
summary: Over the past few decades, climate change has been receiving huge attention among the stakeholders, international organizations, and the public due to its severe impacts on the society and environment. The main reason for human-induced clim
content: Over the past few decades, climate change has been receiving huge attention among the stakeholders, international organizations, and the public due to its severe impacts on the society and environment. The main reason for human-induced climate change is greenhouse gas emissions. Climate change has a significant impact on Indigenous people, who are particularly vulnerable despite contributing relatively little to greenhouse gas emissions. Indigenous people hold four-fifths of the land in the world, and possess extensive knowledge of protecting and conserving natural ecosystems. Their lives and livelihoods are closely connected to the natural ecosystem, which makes them both important actors in environmental conservation and vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change. At the international level there are several conventions, agreements, and protocols for climate change that provide measures for adapting to and mitigating climate change. Although Indigenous rights were recognized internationally only relatively recently, the adoption of UNDRIP strengthened their recognition within international environmental and human rights frameworks. However, Indigenous representation in international climate discussions remains limited, despite growing recognition of their role in addressing climate change. In this paper, the author will be discussing the effects of climate change on indigenous people, their important role in combating climate change, and their response to effects of climate change with real examples that demonstrate the contribution of Indigenous knowledge to climate change adaptation and mitigation. The paper also examines the extent of Indigenous recognition and representation in international forums compared to the past.

title: Layer-specific soil water dynamics and root-zone partitioning in alfalfa under regulated deficit irrigation
summary: Continuous root elongation in alfalfa ( Medicago sativa L.) generates distinct root-zone hydrodynamics, for which vertical water storage and extraction are essential to optimize regulated deficit irrigation (RDI); however, accurate assessme
content: Continuous root elongation in alfalfa ( Medicago sativa L.) generates distinct root-zone hydrodynamics, for which vertical water storage and extraction are essential to optimize regulated deficit irrigation (RDI); however, accurate assessment of RDI efficacy and water use is impeded by limited stratified soil-water data. A three-year field trial (2017–2019) was conducted in arid northwestern China to evaluate seven RDI treatments on alfalfa, including full irrigation and seasonal or phenological-stage-specific deficits. A simplified one-dimensional layered soil water balance model was developed for root-zone water simulation, aggregating simulated water contents into three observation layers (0–60, 60–120, and 120–180 cm). Sensitivity analysis indicated that the model response was primarily controlled by soil hydraulic properties, particularly VG n . Across 1302 observations, an R ² of 0.73, RMSE of 3.15, MAE of 2.45, and mean bias of + 0.13 %age points were achieved, although weak temporal agreement was found in the deepest layer. A depth-stratified RDI response was observed in the simulated soil-water dynamics, with the 0–60 cm layer exhibiting the largest seasonal fluctuations and strongest response to surface water inputs and atmospheric demand. Root water uptake below 60 cm increased with stand age, from 2.1% in 2017 to30.0% in 2019, while uptake from the 120–180 cm layer was detected only in 2019 and accounted for 6.2% of total uptake, indicating a growing dependence on subsoil water during stand maturation. Collectively, depth-specific soil water dynamics in deep-rooted alfalfa were quantified by the process-based layered soil-water model, thereby informing arid irrigation management.

title: Mesurer la résilience budgétaire climatique de l'État : un indice composite articulant le management des risques et la gestion des crises. Cadre conceptuel et méthodologie dans le contexte marocain
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Le management des risques et la gestion des crises sont fréquemment évoqués comme des leviers de résilience des États face au changement climatique. Cet article s'intéresse à leur articulation avec la dimension budgétaire des finances publi
content: Le management des risques et la gestion des crises sont fréquemment évoqués comme des leviers de résilience des États face au changement climatique. Cet article s'intéresse à leur articulation avec la dimension budgétaire des finances publiques. Cet article soulève la problématique suivante : comment articuler et opérationnaliser le management des risques et la gestion des crises pour construire un indice de résilience budgétaire climatique applicable au Maroc ? Cette recherche théorique repose sur une revue narrative de la littérature (24 références, 1973-2022). Elle s'appuie sur la distinction entre la vulnérabilité structurelle et la résilience découlant des politiques publiques, comme l'indiquent Briguglio et al. (2009). Elle s’appuie également sur la méthodologie élaborée par l'OCDE et le JRC (Nardo et al., 2008), dont les dix étapes sont regroupées ici en huit. Elle présente quatre sous-indicateurs (effort préventif, capacité de réponse, recettes fiscales, marge de dette) ainsi que des variables de pression climatique en vue d'une estimation ARDL ultérieure. La décision entre l'application d'une pondération égale et celle d'une pondération fondée sur l'analyse en composantes principales (ACP) est arbitrée par les tests de pertinence, conformément à une règle préétablie.

title: Revisiting the social costs of solar radiation management
summary: A claim by Bronsther & Xu was published in this journal that Stratospheric Aerosol Injection (SAI) would generate up to $809 billion annually in side effect harms 1 . This assertion is the main strand in a broader argument that the “all thi
content: A claim by Bronsther & Xu was published in this journal that Stratospheric Aerosol Injection (SAI) would generate up to $809 billion annually in side effect harms 1 . This assertion is the main strand in a broader argument that the “all things considered price” of SAI is much greater than its modest technical costs would indicate. While it is true that the impacts of SAI are likely to vastly outweigh its technical costs, those impacts are likely to be substantially more positive than negative. The authors claim to evaluate the “holistic ‘true’ cost” of SAI but consider only costs and not benefits. That of course, presents an incomplete and distorted picture.

title: Flood simulation study of the lower tumen river based on a hydrological-hydrodynamic coupled model
summary: Climate change has profoundly altered global hydrological regimes and significantly intensified the occurrence of extreme flooding. Although discharge constitutes the dominant driver of flood genesis, flood propagation is also strongly cont
content: Climate change has profoundly altered global hydrological regimes and significantly intensified the occurrence of extreme flooding. Although discharge constitutes the dominant driver of flood genesis, flood propagation is also strongly controlled by channel and surface roughness conditions. Nevertheless, the magnitude of roughness impacts on flood responses, and their interactive effects with climate change, remain inadequately explored, especially in transboundary river basins with limited observational data. This paper uses a coupled hydrological-hydrodynamic model to simulate flood inundation patterns in the lower part of Tumen River under different climatic conditions and main channel roughness scenarios. The findings show: (1) Under the same roughness condition in the main channel, the SSP5-8.5 climate scenario shows more severe flooding. At roughness coefficients of 0.03 and 0.045, the total inundated area differs by 0.19 km 2 and 0.08 km 2 between the two climate scenarios, with corresponding differences of 0.02 and 0.01 percentage points in the inundation area ratio, respectively. (2) Under the same climate scenario, an increased roughness coefficient in the main channel results in more severe flooding. For the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, increasing roughness from 0.03 to 0.045 raises the total inundated area by 0.39 km 2 and 0.28 km 2 , and increases the inundation area ratio by 0.04 and 0.03 percentage points, respectively. These findings advance the quantitative understanding of how climate change and channel hydraulic properties jointly shape flood behavior, and underscore the non-negligible role of channel roughness in modulating flood risk under a warming climate. Beyond supporting targeted local flood prevention and climate adaptation strategies for transboundary river reaches, this study provides a valuable analytical framework and reference for flood risk assessment in other data-constrained river basins worldwide.

title: Light Environment Control to Enhance Recombinant Protein Yield Per Unit Area With Dense Nicotiana benthamiana Canopy in a Transient Gene Expression System
summary: ABSTRACT Transient expression systems enable rapid and scalable production of plant‐made pharmaceuticals (PMPs). However, maximizing PMP productivity while optimizing electricity use on vertical farms remains challenging. Increasing plantin
content: ABSTRACT Transient expression systems enable rapid and scalable production of plant‐made pharmaceuticals (PMPs). However, maximizing PMP productivity while optimizing electricity use on vertical farms remains challenging. Increasing planting density improves biomass per area but can reduce PMP content per biomass due to self‐shading. Supplemental lighting (sL) can mitigate shading but increases electricity use. Here, we study sL lighting strategies with reasonable electricity use under high‐density Nicotiana benthamiana cultivation (800 plants m –2 ) with hemagglutinin (HA, an influenza vaccine antigen) and an antibody. Gene transfer (GT) was conducted 35–36 days post‐sowing, followed by plant harvest 6–7 days later. Plants were categorized based on the timing of sL treatment: pre‐GT (1 week before GT), post‐GT, pre‐ & post‐GT, and control (no sL). One week before GT, top‐lighting photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD) increased from 200 to 400 μmol m –2 s –1 in all groups, and sL power input was set to half the top‐lighting level. The pre‐ & post‐GT achieved the highest PMP yields per unit area, with a 16%–26% increase in PMP yield per unit lighting energy compared with the control. Overall, this lighting strategy offers a practical, scalable approach to more energy‐efficient PMP production under high‐density cultivation.

title: ENGENHARIA ELÉTRICA, ENERGIAS VERDES E MUDANÇAS CLIMÁTICAS: GERAÇÃO RENOVÁVEL, ARMAZENAMENTO DE ENERGIA E DESENVOLVIMENTO DE REDES INTELIGENTES
summary: A transição energética e as exigências de mitigação das mudanças climáticas têm intensificado a necessidade de modernização dos sistemas elétricos, especialmente diante da crescente participação de fontes renováveis na matriz energética. Ne
content: A transição energética e as exigências de mitigação das mudanças climáticas têm intensificado a necessidade de modernização dos sistemas elétricos, especialmente diante da crescente participação de fontes renováveis na matriz energética. Nesse contexto, objetivou-se analisar as contribuições das inovações tecnológicas relacionadas à geração renovável, ao armazenamento de energia e ao desenvolvimento de redes elétricas inteligentes para a eficiência, a confiabilidade e a sustentabilidade dos sistemas de potência. Metodologicamente, adotou-se uma abordagem qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica, fundamentada na análise descritiva e interpretativa de produções científicas relacionadas às tecnologias energéticas e aos desafios da Engenharia Elétrica. Os resultados evidenciaram que a expansão das fontes solar e eólica demanda mecanismos complementares de flexibilidade operacional, considerando a variabilidade da geração e as limitações da infraestrutura elétrica. Identificou-se que os sistemas de armazenamento apresentam potencial para otimizar o aproveitamento energético, reduzir restrições operacionais e contribuir para a estabilidade do fornecimento. Paralelamente, as redes inteligentes favorecem a integração de recursos distribuídos, a automação dos processos e o gerenciamento da demanda, embora sua implementação envolva desafios econômicos, tecnológicos e regulatórios. Conclui-se que a articulação dessas soluções constitui uma estratégia relevante para a descarbonização, a modernização e o fortalecimento da resiliência dos sistemas elétricos diante das transformações climáticas.

title: Путеводитель по природно-климатическим проектам и технологиям
summary: В этом спецвыпуске Исследовательский центр ЭНЕРПО Европейского университета в Санкт-Петербурге представляет фрагмент нового пособия «Путеводитель по природно-климатическим проектам и технологиям», написанного командой экспертов для понимани
content: В этом спецвыпуске Исследовательский центр ЭНЕРПО Европейского университета в Санкт-Петербурге представляет фрагмент нового пособия «Путеводитель по природно-климатическим проектам и технологиям», написанного командой экспертов для понимания современных тенденций зеленого финансирования и требований к природно-климатическим проектам. Как бизнесу не потеряться в лесу, не завязнуть в болотах и разобраться в современных технологиях?

title: Unruly waters: local environmental knowledge and the erosion of Holocene stability
summary: Abstract Coastal regions around the world are experiencing accelerated and uneven levels of change in the Anthropocene. These ongoing transformations are not only experienced through sea-level projections, but are lived and narrated in spec
content: Abstract Coastal regions around the world are experiencing accelerated and uneven levels of change in the Anthropocene. These ongoing transformations are not only experienced through sea-level projections, but are lived and narrated in specific places. This article explores what it means to live alongside unruly waters through an ethnographic study of Lemvig, a small rural community on the west coast of Denmark. Based on six months of immersive fieldwork between 2018 and 2020, the article examines how residents here experience environmental changes, such as storms and floods, and how these encounters shape coastal identities and local understandings of climate change. The article traces three intertwined dimensions of adaptation to environmental change: (1) local environmental knowledge and moral framings of the sea as a powerful, recurring presence; (2) the material politics of coastal protections, from stone groins and sand nourishment to new climate mitigation strategies; and (3) emerging tensions between modern, post-Enlightenment imaginaries of Holocene stability and the unsettling dynamics of the Anthropocene. Drawing on these situated experiences, the paper argues that resilience along dynamic coasts is not simply a technical matter of engineering defenses, but an ongoing cultural and ethical practice. More specifically, the coastal histories in Lemvig highlight the importance of humility and relational thinking when it comes to coastal adaptation, offering insights for reimagining how communities might live with increasingly unpredictable seas.

title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
summary: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and env
content: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

title: Multi-Scale Modeling of the Effects of Optimizing Speed Bumps and Speed Humps on Patients, Occupants, and Drivers: A Convolutional Neural Network and Biomechanical Modeling Approach
summary: Abstract Traffic calming is recognized as a set of physical interventions aimed at reducing vehicle speeds and enhancing the safety of vulnerable road users. However, speed bumps and speed humps can exert considerable adverse effects on pat
content: Abstract Traffic calming is recognized as a set of physical interventions aimed at reducing vehicle speeds and enhancing the safety of vulnerable road users. However, speed bumps and speed humps can exert considerable adverse effects on patients, occupants, and drivers. This study aimed to conduct multi-scale modeling of the effects of optimizing the number and location of speed bumps and speed humps on these three groups. To this end, a convolutional neural network was employed to determine the optimal number of obstacles across 48 urban roadways. Subsequently, the effects of reducing obstacles on eight patient groups (cardiovascular, spinal, intubated, CPR, post-surgical, pregnant women, osteoporosis, and stroke) and on occupant and driver groups were quantified using biomechanical and clinical models. The results indicated that scenario S5, with 39 speed bumps and 45 speed humps, exhibits the best performance, achieving a 51.3% reduction in the number of speed bumps and a 55.9% reduction in the number of speed humps compared with the existing condition. This reduction led to a 51.7% decrease in the cumulative driver anger index, a 51.3% reduction in zero occupant comfort, a 42.6% reduction in cardiovascular risk, a 66.7% reduction in endotracheal tube displacement, and a 45.5% improvement in CPR quality. Dynamic analysis using the reference vehicle demonstrated that although the road acceleration at speed bumps is 16.8 times that at speed humps, due to suspension damping, the actual acceleration on the vehicle seat is only 22.8 times greater, and the actual VDV is approximately 3.3 times greater. The findings indicate that reducing the number of speed bumps takes higher priority than reducing speed humps.

title: Advancing Tier 2 Methane Flux Measurement in Smallholder Rice Systems: Operational Lessons from Five Agroecological Zones of Ghana
summary: Abstract Distributed closed-chamber networks are increasingly used to derive national methane emission factors for rice systems in sub-Saharan Africa. However, methodological guidance emphasizes statistical estimation while overlooking oper
content: Abstract Distributed closed-chamber networks are increasingly used to derive national methane emission factors for rice systems in sub-Saharan Africa. However, methodological guidance emphasizes statistical estimation while overlooking operational failures that can silently disconnect measurements from their plots, operators, instruments, or sampling dates, causing valid emissions to be discarded. Drawing on the establishment phase of a rice methane-monitoring network spanning five agroecological zones in Ghana, we identify twelve evidence-based design requirements for Tier 2 emission-factor development. Of 36 chamber closures evaluated at the first site, only two met all conventional quality criteria; the remaining 34 provided diagnostic evidence. Analyzer over-range represented data censoring rather than instrument failure: 96.9% of 2,836 flagged records from one unit exceeded an empirical clean-data ceiling of approximately 40,000 ppb, despite a nominal 100-ppm instrument range. Excluding the only modeled over-range closure reduced mean flux by 38% (from 20.34 to 12.56 mg CH₄ m⁻² h⁻¹). Closures with R² below 0.5 contributed 20.4% of positive flux, while the broader low-fit class contributed 47.6%, demonstrating that poor fit alone does not establish measurement failure or ebullition. Using analyzer-cavity rather than ambient pressure underestimated flux by approximately 60%. Mid-morning fluxes cannot be treated as emission factors, particularly because one burst-dominated closure contributed 41% of cumulative flux. Water vapor also showed promise for distinguishing genuine zero flux from seal failure. The framework strengthens national inventories, mitigation accounting, and internationally comparable methane reporting under the Paris Agreement. It thereby supports credible national climate action and transparent global assessment of agricultural methane mitigation.

title: 3D Digital vs. Conventional Workflows: A Comparative Analysis of Sustainability, Clinical Time, and Cost
source: Odovtos - International Journal of Dental Sciences
summary: The transition toward digital dentistry is transforming clinical workflows. While 3D printing offers operational advantages, its actual impact on sustainability, time efficiency, and economic profitability compared to traditional analog met
content: The transition toward digital dentistry is transforming clinical workflows. While 3D printing offers operational advantages, its actual impact on sustainability, time efficiency, and economic profitability compared to traditional analog methods remains a subject of debate, especially in academic training settings. This study aimed to comparatively evaluate the environmental impact (solid waste generation), execution time, and production cost of bimaxillary study models fabricated via a digital workflow (SLA 3D printing) versus the conventional method (alginate and plaster). A paired observational comparative study was conducted on 53 patients. Each participant was evaluated using both methods (paired-measures design). Sustainability was determined by weighing solid waste (grams); cost was calculated by integrating raw materials, labor, and indirect costs; and execution time was measured from the impression acquisition to the attainment of the final model. Differences were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (α=0,05). The 3D digital technique generated a significant reduction in solid waste production, with a median of -669 g (95% CI: -741 to -591) compared to the conventional method (p<0.001). However, the digital workflow presented higher costs, with a median of 86.69 soles (95% CI: 84.15 to 89.24), and a longer production time (median of 2.85 hours vs. 1.38 hours; p<0.001), with a 96.5% probability of superiority regarding speed in favor of the conventional method. Digital manufacturing significantly reduces the solid waste footprint, positioning it as a more sustainable alternative in the academic environment. However, this environmental advantage entails a higher economic and time investment.

title: Compound environmental events in Washington coastal waters from high-resolution downscaled projections
summary: Coastal temperate upwelling ecosystems face increasingly frequent and persistent environmental extremes including warming, deoxygenation, and acidification, yet integrated regional assessments of future change remain limited. Here we apply
content: Coastal temperate upwelling ecosystems face increasingly frequent and persistent environmental extremes including warming, deoxygenation, and acidification, yet integrated regional assessments of future change remain limited. Here we apply high-resolution statistically downscaled CMIP6 projections (SSP2-4.5, 2017–2060) to Washington coastal waters, combining threshold-based detection to characterize individual and compound event dynamics including ocean warming (surface/bottom marine heatwaves (SHW/BHW)), deoxygenation (hypoxia), and ocean acidification (OA). We further introduce a dual-baseline framework that contrasts a fixed (historical) reference against a shifting (rolling) reference to separate long-term warming from genuine extreme short-term variability, and we quantify the time of emergence (ToE) of chronic exposure regimes (≥ 50% annual exposure sustained for three consecutive years) along with cascade lift (the conditional probability of one event type following another above its unconditional baseline). Surface waters warm at 0.032 °C yr − 1 , 67% faster than bottom waters (0.019 °C yr − 1 ), accumulating to projected increases of ~ 1.4 °C (surface) and ~ 0.8–1.2 °C (bottom) by 2060 under SSP2-4.5. Hypoxia and acidification are already chronic at baseline, with bottom oxygen declining at − 0.0034 − 1 decade -1 and pH at − 0.0011 units yr − 1 , reaching an estimated pH of ~ 7.7 by 2060. Under the fixed baseline, OA is the first chronic regime to emerge (median ToE ≈ 2028), followed by SHW (~ 2029), BHW (~ 2037) and hypoxia (~ 2038); under the shifting baseline, SHW and BHW never reach the chronic threshold over most of the domain, isolating OA and hypoxia as the persistent long-term signals. The coastal waters exhibit pervasive compound-event exposure, with 58.8% of the area experiencing high to extreme combined event exposure. Cascade-lift analysis confirms that bottom warming significantly increases the probability of subsequent hypoxia (lift ≈ 1.5–1.7 around 2025–2030), whereas acidification operates largely independently. These findings illustrate a transition from episodic to chronic compound-event regimes and underscore the need for spatially explicit frameworks to inform adaptive management in temperate upwelling systems globally.

title: Prior Colonization Shapes Bacterial Communities on Tire Wear Particles in Agricultural Soil
summary: Abstract Tire wear particles (TWPs) are an increasingly important source of microplastic contamination in agricultural soils, yet little is known about the processes governing bacterial colonization of their surfaces. We investigated how ex
content: Abstract Tire wear particles (TWPs) are an increasingly important source of microplastic contamination in agricultural soils, yet little is known about the processes governing bacterial colonization of their surfaces. We investigated how experimental pre-colonization and soil pretreatment influence TWP-associated bacterial communities across three independent 30-day greenhouse trials using agricultural soil collected adjacent to barley plots during the growing season. Initially uncolonized TWPs and TWPs pre-colonized with Pseudomonas congelans were incubated in non-autoclaved and autoclaved agricultural soil. Scanning electron microscopy, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, community-overlap analyses, and measurements of soil pH and carbon-to-nitrogen (C:N) ratios were used to characterize particle colonization, bacterial communities, and bulk soil responses. Treatment effects on bulk soil chemistry were limited, with no significant differences in C:N ratios and an overall pH effect in only one trial, for which adjusted pairwise comparisons were not significant. TWPs exhibited microbial attachment and biofilm-like material and supported bacterial communities that, despite sharing substantial proportions of taxa with surrounding soil, remained compositionally distinct. The genera enriched on particles varied among trials with prior colonization treatments and soil pretreatment, suggesting that colonization history and soil context contribute to variation in TWP-associated communities. Together, these findings indicate that TWPs support distinct, context-dependent bacterial communities despite limited changes in bulk soil chemistry. Further work is needed to determine whether this community variation affects soil processes and agricultural outcomes.

title: Dynamical characterisation of past and future changes in the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation from CMIP6
summary: Abstract. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a leading candidate tipping element, yet most evidence for its destabilisation rests on critical slowing down indicators applied to scalar time series. Here we instead trea
content: Abstract. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a leading candidate tipping element, yet most evidence for its destabilisation rests on critical slowing down indicators applied to scalar time series. Here we instead treat a high dimensional slice of the circulation state as a dynamical system, using ACCESS-ESM1.5 CMIP6 ensembles from 1850 to 2300 under a low, an intermediate, a high, and an overshoot forcing pathway. A low dimensional embedding by uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) shows whether the circulation stays in one dynamical regime or moves between several. We check it against the local dimension of the attractor, computed in the original phase space, and the two diagnostics agree. Under high forcing, the circulation moves permanently to a new regime via a lower dimensional intermediate stage, which is a change in the dynamics and not only a weakening. Under intermediate forcing, it has reached that intermediate stage by 2100. Under low forcing and under overshoot, it is displaced but returns to its original regime once CO2 declines, so in this model the overshoot is a safe one. We discuss the implications for assessments of AMOC stability and for overshoot pathways.

title: Combining KA Oil Oxidation and O2 Reduction to H2O2 Enables Kinetically and Energetically Favored Adipic Acid Production Pathways
summary: Abstract Adipic acid (AA), produced via oxidation of KA oil (a mixture of cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone), is a crucial monomer for nylon-6,6 synthesis. Electrochemical oxidation of KA oil eliminates the use of the nitric acid oxidant in th
content: Abstract Adipic acid (AA), produced via oxidation of KA oil (a mixture of cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone), is a crucial monomer for nylon-6,6 synthesis. Electrochemical oxidation of KA oil eliminates the use of the nitric acid oxidant in the conventional process, offering a greener approach. However, electrochemical KA oil oxidation is slow; in particular, the 6e– oxidation of cyclohexanone to AA is sluggish, increasing electrical energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate that pairing KA oil oxidation with the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) mitigates energetic and kinetic limitations. By replacing the commonly used hydrogen evolution reaction with the ORR, the operating voltage is greatly reduced. More importantly, we discovered that H2O2 generated from the 2e– ORR can oxidize cyclohexanone to 6-hydroperoxyhexanoic acid (HPHA), a reaction not previously reported in the literature. HPHA can then be further electrochemically oxidized to AA with significantly faster kinetics than cyclohexanone, effectively eliminating the kinetic bottleneck of electrochemical cyclohexanone oxidation. This discovery enables a three-step pathway for AA production: electrochemical oxidation of cyclohexanol to cyclohexanone, chemical oxidation of cyclohexanone to HPHA by H2O2, and electrochemical oxidation of HPHA to AA. The selectivity and efficiency of each reaction, as well as those of the overall process, are investigated in detail.

title: Conflitti armati ed ecosistemi forestali: impatti ecologici, servizi ecosistemici e sfide per il ripristino
summary: I conflitti armati costituiscono una delle minacce emergenti per gli ecosistemi forestali, determinando processi di degradazione che si estendono ben oltre la durata delle ostilità. Le operazioni militari producono effetti diretti, quali di
content: I conflitti armati costituiscono una delle minacce emergenti per gli ecosistemi forestali, determinando processi di degradazione che si estendono ben oltre la durata delle ostilità. Le operazioni militari producono effetti diretti, quali distruzione della vegetazione, incendi, frammentazione degli habitat, contaminazione di suoli e acque e mortalità della fauna, compromettendo immediatamente la struttura e il funzionamento degli ecosistemi. A questi si affiancano effetti indiretti, riconducibili al collasso della governance ambientale, allo sfruttamento non sostenibile delle risorse forestali, all’interruzione delle attività di gestione e monitoraggio, alla diffusione di specie aliene invasive e alla perdita di resilienza socio-ecologica, con conseguenze che possono persistere per decenni. Il contributo analizza i principali meccanismi di degradazione degli ecosistemi forestali sulla base della più recente letteratura scientifica, dei principali rapporti internazionali e delle evidenze riportate nel Global Environment Outlook 7 (GEO-7) dell’UNEP, con riferimenti a casi di studio in Ucraina, Balcani, Tigray e Medio Oriente. Vengono inoltre esaminati gli approcci al ripristino forestale nei contesti post-conflitto, evidenziandone metodologie, costi, tempi di recupero e principali fattori di incertezza. Infine, il lavoro mette in luce il ruolo della cooperazione ambientale internazionale e del rafforzamento delle capacità istituzionali quali strumenti essenziali per promuovere il recupero degli ecosistemi forestali e contribuire alla ricostruzione ecologica, alla resilienza socio-ecologica e a una pace duratura.

title: Bio-inspired Self-Healing Concrete for Sustainable Structures: A Critical Review
source: Journal of Green Chemical and Environmental Engineering
summary: Cracks provide pathways for water, chlorides, sulfates, and carbon dioxide to penetrate reinforced concrete, while conventional crack repairs are often costly, disruptive, and environmentally burdensome. Bio-inspired self-healing concrete i
content: Cracks provide pathways for water, chlorides, sulfates, and carbon dioxide to penetrate reinforced concrete, while conventional crack repairs are often costly, disruptive, and environmentally burdensome. Bio-inspired self-healing concrete incorporates bacteria, enzymes, fungi, or vascular networks to promote autonomous crack sealing and extend service life. This critical review addresses four research questions: (i) how bio-inspired healing compares with autogenous and non-biological engineered healing; (ii) how biological-agent selection, encapsulation and mix design influence trade-offs among healing performance, mechanical properties and cost; (iii) how reliable and comparable laboratory and field evidence is; and (iv) under which conditions self-healing concrete provides environmental and economic benefits. Literature retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science was screened using predefined criteria and critically synthesised, with emphasis on experimental and field evidence. Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) generally seals cracks 0.3-0.5 mm wide, although laboratory studies report closure of cracks up to 0.8-0.97 mm and reductions in water permeability exceeding 90%. However, healing-agent production can increase embodied carbon by 36% per m³ in one recent assessment. Environmental benefits therefore depend on achieved service-life extension, avoided repairs and targeted application. Reported life-cycle benefits range from approximately 12% to 75%, depending on assessment boundaries and assumptions. Major limitations include non-standardised testing, uncertain long-term bacterial viability and repeated-healing capacity, limited field evidence and regulatory uncertainty. Research priorities include standardised testing, long-term field monitoring, hybrid healing systems, predictive modelling and engineered living materials.

title: From Plans to Finance: Climate finance needs, reported support and multilateral funding across the 79 OACPS Member States
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Published on COP31 Finance and Trade Day, the independent study From Plans to Finance examines how climate finance needs and support are reflected in the national climate plans and reports of the 79 countries that are members of the Organis
content: Published on COP31 Finance and Trade Day, the independent study From Plans to Finance examines how climate finance needs and support are reflected in the national climate plans and reports of the 79 countries that are members of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS). The study draws on 431 national documents and data from multilateral climate funds. The countries examined include 36 least developed countries (LDCs) and 38 small island developing States (SIDS), with seven countries belonging to both groups. The findings point to an important gap: although the countries identify climate priorities and estimate their financing needs, the available information does not yet provide a sufficiently consistent picture of how those needs relate to reported support. Adaptation appears particularly under-represented. This record contains the Main Report and the Summary for Policymakers. The annexes referred to in the report are published separately. PENDO Policy Series No. 1. The views expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of the OACPS or any institution mentioned.

title: Growth and physiological responses of Populus nigra L. to salinity stress following inoculation with indigenous arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi
summary: Populus nigra L. is an economically important tree species whose growth and physiological performance can be adversely affected by salinity. Given that mycorrhizal fungi can provide external assistance to plants under adverse environmental
content: Populus nigra L. is an economically important tree species whose growth and physiological performance can be adversely affected by salinity. Given that mycorrhizal fungi can provide external assistance to plants under adverse environmental conditions, this study aimed to evaluate the salt tolerance of one-year-old P. nigra “62/154” plants following inoculation with indigenous arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF). We conducted a greenhouse experiment using a randomized complete block design involving two factors: (1) mycorrhizal status (inoculated with native AMF or not) and (2) salinity stress (0, 50, 100, 150, and 200 mM NaCl). Subsequently, morphological, biochemical, and physiological responses of the poplar plants were measured. Our results showed a marked decrease in survival, growth, biomass, leaf relative water content (RWC), and nitrogen (N), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) concentrations of plant tissues with increasing salinity stress. In contrast, salt stress increased antioxidant activities and the concentrations of sodium (Na), chloride (Cl), phosphorus (P), and micronutrients in plant tissues. AMF-inoculated (AMF+) plants showed improved growth, biomass, leaf RWC, and some macronutrient concentrations at low to moderate salinity (0–100 mM NaCl), and enhanced some antioxidant activities at 0 and 50 mM NaCl. AMF reduced shoot sodium and chloride concentrations only at 100 mM NaCl, while the positive effects of AMF on micronutrient concentrations persisted at higher salinity levels. The reductions in survival, growth and biomass, together with changes in physiological traits, nutrient balance, and shoot accumulation of proline, sodium, and chloride, indicate that P. nigra “62/154” is sensitive to salinity. These findings highlight the importance of managing soil salinity to maintain the optimal performance of this poplar clone. Moreover, the observed benefits of inoculation with indigenous AMF indicate their potential to contribute to salinity tolerance under low to moderate salinity. Further long-term field studies are needed to determine whether these effects persist under prolonged salinity stress and variable field conditions.

title: Modelling and Validation of Performance Characteristics and Emission Reduction in GDI Engine using Port Water Injection
summary: Environmental regulations necessitate reductions in pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions from internal combustion engines. While downsized gasoline direct injection (GDI) engines improve thermal efficiency, they remain constrained by end
content: Environmental regulations necessitate reductions in pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions from internal combustion engines. While downsized gasoline direct injection (GDI) engines improve thermal efficiency, they remain constrained by end-gas autoignition (knocking) and produce elevated nitrogen oxides (NOx). This manuscript investigates the impact of port water injection (PWI) on the combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of a GDI engine fuelled with gasohol E20 under steady-state cruising conditions. A 1D numerical simulation was developed using AVL Cruise M and validated against experimental data, evaluating water-to-fuel (W/F) mass ratios up to 30%. Results demonstrate that introducing 30% water completely suppresses knocking, allowing spark-ignition timing optimisation to recover brake thermal efficiency. The combined effects of water's high latent heat and dilution yield up to 80% reduction in engine-out NOx emissions. Additionally, the findings validate PWI as an effective thermodynamic intervention to mitigate knocking, NOx, and other emissions without requiring aftertreatment.

title: Financing Climate Resilience in Palestine: A Secondary Evidence Assessment
summary: Abstract This paper assesses what published evidence can establish about green-purpose finance and climate-smart agricultural practices in Palestine. It synthesizes official agricultural census statistics, a farmer survey conducted in parts
content: Abstract This paper assesses what published evidence can establish about green-purpose finance and climate-smart agricultural practices in Palestine. It synthesizes official agricultural census statistics, a farmer survey conducted in parts of Hebron, and financial-sector evidence. These sources describe different populations, geographic areas, units of observation, and periods; they cannot be linked to estimate whether farmers who receive green finance adopt more practices or obtain better outcomes. The census records 140,568 agricultural holdings in 2020/2021, compared with 111,310 in 2009/2010, and cultivated area of 1,096,321 dunums, compared with 911,556 dunums. In a separate local sample of 205 farmers, Sultan (2021) reported mean scores of 3.85 for sustainable traditional practices, 4.31 for observing climate-change effects, and 3.82 for receptivity to climate-smart agriculture. A 2023 financial-sector survey reported green-purpose financing by 62% of banks and 44% of microfinance institutions, alongside gaps in climate-risk planning and disclosure. These descriptive indicators do not measure farmer access to green credit or its effects. The paper therefore identifies a data gap and outlines a testable farmer-level research design. Its policy implications are conditional: finance may support adoption when products fit farm conditions and are accompanied by appropriate technical advice, safeguards, and outcome monitoring.

title: Will climate change worsen the groundwater situation in India?
summary: Abstract Groundwater is the major source of water for irrigation and domestic use in India, and increasing groundwater stress has raised concerns about the potential effects of climate change on groundwater resources. This study assesses wh
content: Abstract Groundwater is the major source of water for irrigation and domestic use in India, and increasing groundwater stress has raised concerns about the potential effects of climate change on groundwater resources. This study assesses whether projected changes in precipitation could adversely affect natural groundwater recharge across India. Daily precipitation data from the INDRA-CMIP6 dataset, based on 14 CMIP6 climate models and a multi-model ensemble at 0.1° × 0.1° resolution, were analysed under the SSP2-4.5 scenario. Changes in rainfall amount and the number of rainy days were assessed for all the 800 districts in India by comparing 2050–2059 with the baseline period 2020–2029. The analysis was carried out separately for annual, monsoon and non-monsoon periods, and districts were classified into six categories according to the combined changes in rainfall and rainy-day frequency. The results indicate a generally favourable annual precipitation regime, with mean annual rainfall projected to increase by 6.36% and rainy days by 2.93%. During the monsoon, 681 districts (85.1%) show improved recharge conditions, while none shows deterioration. However, 158 districts show potentially declining recharge conditions during the non-monsoon period, particularly in Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Delhi and the Bundelkhand Region.
