title: Multi-stress tolerant Bacillus from salt-affected arid soil
summary: Abstract Salinity, drought, and heat severely constrain microbial activity in arid soils. This study investigated whether multi-stress tolerance in Bacillus isolated from the rhizosphere of Suaeda vera is associated with a genomic complemen
content: Abstract Salinity, drought, and heat severely constrain microbial activity in arid soils. This study investigated whether multi-stress tolerance in Bacillus isolated from the rhizosphere of Suaeda vera is associated with a genomic complement of stress-response and plant growth-promoting genes. We isolated 150 bacterial isolates from this rhizosphere soil at saline sites (16–32 dS/m) of Sehb El Mesjoune, central Morocco. Among these isolates, 65 were classified as multi-stress tolerant, as they grew in culture media under salinity (1.7–3.4 M NaCl), drought (10–20% PEG), and elevated temperatures (≥47°C), with Bacillus (33%) as the dominant genus. Out of these isolates, five Bacillus strains were selected for further analysis. Whole-genome sequencing revealed a genomic architecture with multiple abiotic stress tolerance mechanisms, including KtrABCD transporters, Na+/H+ antiporters, the opuABCD pathway, and the stressosome sensory complex, with operons for biofilm formation (epsA-O, tasA, bslA) potentially relevant to root association. Comparative ortholog analysis detected 444 orthogroups common to the strains from Sehb El Mesjoune and the saline reference B. halotolerans ZB201702 but absent from the non-saline reference B. velezensis FZB42. Of these, 81 were annotated as stress tolerance or plant growth-promoting genes, a pattern that may reflect environmental filtering, although species-level ancestry cannot be excluded. Additionally, in vitro assays and SEM imaging confirmed these traits were functionally expressed, resulting in Bacillus strains attaching to wheat seeds. These findings suggest that the five selected Bacillus strains represent promising candidates for future greenhouse and field testing as bacterial inoculants for crops grown in salt-affected arid soils.

title: High spatial resolution emissions inventory (2005–2022) in Chile from livestock and waste sectors
summary: Abstract. Methane (CH4) is a critical short-lived climate forcer (SLCF), and emissions inventories provide key information to mitigate its impact. The agricultural and waste sectors are among the most significant global anthropogenic source
content: Abstract. Methane (CH4) is a critical short-lived climate forcer (SLCF), and emissions inventories provide key information to mitigate its impact. The agricultural and waste sectors are among the most significant global anthropogenic sources of CH4 and other atmospheric species, yet in Chile, the national greenhouse gas inventory reports them only at the regional (administrative) level. Here methane, together with other greenhouse gases and air quality pollutants from agricultural livestock, solid waste disposal, and wastewater treatment and discharge, was estimated at high spatial resolution as part of the high-resolution national inventory of anthropogenic emissions (INEMA). Annual emissions of CH4, nitrous oxide (N2O), ammonia (NH3), and non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) were quantified for 2005–2022, using national activity data, country-specific emission factors where available, and national spatial proxies. Over this period, combined CH4 emissions rose by about 37 % to 574 Gg in 2022, dominated by solid waste disposal and livestock enteric fermentation, while livestock manure management was the main source of N2O, NH3, and NMVOC. Emissions concentrate in the central and southern zones of the country, consistent with previous inventories; however, the high resolution of INEMA resolves the specific sources behind these patterns, distinguishing diffuse pasture-based livestock emissions in the south from discrete waste disposal point sources in the central zone. By identifying the specific sources that dominate national emissions, notably a small number of high-emitting waste-disposal sites, the updated INEMA dataset (version 3.0, which integrates these livestock and waste sectors into the full national inventory; available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23169719, Álamos Correa et al., 2026) supports atmospheric modelling, complements national and global emissions inventories, and informs targeted public policies.

title: Bridging local knowledge and system modeling for land-use-based climate action: a co-created decision-support system
summary: Abstract Land-use planning is essential for climate adaptation and mitigation, but local authorities often lack decision-support tools that effectively link scientific modeling with place-based knowledge. This paper shares findings from Ret
content: Abstract Land-use planning is essential for climate adaptation and mitigation, but local authorities often lack decision-support tools that effectively link scientific modeling with place-based knowledge. This paper shares findings from RethinkAction, a project that co-developed an Integrated Assessment Platform with stakeholders across six diverse European regions: semi-arid, island, alpine, temperate, continental, and Atlantic. The approach combined a structured six-workshop co-creation process with data-driven elements. These included downscaled climate indicators, high-resolution land-use and suitability maps, impact-chain-based risk assessments, a catalog of land-use-based adaptation and mitigation solutions (LAMS), and linked simulation engines utilizing local system dynamics models and the WILIAM model at European and global scales. Co-creation improved the platform’s usability and credibility by translating local priorities into measurable objectives and actionable LAMS packages. Results show that participatory design can successfully bridge the gap between expert modeling and local knowledge, enabling transparent workflows and scenario testing for proactive policy evaluation. Across cases, this method altered solution rankings and spatial targeting compared to expert-only baselines, especially regarding water-energy trade-offs. Key lessons emphasize the importance of early scope clarity, accessible communication, iterative feedback, and realistic expectation management. Ongoing challenges include uneven data availability and integrating qualitative insights. Overall, this study demonstrates how participatory, data-driven modeling can create decision-support systems that are both scientifically sound and socially robust, offering valuable guidance for future data infrastructure, capacity building, and long-term upkeep.

title: Influence of Nutrient Sources and Application Timings on Grafting Success, Growth, and Physiology of Mango ( Mangifera indica L.) Nursery Plants Under the Agroecological Conditions of Multan, Pakistan
source: New Zealand Journal of Crop and Horticultural Science
summary: The production of vigorous and uniform mango nursery plants largely depends on successful graft union formation and optimized nutrient management. Therefore, the present study evaluated the influence of different nutrient sources and applic
content: The production of vigorous and uniform mango nursery plants largely depends on successful graft union formation and optimized nutrient management. Therefore, the present study evaluated the influence of different nutrient sources and application timings on graft success, growth, and physiological performance of grafted mango nursery plants. Cleft grafting was performed on 28 February during the 2024–25 nursery season. The experiment was designed using a completely randomized design (CRD) in a factorial arrangement with three replications. Plants received four nutrition sources, i.e., S 0 : Control, S 1 : N:P:K (20:20:20) (5 g), S 2 : diammonium phosphate (DAP) (2.17 g) + sulphate of potash (SOP) (1.7 g) + urea (1.78 g), and S 3 : nitrophos (NP) (5 g) + SOP (1.7 g), applied at four different timings: (T 1 ) at grafting, (T 2 ) 1 week after grafting, (T 3 ) 2 weeks after grafting, and (T 4 ) 3 weeks after grafting. Results showed that higher plant height (78.96 cm), graft success (78.88%), number of flushes (6.33), stem girth (1.11 cm), photosynthetic rate (19.52 µ mol CO 2 m −2 s −1 ), stomatal conductance, and transpiration rate (90.25 and 50 mmol H 2 O m −2 S −1 respectively), as well as nitrogen (1.80%), phosphorus (0.29%), and potassium (0.64%) contents were recorded in S 2 , while lower values were observed in S 0 . Similarly, for application times, T 4 exhibited higher plant growth, physiological parameters, and chlorophyll contents. However, enzymatic activities such as superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, and catalase (55.81, 30.55, 33.36 U mg −1 protein, respectively) were higher in S 0 at T 1 . Therefore, it was concluded that S 2 : DAP (2.17 g) + SOP (1.7 g) applied at T 4 (3 weeks) after grafting is more effective for graft success, physiology, vigor, and overall health of mango nursery plants. This treatment is recommended for mango nurseries in the study area and has practical implications for other regions with similar agroecological conditions.

title: Interdecadal Pacific variability modulates recent drying and near-term changes in early-spring precipitation over subtropical East Asia
summary: Abstract Subtropical East Asia, among the world's most densely populated regions and a major agricultural region, has experienced pronounced early-spring drying since the 1980s, posing growing risks to water resources and agriculture. Howev
content: Abstract Subtropical East Asia, among the world's most densely populated regions and a major agricultural region, has experienced pronounced early-spring drying since the 1980s, posing growing risks to water resources and agriculture. However, the relative contributions of external forcing and internal variability to the drying trend, as well as the associated dynamic and thermodynamic processes, remain unclear. The circulation analogues-based dynamic adjustment reveals that atmospheric circulation changes explain approximately 108% of the observed drying trend, which were largely driven by internal variability. These circulation changes are closely linked to a positive-to-negative phase transition of the Interdecadal Pacific Variability (IPV), which can suppress precipitation by weakening the Northwest Pacific anticyclone and inducing anomalous subsidence over subtropical East Asia. The IPV also modulates near-term precipitation projections. Based on the projected IPV inferred from ensemble members that realistically capture the historical IPV, we identify a likely reversal toward wetter conditions in the near future.

title: Light‐Assisted Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Seawater Electrolysis on a Core–Shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O Catalyst
summary: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration be
content: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration between light‐responsive catalysts and membrane electrolyzer systems. Here, we report a hierarchical core–shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O catalyst that enables efficient light‐assisted hydrogen evolution and is directly interfaced with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. The Cu 2 O nanowire core serves as a light‐harvesting scaffold, while the Co‐P nanosheet shell provides active sites, collectively enabling strong light absorption, suppressed reflectivity, and efficient photothermal conversion with localized interfacial heating. The interfacial interaction between Co‐P and Cu 2 O facilitates catalytic kinetics, as supported by experimental analyses, while theoretical calculations reveal optimized charge redistribution and a reduced water dissociation barrier. Under one‐sun irradiation, the catalyst achieves overpotentials of 62 and 253 mV at 10 and 500 mA cm −2 , respectively, in 1 M KOH, with activity enhancement predominantly governed by photothermal effects. When integrated into a light‐assisted AEM electrolyzer, the Co‐P@Cu 2 O||NiFe LDH pair delivers efficient and durable overall water and seawater electrolysis at large current densities. This work establishes a viable strategy for coupling photothermal‐assisted electrocatalysis with membrane electrolyzer systems, advancing solar‐assisted hydrogen production from diverse water resources.

title: Weather-Related Navigational Hazard Exposure Along Alternative Shipping Routes in the Straits of Malacca, the South China Sea, and the Indian Ocean
summary: Weather-informed route selection is essential for improving navigational safety and operational decision-making, particularly in maritime regions exposed to variable wind and wave conditions. This study evaluates and compares forecast-based
content: Weather-informed route selection is essential for improving navigational safety and operational decision-making, particularly in maritime regions exposed to variable wind and wave conditions. This study evaluates and compares forecast-based environmental hazard exposure along six alternative shipping routes across three major maritime regions: the Straits of Malacca, South China Sea, and Indian Ocean. Meteorological data were obtained from PredictWind and Windy.com over 18 weekly observation periods between July and October 2025, covering five sampling positions along each route. Descriptive statistical analysis, wave-height exceedance frequencies, weekly route comparisons, and threshold-sensitivity assessments were employed to identify spatial and temporal differences in forecast environmental conditions. The findings revealed substantial variations in wave and wind exposure among the alternative routes. The Indian Ocean Route C2 exhibited the highest recorded mean wave heights of 2.19 m and 2.55 m from PredictWind and Windy.com, respectively, compared with 0.84 m and 0.99 m for Route C1. Approximately 60% of valid C2 wave-height readings reached or exceeded the illustrative 2.0 m screening threshold, compared with 1.1%–3.3% for C1. Weekly comparisons consistently identified the same direction of mean wave-height differences between paired routes across both forecasting platforms. Additional threshold-sensitivity analysis reinforced the comparatively elevated wave exposure along Route C2. These findings demonstrate the importance of incorporating route-specific meteorological information into preliminary voyage planning and environmental hazard screening. However, the results represent sampled forecast conditions rather than verified sea states or quantified navigational risks. The study provides an evidence-based foundation for developing more comprehensive weather-routing decision-support frameworks that integrate vessel-specific operational limitations, environmental forecasting, and navigational safety considerations.

title: Uzbekistan FABLE Calculator UP52
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The FABLE Calculator (FABLE-C) is an open tool created in 2018 for the FABLE initiative (fableconsortium.org).Since its launch, it has been developed, regularly updated and improved through the release of update packages by the FABLE Secret
content: The FABLE Calculator (FABLE-C) is an open tool created in 2018 for the FABLE initiative (fableconsortium.org).Since its launch, it has been developed, regularly updated and improved through the release of update packages by the FABLE Secretariat in collaboration with members of the FABLE Consortium (source: FABLE Calculator documentation, 2020). This version of the FABLE Calculator for Uzbekistan includes all updates up to UP52 and presents two Current Trends pathways and one National Commitments pathway, developed by taking into consideration several national policy documents, including NDC 3.0, as well as inputs from Uzbek partners. Further details on the results, underlying assumptions, data sources, and model calibration are provided in the Uzbekistan Sustainable Development Report 2026, presenting the outcomes of the cooperation between the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MoEF) of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) (upcoming report). For more information on the FABLE Consortium activities, please visit https://www.fableconsortium.org/

title: Heavy precipitation and meteorological drought responses to solar irradiance reduction and stratospheric sulfate aerosol intervention
summary: Abstract Solar radiation modification can reduce warming, but heavy precipitation and meteorological drought may respond differently. Using one ensemble member of IPSL-CM6A-LR, we compare G6solar and G6sulfur with SSP5-8.5 over land north o
content: Abstract Solar radiation modification can reduce warming, but heavy precipitation and meteorological drought may respond differently. Using one ensemble member of IPSL-CM6A-LR, we compare G6solar and G6sulfur with SSP5-8.5 over land north of 60°S during 2021–2100, focusing on 2081–2100. We assess annual maximum five-day precipitation (Rx5day), days with precipitation ≥10 mm (R10mm), consecutive dry days (CDD), and the fraction of months with a 12-month standardized precipitation index (SPI-12) ≤−1 relative to 1985–2014. Both interventions produce similar global mean surface temperatures but different land precipitation responses. During 2081–2100, land mean Rx5day decreases by 13.62 and 12.42 mm under G6solar and G6sulfur, respectively, while R10mm decreases by 3.13 and 4.15 days. The drought-month fraction increases by 0.60 and 4.03 percentage points; the 95% block bootstrap interval includes zero for G6solar but excludes zero for G6sulfur. East Asia shows lower Rx5day and more drought months, with small CDD changes. In western southern Africa, G6sulfur shortens CDD while increasing drought months. These single-model results show that weaker heavy precipitation and shorter dry spells do not necessarily indicate reduced accumulated precipitation deficits. Their assessment requires considering these distinct features of rainfall together.

title: Seaweed-based biostimulants alleviate drought stress in sesame by modulating antioxidant defense and gene expression
summary: Abstract Drought stress significantly hampers sesame growth, yield, and oil quality. As environmentally sustainable solutions gain attention, seaweed-derived biostimulants have emerged as promising tools for improving stress tolerance, thou
content: Abstract Drought stress significantly hampers sesame growth, yield, and oil quality. As environmentally sustainable solutions gain attention, seaweed-derived biostimulants have emerged as promising tools for improving stress tolerance, though their application in drought-stressed sesame remains underexplored. A greenhouse experiment was conducted under controlled drought and seaweed treatment conditions. Growth attributes, yield components, nutrient accumulation, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, APX, GR), seed biochemical composition (lipid, protein, fiber, carbohydrate), fatty acid profiles, and gene expression of Hsp70 , DREB1 , HDZ7 , and HDZ10 were analyzed to evaluate the response of sesame to drought and seaweed application. Drought stress caused significant reductions in plant height (− 15%), capsule number per plant (− 38%), seeds per capsule (− 36.6%), and seed weight (− 12.4%). Seaweed applications, particularly S. subrepandum , improved these yield traits, with capsule and seed numbers recovering by 17–28% under drought. Antioxidant enzyme activities increased sharply under drought (GR rose by over 3-fold), indicating oxidative stress. Seaweed treatments significantly reduced ROS-detoxifying enzyme levels, suggesting mitigation of oxidative damage. Drought also reduced key nutrients such as K (− 58%) and Ca (− 39%), while seaweed application restored their levels by up to 46% and 25%, respectively. Biochemical analyses revealed a 23% drop in lipid content under drought, while U. lactuca reversed this trend, increasing lipid levels to 52.87%. Seaweed treatments also enhanced protein content by up to 42.2% and moderated fiber and sugar fluctuations. Fatty acid profiling showed substantial drought-induced declines in total fatty acids (TFA), MUFA, and PUFA, which were partially restored by both seaweed extracts, with S. subrepandum better preserving PUFA content. At the molecular level, drought stress upregulated key stress-responsive genes ( DREB1 up to 39-fold), and seaweed application further enhanced expression, especially in S. subrepandum -treated plants (up to 43-fold), suggesting a transcriptional priming effect. The study provides novel, integrative evidence that foliar-applied seaweed extracts particularly S. subrepandum effectively alleviate drought-induced damage in sesame by enhancing growth, nutrient assimilation, antioxidant balance, seed biochemical quality, lipid metabolism, and stress-responsive gene expression. These findings underscore the potential of marine algae as natural, sustainable biostimulants for improving drought tolerance and nutritional quality in oilseed crops.

title: Synthesis of cellulose nanofibers from corn husks via microwave-assisted chemical extraction and sequential mechanical fibrillation
summary: As a major agricultural byproduct, corn husks contain up to 40% cellulose offering a low-cost, sustainable precursor for high-performance cellulose nanofibers (CNF). Despite this potential, most husk waste is currently managed through envir
content: As a major agricultural byproduct, corn husks contain up to 40% cellulose offering a low-cost, sustainable precursor for high-performance cellulose nanofibers (CNF). Despite this potential, most husk waste is currently managed through environmentally damaging incineration or open-field disposal. The transition to a circular economy is hindered by the recalcitrant lignocellulosic matrix, which makes fiber isolation energy-intensive and chemically demanding. This study presents an energy-efficient synthesis of chemically-purified CNF from corn husks, utilizing agricultural waste as a sustainable resource. The process combines microwave-assisted chemical extraction (removing lignin/hemicellulose) with a sequential, two-step mechanical fibrillation. Following chemical purification and a structural pre-treatment, the material was subjected to planetary ball milling for bulk fracture and subsequent ultrasonication for refinement. Morphological evolution monitored by Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) confirmed the reduction of micro-fibers into an entangled nanoscale network, yielding ball-milled nanofibers with a mean diameter of 19.33 ± 3.09 nm (D50 =18.9 nm). The effect of ultrasonication time (0.5–2.0 h) on fibril refinement was quantitatively evaluated using ImageJ image analysis. A Linear Mixed Effects Model (LMM), accounting for hierarchical batch clustering, established that ultrasonication significantly refined the fiber diameter from the 0.5 h baseline (18.92 ± 0.65 nm) to 1.5 h (16.97 ± 1.52 nm; β=−2.16 nm,p < 0.001). Extending treatment to 2.0 h yielded a final mean diameter of 16.56 ± 0.92 nm (β=−2.43 nm). Subsequent Tukey’s HSD post-hoc analysis (α=0.05) revealed that 1.5 h and 2.0 h share the same statistical subset (group b, p > 0.05), with an incremental reduction of only −0.27 nm. This demonstrates diminishing morphological returns beyond 1.5 h, identifying it as a practical operational processing benchmark. This study elucidates the sequential mechanics of microwave-assisted extraction coupled with planetary ball milling and cavitation, establishing practical processing benchmarks for isolating corn-husk-derived CNFs tailored for advanced biocomposite applications, successfully bridging the gap between agricultural waste management and advanced materials innovation.

title: Responsible AI in Public-Serving Institutions: Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
source: International journal of research and scientific innovation
summary: Public-serving institutions (government agencies, courts, health systems, social-welfare bodies, and regulators) are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to triage caseloads, allocate resources, detect fraud, and personalize services. Beca
content: Public-serving institutions (government agencies, courts, health systems, social-welfare bodies, and regulators) are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to triage caseloads, allocate resources, detect fraud, and personalize services. Because these institutions exercise coercive and distributive authority over citizens who cannot easily exit the relationship, the stakes of getting AI wrong are qualitatively different from those in commercial settings. This paper surveys the advances, challenges, and future directions of responsible AI in the public sector, synthesizing scholarship on AI in government, algorithmic fairness, transparency, and AI ethics with practitioner-facing governance instruments. We first delimit what makes public-serving institutions distinctive: statutory mandates, due-process obligations, and diffuse accountability. We then map the state of the art across four dimensions (use cases, governance and policy instruments, fairness/transparency/accountability practices, and organizational capacity and procurement) and consolidate representative advances in a described table. We argue that the field has matured from principle proliferation toward operational risk management, exemplified by the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the OECD AI Principles, yet a persistent gap remains between high-level commitments and verifiable practice on the ground. Core challenges include bias and equity harms, threats to legitimacy and due process, opacity and contestability, thin institutional capacity, and fragmented accountability. We conclude with a research and practice agenda emphasizing contestable-by-design systems, sociotechnical evaluation, procurement as governance, participatory oversight, and workforce capability. Responsible AI in public service is less a technical property of models than an institutional achievement sustained over time.

title: BEYOND SUBSIDY VOLUME: INSTITUTIONAL QUALITY AS THE TRANSMISSION INFRASTRUCTURE OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL TRANSFORMATION. A CRITICAL MECHANISTIC REVIEW
summary: Public agricultural support is often evaluated by expenditure, coverage, or average treatment effects, yet similar instruments generate sharply different productivity, welfare, and environmental outcomes across agricultural systems. This cr
content: Public agricultural support is often evaluated by expenditure, coverage, or average treatment effects, yet similar instruments generate sharply different productivity, welfare, and environmental outcomes across agricultural systems. This critical mechanistic review asks where that divergence is produced. Synthesizing recent peer-reviewed empirical studies, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, and comparative policy research, we conceptualize institutional quality as the transmission infrastructure linking policy design to targeting, delivery, complementary services, farmer response, and multidimensional outcomes. Five mechanisms recur across settings: administrative capability and accountability; land and property institutions; market and financial coordination; knowledge, extension, and digital systems; and collective organizations. Evidence from input-support programmes in sub-Saharan Africa, the European Union’s agricultural support architecture, and emerging-economy reforms shows that institutions do not merely add to subsidy effects; they alter targeting, additionality, investment horizons, technology uptake, market participation, and environmental leakage. The synthesis also rejects a simple ‘strong institutions equal good outcomes’ interpretation: capable administrations can efficiently implement incentives that remain environmentally misaligned, while land formalization, credit, or digital tools can underperform when complementary constraints bind. We propose a policy-transmission framework with observable failure signatures for diagnosing where support loses effectiveness and identify mechanism-specific priorities for future causal research.

title: Exploring Canadian beef farmers' perceptions of participation in climate change mitigation: Insights from Prince Edward Island.
summary: Beef farmers can play a significant role in reducing and sequestering greenhouse gas emissions through specific farm management practices. Understanding how farmers perceive this role is essential for effective knowledge exchange and commun
content: Beef farmers can play a significant role in reducing and sequestering greenhouse gas emissions through specific farm management practices. Understanding how farmers perceive this role is essential for effective knowledge exchange and communication strategies that promote climate change mitigation. This study investigates how beef farmers in Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada, perceive their involvement in farm-level mitigation efforts. Using identity theory as a framework, the study conducted a framing analysis to examine how participating farmers communicated their actions through four identity lenses: productivist, conservationist, hero, and scientist. Through purposive sampling, nine in-depth interviews were conducted with PEI beef farmers actively engaged in mitigative practices. Findings reveal that farmers often drew on multiple identities, with the productivist frame emerging most prominently. To foster broader engagement in climate mitigation, communication strategies should reflect the range of identities farmers associate with. Future research should explore perceptions among those not currently participating in mitigative practices.

title: Impact of Banditry on Food Production in Shiroro Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria
source: International journal of research and scientific innovation
summary: Banditry has emerged as one of the most serious security challenges confronting Nigeria, particularly in rural communities where violent attacks, kidnapping, cattle rustling, and destruction of property have negatively affected agricultural
content: Banditry has emerged as one of the most serious security challenges confronting Nigeria, particularly in rural communities where violent attacks, kidnapping, cattle rustling, and destruction of property have negatively affected agricultural activities and food production. This worsening situation necessitated the present study which examined the impact of banditry on food production in Shiroro Local Government Area of Niger State. The study specifically investigated the nature and prevalence of banditry, its effects on agricultural production and food security, measures adopted to address the menace, and the challenges affecting effective responses. The study adopted the Political Economy Theory because it explains how poverty, unemployment, inequality, weak governance, and competition over scarce resources contribute to insecurity and criminal activities in society. A survey research method was utilized through the administration of questionnaires and in-depth interviews. Data collected through questionnaires were analyzed using simple percentage, while interview responses and secondary sources were analyzed qualitatively through content analysis. Findings revealed that banditry has become widespread, organized, and destructive, resulting in fear, displacement, abandonment of farmlands, and severe threats to food production in Shiroro Local Government Area. The study further showed that banditry reduced food output, discouraged farming activities, increased production costs, and threatened food security and livelihoods. Community vigilante groups and resettlement programmes emerged as more effective mitigation measures, whereas security deployment and financial support remained inadequate. Persistent challenges identified included inadequate funding, poor equipment, poverty, corruption, and political interference. The study concluded that sustainable solutions require community-based security, technology-driven surveillance, youth empowerment, accountability, and depoliticized security operations. The study therefore recommends among others that government should strengthen community-based security structures by supporting vigilante groups, expand youth empowerment programmes through agricultural loans and vocational training, and ensure transparency and accountability in security operations free from corruption and political interference.

title: Mitigation Efficacy of Dietary Additives and Nutritional Strategies on Enteric Methane Emissions in Ruminant Livestock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
source: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
summary: Ruminant livestock are a major source of enteric methane, a short-lived and potent greenhouse gas. In low- and middle-income countries, low-quality feed and low animal productivity raise the methane emitted per unit of milk or meat, yet mos
content: Ruminant livestock are a major source of enteric methane, a short-lived and potent greenhouse gas. In low- and middle-income countries, low-quality feed and low animal productivity raise the methane emitted per unit of milk or meat, yet most mitigation strategies were designed for developed countries. It is unclear how much feed and nutrition strategies reduce methane in these systems.

title: Enhanced microalgal biomass cultivation on anaerobic digestate depends on species selection, media characteristics and ammonium concentration
source: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: Abstract Microalgae cultivation on anaerobic digestate can contribute to the recovery and reuse of nutrients, but special attention is needed to achieve optimum digestate pre-treatment to support algal growth. Assessing culture performance
content: Abstract Microalgae cultivation on anaerobic digestate can contribute to the recovery and reuse of nutrients, but special attention is needed to achieve optimum digestate pre-treatment to support algal growth. Assessing culture performance based on feedstock dilution factors as the sole pre-treatment overlooks temporal variability in digestate composition, leading to poor performance reproducibility and potential operational failure at large scale. To address this, we implemented a one-variable approach to systematically isolate and evaluate the effects of key growth-limiting factors across digestates from pig waste, food waste and sewage sludge. We screened six microalgal species, identifying Chlorella sorokiniana and Chlorella vulgaris as the most resilient species, although their performance varied according to digestate source and dilution factor. Using the one-variable framework, we assessed the impact of increasing ammonium (NH 4 –N) concentrations and their interactions with turbidity and organic matter in autoclaved digestate. This allowed for a systematic assessment of the effect of increasing ammonium concentrations on microalgal growth and interactions with other digestate characteristics, while removing bacterial effects. C. sorokinana was more affected by organic matter and NH 4 –N concentrations than NH 4 –N alone. C. vulgaris was more affected by turbidity but displayed improved growth in high organic-content with elevated NH 4 –N levels (up to 300 mg-N L −1 ). These findings are interpreted within the context of photosynthesis, respiration and NH 4 –N assimilation and they were used to demonstrate that microalgal growth is highly dependent on species selection and media characteristics, that cannot be reproduced by simply choosing a set dilution factor. Tailoring cultivation conditions based on this framework is therefore essential to improve reproducibility and scalability in digestate-based microalgal systems.

title: Multi-sensor satellite analysis reveals latitudinal and morphometric controls on ice phenology across 31 000 lakes on the Alaska North Slope
summary: Thermokarst lakes are critical components of Arctic carbon cycling, yet their ice phenology remains poorly characterized at regional scales. We present the first comprehensive analysis of ice-on and ice-off timing across 30 774 lakes on the
content: Thermokarst lakes are critical components of Arctic carbon cycling, yet their ice phenology remains poorly characterized at regional scales. We present the first comprehensive analysis of ice-on and ice-off timing across 30 774 lakes on the Alaska North Slope using Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) classified by a Random Forest (RF) model trained using labels derived from Sentinel-2 optical imagery and ERA5 temperature data for the period 2019–2023. Our RF classifier achieved 94 % accuracy for ice state detection, enabling phenology retrieval for 97 % of lake-years. Results revealed a mean ice-free period of 114 d (standard deviation = 25 d), with ice-off occurring at day-of-year 159 (8 June) and ice-on at day-of-year 273 (30 September). Spatial analysis demonstrated strong latitudinal control on ice phenology, with ice-free duration decreasing by 23 d per degree northward. Lake morphology (area, circularity, convexity, and shoreline development index) showed modest but significant effects on ice timing after controlling for latitude effects, with shoreline development index and convexity each contributing ∼ 3 d variation across typical lake ranges. Comparison of the RF model and simplistic accumulated degree-day (ADD) model-detected ice phenology yielded a convincing match, where the offsets in ice phenology between the models fell within twice the per-detection observation gap for approximately 80 % of the lakes. Furthermore, these offsets exhibited the same strong latitudinal control and negligible effects of lake morphology. These lake-specific phenology dates provide timing and duration constraints for future methane studies using high-resolution sensors and provide baseline phenology data essential for understanding how continued Arctic warming will affect thermokarst lake dynamics and associated carbon cycle feedbacks.

title: Future projections of compound events around the Main Hawaiian Islands
summary: The consequences of overlapping environmental stressors – referred to as compound events – may be more harmful to marine ecosystems than as individual stressors. Using recently conducted submesoscale-permitting future projections for the Ma
content: The consequences of overlapping environmental stressors – referred to as compound events – may be more harmful to marine ecosystems than as individual stressors. Using recently conducted submesoscale-permitting future projections for the Main Hawaiian Islands, we present the first assessment of future compound events for Hawaiian waters. Our analysis focuses on surface and sub-surface heat-stress, ocean acidification, and low-oxygen events and is based on three different greenhouse gas emission scenarios. We show that a large fraction of ocean around Hawai'i will be subject to compound events in the near future. However, the projected event characteristics such as duration and intensity vary substantially across the region suggesting that potential ecosystem impacts may differ over short distances. Our results reveal that these spatial differences are mainly driven by considerably different magnitudes of natural variability in ocean physics and chemistry across the domain driven by mesoscale processes, while anthropogenic trends exhibit only minor spatial differences. Our analysis demonstrates that small-scale tidal variability can significantly mitigate compound events in near-shore regions, including some designated Marine Protected Areas. Overall, our findings highlight the need for high-resolution numerical models as well as for an extended observation network for robust future projections of local extreme events.

title: Prediction of ephemeral plant diversity patterns and identification of conservation priority areas in the Gurbantunggut Desert
summary: Ephemeral plants are a key functional group in the Gurbantunggut Desert, contributing to windbreak, sand fixation, and biodiversity maintenance, and are highly sensitive to climate change. Understanding their spatial diversity patterns can
content: Ephemeral plants are a key functional group in the Gurbantunggut Desert, contributing to windbreak, sand fixation, and biodiversity maintenance, and are highly sensitive to climate change. Understanding their spatial diversity patterns can reveal desert ecosystem adaptation mechanisms and inform conservation planning. This study examined 35 dominant ephemeral plant species in the Gurbantunggut Desert, Xinjiang. Using species occurrence data and 12 environmental variables, we applied an ensemble species distribution model to simulate spatial patterns of species richness and migration under current and future (2050s) climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5). Climate velocity was calculated using the KNN algorithm. The Zonation model, integrating species richness, species loss, and climate velocity, was used to identify and optimize priority conservation areas. The results showed that: (1) species richness is projected to decline by the 2050s under all scenarios, with greater losses under higher emission pathways; the central southern margin consistently remains a biodiversity hotspot. (2) The climate velocity of temperature variables is higher in the eastern and western regions, whereas that of precipitation variables is higher in the east; overall, precipitation velocity exceeds temperature velocity. (3) Current conservation areas (2.103 × 10 4 km 2 ) are mainly located in the southern, western, and eastern regions. By the 2050s, conservation areas are projected to shrink (≈ 1.48–1.58 × 10 4 km 2 ) and shift spatially, with higher-priority areas increasingly concentrated in the central southern margin and western desert under higher emission scenarios. Future climate change will reduce ephemeral plant diversity and shift priority conservation areas, highlighting the need to protect the central southern margin and western desert.

title: A Systematic Exploration of the Role of Al₂O₃ Nanoparticles in CI Engines Fuelled with Co-Pyrolytic Bio-Oil
source: Journal of Research and Applications in Mechanical Engineering
summary: The rising demand for sustainable energy solutions has prompted research into alternative fuels and advanced technologies aimed at enhancing engine performance and minimising emissions. Al oxide (Al2O3) nanoparticles' impact on performance
content: The rising demand for sustainable energy solutions has prompted research into alternative fuels and advanced technologies aimed at enhancing engine performance and minimising emissions. Al oxide (Al2O3) nanoparticles' impact on performance and emission properties of compression ignition (CI) engines driven with co-pyrolytic bio-oil is investigated in this paper. Derived from biomass pyrolysed, co-pyrolytic bio-oil presents a renewable substitute for conventional diesel but suffers lower energy density and more emissions. Prominent for their catalytic and thermal characteristics, Al₂O₃ nanoparticles have showed potential in improving performance and lowering of hazardous emissions. Existing paper is compiled in this work to show the processes by which Al₂O₃ nanoparticles enhance engine performance and reduce emissions. Investigation also points up areas of research lacking and suggests potential paths for the integration of nanotechnology into biofuel uses.

title: Advances in Metaheuristics and Learnheuristics (2019–2026): A Comprehensive Review, Taxonomy, and Future Directions
source: Journal of Data Science and Intelligent Systems
summary: This review examines more than 150 recent metaheuristics introduced between 2019 and 2026, emphasizing their significant impact and performance in solving complex optimization problems. In the past three decades, more than 500 metaheuristic
content: This review examines more than 150 recent metaheuristics introduced between 2019 and 2026, emphasizing their significant impact and performance in solving complex optimization problems. In the past three decades, more than 500 metaheuristic algorithms have been proposed, with no sign of deceleration, resulting in a vast and growing landscape that makes it increasingly difficult to select, compare, and evaluate the most suitable methods for specific challenges. Our analysis considers several important aspects, including citation trends, application areas, the availability of source code, parameter configuration, the originality of proposed mechanisms and operators, and the ability of these methods to address common challenges such as stagnation and premature convergence. We also examine the practical applications and performance of the 15 most influential metaheuristic algorithms proposed over the past six years. Particular attention is given to learnheuristics, an emerging research area that combines machine learning with metaheuristic optimization to address dynamic and data-driven problems. To provide a clearer view of this growing field, we introduce a unified taxonomy covering both metaheuristics and learnheuristics. The taxonomy classifies these methods according to the level of learning integration, problem type, learning approach, and intended purpose. We believe that this classification can help researchers better understand the current state of the field and identify potential opportunities for future research. Data Availability Statement Data sharing is not applicable to this article, as no new data were created or analyzed in this study. title: Health, nutrition, and sustainability analysis of commonly consumed grain products in Sweden
summary: Inroduction Grain-based products are a key part of human diets globally and generally have lower climate impact, but their nutritional composition and environmental impacts vary widely among products. The health nutritional index (HENI) qua
content: Inroduction Grain-based products are a key part of human diets globally and generally have lower climate impact, but their nutritional composition and environmental impacts vary widely among products. The health nutritional index (HENI) quantifies the health impact of foods and can be linked to environmental data, enabling combined assessments of nutritional and ecological aspects. The aim of this project was to rank grain-based food categories commonly consumed in Sweden by HENI scores, the nutrient rich foods (NRF) index 11.3, greenhouse gas emissions (GHGEs), and biodiversity loss and to explore how HENI scores correlate with NRF11.3, GHGEs, and biodiversity loss. Methods HENI and NRF11.3 were calculated for 297 grain-based products using Sweden-specific dietary risk factors and nutrient requirements. Environmental data was obtained from two databases. Results The highest positive median HENI score was found in “ breakfast cereals and muesli ”, while “ rice ” had the lowest negative score. The widest range occurred in “ buns, soft cakes, pastry and other ”. Sodium, whole grains and fibre contributed most to the variation of HENI. Median across all products was 5 min of healthy life/100 g gained for HENI, 42 for NRF11.3, 0.10 kg CO₂Eq/100 g for GHGEs and 4E −14 E/MSY/100 g for biodiversity loss. A moderate correlation was found between HENI and NRF11.3, suggesting that health impact and nutrient density often align. Results also reveal trade-offs within the grain product categories, suggesting that analyses at this level may be most appropriate for highlighting where such trade-offs between health and environment are most evident. No correlation with GHGEs, but a weak correlation between HENI and biodiversity loss could be identified, suggesting that nutrition-related health impacts do not necessarily align with biodiversity nor GHGEs. Conclusion Grain products in Sweden vary in nutrient density, health and environmental impacts. While some products rank high in nutritional density and positive health impact, their environmental footprint varies. HENI can help identify trade-offs between health and sustainability, which may inform the development of more sustainable dietary guidelines and support food labeling, improved product development, and public health strategies.

title: Hydrodynamic Impact of Cavitating Jets on Marine-Coated Steel Surfaces: Parametric Analysis and Non-Destructive Cleaning Performance
summary: Abstract Biofouling on ship hulls increases hydrodynamic drag, fuel consumption, and lifecycle maintenance costs. This work presents a quantitative experimental investigation of normal impact forces generated by cavitating and conventional
content: Abstract Biofouling on ship hulls increases hydrodynamic drag, fuel consumption, and lifecycle maintenance costs. This work presents a quantitative experimental investigation of normal impact forces generated by cavitating and conventional high-pressure water jets on marine-coated carbon-steel surfaces. Analytical calculations and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed to evaluate internal flow and cavitation dynamics. Normal forces were measured using a calibrated load cell as a function of stand-off distance ([0,01 − 0,35] m) and jet incidence angle ([0,349–1,57] rad) under submerged conditions. The cavitating jet was generated by an in-house developed Venturi-type stainless-steel nozzle costing under €40. Results show that the cavitating jet delivered a quasi-stable normal force of 4.5 ± 0.2 N over [0,01–0,04] m, decaying by only 22% at 0,35 m (3.5 N), whereas the conventional jet force decayed rapidly. Surface characterization combining profilometry and dry-film-thickness monitoring confirmed a cleaning efficiency of 72 ± 6% at the optimal window ( d = [0,02–0,04] m, θ = [0,524– 0.786] rad) with no measurable coating degradation. These results demonstrate the suitability of low-cost cavitating jets for coating-safe underwater maintenance and provide operational guidelines directly applicable to autonomous marine cleaning systems.

title: Women’s perceived socioeconomic gains and the illusion of equity in climate-smart agriculture in northern Benin
summary: Although previous studies have highlighted advantages of adopting climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices, their actual capacity to generate long-term and inclusive effects remains unclear. Beneficiaries report positive effects on their l
content: Although previous studies have highlighted advantages of adopting climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices, their actual capacity to generate long-term and inclusive effects remains unclear. Beneficiaries report positive effects on their living conditions, yet many continue to face limited access to productive resources. This study assesses the socioeconomic impacts of CSA practices as perceived by beneficiaries, characterizes the profiles of the actors reporting the main impacts, and identifies the factors influencing these perceptions. A mixed-methods approach combining a quantitative survey ( N = 200) and qualitative interviews with 18 of these respondents was applied to 200 producers benefiting from CSA initiatives in northern Benin, primarily in the communes of N’Dali and Tchaourou. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was applied: the two strands were collected concurrently and merged at the interpretation stage through a joint display. Quantitative data were analyzed using cross-tabulations with chi-square tests, Spearman rank correlations and binary logistic regressions reporting odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals; the interviews were analyzed thematically. Positive impacts on income are reported by 70.5% of beneficiaries, while, among those reporting improved income, most consider their access to land (58.9%) and water (67.4%) unchanged. The findings reveal three paradoxes that characterize a situation of partial emancipation. First, women, who report gains in proportions similar to those of men, perceive economic gains associated with CSA practices without necessarily achieving structural autonomy or land tenure security: reported autonomy coexists with access to land and water that beneficiaries describe as unchanged. Second, the study highlights a form of economic mobility without security of productive resources (land, water, seeds, and credit). Third, social recognition is not accompanied by a proportional strengthening of real economic power. Perceived impacts are most strongly associated with technical training, age and access to seeds and financing, rather than with land or water security. Because the design is cross-sectional and based on self-reported perceptions, the findings identify associations and perceived experiences rather than causal effects of the interventions. These observations call into question the effectiveness of current gender-sensitive approaches in CSA-focused projects.

title: Country-Specific Constraints Reshape Global AFOLU Mitigation Potential
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Agriculture, forestry, and other land use (AFOLU) is expected to deliver around 22% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions, yet most assessments rely on regionally aggregated assumptions that overlooked how land-use systems, bio
content: Agriculture, forestry, and other land use (AFOLU) is expected to deliver around 22% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions, yet most assessments rely on regionally aggregated assumptions that overlooked how land-use systems, biophysical conditions, and technology feasibility differ between countries. Here we explore AFOLU mitigation potential across 149 countries using the AFOLU Bottom-up technology selection model (AFOLU-B), with two refinements: technology availability linked to national income levels, and country-specific parameterization of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) options, for afforestation, soil carbon sequestration, and biochar. Sequestration potentials are derived from gridded land-use and biophysical datasets and aggregated to the national level. Under the SSP2-2°C scenario, global AFOLU mitigation potential reaches 8.5 GtCO₂eq yr⁻¹ by 2100, about 35% lower than previous estimates. This drop is driven primarily by a much smaller CDR contribution, which falls to around 1.8 GtCO₂eq yr⁻¹, with afforestation and biochar hit hardest. Agricultural non-CO₂ mitigation, by contrast, remains stable across countries, and livestock and manure management offer the largest low-cost opportunities. Accounting for country-specific constraints therefore reshapes the global AFOLU mitigation picture and provides a more realistic foundation for national net-zero pledge.

title: Real-Time Detection of Islanding in Solar-Based Microgrids Through Voltage Positive Feedback Mechanism
source: Muthanna Journal of Engineering and Technology
summary: Microgrid islanding detection is one of the important requirements in the use of solar microgrids to ensure personnel safety and prevent equipment damage. This paper presents a fast online islanding detection method using voltage positive f
content: Microgrid islanding detection is one of the important requirements in the use of solar microgrids to ensure personnel safety and prevent equipment damage. This paper presents a fast online islanding detection method using voltage positive feedback (VPF) measured at the PCC point. In the proposed method, the voltage amplitude value is monitored instantaneously at the PCC point, and if the voltage deviation, which ultimately causes frequency deviation, occurs and exceeds the specified allowable value, VPF is applied to accelerate the frequency change and reduce the detection time. The method has been evaluated using simulation in MATLAB/Simulink environment on a 10 kW photovoltaic microgrid under different load conditions. The results show that the proposed VPF method detects islanding in the worst case of power imbalance within 50 ms, which is much faster than conventional passive methods (500 ms or more) and has a performance comparable to active methods without power quality degradation. The non-detection zone is also reduced to less than 0.5% of active power imbalance. Meanwhile, while operating in islanded mode, the frequency and voltage remain within the permissible range of the IEEE 1547 standard. These findings confirm that the proposed approach provides a reliable, fast, and non-intrusive solution for islanding detection in solar microgrids.

title: A new tool, new possibilities? Ecobudget in participatory climate change adaptation: the case of Łódź
summary: This article evaluates the Ecobudget for Łódź, Poland, as an innovative instrument for the city’s participatory climate change adaptation, and identifies the benefits and limitations in its design and implementation. The article’s theoretic
content: This article evaluates the Ecobudget for Łódź, Poland, as an innovative instrument for the city’s participatory climate change adaptation, and identifies the benefits and limitations in its design and implementation. The article’s theoretical framework is based on three integrally linked themes: public participation in environmental protection, deliberative democracy (mini-public), and participatory climate change adaptation instruments. The empirical research was conducted as a qualitative case study of the first edition of the Ecobudget. It included participant observations, a focus group interview with representatives of institutions involved in the implementation, and six individual in-depth interviews with project applicants. The results indicate that the Ecobudget effectively mobilised residents around specific green spaces, drawing on their attachment to the place and their concern for its future. At the same time, it fostered cooperation between residents, experts, and the public administration. Its main strengths include its strong local roots, its educational function, and its tripartite cooperation model. The most significant limitation lay in the implementation phase of the selected projects and the communication issues that accompanied it. The case study of the Ecobudget for Łódź may serve as a source of inspiration for cities seeking new participatory tools. The strengths and barriers of the instrument identified in this study can help other cities make use of its potential and avoid mistakes.

title: Properties of palm fruit stalk fibres and palm kernel shell ash for sustainable construction applications
summary: This study explores palm fruit stalk fibres (PFSF) and palm kernel shell ash (PKSA) as sustainable materials for construction. Both are palm oil by-products often discarded or burned, causing pollution. The research examined their mechanica
content: This study explores palm fruit stalk fibres (PFSF) and palm kernel shell ash (PKSA) as sustainable materials for construction. Both are palm oil by-products often discarded or burned, causing pollution. The research examined their mechanical, chemical, physical, and microstructural characteristics to assess their suitability in building materials. PKSA showed high fineness (87%), low specific gravity (1.212), and pozzolanic–filler properties, mainly composed of quartz (85%), with minor kaolinite and calcite. PFSF exhibited a high aspect ratio (4862:1), tensile strength (6.93 N/mm²), and water absorption (206.21%), suggesting improved ductility and crack resistance, though moisture treatment is needed. Microstructural analysis confirmed good bonding potential between fibres and cement matrix. The findings demonstrate that PFSF and PKSA offer eco-friendly, cost-effective options for lightweight, thermally efficient, and sustainable construction materials.

title: Agricultural GHG Emission Trajectories and Mitigation Pathways for India: A Scenario-Based Analysis using the AFOLU_India Model
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Agriculture accounts for over 14% of India's total greenhouse gas emissions and is one of the most complex sector to decarbonize due to its inextricable connections to food security, rural livelihoods, and demographic expansion. This study
content: Agriculture accounts for over 14% of India's total greenhouse gas emissions and is one of the most complex sector to decarbonize due to its inextricable connections to food security, rural livelihoods, and demographic expansion. This study introduces the AFOLU-India model, a customized adaptation of the AFOLUB model that is recalibrated for Indian agricultural systems, emission factors, and policy parameters. It aims to project greenhouse gas emissions and assess the mitigation potential and abatement costs of countermeasures applied to four agricultural emission sources: enteric fermentation, manure management, managed soils, and rice cultivation, for the year 2050. Four scenarios are constructed based on two government reports: a CPS that mirrors existing trajectories; a Viksit Bharat scenario that corresponds with India’s high-income growth aspirations; a Net Zero (NZ) scenario aimed at deep decarbonization; and an integrated scenario that combines both developmental and climatic objectives. Total agricultural greenhouse gas emissions are projected to increase from roughly 345 Mt CO₂eq in 2005 to between 390 and 505 Mt CO₂eq by 2050 across all four scenarios, with enteric fermentation consistently accounting for 55% of the total emissions. Across scenarios, the key findings are: (a) the total mitigation potential without a carbon price is estimated to be between 16 and 22 Mt CO₂eq by 2050 (4–6% of projected emissions), with minimal additional benefits from a USD 25/t CO₂eq carbon price, highlighting the importance of non-price policy instruments in India's agricultural climate transition; (b) most of the countermeasures are ‘No Regret’ options, as they simultaneously reduce emissions while saving cost; (c) the following are the most cost effective countermeasures by source of emission, Feeding Bypass Protein and balanced ration for enteric fermentation, System of Rice Intensification (SRI) for rice, and Need based fertilizer application instead of complete fertilizer subsidy elimination for managed soil.

title: Co-composted biochar–manure sustains rapeseed and cereal yields across a three-year rotation by moderating microbial substrate responsiveness
summary: Reconciling carbon sequestration with sustained crop productivity remains a central challenge in biochar-based soil management. Carbon-stabilizing practices often intensify microbial nutrient immobilization and microbe–crop competition. Whe
content: Reconciling carbon sequestration with sustained crop productivity remains a central challenge in biochar-based soil management. Carbon-stabilizing practices often intensify microbial nutrient immobilization and microbe–crop competition. Whether biochar can realign microbial carbon–nitrogen accessibility to resolve this trade-off remains unclear. We conducted a three-year field experiment under a maize-wheat-rapeseed rotation to test whether a one-time co-composted biochar–manure application reshapes microbial resource accessibility and optimizes nutrient pathways regulating crop productivity. Five treatments were compared: control (CK), biochar (B), manure (M), biochar plus manure (M+B), and co-composted biochar–manure (M+AB). Soil physicochemical properties, potential microbial substrate-utilization response (hereinafter referred to as sum of C and N substrate-induced respiration: ΣIR_C and ΣIR_N), carbon and nitrogen accessibility indices (CAI and NAI), microbial abundance, enzyme activities in 0–10 cm and 10–20 cm soil layers, and cumulative crop yield were evaluated. Compared with CK, M + AB increased soil organic carbon by 17% and improved aggregate stability relative to biochar alone. M stimulated respiration and nutrient utilization, whereas B moderated microbial activity but provided limited yield benefits. In contrast, M + AB balanced ΣIR_C and ΣIR_N responses, reduced nutrient utilization in surface soil, and enhanced nitrifier abundance in deeper soil by (115%), over M+B. CAI and NAI remained tightly coupled (R² = 0.89, P < 0.001), indicating coordinated microbial regulation of resource acquisition under M + AB, whereby CAI strongly predicted crop yield (R² up to 0.95), whereas NAI showed no independent direct relationship. Crucially, by increasing SOC while suppressing excessive microbial activity, the M + AB treatment resolved the carbon–productivity trade-off and achieved the highest cumulative yield (19%) across maize-wheat-rapeseed rotations. This was supported by PLS-PM which showed manure-driven microbial substrate-utilization response in surface soil directly constrained yield, while co-composting weakened this constraint and improved nutrient accessibility, resulting in the highest cumulative crop yield. These findings demonstrate that M + AB reshapes microbial resource accessibility rather than simply supplying nutrients, enabling sustained productivity from a single application. Managing carbon accessibility and microbial substrate-utilization response regulation is therefore critical for synchronizing soil carbon sequestration with crop productivity.

title: Are climate targets consistent with biodiversity goals? A hard-linked IAM assessment for Brazil
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Climate mitigation and biodiversity conservation are often addressed separately, despite their strong interdependencies, particularly in land-use-intensive economies such as Brazil. This study develops a framework to integrate biodiversity
content: Climate mitigation and biodiversity conservation are often addressed separately, despite their strong interdependencies, particularly in land-use-intensive economies such as Brazil. This study develops a framework to integrate biodiversity constraints into an integrated assessment model (IAM) and to assess their implications for Brazil’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). Using the Brazilian Land Use and Energy Systems (BLUES) model, biodiversity is incorporated through a hard-link approach based on indicators such as the Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII), species richness, and human pressure. These indicators are translated into model constraints, directly influencing land-use allocation and mitigation strategies. Two scenarios are analysed: a baseline scenario reflecting Brazil’s current NDC and a biodiversity-constrained pathway aligned with national and global conservation targets. This framework allows the exploration of how ecological limits may reshape mitigation strategies, particularly in the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector, where land-based mitigation options play a central role. This approach further allows the exploration of how explicitly accounting for biodiversity constraints may alter the composition of mitigation portfolios, limiting the expansion of land-intensive options and promoting more balanced strategies across sectors. Our findings suggest that climate pathways aligned with Brazil’s NDC may not be consistent with biodiversity objectives if ecological constraints are not explicitly incorporated. By integrating biodiversity directly into an optimisation framework, this study contributes to advancing IAM methodologies and supports the development of more coherent policy strategies that align climate mitigation with biodiversity conservation goals.

title: Synergizing Local Culture And Religious Values For Inclusive Human Resource Development: Evidence From Muslim-Majority Organizations in Southeast Asia
source: Dirasah International Journal of Islamic Studies
summary: Religious organizations in Southeast Asia face increasing challenges in preserving local cultural and religious identities while developing human resources capable of responding to globalization, digital transformation, and growing demands
content: Religious organizations in Southeast Asia face increasing challenges in preserving local cultural and religious identities while developing human resources capable of responding to globalization, digital transformation, and growing demands for organizational inclusivity. Although cultural and religious values are widely recognized in human resource management research, they are often treated as contextual factors rather than as core resources shaping organizational practices. This study aims to identify and analyze the cultural-religious values underlying human resource development in Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) and Muhammadiyah, examine how these values are operationalized in inclusive practices, and develop a conceptual framework of value synergy for inclusive human resource development. This research employed a qualitative comparative case study involving twenty-eight purposively selected participants, including organizational leaders, higher education administrators, cadre development managers, and members of both organizations. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, document analysis, and limited participant observation and analyzed using thematic within-case and cross-case strategies. The findings reveal two distinct models of value-based human resource development. NU develops a relational-spiritual model grounded in Aswaja, sanad, tasamuh, tawazun, and ukhuwah. In contrast, Muhammadiyah applies a formal, structured model based on tajdid, amanah, ‘adl, ihsan, and rahmatan lil ‘alamin. Both models promote inclusivity through different mechanisms, although NU faces potential network exclusivity and Muhammadiyah experiences tensions related to performance pressure. The study implies that cultural and religious values can function as strategic organizational resources when systematically translated into inclusive human resource development practices, contributing to sustainable organizational capability.

title: Improved Daily Fertilizer-Induced Ammonia Emission Inventory for China by Combining Satellite Remote Sensing and Machine Learning
summary: Abstract. Temporal variability of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution is strongly influenced by ammonia (NH3) emissions, particularly their high-frequency variation driven by nitrogen fertilization. However, the unavailability of dail
content: Abstract. Temporal variability of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution is strongly influenced by ammonia (NH3) emissions, particularly their high-frequency variation driven by nitrogen fertilization. However, the unavailability of daily fertilization dates renders the spatiotemporal distribution of fertilizer-induced NH3 emissions unclear, thereby limiting the accuracy of NH3 emission estimates and PM2.5 prediction. We developed a new method that identifies daily fertilization dates from multisource satellite observations and quantifies daily NH3 emissions using machine learning. The identified fertilization dates correlated well with reported fertilization dates (mean correlation coefficient R = 0.96). Total NH3 emissions from major crop fertilization were estimated at 3.01 Tg in 2021. The 10 % of days with the highest emissions accounted for 33.11 % of the annual total, with an average of 31.15 Gg d−1 on these days. The new inventory substantially improved the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF-Chem) simulation of PM2.5, reducing the average root mean square error (RMSE) by 35.34 % during typical fertilization events. These daily datasets enable a shift from annual emission controls to temporally targeted mitigation strategies, and suggest that optimizing fertilization timing could mitigate severe PM2.5 pollution.

title: Changing with the climate: A review of on-farm adaptation behaviour dynamics for research, practice, and policy
summary: Understanding behavioural dynamics behind farm-level climate adaptation is crucial for research, policy, and practice. This systematic scoping review synthesises 72 empirical studies (2013-2024) across high-income countries in Europe, North
content: Understanding behavioural dynamics behind farm-level climate adaptation is crucial for research, policy, and practice. This systematic scoping review synthesises 72 empirical studies (2013-2024) across high-income countries in Europe, North America, Australia, and New Zealand to resolve evidence fragmentation across disciplines and sectors. Based on PRISMA guidelines and combining narrative synthesis and content analysis, we analyse drivers and barriers of farm-level behaviour across five key thematic categories: cognitive-perceptual, experiential-identity, structural-environmental, social-normative, and informational. We establish an integrative conceptual framework revealing two core psychosocial decision pathways: one via attitude-shaped by climate change appraisal, beliefs, and risk perceptions-and another driven by perceived behavioural control (PBC), influenced by structural, financial, policy, and social conditions. Incremental adaptations rely heavily on the practical PBC-pathway, whereas transformative adaptations are more shock-driven and ideological, operating through the attitude-pathway. The framework provides actionable leverage points for context-specific policies, multi-actor knowledge exchange, and social learning.

title: The Role of Clean Energy Policies in Promoting Green Finance and Sustainable Economic Development in Emerging Economies
summary: Abstract The global reliance on fossil fuels can be alleviated through green investment in sustainable energy. This study critically analyses the effectiveness of current RE policy instruments in attracting green investment for developing h
content: Abstract The global reliance on fossil fuels can be alleviated through green investment in sustainable energy. This study critically analyses the effectiveness of current RE policy instruments in attracting green investment for developing household wind turbines (HWT) in Pakistan. The foremost purpose of the research is to evaluate the most significant policy instruments for implementing wind technology. The study used a purposive (non-probability) sampling approach to administer an opinion poll on energy strategy and collect data from 476 respondents (response rate 81.65%). The study used partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the hypotheses. The results empirically support the proposed hypothesis, suggesting that the designated variables have a significant positive impact on HWT adoption. The model explained 54.6% of the variation in intention (R²) and supported H1, H3, H4, H6, and H7. However, the results did not support H2. The outcomes suggest that Feed-in Tariffs are the most efficient strategy for attracting green investment in the country's HWT sector. The results also indicate that AI-based good governance positively and significantly moderates the nexus between RE policy instruments and green investment for HWT. Regulatory authorities must prioritize energy-related policies. In both developed and developing nations, renewable energy (RE) policies have emerged as a critical concern. The study results offer a practical guide and key policy recommendations for energy-sector officials, legislators, and administrative institutions to implement innovative RE strategy tools that encourage residents to invest in green energy in Pakistan.

title: The Green Envelope: Facade Design Strategies for Sustainable Architecture in Developing Countries like Bangladesh
source: International Journal of Architecture Arts and Applications
summary: The building sector is a first-rate contributor to energy consumption and carbon emissions, making the development of climate-responsive building envelopes increasingly vital for countries experiencing rapid urbanization and environmental p
content: The building sector is a first-rate contributor to energy consumption and carbon emissions, making the development of climate-responsive building envelopes increasingly vital for countries experiencing rapid urbanization and environmental pressure. In Bangladesh, where high temperatures, humidity, solar exposure, and the growing intensity of urban heat create significant challenges to building performance, facade design has considerable potential to reduce energy demand and improve indoor environmental conditions. Although previous studies have examined individual sustainable facade techniques, including adaptive shading, high-performance materials, green walls, and other green facade technologies, there remains a lack of an integrated approach that evaluates these techniques collectively under the climatic and architectural conditions of Bangladesh. In particular, limited research has connected facade-level interventions with energy performance, indoor thermal comfort, and urban heat mitigation within a coherent green-envelope framework. This research, therefore, aims to examine the potential of the Green Envelope as an integrated approach to sustainable facade design in Bangladesh. The study has four major objectives: (1) to identify and critically examine sustainable facade techniques applicable to the climatic and environmental conditions of Bangladesh; (2) to evaluate the effectiveness of adaptive shading, high-performance materials, and green-wall systems in improving building energy performance and indoor thermal comfort; (3) to investigate the potential contribution of green facade interventions to reducing heat gain and mitigating urban heat-island effects; and (4) to develop design recommendations for integrating these strategies into climate-responsive and resilient building facades. The research combines a review of relevant literature with architectural case-study analysis, field-based observations, and environmental performance simulations to assess facade strategies under local climatic conditions. The findings are intended to establish a more integrated understanding of how green-envelope interventions can be combined rather than implemented as isolated measures. The study contributes a context-responsive framework for architects, urban planners, and policymakers seeking to improve building environmental performance and climate resilience in Bangladesh. While the research focuses mainly on facade-level strategies and simulated performance, further investigation through long-term monitoring and post-occupancy assessment is recommended. The proposed method can also provide a foundation for adapting green-envelope strategies to other developing-country contexts facing comparable climatic and urban challenges.

title: Cost Provenance Influences the Economic Ranking of Battery and Green Hydrogen Storage under Solar Surplus in Nusantara Capital City
summary: Abstract Comparing battery and green hydrogen storage requires a common energy boundary and consistent component-cost provenance, particularly when planning renewable-energy infrastructure. This study evaluates both pathways for a represent
content: Abstract Comparing battery and green hydrogen storage requires a common energy boundary and consistent component-cost provenance, particularly when planning renewable-energy infrastructure.
