We provide these extensions both in energy and exergy terms — exergy is a quality-adjusted measure of energy closely linked to economic activity when quantified at the useful stage. For comprehensiveness, we also compute and release the country-level production- and consumption-based (footprint) energy accounts. The dataset we release is the most detailed set of final- and useful-stage energy extensions for a major EE-MRIO model.

title: Predictors of climate anxiety and climate policy support in a British public
summary: The current study investigates the existence of climate anxiety amongst a British public. Given the threat presented to human wellbeing from a changing climate, this study adds to a growing research body that seeks to understand and improve
content: The current study investigates the existence of climate anxiety amongst a British public. Given the threat presented to human wellbeing from a changing climate, this study adds to a growing research body that seeks to understand and improve efforts to help deal with the mental health challenge climate change is increasingly presenting to the public. Using an online sample, 898 participants were asked to complete various survey measures including climate anxiety, storm fear, existential thinking, compassion, risk perceptions, policy support and various demographics. Participants were also asked to provide top-of-mind image associations with climate change. Results revealed that although prevalence of climate anxiety is low, the strongest predictors of this construct included age, storm fear, risk perception and existential thinking with younger participants, those who are fearful of severe weather, those who perceive climate change as a serious threat and those who engage in existential thinking behaviours reporting higher levels of climate anxiety. Additionally, ‘alarm’ based image associations were the most frequent top-of-mind thoughts participants associated with climate change with phrases including ‘destruction of our planet’, ‘emergency’ and ‘existential climate disaster’ being provided. Climate anxiety was also a strong predictor in a regression analysis of climate policy support alongside risk perception, political ideology and compassion. The results demonstrate the important need to better understand climate anxiety and the role it is playing as a growing problem amongst a British public.

title: Efficiency and Equity of Gasoline Taxes with Increasing Electric-Powered Vehicle Adoption
summary: Gasoline taxes can incentivize the adoption of electric-powered vehicles, but their higher upfront costs raise concerns about potential regressive effects. This paper examines the efficiency and equity of gasoline taxes in the context of Sp
content: Gasoline taxes can incentivize the adoption of electric-powered vehicles, but their higher upfront costs raise concerns about potential regressive effects. This paper examines the efficiency and equity of gasoline taxes in the context of Spain. Using the universe of vehicle registrations and exploiting temporal and cross-sectional variation, I find that a one-cent increase in the gasoline tax reduces the CO2 emissions rate of purchased vehicles by 0.25%, driven primarily by increased adoption of hybrid and electric-powered vehicles among higher-income households. However, wealthier households' relative tax savings are modest on average. Leveraging a tax reform that sharply increased gasoline prices in nearly half the country, I calculate CO2 savings of 31 kilotons over the vehicles' lifetimes, while the relative additional tax burden on lower-income households increased by 40€ per vehicle under a conservative calculation. A counterfactual revenue-equivalent mileage tax would be slightly less regressive but would not achieve comparable emissions reductions.

title: El Kawsay Raymi como matriz epistémica andina: diálogo de saberes, territorialidad y respuestas comunitarias ante el cambio climático
summary: Este artículo examina el potencial interpretativo del Kawsay Raymi como matriz epistémica situada para comprender relaciones entre temporalidad ritual, territorialidad, reciprocidad y decisiones comunitarias vinculadas con la variabilidad c
content: Este artículo examina el potencial interpretativo del Kawsay Raymi como matriz epistémica situada para comprender relaciones entre temporalidad ritual, territorialidad, reciprocidad y decisiones comunitarias vinculadas con la variabilidad climática. Se desarrolla una investigación cualitativa de carácter documental, hermenéutico y comparativo, basada en literatura científica y documentos institucionales sobre conocimientos indígenas, adaptación climática y experiencias agroecológicas de la región andina y Mesoamérica. Se propone un modelo analítico de cuatro dimensiones —relacionalidad, temporalidad socioecológica, reciprocidad organizativa y reproducción biocultural— que permite diferenciar la noción de matriz epistémica de los marcos ético-políticos del Buen Vivir y el Sumak Kawsay. Los hallazgos consisten en una síntesis interpretativa de experiencias documentadas: la siembra y cosecha de agua en Ayacucho, los diálogos entre conocimiento local y ciencia climática en los Andes ecuatorianos, la milpa maya y las formas de planificación indígena territorial del Cauca como referencia que requiere ampliación documental específica. Se advierte que la evidencia disponible no demuestra la eficacia universal de los Raymis como tecnología climática ni permite identificar reducción cuantificada de emisiones. Se concluye que las prácticas socioculturales ligadas a los ciclos agrícolas pueden constituir espacios de aprendizaje colectivo y gobernanza adaptativa bajo condiciones territoriales concretas; para evaluar sus resultados se requieren diseños participativos, indicadores situados y acuerdos de gobernanza de datos.

title: Data Center Governance Under AI Expansion Pressures
summary: The promised benefits of data centers are global, but their negative impacts are very much local, affecting the energy bills, aquifers and living environments of citizens across the United States. While governments and authorities have hist
content: The promised benefits of data centers are global, but their negative impacts are very much local, affecting the energy bills, aquifers and living environments of citizens across the United States. While governments and authorities have historically provided data centers with incentives such as tax credits and exemptions, AI's aggressive growth in scale has changed this dynamic, and recent months have seen them issue bills and file lawsuits in order to ensure that data centers remain a net positive influence on their legislatures. Existing pieces of federal legislation -- such as the Public Trust Doctrine, the Pollution Prevention, Clean Air and Safe Drinking Water Acts -- exist to manage natural resources, but their scope remains contested, and the current federal government's stance on competitiveness and growth of AI has put the onus on regional governments to endeavor to protect local resources. There are also state- and regional laws and regulations that are relevant for building and operating data centers since, in practice, they require substantial land, electricity, water, and infrastructure at a local level. Given this situation, communities are currently provided with the opportunity to raise their concerns regarding the potential negative impacts of how data centers are built and operated, and have existing regulations that can be used to put pressure on data center operators.

title: Spatially targeted straw gasification pathways for rural energy decarbonization in China.
summary: The transition to sustainable rural energy in China is impeded by spatial decoupling between rural energy demand and regional biomass availability. To accommodate these constraints, this study develops an integrated spatial and synergistic
content: The transition to sustainable rural energy in China is impeded by spatial decoupling between rural energy demand and regional biomass availability. To accommodate these constraints, this study develops an integrated spatial and synergistic evaluation framework to assess the deployment feasibility of distributed straw gasification. We construct the straw-to-energy self-sufficiency ratio to assess provincial biomass substitution capacity and employ a life cycle assessment-based synergistic index to quantify the relative co-benefits of pollution abatement against climate mitigation. Spatial analysis reveals mismatch between rural energy demand and straw availability, shaped by population concentration, regional energy intensity, and fossil-fuel dependence. Furthermore, evaluation across three representative technology pathways demonstrates that as technological scale and integration expand, the dominant environmental benefit transitions from local pollution reduction in small-scale mobile systems to deep decarbonization in straw gasification poly-generation (SGP). Under the assumed SGP deployment scenario, fossil fuel substitution (54%) and biochar carbon sequestration (46%) together provide a theoretical emissions offsetting potential equivalent to 1.5-14.3 times baseline rural energy emissions in nearly half of the provincial-level regions. These findings highlight the importance of region-specific and staged deployment strategies for aligning straw resource availability, rural energy demand, and long-term decarbonization objectives.

title: The suspension of the Indus Water Treaty and its socio-economic
summary: The Indus Water Treaty is a well-known transboundary water-sharing agreement between 18 Pakistan and India. It ensures equitable water distribution between the two countries and plays 19 an important role in economic development and food se
content: The Indus Water Treaty is a well-known transboundary water-sharing agreement between 18 Pakistan and India. It ensures equitable water distribution between the two countries and plays 19 an important role in economic development and food security, especially for Pakistan as a 20 downstream riparian country. In April 2025, India suspended the Indus Water Treaty following 21 a political escalation. This study investigates the potential socio-economic and environmental 22 impacts of surface water supply disruptions in Pakistan’s irrigated agriculture during the 23 treaty’s suspension. Using a scenario-based approach, we estimate changes in site-specific 24 net profits, groundwater consumption, CO2 emissions, and social consequences. Under 25 baseline conditions, average annual net profit is estimated at 9.6 billion US$, with groundwater 26 withdrawals at 66 km3 and irrigated-related emissions of 3.67 Mt CO2. Simulated reductions in 27 surface water availability of 10-50%, representing plausible future disruptions and a rapid shift 28 toward energy‑intensive groundwater dependence, show net profit declines of up to 74%, while 29 groundwater use and CO2 emissions increase by up to 51% and 44%, respectively. The Socio-30 Economic Impact Perception Index, estimated at 3.16 on a 1–4 scale, indicates a high level of 31 perceived vulnerability among farmers, driven by uncertainty, increased production costs, and 32 reliance on energy-intensive groundwater pumping. These findings highlight that the 33 suspension of the Indus Water Treaty likely amplifies economic, environmental, and social 34 risks in Pakistan by accelerating unsustainable groundwater use. 35

title: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network
summary: Accurate temperatures forecasting relies on traditional meteorological parameters that are essential for monitoring weather informatics and guiding forecasting efforts. This study presents Deep DualMamba, a novel deep learning framework for
content: Accurate temperatures forecasting relies on traditional meteorological parameters that are essential for monitoring weather informatics and guiding forecasting efforts. This study presents Deep DualMamba, a novel deep learning framework for temporal temperature prediction, built upon an enhanced variant of the recently proposed Mamba network. Unlike conventional Transformer-based architectures, which dominate foundation models but suffer from computational inefficiencies on long sequences, Deep DualMamba leverages selective structured state space models (SSMs) to achieve both scalability and performance. We identify a core limitation of prior subquadratic-time models-namely, their inability to perform long-term and robust forecasting and introduce two key innovations. First, we propose an adaptive bidirectional Mamba as encoders to learn complex and efficient features. Second, we develop a hardware-aware, parallel recurrent algorithm to compensate for the loss of convolutional efficiency, ensuring practical viability at scale. Last, the Deep DualMamba's approximation ability and convergence is theoretical analyzed. These design choices culminate in a simplified, attention- and MLP-free neural architecture that exhibits linear complexity with sequence length and significantly improved inference throughput. To demonstrate its applicability in climate informatics, we implement a full forecasting pipeline using historical meteorological data from UK monitoring stations.

title: Rural Activities and Land Degradation in Afghanistan: A Case Study of Sanchark District, Sar-e Pol Province
summary: Human activities driven by pressure on natural resources and unsustainable exploitation are important factors associated with land degradation. This study examines the economic, social, cultural, and agricultural factors associated with lan
content: Human activities driven by pressure on natural resources and unsustainable exploitation are important factors associated with land degradation. This study examines the economic, social, cultural, and agricultural factors associated with land degradation in rural areas of Sanchark District, Afghanistan. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey of 100 rural residents, with the sample size determined using Cochran's formula. The questionnaire covered four dimensions: economic, social, cultural, and agricultural factors. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS and Excel. The findings indicated that financial poverty, limited alternative income opportunities, dependence on forest resources, and low environmental awareness were among the important factors respondents perceived as associated with land degradation. Agricultural practices, including converting rangelands into agricultural land, deforestation, and improper plowing, were also identified as important concerns. Furthermore, 89% of respondents were male, and 11% were female, indicating an imbalance in gender representation. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of considering local economic and social conditions, environmental awareness, and agricultural practices in developing strategies for sustainable land and natural resource management.

title: Remediation of Petroleum-Contaminated Soils Using Coconut Shell-Derived Activated Carbon: A Systematic Review of Adsorption Mechanisms, Comparative Performance, and Field-Scale Challenges
source: Journal of Agricultural and Environmental Science Research
summary: Petroleum hydrocarbon contamination of soil remains a persistent environmental challenge, particularly in oil-producing regions where conventional remediation technologies are often constrained by high cost, secondary pollution, and limited
content: Petroleum hydrocarbon contamination of soil remains a persistent environmental challenge, particularly in oil-producing regions where conventional remediation technologies are often constrained by high cost, secondary pollution, and limited field effectiveness. Activated carbon–based remediation has emerged as a promising alternative; however, existing studies are fragmented across feedstocks and environmental matrices, making it difficult to identify materials with consistent soil-specific performance. This review systematically identifies and evaluates experimental and comparative studies on the use of activated carbon derived from coconut shell (CSAC) for the remediation of petroleum-polluted soils, with emphasis on adsorption mechanisms, material properties, and soil-relevant performance metrics. Evidence from laboratory and soil-based studies indicates that CSAC exhibits high adsorption efficiency for petroleum hydrocarbons, achieving total petroleum hydrocarbon removal efficiencies ranging from approximately 56 to over 90%, depending on adsorbent dosage, contact time, and soil characteristics. Its predominantly microporous structure, high surface area, mechanical stability, and low ash content underpin strong affinity for non-polar hydrocarbons and sustained contaminant immobilization. Compared with other biomass-derived activated carbons, CSAC consistently demonstrates superior removal efficiency at lower amendment rates, while remaining economically viable due to the abundance of coconut shell waste. The review further highlights key limitations related to field-scale application, regeneration, and integration with biological processes, and identifies priority research directions for advancing CSAC-based soil remediation. The findings position CSAC as a cost-effective, sustainable, and scalable material capable of supporting long-term restoration of petroleum-contaminated soils in alignment with global soil protection and circular economy goals.

content: Azolla-based nutrient management was examined in a completely randomized flooded-rice pot experiment with four treatments (T1, control; T2, urea; T3, Azolla; T4, Azolla plus urea), three independent pots per treatment, and five plant subsamples per pot. Pot-level exact treatment-label permutation sensitivity analyses indicated treatment differences in time-averaged height and tillering and in centered temporal profiles (exact p < 0.05). Final-assessment height means were 42.03, 86.99, 101.33 and 101.92 cm for T1–T4. The investigator confirmed that manually separated, sun-dried filled-grain mass was recorded in g plant⁻¹ and averaged within pots; treatment means were 0.13, 1.40, 3.53 and 3.60 g plant⁻¹. The grain-mass omnibus permutation test gave p = 0.006169, but multiplicity-adjusted pairwise comparisons did not establish superiority. Grain moisture was estimated, not standardized. These pot results do not establish field yield, N equivalence or fertilizer replacement.

title: The Role of Supply Chains in Climate Disclosure
summary: ABSTRACT We examine the role of supply chains in shaping the public disclosure of climate information. We leverage a unique empirical setting enabled by CDP—the leading platform for corporate climate risk reporting—which allows customers to
content: ABSTRACT We examine the role of supply chains in shaping the public disclosure of climate information. We leverage a unique empirical setting enabled by CDP—the leading platform for corporate climate risk reporting—which allows customers to demand climate‐related information from their suppliers. Using a large international sample of customer–supplier pairs, we find a positive association between customers’ information demand and suppliers’ public disclosure on the CDP. While the estimated association is modest on average, it exhibits substantial cross‐sectional variation reflecting the disclosure incentives of both customers and suppliers as well as their relative bargaining power. We also find descriptive evidence consistent with one potential implication of the documented association for corporate decision‐making: shifts in supply network relationships toward greener and more transparent suppliers. Overall, our findings contribute to ongoing debates on how to foster climate disclosure.

title: Beyond the grid: policies and economic factors behind renewable energy consumption
source: Journal of Environmental Economics and Policy
summary: The global community is facing increasing risks associated with climate change and a continuously growing demand for energy. This development has made apparent the necessity of transitioning from high-emission fossil fuels to cleaner, more
content: The global community is facing increasing risks associated with climate change and a continuously growing demand for energy. This development has made apparent the necessity of transitioning from high-emission fossil fuels to cleaner, more sustainable energy sources and renewable energy is a key pillar of this transition. This paper studies the influence of various environmental, economic, fiscal and monetary policy factors on the expansion of renewable energy consumption. The analysis uses a global sample of 40 countries over the period 1990–2020 to study how these policy dimensions and economic factors shape the share of renewable energy within national energy mixes. The findings indicate that environmental policies, particularly market-based instruments and technology support measures, have a positive and significant impact on the change of renewable energy consumption (REC). Fiscal policy variables have more consistent statistically significant relationships with REC than the monetary policy variables examined. The split-sample analysis indicates that the Environmental Policy Stringency indicator is statistically significant only among EU member states. Additionally, private investment has a delayed significant effect for this subgroup, which implies potential differences in policy effectiveness and institutional frameworks between EU and Non-EU countries.

title: Probabilities of detection of methane plumes by remote sensing and implications for inferred emissions distributions
summary: Strategies for mitigating methane emissions rely on understanding the underlying drivers of methane emissions to the atmosphere. Observations of methane plumes emerging from point sources, combined with correct statistical interpretation, c
content: Strategies for mitigating methane emissions rely on understanding the underlying drivers of methane emissions to the atmosphere. Observations of methane plumes emerging from point sources, combined with correct statistical interpretation, can provide key information. In this work, we examine a critical parameter, the probability of detection of a plume. For a given observing system, probability of detection is affected by the properties of the sensor, plume detection algorithm, observing conditions, and emission rate of the source. We parameterize relevant aspects of remotely sensed scenes containing plumes using a nondimensional observability parameter that predicts probability of detection. Our probability of detection model is trained using simulated plumes to capture natural variability in different meteorological conditions, and validated with data from controlled release experiments. We model probability of detection for two airborne imaging spectrometer systems, MethaneAIR and Insight M LeakSurveyor™, and one high resolution satellite system, MethaneSAT. Monte Carlo simulations of emissions distributions implied by data from the extensive 2023 MAIRX campaign of MethaneAIR demonstrate the importance of an accurate probability of detection model to analyze observations from systems with higher emission rate thresholds for detection, due to the heavy tailed emission rate distribution found in most North American oil and gas basins. Additionally, we find that the frequency of rare, high impact emission events drives high uncertainty in distributions of total emissions by emission rate.

title: Bio-inspired mineralization of CO2 to nanoscaled hydrozincite mediated via Zea mays saccharata
summary: Abstract The bio-inspired mineralization of CO 2 to single-phase Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 was demonstrated for the first time in this contribution utilising aqueous extracts of Zea mays saccharata (ZMS). The latter has been a succ
content: Abstract The bio-inspired mineralization of CO 2 to single-phase Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 was demonstrated for the first time in this contribution utilising aqueous extracts of Zea mays saccharata (ZMS). The latter has been a successful chelating and capping agent. Under ambient circumstances (room temperature & atmospheric pressure), this novel method produced single-phase crystalline hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 with an average crystallite size of 38.5 nm. The UV–VIS–DRS, PL, FT-IR, XRD, and SEM–EDS studies sustained the potential of the bio-engineered nanoscaled Hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 as a highly reflective material (Diffuse reflectance > 95%) and an effective blue luminescence (λ MaxEmission ≈ 457.3 nm). Electrochemical properties were investigated in 1 M NaOH electrolyte using cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). CV studies demonstrated a significant increase in current response with distinct Faradaic peaks at + 0.07 V, + 0.18 V, and − 0.16 V (vs. Ag|AgCl), confirming the inherent electrochemical activity and surface redox behaviour of the nanoparticles. This was further corroborated by EIS, which showed a substantial reduction in charge transfer resistance (R ct ) from 845.84 kΩ for the bare glassy carbon electrode (GCE) to 94.30 kΩ for the Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 modified GCE, indicating enhanced charge-transfer kinetics. These results demonstrate a bio-engineering route for synthesizing single-phase crystalline hydrozincite Zn 5 (CO 3 ) 2 (OH) 6 nanoparticles with favorable opto-electrochemical properties, including enhanced electrochemical behaviour and charge transfer characteristics. Furthermore, the study demonstrates the feasibility of CO 2 mineralization to hydrozincite under ambient conditions.

title: The social–ecological system framework for farming adaptation: the influence of social capital on eco-practices
summary: Climate change has intensified the urgency of ecological transitions, particularly within small-scale farming systems, which are vital for food supply but highly vulnerable to environmental pressures. This study applies the Social-Ecologica
content: Climate change has intensified the urgency of ecological transitions, particularly within small-scale farming systems, which are vital for food supply but highly vulnerable to environmental pressures. This study applies the Social-Ecological System framework to examine how different forms of social capital (bonding, bridging, and linking) shape ecological practices and identifies climate change as a collective action issue. Using survey data from Sardinian sheep farmers, a Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) disentangles the effects of social capital on the adoption of ecological innovations. Results show that bonding social capital reinforces traditional ecological practices, while trust in agricultural institutions ( agro-linking ) is the most consistent predictor of adoption across both traditional and innovative pathways. In contrast, bridging and institutional linking show no statistically significant effect in this context. Productivity expectations and eco-technical knowledge further mediate adoption, highlighting both economic and cognitive drivers of the adoption process. The findings provide empirical evidence of the multidimensional effects of social capital on distinct ecological pathways, offering policy-relevant insights. Sustaining traditional practices requires leveraging local networks and community knowledge, whereas innovation-oriented policies should focus on building institutional trust, technical knowledge, and closer farmer–institution linkages.

title: Organic matter composition and origin differ between restored and natural UK saltmarshes up to 100 years after the breach
summary: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. While carbon stocks in restored marshes were found to reach equivalence with natural sites, the shares of autoc
content: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. While carbon stocks in restored marshes were found to reach equivalence with natural sites, the shares of autochthonous and allochthonous carbon sources entering these marshes are less well known. This issue is important because allochthonous carbon is usually excluded from stock calculations. To determine if differences do exist, the conventional tools for determining organic matter source – elemental, stable isotope and thermogravimetric analyses – were applied to sediments from four restored saltmarshes of different ages. Comparisons were then made with existing data from nearby natural marshes. Breach depth horizons in individual cores were successfully identified using foraminifera, unicellular marine protists. The OC/N-ratio was persistently lower in restored saltmarshes compared with natural counterparts even 100 years after the creation of a breach. Additionally, δ 13 C signals indicated a mixture of organic matter sources to the restored sites and there was often a higher proportion, based upon thermal sensitivity, of recalcitrant material in the organic matter of the restored marshes. Together, these results indicated that a higher proportion of allochthonous organic matter was entering these restored marshes. Understanding the composition of the organic matter in restored marsh sediment will allow the development of robust and constructive climate change mitigation methods.

title: Compact Wafer-Bonded Fabry–Perot Cavity-Based Photothermal Spectroscopy for Gas Sensing
summary: Abstract Currently available electrochemical and direct absorption gas sensor approaches suffer from weak molecular selectivity, challenges in miniaturization, and constraints in cost-effective large-scale manufacturing. In contrast, the in
content: Abstract Currently available electrochemical and direct absorption gas sensor approaches suffer from weak molecular selectivity, challenges in miniaturization, and constraints in cost-effective large-scale manufacturing. In contrast, the integration of an interferometric cavity-assisted technique with photothermal spectroscopy (PTS) provides an alternative solution promising improved sensitivity and increased dynamic range. Here, we report a compact wafer-bonded Fabry–Perot (WB-FP) cavity fabricated using a Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) and demonstrate its use as a photothermal transducer for gas sensing. Unlike conventional manually assembled Fabry–Perot (FP) cavities, the proposed design defines cavity permenant alignment during fabrication, providing a pathway toward scalable and reproducible photonic gas sensors. In this architecture, a near-infrared (NIR) beam is collimated and propagated through a 500 μm spaced FP cavity to probe the photothermal effects induced by interactions between the target gas molecules and the optical pump beam inside the cavity volume. To demonstrate the applicability of the developed sensor system, the metrological figures of merit were evaluated using methane (CH4) as the targeted analyte across a range of concentrations. Targeting the absorption band centered at 6047 cm–1, the system achieves a minimum detection limit (MDL) of 42 ppm with a 1 s integration time. Allan deviation analysis further indicates an improved MDL of 5.1 ppm at an optimal integration time of 100 s, corresponding to a normalized noise-equivalent absorption (NNEA) coefficient of 3.27 × 10–7 cm–1 W Hz–1/2. These results highlight the potential of the wafer-bonded FP cavity as a scalable, compact transducer for photothermal gas sensing, bridging the route toward miniaturized, stable, cost-effective, and high-sensitivity gas technologies.

title: Co-creating Taita-Taveta County energy demand projections for integrated national energy planning in Kenya through a mixed methods modelling approach
summary: Energy devolution in Kenya has progressed unevenly, with many counties yet to complete their County Energy Plans (CEPs), posing challenges for integration into the forthcoming Integrated National Energy Plan (INEP). A key gap lies in transl
content: Energy devolution in Kenya has progressed unevenly, with many counties yet to complete their County Energy Plans (CEPs), posing challenges for integration into the forthcoming Integrated National Energy Plan (INEP). A key gap lies in translating qualitative, needs-based insights from county planning documents into quantitative inputs for energy demand modelling. This study applies a mixed-methods approach to address this gap. Building on existing Model for the Analysis of Energy Demand (MAED)-based datasets and multi-scale modelling frameworks, we develop a structured process to translate qualitative planning narratives into quantitative scenario assumptions. Using Taita Taveta County (TTC) as a case study, we construct four demand scenarios (baseline, ambitious, reserved, and a county priorities scenario). The latter is co-developed through interviews, a workshop, and analysis of CEP and County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) documents with 26 county and national stakeholders. The county priorities scenario is operationalised by systematically mapping qualitative insights, such as electrification ambitions, cooking transitions, and sectoral development priorities, onto model parameters, including electrification rates, fuel shares, sectoral composition, and technical coefficients. The resulting scenarios illustrate how aligning modelling assumptions with county planning narratives produces different demand trajectories and sectoral structures compared to nationally aligned socio-economic scenarios. The findings highlight both the value and challenges of incorporating locally grounded qualitative insights into energy demand modelling, particularly regarding transparency, uncertainty, and inclusivity. This study provides an applied demonstration of how county-level planning documents can be translated into structured inputs for energy demand modelling, supporting alignment between devolved planning processes and national modelling efforts in Kenya. Results should be interpreted as exploratory rather than predictive.

title: Developing a deep learning–based model to predict simulated building performance using the spatial layout of residential apartments in Isfahan
summary: Spatial configuration is a primary determinant of residential building performance, yet evaluating trade-offs across design alternatives remains computationally intensive. This study introduces an integrated computational framework combinin
content: Spatial configuration is a primary determinant of residential building performance, yet evaluating trade-offs across design alternatives remains computationally intensive. This study introduces an integrated computational framework combining a Generative Spatial Layout (GSL) algorithm, Building Performance Simulation, and a hybrid multi-input Deep Learning (DL) model to rapidly predict multi-objective performance. Focusing on south-facing rectangular apartments in Isfahan, 27,000 distinct design configurations were generated and evaluated across six performance metrics: cooling demand, heating demand, useful daylight illuminance (UDI), embodied carbon, operational carbon, and embodied water. The dataset was partitioned into training (70%), validation (10%), and testing (20%) subsets to train the hybrid DL architecture, which integrates dense numerical layers and Transformer-based spatial sequence processing. The Mean Squared Error (MSE) value demonstrates the optimal performance of the study’s ML model, indicating high prediction accuracy. Moreover, the coefficients of determination (R 2 ) for all performance indicators range between 0.95 and 0.997, demonstrating strong predictive performance within the evaluated dataset. Analysis further reveals the significant influence of the dimensions, location, and number of Indoor Spaces, particularly the living room and Vertical Circulation Core, on energy and environmental performance. The hybrid DL approach proves effective for predicting residential building performance using multidimensional GSL datasets. Findings identify spatial optimization and strategic Vertical Circulation Core placement as critical factors for improving overall building efficiency.

title: Targeted Meshing Guidelines for Accurate Axisymmetric CFD Prediction of Supersonic Ejector Performance for Sustainable Refrigeration Systems
summary: Supersonic ejectors are axisymmetric devices governed by radially symmetric flow phenomena and employed in cooling and refrigeration systems. This paper investigates the sensitivity of their numerical simulation to the meshing strategy by e
content: Supersonic ejectors are axisymmetric devices governed by radially symmetric flow phenomena and employed in cooling and refrigeration systems. This paper investigates the sensitivity of their numerical simulation to the meshing strategy by evaluating eight distinct mesh configurations against three criteria: entrainment ratio, internal flow characteristics, and computational time. The meshes are grouped into three categories according to the location of the remeshing relative to the point at which the secondary flow enters, and compared against a reference case. The global performance analysis reveals that coarse meshes underestimate the ejector’s operating range by nearly 10% and fail to resolve a distinct critical point, whereas insufficient refinement of the upper part of the first flow contact region overpredicts the entrainment ratio by nearly 1% under critical conditions. As a consequence, the effective area of the secondary throat proves sensitive to mesh density, producing deviations of around 0.5% in the secondary mass flow. The study also quantifies the computational trade-off, demonstrating that calculation time in subcritical working conditions scales super-linearly with cell count. Notably, meshes that precisely resolve the initial flow interaction zone achieve better numerical stability and require fewer iterations per cell than topologically inefficient meshes with fewer cells.

title: Synthesis, properties and applications nanoporous carbons with graphene sheets
summary: Incorporation of graphene layers into amorphous porous carbon affords hybrid carbonaceous nanostructures with a large specific surface area and high porosity originating from nanoporous carbons and enhanced electrical conductivity, and mech
content: Incorporation of graphene layers into amorphous porous carbon affords hybrid carbonaceous nanostructures with a large specific surface area and high porosity originating from nanoporous carbons and enhanced electrical conductivity, and mechanical strength originating from graphene. These hybrid carbon structures are useful for many important applications, including environmental protection (particularly in air and water purification), catalysis, sensors, energy storage, electronics and batteries, tissue engineering, and many others. Since the methods used to produce these materials strongly influence the final pore architecture, as well as their chemical and mechanical properties and consequently, their applications, it is essential to identify correlations between the properties and functionality of such materials. This review provides a detailed assessment of various methods for producing porous carbon structures with graphene layers, with particular emphasis on graphene oxide as a main component. It presents synthesis methods in relation to the resulting morphologies, adsorption properties, mechanical characteristics, and typical applications. Special attention is given to the syntheses that allow for different contents of graphene oxide and its impact on the properties required for specific applications. The main objective of this review is to present various strategies for creating graphene-based nanoporous materials, with particular emphasis on those in which graphene oxide significantly affects the properties of the final material. The review also highlights the relationship between the carbon precursor materials, the synthesis procedures, and the resulting properties, with special focus on adsorption characteristics that determine their potential applications. A comprehensive analysis of the proposed synthesis strategies could be useful for researchers interested in the preparation and characterization of graphene-based nanoporous materials.

title: Model run and scenario data for study "Cost effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions"

summary: This data archive contains model runs and data analysis files to the research article Cost effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions by Leon Merfort, Alexander Popp, Nico Bauer, Florian Humpenöder, Gabriel Abrahã
content: This data archive contains model runs and data analysis files to the research article Cost effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions by Leon Merfort, Alexander Popp, Nico Bauer, Florian Humpenöder, Gabriel Abrahão, Benjamin Leon Bodirsky, David Meng-Chuen Chen, Laurin Köhler-Schindler, Gunnar Luderer, Rahel Mandaroux, Anne Merfort, Jessica Strefler, Elmar Kriegler published in Nature Sustainability (2026). Merfort2026_LandContributions_ModelRuns_Final.tar.gz (directory) contains all REMIND-MAgPIE model runs of the scenarios underlying the paper. Merfort2026_LandContributions_DataAnalysis_Final.zip (directory) contains an RStudio Project that was used for the data analysis and the generation of the figures of the paper. It additionally contains all scenario source data to reproduce the figures. README.docx contains the mapping from scenario names used in the paper to the model experiment names (in the model run directories).

title: Closing the research–practice gap in waterlogging modelling through holistic systems thinking and spatially explicit simulation
summary: Soil waterlogging is a major constraint to global crop production yet remains poorly integrated into agricultural monitoring and decision-support frameworks because waterlogging events are episodic and spatially heterogeneous, while existin
content: Soil waterlogging is a major constraint to global crop production yet remains poorly integrated into agricultural monitoring and decision-support frameworks because waterlogging events are episodic and spatially heterogeneous, while existing modelling approaches largely address individual components of the problem in isolation. We argue that, alongside continued improvement in the representation of key processes, a major and under-addressed bottleneck lies in integrating existing modelling capabilities into an operational decision-support pipeline. Here we propose a conceptual, systems-oriented framework, intended for further development and testing rather than as an implemented decision-support system, that links spatially explicit hazard assessment, crop response simulation and multi-objective evaluation to support adaptation planning. We outline a three-stage modelling pipeline that identifies where and when waterlogging is likely to occur, evaluates alternative engineering, agronomic and genetic interventions, and quantifies trade-offs among productivity, profitability and environmental outcomes. We specify the information exchanged between stages, illustrate the pipeline with a literature-based example, and outline how it could be evaluated and how uncertainty could be handled. Finally, we identify key priorities for advancing waterlogging modelling, including improved process representation of drainage, raised beds, irrigation–groundwater interactions and other adaptation strategies, stronger integration across modelling domains, and closer alignment between modelling outputs and stakeholder needs, beginning with joint framing of the decision problem. By providing a structured pathway for integrating current and future modelling advances into decision support, this framework aims to accelerate the translation of waterlogging research into practical adaptation.

content: يقدم هذا التقرير الهندسي تصميماً ثورياً لـ "منظومة أوزوريس"، وهي مصفوفة كوكبية لامركزية ومجزأة تتكون من ملايين العوامات الميكروية المصغرة المصممة لحصاد الطاقة الكهربائية الحرة من الغلاف الجوي عبر الرنين الاهتزازي وضبط توازن المناخ لعلاج الاحتباس الحراري. تعتمد المنظومة على حلول هندسية مبتكرة بالمواد المتاحة تجارياً اليوم؛ حيث تحل معضلة كثافة التيار وعازلية الهواء باستخدام "التأريض المائي السائل" في المحيطات وعموم قنوات الرذاذ الأيوني المستمر المدفوع بالضغط الحراري الجوفي. كما توظف المنظومة دارات تقويم فائقة من نيتريد الغاليوم (GaN) ومكثفات كربونية فائقة السعة لتخزين وضبط تدفق الطاقة بأمان مطلق بنسبة 100% ودون إنتاج صواعق تدميرية، لتأمين مورد طاقة كوني مستقر ومستدام يعادل 3.2 تيراواط يسد حاجة الكوكب بالكامل. 📄 Description in English: This engineering report presents a revolutionary design for the "Osiris System", a planetary decentralized micro-array network composed of millions of miniature energy buoys engineered to harvest atmospheric electricity via vibrational resonance while mitigating global warming. Built entirely with currently available commercial materials, the system solves the low current density and air insulation dilemmas by utilizing "liquid hydraulic grounding" in oceans and self-sustaining ionic vapor columns driven by geothermal and wave energy. The design integrates gallium nitride (GaN) solid-state rectifiers and carbon-based supercapacitors to safely regulate and store energy bursts with 100% lightning immunity, providing a rock-solid, sustainable cosmic power output of 3.2 Terawatts to completely fulfill global energy demands.

title: Strong on Diagnosis, Weak on Delivery: A Structured Assessment of Urban Nature-based Solutions Frameworks
summary: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly promoted as essential instruments for urban climate adaptation, biodiversity recovery, and sustainable development. Yet their implementation remains slow and insufficiently monitored. Frameworks
content: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly promoted as essential instruments for urban climate adaptation, biodiversity recovery, and sustainable development. Yet their implementation remains slow and insufficiently monitored. Frameworks, including standards, guidelines, tools, and indicator sets, are meant to bridge the gap between NbS ambition and practice, but it is unclear how comprehensively they support cities across the full range of operational tasks. We conducted a structured qualitative content analysis, with dual-reviewer coding, of 30 NbS frameworks relevant to urban contexts. Each framework was assessed across six operational dimensions: baseline assessment and ecological performance; planning and design; implementation; financing and funding mechanisms; monitoring and evaluation; and impacts and co-benefits. We also evaluated the presence of practical “how-to” guidance and classified each framework into one of four functional archetypes: Integrator, Designer, Financier, or Monitor. Results revealed a structural imbalance: approximately two-thirds of frameworks provided guidance on baseline assessment and planning, while only 36.7% addressed implementation, the lowest of any dimension. Gaps in operational guidance, financing, and monitoring co-occurred systematically, consistent with shared structural causes rooted in disciplinary biases. Only five frameworks achieved consistently high coverage across all functional dimensions. The archetype typology offers practitioners a navigation tool for assembling complementary resources matched to their functional dimensions and governance context. Policy implications include requiring comprehensive planning that addresses both diagnostic and delivery dimensions as a condition of NbS funding. These also include embedding comprehensive monitoring and verification requirements and investing in cross-disciplinary institutional capacity to support scaled implementation.

title: Framing the Past and the Future of Oil in Norwegian Political Manifestos
summary: In this chapter, I explore how Norwegian political parties, from the left to the right side of the political spectrum, use references to the past in their party manifestos to construct narratives about politics concerning the petroleum sect
content: In this chapter, I explore how Norwegian political parties, from the left to the right side of the political spectrum, use references to the past in their party manifestos to construct narratives about politics concerning the petroleum sector and climate change. Norway has historically benefited tremendously from the petroleum industry, organised to secure the prosperity and welfare of the Norwegian population through the Government Pension Fund Global (‘the Oil Fund’). At the same time, climate change has rendered ‘green’ politics increasingly salient, generating a paradoxical communicative environment that makes Norway a compelling case from the perspective of memory studies and political communication. Methodologically, the study rests on a framing analysis of written party manifestos from the election periods 2021–2025. Party programs represent a specific form of strategic communication where political parties present themselves and their visions for the future to the public. In the chapter, I illuminate how references to the past are predominantly formulated as general and pragmatic statements, refraining from nostalgic invocations or long historical arcs. While there seems to be a hesitancy in making strong casual trajectories to the past, it nevertheless represents an important implicit memory for the moral framing of future policies and to what degree oil production should be phased out or continued.

title: Oil and Gas Production Emissions
summary: This chapter argues that the most effective way for the oil and gas industry to contribute to climate mitigation is not through large-scale carbon removal, but by reducing the emissions generated during production itself. Using carbon captu
content: This chapter argues that the most effective way for the oil and gas industry to contribute to climate mitigation is not through large-scale carbon removal, but by reducing the emissions generated during production itself. Using carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) as a benchmark, it shows that upstream production emissions exceed global CCS capacity by more than a factor of 70, making prevention far more impactful than cure. The chapter examines the principal sources of production emissions: routine and non-routine flaring, methane venting and leaks, produced-water handling, refining, and emissions from marginal and abandoned wells, and demonstrates that most are technically solvable with existing technologies. Large differences in emissions intensity across countries and operators reveal that these emissions are driven less by geology than by investment decisions, regulation, and operational practices. The chapter argues that responsible production is both economically and technically achievable, citing examples such as Norway, where low-emission operations coexist with strong profitability. It concludes that decarbonizing production is one of the largest and most practical climate opportunities available to the industry, requiring implementation and accountability rather than scientific breakthroughs.

title: Toward Compatibility Enhancement of Biodegradable Plasticized Cellulose Acetate and Polyhydroxyalkanoate Blends: Effect of Calcium Carbonate and Maleated Hybrid Blend on Material Performance
summary: ABSTRACT The brittleness of plasticized cellulose acetate (pCA) limits its broader application. Blending with tougher biopolymers is a common strategy to improve toughness, but performance is often restricted by poor compatibility between b
content: ABSTRACT The brittleness of plasticized cellulose acetate (pCA) limits its broader application. Blending with tougher biopolymers is a common strategy to improve toughness, but performance is often restricted by poor compatibility between blend components. In this study, poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate‐co‐4‐hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB), an amorphous polyhydroxyalkanoate (aPHA), was incorporated into pCA at three blend ratios. Although solubility parameter calculations suggested partial miscibility, glass transition temperature (T g ) analysis and morphological studies confirmed complete immiscibility. To improve the compatibility, a maleic anhydride (MA)‐grafted hybrid blend compatibilizer and CaCO 3 were introduced into the optimized blend formulation. Morphological and surface analyses revealed a droplet‐matrix structure, where the MA‐based compatibilizer reduced the size of dispersed aPHA domains and promoted smoother modulus transitions across the interface. As a result, elongation at break, impact strength, and heat deflection temperature increased by up to 63%, 36%, and 12%, respectively, compared with the neat blend. Rheological properties showed slight improvement, while in terms of thermal stability the onset degradation temperature rose by up to 21°C. No synergistic effect was observed when both additives were combined. The optimized pCA/aPHA blend exhibited a favorable balance of mechanical, thermal, and thermomechanical properties, demonstrating its potential for rigid packaging applications.

title: A dataset of soil bacterial communities and physicochemical properties under different biogas slurry application patterns during oat growth in the agro-pastoral ecotone
summary: Biogas slurry recycling is an essential practice for improving soil fertility and advancing sustainable agriculture in intensive farmland ecosystems. The application method of biogas slurry strongly affects soil nutrient availability, pH dy
content: Biogas slurry recycling is an essential practice for improving soil fertility and advancing sustainable agriculture in intensive farmland ecosystems. The application method of biogas slurry strongly affects soil nutrient availability, pH dynamics, and microbial community structure. However, systematic datasets covering the combined effects of application patterns, growth stages, and soil depths on soil physicochemical properties and bacterial communities remain limited. This study provides detailed microbiome data with two biogas slurry treatments: surface broadcasting and deep injection, three key growth stages (seedling, jointing, maturity) and two soil depths (0–20 cm and 20–40 cm) collected from semi-arid agro-pastoral ecotones-fragile ecosystem of North China, including 12 samples in total with three replicates per sample. Through high-throughput sequencing of 16S rRNA gene, we generated an extensive dataset with an average of 51,685 high-quality reads per sample. This dataset provides a valuable resource for exploring microbial responses to organic fertilization and supports data reuse in soil nutrient cycling, agroecological modeling, and sustainable management of biogas slurry application.

title: Elicitors-induced modulation of plant performance, essential oil composition, and iridoid biosynthesis in Valeriana jatamansi Jones cultivated under controlled vertical aeroponics
summary: Abstract The integration of aeroponic cultivation and elicitation offers an efficient strategy for enhancing biomass production and specialized metabolite accumulation in medicinal plants. In the current investigation, foliar application of
content: Abstract The integration of aeroponic cultivation and elicitation offers an efficient strategy for enhancing biomass production and specialized metabolite accumulation in medicinal plants. In the current investigation, foliar application of fungal endophyte (FE), seaweed extract (SWE), and salicylic acid (SA) were applied to aeroponically cultivated Valeriana jatamansi to evaluate their effect on morphological growth, biomass yield, physiological performance, antioxidant defence, essential oil production, valepotriate accumulation, biosynthetic gene expression, and antimicrobial activity. SA treatment significantly enhances morphological growth, whereas FE promotes biomass accumulation. Elicitor treatment showed improved photochemical performance and antioxidant defence as indicated by reduced malondialdehyde and H₂O₂ levels and enhanced superoxide dismutase and catalase activities in leaf and root tissues. SWE produced the highest essential oil yield (2.50%) (v/w) and patchouli alcohol concentration (238.31 mg/L), while FE resulted in the highest relative abundance of patchouli alcohol (43.27%) in the oil. FE also markedly enhanced root valepotriate accumulation, with maximum acevaltrate (0.47%), didrovaltrate (0.53%), and valtrate (3.10%) contents. Consistently, qRT-PCR profiling revealed enhanced expression of iridoid pathway genes, including SLS , IS , 7DLGT and 7DLS , following elicitor treatment in leaf and root tissue. Essential oil exhibited strain-dependent antimicrobial activity, with Bacillus subtilis being the most susceptible strain (MIC 0.06 mg/mL). Overall, these findings demonstrate that combining aeroponic cultivation with targeted elicitation can effectively enhance biomass productivity, physiological resilience, essential oil quality, and valuable specialized metabolites in V. jatamansi , presenting a potential strategy for sustainable, scalable production of high-value medicinal plant products.

title: Coupling planning and operations to quantify reliability, investment and market performance in decarbonising electricity systems
summary: Abstract Ensuring the reliable and economic performance of electricity systems with very low emissions are critical challenges that span the planning and operational timescales. This paper therefore presents a modelling framework that unifi
content: Abstract Ensuring the reliable and economic performance of electricity systems with very low emissions are critical challenges that span the planning and operational timescales. This paper therefore presents a modelling framework that unifies investment planning with wholesale electricity market operations by including the operational forecast uncertainties of both variable renewable generation (VRG) and demand as well as full unit commitment constraints. This allows us to assess the impacts of operational uncertainty on wholesale electricity market performance as electricity systems decarbonise. The most decarbonised, reliable fleets without clean firm generation then feature VRG uptake of 80% or more of annual demand, whilst then also requiring reserve margins that are comparable to the average electricity demand. This not only raises total costs significantly to maintain reliability, it can also compromise price signalling and increase investment risk. Since these problems are a consequence of stochastic supply/demand mismatches caused by operationally uncertain VRG, they cannot be solved by improved market design. Rather, these findings suggest that improving the operational forecasting of VRG and enabling the deployment of hydropower, nuclear and other forms of clean firm generation are both urgent priorities if we wish to decarbonise rapidly, reliably and more affordably.

title: An integrated modeling approach for sugar beet cultivation: achieving economic and environmental compatibility in water, food, and energy systems
summary: The increasing challenges of water scarcity, climate change, and energy transition require a redefinition of agricultural systems. In Iran, current land allocation strategies for sugar beet fail to capture its full economic and environmenta
content: The increasing challenges of water scarcity, climate change, and energy transition require a redefinition of agricultural systems. In Iran, current land allocation strategies for sugar beet fail to capture its full economic and environmental value, particularly that of post-harvest residues. This study aimed to develop and apply an integrated national-scale optimization model to maximize the economic performance of Iran’s sugar beet value chain by optimizing provincial cultivation area under a national water-use constraint while incorporating biomethane and biofertilizer production from post-harvest residues. The model integrates province-level data on yield, irrigation demand, and processing capacity, together with cultivation costs and residue valorization through anaerobic digestion into biomethane and biofertilizer. Environmental performance was characterized using proxy indicators, including the potential for CO₂ emissions reduction through biomethane substitution and reduced dependence on synthetic fertilizers, rather than a full life cycle assessment. A differential evolution algorithm is used to maximize total system profitability under a national water-use limitation implemented through a penalty-based constraint handling approach. Results show that reallocating cultivation areas based on water productivity and processing potential increases national net profit by 23.0% without increasing total water consumption. High-efficiency provinces, such as Khuzestan and Golestan, are prioritized, while less efficient regions are downscaled. By incorporating biomethane and biofertilizer production into the economic optimization framework, the model captures the additional value up to 22.13% potential revenue of post-harvest residues while simultaneously improving resource circularity and reducing dependence on synthetic fertilizers. This systems-based approach provides a scalable framework for sustainable and economically efficient agricultural planning.

title: Demand-Side Greenhouse Gas Emission Mitigation in Agri-food Systems in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Protocol for Evidence and Gap Map of Sustainable Dietary Shifts, Food Loss and Waste Reduction, and Food-Mileage Interventions
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: BackgroundAgri-food systems are a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) recognises demand-side measures, particularly sustainable dietary shifts and food loss and waste redu
content: BackgroundAgri-food systems are a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) recognises demand-side measures, particularly sustainable dietary shifts and food loss and waste reduction, as important mitigation pathways, with food-mileage reduction a complementary strategy. Yet existing syntheses draw overwhelmingly on high-income settings: in a recent meta-analysis of 139 demand-side studies, European countries alone accounted for 75% of food-consumption studies. Food-mileage interventions and cost-effectiveness outcomes are rarely mapped. Evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where most future growth in livestock-product consumption is projected, remains poorly characterised. This evidence and gap map (EGM) therefore aims to characterise the nature and distribution of evidence on demand-side GHG mitigation interventions in LMIC agri-food systems.MethodsAgricultural systems around the world are being impacted by climate stressors and hazards. These shocks are felt disproportionately by agricultural producers in LMICs due to existing socio-economic vulnerabilities. In this context, climate adaptation interventions seek to catalyze adaptation processes and outcomes to help producers manage impacts and reduce climate-induced risks to their livelihoods. These interventions and their effectiveness are assessed through a variety of ways, including output and outcomes indicators as a part of M&E systems, qualitative measures of coping capacity, and quantitative resilience indices. Collectively, these concepts represent different approaches to measuring adaptation and constitute the primary focus of this review.

title: Resilience to Landslides in the Lower Shullcas River Basin under Climate Change
summary: The lower Shullcas River basin has a medium-high to low level of risk from landslides. This risk is made worse by geological, climatic, and topographic factors. Climate change, especially through intense rainfall and higher temperatures, in
content: The lower Shullcas River basin has a medium-high to low level of risk from landslides. This risk is made worse by geological, climatic, and topographic factors. Climate change, especially through intense rainfall and higher temperatures, increases this risk and makes it necessary to use proper mitigation strategies and more efficient urban development plans. Even so, there are still weaknesses in how risk management is integrated among the people and institutions involved in the territory. The purpose of this research was to identify the areas with the highest risk through mapping, and also to measure the resilience of the population exposed to the highest level of risk, in order to understand how they might respond and act during a possible disaster. For this purpose, methodologies based on risk prevention systems were used, aligned with SIGRID, CENEPRED, and INGEMMET. The results show favorable findings in some respects, since the study area, which includes the districts of Huancayo and El Tambo, presents medium-to-low landslide risk levels, with slopes ranging from 2% to 8%. The most critical zones are located along the marginal strip of the Shullcas River, where slopes reach up to 90% and where conditioning factors such as rainfall, river undercutting, and geomorphology turn these areas into constant hazards. The resilience evaluation shows less encouraging results, since most of the 50 residents surveyed near the highest-risk zone showed low levels of resilience compared with the coastal population of the country. Finally, it is recommended that more studies be carried out on different types of risk, including other triggering factors such as earthquakes, informal human activity, and geological aspects. It is also recommended to study wider areas because of the rapid population growth.

title: Transcontinental stratospheric and upper tropospheric measurements with the new GLORIA-Lite instrument
summary: Abstract. Accurate observations of the vertical distribution and temporal variability of atmospheric trace gases are essential for understanding atmospheric composition and chemistry and for evaluating atmospheric models. The Gimballed Limb
content: Abstract. Accurate observations of the vertical distribution and temporal variability of atmospheric trace gases are essential for understanding atmospheric composition and chemistry and for evaluating atmospheric models. The Gimballed Limb Observer for Radiance Imaging of the Atmosphere (GLORIA) is a cooled limb-imaging Fourier-Transform Spectrometer (iFTS) providing mid-infrared spectra with high spectral resolution. The newly developed, compact and uncooled instrument GLORIA-Lite (GLITE) is significantly smaller and lighter than its predecessor GLORIA, thanks to recent advances in infrared sensors, tailored electronics, and innovative manufacturing technology. The first balloon version, GLITE-B, was deployed during a transcontinental stratospheric flight from Kiruna (Sweden) via Greenland to Canada in June 2024. Hyperspectral limb-emission measurements in the 750–1450 cm−1 spectral range were obtained from 22 to 24 June, covering an altitude range of 5 to 40 km. The observations were used to retrieve temperature and a wide range of ozone and other species involved in stratospheric ozone chemistry, tracers of stratospheric air motions, and tropospheric air pollutants. Comparisons of the retrieved mean vertical volume mixing ratio (VMR) profiles with Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS) version 6 observations show good agreement over wide altitude ranges, with differences generally within the combined error limits and typically within ±2 K for temperature and ±10 % for O3, HNO3, and H2O. A negative bias of approximately 20 % was found in the MLS N2O data below 27 km relative to GLITE-B. Comparisons with the ECHAM5/MESSy Atmospheric Chemistry (EMAC) model indicate that the model successfully reproduces observed stratospheric trace-gas variability, chemistry (ClONO2, NO2, PAN), and transport characteristics (chlorofluorocarbons, SF6) in the sunlit summer polar stratosphere, while discrepancies for HCOOH and CH3OH highlight uncertainties in their sources and atmospheric processing. The CFC-11/CFC-12 tracer–tracer relationship agrees well with previous observations, and the observed SF6 profiles are consistent with current understanding of stratospheric transport. The results of this first flight demonstrate that GLITE‑B can provide accurate trace gas profiles with high vertical resolution during long-duration balloon flights. Such measurements capture the temporal evolution of atmospheric composition over several days, providing valuable information on transport and photochemical processes and supporting the evaluation and improvement of atmospheric chemistry models.

title: Evaluating Preliminary Estimation Bias and Operational Delays in Indian Public Procurement: Evidence from Infrastructure Projects and Alignment with SDGs
summary: This study examines the empirical nexus between early-stage budgeting bias, post-award contract execution timelines, and macroeconomic sustainability within India’s premier construction agency, the Central Public Works Department (CPWD). Mo
content: This study examines the empirical nexus between early-stage budgeting bias, post-award contract execution timelines, and macroeconomic sustainability within India’s premier construction agency, the Central Public Works Department (CPWD). Moving away from subjective stakeholder surveys, this paper uses an unaggregated, project-specific baseline built from two large-scale historical datasets (n = 994 for planning; n = 861 for execution). A parametric paired t-test confirms a systemic pre-award overestimation trend (t (993) = 14.83, p < .001), with baseline preliminary estimates exceeding final expenditures by an average of ₹1,319.98 lakhs. This practice creates an artificial capital lock-up that directly undermines SDG 9. Conversely, multiple linear regression reveals that post-award schedule delays exhibit a minor but statistically significant negative partial correlation with cost overruns (β = -.09, p = .012), supporting the budgetary cushion hypothesis. Prolonged project standstills do not drive linear cost growth; instead, they cause execution halts that freeze expenditures while causing severe environmental degradation, raw material waste, and compromises on green design standards (SDG 12, SDG 13). Ultimately, this paper outlines data-driven validation filters, such as Reference Class Forecasting, to mitigate artificial resource tie-ups and optimize public funds for sustainable infrastructure networks.

title: Ecological Impact of Climate Change in Oyo State: An Exploratory Inquiry
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Climate change is happening on a global scale but the ecological impact is often local and vary from place to place. A comprehensive account of ecological impact of climate change in Oyo State from the perspective of experts is missing in p
content: Climate change is happening on a global scale but the ecological impact is often local and vary from place to place. A comprehensive account of ecological impact of climate change in Oyo State from the perspective of experts is missing in previous studies. Therefore, in this study for an in depth understanding of what the ecological impacts are in Oyo State and how to create enabling environment for the adaptation and mitigation, structured interviews with three (3) experts were conducted. 137 interview guides were administered on the experts to elicit information on the practical evidence of ecological impact of climate change, the drivers and adaptation and mitigation strategies in Oyo State. The study adopted descriptive statistics: mean, standard deviation, and relative importance index (RII) in a 4-point Likert scale to analyze the data. The study from the analysis revealed from the listed options the practical evidence of ecological impact of climate change in various parts of Oyo State, the drivers and adaption and migration strategies adopted which enhance knowledge sharing between the experts, the policy makers and the individuals. It is hereby recommended that the transition to a low – carbon economy through investment in green building, sustainable agriculture and renewable energies are necessary in Nigeria in general and Oyo State in particular. The need to reduce its reliance on the Climate sensitive sectors and investment in resilience infrastructure particularly for water management, Agricultural practitioners and farmer should be encouraged to adopt best practice that will reduce ozone layers depletion and global warming and encourage Afforestation and agro forestry systems.
