title: Band-Dependent Effects of Diesel and Electric Propulsion on Naval Infrared Signature Under Solar-Exposed and Solar-Free Conditions: A Full-Scale Sea-Trial Case Study
source: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
summary: The choice between diesel and electric propulsion is an operational decision that requires no additional hardware, yet its effect on the infrared signature of a naval vessel has not been quantified in full-scale sea trials reported in the o
content: The choice between diesel and electric propulsion is an operational decision that requires no additional hardware, yet its effect on the infrared signature of a naval vessel has not been quantified in full-scale sea trials reported in the open literature. This case study compares the infrared radiation intensity of a single naval vessel under diesel and electric propulsion in the mid-wave (MWIR, 3–5 μm) and long-wave (LWIR, 8–12 μm) bands, under solar-exposed and solar-free conditions, with each measurement case recorded by a radiometrically calibrated system during a single continuous 0–360° turn. Under solar exposure, the diesel-to-electric ratio of median intensity was 1.31 in MWIR and 1.15 in LWIR, with a median angular reduction of 22–27% under electric propulsion; the LWIR result was more sensitive to the segmentation threshold than the MWIR result. Without solar exposure, the relationship persisted in MWIR (1.27) but reversed in LWIR (0.87). The solar-exposed and solar-free measurements differed in time of day and ambient conditions, and a sister vessel, measured only under solar exposure and under a different illumination geometry, showed the same overall direction but is used only qualitatively; the results are therefore specific to the observed acquisitions. The effect of propulsion configuration on radiation intensity depended jointly on spectral band and solar condition. Detection range and probability of detection were not assessed; the results nonetheless support further investigation of propulsion configuration as a potential operational variable in naval infrared signature management.

title: Computing Corridor or Ecological Cost Conveyor? Regional Equity in China’s East‐Data‐West‐Computing Project
summary: Over the past decade, advances in artificial intelligence and related digital technologies have increased demand for computing power. Because the artificial intelligence sector relies heavily on electricity, land, and water, its resource fo
content: Over the past decade, advances in artificial intelligence and related digital technologies have increased demand for computing power. Because the artificial intelligence sector relies heavily on electricity, land, and water, its resource footprint has raised growing concerns regarding pressures on environmental carrying capacity and infrastructure resilience. In response, China launched the East-Data-West-Computing Project in 2020. With eight national computing hubs designated, the project seeks to redirect both large-scale data center clusters and latency-tolerant computing tasks from eastern regions, where demand is concentrated, to central and western China. It aims to ease eastern capacity constraints by reallocating infrastructure and workloads, but it may also reshape the geographic distribution of ecological costs within China, potentially intensifying pressures in central and western regions. Such a pattern may emerge because ecological costs remain insufficiently visible under existing project-by-project assessment frameworks, while efficiency targets are more readily translated into enforceable metrics than equity and coordination objectives. As a result, central and western regions may face growing belated ecological risks, together with resource and fiscal bottlenecks, while the benefits they receive may not be commensurate with the responsibilities they bear. If this mismatch persists, central and western regions may get stuck into less sustainable development paths, which would reinforce development disparities between eastern and western China. To address this challenge, this article proposes a three-pronged institutional framework: MRV-based ecological cost accounting with interregional compensation and benefit-sharing mechanisms; adaptive governance supported by monitoring, disclosure, and participation that enables periodic adjustment; and technological innovation as a transitional measure to reduce unit-level impacts.

title: The role of attitude, food heritage, and good food perceptions in shaping intentions to consume local dairy products
summary: Aim: Food is a fundamental human necessity and integral to cultural identity. This study investigates the intention of urban citizens to consume local dairy products in Rasht, Iran. Drawing upon improved planned behavior theory, the study e
content: Aim: Food is a fundamental human necessity and integral to cultural identity. This study investigates the intention of urban citizens to consume local dairy products in Rasht, Iran. Drawing upon improved planned behavior theory, the study examines the influence of factors such as attitudes towards local dairy products, food heritage, perceptions of food health (good food), willingness to pay, and socio-demographic characteristics on consumer intention. Methods: Data were collected from 220 randomly selected urban citizens of Rasht using a survey questionnaire. Path analysis using partial least squares (PLS) was employed to analyze the data. Results: The final structural model demonstrated strong explanatory power, accounting for approximately 63% of the variance in attitudes toward local dairy consumption (R2 = 0.631) and approximately 60% of the variance in the intention to consume local dairy products (R2 = 0.598). Path analysis revealed that perceptions of good food (β = 0.512, p < 0.01) and food heritage (β = 0.366, p < 0.01) were the strongest positive predictors of attitudes toward local dairy products. Attitudes toward local and traditional dairy products significantly influenced both willingness to pay (β = 0.682, p < 0.01) and purchase intention (β = 0.387, p < 0.01). Furthermore, willingness to pay exerted a significant direct effect on purchase intention (β = 0.455, p < 0.01), serving as a partial mediator in the relationship between attitude and purchase behavior. Conclusions: These findings highlight the continued relevance of local dairy products in urban settings and provide valuable insights for local producers and policymakers to promote the consumption of local and sustainable food systems. The strong mediating role of willingness to pay suggests that strategies emphasizing the environmental and cultural value of local dairy may effectively enhance consumer purchase intentions.

title: Geography education and climate change awareness among secondary school teachers and learners in Tubah Subdivision, Cameroon
source: The Journal of Geography Education in Africa
summary: By integrating physical and human environmental processes, Geography education is increasingly recognised as an important vehicle for climate literacy. However, evidence on its contribution to climate change awareness and adaptation-oriente
content: By integrating physical and human environmental processes, Geography education is increasingly recognised as an important vehicle for climate literacy. However, evidence on its contribution to climate change awareness and adaptation-oriented learning at school level remains limited. This study examines how Geography teachers and learners in secondary schools in Tubah Subdivision, Cameroon, perceive the contribution of Geography education to climate change awareness. Structured questionnaires were administered to 68 Geography teachers and 150 learners in five secondary schools, supported by semi-structured interviews with five teachers. All teachers (100%, n=68) reported that climate change topics were included in the Geography curriculum, while 81% reported high confidence in teaching them. Teaching experience was significantly associated with teaching confidence. Amongst learners, 92% reported observing local climate-related changes, and 79% identified Geography as their primary source of climate information. These findings indicate that Geography education is an important source of climate change knowledge and adaptation-oriented learning among secondaryschool teachers and learners. However, constraints on climate-change education relate to teaching pedagogy, differences in school resources, and limited opportunities for fieldbased learning.

title: AI-enabled rooftop solar mapping and optimization: A computer vision approach for photovoltaic systems
summary: The rapid growth in energy and environmental issues, rooftop PV systems are rapidly gaining popularity. But one of the problems that needs to be addressed in large-scale deployment of solar is the problem of identifying appropriate rooftops
content: The rapid growth in energy and environmental issues, rooftop PV systems are rapidly gaining popularity. But one of the problems that needs to be addressed in large-scale deployment of solar is the problem of identifying appropriate rooftops accurately and in a scalable way. In this study, an integrated AI vision system is proposed that uses YOLOv8 and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to detect and segment rooftops in high-resolution satellite imagery. YOLOv8 was optimized on a dataset with 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test data of urban rooftops from the cities of Pakistan, mainly Karachi and Lahore, and was trained for 300 epochs with the AdamW optimizer. SAM was then used to refine the YOLOv8-detected bounding boxes to produce accurate pixel-wise segmentation masks. The proposed approach outperforms current methods such as U-Net, Mask R-CNN, and Deep Roof with a detection precision of 92.8%, recall of 90.7%, mAP@0.5 of 94.1%, and SAM segmentation IoU of 89.3%. To estimate PV installation capacity, segmented roof areas were estimated using geospatial metadata. The findings show that the YOLOv8-SAM pipeline is a repeatable and scalable solution to manual surveying of rooftops and can be used to aid in solar energy planning in urban areas where data is limited.

title: Prediction of flavonoid components and antioxidant activity in tangerine peel based on machine learning
summary: Tangerine peel is a valuable citrus by-product enriched with flavonoids and antioxidant compounds, possessing considerable potential for applications in the functional food and nutraceutical industries. Conventional analytical techniques fo
content: Tangerine peel is a valuable citrus by-product enriched with flavonoids and antioxidant compounds, possessing considerable potential for applications in the functional food and nutraceutical industries. Conventional analytical techniques for flavonoid determination are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for high-throughput quality evaluation. This study developed a machine learning-based prediction framework for the rapid assessment of major flavonoid components and antioxidant activity in tangerine peel using physicochemical characteristics and near-infrared spectral information. A total of 320 tangerine peel samples were analyzed, incorporating moisture content, soluble solids, color parameters, total phenolic content, and spectral variables as predictors. Hesperidin, nobiletin, and tangeretin concentrations were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography, while antioxidant activity was determined using the DPPH radical scavenging assay. Three machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were evaluated and compared. The results demonstrated that XGBoost exhibited the highest predictive accuracy, achieving coefficient of determination (R²) values of 0.945, 0.921, and 0.907 for hesperidin, nobiletin, and tangeretin, respectively. Antioxidant activity prediction achieved an R² of 0.959, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.73%, which demonstrates the reliability and generalization capability of the model. Feature importance analysis revealed that total phenolic content (24.8%), absorbance at 1450 nm (18.6%), and peel color parameter a* (12.9%) were the most influential predictors. Compared with conventional laboratory analysis, the proposed framework reduced analytical time from approximately 51.6 min per sample to less than 2.5 s while maintaining prediction accuracy above 95%. These findings confirm that machine learning integrated with spectral sensing technologies provides an efficient, accurate, and non-destructive strategy for predicting flavonoid composition and antioxidant capacity, offering substantial potential for intelligent quality control and high-value utilization of citrus processing by-products.

title: Hydrogel-based biosensors for sweat analysis in sports medicine: recent advances and future prospects
summary: Sweat is a physiological fluid that can be collected non-invasively and is continuously secreted by the human body. It contains a wide variety of biomarkers, including electrolytes, metabolites, hormones, and proteins, which may provide com
content: Sweat is a physiological fluid that can be collected non-invasively and is continuously secreted by the human body. It contains a wide variety of biomarkers, including electrolytes, metabolites, hormones, and proteins, which may provide complementary information about physical activity and selected aspects of physiological status. In recent years, wearable biosensors based on hydrogels have drawn increasing interest in exercise monitoring and sports medicine because of the material’s flexibility, hydrophilicity, and biocompatibility. This review summarizes recent advances in hydrogel-based sweat detection, highlighting sensing mechanisms and representative applications for four major biomarker categories: electrolytes, metabolites, hormones, and proteins. It also discusses potential applications in hydration assessment, fatigue-related monitoring, sports-injury risk assessment, and rehabilitation management. The discussion addresses current challenges, including material durability, signal stability, physiological interpretation, clinical translation, and large-scale manufacturing. Looking ahead, future progress will likely focus on multifunctional hydrogels, integration with artificial intelligence and data-driven methods, personalized monitoring, and standardized testing and validation protocols. Overall, hydrogel-based sweat biosensing offers a promising complementary approach for non-invasive physiological monitoring, although broader sports-medicine use will require rigorous validation under real-world exercise conditions.

title: Roles of industry associations in industrial ecosystems – The case of Hungarian battery association
summary: Industry associations play important roles in industrial ecosystems, yet their multiple functions are difficult to capture through a single theoretical perspective. This study examines the role configuration of the Hungarian Battery Associa
content: Industry associations play important roles in industrial ecosystems, yet their multiple functions are difficult to capture through a single theoretical perspective. This study examines the role configuration of the Hungarian Battery Association and evaluates the explanatory contributions of industrial network management, meta-organization theory, and civil society organization scholarship. Using a single-case design, the authors conducted a deductive codebook thematic analysis of HUBAs activities from its inception in 2021 to 2026. They find that all roles identified by industrial network management and meta-organization theory are evident in HUBA’s activities, but their presence varies while some roles predicted by CSO literature were either absent or partially evident in HUBA’s activities. The findings reveal that the same organization activity can fulfil theoretically distinct roles depending on their purpose, beneficiaries, and relational context. The study shows that combining the three perspectives provides a more comprehensive functional explanation of industry associations operating within strategic industrial ecosystems.

title: Short‐Term Effect of Fishmeal‐Free Feed Formulation on Growth Performance, Feed Efficiency and Transcriptomic Profile of Hypothalamus and Liver in Atlantic Salmon
summary: ABSTRACT Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) aquaculture is increasingly seeking alternatives to marine‐derived ingredients, but the physiological and molecular consequences of fishmeal (FM) replacement remain incompletely understood. This stud
content: ABSTRACT Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) aquaculture is increasingly seeking alternatives to marine‐derived ingredients, but the physiological and molecular consequences of fishmeal (FM) replacement remain incompletely understood. This study assessed the effects of two nutritionally equivalent summer diets for Atlantic salmon under simulated Tasmanian summer conditions (18°C): FM and FM‐free (FMF). Growth performance, feed efficiency and transcriptomic responses in the hypothalamus and liver were evaluated to assess the impacts of FM replacement. After 40 days, FM showed significantly higher final body weight and condition factor. The transcriptome showed diet‐specific responses. Genes linked to neuropeptide melanin‐concentrating hormone (MCH) activity and fatty acid nutrient sensing were significantly upregulated in the hypothalamus of FM‐fed fish relative to FMF, suggesting a stimulatory effect on feed intake and energy regulation. In the liver, the FM treatment induced significant lipid activation, signalling and remodelling pathways, indicating a higher availability of essential fatty acids. The FMF treatment significantly upregulated genes involved in hepatic de novo lipogenesis, implying a limited supply of fatty acids. The study identifies diet‐dependent hypothalamic gene expression patterns consistent with altered feed intake regulation, particularly within the MCH pathway, alongside compensatory hepatic lipogenic responses in FMF‐fed fish. These transcriptomic findings advance our understanding of the molecular consequences of complete FM replacement in Atlantic salmon under summer temperature conditions.

title: White-clover biomass amendment as a biological conditioning strategy for radish cultivation in Mars global regolith simulant
summary: Long-duration human missions to Mars will require crop-production systems that reduce dependence on transported growth media and fertilizers. Martian regolith may provide a locally available mineral substrate, but its poor agronomic propert
content: Long-duration human missions to Mars will require crop-production systems that reduce dependence on transported growth media and fertilizers. Martian regolith may provide a locally available mineral substrate, but its poor agronomic properties constrain direct agricultural use. This study evaluated dried whole-plant white clover ( Trifolium repens L. ) biomass as a 5% (w/w) plant-derived amendment for improving Japanese 20-day daikon radish (Raphanus sativus L. ‘Kiss Me Hatsuka Daikon’) performance in Mars Global Simulant (MGS-1). Plants were cultivated for 21 days in a peat-based control, untreated MGS-1, clover-amended MGS-1, and previously cultivated MGS-1. The proportion of planted units with visible living tissue, survivor-only mean shoot height, edible biomass, and anthocyanin concentration were evaluated. Untreated MGS-1 showed a progressive decline in visual viability over the cultivation period. By DAP 21, final survival was 78.6% in clover-amended MGS-1, compared with 9.5% in untreated MGS-1, 26.2% in previously cultivated MGS-1, and 95.2% in the peat-based control. The longitudinal viability response differed significantly among treatments (treatment × DAP interaction, p < 0.001). The clover amendment also produced significantly greater survivor-only mean shoot height than untreated MGS-1, although biomass production remained substantially below that of the control. Despite reduced biomass production in the MGS-1 treatments, fresh-mass-normalized anthocyanin concentration followed the descriptive pattern: control < clover-amended < previously cultivated < untreated MGS-1. Among treatments with replicated anthocyanin measurements, concentration differed significantly (p = 0.031), with previously cultivated MGS-1 exceeding the control (p = 0.025). The untreated treatment showed the highest observed concentration, but only one tray produced sufficient tissue for analysis. These findings demonstrate that a 5% plant-biomass amendment altered the crop-response trajectory in MGS-1 from progressive loss of visible living plant presence to sustained plant persistence, even with substantial biomass limitation. The divergence between plant persistence, productivity, and anthocyanin response indicates that successful early conditioning of regolith-based substrates should not be evaluated by viability alone. Minimally processed plant biomass may therefore provide a low-input first stage in the progressive conversion of regolith from a mineral substrate associated with crop failure toward a biologically usable cultivation medium.

title: Full Pore System Characteristics, Fractal Dimensions, and Controlling Factors of Lacustrine Laminated Shale: Implications for Shale Oil Reservoirs in the Liaohe Depression, NE China
summary: Abstract Clarifying the pore system of unconventional oil and gas reservoirs is essential for understanding hydrocarbon accumulation, improving recovery efficiency, and accurately assessing resource potential. However, research on pore syst
content: Abstract Clarifying the pore system of unconventional oil and gas reservoirs is essential for understanding hydrocarbon accumulation, improving recovery efficiency, and accurately assessing resource potential. However, research on pore systems in lacustrine shales remains limited, largely because the development of diverse laminas produces strong heterogeneity. In the current research, 20 samples from the fourth member of the Shahejie Formation in the Western Sag, Liaohe Depression of the Bohai Bay Basin were systematically characterized through a combined approach that includes CO2 adsorption, N2 adsorption, and high-pressure mercury intrusion (HPMI) experiments. Fractal dimensions for micropores (D1), mesopores (D2), and macropores (D3) were obtained using the V–S model for CO2 adsorption, the FHH model for N2 adsorption, and the MSP model for HPMI. The results demonstrate that the laminated shale is composed of light-colored layers rich in quartz, feldspar, calcite, and dolomite, which often alternate with darker layers primarily consisting of clay minerals and organic matter. The pore system of the laminated shale consists mainly of intergranular pores, intercrystalline pores, dissolution pores, and microfractures within the matrix, excluding pores associated with organic matter. In terms of pore volume, the pore system is primarily characterized by mesopores and macropores, while micropores significantly contribute to the specific surface area. The fractal dimensions are observed to range from 2.565 to 2.880 for D1, 2.458 to 2.659 for D2, and 2.929 to 2.999 for D3. This indicates that macropores display the greatest heterogeneity, followed by micropores, with mesopores being comparatively homogeneous. Correlation analysis indicates a strong positive relationship between D1 and both the micropore specific surface area and the pore volume of micropores. The correlation is influenced by the total organic carbon (TOC) content, thermal maturity (Ro), and clay mineral content. While D2 demonstrates a positive correlation with mesopore parameters, its overall heterogeneity remains relatively low due to compaction-induced homogenization. D3 is mainly affected by the dissolution of carbonates and the presence of microfracture networks, often reaching the theoretical upper limit in the majority of samples. The composition of minerals has a varying impact based on scale: clay minerals facilitate the formation of micropores and mesopores; felsic minerals contribute moderately to the volumes of mesopores and macropores; carbonate minerals encourage the formation of irregular dissolution pores, which in turn enhances D3. Within the low-mature to mature oil window (Ro = 0.65–1.00%), the pore system is predominantly controlled by the diagenetic evolution of the mineral matrix rather than organic matter pores. This research presents a quantitative framework for characterizing the complete pore system in laminated shale and provides insights for reservoir eva

title: Covalent Integration of Polyoxometalates Onto Covalent Organic Frameworks (POM‐COFs): From Molecular Design to Multifunctional Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Polyoxometalates (POMs) have attracted widespread attention across disciplines for their precisely tunable molecular structures and superior redox properties, but their practical applications are hindered by self‐aggregation, low s
content: ABSTRACT Polyoxometalates (POMs) have attracted widespread attention across disciplines for their precisely tunable molecular structures and superior redox properties, but their practical applications are hindered by self‐aggregation, low specific surface area, and stability issues. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), as emerging crystalline porous platforms, provide ordered spatial environments for heterogeneous POM immobilization, enabling complementary advantages and synergistic effects. However, conventional POM/COF hybrids typically rely on weak interactions (electrostatic forces, hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces), leading to uneven loading, facile leaching, severe agglomeration, and difficulty in characterization at the single‐cluster level. In contrast, covalently linked POM‐COFs achieve molecular‐level integration via covalent bonds, realizing precise positioning and uniform distribution of POMs. This strategy markedly suppresses active component leaching and aggregation, induces pronounced electronic synergy, enhances interfacial charge‐transfer dynamics, and enables single‐cluster utilization and characterization. This review systematically summarizes POM‐COF synthesis paradigms based on in situ construction and post‐synthetic modification, discusses their breakthrough applications in heterogeneous catalysis, electrochemical energy storage, proton conduction, chemical sensing, and environmental pollutant treatment, and analyzes current challenges in structural analysis, in situ mechanism exploration, and stimuli‐responsive applications, providing guidance for developing next‐generation multifunctional covalent hybrid materials.

title: Ανάπτυξη νανοσωλήνων άνθρακα σε ανθρακονήματα μέσω Χημικής Εναπόθεσης Ατμών από παραπροϊόντα ανακύκλωσης πολυμερικών συνθέτων
source: DSpace - NTUA (National Technical University of Athens)
summary: Carbon fiber reinforced composites (CFRPs) when enhanced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) can be particularly promising as multiscale materials, as they combine the excellent mechanical properties of carbon fibers with the unique properties of
content: Carbon fiber reinforced composites (CFRPs) when enhanced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) can be particularly promising as multiscale materials, as they combine the excellent mechanical properties of carbon fibers with the unique properties of these nanostructures.The direct growth of CNTs on the surface of carbon fibers (CFs) significantly improves interfacial adhesion and charge transport, leading to composites with higher strength and durability.An easy and simple method to synthesize CNTs on carbon fibers is through Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD).A variety of hydrocarbon sources as well as catalysts can be exploited for the growth of CNTs.However, the utilization of by-products as alternative hydrocarbon precursor source offers a sustainable and circular approach, promoting the recycling and upcycling of wastes.In this diploma thesis, five different precursors were used for the growth of CNTs on CFs via CVD; ethanol, camphor, LDPE, pyrolysis and solvolysis by-products.Also, four catalysts were utilized through both floating and supported catalyst approaches; ferrocene, nickel, cobalt and platinum.A parametric analysis, concerning the reaction time and the catalyst concentration among other parameters, was carried out.Using different combination of precursors and catalysts, CNTs were synthesized on the surface of CFs and were characterized by SEM, EDS, Raman and contact angle.

title: Maximal Fat Oxidation Testing in Gilbert’s Syndrome: Plasma Lipid-Mobilization Signatures from Untargeted Metabolomics
summary: BACKGROUND: Gilbert's syndrome (GS), defined by an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, has been linked to favorable metabolic traits, including greater fat oxidation and distinct metabolite profiles. Whether GS confers a different acute plasma
content: BACKGROUND: Gilbert's syndrome (GS), defined by an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, has been linked to favorable metabolic traits, including greater fat oxidation and distinct metabolite profiles. Whether GS confers a different acute plasma metabolomic response to a FatMax test remains unknown. METHODS: A human age- and sex-matched case-control (GS vs normobilirubinemic controls) study was conducted from March 2023 to December 2023 at the University of Vienna. After a 12-h-overnight-fast 80 participants completed a FatMax test on a cycle ergometer and from 79 the plasma metabolome was analyzed. Blood samples were collected before (baseline) and immediately after exercise. An untargeted plasma metabolomics analysis was performed via LC-MS. RESULTS: GS and controls differed significantly in serum bilirubin concentrations (GS: 33.5 ± 13.3; C: 12.2 ± 2.72; p < 0.001, in µmol/L). Apart from the expected elevations in the subclass of bilirubin in GS, the global acute metabolomic response to FatMax was broadly similar between groups. Exercise-response was similar in all participants, displaying a fat-oxidation signature post-exercise (increase in several acetylcarnitines (dodecoanylcarnitine, tetradecenoyl carnitine, (10Z,13Z,16Z,19Z)-Docosatetraenoylcarnitine), and several fatty acids (especially unsaturated fatty acids)), with a total of 231 metabolites changing in response to exercise. Individuals with higher maximal fat oxidation displayed larger immediate post-exercise increases in selected metabolites, such as fatty acids. CONCLUSION: A submaximal FatMax exercise test elicits a robust plasma signature consistent with fatty-acid mobilization and increased fatty-acid availability for oxidation. However, within the constraints of a 12-h fast and exercise at this workload and duration, GS did not demonstrate a distinct acute metabolomic response beyond elevations in bilirubins.

title: Mesophase-Derived Polymer Membranes with Precisely Defined Pores for Molecular and Ion Separations
summary: Abstract Polymer membranes are central components in critical technologies, including energy generation and storage, water purification, and chemical separations. There are pressing needs for membranes that transport uncharged and charged m
content: Abstract Polymer membranes are central components in critical technologies, including energy generation and storage, water purification, and chemical separations. There are pressing needs for membranes that transport uncharged and charged molecular, or ionic species, with bespoke selectivity and high permeability in these technological areas, including the growing need for efficient critical mineral separations and resource recovery. For these and other challenging molecular or ionic separations, the focus is on membranes with 1 nm scale (0.5–2 nm) pores that can offer both size- and affinity-based mechanisms for separation. This perspective discusses the current state of the art in nanoporous polymer membranes and reviews recent progress toward the realization of ideal membranes for such separations—i.e., membranes with uniform, continuous, and precisely defined pores at the 1 nm length scale. Emphasis is placed on materials derived from molecular self-assembly, particularly lyotropic mesophases formed from amphiphilic monomers that can be crosslinked to produce monolithic membranes with well-defined, continuous transport pathways. These materials represent a potentially important advance given their attractive separation performance, and the versatility with which their properties can be modified. Developments in fabrication, pore shape, and pore chemistry control are discussed, along with opportunities to address important contemporary and emerging applications.

title: Molecular Bridging Flexibility Enables Closed‐Pore Engineering in Hard Carbon for Enhanced Plateau Sodium Storage
summary: ABSTRACT Closed pores are critical structural motifs that enable low‐voltage plateau capacity in hard carbon (HC) anodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet their controllable construction through precursor molecular design remains challenging. H
content: ABSTRACT Closed pores are critical structural motifs that enable low‐voltage plateau capacity in hard carbon (HC) anodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet their controllable construction through precursor molecular design remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate molecular bridging flexibility as an effective design principle for regulating closed‐pore formation in HCs. The flexibility/rigidity of polymer precursors is tailored by distinct bridging configurations, namely Ar─CH 2 ─Ar and Ar─O─C bridges, where oxygen‐containing bridges enhance segmental flexibility. During early‐stage pyrolysis, flexible precursor segments provide higher conformational freedom, inducing curved carbon skeletons and promoting the formation of semi‐open sub‐1 nm pores. Driven by high surface energy, these semi‐open pores undergo pore‐mouth closure during high‐temperature pyrolysis, generating abundant closed pores. The resulting HC exhibits a closed porosity of 0.12 cm 3 g −1 and a pore size 1.13 nm, which enhances plateau capacity and sodium‐ion diffusion kinetics. Consequently, the flexible‐precursor‐derived HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 356.1 mAh g −1 and a plateau capacity of 242.7 mAh g −1 . Moreover, a practical 1.2 Ah pouch cell achieves 217.2 Wh kg −1 and retains 81.2% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work establishes a molecular‐level strategy for closed‐pore engineering in HC anodes for high‐performance sodium‐ion batteries.

title: Precipitation-based indices for climate-resilient viticulture: A systematic review for practical application
summary: Climate change impacts crop production through rising temperatures, water stress, and seasonal shifts. While agroclimatic and ecoclimatic indices summarize these environmental conditions, overwhelming diversity, and fragmented application c
content: Climate change impacts crop production through rising temperatures, water stress, and seasonal shifts. While agroclimatic and ecoclimatic indices summarize these environmental conditions, overwhelming diversity, and fragmented application currently complicate selection for adaptation decision-making. To improve index selection and enhance application, this review compiles widely used precipitation-based indices and assesses their performance and potential use in viticulture. Using a combined bibliometric and exploratory approach (2005–2025), we analyzed 70 core studies to identify index applications across varying precipitation regimes. Thirty-one indices were then categorized into three functional groups: (1) direct precipitation metrics; (2) temperature and insolation adjusted precipitation indices; and (3) water-balance indices. Our findings reveal that Group 1 indices offer simplicity for rapid site characterization, and Group 3 metrics can improve informed decisions regarding vineyard water management and yield-quality trade-offs under future climate scenarios with the additional consideration of evapotranspiration and water balance. Both exploratory and bibliometric analyses highlighted how these tools are used to assess viticulture suitability at various scales, evaluate current and future climate change impacts such as extreme weather and drought, and analyze their influence on crop yield and quality. Climate change adaptation was a key context, and the findings of the studies indicated they could result in climate service applications of terroir zoning management for quality and yield, seasonal climate-informed decision-making, and guidance for sustainable agricultural water management. This synthesis offers a comprehensive summary of the state-of-the-science of precipitation-based indices to support climate-informed decision-making in viticulture, with potential relevance for other climate-sensitive perennial crops.

title: Nanoporous Stacked Polytriazine With Sulfur Enrichment for Detection of Near Infrared Radiation
summary: ABSTRACT Structural reorientation owing to the incorporation of sulfur in nitrogen enriched nanoporous polytriazine (SNENP) leads to the formation of a stacked polymeric framework. This stacking aligns the electron density in the framework
content: ABSTRACT Structural reorientation owing to the incorporation of sulfur in nitrogen enriched nanoporous polytriazine (SNENP) leads to the formation of a stacked polymeric framework. This stacking aligns the electron density in the framework through facilitating the delocalization of electrons leading to a reduction in the bandgap with an increase in electrical conductivity. A significant reduction in bandgap from 3.10 eV in the pristine nitrogen enriched nanoporous polytriazine (NENP) to 1.14 eV in SNENP was observed, which indicates a transition in optical absorption from ultraviolet (UV) to near infrared (NIR) region. The sulfur enrichment improves the electrical conductivity from 6.54 to 28.84 S m −1 at room temperature. The SNENP‐based photodetector devices show a high photocurrent of 10.63 mA (vs 1.01 mA in NENP) and a responsivity of 107.69 A W −1 (vs 34.61 A W −1 in NENP) at a voltage of −10 V with an 808 nm incident light with optical power density of 1.0 µW mm −2 . This enhanced photodetection performance is associated with the increased charge carrier density, high electrical conductivity, and reduced trap density within stacked nanoporous structure of SNENP. These findings demonstrate that dual‐heteroatom nanoporous polytriazine framework (SNENP) provides an effective platform for the development of high‐performance NIR photodetectors.

title: The Outsized Effect of Minute Contaminants on the Physical Properties of H2 as Shown Through the Example of Industrial Forced Draft Burners
summary: As of today, multiple gaseous H2 quality specifications and a single H2 quality standard (ISO 14687:2025) exist. These specifications allow a varying amount of contaminant gases, including contaminants which have no heating value, such as C
content: As of today, multiple gaseous H2 quality specifications and a single H2 quality standard (ISO 14687:2025) exist. These specifications allow a varying amount of contaminant gases, including contaminants which have no heating value, such as CO2 or N2. Due to the large difference in the physical properties (e.g. density) between these contaminants and H2, even minute amount of contaminant can change the properties of the mixed gas significantly. For example, allowing 2% CO2 in H2 means that the density increases by approximately 40% and the Wobbe index decreases by almost 20% compared to pure H2. As pure H2 fulfils all the specifications and quality grades, changes between high-quality H2 and H2 with contaminants might happen in a supply chain hour-by-hour along with the changes in physical properties; this might lead to significant challenges, for example in metering, dimensioning the infrastructure or the like. In this paper an example of forced draft burners is presented, and it is shown that changes in the gas quality can lead to potentially dangerous working points while still fulfilling the requirements of ISO 14687:2025 Grade A, if no mitigating steps are taken. A guideline for adjusting large, forced draft burners to ensure safe working conditions is presented, along with an estimate on lost efficiency if no other action is provided underlining the importance of an oxygen trim system. Showing these effects in a specific example highlights the importance of taking gas quality, and specifically the possibility of minute amounts of heavy contaminants into account, when considering the safety of H2 containing systems or modeling and simulating the behavior of these.

title: Multifunctional Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate/Cuprous Oxide Nanocomposites in MEX 3D Printing: Rheological, Thermomechanical and Antibacterial Metrics
summary: ABSTRACT To address the critical need for robust and self‐sterilizing materials for challenging environments, this research introduces the use of cuprous oxide (Cu 2 O) nanoparticles in weatherproof acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA) thro
content: ABSTRACT To address the critical need for robust and self‐sterilizing materials for challenging environments, this research introduces the use of cuprous oxide (Cu 2 O) nanoparticles in weatherproof acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA) through material extrusion (MEX) 3D printing to produce multifunctional nanocomposites with improved mechanical, rheological, and antibacterial properties. A range of ASA/Cu 2 O compositions (0.5–3.0 wt.% filler loading) was compounded and extruded into filament, and then specimens were fabricated using MEX 3D printing. Thermal properties of the nanocomposites were evaluated by thermogravimetric analysis and differential scanning calorimetry; the rheological behavior and printability were determined by melt viscosity and melt flow rate measurements. The influence of Cu 2 O content on printed part quality was evaluated by using micro‐computed tomography (dimensional accuracy and porosity were quantified). Incorporation of Cu 2 O improved the mechanical properties by 13%–30% (tensile strength 16.6%–46.4 MPa, flexural strength 23.2%–67.5 MPa, toughness about 30%) compared to the neat matrix. The 1.5 wt.% composition showed the best overall mechanical performance. The antibacterial properties were confirmed by the agar well diffusion method against Gram‐negative bacteria ( E. coli ) and Gram‐positive bacteria ( S. aureus ). The simultaneous structural reinforcement and biocidal properties in a single material without sacrificing processability or geometrical accuracy render ASA/Cu 2 O a promising nanocomposite for components in the MEX 3D printing process in outdoor and public‐hygiene applications.

title: Proton Competition Induced Stabilization in TEMPO‐Based Redox‐Targeting Flow Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stabil
content: ABSTRACT 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stability issues with molecule degradation. In this work, a unique stabilization strategy beyond molecular engineering is developed by designing a TEMPO‐based redox‐targeting (RT) flow battery via a proton‐competition mechanism. A RT flow battery is constructed with 4‐acetamido‐TEMPO as redox mediator and polyaniline (PANI) as the solid material, achieving 4.37‐fold enhancement in capacity (35.72 Ah L −1 ), high coulombic efficiency (99.99%) and excellent capacity retention (99.94% per cycle over 500 cycles within 840.82 h). The outstanding stability of the TEMPO‐based flow battery is attributed to the synergistic interaction between proton buffering and RT reactions. This study elucidates a key pathway for suppressing TEMPO radical hydrogenation through a proton competition mechanism, which relies on the reversible doping/de‐doping cycles of the PANI. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory calculations elucidate the mechanism, revealing an intermediate transition state and confirming that proton competition by PANI is pivotal for radical stabilization. This work delves into the mechanism of TEMPO‐based RT flow battery, providing design principles for advancing stable AORFB systems toward long‐duration energy storage applications.

title: Fabrication of Tri‐Phase Lithium Alloy in Seconds via an Implosion‐Popcorn Reaction Toward Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Introducing non‐lithium components to fabricate lithium‐based alloy anodes has emerged as a paramount strategy to enhance the processability and stability of lithium metal batteries. However, conventional fabrication suffers from t
content: ABSTRACT Introducing non‐lithium components to fabricate lithium‐based alloy anodes has emerged as a paramount strategy to enhance the processability and stability of lithium metal batteries. However, conventional fabrication suffers from the sluggish wetting kinetics of lithium with non‐lithium components, inducing severe phase heterogeneity and component agglomeration. Herein, we report an ultrafast, spontaneous implosion‐popcorn reaction that explosively disintegrates centimeter‐scale precursor ingots into ultra‐fine particles within seconds, yielding a uniformly dispersed tri‐phase alloy with an interpenetrating network of Fe, Li 3 P, and Li. The as‐obtained lithium alloy exhibits a significantly enhanced Young's modulus and can be processed into different forms, including coatable slurries, self‐standing foils, and active powders. This fabrication method shifts from traditional passive alloying to an active, highly efficient, and homogenous approach. When used as an anode, the homogeneous Li/Fe/Li 3 P architecture facilitates interfacial Li‐ion transfer and regulates initial Li nucleation, thereby promoting dense and uniform Li growth and enabling a cycling lifespan of over 3000 h, together with improved full‐cell stability.

title: Engineering asymmetric CC coupling via Ce‐promoted water activation at CuOCe interfaces for CO 2 electroreduction
summary: Abstract Electrochemical CO 2 reduction to multi‐carbon products is hindered by Cu + instability and sluggish CC coupling kinetics. We construct CuOCe interfaces that synergistically stabilize Cu + and modulate hydrogenation pathways. Th
content: Abstract Electrochemical CO 2 reduction to multi‐carbon products is hindered by Cu + instability and sluggish CC coupling kinetics. We construct CuOCe interfaces that synergistically stabilize Cu + and modulate hydrogenation pathways. The Ce 4+ /Ce 3+ redox pair preserves Cu + under cathodic bias via Cu 3d‐O 2p‐Ce 4f hybridization. Critically, Ce sites lower the H 2 O dissociation barrier from 0.67 to 0.43 eV, increasing *H supply. This *H flux promotes *CO hydrogenation to *COH, redirecting coupling from *CO dimerization to an asymmetric CO–COH route toward *OCCOH. The optimized catalyst achieves a C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 80.17% at 600 mA cm −2 with stability exceeding 185 h. Our findings establish that modulating water dissociation kinetics at oxide–oxide interfaces provides a generalizable strategy for steering CC coupling, shifting the design paradigm from maximizing *CO coverage to managing *H supply.

title: Biomimetic Multifunctional Surfaces: Engineering Intelligent Multifunctionality Through Bioinspired Structures
summary: ABSTRACT Biomimetic multifunctional surfaces hold promising prospects in numerous fields, including aerospace, marine engineering, biomedicine, flexible electronics, and environmental protection. This is primarily attributed to their unique
content: ABSTRACT Biomimetic multifunctional surfaces hold promising prospects in numerous fields, including aerospace, marine engineering, biomedicine, flexible electronics, and environmental protection. This is primarily attributed to their unique capability for structural regulation and multifunctional synergy. The structures and fabrication strategies of these surfaces play a critical role in their performance and applications. Herein, a concise overview of biomimetic multifunctional surfaces is presented, focusing on their structures, fabrication, applications, and prospects. Initially, the structural characteristics and underlying mechanisms of typical functional surfaces are discussed. Next, various advanced fabrication techniques, including additive manufacturing, are analyzed. Subsequently, recent advances in biomimetic multifunctional surfaces across various applications are summarized. Finally, the trend of biomimetic multifunctional surfaces and the perspectives for this exciting new field are highlighted.

title: Operando Infrared Spectroscopy of Rh/Al2O3 Washcoated Monolithic Catalysts: Influence of Preparation and Aging
summary: Abstract Diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) is widely used to investigate surface species and metal–support interactions in heterogeneous catalysis, but is typically applied to powder samples. In contrast,
content: Abstract Diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) is widely used to investigate surface species and metal–support interactions in heterogeneous catalysis, but is typically applied to powder samples. In contrast, industrial catalysts are often used as structured bodies, for which differences in preparation, geometry, and flow behavior may affect both catalytic performance and spectroscopic observations. Here, we present a proof-of-concept operando DRIFTS study of CO oxidation over intact 3 × 3-channel Rh/Al2O3 washcoated cordierite monolith cores. The catalytic light-off behavior of monolith cores and corresponding washcoat powders was comparable. However, the *NCO bands associated with nitric acid used during catalyst preparation were observed predominantly for the monolith cores, demonstrating that preparation-dependent features can be underrepresented in powder analogues. Reversing the gas-flow direction changed the position of the DRIFTS sampling region relative to the reaction zone without substantially affecting the overall CO oxidation activity, showing an additional capability of measurements on intact structured catalysts. To mimic catalyst deactivation during industrial operation, samples were subjected to aging in H2, air, and hydrothermal redox-cycling (HRC; alternating H2/O2 in the presence of water vapor). While H2 aging resulted in little change in catalytic activity and IR spectra, air aging led to a decrease in adsorbed CO IR band intensity and an increased light-off temperature, consistent with a change in the Rh-containing surface species, potentially involving Rh incorporation into the alumina support. HRC aging resulted in slight deactivation, and enhanced IR bands of CO adsorbed on metallic Rh, due to Rh nanoparticle sintering. These results demonstrate that operando DRIFTS on intact washcoated monolith cores can reveal preparation- and aging-dependent surface-chemistry differences while retaining features of the structured catalyst geometry.

title: Organic Photodetectors With Surpassing 50% External Quantum Efficiency at 1100 nm Using a Narrow Bandgap Donor Polymer
summary: ABSTRACT Organic photodetectors (OPDs) have garnered significant attention for their low‐cost fabrication, mechanical flexibility, and tunable spectral response. However, low external quantum efficiency (EQE) in short‐wave infrared (SWIR),
content: ABSTRACT Organic photodetectors (OPDs) have garnered significant attention for their low‐cost fabrication, mechanical flexibility, and tunable spectral response. However, low external quantum efficiency (EQE) in short‐wave infrared (SWIR), especially above silicon's cutoff (≈1100 nm), limits their application. Herein, we report SWIR‐OPDs using a narrow‐bandgap donor polymer, PDCBT‐DP2O, blended with the acceptor BTPCN. The devices achieve an EQE of 51.1% at 1100 nm under −3 V bias. The incorporation of 5,6‐dicyano‐2,1,3‐benzothiadiazole and 3,3′‐dimethoxy‐2,2′‐bithiophene units significantly narrows the polymer bandgap, pushing absorption past silicon's limit. Moreover, the finely tuned alkyl side chains improve the skeleton coplanarity and solid‐state packing, resulting in a longer exciton diffusion length, higher carrier mobility, and reduced trap density. These combined effects facilitate the conversion of absorbed photons into collected charge carriers. As a result, the OPD achieves detectivity ( D sh * ) over 10 11 Jones across 320–1250 nm at −0.5 V, which ranks among the highest reported for SWIR‐OPDs. We also demonstrate sensitive SWIR sensing in representative application prototypes including optical communication, noncontact photoplethysmography, broadband spectroscopy and SWIR imaging. This work proves narrow bandgap donor polymers as a distinct material pathway for high‐performance SWIR photodetection.

title: Nanosensors: Physical, Chemical, and Biological
summary: Nanosensors are innovative devices that exploit the unique properties exhibited by matter at the nanoscale. A growing and exciting field, nanosensors have spurred considerable research worldwide, driving the development of new device concep
content: Nanosensors are innovative devices that exploit the unique properties exhibited by matter at the nanoscale. A growing and exciting field, nanosensors have spurred considerable research worldwide, driving the development of new device concepts and the engineering of nanostructured materials with controlled properties. Nanosensors: Physical, Chemical, and Biological, Third Edition offers a panoramic view of the field and related nanotechnologies with extraordinary clarity and depth. Presenting an interdisciplinary approach that blends physics, chemistry, and biology, this new edition is broad in scope and organized into seven parts, beginning with the fundamentals before moving on to nanomaterials and nanofabrication technologies in the second part. The third and fourth parts provide a critical appraisal of physical nanosensors and explore the chemical and biological categories of nanosensors. The fifth part sheds light on the emerging applications of nanosensors across society, industry, and defense, and detail the cutting-edge applications of state-of-the-art nanosensors in environmental science, food technology, medical diagnostics, and biotechnology. The sixth part addresses self-powering and networking issues of nanosensors. The newly added seventh part addresses intelligent nanosensors and current research trends, describing machine learning techniques and artificial intelligence (AI)- enhanced nanosensors. The third edition has been updated to reflect recent advancements in nanosensors that integrate nanotechnology and AI. This is an ideal reference for researchers and industry professionals working at the forefront of materials science and semiconductor fabrication, as well as for graduate students in physics and engineering pursuing electrical engineering and electronics courses with a focus on nanoscience and nanotechnology. Key features: • Provides an updated, all-encompassing exploration of contemporary nanosensors and highlights the exclusive nanoscale properties on which nanosensors are designed. • Presents an accessible approach with a question-and-answer format to allow an easy grasp of the intricacies involved in the complex working mechanisms of devices. • Contains clear, illustrative diagrams that enable visualization of nanosensor operations, along with worked examples, end-of-chapter questions, and exhaustive, up-to-date bibliographies appended to each chapter.

title: Advancements in Pipeline Corrosion Monitoring for Supercritical CO2 Environments: A Review
source: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
summary: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) technology ensures that captured CO2 is compressed and transported through pipelines in its supercritical state (SC-CO2) to allow for large-scale storage and utilization. SC-CO2 corrosion is a
content: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) technology ensures that captured CO2 is compressed and transported through pipelines in its supercritical state (SC-CO2) to allow for large-scale storage and utilization. SC-CO2 corrosion is a difficult challenge to pipeline transportation due to the extremely high-temperature-pressure conditions and impurities such as water, SO2, O2, H2S, and NO2. Review articles on the subject have mostly focused on the mechanism, factors contributing to the corrosion, and prevention/control strategies, with limited attention paid to monitoring techniques. This study aimed to review the extant literature on corrosion evaluation and monitoring, to supplement previous reviews. The sources of impurities and their mechanistic influence on the corrosion behavior are examined to contextualize the monitoring requirement. Traditional predictive models are critically assessed, highlighting their inaccuracy and limited applicability to impurity-rich supercritical conditions. Laboratory techniques, including weight loss, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), linear polarization resistance (LPR), and potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), are evaluated, demonstrating their value for mechanistic insight but limited suitability for continuous, field-scale, real-time monitoring. The review further analyzes recent machine learning (ML) models, identifying persistent inaccuracy and generalization issues arising from small, fragmented training datasets and suboptimal training. Key challenges highlighted include data scarcity, lack of in-situ sensing devices, and absence of real-time monitoring frameworks. Metaheuristic optimization strategies, data expansion, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and mechanism-data fusion are proposed to improve model robustness. Emerging technologies such as distributed fiber-optic sensors and non-destructive methods are examined for their potential to enable continuous, non-intrusive monitoring. Their integration with AI and ML-driven solutions is also proposed as a shift from post-corrosion detection toward predictive, process-integrated integrity management. By consolidating fragmented research, identifying unresolved technical challenges, and outlining a pathway toward integrated sensing frameworks, this work provides a structured roadmap for advancing real-time corrosion monitoring and integrity management.

title: Galerkin finite element analysis of double-diffusive magnetohydrodynamic convection in a wavy-walled enclosure containing a hybrid nanofluid
summary: Double-diffusive natural convection, governed by the coupled interplay of thermal and solutal buoyancy forces, is markedly influenced by magnetic damping and geometric confinement, motivating deeper numerical exploration of such complex tra
content: Double-diffusive natural convection, governed by the coupled interplay of thermal and solutal buoyancy forces, is markedly influenced by magnetic damping and geometric confinement, motivating deeper numerical exploration of such complex transport phenomena. This study presents a numerical investigation of magnetohydrodynamic thermo-solutal convection within a wavy-walled enclosure filled with a [Formula: see text]₃/water hybrid nanofluid, embedded with an internally heated circular cylinder, wherein the bottom wall and cylinder are maintained at elevated temperature while the undulating side walls are held at comparatively lower temperature and concentration. The governing conservation equations are solved via the Galerkin Finite Element Method (GFEM), enabling a comprehensive parametric analysis of the Rayleigh number, Hartmann number, hybrid nanoparticle volume fraction, Lewis number, and cylinder position, to elucidate their combined influence on flow structure, heat transfer, and mass transfer characteristics. The results reveal that increasing the Rayleigh number from 10⁴ to 10⁶ substantially intensifies buoyancy-driven circulation by 97.27%, promoting stronger thermal plume development and a corresponding 66.53% enhancement in the local Nusselt number[Formula: see text]; conversely, elevating the Hartmann number to 100 introduces dominant Lorentz forces that suppress velocity gradients, diminishing the ([Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]) by 40.3% and 15.7%, respectively. Increasing the Lewis number from 1 to 10 further reduces thermal diffusion by 48.26% while simultaneously amplifying mass diffusion by 88.5%, and cylinder position significantly affects thermal performance by modifying the flow structure, thermal plumes, and boundary-layer interactions. Collectively, these findings offer valuable insight into optimizing hybrid nanofluid-based thermo-solutal systems for enhanced energy and mass transport efficiency under magnetic field control.

title: Brown adipose tissue sustains thermogenesis through metabolic flexibility in glucose utilization
summary: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a cold-activated organ that uncouples mitochondrial respiration from ATP synthesis to produce heat. Activated BAT can consume an extreme amount of glucose, per gram of tissue, in both mice and humans. However,
content: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a cold-activated organ that uncouples mitochondrial respiration from ATP synthesis to produce heat. Activated BAT can consume an extreme amount of glucose, per gram of tissue, in both mice and humans. However, the contexts, mechanisms and necessity for BAT glucose utilization remain surprisingly undefined in vivo. Here we show that while BAT thermogenesis is maintained across diverse dietary contexts, its glucose utilization is particularly responsive to diet. Importantly, we find cold-induced BAT glucose uptake and thermogenesis to be independent of the previously proposed critical transporter, GLUT1. Instead, inducible GLUT4 loss eliminates cold-induced glucose uptake and compromises BAT thermogenesis only when dietary lipids are low during cold stress. We furthermore illustrate the unexpected capacity for brown adipocytes to sustain ATP levels without glycolysis, even during substantial mitochondrial uncoupling, when alternative nutrients are abundant. Collectively, our work demonstrates that BAT sustains thermogenesis through marked metabolic flexibility across nutrient contexts.

title: A prediction method for the compression‐bending capacity of horizontal joints in externally prestressed wind turbine towers
summary: Abstract Accurate evaluation of compression‐bending capacity is essential for the design of concrete wind turbine towers. After a horizontal joint opens, the unbonded external tendons do not follow the local concrete strain distribution, li
content: Abstract Accurate evaluation of compression‐bending capacity is essential for the design of concrete wind turbine towers. After a horizontal joint opens, the unbonded external tendons do not follow the local concrete strain distribution, limiting the applicability of conventional annular‐section design methods. This study proposes a non‐iterative method that derives tendon strain increments from the global deformation of the tower using an equivalent plastic‐hinge model. The resulting expressions are combined with sectional force and moment equilibrium to predict ultimate bending capacity. Predictions are evaluated against 14 externally prestressed annular specimens reported in six studies and compared with two existing analytical models and three code‐based methods. The code‐based methods give mean predicted‐to‐measured moment ratios of 1.50, 1.53, and 1.79, corresponding to average overestimations of approximately 50%, 53%, and 79%. The proposed method gives a mean ratio of 0.95 and a coefficient of variation of 0.16. Its absolute mean bias is 5.4%, compared with 8.1% for the Tan JK model and 13.3% for the Ren W model—reductions of 33% and 59%, respectively. Parametric analysis indicates that capacity increases with concrete strength, varies non‐monotonically with precompression ratio, and decreases as the prestressing reinforcement ratio increases at a fixed precompression ratio. The method offers a direct calculation procedure for horizontal‐joint design, although validation at the larger diameter‐to‐thickness ratios typical of prototype towers is still needed.

title: A Generic and High‐Throughput Capillary‐Driven Shear Assembly for Fabrication of Highly Aligned Nanomaterials
summary: ABSTRACT Assembling two‐dimensional (2D) nanomaterials into macroscopic architectures that retain their exceptional intrinsic properties is pivotal for next‐generation functional devices. However, a persistent trade‐off remains between stru
content: ABSTRACT Assembling two‐dimensional (2D) nanomaterials into macroscopic architectures that retain their exceptional intrinsic properties is pivotal for next‐generation functional devices. However, a persistent trade‐off remains between structural precision and fabrication throughput: scalable techniques often succumb to Brownian‐induced orientation relaxation, yielding loosely packed, isotropic networks, while precision‐oriented methods lack industrial scalability. Herein, we demonstrate a capillary‐driven shear assembly (CDSA) strategy—a continuous, hydrodynamically driven approach that leverages the synergy of capillary pressure and fluid dynamics to fabricate highly aligned, densified nanocomposites. Unlike conventional strategies, the CDSA strategy utilizes capillary forces generated by porous media to create a confined horizontal shear flow, which aligns the nanosheets horizontally at the interface. This strategy not only boosts assembly speed, but also proves universally applicable to a diverse library of 2D materials, including graphene oxide (GO), MXene, MoS 2 , and h‐BN. Importantly, after graphitization treatments, g‐CDSA‐GO exhibits a high in‐plane thermal conductivity. Further incorporation of polyimide‐derived graphitic bridges increases the through‐plane thermal conductivity to 21.3 W m −1 K −1 while maintaining an in‐plane value of 1406 W m −1 K −1 . These results establish CDSA as a scalable route for constructing highly ordered 2D architectures.

title: Dietary Human HSP90 Promotes Longevity and Healthspan in Caenorhabditis elegans via a Multi-Branched Stress Signaling Pathway
summary: The loss of proteostasis is one of the primary drivers of aging. Despite the important role of the molecular chaperone HSP90 in maintaining proteostasis, its systemic role in aging appears contradictory because its inhibitors can effectivel
content: The loss of proteostasis is one of the primary drivers of aging. Despite the important role of the molecular chaperone HSP90 in maintaining proteostasis, its systemic role in aging appears contradictory because its inhibitors can effectively extend lifespan across diverse species. This study showed that dietary HSP90 supplementation via Escherichia coli significantly extended lifespan and healthspan of Caenorhabditis elegans without fertility trade-offs. Exogenous HSP90 likely acts as an extracellular signaling ligand that engages downstream kinase networks to drive the activation of three major longevity-associated transcription factors: DAF-16, SKN-1, and HSF-1. In addition, we demonstrated the additive effect of combining dietary HSP90 supplementation with the senolytic HSP90 inhibitor tanespimycin, indicating that extracellular proteostatic signaling and the intracellular inhibition of HSP90 can work together to enhance longevity. Finally, we engineered an antibiotic-free E. coli Nissle 1917 probiotic that constitutively expresses HSP90, which successfully extended the lifespan of C. elegans.

title: DGIM-SAM: dual-kernel gated interaction modulation and spectral adaptive modulation for real-time wildfire detection
summary: Abstract Wildfire detection in unconstrained natural scenes is challenging due to weak fire responses, ambiguous smoke boundaries, and interference from clouds, haze, vegetation, and illumination changes. To address these challenges, we pro
content: Abstract Wildfire detection in unconstrained natural scenes is challenging due to weak fire responses, ambiguous smoke boundaries, and interference from clouds, haze, vegetation, and illumination changes. To address these challenges, we propose DGIM-SAM , a real-time wildfire detection framework that combines dual-kernel gated interaction modulation with spectral adaptive modulation. DGIM-SAM consists of three key components. First, the Dual-Kernel Enhanced Cross Stage Partial block enlarges the effective receptive field through dual 3 × 3 convolutions, improving the representation of irregular flames and diffuse smoke. Second, the Spectral Adaptive Feed Forward Network adaptively modulates frequency responses to enhance discriminative high-frequency fire cues while suppressing low-frequency environmental noise. Third, the Channel Linearized Alignment Gating Fusion module aligns multi-scale features by jointly modeling grid-level spatial dependencies and channel-wise semantic importance, reducing feature mismatch during fusion. Experiments on D-Fire, FASDD, FLAME and a Self-Constructed Wildfire Dataset with 18 000 images demonstrate that DGIM-SAM achieves strong accuracy and efficiency. DGIM-SAM achieves an average mAP 50 : 95 of 55.6% and 145 FPS on a desktop GPU, while reaching 38.7 FPS with 25.8 ms latency on the Jetson Orin Nano, demonstrating strong accuracy, efficiency, and edge-deployment feasibility. These results show that DGIM-SAM provides an effective and scalable solution for real-time forest surveillance on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: Hydrogen Bubble Engineering of Lewis Acid Sites in Phosphorene for Efficient Nitrogen Reduction
summary: ABSTRACT The electrochemical synthesis of ammonia through nitrogen reduction (ENRR) is hindered by N 2 inertness and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Phosphorene, despite its promise, inherently lacks the eletron‐backdonation ca
content: ABSTRACT The electrochemical synthesis of ammonia through nitrogen reduction (ENRR) is hindered by N 2 inertness and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Phosphorene, despite its promise, inherently lacks the eletron‐backdonation capability for effective N 2 activation. Herein, we present a water‐free hydrogen bubble electroetching strategy to simultaneously exfoliate and engineer black phosphorus into defect‐rich porous phosphorene (D‐BP ene ) with abundant in‐plane phosphorus vacancies for ENRR catalysis. Four‐dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy resolves distorted hexagonal rings where pairs of P atoms from the upper and lower sub‐layers show mutually perpendicular orientations. D‐BP ene exhibits superior electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction performance, achieving a high NH 3 yield of 14.94 µg h −1 mg cat −1 at −0.05 V versus RHE and a Faradaic efficiency of 35.51% at 0 V versus RHE that corresponds to an ultralow overpotential of 92 mV, outperforming most metal‐free catalysts, while remaining stable for over 36 h. Density functional theory calculations reveal that phosphorus vacancies act as Lewis acid sites, reducing the energy barrier for the potential‐determining step from 2.012 to 1.387 eV via strengthened σ‐donation and π‐backdonation, while increasing the HER kinetic barrier by inhibiting *H desorption. This work presents an effective synthetic route to vacancy‐engineered two‐dimensional materials with potential applications extending beyond nitrogen fixation.

title: Rechargeable Metal‐Catalysis Batteries for Energy‐Storing Decoupled Electrosynthesis
summary: Renewable-electricity-driven electrosynthesis is a key route to carbon-neutral chemical manufacturing, but conventional systems rely on obligatorily coupled anodic and cathodic reactions under continuous bias, causing kinetic mismatch, ener
content: Renewable-electricity-driven electrosynthesis is a key route to carbon-neutral chemical manufacturing, but conventional systems rely on obligatorily coupled anodic and cathodic reactions under continuous bias, causing kinetic mismatch, energy loss, competing optimization, crossover, and poor compatibility with intermittent energy input. Rechargeable metal-catalysis batteries enable temporally decoupled electrosynthesis by storing electrical or solar energy as chemical potential and releasing it on demand for catalysis independent of instantaneous power input, enabling programmable electrosynthesis. This Review establishes a unified thermodynamic and mechanistic framework for energy-storing decoupled systems, categorizes key storage media and their regulatory roles, and introduces full-cycle energy accounting metrics. Representative advances in hydrogen production, carbon conversion, nitrogen transformation, and photo-coupled systems are summarized, highlighting how intermediate storage reshapes reaction pathways beyond conventional electrolysis. Finally, we identify key challenges in full-cycle efficiency quantification, storage medium cycling stability, coupled-process mechanistic elucidation, and reactor engineering, and envision future development of integrated energy storage-catalysis systems toward sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Coordinative Organic–Inorganic Heterostructured Hierarchical Composite Gel Polymer Electrolytes Enabling Ultrahigh‐Power and Ultra‐Durable Solid‐State Zinc–Air Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Rechargeable solid‐state zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) are highly promising energy storage devices for next‐generation portable electronics, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by issues of dehydration of gel polymer el
content: ABSTRACT Rechargeable solid‐state zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) are highly promising energy storage devices for next‐generation portable electronics, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by issues of dehydration of gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) and dendrite formation on Zn electrodes. We report an organic‐inorganic heterostructured hierarchical composite GPE, PANa‐NCF‐NiFeLDH, featuring sodium polyacrylate (PANa), nitrogen‐doped carbon foam (NCF), and NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFeLDH). Electrostatic coordination between Ni/Fe Lewis acid sites of NiFeLDH and carboxylate groups of PANa, creates nano‐crack network to facilitate electrolyte adsorption and ion transport, modulates electron density and polarity of PANa chains to promote uniform Zn deposition, and provides energy adsorption heterojunctions to enhance mechanical strength. Exceptional liquid electrolyte uptake (1700%) and retention (92.9%), ionic conductivity (322 m S/cm), and tensile strength (2500 kPa) are achieved. The abundant hydroxyl groups of NiFeLDH facilitates hydroxyl ion transport, reconstructs hydrogen bond network, and immobilizes free water molecules, leading to enhanced liquid electrolyte uptake and retention and suppression of parasitic reactions. The PANa‐NCF‐NiFeLDH GPE based solid‐state ZAB delivers an ultrahigh peak power density of 229 mW/cm 2 and sustains an outstanding lifespan of 1494 cycles (249 h). Even after a three‐week storage in concentrated alkaline media, the PANa‐NCF‐NiFeLDH GPE maintains its performance without noticeable degradation.

title: Smart Swarming Micro/Nanorobots for Translational Therapeutic Applications
summary: Swarming behavior is a common phenomenon in nature. Living organisms interact with their surroundings and other individuals, demonstrating coordination and cooperation to accomplish complex tasks. The emerging characteristics of interacting
content: Swarming behavior is a common phenomenon in nature. Living organisms interact with their surroundings and other individuals, demonstrating coordination and cooperation to accomplish complex tasks. The emerging characteristics of interacting individuals are widespread across scales, ranging from collective cell migrations and fish schools moving in synchrony to animal migrations across continents. Inspired by swarming intelligence in nature, self-propelled micro- and nanorobots have been proposed that can move collectively in response to environmental inputs, including magnetic fields, light, ultrasound, electric fields, and chemicals. Unlike a single unit, these synthetic swarms can perform multiple tasks, such as cargo delivery, analyte capture, and purification, for biomedical applications. Here, we review and discuss the collective behavior of synthetic swarms and their biological counterparts. In particular, we will focus on translational synthetic swarm systems for advanced drug delivery and therapeutic applications, in comparison with conventional drug delivery systems. Finally, we will discuss challenges, including communication between swarms, energy-conversion efficiencies, and biosafety, and describe prospects for further translational applications of swarming systems.

title: Femtosecond Laser‐Induced Self‐Organized 3D Graphene Microcones for Programmable Photothermal Information Encryption
summary: ABSTRACT Owing to its unique capabilities of in situ functionalization, multiscale structural construction, and single‐step fabrication, femtosecond laser‐induced graphene demonstrates significant potential in flexible sensing and micro/nan
content: ABSTRACT Owing to its unique capabilities of in situ functionalization, multiscale structural construction, and single‐step fabrication, femtosecond laser‐induced graphene demonstrates significant potential in flexible sensing and micro/nano optoelectronic devices. However, most studies focus on two‐dimensional (2D) graphene, while three‐dimensional (3D) architectures and their formation mechanisms remain less explored. Here, femtosecond (fs) laser direct writing is employed to fabricate morphologically controllable microcone structures on polyimide (PI) substrates, and the underlying graphitization and structural evolution are systematically investigated. By integrating pump‐probe and intensified charge‐coupled device imaging, we resolve the multiscale dynamics of fs laser‐PI interaction, spanning ultrafast energy deposition, plasma expansion, particle ejection, and surface restructuring. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a chemical pathway involving ring opening, oxygen incorporation, deoxygenation, and carbon‐ring reconstruction toward an sp 2 ‐hybridized network. Raman spectroscopy confirms defect healing and improved graphene quality, while molecular dynamics simulations provide atomic‐level insight into bond breaking and carbon‐ring reconstruction. Through regulation of microcone morphology and inter‐cone spacing, the 3D graphene structures exhibit tunable broadband absorptance (66.2–98.2%) and photothermal response (40.8–60.2 °C), enabling programmable photothermal encoding and information encryption. This work presents a facile strategy for fabricating graphene microcones and elucidates the multiscale evolution of laser‐induced carbonization, providing inspiration for designing high‐performance 3D graphene structures.

title: Luminescent Molecular Logic: Fundamentals, Implementation Strategies, and Emerging Architectures
summary: ABSTRACT The increasing demand for energy‐efficient, adaptable, and environment‐responsive information processing is motivating the exploration of computing paradigms that complement conventional silicon electronics. Among these, luminescen
