content: ABSTRACT The increasing demand for energy‐efficient, adaptable, and environment‐responsive information processing is motivating the exploration of computing paradigms that complement conventional silicon electronics. Among these, luminescent molecular logic offers a versatile approach in which chemical, physical, or optical stimuli are converted into measurable photophysical outputs and interpreted according to Boolean operations. This Review critically examines the principles, implementation, and validation of luminescent molecular logic, with particular emphasis on the methodological transition from continuous optical signals to reproducible digital outputs. A systematic framework is discussed encompassing photophysical measurements, response‐function selection, uncertainty propagation, signal digitization, threshold definition, truth‐table construction, and logic‐gate assignment. Particular attention is also given to the distinction between independent optical channels and mathematically derived response functions, as well as to interrogation‐level reconfiguration, data‐analysis‐level reassignment, and material‐level reprogramming. Quantitative figures of merit are introduced to assess state discrimination, reproducibility, stability, crosstalk, and scalability beyond qualitative gate assignment. Representative supramolecular, photochromic, DNA‐based, carbon‐dot, and trivalent‐lanthanide platforms are critically compared in terms of their capabilities, limitations, and prospects for integration. Finally, current bottlenecks and emerging opportunities in multidimensional luminescence, adaptive architectures, and hybrid molecular–photonic and molecular–electronic systems are discussed.

title: Breaking the Porosity‐Strength Trade‐Off in Hierarchical Current Collectors for Lithium Metal Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Porous metallic current collectors can homogenize lithium (Li) deposition and accommodate volume change, but increasing porosity generally compromises mechanical integrity under stack pressure. Here, a mechanically reinforced, grad
content: ABSTRACT Porous metallic current collectors can homogenize lithium (Li) deposition and accommodate volume change, but increasing porosity generally compromises mechanical integrity under stack pressure. Here, a mechanically reinforced, gradient‐designed hierarchical current collector (GDH CC) is constructed from an FeNi alloy skeleton, a conformal Cu shell, and Al 2 O 3 ‐modified outer faces. The FeNi‐containing framework reinforces the porous architecture while the spatially differentiated interfaces are designed to favor internal Li accommodation. The 50 µm‐thick CC combines a retained porosity of 80.13% with a compressive yield strength of 0.309 MPa and was examined after passing a nominal Li deposition charge of 8 mAh cm −2 . Cross‐sectional microscopy and in situ optical observations indicate center‐outward plating and reverse stripping within the scaffold. The GDH CC delivers an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.7% for 400 cycles at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 and supports stable bidirectional cycling in pouch‐type cells. A multilayer LFP | Li/GDH CC | LFP pouch cell delivers 145 mAh g −1 at 1 C, corresponding to cell‐level gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 172.49 Wh kg −1 and 297.78 Wh L −1 , respectively. These results identify mechanical reinforcement as an important design dimension for high‐porosity Li hosts.

title: Technologies for Extracting Bioactive Compounds from Rice Bran: Advances and Prospects
source: Caraka Tani Journal of Sustainable Agriculture
summary: Rice bran, an agro-industrial by-product, is rich in a variety of bioactive constituents with potential applications in food and related industries. This review critically evaluates extraction technologies for recovering these constituents,
content: Rice bran, an agro-industrial by-product, is rich in a variety of bioactive constituents with potential applications in food and related industries. This review critically evaluates extraction technologies for recovering these constituents, focusing on the relationships among extraction mechanisms, solvent selection, process optimization, product quality, and industrial feasibility. The traditional techniques are compared with ultrasound-assisted extraction, microwave-assisted extraction, enzyme-assisted extraction, supercritical carbon dioxide extraction, and integrated approaches. The review compares their operating principles, compound-specific recovery, extraction efficiency, and reported antioxidant-related properties, while taking into consideration the differences in feedstock characteristics and analytical reporting. Moreover, special attention is given to solvent polarity, solvent-solute interactions, and emerging solvent systems, as factors influencing extraction selectivity and product composition. Authors also discuss response surface methodology, kinetic modeling, and other process-design approaches to identify opportunities and limitations in extraction optimization and scale-up. The main challenges are inconsistent reporting of extraction results, limited comparability between studies, insufficient industrial validation, and the need to thoroughly evaluate solvent safety, environmental impact, and economic viability. This review offers a framework for the selection and development of extraction methods balancing the recovery of bioactive compounds, product functionality, and the sustainable valorization of rice bran by integrating technological, physicochemical, and engineering perspectives.

title: A Green Reduced-Alkali Hydrothermal Route for the Valorisation of Indian Coal Fly Ash into Zeolitic Aluminosilicates: Structural, Morphological and Textural Characterisation
summary: Coal combustion in India generates over 270 million tonnes of fly ash annually, much of which remains stored in ash ponds. Converting this waste into zeolitic aluminosilicates is scientifically promising, as fly ash possesses significant si
content: Coal combustion in India generates over 270 million tonnes of fly ash annually, much of which remains stored in ash ponds. Converting this waste into zeolitic aluminosilicates is scientifically promising, as fly ash possesses significant silica and alumina content comparable to conventional zeolite precursor materials. However, most synthesis methods require concentrated alkali, high temperatures, or alkali-fusion pre-treatment, raising environmental and economic costs. This study investigates a mild hydrothermal route using only 0.5-1.5 mol L⁻¹ sodium hydroxide at 80-120 °C, without fusion or acid neutralisation, to selectively activate the amorphous fraction of fly ash from the Gandhinagar Thermal Power Plant. Raw and treated samples were characterised by particle size analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) , Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area measurement, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The median particle diameter decreased from approximately 30 µm to 4 µm. Quartz and mullite reflections weakened while new sodium aluminosilicate phases emerged. Infrared bands sharpened in the 950-1050 cm⁻¹ and 550-650 cm⁻¹ regions. Polyhedral microcrystals replaced spherical particles, and specific surface area rose from approximately 6 to 310 m²g⁻¹. These findings confirm that selective mild activation converts fly ash into functional zeolitic materials with reduced reagent use, lower energy demand, and potential for adsorption, ion exchange, and catalytic applications.

title: Toward practical irrigation decision support: Predicting grapevine stem water potential from soil moisture and atmospheric demand
summary: Water scarcity and recurrent drought in California continue to challenge vineyard productivity and fruit quality, increasing the need for irrigation scheduling tools that improve water use efficiency while maintaining vine performance. This
content: Water scarcity and recurrent drought in California continue to challenge vineyard productivity and fruit quality, increasing the need for irrigation scheduling tools that improve water use efficiency while maintaining vine performance. This proof-of-concept study evaluated whether grapevine stem water potential can be estimated from a practical combination of soil moisture sensing and local weather station observations to support irrigation decisions in a hot viticultural region. The experiment was conducted in a Barbera ( Vitis vinifera L.) vineyard in Fresno, California, over three growing seasons (2023–2025) under four irrigation regimes (50%, 75%, and 100% crop evapotranspiration (ET c ) replacement, and an over-irrigated treatment). Soil moisture was monitored using spatial frequency domain transmissometry (SFDT) and time-domain reflectometry (TDR) sensors installed at 20, 37.5, and 75 cm, with an additional 150 cm TDR sensor installed to characterize deeper profile dynamics. Weather variables were obtained from the nearest California Irrigation Management Information System (CIMIS) station. Midday stem water potential (Ψ stem ) was measured and used to train and evaluate predictive models intended to provide continuous, sensor-based inference of vine water status. Permutation feature importance (PFI) analyses across algorithms consistently identified deep soil moisture (75 cm) and air temperature as dominant predictors, with relative humidity providing limited explanatory value. Model selection based on repeated held-out testing identified partial least squares (PLS) regression as the most stable approach across the expanding datasets. In the final three-year full data regression fits, the two-variable model (soil moisture at 75 cm + air temperature) produced R 2 = 0.629 (RMSE = 0.141 MPa) and the three-variable model (soil moisture at 75 cm + air temperature + relative humidity) produced R 2 = 0.639 (RMSE = 0.139 MPa) for Ψ stem prediction. When models were applied without recalibration to an independent commercial vineyard in 2026, they retained moderate predictive relationships with measured Ψ stem , with R 2 values ranging from 0.515 to 0.619. Overall, the results demonstrated the feasibility of estimating grapevine Ψ stem from a minimal, adoption-oriented sensor package, supporting a practical framework for irrigation decision support under hot, water-limited vineyard conditions.

title: Interfacial coordination reconstruction via electrochemical phase transformation for stable zinc powder anodes
summary: The practical development of aqueous zinc-ion batteries is hampered by the intrinsic thermodynamic instability of zinc powder anodes, where uncontrolled parasitic reactions and dendritic growth lead to rapid capacity decay. Conventional int
content: The practical development of aqueous zinc-ion batteries is hampered by the intrinsic thermodynamic instability of zinc powder anodes, where uncontrolled parasitic reactions and dendritic growth lead to rapid capacity decay. Conventional interfacial protection layers, whether pre-fabricated or in-situ formed, suffer from mechanical and chemical degradation under dynamic cycling conditions. Here, we report an interface regulation strategy based on an electrochemically driven phase transformation of copper oxalate (CuC2O4) embedded in the zinc powder electrode. Upon discharge, the CuC2O4 undergoes a structural reconstruction involving the conversion of C=O to C-O coordination environments and the partial reduction of Cu2+ to Cu+, as evidenced by multi-modal spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. This reconstructed interface, enriched with C-O groups and Cu+ sites, exhibits enhanced zinc affinity and water confinement, as quantified by density functional theory calculations, thereby suppressing parasitic hydrogen evolution and guiding uniform zinc deposition. As a result, the modified zinc powder anode (ZP@CuC2O4) delivers a stable cycling lifetime of approximately 600 h under high-rate conditions (7 mA cm-2/1 mAh cm-2) in symmetric cells and enables pouch-type full cells to deliver a cumulative capacity of 11.7 Ah after 1,000 cycles at 7 A g-1. This work demonstrates a paradigm of dynamic interfacial engineering through intrinsic phase-transition-induced coordination reconstruction, addressing a key barrier for practical zinc powder anodes.

title: Optimized Vacuum-Sputtered Gold Nanoparticle-Modified Titanium Dioxide Nanotubes for Ultrasensitive Myocardial Infarction Multi-Biomarker Detection
summary: Myocardial infarction, a sudden reduction in blood flow to the heart, requires rapid and sensitive detection of biomarkers reflecting different stages of cardiac injury and plaque destabilization. Herein, a universal electrochemical biosens
content: Myocardial infarction, a sudden reduction in blood flow to the heart, requires rapid and sensitive detection of biomarkers reflecting different stages of cardiac injury and plaque destabilization. Herein, a universal electrochemical biosensing platform based on gold nanoparticle-modified titanium dioxide nanotubes (AuNPs/TNTs) was developed for the detection of cardiac troponin T (cTnT), heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A). Titanium dioxide nanotubes with a diameter of 50 ± 5 nm and a length of 1000 ± 100 nm, previously optimized for electrochemical and adsorption properties, were modified with AuNPs by vacuum sputtering at 20 mA for 10, 20, and 40 s. The influence of nanoparticle deposition on the morphology, phase composition, surface chemistry, wettability, and electrochemical properties of AuNPs/TNTs was systematically investigated. The AuNPs/TNTs sample prepared by Au sputtering for 10 s exhibited the most favorable physicochemical properties for biosensing applications. After nanocomposite functionalization, the platform enabled impedimetric detection of cTnT, H-FABP, and PAPP-A in clinically relevant concentration ranges. The obtained limits of detection for cTnT, H-FABP, and PAPP-A were 0.01, 0.23, and 0.008 ng/mL, respectively. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first AuNPs/TNTs-based electrochemical platform for the detection of cTnT, H-FABP, and PAPP-A. In addition, no AuNPs/TNTs electrochemical biosensor for PAPP-A determination has been reported to date.

title: Printable Monolayer of Binary Polymer-Co-Grafted Au Nanoparticles for Nano-Floating-Gate Transistor Memory
summary: Abstract Nano-floating-gate organic field-effect transistor (NFGOFET) memories are promising candidates for flexible, low-cost, and solution-processable nonvolatile memory devices. Their performance relies critically on the construction of
content: Abstract Nano-floating-gate organic field-effect transistor (NFGOFET) memories are promising candidates for flexible, low-cost, and solution-processable nonvolatile memory devices. Their performance relies critically on the construction of a uniform nano-floating-gate/tunneling-dielectric (NFG/TD) layer, in which discrete nanoparticles serve as charge-storage sites and the surrounding polymer matrix functions as the tunneling dielectric. However, the solution processing of the upper organic semiconductor layer often causes solvent-induced erosion of polymer tunneling layers, disrupting the nanoparticle distribution and degrading charge transport and storage. Here, we report a solvent-resistant NFG/TD layer based on binary polymer-co-modified gold nanoparticles and in situ SiO2 interfacial engineering. Gold nanoparticles co-grafted with polystyrene and poly(4-vinylpyridine) form a printable monolayer in which polystyrene serves as the tunneling dielectric and poly(4-vinylpyridine) provides anchoring sites for TEOS hydrolysis. The SiO2 layer preserves the nanoparticle monolayer during active-layer printing and provides a stable inorganic tunneling barrier and a modifiable interface for improving semiconductor crystallization. This work establishes a general and scalable interfacial regulation strategy for the solution-process of printable multi-layered organic thin-film devices.

title: Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation to Multicarbon Products: Mechanisms, Catalyst Design, and Scale Demonstration
summary: Abstract Photothermal CO 2 hydrogenation to multicarbon products presents a promising route to mitigate global climate change while simultaneously generating valuable C 2+ products for industrial use. However, realizing high activity and se
content: Abstract Photothermal CO 2 hydrogenation to multicarbon products presents a promising route to mitigate global climate change while simultaneously generating valuable C 2+ products for industrial use. However, realizing high activity and selectivity toward multicarbon products remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the intricate nature of reactant activation and the inherently sluggish kinetics of C−C coupling. This review elucidates the fundamental principles of photothermal catalysis, with a particular focus on the synergistic interplay between light and thermal energy. In addition, the activation pathways of CO 2 to C 1 intermediates and the subsequent mechanisms of C−C bond formation leading to multicarbon products are systematically examined. On this basis, catalyst design and modification strategies are categorized to enhance reactant activation and facilitate efficient C−C coupling. Furthermore, recent progress in pilot-scale demonstrations is highlighted to showcase the potential for scalable and sustainable CO 2 hydrogenation technologies. By addressing the current challenges and outlining future research directions, this review aims to accelerate the development of efficient photothermal processes for CO 2 valorization.

title: Predictive Model for Assessing Reservoir Formation Suitability for CCUS in the Niger Delta, Nigeria
source: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering Management & Applied Science
summary: There is a need for an efficient way of ranking potential CCUS reservoirs before site characterization, whereas previous Niger Delta CCUS reservoir screenings have been carried out using field-specific criteria. In this work, we ranked 12,7
content: There is a need for an efficient way of ranking potential CCUS reservoirs before site characterization, whereas previous Niger Delta CCUS reservoir screenings have been carried out using field-specific criteria. In this work, we ranked 12,734 selected data points of Niger Delta reservoirs provided by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) in a standardized manner, and we investigated the performance of machine learning (ML) methods in reproducing such ranking. Nine storage-related variables including relative permeability to oil, depth, porosity, pore volume, permeability, reservoir pressure, reservoir temperature, grain size, and water saturation were considered as normalized variables in favor of storage capacity. A suitability index (SI) was defined based on a weighted sum of these nine variables with weights obtained using principal component analysis in line with the composite-indicator development OECD/JRC approach and 12,734 data points were classified into four quartile classes. The ranking was found to be robust against changes in the weights as an equally weighted index showed a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.97 with the main index, and classified 82% of the data points in the same quartile classes. The FNN performed best in reproducing the index (test R² = 0.9997; cross-validated R² = 0.9999 ± 0.0002) with a classification accuracy of 98.4% for the test set, outperforming XGBoost (R² = 0.9955; 95.1%) and RF (R² = 0.9829; 91.1%); nearly all misclassification occurred near the boundary between classes. As the index depends on the inputs, these metrics represent the ability of the models to reproduce the index as opposed to storage capacity. The present research offers a fully transparent, reproducible screening index with weights validated using independent data, as well as surrogate models for rapid screening of reservoirs.

title: Nutrient-derived metabolic signals in tumor immune regulation: bioavailability, compartmental allocation, and translational boundaries
summary: The relationship between dietary factors and antitumor immunity has attracted growing attention, but dietary intake, circulating biomarkers, and biological activity within tumor-associated tissues occupy different positions along the path f
content: The relationship between dietary factors and antitumor immunity has attracted growing attention, but dietary intake, circulating biomarkers, and biological activity within tumor-associated tissues occupy different positions along the path from exposure to function. Nutrient signals are continually reshaped by host processing and local delivery. Their effects depend less on the nutrient label itself than on the molecular form that reaches a given cell and the function that is actually limiting in that cell. This review integrates mechanistic and clinical evidence to explain why the same nutritional change may preserve effector-cell function or support tumor adaptation, with opposing compartment-specific effects most clearly demonstrated for lipid-related pathways. We also distinguish interventions that directly act on tumor-immune processes from nutritional support strategies designed mainly to maintain patient reserve and treatment tolerance. Claims of immune regulation should match the level of measurement. When tumor cells and immune cells may respond differently, paired compartment-specific readouts are needed. Nutritional strategies have translational value only when they target a defined and reversible limitation in a specific patient group and treatment window.

title: Irrigation-Nitrogen Synergies Shaping Fodder Yield, Quality and Water Productivity in Spring Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L.)
summary: Abstract Sorghum is known for its drought tolerance and climate resilience grown in water limiting conditions. The cultivation of sorghum in Punjab as low water requiring crop may help in arresting fast declining water table. The nitrogen f
content: Abstract Sorghum is known for its drought tolerance and climate resilience grown in water limiting conditions. The cultivation of sorghum in Punjab as low water requiring crop may help in arresting fast declining water table. The nitrogen fertilisation and irrigation management crucial role in the success of any crop. Therefore, this study was carried out to determine the potential effects of irrigation water and nitrogen management on growth, green fodder yield quality of sorghum. The treatments comprised of combinations of four different irrigation levels (I 1 -IW/CPE 1.2, I 2 -IW/CPE 1.0, I 3 -IW/CPE 0.8, I 4 -IW/CPE 0.6) and four nitrogen doses (N 1 -75 kg N/ha − 1 , N 2 -100 kg N/ha − 1 , N 3 -125 kg N/ha − 1 , N 4 -150 kg N/ha − 1 ) applied in an experiment conducted in split plots design during the years 2024 and 2025. Key findings revealed that irrigation and N application significantly influenced plant height, fodder yield, quality attributes and nutrient uptake. The highest plant height (227.79, 227.20 cm), fodder yield (6.90, 6.93 t ha − 1 ), nitrogen uptake (34.37, 34.77 kg ha − 1 ) and Crude protein (14.90, 14.98%) were observed under IW/CPE 1.2 in the year of 2024 and 2025 respectively. In nitrogen management scenario highest growth, yield and nitrogen uptake was observed under (N 4 ) 150 kg N/ha − 1 treatment. While increase the dose of nitrogen (N 4 ) Crude protein (15.0, 15.20%) and In Vitro Dry Matter Digestibility (56.78, 56.93%) also increase while NDF (%), ADF (%) and Crude Fibre (%) decrease. Effect of irrigation and nitrogen on most of the soil properties was observed non-significant while application of irrigation on IW/CPE 1.0 base increase the evapotranspiration and decrease the drainage losses of water in field condition. Therefore, an adequate water supply (I 2 -IW/CPE 1.0) and normal nitrogen application (125 kg N/ha − 1 ) is recommended for sorghum culture without any significant losses in yield and quality parameters.

title: Polymer-Mediated Gold Deposition on Magnetic Nanoparticles: Structure–Property Relationships for Ultra-Sensitive Electrochemical Interfaces Detection of Leptospira DNA
summary: Abstract Gold-decorated magnetic particles (GMPs) were successfully synthesized through the coprecipitation of oleic acid-stabilized magnetic particles followed by citrate reduction of HAuCl4. Here, we reported the impact of the polymer on
content: Abstract Gold-decorated magnetic particles (GMPs) were successfully synthesized through the coprecipitation of oleic acid-stabilized magnetic particles followed by citrate reduction of HAuCl4. Here, we reported the impact of the polymer on the formation of gold-decorated magnetic particles. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed uniformly distributed gold nanoparticles on the surface of the magnetic cores in GMP, whereas seed-mediated synthesis produced GMP-seed with larger particles due to further reduction and growth of gold on pre-existing gold nanoparticles, and more homogeneously distributed gold nanoparticles. The estimated gold mass fraction increased from 47.35% to 58.67% for GMP-seed1 and GMP-seed2, respectively, confirming increased gold deposition during seed-mediated synthesis. Five polymers aminodextran, poly(acrylic acid), poly(vinyl alcohol), poly(ethylenimine), and poly(vinylpyrrolidone)─were first adsorbed onto the magnetic particles prior to gold deposition to investigate polymer-mediated gold nanoparticle formation. Zeta potential and TEM analyses verified successful polymer coating and gold deposition, with variations in surface charge confirming distinct polymer functionalities. The incorporation of gold-decorated magnetic nanostructures into the electrochemical platform enhanced the measured electrochemical response compared with magnetic particles alone, as supported by the quantitative CV peak-current comparison. The GMPs showed successful functionalization with an ssDNA probe complementary to a conserved Leptospira interrogans gene sequence, enabling selective hybridization-based detection by electrochemical assay. The platform demonstrated detection of Leptospira ssDNA down to the lowest tested concentration of 0.1 ng/mL within 20 min, without cross-reactivity with nontarget DNA, demonstrating potential for rapid, field-deployable leptospirosis diagnostics. This nanobiosensor trades extreme sensitivity for rapid, point-of-care operation without thermal cycling─making it far more viable for field deployment in resource-limited, endemic tropical regions.

title: Determination of organic carbon concentrations in marine sediments across different dates by visible and near-infrared spectroscopy
summary: The application of spectral models across different monitoring dates remains a challenge in fixed-point monitoring. Here, we studied the temporal dynamics of the organic carbon concentrations in sediments from the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea w
content: The application of spectral models across different monitoring dates remains a challenge in fixed-point monitoring. Here, we studied the temporal dynamics of the organic carbon concentrations in sediments from the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea with visible and near-infrared spectroscopy using the established spectral models. In this study, 96 surface sediment samples were collected from the same sites in 2020 and 2023. These samples were prepared as dried powder samples, and their total organic carbon (TOC) concentrations were determined. Their visible and near-infrared spectra were also recorded. Firstly, TOC spectral models were established based on partial least squares regression (PLSR) and least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) using the samples collected in 2020. The results showed that these models had strong analytical capabilities. The coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) of the spectral models established by PLSR were 0.982 for the calibration set and 0.777 for the validation set. The R 2 of the spectral models established by LSSVM were 0.998 for the calibration set and 0.839 for the validation set. Subsequently, the two established models were used to analyze the TOC concentrations in the samples collected in 2023. The detection errors of the TOC in the samples collected in 2023 were large with direct use of the established models. After correction using the piecewise direct standardization (PDS) and intercept/slope ( S / B ) algorithms, the errors were significantly reduced. Specifically, after PDS and S / B correction, the R 2 increased from 0.292 to 0.710 and 0.732, while the root mean square error (RMSE) decreased from 0.302 to 0.193 and 0.186, respectively, as detected by the PLSR model. On the other hand, the R 2 increased from 0.409 to 0.745 and 0.760 and the RMSE decreased from 0.276 to 0.181 and 0.176, respectively, as detected by the LSSVM model. This study investigated the application of spectral analysis in fixed-point monitoring, providing an effective reference for high-frequency and even continuous time-series analysis in fixed-point monitoring.

title: Magnetic GO@AlFe2O4@SO3H nanocatalyst: a sustainable approach for the synthesis of 5-phenyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amines
summary: A novel magnetic nanocatalyst, denoted as GO@AlFe 2 O 4 @SO 3 H, has been successfully designed and applied as an efficient and sustainable heterogeneous catalyst for the synthesis of 5-phenyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amines. This one-pot methodo
content: A novel magnetic nanocatalyst, denoted as GO@AlFe 2 O 4 @SO 3 H, has been successfully designed and applied as an efficient and sustainable heterogeneous catalyst for the synthesis of 5-phenyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-amines. This one-pot methodology involves the direct cyclocondensation reaction of readily available benzoic acid derivatives with thiosemicarbazide, employing phosphorus oxychloride (POCl 3 ) as a cyclodehydrating agent. Remarkably, the reaction proceeds smoothly in water as a green solvent at a mild temperature of 50 °C, completing within 30 min. The protocol demonstrates excellent substrate generality, affording a diverse library of 19 target heterocyclic compounds in consistently high yields ranging from 87% to 96%. The robust GO@AlFe 2 O 4 @SO 3 H nanocomposite, which integrates the high surface area of functionalized graphene oxide (GO) with the superparamagnetic properties of aluminium-doped iron oxide (AlFe 2 O 4 ) and Brønsted-acidic sulfonic sites (-SO 3 H), facilitates straightforward magnetic separation from the reaction mixture. This feature underpins the catalyst’s exceptional reusability, as it could be recovered and successively reused for up to seven consecutive cycles without a significant loss in its catalytic performance. The presented work underscores a sustainable, rapid, and practical approach for accessing biologically relevant 1,3,4-thiadiazole frameworks, highlighting the advantages of magnetically recoverable nanocatalyst in promoting sustainable synthetic methodologies.

title: Mesoporous curvature-induced proton coupled electron transfer for rapid photoredox of CO2 to CH4
summary: Abstract The photoreduction of CO 2 is usually terminated by two-electron processes resulting in predominantly products CO, the formulation of eight-electron products CH 4 still remains a great challenge limited by proton coupled electron t
content: Abstract The photoreduction of CO 2 is usually terminated by two-electron processes resulting in predominantly products CO, the formulation of eight-electron products CH 4 still remains a great challenge limited by proton coupled electron transfer (PCET) abilities. Here, a novel type of two-dimensional (2-D) mesoporous TiO 2 (mTiO 2 ) has been synthesized based on the nanoscale titanium-oxo cluster units for rapid photoredox of CO 2 to CH 4 . In this unique 2-D structure, a mesoporous sheet with ~ 2.7 nm in thickness and several micrometers in size, can be stably formed into uniform hexagonal arrays. The size of the mesopores can be precisely controlled from 8.0 to 18.0 nm by utilizing the amphiphilic di-block copolymer poly(styrene- block -acrylic acid) (PS- b -PAA) micelles with tunable block lengths. With a curvature-governed Ti 3+ density, such mesoporous sheets demonstrate excellent photocatalytic CO 2 reduction capability by accelerating the PCET processes, achieving a record-high CH 4 production rate of 0.49 mmol g − 1 h − 1 with near-unique selectivity up to 99.6% under full-spectrum solar irradiation, without sacrificial reagents and co-catalysts, and the 2-D mTiO 2 can retain their photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles. An equivariant geometric deep learning model was constructed to simulate the spin density of mesoporous TiO 2 , with the objective of identifying exposed active sites. Synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy combined with EELS characterizations unambiguously verify that curved mesoporous interfaces induce reduced Ti − O coordination, concentrated oxygen vacancies and abundant low-valent Ti 3+ sites while retaining the anatase crystalline phase. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that curvature-enriched Ti 3+ sites can accelerate Volmer step and promote preferential hydrogenation to the carbon atom rather than oxygen (0.73 eV vs. 2.05 eV) due to a bent configuration of the Ti − O−Ti linkage. This atomic-scale selectivity suppresses CO formation and drives the reaction exclusively toward CH 4 , establishing a direct link between mesoporous curvature and multi-electron and proton coupling pathways. This work demonstrates that efficient and selective photocatalytic process can be achived by constructing rich Ti 3+ 2-D mesoporous structure via nanocluster assembly.

title: A Review of Soft Robots for Entangling-style Grasping: Structural Classification, Grasping Mechanisms and Key Challenges
summary: Abstract This review synthesizes recent advances in soft robots that utilize entangling-style grasping, categorizing them into two principal domains: soft grippers designed for target entangling, and continuum robots that leverage their ent
content: Abstract This review synthesizes recent advances in soft robots that utilize entangling-style grasping, categorizing them into two principal domains: soft grippers designed for target entangling, and continuum robots that leverage their entire body for both entangling and manipulation. Within the first category, we examine various end-effector structures, including pneumatic network structures, high aspect ratio slender elements and arrays, stimulus responsive materials with preset configuration programming, fabric constraints and textile forming, and tendon driven structures with configuration design. The second category focuses on systems where the continuum robot body directly engages in grasping, following a conceptual development overview, these systems are classified into basic bending and enveloping, variable cross section, elongating and coiling, specialized, and functionally augmented robots. This framework elucidates that entangling-style grasping is fundamentally governed by continuous contact, geometric enveloping, entanglement-induced interlocking, and stiffness modulation. Furthermore, the review explores the modeling and control strategies integral to these continuum systems. Finally, we identify persistent challenges regarding the modeling and regulation of wrapping deformation, the quantification of wrapping, the maintenance of stiffness, and the implementation of model and sensor closed-loop control. Collectively, this synthesis provides a structured foundation for advancing the engineering applicability of soft robots for entangling-style grasping.

title: ANN–GA based adaptive predictive energy management for renewable energy optimization in solar-diesel hybrid systems
summary: The intermittent nature of solar energy continues to constrain the effective utilization of photovoltaic (PV) systems in solar-diesel hybrid energy systems, particularly in tropical semi-arid regions where solar irradiance fluctuates consid
content: The intermittent nature of solar energy continues to constrain the effective utilization of photovoltaic (PV) systems in solar-diesel hybrid energy systems, particularly in tropical semi-arid regions where solar irradiance fluctuates considerably throughout the day. This study proposes a predictive energy management framework that integrates artificial neural network (ANN)-based irradiance forecasting with genetic algorithm (GA)-based optimization to support adaptive selection of energy sources between PV systems and diesel generators. Environmental data, including air temperature, relative humidity, and solar irradiance, were collected at the Badan Perakitan dan Modernisasi Pertanian (BRMP, Agricultural Assembly and Modernization Agency) experimental field in Naibonat, Kupang Regency, Indonesia. A multilayer perceptron ANN was developed to forecast short-term solar irradiance, and its predicted output was subsequently adopted as the fitness function for the GA to identify the optimal operating condition using an irradiance threshold of 300 W m−2. The ANN produced reliable short-term irradiance predictions, while the GA converged to a stable solution within approximately 15 generations, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed predictive energy management framework. The developed approach achieved a renewable energy utilization rate of 75.0%, reduced diesel fuel consumption by 52.8% compared with the conventional threshold-based strategy, and lowered carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 53%. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework transforms irradiance forecasting into adaptive operational decision-making, allowing energy source selection to anticipate future solar energy availability instead of relying solely on instantaneous irradiance measurements. Accordingly, the proposed framework offers a practical and scalable strategy for enhancing renewable energy utilization and reducing diesel dependency, and improving the sustainability of solar-diesel hybrid energy systems operating under highly variable tropical environmental conditions.

title: Extraction of critical metals from chrysotile asbestos tailings via an ammonium sulfate roasting-water leaching process
summary: , and magnesium sulfate, which were subsequently dissolved during water leaching. The results demonstrate that the proposed process achieves high simultaneous extraction efficiencies for multiple valuable metals while minimizing secondary p
content: , and magnesium sulfate, which were subsequently dissolved during water leaching. The results demonstrate that the proposed process achieves high simultaneous extraction efficiencies for multiple valuable metals while minimizing secondary pollution. This study provides a feasible and cleaner production route for the sustainable utilization of CATs.

title: Smart Monitoring and Energy Performance Optimization of Electrical Distribution Systems in Saudi Arabia
summary: Saudi Arabia’s electrical distribution networks are entering a period in which intelligent monitoring must inform operational energy efficiency rather than merely report equipment status. This review examines how feeder observability, data
content: Saudi Arabia’s electrical distribution networks are entering a period in which intelligent monitoring must inform operational energy efficiency rather than merely report equipment status. This review examines how feeder observability, data quality, voltage regulation, loss estimation and coordinated distributed resources can be integrated into a defensible performance framework. A structured thematic synthesis of peer reviewed research published between 2020 and 2025 differentiates demonstrated algorithmic capabilities from unverified claims about Saudi deployments. The analysis compares supervisory measurement, physics based optimization, predictive control and data-driven techniques against operational constraints including summer demand peaks, network heterogeneity, photovoltaic variability and communications reliability. It argues that credible savings require feeder-specific baselines, voltage-dependent load characterization and independent confirmation of delivered energy, not improvements in simulated objective functions alone. A staged monitoring to control architecture and an evaluation protocol are proposed for Saudi utilities. The contribution is a critical synthesis linking sensing decisions to measurable energy outcomes, while identifying transferability, cyber physical resilience and validation gaps that require field investigation.

title: Beyond the yuck factor: cognitive risk and affective pathways to recycled water receptivity
summary: Abstract This research aims to support sustainable water-resource management by investigating cognitive and affective perceptions of recycled water and their influence on public receptivity across multiple usage contexts. It analyzes how re
content: Abstract This research aims to support sustainable water-resource management by investigating cognitive and affective perceptions of recycled water and their influence on public receptivity across multiple usage contexts. It analyzes how regulatory availability and water quality affect receptivity for domestic, public, and supplementary uses. It also analyzes the mediating role of perceived performance and physical risks, which are moderated by affective reactions, with the “yuck factor” concept reflected in these negative emotional responses. To this end, a cross-sectional quantitative approach was adopted, drawing on responses gathered from a sample of 550 participants, with PROCESS macro techniques applied to analyze the data. Results indicate that perceived performance risk consistently mediates the associations between regulatory availability, water quality, and overall receptivity across all use categories. Partial mediation is observed in most cases, while full mediation is observed for public use with respect to water quality. Perceived physical risk also acts as a mediator, although its effects differ by context. Specifically, no mediation is observed for domestic use under regulatory availability, whereas partial and full mediation effects are present in other contexts. The results further demonstrate that affective reactions significantly moderate the relationships between regulatory availability and water quality and perceived performance risk, as well as between water quality and perceived physical risk. These moderating effects are most pronounced at low to moderate levels of negative emotional reactions and diminish at higher levels. Overall, the study underscores the essential roles of cognitive risk assessments and emotional responses in shaping public receptivity of recycled water, providing actionable insights for policymakers and practitioners seeking to support water reuse implementation and sustainable water-resource management.

title: Circular Design Frameworks and Tools for Energy-Using Components in the Automotive Industry: A Systematic Literature Review on Usability, Integration, and Sustainability Trade-Offs
summary: The transition toward a Circular Economy in the automotive industry demands robust eco-design strategies for complex, energy-using, mechatronic systems. This systematic literature review critically evaluates 30 publications representing 27
content: The transition toward a Circular Economy in the automotive industry demands robust eco-design strategies for complex, energy-using, mechatronic systems. This systematic literature review critically evaluates 30 publications representing 27 distinct frameworks and computational tools for active automotive components. Using a customized Usability Scorecard on a 1–5 quantitative scale, solutions were benchmarked across workflow integration, performance trade-offs, End-of-Life, and Critical Raw Material (CRM) management. Systematic review findings reveal significant methodological gaps: circa 52% of evaluated tools exhibit low CAD/PLM workflow integration relying on manual data entry, while only 30% achieve high integration. For trade-off analysis, most tools, about 80%, rely on static multi-criteria weighting or use offline optimization. Furthermore, CRM tracking is unaddressed in 44% of the tools, rising to circa 60% including purely conceptual methods, with only 22% offering dedicated metrics or Digital Product Passport (DPP) readiness for material traceability. Based on these review findings, future research should investigate and validate automated, open-source AI-driven plug-ins leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and Digital Twins embedded directly in engineering environments to translate Circular Economy principles and metrics into daily design practices.

title: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geome
content: Abstract Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.

title: A two-stage waveform-driven cross-differential protection scheme for PV-integrated parallel transmission lines
summary: The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation in modern power systems introduces significant challenges to the protection of parallel transmission lines, primarily due to limited and highly variable fault current characteristic
content: The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation in modern power systems introduces significant challenges to the protection of parallel transmission lines, primarily due to limited and highly variable fault current characteristics. Conventional cross-differential relay (CDR) schemes provide fast and selective protection for parallel transmission lines, but their reliance on current-magnitude comparison can limit their discrimination capability in PV-integrated systems. An enhanced CDR approach has addressed this limitation by incorporating remote-end voltage information to estimate the grid-voltage angle. However, this estimation relies on voltage measurement at the PV bus, the line impedance, and the equivalent grid impedance determined using voltage and current measurements at the grid bus. To address these measurement requirements, this paper proposes a two-stage waveform-driven cross-differential protection scheme for PV-integrated parallel transmission lines that relies solely on the currents of the parallel lines measured at the PV bus. In the first stage, internal fault detection is achieved using a normalized cross-correlation (NCC)-based fault detection index that captures waveform similarity between parallel line currents, thereby reducing the dependence on current amplitude under challenging operating conditions. In the second stage, faulty line identification is performed using the polarity of the fault-imposed positive-sequence current extracted via a delta filtering approach, enabling reliable direction-sensitive decision-making without requiring voltage measurements or communication links. The proposed method is extensively evaluated on a modified IEEE 39-bus system under diverse scenarios, including high-resistance faults, measurement noise, line parameter asymmetry, varying fault inception angles, PV generation intermittency, grid-code compliant reactive power support, and external faults. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves fast, robust, and accurate fault detection and identification across a wide range of operating conditions.

title: Fear of Feral Predators Alters Nutritional Responses in Desert Lizards
summary: ABSTRACT Human‐induced changes in predator densities affect various aspects of prey biology, yet their consequences for prey nutrition are rarely quantified. We investigated how feral dogs shape the nutritional ecology of the desert lizard
content: ABSTRACT Human‐induced changes in predator densities affect various aspects of prey biology, yet their consequences for prey nutrition are rarely quantified. We investigated how feral dogs shape the nutritional ecology of the desert lizard Saara hardwickii . In parts of the Thar desert, extremely high feral dog densities create hotspots of elevated predation risk for S. hardwickii . We combined focal observations of foraging behavior, stress physiology, and stoichiometry of diet and feces to assess nutritional responses of lizards to human‐mediated increase in predation risk. We found no difference in corticosterone levels, but lizards consumed less food and had lower glucose levels in high‐risk areas. Despite reduced carbon and nitrogen consumption, elemental composition of diet remained unchanged across habitats. However, fecal carbon and nitrogen percentages reduced under risk, indicating higher overall nutrient retention. We show that predation risk suppresses dietary intakes while enhancing nutrient conservation, revealing a key mechanism by which introduced feral predators can shape prey behavior, physiology, and nutrient flow in critical ecosystems.

title: A Master Curve for Magnetically Tuned Mechanical Hysteresis in Strain-Stiffening, Self-Healing Polysaccharide Hydrogels
summary: Abstract Precise control over the mechanical properties of biomimetic hydrogels is critical for applications in biomedicine, tissue engineering, and soft robotics. In this study, we present a strategy to finely tune the mechanical hysteresi
content: Abstract Precise control over the mechanical properties of biomimetic hydrogels is critical for applications in biomedicine, tissue engineering, and soft robotics. In this study, we present a strategy to finely tune the mechanical hysteresis of strain-stiffening, self-healing magnetic hydrogels by applying external uniaxial magnetic fields during gelation. The hydrogel network is formed via dynamic covalent imine bonds between chitosan and oxidized hyaluronic acid, while embedded iron microparticles generate anisotropic microstructures under steady magnetic fields, providing directional reinforcement. The mechanical response of the hydrogels is governed by two key parameters: the strain amplitude under oscillatory shear and the strength of the applied magnetic field. By combining magnetostatic finite element simulations with rheological experiments, we define a scaling variable that combines field and strain effects, enabling a master-curve representation. The magnetic hysteresis parameter, ranging from –78.8 to +147.6, quantitatively captures this tunable behavior across strain amplitudes up to 3000% and magnetic field strengths up to 354 kA·m–1. Such predictability allows for the rational design of hydrogels with tailored mechanical responses. Furthermore, short-term in vitro assays with human fibroblasts showed no detectable cytotoxic effects under the conditions tested, providing an initial indication of cytocompatibility and motivating further investigation of these materials for potential biomedical applications.

title: A Surface-Imprinted Fluorescent Sensor Exploiting CsPbBr3@ZIF-8 for Selective and Sensitive Detection of Dopamine
summary: Abstract Accurate detection of dopamine (DA), a vital catecholamine neurotransmitter, is crucial for evaluating neurological functions and diagnosing related disorders. To address the challenges posed by complex biological matrices and trac
content: Abstract Accurate detection of dopamine (DA), a vital catecholamine neurotransmitter, is crucial for evaluating neurological functions and diagnosing related disorders. To address the challenges posed by complex biological matrices and trace DA concentrations, a robust fluorescent sensor was constructed by integrating molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) with ZIF-8-encapsulated CsPbBr 3 perovskite quantum dots (CsPbBr 3 @ZIF-8@MIPs). In this rational design, the ZIF-8 shell serves as a protective barrier, effectively preventing CsPbBr 3 from degradation in polar solvents, while the surface-imprinted layer provides high-affinity and selective recognition sites for DA. The sensor exhibits a favorable linear response in the range of 5–400 nM, with an ultralow detection limit of 4.85 nM and a rapid response within 30s. When applied to clinical serum samples from Parkinson’s disease patients, the sensor achieved satisfactory recoveries ranging from 96.83% to 109.72%, showing high consistency with the results obtained by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). This work provides a reliable strategy for DA detection and demonstrates promising potential for biomedical sensing and clinical diagnosis.

title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
summary: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-
content: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-atom catalysts (SACs), in which isolated atoms lack extended coordination and are prone to oxidative instability. Here we design atomically dispersed Ru−O−Cr motifs that enable oxidation damping during acidic oxygen evolution. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows attenuated Ru oxidation synchronized with anticorrelated and partially reversible Cr redox evolution, consistent with proximity-dependent redox coupling. This buffered redox response is accompanied by bounded and partially reversible changes in the local metal−oxygen coordination environment. These coupled dynamics support proximity-coupled Ru−O−Cr redox units, enabling a 55.7-fold increased resistance against oxidation-induced Ru dissolution compared with conventional SACs. In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, catalysts incorporating proximal Ru−O−Cr configurations exhibit degradation rates that are 6.8-fold and 14.4-fold lower than those of Ru SACs and commercial RuO2, respectively, at 1 A cm−2. These results suggest proximal oxidation damping as a potential design principle for stabilizing atomically precise electrocatalysts. Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

title: Exploring On-Skin Interfaces as Interactive Intelligent Technologies for Health Diagnostics: Systematic Review of Current Practices and Future Directions
source: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems
summary: On-skin interfaces are emerging as intelligent, non-invasive technologies that enable continuous physiological monitoring and health diagnostics. This systematic review explores the current landscape, design practices, effectiveness, and et
content: On-skin interfaces are emerging as intelligent, non-invasive technologies that enable continuous physiological monitoring and health diagnostics. This systematic review explores the current landscape, design practices, effectiveness, and ethical implications of on-skin interfaces in healthcare. A total of 174 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 were identified across six major databases and analyzed to synthesize trends in sensor application, body placement, user interaction, and diagnostic focus. Findings reveal that most systems are concentrated on physical health (e.g., cardiac, respiratory, hydration), with limited but growing attention to mental and behavioral health contexts. Despite promising technical performance, the widespread clinical adoption of these technologies is hindered by challenges in real-world validation, signal robustness, long-term wearability, and a lack of personalized feedback, and only 21 studies (12.1%) evaluated the technology from the perspective of its users. Five core design recommendations emerged: enhancing clinical feasibility, ensuring user comfort, improving signal generalizability, incorporating intervention-driven interfaces, and embedding ethical safeguards. This review highlights a growing need for user-centered and ethically responsible design strategies that extend beyond monitoring to actionable interventions. The findings offer a roadmap for advancing on-skin interfaces into intelligent, interactive health companions capable of supporting both short- and long-term care. Bridging research innovations with clinical application will be essential to realizing the full potential of these technologies in personalized and preventive healthcare.

title: A Review of Image-Based and AI-Driven Water Level Monitoring: Methods, Datasets, and Deployment Considerations
summary: Abstract Accurate and continuous water-level monitoring is essential for agriculture, flood management, and water resources planning. However, many rivers and agricultural canals remain ungauged because conventional sensing infrastructure i
content: Abstract Accurate and continuous water-level monitoring is essential for agriculture, flood management, and water resources planning. However, many rivers and agricultural canals remain ungauged because conventional sensing infrastructure is costly to install and maintain, limiting basin-scale water accounting and conservation policies such as water banking and leasing. Computer vision enables water-level estimation from ground-based cameras, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and satellites, offering a low-cost, non-contact alternative to conventional sensors. This review synthesizes 93 studies selected from 168 articles retrieved from five databases, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We summarize contact-based and non-contact sensing methods and examine image-based approaches, including traditional image processing, classical machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL), alongside their imaging modalities and datasets. DL methods, particularly object detection, semantic segmentation, and transformer-based models, are more robust than earlier approaches under low light, reflections, and cluttered backgrounds, with several studies reporting field errors of approximately 1–3 cm. However, these results are not directly comparable because studies differ in datasets, reference measurements, and evaluation metrics. Three major research gaps emerge: (1) fragmented datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols; (2) limited cross-site validation and model generalization; and (3) insufficient long-term field evaluation and robustness to illumination changes, reflections, and camera displacement. Future research should prioritize standardized, publicly available multi-site datasets, common evaluation protocols, cross-site and seasonal testing, and adaptive models that maintain reliability under changing field conditions.

title: Dual urease-CA profiling, optimization, and CaCO 3 biomineralization by environmental bacteria
summary: Abstract Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) has mostly been studied through the ureolytic pathway, while carbonic anhydrase (CA)-assisted CO 2 hydration is typically examined separately. We screened 50 environmental
content: Abstract Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) has mostly been studied through the ureolytic pathway, while carbonic anhydrase (CA)-assisted CO 2 hydration is typically examined separately. We screened 50 environmental bacterial isolates to identify dual enzyme activity. Three high-activity isolates (MS1, LS1, and SED) underwent phenotypic, biochemical, enzymatic, mineralogical, and partial 16S rRNA analysis. MS1 and LS1 were identified as Lysinibacillus spp ., and SED as Bacillus sp . Growth and enzyme activities were evaluated across various environmental conditions. All 21 condition–response models showed significant effects of the tested variables. Optimal conditions were 35°C, pH 8, 2% NaCl, LB medium, ~ 4 mM KCl, and 2% inoculum. Under these, LS1 showed the highest urease activity (31.3 U/mL), SED showed the highest CA-associated esterase activity (4.1 U/mL). Urease-mediated CaCO 3 production was highest in LS1 (5.35 g/L) and MS1 (5.32 g/L); CA-associated CaCO 3 was highest in MS1 (1.19 g/L). CO 2 -hydration activity (WAU/mg) was greatest in SED (44.4), followed by LS1 (26.6) and MS1 (23.8). Zymography confirmed both enzyme activities, and genome annotation supported relevant gene presence (predicted β-class CA and UreC proteins). SED had the highest biofilm biomass but lowest mineral yield, suggesting no direct correlation among biofilm formation, enzyme activity, and mineral production. Microscopy, SEM–EDX, and XRD identified calcite, vaterite, and aragonite. While the isolates showed dual enzyme capability, synergy remains unconfirmed as the pathways were assessed independently.
