title: Temperature–Pressure–Time Dependent Microstructural Evolution of Caprock during CO2 Geological Storage: An Experimental Study Integrating CT Scanning and Pore Network Analysis
summary: Abstract The properties of the caprock critically influence the sealing performance of CO 2 geological storage systems. This study systematically investigates the microstructural evolution and stability of caprock under CO 2 exposure, using
content: Abstract The properties of the caprock critically influence the sealing performance of CO 2 geological storage systems. This study systematically investigates the microstructural evolution and stability of caprock under CO 2 exposure, using high-precision computed tomography scanning combined with a factorial experimental design that incorporated temperature and pressure, with a supplementary time-extension experiment. Rock samples from the Chang4+5 layer of the Ordos Basin were characterized in three dimensions before and after reaction. The results demonstrate that CO 2 storage increases porosity and permeability, generating “branch-like” or “root-like” dissolution networks that compromise rock integrity. Temperature elevation significantly accelerates mineral dissolution kinetics, promoting pore expansion and enhancing pore-throat connectivity. Increased pressure enhances CO 2 solubility and diffusivity in pore fluids, intensifying localized acidification and heterogeneous dissolution with a particular effect on throat-scale structural adjustments. Prolonged exposure drives the progressive advancement of the dissolution front and the gradual merging of isolated pores, facilitating the formation of continuous dissolution channels. These findings elucidate the coupled interaction mechanisms between CO 2 and caprock, providing both experimental evidence and theoretical support for site integrity assessment and long-term storage safety evaluation. This work provides direct support for site selection and the advancement of carbon dioxide capture, utilization, and storage technology.

title: Exploring institutional challenges to entrepreneurial development: Insights from Northern and Southern BSCIC Zones in Bangladesh
source: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
summary: Entrepreneurial development is essential for industrialization, employment generation, poverty reduction, and sustainable economic growth. Despite the institutional support provided by the BSCIC, entrepreneurs continue to face significant b
content: Entrepreneurial development is essential for industrialization, employment generation, poverty reduction, and sustainable economic growth. Despite the institutional support provided by the BSCIC, entrepreneurs continue to face significant barriers to business establishment, operation, and expansion. This study explores the institutional challenges affecting entrepreneurial development in the Northern and Southern BSCIC Zones of Bangladesh. A qualitative research approach was employed, using purposive sampling to collect data through 55 IDIs, 13 KIIs, and six FGDs, involving 74 participants across ten districts. Data were analyzed thematically to identify recurring challenges and contextual differences. The findings reveal six major themes: misalignment of services, bureaucratic delays, credit access challenges, lack of regional focus, weak monitoring systems, and unawareness of entrepreneurs. Inadequate financial assistance, restrictive collateral requirements, administrative complexities, insufficient infrastructure, weak institutional coordination, limited market access, and inadequate entrepreneurial capabilities emerged as critical barriers. The findings also highlight the need for region-specific interventions, transparent administrative procedures, improved infrastructure, accessible financing, stronger monitoring mechanisms, and demand-oriented entrepreneurial training. The study contributes contextual insights into institutional barriers affecting entrepreneurial development within BSCIC industrial estates and among entrepreneurs operating outside them. The cross-sectional design, purposive sampling, and geographically bounded study limit statistical generalizability and may not capture all the experiences of entrepreneurs and other stakeholders across Bangladesh. It recommends coordinated policy interventions and enhanced institutional responsiveness to promote inclusive industrialization, employment generation, and balanced regional development in Bangladesh.

title: Graph-theoretic modeling of thermal cycles for immersive art exhibition and sustainable museum design
source: AKCE International Journal of Graphs and Combinatorics
summary: This paper analyzes the shortcomings of the current museum in thermal energy management and exhibition design, establishes the research objectives, and introduces the basic theory of virtual reality technology, including the panorama image
content: This paper analyzes the shortcomings of the current museum in thermal energy management and exhibition design, establishes the research objectives, and introduces the basic theory of virtual reality technology, including the panorama image generation process, image acquisition and processing algorithm. These technologies provide strong support for the design of thermal energy circulation and immersive art exhibitions. In terms of system design, this paper proposes an immersive art exhibition interactive system based on virtual reality, which covers user demand analysis, module construction, real-time interactive perception module design and exhibition image registration and storage. Through experimental verification, the human-computer interaction performance of the system has been significantly improved, the success rate of interactive tasks has been improved, and users have a warm response to the application effect of virtual exhibition.

title: Acetyl-CoA synthetase 2: metabolic-epigenetic regulation, tumor immunity, and therapeutic opportunities in cancer
summary: Acetate is an important carbon source linking tumor metabolic adaptation to acylation-dependent regulation. Under hypoxia, nutrient limitation, and therapeutic stress, acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2)-mediated conversion of acetate to acetyl
content: Acetate is an important carbon source linking tumor metabolic adaptation to acylation-dependent regulation. Under hypoxia, nutrient limitation, and therapeutic stress, acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2)-mediated conversion of acetate to acetyl-CoA can support cytoplasmic anabolic metabolism while also contributing to local nuclear acetyl-CoA production and acylation-dependent transcriptional regulation. ACSS2-dependent acetate metabolism has further been implicated in autophagy-lysosome regulation, tumor-cell immune evasion, immune-cell metabolic adaptation, ferroptosis, and treatment tolerance. However, these functions are jointly shaped by tissue of origin, acetate availability, subcellular localization, post-translational modifications, driver alterations, and compensatory metabolic pathways, precluding a simple classification of ACSS2 as a uniformly tumor-promoting factor across cancer types. Here, we synthesize mechanistic evidence linking ACSS2 to hypoxic adaptation, epigenetic regulation, autophagy, tumor immunity, ferroptosis, and therapeutic adaptation, highlighting its context-dependent roles across tumor types and reviewing advances in the development of ACSS2 inhibitors. The immunological consequences of ACSS2 activity may differ between tumor cells and effector T cells under metabolic stress, complicating predictions about the immunological effects of systemic ACSS2 inhibition. Current evidence supports ACSS2 as a context-dependent metabolic vulnerability that may be actionable in biomarker-defined tumor states rather than as a universal therapeutic target. Clinical translation will require the identification of acetate-dependent tumor subsets, the development of biomarkers integrating ACSS2 localization with metabolic state, and rigorous evaluation of compensatory mechanisms, long-term safety, and rational combination-treatment windows.

title: Urbanization restructures wetland nitrogen cycling via soil properties and microbial functional communities
summary: Urban expansion, characterized by growing impervious surface area, severely disrupts wetland ecosystem functions and nutrient cycling processes. However, a holistic understanding of how urbanization affects wetland soil nitrogen cycling and
content: Urban expansion, characterized by growing impervious surface area, severely disrupts wetland ecosystem functions and nutrient cycling processes. However, a holistic understanding of how urbanization affects wetland soil nitrogen cycling and the associated functional microorganisms remains unclear. In this study, the key soil nitrogen cycling processes and their associated core microbial functional genes across 22 wetlands were investigated along a rural–suburban–urban gradient. Results showed that soil total nitrogen and ammonium content in urban sites were significantly lower than those in rural sites. Although microbial alpha diversity did not change significantly, the E/O ratio (the abundance ratio of eutrophic to oligotrophic phyla) decreased sharply along the urbanization gradient. Metagenomic analysis revealed a systematic functional restructuring: urban wetlands exhibited upregulated genetic potential for nitrate scavenging and conservation (assimilatory and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium—ANRA/DNRA— and nitrate transport) but downregulated pathways for nitrogen acquisition (fixation) and organic matter processing. This shift indicates a microbial adaptation to nitrogen limitation in urban wetlands, where enhanced DNRA and ANRA pathways compete with nitrification and denitrification, crucially regulating nitrogen transformation rates. The study identifies soil organic carbon, pH, bulk density, and the interaction between key microbial taxa and nitrogen cycle gene groups as the primary factors controlling wetland soil nitrogen status under urban pressure. We conclude that urbanization threatens wetland nutrient functions not merely by habitat loss, but by inducing a functional microbial shift. These findings underscore the need for urban planning strategies that mitigate soil property changes to preserve the microbial basis of wetland ecosystem services.

title: Make Do or Renew? How Market Turbulence Reshapes the Sources of Competitive Advantage in Pakistan's Textile Industry
source: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
summary: The exporters of textiles from Pakistan have to compete on value as they have to deal with record energy costs, new tariff barriers, and fluctuating demand from buyers. This study is about what resource-deployment practices (innovation, kno
content: The exporters of textiles from Pakistan have to compete on value as they have to deal with record energy costs, new tariff barriers, and fluctuating demand from buyers. This study is about what resource-deployment practices (innovation, knowledge management and entrepreneurial bricolage) generate a competitive advantage for these firms. It also poses the question of how two factors affect those effects: absorptive capacity (internal) and market turbulence (external). The model is an integration of the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities perspective and contingency theory. A total of 113 bed-linen and upholstery manufacturers' owners and senior managers responded to the survey. Systematic random sampling was used to select the firms from a population of 362 members of the association. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and 5000 bootstrap subsamples were used to test the hypotheses. Entrepreneurial bricolage had the most significant impact on competitive advantage (β = 0.338, p = .001), with innovation being the second most significant impact (β = 0.172, p = .038). There was no significant direct effect of the knowledge management. Absorptive capacity did not moderate any of the three relationships. Market turbulence took a dual impact on the market. It increased the innovation–advantage relationship (β = 0.212, p = .047) and significantly reduced the bricolage–advantage relationship (β = −0.434, p = .006). The model accounted for 65.1% of the variance in competitive advantage. The contribution of the interaction terms was 6.7 percentage points (f² = 0.19). The study illustrates how bricolage and innovation are not synonymous strategies for gaining an edge. Bricolage is better suited to stable markets and innovation is better suited to markets that churn. This boundary condition will help clarify resource arguments such as "making do" with resources on hand. It also provides a guideline to textile exporters as to when to be resourceful and when to invest in renewal.

title: Atomically Dispersed In 3+ Anchored on Rigid MOF‐808 for Highly Selective CO 2 Electroreduction with Long‐Term Stability in Acidic Media
summary: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction offers a promising pathway for carbon utilization but is severely hindered by the aggressive hydrogen evolution reaction and the structural instability of main‐group metal catalysts
content: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction offers a promising pathway for carbon utilization but is severely hindered by the aggressive hydrogen evolution reaction and the structural instability of main‐group metal catalysts in strong acidic solution. Herein, we report the precise anchoring of atomically dispersed In 3+ onto the inorganic nodes of MOF‐808, achieving an extraordinarily high loading of 21.8 wt%. The rigid framework of MOF‐808 has abundant open metal sites that securely coordinate with In 3+ , while its well‐defined 1.8 nm pores ensure rapid mass transport during electrocatalysis. Mechanistic studies reveal that intense electronic coupling of In 3+ with the Zr 6 ‐oxo clusters efficiently improves the local electronic structure of the isolated In 3+ sites. Consequently, the high In 3+ density delivers exceptional performance for selective CO 2 reduction to formic acid in acidic electrolyte, achieving an outstanding Faradaic efficiency of 97.1% at −1.2 V vs. RHE. More importantly, the robust spatial confinement for the anchored In 3+ within the framework efficiently prevents their chemical leaching and reductive migration, enabling an outstanding long‐term stability of 216 h. This study demonstrates an effective strategy for constructing highly stable and atomically dispersed In 3+ catalysts for electrochemical applications in acidic media.

title: Probabilistic energy management of renewable-based charging stations hub for urban electric public transportation fleets
summary: Urban public transport electrification increasingly couples charging demand with variable renewable supply, creating operating conditions that deterministic station scheduling does not represent well. This work addresses that limitation thr
content: Urban public transport electrification increasingly couples charging demand with variable renewable supply, creating operating conditions that deterministic station scheduling does not represent well. This work addresses that limitation through a probabilistic energy-management framework for a grid-connected charging station supplied by photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation. Solar irradiance and wind speed were represented by Beta and Weibull distributions, while fleet-side uncertainty was modeled through the initial state of charge and price-responsive charging or discharging behavior. Monte Carlo simulation generated stochastic realizations, and the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) determined 24-hour grid exchange and fleet power decisions subject to power-balance and operating constraints. The same scheduling problem was solved under deterministic and uncertainty-aware scenarios and benchmarked against four metaheuristic methods. Uncertainty raised the COA operating cost from 190.97 USD to 197.84 USD, indicating the economic effect of simultaneous supply- and demand-side variability. Even so, COA retained the lowest cost among the tested methods; under uncertainty, its cost was 15.70% below that obtained by particle swarm optimization. The stochastic results also preserved hourly power balance while capturing changes in renewable output and bidirectional fleet demand. The framework therefore provides a tractable basis for uncertainty-aware scheduling of renewable-supported public-transport charging stations and for assessing optimizer behavior under coupled generation and charging variability.

title: Integrating BIM and material passports to foster circularity in offsite construction: a five-layer digital framework
source: International Journal of Building Pathology and Adaptation
summary: Purpose Circular economy (CE) integration in offsite construction (OSC) is increasingly recognised as a pathway to reduce waste, carbon emissions and inefficient material practices. However, the digital mechanisms required to operationalise
content: Purpose Circular economy (CE) integration in offsite construction (OSC) is increasingly recognised as a pathway to reduce waste, carbon emissions and inefficient material practices. However, the digital mechanisms required to operationalise circularity across design, construction and reuse phases in OSC remain fragmented and underdeveloped. Design/methodology/approach This study develops a five-layer digital integration framework that aligns building information modelling (BIM) with material passports (MPs) to support circular workflows. Drawing on a systematic literature review (SLR) of 40 peer-reviewed studies, the framework comprises: (1) Data Input Layer, (2) BIM Platform Layer, (3) Integration Layer, (4) Lifecycle Feedback Layer and (5) Circular Decision Support Layer. Findings The synthesis layer identifies key digital bottlenecks across the five layers, including missing CE metadata, poor interoperability and a lack of lifecycle feedback loops. By embedding circular material intelligence within BIM environments, the framework offers a scalable roadmap for traceability, reuse planning and CE-driven decision-making in OSC. Practical implications The framework provides industry stakeholders with a scalable roadmap to enable material traceability, reuse planning and circular decision-making across the OSC lifecycle. It supports practical alignment with emerging CE policies and market incentives. Originality/value This study contributes a theoretically grounded framework and practical recommendations for advancing digital circular construction. It lays the groundwork for future digital tool development and policy alignment to supports CE adoption in the built environment.

title: A Multielectron Macromolecular Ruthenium–Bipyridine Electrolyte for Redox Flow Batteries
summary: Abstract Renewable power sources offer a compelling path to decarbonized electricity generation, but their inherent intermittency often mismatches real-world demand. Efficient, scalable energy storage is therefore essential to capture surpl
content: Abstract Renewable power sources offer a compelling path to decarbonized electricity generation, but their inherent intermittency often mismatches real-world demand. Efficient, scalable energy storage is therefore essential to capture surplus generation and deliver power on demand. Redox flow batteries (RFBs) are particularly attractive for grid applications, yet their practical energy density is frequently limited by the narrow electrochemical stability window of aqueous electrolytes and by predominantly one-electron redox chemistries. Here we report the synthesis and electrochemical characterization of a macromolecular ruthenium complex soluble in organic solvents that undergoes a reversible three-electron redox process. Cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic charge–discharge measurements confirm multielectron accessibility and stable cycling behavior. Notably, the complex retains electrochemical performance over 100 charge–discharge cycles, highlighting the promise of multielectron, macromolecular redox couples in organic electrolytes as a strategy to increase RFB energy density.

title: Reproducible Laser-Induced Graphene Electrodes for Electrochemical Conductivity Sensing Enabled by Full Factorial Design of Experiments
summary: Abstract Laser-induced graphene (LIG) enables scalable fabrication of conductive carbon electrodes directly on polymer substrates, but variations in laser-processing conditions can affect electrode properties and sensing reliability. In thi
content: Abstract Laser-induced graphene (LIG) enables scalable fabrication of conductive carbon electrodes directly on polymer substrates, but variations in laser-processing conditions can affect electrode properties and sensing reliability. In this work, a full factorial design of experiments was used to investigate how laser power, scan speed, focus offset, and scan cycle number influence LIG fabrication and quantitative aqueous conductivity sensing. Sheet resistance was used to identify under-exposed, optimized, and over-exposed processing regimes. Representative conditions were further characterized using surface and quasi-cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, dynamic water contact-angle measurements, and cyclic voltammetry. Optimized conditions produced continuous porous LIG layers approximately 25–27 µm thick, with lower sheet resistance, more uniform graphitic structure, larger apparent electroactive surface area, and more defined ferri/ferrocyanide redox responses. Dynamic contact-angle measurements also revealed processing-dependent wetting behavior. Optimized and non-optimized electrodes were then compared as functionalization-free conductivity sensors using broadband electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and equivalent-circuit fitting to isolate bulk solution resistance. Over 13.33–3740 µS cm⁻¹, the optimized electrode produced a log–log resistance–conductivity slope of −0.944, approaching the theoretical inverse relationship, with measurement-to-measurement and sensor-to-sensor relative standard deviations of 1.79% and 3.00%, respectively. These results establish a fabrication–structure–impedance–conductivity relationship for reproducible LIG-based conductivity sensing in aqueous environmental monitoring applications.

title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters
summary: Sustainable uranium supply is critical for nuclear energy, yet its practical recovery is severely hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium in natural waters. In dynamic aqueous environments, uranium continuously shifts between large,
content: Sustainable uranium supply is critical for nuclear energy, yet its practical recovery is severely hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium in natural waters. In dynamic aqueous environments, uranium continuously shifts between large, cationic hydrolyzed clusters (acidic/neutral) and compact, anionic carbonate complexes (alkaline). Conventional static adsorbents fail to accommodate these contrasting charges and geometries. Here, we report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework (COF), TAM-DTDA-AMM, to overcome this speciation barrier. Featuring a three-fold interpenetrated dia topology, the functional COF enables environment-driven reversible −COO−···NH4+ ion-pair reconfiguration, coupling adaptive pore-surface chemistry with dynamic spatial confinement. Under alkaline environments, cationic microdomains stabilize [UO2(CO3)3]4− via electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions, whereas under near-neutral to acidic conditions, protonated carboxyl groups directly coordinate hydrolyzed uranyl clusters. This dual-adaptive mechanism enables rapid, selective, and high-capacity uranium extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries and offers a general strategy for recognizing multiple metal species in complex environments. Uranium recovery is hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium ions in natural waters. Here the authors report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework which enables rapid and selective uranium-extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries.

title: Genome-scale mathematical model of cannabis glandular trichome metabolism and identification of a missing link in terpenoid biosynthesis
summary: Introduction Cannabis ( Cannabis sativa L.) glandular trichomes (GTs) are specialized structures on female inflorescences that serve as the primary sites for the biosynthesis and storage of metabolites responsible for potency and aroma, inc
content: Introduction Cannabis ( Cannabis sativa L.) glandular trichomes (GTs) are specialized structures on female inflorescences that serve as the primary sites for the biosynthesis and storage of metabolites responsible for potency and aroma, including cannabinoids, terpenoids, flavonoids, stilbenoids, phenolic amides, and volatile compounds. Despite substantial advances in cannabis biochemistry, uncertainties remain regarding key metabolic processes, including the biosynthetic origin of hexanoyl-CoA, the precursor supplying the cannabinoid side chain, and the formation of certain terpenoids such as 1,8-cineole. To address these knowledge gaps, we developed a genome-scale metabolic framework for cannabis GT metabolism. Methods An extensive literature review was used to reconstruct a cannabis GT metabolic network comprising approximately 772 metabolic and transport reactions. Comprehensive metabolite datasets encompassing cannabinoids, terpenoids, flavonoids, stilbenoids, phenolic amides, and non-terpenoid volatiles were integrated to parameterize the biomass objective function of the genome-scale metabolic model, CanSatGT_2025. Flux balance analysis was employed to evaluate competing hypotheses for hexanoyl-CoA biosynthesis, including: (i) early termination of fatty acid elongation, (ii) production through the oxylipin pathway following lipid degradation, and (iii) incomplete fatty acid β-oxidation. In addition, the hypothesis that ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RubisCO) is nonfunctional in non-photosynthetic GTs was assessed. To investigate the biosynthesis of 1,8-cineole, sequence and structural homology analyses were performed to identify candidate terpene synthases, followed by heterologous expression and biochemical characterization of selected enzymes. Results The reconstructed network enabled the development of the genome-scale model CanSatGT_2025 and its application to metabolic flux analysis across multiple cannabis cultivars. Flux balance analysis identified the most parsimonious solution as a combination of acyl-lipid thioesterase activity and a nonfunctional RubisCO. This configuration minimized total metabolic flux, ATP demand, and carbon dioxide loss while supporting GT metabolism. The analyses also revealed a gap in current knowledge of cannabis monoterpene biosynthesis. Although 1,8-cineole was detected in several cultivars, the enzyme responsible for its formation had not previously been identified. Subsequent sequence, structural, and biochemical studies led to the identification and validation of a terpene synthase that produces 1,8-cineole as its primary product. Discussion Our findings support acyl-lipid thioesterase-mediated hexanoyl-CoA production and the absence of functional RubisCO activity as the most metabolically efficient explanation for cannabinoid precursor biosynthesis in cannabis GTs. Furthermore, the discovery of a 1,8-cineole synthase resolves a previously unidentified step in cannabis monoterpene metab

title: Coupled MHD and heat generation effects on magnetite–blood nanofluid in a stenosed artery
summary: nanoparticles to enhance magnetic intensity and thermal diffusion, which are applicable to targeted drug delivery and hyperthermia based medical treatment. An incompressible, two-dimensional, laminar model is governed by the consideration o
content: nanoparticles to enhance magnetic intensity and thermal diffusion, which are applicable to targeted drug delivery and hyperthermia based medical treatment. An incompressible, two-dimensional, laminar model is governed by the consideration of Magnetic force, heat generation effects, and the symmetrical characteristics of the arterial stenosis. The non-linear equations of momentum and energy were computed with boundary layer restrictions and then solved computationally in MATLAB software. Key variables, including the magnetic field strength, the volume fraction for nanoparticles, the altitude of the stenosis, the coefficient of heat production, and the Prandtl number were systematically analyzed and the effects of these variables on the axial flow rate, wall shear stress, thermal distribution and Nusselt number were examined. The results show that magnetic field significantly decreases the value of the axial velocity and the heat transfer rate, and increases the concentration of magnetite nanoparticles, which increases thermal transport. The Nusselt number increases by 104.95% as the Prandtl number increases, while it decreases by 35.87% as the parameter of the heat source increases, making it clear that thermal parameters have a high impact on the blood flow in the arteries with a stenosis. The results might prove helpful for the control of drugs by magnetism, targeted drug delivery using nanoparticles, thermal control in bio-medical systems and control of blood flow in stenosed arteries.

title: AgriTech: Foundations, Emerging Technologies, System Architectures, and Deployment Readiness—A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Agricultural technology (AgriTech) is transforming agricultural production through advances in artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, robotics, remote sensing, digital twins, and intelligent decision-support systems. Despite these dev
content: Agricultural technology (AgriTech) is transforming agricultural production through advances in artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, robotics, remote sensing, digital twins, and intelligent decision-support systems. Despite these developments, the transition from technological innovation to effective agricultural deployment remains constrained by technical, operational, economic, and institutional challenges. Existing research frequently emphasizes individual technologies, applications, or performance indicators, providing limited integration of system architectures, operational reliability, affordability, interoperability, and deployment readiness. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of AgriTech foundations, enabling technologies, architectural approaches, agricultural applications, and performance evaluation methods. It examines centralized, distributed, cloud, edge, and hybrid architectures alongside intelligent agricultural systems and autonomous technologies. A comparative analysis identifies their capabilities, limitations, infrastructure requirements, and operational trade-offs. The survey further investigates agricultural data quality, environmental variability, cybersecurity, maintenance, financial sustainability, digital inclusion, and governance challenges affecting practical implementation. Building on this synthesis, the paper proposes the Integrated AgriTech Effectiveness and Deployment Readiness Framework (IAEDRF), which connects agricultural requirements, technology selection, system integration, performance validation, economic feasibility, organizational preparedness, and responsible governance. The framework introduces context-dependent assessment criteria, mandatory deployment requirements, and continuous operational reassessment. Its proposed suitability model remains conceptual and requires empirical validation. Finally, the survey identifies research priorities involving generalizable agricultural AI, interoperable infrastructures, affordable technologies, real-world benchmarking, and sustainable scaling. The findings emphasize that AgriTech effectiveness depends not only on technological capability but also on reliable, affordable, interoperable, and context-appropriate deployment. The survey provides an integrated foundation for future research, technology development, and evidence-based agricultural implementation.

title: The electron impedance spectroscopic study of Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-Poly (sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) modified with organic (RGO) and inorganic (TiO2) compounds
summary: Cross-formalism electrochemical impedance spectroscopy is used to establish quantitative structure–property correlations in chemical-oxidatively synthesized Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) PEDOT-PSS, PEDOT-PSS/TiO₂
content: Cross-formalism electrochemical impedance spectroscopy is used to establish quantitative structure–property correlations in chemical-oxidatively synthesized Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) PEDOT-PSS, PEDOT-PSS/TiO₂ (PPT) and PEDOT-PSS/ Reduced Graphene Oxide (PPR) binary nanocomposites screen-printed on cellulose paper. Multi-start nonlinear least-squares fitting of raw impedance data over 4 Hz – 5 MHz identifies a single Rₛ–(R b ∥CPE) circuit for all five compositions (R² > 0.87) with weighted chi-squared values χ² ranging from 2.1 × 10⁻³ to 8.7 × 10⁻³ (all below the 0.01 acceptance threshold) confirming the goodness of fit and yields Jonscher exponents s = 0.80–0.93 (all < 1, confirming hopping conduction across the series). Three quantitative correlations link the XRD-derived structural parameters to the dielectric response. Larger crystallite size T and lower dislocation density δ increase σ dc by one order of magnitude between pristine PEDOT-PSS (T = 0.92 nm) and PPT 20% (T = 15.65 nm); effective capacitance C eff scales with percent crystallinity within the TiO₂ series (127 pF at 58.5%, 18.3 pF at 44.0%); and the CPE exponent n tracks RGO platelet aggregation, dropping from 0.93 at 1.09 nm crystallite size (PPR 20%) to 0.81 at 2.13 nm (PPR 30%). Admittance and electric-modulus spectra confirm a single bulk relaxation (τ Z / τ M = 0.5–6.5) and give a high-frequency permittivity ε ∞ of 5.32 for PPT 20% , consistent with the high electronic polarisability of the anatase (101) lattice imaged by HR-TEM (d = 0.353 nm). The dielectric response of PPT 20% is dominated by Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization at the polymer–anatase interface, while PPR 20% approaches ideal Debye relaxation. The 20 wt% loading is the percolation–aggregation optimum for both filler systems, delivering two device-grade compositions tailored, respectively, for interfacial-polarisation transducers and low-distortion broadband capacitors.

title: Oncolytic viruses in combination cancer therapy: clinical lessons, biomarker-guided strategies, and future treatment directions
summary: Oncolytic viruses (OVs) preferentially infect and replicate within tumors, induce immunogenic cell death, and remodel immune-poor microenvironments to support T-cell infiltration. These features provide a rationale for combining OVs with im
content: Oncolytic viruses (OVs) preferentially infect and replicate within tumors, induce immunogenic cell death, and remodel immune-poor microenvironments to support T-cell infiltration. These features provide a rationale for combining OVs with immune checkpoint blockade, adoptive cellular therapies, bispecific T-cell engagers, cancer vaccines, and innate immune agonists, and for engineering viruses to express immunostimulatory cytokines. Clinical outcomes, however, have been inconsistent. In MASTERKEY-265, adding intratumoral talimogene laherparepvec to pembrolizumab did not significantly improve progression-free or overall survival in advanced melanoma, despite a 62% objective response rate in the preceding 21-patient phase Ib cohort and evidence of increased intratumoral CD8+ T cells and PD-L1 expression. In contrast, single-arm clinical data for RP1 plus nivolumab in anti-PD-1-refractory melanoma showed objective responses, including durable responses in a subset; the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval for the regimen, but randomized confirmation remains required. Together with the failure of PHOCUS, these findings indicate that benefit is determined by viral platform, tumor immune state, disease and prior-treatment setting, delivery feasibility, and resistance biology rather than immune activation alone. We critically synthesize positive and negative evidence across checkpoint and non-checkpoint strategies and distinguish biomarkers derived from OV studies from those extrapolated from checkpoint-inhibitor trials. Candidate biomarkers and pharmacodynamic readouts are organized into a three-tier research framework covering pretreatment characterization, platform–partner hypotheses, and on-treatment monitoring; their utility for selecting OV-based combinations still requires validation. We further examine delivery barriers, antiviral immunity, tumor heterogeneity and resistance, next-generation vector engineering, and computational approaches to molecularly guided patient selection. Prospective validation in biomarker-stratified, adaptive trials is needed to improve patient selection, match viral platforms with rational partners, and translate biological activity into durable clinical benefit.

title: Reactive power regulation of power system using an SVC with fixed, optimized, and CNN-based PI controllers
source: Multiscale and Multidisciplinary Modeling Experiments and Design
summary: Abstract Fluctuating wind generation and rapid load variations in an isolated Wind-Diesel Hybrid Power System (WDHPS) cause oscillations in generator reactive power and bus voltage, thereby affecting the stability and reliability of the sys
content: Abstract Fluctuating wind generation and rapid load variations in an isolated Wind-Diesel Hybrid Power System (WDHPS) cause oscillations in generator reactive power and bus voltage, thereby affecting the stability and reliability of the system. The present work proposes a hybrid optimization-learning control framework for WDHPS employing a Static Var Compensator (SVC) where a PI controller is used for generating the SVC control signal. The three different controllers are Fixed PI, Enhanced Snake Optimization (ESO)-PI, and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-PI, thereby determining the effectiveness of SVC reactive power regulation and voltage stability enhancement. First, the ESO algorithm is implemented for obtaining the optimal PI gains offline initially by minimizing the performance index Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE). The gains from ESO, along with the deviations in terminal voltage, synchronous generator reactive power, induction generator reactive power, and SVC reactive power are then used in training CNN for learning the non-linear mapping between optimal controller gains and system dynamics. This work combines metaheuristic-based offline optimization (ESO) with data-driven gain prediction (CNN) and maintains an identical PI controller structure for fair performance comparison. The ESO-PI achieves the fastest settling time (≈0.010 s) of voltage deviation and minimum ITAE. A near-optimal performance is shown by the CNN-PI controller with a settling time (≈0.013 s). Under an additional unseen operating condition, CNN-PI demonstrates faster settling than freshly re-optimized ESO-PI, and confirms genuine generalization beyond the training dataset rather than mere reproduction of ESO-tuned gains. The robustness is further validated under a substantially larger (5%) disturbance magnitude, where ESO-PI and CNN-PI consistently outperform Fixed-PI. These results demonstrate that the CNN has learned a generalizable gain-mapping behaviour rather than merely reproducing ESO’s condition-specific optimum, underscoring the practical value of an adaptive/predictive tuning approach for varying operating conditions.

title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I2 batteries
summary: Abstract Four-electron iodine redox chemistry offers a high theoretical specific energy of ~1324 Wh kgI −1 , yet its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the conflicting demands of rapid I 0 /I + oxidation, effective suppressio
content: Abstract Four-electron iodine redox chemistry offers a high theoretical specific energy of ~1324 Wh kgI −1 , yet its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the conflicting demands of rapid I 0 /I + oxidation, effective suppression of iodine shuttling, and stabilization of highly reactive I + species. Here we report a redox-active, Lewis acid/base-tunable phthalimide that resolves these constraints through a single-molecule polarity-switching mechanism. Upon electrochemical oxidation, electrophilic phthalimide δ+ strongly interacts with nucleophilic iodine and polyiodide species, concurrently suppressing polyiodide shuttling and promoting their conversion to I + . The consecutively generated phthalimide δ− acts as a nucleophilic stabilizer for the resulting I + species. This electrochemically driven polarity switching of phthalimide enables flexible four-electron Li-I 2 pouch cells that deliver ~400 mAh gI −1 capacity, a specific energy exceeding 1200 Wh kgI −1 , a high cathode-level specific energy ( ~ 883.4 Wh kg(cathode) −1 ), and stable cycling over 1000 cycles. The successful integration of these cells into wearable wireless charging and motion-sensing systems demonstrates the potential of polarity-switchable iodine chemistry for next-generation flexible energy-storage devices.

title: Hidden biodiversity threats from fixed capital depreciation and regional inequality in China: Implications for conservation solutions
summary: The continuous resource consumption and ecological externalities associated with the depreciation of China’s fixed assets pose systematic, yet often invisible, threats to biodiversity. This study constructs China’s yearly consecutive multi-
content: The continuous resource consumption and ecological externalities associated with the depreciation of China’s fixed assets pose systematic, yet often invisible, threats to biodiversity. This study constructs China’s yearly consecutive multi-regional input-output tables and a refined fixed capital investment database from 2000 to 2020, to support the spatial mismatch analysis between biodiversity responsibility and economic returns driven by capital depreciation. A structural decoupling, reflected in a Gini coefficient of 0.47, is observed as the ecological burdens are concentrated in southwestern resource-exporting provinces but eastern developed provinces capture value added through ecological outsourcing, and the use of assets in the transportation and real estate industries is the main factor causing the relocation of biodiversity risk areas. Strengthening budget management for fixed asset investment projects and extending the life of construction-related fixed assets can help reduce the biodiversity footprint, but have limited effects on reducing the inequality between provincial biodiversity loss and economic gains. This study underscores the urgent need to incorporate biodiversity metrics into fixed asset management and integrate regional policies to balance capital efficiency with ecological equity.

title: TOWARD INTUITIVE CONTROL OF ANKLE-FOOT PROSTHESES: A HIGH-LEVEL FRAMEWORK FOR INTELLIGENT AND ADAPTIVE LOCOMOTION OVER COMPLIANT TERRAINS
source: Library, Museums and Press - UDSpace (University of Delaware)
summary: The ability to walk safely and efficiently across dynamic and compliant terrains remains a fundamental challenge for individuals with lower-limb amputation. Despite significant advances in powered prosthetic technology, most existing contro
content: The ability to walk safely and efficiently across dynamic and compliant terrains remains a fundamental challenge for individuals with lower-limb amputation. Despite significant advances in powered prosthetic technology, most existing control strategies are designed around structured environments and predefined behaviors, limiting their ability to adapt to the variability and uncertainty of real-world conditions. This dissertation explores a paradigm for prosthetic control that is grounded in the principles of human locomotion and seeks to integrate both predictive and feedback-driven mechanisms to enable more natural and intuitive interaction with the environment. This work specifically investigates how information from the human user and the environment can be jointly leveraged to improve prosthetic adaptation. By studying anticipatory neuromechanical behavior, this dissertation demonstrates that humans anticipate upcoming terrain changes prior to physical interaction, and that this information can be decoded to inform control decisions. Complementing this, this work also shows that direct interaction with the environment provides rich feedback that can be used to rapidly infer terrain properties and refine prosthetic behavior in real time. Together, these perspectives motivate a unified high-level framework in which anticipation and reaction are treated as complementary components of a continuous control strategy. Beyond methodological contributions, this dissertation also addresses a critical gap in the field by providing a systematic study of locomotion over compliant terrains in an effort to contribute to a deeper understanding of human adaptation in complex environments. The results presented in this work highlight the potential of human-centered, adaptive control strategies. While significant challenges remain in translating these approaches to clinical and real-world settings, this dissertation outlines a path forward toward prosthetic systems that are not only functional, but intuitive, responsive, and aligned with the natural dynamics of human movement

title: SiC nanoparticles, graphene oxide and magnesium matrix composites: Recent advances in corrosion resistance and biomedical applications
summary: Magnesium alloys are highly attractive for lightweight and biomedical applications. However, they suffer from poor corrosion resistance and limited durability in physiological environments. Existing reviews typically focus on surface coatin
content: Magnesium alloys are highly attractive for lightweight and biomedical applications. However, they suffer from poor corrosion resistance and limited durability in physiological environments. Existing reviews typically focus on surface coatings including polymer-derived ceramic nanocomposites or internal reinforcements as separate topics. There is a lack of integrated discussions combining silicon carbide (SiC) nanoparticles and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) systems in multifunctional composites. This limits holistic understanding, prevents cross‑comparison of mechanisms, and slows development of truly multifunctional composites. This review presents a comprehensive synthesis of SiC nanoparticles, rGO coatings and/or reinforcements, polymer-derived ceramic nanocomposites and magnesium matrix composites. Generalizable studies in other light metal matrices also form part of the study. The synergistic roles of these materials in enhancing corrosion resistance and biomedical performance are highlighted. The primary objective was to systematically review recent advances in the research area. A cluster-based review was conducted. Thematic analysis and classification were performed using Python version 3.14.7 and VOSviewer version1.16.21 in Dell Precision Tower series and Windows 11 environment. Additionally, a systematic comparison of critical performance indicators is presented. The analysis identifies major synergies between protective coatings and structural reinforcements. Key findings demonstrate that SiC nanoparticles significantly improve resistance to wear and high-temperature oxidation. rGO-based coatings have shown potential to improve corrosion protection, while selected studies report favourable cell-viability outcomes under the biological testing conditions examined. Hybrid strategies combining SiC-based reinforcements and graphene oxide coatings offer potential multifunctional benefits. This review provides a clear roadmap for integrating coatings and reinforcements in magnesium matrix composites.

title: A century of secretarial governance: a longitudinal analysis of USDA executive actions, welfare symbiosis, and Extension 4.0 operations from the 1914 Smith-lever act to 2026
summary: Introduction National policy discourse frames security, industrial, technological, and immigration sectors, while the economic stabilization of agricultural supply networks runs concurrently through parallel executive frameworks. Purpose Ev
content: Introduction National policy discourse frames security, industrial, technological, and immigration sectors, while the economic stabilization of agricultural supply networks runs concurrently through parallel executive frameworks. Purpose Evaluate a century of institutional developments across 28 USDA secretarial tenures to analyze financial regulation, risk management, and administrative continuity. Framework Applies historical institutionalism and public choice theory using a Three Pillar Matrix balancing producer, consumer, and innovator dimensions. Methods Employs an integrated design blending historical longitudinal content analysis (1914–2026) with contemporary autoethnography (2016–2026) across legislative texts, budgets, Senate confirmation transcripts, and personal field journals. Results Evaluated through the Producer Pillar, early voluntary cooperatives required adjustments to shield producers from asset deflation, mathematically necessitating mandatory legal price floors in the 1933 Farm Bill, which late-century globalization later restructured into complex, public-private revenue insurance frameworks. Under the Consumer Pillar, the department defended rural production budgets from shifting demographic weights by establishing the Food Stamp Act of 1964, transforming urban consumer nutrition allocations into a structural release valve to absorb excess commodity values. Within the Innovator Pillar, mechanical innovations following the 1914 Smith-Lever Act triggered chronic oversupply, causing a shift toward mid-century chemical adoptions and patented biotechnology lines governed under the Agriculture Risk Protection Act of 2000. Following post-2001 biological risks, the Public Health Security and Bioterrorism Preparedness and Response Act of 2002 legally integrated centralized processing facilities into national risk matrices. This structural defense culminates in the contemporary Extension 4.0 automation and carbon-tracking paradigms backed by the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. Integrating these three dimensions reveals a precise theoretical alignment. Applying historical institutionalism and public choice theory indicates how these cross-sector updates operate as a single, symbiotic, self-preserving bureaucratic network. This path-dependent momentum and structural alliance consistently insulates national food systems from partisan transitions and electoral shifts. Conclusions/implications This study demonstrates that domestic nutrition assistance and agricultural capitalism function as a single, symbiotic bureaucratic network. Stabilizing a sovereign state’s food supply within the global economy requires permanent regulatory intervention. Future statesmanship must innovate its financial frameworks to navigate emergent data monopolies, corporate market barriers, entrenched soil-free calorie systems, evolving macroeconomic shocks, and policy realignments like the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 and future omnibus bills.

title: Benzenehexathiol-Based Conductive Two-Dimensional Metal–Organic Frameworks as HER Cocatalysts for Photocatalytic Overall Water Splitting: Influence of the Metal Center
summary: Abstract While overall water splitting (OWS) based on particulate photocatalysts is a promising method for green hydrogen production, conventional hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) cocatalysts have the drawback of inducing unwanted side rea
content: Abstract While overall water splitting (OWS) based on particulate photocatalysts is a promising method for green hydrogen production, conventional hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) cocatalysts have the drawback of inducing unwanted side reactions related to oxygen, such as the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), which reduces the OWS efficiency. In the present study, a series of conductive two-dimensional metal–organic frameworks based on benzenehexathiol (MBHT, M = Co, Ni, Cu) was applied as an HER cocatalyst to Al-doped SrTiO3 (SrTiO3:Al) photocatalyst, and the effect of the central metal on the cocatalyst activity was evaluated. After single-phase synthesis and subsequent loading of miniaturized MBHT on SrTiO3:Al, CoBHT afforded the highest OWS activity, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 7.2% at 365 nm. Furthermore, CoBHT on SrTiO3:Al boasted of stability after 20 h of operation. Electrochemical measurements and DFT calculations revealed that CoBHT exhibited good HER electrocatalytic activity while possessing reaction selectivity suitable for HER cocatalysts or inherent inertness to ORR. This series of features enabled CoBHT to drive stable OWS operation over SrTiO3:Al without an oxygen barrier layer that is essential for conventional HER cocatalysts.

title: Karst wetland reclamation increases the proportion of inorganic sulfur in total sulfur: associations with sulfate-reducing bacteria abundance and soil enzyme activity
summary: Karst wetlands are fragile and critical ecosystems for soil sulfur biogeochemical cycling. In this study, six typical land-use types in the Huixian karst wetland of Guilin, southern China, were selected to investigate the variations in soil
content: Karst wetlands are fragile and critical ecosystems for soil sulfur biogeochemical cycling. In this study, six typical land-use types in the Huixian karst wetland of Guilin, southern China, were selected to investigate the variations in soil physicochemical properties, four inorganic sulfur fractions, soil enzyme activities, and sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) abundance across 0–40 cm soil profiles. The results showed that wetland reclamation significantly reduced soil pH, soil organic carbon (SOC), silt content, total nitrogen, and total sulfur, while increasing soil bulk density, electrical conductivity (EC), and redox potential (Eh). Reclamation reduced the content of total inorganic sulfur, while elevating its proportion in total sulfur; water-soluble sulfur dominated the inorganic sulfur pool. The composition of inorganic sulfur fractions differed markedly across land-use types. Reclamation increased SRB abundance but inhibited soil enzyme activities. Correlation analysis indicated that soil enzyme activities were negatively correlated with inorganic sulfur contents in abandoned land, whereas positive correlations were observed in other land-use types. Close internal correlations existed among different inorganic sulfur fractions. Soil pH and SOC were associated with greater inorganic sulfur accumulation, while Eh showed an inhibitory association. SOC, Eh, EC, pH, and silt content were the key environmental factors associated with SRB abundance and soil enzyme activities. Collectively, wetland reclamation reduced absolute concentrations of both total inorganic sulfur (TIS) and total organic sulfur (TOS), and preferential loss of TOS increased the TIS/TS ratio, altered sulfur transformation processes, and were accompanied by higher SRB abundance and lower soil enzyme activity. This study reveals the responses of soil sulfur biogeochemical processes to land-use conversion in subtropical karst wetlands and provides insights into sulfur cycle regulation under wetland disturbance.

title: Polymeric nanoparticles for chronic wound therapy: integrating polymer bioactivity, semisolid formulation, and the wound microenvironment
summary: Abstract Background Wound healing is governed by the wound microenvironment, which coordinates the cellular and molecular processes required for tissue repair. In chronic wounds, persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, infection, hypoxia
content: Abstract Background Wound healing is governed by the wound microenvironment, which coordinates the cellular and molecular processes required for tissue repair. In chronic wounds, persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, infection, hypoxia, excessive protease activity, and impaired angiogenesis become closely interconnected, creating pathological conditions that sustain tissue damage and delay regeneration. Although topical semisolid formulations are widely used in wound management, they often exhibit limitations that reduce local bioavailability and efficacy. Incorporating polymeric nanoparticles into semisolid matrices has therefore emerged as a promising strategy for combining the practical advantages of topical formulations with the multifunctional capabilities of nanodelivery systems. Area covered This review examines the biochemical and pathological features of the chronic wound microenvironment and their impact on impaired healing. It then discusses nanoparticle-loaded semisolid platforms, including semisolid formulations, the therapeutic benefits of polymeric nanoparticles, and nanoparticle-forming polymers. Particular emphasis is placed on the bioactivity of polymers, which can actively support wound repair through anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, hemostatic, regenerative, antioxidant, and stimuli-responsive functions beyond their role as carriers. These properties provide a basis for matching polymer chemistry and nanoparticle functionality to dominant pathological barriers within specific wound microenvironments. Expert opinion Finally, we advance a formulation-system perspective in which polymer chemistry, nanoparticle functionality, semisolid matrix behavior, and wound microenvironmental conditions are treated as interdependent design variables. Polymeric nanoparticles offer therapeutic protection, targeted delivery, controlled release, and bioactivity, while the semisolid matrix regulates applicability, retention, dispersion, and release behavior. This microenvironment-matched and matrix-integrated framework may provide a rational foundation for developing precise, multifunctional, and effective next-generation therapies for chronic wounds.

title: Depression is associated with endometrial polyp occurrence and convergent gut microbiota-mitochondrial alterations: a multi-omics case-control study
source: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
summary: Endometrial polyps (EPs) affect 7.8%–34.9% of women and cause abnormal uterine bleeding and reproductive failure, yet their pathogenesis is unclear. Depression is over-represented among women with EPs but is usually read as reactive distres
content: Endometrial polyps (EPs) affect 7.8%–34.9% of women and cause abnormal uterine bleeding and reproductive failure, yet their pathogenesis is unclear. Depression is over-represented among women with EPs but is usually read as reactive distress; whether that association involves the gut microbiota and mitochondrial biology is unknown. We combined a hospital-based case–control analysis (n = 466), faecal full-length 16S rRNA and blood leukocyte RNA-seq in 30 participants (PD n = 11, PND n = 12, NPND n = 7), and a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model with bacterial supplementation. Depression was significantly associated with higher odds of EP in the full cohort (unadjusted OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.55–3.34; P < 0.001), and this trend remained stable following confounder adjustment, propensity-score matching and multiple sensitivity analyses. Signals were partitioned into EP-specific, depression-specific and dual-associated classes. In the EP-specific class, predicted microbial functions showed less electron-transfer gene content (complexes I–II), while host ETC subunits spanning complexes I, III and IV ( NDUFA1, UQCRH, COX6B1, COX7A2 ) were coordinately downregulated and CCR2, CCR5 and UMPS upregulated, with enrichment for oxidative phosphorylation. Dual-associated signals comprised higher Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and lower Eggerthella lenta , negatively correlated (Kendall τ = −0.37, P = 0.007; PD > PND > NPND), together with downregulation of GDF15, HIC1, TCF7L2 and ICAM1 . In mice, restraint stress was accompanied by stromal proliferation exceeding that in estradiol-treated controls and by reduced uterine TOMM20; oral F. prausnitzii given after stress was associated with higher TOMM20 and lower proliferation, whereas E. lenta was not. These findings place a convergent gut microbiota–mitochondrial axis at the intersection of depression and endometrial proliferation, and nominate candidate taxa and transcripts for hypothesis-driven validation. Limitations: multi-omics profiling included 30 participants (11, 12 and 7) with no depression-only cell; microbial functions were predicted by PICRUSt2 and no metabolite was measured; medication use, diet, physical activity, sleep and hormonal status were incompletely captured; and each bacterial group contained three animals. The axis proposed here is therefore hypothesis-generating and requires longitudinal, metabolomic and tissue-specific validation.

title: Effects of sulfur on the growth and metabolism of sulfur and nitrogen in cabbage
summary: Sulfur the fourth essential nutrient element required for plants after nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium plays a crucial physiological role in plant growth and stress resistance. This study aims to investigate the influence of sulfur on ca
content: Sulfur the fourth essential nutrient element required for plants after nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium plays a crucial physiological role in plant growth and stress resistance. This study aims to investigate the influence of sulfur on cabbage growth. In this study, cabbage was treated with sulfur-free Hoagland nutrient solution (control; - S; 0 mmol//L),or normal Hoagland nutrient solution(treatment; + S; 2 mmol/L). By measuring the cabbage growth index, antioxidant system, Nitrogen and Sulffur metabolism at different periods, this study explored S's regulation mechanism for growth, nitrogen metabolism and sulfur metabolism. The results showed that sulfur could significantly promote the growth of cabbage. Under + S treatment, plant height and stem diameter were 15.1% and 15.6% higher than that of -S treatment, and the root dry matter distribution rate was the highest at the rosette and heading stage. 15.47% and 13.09% under + S treatment; 10.15% and 10.4% under -S treatment. Additionally, sulfur promoted photosynthesis, fluorescence, antioxidant enzyme system and glutathione cycle of cabbage. During the period when the Ci was the highest and the Pn reached its maximum, the Ci of + S treatment was 15% higher than that of -S treatment. We discovered that sulfur promoted both nitrogen and sulfur metabolism in cabbage, and + S treatment significantly increased the activities of ATP sulfase (ATPS) and APS reductase (APR) in cabbage. During the whole growth period of cabbage, + S treatment increased ATPS activity by 15.5%, 13.8%, 45.2% and 25.7%, respectively. To sum up, sulfur not only participates in the regulation of basal metabolism during cabbage growth and development but also plays a imperative role in key physiological processes such as activation of the antioxidant system, optimization of the photosynthetic efficiency, and synergistic metabolism of nitrogen and sulfur assimilation. This study provides a theoretical basis for a indepth understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which sulfur nutrition regulates crop growth and metabolic networks, and also lays an important foundation for the precision application of sulfur fertilizers and the optimization of crop sulfur nutrition management strategies.

title: Utilization of Sargassum Natans in Sand Crete Block Production for Sustainable Walling Solutions
summary: Seaweeds are a diverse and abundant group of marine algae that offer a promising sustainable alternative to conventional cementitious materials, which are increasingly associated with high environmental impact. This study investigated the f
content: Seaweeds are a diverse and abundant group of marine algae that offer a promising sustainable alternative to conventional cementitious materials, which are increasingly associated with high environmental impact. This study investigated the feasibility of incorporating locally sourced Sargassumnatans powder into cement–sandcrete blocks as a bio-based additive for sustainable walling. Seaweed collected at Eleko Beach, Lagos State, Nigeria, was washed, sun-dried, oven-dried, pulverized, and sieved before incorporation at 0% (control), 5%, and 7.5% by mass of cement in a 1:5 cement-to-sand mix. Specimens were produced in 230 × 110 × 80 mm moulds and evaluated using material characterization, sieve analysis, specific gravity, compressive-strength testing at 7, 14, and 28 days, water absorption, thermal screening, efflorescence observation, and a stakeholder perception survey (n = 55). This study evaluates the physical, chemical, mechanical, and thermal properties of seaweed-based (Sargassum natans) sandcrete blocks to support more environmentally friendly and cost-effective construction practices. Locally sourced Sargassum natans was processed into powder and incorporated as a cement additive at 5% and 7.5% by weight. Laboratory tests—including chemical composition analysis and microstructure using (optical microscopy and SEM-EDX), sieve analysis, specific gravity, compressive strength, water absorption, and thermal conductivity—were carried out in line with relevant BS and AASHTO standards. Results showed that Sargassum natans contains substantial amounts of SiO₂ (41.6%) and CaO (29.9%), indicating pozzolanic potential. The mix with 5% additive achieved at 28-days compressive strength of 8.22 N/mm², closely matching the 7.5% mix (7.08 N/mm²) and satisfying the Nigerian Industrial Standard (NIS 87:2000) for load-bearing blocks.

title: Cross-vector flexibility in sector-coupled low-carbon energy systems
summary: This paper holistically assesses the current literature by examining how cross-vector flexibility is observed, coordinated, and verified in low-carbon energy systems based on sector coupling. To this end, the interplay between cross-vector
content: This paper holistically assesses the current literature by examining how cross-vector flexibility is observed, coordinated, and verified in low-carbon energy systems based on sector coupling. To this end, the interplay between cross-vector flexibility, digital twins and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled observability, predictive control approaches, local coordination mechanisms, and flexibility markets is addressed within a common analytical framework. This review shows that cross-vector flexibility is more than an energy conversion technology problem; it is also a coordination problem. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, a systematic Scopus search and screening process yielded an analytical core of 107 studies. Within this core, only 19 studies (17.8%) progress beyond synthetic simulation: thirteen use real or case-based data, six provide co-simulation, hardware-in-the-loop or closed-loop field evidence, and none verifies delivered flexibility against a baseline. Observability is addressed as a primary concern in only seven of the 107 studies, making it the least represented layer of the coordination stack. In addition, 88 studies (82.2% of the core) represent no socio-technical conditions. The value of flexibility depends not only on the capacity to shift, store, or convert energy, but also on the ability to monitor system states, ensure coordination between different actors and energy carriers, verify the service provided, and create mechanisms by which flexibility can be procured and evaluated as a service. When these layers are considered together, the observability and validation deficiencies spread upwards throughout the coordination stack, which limits the applicability of advanced control approaches and market designs in real systems. Therefore, greater emphasis should be placed on observability infrastructures that support validation, transparent interface definitions between coordination layers, validation processes that extend beyond simulation, and assessment frameworks that explicitly consider behavioral and institutional realities. Developing these elements is critical to transforming cross-vector flexibility from a concept primarily assessed in simulation environments into a verifiable, transferable, and operationally deployable service in decarbonized multi-energy systems.

title: Nanomaterials applied in biosensor development
summary: Nanomaterials have significantly advanced biosensor development by enabling highly efficient sensing interfaces with enhanced sensitivity, selectivity, signal amplification, and analytical performance. This narrative review provides a compr
content: Nanomaterials have significantly advanced biosensor development by enabling highly efficient sensing interfaces with enhanced sensitivity, selectivity, signal amplification, and analytical performance. This narrative review provides a comprehensive overview of the main classes of nanomaterials used in biosensing, including metallic nanoparticles, carbon-based nanomaterials, quantum dots, and hybrid nanocomposites. This review focuses on the physicochemical mechanisms by which these materials improve biosensor performance, including increased electroactive surface area, accelerated electron transfer, electrocatalytic activity, optical signal enhancement, and stable biofunctionalization of recognition elements. This review discusses key immobilization strategies in relation to their effects on sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility, and operational stability. Representative biosensor platforms are critically evaluated according to their detection mechanisms, analytical performance, advantages, limitations, and applications in clinical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, food safety, and pharmaceutical analysis. Hybrid nanomaterials emerge as particularly promising because they combine complementary properties within a single sensing interface, enabling improved electron transfer, greater active surface area, enhanced bioreceptor immobilization, reduced overpotentials, and amplified analytical signals. Despite substantial progress, important challenges remain regarding reproducibility, long-term stability, biocompatibility, selectivity in complex matrices, standardized fabrication, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory validation. Future research should therefore prioritize translating high-performance laboratory prototypes into robust, scalable analytical platforms validated on complex real samples. Integrating nanomaterials with screen-printed electrodes, paper-based devices, wearable sensors, microfluidics, smartphone-assisted platforms, and artificial intelligence is expected to drive the next generation of biosensing technologies. These advances may enable more accessible, portable, cost-effective, and reliable biosensors for point-of-care diagnostics, personalized healthcare, environmental monitoring, food safety, and pharmaceutical analysis.
