We also highlight another dilemma: unless business contributions to political parties are entirely excluded, increased transparency in party funding sources is more likely to reduce trust than increase it.

title: Faktor Penentu Keputusan Investasi Generasi Z Di Pontianak
summary: This study examines whether financial literacy and media exposure are associated with the investment decisions of Generation Z in Pontianak City. The researchers distributed questionnaires to 154 respondents aged 17–29 who lived in Pontiana
content: This study examines whether financial literacy and media exposure are associated with the investment decisions of Generation Z in Pontianak City. The researchers distributed questionnaires to 154 respondents aged 17–29 who lived in Pontianak, had personal income, and had invested, or were currently investing, in the capital market. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS, and the measurement model met the criteria for validity and reliability. The results show that both financial literacy and media exposure have a positive and significant relationship with investment decisions, although the effect sizes are small. Because the survey was conducted at a single point in time, these findings indicate association and do not establish causation. Organizers of investment education programs for young people are advised to develop participants’ financial skills while also paying attention to their media habits.

title: Species of the Family Salicaceae Mirb. in the Landscaping of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
summary: In the modern period, special attention is paid not only to the decorative characteristics of plants used in the landscaping of cities and settlements, but also to their ecological suitability, biodiversity conservation, and contribution to
content: In the modern period, special attention is paid not only to the decorative characteristics of plants used in the landscaping of cities and settlements, but also to their ecological suitability, biodiversity conservation, and contribution to ecosystem sustainability. In this regard, representatives of the family Salicaceae Mirb., comprising trees and shrubs, are considered one of the plant groups with diverse ecological and economic significance. The aim of this study was to summarize the ecological characteristics of Salicaceae species occurring in the flora of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic and to assess their potential for use in ecological landscaping. Based on literature data, the results of previous floristic studies, and field observations conducted in 2023–2024, 17 species belonging to two genera, Salix L. and Populus L., were analyzed. The predominantly mesophytic characteristics of the studied species, their distribution across different altitudinal belts, and their occurrence particularly in river valleys, moist habitats, and forest-shrub vegetation were considered key indicators determining their importance for ecological landscaping. The potential use of willow and poplar species for stabilizing riverbanks, reducing erosion processes, landscaping settlements, and enhancing the ecological stability of landscapes was identified. The results of the study demonstrate that the incorporation of tree and shrub species native to the local flora into ecological landscaping systems is important for biodiversity conservation and the development of sustainable landscapes.

title: Ledger Sovereignty: Debt, Accounting, and the Structure of Money in Colonial Mexican Haciendas
summary: ABSTRACT This article introduces the concept of “ledger sovereignty” to examine how colonial Mexican haciendas functioned as nonstate monetary institutions in contexts of chronic coin scarcity. Ledger sovereignty describes the capacity of n
content: ABSTRACT This article introduces the concept of “ledger sovereignty” to examine how colonial Mexican haciendas functioned as nonstate monetary institutions in contexts of chronic coin scarcity. Ledger sovereignty describes the capacity of nonstate institutions to (1) define a unit of account, (2) issue and redeem credit, (3) track obligations, and (4) enforce repayment through accounting rather than by taxation or currency issuance. Rather than treating monetary authority as exclusively state‐based, this study demonstrates how haciendas exercised de facto monetary power by monopolizing the means of specification and redemption within their own internal economies. Hacienda ledgers were not merely passive records documenting monetary transactions but actually constituted money itself, transforming subsistence and labor into a durable, debt‐based economy that bound workers to the estate. Examining the organization of credit and labor within the hacienda reveals bookkeeping itself as a technology of governance, collapsing economic calculation and social control into a single administrative framework. By highlighting the role of accounting in the creation of money, this article expands anthropological approaches to money, power, and debt beyond the state, offering a comparative framework for analyzing nonstate monetary regimes.

title: PACKAGING BARRIER EFFECTS ON PHYSICOCHEMICAL STABILITY AND COLOR CHANGES OF FLAVORED YERBA MATE (Ilex paraguariensis) DURING STORAGE
source: Revista E-Tech Tecnologias para Competitividade Industrial
summary: Yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis) tea is one of the most consumed beverages in South America. Environmental conditions and packaging barrier properties strongly influence the quality of stored yerba mate, but despite its commercial importanc
content: Yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis) tea is one of the most consumed beverages in South America. Environmental conditions and packaging barrier properties strongly influence the quality of stored yerba mate, but despite its commercial importance, few studies have evaluated the effects of packaging systems on the stability of artificially flavored yerba mate. Therefore, this study investigates the influence of different packaging materials (such as transparent polyethylene plastic, stand-up pouches, glass jars, and plastic combined with metal cans) on the physicochemical properties and color stability of mint-flavored yerba mate during storage. Yerba mate leaves were flavored with mint flavoring (3% w/w) and stored for 62 days under environmental conditions simulating commercial storage. Moisture content, pH, water activity (aw), and color parameters (L*, a*, b*, chroma, and total color difference ΔE) were evaluated at 0, 30, and 62 days. The results showed a gradual increase in pH and significant variations in water activity (Aw) during storage, with plastic packaging exhibiting higher Aw values than the other systems. Color analysis revealed a decrease in luminosity (L*) and shifts in chromatic coordinates (a* and b*), suggesting pigment degradation and oxidative reactions during storage. Among the evaluated systems, a stand-up pouch combined with a metal can showed the least significant loss of yerba mate's green and yellow color. These results highlight the importance of selecting packaging materials with improved barrier properties to preserve the physicochemical quality of flavored yerba mate during storage.

title: Understanding drivers of household food waste reduction among Asian young adults
summary: Purpose Food waste and food scarcity, unfortunately, coexist in today's society. Young people have been found to produce larger amounts of food waste than older age groups. Although there has been significant research on food waste, the ext
content: Purpose Food waste and food scarcity, unfortunately, coexist in today's society. Young people have been found to produce larger amounts of food waste than older age groups. Although there has been significant research on food waste, the extant research offers limited understanding of food waste among young adults and cross-national comparisons. The main objective of this research is to investigate the determinants of household food waste among Asian young adults, based on psychosocial factors and household-related factors (household skills and shopping/planning behaviors), across five Asian countries. Design/methodology/approach A research framework was developed based on pro-environmental theory, the theory of planned behavior (TPB), and the norm activation model (NAM). A questionnaire survey was distributed in Taiwan, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Thailand. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to analyze the full sample (N = 672). Findings Environmental concern shaped moral attitude, perceived behavioral control, and injunctive norms, which influenced intentions not to waste food and to reuse leftovers. Household skills and past shopping/planning behavior significantly predicted food waste, while intentions did not. Both intentions, however, significantly predicted purchase reduction in the full sample. The relative impact of psychosocial versus household factors on food waste varied across countries. Multi-group analysis (MGA) showed variations in the relationships across countries. Originality/value This study contributes to the extant literature by building a theoretical framework comprising two distinct routes, an intentional route (psychosocial factors) and a household route (household skills and shopping/planning behaviors), for understanding food waste, and by performing a cross-national comparison across five Asian countries.

title: EFFICIENCY ASSESSMENT MODELS FOR SMART ECONOMY: A THEORETICAL-METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK AND SPECIFIC FEATURES OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT IN THE REPUBLIC OF SERBIA
source: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
summary: Modern urban paradigms necessitate a holistic transition toward the smart city concept, where the smart economy is established as an imperative for sustainable urban competitiveness. However, its efficiency evaluation within national framew
content: Modern urban paradigms necessitate a holistic transition toward the smart city concept, where the smart economy is established as an imperative for sustainable urban competitiveness. However, its efficiency evaluation within national frameworks remains under-researched. This paper analyzes the applicability of global smart urban economy efficiency models to identify indicators tailored to the Serbian context, addressing asymmetric data availability and quality. The central result is an innovative hybrid model integrating multi-criteria TOPSIS analysis and non-parametric DEA, neutralizing the inherent limitations of individual methods. The scientific contribution lies in constituting an original conceptual framework for assessing 28 Serbian cities, providing an operational basis for future research and strategic management of smart urban transitions under budgetary constraints.

title: Institutional Governance for Reducing Regional Industrial Disparities: An Empirical Legal Approach
summary: Regional industrial productivity disparities remain a significant challenge to Indonesia’s efforts to achieve balanced economic transformation. This study examines the structural factors underlying productivity differences between Western a
content: Regional industrial productivity disparities remain a significant challenge to Indonesia’s efforts to achieve balanced economic transformation. This study examines the structural factors underlying productivity differences between Western and Eastern Indonesia, evaluates the legal and regulatory frameworks governing regional industrial development, and assesses the implementation of policies aimed at reducing regional disparities. It employs a mixed-methods approach with qualitative socio-legal analysis. The legal analysis examines relevant legislation, institutional arrangements, and policy instruments governing industrial development, investment, regional autonomy, and intergovernmental coordination. Qualitative evidence from focus group discussions further explores the relationship between regulatory provisions, institutional capacity, and policy implementation. The study connects empirical evidence of industrial productivity disparities with the effectiveness of existing regulatory and institutional arrangements. It emphasizes the need to strengthen regulatory coherence, intergovernmental coordination, regional institutional capacity, and targeted policy interventions. Integrating productivity-oriented economic policies with responsive legal and institutional governance is essential to addressing structural barriers and promoting more balanced industrial development between Western and Eastern Indonesia.

title: Direct Export Strategies, Regulatory Framework, and Competitive Advantage in Fresh Produce Exporting Firms: An Integrative Review and Research Agenda
source: Research Journal of Business and Finance
summary: Direct export strategies are widely promoted as a pathway to superior competitive performance for agribusiness firms in emerging markets, yet the conditions under which they succeed remain poorly integrated across the strategic management,
content: Direct export strategies are widely promoted as a pathway to superior competitive performance for agribusiness firms in emerging markets, yet the conditions under which they succeed remain poorly integrated across the strategic management, international business, and institutional literatures. This article synthesises theoretical and empirical scholarship on direct sales, e-commerce, and strategic partnerships as drivers of competitive advantage among fresh produce exporting firms, and examines regulatory framework as the institutional mechanism moderating this relationship. The study adopts an integrative literature review approach. It integrates four theoretical traditions: the Resource-Based View (anchor theory), the Uppsala Internationalisation Model, Institutional Theory, and Porter's Diamond Model of National Competitive Advantage. It also synthesises 21 empirical studies spanning Asian, European, and African contexts, including Kenya. The reviewed literature demonstrates consistent, though theoretically fragmented, support for a positive association between direct export strategies and competitive advantage. However, fewer than one-fifth of the 21 studies are explicitly grounded in a named theory, and none integrates firm-level, process-level, institutional, and national-competitiveness perspectives simultaneously. The evidence is dominated by quantitative, cross-sectional designs and is concentrated outside agriculture. Only four of the 21 studies are Kenyan. None examines fresh produce exporters using the full construct set of direct export strategy, regulatory framework, and competitive advantage. A recurring tension is whether regulatory stringency constrains direct exporting or triggers firms to internalise control through direct channels. The review advances an integrated, multi-level theoretical framework spanning firm resources, internationalisation process, institutional legitimacy, and national-competitiveness conditions. It also proposes a moderated conceptual model in which regulatory framework strengthens or weakens the effects of direct sales, e-commerce, and strategic partnerships on competitive advantage. It offers testable propositions, a research agenda, and implications for exporters, industry bodies, and regulators in Kenya's horticultural sector.

title: From ESG exposure to investment intention: the role of social media engagement, greenwashing risk, and investor trust
summary: Social media has become a primary channel for firms to communicate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information to retail investors, yet the promotional nature of this content raises greenwashing concerns, and its role in shaping
content: Social media has become a primary channel for firms to communicate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information to retail investors, yet the promotional nature of this content raises greenwashing concerns, and its role in shaping investor trust remains underexplored. This study examines how exposure to ESG content on social media, engagement with ESG content, and perceived greenwashing risk affect investor trust and investment intention toward ESG assets. The study employs cross-sectional survey data collected from retail investors through a closed-ended questionnaire and tests six hypothesized paths using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that the measurement model is reliable and valid, with composite reliability between 0.853 and 0.902 and average variance extracted between 0.592 and 0.698. Engagement with ESG content raises investor trust (β = 0.285, p < 0.001) and investment intention (β = 0.163, p = 0.006). ESG content exposure increases investment intention (β = 0.184, p < 0.001) but does not significantly affect investor trust (β = 0.042, p = 0.451). Contrary to expectations, perceived greenwashing risk is positively associated with investor trust (β = 0.292, p < 0.001) and investment intention (β = 0.302, p < 0.001). The model explains 29.8% of the variance in investor trust and 30.4% in investment intention. The findings suggest that active engagement with ESG content, rather than passive exposure, is a stronger driver of retail investors’ trust, and that awareness of greenwashing risk coexists with, rather than suppresses, trust and investment intention. JEL Classification Codes: G11, G41, M14, M31, Q56.

title: Public sector sustainability reporting: Opportunities and challenges of the release of IPSASB SRS 1st Edition
summary: Sustainability reporting in the public sector is a growing strategic necessity amid increasing demands for transparency, accountability, and climate policy integration into national governance systems. This study aims to analyze the opportu
content: Sustainability reporting in the public sector is a growing strategic necessity amid increasing demands for transparency, accountability, and climate policy integration into national governance systems. This study aims to analyze the opportunities and challenges of implementing the Sustainability Reporting Standard Exposure Draft 1 (SRS ED-1) issued by IPSASB as a global framework for public sector sustainability disclosures. The research was conducted using the PRISMA flow diagram of 180 international and national scholarly sources, narrowed down to 24 relevant articles. Findings reveal that SRS ED-1 presents opportunities to enhance governance quality, fiscal sustainability, and access to green financing. Nevertheless, structural challenges such as limited human resources, low technological readiness, data fragmentation, and institutional resistance remain significant barriers. Therefore, concrete measures such as establishing national regulation, capacity-building programs, digital system strengthening, and cross-ministerial pilot projects are necessary to support its gradual implementation.

title: Formal modeling and verification of parachain candidate validation and inclusion in relay chain polkadot
summary: Polkadot is a next-generation blockchain platform that achieves scalability and interoperability through a heterogeneous multi-chain architecture, where multiple parachains operate concurrently under a shared security model. A fundamental c
content: Polkadot is a next-generation blockchain platform that achieves scalability and interoperability through a heterogeneous multi-chain architecture, where multiple parachains operate concurrently under a shared security model. A fundamental component of this architecture is the candidate backing and inclusion mechanism, which governs the validation, verification, and incorporation of parachain blocks into the relay chain. This process involves coordinated interactions among collators, validators, parachains, and the relay chain, and proceeds through multiple stages, including candidate generation, validation, backing, availability checking, approval voting, and finalization. Subtle inconsistencies or design flaws within these stages may compromise system correctness, potentially resulting in invalid block inclusion or data unavailability. Consequently, rigorous formal verification is essential to ensure system reliability and robustness. Existing research predominantly emphasizes architectural design and empirical evaluation, with limited attention to formal verification of the candidate lifecycle. To address this gap, this study develops a comprehensive behavioral model using Promela, capturing key system interactions and concurrency aspects. Critical safety and liveness properties, including integrity, fairness, and fault tolerance, are formally specified in Linear Temporal Logic and verified using the SPIN model checker. The verification results confirm system correctness while highlighting state-space complexity and scalability considerations.

title: Replication code and Supplementary Material: Pricing geopolitical risk into delivered green hydrogen costs (Algeria-EU, 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Route-explicit deterministic delivered-cost model for green hydrogen supplied to the EU from Algeria (pipeline and ammonia) and five competitors (Morocco, Egypt, Oman, Australia, Chile), with country WACC and default-spread betas, bottom-up
content: Route-explicit deterministic delivered-cost model for green hydrogen supplied to the EU from Algeria (pipeline and ammonia) and five competitors (Morocco, Egypt, Oman, Australia, Chile), with country WACC and default-spread betas, bottom-up shipping, canal tolls and war-risk insurance with rerouting; Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 draws), Shapley decomposition, ES95 security premium, break-even GPR, Sobol indices, and an ex-post scenario tested on the observed 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure. All inputs are documented with their sources in params/; outputs are regenerated by src/run_model.py. Version 2.1.0 accompanies the revised article: the PV electricity cost uses the yield after clipping, the reference voyage of the ammonia chain is valued at the baseline production cost, three bounding variants are added (midstream financing, fuel valuation, independent PV yield factors) and further dated 2026 war-risk quotes are included (see CHANGELOG.md). It supersedes v2.0.0 and v1.0.0.

title: Learning from COVID-19 to strengthen hantavirus preparedness and public health response
summary: Years after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the world continues to face significant health, social, and economic challenges, while emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases remain a growing global public health concern.
content: Years after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the world continues to face significant health, social, and economic challenges, while emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases remain a growing global public health concern. This trend highlights the importance of interconnected health systems and reveals both the strengths and weaknesses of global public health preparedness and response. In this context, we present a comparative analysis of the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent Andes virus outbreak, focusing on their epidemiological and virological characteristics, and discussing the effectiveness of the COVID-19 public health responses. We also explore key lessons that can be applied to future zoonotic threats in the context of rapidly changing ecosystems. The results reveal that COVID-19 and hantavirus infections share several molecular and clinical features but differ in their transmission patterns. COVID-19 spreads efficiently between humans and caused a global pandemic, whereas Hantavirus infections are mainly transmitted from rodents to humans and remain geographically localized despite a higher case fatality rate. While vaccines are available for COVID-19, none exist for Hantavirus disease. The study also highlights the value of artificial intelligence, epidemic intelligence, and the One Health approach for improving outbreak prediction, detection, and surveillance.

title: Integrating transport planning and infrastructure to reduce urban flood risk in Accra, Ghana
summary: Accra's repeated urban flooding has been predominantly attributed to rainfall variability and inadequate drainage; however, the structural role of transport infrastructure influencing flood exposure remains empirically underexplored. This s
content: Accra's repeated urban flooding has been predominantly attributed to rainfall variability and inadequate drainage; however, the structural role of transport infrastructure influencing flood exposure remains empirically underexplored. This study examines the spatial and statistical relationships between transport infrastructure characteristics and flood occurrence across thirty road segments in the Accra Metropolitan Area (AMA), drawing on data from the National Disaster Management Organization (NADMO), the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet), and the Department of Urban Roads for the period 2010–2023. A quantitative cross-sectional design combining Pearson correlation analysis and ordinary least squares (OLS) multiple regression was employed to evaluate how road elevation, distance to drainage infrastructure, and annual rainfall jointly predict flood frequency. The regression model explained 93.4% of the variation in flood events (adjusted R 2 = 0.927). Road elevation emerged as the strongest individual predictor ( r = −0.941, p < 0.001), while distance to drainage infrastructure showed a strong positive relationship with flood frequency ( r = 0.898, p < 0.001). Temporal analysis (2010−2023) further revealed a divergence between rainfall levels and flood occurrences, indicating that infrastructure configuration is also a key structural driver of recurrent inundation, alongside rainfall and unregulated urban development practices. Arterial roads concentrated the highest flood exposure (41% of events), with flood conditions reducing average travel speeds by 68% and increasing commute times by 174%. The results support repositioning transport planning as a core instrument of urban flood containment, through transport–drainage co-design mandates, integrated spatial governance, and targeted resilience retrofitting of major road corridors.

title: Polikriz Çağında Yeşil Bütçeleme: Türkiye’de Kamu Maliyesinin Yeşil Dönüşümü
source: BİLTÜRK Journal of Economics and Related Studies
summary: Türkiye’de yeşil bütçeleme, çevresel sürdürülebilirliği kamu mali yönetimine entegre etmeyi amaçlayan kurumsal bir dönüşüm süreci olarak gelişmektedir. Kalkınma planları, orta vadeli programlar ve performans esaslı bütçeleme uygulamalarıyla
content: Türkiye’de yeşil bütçeleme, çevresel sürdürülebilirliği kamu mali yönetimine entegre etmeyi amaçlayan kurumsal bir dönüşüm süreci olarak gelişmektedir. Kalkınma planları, orta vadeli programlar ve performans esaslı bütçeleme uygulamalarıyla desteklenen bu yaklaşım, ekonomik büyüme ve mali istikrar hedeflerini çevresel amaçlarla uyumlaştırmayı ve emisyon yoğun sektörlerde kaynak tahsisinin yeşil dönüşüm doğrultusunda yeniden şekillendirilmesini hedeflemektedir. Bu çalışma, polikriz olgusunun kamu maliyesi üzerindeki etkilerini açıklayarak, Türkiye’nin yeşil dönüşüm politikaları ve yeşil bütçeleme uygulamalarını uluslararası literatür ışığında incelemekte; sürdürülebilir kalkınma hedeflerine ulaşmada maliye politikalarının dönüştürücü rolünü tartışmayı amaçlamaktadır. Çalışmada doküman analizi yöntemi kullanılarak ulusal planlama belgeleri, bütçe programları ve ilgili mevzuat karşılaştırmalı olarak ele alınmaktadır. Değerlendirme, kurumsal çerçeve ile uygulama arasındaki ilişkiye odaklanmakta; yeşil etiketleme, şeffaf raporlama, bağımsız denetim ve kurumsal kapasitenin geliştirilmesine yönelik gereksinimleri ortaya koymaktadır. Çalışma birincil bütçe verilerine dayalı ampirik analiz içermemektedir

title: Planar Equivalent Layers for Potential Fields: 1. Theoretical Insights
summary: Abstract A comprehensive theoretical framework is developed for potential-field transformations based on planar equivalent layers, a technique empirically used in applied geophysics since the 1960s. The formulation replaces the widely accep
content: Abstract A comprehensive theoretical framework is developed for potential-field transformations based on planar equivalent layers, a technique empirically used in applied geophysics since the 1960s. The formulation replaces the widely accepted equivalent-layer principle—primarily founded on empirical generalizations—with a rigorous theoretical foundation. The planar equivalent-layer theorem establishes the existence of continuous planar layers capable of reproducing potential-field data exactly when they reside strictly in the source-free region above the sources, or within a predefined error level when they intersect the true sources. Closed-form expressions for planar equivalent layers are derived by modifying the classical solutions of Dirichlet’s and Neumann’s problems, revealing that these layers possess tangible physical meaning related to boundary-value problems in potential theory. The theoretical framework also demonstrates the mathematical equivalence between potential-field transformations computed via the equivalent-layer technique and those obtained through Fourier-domain approaches. Distinct classes of equivalent layers are formally defined, together with their relationships to the observed data, true sources, and potential-field transformations. The resulting formulation provides a rigorous explanation for the long-standing success of the equivalent-layer technique in potential-field analysis.

title: Halal Slaughterers’ Lived Experiences of Pre-Slaughter Stunning in Indonesian Abattoirs
source: Journal of Animal Health and Production
summary: This study investigates how halal slaughterers in Indonesian slaughterhouses perceive the use of preslaughter stunning.Stunning remains controversial in modern halal practice due to concerns about sharia compliance and animal welfare, makin
content: This study investigates how halal slaughterers in Indonesian slaughterhouses perceive the use of preslaughter stunning.Stunning remains controversial in modern halal practice due to concerns about sharia compliance and animal welfare, making the perspectives of slaughterers as frontline practitioners crucial to understand.A qualitative descriptive design with a phenomenological approach was employed, involving 13 purposively selected halal slaughterers with at least three years of experience and prior involvement in slaughtering cattle with and without stunning.Data were collected through in-depth face-to-face and online interviews, focusing on perceived challenges and the perceived ease of slaughter with or without stunning, as well as arguments for and against stunning.Data were validated through triangulation of interviews, field observations, and Islamic legal documents, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman framework of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing.The findings indicate a nuanced spectrum of responses, in which most slaughterers conditionally accept pre-slaughter stunning under strict technical and sharia safeguards.At the same time, a minority firmly rejects it due to concerns over mis-stunning, animal suffering, and doubts about halal validity.This study concludes that slaughterers' perceptions are pivotal for the practical implementation of halal-compliant stunning and may provide an initial exploratory reference for reflecting on policy orientation and training needs to better align stunning practices with Islamic principles and animal welfare.

title: Two-year randomized clinical evaluation of catechin doped in a universal adhesive on non-carious cervical lesions restorations
summary: OBJECTIVES: This randomized, blinded clinical trial evaluated the 24-month clinical performance of a universal adhesive (Single Bond Universal) containing 0.1 wt% epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) for the restoration of non-carious cervical
content: OBJECTIVES: This randomized, blinded clinical trial evaluated the 24-month clinical performance of a universal adhesive (Single Bond Universal) containing 0.1 wt% epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) for the restoration of non-carious cervical lesions (NCCLs using self-etch and etch-and-rinse strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 160 restorations were placed in 29 patients and randomly allocated to four groups: etch-and-rinse (ER), etch-and-rinse with EGCG (ER-EGCG), self-etch (SE), and self-etch with EGCG (SE-EGCG). EGCG was directly incorporated into the adhesive, which was applied according to the manufacturer's instructions. All lesions were restored with a nanofilled composite resin (Filtek Z350XT) and evaluated at baseline and after 6, 12, 18, and 24 months according to the World Dental Federation criteria. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis and McNemar tests (α = 0.05). RESULTS: Participant recall rates were 100% at baseline and 6 months, and 93.1%, 89.7%, and 72.4% at 12, 18, and 24 months, respectively. No significant differences were observed among groups for any evaluated clinical criterion throughout the 24-month follow-up (p > 0.05). At 24 months, retention rates were 90% for SE and SE-EGCG and 100% for ER and ER-EGCG. No significant differences were observed between baseline and 24-month evaluations within any group (p > 0.05). Incorporation of 0.1 wt% EGCG into the universal adhesive did not compromise the clinical performance of NCCL restorations over 24 months, regardless of the bonding strategy. CONCLUSIONS: Incorporation of 0.1 wt% EGCG into a universal adhesive did not affect the clinical performance of NCCL restorations over 24 months. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Incorporation of 0.1 wt% EGCG into a universal adhesive did not improve the clinical performance of NCCL restorations over 24 months compared with the unmodified adhesive. However, EGCG incorporation did not adversely affect restoration performance when the adhesive was used with either etch-and-rinse or self-etch strategies.

title: Mapping methodologies: Exploring visual narratives of identities, families, and power with immigrant‐origin and marginalized youth
summary: Mapping methodologies offer a versatile and innovative approach to understanding the complexity of youth identities, families, and communities, while also attending to the systems of power, privilege, and marginality in which they are embed
content: Mapping methodologies offer a versatile and innovative approach to understanding the complexity of youth identities, families, and communities, while also attending to the systems of power, privilege, and marginality in which they are embedded. Mapping involves participant-generated drawings that are integrated into broader qualitative interview protocols, amplifying youth voices in the process. Participants are given colored pencils, paper, and an open-ended prompt inviting them to depict their identities, families, and/or communities. These "visual narratives" serve as entry points for deeper qualitative inquiries into topics that are often multifaceted, sensitive, and especially salient for individuals at the intersections of multiple marginalities. This methodological paper presents mapping as a qualitative research tool and offers a practical guide for planning, implementing, and analyzing maps with diverse adolescent and emerging adult populations.

title: Influential dynamic interactions of safe havens with facets of economic and monetary uncertainty
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dynamic causal connectedness that a range of innovative uncertainty measures presents with gold and silver prices. Design/methodology/approach Monthly data from January 1985 to January 2024 and ave
content: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dynamic causal connectedness that a range of innovative uncertainty measures presents with gold and silver prices. Design/methodology/approach Monthly data from January 1985 to January 2024 and averaged dynamic connectedness and network dynamic connectedness based on the advanced quantile-vector autoregression framework are used. Findings The impact that risk stemming from economic, monetary, fiscal or trade uncertainty has on precious metals is estimated. Gold and silver are found to behave as drivers of impacts in bear markets but as absorbers of spillovers in bull markets, especially silver. This also holds for economic policy uncertainty (EPU), which is succinctly the dominant form of risk and is mostly linked with monetary policy uncertainty. Fiscal and trade policies create risk in flourishing eras when absorbers such as silver, gold or EPU are most needed to mitigate uncertainty in markets. Originality/value This paper provides insights for policymakers and investors in normal and crisis periods.

title: Impact of HIV infection, immune status, and integrase inhibitor-based antiretroviral therapy on the gut microbiota in men who have sex with men with and without HIV
summary: HIV infection and antiretroviral therapy (ART) influence gut microbiota, affecting immune function and systemic inflammation. However, isolating the effects of integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based ART on gut microbiota is chall
tags: Men who have sex with men
content: HIV infection and antiretroviral therapy (ART) influence gut microbiota, affecting immune function and systemic inflammation. However, isolating the effects of integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based ART on gut microbiota is challenging due to confounding by HIV status, immunosuppression, and behavioral factors. We examined three cohorts of men who have sex with men (MSM) (n = 62): (1) HIV-negative individuals using post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) (n = 22), (2) people with HIV (PWH) with < 350 CD4 cells/µL sampled before and 48 weeks after ART initiation (n = 23), (3) PWH on long-term INSTI-based ART with immune recovery (n = 17). Fecal samples were collected longitudinally in cohorts 1 (at baseline and after 4 weeks of PEP) and 2 (at baseline and 48 weeks after ART initiation), and at a single timepoint in cohort 3. Microbiota composition was analyzed by 16 S rRNA sequencing, and functional profiling inferred with PICRUSt2. Differential abundance was assessed using ANCOM-BC2. HIV-negative participants showed significantly lower alpha diversity than PWH, and beta diversity differed by HIV status. Short-term INSTI-based ART in PEP users was associated with limited microbiota changes. Pro-inflammatory taxa, such as Prevotellaceae , were enriched in PWH. Functional predictions indicated enrichment of pathways related to cell envelope structure, membrane transport, and stress response. Long-term ART was associated with modest taxonomic and functional shifts, including enrichment of Barnesiella in individuals with immune recovery (ANCOM-BC2, LFC = 3.6, adjusted p = 0.02). HIV infection and immune suppression are the main drivers of gut microbiota alterations in MSM, whereas INSTI-based ART is associated with comparatively modest changes. These findings support a limited impact of INSTI-based ART on microbiota composition and function.

title: Tackling Estimation Risk in Kelly Investing Using Options
summary: The Kelly criterion provides a general framework for optimizing the growth rate of an investment portfolio over time by maximizing the expected logarithmic utility of wealth. However, the optimality condition of the Kelly criterion is highl
content: The Kelly criterion provides a general framework for optimizing the growth rate of an investment portfolio over time by maximizing the expected logarithmic utility of wealth. However, the optimality condition of the Kelly criterion is highly sensitive to accurate estimates of the probabilities and investment payoffs. Estimation risk can lead to greatly suboptimal portfolios. In a binomial model, we show that the introduction of a European option generates a family of alternative replications of the same log-optimal terminal payoff. Under the misspecification of the payoff, these replications respond differently to model error, allowing combinations of option-based strategies that improve realized long-run growth relative to the standard Kelly strategy.

title: Rule Forest: Interpretable Ensembles of LLM-Generated Questions for Rare-Outcome Prediction
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: Many high-stakes screening decisions in finance amount to predicting a rare outcome from unstructured text, such as whether a founder will successfully build a large company, or which crowdfunded loan will fail to attract funding. When posi
content: Many high-stakes screening decisions in finance amount to predicting a rare outcome from unstructured text, such as whether a founder will successfully build a large company, or which crowdfunded loan will fail to attract funding. When positives are this rare, simple models may be preferable to more complex ones. For example, a model that learns a weight for each feature may have too little signal to estimate those weights reliably, and also inspecting the model means reading a list of fitted coefficients rather than a simple rule that can be checked by eye. We introduce Rule Forest, which uses a large language model to generate simple YES/NO questions, rather than using it to directly predict outcomes, and combines the strongest questions into an equal-weight “green-flags” scorecard. This scorecard is as accurate as an equivalent model that learns a weight per question, within noise, and its advantage appears largest when positives are rarest. The result is an interpretable list of rules that a domain expert can edit and extend. When predicting founder success, the fraction of shortlisted founders who succeed increases from about 1 in 50 to 1 in 10, and to about 1 in 6 with a handful of expert-written questions. A second dataset which focuses on identifying failed loans, Kiva microloans, shows the same qualitative pattern. Across both tasks, the lesson is the same: a language model is most useful not as the predictor but as a generator of features a person can read, edit, and improve, and when positives are scarce that interpretability costs no measurable accuracy.

title: Rosette formations as symmetry breaking events
summary: Multicellular rosettes are ubiquitous structures in biological systems, observed in contexts ranging from morphogenesis to wound healing and cancer progression. Although some molecular insights have been gained to explain the presence of th
content: Multicellular rosettes are ubiquitous structures in biological systems, observed in contexts ranging from morphogenesis to wound healing and cancer progression. Although some molecular insights have been gained to explain the presence of these assemblies of cells around a common center, the tunable global features that favor/hinder their formation are still largely undefined. Here, we use a Voronoi dynamical model in combination with fluorescence microscopy experiments on neural cell populations derived from induced pluripotent stem cells to investigate the ingredients driving the emergence of rosettes. We find that (i) breaking the local spatial symmetry of the system by introducing local curvature-inducing defects allows for the emergence of rosette-like structures, (ii) whose probability of formation depends on the characteristics of the cellular layer. A trade-off between tissue fluidity and single-cell deformability controls the assembly of transient rosettes, which are stabilized in the presence of cell self-alignment interactions. This work provides a physical framework for interpreting the organization of the rosette in developing tissues.

title: Connectome Similarity Varies with Global Metastability in Naturalistic fMRI
summary: Abstract Recent evidence supports that non-linear segments of brain activity carries most of the individual-specific information which allows unique identification based on functional connectomes (e.g. connectome fingerprints) in MEG. In fM
content: Abstract Recent evidence supports that non-linear segments of brain activity carries most of the individual-specific information which allows unique identification based on functional connectomes (e.g. connectome fingerprints) in MEG. In fMRI, metastability has emerged as a reliable and robust summary measure of brain dynamics. Here, we set out to test the hypothesis that metastability is associated with connectome fingerprinting in naturalistic fMRI. We further examined whether this putative association varies with time scales, across brain functional networks, and across different movies datasets.We analyzed fMRI data from 86 participants of the Naturalistic Neuroimaging Database. Data was collected during movie-watching of 10 entire movies of different genres. Global and network-level metastability were calculated using an fMRI-appropriate proxy measure based on the variability of spatial dispersion of BOLD activity across regions. The stability within-subject (Iself) and between-subjects similarity (Iothers) of individual functional connectomes were also calculated. Linear mixed-effects models and appropriate contrasts were used to test associations between metastability and fingerprinting indices. At the whole-brain level and considering data from all movies, an association across windows was found between metastability, Iself, and Iothers, with stronger effects and FDR corrected significance observed for larger windows, such as the 600-second window (Iself: b = −0.13, SE = 0.032, p = 0.0015; Iothers: b = −0.23, SE = 0.028, p = 0.0015). Associations were also observed with distinct magnitudes within the eight large-scale functional networks, with particularly strong effects in the Motor Network (Iself: b = −0.34, SE = 0.027, p = 0.0013; Iothers: b = −0.27, SE = 0.021, p = 0.0013). Although no whole-brain differences were observed, movie content exhibited distinct association patterns within networks, notably for the prediction of Iself in the Visual Network for 500 Days of Summer (Δ = −0.22, SE = 0.11, p = 0.044). For Iothers, significant between-movie differences were found in the AMN (Δ = −0.25, SE = 0.062, p = 0.004), Dorsal Attention (Δ = 0.16, SE = 0.08, p = 0.038), Ventral Attention (Δ = 0.14, SE = 0.060, p = 0.034), and Visual Networks (Δ = −0.17, SE = 0.081, p = 0.038). Metastability is systematically related to functional connectome fingerprints. This relationship is time-scale dependent and varies across functional networks. Our findings bridge nonlinear brain dynamics and connectome identifiability, highlighting naturalistic paradigms as a powerful framework for individualized precision neuroimaging.

title: The plasma proteins GSN, F2, CRTAC1, and HP are associated with multigenerational health, longevity, and resilience
summary: Background The risk of chronic diseases and multimorbidity increases with age, yet, individuals of the same age can strongly differ in healthspan, ranging from early manifestation of age-related disease to robust health into very old age. P
content: Background The risk of chronic diseases and multimorbidity increases with age, yet, individuals of the same age can strongly differ in healthspan, ranging from early manifestation of age-related disease to robust health into very old age. Plasma biomarkers, including metabolites and proteins, can capture intrinsic health status, thereby providing insights into the nature of this variation. These biomarkers have been widely explored to understand chronic and early disease risk, but less so for disease resilience in mid- and late-life survival (i.e. after 90 years), or for multigenerational longevity. Methods We quantified 326 plasma proteins using data-independent mass spectrometry in two generations of the Leiden Longevity Study cohort: F1 nonagenarian siblings (late-life; age ≥89; N=852) and F2 offspring and their partners (mid-life; age 30–80; N=2282). Baseline plasma protein levels were tested for association with mid- and late-life survival, with up to 22 years of follow-up, and cardiometabolic healthspan, with up to 16 years of follow-up. By comparing F2 offspring and partners, we tested for plasma proteins associating with familial longevity. Findings Four proteins: gelsolin (GSN), prothrombin (F2), cartilage acidic protein 1 (CRTAC1), and haptoglobin (HP), consistently associated with increased mid- and late-life survival, prolonged cardiometabolic healthspan, and familial longevity; representing overall resilience. Moreover, six proteins: serum amyloid P-component (APCS), complement C7 (C7), ficolin 2 (FCN2), haptoglobin-related protein (HPR), polymeric immunoglobulin receptor (PIGR), and GSN, associated with mortality independent of MetaboHealth, a well-established metabolomics-based mortality score. Interpretation We identified GSN, F2, CRTAC1, and HP as promising candidate indicators of healthy ageing and resilience, meriting further study. Funding ZonMw, LUF, BBMRI-NL, VOILA, DFG, Jörg Bernards-Stiftung, Köln Fortune, and CECAD.

title: Accelerated Online Risk-Averse Policy Evaluation in POMDPs with Theoretical Guarantees and Novel CVaR Bounds
summary: Background: Risk-averse decision-making under partial observability involves evaluating a risk measure, such as the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), of the cumulative return, a computationally demanding task in POMDPs. Objectives: This wor
content: Background: Risk-averse decision-making under partial observability involves evaluating a risk measure, such as the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), of the cumulative return, a computationally demanding task in POMDPs. Objectives: This work introduces a framework for accelerating CVaR value function evaluation by replacing the original POMDP dynamics with a computationally tractable surrogate model while providing formal performance guarantees. Methods: As the mathematical foundation, we derive bounds on the CVaR of a random variable X using an auxiliary random variable Y under assumptions relating their cumulative distribution functions. We introduce a truncation decomposition that separates CVaR estimation from n samples into a data-driven term -- bounded at rate O(1/√n) without support knowledge -- and a tail correction where the support bound enters only through an O(1/n) term, strictly improving existing concentration bounds. These bounds are further tightened via local CDF concentration parameters that exploit the quantile structure of CVaR. Building on this foundation, we establish upper and lower bounds on the CVaR value function computable from a simplified belief-MDP, accommodating general simplifications of the transition dynamics. We develop sample-based estimators for computing these bounds during online policy evaluation with probabilistic performance guarantees. These bounds enable computational acceleration via action elimination: actions whose bounds indicate suboptimality under the simplified model are safely discarded while ensuring consistency with the original POMDP. Results: Empirical evaluation across multiple POMDP domains confirms that the bounds reliably distinguish safe from dangerous policies while achieving 9-21× computational speedups on the evaluated benchmarks. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides a principled and practical approach for accelerating risk-averse policy evaluation in POMDPs, with theoretical guarantees and significant computational gains demonstrated across multiple domains.

title: AI and Stress
summary: ABSTRACT Given the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at work, understanding their health implications is critically important. We use rich survey data from Finland and apply propensity score matching that accounts for observable
content: ABSTRACT Given the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at work, understanding their health implications is critically important. We use rich survey data from Finland and apply propensity score matching that accounts for observable differences between regular AI users and non‐users to estimate the relationship between reported AI usage at work and workers’ reported stress. Regular AI use is associated with a 4.4 percentage point higher probability of reporting stress, equivalent to a 25.6% increase relative to baseline. Comparing two competing explanations, we find that this pattern is more consistent with heavier work demands than with concerns about job loss: AI use is associated with more unpaid work outside working hours and, less precisely, with intense work absorption, but not with job insecurity. Exploratory subgroup estimates are larger and individually significant for men, non‐supervisors, unionized workers and employees in medium‐sized workplaces, although the differences across subgroups are not statistically significant.

title: Optimizing photon-number distributions of Gaussian states in the presence of loss
summary: We analyze the impact of photon loss on the photon-number statistics of Gaussian states. Specifically, we propose and carefully evaluate several methods to mitigate deviations in the photon-number distributions of lossy (displaced) squeezed
content: We analyze the impact of photon loss on the photon-number statistics of Gaussian states. Specifically, we propose and carefully evaluate several methods to mitigate deviations in the photon-number distributions of lossy (displaced) squeezed vacuum states from those of their lossless counterparts. These methods rely on appropriately redefining the parameters of Gaussian states when the loss budget is known in order to recover, as closely as possible, the desired photon-number distribution associated with each target state. While it is intrinsically hard to directly optimize the photon-number distribution of high-dimensional, correlated multimode Gaussian states, the proposed methods are instead based on optimizing specific key properties such as fidelity, phase-space functions, low-order moments of the underlying photon-number statistics, or overlap with the vacuum state. In particular, our results show that optimizing the fidelity between a pure Gaussian target state and a modified Gaussian state that has passed through a loss channel does typically not result in closeness of the corresponding photon-number distributions. Furthermore, we show that correcting for the vacuum overlap minimizes the deviation in the photon-number distribution for large parameter ranges which we explicitly prove for single-mode squeezed vacuum and provide numerical evidence for general (displaced) squeezed vacuum states. As photon loss is a key limitation for Gaussian boson sampling, our results provide insights into the feasibility and limitations of such photonic quantum simulations in lossy environments and offer guidelines for mitigating these imperfections.

title: Information-theoretic bound on thermodynamic efficiency and the generalized Carnot theorem
summary: We derive a bound on the efficiency of thermal engines that can be sharper than Carnot's limit. It is a function of statistical correlations between the engine internal state and Hamiltonian, can be saturated even in finite-time cycles, and
content: We derive a bound on the efficiency of thermal engines that can be sharper than Carnot's limit. It is a function of statistical correlations between the engine internal state and Hamiltonian, can be saturated even in finite-time cycles, and applies to both classical and quantum engines. Specifically, the bound establishes the exact maximal efficiency of engines operating with multiple baths, tightening the upper limit set by Carnot's theorem. Then, we show that an engine made of a quantum dot coupled with fermionic baths can achieve the bound, even when operating beyond the quasistatic regime. The result provides a design principle for realistic energy harvesting machines.

title: Social capital and ambidextrous leadership as drivers of sustainable competitive advantage in export SMEs: The mediating roles of knowledge management and innovation capability -- evidence from Bali, Indonesia
summary: Prior research has examined social capital, leadership, knowledge management, and innovation largely in separation, and it has often treated business performance as if it were sustainable competitive advantage. What remains unclear is how s
content: Prior research has examined social capital, leadership, knowledge management, and innovation largely in separation, and it has often treated business performance as if it were sustainable competitive advantage. What remains unclear is how social capital and ambidextrous leadership are jointly associated with enduring competitiveness through knowledge management and innovation capability, and whether business performance is a distinct pathway. This study investigates those associations in export-oriented small and medium-sized enterprises. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities perspective, survey data were collected from 114 export-oriented SMEs in Bali, Indonesia, and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that social capital and ambidextrous leadership are both positively related to knowledge management, which in turn is associated with stronger innovation capability. Innovation capability is positively related to both business performance and sustainable competitive advantage, whereas business performance is not significantly associated with sustainable competitive advantage. Mediation analysis further indicates that knowledge management mediates the relationships between social capital and ambidextrous leadership and innovation capability. In addition, the serial mediation pathway from ambidextrous leadership to sustainable competitive advantage through knowledge management and innovation capability is significant, whereas the corresponding pathway from social capital is not. These findings suggest that sustainable competitive advantage in export-oriented SMEs is shaped more by capability development than by short-term performance outcomes, and that leadership shows the stronger association with the pathway through which relational resources are linked to sustained strategic value. For managers, the results imply that export SMEs should institutionalize knowledge management practices, develop ambidextrous leadership that balances exploration and exploitation, and invest in innovation capability rather than relying on short-term performance indicators as evidence of enduring competitiveness. The study contributes to strategic management research by clarifying how relational and managerial resources are associated with long-term competitiveness in dynamic export markets.

title: Train Often, Deploy Selectively: Forward-Gated Model Replacement in Crypto Markets
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: Retraining creates a candidate model; it does not establish that the candidate should replace a forecaster that has continued to learn. We introduce Shadow Before Swap (SBS), a deployment policy that warm-refits a challenger off the serving
content: Retraining creates a candidate model; it does not establish that the candidate should replace a forecaster that has continued to learn. We introduce Shadow Before Swap (SBS), a deployment policy that warm-refits a challenger off the serving path, compares it with the maintained incumbent on the same next week of delayed labels, and promotes only after a fixed paired negative-log-likelihood (NLL) advantage. In historical replay over two nonoverlapping Binance episodes totaling 48 UTC weeks, three seeds, eight underlyings, and two perpetual-futures contract types, SBS reduces NLL by 0.1472% relative to calendar replacement, 0.0755% relative to schedule-matched automatic promotion, and 0.0428% relative to continuous maintenance. The corresponding episode-stratified four-week block intervals are 0.1139%–0.1754%, 0.0521%–0.0980%, and 0.0301%–0.0554%. SBS promotes 114 of 528 challengers, reducing deployed model changes by 78.4% compared with automatic promotion while improving the serving trajectory. The direction is unchanged across every seed, one- to three-week trial budgets, four promotion margins, an earlier 20-asset panel, and a topology-matched supervised training objective. SBS also beats a conventional validation-gated promotion rule by 0.1211% and a paired significance-test gate by 0.0343%. The margin implies an explicit per-deployment cost, and gate errors concentrate in low-information trials. Forward authorization is thus a practical control for maintained probabilistic forecasters: better probability forecasts with far fewer state transitions.

title: Why risk‐based premiums will not close the catastrophe protection gap: Conventional pricing, reinsurance capacity, and public scheme design
summary: Abstract Only about one‐fifth to one‐quarter of the economic losses caused by natural catastrophes in the European Union are insured, and the gap is widening as climate‐related losses grow. EIOPA and the ECB have proposed an EU‐level scheme
content: Abstract Only about one‐fifth to one‐quarter of the economic losses caused by natural catastrophes in the European Union are insured, and the gap is widening as climate‐related losses grow. EIOPA and the ECB have proposed an EU‐level scheme combining a public–private reinsurance pool, funded by risk‐based premiums, with a public disaster fund. This paper asks whether risk‐based pricing at a public layer can close a gap that risk‐based pricing at the private layer has not. The capital‐market‐imperfections account of catastrophe insurance failure presupposes a knowable loss distribution; climate non‐stationarity removes that condition, and catastrophe pricing is better understood as conventional valuation under fundamental uncertainty. A five‐equation model of conventional pricing, with a demand side, makes reinsurance capacity endogenously cyclical and generates a rationing ratchet whose threshold is derived analytically and verified by simulation: prices soften within a few periods of a market break while attachment points and terms do not, and once climate‐driven model revisions recur before risk‐adjusted prices recover, rationing ratchets up and the insured share falls persistently. Simulated coverage is 15 points lower under conventional pricing with drifting losses than under a constant‐load benchmark, and the model reproduces the documented moments of the 2022–2026 cycle. Drawing on the French and Spanish schemes, the paper sets out the design features a workable public layer requires: solidarity pricing, an explicit public tail guarantee, and countercyclical funding.

title: Actionable Signals in Prediction Markets: Evaluating Public and Private Information through Systematic Trading
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: Prediction markets aggregate the private beliefs of many participants into publicly observable probability estimates. Beyond prices alone, the trading behavior they generate may reveal public and private signals that are actionable for auto
content: Prediction markets aggregate the private beliefs of many participants into publicly observable probability estimates. Beyond prices alone, the trading behavior they generate may reveal public and private signals that are actionable for automated trading agents. We study whether these observable market signals reliably identify profitable trading opportunities. Specifically, we evaluate two complementary classes of trading signals: Risk Arbitrage , which exploits periods where publicly available information has effectively determined an outcome before prices fully converge, and Information Asymmetry , which exploits large positions accumulated while market prices still reflect substantial uncertainty. Using the complete history of matched trades from Polymarket, spanning 26,964 markets between January 2024 and January 2026, we evaluate the reliability of these two classes of signals. We find that they exhibit markedly different levels of reliability. Risk Arbitrage identifies substantial opportunities around effective resolution but suffers significant losses from false positives, yielding a net loss of $23.4M despite $15.3M in gross profit. Information Asymmetry is considerably more concentrated, generating $139.3M in gross profit but only $7.8M net, with activity overwhelmingly driven by the 2024 U.S. presidential election. Across both regimes, profits concentrate among a small number of accounts, while position size reflects capital commitment more strongly than predictive skill.

title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: When a trader executes a large order, the relevant question is not what will the price be? but what would the price have been had I not traded? Market impact is thus a causal quantity, yet classical models regress price on flow, which is bi
content: When a trader executes a large order, the relevant question is not what will the price be? but what would the price have been had I not traded? Market impact is thus a causal quantity, yet classical models regress price on flow, which is biased whenever informed flow moves prices through information as well as trading. We present a proof-of-concept Causal Market Simulator: a continuous-time causal prior-data fitted network (PFN) trained on a synthetic market prior in which a hidden informational flow confounds the flow–price relation, with confounding strength an exact per-episode knob. The naive estimator’s bias follows a closed form we confirm empirically (up to 68% overestimation), while the PFN approaches the unbiased oracle in the high-confounding regime. Its do-ablated twin, the same model without its intervention inputs, collapses onto the pre-window mean. Zero-shot on ABIDES, the paired causal-minus-ablated prediction difference is + 0.38 pre-onset standard deviations, while independently measured seed-replay mean impact is + 0.28. On about 2,300 detected flow bursts in BTC/ETH/SOL perpetuals and 3,800 Nasdaq equity bursts, the intervention-sensitive predictions are consistent with market impact but cannot establish causal identification without counterfactuals. Off-prior the response degrades gracefully, and split-conformal recalibration restores coverage on held-out ABIDES counterfactuals, while real-market calibration is necessarily factual. Transfer hinges on encoding the metaorder as added flow rather than a clamped flow level. A recurrent state-space variant closes the remaining shape gap: its impact accrues over execution duration where the transformer’s stays flat, raising the correlation with measured metaorder impact from + 0.68 to between + 0.92 and + 0.96, though absolute magnitude still needs per-domain calibration and its training recipe weakens on-prior deconfounding.

title: Leveraging Time-Series Foundation Models for Financial Crime Detection
source: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)
summary: Financial crime detection requires identifying illicit activity within large transaction networks, where suspicious behaviour is rare and unfolds over time. Existing graph-based methods capture relationships among accounts but typically und
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Financial crime detection requires identifying illicit activity within large transaction networks, where suspicious behaviour is rare and unfolds over time. Existing graph-based methods capture relationships among accounts but typically underuse the temporal behaviour encoded in account transaction histories. We introduce Temporal-Context Edge Enrichment (TCEE), a framework that addresses this gap by summarising each account’s transaction history with a frozen time-series foundation model (TSFM), and enriching each transaction’s representation with the relevant temporal context from these summaries. These enriched representations can be scored directly for edge classification, or fed into a graph neural network (GNN) as edge features to capture broader structural information. Across six AMLWorld datasets, TCEE improves PR-AUC over the strongest evaluated baseline on five by a relative \(10.8\%\) on average, while training 6.0 × faster end-to-end. Feeding TCEE’s representations into a GNN raises PR-AUC a further \(4.8\%\) on the four smaller datasets. On an Ethereum phishing dataset, we show that TSFM-generated account representations fed into a GNN are also effective for node classification, improving PR-AUC by \(14.5\%\) over the strongest baseline. As TSFMs continue to advance, our results suggest they can strengthen financial crime detection by capturing temporal signals that complement graph-based approaches.
