title: SOFT SKILLS ЯК ІНСТИТУЦІЙНИЙ ЧИННИК РЕАЛІЗАЦІЇ СОЦІАЛЬНОЇ ТА УПРАВЛІНСЬКОЇ СКЛАДОВИХ ESG-КОНЦЕПЦІЇ СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ
summary: У статті досліджено роль soft skills як інституційного чинника реалізації соціальної та управлінської складових ESG-концепції сталого розвитку. Обґрунтовано, що ефективне впровадження ESG-принципів залежить не лише від формальних політик і
content: У статті досліджено роль soft skills як інституційного чинника реалізації соціальної та управлінської складових ESG-концепції сталого розвитку. Обґрунтовано, що ефективне впровадження ESG-принципів залежить не лише від формальних політик і процедур, а й від сформованих моделей поведінки, комунікації та управлінської взаємодії в організації. На основі узагальнення сучасних наукових досліджень, аналітичних матеріалів обґрунтовано, що однією з ключових перешкод ефективної ESG-реалізації є втрата неформалізованих знань, практичного досвіду та управлінських компетентностей. Доведено, що саме soft skills виступають носіями tacit knowledge (неявних знань), які накопичуються в процесі щоденної професійної діяльності та забезпечують ефективну комунікацію, командну взаємодію, лідерство, довіру, етичну поведінку та відповідальне прийняття рішень. Від рівня розвитку таких компетентностей залежить узгодженість дій працівників, стабільність корпоративного управління і результативність практичного впровадження соціальних та управлінських ESG-принципів.

title: Prof. Judgment Before Answers: Generative AI in First-Year Mathematical Analysis
source: Journal of Education and Culture Studies
summary: Generative AI now produces plausible solutions to many standard exercises in first-year Mathematical Analysis, yet the same systems mishandle quantifier scope, omit essential hypotheses, and invite students to substitute fluent text for mat
content: Generative AI now produces plausible solutions to many standard exercises in first-year Mathematical Analysis, yet the same systems mishandle quantifier scope, omit essential hypotheses, and invite students to substitute fluent text for mathematical judgment. This paper argues that the pedagogical question is not whether GenAI should enter the analysis classroom, but how its use can be designed so that the student, rather than the tool, performs the cognitive labor the course exists to cultivate. Drawing on recent evidence concerning AI in proof-based undergraduate courses, the paper develops a three-principle design framework—tiered access, error-centered inquiry, and judgment-oriented assessment—and instantiates it through worked examples from the first-year syllabus. The examples span limit computations ( and arguments, rationalization, boundedness), integral computations (substitution, integration by parts, symmetry, the Riemann integral and its limitations), and the convergence of function sequences. In each case the AI output is treated not as an answer key but as a case to be diagnosed, and the student's task is to supply the judgment that distinguishes a valid argument from a plausible one.

title: Beyond escape: psychological restoration, nostalgia, and meaning-making in domestic rural tourism destination in Indonesia
summary: Understanding domestic tourists’ motivations for rural tourism requires moving beyond conventional Push-Pull Theory, which often treats motivations as static, decontextualized variables. Such approaches may overlook how tourist motivations
content: Understanding domestic tourists’ motivations for rural tourism requires moving beyond conventional Push-Pull Theory, which often treats motivations as static, decontextualized variables. Such approaches may overlook how tourist motivations are shaped by personal memory, identity, social relationships, and cultural contexts. Addressing this limitation, this study investigates how domestic tourists in Indonesia construct and experience their motivations for visiting rural tourism destinations and how internal and destination-based factors interact. Drawing on in-depth semi-structured interviews with 35 domestic tourists and thematic analysis, the findings identify three interrelated experiential processes: psychological restoration through emotional regulation, nostalgia through the reconstruction of personal and cultural memories, and experiential learning through embodied engagement with rural social life. These findings suggest that rural tourism motivations extend beyond escape and leisure, emerging through tourists’ interactions with destination environments, local communities, and personal histories. Accordingly, push and pull factors are better understood as relationally interpreted processes than as independent motivational antecedents. By conceptualizing rural tourism motivation as a relational and restorative practice embedded in Indonesia’s socio-cultural context, this study advances an interpretive understanding of domestic tourist motivation and offers insights for sustainable rural tourism development.

title: Amyloid formation as local environment-dependent process
summary: Treatment for AD/PD should be based on three solutions: (1) preventing the formation of amyloid fibrils; (2) stopping the propagation of an existing fibril and (3) the potential fragmentation of an existing fibril. Proposals (the first two)
content: Treatment for AD/PD should be based on three solutions: (1) preventing the formation of amyloid fibrils; (2) stopping the propagation of an existing fibril and (3) the potential fragmentation of an existing fibril. Proposals (the first two) for solving this problem at the molecular level are based on method using the analysis of the distribution of hydrophobicity in native proteins compared with this distribution in amyloid forms. This analysis is conducted using the fuzzy oil drop model (FOD-M). The approach based on the polarity/hydrophobicity relationship stems from the water-based environments present within a living organism, as water constitutes the fundamental environment in which proteins are active in living organisms. The main finding is in form of proposed solution for point 1 concerns the identification of factors that alter the characteristics of an aqueous environment acting as an external force field for folding proteins. The proposal for point 2 recalls the solution elaborated by evolution in the case of solenoid proteins using the short polypeptide chains preventing the unlimited propagation. The conclusions arising from the presented analysis lead to proposals for a series of experimental studies to confirm or reject the proposed solutions. The key question, however, is: Why does a fibril structure with unlimited potential for propagation form in the first place? An attempt to answer this question is postulated in this paper. The limitation of the presented model is that it operates on the known structures.

title: Perceived priorities, experiences and provision gaps in urban green spaces: evidence from university students in Pécs, Hungary
summary: Urban green spaces play a vital role in enhancing the liveability and sustainability of cities, particularly for university students. This study applies a socially differentiated importance–experience framework to the evaluation of urban gr
content: Urban green spaces play a vital role in enhancing the liveability and sustainability of cities, particularly for university students. This study applies a socially differentiated importance–experience framework to the evaluation of urban green spaces by university students in Pécs, Hungary. The sample was not representative of the target population, primarily because foreign students were overrepresented. Post-stratification weights were therefore applied to align the sample with the composition of the student population at the University of Pécs. Using these weights, Multiple Factor Analysis identified three dimensions for both the importance and experience measures, as well as six dimensions representing the gap between the corresponding importance and experience ratings. Each dimension was subsequently modelled using post-stratification-weighted linear regression. The explanatory variables describing patterns of green-space use were preselected using the Boruta feature-selection algorithm. The findings reveal substantial importance–experience gaps for several basic attributes, including public toilets, accessibility for people with reduced mobility, benches, cleanliness, waste bins and vegetation. Associations with citizenship and patterns of green space use were dimension-specific rather than indicating consistently less experiences among respondents with foreign citizenship. The results suggest that the students’ evaluations of urban green spaces reflect a multidimensional interplay of practical, environmental, and social attributes. Future research should examine comparative settings and incorporate qualitative methods to explore variation among more precisely defined user groups and across urban contexts. Given the non-representative sample and the aggregation of respondents with foreign citizenship into a single group, the results should be interpreted cautiously, particularly regarding gender-specific patterns and heterogeneity within the foreign-citizenship group.

title: The neural basis of regret and disappointment and its influence on pricing decisions: insights from self-agency and other-agency responsibility pricing experiments
summary: Abstract By incorporating neuroscientific methods into the classical pricing framework, we studied participants' neural responses to regret and disappointment, measured by ERP waveforms and scalp potential spatial distributions. We observed
content: Abstract By incorporating neuroscientific methods into the classical pricing framework, we studied participants' neural responses to regret and disappointment, measured by ERP waveforms and scalp potential spatial distributions. We observed significant neural activation for underpricing and overpricing regret, as well as marginally significant neural activation for underpricing disappointment, whereas no notable activation was found for overpricing disappointment. We found heterogeneity in individual ERP responses and used negative differences in FRN amplitudes across cases as representative variables for underpricing and overpricing regret. These measures were then employed to investigate their effects on participants' pricing behaviors. Our findings contradict the common belief in behavioral economics that individuals strategically make decisions to avoid regret-related negative emotions.

title: Ethics of Generative AI in Translation: Literacy, Guidelines, and Implementation
summary: Advancing research on the ethics of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in translation, this book moves the discussion beyond abstract ethical concerns, towards empirical inquiry and evidence-based recommendations that inform future
content: Advancing research on the ethics of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in translation, this book moves the discussion beyond abstract ethical concerns, towards empirical inquiry and evidence-based recommendations that inform future research and practice. Drawing on three empirical studies involving international samples, this book introduces an empirically grounded ethical-capacity framework that integrates tools for assessing GenAI ethical literacy, practical guidelines developed through expert consensus, and strategies for addressing implementation challenges in professional practice. Ethical capacity is a central theme throughout, emphasising the importance of equipping translators with the knowledge and skills needed to engage responsibly with GenAI, as well as with the professional and institutional support required to put ethical principles into action. An essential resource for researchers in translation technology, AI ethics, and professional ethics, the book will also be valuable to educators, professional translators, language-service providers, translator associations, and policymakers seeking to address the ethical challenges surrounding the use of GenAI in translation.

title: Greenness, Air Pollution, and Insulin Resistance in a Latin American Megacity: A Longitudinal Mediation Analysis of the ELSA‑Brasil Cohort
summary: Abstract Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. The role of air pollution on this association remains unclear. We investigated
content: Abstract Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. The role of air pollution on this association remains unclear. We investigated whether air pollution mediated the association between greenness and insulin resistance, among non-diabetic participants ( N = 2715) from the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA-Brasil) in São Paulo megacity, Brazil, followed-up for approximately 8 years (2008–2010, 2012–2014, 2017–2019). Neighborhood greenness (NDVI, in quartiles), air pollution (PM 2.5 and PM 10 ), and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) were examined using mediation analysis, allowing for exposure-mediator interaction. Total, natural direct, and natural indirect effects were estimated, using mixed-effects models, stratified by the neighborhood socioeconomic status (NSES) and adjusted for individual age, sex, education and income. In PM 10 analysis for participants from low NSES, higher neighborhood greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance, in a dose-response pattern, as indicated by the total ( β = −0.49, 95% CI −0.91, −0.05; β = −0.20, 95% CI −0.54, 0.16; and β = −0.07, 95% CI −0.38, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively) and natural direct effects ( β = −0.59, 95% CI −1.06, −0.09; β = −0.32, 95% CI −0.67, 0.03; and β = −0.05, 95% CI −0.37, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively). The natural indirect effect indicated no mediation by PM 10 . Similar results were found for the PM 2.5 analysis. Greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance among adults living in low NSES areas. However, no evidence of air pollution mediation was found. These results suggest that greater neighborhood greenness may be associated with better cardiometabolic health in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas.

title: GAZ SANOATI KORXONALARIDA YASHIL IQTISODIY FAOLIYATGA TA’SIR ETUVCHI INSTITUTSIONAL, TEXNOLOGIK VA MOLIYAVIY OMILLAR TAHLILI
summary: This article uses a systems approach to analyse the institutional, technological and financial factors affecting the development of green economic activity in gas industry enterprises. Across gas production, processing, transmission and dis
content: This article uses a systems approach to analyse the institutional, technological and financial factors affecting the development of green economic activity in gas industry enterprises. Across gas production, processing, transmission and distribution, energy consumption, methane losses, equipment condition and compliance with environmental requirements are considered key aspects of green transformation. Institutional factors include legislation and standards, public oversight, corporate governance and environmental disclosure; technological factors include equipment modernisation, methane leak detection, energy efficiency and digital monitoring; financial factors cover investment resources, lending conditions, green finance and project returns. The article proposes an analytical matrix for integrated factor diagnosis. The analysis is conceptual and qualitative; in the absence of company-level statistics, no quantitative empirical findings are claimed. The approach can be tested using data from Transgaz

title: Multivalent mRNA tuberculosis vaccines protect against mycobacterial infection in zebrafish, mice and guinea pigs
summary: Despite a century of BCG use, tuberculosis remains a leading cause of death from infectious diseases and more effective vaccines are urgently needed. Here we combined antigen discovery in zebrafish with mRNA vaccine technology to generate m
content: Despite a century of BCG use, tuberculosis remains a leading cause of death from infectious diseases and more effective vaccines are urgently needed. Here we combined antigen discovery in zebrafish with mRNA vaccine technology to generate multivalent vaccine candidates, TUmRNA 4 , TUmRNA 6 and TUmRNA 9 , encoding four, six, or nine Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens, respectively. The vaccines were well tolerated, and induced robust antigen-specific cellular immune responses, including IFNγ production and expansion of memory T-cell populations. In mice, TUmRNA 4 and TUmRNA 6 reduced pulmonary M. tuberculosis burden and lung pathology to levels comparable to BCG vaccination and TUmRNA 6 enhanced BCG-mediated protection when used as a booster vaccine. In guinea pigs, TUmRNA 9 reduced bacterial burden in the lungs, spleen, and lymph nodes and decreased pulmonary lesions. These findings demonstrate that protective antigens identified in zebrafish can be translated into effective multivalent mRNA vaccines and establish a framework for tuberculosis vaccine development across multiple preclinical models.

title: Modeling and application of multi-objective optimization algorithm in green asset allocation
summary: Faced with the multi-objective conflict problem of risk minimisation and environmental benefit maximisation in green asset allocation, the traditional single-objective optimisation method has obvious limitations. This study innovatively pro
content: Faced with the multi-objective conflict problem of risk minimisation and environmental benefit maximisation in green asset allocation, the traditional single-objective optimisation method has obvious limitations. This study innovatively proposes a hybrid multi-objective optimisation algorithm (HMOA). The algorithm combines the Pareto optimisation ability of the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm 2 (NSGA-II), the dynamic convergence of particle swarm optimisation, and the subjective viewpoint quantification mechanism of the Black–Litterman model; it introduces a displacement fluctuation strategy to enhance diversity and uses a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to dynamically generate prior information. The test results show that HMOA is significantly better than the baseline model in terms of hypervolume (HV) = 0.85, inversion generation distance = 0.12, and other indicators (such as 8.97% higher than the HV of NSGA-II). In practical verification, its Sharpe ratio reached 1.25, and its carbon dioxide (CO2) emission reduction reached 1.256 million tons of carbon dioxide. In addition, the robustness test shows that the HV change rate of the algorithm is only 5.2% under noise, which proves that the algorithm can effectively balance multi-objective conflicts. Therefore, this study provides a new method with complete theory and strong practicability for green asset allocation, and promotes the innovative application of multi-objective optimisation theory in sustainable finance.

title: The Agrarian Matrix: A Conceptual Agriculture–Energy–Telecommunications Framework for Rural Infrastructure in Nigeria
summary: Nigeria’s rural economy is constrained at the same time by unreliable electricity, high post-harvest losses and uneven telecommunications coverage, yet these problems are planned and financed in separate sectoral programmes. This article is
content: Nigeria’s rural economy is constrained at the same time by unreliable electricity, high post-harvest losses and uneven telecommunications coverage, yet these problems are planned and financed in separate sectoral programmes. This article is a desk-based conceptual study; it is not a deployed or experimentally validated system. It proposes the “Agrarian Matrix”, a framework in which agricultural production, embedded electronic systems and telecommunications infrastructure are designed together around shared solar-powered rural infrastructure. Using a purposive, tiered compilation of secondary evidence from regulatory, multilateral, peer-reviewed, programme and media sources, the study reports that rural electricity access was about 33% in 2023 against about 89% in urban areas (access, not reliability); that the grid has about 13,000 MW of installed capacity but only 5,151 MW was available for dispatch in December 2025, with delivered energy lower still; and that reported post-harvest losses range from 5–20% for grains to 50–60% for tubers, fruits and vegetables, with a media-reported valuation of about ₦3.5 trillion a year that could not be verified against primary data. The framework comprises a five-layer node architecture, illustrative sizing assumptions, three testable hypotheses on the benefits of co-engineering, and a phased roadmap. Components of the framework have been piloted separately in Nigeria, but no integrated field validation exists, so the benefits attributed to co-engineering remain hypotheses. The contribution is an organising framework and research agenda; scenario-based techno-economic analysis and paired pilot comparisons are the priority next steps.

title: Operationalizing green governance and environmental SDGs through local planning and budgeting in federal Nepal: Evidence from Palpa district
summary: Local governments are increasingly responsible for translating environment-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into practical actions, yet evidence remains limited on whether national commitments materially shape local plans, budge
content: Local governments are increasingly responsible for translating environment-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into practical actions, yet evidence remains limited on whether national commitments materially shape local plans, budgets, and implementation in federal Nepal. This study aims to assess how green governance and environmental SDGs 6, 11, 13, and 15 are operationalized through planning and budgeting in four local governments of Palpa District. A qualitative-dominant mixed-methods case study combines national and local policy and planning documents, five fiscal years of budget and expenditure data, 31 key informant interviews, and six focus group discussions. Results show that all periodic plans reference the SDGs, but measurable environmental targets and indicators remain weak. Environmental SDG-related expenditure accounts for approximately 6.0% to 18.2% of total expenditure across cases and years, with allocations concentrated on SDG 6 and SDG 11, while SDG 13 and especially SDG 15 receive smaller and more fragmented funding. Intergovernmental fiscal rules, limited technical capacity, political incentives for visible projects, and unequal participation help explain the gap between policy commitments and budget choices. The study concludes that stronger environmental budget tagging, performance-linked grants, measurable indicators, and local technical capacity are required to convert SDG references into sustained environmental outcomes.

title: AlphaScreen profiling of extracellular vesicle-associated platelet, immune, and vascular markers reveals disease-specific signatures in ME/CFS, fibromyalgia, and long COVID
summary: Introduction: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), fibromyalgia (FM), and long COVID (LC-19) are chronic diseases with overlapping clinical features and poorly understood pathophysiology. Increasing evidence suggests
content: Introduction: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), fibromyalgia (FM), and long COVID (LC-19) are chronic diseases with overlapping clinical features and poorly understood pathophysiology. Increasing evidence suggests the involvement of immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered vascular physiology. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication and are envisioned as sensors of homeostasis and disease. The aim of this study was to determine whether EV marker profiling could provide a basis for the differential diagnosis of ME/CFS, FM and LC-19 and/or patient stratification. Methods: EV-enriched plasma from ME/CFS, FM, cases co-diagnosed with ME/CFS and FM, LC-19 patients, and matched healthy controls (n = 10 per study group) were analyzed. EV concentration and size distribution were assessed by nanoparticle tracking analysis, followed by targeted profiling of EV-associated surface markers via AlphaScreen, including tetraspanins CD9 and CD63, platelet- (CD41/CD61), myeloid- (CD13), immune- (CD74 and CX3CR1), and renin-angiotensin system- associated ACE1 (also known as CD143), and ACE2 surface markers. Results: The studied disease groups presented distinct EV signatures. LC-19 samples exhibited the most pronounced and coordinated alterations, characterized by increased levels of CD9/CD74, CD9/CX3CR1, and CD9/ACE1-positive EVs, along with reduced overall particle concentrations. Notably, platelet-derived CD9/CD41/CD61-positive EVs were significantly elevated in both LC-19 and ME/CFS, as compared to healthy controls, indicating enhanced platelet activation. Immune-associated markers revealed differential pathway activation in LC-19, with CD74-positive EVs reflecting antigen presentation and inflammatory signaling, and CX3CR1-positive EVs indicating altered leukocyte trafficking and vascular interaction. Increased ACE1-positive EVs in LC-19 further suggested a shift toward pro-inflammatory renin-angiotensin signaling. Conclusion: Collectively, these findings support a disease-specific dysregulation of platelet, immune, and vascular pathways. The integrated EV signatures distinguish LC-19 from the related chronic conditions ME/CFS and FM, highlighting the potential of EV-based profiling for differential diagnosis. Our results provide a systems-level perspective on the differential pathophysiology of these disorders and identify EV-associated markers as candidate biomarkers with clinical value.

title: Bio-ILs: Sustainable Biosurfactant-Derived Ionic Liquids Based on Rhamnolipid against Listeria monocytogenes
summary: Abstract Surfactants (surface-active agents) have dual characteristics of hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity, which lead them to concentrate at interfaces, as well as to aggregate into several supramolecular architectures, thereby conferring
content: Abstract Surfactants (surface-active agents) have dual characteristics of hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity, which lead them to concentrate at interfaces, as well as to aggregate into several supramolecular architectures, thereby conferring unique physicochemical properties. The possibility of exploring these properties in combination with ionic liquids (ILs) has gained significant attention in recent years. In this work, a biosurfactant produced by a microbial strain, rhamnolipid (RL), a glycolipid with l-rhamnose and β-hydroxy fatty acids, isolated from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, was paired in its anionic form with cations of interest to synthesize ILs for antimicrobial applications. The new RL-based ILs (RL-ILs) were prepared using sustainable processes and then tested on several bacteria, yielding a promising minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.21 mg/mL for [EMIM][RL] on Listeria monocytogenes. The use of RL-ILs represents a bacteriostatic approach, which is less likely to promote resistant bacterial populations, compared with strategies based on traditional drugs. The resulting RL-ILs were comprehensively characterized using established analytical techniques, including nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), among others. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first demonstration of biosurfactants serving as ionic liquid anions. This establishes a new class of bio-derived ILs (bio-ILs) with unique amphiphilic and supramolecular properties, expanding the design principles of ionic liquids beyond conventional synthetic salts.

title: Seasonal Digital Coordination in Hani Terrace Farming: A Longitudinal Field Study of WeChat–SMS Infrastructure in Rural Yunnan, China
summary: Abstract Background Rice terrace farmers in remote mountainous areas have long struggled to access agricultural information easily, coordinate collective efforts, and address shared resource dilemmas for which straightforward remedies are l
content: Abstract Background Rice terrace farmers in remote mountainous areas have long struggled to access agricultural information easily, coordinate collective efforts, and address shared resource dilemmas for which straightforward remedies are lacking. While mobile-based communication systems seem to provide a frugal solution to these structural barriers, systematic field data documenting real-world adoption patterns, realized economic gains, and emergent friction remains limited. This empirical gap is particularly acute for the ethnic minority farming systems of Southwest China, where traditional social structures, land management, and linguistic traditions differ significantly from those in the African and South Asian contexts typically examined in the current literature. Methods We tracked 300 Hani terrace farmers over 12 months (January–December 2025) in rural Yunnan Province, using a mixed-methods design that combined structured platform logs, monthly interaction records, coordination event documentation, information flow assessments, and an obstacle register spanning five data instruments. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative obstacle narratives were thematically coded. Results Platform membership grew nearly eightfold, from 37 to 295 members, representing 98.3% adoption by December. Forty coordination events yielded combined economic savings of ¥28,040 (mean ¥701 per event; median ¥300), with labor coordination accounting for the largest share (32.5%). Information delivery accelerated by up to 350-fold for market prices, and trust scores for market and weather data doubled from 2 to 4 on a five-point scale. However, active participation averaged only 23.7% across the year, and 45% of the 40 recorded obstacles were only partially resolved. Conclusions WeChat and SMS platforms can work as real coordination infrastructure in smallholder terrace farming, but their benefits are bunched in particular seasons, concentrated in specific functions, and contingent on social and institutional conditions that technology alone cannot create. Design implications, policy recommendations, and directions for future research are discussed.

title: Brazilian Diaspora in the Czech Republic: An Ethnographic Probe into the Brazilian Community
summary: This research draws on an online survey and semi-structured qualitative interviews with Brazilians living in the Czech Republic. Despite the limitation of a relatively small sample size, this research offers a compelling exploration of the
content: This research draws on an online survey and semi-structured qualitative interviews with Brazilians living in the Czech Republic. Despite the limitation of a relatively small sample size, this research offers a compelling exploration of the Brazilian community's life in the Czech Republic, contributing to a broader understanding of diaspora dynamics in the region. While the number of Brazilians in the Czech Republic remains low and there are no significant historical ties between the countries, it nevertheless represents an important research topic in the field of ‘new diasporas’ that may arise in different parts of the world. In our paper, we discuss different themes that relate to the migrants’ experience of living abroad and how they conceptualise their Brazilian identity under new conditions. We use an interpretive approach to understand the subjective meanings ascribed by the members of the diaspora to relations in the country of origin and in the Czech Republic.

title: Marsupial fossil tracks reveal Eocene arboreal life in Antarctica
summary: Antarctica is the only continent where land mammals are extinct today. Before the Eocene-Oligocene boundary (>38 million years ago), however, the "white continent" had a much milder climate that sustained a diverse fauna of terrestrial mamm
content: Antarctica is the only continent where land mammals are extinct today. Before the Eocene-Oligocene boundary (>38 million years ago), however, the "white continent" had a much milder climate that sustained a diverse fauna of terrestrial mammals. Several discoveries of fragmentary Eocene fossils suggest that Antarctica acted as a land bridge connecting South America to Australia, most notably marsupials. However, fossil mammals are scarce and restricted to a single location-Seymour Island. Here we present two well-preserved fossil tracks which are the second Antarctic fossil mammal outside Seymour Island and the oldest fossil tracks assigned to an opossum-like animal in the Cenozoic. They were found in the Fossil Hill Formation on King George Island (lower-middle Eocene) and exhibit possible opposable thumbs, suggesting an arboreal behavior observable in microbiotheriid and some extant didelphid marsupials living in South America today. They further coincide in time with the rise of scansorial lifestyle in several mammalian lineages. This ichnologic record offers a more comprehensive look into the dispersion and ecology of mammals through the Early Cenozoic of Antarctica, evidencing that small arboreal marsupials inhabited the South Shetland Islands during the Eocene. In addition, the new finding indicates that Antarctica was not merely a corridor, but a rich habitat of dense and productive forest canopies during the middle Eocene.

title: Why Does Gamification Fail? The Impact Mechanisms of Gamification Design Flaws on Consumers' Continuous Purchase Intention
summary: ABSTRACT Although e‐commerce platforms widely implement gamification designs, the potential negative effects on consumers and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, this study employs a two‐stage mixed‐methods approa
content: ABSTRACT Although e‐commerce platforms widely implement gamification designs, the potential negative effects on consumers and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, this study employs a two‐stage mixed‐methods approach to uncover the influence mechanisms of gamification design flaws. In Study 1, we collected 24,749 consumer comments describing negative experiences with gamified shopping festivals. By combining BERTopic modeling with a human‐LLM collaboration, we identified seven latent concepts. Further analysis grounded in psychological reactance theory and affective events theory indicated that four gamification design flaws, namely narrative rhythm disruption, game interaction complexity, reward value distortion, and gameplay replaceability, affect consumers' continuous purchase intention through perceived manipulation and frustration. In Study 2, we collected survey responses from 398 consumers who participated in the gamified shopping festivals and used PLS‐SEM to test the proposed hypotheses. This research deepens understanding of the adverse side of gamification, contributes to theoretical perspectives on the mechanisms of gamification design flaws, and provides novel insights for optimizing gamification in e‐commerce platforms.

title: The Effect of Financial Literacy and Financial Planning on the Financial Control Ability of MSMEs
summary: Financial control is a critical managerial function for MSME sustainability because it enables owners to compare actual outcomes with plans, identify deviations, and take corrective action. This study examines the associations of financial
content: Financial control is a critical managerial function for MSME sustainability because it enables owners to compare actual outcomes with plans, identify deviations, and take corrective action. This study examines the associations of financial literacy and financial planning ability with financial control ability among MSMEs. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted using purposive sampling of 91 MSME owners or managers who completed 24 five-point Likert items. Variable scores were calculated as item means and analyzed using multiple linear regression, supported by reliability assessment, residual diagnostics, and HC3 robust standard errors. Mean scores for financial literacy, financial planning, and financial control were 4.615, 3.892, and 4.369, respectively. Financial literacy (B=0.332; β=0.331; p<0.001) and financial planning (B=0.317; β=0.655; p<0.001) were positively associated with financial control. The model was significant, F(2,88)=136.829; p<0.001, with R²=75.67%. However, financial control reliability was low (α=0.424), and residuals were non-normal. The findings suggest that financial planning has a stronger standardized association with financial control than financial literacy, although interpretation should remain exploratory because of measurement-quality limitations and the observational design.

title: SST‑Gradient Driven Asymmetric Decline of Coastal Wind Power in Northwest Africa: Multi‑Model Attribution and Projections to 2100
summary: Abstract This study quantifies the asymmetric decline in wind power density along Morocco's Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts and develops a multi-model projection framework. Analysis of ERA5 reanalysis data (1981–2020), evaluated against i
content: Abstract This study quantifies the asymmetric decline in wind power density along Morocco's Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts and develops a multi-model projection framework. Analysis of ERA5 reanalysis data (1981–2020), evaluated against independent NASA POWER, MERRA-2, and NOAA OISST datasets, reveals a pronounced north–south contrast: the southern coast exhibits wind power density approximately 1.6 times higher than the northern coast, whereas the northern region shows 1.9 times greater inter-annual variability and an 11% faster rate of decline. A Random Forest attribution model identifies the Mediterranean–Canary Current sea-surface-temperature gradient as a dominant predictor of the north–south wind-speed differential, with the two SST predictors accounting for approximately 68% of the total permutation importance. The statistical relationship is consistent with a physical mechanism involving differential ocean warming and associated changes in the regional pressure gradient. Comparative analysis of constrained linear, logistic, quadratic, and CMIP6-informed projection approaches indicates that methodological choice introduces a 10–20-year range in projected threshold-crossing times. Five CMIP6 models were used to characterize structural model uncertainty under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5. The results indicate substantially earlier loss of the 150 W m⁻² viability threshold in the northern region than in the southern region, although the precise crossing time depends strongly on the projection method and emissions scenario. These findings highlight the importance of physically informed, multi-model approaches for assessing climate-related risks to coastal wind-energy resources in Morocco.

title: Volumetric Titrations with (Non-)Visual Indicators: How Low-Cost Assistive Technology Can Make Existing Experiments More Accessible
summary: Abstract Quality education is one of the requirements for sustainable development, as identified by the United Nations. Achieving this goal requires educational practices that are accessible and understandable for all students, including th
content: Abstract Quality education is one of the requirements for sustainable development, as identified by the United Nations. Achieving this goal requires educational practices that are accessible and understandable for all students, including those with disabilities. Traditional chemistry teaching experiments, such as volumetric titrations, often rely on visual indicators to demonstrate chemical changes in solution and are often used to teach chemical equilibria. However, different students may perceive color changes differently, affecting their learning experience. To address this challenge, this paper presents a framework for creating alternative representations of solution color change in real time during volumetric titration experiments, relying on low-cost and easy-to-fabricate assistive technologies. Our proposed framework allows for the real-time translation of solution color changes to other sensory stimuli, like sound, and can be used to support accessible education in accordance with the principles of the universal design for learning. We take this approach to neutralization and redox volumetric titrations, making these practices, which rely on visual indicators of the equivalence point, more accessible in educational chemistry laboratories.

title: The Cost of Scientific Knowledge in the Era of Open Access: Economic Equity, Academic Integrity, and the Sustainability of Scholarly Publishing
summary: BACKGROUND: Open Access (OA) has fundamentally transformed scholarly communication by enabling free and unrestricted online access to research publications. However, removing price barriers for readers does not automatically eliminate under
content: BACKGROUND: Open Access (OA) has fundamentally transformed scholarly communication by enabling free and unrestricted online access to research publications. However, removing price barriers for readers does not automatically eliminate underlying economic, structural, and institutional inequalities. In business models financed through Article Processing Charges (APCs), a substantial portion of the financial burden is shifted from users onto authors and their home institutions, thereby creating new forms of exclusion for less-funded research environments. OBJECTIVE: To conduct a comprehensive analytical and critical evaluation of the distribution of costs, benefits, and socio-economic implications in contemporary scholarly publishing. Particular focus is directed toward the equity of various OA models, the position of researchers from developing and smaller academic systems, and the essential conditions required for the sustainable development and digital transformation of scholarly journals in Macedonia. METHODS: A narrative, conceptual-analytical approach was applied, drawing upon thematic synthesis of the presentation “The Price of Knowledge” (Open Access Week, 2 November 2026), international declarations (Budapest BOAI, UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science, DORA Declaration, Leiden Manifesto), framework documents (Action Plan for Diamond OA, DIAMAS project), and contemporary literature on Open Science and scholarly publishing. RESULTS: The analysis reveals that Open Access does not eliminate the economic costs of scholarly publishing, but rather redistributes them across stakeholders. The traditional subscription model imposes severe access barriers for readers, whereas Gold OA financed through APCs creates substantial barriers for authors lacking research grants or institutional backing. Diamond OA and Green OA models offer equitable avenues to eliminate financial barriers, yet their long-term sustainability hinges upon stable institutional infrastructure, consortium funding, explicit Creative Commons licensing, and permanent digital preservation. Editorial and peer-review labour, server infrastructure, and the environmental footprint represent essential components of the total cost of scholarly communication. CONCLUSION: A fair and sustainable scholarly publishing ecosystem must simultaneously guarantee universal access for readers, equal publishing opportunities for authors, and independent research integrity. For the Macedonian context, institutional support for Diamond OA journals, the development of robust institutional repositories, financial transparency, and formal recognition of editorial and peer-review contributions within academic promotion criteria are recommended.

title: Have we already lost it? Geoprivacy in the age of AI, uncertainty, and corporate gatekeeping
summary: Geoprivacy is often framed as a problem of protecting coordinates, masking traces, or managing user consent. This framing is now insufficient. In an era of pervasive datafication, AI-enabled inference, platform dependence, and corporate con
content: Geoprivacy is often framed as a problem of protecting coordinates, masking traces, or managing user consent. This framing is now insufficient. In an era of pervasive datafication, AI-enabled inference, platform dependence, and corporate control over location and mobility data, the central question is no longer whether exact locations can be hidden, but whether meaningful control over location-derived knowledge remains possible at all. This paper asks: have we already lost geoprivacy? We argue that geoprivacy has not disappeared, but its conditions have fundamentally changed. Location data are now continuously produced through everyday digital participation, linked across platforms and modalities, and transformed by machine learning, large language models, and agentic systems into sensitive inferences about identity, behavior, association, vulnerability, and future action. At the same time, risks and protections are unevenly distributed: privacy increasingly functions as socioeconomic, political, and institutional privilege, while marginalized communities, sensitive places, non-human environments, and collective forms of knowledge face heightened exposure and risk. These challenges are intensified by corporate gateke eping, regulatory lag, harmful defaults, limited transparency, and epistemic blind spots within existing geoprivacy norms and directions. We therefore reposition geoprivacy as a socio-technical, legal, institutional, and political problem, not merely a technical one. Looking forward, we outline responsibilities for policymakers, researchers, communities, and industry, including privacy-protective defaults, regulation of spatial inference, public-good data governance, geoprivacy literacy, cyber-threat exercises, and community-controlled infrastructures. Rather than declaring geoprivacy lost, we argue that it must be continually renegotiated as a moving boundary, one that requires GI science to act not only as a technical field, but as a bridge between spatial reasoning, governance, justice, and democratic control over location-based data and futures.

title: Twenty‐Year Forecast of Thoracic Surgeon Demand in Chile: Simulated Scenarios Using Bayesian Methods and Publicly Available Data
summary: INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots ne
content: INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years. METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024). Surgeons practicing cardiac or vascular surgery, retirees, and those living abroad were excluded. A Bayesian projection model was developed that incorporates parameters such as retirement age, entry of new surgeons (including graduates and foreign-certified individuals), accidental mortality, population growth, and dynamic demand growth. Monte Carlo simulations (1000 iterations) were conducted across five scenarios (1 to 5 graduates/year, plus one certified surgeon/year). Absolute error analysis identified the optimal annual number of new graduates. RESULTS: Of the 107 thoracic surgeons listed in Chile, only 67 were actively practicing non-cardiac thoracic surgery. The majority were concentrated in the Metropolitan Region (capital). Sex distribution was predominantly male (83.5%), with a mean age of 50.2 years. The corrected model (using 67 active surgeons as the baseline) shows that a scenario with 1 graduate per year results in a projected shortage, while scenarios with 3-5 graduates per year lead to potential oversupply. The optimal scenario, minimizing supply-demand mismatch, was training approximately two to three surgeons per year (2.6 graduates/year). CONCLUSIONS: Strategic workforce planning is essential to avoid future imbalances in thoracic surgeon availability. Bayesian modeling provides a robust framework for anticipating demand, guiding training capacity, and ensuring equitable distribution across regions, thereby avoiding both shortages and saturation of the specialty in Chile.

title: Phylogenomics and taxonomic revision of Macropeplus (Monimiaceae, Laurales) reveal a remarkable hidden species and its unique habitat
summary: Abstract Macropeplus is endemic to Brazil and found above 1000 m elevation in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado . Until this work, the four recognised species M. dentatus , M. friburgensis , M. ligustrinus and M. schwackeanus were initially s
content: Abstract Macropeplus is endemic to Brazil and found above 1000 m elevation in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado . Until this work, the four recognised species M. dentatus , M. friburgensis , M. ligustrinus and M. schwackeanus were initially separated by morphology and geographical distribution, with allopatric ranges. However, increased specimen collection and digital data have since revealed overlapping traits and sympatric distributions, making species delimitation challenging. This highlights the need for a new taxonomic revision incorporating molecular phylogenetics. Despite recent advances in molecular studies clarifying Monimiaceae classification, phylogenetic relationships among its genera and species remain underexplored. In this work, we present a molecular phylogeny of Macropeplus using the Angiosperm353 toolkit based on 23 specimens, assessing its monophyly, species relationships, and position within the family. Based on its phylogeny, we provide the taxonomic revision, typifications of all species, plus botanical plates, distribution maps, conservation assessments, as well as the discovery of a cryptic species occurring in the Campos Rupestres , an unexpected habitat.

title: Internal marketing and employee performance in higher education: the mediating role of self-motivation
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: This study aims to evaluate the impact of internal marketing on the creative performance of university officers in Bangladesh. Furthermore, it investigates the mediating effect of self-motivation on the relationships between these personal
content: This study aims to evaluate the impact of internal marketing on the creative performance of university officers in Bangladesh. Furthermore, it investigates the mediating effect of self-motivation on the relationships between these personal characteristics and creative performance. The present study adopts a quantitative research design, utilizing primary data collected through a structured questionnaire. Data were obtained from a sample of 350 officers representing 30 purposively selected private universities in Bangladesh. The collected data were subsequently analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results reveal that personality traits and creativity relevant personal characteristics significantly influence institutional performance. Moreover, self-motivation mediates the relationship between personality traits, creativity relevant personal characteristics and creative performance. Private universities should revise their recruitment, appraisal, and training practices. Secondly, job enrichment strategies should be enriched. Thirdly, organizational culture should value learning, experimentation, and psychological safety. Finally, national regulatory bodies like UGC can incentivize creativity of officers.

title: Beyond Patents: External R&D Conditions, Organisational Capabilities, and Technical Efficiency in Agri‐Food Firms
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether the external R&D environment is associated with the technical efficiency of agri‐food firms and whether this relationship differs between patenting and non‐patenting enterprises. Using 1668 observations
content: ABSTRACT This study examines whether the external R&D environment is associated with the technical efficiency of agri‐food firms and whether this relationship differs between patenting and non‐patenting enterprises. Using 1668 observations for 243 firms over 2004–2021, including 27 patenting and 216 non‐patenting firms, with substantially broader coverage from 2012 onwards, the analysis applies conditional data envelopment analysis (DEA), complemented by firm fixed‐effects regressions and a Simar–Wilson bootstrapped truncated regression. Comparing conditional and unconditional frontiers shows that external R&D conditions alter firms' positions relative to the production frontier. The preferred fixed‐effects specification finds no robust differential association by patenting status after controlling for persistent firm heterogeneity and year shocks. The complementary Simar–Wilson analysis suggests a stronger association among non‐patenting firms and no significant association among patenting firms, consistent with a possible compensatory role of external R&D conditions. These associations are non‐causal and highlight the organisational relevance of external knowledge and innovation ecosystems.

title: Servant Leadership, Organizational Commitment, and Work Ability in Relation to Employee Motivation and Performance in the Samarinda City Government
summary: This study examines the relationships of servant leadership, organizational commitment, and work ability with work motivation and employee performance among part-time Government Employees with Work Agreements (PPPK) in the Samarinda City Go
content: This study examines the relationships of servant leadership, organizational commitment, and work ability with work motivation and employee performance among part-time Government Employees with Work Agreements (PPPK) in the Samarinda City Government. The study addresses the need to strengthen employee motivation and performance following the integration of part-time PPPK into the public-sector workforce. A quantitative explanatory design was applied to 215 part-time PPPK employees across six Samarinda City Government agencies. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS. The results show that servant leadership significantly affects work motivation (β = 0.477, p < 0.001), as does organizational commitment (β = 0.455, p < 0.001). Work ability does not significantly affect work motivation (β = 0.038, p = 0.395), but significantly affects employee performance (β = 0.470, p < 0.001). Work motivation also significantly affects employee performance (β = 0.484, p < 0.001), while servant leadership and organizational commitment have no significant direct effects on performance. Indirect effects indicate that work motivation significantly mediates the relationships of servant leadership and organizational commitment with employee performance. The findings suggest that improving PPPK performance requires strengthening work ability and motivation, supported by servant leadership and organizational commitment. The study contributes empirical evidence on human resource management among part-time PPPK employees in local government.

title: ‘The More We Could Be Involved in Stuff, the More Effective It'd Be’: The Need for More Employer Involvement in Active Labour Market Policy
summary: ABSTRACT While internationally, interest has grown in employer engagement with active labour market policy (ALMP), their involvement in policy development has been limited—especially in liberal market economies, which lack the institutional
content: ABSTRACT While internationally, interest has grown in employer engagement with active labour market policy (ALMP), their involvement in policy development has been limited—especially in liberal market economies, which lack the institutional frameworks and traditions of social partnership observed elsewhere. Applying a social dialogue lens to interviews with 124 employers, policymakers and other social actors in the UK context, we consider its potential expressive and instrumental functions, and the extent to which facilitating conditions exist to enable it. As in‐work poverty and poor job quality present key intractable challenges for policymakers at national and local levels, we present a revival in social dialogue in ALM policymaking as a critical factor for preventing institutional failure and unlocking innovative policy solutions, especially where supporting people to access and progress in ‘good work’ is a policy priority.

title: Monitoring‐to‐Response Systems for Human‐Elephant Coexistence in Yunnan, China: Lessons From a Decade of Early Warning
summary: ABSTRACT Introduction The recovery and range expansion of Chinese Asian elephants in Yunnan have increased human–elephant spatial overlap, driving demands for conflict mitigation and targeted conservation tools. Yunnan's Monitoring and Earl
content: ABSTRACT Introduction The recovery and range expansion of Chinese Asian elephants in Yunnan have increased human–elephant spatial overlap, driving demands for conflict mitigation and targeted conservation tools. Yunnan's Monitoring and Early‐Warning System (MEWS) integrates elephant detection, manual verification, alert release and joint response. Aim We review the decade‐long development and application of MEWS across elephant habitats in Yunnan, summarizing empirical experiences and key lessons learned. Methods Using triangulation, we synthesize evidence from peer‐reviewed literature, technical documents, procurement records, practitioner reports and media sources. Results Among the 80 MEWS‐related sources, grey literature and media articles focus almost exclusively on platform technical performance and development, whereas the 27 peer‐reviewed publications are skewed heavily toward population monitoring, conservation applications and habitat‐related analysis. Critically, peer‐reviewed work drawing on MEWS to examine elephant social behaviour and fine‐scale movement ecology is nearly absent, constituting a substantial knowledge gap for Asian elephant research in this region. Discussion Available evidence on MEWS indicates substantial deployment, high local uptake, rapid warning dissemination, and practical value for real‐time tracking and incident management. Current evaluations are strongest for operational outputs and intermediate performance indicators, while formal assessment of long‐term social and conservation outcomes remains limited. Beyond immediate risk mitigation, MEWS generates geo‐referenced and time‐stamped data that have supported population assessment, habitat‐suitability modelling, conflict‐risk mapping, and studies of elephant movement and group organization. Key challenges include interoperability, data governance, long‐term financing, staff capacity, and transferability beyond China. These challenges must be addressed to sustain MEWS performance and increase the long‐term management and research value of MEWS‐derived data. Conclusion MEWS should be viewed not as a single replicable blueprint, but as a monitoring‐to‐response architecture whose core design principles—multi‐sensor detection, human‐in‐the‐loop verification, multi‐channel warning, and coordinated response—can inform conflict mitigation for elephants and other large mammals in human‐dominated landscapes.

title: A New Galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source Candidate
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Abstract The identification of a new galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source (CBSS) candidate, whose main ID is ZTF J043609.49+364057.7, is presented on the basis of the analysis of its optical spectrum, light curve and Spectral Energy Distr
content: Abstract The identification of a new galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source (CBSS) candidate, whose main ID is ZTF J043609.49+364057.7, is presented on the basis of the analysis of its optical spectrum, light curve and Spectral Energy Distribution (SED). During a survey designed to find candidates to the aforementioned class independently of X-ray emissions, this object’s optical spectrum was found to exhibit the typical emission features expected for a CBSS. The available photometric data show a quasi-sinusoidal modulation, with a period of 5.42 h, compatible with the orbital modulation of the system. Although there is no current identification of X-ray emission from this source, its SED displays a highly absorbed bright FUV component, given the estimated E(B − V) ~ 0.7 mag.

title: Peran Informasi ESG dalam Pasar Saham: Systematic Literature Review atas Reaksi Investor, Kualitas Informasi, dan Risiko Crash Harga Saham
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) menjadi bagian penting bagi investor dalam pengambilan keputusan dan penilaian perusahaan di pasar modal. Namun, pengaruh ESG terhadap harga saham tidak selalu menunjukkan pola yang seragam. Penel
content: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) menjadi bagian penting bagi investor dalam pengambilan keputusan dan penilaian perusahaan di pasar modal. Namun, pengaruh ESG terhadap harga saham tidak selalu menunjukkan pola yang seragam. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji secara sistematis hubungan antara ESG dan harga saham dengan menitikberatkan pada tiga aspek utama, yaitu reaksi investor, kualitas informasi ESG, dan risiko stock price crash. Penelitian dilakukan melalui systematic literature review terhadap artikel yang membahas ESG dan pasar modal dalam berbagai konteks negara dan periode penelitian. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ESG dapat memengaruhi harga saham melalui mekanisme informasi dan persepsi investor. Kinerja dan keterlibatan ESG yang baik cenderung berkaitan dengan penurunan risiko jatuhnya harga saham, sedangkan informasi ESG yang tidak kredibel, seperti greenwashing dan perbedaan penilaian antarlembaga pemeringkat ESG, dapat meningkatkan asimetri informasi dan risiko stock price crash. Selain itu, berita dan peristiwa ESG terbukti dapat menimbulkan reaksi harga saham secara langsung, dengan berita ESG negatif cenderung menghasilkan reaksi pasar yang lebih kuat dibandingkan berita positif. Penelitian juga menunjukkan bahwa informasi ESG yang memiliki visibilitas tinggi dapat lebih cepat tercermin dalam harga saham dibandingkan perubahan rating ESG yang bersifat agregatif. Secara keseluruhan, temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pengaruh ESG terhadap harga saham tidak hanya ditentukan oleh tingkat kinerja ESG perusahaan, tetapi juga oleh kualitas, konsistensi, kredibilitas, dan ketepatan waktu informasi ESG yang diterima pasar. Penelitian ini memberikan gambaran mengenai mekanisme hubungan ESG dan harga saham serta mengidentifikasi pentingnya kualitas informasi ESG dalam menjelaskan perbedaan reaksi pasar dan risiko jatuhnya harga saham. Kata kunci: ESG, harga saham, reaksi investor, kualitas informasi, greenwashing, stock price crash,

title: Faculty Support for NCAA Division I Reclassification
source: Journal of Higher Education Athletics Labor & Innovation
summary: This study examines faculty members’ attitudes about their university moving to a higher NCAA classification (from the Football Championship Subdivision into the Football Bowl Subdivision). The faculty at a medium-sized, regional university
content: This study examines faculty members’ attitudes about their university moving to a higher NCAA classification (from the Football Championship Subdivision into the Football Bowl Subdivision). The faculty at a medium-sized, regional university in the South were surveyed during their university’s recent attempt to reclassify. While largely opposed to the school’s efforts to move its athletics program, the faculty are not uniform in their beliefs. Those who expect to attend more games against better opponents are most likely to be supportive and to support the move more strongly. Attending football games before reclassification, thinking sports are important, and being younger are also linked with support. Since faculty engagement with athletics and athletes improves faculty perceptions of athletics, increasing faculty interaction with the athletics portion of the university will increase faculty beliefs about its relevance and importance. This will increase faculty support for reclassification. This extends the literature examining how university stakeholders view NCAA reclassification which has found that both students and alumni are also strongly influenced by the quality of potential opponents.

title: NURBS KULLANARAK DEĞİŞKEN SERTLİKLİ KAVİSLİ KOMPOZİT KANAT PANELLERİN OPTİMİZASYONU
summary: This study focuses on optimizing variable stiffness curved composite wing panels by modeling fiber paths using Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines (NURBS). The objective is to maximize strength and stability or minimize strain energy under diffe
content: This study focuses on optimizing variable stiffness curved composite wing panels by modeling fiber paths using Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines (NURBS). The objective is to maximize strength and stability or minimize strain energy under different loading conditions. The methodology involves the idealization of the wing panel structure, generating a Hypermesh model, conducting Nastran runs, and post-processing results. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is employed to determine optimum fiber path. Results show that the NURBS-based optimization approach provides significant improvements in strength and stability compared to quasi isotropic layup.

title: Beyond the Environment: How Green Innovation Drives the Political, Economic and Social Performance of Chemical SMEs through Green Human Resource Practices
summary: Small and medium-sized firms, particularly those in polluting industries, are facing increasing pressure. They must demonstrate that green innovation is not only good for the environment, but also beneficial for business. Researchers have a
content: Small and medium-sized firms, particularly those in polluting industries, are facing increasing pressure. They must demonstrate that green innovation is not only good for the environment, but also beneficial for business. Researchers have always viewed human resource management as the driving element behind green innovation. They have also measured innovation primarily by the environmental benefits it produces. Two questions remain unanswered: whether green innovation benefits the firm's political, economic, and social standing in addition to the environment, and whether enterprises that innovate green must also develop green human resource practices for that innovation to work. This study begins with innovation and connects it to green human resource practices, based on the natural resource concept. It investigates how these concepts affect economic and social performance in small chemical enterprises. Data from 600 personnel in Faisalabad, Lahore, and Multan, Pakistan, were analyzed using least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that green innovation improves political, economic, and social performance while also strengthening green human resource practices. Green human resource practices, in turn, have a favorable impact on all three types of performance and somewhat mitigate the effect of green innovation on each. The model explains 39.8 percent of the variance in performance (34.0 percent in economic performance and 32.7 percent in social performance). The data reveal that green innovation benefits SMEs most when it is combined with recruitment, training, appraisal, awards, and employee engagement. According to the report, green skills provide not only economic but also social and political benefits. It advises owners, managers, and policymakers in emerging economies. Keywords: green innovation; green human resource practices; political performance; economic performance; social performance; natural-resource-based view; SMEs; PLS-SEM

title: REPRESENTATIVIDADE DE HOSPITAIS SUSTENTÁVEIS NOS RIS
summary: This study diagnoses the presence and representativeness of "sustainable, green and healthy hospitals" themes in the institutional repositories of 69 Brazilian federal universities registered in the e-MEC Registry. The exploratory research
content: This study diagnoses the presence and representativeness of "sustainable, green and healthy hospitals" themes in the institutional repositories of 69 Brazilian federal universities registered in the e-MEC Registry. The exploratory research analyzed 52 functional repositories (75.4% coverage), verifying specific collections, metadata, digital preservation policies and documented sustainable practices. Results identified only 6 repositories with content on sustainable hospitals: Federal University of Pernambuco, Federal Technological University of Paraná, Federal University of Uberlândia, Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul, Federal University of Santa Catarina and University Hospital of the Federal University of Rio Grande. Themes found include hospital sustainability, waste management, sustainable architecture, solar energy and green practices financing. CRITICAL representativeness (11.5%) is revealed, evidencing significant gap in documentation and digital preservation of green hospital knowledge in federal repositories. The study contributes to informational inclusion policies, environmental sustainability and dissemination of sustainable health best practices in Brazilian federal higher education institutions.

title: Development of DCIRV based on AI-NLP for ed-comm in Asia, Europe and Canada
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: The development and utilisation of Virtual Community Digital Learning Nusantara products have been successful in Indonesia, Japan, and Korea through experts from Bordeaux, France, and Canada. Furthermore, research from 2025 to 2026 will bui
content: The development and utilisation of Virtual Community Digital Learning Nusantara products have been successful in Indonesia, Japan, and Korea through experts from Bordeaux, France, and Canada. Furthermore, research from 2025 to 2026 will build a Digital Centre Innovation for Robotics VCDLN (DCIRV) based on artificial intelligence with natural language processing to strengthen and expand future innovation. The research focuses on redesigning DCIRV by implementing APIs for notification communication. Thus, the method that has been used with the mixed method for the development of DCIRV through the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) is then to test the impact using an explanatory survey with Path Diagram Analysis Statistics. The results of the study show that (1) the redesign and development of DCIRV content was carried out by adding features and APIs for notification of content and new members from the database system to all users; (2) the results of experts from Europe, Asia and Canada were very positive about DCIRV with the implementation of APIs for notifications which were also based on AI-NLP in the form of Chatbot content that could be used in various parts of the world; (3) The development of AI-NP-based DCIRV was carried out through five strategic aspects in supporting the location of the ongoing communication of Educational Technology in the world; (4) The impact of digital communication and DCIRV, both through AI-NLP and API technology, was able to improve Ed-communication services positively and significantly for distance learning in Europe, Asia and Canada.

title: Intimate betrayal, relational harm, and female agency in Oka Rusmini's short stories
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: This study analyzes the representation of intimate betrayal and relational harm in Oka Rusmini's short stories Palung and Sipleg, focusing on the interpersonal dynamics that produce relational disintegration in the female characters and the
content: This study analyzes the representation of intimate betrayal and relational harm in Oka Rusmini's short stories Palung and Sipleg, focusing on the interpersonal dynamics that produce relational disintegration in the female characters and the forms of agency they develop in response to coercive intimate and familial relationships. Addressing a conceptual gap in feminist literary scholarship, which has documented oppression and resistance in Rusmini's work at the macro-structural level but has not examined the micro-relational mechanisms through which they operate, the theoretical framework integrates Betrayal Trauma Theory, Relational-Cultural Theory, a female agency framework, and feminist literary criticism. Employing qualitative content analysis combined with feminist narrative analysis, the study conducted close reading and systematic coding of both texts. Four findings emerge. First, betrayal in Palung is represented as progressive relational disintegration reflecting betrayal blindness within a Balinese cultural idiom. Second, Sipleg constructs an architecture of coercive control operating through three family dyads and sustained by patrilineal ideology. Third, the strategic silence and metaphorical language of both characters constitute a calculated form of agency rather than passive compliance. Fourth, Rusmini's narratives refine rather than merely confirm Western theories of betrayal, coercive control, and agency from a non-Western feminist standpoint. The study thus complements feminist-structural readings of Rusmini with a micro-relational analysis while extending interpersonal relationship theories to non-Western contexts. Its originality lies in bringing an interpersonal relationship science framework into dialogue with feminist literary criticism to interpret Indonesian women's writing, thereby contributing to Global South feminist scholarship on how relational harm and agency are narratively encoded.

title: Contribution of microfinance for sustainable development – a case analysis of selected small finance banks
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: Sustainable microfinance has emerged as a critical instrument for promoting financial inclusion, poverty alleviation, and sustainable livelihood development, particularly in developing economies like India. This study examines the contribut
content: Sustainable microfinance has emerged as a critical instrument for promoting financial inclusion, poverty alleviation, and sustainable livelihood development, particularly in developing economies like India. This study examines the contribution of sustainable microfinance institutions (MFIs) and selected Small Finance Banks (SFBs) toward reducing poverty and enhancing socio-economic conditions. The research is based on secondary data collected from sources such as RBI reports, NABARD publications, and Microfinance Pulse reports for the period 2021–2025. The study employs descriptive and inferential statistical techniques, including trend analysis, correlation analysis, and t-tests, to evaluate the performance of microfinance institutions in terms of loan disbursement, portfolio quality, and capital adequacy. The findings reveal that while microfinance has significantly expanded outreach and improved access to credit—especially among women and low-income groups—there are concerns regarding declining credit indicators and increasing repayment stress in recent years. The study concludes that sustainable microfinance plays a vital role in inclusive development; however, strengthening regulatory frameworks, improving digital financial integration, and ensuring responsible lending practices are essential for long-term sustainability.

title: Epistemic configurations of critical thinking in the meaningful learning of abstract mathematics: a phenomenological study in public higher education
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: The transition from procedural and algorithmic thinking to formal abstraction in university mathematics constitutes a critical cognitive and epistemological challenge within public higher education. The objective of this study was to unders
content: The transition from procedural and algorithmic thinking to formal abstraction in university mathematics constitutes a critical cognitive and epistemological challenge within public higher education. The objective of this study was to understand and model the epistemic configurations of critical thinking in the meaningful learning experiences of mathematics students at a public university in Peru. A qualitative research approach with a hermeneutic phenomenological focus was designed, complemented by the analytical procedures of Grounded Theory. The sample consisted of students in their final academic years, selected through purposive sampling based on criteria of maximum variation until theoretical saturation was reached. Data collection was carried out through semi-structured in-depth interviews and the analysis of logs of logical error deconstruction. The resulting textual corpus was rigorously processed using ATLAS.ti v24 software. The findings revealed the emergence of a central model called "The Reflective Architecture of Mathematical Discovery," which is articulated through three fundamental underlying dimensions: (a) the deconstruction of error as a reflective catalyst in the face of cognitive friction, (b) the linguistic transmutation from intuitive metaphors to axiomatic formal syntax, and (c) the development of metacognitive autonomy in the internal validation of abstract proofs. It is concluded that meaningful learning in advanced mathematics does not occur through the passive accumulation of theorems, but rather through a disruptive cycle of logical reconfiguration and the breaking down of ordinary intuition, guided exclusively by the learner's critical and self-regulated judgment. The study provides a comprehensive framework for curricular and pedagogical redesign in the exact sciences.

title: Determinants of Medical students’ attitudes toward institutional facility conservation at Can Tho University of Medicine and Pharmacy
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: Background: In higher education settings, institutional facilities (CSVC, Vietnamese acronym) are a critical component that directly affects training quality. Objective: To examine the status of-and factors associated with-medical students’
content: Background: In higher education settings, institutional facilities (CSVC, Vietnamese acronym) are a critical component that directly affects training quality. Objective: To examine the status of-and factors associated with-medical students’ attitudes toward conserving institutional facilities at Can Tho University of Medicine and Pharmacy (CTUMP). Materials and methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 504 full-time medical students from cohorts K45-K50 in the 2024-2025 academic year at CTUMP. Data were summarized and analyzed using Microsoft Excel and SPSS 22.0.
