The number of documents increased significantly after 2010 and peaked in 2024; however, caution is advised in comparing citations of recent publications because citation impact depends on the age of a document and the year 2025 was not complete at the time of analysis on 9 August 2025. The USA dominated the literature in terms of quantity and impact, followed by India and China, with the UK, Spain, Germany, and the Netherlands producing a considerable number of articles and citations. The analysis also revealed that keywords and themes were concentrated in performance, risk, returns, flows, and fund-related subjects, as well as behavioural and consumer-related areas, such as risk perception, overconfidence, heuristics, Prospect Theory, financial literacy, information search, preferences, and consumer behaviour, with sustainability- and digital-finance related topics also playing an important role in the literature, albeit as emerging and specialised fields. The study discusses the findings in relation to key theories and approaches, including behavioural finance, consumer behaviour, financial services marketing, and technology adoption, but does not attempt to establish causal relationships or theoretical influences due to the limitations of bibliometric analysis. The study also highlights research opportunities, including digital trust, consumer behaviour in FinTech, ESG and ethical investing, consumer segmentation, and regulatory protection, as well as methodological innovation, for future empirical and theoretical studies. In conclusion, the study provides an evidence-based overview of the intellectual and thematic evolution of mutual fund investment research and identifies potential areas of investigation for future studies.

title: Biodiversity and wilderness sustainability in environmental ethics: What can Yoruba eco-philosophy offer?
source: Journal of Asian and African Studies
summary: This work interrogates some theories of environmental ethics. It identifies biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation as pivotal environmental problems facing our world today. This is because the local and global environment is presently
content: This work interrogates some theories of environmental ethics. It identifies biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation as pivotal environmental problems facing our world today. This is because the local and global environment is presently experiencing biodiversity loss and wilderness degradation, traceable to destructive anthropogenic activities such as deforestation, pollution, hunting, urbanisation and uncontrolled capitalist-inspired agricultural practices. Using relationalism as a theoretical framework, the work examines the practice of Igbo oro in Yoruba eco-philosophy and untangles the inherent similarity and the point of divergence between Yoruba eco-philosophy and deep ecology of the western philosophical tradition. It argues that the practice of Igbo oro among the Yoruba people embodies and goes beyond what deep ecology stands for. The work goes further to demonstrate how the practice of Igbo oro pragmatically shows respect for nature, thereby constituting an indigenous African paradigm for environmental sustainability. This argument is significant since it debunks the position held in certain quarters that the practice of Igbo oro in Yorubaland is only for the fulfilment of religious aspirations of the Yoruba people.

content:
总体平稳 向新向优——透视10月国民经济运行态势
2026-11-16 20:39
字号：默认
新华社北京11月16日电 题：总体平稳 向新向优——透视10月国民经济运行态势
新华社记者王雨萧、张晓洁
10月份我国主要经济指标运行情况如何？国民经济呈现哪些特点？如何研判全年经济走势？在国新办16日举行的新闻发布会上，国家统计局新闻发言人就相关情况进行介绍。
经济运行“稳”的特质明显
国家统计局新闻发言人付凌晖表示，10月份国际环境动荡不安，地缘政治冲突延宕发酵，全球能源、航运市场持续波动，我国经济顶住压力，继续保持总体平稳、向新向优发展态势，展现出强大韧性和活力，“稳”的特质明显、“稳”的底气增强。
生产供给增加稳。10月份，规模以上工业增加值同比增长4.8%，保持平稳较快增长；服务业生产指数同比增长4.6%。
消费市场运行稳。1至10月，社会消费商品和服务零售总额同比增长2.5%，其中服务零售额增长4.9%，成为消费市场扩容的重要推动力。
外贸增长势头稳。10月份，我国进出口总额同比增长31.2%，今年以来持续保持较快增长。
“稳”还反映在就业和物价的稳定。
“随着季节性因素影响消退，全国城镇调查失业率从9月份开始连续两个月下降，10月份全国城镇调查失业率为5.1%。从物价情况看，尽管受国际能源市场波动带来的输入性冲击影响，我国加大保供稳价力度，价格形势总体稳定。”付凌晖说。
针对10月部分指标增速出现回落，国家统计局新闻发言人王冠华表示，月度指标出现波动是经济运行中比较常见的现象，比如10月部分指标回落一定程度上受到中秋错月因素影响，部分需求在9月提前释放，客观上会对10月服务业消费等指标形成一定下拉影响。判断经济走势，既要看当月也要看累计，既要看总量更要看结构，既要跟自己比，也要放在全球经济坐标中来看。
“今年前三季度中国经济增长4.6%，在全球范围内也是一个非常亮眼的表现。进入四季度，经济平稳运行的态势没有改变。”王冠华说，中国经济在复杂环境中保持总体稳定的发展势头，这种“稳”本身就是全球的稀缺资源和宝贵资产。
向新向优发展态势延续
超过五成——这是今年前10个月以高端制造、智能制造为代表的新动能对规模以上工业增加值增长的贡献。
“新动能快速成长，对经济增长的贡献稳步提升，有力助推了经济高质量发展，成为今年以来经济运行的突出亮点。”付凌晖说。
市场需求加快向“新”拓展。
从消费看，文体旅游服务消费和智能绿色商品消费持续扩大。10月份，高能效等级家电和可穿戴智能设备零售额保持较快增长，旅游咨询租赁服务类零售额保持两位数增长。
从外贸看，高技术产品和绿色产品增势较好。10月份，我国高技术产品和“新三样”产品出口额同比增长均超过50%。
从投资看，资金和建设项目向创新驱动和产业升级等重点领域集聚。1至10月份，知识产权产品投资、设备工器具购置投资分别增长9.2%和8.9%。
“前10个月固定资产投资降幅有所扩大，主要是经济发展阶段变化、产业结构调整等多方面因素导致的。我们要客观理性全面看待，既要看到投资总量变化情况，更要看投资结构、质量、效益的改善。”付凌晖说。
产业向“新”发展同步加快。10月份，数字产品制造业增加值同比增长18.4%，工业机器人、集成电路产量增速均在20%以上；不少传统行业含“新”量提升，铁路、船舶、航空航天和其他运输设备制造业增加值同比增长9.2%。
绿色生产力加快打造，日益成为拉动经济的新增长点。
“清洁能源利用占比稳步提升，绿色产品增长势头良好，10月汽车用锂离子电池产量同比增长33.9%，碳纤维及其复合材料产量增长52.2%。”付凌晖说。
实现全年预期目标有支撑有条件
展望全年，经济发展预期目标能否顺利实现？
“当前经济发展确实面临着一些困难和挑战，需要采取有针对性的措施解决。但在应对挑战、攻坚克难的过程中，支撑高质量发展的有利条件和独特优势也在不断巩固拓展。”王冠华说。
从运行基础看，前10个月供需两端指标比较平稳，城镇调查失业率稳定，物价温和上涨，能源供给充足，为全年目标顺利实现奠定良好基础。
从支撑因素看，新动能的驱动力越来越强。前10个月，规模以上高技术制造业、专精特新“小巨人”工业企业增加值分别增长14.6%和11.1%。
“在新旧动能转换过程中，一些传统行业面临转型调整的压力，同时也有一大批新产业、新业态、新模式冒出来、跑起来，这种新旧动能的彼长此消、接力转换，正是当前中国经济最为鲜明的特征。”王冠华说，新兴领域发展潜能大、成长势头好，无疑将有利于全年经济的平稳运行。
此外，外贸韧性和优势将持续彰显。
王冠华表示，面对全球经贸环境起伏不定，我国出口额和进口额连续多个月保持两位数快速增长，靠的是我国完备的产业体系和超大规模市场优势。依托完备产业链、多元化市场布局以及持续扩大的制度型开放，外贸对经济增长的支撑作用还将有效发挥。
“随着各项宏观政策协同发力不断显效，中国经济有望延续向新向优向好的发展态势，实现全年预期目标有支撑、有条件。”王冠华说。

title: Adenosine deaminase co-immunization reverses age‑associated immunosenescence by restoring germinal center T follicular helper cell function
summary: Abstract Older adults experience disproportionate morbidity and mortality from Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI); however, existing toxoid- and receptor binding domain (RBD)-based vaccines elicit suboptimal protection in aged hosts d
content: Abstract Older adults experience disproportionate morbidity and mortality from Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI); however, existing toxoid- and receptor binding domain (RBD)-based vaccines elicit suboptimal protection in aged hosts due to the age-associated defects in CD4 + T cell function, T follicular helper (T FH ) cell activation, and antibody quality. We evaluated whether adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzymatic immune modulator that degrades immunosuppressive adenosine, and improves GC T FH differentiation and survival, could reverse these age-related impairments when co-delivered with DNA vaccine plasmids targeting toxin A and B RBDs (pRBD). In aged mice, pRBD vaccination alone produced markedly reduced toxin-specific effector/memory CD4 + T cells, diminished T FH activation, and poor toxin A neutralization compared to vaccinated young mice. Co-immunization with plasmid-encoded adenosine deaminase-1 (pADA) restored toxin-specific CD4 + T cell generation and cytokine production, activation-induced marker (AIM) T FH responses, and antibody-mediate toxin neutralization to levels comparable to young adults. Mechanistically, pADA co-immunization was associated with the reduction of CXCR4 on germinal center (GC) T FH cells—an age-related defect linked to impaired GC positioning and diminished B cell help—suggesting that ADA improves humoral quality by correcting GC T FH mislocalization. These immune enhancements corresponded with improved clinical outcomes in morbidity, mortality, and weight-loss following C. difficile spore challenge of aged mice. Finally, pADA significantly reduced adenosine levels in aged lymph nodes, implicating a potential enzymatic-based regulation of GC immunosenescence. Together, these findings identify ADA as a metabolic adjuvant capable of reversing key features of vaccine immunosenescence and highlight adenosine dependent CXCR4 regulation as a tractable axis for improving vaccine efficacy in older populations.

title: Firefly-Geni: Automated Iteration-Guided Generative Discovery of Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Molecules
summary: Abstract The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure–property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely f
content: Abstract The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure–property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely fragmented and underutilized. Here, we present Firefly-Geni, an automated and interpretable active-evolution framework that transforms dispersed literature knowledge into structurally novel TADF candidates through a closed-loop workflow. Firefly-Geni integrates large-language-model (LLM)-assisted data extraction, multitask property prediction, conditional molecular generation, and theoretical evaluation. Its data-mining module converts unstructured literature into a curated database of experimental property entries. A dual-molecular-graph multitask predictor and a conditional generator are integrated with quantum-chemical feedback, enabling iterative refinement toward structural novelty. From 100,000 molecules generated under target conditions of a singlet–triplet energy gap ΔEST = 0.05 eV and a synthetic accessibility (SA) score of 2.5, Firefly-Geni identifies 100 structurally novel candidates computationally predicted to support reverse intersystem crossing and to be synthetically tractable, spanning diverse emission wavelengths. One synthesized candidate exhibited an experimental ΔEST of 0.019 eV and a film photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 84% under nitrogen, broadly consistent with the predicted small gap and high PLQY. Interpretability analyses further reveal chemically meaningful structure–property relationships and generation preferences, confirming that the candidates encode physically relevant low-ΔEST design motifs. This work offers a closed-loop, explainable strategy for actively evolving TADF candidates from literature knowledge, providing a generalizable route for data-driven molecular discovery.

title: Eco-conscious synthesis of a starch-based magnetic hydrogel for effective methylene blue decontamination in wastewater treatment
summary: Abstract Novel magnetic hydrogels based on native Peruvian Amarilla Reyna potato starch were synthesized via radical copolymerization, followed by in situ co-precipitation of magnetite, nanoparticles for Methylene Blue (MB) removal from aqu
content: Abstract Novel magnetic hydrogels based on native Peruvian Amarilla Reyna potato starch were synthesized via radical copolymerization, followed by in situ co-precipitation of magnetite, nanoparticles for Methylene Blue (MB) removal from aqueous matrices. The materials were characterized by FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDS, VSM, swelling measurements, and pH PZC determination, confirming successful polymer grafting, a homogeneous Fe₃O₄ incorporation, magnetic recoverability, and a high swelling capacity (352.1 g/g). The magnetic hydrogel achieved a MB removal efficiency of 96% and an equilibrium adsorption capacity of 1148.3 mg/g at pH 10 and 30°C. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-first-order (PFO) kinetic model, reaching the equilibrium within 3 h, while the good fitting to the Langmuir isotherm model confirmed a monolayer adsorption behaviour. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic, while Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations indicated a highly delocalized positive charge over the MB molecule, providing a molecular-level explanation for its weaker competition with small inorganic cations for negatively charged adsorption sites in complex aqueous matrices. Likewise, the hydrogel retained over 90% MB removal efficiency after five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, demonstrating an excellent reusability of the material. Tests in real water matrices showed a decreasing in the MB removal efficiency, c.a. 30-38%, due to ionic competition for the active sites and organic matter interference. The synthesized magnetic hydrogel demonstrated environmental safety, with no significant toxicity after treatment of the real effluents. These findings highlighted the potential of the obtained magnetic hydrogel as a sustainable and reusable adsorbent for dyes removal from complex aqueous matrices.

title: Experimental decoherence mitigation using a weak measurement-based scheme and the duality quantum algorithm
summary: Abstract We experimentally demonstrate a weak measurement and measurement reversal-based scheme to ameliorate the effects of decoherence due to amplitude damping, on an NMR quantum processor. The weak measurement and measurement reversal pr
content: Abstract We experimentally demonstrate a weak measurement and measurement reversal-based scheme to ameliorate the effects of decoherence due to amplitude damping, on an NMR quantum processor. The weak measurement and measurement reversal processes require the implementation of non-unitary operations, which are typically infeasible on conventional quantum processors, where only unitary quantum operations are allowed. We employed the duality quantum algorithm (DQA) for experimentally realizing the amplitude damping channel and non-unitary quantum operations corresponding to weak measurement and measurement reversal. We experimentally validate the efficacy of the weak measurement-based decoherence mitigation scheme by showing state protection on a four-qubit system, with one qubit being designated as the ‘system qubit’, while the remaining three qubits serve as ‘ancilla qubits’. Our experimental results clearly demonstrate the success of the weak measurement-based decoherence mitigation scheme in protecting the desired state. Since the measurement process involved has trace less than unity, the scheme can be thought of as a filtration scheme, where a subset of the spins is protected while the rest of the spins can be discarded.

title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
summary: Abstract Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, su
content: Abstract Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

title: Residential and workplace segregation are differently associated with gaps in ambient air pollution exposure across US metropolitan areas
summary: Structural racism contributes to health disparities partly through residential segregation and unequal environmental exposures, but workplaces may constitute a distinct geography of segregation. Using home and workplace locations for approx
content: Structural racism contributes to health disparities partly through residential segregation and unequal environmental exposures, but workplaces may constitute a distinct geography of segregation. Using home and workplace locations for approximately 95% of the U.S. workforce across 380 metropolitan areas, we measured residential and workplace segregation at metropolitan and census tract scales for Black-White, Hispanic-non-Hispanic, and less-than-high-school vs. college contrasts and linked them to worker-weighted PM 2.5 and NO 2 concentrations in 2018. Metropolitan residential segregation was consistently associated with wider exposure gaps across all groups, pollutants, and locations. Metropolitan workplace segregation was associated with a wider Black-White workplace NO 2 gap (0.042 ppb per SD; 95% CI 0.005, 0.078), an association largely accounted for by group differences in the centrality of each group’s jobs, but with narrower or reversed workplace gaps for Hispanic and less-educated workers. Workplace segregation is therefore associated with exposure inequality in group-specific ways that are obscured by residence-only or single-contrast analyses.

title: Evolution of size-regulated microstructure enabling non-monotonic mechanical deformation transition in pyrolyzed carbon
summary: Reducing material dimensions to the nano- or microscale often enhances mechanical properties, a trend commonly attributed to generic “size confinement effects” that suppress defects and weak-link activation. Here, we show that size confinem
content: Reducing material dimensions to the nano- or microscale often enhances mechanical properties, a trend commonly attributed to generic “size confinement effects” that suppress defects and weak-link activation. Here, we show that size confinement not only limits defects and weak links, but also actively influences microstructure formation during fabrication, so that size-constrained processing dictates microstructure and, in turn, mechanical response. Specifically, we uncovered a size-dependent mechanical behavior in pyrolyzed carbon, with a transition from brittle-like (ε f = 22%) to ductile-like (ε f = 65%) and back to brittle-like (ε f = 34%) as the diameter decreases from the microscale to the submicron range. Through detailed characterization and atomistic simulations, it is revealed that the origin of this transition is closely tied to microstructural changes induced during pyrolysis, where the changes are strongly dependent on the sample size. In particular, molecular simulations attribute the material’s ductile-like deformation to a gradient microstructure, whereas brittle-like failure is associated with (i) a relatively high density of impurities and more pronounced voids at larger length scales even when a gradient is present, and (ii) a relatively homogeneous microstructure lacking such gradients at the small scales. Overall, these findings demonstrate that microstructure evolution allows on-demand control of deformation behavior, here assessed by varying sample size, thereby enabling the mechanical properties of carbon materials to be tailored, including strength ( σ f = 5–16 GPa), toughness (981–4,167 MJ/m 3 ), and elastic limit (ε elastic = 20%-34%). More broadly, this work highlights size-enabled microstructural programming during fabrication as a general pathway to optimize and tune the properties of nanostructured materials.

title: Highly conductive halide Na-ion conductor enabled by cost-effective aliovalent carbonate polyanion substitution for all-solid-state sodium batteries
summary: Halide-based Na-ion conductors have attracted intense attention due to their favorable (electro)chemical compatibility with oxide positive electrodes. Among these, zirconium (Zr)-based halide solid electrolytes (SEs) offer a cost advantage
content: Halide-based Na-ion conductors have attracted intense attention due to their favorable (electro)chemical compatibility with oxide positive electrodes. Among these, zirconium (Zr)-based halide solid electrolytes (SEs) offer a cost advantage over halide SEs based on rare metals, but the relatively low ionic conductivity has limited their application in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Here, we report employing soda ash (Na2CO3) as a low-cost precursor to introduce an aliovalent carbonate polyanion and produce a family of Na-Zr-Cl-CO3 conductors with nominal compositions of (2-x)NaCl-xNa2CO3-ZrCl4. This substitution increases structural disorder and amorphization, creating structural environments that facilitate Na+ transport. At the optimal composition, its ionic conductivity reaches 1.02 mS cm−1 at 25 °C. The optimized Na-Zr-Cl-CO3 SE also exhibits stable electrochemical behavior and favorable mechanical properties. When paired with NaCrO2 positive electrode, the assembled ASSBs deliver an initial discharge capacity of 117 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and demonstrate a long-term cycling stability at 0.3 C for 850 cycles. This work highlights carbonate polyanion substitution as a practical strategy for improving low-cost Zr-based halide SEs, offering a promising route toward ASSBs with high performance. Zr-based halide solid electrolytes are promising for their lower cost but suffer from limited ionic conductivity. Here, authors introduce carbonate polyanion using cost-competitive soda ash to enhance structural disorder and Na+ transport, achieving 1.02 mS cm−1 ionic conductivity and stable all-solid-state battery cycling for 850 cycles.

title: Modelling N 2 O emissions in fertilized grasslands with machine learning: a multi-site LSTM approach
summary: Accurate quantification of GHG emissions from agricultural soils based on key environmental and management factors, is crucial for developing effective mitigation strategies. This study applies a machine learning approach using data from mu
content: Accurate quantification of GHG emissions from agricultural soils based on key environmental and management factors, is crucial for developing effective mitigation strategies. This study applies a machine learning approach using data from multiple montane grasslands in central Europe to model the spatial and temporal dynamics of N 2 O emissions, using meteorological, soil, and management data. The primary aim is to advance predictive modelling of N 2 O emissions from grassland soils for spatial upscaling and scenario analysis. Specifically, we assess whether a regionally trained model can accurately estimate N 2 O emissions from an independent site excluded from training. We collected data from five fertilized grasslands across southern Germany, northern Switzerland and western Austria (122 soil-site-treatment-year combinations), and trained a long short-term memory (LSTM) algorithm to model the influence of drivers within 5 subsequent days on N 2 O emissions. The dataset includes daily N 2 O emission measurements along with key emission drivers such as soil moisture and temperature in 10 cm soil depth, daily precipitation, occurrence of fertilization events (zero or one flag), as well as static soil characteristics such as pH and bulk density. The trained LSTM model showed varying predictive performance when evaluated on two test datasets, with higher performance at some site-years and lower at others. One test set included temporally independent data (hold-out years) (RMSE = 28 µg N 2 O-N m −2 h −1 ), while the other included cross-site data from a soil type withheld from training (RMSE = 11 µg N 2 O-N m −2 h −1 ). The model captured N 2 O dynamics, including the magnitude and timing of emission peaks driven by slurry application and environmental factors, though predictive performance varied across individual site-years. These results demonstrate that LSTM-based models can predict N 2 O emissions for most site-years across test sites with similar environmental and soil characteristics, representing an alternative to process-based models for predicting soil N 2 O emissions.

title: Vorticity-induced surfing and trapping in porous media
summary: Microorganisms often encounter strong confinement and complex hydrodynamic flows while navigating their habitats. Combining finite-element methods and stochastic simulations, we study the interplay of active transport and heterogeneous flow
content: Microorganisms often encounter strong confinement and complex hydrodynamic flows while navigating their habitats. Combining finite-element methods and stochastic simulations, we study the interplay of active transport and heterogeneous flows in dense porous channels. We find that swimming slows down the traversal of agents across the channel, giving rise to robust power-law tails of their exit-time distributions. These exit-time distributions collapse onto a universal master curve with a scaling exponent of ≈ 3/2 across a wide range of packing fractions and motility parameters, which can be rationalized by a scaling relation. We further identify a new motility pattern where agents alternate between surfing along fast streams and extended trapping phases, the latter determining the power-law exponent. Unexpectedly, trapping occurs in the flow backbone itself – not only at obstacle boundaries – due to vorticity-induced reorientation in the highly-heterogeneous fluid environment. These findings provide a new active transport mechanism with implications for biofilm clogging and the design of novel microrobots capable of operating in heterogeneous media.

title: Guided spin wave in monolayer CrSBr: Localization and spin-orbit coupling from dipolar field
summary: Spin-wave spectrum of monolayer CrSBr waveguides was studied by numerically diagonalizing the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian derived from linearising the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. In contrast to its short-range counterparts, the l
content: Spin-wave spectrum of monolayer CrSBr waveguides was studied by numerically diagonalizing the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian derived from linearising the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. In contrast to its short-range counterparts, the long-range dipolar field acts statically as a confining potential for spin wave, while the dynamic part couples the spin and orbit degrees of freedom, thus giving rise to spin-orbit coupling for spin wave. Due to the inversion symmetry of the Hamiltonian and the spinor structure of the wave function, spin-wave eigenstates form doublets with definite parity. Micromagnetic simulation tallies well with numerical calculation. Our study on spin-wave eigenstates in CrSBr waveguides sheds light on the nature of exchange-dipole spin wave in ferromagnetic slabs. We confirm particularly that the robustness of the Damon-Eshbach mode is not derived from topology, but rather from the static dipolar field. Moreover, a thorough knowledge on spin wave in monolayer CrSBr itself represents a step forward to understanding the more complicated antiferromagnetic resonance in bulk CrSBr.

title: Color centers and hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hexagonal boron nitride: A new platform for quantum optics
summary: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPPs) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) confine mid-infrared light to deep-subwavelength scales and may offer a powerful route to achieve strong light-matter interactions. Generation and control of HPPs are typi
content: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPPs) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) confine mid-infrared light to deep-subwavelength scales and may offer a powerful route to achieve strong light-matter interactions. Generation and control of HPPs are typically accessed using near-field probes driven by strong light fields, which do not allow for exploring the quantum regime. A different frontier in hBN research focuses on color centers: these bright, stable, atomically localized quantum emitters that have rapidly emerged as a promising platform for solid-state quantum optics and quantum sensing. Here we establish a link between these two directions by developing a cavity-QED framework in which a single hBN color center serves as a quantum source of HPPs. We quantify the emitter-HPP interaction and analyze both spontaneous and stimulated Raman scattering into the phonon sideband, generating a single HPP. While both methods result in generation of a quantum state of HPP, stimulation of the Raman scattering by a laser field or an optical cavity mode provides enhanced optical photon to single-frequency HPP conversion. Optical excitation thus launches ray-like proposagation of HPPs with a spatial extent ultimately determined by the size of the quantum emitter. Photon antibunching in a two-emitter correlation measurement can directly test the single-polariton character of these emissions.

title: Workforce reskilling and training-finance optimization for Laem Chabang Port Phase 3: a scenario-based MILP framework
summary: Laem Chabang Port Phase 3 is intended to increase container-handling capacity from approximately 11 to 18 million TEU while strengthening rail connectivity within Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor. This study develops a scenario-based de
content: Laem Chabang Port Phase 3 is intended to increase container-handling capacity from approximately 11 to 18 million TEU while strengthening rail connectivity within Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor. This study develops a scenario-based decision-support framework that links throughput and rail-share assumptions to occupation- and region-specific workforce requirements and a policy-constrained mixed-integer linear programming model. The final reproducibility calibration uses public project and labour-market data, benchmark-derived labour-intensity parameters, explicitly labelled policy scenarios, and probability-adjusted training outcomes. Under an 80% workforce-coverage target, the corrected model requires approximately 1,612 enrollments under a 15% rail-share scenario and 1,739 under a 25% scenario over 2026–2027. Two-year training expenditure is estimated at THB 137.5–148.3 million against a THB 118 million envelope, while support expenditure reaches THB 37.2–40.1 million against a THB 22 million envelope. One-way sensitivity analysis shows that both financing gaps persist under coverage targets of 70–90%, completion-placement probabilities of ±10%, and support-cost changes of ±20%. The results indicate that workforce-transition feasibility depends on probability-adjusted labour absorption, the joint adequacy of training and post-training support finance, and transparent calibration rather than headline training capacity alone.

title: Lytic polysaccharide monooxygenase (LPMO) expression in Arabidopsis reduces cell wall recalcitrance and boosts immunity against Pseudomonas syringae
summary: Abstract Background Lytic Polysaccharide Monooxygenases (LPMOs) are well known for their ability to boost the efficiency of enzyme mixtures used for breaking down lignocellulosic biomass in vitro . Nonetheless, the impact of LPMO expression
content: Abstract Background Lytic Polysaccharide Monooxygenases (LPMOs) are well known for their ability to boost the efficiency of enzyme mixtures used for breaking down lignocellulosic biomass in vitro . Nonetheless, the impact of LPMO expression within plants and its influence on cell wall characteristics remains largely unexplored. Several studies have indicated that introducing cell wall degrading enzymes heterologously in plants can enhance saccharification efficiency. Hence, to understand the effects of LPMO expression in planta , we introduced the Auxiliary Activity (AA14) family gene from Pycnoporus coccineus ( PcAA14 ) into Arabidopsis thaliana . This was performed using a native signal peptide and was driven by both a constitutive ( 35S ) promoter and a xylem-specific ( Cinnamate-4-hydroxylase ) promoter. We then assessed how PcAA14 expression influenced plant growth, immune response, cell wall composition, and the efficiency of saccharification. Result PcAA14 was found to localise to the plasma membrane. Transgenic Arabidopsis lines expressing PcAA14 accumulated higher levels of oxidized xylo-oligosaccharides relative to wild-type plants after xylanase digestion which confirmed LPMO can be active in plants. Fourier Transform Infrared and mass spectroscopy analysis further revealed presence of oxidized polysaccharides in PcAA14 expressing plants. Furthermore, these transgenic plants exhibited increased cellulose content and reduced lignin content compared to wild-type. Cell walls from PcAA14 -expressing plants were more digested by Cellic CTec2 enzymatic cocktail and GH11 xylanase, indicating improved digestibility of major cell wall polysaccharides. Furthermore, expression of PcAA14 did not result in any observable morphological or anatomical abnormalities instead, these plants observed with improved immunity against Pseudomonas syringae. Conclusion Our study provides the first evidence that the heterologous expression of LPMO from PcAA14 in plants enhances the digestibility of cellulose and xylan, both with and without pretreatment. This approach holds promise for tailoring bioenergy crops to support the sustainable production of biobased products.

title: A post-growth deal for Italy: Exploring the coalition-building potential of non-reformist reforms
summary: Challenging green growth narratives, degrowth argues that achieving ecological sustainability in high-income countries requires a democratically planned and socially just downscaling of production and consumption, alongside a reorientation
content: Challenging green growth narratives, degrowth argues that achieving ecological sustainability in high-income countries requires a democratically planned and socially just downscaling of production and consumption, alongside a reorientation of economic institutions toward collective wellbeing within planetary boundaries. While post-growth and degrowth scholarship has increasingly shifted from critique to policy proposals, limited attention has been paid to the political agency and coalition-building capacity required to implement such policies. This paper asks whether a post-growth policy package can function as an emancipatory tool for building a counter-hegemonic alliance capable of contesting growth-dependent capitalism. We examine perceptions of a “Post-Growth Deal” composed of five non-reformist reforms – Universal Care Income, Universal Public Services, Working Time Reduction, a Public Job Guarantee, and Deliberative Forums – among three strategically positioned actor groups: environmental activists, labor union members, and progressive political party members. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines focus group discussions with a survey, we analyze the desirability, communicability, achievability, and perceived popularity of these measures. Our findings show that work-centered policies, particularly Working Time Reduction and a Green Job Guarantee, display the strongest potential for cross-group alignment, while more redistributive and participatory measures face greater ideological and communicative barriers. The study contributes to ecological economics by empirically assessing the coalition-building potential of post-growth policies, foregrounding compromise and political strategy, and situating degrowth debates within a southern European context, by focussing on the case-study of Italy.

title: Temporal accumulation patterns of paeonol, paeoniflorin, and tannins in leaves of five tree peony (Paeonia suffruticosa) cultivars
source: Plant Biosystems - An International Journal Dealing with all Aspects of Plant Biology
summary: Abstract As a significant by-product of the tree peony industry, tree peony leaves are a valuable source of bioactive compounds, making the analysis of their composition and accumulation patterns vital for exploitation. This study systemati
content: Abstract As a significant by-product of the tree peony industry, tree peony leaves are a valuable source of bioactive compounds, making the analysis of their composition and accumulation patterns vital for exploitation. This study systematically investigated the temporal accumulation patterns of three bioactive compounds—paeonol, paeoniflorin, and tannic acid—in the leaves of five major tree peony cultivars ('Luoyanghong', 'Fengdan', 'Jingyu', 'Erqiao', and 'Huhong') across different growth stages in Henan, China. Using HPLC and UV-Vis methods, we quantified the contents of these components at five key harvest timepoints from March to September. The results revealed distinct temporal dynamics. Paeoniflorin content decreased sharply after flowering, with reductions of 70%-80% by September compared to March levels across all cultivars. Paeonol accumulation was cultivar-dependent, generally peaking in May-July; for instance, 'Jingyu' reached 761.48 µg/g in July, while 'Fengdan' showed a declining trend from 554.05 µg/g in March. Tannic acid content was highest in spring (e.g., 'Luoyanghong' at 643.98 mg/g in April), then declined significantly by autumn, with reductions of 50%-60% across cultivars. These findings demonstrate significant temporal and varietal variations in bioactive compound accumulation in tree peony leaves. The study provides a scientific basis for optimizing harvest timing to maximize the yield of specific compounds, supporting the valorization of tree peony leaf resources in pharmaceutical and functional product applications.

title: Study on carbon sequestration and carbon neutrality spatial service scope in the Qinling Mountains of China
summary: Quantifying the carbon sequestration capacity of the Qinling Mountains and delineating its carbon neutrality service scope are of great significance for rational territorial carbon management under China’s “dual carbon” strategy. Using vege
content: Quantifying the carbon sequestration capacity of the Qinling Mountains and delineating its carbon neutrality service scope are of great significance for rational territorial carbon management under China’s “dual carbon” strategy. Using vegetation net primary productivity from 2000 to 2022, this study estimated the net ecosystem productivity (NEP) and carbon absorption of the Qinling Mountains, estimated and spatially downscaled energy-related CO 2 emissions using nighttime-light data, analyzed the spatiotemporal characteristics of carbon neutrality, and delineated the carbon neutrality service scope based on a CO 2 diffusion framework. The main findings are as follows. (1) From 2000 to 2022, the net ecosystem productivity of the Qinling Mountains showed a fluctuating upward trend, with higher values in the west and lower values in the east. (2) Both carbon absorption and carbon emissions (in CO 2 -equivalent mass) exhibited significant fluctuating upward trends, whereas carbon sequestration increased without statistical significance. Carbon sequestration capacity differed markedly across regions: high- and medium-sequestration areas were concentrated in the western and central parts of the study area, while low- and negative-sequestration areas occurred mainly along its northern and eastern edges. (3) The carbon neutrality service radius ranged from 196.67 km to 262.84 km (mean 231.37 km), showing a statistically insignificant expanding trend, with the radiation range covering Gansu, Ningxia, Shanxi, Henan, Hubei, Chongqing and Sichuan. Following the mass‑conservation principle, this study theoretically quantifies the maximum spatial extent of forest carbon‑offsetting capacity instead of simulating actual atmospheric CO₂ transport and neutralization. Multi‑regional carbon‑flux observations will be adopted in future work to validate and refine the simulated service scope, offering solid cases and methodological support for spatial carbon governance of global mid‑latitude mountain ecotones. These results provide a spatially explicit basis for coordinating carbon neutrality actions between the Qinling Mountains and their surrounding regions.

title: Component-Based Reduced-Order Modeling Framework for Rocket Combustion Dynamics in Multi-Injector Configurations
summary: Even with the most advanced computational capabilities, high-fidelity (e.g., large-eddy) simulations of large-scale rocket engines remain far out of reach. In the current work, we develop and establish a component-based reduced-order modeli
content: Even with the most advanced computational capabilities, high-fidelity (e.g., large-eddy) simulations of large-scale rocket engines remain far out of reach. In the current work, we develop and establish a component-based reduced-order modeling (CBROM) framework to enable accurate and efficient parametric modeling of large-scale rocket engines by geometrically decomposing a single domain into a combination of several representative components, including injectors, combustor, and nozzle. Individual component-based reduced-order models (ROMs) are trained for each component with fabricated system-level responses enforced through carefully formulated boundary conditions during the training, which only require high-fidelity simulations of a much smaller computational domain, thereby significantly reducing the costs of ROM training. The trained component-based ROMs are then coupled together to enable full-system simulations. Specifically, we pursue an advanced adaptive ROM formulation leveraging a model-form-preserving least-squares with variable transformation projection to construct the component-based ROMs. The CBROM framework is evaluated using a seven-injector model rocket combustor configuration that exhibits self-excited combustion dynamics with distinct characteristics that vary with operating condition and geometric design variations. The framework is demonstrated to provide accurate parametric predictions of the changes in dynamic behaviors, expressed in the spectra from dynamic mode decomposition analysis and features in the time-averaged and root-mean-squared fields of target state variables.

title: Mineral dust concentration controlling convective cirrus structure and persistence: a large-eddy simulation study with observational constraints
summary: Dusty cirrus clouds are optically thick, convectively organized ice clouds that occur during intense mineral dust outbreaks. Previous modeling studies have found a link between mineral dust and convectively generated cirrus, but have been u
content: Dusty cirrus clouds are optically thick, convectively organized ice clouds that occur during intense mineral dust outbreaks. Previous modeling studies have found a link between mineral dust and convectively generated cirrus, but have been unable to explicitly resolve the associated convective dynamics due to limited spatial resolution. Here, we investigate the evolution and persistence of dusty cirrus using large-eddy simulations constrained by in-situ aircraft observations from the ML-CIRRUS 2014 campaign and complementary remote sensing data. The simulations indicate that sustained convective cirrus requires mineral dust concentrations exceeding climatological values by approximately one to two orders of magnitude, corresponding to number concentrations on the order of N D ∼1 cm −3 . Under these conditions, heterogeneous freezing on mineral dust dominates ice formation and maintains sufficiently high ice crystal number concentrations to sustain strong longwave cooling at cloud top and preserve convective overturning under shortwave radiative warming. In contrast, homogeneous freezing remains largely suppressed across a wide range of simulated conditions. The direct radiative effect of mineral dust is comparatively weak relative to cloud radiative feedbacks and does not significantly influence cirrus evolution. The simulated cirrus is also highly sensitive to the choice of deposition ice nucleation parameterization, highlighting a major source of uncertainty in representing dust–ice interactions. Overall, the results identify mineral dust availability as the primary control on dusty cirrus persistence and emphasize the need for improved representation of heterogeneous ice nucleation in atmospheric models.

title: First observations of aerosol mass fluxes over open water using a large-aperture scintillometer
summary: Near-surface aerosol mass exchange over water remains poorly constrained because direct flux observations are scarce and conventional point measurements have limited spatial representativeness. This study presents the first application of a
content: Near-surface aerosol mass exchange over water remains poorly constrained because direct flux observations are scarce and conventional point measurements have limited spatial representativeness. This study presents the first application of a large-aperture scintillometer (LAS) to retrieve path-averaged aerosol mass-flux magnitudes over open-water-dominated environments, based on four field campaigns at an inland lake and a coastal bay in eastern China. Building on the LAS framework previously applied over terrestrial surfaces, we separated the aerosol-related imaginary and thermodynamic real refractive-index contributions from the log-intensity spectrum. We further replaced the conventional constant aerosol mass-to-optical conversion factor with a campaign-specific continuous relationship, R MN (RH), calibrated using PM 10 , visibility, and relative-humidity observations. The characteristic spectral crossover between the two refractive-index components was identifiable in all four campaigns, while R MN decreased consistently with increasing humidity. Campaign-median flux magnitudes ranged from 0.091 to 0.399 µgm-2s-1. All campaigns exhibited daytime flux enhancements, although the relative contributions of turbulent exchange and aerosol mass-concentration variability differed among campaigns. The coastal observations also showed that dense fog and associated optical attenuation constituted the principal operational limitation. The fitted R MN (RH) relationship strengthened covariation with calculated dry-deposition fluxes. These results extend the LAS aerosol-flux framework from terrestrial to open-water-dominated surfaces and support its use for spatially integrated estimates of the magnitude and temporal variability of turbulent aerosol mass exchange when optical conditions permit.

title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
summary: Abstract Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decad
content: Abstract Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. Further work is necessary to understand how this mechanism might produce more delayed detonation initiation and potentially fail, thereby yielding Type Iax supernovae.

title: Detecting and Isolating Flare Plumes from Upstream Oil and Gas Sites Using Aircraft Sampling
summary: Abstract Aircraft flights have been used in multiple studies to attempt to isolate and measure the compositions of flare plumes. In this work, flare plumes from oil and gas facilities in the Permian Basin of West Texas were simulated, in co
content: Abstract Aircraft flights have been used in multiple studies to attempt to isolate and measure the compositions of flare plumes. In this work, flare plumes from oil and gas facilities in the Permian Basin of West Texas were simulated, in combination with other plumes from the facilities, to predict concentrations along typical aircraft flight paths. Multiple types of flight paths were simulated. Aircraft spirals around sites with active flares, which transected flare plumes approximately 1000 m downwind of the flare, encountered intersecting simulated plumes from multiple sources on the oil and gas sites, making unambiguous sampling of flare plumes very difficult under most conditions. Aircraft flight paths that followed flare plume centerlines toward active flares were typically able to isolate simulated flare plumes, but only within a few hundred meters of the flare and only if the flare plume centerline closely matched the flight path. Predicted concentration ratios in the simulations were qualitatively consistent with observed data from aircraft flights for the simulated facilities. These results demonstrate the need for very careful interpretation of flare combustion efficiencies derived from data collected by instrumented aircraft flying downwind of oil and gas sites.

title: Targeted siRNA-lactobionic lipid nanoparticles with novel ionizable lipid inhibit antithrombin III expression in hepatocytes
summary: Targeted reduction of hepatic antithrombin (AT) via siRNA offers a promising strategy to enhance thrombin (TMB) generation in bleeding disorders, though efficient hepatocyte delivery remains challenging. This study developed and evaluated a
content: Targeted reduction of hepatic antithrombin (AT) via siRNA offers a promising strategy to enhance thrombin (TMB) generation in bleeding disorders, though efficient hepatocyte delivery remains challenging. This study developed and evaluated a targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation incorporating a novel morpholine-based ionizable lipid (MIL) and a lactobionic-octadecylamine conjugate (LBN) for hepatocyte-specific delivery of AT-siRNA (siAT). Following synthesis of MIL and LBN, siAT-loaded LNP (siAT LNP LBN) were prepared using microfluidics and characterized for size, morphology, zeta potential, polydispersity index, and encapsulation efficiency (EE). Functional assays on HepG2 cells assessed cellular uptake, protein knockdown, and AT activity. The optimized formulation exhibited uniform particles (124 nm, PDI 0.125, zeta potential − 8.9 mV) and high EE (90%). Cytotoxicity assays confirmed safety up to 65 pmol siRNA. LBN-decorated LNP significantly enhanced hepatocyte uptake compared to non-targeted LNP and naked siRNA. Optimal AT mRNA suppression occurred at ~ 65 pmol siRNA and 16 h, with protein knockdown confirmed at 48 h. Functionally, siAT LNP LBN reduced AT activity to 48.1 ± 5.5%, substantially outperforming non-targeted LNP (64.1%) and naked siRNA (86.6%). The developed siAT-LNP-LBN platform demonstrated efficient hepatocyte uptake, robust AT knockdown, and low cytotoxicity in vitro, providing preliminary evidence for its potential as a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA delivery platform. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate its biodistribution, liver-targeting efficiency, pharmacodynamic effects, therapeutic efficacy, and biosafety.

title: Evidence of expanding range and environmental suitability for Culex perexiguus in Northern Italy (Emilia-Romagna, 2025)
summary: Culex perexiguus , a mosquito typically associated with hot and semi‑arid environments across North Africa, the Middle East, and southwestern Asia, has recently emerged as a potential public health concern in parts of southern Europe due to
content: Culex perexiguus , a mosquito typically associated with hot and semi‑arid environments across North Africa, the Middle East, and southwestern Asia, has recently emerged as a potential public health concern in parts of southern Europe due to its demonstrated vector capacity for multiple arboviruses, particularly West Nile virus (WNV). In 2025, 84 specimens of this mosquito were collected across 22 sites in Emilia‑Romagna, northern Italy, within the regional WNV entomological surveillance program; DNA barcoding of 21 individuals confirmed morphological identification. Comparison with entomological data from 2009 revealed a concurrent decrease of another mosquito, Culex modestus , suggesting a possible northward shift in suitable areas for both species. Ecological niche modelling based on presence records of Cx. perexiguus indicated an estimated distribution primarily linked to the availability of suitable breeding habitats, and the meteorological anomalies recorded in 2025 (compared to 2001–2020) likely favoured its presence. The unexpected expansion of Cx. perexiguus into Emilia‑Romagna, in an area characterised by a temperate continental climate, underscores the broader changes in mosquito distribution potentially linked to climate change. Its presence may have significant implications for public health, vector surveillance, and control strategies, and will therefore require careful monitoring in the coming years.

title: Cumulative Response of a Base-Isolated Building With Fiber-Reinforced Elastomeric Isolators Under 3D Shaking Table Tests
summary: Fiber-reinforced elastomeric isolators (FREIs) have recently been extensively investigated as a base isolation system through tests on a full scale 2-storey building within the framework of the ERIES-FREISUST research project. To assess the
content: Fiber-reinforced elastomeric isolators (FREIs) have recently been extensively investigated as a base isolation system through tests on a full scale 2-storey building within the framework of the ERIES-FREISUST research project. To assess the influence of multi-component (X, Y, Z) excitations at different intensity levels, two different FREI systems were tested in unbonded configuration at the ST3D shaking table facility of LNEC, Lisbon, Portugal. The testing sequence, which comprised 107 steps including dynamic identification and seismic tests, featured one-direction (1D), 2D and 3D ground motion shaking with increasing scale factors. The isolators exhibited peak displacements of 130 mm, resulting in stable response with no damage to either structural or nonstructural components. Before and after the ground-motion tests, random noise dynamic identification was performed to detect any changes due to potential damage. Based on the cumulative displacement response records measured in both horizontal and vertical directions, it was concluded that the structure sustained no damage, as confirmed by negligible residual values and significant attenuation of floor accelerations recorded with increasing scaling of the ground motions. The experimental program demonstrated the effectiveness of FREIs in providing resilient and sustainable solutions for seismic protection and post-earthquake functionality.

title: Wind Tunnel Study of Wind Loads on a Ship-to-Shore Container Crane Under Synoptic and Non-Synoptic Inflow
summary: The increasing size of ultra-large container vessels has led to the development of larger ship-to-shore (STS) cranes. These cranes are characterized by greater structural slenderness and increased sensitivity to wind-induced loads. Current
content: The increasing size of ultra-large container vessels has led to the development of larger ship-to-shore (STS) cranes. These cranes are characterized by greater structural slenderness and increased sensitivity to wind-induced loads. Current design standards, such as EN 13001-2, typically rely on stationary synoptic wind models, which may not accurately represent the complex, non-synoptic wind climates frequently observed in coastal port environments, particularly thunderstorm and Low-Level Jet outflows. This paper presents the results of an experimental investigation conducted in the Giovanni Solari wind tunnel at the University of Genoa that addresses this limitation. A 1:250 scale STS crane model was tested in three configurations (operational, stowed, and loaded) under synoptic boundary-layer inflow and two non-synoptic outflow profiles (TS1 and TS2), which were characterized by comparable “core” heights and peak speeds, but different turbulence intensities. Results show that, while synoptic inflow generally produces the largest absolute peak coefficients, the more turbulent TS2 condition generates overturning demands approaching those of the synoptic case (up to 95 %). The stowed configuration is identified as the most critical for global stability, exhibiting a 57 % increase in rolling moment relative to the operational condition. Peak factors up to $$g \approx 4.0$$ were observed, exceeding the range (3.0–3.5) typically assumed in engineering practice; however, this is associated with non-Gaussian load behavior and should be interpreted with appropriate statistical caution. These findings suggest that turbulence intensity and the vertical profile of the velocity may significantly influence peak loading and should be considered when assessing the wind-induced response of STS cranes.

title: Does PEO-PDA Coating with Zoledronic Acid Have Antitumor Potential?
summary: Abstract The technologies for implant fabrication are improving every year. Currently, there is a significant demand for implants that not only exhibit high biocompatibility but also possess antibacterial, antiresorptive, and antitumor prop
content: Abstract The technologies for implant fabrication are improving every year. Currently, there is a significant demand for implants that not only exhibit high biocompatibility but also possess antibacterial, antiresorptive, and antitumor properties. In this study, we present a new method for creating implants based on the Ti6Al4V alloy, which surface was modified using plasma electrolytic oxidation followed by the formation of a polydopamine layer with bioactive substances. Vancomycin was used as the antibacterial component of the coating, while bisphosphonate (zoledronic acid) served as the antiresorptive agent. The presence of zoledronic acid and vancomycin in the surface layers was confirmed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy combined with energy-dispersive spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy. During MTS analysis, the culture medium extracted from the samples exhibited cytotoxic activity against human osteosarcoma cells (MNNG/HOS). The data obtained suggests the successful formation of a coating based on the titanium alloy and demonstrates the bioactive properties of the surface layers.

title: Optically resolved excited state hyperfine structure of a silicon color center in the telecom bands
summary: Nuclear spin qubits in silicon offer exceptionally coherent quantum memory, and optically interfaced spins are a promising platform for both quantum networking and distributed quantum computing. It has been proposed that emitters with diama
content: Nuclear spin qubits in silicon offer exceptionally coherent quantum memory, and optically interfaced spins are a promising platform for both quantum networking and distributed quantum computing. It has been proposed that emitters with diamagnetic ground states may permit an optical interface to nuclear spin memories via metastable, hyperfine-coupled excited states while suppressing key sources of decoherence. Until now, direct optical observation of suitable transitions in silicon colour centres has remained elusive. Here we characterize the singly-ionized interstitial aluminum donor (Ali+) in isotopically purified 28Si and find several novel features of this little-studied defect. We measure bright emission and strong optical transitions and, in contrast to previous studies of this centre, attribute its emission to an exchange-split spin triplet and singlet level of the lowest-energy 1s:T2 excited state. We measure the excited-state lifetimes and, as a consequence of its narrow emission linewidth, observe the fine and hyperfine structure of the long-lived triplet state. This constitutes the first measurement of an optically-resolved hyperfine structure in the excited state of a diamagnetic silicon colour centre.

title: Chitosan-intercalated FePS3 as novel and efficient adsorbent for Congo-red dye removal from aqueous solution
summary: Abstract This study investigates surface adsorption of Congo red dye (CR) by iron phosphorus trisulphide (FePS 3 ) before and after chitosan (CS) intercalation. The novel intercalation of CS into the layered nanomaterial FePS 3 was processe
content: Abstract This study investigates surface adsorption of Congo red dye (CR) by iron phosphorus trisulphide (FePS 3 ) before and after chitosan (CS) intercalation. The novel intercalation of CS into the layered nanomaterial FePS 3 was processed to obtain FePS 3 -CS. The materials of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS were characterized by XRD, FTIR, SEM–EDX, and BET techniques. These tests verified the effective intercalation of the chitosan into the layered nanomaterial FePS 3 with improved characteristics for applications involving adsorption. XRD measurements show a slight shift and partial intercalation of CS into FePS 3 layers, and some diffraction peaks have disappeared. This behavior may be due to CS as a polymer interacting with FePS 3 through electrostatic interactions between the amino/hydroxyl groups of CS and S-containing FePS 3 , surfaces, and hydrogen bonding. IR and SEM–EDX confirm the presence of CS functional groups and main elements after intercalation with FePS 3 . FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS exhibited notable removal of Congo-Red from artificial aqueous solutions. The best adsorption circumstances of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS were found in the presence of a dye concentration of 50 mg/L, a dose of (0.05 g and 0.025 g), and pH 5 and 6, respectively, and a contact time of 90 min. Under these conditions, the maximum adsorption efficiencies of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS are 91.4 and 99%, respectively. The results of the kinetic study indicated that a pseudo-second-order kinetic model described the adsorption process with a high degree of agreement between the experimental data and the kinetic model. Moreover, the best kinetic model describing the equilibrium data is the Freundlich isotherm, and this model demonstrates multilayer adsorption behavior. These results highlight the proper effectiveness and promise of FePS 3 and FePS 3 -CS as novel adsorbents for CR dye removal applications.

title: Deep X-Ray View of a Distant Protocluster Anchored by a Quasar at z = 6.63: No Evidence for Enhanced X-Ray AGN Activity
summary: Abstract Whether dense environments accelerate SMBH growth during cosmic reionization remains uncertain because X-ray constraints on z > 6 protoclusters are rare. We analyze ∼865 ks of Chandra observations of the J0910−0414 quasar field, a
content: Abstract Whether dense environments accelerate SMBH growth during cosmic reionization remains uncertain because X-ray constraints on z > 6 protoclusters are rare. We analyze ∼865 ks of Chandra observations of the J0910−0414 quasar field, a massive protocluster at z = 6.63. We construct a catalog of 251 X-ray sources and search for AGN among 21 spectroscopically confirmed members, excluding the central quasar. This is the first systematic X-ray AGN census in a z > 6 protocluster; none of the members are individually detected. Stacking all members (∼17 Ms total exposure) yields no significant signal and limits the average rest-frame 2–10 keV luminosity to 〈 L 2−10 keV 〉≤9.54 × 10 42 erg s −1 . The null result gives a central 90% Jeffreys upper bound of f AGN < 0.09. After accounting for the spatially varying sensitivity, the field Compton-thin X-ray luminosity function predicts N exp , field = 0.0356 AGN in the surveyed volume. Assuming the overdensity profile of AGNs in this protocluster is the same as that of galaxies determined by F. Wang et al., the expected AGN count becomes N exp = 0.131 . Zero detections then imply a one-sided 90% upper limit of η rel < 17.5 on any additional X-ray AGN enhancement beyond that associated with the galaxy overdensity. Although η rel < 17.5 permits more than an order-of-magnitude enhancement, the data show no significant excess of X-ray-detectable AGN in J0910−0414 protocluster. The present X-ray data may miss heavily obscured, intrinsically X-ray-weak, or intermittently accreting SMBHs; the nondetection therefore does not rule out AGNs among the member galaxies.

title: Surgical treatment of a hypercalcemic crisis caused by a parathyroid tumor complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency: a case report
summary: The most common cause of hypercalcemia is a parathyroid tumor (PT). These rare tumors disrupt calcium and phosphorus metabolism and cause multiorgan dysfunction; surgical resection remains the standard treatment for parathyroid tumors. This
content: The most common cause of hypercalcemia is a parathyroid tumor (PT). These rare tumors disrupt calcium and phosphorus metabolism and cause multiorgan dysfunction; surgical resection remains the standard treatment for parathyroid tumors. This case highlights the challenges faced in the diagnosis and management of patients with complex underlying conditions: for patients experiencing a hypercalcemic crisis complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency, perioperative management presents a clinical dilemma between fluid resuscitation and cardiac tolerance, posing significant clinical challenges. A 61-year-old male patient presented with a hypercalcemic crisis caused by a parathyroid tumor, complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency. He complained of excruciating pain in the lower back and extremities, polydipsia, polyuria, and constipation. Laboratory findings showed a serum calcium level of 4.27 mmol/L, an eGFR of 15.97 mL/min/1.73 m \(^{2}\) , and an NT-proBNP level of 1771 pg/mL. Based on these laboratory findings and clinical symptoms, a hypercalcemic crisis complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency was diagnosed; imaging studies revealed a parathyroid adenoma in the right lower pole. Three months after parathyroid tumor resection, serum creatinine decreased from 340 \(\mu\) mol/L to 112 \(\mu\) mol/L. This case demonstrates that parathyroidectomy can be safely performed through the development of an individualized perioperative management plan based on multidisciplinary collaboration. The key lies in carefully balancing fluid resuscitation with cardiac tolerance, the appropriate use of diuretics, and the cautious interpretation of cardiac biomarkers such as NT-proBNP in the context of renal failure.

title: Extended cognitive recovery in down syndrome mice via sustained release of AM404 from microplates
summary: Abstract Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are often characterized by cognitive deficits associated with hippocampal dysfunction and microglial activation. In the in the Dp(16) and Ts65Dn mouse models of Down syndrome (DS), paracetamol (P
content: Abstract Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are often characterized by cognitive deficits associated with hippocampal dysfunction and microglial activation. In the in the Dp(16) and Ts65Dn mouse models of Down syndrome (DS), paracetamol (PRC) has been shown to modulate microglia-mediated neuroinflammation and rescue memory tasks. However, the high doses of PRC typically required limit its long-term use due to dose-related toxicity, including reported hepatotoxicity and cardiotoxicity. Here, we employed polymeric microPLates (µPL) made of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) to sustain delivery of AM404 (AM404-µPL), the primary PRC metabolite with glia-directed anti-inflammatory activity. Using a top-down fabrication approach, AM404 was loaded into square-shaped µPL and evaluated for activity in vitro and in vivo . Free AM404 enhanced microglial metabolism and exerted anti-inflammatory effects comparable to paracetamol in activated microglia from Dp(16) mice. In vivo , low-dose free AM404 (1 mg/kg for three days) improved cognitive deficits in DS mice without affecting control mice; whereas higher doses (10 mg/kg) impaired cognition in healthy mice and had no effect on DS mice. In contrast, a single injection of AM404-µPL improved DS mice cognition for two weeks without harming healthy mice. Notably, after one week, cognitive abilities in DS mice matched those achieved with repeated low-dose of free AM404. These findings support AM404 sustained delivery as a strategy to maintain therapeutic efficacy while reducing dosing frequency and toxicity, offering a promising approach for treating DS as well as other NDDs.

title: Taming the Morning Surge: A QbD-Engineered Multiparticulate Capsule for Sequential RAAS and β₁-Blockade in Circadian Hypertension
summary: Abstract Purpose: Morning blood pressure surge increases cardiovascular risk due to circadian activation of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone and sympathetic nervous systems. This study developed a Quality by Design (QbD)-based dual-release
content: Abstract Purpose: Morning blood pressure surge increases cardiovascular risk due to circadian activation of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone and sympathetic nervous systems. This study developed a Quality by Design (QbD)-based dual-release multiparticulate capsule providing immediate release of olmesartan medoxomil followed by pH-responsive delayed release of metoprolol succinate for chronotherapeutic management of circadian hypertension. Methods: Immediate and delayed-release pellets were prepared by extrusion-spheronization and optimized using Response Surface Methodology with a Box-Behnken Design. Critical formulation variables were optimized to maximize entrapment efficiency, production yield, and drug release. Optimized formulations were evaluated by FTIR, SEM, dissolution studies, release kinetics, and accelerated stability testing. Results: Optimized formulations showed excellent agreement with the quadratic models (R² = 0.9915–0.9988; p < 0.0001). Immediate-release olmesartan pellets provided rapid drug release, while Eudragit-coated metoprolol pellets minimized gastric release and achieved controlled intestinal release. The optimized capsule exhibited satisfactory physicochemical properties, high content uniformity, low friability, reproducible sequential drug release, and acceptable accelerated stability. Conclusion: The QbD-based multiparticulate system successfully combined immediate and delayed drug release in a single chronotherapeutic dosage form. The optimized formulation established a robust design space and demonstrated the potential of sequential multiparticulate delivery for improving management of the early morning hypertension surge.

title: Simultaneous Determination of 20 Veterinary Drugs in Grass Carp by HPLC-MS/MS
summary: Abstract An analytical method was established for the simultaneous determination of 20 veterinary drug residues, including seven fluoroquinolones, 12 sulfonamides, and trimethoprim, in grass carp using pass-through solid-phase extraction (S
content: Abstract An analytical method was established for the simultaneous determination of 20 veterinary drug residues, including seven fluoroquinolones, 12 sulfonamides, and trimethoprim, in grass carp using pass-through solid-phase extraction (SPE) combined with isotope dilution-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS). Samples were extracted by horizontal oscillation with acetonitrile and dehydrated with 1.0 g anhydrous sodium sulfate. The extract was purified using a C18 SPE cartridge in pass-through mode. Chromatographic separation was performed on an Eclipse plus C18 column with gradient elution using 0.1% formic acid in water and methanol as the mobile phases. Detection was conducted using electrospray ionization in positive-ion multiple-reaction-monitoring mode, and quantification was applied by using isotope internal standards. The 20 veterinary drugs showed good linearity over the concentration range of 1–200 μg/L, with correlation coefficients greater than 0.996. Average recoveries at three spiked concentration levels ranged from 78.8% to 115.6%, with relative standard deviations below 15%. The method is simple, accurate, and suitable for the qualitative and quantitative determination of these 20 veterinary drug residues in grass carp.

title: Energy and thermal comfort assessment of insulation strategies in Moroccan residential buildings: a multi-zone simulation study based on the Moroccan thermal construction regulation
source: Journal of Building Pathology and Rehabilitation
summary: Abstract Thermal insulation is the main lever for cutting building energy demand in Morocco, yet no unified comparison of insulation materials exists across the six climatic zones of the Moroccan Thermal Construction Regulation. One two-sto
content: Abstract Thermal insulation is the main lever for cutting building energy demand in Morocco, yet no unified comparison of insulation materials exists across the six climatic zones of the Moroccan Thermal Construction Regulation. One two-storey dwelling of 100.05 m² was simulated in all six zones with DesignBuilder and EnergyPlus: 562 runs covering six conventional insulation materials at five thicknesses, three envelope configurations, and one phase-change material treated separately. Heating and cooling are reported as ideal sensible loads. The conduction and surface heat-balance formulation is first verified against published cavity measurements from Errachidia, reproducing the measured outer surface temperature with a root mean square error of 0.41 K during charging and 0.95 K over a 22-hour cycle, without parameter fitting. Extruded polystyrene applied to walls and roof at 6/6 cm gives the largest reduction in annual demand in every zone, from 12.55% in Agadir to 27.19% in Ifrane. Compared at equal thermal resistance rather than equal thickness, however, the six materials agree to within 0.05 percentage points: the advantage of polymer foams reflects only the thickness needed to reach a given resistance, 4.63 cm of XPS against 6.63 cm of wood fiber. Lowest demand does not coincide with best comfort. Wall insulation raises discomfort hours in every scenario tested in Agadir and Errachidia, because it suppresses the opaque envelope, the dwelling's dominant heat sink, removing 19199 kWh yearly in the reference case; roof insulation degrades comfort nowhere. Insulation should be selected by climatic zone and envelope component, not by conductivity alone.

title: Essential roles of autophagy in multi-organelle reduction and remodeling during Arabidopsis seed maturation
summary: Abstract To establish functional seed traits, the accomplishment of proper seed maturation on mother plants is essential. During seed development and maturation, organelles undergo dynamic changes to transition into a metabolically quiescen
content: Abstract To establish functional seed traits, the accomplishment of proper seed maturation on mother plants is essential. During seed development and maturation, organelles undergo dynamic changes to transition into a metabolically quiescent state in mature seeds, ensuring the capacity for eventual germination and seedling establishment. Although this maturation process is known to be controlled by seed-specific transcriptional regulatory networks, how organelle populations are reduced or remodeled to adapt the intracellular environment to a dry seed state remains poorly understood. In this study, using transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana seeds expressing organelle-specific fluorescent markers, we showed that multiple organelles, including plastids, the endoplasmic reticulum, peroxisomes, and mitochondria, undergo rapid reduction and remodeling during seed maturation. Furthermore, we demonstrated that autophagy, a major intracellular degradation system, is essential for these maturation-associated changes, as evidenced by the abnormal retention or accumulation of organelles and organelle-derived components in autophagy-defective mutants. Crucially, our study reveals that autophagy establishes the intracellular state of mature seeds by promoting multi-organelle reduction and remodeling during seed maturation.
