title: Syntropic infrastructure for regenerative urban metabolic reorganization in an Atlantic island city
summary: Urban climate vulnerability is increasingly associated with ecological fragmentation, thermal amplification, hydrological disruption, and declining ecosystem functionality across densely urbanized territories. This study proposes syntropic
content: Urban climate vulnerability is increasingly associated with ecological fragmentation, thermal amplification, hydrological disruption, and declining ecosystem functionality across densely urbanized territories. This study proposes syntropic infrastructure as a regenerative urban framework capable of reorganizing ecological, hydrological, and thermal regulation processes through multiscalar spatial connectivity. Using Santa Cruz de Tenerife as a case study, the research integrates ecological connectivity metrics, land surface temperature (LST), soil organic carbon (SOC), hydrological runoff modeling, and socioecological accessibility indicators within a GIS-based spatial assessment framework standardized at 250 m grid resolution. Results revealed severe ecological fragmentation across the consolidated metropolitan matrix, with Probability of Connectivity values below 0.15 and Integral Index of Connectivity values below 0.10 throughout most coastal urban sectors. Thermal analyses identified persistent surface temperature anomalies ranging between +3 °C and +5 °C relative to peri-urban vegetated reference areas. Pearson correlation analyses demonstrated significant inverse relationships between SOC and LST ( r = −0.64, p < 0.01), while imperviousness intensity showed a strong positive association with thermal amplification ( r = 0.71, p < 0.01). Spatial autocorrelation analyses additionally confirmed significant clustering of thermal hotspots and degraded soils. The findings suggest that syntropic infrastructure may operate as a regenerative planning framework capable of increasing ecological connectivity, evapotranspirative cooling, hydrological retention, and socioecological resilience through integrated adaptive interventions in vulnerable coastal and island metropolitan systems.

title: From Bird Migration to Market Prices: How Will Offshore Wind Curtailment Affect Future Sustainable Electricity Systems?
summary: Bird-related offshore wind curtailment is increasingly used to reduce collision risk during periods of intense bird migration, but its energy and electricity-market consequences depend strongly on when curtailment occurs. This study combine
content: Bird-related offshore wind curtailment is increasingly used to reduce collision risk during periods of intense bird migration, but its energy and electricity-market consequences depend strongly on when curtailment occurs. This study combines a historical analysis of Dutch Start/Stop events with a forward-looking electricity-market assessment. First, Start/Stop notifications between 2023 and 2026 are analysed using observed offshore wind conditions and aggregated offshore wind production to characterise the meteorological and generation conditions associated with individual events. The selected events occurred under markedly different wind conditions, with mean wind speeds during the notified periods ranging from approximately 5.0 to 10.5 m/s, indicating substantial variation in the wind-generation potential available during curtailment periods. Second, the EYE electricity-market model is used to assess the potential future electricity-system consequences of bird-related offshore wind curtailment under the National Drivers 2030 scenario. Sensitivity cases with offshore wind availability reduced by 40%, 60%, and 90% are compared with a reference case with full offshore wind availability. In the 2030 simulations, reduced offshore wind generation is compensated through changes in imports, dispatchable generation, storage, and other flexibility options. Daily-average market-clearing prices increase by approximately 2.0–5.0%, while larger price deviations are concentrated within the actual curtailment hours. The results demonstrate that the consequences of Start/Stop operation are both time-specific and resource-dependent, reflecting not only curtailment duration but also wind availability and electricity-system conditions during the affected hours. These scenario-specific results provide an assessment approach potentially relevant to other offshore wind regions with migration-related restrictions; the quantitative impacts depend on local wind, market and regulatory conditions. The findings can inform the integration of biodiversity protection into sustainable offshore wind and electricity-system development.

title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Abstract Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis, and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological, and human health studies. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG
content: Abstract Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis, and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological, and human health studies. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models─including both endogenous and synthetic molecules─to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% of target molecular volumes and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems, the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility of the OLIVES and Go̅Martini models makes them best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. Finally, models were validated in interaction with membranes by comparison to reference atomistic data. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

title: The stellar populations of resolved galaxies
summary: The study of galaxies outside the Milky Way using observations of resolved stellar populations has experienced extraordinary growth over the past two decades. There now exist panchromatic photometry and precise astrometry for hundreds of mi
content: The study of galaxies outside the Milky Way using observations of resolved stellar populations has experienced extraordinary growth over the past two decades. There now exist panchromatic photometry and precise astrometry for hundreds of millions of individually resolved stars in hundreds of galaxies that span $\sim10^9$ in luminosity, $\sim10^3$ in metallicity, and sample a wide range of environments. Here, we review advances in extragalactic astronomy enabled by resolved stellar population imaging. We summarize major observational programs and focus on four interconnected science areas: the star formation histories of galaxies, 'bursty' star formation, the stellar initial mass function, and the orbital histories of Local Group galaxies. We review the literature in each area, synthesize key findings, identify emerging trends, and discuss how new and future facilities (e.g., JWST, LSST, Euclid, Roman, CSST, ELTs, HWO) will enable further progress. Finally, we highlight shortcomings in current datasets and discuss promising directions for new areas of investigation.

title: Thorium and europium production in the early Galaxy. Implications for nucleocosmochronology
summary: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology. Among the available chronometers, the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio provides a promising age indicator. We investigated the reliability of t
content: The ages of the oldest stellar populations can be investigated through nucleocosmochronology. Among the available chronometers, the thorium-to-europium abundance ratio provides a promising age indicator. We investigated the reliability of the log( Th / Eu ) ratio as a chronometer for old stellar populations by testing whether thorium and europium are produced in a consistent ratio in metal-poor stars. We also assessed the precision with which this abundance ratio can be measured and the resulting uncertainties in stellar ages, adopting the best available theoretical estimate of the initial production ratio to establish the absolute age scale. We present new thorium and europium abundance measurements for a sample of eight / reference stars observed with UVES at the VLT. We combined these measurements with homogeneous samples from the literature and analysed the evolution of log( Th Eu ) as a function of metallicity. Adopting a theoretical r-process production ratio, we derived stellar ages and investigated the impact of observational uncertainties and sample statistics on the resulting age constraints. At low metallicities, the observed log( Th / Eu ) ratios show no significant dependence on metallicity once stars with anomalous actinide abundances are excluded, supporting the assumption that thorium and europium were typically co-produced in the early Galaxy. The derived ages are broadly consistent with those expected for metal-poor halo stars, although uncertainties in individual ages remain large. We show that higher spectral resolution is required to improve the precision of Th measurements, while combining measurements from several stars in coeval populations could provide an additional statistical improvement. Nucleocosmochronology is a valuable independent method for dating the oldest stellar populations. Although individual stellar ages are currently limited by observational and theoretical uncertainties, the analysis of homogeneous samples of coeval stars, such as members of globular clusters, could provide significantly stronger constraints. Future high-resolution multi-object spectroscopic facilities will facilitate this approach and provide independent constraints on the early formation history of the Milky Way and the age of the Universe.

title: Sertoli Tfeb and Tfe3 Redundantly Sustain Spermatogenesis via Cycs-Mediated Mitochondrial Bioenergetics
summary: Abstract Sertoli cells provide essential metabolic and bioenergetic support to developing germ cells, thereby sustaining male fertility. However, the transcriptional networks that safeguard somatic mitochondrial homeostasis, and their poten
content: Abstract Sertoli cells provide essential metabolic and bioenergetic support to developing germ cells, thereby sustaining male fertility. However, the transcriptional networks that safeguard somatic mitochondrial homeostasis, and their potential involvement in idiopathic male infertility, remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that the MiT/TFE transcription factors Tfeb and Tfe3 function redundantly to maintain Sertoli cell function; their concurrent deletion in mice results in severe oligo-astheno-teratozoospermia (OAT) and profound subfertility. Single-cell transcriptomic, metabolomic, and ultrastructural analyses reveal that simultaneous Tfeb and Tfe3 deficiency collapses mitochondrial bioenergetic homeostasis in Sertoli cells, characterized by a depleted tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and markedly reduced ATP production. Mechanistically, by integrating CUT&Tag and transcriptomic profiling, we identify Cycs (encoding cytochrome c) as a direct transcriptional target. Both Tfeb and Tfe3 bind to discrete cis -regulatory elements within the Cycs promoter to drive its expression, which is required to maintain respiratory chain integrity. Together, these findings establish a crucial Tfeb/Tfe3-Cycs-ATP signaling axis that couples somatic mitochondrial energetics to germ cell development, providing a conceptual framework and potential therapeutic targets for male reproductive disorders.

title: Solvation structure induced solvent-mediated growth of Li 2 O 2 and uniform deposition of Li + for high-performance lithium-oxygen batteries
summary: Abstract The practical application of Li-O2 batteries is limited by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and dendritic Li growth. Here, we introduce 6-bromoxoindole (6-Br-Oxind) as a multifunctional electrolyte additive to regulate Li+ solvation,
content: Abstract The practical application of Li-O2 batteries is limited by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and dendritic Li growth. Here, we introduce 6-bromoxoindole (6-Br-Oxind) as a multifunctional electrolyte additive to regulate Li+ solvation, guide solution-mediated Li2O2 growth, and stabilize Li plating. After partial deprotonation, 6-Br-Oxind coordinates with Li+ to form 6-Br-Oxind···Li+ species that capture soluble O2-/LiO2 intermediates and promote their conversion into Li2O2 through a solution-mediated pathway. The same solvation structure weakens Li+-TEGDME coordination, lowers the Li+ desolvation barrier, and establishes a more uniform Li+ flux at the anode. Meanwhile, Br- released from 6-Br-Oxind and F- generated from TFSI- decomposition form a LiBr@LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase that further suppresses dendritic Li deposition. As a result, Li-O2 batteries with 6-Br-Oxind show enhanced reversibility, a low overpotential of 0.81 V, and extended cycling stability, while Li||Li symmetric cells operate stably for 1,300 h. This work demonstrates a solvation-structure strategy for coupling cathode reaction regulation with anode interphase stabilization in Li-O2 batteries.

title: Alkaline Hydrogen Peroxide Pretreatment of Oil Palm Empty Fruit Bunches: Delignification, Digestibility, and Bioethanol
source: AJARCDE (Asian Journal of Applied Research for Community Development and Empowerment)
summary: Oil palm empty fruit bunches (OPEFB) are an abundant lignocellulosic residue for second-generation bioethanol, but lignin-induced recalcitrance limits enzymatic conversion, and maximal delignification does not necessarily maximize downstrea
content: Oil palm empty fruit bunches (OPEFB) are an abundant lignocellulosic residue for second-generation bioethanol, but lignin-induced recalcitrance limits enzymatic conversion, and maximal delignification does not necessarily maximize downstream yield. This study tested whether the alkaline hydrogen peroxide (AHP) condition that maximizes lignin removal also maximizes reducing sugar release and bioethanol response. OPEFB (30 mesh) was pretreated with 1–11% (w/v) H?O? at 30, 50, and 70°C for 1 h at pH 11.5, characterized by Chesson–Datta compositional analysis, SEM, and FTIR, hydrolyzed with Viscozyme® L, and fermented with Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Relative to untreated OPEFB (25.81% lignin, 31.39% cellulose), the lowest residual lignin (16.34%; 35.68% lignin removal) occurred at 5% H?O? and 50°C, whereas the highest cellulose content (50.38%, a 60.5% relative increase) and the highest apparent bioethanol response occurred at 5% H?O? and 70°C. Reducing sugar ranged from approximately 21 to 30 mg/mL, with the lowest value at 5% H?O? and 50°C, the condition of maximum delignification. Increasing H?O? beyond 5% did not further delignify the fibres. SEM and FTIR showed an opened fiber structure with retained carbohydrate-related bands. AHP pretreatment of OPEFB should therefore be optimized across lignin removal, carbohydrate retention, and fermentation response rather than delignification alone, supporting SDG 7, SDG 12, and SDG 13 through valorization of palm oil residues. Contribution to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):SDG 7: Affordable and Clean EnergySDG 12: Responsible Consumption and ProductionSDG 13: Climate Action

title: Pd-doped MoS2 thin films grown by sol–gel spray coating: structural, vibrational and optical modifications and their impact on photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue under LED irradiation
source: Journal of Applied Materials and Technology
summary: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) is an attractive visible-light photocatalyst, but fast electron–hole recombination limits its performance. Here, undoped and Pd-doped MoS2 thin films (2, 4 and 6 wt.% nominal Pd) were deposited on quartz by sol–g
content: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) is an attractive visible-light photocatalyst, but fast electron–hole recombination limits its performance. Here, undoped and Pd-doped MoS2 thin films (2, 4 and 6 wt.% nominal Pd) were deposited on quartz by sol–gel spray coating and sulfurized at 800 °C in a sulfur-rich atmosphere. X-ray diffraction confirmed hexagonal 2H-MoS2 in all films with dominant (002) texture, indicating lamellae parallel to the substrate. Pd incorporation contracted the c lattice parameter and strongly narrowed the (002) reflection: the Scherrer coherent domain size increased from 4.7 nm (undoped) to 62.3 nm at 4% Pd and decreased again to 16.9 nm at 6% Pd. Raman spectroscopy confirmed this trend, with E12g and A1g modes blue-shifting and narrowing from 15 to 5 cm-1 for 2–4% Pd, then broadening at 6% Pd. FTIR showed the Mo–S band near 600 cm-1 in every film with no Pd-related phase. The optical gap remained at 1.087 ± 0.076 eV (indirect) and 1.132 ± 0.005 eV (direct), consistent with multilayer MoS2, while absorption intensity increased with Pd. Under 20 W LED irradiation, all films outperformed photolysis (8.0% in 40 min). The 4% Pd film reached 88.1% methylene blue degradation with kap= 0.0483 min-1, 1.29 times the undoped film, while 6% Pd fell to 57.8%. Because the optical gap is invariant across the series, this gain is attributed to improved crystalline order and to Pd-mediated interfacial charge separation, both optimal at intermediate loading; a mechanism consistent with, but not independently verified by, the present data.

title: Carbon quota compensation mechanism for deep peak regulation of thermal power units to enhance renewable energy accommodation
summary: During deep peak regulation, thermal power units face increased low-carbon compliance pressure because carbon-emission intensity rises non-linearly at low loads. Existing studies generally rely on fixed emission factors or simplified linear
content: During deep peak regulation, thermal power units face increased low-carbon compliance pressure because carbon-emission intensity rises non-linearly at low loads. Existing studies generally rely on fixed emission factors or simplified linear models and fail to characterize carbon-quota surpluses and deficits under current settlement policies or provide compensation mechanisms for flexible thermal-power regulation. In this study, we propose a carbon quota compensation mechanism to enhance renewable energy accommodation. First, a full-operating-condition carbon-emission model is established considering non-linear emission-intensity variation and the startup/shutdown rebound effect. Analysis based on this model reveals that carbon emissions may decrease while carbon quota demand increases during deep peak regulation. Second, a dynamic green certificate–carbon quota conversion coefficient is derived by matching additional carbon quota demand with incremental renewable energy accommodation, establishing a physically interpretable linkage between convertible green certificates and dedicated carbon offsets. Finally, a multi-time-scale rolling optimization and compensation strategy is developed based on model predictive control. Annual, monthly, and daily operations are coordinated through dynamic environmental-rights inventories, rolling updates, and ex post compensation accounting, thereby incorporating long-term environmental costs into short-term scheduling. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed mechanism alleviates deep peak-regulation pressure on thermal power units, improves renewable energy accommodation, and enhances the low-carbon economic performance of the power system.

title: Data for "A Small-Scale High-Temperature Furnace for Gas-Atomization of Novel Reduced-Activation Copper Alloys"
summary: This research experiment aimed to design a small-scale, high-temperature furnace capable of reaching temperatures of at least 1800ºC. This furnace is to be used as part of an in-house gas-atomizing chamber that will allow for rapid developm
content: This research experiment aimed to design a small-scale, high-temperature furnace capable of reaching temperatures of at least 1800ºC. This furnace is to be used as part of an in-house gas-atomizing chamber that will allow for rapid development and testing of novel copper alloys in order to find a material comparable to GRCop-42, to use in the additive manufacturing of fusion components, without the issue of neutron activation that GRCop-42 has. After conducting validation experiments, a small-scale furnace has been developed that can reach temperatures of ~2300ºC. This archive contains the CAD files used to prototype the final furnace design and the MATLAB files used to analyze data during validation experiments. MATLAB files contain the raw validation data from our temperature profile, power vs. temperature, rise-fall time, and PID oscillations tests, as well as the script created to run the analysis. Names of MATLAB files and associated data: PID_Pyrometer_Tests.xlsx: Raw temperature data from pyrometer during each test rise-time + temperature oscillation test with the various PID settings. Comparing_PID_settings.m: The various rise times and oscillations of all PID settings tested on the power supply. Furnace_rise_fall_time_150amps.m: The rise and fall time of the furnace when power supply current was set at a constant value, 150 amp. PID_rise_rates.m: Displays the rise rates of each PID setting for the first 5 seconds after reaching 800ºC in command window. PID_Tests_Fluct.m: Outputs the Zoomed-in graph of system behavior around the target temperature for each PID setting and outputs the oscillation period for each setting. Oscillation period values were only considered/recorded for behaviors that were oscillatory and neglected for those that were not. PID_Tests_Functions.m is a function used to extract the data from the .xlsx files pkpk_bar_graph.m: Outputs a bar graph and numerical values of the average peak-to-peak temperature values for each PID setting. Helped delineate which settings were oscillatory and which were not. Power_v_Temp_no_Tant_inner_outer.m: Graphs the furnace's core (left y-axis) and outer (right y-axis) temperatures as a function of power, without the use of tantulum, as well as best-fit lines—the core temperature was fitted to the equation connecting conductive and radiative heat lost to power. Temperature_Profile_1000_1400_1800.m: Plots the inner temperature of the carbon tube as a function of distance from the center, when the furnace was set to 1000ºC, 1400ºC, and 1800ºC. Furnace_temp_profile_Data.xlsx: Raw data collected from temperature profile testing. Power_v_Temp_rad_cond_losses.m: This plots the data from the Temp C Power Test (inverted to Power V Temp), along with the portion of heat loss due to radiative and conductive losses.

title: Radioactive disequilibrium chronometry of uranium and radium loss from weathering gold mine tailings in tropical Ghana
summary: Abstract Radiological surveys of gold tailings can only provide activity concentrations, and not indicate whether uranium and radium are being lost. On a 1–49 year chronosequence of 54 Ghanaian tailings, 226 Ra/ 238 U rose from 1.02 to 1.44
content: Abstract Radiological surveys of gold tailings can only provide activity concentrations, and not indicate whether uranium and radium are being lost. On a 1–49 year chronosequence of 54 Ghanaian tailings, 226 Ra/ 238 U rose from 1.02 to 1.44 and 228 Ra/ 232 Th fell from 1.02 to 0.92. Loss rate constants derived from these chronometers are 1.7–2.2 × 10 − 2 y − 1 for uranium and 1.0–1.3 × 10 − 2 y − 1 for radium, a little higher than the measured losses, though the numbers are still subject to uncertainty and are treated as upper limits. Leachate 234 U/ 238 U, determined using alpha spectrometry, rose from 1.05 (acid-reactive) to 1.29 (oxide-rich) tailings, which falls within the range of 1.27–1.38 reported for local groundwater. Radionuclide mobility is determined by the weathering stage rather than the activity level.

title: Multi-decadal trends in SST, chlorophyll-a, NPP and atmospheric forcing across oligotrophic and upwelling regions of the Northeast Atlantic
summary: Abstract Climate change is reshaping the Northeast Atlantic, yet its impact differs between oligotrophic and upwelling ecosystems. We analysed multi-decadal trends from satellite and reanalysis datasets of sea surface temperature (SST), chl
content: Abstract Climate change is reshaping the Northeast Atlantic, yet its impact differs between oligotrophic and upwelling ecosystems. We analysed multi-decadal trends from satellite and reanalysis datasets of sea surface temperature (SST), chlorophyll- a (chl- a ), net primary production (NPP), and wind stress across the Northeast Atlantic Subtropical Gyre and adjacent upwelling regions. SST increased across the region, with the strongest warming in the Azores (+ 3.18°C century⁻¹) and the weakest in the Permanent Upwelling (PU) region (+ 1.37°C century⁻¹). Chl- a trends were predominantly negative, with the largest decline in PU (− 1.62 mg m⁻³ century⁻¹), accompanied by a reduction in highly productive area (− 6.25% century⁻¹). NPP also declined, with the strongest trends in the Cape Juby Weak Permanent Upwelling and Seasonal Upwelling region (− 459.56 and − 351.38 mg C m⁻² day⁻¹ century⁻¹, respectively). Upwelling-favourable wind stress intensified in the Northwest African upwelling system, reaching + 15.98 mN m⁻² century⁻¹ in PU and + 12.32 mN m⁻² century⁻¹ in Cape Juby, but without increased chl- a concentrations. Comparison with trends ending in 2019 indicated stronger SST and chl- a trends, suggesting that the 2023–2024 North Atlantic marine heatwave influenced warming estimates.

title: Effect of steady magnetic field on microstructure and microhardness of laser-directed energy-deposited Ti6Al4V/TiC composite coatings
summary: Coarse microstructures, reinforcement agglomeration, and non-uniform property distribution are critical issues in laser-directed energy-deposited Ti6Al4V/TiC composite coatings. To address these issues, this study adopts a steady magnetic f
content: Coarse microstructures, reinforcement agglomeration, and non-uniform property distribution are critical issues in laser-directed energy-deposited Ti6Al4V/TiC composite coatings. To address these issues, this study adopts a steady magnetic field with gradient intensities to assist the laser-directed energy deposition process. Ti-based composite coatings were fabricated on Ti6Al4V substrates under three laser processes with different heat inputs. Macroscopic observation, microstructural characterization, and microhardness tests were performed to investigate the coupled effects of magnetic field strength and laser heat input on coating formation quality, microstructural evolution, and microhardness. A magnetic modulation coupling coefficient K was proposed to quantitatively evaluate the modulation performance. The results show that the steady magnetic field effectively improved the macroscopic forming quality of the coatings. Surface defects decreased, and the wetting angle increased monotonically with rising magnetic field strength. The magnetic field’s modulation of microstructure and hardness was highly process-dependent. Under medium- (1,000 W, 350 mm/min, 1.2 r/min) and low-heat-input processes (800 W, 350 mm/min, 1.0 r/min), a low magnetic field of 4.07 mT yielded the optimal grain refinement and TiC dispersion uniformity. For the low-heat-input process, coating hardness first decreased slightly and then increased continuously with increasing magnetic field strength. For the medium-heat-input process, hardness increased monotonically, reaching its maximum at 12.11 mT. Under the high-heat-input process (1,200 W, 250 mm/min, 1.0 r/min), a low magnetic field aggravated microstructural coarsening, and significant strengthening was achieved only when the field strength reached 12.11 mT. The maximum coating hardness reached 1155.16 HV0.2, 50.85% higher than that of the sample without a magnetic field. The hardness evolution is governed by the combined effect of grain refinement and second-phase evolution. The proposed coupling coefficient can effectively quantify the interaction between the magnetic field and laser energy, providing a theoretical reference for optimizing steady-magnetic-field-assisted laser-directed energy deposition.

title: Do Traffic Congestion Indicators Improve PM2.5 Forecasting? Evidence from Machine Learning Models in Kampala
summary: Abstract Air pollution remains a major environmental and public health challenge in Kampala, Uganda, where PM 2.5 concentrations frequently exceed World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines values. Although traffic emissions are widely reco
content: Abstract Air pollution remains a major environmental and public health challenge in Kampala, Uganda, where PM 2.5 concentrations frequently exceed World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines values. Although traffic emissions are widely recognized as contributors to urban air pollution, limited empirical evidence exists on whether traffic-congestion indicators improve PM 2.5 forecasting beyond information provided by meteorological and temporal variables. This study evaluated the predictive contribution of traffic-congestion indicators to PM 2.5 using machine learning models. PM 2.5 , temperature, and humidity observations were obtained from the AirQo monitoring network, while traffic data were collected along the Jinja Road transport using the Google Routes API. After preprocessing and temporal synchronization, a dataset consisting of 696 hourly observations was used to implement Random Forest and HistGradientBoosting forecasting models. Environmental baseline models were compared with traffic-enhanced models incorporating mean speed, travel duration, and Traffic Performance Index (TPI). Model performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and the coefficient of determination (R 2 ). Results showed that the best environmental baseline model, HistGradientBoosting, achieved superior performance (MAE = 15.28, RMSE = 21.40, R 2 = 0.5752) compared with the best traffic-enhanced model (MAE = 23.16, RMSE = 31.70, R 2 = 0.4753). Correlation and feature-importance analysis further indicated that traffic-congestion indicators exhibited weak relationships with PM2.5 concentrations and contributed substantially to less predictive information than temporal and meteorological variables. An additional analysis incorporating lagged PM 2.5 variables achieved the highest explanatory performance (R 2 = 0.6245), highlighting the importance of historical pollution measurements in forecasting future PM 2.5 concentrations. The findings suggest that, within the study context, corridor-level congestion indicators provided limited incremental forecasting value, while temporal patterns, meteorological conditions, and historical PM 2.5 measurements were more influential predictors. The study contributes empirical evidence for evaluating predictor relevance in machine-learning based air-quality forecasting and provides insights for the design of efficient forecasting systems in rapidly urbanizing cities.

title: Changes in the suitable habitat of Ectropis grisescens (Warren, 1894) (Lepidoptera: Geometridae) in China under climate change
summary: Introduction Ectropis grisescens is a major pest species infesting tea plants ( Camellia sinensis ). In this study, we developed an ensemble species distribution model using the Biomod2 framework to predict the potential suitable habitat of
content: Introduction Ectropis grisescens is a major pest species infesting tea plants ( Camellia sinensis ). In this study, we developed an ensemble species distribution model using the Biomod2 framework to predict the potential suitable habitat of E. grisescens and identify the key environmental factors limiting its distribution, thereby providing a theoretical basis for effective prevention and control strategies. Methods A total of 149 geographic occurrence records and 12 environmental predictors were used to simulate the current potential distribution of E. grisescens and to analyze the dominant driving variables. Future changes in suitable habitat were also projected under three climate scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585) for the 2050s and 2070s. Results The Biomod2 ensemble model demonstrated high predictive accuracy and reliability (AUC = 0.973, TSS = 0.845). Among the 12 selected environmental predictors, bio1, bio2, elevation, and bio17 were identified as the key factors, with contribution rates of 32.46%, 26.01%, 18.78%, and 15.71%, respectively. Under current climate conditions, the suitable habitat of E. grisescens is mainly distributed in southeastern China (Sichuan, Shaanxi, Chongqing, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangxi, and Guangdong provinces), covering an area of 169.33 × 10⁴ km². Under future climate scenarios, the suitable habitat area decreased in all cases, declining to 168.83 × 10⁴ km² under SSP126 in the 2070s and to 100.28 × 10⁴ km² under SSP585 in the 2070s. Under future climate scenarios, the centroid of the suitable habitat of E. grisescens shifted northward in all cases, with the greatest cumulative displacement of 171.56 km (SSP585) and the smallest cumulative displacement of 86.05 km (SSP126). Discussion These findings provide important scientific evidence for the future management and monitoring of E. grisescens .

title: Unlock the potential of power-to-ammonia in future multi-energy transition pathways
summary: The high-renewable-energy transition toward a global carbon peak and neutrality represents a long-standing and formidable challenge. Although increasing attention has been paid to sector coupling and emerging energy carriers, how power-to-a
content: The high-renewable-energy transition toward a global carbon peak and neutrality represents a long-standing and formidable challenge. Although increasing attention has been paid to sector coupling and emerging energy carriers, how power-to-ammonia (P2A) may reshape spatiotemporal energy transitions amid technological and financial uncertainties has not been addressed. Here, we develop a risk-aware P2A-driven multi-energy transition pathway based on synergistic effects among electrical, ammonia, and thermal energy carriers. Taking Hubei Province and China as case studies across various technological and financial scenarios, we show that geographically spatiotemporal P2A and renewable energy development can reinforce each other, reducing conventional thermal generation by over 98.81% from 2030 to 2050 under high-renewable scenarios. We conclude that although the transition trajectory varies substantially with technological and financial risks, P2A-driven cross-sector multi-energy coupling can provide a promising pathway for accelerating energy system transition, particularly under the highly optimistic and exploratory P2A cost scenario of $100/kW.

title: Regime-Dependent Resilience in Climate Equity Markets: Evidence from Markov Switching and Drawdown Analysis
source: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
summary: This study investigates whether climate-oriented equity indices exhibit resilience during periods of extreme financial and geopolitical stress. Using daily data from 2015 to 2025, we examine six major global and regional climate benchmarks
content: This study investigates whether climate-oriented equity indices exhibit resilience during periods of extreme financial and geopolitical stress. Using daily data from 2015 to 2025, we examine six major global and regional climate benchmarks through a two-regime Markov-switching framework. Model selection tests confirm the presence of nonlinear regime dynamics. Importantly, variance switching emerges as the dominant driver of regime dependence. Transition probabilities indicate strong persistence of climate market indexes in bullish regimes and relatively short-lived bearish episodes, particularly outside major systemic shocks such as COVID-19 and the 2022 energy crisis. To complement the regime analysis, resilience is further assessed using Maximum Drawdown (MaxDD) and Time to Recovery (TTR) indicators. Among the indices examined, the MSCI World Climate Change Low Carbon Index demonstrates the shortest time to recovery, indicating comparatively stronger post-shock resilience.

title: Multi-agent dual federated learning for intelligent task offloading in hierarchical edge–fog–cloud 6G networks
summary: The rapid emergence of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks is driving the need for intelligent task offloading frameworks capable of simultaneously satisfying stringent latency, energy efficiency, scalability, and privacy requirements.
content: The rapid emergence of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks is driving the need for intelligent task offloading frameworks capable of simultaneously satisfying stringent latency, energy efficiency, scalability, and privacy requirements. Existing task offloading approaches are constrained by centralized learning architectures, binary offloading decisions, inadequate handling of heterogeneous non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, and limited awareness of wireless interference dynamics, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization in hierarchical Edge–Fog–Cloud (EFC) environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes MADFL-6G, a Multi-Agent Dual Federated Learning framework for intelligent task offloading in hierarchical 6G networks — ‘Dual’ referring to MWFA’s two-component aggregation weighting, which jointly combines data-volume proportionality and KL-divergence-based distribution-similarity penalization (Sect. 3.5, Eq. 9). The proposed framework integrates distributed Dueling Deep Q-Network (Dueling DQN) agents with Prioritized Experience Replay (PER), a Mobility-Weighted Federated Averaging (MWFA) strategy for robust aggregation under heterogeneous data distributions, an interference-aware seven-dimensional state representation, and a five-action adaptive partial task offloading mechanism that dynamically distributes computational workloads across edge, fog, and cloud resources. The task offloading process is formulated as a set of coupled, independently learning agents operating within a shared, non-stationary Edge–Fog–Cloud environment, incorporating stochastic wireless channel conditions and queueing dynamics to accurately model realistic 6G environments. Extensive experiments conducted on more than 200,000 real task execution records demonstrate that MADFL-6G achieves an average latency of 61 ms, energy consumption of 0.31 J, and a 98.7% task success rate, outperforming conventional federated deep Q-learning by 28.2%, 31.1%, and 2.6%, respectively, while substantially exceeding heuristic and centralized baselines. Additional analyses, including scalability evaluation, component ablation, statistical significance testing, robustness under non-IID settings, and SHAP-based explainability, confirm the effectiveness, interpretability, and reliability of the proposed framework. These findings demonstrate that MADFL-6G provides a scalable, privacy-aware, raw-data-preserving, and explainable solution for intelligent resource management in emerging 6G applications, including autonomous transportation, industrial Internet of Things, smart cities, and extended reality services.

title: Small‐Molecule Protein Kinase Inhibitors Approved by the U.S. FDA as Anticancer Agents From 2021 to 2025
summary: Protein kinases coordinate cellular proliferation, differentiation, survival, metabolism, and stress responses, and dysregulated kinase signalingf is a defining feature of many malignancies. From 2021 through 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Ad
content: Protein kinases coordinate cellular proliferation, differentiation, survival, metabolism, and stress responses, and dysregulated kinase signalingf is a defining feature of many malignancies. From 2021 through 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) approved 26 small-molecule kinase inhibitors for cancer therapy, extending precision treatment across non-small-cell lung cancer, hematologic malignancies, breast and ovarian cancers, cholangiocarcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, glioma, and other kinase-driven tumors. The approved agents illustrate advances in medicinal chemistry and translational pharmacology that include covalent inhibitors such as sotorasib and futibatinib, mutation-selective inhibitors such as taletrectinib and zongertinib, allosteric inhibitors such as asciminib and mirdametinib, and multitarget or combination strategies such as avutometinib plus defactinib. Improvements in central nervous system exposure, mutant selectivity, dosing durability, and biomarker-defined patient selection have broadened clinical utility. This Review integrates the discovery background, mechanism of action, synthetic route, pharmacological properties, clinical efficacy, safety, and regulatory context of these agents. It also evaluates acquired resistance, target-related and off-target toxicities, heterogeneous evidence supporting accelerated approvals, and the uncertain translation of biochemical potency into durable survival benefit. Successful kinase drug development therefore requires molecular design to be aligned with clinically achievable exposure, validated biomarkers, resistance surveillance, and confirmatory evidence.

title: Urea-induced acidification drives bacterial succession and hysteretic metal mobilization in a wheat-peanut rotation soil system in China
summary: Abstract Excessive nitrogen fertilization is a primary driver of farmland soil acidification, yet the dose-dependent coupling among acidification, heavy metal mobilization, and microbial community succession remains poorly resolved. In this
content: Abstract Excessive nitrogen fertilization is a primary driver of farmland soil acidification, yet the dose-dependent coupling among acidification, heavy metal mobilization, and microbial community succession remains poorly resolved. In this study, a 60-day aerobic incubation of a wheat-peanut rotation soil amended with urea at 0, 100, 300, and 500 µg/g dry weight soil, integrating soil physicochemical analysis, DTPA‑extractable metal monitoring, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, and FAPROTAX functional prediction. Soil pH declined to its minimum on day 28, with reductions increasing with urea rate, and recovery by day 60 was limited and negatively correlated with nitrogen input. NH 4 + -N peaked on day 14 and remained elevated under high nitrogen, whereas a transient NO 2 - -N pulse coincided with the pH minimum, confirming nitrification as the dominant proton‑producing pathway. Notably, Urea300 and Urea500 reached comparable NH 4 + and NO 3 - levels despite differing inputs, indicating disproportionately active nitrification at the intermediate dose. Heavy metal mobilization exhibited a pronounced hysteresis: pH reached its minimum on day 28, whereas Cd, Cu, and Zn mobilization peaked on day 60—a lag of approximately one month—decoupling metal toxicity from pH recovery, although all metals remained below GB 15618‑2018 thresholds. For bacterial communities, Urea100 had minimal effects, Urea300 triggered drastic functional reorganization (nitrification and manganese oxidation increased; aerobic chemo-heterotrophy halved; nitrogen fixation and hydrocarbon degradation nearly lost), and Urea500 exhibited partial functional recovery and greater stability, reflecting rebalancing rather than a simple dose‑dependent decline. These shifts were tightly coupled with taxonomic reorganization, with Gammaproteobacteria and its representative genus Chujaibacter driving enhanced nitrification, while Alphaproteobacteria and Sphingomonas showed inverse trends. These findings reveal a nonlinear, threshold‑like response of soil microbial communities to nitrogen‑induced acidification and highlight the need to control single urea applications below 300 kg N/ha with intervals of no less than 60 days to safeguard soil ecological health.

title: A standardized integrated workflow to generate cellularized and decellularized silk fibroin scaffolds for bone tissue engineering
summary: Purpose Silk fibroin (SF) is a biocompatible and biodegradable protein polymer widely used in bone tissue engineering due to its mechanical robustness, tuneable degradation profile, and ability to support osteogenic differentiation. In this
content: Purpose Silk fibroin (SF) is a biocompatible and biodegradable protein polymer widely used in bone tissue engineering due to its mechanical robustness, tuneable degradation profile, and ability to support osteogenic differentiation. In this study, an integrated experimental workflow was used to generate an acellular bone extracellular matrix (ECM)-laden SF construct, encompassing the fabrication of porous three-dimensional SF scaffolds by salt leaching, their cellularization with human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs), and subsequent decellularization. Methods Scaffolds were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), while cell colonization and osteogenic differentiation were assessed by immunofluorescence and real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR); decellularization efficiency was evaluated by complementary approaches. Results The results demonstrated that SF scaffolds provided a structural template that promoted cell colonization, ECM deposition, and osteogenic marker expression, while retaining their three-dimensional architecture through methanol stabilization, salt leaching, autoclaving, osteogenic culture, and decellularization. The porogen shows a median particle size (D50) of 207.3 µm (D10-D90 range: 136.8–293.7 µm). Calcium (K = 38.35) and phosphorus (K = 25.92) are detected by EDX in hASC-seeded scaffolds after osteogenic culture and are absent in empty scaffolds. Decellularization reduces the nuclear density from approximately 312 nuclei/mm 2 by more than 99%, while calcium (K = 8.03) and phosphorus (K = 10.83) remain detectable in the retained matrix. Conclusion These findings supported the potential of SF-based constructs as platforms for bone tissue engineering and ECM-derived biomaterial production. Furthermore, the decellularized ECM-coated scaffolds could serve as a starting point for more complex experimental models, including the introduction of vascular components through co-culture or perfusion-based strategies, thereby representing a step towards the engineering of fully vascularized bone constructs.

title: Assessment of Psychrotolerant Microbial Consortium for Enhanced Paddy Straw Decomposition under Low-Temperature Conditions
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Paddy straw management still remains a key issue in the rice-wheat cropping systems of North India, especially during the post-harvest phase because low temperatures limit microbial activity, which leads to delayed straw decomposition. Resi
content: Paddy straw management still remains a key issue in the rice-wheat cropping systems of North India, especially during the post-harvest phase because low temperatures limit microbial activity, which leads to delayed straw decomposition. Residue burning, one of the conventional practices followed for quick disposal of straw, greatly impacts the environment, nutrient cycling, and emissions of greenhouse gases. This study assessed the efficiency of using a psychrotolerant microbial consortium for accelerating paddy straw decomposition at low temperatures. The fungal strains were isolated from paddy straw and soil in winter season, and their lignocellulase production capability was screened at 10°C. Three isolates (T. harzianum S14, C. globosum S17, and T. asperellum S20) were chosen after considering their compatibility and efficiency in hydrolysis to prepare the psychrotolerant consortium. Decomposition potential of the consortia was determined by laboratory experiments and validated using in situ field experiments carried out at Amritsar, Punjab, India, at average winter temperatures of about 10°C. The effect of various rates of the consortium (from 2.5 to 10.0 L ha⁻¹) on the decomposition rate was determined. The results indicated significantly higher rates of breakdown of paddy straw in the treatment plots than in control plots, with 30.42% biomass reduction occurring after 21 days from application of the consortia, while in the control plots, it was recorded as 20.62%. Higher biomass reduction was achieved when the highest consortia dose, T5 (10 L ha⁻¹) was applied as indicated by high microbial population, improved soil enzyme activity (dehydrogenase, urease, and alkaline phosphatase), nutrient availability, with maximum available nitrogen (323 kg ha⁻¹), phosphorus (20.97 kg ha⁻¹), and potassium (271 kg ha⁻¹). This study indicate that a combination of psychrotolerant microorganisms provides a promising and environmentally friendly approach to paddy straw management in cold climate conditions, thereby minimizing residue burning without affecting the fertility of the soil.

title: Ecosystem CO 2 flux of a lake habitat with submerged vegetation
summary: Abstract. Although submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) can grow rapidly in shallow lakes, their role in controlling CO2 exchange between lakes and the atmosphere remains poorly understood. In this study, the air-water CO2 flux was measured w
content: Abstract. Although submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) can grow rapidly in shallow lakes, their role in controlling CO2 exchange between lakes and the atmosphere remains poorly understood. In this study, the air-water CO2 flux was measured with a closed-path eddy covariance system in a SAV zone of Lake Taihu, China, from July 2020 to December 2023. Satellite-derived vegetation indices and dissolved CO2 measurements were used to investigate the influence of vegetation seasonality and water-column CO2 storage on the flux. The habitat was a net CO2 source during the winter and spring and a sink in the late summer to early autumn. The annual net flux was positive, indicating emission, at 45 and 89 g CO2 m-2 yr-1 in 2022 and 2023, respectively, indicating that uptake during peak SAV coverage was insufficient to offset emission in the other months. At the monthly scale, the normalized difference vegetation index explained 45% of the observed flux variability. At the half-hourly scale, the flux showed no clear dependence on solar radiation or water temperature. The water-column storage flux had a greater diurnal amplitude than the air–water flux measured by eddy covariance, suggesting that the dissolved CO2 pool buffered the exchange between underwater vegetation and the atmosphere. Nighttime CO2 uptake and declining dissolved CO2 concentrations during the first half of the night provided some evidence for Crassulacean Acid Metabolism. These observations show that water-column carbon storage plays an important role in supporting SAV CO2 uptake and weakens its temporal coupling with atmospheric CO2 exchange.

title: A Highly Active and Promiscuous Esterase for Amide Bond Synthesis under Aqueous Conditions
summary: Abstract A growing number of hydrolase enzymes show acyltransferase activity under aqueous conditions. However, the competing hydrolysis reaction and the limited catalytic rates for these enzymes prevent them from being routinely used for s
content: Abstract A growing number of hydrolase enzymes show acyltransferase activity under aqueous conditions. However, the competing hydrolysis reaction and the limited catalytic rates for these enzymes prevent them from being routinely used for synthetic applications. To find improved enzymes, we generated an enzyme panel based on promiscuous acyltransferase template enzymes. We identified SoEst12, a highly active and selective enzyme belonging to the family VIII carboxylesterases. Kinetics show that this enzyme is up to 8600× faster (kcatapp) than the well-studied PestE using a model reaction for amidation and that its impressive activity is not limited to the model ester. Enzyme loading studies coupled with the kinetics showed a kinetically controlled selectivity for amidation over hydrolysis, which can be best exploited when using a low enzyme loading. SoEst12 displays a wide amine substrate scope with no hydrolysis of the amide product formed. Competing hydrolysis with some of the ester substrates has been reduced by the introduction of a point mutation in the family-conserved WGG motif. Modeling of these point mutants showed that the reduced hydrolysis activity is correlated with an improved affinity for the amine. The SoEst12 crystal structure was solved, and the N-terminus of a cleaved tag of a symmetry neighbor was found inserted into the active site of the enzyme close to a bound acetate, suggesting a “cleaved amide” and giving mechanistic insight into the high activity and selectivity shown by SoEst12. We demonstrate the synthetic potential of SoEst12 by synthesizing the antiarrhythmic drug procainamide and an AKT inhibitor intermediate in buffer using a low biocatalyst loading.

title: Terrain Architecture & Soil Vulnerability across the Narmada Rift Valley Gradient in Barwani, Central India
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: This study evaluates the relationship between landforms and soil properties within the Narmada Valley Basin of Barwani District, Madhya Pradesh, exploring how geomorphological architecture drives spatial soil variability, nutrient distribut
content: This study evaluates the relationship between landforms and soil properties within the Narmada Valley Basin of Barwani District, Madhya Pradesh, exploring how geomorphological architecture drives spatial soil variability, nutrient distribution, and land degradation severity. Integrating high-resolution Remote Sensing and GIS frameworks (SRTM-DEM data processed via ArcGIS) with field-based laboratory testing across Barwani, Rajpur, and Sendhwa blocks, we map a distinct toposequence gradient from low-lying alluvial plains to the rugged basaltic terrains of the Satpura Mountain Range.The empirical findings reveal a topographically driven nutrient and physical breakdown across the basin. The flat Narmada Valley Basin Plain (150m–180m MSL) operates as a depositional sink dominated by heavy, clay-rich Vertisols (Black Cotton Soils) exhibiting high water-retention capacity (>47% clay), optimal neutral-to-alkaline pH scales (7.58–7.65), and robust available Potassium pools (up to 402.0 kg/ha). Conversely, as the terrain ascends into the rugged Satpura Structural Foothills (>400m MSL), steep slopes and dense dendritic drainage configurations trigger rapid surface runoff and intense gully erosion. This process physically alters the soil into porous, gravelly skeletal matrices (locally called Bardi) marked by a surge in Soil Degradation Score to a critical peak of 9.4, severe depletion of Organic Carbon (dropping to 0.18%), low available Nitrogen (125.0 kg/ha), and slight acidification (pH 6.22).These structural variations directly govern the local botany, restricting highland vegetation to droughtresistant indigenous millets and dry-deciduous floral clusters (Boswellia serrata). The paper concludes that uniform agroenvironmental policies are ineffective for Barwani’s diverse landscape. We recommend localized drainage controls for the clayheavy plains alongside immediate contour trenching, check-dam construction, and targeted native afforestation to stabilize the fragile highland ecosystems.

title: Local agglomeration and hydrogen investment decisions: evidence from a global project panel
summary: Abstract Announced hydrogen capacity greatly exceeds the capacity that has reached a final in vestment decision, and European policy promotes local clusters, hydrogen valleys, that co-locate production, demand and infrastructure. Whether pr
content: Abstract Announced hydrogen capacity greatly exceeds the capacity that has reached a final in vestment decision, and European policy promotes local clusters, hydrogen valleys, that co-locate production, demand and infrastructure. Whether producers already commit ted pull other producers across the decision margin is a further hypothesis, which that policy does not state. We test it: are hydrogen projects already committed or operating within 50 km associated with the transition of a neighbouring pre-decision project to a final investment decision? Six vintages of the International Energy Agency hydrogen project database, harmonized across a changing status vocabulary and aggregated into documented investment units, yield a risk panel of 3,211 unit-period observations and 128 transitions between 2023 and 2026. A discrete-time hazard model with country and vintage fixed effects gives an association of −0.04 percentage points per standard deviation of local commitment, against a mean transition probability of 4.0%, with a 90% interval of [−0.83,+0.74]. The estimate is statistically equivalent to zero within a 1.08-point benchmark, under the primary specification and not under country-by vintage effects, where the association moves to +0.51 points. The panel records status changes between vintages, not decision dates, and the association is not causal. JEL Classification R12 · Q42 · C81

title: Partitioning Local and Long-Range Black Carbon in the High Arctic: Microphysical Aerosol Properties from the SP2-XR in Northwest, Greenland
summary: Abstract. Black carbon deposition on the Greenland Ice Sheet significantly reduces surface albedo and accelerates melt, yet the microphysical properties that distinguish local emissions from long-range wildfire smoke remain poorly constrain
content: Abstract. Black carbon deposition on the Greenland Ice Sheet significantly reduces surface albedo and accelerates melt, yet the microphysical properties that distinguish local emissions from long-range wildfire smoke remain poorly constrained. We characterized single-particle refractory black carbon (rBC) using an Extended Range Single Particle Soot Photometer (SP2-XR) at the Thule High Arctic Atmospheric Observatory in northwest Greenland from June to September 2024. By pairing real-time measurements with local meteorology and Navy Aerosol Analysis and Prediction System Reanalysis (NAAPS-RA) smoke concentrations, we partitioned aerosol measurements into local, long-range, and mixed regimes. Here we report microphysical properties of rBC as core mass-equivalent diameter (EMD), equivalent optical diameter (EOD), and equivalent coating thickness (ECT). Fresh emissions from local infrastructure (Pituffik Space Base) were characterized by larger median rBC mass cores (EMD = 196.3 nm), smaller total optical diameters (EOD = 316.1 nm), and thin coatings (ECT = 56.7 nm). In contrast, long-range biomass burning smoke from North America exhibited smaller rBC cores (EMD = 184.7 nm), significantly larger overall optical diameters (EOD = 343.1 nm; 𝑝 < 0.01) and statistically significantly thicker secondary aerosol coatings (ECT = 60.8 nm; 𝑝 < 0.05). Consistent with previous studies, this inverse relationship between core and optical size provides near-surface validation that secondary non-rBC coating accumulation drives the total optical volume of aged Arctic smoke. As Arctic shipping, local industrialization, and high-latitude wildfires increase, these distinct optical and microphysical signatures provide essential observational constraints for climate models to accurately simulate BC optical properties, atmospheric deposition, and snow-albedo feedbacks.

title: Aczel-Alsina prioritized aggregation operators for interval-valued p,q-rung orthopair fuzzy sets and their application to multi-criteria decision-making
summary: This study introduces a new approach to prioritized aggregation operators (AOs) for interval-valued p,q-rung orthopair fuzzy (IVpqRF) information. Using the theory of unknown weight vectors, we develop novel methods for pqRF environments, i
content: This study introduces a new approach to prioritized aggregation operators (AOs) for interval-valued p,q-rung orthopair fuzzy (IVpqRF) information. Using the theory of unknown weight vectors, we develop novel methods for pqRF environments, including the IVpqRF Aczel-Alsina (AA) prioritized average (IVpqRFAAPA) and IVpqRF AA prioritized geometric (IVpqRFAAPG) operators. We also present weighted prioritized AOs, such as the IVpqRF AA prioritized weighted average (IVpqRFAAPWA) and IVpqRF Aczel AA prioritized weighted geometric (IVpqRFAAPWG) operators. Key properties of these operators are discussed to highlight their versatility. Building on these developments, we propose an algorithm for multi-criteria decision-making and apply it to a case study on selecting a smart parking system using IVpqRF information. Comparative analyses with existing literature demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our approach.

title: Integrating Satellite-Derived Vegetation Indices and Field Observations for Monitoring Seasonal Wetland Changes
summary: The wetlands in monsoon environments experience rapid changes in water cover, aquatic plants, and bare substrate, although systematic monitoring programs fail to record such events on a management scale. In this study, the combination of ve
content: The wetlands in monsoon environments experience rapid changes in water cover, aquatic plants, and bare substrate, although systematic monitoring programs fail to record such events on a management scale. In this study, the combination of vegetation and water indices derived from Sentinel-2 images was linked with repeated field observations in order to analyze the intra- and inter-annual variability of the Vedanthangal tank wetland in a monsoon-driven environment in India. The monthly timeseries of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index (SAVI), and Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) were constructed using 76 satellite images without clouds, together with field sampling conducted 12 times throughout the year and involving 24 fixed plots that collected data on vegetation cover, height of macrophytes, leaf chlorophyll, and water depth. Wetland condition showed a clear annual pattern that was regulated by the northeast monsoon: maximum water cover occurred in December and January, while the development of floating and emergent vegetation took place in the post-monsoon drawdown period. The MNDWI index captured field water depths well, while NDVI, SAVI, and EVI largely accounted for variability in vegetation cover. The NDVI index alone was affected by the presence of water under the plant canopy cover as well as saturation in thick floating vegetation cover; the combination of NDVI with MNDWI gave more accurate vegetation maps. The dry 2022-23 hydrological year caused delayed filling and shortened the inundation period by one month, resulting in a delay in the vegetation peak. The combination of multiple indices from time series of satellite images and a limited number of field measurements provides a reliable framework for monitoring changes in wetlands.

title: WASP-39 b: The 4.3 Micrometre Carbon Dioxide Feature in Scale Heights, Its Amplitude Budget and Detection Significance
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: WASP-39 b, a 0.28 Jupiter-mass, 1.27 Jupiter-radius planet on a 4.06-day orbit, delivered the first clear carbon dioxide detection in an exoplanet atmosphere when JWST near-infrared spectroscopy recorded a prominent absorption peak near 4.3
content: WASP-39 b, a 0.28 Jupiter-mass, 1.27 Jupiter-radius planet on a 4.06-day orbit, delivered the first clear carbon dioxide detection in an exoplanet atmosphere when JWST near-infrared spectroscopy recorded a prominent absorption peak near 4.3 micrometres during 2022 commissioning-era observations. A strong molecular band raises the apparent planetary radius by several scale heights at its core relative to the neighbouring continuum; dividing the measured peak-to-continuum depth difference by the one-height geometric amplitude counts those heights directly, and the count, set against the band's opacity, constrains the absorber's abundance without a full retrieval. Headline values are wasp39 surface gravity m per s2 wasp39b = 4.302; wasp39 scale height km wasp39b = 930.9; wasp39 one height amplitude ppm wasp39b = 431.2; wasp39 co2 feature ppm wasp39b = 2100; wasp39 co2 heights spanned wasp39b = 4.87; wasp39 detection significance sigma wasp39b = 14. Counting the feature in heights rather than parts per million alone exposes how much of its prominence the planet's low gravity supplies.

title: Biochar-treated cropland fields show variable soil organic carbon response but low nitrogen demand for carbon sequestration
summary: Biochar (BC) amendment is a means of increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) and has been explored frequently using high application rates in controlled experiments. Smaller rates and application under on-farm experimental conditions are less
content: Biochar (BC) amendment is a means of increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) and has been explored frequently using high application rates in controlled experiments. Smaller rates and application under on-farm experimental conditions are less studied but considered more realistic. Here, we report results from field-scale BC application on five commercial arable farms in Switzerland with annual doses of 1 t BC/ha over 3–5 years. We analysed SOC and nitrogen changes and soil organic matter thermal stability using high-resolution volumetric soil sampling, including subsoil down to 60 cm for fields split into BC-treated and control. Our analysis revealed three main findings. First, unlike in controlled field experiments with high BC application, using low BC rates at the field level showed no uniform SOC stock increase, but differences were noted between farms, with some controls even outperforming the BC treatment. Second, for fields where SOC increased more than the amount of BC applied relative to the control field, thermal analysis revealed a relative increase not only in the high-temperature region of BC itself (> 450 °C) but also in the thermally more labile fraction below 350 °C. By contrast, the same labile thermal region declined for fields where SOC increased less than expected with BC addition. Finally, SOC accrual with BC required significantly less nitrogen than the same increase without BC, a finding that deserves further attention, as it suggests that SOC sequestration with BC is particularly nitrogen efficient.

title: Deep Hydrocarbon Sources, Charging History, and Late-Stage Tectonic Modification in the Qimeigan Area, Southwestern Tarim Basin
summary: Abstract The Qimeigan area in the southwestern Tarim Basin contains multiple potential source intervals and records multistage hydrocarbon charging followed by tectonic modification. This study integrates biomarker data from five Carbonifer
content: Abstract The Qimeigan area in the southwestern Tarim Basin contains multiple potential source intervals and records multistage hydrocarbon charging followed by tectonic modification. This study integrates biomarker data from five Carboniferous source-rock samples (three from Well Shatan-1 and two from Well Qiqian-2), 11 Qipan Formation source-rock samples (three from Well Shatan-1, three from Well Qiqian-1, and five from Well Kuntan-1), and three Kangkelin Formation reservoir-rock extracts from Well Shatan-1. Natural-gas geochemical data include seven gas samples from Wells Shatan-1 and Kuntan-1, among which four samples (three from Well Shatan-1 and one from Well Kuntan-1) were analyzed for carbon isotopes, together with fluid-inclusion petrography and microthermometry and burial–thermal history. The reservoir liquid hydrocarbons show a stronger geochemical affinity with the Carboniferous source rocks, although a Qipan Formation contribution cannot be excluded. Natural gas has dryness coefficients of 0.985–0.999 and isotopic characteristics of high- to overmature thermogenic dry gas. The Carboniferous is interpreted as the most likely gas-supplying interval based on its deep burial, advanced thermal evolution, and regional petroleum-system framework, although contributions from other mature source intervals cannot be excluded. Petrographic relationships distinguish earlier and later fluid assemblages, with associated aqueous inclusions defining broad Th populations at 120–125 °C and 140–145 °C. Projection onto the burial–thermal history yields approximate fluid-activity windows of 20–14 Ma and 9–4 Ma. The earlier stage is oil-related, whereas the later stage records gas-dominated overprinting of earlier liquid hydrocarbons. Late tectonic activity mainly controlled remigration, redistribution, and differential preservation rather than a third independent charging event. The present reservoir state therefore reflects the coupling of hydrocarbon supply, fluid-phase evolution, fault effectiveness, and late-stage preservation.

title: Pharmacognostic Standardization, Phytochemical Profiling And In Vitro Antimycobacterial Evaluation Of Nelumbo Nucifera Gaertn. Seedpod
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: In this study, we examined the pharmacognostic properties, phytochemical constituents, and anti-tuberculosis activity of seeds from Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn (Sacred Lotus), a plant traditionally regarded as inedible waste and a source of bio
content: In this study, we examined the pharmacognostic properties, phytochemical constituents, and anti-tuberculosis activity of seeds from Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn (Sacred Lotus), a plant traditionally regarded as inedible waste and a source of bioactive compounds. A pharmacognostic evaluation was performed on the crude drug and involved macroscopic and microscopic inspections for diagnostic and quality control purposes. In accordance with guidelines from the World Health Organization, total ash, acid-insoluble ash, water-soluble ash, sulphated ash, moisture content, and extractive value were used to analyze plant material purity. With successive Soxhlet extraction using petroleum ether, chloroform, ethanol and water, the plant was extracted, and then examined for phytochemical characteristics, chromatographic evaluation (Paper and thin layer chromatography), and anti-tuberculosis screening in vitro. A phytochemical analysis of the ethanolic extract revealed alkaloids, steroids, carbohydrates, phenolic compounds, flavonoids, glycosides, terpenoids, and tannins. An ethanolic extract demonstrated good antimycobacterial activity with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 50 to 100 µg/mL against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv in the Microplate Alamar Blue Assay (MABA). The bioactivity was strongly correlated with a prominent sample spot (Rf 0.495–0.501) and the reference standard (Rf 0.496) by thin-layer chromatography (TLC) at 254 nm, suggesting quercetin and its glycosides may be responsible for the bioactivity. These findings provide a scientific basis for the continued investigation of N.nucifera's potential as an antitubercular agent.

title: Motorcycle Helmet Shell Silhouettes, Paintable UV Zones and Surface Finishes Dataset
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Structured 3D reference catalog covering 33 motorcycle helmet shell silhouettes across 5 rider categories (12 full face, 7 motocross, 2 adventure dual sport, 6 open face and 6 half helmets), paired with hardware traits (sun peak and chin ba
content: Structured 3D reference catalog covering 33 motorcycle helmet shell silhouettes across 5 rider categories (12 full face, 7 motocross, 2 adventure dual sport, 6 open face and 6 half helmets), paired with hardware traits (sun peak and chin bar presence), 6 paintable shell zone keys and 5 surface finish presets (gloss, matte, chrome, pearl and carbon fiber). Includes flat tabular JSON Lines (records.jsonl) and complete JSON specification (styles.json) for 3D graphic layout and wrap zone mapping. Data Source and Live 3D Studio: Published by Custom Motorcycle Helmet, an AI 3D helmet customization platform where riders generate artwork onto any of the 33 helmet shells and fine-tune zones and finishes in the 3D motorcycle helmet designer. Interactive catalog at dirt-bike-graphics.github.io/custom-motorcycle-helmet.

title: Linking evaporitic crust texture to microbial community structure in a hypersaline environment
summary: Introduction Hypersaline evaporitic environments are considered terrestrial analogues for planetary settings, because they preserve mineralogical and biological signatures formed under extreme salinity, high UV radiation, and arid condition
content: Introduction Hypersaline evaporitic environments are considered terrestrial analogues for planetary settings, because they preserve mineralogical and biological signatures formed under extreme salinity, high UV radiation, and arid conditions. However, the relationships between the surface texture of evaporitic crusts and the underlying microbial communities are largely disregarded. In this study, we investigated the relationship between the texture of evaporitic crusts and the microbial community structure, affecting the biogeochemical processes in a hypersaline pan environment (Kudiakam Pan, Makgadikgadi Basin, Botswana). Methods Five crust textures (i.e., silcrete pavement, tee-pee structures, irregular, wrinkled-up, bulbous crusts) were characterized using physical–chemical measurements and 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding, complemented by predicted functional profiles. Results Physicochemical parameters showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with alkaline conditions throughout the study area. Bacterial and archaeal communities differed markedly between samples from the pan and the outside floor. Crust surface texture explained a large and significant fraction of the variation in bacterial community composition. Cyanobacterial communities showed particularly strong differentiation among textures, with Xenococcaceae predominating in silcrete pavement and tee-pee A crusts, and Nodosilineaceae, Nostocaceae, and Oscillatoriaceae enriched in irregular, wrinkled-up, and bulbous crusts. Functional prediction revealed widespread organic carbon degradation, sulfur cycling, and methanogenesis co-occurring with phototrophic activity. Discussion These findings indicate evaporite texture is associated with microbial community structure, making evaporitic crusts potentially informative samples for interpreting biosignatures on Mars.

title: Mitigation of Interfacial Phonon Scattering in Polyimine/Graphene Composites Through Controllable In Situ Construction of Liquid Crystal Networks
summary: ABSTRACT Thermally conductive polymer composites are promising candidates for advanced thermal management. However, their performance is often limited by severe interfacial phonon scattering and low intrinsic thermal conductivity ( λ ) of p
content: ABSTRACT Thermally conductive polymer composites are promising candidates for advanced thermal management. However, their performance is often limited by severe interfacial phonon scattering and low intrinsic thermal conductivity ( λ ) of polymers. Herein, a strategy was proposed for mitigating interfacial phonon scattering via controllable in situ construction of liquid crystal polyimines and their composites with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs). Ordered liquid crystalline domains with enhanced π–π stacking interactions are in situ introduced into the polyimines by tailoring the ratio of diamine crosslinkers, thereby improving intrinsic λ and interfacial affinity with GNPs. Optimized TD 7 B 3 polyimines exhibit a λ of 0.35 W m −1 K −1 , which is significantly higher than amorphous counterparts. When combined with 50 wt.% GNPs, as‐prepared composite achieves superior in‐plane and out‐of‐plane λ of 35.51 and 6.53 W m −1 K −1 , respectively, along with low thermal resistance of ∼0.70 K In 2 W −1 . Structural characterizations and molecular simulations reveal enhanced performance originates from the formation of ordered laminated structures, strong π–π interfacial interactions, and matched phonon spectra. Furthermore, TD 7 B 3 G 50 composites demonstrate superior thermal stability and heat dissipation capability in LED thermal management. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high‐performance polymer composites by synergistically optimizing intrinsic thermal transport and interfacial phonon coupling.

title: The Use of Experimentally Determined Aerodynamic Coefficients for the Reconstruction of Wind Loads on Antenna Masts
summary: Experimental identification of wind loads provides a tool for understanding the structural behavior of dynamically sensitive infrastructure and enhancing its resilience. This task is particularly challenging for guyed antenna masts, which e
content: Experimental identification of wind loads provides a tool for understanding the structural behavior of dynamically sensitive infrastructure and enhancing its resilience. This task is particularly challenging for guyed antenna masts, which exhibit a non-linear response and feature multiple ancillaries that significantly alter aerodynamic effects. Both in the identification of the static and the dynamic wind loads, the aerodynamic coefficients (mainly drag and lift) play a key role. This paper first presents a methodology for the identification of static and dynamic wind loads for guyed antenna masts that takes into account the nonlinear behavior of the structure. Next, we recapitulate the results of wind tunnel tests on a scaled model of an 80-m-tall guyed antenna mast, that have been carried out at the Giovanni Solari Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel at the University of Genova, in order to estimate its aerodynamic coefficients. Through numerical simulations it is demonstrated how the identified aerodynamic coefficients are used to estimate the static wind field parameters on the structure as characterized by the angle of attack $$\alpha $$ and the reference wind velocity $$\bar{U}_{10}$$ .

title: Synthesis and SERS Evaluation of Cu/Cu2O Microtubes
summary: Abstract In this work, Cu/Cu2O microtubes were fabricated by electroless deposition on polymer templates and evaluated as substrates for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). The structural, morphological, and optical properties of th
