content: Abstract In this work, Cu/Cu2O microtubes were fabricated by electroless deposition on polymer templates and evaluated as substrates for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). The structural, morphological, and optical properties of the substrate were characterized by XRD, SEM/EDS, XPS, and UV–vis spectroscopy. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of face-centered cubic copper (90.1%) with a minor Cu2O phase (9.9%), while XPS showed that the surface was dominated by Cu0/Cu+ species with a minor contribution from Cu2+ species. UV–vis absorption spectroscopy revealed a broad absorption band in the 400–600 nm range. Additional electromagnetic modeling was used to evaluate the optical and near-field response of the Cu structures. The SERS performance of the substrate was evaluated using four probe analytes: methylene blue, methyl violet, eosin yellow, and potassium chromate. Analytical enhancement factors ranging from 0.2 × 103 to 0.8 × 104 were obtained, depending on the analyte.

title: HIF-2α Drives NF-κB–NLRP3–Dependent Inflammatory Lung Injury Following Trauma
summary: Abstract Lung contusion (LC) is a common consequence of blunt thoracic trauma and a major risk factor for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Although tissue hypoxia is a hallmark of LC, the mechanisms linking hypoxic signaling to p
content: Abstract Lung contusion (LC) is a common consequence of blunt thoracic trauma and a major risk factor for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Although tissue hypoxia is a hallmark of LC, the mechanisms linking hypoxic signaling to persistent inflammation and lung injury remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of hypoxia-inducible factor-2α (HIF-2α), encoded by EPAS1 , using a translational approach combining human and porcine-contused lung tissues, a murine model of isolated LC with alveolar epithelial cell-specific HIF-2α deletion, a bacterial pneumonia model, and in vitro macrophage studies. Postmortem human contused lung tissues showed increased HIF-2α expression in the alveolar epithelium, consistent with published single-cell transcriptomic data demonstrating increased EPAS1 expression in epithelial cells and macrophages from injured lungs. In a porcine model of combined hemorrhagic shock and pulmonary contusion, HIF-2α expression was increased in contused regions compared with uninjured regions of the same animal. In mice, conditional deletion of HIF-2α in type II alveolar epithelial cells reduced bronchoalveolar lavage albumin levels, attenuated injury-associated changes in lung mechanics, and decreased inflammatory cytokine and chemokine production. These effects were accompanied by reduced NF-κB, NLRP3 inflammasome-associated, and VEGFA signaling. Mice lacking epithelial HIF-2α also exhibited improved survival following lethal Klebsiella pneumoniae challenge. In macrophages, pharmacological HIF stabilization enhanced inflammatory gene expression, whereas selective HIF-2α inhibition with PT2385 reduced IL-1β promoter activity and caspase-1 activation. Collectively, these findings implicate HIF-2α in the regulation of inflammatory signaling and lung injury following trauma and support further investigation of HIF-2α-dependent pathways as potential therapeutic targets in ARDS.

title: Mechanism Analysis of Interaction Between GFL and GFM Converters
summary: As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, converter control dynamics play a critical role in power system synchronization, making small-signal synchronization stability an important concern in converter-dominated power systems.
content: As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, converter control dynamics play a critical role in power system synchronization, making small-signal synchronization stability an important concern in converter-dominated power systems. Grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) converters differ in synchronization mechanisms and stability characteristics, and their coordinated operation may introduce complex dynamic interactions. These differences and interactions make it challenging to clarify how converter control dynamics affect synchronization stability, both individually and through their interaction. This paper develops a unified small-signal modeling and path decomposition method (PDM) for GFL and GFM converters in single- and two-converter systems. Based on this, a stability contribution index is introduced to quantify and compare the effect of each path on the dominant oscillatory mode. The proposed method separates the effects of AC network, single converter, and inter-converter interaction paths and reveals how key control parameters affect system stability, thereby providing a theoretical basis for stability assessment and coordinated parameter design in multi-converter systems.

title: ATR-FTIR and GC–MS Profiling of Ascaridia galli: Preliminary Characterization of Functional Groups and Chemical Constituents
summary: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) were used to provide a preliminary chemical characterisation of the avian nematode parasite Ascaridia galli. Adult parasite specimens recovered
content: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) were used to provide a preliminary chemical characterisation of the avian nematode parasite Ascaridia galli. Adult parasite specimens recovered from discarded poultry intestinal tissue were subjected to washing, morphological identification, drying, and pulverisation. The resulting dried powder was analysed using attenuated total reflectance FTIR, whereas an ethanolic extract was analysed by GC–MS. The FTIR spectra showed characteristic absorption bands at 3797, 3643, 3279, 2926, 2330, 1643, 1538, 1449, 1312, 1236, 1025, 927, 762, and 702 cm⁻¹. The principal biologically relevant spectral regions were assigned to hydroxyl/O–H and N–H stretching vibrations, aliphatic C–H stretching modes, amide I and II vibrational bands, C–N/C–O-associated vibrational features, and carbohydrate-related absorption phenomena. The band at 2330 cm⁻¹ was interpreted as an atmospheric carbon dioxide artefact rather than a parasite constituent. GC–MS examination of the ethanolic extract showed 23 chromatographic peaks with a cumulative integrated area of 339,249,153 and normalised total area of 100%. The predominant chromatographic peak occurred at 1.126 min (91.24% relative area) and was provisionally assigned by spectral-library matching to a sulphur-containing organic compound. The second major peak occurred at 2.173 min (5.79% relative area) and was identified as Ethane, 1,1-diethoxy-. Later peaks yielded provisional sterol-related assignments at 24.030 and 24.060 min. Given that spectral library matching alone is insufficient for definitive chemical identification, all GC–MS identifications remain provisional. Together, FTIR and GC–MS provided complementary preliminary evidence of a chemically heterogeneous composition involving protein-, lipid-, carbohydrate-, oxygen-, nitrogen- and sulphur-associated constituents in A. galli.

title: Aqueous carbon dot-melatonin nanoassembly combined with Cu(II) for bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
summary: Introduction Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen responsible for antibiotic-resistant infections in healthcare facilities. To combat antibiotic resistance, researchers are seeking alternative therapies using new molecules or
content: Introduction Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen responsible for antibiotic-resistant infections in healthcare facilities. To combat antibiotic resistance, researchers are seeking alternative therapies using new molecules or nanomaterials. Methods We synthesized carbon dots (CDs) from melatonin (Mel), and the resulting assembly was further mixed with copper chloride. The hydrosoluble nanocomposite was primarily characterized by Raman, PL, FTIR, and EPR spectroscopy, with interpretation supported by DFT calculations. The formulations were tested against an ATCC 27853 strain and a multidrug-resistant clinical isolate. Results CDs retained excess Mel molecules via a spontaneous process (ΔΔG = –1.64 kcal/mol). The formulations exhibited potent bactericidal activity and strong inhibition of biofilm formation. Biochemical assays (catalase activity, ABTS•+ scavenging capacity) and LysR-PA2206 expression analysis suggested strain-dependent redox responses and a possible role for oxidative stress in antibacterial activity. Scanning electron microscopy images evidenced disruption of the cellular structures and biofilm inhibition. Discussion The findings support the potential of CD/Mel formulations containing Cu(II) as antimicrobial candidates for controlling biofilm-associated and antibiotic-resistant infections of P. aeruginosa .

title: Double Detonation with a Thin Helium Shell: Shell Mass, Nickel Yield and Peak Power Budget
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: In the double-detonation picture a helium shell accumulated on a carbon-oxygen white dwarf ignites first; its shock converges inside the core and lights carbon, unbinding a star whose total mass, here 1.021 solar units, never approaches the
content: In the double-detonation picture a helium shell accumulated on a carbon-oxygen white dwarf ignites first; its shock converges inside the core and lights carbon, unbinding a star whose total mass, here 1.021 solar units, never approaches the Chandrasekhar value, while modern thin shells near 0.02 solar units keep the outer ejecta from being polluted by shell ashes. The budget weighs shell against core, converts the adopted nickel yield of published model grids into a predicted peak luminosity through the decay chain, prices the kinetic energy of the fully unbound ejecta, and contrasts the thin shell with the tenth-of-a-solar-mass shells older models required. Headline values are ddet core mass solar ddet = 1; ddet shell mass solar ddet = 0.021; ddet total mass solar ddet = 1.021; ddet total to chandrasekhar ratio ddet = 0.709; ddet shell to core percent ddet = 2.1; ddet nickel yield solar ddet = 0.58. The shell-to-kinetic energy percentage is printed to keep the trigger-versus-engine distinction quantitative rather than rhetorical.

title: Fabrication of eco-friendly rice starch films modified with Cassia tora gum: influence of gum concentration on physicochemical, mechanical, and barrier properties
source: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
summary: Biodegradable and edible films have earned significant interest as sustainable alternatives to conventional packaging, however the limitations in mechanical and barrier performance of starch-based films can restrict their application in foo
content: Biodegradable and edible films have earned significant interest as sustainable alternatives to conventional packaging, however the limitations in mechanical and barrier performance of starch-based films can restrict their application in food-packaging. This study aimed to investigate the effect of varying concentration of Cassia gum (1-1.75% (w/v) on the physicochemical, mechanical, barrier, functional and structural properties of rice strach film. The incorporation of Cassia gum enhanced the viscosity and viscoelastic behaviour of the film-forming solution. The fabricated films were characterised for their physicochemical, mechanical, functional, and structural attributes. The incorporation of gum increased the moisture content, water activity and solubility. The addition of Cassia gum improved the barrier properties of starch films. The film with 1.75% (w/v) Cassia gum exhibited the lowest water vapour transmission rate (WVTR; 33.34 mg m −2 s −1 ) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CDTR; 5.01 ×10 −2 mg m −2 s −1 ), compared to 40.13 mg m −2 s −1 and 6.23 ×10 −2 mg m −2 s −1 , respectively for the control film. The lowest oxygen transmission rate (OTR; 0.75 mg m −2 s −1 ), was observed for films with 1,25% & 1.75% Cassia gum compared with 0.87 mg m −2 s −1 for the control film. The highest tensile strength (6.14 MPa) was obtained with 1.50%, whereas the highest elongation at break (98.33%) was observed with 1.75% gum, indicating improved mechanical performance relative to the control film. The DPPH radical- scavenging antioxidant activity increased from 8.6% in the control film to 35.64% in the film containing 1.75% of Cassia gum. The findings demonstrate the potential of Cassia gum as a natural additive for tailoring the mechanical, barrier and functional properties of starch films. The concentration-dependent changes in film properties support the use of Cassia tora gum-modified rice starch films for sustainable and functional food-packaging applications.

title: Pd and Pd–Au in Zeolites A and Y Catalyze the Selective Acetylene Semihydrogenation Reaction in Ethylene-Rich Feedstocks
summary: Abstract Pd and Pd–Au supported on zeolites A and Y are selective catalysts for the acetylene semihydrogenation reaction under industrial front-end conditions. While the Pd@MS 5 Å offers a strong confinement–diffusion balance, enabling high
content: Abstract Pd and Pd–Au supported on zeolites A and Y are selective catalysts for the acetylene semihydrogenation reaction under industrial front-end conditions. While the Pd@MS 5 Å offers a strong confinement–diffusion balance, enabling high acetylene conversion down to 420 ppm residual with 94.1% ethylene selectivity, the bimetallic Pd1–Au2@MS 5 Å catalyst shows the best overall balance in activity, selectivity, and stability, achieving over 94%–96% ethylene selectivity at deep acetylene conversion (420–1652 ppm), demonstrating that the combination of controlled pore environment and tailored bimetallic sites is an effective strategy for selective alkyne hydrogenation in metal zeolites.

title: Shake Table Tests on a Post-tensioned CLT Rocking Structure with Damage-Avoidance Detailing
summary: This paper presents some initial observations of a large-scale shaking table testing campaign conducted on a three-storey mass-timber rocking structure designed to achieve low damage and rapid post-earthquake recovery. The testing, conducte
content: This paper presents some initial observations of a large-scale shaking table testing campaign conducted on a three-storey mass-timber rocking structure designed to achieve low damage and rapid post-earthquake recovery. The testing, conducted at the Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Engineering Seismology, North Macedonia, involved three phases. The specimen employed post-tensioned cross-laminated timber rocking walls that provided self centring, while inelastic deformations were initially concentrated in replaceable energy dissipation components. To enhance the control of peak storey drifts and floor accelerations, supplemental inerter-based devices, designed to engage inertial action only when beneficial, were incorporated to the structural system in phase 2. In addition, the wall to foundation rocking interface was modified through rounded toe profiling to reduce stress concentrations and mitigate local crushing during repeated uplift and re-contact cycles during phase 3. The paper briefly describes the structural concept, specimen design, and experimental configuration, including the design procedure, instrumentation, and shaking table testing programme. Then, a preliminary analysis of experimental results is presented, providing insights into the global seismic response of the rocking system as well as the local behaviour of the rocking interface and supplemental devices. Particular attention is given to the influence of inerter devices on drift and acceleration demands and to the effectiveness of toe profiling in maintaining stable rocking behaviour under repeated impacts.

title: Dose-resolved untargeted metabolomics of NaB-treated CHO-K1 cells reveals broad catabolic suppression, Warburg-like metabolic reorientation, and coordinated tryptophan pathway alterations as hallmarks of the NaB-responsive state
summary: Sodium butyrate (NaB) is widely used in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell bioprocessing to enhance recombinant protein productivity, yet the systems-level metabolic consequences of NaB treatment across its pharmacological dose range remain p
content: Sodium butyrate (NaB) is widely used in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell bioprocessing to enhance recombinant protein productivity, yet the systems-level metabolic consequences of NaB treatment across its pharmacological dose range remain poorly characterised. Here, we performed dose-resolved untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based metabolomics of CHO-K1 cells treated across eight concentrations of NaB (0–8.0 mM) and identified 469 annotated metabolite features. A ten-stage computational pipeline, comprising probabilistic quotient normalisation, principal component analysis (PCA), differential abundance analysis, Spearman dose-correlation, metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA), KEGG topology analysis, Random Forest, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, was applied without pathway pre-selection. PCA resolved three concentration-dependent metabolic states: sub-threshold [homeostatic] (0–0.25 mM), NaB-responsive [metabolically reoriented (for growth-arrest and potential increased productivity)] (0.5–2.0 mM), and cytostressed (4.0–8.0 mM). At 2.0 mM, 243 differentially abundant metabolites were identified, with decreased metabolites outnumbering increased ones (152 vs. 91; ratio 1.67:1), indicating broad catabolic suppression and selective activation of (stress regulating) pathways. The most enriched pathways included the Warburg Effect, Tryptophan Metabolism, and Glutamate Metabolism. Dominant metabolic changes comprised decreased abundance of metabolites associated with fatty acid oxidation and amino acid catabolism, alongside concurrent increases in metabolites associated with TCA anaplerosis and the glutathione cycle, patterns consistent with, but not a direct measurement of, altered flux through these pathways. Nine metabolites from tryptophan pathway were coordinately altered, with depletion of indole-derived species and induction of NAD-related metabolites. Machine learning identified Oxoproline, Serine, Heptanoate, Cyclohexanoic Acid, and Indole-3-Lactic Acid as the top candidate dose-responsive biomarkers within this dataset; their predictive performance in independent datasets and their identity have not yet been externally or analytically validated. PPI network analysis identified SIRT1, HDAC1, and IDO1 as the most central regulatory nodes. Together, these findings provide a systems-level metabolic framework for NaB-induced CHO cell physiology and nominate SIRT1, IDO1, CPT1A, and NAMPT as candidate targets for functional validation in recombinant producer cell lines.

title: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo‐Assisted CO 2 ‐to‐Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
summary: ABSTRACT Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO 2 ‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted b
content: ABSTRACT Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO 2 ‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR‐1 bioanode functionalized with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA). Cell‐associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination‐dependent current contribution. The MQDs‐enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm −2 under illumination. In the coupled CO 2 ‐fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L −1 d −1 at −0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total‐energy‐to‐PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate‐derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET‐coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme‐associated components within the native EET network. This interface‐to‐synthesis strategy links photo‐assisted microbial electron harvesting to H 2 ‐mediated CO 2 ‐to‐PHB biosynthesis.

title: Impact of Biomass Burning Aerosols on Warm Cloud Microphysics and Rain Suppression in Northern Thailand
summary: This study investigates the microphysical properties and temporal evolution of warm cumulus clouds over Northern Thailand during the biomass burning season. In-situ measurements were conducted using a research aircraft equipped with full-sp
content: This study investigates the microphysical properties and temporal evolution of warm cumulus clouds over Northern Thailand during the biomass burning season. In-situ measurements were conducted using a research aircraft equipped with full-spectrum aerosol and cloud probes (UHSAS, PCASP, FSSP). The observations reveal distinct aerosol signatures: fresh plumes dominated by the Aitken mode (<0.1 µm) and aged plumes characterized by the accumulation mode (0.1-0.3 µm). Despite high Cloud Condensation Nuclei (CCN) loading, cloud droplet growth was severely suppressed. In-cloud measurements showed narrow droplet size distributions with a sharp cutoff at 15-18 µm, preventing the onset of collision-coalescence. Temporal tracking of cloud turrets (t 20 min) revealed a dominant trend of rapid dissipation, with Liquid Water Content (LWC) decreasing by 30-60% due to dry air entrainment. An extreme “cloud choking” event was observed where massive aerosol intrusion (concentration >7,000 cm-3) accelerated evaporation via the semi-direct effect. These findings indicate that high aerosol loading in this region not only suppresses precipitation initiation but also shortens cloud lifetime.

title: Methane Distribution in the East (Japan) Sea: Baseline for Donghae Gas Field Carbon Storage Project
summary: Abstract. Methane (CH4), the second most potent greenhouse gas, is poorly characterized in coastal waters along the Korean Peninsula. We investigated dissolved CH4 across depths and distances from shore in the southwestern East (Japan) Sea
content: Abstract. Methane (CH4), the second most potent greenhouse gas, is poorly characterized in coastal waters along the Korean Peninsula. We investigated dissolved CH4 across depths and distances from shore in the southwestern East (Japan) Sea (EJS) and the adjacent Ulleung Basin. Concentrations ranged from 1.7 to 48.7 nM, with maxima near the coast and seafloor, though the mixed layer held the maximum at some stations. Bottom-water CH4 (1.7–28.2 nM, mean: 7.0 ± 4.5 nM, n = 44) was 2- to 10-fold higher than surface water (2.0–4.4 nM, mean: 3.2 ± 0.6 nM, n = 48), consistent with a sedimentary source typical of shallow continental shelves. In the Ulleung Basin, however, the CH4 maximum occurred in the mixed layer, likely reflecting stratification-driven microbial production and possible lateral advection. CH4 declined from coast to offshore along a consistent density layer in October 2025, suggesting lateral transport to the open ocean. Sea-to-air CH4 flux from the southwestern EJS ranged from −2.1 to 35.6 μmol m−2 d−1 (mean: 8.6 ± 10.6 μmol m−2 d−1), comparable to other global continental margins, with greater release in warm seasons. Given ongoing warming in the EJS, atmospheric CH4 emissions may increase further. Several stations lie within the Donghae gas field, a depleted reservoir considered for CO2 storage; CH4 there (7–10 nM) matched regional background, providing a pre-injection baseline for future leakage monitoring. This is the first multi-season water-column CH4 dataset for this sector of the Korean coast, though CH4 sources remain poorly constrained.

title: GreenSense: controlled predictive, computational, and carbon-aware evaluation of efficient neural models for fraud detection
summary: Abstract Green artificial intelligence requires model quality to be evaluated together with computational cost, model size, and estimated environmental impact. This study presents GreenSense as a controlled benchmarking framework for energy
content: Abstract Green artificial intelligence requires model quality to be evaluated together with computational cost, model size, and estimated environmental impact. This study presents GreenSense as a controlled benchmarking framework for energy-aware fraud detection. Seven configurations are compared on two imbalanced transaction datasets: Compact Nonlinear Dense (CND), full-precision and dynamically quantized tabular CNNs and MLPs, an LTC-style state-refinement network, and a sparse NCP-CfC-style network. All training, quantization, and inference measurements were repeated on a single dedicated workstation (Intel Core i5-13500, Windows 11) under one fixed software stack, thread and CPU-affinity setting, and measurement protocol. Each model–dataset configuration is evaluated over five independently seeded training runs, and each inference measurement is repeated five times in fixed-work windows of at least 30 s. CPU-package energy is measured with CodeCarbon and cross-checked against a second software readout of the same hardware energy counter; CO $$_2$$ is derived from a cited national grid-emission factor. Predictive evaluation emphasizes precision–recall area under the curve (PR-AUC), $$F_1$$ , recall, precision, and ROC-AUC. On FraudTrain, the LTC-style model achieved the highest mean PR-AUC (0.8015, 95% CI 0.7947–0.8082), followed by MLP-FP32 (0.7679) and NCP-CfC-style (0.7654). On the ULB Credit Card benchmark, MLP-FP32 (0.7554) and CND (0.7528) had the highest mean PR-AUC with overlapping intervals, while CNN-FP32 had the highest mean $$F_1$$ (0.1889). Training accounted for more than 99.9% of lifecycle-equivalent energy for every configuration. Dynamic INT8 quantization reduced MLP storage size by 1.94 $$\times $$ (FraudTrain) and 2.09 $$\times $$ (ULB) but increased inference energy per transaction in all four FP32–INT8 pairs (by 43–47% for the MLP and 4–6% for the CNN; all paired intervals excluded zero). Its predictive effect was dataset-dependent: FraudTrain MLP PR-AUC decreased by 0.301 (95% CI $$-0.358$$ to $$-0.247$$ ), whereas the ULB change was only $$-0.003$$ . The PR-AUC/lifecycle-energy Pareto sets were CND, MLP-FP32, and LTC-style on FraudTrain and CND and MLP-FP32 on ULB. GreenSense provides a reproducible, task-specific basis for comparing predictive, computational, and estimated environmental operating points; all code, configurations, raw energy logs, and manifests are archived with a DOI.

title: Water Microenvironments Dictate Kinetic Control of Nucleophilic Attack vs Deprotonation Pathways of Olefin-Based Cation Radical Reactions in BMIM/BF4 Ionic Liquid
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
summary: Abstract Anodic outer-sphere oxidation of olefins to cation radical intermediates that undergo spontaneous reactions has potential synthetic utility but is often limited by low selectivity in the absence of catalysts. In this computational
content: Abstract Anodic outer-sphere oxidation of olefins to cation radical intermediates that undergo spontaneous reactions has potential synthetic utility but is often limited by low selectivity in the absence of catalysts. In this computational work, we investigate the hypothesis that the competing kinetics of nucleophilic attack and deprotonation pathways of cation radical intermediates can be modulated by tuning water microenvironments, leading to higher reaction selectivity. We investigate cation radical reaction pathways of three olefin substrates, cyclohexene, tetramethylethylene, and α-methylstyrene, within the BMIM/BF4 ionic liquid at low water content. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of electrochemical cells with the BMIM/BF4 electrolyte are utilized to characterize the anodic electrochemical double layer (EDL) structure and water cluster distributions and to compute potentials of mean force (PMFs) and residence times for electrogenerated cation radical intermediates near the anode under working potentials. Subsequent QM/MM free-energy simulations are conducted to investigate how water microenvironment dictates nucleophilic attack and deprotonation reaction kinetics of the cation radical intermediates. While cyclohexene cation radical reactions remain non-selective via barrierless kinetics, the α-methylstyrene cation radical consistently favors nucleophilic attack due to inherent electronic barriers to deprotonation. The tetramethylethylene cation radical demonstrates high selectivity for nucleophilic attack at low water concentrations but loses this selectivity at higher water concentrations, due to modulation of the deprotonation barrier from hydronium solvation within water clusters. The key takeaway is the “proof of concept” that significantly higher product selectivity for anodic olefin functionalization reactions (of certain substrates) may be achieved by tuning the water microenvironment to modulate the cation radical reaction kinetics.

title: Agro-Biomass Biochars from Pyrolysis to Rhizosphere: Feedstock Controls, Carbon Stability, and Ecological Synergies
summary: This study comprehensively evaluates the thermochemical valorization of agricultural residues into biochar, examining its integration into advanced closed-loop agro-ecological frameworks such as the plant-driven enhanced rock weathering (ER
content: This study comprehensively evaluates the thermochemical valorization of agricultural residues into biochar, examining its integration into advanced closed-loop agro-ecological frameworks such as the plant-driven enhanced rock weathering (ERW) system (e.g., the Lupinus albus–basalt model). By classifying precursor biomass feedstocks into three primary categories—leguminous and specialty herbaceous residues, staple cereal straws and stalks, and lignocellulosic woody biomass and orchard prunings—the review investigates how biochemical composition and pyrolysis operational parameters (such as peak temperature, heating rate, and residence time) critically dictate solid mass recovery, structural porosity, Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC), and carbon stability. While leguminous and herbaceous residues yield nutrient-rich biochars with high inorganic alkalinity optimal for neutralizing soil acidity, cereal straws offer versatile porous networks suitable for soil conditioning and environmental remediation. Conversely, lignin-rich woody residues and orchard prunings provide exceptional environmental recalcitrance and multi-century mean residence times, making them premier candidates for permanent carbon sequestration, structural construction materials, and phase-change material encapsulation. The findings demonstrate that strategic feedstock selection and precise thermal control enable the design of bespoke biochars that simultaneously drive negative emission technologies, soil restoration, and circular bioeconomy pathways.

title: Beyond the Metal Core: In Silico Safety Profiling of the Capping Phytoconstituents of Oxystelma esculentum Ag/AgCl Nanoparticles for Cardiac, Endocrine and Cytochrome P450 Risk
summary: Abstract Green-synthesised silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) nanoparticles carry a surface layer of the plant constituents that reduce and cap them, and that capping layer is part of what a biological system meets. We profiled the safety-rel
content: Abstract Green-synthesised silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) nanoparticles carry a surface layer of the plant constituents that reduce and cap them, and that capping layer is part of what a biological system meets. We profiled the safety-related behaviour of twelve capping phytoconstituents of Oxystelma esculentum Ag/AgCl nanoparticles epicatechin, kaempferol, lupeol, stigmasterol, esculin, chlorogenic acid, gallic acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, caffeic acid, ferulic acid and coumarin, with silybin as a reference standard across five computational work packages: physicochemical and drug-likeness descriptors, structural-alert screening, toxicity prediction with two independent predictors, docking against a cardiac, endocrine and cytochrome P450 panel, and a reasoned safety synthesis. No constituent was predicted hepatotoxic by ProTox 3.0, and none was predicted mutagenic by the same predictor, but the predictors disagreed on mutagenicity for three constituents and on hepatotoxicity for one, and both disagreements are reported rather than resolved by fiat. Three constituents lupeol, stigmasterol and silybin combined the strongest predicted hERG pore-site binding (− 9.09, − 7.94 and − 8.93 kcal/mol) with positive hERG II predictions, a qualitative agreement that marks them for experimental cardiac follow-up. Coumarin carried the strongest acute-toxicity signal (predicted LD50 196 mg/kg, the only GHS Class 3 value). Lupeol was the most selective binder in the panel: the strongest at CYP3A4 (− 10.50 kcal/mol) and hERG yet a non-binder at the androgen receptor, CYP2D6 and CYP1A2. Silybin, the strongest oestrogen-receptor-α binder (− 9.29 kcal/mol), was a non-binder at the androgen receptor and CYP1A2 and carried the only predicted cardiotoxicity flag. All findings are predictions, not experimental toxicity data. Two 10 ns molecular dynamics runs support the docked endocrine poses: silybin remained bound in oestrogen receptor α (mean 1.70 protein–ligand hydrogen bonds per frame, anchored at Glu353 in 96% of frames) and epicatechin remained bound in the androgen receptor (mean 2.26 hydrogen bonds per frame, anchored at Thr877 in 53% of frames), with ligand root-mean-square deviation of 0.18 and 0.16 nm after protein fitting.

title: Enhanced conductivity and chemical durability of SPEEK membranes by cerium-silica incorporation for low-humidity PEM fuel cells
summary: This study addresses the conductivity durability trade-off that limits sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) membranes under low-humidity proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) operation by incorporating a single sol–gel-derived C
content: This study addresses the conductivity durability trade-off that limits sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) membranes under low-humidity proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) operation by incorporating a single sol–gel-derived Ce:SiO 2 hybrid nanofiller that combines hygroscopic water retention with radical-scavenging functionality. Raman spectroscopy confirmed the formation of a CeO 2 /SiO 2 composite in which crystalline cubic CeO2 (F 2 g mode at 465 cm⁻¹, with defect-related bands near 525 and 608 cm⁻¹) coexists with an amorphous silica phase, and together with FTIR provided evidence of interfacial Si–O–Ce bonding. SPEEK–Ce:SiO 2 composite membranes with 1, 5, and 10 wt% filler loadings were prepared by solution casting. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed filler incorporation but revealed partial agglomeration that became pronounced at 10 wt%, while AFM showed that filler addition markedly increased surface roughness and produced hill-like protrusions corresponding to the nanofiller and its agglomerates, consistent with the mechanical and conductivity trends. The SPEEK-Ce:SiO 2 (5%) composite gave the best balance of properties: proton conductivity reached 3.7 × 10⁻² S/cm at 30 °C, compared with 4.07 × 10⁻³ S/cm for bare SPEEK, and tensile strength increased from 1185.44 to 3144.07 kPa. Oxidative stability testing at 80 °C with 3 ppm Fe²⁺ showed the highest residual weight (81.6%) for the 5 wt% membrane after 250 min. In single-cell tests at 60 °C and 40% relative humidity, this membrane delivered a maximum power density of 50 mW/cm² at 130.2 mA/cm², versus 35 mW/cm² for bare SPEEK, and exhibited an open-circuit-voltage decay rate of only 0.04 mV/h compared with 0.35 mV/h for the pristine membrane. These results show that a 5 wt% Ce:SiO 2 loading simultaneously improves conductivity, oxidative stability, and low-humidity fuel-cell durability, indicating that the hybrid filler is a promising route to more robust SPEEK-based PEMs.

title: Influence of CO 3 2- and SO 4 2- on the chloride binding capacity of AAMs with municipal solid waste incineration fly ash
summary: Abstract Alkali-activated materials (AAMs) are widely used for the treatment of chloride-rich municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MSWI FA). However, there is a lack of study on the influence of inevitable CO32- and SO42- from MSWI F
content: Abstract Alkali-activated materials (AAMs) are widely used for the treatment of chloride-rich municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MSWI FA). However, there is a lack of study on the influence of inevitable CO32- and SO42- from MSWI FA on the chloride binding capacity of AAMs. In this study, AAMs with different levels of internal Cl-, SO42- and CO32- were prepared to simulate the systems with MSWI FA to provide insights into the intricate competition of three anions for being bound by in-situ formed hydrotalcites (Ht) in AAMs. The results showed that at 5 wt% internal Cl-, CO32- reduced bound chloride by 0.81~3.4%, whereas SO42- increased it by 3.7~10.2%, and the influence of both anions decreased with prolonging curing time from 7d to 28d. Ht formation in AAMs with 3 wt% Cl- increased from 5.6 wt% to 6.3 wt% and to 7.1 wt% with the presence of CO32- and SO42-, respectively, while an increase in Cl- from 3 wt% to 5 wt% slightly varied the Ht content. Cold-water extraction for chloride binding capacity quantification varied the phase assemblage due to dissolution, and the optimal extraction time was 2h for powder samples. Spatial distribution of Ht was obtained by quantitative SEM-EDS hypermaps analysis, which revealed that Ca-Al Ht and Mg-Al Ht coexisted around GGBS, but Cl- and SO42- showed preference for intercalation into the Ca-Al Ht. The SO42- from dissolved GGBS competed with Cl- for intercalating into Ht, and the statistic distribution of S and Cl in the Ht formed in AAMs was probably independent of the relative concentration of two anions in the raw materials. The findings suggest that stabilizing the sulfate by other phases rather than Ht to reduce the competition with chloride is vital to achieve high chloride binding by Ht in AAMs with MSWI FA.

title: Lightweight concrete Structure for Seismic Areas—Dynamic Test Challenges and Outcomes
summary: The ECORE project features shaking table tests performed on a two stories high lightweight structure with a square plan layout of approximately 4x4 m. Each story is 2.5 m high and each main direction is split into two uneven spans of 2 m an
content: The ECORE project features shaking table tests performed on a two stories high lightweight structure with a square plan layout of approximately 4x4 m. Each story is 2.5 m high and each main direction is split into two uneven spans of 2 m and 1.5 m. The tested structure is a concrete frame structure built of normal weight columns and lightweight concrete slabs and beams. Exterior and partition walls are built out of autoclaved aerated concrete. Multi-role materials were applied: autoclaved aerated concrete and lightweight concrete join structural and thermal insulation properties, AAC blocks ensure the formwork for some concrete columns. The structure withstood several seismic events induced by the shaking table, up to an acceleration level of 0.9 g in both main directions. This acceleration level was monitored on the shaking table, whereas the acceleration level reached almost 3.0 g at one of the top story slab corners. After the last run autoclaved aerated concrete walls suffered severe damage, however concrete elements showed still no important damage. This paper describes some main challenges faced during the test preparation and explains seismic response findings that encourage the use of the tested structural system in mean and strong seismic areas.

title: Bioelectricity Generation from Palm Oil Mill Effluent Using Microbial Fuel Cells: Electroactive Bacterial Identification and Bioelectrochemical Performance Evaluation
summary: Palm oil mill effluent (POME) is a high-strength agro-industrial wastewater with a high organic content, offering considerable potential as a renewable substrate for bioelectricity generation through microbial fuel cell (MFC) technology. Ho
content: Palm oil mill effluent (POME) is a high-strength agro-industrial wastewater with a high organic content, offering considerable potential as a renewable substrate for bioelectricity generation through microbial fuel cell (MFC) technology. However, the bioelectrochemical performance of MFCs treating POME remains strongly influenced by wastewater characteristics and the activity of electroactive microorganisms. This study evaluated the bioelectrochemical performance of a dual-chamber MFC using POME as the substrate by investigating wastewater characteristics, electricity generation, and electroactive bacterial communities. The MFC consisted of graphite electrodes separated by a proton-exchange membrane and was operated under continuous monitoring using an Arduino Uno-based data-acquisition system. The POME sludge exhibited total suspended solids, volatile suspended solids, and chemical oxygen demand of 103,070, 21,340, and 72,365 mg/L, respectively. The reactor achieved maximum electrical performance on day 8, producing a current density of 481,79 mA/m² and a power density of 765,32 mW/m². Microbiological analysis identified Alcaligenes as the dominant electroactive bacterium colonizing the anode, indicating its potential role in extracellular electron transfer and bioelectricity generation. These results demonstrate that POME is a promising feedstock for the simultaneous valorization of wastewater and the production of renewable bioelectricity. Furthermore, integrating physicochemical characterization, bioelectrochemical performance evaluation, and electroactive bacterial identification provides a comprehensive understanding of the factors governing MFC performance. It offers valuable insights for the development of bioelectrochemical systems for palm oil wastewater treatment.

title: Lignin-based gels from sugarcane biomass residues via chemical cascading
summary: Abstract In recent years, efforts have been made to bring value to lignin, a mostly overlooked and highly abundant polyphenolic biopolymer. Herein, the present study pioneers the use of lignin from sugarcane biomass residues: bagasse (SB) a
content: Abstract In recent years, efforts have been made to bring value to lignin, a mostly overlooked and highly abundant polyphenolic biopolymer. Herein, the present study pioneers the use of lignin from sugarcane biomass residues: bagasse (SB) and straw (SS), in developing highly renewable xerogels and cryogels (up to 75%) as suitable precursors for porous carbon materials. Systematic studies were performed to investigate the effects of different lignin precursors (SB and SS- kraft lignin and commercial lignosulfonates), cross-linking agents (glutaraldehyde and PEGDGE) and processing time (6, 12, 24 h). Their structural and surface profiles revealed unique compositional patterns and porosity depending on the selection of lignin precursor, cross-linking agent and drying approach. Sustainable xerogels and cryogels exhibited porosities of up to 50.7% and 73.0%, respectively, with cryogels presenting overall higher values than xerogels equivalents. SB gels conferred highly porous structures, with pore sizes ranging from 1.60 μm to 10.97 μm. XPS analyses revealed that the addition of NiSO₄, here demonstrated to assist in lignin gel polymerization, brings no major alterations to the materials’ matrices while enabling the production of lignosulfonate gels in a shorter time, thereby improving their potential for large-scale production through a faster synthesis and the use of residue-derived feedstocks. FTIR data suggest that higher processing times do not significantly alter the materials’ chemical structure, as it rather hinders the formation of vacancies. These easy-to-prepare materials are expected to be used in electrochemical applications, lighter packaging materials and nanomaterials, further promoting a circular economy. Graphical Abstract

title: AIRMESHZ: A ZigBee-Orchestrated Edge-AI Mesh for Adaptive Indoor Air Quality Management and Emergency Ventilation in University Laboratories
summary: University engineering laboratories frequently handle solvents, soldering fumes, and particulate-generating processes that degrade indoor air quality (IAQ). Commercial monitors are typically stand-alone units without coordinated ventilation
content: University engineering laboratories frequently handle solvents, soldering fumes, and particulate-generating processes that degrade indoor air quality (IAQ). Commercial monitors are typically stand-alone units without coordinated ventilation response, and building management systems rely on scheduled ventilation rather than demand-based control. This paper proposes AIRMESHZ, ZigBee-powered edge-artificial-intelligence mesh that includes a low-cost multi sensor nodes with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) interference connected on a Raspberry Pi, servo-actuated damper control, and proportional-integral-derivative-regulated exhaust ventilation, combining together to create a powerful mesh that protects students who are performing experiments in an engineering laboratory. Results showed a mean ZigBee coordination latency of 1.86 s, a peak carbon-dioxide abatement of 31.42 percent relative to fixed-schedule ventilation, a damper actuator response of 0.42 s, and a 99.10 percent mesh message-delivery ratio. A comparative analysis of six wireless technologies showed that ZigBee offers the best balance of range, power, mesh support, and latency for multi-node IAQ applications. The paper concludes that multi-node edge-artificial-intelligence coordination over ZigBee is a credible missing layer in current indoor air quality research.

title: Evaluating the Filtration and Breathability of Commercial Respiratory Devices for Potential Wildland and Wildland-Urban Interface Firefighting Operations
summary: Abstract Wildland firefighters are facing frequent and extreme wildfire behavior, placing them at greater risk for concentrated and cumulative inhalation exposures over each fire season. This study evaluated commercially available respirato
content: Abstract Wildland firefighters are facing frequent and extreme wildfire behavior, placing them at greater risk for concentrated and cumulative inhalation exposures over each fire season. This study evaluated commercially available respirators and nontraditional respiratory devices to assess their potential use in wildland/wildland-urban interface (WUI) operations. Filter testing was conducted to identify devices with potential as barrier and/or protective face coverings under current respiratory standards. An animatronic headform was used to evaluate these devices alongside certified respirators through a simulated fit test to measure total filtration efficacy (TFE) and differential pressure (ΔP) at two breathing workloads. From these evaluations, the quality factor (qf) on the headform was predicted to be the most realistic measure of performance. Ultimately, no device was able to maintain qf ≥ 14 kPa–1 with TFE ≥ 50% and ΔP ≤ 5 mm H2O at both light and moderate workloads. Given the arduous workloads typical of wildland/WUI firefighting, this raises concerns about potential applications in the field. However, several of these devices maintained TFE ≥ 50% that could offer short-term solutions to help reduce exposure with intermittent use. More research is needed to ensure these proposed measures of TFE and ΔP are feasible without imposing a significant physiological burden.

title: Seasonal changes in chemical composition, phenology and nutritional potential for goats of woody forages in pyrenean oak silvopastoral systems
summary: Abstract Mediterranean silvo-pastoral systems are challenged by severe seasonal forage shortages, emphasizing the need for resilient feed resources. This study evaluated the seasonal variations in chemical composition and in vitro organic m
content: Abstract Mediterranean silvo-pastoral systems are challenged by severe seasonal forage shortages, emphasizing the need for resilient feed resources. This study evaluated the seasonal variations in chemical composition and in vitro organic matter digestibility (IVOMD) of key browse species and assessed their potential to meet the metabolizable energy and protein requirements of grazing goats. Five browse treatments (species) were studied: one deciduous tree ( Quercus pyrenaica ) and four legume shrubs ( Cytisus scoparius , C. multiflorus , C. striatus , and Genista falcata ). Plant foliage (leaves and twigs) was sampled across five phenological stages over a year. Compared with later mature stages, Q. pyrenaica exhibited the highest ( p < 0.05) nutritional quality during early spring leaf emergence (CP = 161.1 g kg −1 DM; IVOMD = 63.3%), but experienced severe declines ( p < 0.05) in summer and autumn due to rapid lignification. In contrast, all leguminous shrubs maintained higher ( p < 0.05) nitrogen levels year-round compared to the tree species, with the Cytisus genus averaging CP contents of 139.2 g kg −1 DM even outside peak seasons. Nutrient intake simulations for goats revealed that during the critical late-pregnancy stage, C. scoparius and Cy. striatus provided the greatest ( p < 0.05) metabolizable protein (MP) potential, achieving peaks of 308.4 and 260.1 g day −1 of MP, respectively. Conversely, G. falcata acted as a strategic forage during winter dormancy, maintaining a stable ( p < 0.05) nutritional supply when other species declined. The phenological desynchronization between deciduous trees and leguminous shrubs ensures a staggered nutrient availability. Integrating these diverse woody resources into small ruminant grazing systems provides a resilient nutritional buffer, effectively mitigating seasonal forage gaps.

title: Defect-mediated carrier transport in tin oxide transparent electrodes via post- annealing atmosphere engineering for silicon heterojunction solar cells
summary: Abstract Silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells are promising for high-efficiency terrestrial and low-Earth-orbit photovoltaics owing to their high efficiency, low temperature coefficient, and high bifaciality. However, conventional indiu
content: Abstract Silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells are promising for high-efficiency terrestrial and low-Earth-orbit photovoltaics owing to their high efficiency, low temperature coefficient, and high bifaciality. However, conventional indium tin oxide transparent electrodes rely on scarce and costly indium, hindering the sustainable development of SHJ technology. In this work, tantalum-doped tin oxide (TTO) was employed as an alternative transparent conductive material, and the effect of post-annealing atmosphere on the optoelectrical properties of TTO films is investigated. After post-annealing at 220 ℃, N 2 and vacuum annealing yields the highest carrier concentration and mobility, respectively. Vacuum annealing improves crystallinity and reduced localized defect states, thereby suppressing carrier scattering and enhancing mobility; whereas N 2 annealing increases the concentration of oxygen-vacancy-related defects, resulting in a higher carrier concentration. The 100 nm TTO film annealed in N 2 achieves a minimum sheet resistance of 244 Ω sq − 1 and a figure of merit of 2.99 × 10 − 4 Ω −1 . Indium-less SHJ solar cells are subsequently fabricated using TTO transparent electrodes. Compared with the device based on as-deposited TTO film, this device employing post-annealed TTO film exhibits improved fill factor and power conversion efficiency. These results provide insights into the mechanisms governing the electrical properties of tin oxide-based transparent conductive films and demonstrate the potential of TTO for indium-less SHJ solar cells and other optoelectronic applications.

title: ERIES-TLTB: Thunderstorm Loading on Tall Buildings
summary: The ERIES–TLTB project investigates the wind-induced effects of thunderstorms on tall buildings through an experimental campaign conducted in the Giovanni Solari Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel at University of Genova. Thunderstorm outflows diff
content: The ERIES–TLTB project investigates the wind-induced effects of thunderstorms on tall buildings through an experimental campaign conducted in the Giovanni Solari Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel at University of Genova. Thunderstorm outflows differ from synoptic winds, exhibiting nose-shaped vertical wind speed profiles and non-stationary behavior over short intervals (10 min to 1 h). The project employs both a specially designed passive device and an active device capable of generating nose-shaped profiles. Wind tunnel tests on the CAARC building and a real case study (Project X) are carried out using High-Frequency Force Balance and Pressure Integration techniques. Tests under thunderstorm conditions are complemented by boundary layer simulations to allow direct comparison with synoptic winds. By treating synoptic and thunderstorm winds as separate loading conditions, the results of this experimental campaign can be used to compare wind loads varying three key parameters: reference wind velocity, vertical wind profile shape, and turbulence intensity.

title: Surface Passivated Carbon Dots as Sensors for monocrotophos-an Organophosphate Pesticide
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Self-poisoning using pesticides is the most common means of suicide in India. In such cases, the identification of pesticides is of utmost importance in managing the treatment and applying forensic protocols. In the present work fluorescent
content: Self-poisoning using pesticides is the most common means of suicide in India. In such cases, the identification of pesticides is of utmost importance in managing the treatment and applying forensic protocols. In the present work fluorescent carbon dots using phenyl alanine as precursor was synthesized and characterized using FT-IR, NMR and TEM. The carbon dots showed enhanced fluorescence in the presence of organophosphate pesticide monocrotophos. Linearity studies showed a detection limit of 0.13 μM. The carbon dot sensor showed good selectivity in the presence of other pesticides and good stability in the acidic pH.

title: Mutual effects of accelerated carbonation and GGBFS stabilization on the mechanical performance and heavy‐metal immobilization of iron ore tailings
summary: Abstract Pressurized CO 2 carbonation combined with ground granulated blast‐furnace slag (GGBFS) was evaluated as a low‐carbon strategy for valorizing iron ore tailings. Compacted tailings containing 0–9 wt % GGBFS were carbonated at 0.5–1.
content: Abstract Pressurized CO 2 carbonation combined with ground granulated blast‐furnace slag (GGBFS) was evaluated as a low‐carbon strategy for valorizing iron ore tailings. Compacted tailings containing 0–9 wt % GGBFS were carbonated at 0.5–1.5 bar for 2–8 h and examined by UU triaxial testing, SEM–EDS, TGA, TCLP, and LCA. At 200 kPa confinement, untreated tailings reached 503 kPa peak deviator stress, compared with 780 kPa after carbonation alone at 1.5 bar and 1058 kPa with 9 wt % GGBFS, corresponding to increases of 55% and 110%, respectively. Surface porosity decreased from 43.3% to 28.5%, Ca content increased from 9.38 to 20.82 wt %, and TGA supported carbonate‐bearing product formation and matrix densification. The combined treatment reduced leaching of all investigated metals by 70.0–90.5% relative to untreated tailings. Under the adopted system boundary and assumptions, LCA indicated up to 75% reductions in global warming potential and energy demand relative to cement‐based stabilization.

title: Polydopamine-Derived Co3O4/N-Carbon Heterostructures Anchored with Gold Nanorods for High-Performance Plasmonic-Assisted Zinc-Air Batteries
summary: Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (ZABs) offer an exceptionally high theoretical energy density by utilizing atmospheric oxygen as a reactant, rendering them a safer, significantly more compact and lightweight than conventional energy storage
content: Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (ZABs) offer an exceptionally high theoretical energy density by utilizing atmospheric oxygen as a reactant, rendering them a safer, significantly more compact and lightweight than conventional energy storage devices. However, their practical round-trip efficiency is severely hindered during recharging by the sluggish kinetics and high overpotentials associated with the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). To address this bottleneck, this study investigates the plasmonic-enhancement effect on the ZAB system by anchoring gold nanorods (AuNRs) onto an advanced air electrode composed of Co3O4/nitrogen-doped carbon (Co3O4/N-Carbon) heterostructures. This carbon matrix was synthesized utilizing polydopamine (PDA) as a precursor to ensure the robust retention of structural nitrogen networks. Comprehensive structural and morphological characterization confirmed the uniform distribution and synergistic integration of Co3O4 phase and AuNRs over the N-Carbon architecture. Electrochemical analysis revealed that near-infrared (NIR) laser illumination substantially accelerates the electrocatalytic OER kinetics. However, adjusting the AuNR loading is fundamental, as excessive concentration causes a detrimental shielding effect that inhibits the active catalytic sites. Furthermore, the incorporation of AuNRs facilitates a dark electron transfer across the heterojunction from Co3O4 to Au, leaving the latter with an excess of negative charge. This modification of charge transport dynamics, combined with the plasmonic effect of AuNRs under NIR irradiation, significantly enhances performance. When integrated into a working ZAB under in situ laser NIR radiation, significantly enhances the charging process, although an improvement in the discharge process is also observed, even at current densities as high as 31.8 mA cm⁻². At 0.16 mA cm⁻², a round-trip efficiency of 82.4 % has been achieved. These findings provide a novel and strategic paradigm for designing high-performance, light-assisted electrochemical energy storage and conversion systems.

title: No change in skeletal muscle oxidative capacity biomarkers after 6 weeks of twice‐weekly single‐leg cycle interval training in young active adults
summary: Abstract Interval training (INT) of sufficient frequency, intensity and duration can increase biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity in humans. Studies typically involve three to four sessions per week; however, the effect of redu
content: Abstract Interval training (INT) of sufficient frequency, intensity and duration can increase biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity in humans. Studies typically involve three to four sessions per week; however, the effect of reduced training frequency on this response is unclear. Most studies also do not include a non‐exercise control (CON) condition to account for the potential influence of extraneous, uncontrolled factors. We employed a single‐leg, counterweighted cycling model to investigate the effect of twice weekly INT for 6 weeks on biomarkers of skeletal muscle oxidative capacity including mitochondrial content and fibre capillarisation. Sixteen healthy active adults (6 males, 10 females; 22 ± 3 years; peak oxygen uptake: 36.1 ± 6.1 mL kg −1 min −1 ) performed INT with one leg and their contralateral limb served as a CON. INT involved 4 × 5‐min bouts at an intensity of 50%–60% W peak , interspersed with 2.5 min of recovery at 20% W peak . Muscle biopsy samples obtained from the vastus lateralis of both legs before and after the intervention revealed no differences in the primary outcome measure, citrate synthase maximal activity ( P = 0.350, time × leg interaction). There were also no differences in multiple markers of mitochondrial protein content or capillarisation (all P > 0.05), except NDUFB8 protein content, which increased post‐training in the INT leg only ( P = 0.0387). The lack of change in most biomarkers of oxidative capacity may be due to an insufficient training intensity or related to participant fitness or measurement variability as indicated by the typical error of ∼20%˗40% between legs as baseline.

title: Self‐Powered Electronics‐Free Wearable Disposable Electrotherapy (WDE) Platform for Accelerated Wound Healing
summary: ABSTRACT Electrical stimulation accelerates wound repair by modulating endogenous bioelectric signals that regulate inflammation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cellular responses within the wound microenvironment. Howev
content: ABSTRACT Electrical stimulation accelerates wound repair by modulating endogenous bioelectric signals that regulate inflammation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cellular responses within the wound microenvironment. However, clinical translation has been hindered by cumbersome devices that disrupt standard wound‐care workflows, direct electrode contact with the wound bed, and/or limited stimulation output. Wearable Disposable Electrotherapy (WDE) integrates an electronics‐free printed electrochemical architecture into an mm‐thick patch that looks and is applied like a conventional bandage. The device is self‐powered and delivers a single electrotherapy dose simply by application to the skin. Efficacy was evaluated in a full‐thickness excisional wound model in rats against sham and conventional Constant Current (CC) stimulation. WDE reduced the time required to achieve 50% wound closure by 2.08 days (∼29%) relative to sham. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses at day 14 demonstrated increased collagen deposition (∼25%), tissue cellularity (∼73%), αSMA (∼2.6‐fold), CD31 (∼2.0‐fold), CD206 (∼2.0‐fold), and iNOS (∼1.7‐fold) expression compared with sham. A cellular‐resolution dosimetry model using BEM‐FMM provides a biophysical framework linking electrical stimulation with the wound microenvironment and tissue repair mechanisms. Together, these findings establish WDE as a practical bioelectric wound dressing with the simplicity and scalability of disposable bandages.

title: Electrospun Biopolymer–Nanoparticle Hybrids With Amplified Piezoelectricity for Flexible Human–Machine Interfaces
summary: ABSTRACT Flexible and wearable piezoelectric sensors are attracting increasing interest in motion monitoring and human–machine interface applications, as they enable self‐powered signal transduction from mechanical deformation into electric
content: ABSTRACT Flexible and wearable piezoelectric sensors are attracting increasing interest in motion monitoring and human–machine interface applications, as they enable self‐powered signal transduction from mechanical deformation into electrical output. In this work, electrospun poly (3‐hydroxybutyrate‐co‐3‐hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) fibres incorporating zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles (NPs) are developed as hybrid piezoelectric materials. The effects of electrospinning parameters and ZnO NP loading on fibre morphology, NP dispersion, structure, and piezoelectric performance are systematically investigated. Raman spectroscopy, XRD, FTIR, and XPS confirm the successful incorporation of crystalline wurtzite ZnO within a semi‐crystalline PHBV matrix, while preserving the main chemical structure of the polymer. Surface chemical analysis further indicates Zn–O contributions and changes in the oxygen‐containing ester/carbonyl environments of PHBV, supporting interfacial interactions between ZnO nanoparticles and the polymer matrix. Piezoelectric measurements show enhanced performance, with the piezoelectric coefficient, d 33 , increasing to 0.320 pC N −1 for PHBV/ZnO composites, corresponding to a 213.7% improvement compared with pristine PHBV fibres prepared under the same conditions. Vector network analyser measurements further reveal composition‐dependent values of the effective electromechanical coupling coefficient, k eff , ranging from 13.13% to 18.64%. The fibres are encapsulated in PDMS to fabricate flexible strain sensors, which demonstrate stable and repeatable voltage outputs under different bending angles, as well as reliable hand‐gesture recognition capability. These results highlight PHBV/ZnO composite fibres as an effective platform for flexible and self‐powered wearable sensing applications.

title: Integration of Safranbolu Houses into Contemporary Architecture: Reinterpreting Traditional Elements through Sustainable Design Strategies
source: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science
summary: This study examines the courtyard, sofa, eaves, portico, façade solid–void composition, wooden lattice window system, stone–timber material use, and summer-winter room arrangement found in traditional Safranbolu residential architecture wit
content: This study examines the courtyard, sofa, eaves, portico, façade solid–void composition, wooden lattice window system, stone–timber material use, and summer-winter room arrangement found in traditional Safranbolu residential architecture within the framework of functional, climatic, and sustainability-oriented design principles. The main aim of the study is to investigate how these traditional architectural elements can be transferred to and reinterpreted in contemporary housing design through plan organization, façade design, and three-dimensional modeling studies. In this context, the traditional elements specific to Safranbolu houses were analyzed in terms of privacy, social life, natural ventilation, daylight control, shading, seasonal use, and material rationality. Based on the findings, a design-oriented approach was developed. AutoCAD and SketchUp were used as digital representation tools to support the two-dimensional plan drawing and three-dimensional visualization of the proposed design. The research findings indicate that the courtyard-centered plan layout may contribute to a balanced spatial organization between privacy and social interaction, while architectural elements such as the sofa, eaves, portico, and wooden lattice windows have the potential to be adapted to contemporary housing design in terms of natural ventilation, shading, and daylight control. As a result, the study suggests that Safranbolu’s residential heritage can be evaluated as a holistic set of design principles that may be transferred to contemporary architecture in terms of climatic responsiveness, sustainability-oriented design, and material use. Future studies are recommended to support the proposed design approach through quantitative analysis methods such as energy simulation, daylight analysis, and natural ventilation performance assessment.

title: Magnetic nanoparticle enrichment reveals conserved nitric oxide burst responses in Arabidopsis and wheat
summary: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S
content: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S-nitrosylation. Using Arabidopsis and wheat, we treated plant tissues with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) to simulate a rapid nitric oxide surge. The method was then employed to capture S-nitrosylation dynamics within 24 h after treatment. Our analysis revealed sequence-dependent preferences for cysteines near basic or hydrophobic residues. Proteins showing rapid S-nitrosylation increases were predominantly associated with oxidative stress responses and energy metabolism, consistent with our metabolomic data. Functional studies using wheat TaGR1 mutants identified glutathione reductase 1 as a key regulated target. Modification at a conserved cysteine site rapidly modulated cellular glutathione levels in both species. Here, we provide an analytical tool and a multi-omics resource for investigating S-nitrosylation dynamics.

title: Predicting Small-Scale Building Energy Consumption in Early Design Stages in Mediterranean Climates: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models
source: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science
summary: Accurately forecasting residential energy demand during conceptual architectural design is vital for building decarbonization, yet early models often struggle with balancing input complexity and predictive speed. In this work, we developed
content: Accurately forecasting residential energy demand during conceptual architectural design is vital for building decarbonization, yet early models often struggle with balancing input complexity and predictive speed. In this work, we developed a machine learning-driven decision-support framework evaluating five regression architectures Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Decision Trees (DT), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) across a dataset tailored to Mediterranean residential structures. Eleven architectural and environmental variables were initially evaluated before applying dimensionality reduction to examine how parameter depth affects overall model precision. The results directly challenge the conventional assumption that richer parameter sets automatically improve performance. Rather, reducing input dimensionality down to four decisive parameters floor area, cooling demand, climate classification, and envelope insulation quality minimized data noise and maximized generalization capability, reaching high accuracy (R²> 0.95). Furthermore, introducing vertical spatial analysis showed that story height substantially alters energy behavior: intermediate floors function as passive thermal buffers with stable, minimal loads, whereas envelope-adjacent ground and roof levels exhibit heightened thermal variance and elevated demand. Consequently, embedding vertical floor orientation alongside condensed key parameters establishes a lean, highly reliable protocol for early-stage energy evaluation. Overall, the proposed framework demonstrates that reliable and high-precision energy predictions can be achieved using a limited set of performance-oriented design parameters. The proposed approach provides architects and designers with an efficient, data-driven tool for evaluating energy performance without relying on computationally intensive simulations during the early design process.

title: From heritage to high performance: digital energy and daylight evaluation of Khan Alwakaleh Caravanserai
source: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
summary: This study investigates how digital analysis was used to improve the energy consumption and daylighting of the historic 350-year-old Khan Alwakaleh Caravanserai in Nablus, Palestine. Once a hostel serving merchants, this building suffered s
content: This study investigates how digital analysis was used to improve the energy consumption and daylighting of the historic 350-year-old Khan Alwakaleh Caravanserai in Nablus, Palestine. Once a hostel serving merchants, this building suffered significant damage during the 1927 earthquake and subsequently fell into neglect. It was restored in 2017 and transformed into a vibrant retail and hotel complex. This study couples a SketchUp geometric model with Sefaira’s Radiance‑based daylighting and EnergyPlus‑based energy engines to produce annual energy simulations, PV generation scenarios, and annual and point‑in‑time daylight illuminance maps. Results are reported as annual electricity demand, PV generation, net CO2‑equivalent emissions, annual illuminance distributions, and point‑sampling statistics. The best energy scenario (S3: insulation + liquid‑glass coating + full courtyard PV + packaged terminal heat pumps) reduces annual net CO2‑equivalent emissions by 64.9% and supplies 59.6% of the building’s annual electricity demand, while daylight analyses show that courtyard‑facing rooms remain underlit, with 72% of interior space below 300 lx annually compared to street‑facing rooms which meet typical retail/hospitality targets. Overall, the integration of digital analyses with conserved heritage buildings provides a novel framework for enhancing the long-term sustainability of heritage structures and their resilience against climate and building usage changes.

title: Tunable surface functionalities in coffee-waste–derived carbon enable high-capacity antibiotic adsorption
summary: Agro-waste valorization into functional materials represents a sustainable strategy for mitigating emerging water contaminants. In this study, spent coffee waste collected was converted into activated carbon (AC) via two distinct chemical a
content: Agro-waste valorization into functional materials represents a sustainable strategy for mitigating emerging water contaminants. In this study, spent coffee waste collected was converted into activated carbon (AC) via two distinct chemical activation routes: phosphoric acid activation (AAC) and alkaline activation (BAC). The materials were comprehensively characterized using BET surface area analysis, pH P ZC determination, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM, and SEM, and EDX. AAC exhibited a higher specific surface area, pore volume, and abundance of surface functional groups than BAC, resulting in a superior adsorption performance toward the antibiotic Cephalexin. Batch adsorption experiments revealed maximum removal efficiencies of 88.0 ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for AAC and 70.0 ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for BAC at pH 6.3. The adsorption equilibrium was best described by the Langmuir isotherm, which predicted a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of 78.47 ± 2.1 mg g⁻¹, indicating monolayer adsorption. The kinetic data were best fitted by the pseudo-second-order model, suggesting that chemisorption was the predominant adsorption mechanism. Batch adsorption experiments revealed maximum removal efficiency of 88% ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for AAC and 70% ± 1.3% ( n = 3) for BAC at pH = 6.3. The adsorption equilibrium was best described by the Langmuir isotherm, which predicted a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of 78.47 ± 2.1 mg. g -1 , indicating monolayer adsorption. The kinetic data were best fitted by the pseudo-second-order model, suggesting that chemisorption was the predominant adsorption mechanism. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed that the adsorption process is spontaneous and exothermic, with an activation energy of 91.6 kJ.mol -1 , suggesting that chemisorption plays a significant role in the adsorption process. These findings demonstrate that coffee waste-derived activated carbon is an efficient, low-cost, and sustainable adsorbent for antibiotic removal, offering a promising approach for circular and environmentally friendly water treatment applications.

title: Emerging opportunities in layered transition metal dichalcogenides for chemiresistive gas sensing via structural and surface chemistry modulation
summary: Abstract Among two-dimensional (2D) layered materials, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) constitute a versatile class exhibiting rich electronic diversity beyond the semi-metallic nature of carbon materials. Depending on their composi
content: Abstract Among two-dimensional (2D) layered materials, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) constitute a versatile class exhibiting rich electronic diversity beyond the semi-metallic nature of carbon materials. Depending on their composition and polymorphs, TMDs span semiconductors, metals, semimetals, and superconductors. Their properties can be precisely tailored by engineering a layered structure, stacking sequence control, and surface modifications, making them highly attractive for chemiresistive gas sensing. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of TMD materials, with strong emphasis on correlating sensing behavior with their structural features, synthesis strategies, and morphology control. Further, various advances in synthesis methods, including exfoliation, chemical vapor deposition, wet-chemical techniques, and physical vapor deposition, are discussed. Structural engineering strategies are addressed systematically through defect creation, heterostructure formation, doping, surface functionalization, porosity, and photoactivation, which enhance gas adsorption and charge transfer processes, thereby amplifying the sensing response. Finally, the current technological challenges remain for 2D TMDs-based chemiresistive devices regarding stability, large-scale synthesis, and integration with practical platforms. Emerging opportunities for combining TMDs with flexible electronics, advanced nanostructures, and intelligent signal processing frameworks are also discussed, paving the way toward their deployment in next-generation, energy-efficient gas sensors.

title: Scale-dependent associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM2.5 concentrations across contrasting landscape backgrounds in Beijing
summary: Associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM 2.5 concentrations may vary with spatial scale and landscape background, yet these variations remain insufficiently understood. We examined these relationships using annual mean PM
content: Associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM 2.5 concentrations may vary with spatial scale and landscape background, yet these variations remain insufficiently understood. We examined these relationships using annual mean PM 2.5 concentrations from 13 monitoring stations in Beijing during 2021–2025 and high-resolution urban landscape data. We fitted XGBoost models using eight predictors, including five two-dimensional landscape indicators and three three-dimensional morphological indicators, within 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 km buffers. SHAP analysis was then used to assess the relative importance of these predictors in model predictions. A dominance-ratio approach was used to classify the surroundings of each station into blue-, green-, or grey-space backgrounds. The highest-ranked predictor changed across scales, from frontal area index ( FAI ) at 1.0 km (mean absolute SHAP = 0.824 µg m −2 ) to building height ( BH ) at 1.5 km (0.813 µg m −2 ) and street canyon height-to-width ratio ( HW ) at 2.0 km (0.756 µg m −2 ). At each scale, the single station classified as blue-space had the lowest PM 2.5 concentration, whereas grey-space backgrounds generally showed the highest. Under the 1.0 km classification, the 2023 increase was 1.1 µg m −2 at the blue-space site, compared with mean increases of 3.3 and 3.5 at green- and grey-space stations, respectively.

title: Ecosystem Responsiveness Diverges From Environmental Variability Across Alpine Ecosystems
