summary: Abstract Environmental variability is widely assumed to govern ecosystem responses, yet how GPP response magnitude varies with environmental forcing remains unclear. Using ecosystem sensitivity experiments across the Tibetan Plateau, we qua
content: Abstract Environmental variability is widely assumed to govern ecosystem responses, yet how GPP response magnitude varies with environmental forcing remains unclear. Using ecosystem sensitivity experiments across the Tibetan Plateau, we quantified overall effective gross primary productivity (GPP) responsiveness and composite environmental forcing variability along the elevation gradient. The results showed that environmental forcing variability increased toward high elevations, whereas overall effective GPP responsiveness exhibited a maximum at lower‐mid elevations. This divergence demonstrates that greater environmental fluctuations do not necessarily correspond to a greater GPP response under observed forcing. Maximum responsiveness occurred in transitional environments where moderate forcing variability coincided with relatively strong GPP responses. Comparisons with alternative GPP products showed a broadly consistent pattern, providing corroborating evidence. Our findings highlight the importance of considering both forcing variability and ecosystem responsiveness when identifying regions where carbon uptake responds strongly to environmental change.

title: Chemical Recycling of Acrylonitrile–Butadiene–Styrene (ABS) via Nitrile Reduction and Imine Vitrimer Formation
summary: Abstract As plastic consumption accelerates, acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS) remains a major waste contributor because of its widespread use and limited recyclability. Here, we report a closed-loop chemical recycling strategy in which
content: Abstract As plastic consumption accelerates, acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS) remains a major waste contributor because of its widespread use and limited recyclability. Here, we report a closed-loop chemical recycling strategy in which a boron catalyst selectively reduces ABS nitrile groups to generate amine-functional ABS (AFABS), followed by dynamic imine cross-linking with glutaraldehyde to form an imine-based vitrimer (v-IBS). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirms efficient nitrile-to-amine conversion and subsequent imine formation. Thermal and mechanical analyses reveal enhanced network rigidity (differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) Tg = 115 °C; dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) tan δ peak = 145 °C), while stress relaxation experiments (120–150 °C) show Arrhenius behavior with an activation energy of Ea = 146 kJ·mol–1, consistent with associative imine exchange. In contrast to pristine ABS, which fully dissolves in tetrahydrofuran (THF), v-IBS retains up to 93% of its mass after 24 h, indicating robust cross-linking and solvent resistance. Tensile testing shows reduced strength but substantial stiffness retention, with reprocessed samples maintaining ∼45% of the original modulus, demonstrating partial mechanical recovery enabled by dynamic bond exchange. Notably, acid-catalyzed hydrolysis in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) regenerates AFABS, establishing a reversible pathway for functionalization, vitrimerization, and chemical decross-linking of ABS.

title: Programmable Charge Separation in Heteroleptic Donor–Acceptor Metallacages for Efficient Visible‐Light‐Driven Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
summary: ABSTRACT Precise control over photoinduced charge separation is central to the development of efficient molecular photocatalysts. Herein, we report a family of heteroleptic donor–acceptor metallacages in which charge‐separation dynamics can
content: ABSTRACT Precise control over photoinduced charge separation is central to the development of efficient molecular photocatalysts. Herein, we report a family of heteroleptic donor–acceptor metallacages in which charge‐separation dynamics can be programmed through the electronic modulation of pillar ligands. The metallacages are assembled from tetrapyridyl perylene diimide (PDI) acceptors, electronically distinct tetracarboxylate ligands, and cis ‐Pt(II) corners, thereby organizing donor and acceptor components within a discrete supramolecular architecture. Increasing the electron‐donating ability of the pillar ligands progressively facilitates photoinduced electron transfer and stabilizes PDI radical‐anion character. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the optimized cage undergoes charge separation within 0.6 ps and exhibits a charge‐recombination lifetime of 3.1 ns, in agreement with the calculated thermodynamic driving force for charge separation. The resulting charge‐separated state promotes oxygen activation and enables efficient visible‐light‐driven cross‐dehydrogenative C(sp 3 )–H functionalization in up to 95% yield without sacrificial additives. These results establish a direct structure–function relationship in discrete donor‐acceptor metallacages and provide a supramolecular strategy for programming charge separation in molecular photocatalytic systems.

title: Bacteroid Proteomic Analysis Reveals Host- and Water Regime-Dependent Responses of Rhizobium laguerreae in Symbiosis with Vicia sativa and Pisum sativum
summary: Abstract The establishment of the Rhizobium-legume symbiosis relies on a bidirectional molecular dialogue between both partners, which adjusts their behavior to nodule conditions to ensure an efficient nitrogen-fixing association. Symbiotic
content: Abstract The establishment of the Rhizobium-legume symbiosis relies on a bidirectional molecular dialogue between both partners, which adjusts their behavior to nodule conditions to ensure an efficient nitrogen-fixing association. Symbiotic nitrogen fixation is affected by environmental conditions, and drought is one of the main abiotic factors limiting legume productivity. In this study, a comparative proteomic analysis of bacteroids induced by Rhizobium laguerreae (Rl) V31 in nodules of common vetch (Vicia sativa) and pea (Pisum sativum) grown under well-watered and moderate drought conditions was performed. To provide a genomic framework for proteomic data, a draft genome of Rl V31 was generated and annotated. The results revealed host-dependent differences in bacterial responses that might play a relevant role in the adaptation of rhizobia to plants grown under both water regimens tested. In addition, an NCR-focused proteomic analysis carried out suggested that the relative abundance of several NCR peptides is primarily determined by the host plant, whereas drought acts as a secondary, host dependent modulator. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying host- and water regime-dependent rhizobial responses that may contribute to optimizing Rhizobium-legume combinations with enhanced nitrogen fixation efficiency.

title: Integrating qNMR, Spectroscopic Characterization, and In Silico Screening for Comprehensive Evaluation of Curcumin and Its Drug-Like Derivatives
source: Journal of Drug Delivery and Therapeutics
summary: Curcumin is an important natural polyphenol, but its quality and composition can vary depending on the source, and its poor physicochemical properties limit its pharmaceutical development. This study aimed to compare the quality of curcumin
content: Curcumin is an important natural polyphenol, but its quality and composition can vary depending on the source, and its poor physicochemical properties limit its pharmaceutical development. This study aimed to compare the quality of curcumin obtained from homemade turmeric from Indora, Kangra, Himachal Pradesh, India, and a locally marketed turmeric sample, while also characterizing the extracts and evaluating newly designed curcumin derivatives using computational methods. The turmeric samples were extracted using ethanol-based Soxhlet extraction and analyzed by ¹H NMR, FTIR, and mass spectrometry. Curcumin-related signals were observed in both extracts, with stronger signals in the marketed turmeric sample. Since complete internal-standard and validation data were not available, the NMR comparison was considered semi-quantitative. Mass spectrometry confirmed a protonated molecular ion at m/z 369.3 with characteristic fragments near m/z 177 and 149, while FTIR confirmed the major functional groups of curcumin. Fourteen curcumin derivatives were further evaluated using SwissADME and other in silico tools. Compounds 2, 4, 9, and 12 showed the most favourable overall drug-likeness profiles, although compound 12 showed low predicted gastrointestinal absorption. Compounds 2–7 and 9–11 showed high predicted gastrointestinal absorption, and target prediction suggested possible interactions with kinases, proteases, membrane receptors, and other protein classes. Overall, the study demonstrates a simple integrated approach for turmeric quality assessment, curcumin characterization, and computational screening of curcumin derivatives. Compounds 2, 4, and 9 were identified as promising candidates for further experimental studies, while compound 12 requires structural optimization. Further synthesis, validated qNMR analysis, and biological studies are needed to confirm these findings. Keywords: Curcuma longa, qNMR, FTIR, mass spectrometry, SwissADME, drug-likeness, BOILED-Egg, target prediction, natural-product drug discovery.

title: Elucidating the dielectric, magnetic, and optical properties of PVA/PVP/CS-MWCNTs/NiFe₂O₄ nanocomposite for nanoelectronics applications
summary: The effect of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs)/nickel ferrite (NiFe₂O₄) hybrid nanofiller loading on the electrical transport characteristics and dielectric relaxation behaviour of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) (PV
content: The effect of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs)/nickel ferrite (NiFe₂O₄) hybrid nanofiller loading on the electrical transport characteristics and dielectric relaxation behaviour of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) (PVP)/chitosan (CS) polymer nanocomposite films was investigated. The films were prepared using the solution-casting method. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis revealed changes in the structural characteristics of the polymer blend, with an increase in its amorphous character up to a nanofiller concentration of 2.0 wt%. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicated possible interactions between the nanofillers and the functional groups of the polymer blend. Ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy was used to evaluate the optical properties. Increasing the nanofiller concentration from 0 to 2.0 wt% reduced the indirect optical band gap from approximately 4.8 to 2.8 eV, while the estimated refractive index increased from 1.108 to 2.348. Electrical conductivity and dielectric properties were investigated using alternating-current (AC) impedance spectroscopy. The frequency dependence of AC conductivity followed Jonscher’s power law for all prepared films. At ambient temperature, the film containing 2.0 wt% nanofiller exhibited the highest AC conductivity of 1.54 × 10⁻⁶ S cm⁻¹. The complex dielectric permittivity and loss tangent were analysed to investigate the dielectric response and relaxation behaviour, while the electric modulus spectra indicated non-Debye relaxation. These findings demonstrate that incorporating hybrid nanofillers can modify the optical, dielectric, and electrical properties of the polymer blend, suggesting potential for nanoelectronic and dielectric applications. Further electrochemical evaluation is required to establish its suitability for energy-storage applications.

title: Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome Due to a PHOX2B 20/31 Polyalanine Repeat Expansion Mutation: A Case Report
summary: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the PHOX2B gene, leading to impaired autonomic control of breathing and a blunted ventilatory response to hypercapnia
content: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the PHOX2B gene, leading to impaired autonomic control of breathing and a blunted ventilatory response to hypercapnia and hypoxemia.We report a male infant, born at 38+5 weeks' gestation by elective cesarean section for breech presentation, who developed shallow breathing and oxygen desaturation at birth, followed by recurrent sleep-predominant apnea and progressive hypercapnia despite escalating non-invasive respiratory support.Following transfer to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit at 11 days of age, a comprehensive evaluation excluded primary pulmonary, cardiac, neuromuscular, infectious, and metabolic causes.He was intubated on day of life 14 for worsening hypoventilation, and whole-exome sequencing confirmed a heterozygous PHOX2B polyalanine repeat expansion mutation, c.735_767dup; p.(Ala250_Ala260dup), corresponding to a 20/31 genotype.Tracheostomy was performed at approximately seven weeks of age to enable long-term mechanical ventilation.The infant's course was further complicated by respiratory colonization and infection with AmpC-producing Enterobacter cloacae, requiring carbapenem therapy.Genetic counseling confirmed that the variant had arisen de novo, with a low but non-zero recurrence risk in future pregnancies due to the possibility of parental germline mosaicism.At the time of this report, the infant remains hospitalized, clinically stable on tracheostomy mechanical ventilation, with a multidisciplinary long-term and home-ventilation plan in progress.This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for congenital central hypoventilation syndrome in neonates with unexplained, sleep-predominant hypoventilation once structural, infectious, neuromuscular, and metabolic causes have been excluded, and underscores the value of genotype-informed surveillance planning and structured genetic counseling for affected families.

title: Novel Constraints on Groundwater Flow in Fractured Systems by Combining Isotopic, Hydrochemical, and Microbial Tracers
summary: Abstract Groundwater in mountainous areas plays a critical role in sustaining regional water resources and ecosystem stability. However, characterizing groundwater flow through fractured bedrock remains challenging due to difficult access a
content: Abstract Groundwater in mountainous areas plays a critical role in sustaining regional water resources and ecosystem stability. However, characterizing groundwater flow through fractured bedrock remains challenging due to difficult access and highly heterogeneous geological conditions. In this study, we combined conventional isotopic and hydrochemical analyses with microbial community characterization to investigate groundwater recharge sources and flow paths using a 4‐km‐long horizontal tunnel as a research platform. Results showed that groundwater was recharged by precipitation through independent and inclined fractures, as inferred from the δ 18 O altitude gradient (−0.25‰ per 100 m, determined from 186 precipitation samples from three stations). Radiocarbon dating revealed millennial‐scale groundwater ages and indicated slow flow velocities in the mountain interior. Where hydrochemical variability was limited at the site scale, microbial communities provided sensitive natural tracers for discriminating groundwater from different fractures. This integrated multi‐tracer framework provides new constraints on groundwater flow pathways and connectivity in fractured systems.

title: Short term effects of ambient air pollution exposure on influenza: a multi-city study in Shandong, China
summary: Ambient air pollution is a recognized risk factor for influenza-like illness (ILI). However, it remains unclear how city-specific characteristics modify these associations. This study evaluated the short-term associations between six major
content: Ambient air pollution is a recognized risk factor for influenza-like illness (ILI). However, it remains unclear how city-specific characteristics modify these associations. This study evaluated the short-term associations between six major air pollutants and ILI incidence in Shandong Province, China, and investigated the modifying effects of seasonal, spatial, and socioeconomic factors. Daily air pollutant concentrations and ILI surveillance data from 16 cities in Shandong Province (2015–2019) were analyzed using a two-stage approach. City-specific associations were estimated using quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), followed by a multivariate random-effects meta-analysis to calculate pooled cumulative relative risks (CRRs). Meta-regression and stratified analyses were used to assess effect modification by demographic, geographic, and macroeconomic indicators. A total of 2,145,543 ILI cases were included. Except for O 3 , short-term exposure to all evaluated air pollutants was significantly associated with increased ILI incidence. NO 2 (CRR: 1.041, 95% CI: 1.031–1.052) and SO 2 (CRR: 1.040, 95% CI: 1.023–1.058) exhibited the strongest positive associations, whereas O 3 was inversely associated with ILI. The risks were higher in children aged 5–14 years, during transition seasons (spring and autumn), and in coastal areas. Meta-regression indicated that higher gross domestic product and healthcare resource density mitigated the adverse impacts of particulate matter and carbon monoxide, whereas basin. Basin topography exacerbated pollution-induced ILI risks during severe pollution episodes. Short-term exposure to major air pollutants increases ILI risk, but the magnitude of this risk is significantly modified by city-level socioeconomic and geographic characteristics. These findings highlight the need to develop localized, resource-adjusted air quality early warning systems to protect vulnerable populations.

title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
summary: The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual-inhibitor regimens is hampered
content: The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual-inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine-based photocatalysts as a single-agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self-immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post-treatment. This self-eliminating, metabolism-targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

title: Photo‐ thermal isomerization and degradation of β ‐carotene in a model beverage system under varying pH and oxygen conditions and corresponding protective strategies
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Abstract Background Photo‐thermal stability is a critical indicator of the quality of food products containing β ‐carotene. The differences in the degradation mechanisms of emulsified β ‐carotene in beverage matrices under different light a
content: Abstract Background Photo‐thermal stability is a critical indicator of the quality of food products containing β ‐carotene. The differences in the degradation mechanisms of emulsified β ‐carotene in beverage matrices under different light and thermal conditions, as well as the effects of environmental factors such as pH and oxygen partial pressure, require systematic investigation to develop effective stabilization strategies. Results Accelerated light exposure experiments revealed that cis ‐ β ‐carotene first underwent photo‐isomerization to all‐ trans ‐ β ‐carotene. This was followed by overall degradation, suggesting that cis ‐to‐ trans isomerization might be favored at high cis ‐isomer ratios. Compared with pH 3.0, pH 6.0 markedly enhanced both photo‐stability and thermal stability of cis ‐ β ‐carotene and all‐ trans ‐ β ‐carotene by suppressing protonation‐triggered initiation. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spin trapping confirmed that acid (H + ) promoted the formation of free radicals, which rapidly accelerated β ‐carotene degradation. Oxygen partial pressure significantly accelerated the photo‐degradation of 13‐ cis ‐ β ‐carotene and the thermal degradation of 9‐ cis ‐ β ‐carotene, whereas all‐ trans ‐ β ‐carotene demonstrated the highest stability. The addition of ascorbic acid and water‐soluble rosemary extract effectively enhanced the photo‐thermal stability of β ‐carotene in beverages, extending its shelf life to 20 weeks (under 24 h illumination). Conclusion This study provides insights into the degradation mechanisms of β ‐carotene emulsions in beverages. The stability of β ‐carotene was governed both by structural characteristics and environmental factors. All‐ trans ‐ β ‐carotene remained dominant across all conditions due to its stable conformation. The pH value and oxygen partial pressure were identified as critical factors influencing stability. These results provide strategies for selecting antioxidant combinations to develop more stable β ‐carotene‐fortified beverages with extended shelf life. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Unlocking high photocatalytic H2 generation and tetracycline eradication over 2D/2D/2D nanocomposite of P-doped g-C3N5/WO3/B4C
summary: The imperfections of g-C 3 N 5 cause some photocatalytic weaknesses. Herein, we prepared the 2D P-doped g-C 3 N 5 (PCN x ) photocatalysts via one-pot protocol; then, the 2D materials (i.e., Tungsten Oxide (WO 3 ), and Boron Carbide (B 4 C))
content: The imperfections of g-C 3 N 5 cause some photocatalytic weaknesses. Herein, we prepared the 2D P-doped g-C 3 N 5 (PCN x ) photocatalysts via one-pot protocol; then, the 2D materials (i.e., Tungsten Oxide (WO 3 ), and Boron Carbide (B 4 C)) coupled to PCN 0.25 , which extended visible-light-adsorption domain, attenuated charge complexation rate, and hastened charge carriers’ transportation rate compared to the pristine g-C 3 N 5 (CN). Thereby, the Tetracycline (TC) elimination increased to ~ 95% through H 2 O 2 -assisted photocatalysis, which evinced the abatement rate of TC enhanced to 578% than the primary photocatalysis. The maturation rate of green gram corroborated that the protocol of PCN 0.25 /35WO 3 /10B 4 C//H 2 O 2 //visible-light alleviated the negative impacts of TC. In addition to these, the presence of Pt and a double S-Scheme electron transfer mechanism synergistically increased the values of the Solar-to-Hydrogen (STH (%)) and the Apparent Quantum Yield (AQY (%)), which fortified the H 2 production rate (13.484 mmol g −1 h − 1 ) over the 2D/2D/2D nano-heterostructure of PCN 0.25 /35WO 3 /10B 4 C. This nanocomposite preserved its photo-sustainability after consecutive cycles. The outcomes could divulge new perspectives for improving the photocatalytic activity of g-C 3 N 5 for producing green fuel and treating wastewater.

title: Which design features of a digital simulation predict sustainability competency gains? Evidence from a large first-year business cohort
summary: Digital simulations offer experiential learning environments where students make consequential decisions under constraints. Yet little empirical evidence identifies which specific design features of these environments drive learning outcome
content: Digital simulations offer experiential learning environments where students make consequential decisions under constraints. Yet little empirical evidence identifies which specific design features of these environments drive learning outcomes. This study examines a hotel carbon reduction simulation embedded in a first-year management unit (n=1,079 students, 190 teams) and investigates which of ten simulation design features predict gains in sustainability competencies. Students completed pre- and post-simulation surveys measuring 25 competency items aligned to an eight-domain sustainability competency framework (n=212 matched pairs), alongside a ten-item simulation evaluation scale (alpha=0.92). All self-reported 25 competency items improved significantly (composite d=0.62, p<.001). Regression analysis revealed that active learning engagement (beta=6.13, p<.001) was the strongest predictor of competency gains, followed by feedback quality and realistic scenarios. Full-cohort performance data showed 97.4% of teams maintained profitability while reducing emissions, with 45.8% clustering in a 'productive struggle zone' just below the target. These findings suggest that simulation designers should prioritise active engagement mechanisms and timely feedback over surface-level realism. Implications for the design of technology-enhanced experiential learning environments are discussed.

title: The role of scale in public goods problems: from pandemics to climate change
summary: Climate change is a global emergency, as was the COVID-19 pandemic. But our collective response to COVID-19 was much stronger than our response to climate change, to date. Why is that the case? We hypothesize that one reason for the contras
content: Climate change is a global emergency, as was the COVID-19 pandemic. But our collective response to COVID-19 was much stronger than our response to climate change, to date. Why is that the case? We hypothesize that one reason for the contrasting response in these two systems is their differing scales: not just spatial localization and temporal scale but also personal efficacy, which quantifies how much an intervention directly benefits the individual who adopts it. We introduce a framework that captures regimes of containment, mitigation, and failure to control in social-ecological public goods problems. As parameters governing these three scales are varied, it is possible to shift from a COVID-like system to a climate-like system. The framework replicates both inaction in the case of climate change mitigation, as well as the faster response that we exhibited to COVID-19. The model also exhibits abrupt transitions between regimes and oscillatory dynamics. Our cross-system comparison also suggests actionable ways that cooperation can be improved in large-scale public goods problems, like climate change. More broadly, we argue that considering scale and incorporating human-environment feedbacks are not just interesting special cases within non-cooperative game theory, but rather should be the starting point for the study of altruism and human cooperation.

title: Inverted-Mode Scanning Tunneling Microscopy for Atomically Precise Fabrication
summary: Abstract Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) enables fabrication of atomically precise structures with growing technological potential. However, reproducible manipulation of covalently bonded atoms requires control over the atomic configura
content: Abstract Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) enables fabrication of atomically precise structures with growing technological potential. However, reproducible manipulation of covalently bonded atoms requires control over the atomic configuration of both sample and probe–a challenge in STM. Here, we introduce inverted-mode STM, an approach that enables mechanically controlled chemical reactions for atomically precise fabrication. Tailored molecules on a Si(100) surface enable imaging of extended regions of an annealed probe apex, providing direct experimental access to the probe structure relevant to fabrication. The molecules can also react with the probe, with the two sides of the tunnel junction acting as reactants positioned with subangstrom precision. This allows abstraction or donation of atoms from or to the probe. We demonstrate this by using an alkynyl-terminated molecule to reproducibly abstract hydrogen atoms from the probe at zero volts. We then show that successive reactions can replace specific hydrogen atoms with iodine, followed by removal and manipulation of iodine. The approach is expected to extend to other elements, moieties, and materials, enabling sequential, site-selective chemistry for atomically precise fabrication.

title: Analytical insights into the transient climate response
summary: Abstract The temperature in the transient climate response is lower than the equilibrium temperature for the same amount of forcing. The degree of disequilibrium is not constant in time and depends on various climate parameters. We solve th
content: Abstract The temperature in the transient climate response is lower than the equilibrium temperature for the same amount of forcing. The degree of disequilibrium is not constant in time and depends on various climate parameters. We solve the heat diffusion equation – representing here a dynamical response to a temperature-driven potential difference rather than molecular diffusion – with a surface temperature feedback for linearly increasing forcing. The surface temperature initially evolves at a slower rate than the corresponding steady-state (SS) temperature, and its rate increases until reaching quasi-steady state (QSS), when the SS and QSS temperatures evolve in parallel with a constant offset. The offset depends on the rate of forcing and the total heat capacity of the system, divided by the square of the climate feedback. The timescale over which the climate system approaches QSS depends only on the effective ocean mixing and depth and is on the order of thousands of years. Over societally relevant timescales (∼ 100 years), the top-of-atmosphere energy imbalance increases, and the actual temperature moves farther from the steady-state temperature expected for the same forcing.

title: The Response of Onset and Withdrawal of the Indian Summer Monsoon to Volcanic Aerosols
summary: Abstract Large volcanic eruptions are a source of climate variability, affecting the seasonal mean precipitation of the Indian summer monsoon. However, the extent to which changes in seasonal precipitation can be attributed to variations in
content: Abstract Large volcanic eruptions are a source of climate variability, affecting the seasonal mean precipitation of the Indian summer monsoon. However, the extent to which changes in seasonal precipitation can be attributed to variations in monsoon length versus monsoon intensity has remained unclear. Using large ensemble simulations of idealized volcanic eruptions at varying latitudes, we find that the monsoon onset and withdrawal change by a few weeks compared to an unforced case. Southern (Northern) hemispheric eruptions extend (shorten) the Indian summer monsoon in the year following the eruption. We show that these changes in the length of the monsoon season are more important in controlling the response of total monsoon rainfall to eruptions than changes to the intensity of rainfall. We explain our results using the low‐level jet and Inter‐tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) frameworks, which have been used to explain the internal variability of the monsoon onset.

title: Dynamic risk assessment and safety-case framework for shipboard lithium-ion battery systems
summary: Battery-driven passenger ferries offer meaningful environmental benefits over conventional propulsion, yet the large-scale lithium-ion systems that make this possible bring with them a set of safety challenges that are still poorly understo
content: Battery-driven passenger ferries offer meaningful environmental benefits over conventional propulsion, yet the large-scale lithium-ion systems that make this possible bring with them a set of safety challenges that are still poorly understood in the maritime context. Thermal runaway, flammable gas generation, and the risk of deflagration in confined shipboard compartments cannot be adequately evaluated with the static probability–consequence models that remain standard practice in maritime safety engineering. We address this gap by developing a physics-informed framework for dynamic risk assessment of battery-driven ferry systems. The work begins with a multi-physics model of thermal runaway behavior, gas generation, and compartment accumulation dynamics, then uses those physical insights to construct a time-dependent risk formulation that explicitly tracks hazard escalation and consequence growth. A time-to-unsafe condition (TUC) metric is introduced to measure whether detection and mitigation systems can realistically outpace hazard development. From this foundation we build an integrated safety-case framework that brings together hazard identification, functional and failure analysis, barrier modeling, and quantitative risk evaluation. Fire and gas modeling is embedded throughout to assess ventilation adequacy, flammability thresholds, and detection performance under realistic fault conditions. The full framework is implemented as a coupled-ODE simulation covering five scenarios: one nominal operating case, three single- and combined-degradation failure cases, and one active-mitigation case; a Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis with N = 200 samples quantifies the robustness of the conclusions, and the model is validated against published lithium-ion cell-level data and checked for order-of-magnitude consistency with the documented MF Ytterøyningen maritime incident and an in-service 5 MWh ferry battery installation. The resulting methodology links physical system behavior directly to risk metrics, enabling simulation-based design validation, and translates the analytical results into concrete engineering guidance on ventilation sizing, detection latency limits, and barrier independence requirements. The framework is intended to support both safety-case development and risk-informed design for the next generation of electrified vessels.

title: Constraining the hydrogen soil sink and photochemical source: insights from atmospheric H 2 inversions (2003–2023)
summary: Hydrogen (H 2 ) is expected to become an increasingly important energy carrier during the energy transition, likely leading to higher atmospheric H 2 levels due to losses during production, transport, storage and usage of hydrogen. Multiple
content: Hydrogen (H 2 ) is expected to become an increasingly important energy carrier during the energy transition, likely leading to higher atmospheric H 2 levels due to losses during production, transport, storage and usage of hydrogen. Multiple studies have shown this could impact atmospheric composition through interactions with the hydroxyl radical. However, the magnitude of this impact remains uncertain due to large uncertainties in the global H 2 budget, particularly in the soil sink and photochemical source. To address this, we present a spatiotemporally resolved H 2 budget derived using atmospheric inversions with the TM5 chemical transport model. With this approach, we infer a global mean soil sink of 52.8 [47.8–56.7] Tg yr −1 and a photochemical source of 34.6 [29.2–38.2] Tg yr −1 over 2003–2023. Relative to Ouyang et al. (2025), we estimate a soil sink that is 45 % and 35 % weaker in the Middle East and Oceania, and 45 % and 70 % stronger in South America and Russia, respectively. Our results further suggest that variability in the observed H 2 growth rate between 2003–2023 was primarily driven by changes in the photochemical source from CH 4 oxidation, together with a declining global soil sink at a mean rate of 0.23 Tg yr −2 . Finally, we infer a sensitivity of the soil sink to the El Niño–Southern Oscillation, strongest over diffusion-limited soils in tropical South America, with increased uptake during drier El Niño conditions and reduced uptake during wetter La Niña conditions.

title: Managing investment risk in the transition to low-carbon technologies: A real options analysis of Carbon Contracts for Difference
summary: Carbon-price volatility poses a major barrier to timely investment in low-carbon technologies. Carbon Contracts for Difference (CCfDs) have recently attracted attention as a policy instrument for mitigating carbon-price risk by providing re
content: Carbon-price volatility poses a major barrier to timely investment in low-carbon technologies. Carbon Contracts for Difference (CCfDs) have recently attracted attention as a policy instrument for mitigating carbon-price risk by providing revenue guarantees. To examine their role in low-carbon investment, this study develops a real options framework under carbon-price uncertainty. We derive optimal investment thresholds with and without a CCfD and analyze how carbon-price volatility, strike-price design, and technological characteristics affect investment timing. Numerical results show that CCfDs accelerate low-carbon investment by reducing exposure to downside carbon-price risk, with stronger effects under higher volatility, higher strike prices, and lower emission factors after investment. Monte Carlo simulations further show that CCfDs increase expected project value while improving downside-risk profiles. These findings provide quantitative insights into the design of CCfDs to support low-carbon investment under carbon-price uncertainty.

title: Vertically stratified long-range transport of biomass-burning aerosol over Reunion Island during September 2017
summary: Biomass-burning (BB) aerosols seasonally perturb the otherwise relatively clean atmosphere of the South-West Indian Ocean (SWIO), but vertically resolved observations remain sparse in its eastern sector. We examine an enhanced aerosol episo
content: Biomass-burning (BB) aerosols seasonally perturb the otherwise relatively clean atmosphere of the South-West Indian Ocean (SWIO), but vertically resolved observations remain sparse in its eastern sector. We examine an enhanced aerosol episode over Reunion Island (21° S, 55° E) in September 2017 by combining AERONET sun-photometer measurements, ground-based Raman and elastic lidar retrievals, FTIR CO observations, MODIS and CALIOP products, CAMS EAC4 reanalysis, and FLEXPART simulations. AERONET aerosol optical depth at 550 nm reached unusually high values (0.16–0.42) during the second half of September. CAMS provided temporally continuous total and species-resolved model AOD and simulated organic matter as the largest aerosol contribution. MODIS and CALIOP provided regional context, showing elongated enhanced-AOD corridors and elevated aerosol layers frequently classified as smoke-related over the western SWIO. On 19 September, lidar observations identified one layer between 2.8 and 4.7 km with Å355/532 = 1.32 ± 0.23. On 25 September, two vertically separated layers with distinct optical properties were observed: a lower layer (3.3–5 km, Å = 1.45 ± 0.12) and a drier upper layer (5–9 km, Å = 1.60 ± 0.06). FLEXPART simulations for two selected source regions, evaluated against vertically smoothed FTIR CO observations, support Southern African influence on both cases and an additional South American contribution to the lower layer on 25 September. The observations demonstrate that column-integrated measurements alone cannot resolve the layered aerosol structure over Reunion; the combined evidence provides an illustrative case of vertically distinct long-range transport pathways in the eastern SWIO.

title: ValUr: A High-Fidelity Database for Validation of Urban Pollution Dispersion Models Wind Tunnel Experimental Campaign Overview
summary: Validation is essential in showing the credibility and reliability of computational models, especially when the latter are to be used in social- and safety-critical contexts. Urban air quality has received significant research, political an
content: Validation is essential in showing the credibility and reliability of computational models, especially when the latter are to be used in social- and safety-critical contexts. Urban air quality has received significant research, political and societal attention due to its direct impact on quality of life in cities. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) has established itself as a tool for modelling and analysing the dispersion of various air pollutants with high spatial resolution. However, thorough validation of CFD for such applications has lagged behind. The ERIES-ValUr project aims to generate a comprehensive protocol for validation of pollution dispersion CFD models and to demonstrate the importance of rigorous validation and uncertainty quantification on model reliability, by setting up a validation test campaign on a geometrically scaled model of a region in the city of Sofia, Bulgaria. This paper is a continuation in the series of publications presenting the work on ValUr. It provides an overview of the wind tunnel testing campaign conducted at the atmospheric boundary layer wind tunnel at Eindhoven University of Technology under the ERIES transnational access programme. The campaign featured an array of experiments leading to two independent pollution dispersion datasets, each obtained from a separate point source releases mimicking traffic-related pollution, at 76 near-surface locations. The paper outlines critical characteristics of validation experiments and the steps taken for these to be considered during the ValUr testing campaign. Details about the measurement setup and experiment execution, quantification of measurement uncertainty, and next steps are presented.

title: Fossil carbon transformation in municipal wastewater treatment and its implications for greenhouse gas accounting
summary: Petrochemical-derived compounds from detergents, pharmaceuticals, and industrial discharges can introduce fossil carbon into municipal wastewater, but its transformation into atmospheric CO 2 remains poorly constrained. Here, we integrate o
content: Petrochemical-derived compounds from detergents, pharmaceuticals, and industrial discharges can introduce fossil carbon into municipal wastewater, but its transformation into atmospheric CO 2 remains poorly constrained. Here, we integrate online greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring with radiocarbon ( 14 C) analysis of liquid, solid, and gaseous carbon pools to trace fossil carbon transfer and transformation within municipal wastewater treatment plants and develop a first-order national estimate of fossil-derived CO 2 emissions for China. Fossil carbon accounted for 3.9–23.0% of influent carbon and 2.7–19.1% of CO 2 in treatment off-gases, demonstrating measurable fossil-derived CO 2 emissions across different treatment systems. Plant-level relationships between influent fossil carbon and emitted fossil CO 2 varied substantially, reflecting the combined influence of wastewater composition, treatment configuration, carbon biodegradability, external carbon addition, and operating conditions. Fossil-derived CO 2 contributed up to 52% of measured direct GHG emissions within the monitored system boundaries. Integrating field measurements, literature data, and national wastewater treatment statistics, we estimate 1135.7 Gg of fossil-derived CO 2 emissions in China in 2020, representing ~10% of its direct GHG emissions from municipal wastewater treatment. Despite uncertainty from limited radiocarbon-constrained observations, these results indicate that fossil-derived CO 2 warrants explicit consideration in wastewater GHG accounting.

title: The Politics of Industrial Policy within the Green Division of Labour: Comparing Solar PV Manufacturing in India, Mexico and South Africa
summary: ABSTRACT There is growing optimism about the possibilities of green industrial policy (GIP), as countries in the Global South deal with the twin challenges of reducing carbon emissions and achieving structural transformation. However, this
content: ABSTRACT There is growing optimism about the possibilities of green industrial policy (GIP), as countries in the Global South deal with the twin challenges of reducing carbon emissions and achieving structural transformation. However, this optimism is founded on a narrow analysis of how the politics of GIP operates. This article calls for critical multi‐scalar political economy analysis to explain GIP outcomes in contexts shaped by earlier phases of neoliberal reform. It takes the case of solar photovoltaics (PV) manufacturing, which is characterized by China's dominance in manufacturing segments of the solar PV chain, to examine how the new politics of green energy transition is shaping GIP outcomes in three large economies that have significantly expanded their solar generation capacity: India, Mexico and South Africa. The article shows how first‐mover countries generate new transnational coalitions around green energy that combine with earlier collaborations forged around neoliberalism to undermine productivist green industrial policy. The resulting prioritization of increasing renewable energy generation above supporting domestic manufacturing ensures the continued subordinate integration of these countries within the green division of labour.

title: Policy-driven optimal design of grid-connected hybrid EV charging stations using an optimization-based policy analysis framework
summary: Renewable energy policies play a pivotal role in determining the economic viability of photovoltaic (PV)-based EV charging stations (EVCSs), yet their influence on optimal system design is insufficiently understood because most studies trea
content: Renewable energy policies play a pivotal role in determining the economic viability of photovoltaic (PV)-based EV charging stations (EVCSs), yet their influence on optimal system design is insufficiently understood because most studies treat the regulatory environment as fixed rather than a decision-sensitive design variable. This study introduces an Optimization-Based Policy Analysis Framework (OBPAF), integrating a hybrid EVCS model with NSGA-III, M/M/c queueing theory, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), and TOPSIS to evaluate how six policy scenarios — Baseline, Net Billing (100%/65%), Net Metering (100%/65%), and Carbon Credit — reshape the optimal PV–BESS EVCS configuration under identical models and settings. The optimal configuration proved strongly policy-dependent: Net Billing with full export compensation achieved the highest NPV (IDR 1.81 billion, 11.74-year payback), while Net Metering with full compensation produced the lowest LCOC (IDR 3771.12 kWh⁻¹) and highest life-cycle CO₂ emission reduction (81.5%) but a negative NPV, while Carbon Credit produced only marginal improvements. These findings show OBPAF extends multi-objective optimization into a quantitative framework for evidence-based renewable energy policy evaluation.

title: A harmonization index for comparative assessment of industrial particulate matter emission regulations
summary: Abstract Industrial particulate matter (PM) emissions remain a major environmental management challenge, yet meaningful international comparison of emission regulations is hindered by fundamentally different legal, technical, and institutio
content: Abstract Industrial particulate matter (PM) emissions remain a major environmental management challenge, yet meaningful international comparison of emission regulations is hindered by fundamentally different legal, technical, and institutional approaches adopted by individual jurisdictions. This study presents the first standardized Regulatory Coding Framework and Harmonization Index (HI) for the systematic evaluation and benchmarking of industrial PM emission regulations across technology-based, source-category-based, hybrid, and dispersion-based regulatory systems. The European Union, the United States, China, and Uzbekistan were selected as contrasting case studies. Twenty-one evaluation indicators, identified through systematic analysis of legally binding regulatory documents, were organized into three complementary dimensions:Regulatory Stringency, Institutional Design, and Documented Enforcement Capacity. Regulatory provisions were transformed into standardized documentary coding scores, normalized, and aggregated into a composite Harmonization Index. Framework robustness was evaluated through alternative weighting scenarios and Spearman’s rank correlation analysis. The results reveal substantial regulatory divergence extending beyond numerical emission limits, particularly in technology-based regulation, integrated permitting, continuous emission monitoring, and independent compliance verification. The European Union achieved the highest Harmonization Index (1.000), followed by the United States (0.976), China (0.857), and Uzbekistan (0.500), while jurisdictional rankings remained fully stable under all weighting scenarios (Spearman’s ρ = 1.000).The proposed framework provides a transparent and reproducible decision-support method for regulatory benchmarking and reform prioritization. Its scope is deliberately limited to formal regulatory architecture: the four-case design and document-based coding do not establish associations with measured emissions, ambient air quality, compliance rates, or implementation quality. External validation against outcome data and application to a larger jurisdictional sample are therefore required before the HI can be interpreted beyond documentary regulatory alignment.

title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
summary: ABSTRACT Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a grea
content: ABSTRACT Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for ( E )‐1‐(5‐bromo‐1 H ‐indol‐1‐yl)‐3‐(3,5‐difluorophenyl)prop‐2‐en‐1‐one ( PEOBr 5 F 35 ), this process proceeded via a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second‐step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five‐membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst‐free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane‐fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

title: From Lunch to Lessons: The Case for Promoting Plant-Based Diets in Schools
source: University of Birmingham Research Portal (University of Birmingham)
summary: This paper argues that states should require schools to guide students towards plant-based diets. Concerns about climate change and animals provide strong moral reasons to adopt such diets. We examine whether, and in what ways, schools may
content: This paper argues that states should require schools to guide students towards plant-based diets. Concerns about climate change and animals provide strong moral reasons to adopt such diets. We examine whether, and in what ways, schools may legitimately promote them, focusing on the distinctive normative issues raised by schools as institutions that shape children’s behaviour and beliefs. We draw implications for both catering and curriculum policies – what food schools procure and what they teach. Specifically, we defend procurement restrictions in catering and a curriculum aimed at students coming to endorse reasons for plant-based diets. We argue that schools’ role in educating children about justice provides an important basis for their promotion of plant-based diets, and defend conceptions of justice and legitimacy that take the interests of animals into account. Finally, we address three key objections to schools promoting plant-based diets: that the liberal state should remain neutral on controversial moral issues, that promoting plant-based diets threatens children’s autonomy, and that it conflicts with parental rights. We argue that none of these objections succeed.

title: Within-fire estimates of biomass loss across national forests of the US West Coast: inventory-informed inference with uncertainty
summary: Abstract Wildfire is reshaping forests in the western United States (US), yet estimates of wildfire impacts often rely on burned-area summaries or satellite-derived severity metrics that do not directly quantify changes in forest biomass or
content: Abstract Wildfire is reshaping forests in the western United States (US), yet estimates of wildfire impacts often rely on burned-area summaries or satellite-derived severity metrics that do not directly quantify changes in forest biomass or their uncertainty. We combine US Forest Inventory and Analysis plot measurements with annual 30 m tree canopy cover data in a Bayesian spatio-temporal modeling framework to estimate within-fire changes in live aboveground biomass (AGB) and forest mortality area across National Forest System lands in Washington, Oregon, and California. The model represents both live forest presence or absence and AGB conditional on live forest, allowing posterior predictive estimates of pre- and post-fire conditions at the pixel scale. Applied to 6,308 fire analysis areas from 2000 to 2022, the analysis estimates 117.8 million Mg of wildfire-associated AGB loss and 2.98 million ha of forest mortality area, with the largest aggregate impacts occurring in 2020. Pixel-level estimates reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity within fire perimeters, including large differences between total burned area, forest mortality area, and associated biomass loss. This inventory-informed, uncertainty-aware approach provides a scalable framework for quantifying forest carbon impacts of disturbance across broad regions while retaining within-fire spatial detail.

title: Chemical reactions for the ligand-directed modification of native proteins
summary: Selective modifications of native proteins provide powerful opportunities to study and manipulate biological systems, yet achieving site-selective functionalization remains challenging due to the surfeit of competing amino acids, often addr
content: Selective modifications of native proteins provide powerful opportunities to study and manipulate biological systems, yet achieving site-selective functionalization remains challenging due to the surfeit of competing amino acids, often addressed by genetic engineering of target proteins. Ligand-directed protein modification addresses these limitations by exploiting reversible molecular recognition to position reactive groups in proximity to a defined protein site, thereby enabling selective covalent modification of native proteins under physiological conditions. Importantly, ligand-directed protein modification is evolving from a specialized labeling methodology into a versatile platform for the selective manipulation of protein function in native biological environments. In this review, we discuss recent advances in ligand-directed strategies that employ synthetically accessible small molecules and peptides as recognition elements. Current approaches are categorized into (i) ligation reactions, in which the ligand remains attached to the protein, (ii) transfer reactions, which install a functional moiety while releasing the ligand, and (iii) ligand-directed catalysis, where ligand-tethered catalysts promote protein-substrate reactions with catalytic turnover. For each strategy, employed chemical reactions, amino acid selectivities, and applications in chemical biology and biotechnology are described. We further compare the strengths and limitations of these approaches considering the balance between reactivity, selectivity, and biocompatibility.

title: Irradiated Atmospheres. VII. Effect of Mixing Energy Flux on Atmosphere–Interior Coupling
summary: Abstract Highly irradiated, underdense rocky planets such as puffy Venuses may host strong coupling between their atmospheres and magma-ocean interiors. Previous studies have mainly treated this coupling through radiative transfer and chemi
content: Abstract Highly irradiated, underdense rocky planets such as puffy Venuses may host strong coupling between their atmospheres and magma-ocean interiors. Previous studies have mainly treated this coupling through radiative transfer and chemical equilibrium, leaving the role of vertical mixing unclear. Here we quantify how energy transport associated with vertical mixing modifies the thermal structure, volatile chemistry, and emission spectra of puffy Venuses. Atmospheric circulation and gravity-wave breaking are possible dynamical sources of such transport. We show that this energy transport provides an additional greenhouse-like heating pathway by warming the deep atmosphere, thereby increasing the pressure and temperature at the magma-ocean surface. The resulting thermal changes also reshape the atmospheric composition, especially the abundances of CO and H 2 O, and change the partitioning of C-, H-, and O-bearing volatiles between the atmosphere and the magma ocean. Moreover, these changes reshape the mid-infrared planet–star flux ratio, especially at low equilibrium temperatures and in higher-mass planets. Under high C/O, it slightly increases the flux near 3.5–4.0 μ m but more broadly reduces atmospheric transparency and suppresses the flux. This may affect radius estimates for puffy Venuses over a limited temperature range.

title: DEMOS. II. What the full Lupus demographics tell us about protoplanetary disc evolution
summary: Assessing whether disc evolution is driven by viscosity or magneto hydro-dynamic (MHD) winds is crucial to determine the conditions in which planets form. The rich statistical information encoded in the nearby star-forming regions provides
content: Assessing whether disc evolution is driven by viscosity or magneto hydro-dynamic (MHD) winds is crucial to determine the conditions in which planets form. The rich statistical information encoded in the nearby star-forming regions provides an excellent opportunity to probe disc evolution. In this paper, we apply the Bayesian inference tool , which is designed to fully exploit the statistical properties of disc populations and infer initial conditions and model parameters, to the Lupus disc population. We consider the observed distribution of stellar mass, M_⋆, disc mass, M (obtained from continuum flux), mass accretion rate, . We constrain all parameters for both the viscous model, which includes dispersal driven by internal photoevaporation, and the MHD winds model, with unprecedented precision. The inferred initial conditions suggest that positive correlations between initial disc properties, such as mass, M_0, and truncation radius, R_0, with the stellar mass, M_⋆, must be already present in the population before the disc phase. According to both models, the typical R_0 for a disc around a 0.3 DEMOS and CO disc size, R_ 90%, CO M _⊙ star is 3-5 au, with a strong dependence on stellar mass of ∼ 2 and ∼ 1 for the viscous-photo-evaporative and MHD winds models, respectively. We infer values for the angular momentum transport parameter α (or α_ in both models, for discs around 0.3 of 3-4 10^ -4 M _⊙ stars, and an approximately quadratic dependence on M_⋆. For the viscous-photo-evaporative model, we infer a typical wind mass-loss rate of dot M _ ∼ 10^ w -9 M_⊙ yr -1 $ for a disc around a 0.3 M _⊙ star, and a steep correlation with M_⋆ with an exponent $∼ 2.5. The inferred mean age of the Lupus population differs between models, with łangle t̊angle = 1.6 Myr for the MHD winds model and łangle t̊angle = 0.9 Myr for the viscous-photo-evaporative framework. Despite indicating a slight preference for the viscous-photo-evaporative framework, the Bayesian evidence computed with shows that both models reproduce the data with comparable accuracy and does not allow either scenario to be ruled out. However, the best-fit synthetic populations predict substantially different evolutionary pathways, which suggests that the application of to multiple populations, especially to evolved ones such as Upper Scorpius, will allow us to place stronger constraints on disc evolution mechanisms.
