title: Hole-selective self-assembled monolayers: a molecular platform for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics
summary: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) are among the most promising photovoltaic technologies for surpassing the efficiency limits of single-junction solar cells. A major breakthrough in this field has been the introduction of ultra
content: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) are among the most promising photovoltaic technologies for surpassing the efficiency limits of single-junction solar cells. A major breakthrough in this field has been the introduction of ultrathin hole-selective self-assembled monolayers (HS-SAMs). These molecular interfacial layers enable precise energy-level alignment, efficient hole extraction, and effective passivation of interfacial defects, while remaining compatible with textured silicon and large-area substrates. In this review, we discuss the molecular design principles of HS-SAMs, including anchoring groups, conjugated donor units, linkers, dipole engineering, wettability, and packing density, highlighting how these parameters influence charge extraction, perovskite crystallization, interfacial passivation, and device stability. We also summarize key advances in PSTSCs enabled by HS-SAMs, including a certified PCE of 29.2% with Me-4PACz and efficiencies above 32% with optimized PACz derivatives and 32.5% with 2PACz/IZO interlayers, together with operational stability exceeding 1000 h under damp-heat or continuous illumination conditions. By consolidating recent progress in molecular engineering, interfacial passivation, scalable deposition, and manufacturability, this review identifies HS-SAMs as a cornerstone for the development of efficient, stable, and commercially relevant perovskite and perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics.

title: Starting material syntheses for non-aqueous molecular uranium chemistry
summary: Starting materials for non-aqueous uranium chemistry usually must be synthesised in-house, as they are rarely available commercially. Various routes to uranium precursors in oxidation states +III to +VI have been reported and developed furt
content: Starting materials for non-aqueous uranium chemistry usually must be synthesised in-house, as they are rarely available commercially. Various routes to uranium precursors in oxidation states +III to +VI have been reported and developed further according to the availability of uranium compounds. This tutorial review discusses wet-chemical and selected solid-state routes to anhydrous uranium halide, amide and borohydride starting materials in oxidation states +III to +VI suitable for research laboratories. Oxidative, reductive, as well as halide interconversion routes are discussed to give a comprehensive overview on synthetically established routes and promising directions for future development.

title: Marine Spatial Use Control, Blue Carbon, and Maritime Security in Indonesia: A Scoping Review
summary: Blue carbon ecosystems are increasingly central to climate mitigation, coastal resilience, and maritime governance, but their protection in Indonesia depends on how spatial plans are translated into effective implementation and control. Thi
content: Blue carbon ecosystems are increasingly central to climate mitigation, coastal resilience, and maritime governance, but their protection in Indonesia depends on how spatial plans are translated into effective implementation and control. This scoping review maps the relationship between marine spatial use control and mangrove and seagrass protection in Indonesia and interprets the implications for maritime security. Guided by JBI methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR, searches of Scopus, Web of Science, GARUDA, and DOAJ, complemented by citation searching, yielded a final corpus of 39 studies. The evidence base is strongly asymmetrical: 29 studies focused on mangroves, whereas only three focused specifically on seagrasses; conclusions concerning seagrass governance are therefore exploratory and should not be generalized from the mangrove-dominated corpus. Regional Spatial Plans (RTRW) were the most frequently examined instrument type (12 studies), followed by coastal and small-island zoning plans (RZWP3K) and functional zoning (five each). The most commonly mapped primary evidence gaps concerned policy and governance (15 studies) and implementation and enforcement (12 studies). Only eight studies applied an explicit blue carbon framing. No formal critical appraisal of individual sources was undertaken, so these frequencies are interpreted as patterns in the reviewed literature rather than as estimates of national policy performance or causal effectiveness. Post-extraction interpretation using Bueger's maritime security framework indicated that the reviewed literature is most readily connected to the marine environment, human security, and economic development; except where security was explicitly discussed by source authors, these categories represent reviewer-applied interpretive pathways rather than direct security effects. Overall, the literature most consistently points to an implementation gap between spatial-plan design and effective control, including spatial conformity assessment, monitoring, institutional coordination, follow-up, and enforcement. Strengthening empirical evaluation of these functions, particularly for seagrasses and eastern Indonesia, is necessary before broader conclusions about blue carbon governance and maritime-security outcomes can be sustained.

title: Governance Challenges and Stakeholder Readiness for Collaborative Blue Carbon Management in West Sumatra, Indonesia
summary: Effective blue carbon management requires coordination across institutions, sectors, and stakeholder groups, yet fragmented governance can constrain collaborative action. This study explores perceived governance challenges and stakeholder r
content: Effective blue carbon management requires coordination across institutions, sectors, and stakeholder groups, yet fragmented governance can constrain collaborative action. This study explores perceived governance challenges and stakeholder readiness for collaborative blue carbon management in West Sumatra, Indonesia. An exploratory mixed-methods approach was applied using a short online questionnaire distributed to stakeholders engaged with the Marine Spatial Planning Agency of Padang (BPRL Padang). Twenty-five respondents from government, state-owned enterprises, the private sector, academia, NGOs, and community groups participated. Quantitative responses were analysed descriptively, while open-ended responses were examined using thematic coding. The highest-rated governance challenge was the need for greater clarification of environmental obligations following the issuance of KKPRL, followed by limited spatial data and information on blue carbon ecosystems and weak stakeholder coordination. Institutional coordination and integration also emerged as the most frequently identified theme in open-ended responses. Despite these challenges, respondents demonstrated strong recognition of the need for greater inter-agency collaboration and high stated willingness to support joint rehabilitation or restoration activities, participate in collaborative forums, and share relevant data and information. These findings suggest a potential gap between collaborative readiness and collaborative capacity where participating stakeholders appear willing to collaborate, while institutional mechanisms may remain insufficient to translate this willingness into sustained collective action. Strengthening blue carbon governance may therefore require greater attention to coordination mechanisms, information sharing, institutional clarity, and long-term collaborative arrangements.

title: Measuring What Companies Say about Net Zero and Climate Transition: A Weighted-Lexicon Framework with ClimateBERT Corroboration
summary: Abstract What companies disclose about their net-zero and climate transition is not the same as what they achieve, yet existing text-analytic approaches face a trade-off between scalable but undifferentiated keyword counts and contextually
content: Abstract What companies disclose about their net-zero and climate transition is not the same as what they achieve, yet existing text-analytic approaches face a trade-off between scalable but undifferentiated keyword counts and contextually sensitive but costly manual coding. This paper develops Net-Zero/Climate-Transition Disclosure (NZCTD), a transparent, auditable measure of the volume and specificity of net-zero and climate-transition language in corporate annual reports — not a measure of actual climate performance, emissions reduction, implementation, compliance, or sincerity. NZCTD is built from an eighteen-category, 273-pattern lexicon with evidentiary weights from 0 to 4, applied at the paragraph level with contextual safeguards, and corroborated by an independent, model-based ClimateBERT layer applied only to qualifying paragraphs. Applied to 468 Indian listed companies and 4,048 company-year observations spanning FY2013–FY2025, the measure has a mean score of 319.58 (median 140.0) with pronounced right-skewness and a mean rising from approximately 32.2 in FY2013 to approximately 909.7 in FY2025, an independently recomputed 28.25-fold increase. Weighted and unweighted scores correlate highly (Pearson r = 0.9855; Spearman rho = 0.9919), and principal component analysis indicates a coherent common structure alongside meaningful multidimensionality (PC1 explains 46.85% of variance; r = 0.8655 with the total score), while ClimateBERT confirmation ratios reach approximately 0.684 in later years. NZCTD offers a scalable, transparent framework for measuring climate-transition disclosure that preserves contextual insights and the disclosure-versus-performance distinction throughout.

title: Is low-carbon transition risk affecting the market and credit ratings equally? Evidence for European companies
summary: This paper assesses the relationship between credit risk and different climate variables under a system of equations tested using seemingly unrelated regression. When considering both total emissions and Scope 1 emissions only, carbon inten
content: This paper assesses the relationship between credit risk and different climate variables under a system of equations tested using seemingly unrelated regression. When considering both total emissions and Scope 1 emissions only, carbon intensity is found to be relevant to both the rating level credit risk and the market-implied distance-to-default. However, only the rating level credit risk has grown in importance since the Paris Agreement. With respect to mitigation variables, our findings indicate that the setting of emission targets is relevant in a similar way for both market and rating measures and that the Paris Agreement has had no impact. Furthermore, carbon pricing, a strategy that emerged after the Paris Agreement, was found to be significant for both market and rating agency measures. This finding suggests that markets and rating agencies do not value the same mitigation strategies more highly after the Paris Agreement, but they do value their greater definition and sophistication more highly. Overall, the results indicate that, after the Paris Agreement, rating agencies attribute greater importance to emissions in determining the distance-to-default, while the market assigns greater importance to carbon pricing strategies than the rating agencies do.

title: Seasonal decoupling of local climate zone thermal responses in three cold-climate cities of Northeast China
summary: Urban thermal environments are strongly influenced by urban morphology and land cover, yet the seasonal stability of Local Climate Zone (LCZ)–land surface temperature (LST) relationships in cold-climate cities remains insufficiently underst
content: Urban thermal environments are strongly influenced by urban morphology and land cover, yet the seasonal stability of Local Climate Zone (LCZ)–land surface temperature (LST) relationships in cold-climate cities remains insufficiently understood. In regions with long winters and seasonal snow cover, LCZ-specific surface thermal responses may differ substantially from those observed in temperate cities. This study investigates seasonal thermal responses across LCZ types in three major cold-climate cities in Northeast China—Shenyang, Harbin, and Changchun. LST was retrieved from Landsat 8 imagery on the Google Earth Engine platform, and LCZ maps were produced following the World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT) framework. Seasonal differences in LCZ thermal responses were examined through intra- and inter-city comparisons of mean LST, LCZ-referenced LST contrasts, and mixed-effects model estimates. To further isolate structural thermal effects from background climatic variability, a linear mixed-effects model was applied with LCZ type, season, and their interaction as fixed effects and city as a random effect. Auxiliary snow-cover and solar-radiation indicators were also incorporated to support the interpretation of seasonal mechanisms. The results show that summer LST patterns are strongly controlled by urban morphology and surface radiative properties. Compact built-up zones (LCZ 1–3), industrial or large impervious areas, and exposed hard surfaces exhibit pronounced warming effects, with Changchun showing the highest mean summer LST among the three cities. In winter, inter-LCZ thermal contrasts become substantially weaker, and low-vegetation, open, or exposed surfaces tend to show stronger cooling under snow-covered and low-radiation conditions. Shenyang maintains the warmest winter condition, whereas Harbin exhibits the strongest winter cold background. The mixed-effects model reveals a significant LCZ × season interaction, indicating a seasonal shift in the mechanisms controlling urban surface temperature. Summer thermal patterns are primarily governed by radiative absorption and urban surface structure, whereas winter thermal dynamics are jointly modulated by snow cover, reduced solar radiation, and heating-season urban energy processes. These findings demonstrate that LCZ–LST relationships in cold-climate cities exhibit pronounced seasonal variability and should not be directly generalized from studies conducted in warmer regions. The results provide a scientific basis for seasonally differentiated, LCZ-specific climate adaptation and thermal environment management in high-latitude cities.

title: The Use of Coconut Fiber as an Echo Absorbing Material in Green Technology-Based Building Renovation (Case Study of Dome Smesco Jakarta)
summary: The application of green technology in sustainable building renovation requires environmentally friendly materials that provide effective technical performance while enhancing indoor environmental quality and occupant comfort. One of the pr
content: The application of green technology in sustainable building renovation requires environmentally friendly materials that provide effective technical performance while enhancing indoor environmental quality and occupant comfort. One of the primary challenges in public buildings is maintaining appropriate room acoustics, particularly by controlling excessive reverberation and improving speech intelligibility. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of coconut coir fiber (cocofiber) as a natural sound-absorbing material in reducing reverberation time and improving perceived acoustic comfort. A quantitative descriptive-comparative approach was employed through a case study of the SMESCO Dome Building in Jakarta, Indonesia. Data were collected through reverberation time measurements conducted before and after the installation of coconut coir fiber acoustic treatment, supplemented by a structured questionnaire assessing users' perceptions of acoustic comfort and speech clarity. The acoustic measurements were evaluated with reference to Indonesian National Standard (Standar Nasional Indonesia, SNI) 03-6386-2011, while questionnaire responses were analyzed quantitatively to assess perceived changes in the indoor acoustic environment. The results indicated that the measured reverberation time decreased from 4.34 seconds to 1.93 seconds following the installation of the coconut coir fiber treatment, representing a reduction of approximately 55.5%. Although the post-installation reverberation time remained slightly above the recommended criterion, the measurements demonstrated a substantial improvement in reverberation control. Questionnaire findings further indicated that most respondents perceived improvements in acoustic comfort, particularly in speech clarity and reduced reverberation. These findings suggested that coconut coir fiber could serve as an effective natural sound-absorbing material for improving room acoustics in large public buildings. However, the observed improvements should be interpreted within the context of the case study, as the before-and-after design did not isolate the acoustic contribution of the material from other potential environmental or installation-related factors. Overall, coconut coir fiber demonstrated promising potential as a renewable, bio-based acoustic treatment material for sustainable building renovation and green construction applications.

title: Project ERIES-RecycleSlab—Seismic Behaviour of Flat Slabs with Drop Panels Made with Reinforced Recycled Aggregate Concrete
summary: This paper summarizes the ERIES-RecycleSlab research project, which investigated the seismic performance of a full-scale, two-storey flat-slab building with drop panels constructed using concrete containing coarse recycled concrete aggregat
content: This paper summarizes the ERIES-RecycleSlab research project, which investigated the seismic performance of a full-scale, two-storey flat-slab building with drop panels constructed using concrete containing coarse recycled concrete aggregates (CRCAC). The structure was subjected to combined gravity and lateral loading through a sequence of pseudo-dynamic seismic tests (two levels of seismic motion: one related to Serviceability Limit State and another one to Ultimate Limit State) followed by cyclic horizontal loading (combined gravity and lateral cyclic loading with increasing amplitude to near-failure conditions). The test setup is described in terms of structural design, test protocol, specimen dimensions and materials characterization. The experimental results obtained are presented and analysed. The project also evaluated advanced digital surveying methods for detecting and quantifying seismic damage in flat-slab systems. To achieve this, the specimen was 3D-scanned before and after testing using laser-based technology, enabling the creation of detailed digital models for comparison and damage assessment. The testing of the full-scale two-storey flat slab structure was carried out at the European Laboratory for Structural Assessment (ELSA) of the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre.

title: Autonomous decarbonization: a systematic review of agentic AI in adjacent energy domains and its implications for net zero procurement and supply chain management
summary: Procurement and supply chains account for most organisational greenhouse gas emissions, yet these Scope 3 emissions remain the hardest to measure and reduce. Agentic artificial intelligence (AI), meaning systems that can act with limited hu
content: Procurement and supply chains account for most organisational greenhouse gas emissions, yet these Scope 3 emissions remain the hardest to measure and reduce. Agentic artificial intelligence (AI), meaning systems that can act with limited human intervention, is increasingly promoted as a solution, but it is unclear whether the evidence supports entrusting it with procurement decisions that carry financial, legal and carbon consequences. This review asks what research on AI-driven decarbonisation shows and what it implies for Net Zero procurement. Following PRISMA 2020, we reviewed 167 Scopus-indexed studies (2020–2026), combining topic modelling with qualitative synthesis. Three research streams emerge: carbon data and measurement, autonomous decision-making, and energy-system optimisation. AI has progressed from analysing data, to monitoring systems in real time, to acting autonomously, but almost entirely in buildings, electricity systems and transport; studies of autonomous procurement decisions are effectively absent. We interpret this as a delegation readiness gap: AI capabilities have advanced faster than the conditions needed to delegate procurement decisions responsibly. Three conditions define this gap: decision-grade supplier emissions data, clear decision authority with human oversight, and carbon accounting that includes AI’s own computational footprint. An integrative framework sets out how these conditions could be met. For managers, the priority is to invest in data and governance before autonomy; for researchers and policymakers, the review defines what must be demonstrated before agentic AI can be considered credible for Net Zero procurement. The study shifts attention from whether AI can optimise to whether organisations can delegate.

title: Legacy PFAS fingerprints in New Zealand common dolphins Delphinus delphis over two decades
summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) accumulate in marine food webs, yet their long-term behaviour remains poorly resolved in Southern Hemisphere predators. Tissue archives record past exposure, but changing analytical coverage and cl
content: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) accumulate in marine food webs, yet their long-term behaviour remains poorly resolved in Southern Hemisphere predators. Tissue archives record past exposure, but changing analytical coverage and clustered sampling complicate interpretation. Here we quantified 28 PFAS in the livers of 98 common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) recovered around New Zealand between 2003 and 2025. Burdens were dominated by sulfonates, with PFOS contributing a median 44.0% of burdens and PFDA predominating among carboxylates, whereas associations with life history and stranding region were limited. Concentrations appeared to decline over time, but evidence for this decline weakened when each stranding event was represented by a single value or the largest mass-stranding group was excluded. A growth-coupled kinetic model estimated an effective PFOS half-life of 2.46 years. These findings establish a Southern Hemisphere baseline for legacy PFAS and a framework for separating environmental change from analytical and sampling variation in retrospective wildlife archives.

title: Does Financial Access Enable Carbon Monitoring? Evidence from Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Developing Asia and the Pacific
summary: Carbon monitoring is often the first step toward managing and reducing emissions. Financial constraints can limit small and medium-sized enterprises from investing in environmental management activities, particularly in developing economies
content: Carbon monitoring is often the first step toward managing and reducing emissions. Financial constraints can limit small and medium-sized enterprises from investing in environmental management activities, particularly in developing economies. Using World Bank Enterprise Survey data covering 20,089 small and medium-sized enterprises across 24 developing economies in Asia and the Pacific between 2022 and 2026, this study examines whether access to finance influences firms’ adoption of carbon dioxide emissions monitoring. Survey-weighted logit models are employed to account for the stratified sampling design, and the results are robust to probit and linear probability specifications. The findings suggest that general access to finance is not consistently associated with carbon dioxide emissions monitoring. However, the source of finance matters. Lending from state-owned banks is associated with an increased likelihood of emissions monitoring among small firms, whereas financing from private banks shows no significant effect. Reliance on informal financing is associated with a lower likelihood of monitoring.

title: Antioxidant property of nano-emulsion prepared from rhizome extract of Acorus calamus
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: OPMDs, especially Erosive lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis, and nonhomogeneous leukoplakia, show an increased tendency for malignant transformation. This increased rate of malignant transformation might be due to the generation of fre
content: OPMDs, especially Erosive lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis, and nonhomogeneous leukoplakia, show an increased tendency for malignant transformation. This increased rate of malignant transformation might be due to the generation of free radicals, which induce cell mutation. These free radicals are countered by systemic antioxidants. Due to the lack of absorption at the site where it is needed, there is a need for the topical route of administration. It is predicted that 20% of the systemic antioxidant is taken into action at the particular site of the oral cavity. So, there is a need for the topical route of administration to achieve the complete degeneration of free radicals. The study aims to formulate the Acorus calamus nano-emulsion and check for antioxidant properties. The main objective of the current study is to formulate the nano-emulsion of the Acorus calamus and check for the antioxidant properties by DPPH and ABTS assays. The nano-emulsion was prepared by mixing 10 mg of powder with an oil-in-water emulsion containing 10 mL of water, 60 mL of palm oil, and 30 mL of Tween 20. Further, the mixture was sonicated for 60 min, and the milky white formation indicates the emulsion formation. With the increase in the volume of the nanoemulsion of the Acorus calamus, the particle size distribution also increases to 250 nm when the volume reaches 100%, and then it gradually decreases to 450 nm. Acorus calamus nano-emulsion has antioxidant properties by inhibiting the action of free radicals. Nano-emulsion of the Acorus calamus has higher penetration when the size is less than 100 microns into the human epithelial cells. Therefore, it is more useful in the management of OPMDs when applied topically.

title: The energy module of FRIDA v2.1: endogenous investment and the timing of climate policy in the global energy system
summary: Abstract. Integrated assessment models that derive energy-transition pathways from cost optimization or prescribed scenarios often diverge from observed investment behaviour. Here we present the energy module of FRIDA v2.1, a feedback-based
content: Abstract. Integrated assessment models that derive energy-transition pathways from cost optimization or prescribed scenarios often diverge from observed investment behaviour. Here we present the energy module of FRIDA v2.1, a feedback-based, fully coupled global integrated assessment model built using System Dynamics, in which energy investment is endogenous. Total energy investment is set by a proportional–integral–derivative controller that responds to the relative mismatch between energy supply and demand, and is allocated across coal, oil, gas, solar, wind, hydropower, biofuel and nuclear technologies according to marginal costs that evolve with learning-by-doing, stepping-on-toes effects, resource scarcity, integration costs, climate damages and policy. Energy demand depends on population, GDP per person, energy prices, and climate-driven changes in heating and cooling degree days. Calibrated against 53 historical time series (1980–2023), the module reproduces observed trends in global energy supply, investment and emissions. Using 100 000-member ensembles, we compare endogenous model behaviour with four stylised policy scenarios that differ in the timing of carbon taxes and renewable subsidies. Without additional policy, warming exceeds 3 °C by 2100. All policy scenarios accelerate decarbonization, mainly through supply-side substitution rather than reduced demand, yet median warming remains above 2 °C; implementing both instruments early lowers end-of-century warming by roughly a third of a degree compared with delayed implementation. Abrupt policy introduction carries a substantial risk of persistent macroeconomic disruption, showing that successful decarbonization depends not only on policy strength but also on its timing and sequencing.

title: Beyond diesel: Multi‐objective optimization and multi‐criteria evaluation of hybrid multi‐energy systems for remote northern communities
summary: Abstract Remote northern communities in Canada rely heavily on diesel‐based electricity and heating, resulting in high energy costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and fuel‐supply vulnerabilities. This study develops an integrated techno‐economi
content: Abstract Remote northern communities in Canada rely heavily on diesel‐based electricity and heating, resulting in high energy costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and fuel‐supply vulnerabilities. This study develops an integrated techno‐economic framework for the design and evaluation of hybrid multi‐energy systems (HMES) comprising solar photovoltaic (PV), wind turbines, an organic Rankine cycle (ORC)‐based biomass‐fired combined heat and power (BCHP) unit, battery energy storage, and power converters. A multi‐objective optimization approach is employed to minimize the net present cost (NPC) and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), while TOPSIS‐SOMIT‐based multi‐criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is used to rank candidate system configurations. An off‐grid community in a remote northern region of Canada, with an average daily electricity demand of 8,536 kWh, was selected as the case study. The optimal HMES comprises a 450 kW ORC‐BCHP unit, 350 kW of PV capacity, 460 kW of wind capacity, and 2,200 kWh of battery storage, with an initial capital investment of C$13.5 million. The optimized system achieves an LCOE of C$0.458/kWh and an NPC of C$27.1 million. It generates 3,307 MWh of electricity annually, fully meeting community demand while eliminating 821,600 L/year of diesel consumption. Lifecycle CO 2 emissions decrease from 0.704 to 0.076 kg/kWh, representing an 89% reduction. TOPSIS‐SOMIT‐based MCDA ranks the proposed HMES as the preferred option among seven candidate systems. The results indicate that integrating dispatchable biomass cogeneration with wind, solar, and battery storage can provide a reliable, cost‐effective, and low‐carbon energy solution for remote northern communities.

title: Citric Acid Tunes the Surface Oxygen of Glucose-Derived Carbon Dots for Gram-Selective Bacterial Fluorescence Labeling
summary: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) are inexpensive, Water-dispersible fluorophores whose photoluminescence and interactions with biological surfaces are largely determined by their surface chemistry, which is most often tuned by doping the carbon c
content: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) are inexpensive, Water-dispersible fluorophores whose photoluminescence and interactions with biological surfaces are largely determined by their surface chemistry, which is most often tuned by doping the carbon core with heteroatoms. In the current study, we show that the surface of nitrogen-free, glucose-derived CDs can instead be engineered using citric acid alone. Four samples (G, GC1/0.1, GC1/1, and GC1/3) were prepared by a single 30 min microwave reaction in water, differing only in the glucose-to-citric-acid ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy showed that increasing the amount of citric acid raised the surface oxygen content from 32.6 to 53.3 at. % and enriched the carbonyl (C = O) and carboxyl (O–C = O) groups, whereas the amorphous carbon core and the particle size (3.5–3.7 nm) remained unchanged. This surface oxidation blue-shifted the excitation-dependent emission from 517 to 445 nm, raised the quantum yield from 13.5 to 16.4%, and made the surface more negatively charged (ζ potential from – 23.3 to – 26.1 mV). When applied to a panel of 12 bacteria, the optimized GC1/3 dots labeled all six Gram-positive species but left all six Gram-negative species unstained; brightfield images confirmed that intact cells were present in the unlabeled fields. Electron microscopy further revealed envelope-bound deposits on Bacillus subtilis only after CD treatment, and a CCK-8 assay defined a usable working concentration at or below 200 ppm. Together, these results establish a dopant-free, surface-oxygen strategy for a rapid (5 min) and reagent-simple fluorescence read-out of Gram type.

title: A Systems-Based Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Environmental Sustainability
summary: Environmental sustainability is a result of complex configurations of emissions, air pollution, and environmental infrastructure. This paper investigates environmental sustainability of 154 countries based on four environmental variables an
content: Environmental sustainability is a result of complex configurations of emissions, air pollution, and environmental infrastructure. This paper investigates environmental sustainability of 154 countries based on four environmental variables and the Natural Capital Protection (NCP) score. Principal component analysis (PCA), K-means clustering, prediction models, and explainable AI techniques, such as SHAP and LIME, in addition to network and persistent-homology analysis, are utilized as part of the methodology. Two principal components accounted for 74.70% of the total variance. Five environmental groups were identified to facilitate an interpretation of cross-country heterogeneity. PM2.5 turned out to be the most important model-assigned predictor of NCP, followed by methane and carbon emissions, while water access was the one with the lowest SHAP value on average. Network and persistent-homology analysis provided additional information about patterns of model attributions as well as about the relationships between environmental indicators.

title: Off-axis electron holography with nanosecond photoelectrons in a retrofitted transmission electron microscope
summary: The advancement of time-resolved off-axis electron holography (OAEH) in ultrafast transmission electron microscopy (UTEM) requires pulsed electron sources that simultaneously provide sufficient brightness and coherence for phase-sensitive m
content: The advancement of time-resolved off-axis electron holography (OAEH) in ultrafast transmission electron microscopy (UTEM) requires pulsed electron sources that simultaneously provide sufficient brightness and coherence for phase-sensitive measurements. Here, we demonstrate OAEH using 10 ns electron pulses generated from a Schottky-type field emission cathode in a retrofitted UTEM. We characterize the spectral broadening and transverse coherence of the pulsed photoelectrons and establish experimental protocols for acquiring phase-shifting photoelectron holograms. To address the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) inherent to pulsed photoelectron holography, we introduce a discrete weighted low-pass filter (DW-LPF) that improves hologram quality and enables reliable phase reconstruction. We validate this approach through phase-shifting OAEH of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) and iron nanowires(Fe NWs), demonstrating reduced charging-induced phase artefacts in the carbon nanotube specimen and quantitative visualization of nanoscale magnetic fields around the Fe NWs. These results establish a static proof-of-concept for nanosecond-pulsed OAEH and demonstrate its potential for quantitative electromagnetic-field measurements in charging-prone specimens.

title: Tracing the composition of soil organic matter from a collapsing permafrost peat plateau: Contrasting trajectories between mire and thermokarst pond
summary: Thawing of permafrost peat plateaus can mobilize previously stored organic carbon, potentially releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. Greenhouse gas emissions from degrading peat plateaus are controlled by several factors, among wh
content: Thawing of permafrost peat plateaus can mobilize previously stored organic carbon, potentially releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. Greenhouse gas emissions from degrading peat plateaus are controlled by several factors, among which the composition of soil organic matter (SOM) may play a crucial role. We investigated changes of SOM compositions of a degrading peat plateau along two thaw chronosequences in Finnmark, Northern Norway, describing the transition to a mire and a thermokarst pond. To characterize SOM compositions, we calculated elemental ratios and C oxidation states. A novel inverted mixing model was used to estimate relative changes of major biomolecular classes and resolve the δ 13 C signal. The results indicate that the SOM composition of the active layer and permafrost converge during the early thaw (≤ 3 years). This convergence is driven by the loss of oxidized moieties from the active layer, which have been formed through reoxidation of reduced moieties during the intact plateau period. During the mature thaw (> 3 years), the ratio of lignin-like to carbohydrate fractions was approximately 2:1 along the mire sequence, but 1:1 along the pond sequence. The overall results suggest that SOM composition exerts a stronger influence on C processing during the early thaw, whereas landscape-environmental conditions dominate during the later thaw. Moreover, lignin-like SOM fractions persist in the mire but are degraded through syntrophic processes in the thermokarst pond. The greater degradability of SOM in thermokarst ponds highlights their role as hotspots of C processing in thawing permafrost landscapes.

title: Can commodity chemical processes be electrified without merely shifting emissions upstream
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This revised article addresses Q0181, 'Can commodity chemical processes be electrified without merely shifting emissions upstream?' using a question-specific mathematical construction rather than a generic logarithmic template. The proposed
content: This revised article addresses Q0181, 'Can commodity chemical processes be electrified without merely shifting emissions upstream?' using a question-specific mathematical construction rather than a generic logarithmic template. The proposed model, termed the Electrified Commodity Lifecycle Carbon Model, uses electricity use E_el, grid carbon intensity CI_grid, direct process emissions, material-recycling credit and product output and is ordered along process route and grid scenario. The construction is anchored to external primary research classified as DIRECT SUPPORT in the validation atlas. The external evidence establishes experimentally measurable mechanisms or target performance; it is not conflated with proof of the new equation itself. The model defines explicit state variables, derives a dimensionless objective or hazard, specifies a prospective calibration procedure, and states falsifiable predictions. The experimental constraint carried forward from the atlas is: Commodity processes such as cement can be electrified; true emissions benefit depends on upstream electricity and feedstock process emissions. The article incorporates the required correction: Carbon intensity must be a hard lifecycle constraint.

title: EV Is Not as Green as Advertised: A Life-Cycle and Safety-Risk Evaluation
summary: Electric vehicles (EVs) are widely promoted as “zero emission” and safe, yet tailpipe emissions are only one stage of a vehicle’s life cycle. This paper critically evaluates the life-cycle and safety risks of EVs by synthesizing peer-review
content: Electric vehicles (EVs) are widely promoted as “zero emission” and safe, yet tailpipe emissions are only one stage of a vehicle’s life cycle. This paper critically evaluates the life-cycle and safety risks of EVs by synthesizing peer-reviewed life-cycle assessments, global electricity and emission data, and reported EV fire incidents. EVs reduce tailpipe emissions, but a large share of their carbon footprint arises in production, mainly in battery manufacturing and the mining of lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese. Net benefits depend on the electricity grid: they are clear in renewable-rich countries but weak or absent in fossil-dependent countries such as Bangladesh. Safety concerns include the lack of standardized battery safety ratings, thermal runaway, non-collision fires and low recycling rates. EVs are promising but not yet completely green or completely safe.

title: LCA Data Handover: Linking Product Carbon, Corporate Inventories and Water Context / LCA Veri Devir Notu
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: LCA data handover / LCA veri devri This original bilingual technical practice note explains how teams can retain source evidence, study boundaries and open questions when sharing activity records between life cycle assessment, product carbo
content: LCA data handover / LCA veri devri This original bilingual technical practice note explains how teams can retain source evidence, study boundaries and open questions when sharing activity records between life cycle assessment, product carbon, corporate GHG inventories and water assessment. It distinguishes a source document, an extracted record and a transformed value, with a hypothetical production scenario and an adaptable field dictionary. The package contains a readable PDF, an editable Markdown version and a blank CSV handover template. No measured emissions, default emission factors, research findings or conformity decisions are reported. The proposed fields and working roles are editorial recommendations, not a standardized schema. Bu özgün Türkçe ve İngilizce teknik not, faaliyet kayıtları LCA, ürün karbonu, kurumsal karbon ve su çalışmaları arasında paylaşılırken kaynak, kapsam ve açık soruların korunmasını ele alır. Varsayımsal üretim örneği, inceleme soruları ve uyarlanabilir alan sözlüğü içerir. Ek CSV yalnız başlıklardan oluşan boş bir çalışma şablonudur. Scope and sources / Kapsam ve kaynaklar Source discussions draw on the Life Cycle Initiative, GHG Protocol product and corporate resources, WULCA and the European Commission CBAM overview. Links are cited in the document. This is a technical practice note, not peer-reviewed research or a legal opinion. Publisher resources / Yayımcı kaynakları Dokumantum is the organizational author and commercial publisher of the note. Readers exploring software support can examine its LCA, product carbon footprint, corporate carbon, water footprint and SKDM / CBAM resources. These publisher links are not independent validation of the note. Version 1.0, 16 November 2026. Original text and blank template: CC BY 4.0. Referenced third-party sources retain their own rights. Prepared with AI-assisted drafting, source review and editorial structuring; no independent peer or subject-matter expert endorsement is claimed.

title: Pathways for high-quality development of marine ranching in the Beibu Gulf urban agglomeration
summary: The transition of marine ranching from scale-oriented expansion toward high-quality development requires the simultaneous improvement of production efficiency, ecological sustainability, and farmed-animal welfare. However, increasing stocki
content: The transition of marine ranching from scale-oriented expansion toward high-quality development requires the simultaneous improvement of production efficiency, ecological sustainability, and farmed-animal welfare. However, increasing stocking intensity and technological investment may generate trade-offs among economic output, ecological carrying capacity, animal health, and long-term production sustainability. Existing studies have mainly examined ecological efficiency, resource and environmental carrying capacity, technological innovation, and industrial performance, while farmed aquatic animal welfare and its systemic interactions with ecological and socioeconomic outcomes remain insufficiently addressed. To fill this gap, this study introduces the One Welfare framework and constructs a One Welfare High-Quality Development Index (OWHI) integrating animal welfare, ecological environment, and economic and social development. Based on marine-ranching policy texts and development practices in the Beibu Gulf urban agglomeration, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) is employed to identify configurations associated with high-quality development, while System Dynamics (SD) is used to examine feedback mechanisms and the long-term effects of alternative policy combinations. The results reveal substantial conjunctural causation and equifinality, with no single condition constituting a necessary condition for high OWHI. Three major pathways are identified: technology-policy driven, ecology-market synergistic, and welfare-environment synergistic configurations. Smart technological empowerment and animal welfare management play important cross-path roles. Scenario simulations further show that isolated welfare, technological, or ecological interventions generate limited long-term improvements, whereas the coordinated integration of welfare standards, AI-enabled monitoring, IMTA, and cross-regional governance produces stronger and more persistent synergistic effects. These findings extend conventional ecological-economic-social assessments of marine ranching by explicitly incorporating animal welfare and provide a configurational and dynamic basis for improving marine ranching sustainability.

title: Microalgal Proteins as Food Ingredients: Technological Advances and Remaining Challenges
summary: With rising global food demand, the high resource use of traditional agriculture, and increasing greenhouse gas emissions, alternative proteins are essential for future food security and sustainability. Microalgal protein, with its high pro
content: With rising global food demand, the high resource use of traditional agriculture, and increasing greenhouse gas emissions, alternative proteins are essential for future food security and sustainability. Microalgal protein, with its high protein content, balanced amino acids, efficient carbon fixation, and ability to grow without arable land or freshwater, is a promising sustainable protein source. This paper reviews advances in microalgal protein, including its nutrition and health benefits, large-scale cultivation, harvesting and extraction, and food applications. It also summarizes safety and regulatory issues such as contaminants, toxins, allergenicity, and global regulations, and evaluates environmental benefits in terms of carbon reduction, wastewater use, and resource efficiency. To address current challenges—such as difficult cell disruption, high processing costs, poor flavor and color acceptance, and complex approval processes—strategies like genetic engineering, secretory expression, efficient purification, and flavor improvement are proposed, along with future research and industrialization directions. Compared with previous reviews focusing on individual aspects of microalgal proteins, this review integrates the entire value chain from biomass production to food applications, safety assessment, and sustainability evaluation.

title: Does Conditional Covariance Outperform Empirical Covariance? A Study of Portfolio Optimization Techniques
source: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
summary: This study analyses two academically utilised approaches of dynamic conditional correlation GARCH (DCC-GARCH) and historical/empirical covariance for covariance matrix estimation and their impact on portfolio optimization is studied during
content: This study analyses two academically utilised approaches of dynamic conditional correlation GARCH (DCC-GARCH) and historical/empirical covariance for covariance matrix estimation and their impact on portfolio optimization is studied during crisis periods. The researchers have collected data for a period of 9 months (i.e. the crisis period) of a multi-asset portfolio that is diversified across countries. This paper also compares different optimisation techniques to not only have a more robust comparison between results from the estimation of covariance matrix, but also to study which optimisation technique benefits the most from the change in covariance matrix estimation method and performs the best during the studied crisis period. It evaluates four strategies: mean-variance optimization (MVO), cluster risk parity (CRP), naïve risk parity (NRP), and equal weighting. The results indicate that DCC-GARCH based covariance matrix estimation provides a much better result for portfolio optimisation during the crisis period studied, and that max Sharpe portfolio optimisation technique benefits the most from said estimation method while CRP and NRP witness no benefit from the same. These results add to the existing literature showing the outperformance of DCC-GARCH in covariance estimation and highlights an additional nuance of variance in results based on which optimisation technique is used.

title: A Property Rights Critique of Indonesia’s Extended Producer Responsibility Framework
summary: Indonesia continues to struggle with the collection, disposal, and recovery of pack- aging waste. To deal with this, Regulation No. P.75/2019 was introduced, which re- quired producers to develop roadmaps with the aim of reducing packaging
content: Indonesia continues to struggle with the collection, disposal, and recovery of pack- aging waste. To deal with this, Regulation No. P.75/2019 was introduced, which re- quired producers to develop roadmaps with the aim of reducing packaging waste by 30% by 2029. This paper asks whether the regulation actually assigns responsibility in a way that is likely to lead to better waste outcomes. Drawing on Rothbard (1982) and Cordato (2004), it asks whether producers should be held responsible for the harms caused by other actors and whether that position is consistent with a particular theory of environmental responsibility. It also examines the gap between producers' formal responsibilities and the actual control exercised by local governments, house- holds, and the informal waste sector over waste collection and disposal. A documen- tary analysis of the regulation, national statistics, and the World Bank's assessment of the seven ASEAN Member States provides evidence of this gap but cannot show that the allocation of responsibility caused the observed outcomes. The paper suggests a complementary framework that would impose enforceable duties on waste operators, support locally governed collection systems, and formally include the informal sector, while maintaining appropriate producer obligations related to packaging design.

title: From forest edges to disciplinary boundaries: ecological patterns and structural analogy
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Introduction Ecological boundaries separate habitats, whereas disciplinary boundaries can separate ways of understanding them. Whether empirical ecological patterns can provide a basis for structural analogy across disciplinary boundaries r
content: Introduction Ecological boundaries separate habitats, whereas disciplinary boundaries can separate ways of understanding them. Whether empirical ecological patterns can provide a basis for structural analogy across disciplinary boundaries remains poorly understood. Methods We investigated soil physicochemical properties, microbial communities, enzyme activities, and soil fauna along edge-to-interior gradients at six forest sites spanning an urbanization gradient in Xiamen, China. In parallel, 150 participants from non-ecological professional backgrounds participated in structured field engagement. Cross-disciplinary analogies were assessed through open-ended responses, and their structural depth was evaluated using ordinal logistic regression. Results Microbial diversity, biomass, enzyme activities, and soil-faunal abundance generally increased from the urban core toward near-natural forests, whereas Proteobacteria relative abundance and bacterivorous nematode proportion declined. Ectomycorrhizal fungal relative abundance increased 7.74-fold across the urbanization gradient. Edge-to-interior contrasts were predominantly negative, although Proteobacteria exhibited significant edge enrichment (mean Edge Effect Index [EEI] = +0.191, p = 0.031), whereas available phosphorus showed a positive but non-significant mean EEI = +0.144, p = 0.062). Nematode community maturity showed an exploratory positive association between EEI and urbanization intensity (Spearman ρ = 0.829, n = 6). Following field engagement, 108 participants (72.0%) generated cross-disciplinary analogies, including 81 (54.0%) demonstrating intermediate or deep structural mapping. Longer observation duration was associated with greater analogy depth (odds ratio = 1.54 per 10-min increment, 95% confidence interval: 1.12–2.12; p = 0.007), whereas prior ecological knowledge and professional background showed no statistically detectable associations with depth. Discussion These findings reveal heterogeneous belowground ecological responses to urbanization and forest edges while demonstrating how measured ecological gradients can serve as a reference for cross-disciplinary structural reasoning. The observational design limits causal interpretation, but provides a basis for further investigation of ecological field engagement as a context for interdisciplinary understanding.

title: Priority gaps and governance mismatch in Andalusian olive and almond farming communities
summary: Introduction Participatory sustainability assessments can reveal what farming communities value, but they rarely diagnose where those values are most acutely deteriorating or explain the structural forces behind such dynamics. In this study
content: Introduction Participatory sustainability assessments can reveal what farming communities value, but they rarely diagnose where those values are most acutely deteriorating or explain the structural forces behind such dynamics. In this study, we fill this gap by characterising the sustainability criteria of two Andalusian farming communities, ranked by importance and rated for their perceived trajectory (improving or deteriorating). We also recorded perceived causal influences on the trajectory of these criteria (actors and environmental or structural forces). From this, we identify “priority gaps,” i.e., criteria of high importance with a deteriorating perceived trajectory, as a basis for analysing causal mechanisms and governance responses. Methods The research is based on a three-week Photovoice process with 34 olive and almond farmers across two contrasting Andalusian regions. We analysed 57 farmer-defined criteria and 1,273 observations of causal influences. Results Four criteria were priority gaps in both regions. On three of them, generational succession, fair prices and agricultural policy, no group saw an improvement, pointing to structural failures that transcend local conditions and map onto unresolved challenges of the Common Agricultural Policy. Water protection, the fourth, divided the groups. Lock-in mapping revealed a governance mismatch. Taken together, negative influences on gap criteria concentrated at national-supranational and landscape-structural levels, while positive influences were most frequent at farm-household and community-cooperative levels. Adequate profitability was the single most important criterion in the intensive lowland site yet did not emerge at all in the diversified mountain site, suggesting that the two communities inhabit different lifeworld configurations. The men’s groups ranked generational succession, knowledge transmission, effort and dedication, and fair prices higher than the women’s groups did. The women’s groups ranked water protection and several criteria of care, health and recognition higher, and on average rated the perceived trajectory of fair prices lower, as the lowland women’s group did for profitability. Discussion The study shows that both priority-gap and lock-in mapping based on a participatory assessment can produce diagnostic evidence that aligns with accounts in the literature and thus offer a starting point for identifying areas for intervention, particularly in food-system governance, to address mismatches between governance levels.

title: Anthropogenic Carbon in the Overturning: Annual Ocean Sink, Cumulative Inventory and Basin Storage Budget
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The ocean currently removes about 2.9 petagrams of anthropogenic carbon per year from the atmosphere, roughly a quarter of fossil and land-use emissions, and has accumulated an inventory near 170 petagrams since preindustrial times, stored
content: The ocean currently removes about 2.9 petagrams of anthropogenic carbon per year from the atmosphere, roughly a quarter of fossil and land-use emissions, and has accumulated an inventory near 170 petagrams since preindustrial times, stored disproportionately in the Atlantic, whose deep-water formation carries surface carbon efficiently into the interior, and in the Southern Ocean, where uptake and subduction are strongest. The budget expresses the adopted sink as a fraction of stated total emissions, converts the cumulative inventory into an equivalent atmospheric concentration change, partitions storage among Atlantic, Pacific, Indian and Southern Ocean shares, and computes the mean interior concentration increase and the residence implied by dividing inventory by sink strength. Headline values are carbonup annual sink pg c carbonup = 2.9; carbonup total emissions pg c carbonup = 11; carbonup sink fraction of emissions carbonup = 0.2636; carbonup sink percent carbonup = 26.36; carbonup cumulative inventory pg c carbonup = 170; carbonup inventory atmospheric equiv ppm carbonup = 80.04. The Atlantic storage entry is the one to carry forward, because it ties the carbon budget directly to the deep-water formation rates budgeted elsewhere in this set of calculations.

content: EU CBAM data request handover / SKDM veri talebi devri This original bilingual technical practice note proposes a traceable handover from a buyer request to production evidence, with explicit boundaries, source versions, review notes and unresolved questions. It explains how to preserve the original request, map each response field to evidence, distinguish missing quantities from zero and record transformations without silently validating them. The package includes a PDF, editable Markdown and a blank CSV request-to-evidence register with a bilingual field dictionary. The template is not an official CBAM submission file. No measured emissions, research findings, legal obligations, classification decisions or conformity determinations are reported. title: Large Igneous Province Degassing: Carbon Dioxide and Sulphur Budgets for Steady and Pulsed Eruption of the Deccan and Siberian Traps
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Flood basalts change climate through their gases, not their lava, and the climatic dose depends on whether volatile inventories are averaged over a million years or delivered in the pulses in which the magma actually erupted. Magma mass fro
content: Flood basalts change climate through their gases, not their lava, and the climatic dose depends on whether volatile inventories are averaged over a million years or delivered in the pulses in which the magma actually erupted. Magma mass from volume and density, multiplied by stated volatile weight fractions, gives total carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide inventories for each province; dividing by duration gives mean emission rates, while assigning a thousand-cubic-kilometre flow field to a decade gives the pulsed rate that atmospheres actually experienced, expressed in units of a modern large explosive eruption. Headline values are volc deccan magma mass kg volc = 3.77e+18; volc deccan co2 gigatonnes volc = 9425; volc deccan so2 gigatonnes volc = 9048; volc deccan co2 mean gt per year volc = 0.01428; volc deccan so2 mean gt per year volc = 0.01371; volc siberian magma mass kg volc = 1.254e+19. Mean and pulsed rates are printed side by side because quoting either alone has historically misled the extinction debate in opposite directions.

title: Agroforestry boosts soil multifunctionality in the Yellow River’s desertified region by reshaping abundant microbes and co-occurrence networks
summary: Introduction The desertified area of the Yellow River's original course represents a typical ecologically fragile zone, where the improvement of ecosystem functions and services remains a challenging task. Agroforestry systems are considere
content: Introduction The desertified area of the Yellow River's original course represents a typical ecologically fragile zone, where the improvement of ecosystem functions and services remains a challenging task. Agroforestry systems are considered an important ecological restoration strategy in this region; however, their effects on soil ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) and the underlying microbial mech-anisms remain poorly understood. Methods In this study, eight years after establishment, three typical Gleditsia sinensis-dominated agroforestry systems (i.e., G. sinensis -Lonicera japonica (JYH), G. sinensis - Hemerocallis citrina (HHC), and G. sinensis -Forsythia suspensa (LQ), a pure G. sinensis plantation (ZJ), and bare land (CK) were investigated in the desertified region of the Yellow River's original course. The diversity patterns and co-occurrence networks of rare and abundant bacterial taxa were analyzed, and their contributions to EMF were evaluated. Results The results showed that, compared with CK, both the ZJ and three agroforestry systems significantly enhanced the a-diversity of abundant bacterial taxa. In contrast, the Chao1 index and richness of rare bacterial taxa were highest in the CK. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed that the abundant bacterial taxa under the LQ exhibited the greatest network complexity. Meanwhile, ZJ and the three agroforestry systems significantly improved EMF. Correlation analysis further indicated that abundant bacterial taxa were positively correlated with EMF, while rare taxa showed a negative correlation. Moreover, Partial Least Squares Path Modeling (PLS-PM) revealed that different G. sinensis-dominated agrofor-estry systems regulated EMF by shaping the diversity and co-occurrence network structure of abundant bacterial taxa. Discussion Overall, this study highlights the ecological benefits of agroforestry systems in the restoration of desertified areas and reveals the microbial mechanisms underlying improvements in EMF, thereby providing a theoretical basis for ecological restoration.

title: Advanced Combustion and Emission Phenomenological Modeling of a Dual-Fuel Marine Engine Supplied with Natural Gas
summary: This study investigates natural gas/light fuel oil (LFO) combustion in a large-bore marine research engine, with port-injected natural gas and directly injected LFO. Experiments investigate load, intake pressure, injection timing and durati
content: This study investigates natural gas/light fuel oil (LFO) combustion in a large-bore marine research engine, with port-injected natural gas and directly injected LFO. Experiments investigate load, intake pressure, injection timing and duration, and rail pressure variations. A developed multi-zone phenomenological model combines chemical kinetics with flame propagation and advanced spray/evaporation models. Early injections are captured, producing in-cylinder reactivity stratification and enabling RCCI combustion mode, whereas later injections act as localized ignition kernels that trigger flame propagation. A blending rule switches flame geometry from conical flame fronts typical of late injections to spherical geometries typical of early injections, according to ignition location. The framework also incorporates pollutant emissions models. Simulations match measurements with 10% average error in performance and 5 CAD for main combustion events. The model clarifies how LFO timing and fraction govern combustion and emissions, supporting engine design and optimization for low-carbon fuels and guides calibration strategies.

title: Effects of warming and increased precipitation on soil heterotrophic respiration and its temperature sensitivity in the desert steppe
summary: Abstract Background Feedback between climate change and soil carbon emissions plays an important role in the grassland carbon cycle. However, the response mechanism of soil heterotrophic respiration (Rh) and its temperature sensitivity (Q 1
content: Abstract Background Feedback between climate change and soil carbon emissions plays an important role in the grassland carbon cycle. However, the response mechanism of soil heterotrophic respiration (Rh) and its temperature sensitivity (Q 10 ) to long-term warming, increased precipitation and their interaction in the desert steppe remain unclear, and the effects of monitoring frequency on Rh and Q 10 remain unquantified. Methods After eight years of warming (ambient temperature, T0; warming 2 ℃, T1; warming 4 ℃, T2) and increased precipitation (natural precipitation, W0; precipitation enhancement 25%, W1; precipitation enhancement 50%, W2), soil samples were collected and physical and chemical properties, Rh and Q 10 were monitored. Results Warming significantly increased soil water content, and the interaction between warming and precipitation also significantly affected soil water content. The response of Rh and Q 10 to warming and precipitation showed clear frequency dependence. Specifically, warming significantly reduced high and low frequency Rh. For Q 10 , except for T2, warming and precipitation increased significantly reduced high-frequency Q 10 , while warming and precipitation increase and their interaction reduced low frequency Q 10 . Compared with low-frequency monitoring, high-frequency monitoring resulted in lower Rh and higher Q 10 . Rh in the desert steppe is mainly regulated by SOC, and Q 10 is mainly regulated by soil bulk density. Conclusions High-frequency monitoring is more conducive to accurate assessment of changes in Rh and Q 10 in desert steppe. SOC and soil bulk density are the dominant factors affecting Rh and Q 10 in the desert steppe under future climate change.

title: Multi-criteria optimization of energy retrofit strategies for historical buildings
summary: Energy efficiency interventions can yield environmental and economic benefits; however, they may also cause irreversible impacts on the authenticity and cultural values of historic buildings. This study develops a multi-criteria assessment
content: Energy efficiency interventions can yield environmental and economic benefits; however, they may also cause irreversible impacts on the authenticity and cultural values of historic buildings. This study develops a multi-criteria assessment method to comprehensively evaluate the effects of energy performance improvements on historical values. Parameters related to heritage value were first defined, and the impacts of proposed energy retrofit scenarios were assessed in terms of energy consumption, carbon emissions, and thermal comfort. The method was applied to four retrofit scenarios for the historic Diyarbakır train station. The findings reveal clear differences between energy-driven and conservation-oriented interventions, demonstrating how historical values are affected during efficiency improvements. Ultimately, the proposed approach enables the simultaneous and quantitative evaluation of sustainability and heritage values in decision-making processes.

title: Assessing the Influence of Ocean Acidification on Calcification Patterns in Non-Coral Marine Invertebrates
summary: Ocean acidification, which consists in the changes in carbonate chemistry of the seawater and in the reduction of calcium carbonate availability, is defined as one of the major challenges facing marine species nowadays. Although the topic o
content: Ocean acidification, which consists in the changes in carbonate chemistry of the seawater and in the reduction of calcium carbonate availability, is defined as one of the major challenges facing marine species nowadays. Although the topic of coral calcification received a lot of attention from scientists, it is necessary to conduct the comparative study of how other non-coral marine invertebrates, such as molluscs, echinoderms, crustaceans and bryozoans, respond to the changes in the chemical composition of the seawater. This necessity is associated with the increase in the quantity of the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and potential consequences for marine biodiversity and the process of the shell and skeleton development in marine organisms. The distinctive feature of the proposed research is the attempt to find the approach to establish the correlation between the seawater carbonate parameters and the species-specific patterns of calcification and organism reactions to it. It implies laboratory exposures, assessment of the physicochemical parameters of seawater, shell and skeletal assessment and comparative biological analysis. The research is focused on the difference in the calcification process in various conditions of acidification. The results expected from this research are to understand better the impact of ocean acidification on the formation and structure of calcium carbonate in marine invertebrates that do not include coral reefs. This research shall bring out the significance of marine invertebrates that are not corals in maintaining the stability of the marine ecosystem. The changes in the organism growth rate, formation of the skeleton, and physiological tolerances due to the changes in the carbonates shall be emphasized. Such information could assist in determining which organisms are more susceptible and resistant to acidification. In addition, the research results shall form an important scientific base for the future monitoring programs for marine ecosystems.

title: Impact Investing in Agribusiness: Financial Returns, Food Security and Sustainability Trade-offs
source: Asian Journal of Agricultural Extension Economics & Sociology
summary: Impact investing has become an influential proposition for financing agribusinesses expected to generate both commercial returns and measurable social or environmental benefits. Yet investment intent, enterprise growth and development impac
content: Impact investing has become an influential proposition for financing agribusinesses expected to generate both commercial returns and measurable social or environmental benefits. Yet investment intent, enterprise growth and development impact remain analytically distinct. This critical narrative review examines whether and under what conditions agribusiness impact investment can reconcile financial viability with food security, nutrition, ecological sustainability and distributive justice. Literature published from 2011 to 4 September 2026 was examined through accessible scholarly sources, citation tracing and institutional evidence. The synthesis deliberately distinguishes studies of impact funds from adjacent research on agricultural credit, value-chain finance, land transactions, climate finance and food-system interventions. The evidence suggests that viable agricultural enterprises may address important financing gaps, but the literature does not establish a general triple dividend. Findings on risk-adjusted investor returns are mixed and largely derive from multi-sector portfolios; farm-level gains cannot automatically be interpreted as improvements in diets or household food security. Sustainability claims are similarly contingent on land governance, labour conditions, ecosystem boundaries and credible comparison scenarios. Blended finance and contractual safeguards may improve investability and accountability, although their additionality and opportunity costs require stronger evaluation. The review develops a decision framework linking financial additionality, enterprise behaviour, household welfare, environmental change and distributional effects, with explicit attention to counterfactuals and time horizons. It concludes that impact investment should be evaluated as a conditional, governance-dependent intervention rather than as a financing category that intrinsically delivers social and environmental outcomes. More informative research requires comparable fund-level financial reporting, longitudinal household and ecological indicators, credible causal designs and independent verification of investor contribution.

title: CARBON TAXATION IN NIGERIA: PROSPECTS AND CHALLENGES
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This study examines carbon taxation in Nigeria, with a specific focus on its prospects and challenges as a climate policy instrument. Given Nigeria's heavy reliance on fossil fuels and the increasing pressure to meet global climate commitme
content: This study examines carbon taxation in Nigeria, with a specific focus on its prospects and challenges as a climate policy instrument. Given Nigeria's heavy reliance on fossil fuels and the increasing pressure to meet global climate commitments under the Paris Agreement, fiscal tools that can drive emission reductions are urgently needed. This study adopted a library-based research approach, drawing evidence from peer-reviewed journals, government reports, policy documents, and past empirical studies to synthesize critical insights that contribute to the body of knowledge on environmental taxation in developing economies. The review revealed that fiscal and taxation policies are crucial levers for encouraging green growth, reducing pollution, and driving the transition to a low-carbon economy. In particular, carbon taxation can internalize environmental costs, discourage carbon-intensive production and consumption, and generate revenue that can be reinvested in renewable energy and social protection programs. However, the primary challenge lies in designing policy objectives and instruments to minimize social costs, avoid regressive impacts on low-income households, and ensure equitable tax burden distribution. The study concludes that for environmental taxes to be successfully designed and implemented in Nigeria, the policy framework must be examined methodically. This requires stakeholder engagement, transparent revenue use, and alignment with broader economic and energy policies. The findings have implications for policymakers seeking to balance environmental sustainability with economic growth and social equity.

title: Incorporating Demand Variables via Input Space Compression for STLF: An Assessment on the Spanish Grid
summary: Because power grids require real-time generation-load balance, enhancing Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF) accuracy prevents frequency instability, optimizes unit commitment, and reduces carbon-intensive spinning reserve dispatch, thereby
content: Because power grids require real-time generation-load balance, enhancing Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF) accuracy prevents frequency instability, optimizes unit commitment, and reduces carbon-intensive spinning reserve dispatch, thereby facilitating intermittent renewable energy integration. This study evaluates seven dimensionality reduction techniques (PCA, KPCA, UMAP, RF, XGBoost, AE, and VAE) integrated offline into the Spanish Transmission System Operator’s forecasting architecture. A 169-variable historical demand dataset is incorporated and compressed to feed three modeling paradigms: a linear autoregressive model, an ensemble of 10 nonlinear autoregressive neural networks, and their dynamically weighted hybrid combination. Results show that incorporating these new variables lowers the baseline Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (NRMSE) from 2.38% to 2.17%. Ultimately, compressing the input space to 20–21 variables achieves a 2.16% NRMSE, matching the full variable set. Scaling this accuracy gain to the Spanish grid’s mean load lowers the thermal backup requirement by roughly 198 MW, equivalent to a standard open-cycle gas turbine unit, reducing operational costs and carbon emissions. Finally, dimensionality reduction halves linear model training time while maintaining millisecond inference latency.

title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Specimen Geometry Effects on Temperature Homogeneity of Advanced High-Strength Steels by Direct Electrical Heating
summary: Abstract All kinds of matter are built up from elements in different compositions under physical laws. Thermal processes produce complex compositions, such as metal alloys. The quality of these processes heavily affects precise thermal cond
content: Abstract All kinds of matter are built up from elements in different compositions under physical laws. Thermal processes produce complex compositions, such as metal alloys. The quality of these processes heavily affects precise thermal conditions. Therefore, a homogeneity study of the temperature field on the surface of metal sheets under Direct Electrical Heating (DEH) was performed. The study was focused on measurements by infrared cameras and temperature field analyses. The most frequent steel, 22MnB (Svoboda et al. 2019), was used to prove the simulations. Suggestions for actions to optimize and enlarge homogeneous heating areas are raised up. The steel 22MnB5 is often used in the automotive industry for hot-stamping processes that require high strength, toughness, and durability, such as in structural components. The homogeneity of direct heating temperature depends on the type of heating (AC or DC), the shapes, positions, and dimensions of the electrodes. The relationships and balance among these parameters, as well as the optimum homogeneity, depend on cost, complexity, and technical capabilities. Using simulations, we optimized trench parameters in the samples and compared the results with real measurements.

title: Perceived Barriers to Adoption of Building-Integrated Photovoltaics in the Sustainable Renovation of Buildings: An Exploratory Configurational Analysis of Stakeholders and LLM-Generated Personas in Northern Portugal
summary: Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) can combine the renovation of the building envelope with on-site electricity generation, contributing to the sustainable renovation of buildings (reduction in carbon emissions and increased energy ef
content: Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) can combine the renovation of the building envelope with on-site electricity generation, contributing to the sustainable renovation of buildings (reduction in carbon emissions and increased energy efficiency). Yet their uptake in existing buildings remains limited. This exploratory study examines how 16 property owners, architects and engineers in Northern Portugal, recruited through a purposive convenience sample, perceive fourteen barriers to BIPV adoption, grouped into economic, knowledge, technological and supply-chain categories, and how those perceptions relate to two single-item outcomes: the view that the benefits of BIPV outweigh its additional costs (perception) and the view that BIPV should play an important role in the energy renovation of the existing stock (perspective).
