Linguistic Likert answers were represented as triangular fuzzy numbers (TFNs), converted into crisp scores with the CFCS technique, and analysed descriptively and with fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), accompanied by sensitivity analyses of calibration and thresholds. Sixteen persona-conditioned synthetic respondents, built from the participants’ profiles and generated five times under two prompts, were processed in the same way. Barriers were perceived as at least moderately important, and the lack of information and technical guidance ranked first. Respondents were more favourable towards the future role of BIPV (CFCS = 0.719) than towards its current benefit–cost balance (0.544). In the fsQCA, technological barriers were present in all configurations, leading to the absence of a positive perspective, but detailed configurations were sensitive to calibration choices and are interpreted cautiously. The synthetic samples reproduced the average outcome scores but compressed variance, rated technological barriers lower, depended strongly on the context given in the prompt for incentive-related items and showed no individual-level correspondence with the humans on whose profiles they were based. LLM personas may therefore complement, but not replace, human respondents.

title: Ampicillin and Nanoscale Zero-Valent Iron Nanoparticles Differentially Modulate Extracellular Polymeric Substance Fractions and Cellular Metabolism in a Model Cyanobacterium
summary: Abstract Cyanobacteria respond to environmental stress through coordinated metabolic and extracellular adaptations, yet the relationship between intracellular metabolism and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) remodeling remains poorly
content: Abstract Cyanobacteria respond to environmental stress through coordinated metabolic and extracellular adaptations, yet the relationship between intracellular metabolism and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) remodeling remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of optimal ampicillin and nanoscale zero-valent iron nanoparticles (nZVIs) applied individually or in combination on cellular metabolism and EPS fractionation in the model cyanobacterium Fremyella diplosiphon cultivated under scale-up bioreactor conditions. Ampicillin enhanced chlorophyll a and phycocyanin autofluorescence, ATP luminescence , and lactate accumulation, indicating increased metabolic activity under antibiotic stress. In contrast, nZVI treatment produced the highest ATP levels without a corresponding increase in lactate, suggesting a shift in cellular energy metabolism. The combined treatment produced intermediate ATP levels, while lactate remained comparable to the control. In addition, distinct treatment-specific effects were observed in volumetric EPS accumulation (mg/L). Ampicillin resulted in the highest LB-EPS accumulation, whereas all treatments significantly increased TB-EPS accumulation relative to the control, with no significant differences among the treated groups. The combined treatment resulted in the highest S-EPS accumulation. Soluble EPS protein levels were higher under individual ampicillin and nZVI treatments than the combined treatment , while tightly bound EPS protein was highest in the combined treatment, demonstrating differential extracellular matrix remodeling. Our findings reveal that antibiotic and nanoparticle stressors differentially regulate intracellular metabolism and volumetric EPS accumulation during large-scale cultivation, highlighting coordinated adaptive mechanisms that contribute to cyanobacterial resilience. This integrated adaptive response provides new insights into stress-induced physiological plasticity in cyanobacteria and offers a foundation for optimizing nanoparticle–antibiotic interactions in scalable biotechnological applications.

title: Are Supply Chain Relationships Characterised by Similar Carbon Policies? An Exploratory Study Using Social Network Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT The carbon footprint from manufacturing companies' supply chains presents significant opportunities for climate change mitigation. Supply chain emissions management is gaining increasing importance in the EU, where regulations targ
content: ABSTRACT The carbon footprint from manufacturing companies' supply chains presents significant opportunities for climate change mitigation. Supply chain emissions management is gaining increasing importance in the EU, where regulations target both firms' direct and supply chain impacts. Yet the consistency of carbon regulatory requirements across supply chains and their effects on business relationships remain unclear. This study uses empirical data to explore the association of similar national carbon regulations with the likelihood of observing a tie between two companies in undirected buyer–supplier networks. Using an exponential random graph model (ERGM) on 6027 firms and 11,483 edges, we assess whether companies under similar regulatory conditions are more likely to form undirected buyer–supplier ties. Results indicate that national carbon regulation simultaneously is associated with clustering among regulated firms and cross‐regulatory ties that can enable spillovers. Unregulated firms show weaker clustering, suggesting that even when national regulation is absent, firms remain indirectly exposed to decarbonisation requirements through their connections to regulated partners. Our findings advance sustainable supply chain management by demonstrating how regulatory homophily creates the network conditions through which coercive pressures originating from national carbon regulation may extend indirectly across international supply networks.

title: CaMPground: A simple soil temperature model for integrating permafrost dynamics into large-scale peatland carbon models
summary: Abstract. Permafrost-affected peatlands represent 34 Mha or 31 % of Canada’s peatlands. Estimations of carbon (C) emissions and removals from Canadian peatlands are incomplete without knowing the contributions from these permafrost-affected
content: Abstract. Permafrost-affected peatlands represent 34 Mha or 31 % of Canada’s peatlands. Estimations of carbon (C) emissions and removals from Canadian peatlands are incomplete without knowing the contributions from these permafrost-affected areas. Currently, the Canadian Model for Peatlands (CaMP) does not account for permafrost as it cannot simulate active layer thickness (ALT) to determine the proportion of thawed versus frozen peat. Additionally, although the numerical Northern Ecosystem Soil Temperature (NEST) model predicts temperature and ALT accurately in the Hudson Bay Lowlands (HBL), it is too computationally intensive to be fully integrated within CaMP. Therefore, to integrated permafrost dynamics into CaMP and for carbon peatland models overall, we calibrated a simple sinusoidal model, known as CaMPground, which can estimate ground temperature at multiple depths on annual to sub-annual timescales. The model was validated for four peatland classes based on nutrient type and permafrost (bog, fen, permafrost fen, and permafrost bog) within the HBL. The model was tested for permafrost and non permafrost sites as the initial step in developing a vertically resolved version of CaMP, tracking carbon movement between soil layers. The model performed well for both permafrost and non permafrost classes, producing the lowest root mean square error (RMSE) for fens and permafrost fens monthly (1.8 and 1.6 °C, respectively). However, the model produced the highest error for permafrost bogs monthly (2.3 °C) likely due to the lack of freeze/thaw dynamics, leading to increased error at sites with a substantial zero-curtain effect. Despite this limitation, the errors for CaMPground were comparable to NEST (RMSE of 2.1 and 2.6 °C, respectively). Ground temperatures generated by the model will be used to determine annual ALT within a modified version of CaMP to simulate carbon dynamics in Canadian permafrost peatlands, improving carbon emission estimates in Canada.

title: Discovery of Substituted 1,2,3-Triazolyl-Benzoylacetamides as Potent MMP-9 Inhibitors with Anti-Angiogenic Activity in MDA-MB-231 TripleNegative Breast Cancer
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) contributes to extracellular matrix remodeling, tumor invasion, and angiogenesis, making it an attractive therapeutic target for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The present study aimed to develop non
content: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) contributes to extracellular matrix remodeling, tumor invasion, and angiogenesis, making it an attractive therapeutic target for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The present study aimed to develop non-hydroxamate MMP-9 inhibitors based on a substituted 1,2,3-triazolyl-benzoylacetamide scaffold and evaluate their antiproliferative and anti-angiogenic potentials. An energy-based, structure-guided pharmacophore approach was employed to define the key recognition features of the MMP-9 catalytic domain, including the catalytic Zn²⁺ environment and S1′ specificity pocket. A focused series of 13 derivatives (8a–8m) was subsequently designed through systematic modification of the benzoyl R¹ and terminal phenoxy R² regions, synthesized through a multistep route, and structurally characterized using spectroscopic and mass-spectrometric methods. The synthesized compounds exhibited concentrationdependent MMP-9 inhibition and antiproliferative activity against MDA-MB-231 cells, with the SAR analysis demonstrating a strong dependence on the combined steric, electronic, and lipophilic characteristics of R¹ and R². Compound 8h emerged as the principal lead, whereas 8e and 8l also displayed favorable biochemical and cellular activity profiles. Morphological evaluation further supported the cellular effects of these active derivatives. Functional antiangiogenic assessment demonstrated that 8h concentration-dependently suppressed VEGF-induced HUVEC migration and disrupted capillary-like tube formation, approaching the activity of the reference anti-angiogenic agent at higher tested concentrations. Collectively, these findings identify substituted 1,2,3-triazolyl-benzoylacetamides as a promising nonhydroxamate chemotype for MMP-9-directed anti-angiogenic drug discovery and establish 8h as a lead candidate for further mechanistic, selectivity, pharmacokinetic, and in vivo evaluations.

title: Optimizing CO2-Enhanced Oil Recovery (CO2-EOR) and CO2-Enhanced Gas Recovery (CO2-EGR) while Co-Optimizing Permanent Storage Volumes
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: The dual global imperatives of accelerating energy demand and enforcing stringent carbon emissions reductions have elevated Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) to the forefront of petroleum and environmental engineering. Among v
content: The dual global imperatives of accelerating energy demand and enforcing stringent carbon emissions reductions have elevated Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) to the forefront of petroleum and environmental engineering. Among various utilization avenues, Carbon Dioxide Enhanced Oil Recovery (CO2-EOR) and Enhanced Gas Recovery (CO2-EGR) present distinct economic drivers that offset the steep capital outlays associated with industrial decarbonization infrastructure. However, conventional reservoir management practices have historically operated with a single-minded objective: maximizing short-term hydrocarbon recovery factors without accounting for long-term geologic containment security or regulatory carbon permanence requirements.

title: Low-carbon haulage alternatives for future net-zero surface mines: a systematic review of energy assessment methods and decision frameworks
source: International Journal of Mining Reclamation and Environment
summary: Decarbonisation of surface mine haulage is critical, as transport activities represent a major share of site energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. This paper provides a review of low carbon haulage alternatives, including battery
content: Decarbonisation of surface mine haulage is critical, as transport activities represent a major share of site energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. This paper provides a review of low carbon haulage alternatives, including battery electric trucks, trolley assist systems, fuel cell concepts, and in pit crushing and conveying configurations, with emphasis on their energy performance and operational constraints. It compares analytical, simulation-based, data-driven, and AI-supported methods for energy demand assessment, productivity impacts, and infrastructure constraints. The paper highlights the need for mine-specific energy metrics, adaptive dispatch, renewable-powered charging, and identifies gaps in integrated assessment frameworks for scalable low-carbon haulage planning.

title: Measuring uncertainty and prospects: evaluating blue carbon ecosystem measures in Taiwan
summary: Taiwan has officially included marine carbon as part of its carbon offset framework in its greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction target, set at a level of a 23%–25% reduction by 2030, and net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. This analytical
content: Taiwan has officially included marine carbon as part of its carbon offset framework in its greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction target, set at a level of a 23%–25% reduction by 2030, and net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. This analytical piece thus draws on a simple form of multicriteria analysis to evaluate the status of, and identify issues plaguing, the development of Taiwan’s blue carbon ecosystem (BCE) measures. The picture is quite murky. Contribution of marine carbon to GHG emission reduction is theoretically proven and officially included in Taiwan’s methodology for GHG emission reduction (theoretically proven impact). Subsequent follow-up on the development of Taiwan’s BCE measures is a worthy effort. However, the bureaucratic complex—comprising low bureaucratic capacity, caused by a conglomeration of the prevalence of the developmentalism mindset, overwhelming influences from high-energy-consumption industries, and the resulting fragmented view in policy design of Taiwan’s carbon dioxide removal (CDR) measures—has substantially impacted the development of Taiwan’s BCE measures. Given this reality, it would not be surprising if the effect of BCE measures were attenuated (attenuated effect), while the relevance exhibited in the policy outcome and original objectives remains weak (weak relevance). Policy flexibility and predictability of BCE measures have collaterally been compromised (compromised policy flexibility and predictability) because of the still-evolving inter-agency coordination and lingering rivalry between governmental sectors, along with existing issues, such as budget concerns. The preliminary proposal is to refine the management of wetlands that harbor significant marine carbon, which is also the focus of the initial stage (2019–2023) of Taiwan’s BCE measures policy.

title: Modified track-etched membranes as templates for HKUST-1 immobilization and application to CO2 capture
summary: The development of efficient and reusable materials for CO2 capture is important for reducing carbon dioxide emissions. In this study, an HKUST-1-immobilized track-etched membrane was developed for carbon dioxide capture. PET TeM were first
content: The development of efficient and reusable materials for CO2 capture is important for reducing carbon dioxide emissions. In this study, an HKUST-1-immobilized track-etched membrane was developed for carbon dioxide capture. PET TeM were first modified by photo-induced graft polymerization of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (2-HEMA). The polymerization conditions were optimized to achieve effective surface modification while preserving the porous structure of the membrane. The formation of HKUST-1 on the membrane surface and within the pore structure was confirmed by structural and surface characterization. The structure and properties of the obtained membranes were studied using SEM-EDS, XRD, TGA, BET, FTIR and contact angle analysis. The BET surface area increased from 0.61 m2/g for PET TeM to 629.65 m2/g for the g-pHEMA/HKUST-1@PET TeM. The membrane showed a CO2 adsorption capacity of 2.04 mmol/g at 25°C. Moreover, the membranes retained 94% of the initial adsorption performance after 12 adsorption-desorption cycles, demonstrating good regeneration stability. Thus, the combination of controlled pHEMA modification and HKUST-1 immobilization provides a promising approach for the development of porous and reusable MOF based membranes for CO2 capture.

title: Nonlinear Spatial Associations Between Digital Economy Development and Thermal Power CO2 Emissions: Evidence from Chinese Provincial Panel Data
summary: Digital development connects sustainable energy services with growing electricity demand, but economy-wide carbon measures obscure the production conditions of thermal power. This study links a traceable account of 27 fossil fuel inputs to
content: Digital development connects sustainable energy services with growing electricity demand, but economy-wide carbon measures obscure the production conditions of thermal power. This study links a traceable account of 27 fossil fuel inputs to provincial digital development using Chinese data for 2013–2022. Fixed-effects comparisons separate production scale from emissions intensity, while a nonlinear spatial Durbin model examines a balanced panel of 27 provinces with full-refit province-wild inference. In the policy-adjusted contiguity model, the average total marginal association is −0.2228, with a 95% bootstrap-t interval of [−0.4514, −0.0305]. This negative total association persists across five digital economy measures, including two that exclude information service employment. The indirect marginal association increases with digital development under all five measures; its change rate is 0.0942 in the original index model, with a simultaneous 95% interval of [0.0410, 0.1474]. Adding province-specific linear trends changes the total association to −0.0337 [−0.2139, 0.1365] and redistributes the curvature toward the local component. This study identifies a measurement-consistent, trend-sensitive spatial association rather than a uniform digitalization effect. Its contribution is to connect sector-specific fuel accounting, production conditions, and changing regional associations, informing coordinated evaluation of digital investment and sustainable electricity provision.

title: Opposite Temporal Afterglow Evolution in White Light-Excited Carbon Dots Enabled by Matrix Confinement and Interfacial Engineering
summary: Abstract White light-excited afterglow carbon dots (CDs) with controllable time-dependent emission are highly desirable for advanced optical security but remain challenging because precisely regulating the evolution of multiple long-lived e
content: Abstract White light-excited afterglow carbon dots (CDs) with controllable time-dependent emission are highly desirable for advanced optical security but remain challenging because precisely regulating the evolution of multiple long-lived emissive states is difficult. Herein, we report a matrix-confinement and interfacial-engineering strategy to construct white light-excited afterglow CD composites by integrating CDs into borate and borate–silica hybrid matrices. The resulting G-CDs@B2O3 and G-CDs@SiO2@B2O3 exhibit distinct yellow-to-green and green-to-yellow afterglow evolution under white light excitation. Structural characterization reveals that the rigid borate matrix stabilizes the emissive states through abundant B–O, B–OH, and B–C interactions, whereas the introduction of an APTES-derived silicate network creates additional Si–O–C and Si–C interfacial interactions that redistribute the relative contributions of multiple emissive states without altering the core structure of CDs. Benefiting from these unique dynamic optical properties, the composites enable time-resolved anticounterfeiting and information encryption with enhanced security.

title: Statistics
summary: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, tabulation, and interpretation of numerical data. The first section covers simple linear regression and shows the linear relationship between carbon dioxide emissions and gr
content: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, tabulation, and interpretation of numerical data. The first section covers simple linear regression and shows the linear relationship between carbon dioxide emissions and gross domestic product in the USA from 2000 to 2020. The second section is concerned with stochastic processes and Markov chains, directed graphs are plotted, and convergence to steady states are illustrated with plots. The student's t-test is discussed in the third section, and a simple two-sample t-test is applied to the heights of female and male students in a lecture. The final section introduces powerful Monte-Carlo simulations, and a simple example is presented of gambling on a European roulette wheel, where it is clearly demonstrated that casinos and online betting companies always win in the long term, and why none of us should gamble. Aims and Objectives To show how MATLAB can be used to solve problems in statistics. On completion of this chapter the reader should be able to carry out linear regression on data sets; draw Markov chains and plot stability diagrams; carry out statistical hypotheses tests using the t-test; apply Monte-Carlo simulations to a wide range of applications.

title: Are Europe's Universities Preparing Future Tourism Professionals for a Greener Future?
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Rationale, Aims and ObjectivesThe tourism industry's transition towards net-zero emissions requires future professionals to have the knowledge and practical skills to address climate change and sustainability challenges. Universities play a
content: Rationale, Aims and ObjectivesThe tourism industry's transition towards net-zero emissions requires future professionals to have the knowledge and practical skills to address climate change and sustainability challenges. Universities play a vital role in preparing graduates for this transition. This research examines how effectively European universities integrate sustainability, climate action and carbon reduction into tourism education. It assesses the coverage of these topics within tourism programmes, identifies gaps in existing curricula and explores opportunities to strengthen sustainability education. The research highlights the importance of equipping graduates with the competencies needed to support the tourism industry's transition towards a low-carbon future. Research FindingsDrawing on 95 valid survey responses from 65 higher education institutions across five European countries, the research found that 68% of course directors reported curricula aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. However, only 42% reported programme-level learning outcomes focused on decarbonisation, while just 21% of programmes taught students how to measure tourism emissions. This represented the largest gap identified against the study's climate milestones. The findings highlight a significant disconnect between general sustainability education and the practical skills required to address tourism's contribution to climate change, reinforcing the need to strengthen tourism curricula, provide additional educator training and improve collaboration with industry to better prepare future tourism professionals. Policy ImplicationsThe findings highlight the need for universities and policymakers to strengthen climate action and net-zero principles within tourism education. Higher education policies should promote practical skills in carbon measurement, emissions reduction and sustainable tourism management. Greater collaboration between universities, industry and policymakers is essential to align tourism curricula with climate commitments and the evolving needs of the sector. Improved educator training and clearer curriculum guidelines would help embed climate action and sustainability more consistently across European tourism education. Industry RecommendationsThe tourism industry should work more closely with universities to ensure graduates develop the practical skills needed to support the transition towards net-zero emissions. Industry representatives should contribute to curriculum development, provide real-world case studies and offer opportunities for students to participate in sustainability initiatives. Greater emphasis should be placed on carbon measurement, emissions reduction and sustainable tourism management. Partnerships between tourism businesses, educators and policymakers can help bridge the gap between academic learning and industry needs, ensuring future tourism professionals are equipped to address climate challenges and contribute t

title: The role of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in shaping ecosystem services in agroecosystems
summary: Abstract Intensive agriculture contributes to biodiversity loss, soil degradation and the decline of ecosystem services, creating a need for management strategies that sustain crop production while reducing environmental impacts. Arbuscular
content: Abstract Intensive agriculture contributes to biodiversity loss, soil degradation and the decline of ecosystem services, creating a need for management strategies that sustain crop production while reducing environmental impacts. Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi are often proposed as biological tools for sustainable agriculture, but their contribution to ecosystem service provision in agroecosystems remains context dependent and unevenly quantified. Here, we compiled 1390 effect‐size observations from 115 articles published between 1992 and January 2024. Notably, 91.2% of these observations derived from greenhouse studies, with only 123 representing field experiments. We used a multilevel meta‐analysis to assess AM fungal effects on provisioning, regulation and maintenance services classified according to the Common International Classification of Ecosystem Services framework. We also evaluated whether these effects varied with water availability and fertilization level. AM fungi significantly enhanced the accumulation of beneficial substances, buffering against abiotic stress and belowground biomass‐related variables, whereas effects on production, nutrient accumulation and soil retention were not significant in the general model. Water‐retention proxies showed a negative overall response, although this effect was not significant under drought stress. AM fungal benefits were stronger under drought stress, particularly for plant stress‐buffering responses, while high fertilization reduced detectable benefits. These results show that AM fungi can support several ecosystem‐service‐related processes in agroecosystems, but that their effects are not uniformly positive across all services and depend strongly on abiotic context. We conclude that AM fungi should be considered as components of integrated agroecosystem management strategies, especially under resource‐limited conditions, rather than as universal substitutes for external inputs.

title: Conversion of Mixed Textile Waste into Solid Fuel by Torrefaction
summary: Textile waste generation has reached critical levels, created significant environmental and economic challenges and requires effective valorisation strategies. This study investigates torrefaction as a thermochemical route for converting mi
content: Textile waste generation has reached critical levels, created significant environmental and economic challenges and requires effective valorisation strategies. This study investigates torrefaction as a thermochemical route for converting mixed textile waste into a solid fuel. The process was carried out at temperatures of 200–300 °C under an inert nitrogen atmosphere. The results show that increasing the torrefaction temperature significantly affects the material’s physicochemical and fuel properties. At 300 °C, the moisture and volatile matter contents decreased from 2.75% to 0.4% and from 82.5% to 20.0%, respectively, while the fixed carbon content increased from 13.0% to 74.6%. The mass yield decreased from 89.5% at 200 °C to 41.2% at 300 °C, while the corresponding energy yield decreased from 99.94% to 50.76%. The highest higher heating value (HHV) of 22.267 MJ/kg was obtained at 300 °C, compared to 18.073 MJ/kg for the untreated material. At 300 °C, fuel sales revenue minus torrefaction costs was −11.50 USD/t of dry textile waste. Assuming full avoidance of the corresponding disposal costs, the estimated benefits relative to incineration and landfilling were 108.50 and 58.50 USD/t of dry textile waste, respectively. It was not possible to determine the net effect on greenhouse gas emissions, as the proportion of fossil carbon in the mixed textile raw materials was not determined, and the assessment did not cover all emissions associated with the process. The results confirm the technical potential of torrefaction of mixed textile waste. A full life-cycle analysis of the process is required for a final assessment of environmental performance.

title: PAD_III_GTSD_Audited_Replication
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Title: Replication Materials for “Linking Clinical Effectiveness to Environmental Sustainability in Healthcare: A Scenario-Based Assessment of Endovascular Treatment for Calcified Peripheral Artery Disease” Author: Jorge Navarrete-Dualde, M
content: Title: Replication Materials for “Linking Clinical Effectiveness to Environmental Sustainability in Healthcare: A Scenario-Based Assessment of Endovascular Treatment for Calcified Peripheral Artery Disease” Author: Jorge Navarrete-Dualde, MScAffiliation: Independent Researcher, SpainORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9767-8894Contact: jornavdumedical@gmail.com Description This repository contains the editable replication materials supporting the calculations reported in the manuscript “Integrating Clinical Effectiveness and Environmental Sustainability in Endovascular Treatment of Calcified Peripheral Artery Disease.” The study uses a deterministic scenario-based approach to connect published clinical outcomes from the DISRUPT PAD III programme with published estimates of procedural waste and carbon burden. The analysis is intended to provide a transparent and reproducible framework for exploring potential environmental consequences associated with differences in clinical resource utilization. The calculations should not be interpreted as a comparative life-cycle assessment or as direct evidence of environmental superiority of a specific technology. In particular, the 7.1% repeat-intervention parameter is used as a scenario proxy based on the reported difference in in-stent restenosis and does not represent an observed 7.1% reduction in repeat interventions. Repository contents PAD_III_GTSD_Audited_Replication.xlsx The Microsoft Excel workbook contains the complete editable calculation model and is organized into the following worksheets: Inputs_Audit — clinical and environmental input parameters and associated assumptions. Device_Waste_Model — calculations of potential reductions in single-use-device waste. Repeat_Intervention_Scenarios — scenario calculations for waste and procedure-related carbon burdens associated with potentially avoided repeat interventions. Audit_Checks — automated numerical consistency and replication checks. Read_Me — workbook-level explanation of assumptions, scope, and limitations. All derived calculations are retained as editable Excel formulas rather than hard-coded results. Principal replicated outputs For a standardized scenario of 1,000 index procedures, the workbook reproduces the following estimates: Relative reduction in provisional stent use: 74.9% Estimated avoided stent-related waste: 106.36 kg Relative reduction in post-dilation: 69.4% Estimated avoided post-dilation waste: 98.55 kg Combined device-waste scenario: 204.91 kg Scenario-based avoided repeat-intervention waste: 109.34 kg Scenario-based avoided emissions: 3,862.40 kg CO₂e Scenario-based avoided emissions: 5,557.17 kg CO₂ Scenario-based avoided emissions: 17,253.00 kg CO₂e The three carbon estimates originate from different published sources and system boundaries and therefore should not be pooled or interpreted as confidence limits. Reproducibility The workbook preserves the formulas used to generate the reported results. Users can inspect the in

title: Seeing green in ophthalmology: carbon footprint of surgical waste in a Malaysian Tertiary Eye Centre
summary: AIM: To estimate the carbon footprint of ophthalmic surgical waste in a Malaysian tertiary hospital and to assess its implications for sustainable ophthalmology practice. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in the Ophth
content: AIM: To estimate the carbon footprint of ophthalmic surgical waste in a Malaysian tertiary hospital and to assess its implications for sustainable ophthalmology practice. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in the Ophthalmology Department at University Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) from 14 to 27 March 2025. All waste generated during ophthalmic surgeries was collected, weighed, and categorised as general waste, clinical waste, or sharps. Waste disposal pathways were recorded based on Malaysian hospital practices. Carbon emissions were calculated using emission factors from the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, UK (DEFRA), incorporating production and disposal emissions. RESULTS: A total of 88.2 kg of waste was generated by 46 ophthalmic surgeries during the study period, comprising 19.15 kg of general waste, 62.02 kg of clinical waste, and 7.03 kg of sharps. This corresponded to 353.99 kg of carbon dioxide equivalent (kgCO2e), including 281.11 kgCO2e from production emissions and 72.88 kgCO2e from disposal emissions. Clinical waste was the main contributor (259.18 kgCO2e; 73.2% of total emissions). The average carbon footprint per surgery was 10.41 kgCO2e.Re. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first estimation of the carbon footprint of ophthalmic surgical waste in Malaysia. The findings highlight the significant contribution of ophthalmic consumables to healthcare emissions and underscore the need for sustainable practices, including recycling, reuse, and reduction of single-use items, to align ophthalmology with national and global carbon-neutral healthcare goals.

title: Stuck in Plantations: Why Palm Oil Investment Fails to Deliver Decentralised Inclusive Development?
summary: This study aims to analyze four palm oil investment schemes in Meliau Subdistrict, Sanggau Regency, West Kalimantan, namely the Transmigration-People's Core Plantation/Perkebunan Inti Rakyat-Transmigrasi (PIR-Trans), People's Core Plantatio
content: This study aims to analyze four palm oil investment schemes in Meliau Subdistrict, Sanggau Regency, West Kalimantan, namely the Transmigration-People's Core Plantation/Perkebunan Inti Rakyat-Transmigrasi (PIR-Trans), People's Core Plantation-Plantation/Perkebunan Inti Rakyat-Perkebunan (PIR-Bun), Credit Cooperative for Members/Koperasi Kredit pada Anggota (KKPA), and Independent Farmers/Petani Mandiri (PR), as well as their structural implications for farmers’ socioeconomic well-being. This study employs a multiple-case qualitative method using in-depth interviews, focus group discussions (FGDs), and document analysis. Findings from the study, informed by the Collaborative Inclusive Sustainable Development-Rosyadi Model (CISD-RM), reveal significant differences in land-sharing mechanisms between corporations and landowners, with a dominant 80:20 pattern that disproportionately benefits corporations. Most plasma schemes still lack transparency regarding funding, which encourages long-term dependence among farmers. Institutional fragmentation, elite dominance, and farmers’ weak bargaining positions exacerbate inequities in the distribution of proceeds. Although employment has increased, the majority of palm oil products are still sold outside the region, so the local value added remains relatively limited. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of four oil palm investment schemes. The findings highlight weaknesses in agrarian governance and emphasize the need for more equitable and territorially integrated investment schemes through downstream development and fairer land distribution.

title: Whole-Life-Cycle Decarbonization Potential and Mechanical Performance of All-Steel Excavation Support Systems under Carbon Constraints
summary: Abstract Traditional cast-in-place concrete retaining systems for deep foundation pits generate substantial embodied carbon over their life cycle. Existing comparative studies often decouple mechanical safety verification from carbon emissi
content: Abstract Traditional cast-in-place concrete retaining systems for deep foundation pits generate substantial embodied carbon over their life cycle. Existing comparative studies often decouple mechanical safety verification from carbon emission accounting, lacking multi-dimensional uncertainty evaluation under equivalent deformation constraints. Using a deep foundation pit project in China, this study employs finite element analysis to compare the deformation and mechanical performance of two retaining schemes under identical geometry, soil-water parameters, and excavation conditions. Based on the emission factor method, life-cycle carbon emissions are quantified across four stages: material production, material transportation, on-site construction, and demolition-and-disposal. A total of 5,000 Monte Carlo simulations are performed under normal and uniform distributions, incorporating key parameters such as carbon emission factors, transport distances, steel component reuse cycles, and material loss rates. Results show that both schemes provide comparable deformation control and meet the Grade-I deformation criteria. At baseline, the all-steel retaining system emits 1094.526 tCO2e, only 37.11% of the concrete system's 2949.692 tCO2e, achieving a 62.89% carbon reduction. Sensitivity analysis indicates a break-even reuse number of approximately 3.7 for steel components; the all-steel system becomes more carbon-efficient when reuse reaches 4 or more. It retains its low-carbon advantage even under conservative high material loss scenarios or varied transportation distances and modes. Further Monte Carlo results show that the median life-cycle emission of the concrete system is about 2.2 times that of the all-steel system under the normal-distribution assumption and 2.7 times under the uniform-distribution assumption, and the interquartile ranges barely overlap for both distribution cases, demonstrating statistical robustness. This study confirms that the recyclable all-steel retaining system offers stable emission reduction benefits, providing theoretical and data support for low-carbon scheme selection and quantitative carbon assessment in deep excavations.

title: Climate Crisis as Kinship Crisis
summary: Abstract According to prevailing environmental discourses, which are imbued with kinless investitures, we currently face a climate crisis insofar as the climatological effects of excessive carbon emissions risk destabilizing civilization an
content: Abstract According to prevailing environmental discourses, which are imbued with kinless investitures, we currently face a climate crisis insofar as the climatological effects of excessive carbon emissions risk destabilizing civilization and jeopardizing cherished ways of life. From this vantage point, the threat posed by climate change is unprecedented and demands urgent action to avert apocalyptic conditions that will limit or even erase the future of all humankind. This chapter proposes that this framework perpetuates a discursive infrastructure that commits its proponents to logics that ultimately reinforce the dynamics driving climate change. By instead viewing matters through an Indigenous ecological lens, the climate crisis is properly understood primarily as a manifestation of multidimensional disruptions of kincentric ecologies. It’s a rebound effect of centuries of accumulating colonial injustices against purveyors of extended more-than-human kinship arrangements that are critical for societal adaptability, resilience, and well-being. Framing the climate crisis as a kinship crisis creates conceptual and narrative space for much-needed transformational visions aimed at justly and effectively addressing climate change specifically and colonial violence more broadly. This serves as a pivot to our focus on subverting kinlessness in the chapters that follow.

title: How to Apply Environmental Accounting at Regional General Hospitals in Indonesia? (Paradigm of Bioregionalsm)
source: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
summary: Applying environmental accounting (EA) is a form of the bioregionalism paradigm, which unites economics and ecology. This study aims to find out the application of EA in regional general hospitals (RSUD) in Indonesia today and the benefits
content: Applying environmental accounting (EA) is a form of the bioregionalism paradigm, which unites economics and ecology. This study aims to find out the application of EA in regional general hospitals (RSUD) in Indonesia today and the benefits of implementing the EA. This study uses a library research approach that integrates the findings of previous studies regarding the implementation of existing EA in RSUD. The results show that not all hospitals have a place to treat adequate waste due to the costs charged to the hospitals. Standards and policies governing EA for RSUD still need to be created, so the reference for implementing EA needs to be revised. RSUD still reports EA voluntarily and no EA has been specifically reported. EA needs to be explicitly implemented and correctly. For this reason, the government must actively monitor and create EA standards that can be used as a reference for hospitals to improve environmental and organizational performance. This study contributes to the development of the application of environmental accounting in hospitals in Indonesia.

title: Contesting financialised housing decarbonisation: Radical repair and the crisis of socio-ecological reproduction
summary: This article examines how struggles around landlord-led housing decarbonisation unfold in a context shaped by financialised corporate landlords and permissive regulatory frameworks. Focusing on a working-class housing estate in Frankfurt am
content: This article examines how struggles around landlord-led housing decarbonisation unfold in a context shaped by financialised corporate landlords and permissive regulatory frameworks. Focusing on a working-class housing estate in Frankfurt am Main, it analyses how energy retrofitting reorganises the conditions of socio-ecological reproduction by affecting rent relations, care routines, health, thermal comfort, time, and neighbourhood support. Bringing a feminist political-economy perspective on housing into dialogue with the emerging debate on radical housing repair, the article argues that housing decarbonisation under financialisation is not simply a technical or distributive issue, but a contested field of socio-ecological reproduction. It develops radical repair as a concept for analysing and politicising struggles over maintenance, retrofit, and affordability, and reflects on the promises and limits of scholar-tenant collaboration under conditions of precarity and asymmetrical power. The article argues that decarbonisation without displacement requires both institutional reform and movement infrastructures grounded in situated tenant knowledge.

title: Negotiating green dreams with a spectral state: Struggles over public housing and ecological tending in waterfront redevelopment at the urban-Southern frontier
summary: Following 20 years of waterfront redevelopment in Sant'Elia, a public housing neighbourhood in Cagliari, Sardinia, this paper asks how struggles over public housing can work against the post-politicisation of sustainability discourses enact
content: Following 20 years of waterfront redevelopment in Sant'Elia, a public housing neighbourhood in Cagliari, Sardinia, this paper asks how struggles over public housing can work against the post-politicisation of sustainability discourses enacted by entrepreneurial green urbanism. I show how, in Sant’Elia, municipal green development discourses articulate an apolitical salvific future of landscape restoration that reproduces dichotomies between worthy and unworthy subjectivities and materialities. Testing these narratives against local housing struggles, I trace how residents have repeatedly exposed the state’s denial of accountability for public housing disrepair and territorial stigmatisation. Although not everyone opposes redevelopment, people draw on the collective memory of housing injustice to politicise green dreams in the face of a spectral state. I propose the concept of ecological tending to think about imaginative and anticipatory practices holding together divergent hopes for a shared environment, and opening avenues for transformative contaminations between housing and environmental justice.

title: Spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy’s impact on agricultural carbon emissions
summary: To explore the spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy in promoting low-carbon agricultural transformation, this paper measures digital economy development and agricultural carbon emissions based on panel data for 31 provinces
content: To explore the spatial effects and mechanisms of the digital economy in promoting low-carbon agricultural transformation, this paper measures digital economy development and agricultural carbon emissions based on panel data for 31 provinces in China from 2011 to 2023, and analyzes their spatial distribution characteristics. Spatial Durbin and mediating models are employed to investigate the effects and mechanisms of the digital economy on agricultural carbon emissions. The results show that both the digital economy and agricultural carbon emissions present a “high-high and low-low” spatial agglomeration pattern, and agricultural carbon emissions have a significant positive spatial spillover effect. The digital economy significantly reduces agricultural carbon emissions in local and neighboring provinces, with obvious regional heterogeneity. In major grain-producing areas, the digital economy only inhibits local agricultural carbon emissions. In non-major grain-producing areas, the digital economy has a weaker effect on local emissions but can reduce carbon emissions in adjacent areas through cross-regional technology diffusion. From 2011 to 2018, agricultural carbon emissions exhibit a spatial clustering pattern, while the digital economy significantly reduces emissions in both the local and neighboring provinces. By contrast, in 2019–2023, agricultural carbon emissions shift toward a spatially competitive pattern: the direct local reduction effect of the digital economy gradually diminishes and becomes statistically insignificant, while its inhibitory effect on neighboring provinces also weakens. Fiscal support for agriculture strengthens the carbon reduction effect of the digital economy, and a higher level of economic development enhances this inhibitory effect. Rural entrepreneurship vitality and agricultural total factor productivity play significant mediating roles in the process of digital economy-driven agricultural carbon emission reduction. The conclusions provide empirical support for strengthening the role of the digital economy in agricultural carbon emission reduction and guidance for improving the policy system of low-carbon agricultural development.

title: The supply chain of pasture-based meat: a review
summary: Abstract Livestock production systems occupy approximately 80% of global agricultural land and contribute substantially to food security, providing 18% of dietary energy and 37% of protein supply. With global meat demand projected to increa
content: Abstract Livestock production systems occupy approximately 80% of global agricultural land and contribute substantially to food security, providing 18% of dietary energy and 37% of protein supply. With global meat demand projected to increase by 76% by 2050, sustainable production systems that balance environmental, economic, and social dimensions are increasingly important. This study assessed pasture-based meat production through a bibliometric analysis of publications from 1978 to 2025. A total of 117 publications were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science (WoS), and Dimensions and analysed using R version 4.4.3 and Biblioshiny. The analysis identified key research themes related to grazing management, environmental sustainability, animal welfare, meat quality, climate-change mitigation and sustainable food supply chains. This study indicate that improved grazing practices, particularly rotational grazing, can enhance pasture productivity, vegetation persistence, soil health and soil carbon sequestration, supporting livestock productivity and climate-change mitigation. Pasture-based meat systems also align with consumer interest in animal welfare and environmentally responsible production. However, their development is constrained by fragmented supply chains, inadequate infrastructure, limited market access and post-harvest losses. Sustainable sourcing practices, including environmentally responsible production, appropriate infrastructure, traceability and reliable market access, are essential for strengthening pasture-based meat value chains. Strengthening local food networks can improve market participation among smallholder farmers and the pastoralist pasture-based community, contributing to rural economic development. Improved cold-chain infrastructure can maintain meat quality and reduce post-harvest losses, while consumer education may strengthen demand for pasture-based meat. This study highlight the growing integration of pasture-based meat production with sustainability, climate resilience and food-system transformation.

title: Low-Cost Sensor Monitoring of Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) Temporal Trends in Lackawanna County, Pennsylvania: A Citizen Science Approach
summary: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are hazardous air pollutants associated with adverse respiratory and chronic health outcomes, yet conventional monitoring approaches often lack the spatial coverage needed to address community-leve
content: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are hazardous air pollutants associated with adverse respiratory and chronic health outcomes, yet conventional monitoring approaches often lack the spatial coverage needed to address community-level environmental concerns. Although low-cost air sensors can substantially expand monitoring networks, their application to VOC monitoring remains limited by uncertainty in absolute concentration measurements. This study evaluated whether community-deployed low-cost sensors can reliably identify meaningful temporal VOC patterns across an environmental justice community in Lackawanna County, Pennsylvania, surrounding the Keystone Sanitary Landfill. Community-deployed PurpleAir monitors collected VOC index data at six-hour intervals throughout 2025 across the Lackawanna County study area as part of a citizen science monitoring initiative. Data were analyzed using smoothing, mean-centering, principal component analysis (PCA), and k-means clustering to emphasize relative temporal behavior rather than absolute sensor responses. Smoothed time-series revealed coherent long-term VOC trends across geographically distributed monitoring sites despite substantial short-term variability. PCA showed that a small number of components explained much of the meaningful variance in the dataset, indicating strong temporal consistency across the sensor network. K-means clustering identified two broad sensor groups, although substantial overlap suggested a continuum of VOC temporal responses rather than distinct site-specific regimes. These findings demonstrate that trend-based multivariate approaches can extract meaningful environmental information from low-cost VOC sensors and support the use of citizen science monitoring networks to expand air-quality surveillance, inform environmental management, and strengthen community engagement in environmental decision-making.

title: Beyond Reported Emissions: Uncovering Hidden Corporate Carbon Footprints
summary: ABSTRACT Scope 3 emissions have become central to climate disclosure, but remain the least reliable component of firms' carbon footprints. This paper argues that the core measurement problem lies not only in the aggregate Scope 3 total, but
content: ABSTRACT Scope 3 emissions have become central to climate disclosure, but remain the least reliable component of firms' carbon footprints. This paper argues that the core measurement problem lies not only in the aggregate Scope 3 total, but in the heterogeneous quality of its underlying categories. Because some categories are far more difficult to observe, verify and compare than others, the aggregate figure embeds substantial noise—and, as we show, systematic omission. Using firm‐level disclosures from the CDP (Carbon Disclosure Project) database over 2013–2023, we implement a category‐level framework that first diagnoses, for each of the 15 GHG Protocol categories, whether a firm fully omits, partially under‐reports or soundly discloses it and then estimates the missing magnitude by machine learning. We find that hidden Scope 3 amounts to about 22% of reported emissions on a value‐weighted basis, while under‐reporting is near‐universal across firms—the median firm conceals 64% of its corrected footprint—but concentrated in tonnage among the largest emitters. Omission is not diffuse: it concentrates on use of sold products, the single category that most directly captures a firm's exposure to transition risk and that alone accounts for roughly two‐thirds of hidden emissions. Correcting these disclosures therefore reshapes firms' relative positions in the carbon distribution—44% of declarants change carbon‐intensity quintile—and selectively reveals the most financially material dimension of their carbon exposure. Reported Scope 3 carries a reliability ratio of at most 0.65 with respect to corrected exposure (0.62 within sectors), so carbon‐premium estimates built on it are attenuated by a third or more—distortions that affect ESG scoring, portfolio construction, transition‐risk assessment and the design of disclosure standards.

title: A Mechanism of Release of Iron Ions From Magnetite and Its Implications for Fenton Chemistry in Sonodynamic Treatment of Cancer Cells
summary: Adding magnetite (mixed iron(II) and iron(III) oxide) to sonodynamic cancer treatment protocols reportedly enhances cytotoxic effects both in vitro and in vivo. However, the underlying mechanisms, especially those related to the release of
content: Adding magnetite (mixed iron(II) and iron(III) oxide) to sonodynamic cancer treatment protocols reportedly enhances cytotoxic effects both in vitro and in vivo. However, the underlying mechanisms, especially those related to the release of Fe(II) and to Fenton chemistry, are poorly understood. Using a combined cell culture and chemical approach, we explore some of these mechanisms and their likely biological significance. We apply an in vitro model of sonodynamic treatment utilizing magnetosomes (bacterially derived magnetite nanoparticles). Magnetosomes alone, while showing similar uptake and subcellular distribution, show toxicity toward sarcoid cells but not toward their non‐neoplastic parental cells. Concomitant low‐intensity ultrasound treatment of the cells under strict avoidance of hyperthermia does not increase toxicity despite generating hydroxyl radical‐associated markers in both cell types. Chemical experiments reveal that Fe(II) is released from magnetosomes by ion exchange against other bivalent cations, rather than by dissolution, which is the commonly perceived mechanism. Hypoxia increases the reaction yield, while sonication accelerates its kinetics. We conclude that ion exchange as the main modality of iron release is a pivotal determinant of Fenton chemistry in sonodynamic therapy protocols with magnetite nanoparticles. This critical aspect, especially related to the timing of ultrasound application, should be given the utmost consideration.

title: Simultaneous Wastewater Treatment and Bioelectricity Generation from Tofu Industrial Wastewater Using a Microalgae-Microbial Fuel Cell (MMFC)
source: AJARCDE (Asian Journal of Applied Research for Community Development and Empowerment)
summary: Microalgae-microbial fuel cell (MMFC) technology integrates microalgal photosynthesis with microbial degradation of organic compounds in wastewater, enabling wastewater treatment and bioelectricity generation to occur simultaneously. This s
content: Microalgae-microbial fuel cell (MMFC) technology integrates microalgal photosynthesis with microbial degradation of organic compounds in wastewater, enabling wastewater treatment and bioelectricity generation to occur simultaneously. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different ratios of tofu industrial wastewater to Bacillus sp. inoculum on bioelectricity production, chemical oxygen demand (COD) and total nitrogen (TN) removal, and microbial growth in an MMFC system. Four wastewater-to-inoculum ratios (75:25, 80:20, 85:15, and 90:10 v/v) were tested in the anode compartment, while Chlorella sp. was used in the cathode compartment. The system was operated for 12 days, and voltage and current were measured every 12 hours. The 75:25 ratio produced the highest voltage, current, and power density, reaching 755 mV, 5.945 mA, and 561.0 mW/m², respectively. It also achieved the highest COD and TN removal efficiencies, at 80.68% and 26.5%, respectively. The highest bacterial volatile suspended solids (VSS) concentration and microalgal optical density (OD) were 5,550 mg/L and 0.764, respectively, while total volatile acid (TAV) reached 1,404.6 mg/L. However, the final COD and TN concentrations remained above the applicable wastewater quality standards. These findings demonstrate the potential of MMFC technology for laboratory-scale wastewater treatment and bioelectricity generation, although further optimization is required to improve pollutant removal and support its future application in sustainable wastewater management. Contribution to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation. SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy. SDG 12: Responsible consumption and Production

title: Spatially robust pixel‐based mapping of biotic stress in Pinus nigra using unmanned aerial vehicle multispectral imagery and Random Forest
summary: BACKGROUND: Biotic stress threatens forest health, creating a need for rapid monitoring methods that complement field surveys. This study compared four original multispectral bands, five vegetation indices, and their combination for segment
content: BACKGROUND: Biotic stress threatens forest health, creating a need for rapid monitoring methods that complement field surveys. This study compared four original multispectral bands, five vegetation indices, and their combination for segmentation-free, pixel-based Random Forest mapping of healthy and unhealthy Pinus nigra canopies in Bingöl, Türkiye. Field and laboratory observations confirmed Dothistroma spp. and Tomicus spp. within the stand. RESULTS: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery with a ground sampling distance of 2.31 cm was evaluated using identical five-block spatial cross-validation partitions comprising 113 georeferenced trees (55 healthy and 58 unhealthy), each represented by mean predictor values from a manually delineated within-crown sampling polygon. The combined model achieved the highest pooled overall accuracy (98.23%; Kappa = 0.9646). The vegetation-index model achieved 97.35% accuracy and the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC, 0.9991), with Optimized Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index (OSAVI) showing the greatest mean permutation importance. Exact McNemar tests detected no significant differences among models (all P = 1.000). The vegetation-index model was retained as a parsimonious alternative to the combined model and fitted using 200 reference polygons to generate the operational map. Cross-validated performance does not constitute independent validation of this final map. CONCLUSION: Comparing predictor representations under a common spatial validation framework supports transparent assessment of UAV-based canopy-health mapping without crown segmentation. The approach can guide local field inspections but does not identify individual causal agents. Findings represent within-flight discrimination in one stand; absent reflectance-panel calibration, broader application requires standardized radiometric calibration and independent spatial and temporal validation. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Cement-reduced ternary concrete with fly ash and silica fume for irrigation canal structures: computational mix design with single-composition experimental verification
summary: Irrigation canal linings in Kazakhstan face freeze-thaw cycling, sulfate-bearing water, and abrasive sediment flow, while national programs to rehabilitate more than 14,000 km of canals create sustained demand for lower-clinker concrete. Th
content: Irrigation canal linings in Kazakhstan face freeze-thaw cycling, sulfate-bearing water, and abrasive sediment flow, while national programs to rehabilitate more than 14,000 km of canals create sustained demand for lower-clinker concrete. This study computationally designs a cement-reduced ternary binder (CEM I 42.5N, Ekibastuz low-calcium fly ash, and DSF-95 silica fume, 70:20:10 by mass) that replaces 30% of the cement in a plant control mixture (280 vs 400 kg/m3) while preserving total binder content, paste volume, and aggregate skeleton. The design combines particle-packing simulation, a modified Bolomey model calibrated on the measured plant control (R28 = 44.5 MPa), and Powers-model porosity. Experimentally, a laboratory composition with the same ternary binder proportions was cast and tested in 100 mm cubes, yielding a measured R28 of 52.8 MPa versus 52.6 MPa predicted (0.4% deviation); its fracture surface was examined by scanning electron microscopy. The predicted ternary mixture reaches R28 = 55.2 MPa (+24% over the control, attributable to the lower water content and the assumed packing bonus; mean-based class B40) with a 28-day capillary porosity of 0.160 versus 0.223 (−28%), lowering the paste-permeability index to about one-third of the control’s, and utilizes 120 kg of industrial by-products per cubic meter while avoiding at least 72 kg of binder-related CO2. The GOST durability grades (frost resistance, water impermeability, abrasion, sulfate resistance) are deliberately not predicted and await the ongoing laboratory campaign; the work is therefore a computational mix-design study with a single measured verification composition.

title: Green Project Management and Performance of its Projects in the Telecommunication Companies in Kenya
source: Journal of Entrepreneurship and Project Management
summary: Purpose: The general objective of this study is to examine the effect of green project management on performance of IT projects in the telecommunication companies in Kenya. This study was guided by the following theories; Resource-Based Vie
content: Purpose: The general objective of this study is to examine the effect of green project management on performance of IT projects in the telecommunication companies in Kenya. This study was guided by the following theories; Resource-Based View (RBV) Theory and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). Methodology: This study adopted a descriptive research design and focused on telecommunication companies in Kenya. According to the Communications Authority of Kenya (2024), there are 11 registered telecommunication companies. The target population comprised 352 respondents, including project managers, IT specialists, engineers, sustainability officers, procurement officers, and operations managers involved in green project management and project performance. Using the Krejcie and Morgan (1970) formula, a sample size of 187 employees was determined. Stratified random sampling was used to categorize respondents into strata, after which simple random sampling was applied to select participants. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires, while a pilot study involving 28 respondents was conducted to test the instrument’s validity and reliability. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential statistics, including Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. Findings: The study concludes that resource management and stakeholder engagement have a positive and significant effect on performance of IT projects in the telecommunication companies in Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: Based on the findings, the study recommends that telecommunication companies in Kenya should institutionalize stakeholder engagement by involving key stakeholders throughout the IT project lifecycle. This can be achieved through regular consultations, timely communication, collaborative decision-making, and structured feedback mechanisms to ensure stakeholder needs and expectations are effectively addressed.

title: Building Credible Sustainability Governance: Integrating Sustainability Performance, Sustainability Audits, and Greenwashing Risk
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT As sustainability disclosure requirements expand and regulatory scrutiny intensifies, greenwashing has emerged as a material ethical and governance risk. Drawing on stakeholder, legitimacy, and agency theories, this study develops
content: ABSTRACT As sustainability disclosure requirements expand and regulatory scrutiny intensifies, greenwashing has emerged as a material ethical and governance risk. Drawing on stakeholder, legitimacy, and agency theories, this study develops a governance framework integrating environmental sustainability, social sustainability, sustainability audits, and greenwashing risk indicators. DEMATEL was used to examine expert‐perceived structural interdependencies among the four dimensions, while PIPRECIA derived priority weights for 22 sub‐criteria. The results indicate that sustainability audit independence, occupational health and safety practices, unverifiable sustainability claims, and discrepancies between disclosed information and actual practices received the highest priority weights in the expert‐based assessment. Kendall's W showed varying levels of inter‐expert concordance across dimensions, whereas Leave‐One‐Expert‐Out analysis indicated that the aggregated priority structure remained internally stable when individual experts were excluded. Overall, the findings emphasize substantive performance, independent audit mechanisms, operational transparency, and verifiable disclosures as central to sustainability credibility, supporting a governance‐oriented interpretation of greenwashing as a systemic rather than solely communicative problem.

title: Advanced chemical looping-based reverse water–gas shift for methanol production: A techno-economic analysis
summary: The transition to a low-carbon economy has driven significant interest in green methanol as a sustainable energy vector and potential platform chemical intermediate; however, the incumbent production pathway via the reverse water-gas shift
content: The transition to a low-carbon economy has driven significant interest in green methanol as a sustainable energy vector and potential platform chemical intermediate; however, the incumbent production pathway via the reverse water-gas shift reaction is hindered by thermodynamic equilibrium limitations and energy-intensive separation steps. This study presents a comparative techno-economic assessment of a novel chemical looping reverse water-gas shift process against the conventional reverse water-gas shift route. Integration of experimental reactor data into rigorous process models demonstrates that the chemical looping pathway overcomes equilibrium constraints, achieving high single-pass carbon dioxide conversion (94% at 650°C) and inherent product separation. This process intensification eliminates the need for syngas recycling, resulting in a reduction of approximately 21% in feedstock requirements and a decrease of 49% in electricity consumption compared to the conventional benchmark. Economically, these technical advantages translate into a net production cost of 2.17 USD per kilogram of methanol, representing a 30% reduction from the 3.12 USD per kilogram estimated for the conventional route. Finally, sensitivity analysis identifies the market price of low-carbon hydrogen as the critical economic driver, revealing that, despite the superior efficiency of the chemical looping design, the commercial viability of both pathways remains fundamentally tied to future reductions in feedstock costs.

title: Cell teardown and post mortem degradation analysis of commercial 18650 sodium-ion batteries
summary: Commercial sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are entering the market, increasing the need to understand how cell design and chemistry influence degradation. This single sample case study combines teardown, electrochemical testing and post mortem
content: Commercial sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are entering the market, increasing the need to understand how cell design and chemistry influence degradation. This single sample case study combines teardown, electrochemical testing and post mortem analyses of three commercial 18650 cells: NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM)||hard carbon (HC) cells NFM-1200 and NFM-1500, and a Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF)||HC cell (NVPF-700), named according to manufacturer-specified nominal capacities (mAh). Among the investigated cells, NFM-1500 had the highest cathode loading, areal capacity and cell-level energy density. During long-term cycling, NFM-1500 reached 80% of its initial discharge capacity after approximately 500 cycles, whereas NFM-1200 underwent greater relative capacity loss over extended cycling. NVPF-700 retained approximately 600 mAh after 3000 cycles (97% of its initial 1C discharge capacity, approximately 620 mAh). For the individual cells investigated, higher rate capability was observed for the NFM-based cells compared to NVPF-700. Post mortem analyses revealed pronounced electrolyte decomposition and Ni/Mn/Fe deposition on HC in NFM-1500. In NVPF-700, a mixed NaPF 6 /NaFSI electrolyte with additives (succinonitrile, VC, FEC, BF 4 − and DFP) and V deposition on HC were identified. Different degradation rankings under long-term cycling and C-Rate testing revealed that observed aging depends on active material chemistry, electrode loading, morphology, electrolyte formulation and cycling protocol, with cell-to-cell variability remaining a potential factor.

title: Beyond Concrete: Evaluating the Adoption Potential of Indigenous Building Materials for Sustainable and Affordable Housing in Ado-Ekiti, Nigeria
source: International Journal of Innovative Research in Multidisciplinary Education
summary: A technical committee set up by Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development recently placed the national housing shortfall at 14.925 million units [1] a figure that, however one reads it, still points to a market unable to k
content: A technical committee set up by Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development recently placed the national housing shortfall at 14.925 million units [1] a figure that, however one reads it, still points to a market unable to keep pace with demand. Much of that shortfall traces back to construction costs, and in cities such as Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, that cost pressure sits awkwardly alongside deep reserves of laterite, clay and timber that go largely untapped. This paper sets out to measure how far indigenous materials have actually penetrated construction practice in Ado-Ekiti and to identify, in the words of the professionals and artisans who make the buying decisions, what pushes adoption forward and what holds it back. A structured questionnaire was administered to a stratified random sample of 80 respondents 20 Estate Surveyors and Valuers and 60 bricklayers drawn from a population of 200 registered practitioners, of whom 74 returned usable responses (92.5%). Rather than stopping at frequencies and mean scores, the analysis was carried a step further: a Pearson chi-square goodness-of-fit test was run to check whether the observed pattern of material use could plausibly be due to chance, and the Relative Importance Index (RII) was computed to place every rated benefit, challenge, adoption factor and promotion strategy on a common 0–1 scale. Laterite/earth blocks (47.3%) and mud bricks (27.0%) turned out to dominate usage, a pattern the chi-square test confirms is statistically non-random (χ² = 68.71, df = 5, p < 0.001). Respondents rate lower cost as both the leading benefit (RII = 0.83) and the leading adoption factor (RII = 0.82), while durability (RII = 0.79) and a shortage of technical know-how (RII = 0.78) are flagged as the sharpest constraints. Government subsidy schemes (RII = 0.81) and public enlightenment campaigns (RII = 0.79) are judged the most workable routes to wider adoption. Taken together, the results point toward a policy mix targeted incentives, hands-on artisan training, and formal recognition of local materials in building codes capable of turning Ado-Ekiti's untapped natural resource base into a genuine supply of affordable, low-carbon housing.

title: Advancing Seismic Resilience & Low-Carbon Design: Shake-Table Experiments of Full-Scale Building Envelopes and Partitions
summary: Developing resilient eco-friendly building elements is essential for enhancing occupant safety, reducing monetary loss and minimizing whole-life environmental impacts. This is particularly true for façades and partitions, which influence a
content: Developing resilient eco-friendly building elements is essential for enhancing occupant safety, reducing monetary loss and minimizing whole-life environmental impacts. This is particularly true for façades and partitions, which influence a building’s energy efficiency and can be highly vulnerable during low-to-moderate intensity earthquakes. Yet, despite their widespread use in modern construction, systems such as ventilated façades and glass curtain walls remain insufficiently studied in terms of seismic performance, especially when considering emerging solutions that incorporate low-carbon materials and damage-control detailing. The ERIES-BIOFACE project addresses this knowledge gap through full-scale shake-table testing on alternative components: timber vs. aluminum unitized curtain walls, ventilated façades with bio-based vs. aluminum claddings, and a gypsum partition with corner joints. This paper presents the entire experimental campaign, detailing specimen configurations, test phases and matrices, monitoring approach. Tests were performed on the EUCENTRE 9-D shake table, allowing realistic two-story simulations under combined acceleration and drift demands. Preliminary results indicate minimal or no damage at drift levels exceeding 1.0%, highlighting the strong potential of low-carbon low-damage non-structural solutions for seismic applications.

title: Thematic modeling and quantitative evaluation of China’s silver economy policies: based on the BERTopic and PMC-index model
summary: Introduction As an inevitable outcome of global population aging, the silver economy has been elevated to a national strategic priority for actively responding to demographic aging and fostering new drivers of economic growth. China is curr
content: Introduction As an inevitable outcome of global population aging, the silver economy has been elevated to a national strategic priority for actively responding to demographic aging and fostering new drivers of economic growth. China is currently in a critical phase in which the scope and connotations of the silver economy are undergoing continuous expansion. There is thus an urgent need to systematically assess key issues in its institutional design and policy implementation in order to optimize these processes. This study aims to perform thematic modeling and quantitative evaluation of silver economy policies by integrating the BERTopic model and the Policy Modeling Consistency Index (PMC-Index) model. Methods This study retrieved policy documents from specialized policy databases and official government portals, excluded expired or invalid documents, and ultimately included 127 valid policy texts from which 1,321 provisions with independent policy meanings were extracted as units of analysis. The BERTopic corpus covers the period 2004–2025, encompassing national guidelines and specific action plans. BERTopic was employed to perform thematic clustering and identify latent thematic structures across the policy texts. Drawing on 10 primary variables, this study constructed 50 secondary variables using a binary coding system to objectively quantify policy content. The PMC-Index was then calculated for 14 representative provincial- and municipal-level policy samples issued between 2024 and 2026 via a multi-input–output matrix, and PMC-Surface diagrams were generated using Python to provide an intuitive illustration of policy consistency and deficiencies across dimensions. Results The BERTopic model identified a total of 16 core themes, including the development of the older adult care industry, integrated medical and older adult care services, financial innovation for the older adults, and the senior consumer market, demonstrating significant characteristics of diverse synergy and an industrial ecosystem. The average PMC-Index for the 14 policies was 6.86, placing their design quality in the good category overall. Regionally, policies in East China, South China, Southwest China and Northeast China covered a wider range of topics, whereas those in Central and Northwest China tended to remain concentrated on basic older adult care security, with both depth and breadth requiring further expansion. Dimensionally, Policy Nature and Policy Domain scored the highest at 0.87 and 0.78, while Policy Object, Policy Perspective, and Policy Instruments remained at a moderate level with scores of 0.71, 0.67, and 0.65. Policy Timeliness, Policy Content, and Policy Evaluation constituted the primary areas of weakness with scores of 0.57, 0.62, and 0.63. Discussion Future policy refinement should center on five interrelated priorities: establishing clear target frameworks and implementation roadmaps, strengthening cultural values with technological applications, pro
