title: Integrated hybrid renewable energy systems for produced water treatment: a systematic review of advanced technologies, techno-economics, and industrial scale-up
summary: The most abundant wastewater stream from oil and gas extraction is produced water (PW), which exceeds 250 million barrels per day globally, containing high levels dissolved solids (0.1–400 g/L), hydrocarbons, heavy metals and toxic organics
content: The most abundant wastewater stream from oil and gas extraction is produced water (PW), which exceeds 250 million barrels per day globally, containing high levels dissolved solids (0.1–400 g/L), hydrocarbons, heavy metals and toxic organics that pose serious environmental and operational issues for treatment. Traditional treatment technologies often do not provide sustainable reuse and zero liquid discharge (ZLD), particularly as regulations become more stringent and water becomes scarce. This review critically evaluates the latest developments of hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) (solar, wind, and geothermal) coupled with produced water treatment technologies (conventional, membrane, electrochemical, thermal and zero-liquid discharge), with a focus on techno-economic feasibility, sustainability, specific energy consumption, levelized cost of water, and technology readiness level, and scalability aspects. Reverse osmosis remains the most mature option (TRL 9, 3.0–3.5 kWh/m 3 , $0.50–2.50/m 3 ), but costs rise to $9.00–57.70/m 3 for hypersaline brine management; solar-thermal integration cuts levelized costs from $2.5/m 3 to $1.5/m 3 , and emerging trains such as forward osmosis-membrane distillation recover up to 98% of water from feeds as saline as 133 g/L TDS. This review highlights some of the major hurdles to the commercialisation of the technology, including membrane fouling, scaling, intermittent renewable energy supply and reliance on short (10–30 days) pilots using synthetic rather than real produced water remain the key barriers to industrial adoption. It explores new developments such as the application of artificial intelligence, smart monitoring, new materials for membranes and resource recovery using the principles of the circular economy. The review concludes with an overview of the strategic direction of the oil and gas industry’s produced water management to achieve sustainable, long-duration field validation on real PW, AI-driven adaptive control, standardized techno-economic reporting, and resource recovery (e.g., lithium, strontium) to shift PW management from a disposal burden toward a circular, low-carbon resource stream.

title: Digital rural transformation, financial assets, and rural household wellbeing
summary: Existing research treats rural digitalization mainly as a transaction-cost shock and pays little attention to a second margin: by improving access to financial services, markets and investment opportunities, digital rural transformation may
content: Existing research treats rural digitalization mainly as a transaction-cost shock and pays little attention to a second margin: by improving access to financial services, markets and investment opportunities, digital rural transformation may enable rural households to accumulate financial assets and thereby improve their economic well-being. Using pooled panel data from the 2015, 2017 and 2019 waves of the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS), we empirically analyze the impact of digital rural transformation on rural households' consumption structure and the mediating role of financial assets. The findings reveal that digital rural transformation significantly raises rural households' financial asset holdings and the income those assets generate, and that this accumulation accounts for part of the subsequent shift toward development and enjoyment-oriented consumption. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that younger, more educated, married rural households with higher wage income, loans, and those in less developed regions benefit more from digital rural transformation. The central contribution of this study is to establish financial asset accumulation as a rural livelihood mechanism through which digital rural transformation operates, thereby offering a new theoretical perspective for rural consumption research in the digital economy era.

title: You can swim naked, you can run barefoot. Performance-enhancing technologies in non-technological sports: a restrictive view
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
summary: This article reflects upon innovative performance-enhancing technologies in sports not requiring technological means such as swimming and running. From the perspectives of sport fairness, equal opportunity and the nature of sport as a test
content: This article reflects upon innovative performance-enhancing technologies in sports not requiring technological means such as swimming and running. From the perspectives of sport fairness, equal opportunity and the nature of sport as a test and comparison of individual performance capacity, swimming competition should, arguably be conducted naked. Similarly, humans can run barefoot. Introducing footwear that enhances performance raises the same fairness challenges and discussions on the nature of sport as performance-enhancing swimwear. Performance enhancement due to technological innovation in non-technological sports may introduce unfairness and by upsetting an athlete’s intrinsic performance capacity challenge the nature of sport. Sports technology development in non-technological sports should not be discouraged but needs to be considered from a restrictive perspective.

title: Influence of Technical Vocational Education and Training on Skills Gap in the Masonry Workforce in Moroto District, Eastern Uganda
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: This research report aimed to investigate how Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) influences the skills gap of masonry workers in Moroto District, Eastern Uganda. Even though there has been an emphasis on TVET to address the
content: This research report aimed to investigate how Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) influences the skills gap of masonry workers in Moroto District, Eastern Uganda. Even though there has been an emphasis on TVET to address the skills gap, the masonry trade continues to experience a significant shortage of skilled workers. This study sought to: (i) identify the effect of TVET on the skill level of masonry workers; (ii) establish the skills gap in masonry; and (iii) assess the influence factors on TVET.

title: Extending building longevity: wood-based product–service systems
summary: Wood has been considered renewable, low-carbon and flexible for use in buildings. Product–service system (PSS) configurations related to building longevity are identified by using PSS archetypes as analytical lenses. These PSS configuration
content: Wood has been considered renewable, low-carbon and flexible for use in buildings. Product–service system (PSS) configurations related to building longevity are identified by using PSS archetypes as analytical lenses. These PSS configurations of buildings containing wood are assessed against resource efficiency (RE) and circular economy (CE) hierarchies. Qualitative interviews (n = 31) from Finland provide insights into opportunities for timber products in the building sector. The use of timber in construction and retrofit innovations is examined for flexibility and extending building lifespans. Lower-level practices from CE hierarchies (e.g. material recycling) appeared more institutionalised while higher-level practices from RE hierarchy (e.g. use of vacant spaces) seemed to be more in their early stages. As a response to the expected market growth, innovation bundles were found to centre around new construction, lacking a needed emphasis shift to sharing spaces and building retrofits. PRACTICE RELEVANCE This study makes a case for stronger integration of PSS thinking into timber construction and retrofits. Developing such solutions requires greater co-creation with multiple stakeholders involved during the building life-cycle, including the integration of end-user and living phase aspects into building planning. Future legislation and policy could support this development at the national and city policy levels by encouraging renovation, adaptability and incorporation of services that extend building longevity.

title: Day-Ahead Optimal Scheduling of Port Microgrid Considering the Synergy of Energy, Frequency Regulation, and Carbon Markets
summary: To deeply tap the response potential of flexible resources and expand multi-level market interaction channels, an optimization scheduling strategy for port microgrids is proposed, considering multi-market coordination and refined modeling o
content: To deeply tap the response potential of flexible resources and expand multi-level market interaction channels, an optimization scheduling strategy for port microgrids is proposed, considering multi-market coordination and refined modeling of underlying equipment. First, a collaborative optimization scheduling model for the port microgrid encompassing the day-ahead energy market, frequency regulation ancillary service market, and carbon trading market is constructed. Second, a collaborative response model for differentiated flexible loads is developed on the load side, establishing a multi-step staircase regulation mechanism for interruptible load (IL) and accounting for the sequential regulation characteristics of shiftable load (SL). Simultaneously, the hydrogen production load is categorized under transferable load (TL), and a model for the hydrogen production load with power-efficiency characteristics is established. The piecewise linearization method is utilized to correct scheduling command deviations caused by constant efficiency assumptions in traditional models. Subsequently, a two-stage robust optimization model was constructed for the multiple uncertainties on both the source and load sides, and the Column and Constraint Generation (C&CG) algorithm was adopted for solution. Simulation results under the testbed demonstrate that the proposed strategy exhibits substantial potential in coordinating economic benefits and carbon reduction, providing a viable methodological reference for multi-resource dispatch in port microgrids.

title: Reallocating rural land for sustainable livelihoods: the impact of residential land reform on farmers' incomes in China
summary: Introduction Rural residential land serves as a vital foundation for rural socioeconomic development, and reforming its utilization is crucial for farmers’ livelihoods and sustainable rural development. Methods To systematically evaluate th
content: Introduction Rural residential land serves as a vital foundation for rural socioeconomic development, and reforming its utilization is crucial for farmers’ livelihoods and sustainable rural development. Methods To systematically evaluate the micro-level welfare effects of this land use transition, particularly the reform of the rural residential land system, this paper treats China’s pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment. Using county-level panel data and a staggered difference-in-differences method, we assess the policy’s impact on farmers’ income and its underlying mechanisms. Results The results indicate that the reform of the rural residential land system significantly promotes farmers’ income growth. Mechanism tests suggest that this effect is achieved through the optimal allocation of both land and labor resources: first, the spatial optimization of land resources, which promotes the integration of agricultural industries; and second, the reallocation of household labor, which drives labor participation in non-agricultural employment while optimizing agricultural labor efficiency. Furthermore, the transfer of farmland exerts a significant positive moderating effect, amplifying the reform’s role in promoting farmers’ income growth. Discussion However, further analysis reveals disparities in welfare distribution, as the policy has raised urban residents’ incomes to a greater extent; therefore, institutional arrangements should be further refined to focus on enhancing the welfare gains of rural residents from the reform.

title: Glyphosate and AMPA in a coastal agricultural landscape of Northwestern Mexico: sales, usage, and field-scale impact indicators
summary: Background Glyphosate (GLP) is the most widely used herbicide worldwide, yet understanding of its environmental impacts and patterns of use remains limited. This study evaluates GLP occurrence within a coastal agricultural landscape in nort
content: Background Glyphosate (GLP) is the most widely used herbicide worldwide, yet understanding of its environmental impacts and patterns of use remains limited. This study evaluates GLP occurrence within a coastal agricultural landscape in northwestern Mexico by combining water monitoring, sales patterns, usage proxies derived from container census data, and field-use Environmental Impact Quotient (EIQf) metrics. Methods A total of 51 water samples, including groundwater (wells) and surface water (drains and estuaries), were collected across an approximately 30,000-hectare agricultural area and analyzed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS/MS). Results GLP presented residues in one well water sample (0.80 μg/L), while aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA) presented in well and drain water (0.48–2.85 μg/L). GLP accounted for 93% of total herbicide sales in the study area, and five commercial formulations were identified, with EIQf values ranging from 49.8 to 99.5. Conclusion The integration of environmental detection data, sales patterns, and impact indicators provides new insights into GLP dispersion within a hydrologically connected coastal agricultural system. These findings support the relevance of multi-compartment monitoring approaches for understanding herbicide dynamics in complex agricultural landscapes.

title: Harnessing Circadian Resilience for Demand-Flexible Controlled Environment Agriculture
summary: The increasing penetration of renewable electricity generation creates opportunities for flexible demand-side energy management in Total Controlled Environment Agriculture (TCEA), where artificial lighting represents a major operational cos
content: The increasing penetration of renewable electricity generation creates opportunities for flexible demand-side energy management in Total Controlled Environment Agriculture (TCEA), where artificial lighting represents a major operational cost. However, the biological consequences of demand-responsive lighting strategies remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether photoperiods can be dynamically adjusted to minimise economic costs or maximise renewable energy utilisation while maintaining crop productivity. Using historical electricity market and wind-generation data, we evaluated three demand-flexing strategies: short-term demand-side response (DSR) events, cost-optimised photoperiods aligned with low electricity prices, and wind-optimised photoperiods aligned with periods of high renewable generation. Despite substantial variation in photoperiod length, plants maintained robust circadian rhythms under both cost- and wind-optimised regimes, demonstrating considerable resilience of the circadian system to irregular environmental timing. Commercial-scale trials involving basil, lettuce, mustard greens and rocket revealed that demand-flexed lighting regimes had minimal effects on harvested fresh or dry weight. Our findings demonstrate that TCEA can provide meaningful demand-side flexibility and support renewable energy integration without substantial reductions in crop productivity. Circadian resilience appears to buffer plants against fluctuating photoperiods, providing a biological foundation for the deployment of demand-flexible lighting strategies in future low-carbon agricultural systems.

title: D is for deposit: extending Europe’s carbon storage obligation to account for all hydrocarbons
summary: The European Union has made carbon capture and storage a legal objective, but who pays to unlock geological storage, and on what terms, remains open. Article 23 of the Net-Zero Industry Act obliges only the domestic EU oil and gas producers
content: The European Union has made carbon capture and storage a legal objective, but who pays to unlock geological storage, and on what terms, remains open. Article 23 of the Net-Zero Industry Act obliges only the domestic EU oil and gas producers, while most oil and gas reaches the Single Market with no storage duty. We propose a storage deposit made at first sale of oil and gas, by domestic and imported supply alike, at one rate. It is redeemed only against injected tonnes of CO₂, each counted once whatever its origin; deposits not redeemed within three years forfeit to a ring-fenced fund for transport and storage infrastructure. The rate is set at T&S cost and capped at one stored tonne per tonne sold, beyond which policy for carbon dioxide removal takes over. We size the deposit for three volume scenarios and two storage pathways. Under the European Commission’s pathway, €268bn is paid in over 2030–2050 at €72/tCO₂; most is returned on redemption, and about 10% forfeits if storage runs five years late. The deposit adds €5–17 to a barrel of oil in 2040 and reaches the cap before 2050 in three of six scenario combinations. Tested against six conditions (verification, redemption, ring-fence, coverage, handover, and legal basis), it meets the five design conditions, most with a stated concession, and its legal route is plausible. Extending the take-back logic of Article 23 to every seller would let the EU set the terms of access to its hydrocarbon market.

title: Can UK green hydrogen contracts for difference (CfDs) match the cost-saving success of renewable electricity?
source: Energy Sources Part B Economics Planning and Policy
summary: Contracts for Difference (CfDs) drove down renewable electricity costs and are now applied to low-carbon hydrogen. This paper compares UK hydrogen CfDs under the Hydrogen Allocation Rounds (HAR) with renewable electricity CfDs, combining co
content: Contracts for Difference (CfDs) drove down renewable electricity costs and are now applied to low-carbon hydrogen. This paper compares UK hydrogen CfDs under the Hydrogen Allocation Rounds (HAR) with renewable electricity CfDs, combining cost-structure, variance-decomposition and demand-scenario analysis. Four asymmetries emerge. First, electricity rather than capital dominates the levelised cost of green hydrogen in central cases. Second, the CfD removes output-price risk but leaves input-price and utilization risk, which dominate residual producer variance. Third, volume support is bounded and conditional, and lapses at zero sales, so it protects least when demand collapses. Fourth, weak demand worsens the ratio of public support to abatement rather than raising per-unit subsidy, and the resulting cost per tonne of CO2 avoided remains well above the UK carbon price across the allocation-round trajectory examined. Hydrogen CfDs can support early market formation, but replicating renewable cost reductions requires complementary instruments sequenced across allocation rounds.

title: Creative Overcome Theory: A Systems-Theoretical Approach to How Innovation-Based Learning Drives Evolution
summary: This paper introduces the Creative Overcome Theory (COT), a systems-theoretical approach proposing innovation-based learning as the primary driver of evolution. According to this framework, natural selection is a consequence rather than the
content: This paper introduces the Creative Overcome Theory (COT), a systems-theoretical approach proposing innovation-based learning as the primary driver of evolution. According to this framework, natural selection is a consequence rather than the cause of evolutionary dynamics. Life is defined as matter that learns by improving its capacity for innovation. This is achieved through the integration and progressive refinement of processes that support more responsive, structured and regulated forms of innovation. The organic systems that succeed are those that enhance their search efficiency over time, leading to a progressive accumulation of creative capacity and the consequent expansion of the adaptive adjacent possible. This perspective accounts not only for major evolutionary transitions but also for the emergence of intelligence, agency, cognition, purpose, and free will. Conclusion: With a broad explanatory power, COT provides a more consilient, bottom-up explanation that integrates cosmic, chemical, biological, and cultural dynamics within a unified evolutionary synthesis.

title: Cereal δ15N values link agricultural intensification to rising human nitrogen isotope values in Lithuania
summary: Stable isotope analysis of human bone collagen from Vilnius shows an increase in δ 15 N values from 1500 AD. This increase is conventionally attributed to greater consumption of animal protein. However, the δ 15 N values also reflect the ni
content: Stable isotope analysis of human bone collagen from Vilnius shows an increase in δ 15 N values from 1500 AD. This increase is conventionally attributed to greater consumption of animal protein. However, the δ 15 N values also reflect the nitrogen isotope baseline of food chain, which can be elevated by agricultural intensification and manuring. Because cereals formed a major part of the diet, intensified manuring would have raised crop δ 15 N values and, in turn, those of consumers, causing dietary reconstructions to overestimate animal protein intake. To test this, we compiled δ 15 N values from Lithuania spanning from the Mesolithic to the 18th century for cereals ( n = 285, including 100 newly analyzed grains), wild and domestic fauna ( n = 291) and humans ( n = 584 from 71 site). Cereal and human δ 15 N values both increase starting from Early Modern period (1500-1800 AD), whereas faunal values remain largely stable, consistent with livestock being fed on wild herbs and low-δ 15 N straw and chaff rather than grain. This pattern coincides with Volok Reform of 1557, which imposed a state-wide three-field rotation and more systematic manure management. We argue that agricultural intensification contributed substantially, though probably not exclusively, to the rise in human δ 15 N values, and that crop isotope baselines must be incorporated into paleodietary reconstructions to avoid overestimating animal protein consumption in historical populations.

title: Impact Strength Comparison of Heat-Polymerized PMMA and Graphene-Reinforced Pre-Polymerized PMMA (G-CAM) as Provisional Restorative Materials: An In Vitro Study
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Objective: To evaluate and compare the impact strength of heat-polymerized polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) and graphene-reinforced pre-polymerized PMMA (G-CAM) used as provisional restorative materials. Materials and Methods: Twenty standard
content: Objective: To evaluate and compare the impact strength of heat-polymerized polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) and graphene-reinforced pre-polymerized PMMA (G-CAM) used as provisional restorative materials. Materials and Methods: Twenty standardized specimens were fabricated and divided into two groups (n = 10 each): Group A, heat-polymerized PMMA (DPI Heat Cure); and Group B, graphene-reinforced pre-polymerized PMMA (G-CAM, Graphenano Dental). All specimens were tested using an Izod impact testing machine at 23 ± 2°C. Impact strength values were recorded in kJ/mm², and data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and unpaired t-tests. Results: Group A (heat-polymerized PMMA) demonstrated a mean impact strength of 3.03 kJ/mm² (SD = 1.34), whereas Group B (graphene-reinforced G-CAM) showed a mean of 1.63 kJ/mm² (SD = 0.77). The intergroup difference was statistically significant (t = 2.841; p = 0.011). Conclusions: Conventional heat-polymerized PMMA exhibited significantly superior impact strength compared with the graphene-reinforced pre-polymerized PMMA tested in this study. Although graphene-based materials remain promising for certain dental applications, the specific G-CAM formulation evaluated did not improve impact resistance and is therefore not recommended as a substitute for conventional PMMA when impact strength is a primary clinical consideration.

title: How can polymer upcycling produce products valuable enough to compete economically with virgin petrochemicals
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This revised article addresses Q0149, 'How can polymer upcycling produce products valuable enough to compete economically with virgin petrochemicals?' using a question-specific mathematical construction rather than a generic logarithmic tem
content: This revised article addresses Q0149, 'How can polymer upcycling produce products valuable enough to compete economically with virgin petrochemicals?' using a question-specific mathematical construction rather than a generic logarithmic template. The proposed model, termed the Polymer Upcycling Value-Energy Model, uses product value V_p, product yield Y, process energy E, feedstock cost C_f and carbon/lifecycle penalty L and is ordered along process scale and product slate. The construction is anchored to external primary research classified as DIRECT SUPPORT in the validation atlas. The external evidence establishes experimentally measurable mechanisms or target performance; it is not conflated with proof of the new equation itself. The model defines explicit state variables, derives a dimensionless objective or hazard, specifies a prospective calibration procedure, and states falsifiable predictions. The experimental constraint carried forward from the atlas is: Upcycling produces high-value products and some studies include techno-economic/LCA analysis; broad market competitiveness is context-dependent. The article incorporates the required correction: Add price/energy sensitivity and scale factors.

title: Microorganism Content in Soils of Organic Apple Production in the Elmalı District, Antalya Province, Türkiye
summary: Soil microorganisms play important roles in nutrient cycling, organic matter transformation, plant growth, and the biological regulation of soil-borne organisms. However, information on the culturable microbial populations associated with o
content: Soil microorganisms play important roles in nutrient cycling, organic matter transformation, plant growth, and the biological regulation of soil-borne organisms. However, information on the culturable microbial populations associated with organically managed apple orchards in the Elmalı district of Antalya, Türkiye, remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the culturable bacterial and fungal populations present in soils from organically managed apple orchards and to identify selected microbial isolates using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS). Soil samples were collected from ten organically managed apple orchards in the Elmalı district during the apple harvest period. Culturable bacteria and fungi were isolated using Nutrient Agar and Potato Dextrose Agar, respectively. Microbial population densities were determined by the colony-forming unit (CFU) method. Bacterial isolates were preliminarily characterized according to their Gram reaction using the KOH test, and selected bacterial and fungal isolates were identified by MALDI-TOF MS. The mean culturable bacterial population density across the sampled orchards was (1.21 x 106) CFU/mL, whereas the mean fungal population density was (4.96 x 104) CFU/mL, indicating that the bacterial population was approximately 24-fold higher than the fungal population. Among 93 bacterial isolates, 54 (58.1%) were classified as presumptive Gram-positive and 39 (41.9%) as presumptive Gram-negative. MALDI-TOF MS identified bacterial isolates belonging to Brevundimonas diminuta, Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis, Bacillus subtilis, Bacillus atrophaeus, Pseudomonas chlororaphis, Priestia megaterium and Bacillus mojavensis. The identified fungal taxa included Penicillium citrinum, the Aspergillus flavus/oryzae group, Fusarium proliferatum, Aspergillus ochraceus, and Aspergillus niger. The results provide a preliminary characterization of the culturable microbial fraction of organically managed apple orchard soils in Elmalı and indicate the presence of bacterial and fungal taxa of potential interest for future agricultural studies. In particular, the recovery of several Bacillus, Pseudomonas and Priestia isolates provides a basis for subsequent investigations of plant-growth-promoting and biocontrol-related traits. However, the culture-dependent approach and the database-dependent nature of MALDI-TOF MS identification should be considered when interpreting the results. Further studies combining molecular identification, soil physicochemical analyses, and functional assays are required to determine the ecological and agronomic significance of the recovered microorganisms.

title: Physiological, metabolic and agronomic responses of potato plants to the application type and dosage of a flesh‐coloured potato extract under Rhizoctonia solani inoculation
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: BACKGROUND: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is a major global food crop whose productivity is affected by fungal pathogens such as Rhizoctonia solani. Conventional control relies on synthetic fungicides, which present limitations including pa
content: BACKGROUND: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is a major global food crop whose productivity is affected by fungal pathogens such as Rhizoctonia solani. Conventional control relies on synthetic fungicides, which present limitations including pathogen resistance and adverse physiological effects. Natural alternatives, particularly phenolic-rich extracts, have emerged as a sustainable strategy. Flesh-coloured potato (FCP), rich in anthocyanins and hydroxycinnamic acids, represents a potential source of bioactive compounds. RESULTS: total phenolics) on potato plants inoculated with R. solani, considering different application methods (immersion, soil application and spraying) and commercial fungicides as control. Photosynthetic traits, antioxidant responses, organic acid exudation and agronomic yield were assessed. Compared with inoculated controls and fungicide treatments, FCP treatments were associated with higher photosynthetic performance. Spraying at low dose increased photosynthetic rate and stomatal conductance, whereas soil application at high dose was associated with higher water use efficiency and tuber yield. Antioxidant enzyme activity and phenolic accumulation increased under FCP treatments, while fungicide treatments showed limited physiological responses. FCP also reduced oxalic acid exudation. Principal component analysis (PCA) indicated a dose and method dependent pattern in plant responses. CONCLUSION: Overall, FCP extract was associated with dose and method dependent physiological, metabolic and agronomic responses in potato plants under R. solani inoculation, supporting its potential as an alternative approach for crop management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Design-Stage Assessment of the IE3 Efficiency Margin of a 3 kW Induction Motor for Pump Applications Using Analytical, Finite Element and Equivalent-Circuit Models
source: Sürdürülebilir Mühendislik Uygulamaları ve Teknolojik Gelişmeler Dergisi
summary: Minimum energy performance standards increasingly require line-operated induction motors to reach the IE3 efficiency class, and small four-pole motors in centrifugal pump drives are among the machines most affected. For such motors, the mar
content: Minimum energy performance standards increasingly require line-operated induction motors to reach the IE3 efficiency class, and small four-pole motors in centrifugal pump drives are among the machines most affected. For such motors, the margin between the predicted efficiency and the IE3 limit can be only a few tenths of a percentage point, so its design-stage assessment is sensitive to the modelling tool and to the loss assumptions. This study evaluates the IE3 compliance of a 3 kW, 400 V, 50 Hz, four-pole, 36/28-slot squirrel-cage induction motor with a two-slot short-pitched winding. The motor was designed analytically and analysed with the Ansys RMxprt analytical solver and Maxwell 2D transient finite element analysis (FEA). An equivalent circuit identified from the RMxprt losses, a dynamic dq model and a winding-function model were used to interpret the FEA results, and the efficiency was evaluated for different stray-load-loss bases, lamination grades and supply voltages. RMxprt predicts an efficiency of 87.93%, 0.23 percentage points above the IE3 limit of 87.7%; this margin corresponds to only 8.8 W of additional loss. The uncorrected FEA power balance yields 90.3%; when the core and stray-load losses are included and the result is referred to the rated output of 3.00 kW, the FEA efficiency is 87.9–88.2% for two bookkeeping scenarios of a 12.7 W residual loss, in agreement with RMxprt. The IE3 margin is lost when the stray-load loss is taken from the IEC 60034-2-1 assigned allowance (86.74%), when M400-50A lamination is used (87.64%), or when a friction and windage loss of more than about 7 W is included. Short pitching reduces the fifth MMF harmonic from 4.5% to 0.8%, whereas its estimated effect on the efficiency is only about 0.1 percentage points. The FEA-based locked-rotor current is 6.8 times the rated current. These results are design-stage predictions; they show that IE3 assessments of small motors should be based on an explicit loss budget and confirmed by standardised testing.

title: Circular potential of insulating glass units—a sensitivity study on life cycle impact assessment
summary: Abstract Creating closed material loops through value-retention processes is essential for circular economy (CE) strategies in construction, particularly for energy-intensive materials such as glass in insulating glass units (IGUs). In prac
content: Abstract Creating closed material loops through value-retention processes is essential for circular economy (CE) strategies in construction, particularly for energy-intensive materials such as glass in insulating glass units (IGUs). In practice, IGUs are often demolished with a façade and treated as mixed construction-and-demolition waste, causing material dissipation and avoidable environmental burdens. Although circular approaches for IGUs are emerging, comparative life cycle impact assessments (LCIA) across realistic system boundaries and disassembly practices remain scarce due to construction diversity, limited data availability, and uncertainties in disassembly processes. This study addresses this gap by providing reproducible LCIAs of promising IGU end-of-life (EoL) scenarios based on ecoinvent data and literature. Prospective scenarios for treating obsolete IGUs and processing components into triple IGUs resemble a “grave-to-gate” phase beyond an IGU’s first life. This phase incorporates sequences of disassembly, quality assessment, transport and secondary manufacturing to quantify the Global Warming Potential of the scenarios in kg CO 2 -equivalent per square meter of triple IGU. Modelling approaches include best practice assumptions and scenario-based material flows. Results show promising potential for reducing the impact of triple IGUs through remanufacturing. Sensitivity analyses were conducted for transport and process parameters. The results show that the acceptance rate during qualification is the most important parameter for sustainable pathways. The transport analysis indicates that qualification and disassembly should be located close to the dismantling process where possible. This study’s results contribute to data-driven selection of sustainable pathways and to understanding the relevance of future research topics in circularity of architectural glass.

title: The solar PV supply strategy of the European Union: A cost-risk-diversification trade-off
summary: The European Union is rapidly expanding its solar photovoltaic capacity, yet demand is almost entirely met by imports from China, raising concerns about supply dependence and energy security. This study quantifies the cost-risk-diversificat
content: The European Union is rapidly expanding its solar photovoltaic capacity, yet demand is almost entirely met by imports from China, raising concerns about supply dependence and energy security. This study quantifies the cost-risk-diversification trade-offs in the European Union’s solar photovoltaic module supply strategy for 2030. We develop a global trade model for solar photovoltaic modules that simultaneously minimizes the conflicting objectives of supply costs, geopolitical risk, and supply concentration. A scenario analysis examines three possible pathways in 2030: a policy-as-usual pathway, a globalized market structure driven by cost competitiveness, and a pathway shaped by national reshoring. A Monte Carlo simulation assesses sensitivity to parameter uncertainty. The results reveal that although the European Union’s demand increases, its dependence on imports declines, primarily due to higher domestic production capacity and improved utilization rates. Adjusting the European Union’s supply strategy by reducing geopolitical risk and supply concentration entails additional costs of up to 155 USD/kW relative to 2024 levels, driven mainly by the module prices and trade tariffs of the chosen import suppliers. Based on these results, we derive three policy implications: (i) increasing domestic production capacity to 30 GW and raising the utilization rate above 90% to strengthen the European Union’s internal supply; (ii) expanding strategic partnerships with emerging suppliers such as Vietnam (trade frequency of 82%), Thailand (81%) and Malaysia (75%) to reduce supply concentration; (iii) defining explicit benchmarks for diversification (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index < 0.15 ) and geopolitical risk exposure (43% below 2024 values) to enhance supply-chain resilience.

title: Beyond Greenwashing: A Normative Evaluation of Environmental CSR in the Context of Bangladesh
summary: Bangladesh is a developing country with limited resources and several climate disasters. In this context, this research paper examines the gap between Environmental Corporate Social Responsibility (ECSR) and the underlying greenwashing prac
content: Bangladesh is a developing country with limited resources and several climate disasters. In this context, this research paper examines the gap between Environmental Corporate Social Responsibility (ECSR) and the underlying greenwashing practices. This paper reveals that Bangladesh is achieving significant economic growth through industrial development at the cost of ecological degradation. Corporations are using ECSR to gain an advantage in the competitive business world and to maintain a good public image while ignoring the actual environmental consequences. The root causes of greenwashing in Bangladesh are weak governance and regulatory system, corruption, judicial impediments, and lack of moral conscience. As a result, the genuine purpose of environmental corporate social responsibility goes in vain. This paper aims to construct a normative framework grounded on two philosophical theories for genuine ECSR. Based on the concept of stewardship of nature, eight key principles are suggested to evaluate ECSR activities for ensuring intergenerational justice. According to environmental stewardship, corporations should act as trustees instead of considering themselves as owners of natural resources. They should take initiatives focused on genuine environmental concern and act responsibly was for making the world livable for the future generations. After critical and qualitative analysis, some practical guidance is recommended for government and regulatory reformations, corporations, civil society, and international buyers. Philosophy and Progress, Vol#77-78; No#1-2; Jan-Dec 2025 P 647-675

title: Livelihoods of small-scale fishing communities depend on coastal wetlands
summary: Small-scale coral reef fisheries are a critical resource supporting the livelihoods and food security of tropical coastal communities. Management of these fisheries is generally focused on adult fish and their associated habitats, ignoring
content: Small-scale coral reef fisheries are a critical resource supporting the livelihoods and food security of tropical coastal communities. Management of these fisheries is generally focused on adult fish and their associated habitats, ignoring the juvenile and sub-adult phases and their associated habitats. Here we identified preferred nursery grounds of finfish species in the small-scale fisheries of the Honduran Caribbean, using landed catch data reported by fish buyers from 2019 to 2024. We observed a significant increase in mean landed catch per trip and mean landed value of the fishery across this period. Fish species that preferred coastal wetlands as their nursery habitat comprised 63.9% of the mean landed catch for the entire fishery, with a range of 57.5–76.4% across the departments of Cortés, Atlántida, and Colón. The average value per trip associated with coastal wetlands equated to 75.0% of the total value per trip, with a range of 68.4–80.8% across the three departments. These findings highlight the important role of coastal wetlands to coral reef fisheries and how these critical ecosystems support the livelihoods and local economies of coastal communities. As such, greater consideration needs to be given to a seascape approach to fisheries management, to ensure that the habitats utilized by fish species across their lifecycle are appropriately managed and protected. This is of particular importance as countries move to increase the amount of their exclusive economic zones under protection, in accordance with their 30 × 30 commitments under the Global Biodiversity Framework and Paris Agreement ambitions.

title: Procurement Outsourcing Strategies and Performance of Cement Manufacturing Companies in Machakos County, Kenya
source: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
summary: Purpose: This study focused on establishing the effects of procurement outsourcing strategies on performance of cement manufacturing companies in Machakos County, Kenya. This study was guided by Contingency Theory and Systems Theory. Method
content: Purpose: This study focused on establishing the effects of procurement outsourcing strategies on performance of cement manufacturing companies in Machakos County, Kenya. This study was guided by Contingency Theory and Systems Theory. Methodology: This study adopted a descriptive research design and focused on the seven cement manufacturing firms operating in Kenya: Bamburi Cement Limited, East Africa Portland Cement Company, ARM Africa Limited, Mombasa Cement, Savannah Cement, National Cement, and Lafarge Cement. The target population comprised 150 Procurement, Logistics, Finance, and Administrative Officers, who were selected due to their knowledge of procurement outsourcing practices. Using the Krejcie and Morgan (1970) formula, a sample size of 109 respondents was determined. Stratified random sampling was employed to categorize respondents into relevant strata, while simple random sampling was used to select participants from each stratum. Primary data were collected using questionnaires. Data analysis involved both descriptive and inferential statistics with the aid of SPSS version 25, and findings were presented using tables and figures. Findings: The study concludes that category-specific outsourcing has a positive and significant effect on performance of cement manufacturing companies in Machakos County, Kenya. The study also concludes that end-to-end outsourcing has a positive and significant effect on performance of cement manufacturing companies in Machakos County, Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: Based on the findings, the study recommends that cement manufacturing companies in Kenya should evaluate the performance of outsourcing providers regularly, establish clear contractual obligations and ensure that outsourced activities align with organizational objectives.

title: Ration Optimization and Sensitivity Analysis via Linear Programming in Dairy Farms: A Case Study of Niğde Province
summary: Feed costs constitute a major component of total production costs in dairy farming enterprises. In this study, ration optimization was performed using linear programming (Simplex method) based on field data obtained from dairy farms in Niğd
content: Feed costs constitute a major component of total production costs in dairy farming enterprises. In this study, ration optimization was performed using linear programming (Simplex method) based on field data obtained from dairy farms in Niğde province. The nutritional requirements of dairy cows with an average live weight of 600 kg and a daily milk yield of 23 liters (dry matter, crude protein, metabolizable energy, calcium, and phosphorus) were defined as constraints. The model was solved using MS Excel Solver, and current and optimal rations were compared in terms of cost. The results indicated that the optimized rations provided an average daily cost saving of 61.39 TL per animal (14.98%). title: Traceability as a Quality Cue: How Consumers Respond to Product‐Level Information
summary: ABSTRACT Food supply chains have become longer, more fragmented and less visible to the people at the end of them, leaving consumers unable to verify the safety, provenance and ethical credentials of what they buy and firms unable to demons
content: ABSTRACT Food supply chains have become longer, more fragmented and less visible to the people at the end of them, leaving consumers unable to verify the safety, provenance and ethical credentials of what they buy and firms unable to demonstrate them credibly. Against this background of growing supply chain complexity and consumer uncertainty, we examine whether traceability information functions as a quality cue in meat consumption and how it influences purchase intentions. Focusing on electronic identification (eID)‐enabled lamb traceability in Australia, we employ a multi‐study, mixed‐method design. Study 1 ( n = 10) explores consumer perceptions through in‐depth interviews. Study 2a conducts a pilot, whereas Study 2b uses a Facebook A/B field experiment to test behavioural responses in a natural setting. Study 3 ( n = 402) applies an online experiment to test a moderated mediation model. Qualitative findings show generally favourable attitudes, linking traceability to quality, safety and assurance. Whereas the field experiment shows no significant behavioural effect, the controlled experiment demonstrates that traceability increases purchase intention via perceived product quality, with stronger effects for highly involved consumers. Findings suggest that traceability can serve as a strategic, institutionally verified quality signal but that its effectiveness is conditional on consumer involvement and communication context. For firms and policymakers, this suggests that the consumer‐facing returns on traceability investment depend not only on verifying information but also on how that verified information is communicated at the point of choice.

title: Influence of the rural digital economy on rural innovation and entrepreneurship: evidence from counties in China
summary: The rural digital economy (RDE) has the potential to support innovation and entrepreneurship in rural areas. On the basis of county-level panel data for China, this study systematically examines the effects of the RDE on county-level rural
content: The rural digital economy (RDE) has the potential to support innovation and entrepreneurship in rural areas. On the basis of county-level panel data for China, this study systematically examines the effects of the RDE on county-level rural innovation and entrepreneurship (RIE), as well as the underlying mechanism, by employing a two-way fixed effects model, a mediating effect model, a threshold effect model, and a spatial Durbin model. The results of this study reveal that (1) the RDE is positively and significantly associated with RIE at the county level, an association that survives robustness testing and is consistent with the instrumental-variable estimate, although the exclusion restriction of the instrument cannot be tested directly and part of the association is mechanical because the two indices share an indicator; (2) the relation between the RDE and RIE is nonlinear and is better characterized by a threshold than by a quadratic specification; (3) the estimates are consistent with three mechanisms, namely the development of nonagricultural industries (DNI), higher economic density (ED), and the alleviation of financing constraints (FC), which we interpret as evidence on potential channels rather than as identified causal mediation; (4) a heterogeneity analysis suggests that the positive association between the RDE and RIE is stronger in areas that feature lower levels of modern agriculture, relatively weak information infrastructure, and smaller government size; and (5) the estimates indicate positive spatial spillovers from the RDE to RIE, and the estimated spillover across the truncated weight matrices rises to a maximum and then declines, a pattern consistent with attenuation but conditional on the specified weight matrix. This study provides empirical evidence regarding the intrinsic connection between the RDE and RIE in counties and has important reference value for efforts to promote policy practice and theoretical research in related fields.

title: Procurement Cycle Process and Performance of Public Level 5 Hospitals in Nairobi City County, Kenya
source: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
summary: Purpose: The study sought to establish the effect of procurement planning on performance of public level 5 hospitals in Nairobi City County, Kenya, to determine the effect of sourcing on performance of public level 5 hospitals in Nairobi Ci
content: Purpose: The study sought to establish the effect of procurement planning on performance of public level 5 hospitals in Nairobi City County, Kenya, to determine the effect of sourcing on performance of public level 5 hospitals in Nairobi City County, Kenya. This study was guided by Goal Setting Theory and The Resource-Based View (RBV) Theory. Methodology: This study adopted a descriptive research design. This study targeted level 5 public referral hospitals in Nairobi city county, Kenya. According to MoH report (2024) there are three public level 5 referral hospitals in Nairobi city county and they include; Pumwani Maternity Hospital, Mama Lucy Kibaki Hospital and Mbagathi County Hospital. There are a total of 207 procurement employees in the three hospitals. The Yamane formula was adopted to calculate the study sample of 136 respondents. The study used structured questionnaires as the main data collection instrument. Quantitative data was coded then analyzed using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) computer software version 28. Descriptive statistics was used to analyze the data in frequency distributions and percentages which were presented in tables and figures. The study also analysed the data using inferential statistics which comprised of correlation analysis and regression analysis. Findings: The study concludes that procurement planning has a positive and significant influence on performance of public level 5 hospitals in Nairobi City County, Kenya. In addition, the study concludes that sourcing has a positive and significant effect performance of public level 5 hospitals in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Based on the findings, the study recommends that public level 5 hospitals in Kenya should strengthen sourcing practices by adopting transparent, competitive, and reliable supplier selection processes that prioritize quality, cost-effectiveness, and timely delivery of goods and services. Hospital management should evaluate suppliers based on their capacity, reliability, compliance, and ability to consistently meet hospital requirements.

title: Differentiated Paths to Enhance Tourism Resilience: A Sustainable Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT Enhancing tourism resilience (TR) is vital for absorbing shocks, ensuring sustainability, and boosting regional competitiveness; yet systematic evaluation and tailored improvement strategies remain urgent challenges. This study int
content: ABSTRACT Enhancing tourism resilience (TR) is vital for absorbing shocks, ensuring sustainability, and boosting regional competitiveness; yet systematic evaluation and tailored improvement strategies remain urgent challenges. This study introduces the “R 2 ICE” framework, comprising RESIS (resistance), RECOV (recovery), CONFI (configuration), INNOV (innovation), and ENDUR (endurance), with a concise 30‐indicator TR evaluation system. Using provincial data from China's 31 provinces (2010–2024), we assess TR performance, identify distinct improvement paths, cluster regions by path similarity, and propose differentiated countermeasures. Temporally, regions follow four TR trajectories: steady high performers, catch‐up growers, mild recoverers, and persistently low performers; spatially, TR distribution has become more balanced recently. RESIS emerges as a core condition across all high‐TR paths; low CONFI and INNOV are key barriers; and sustainability remains under‐prioritized. Clustering reveals three TR categories (termed the “Three 3s Category”), each requiring dimension‐specific priorities, stronger stakeholder engagement, and enhanced sustainability. This study advances TR research and practice by embedding sustainability as an important R 2 ICE dimension, shifting the TR paradigm, and delivering actionable, stakeholder‐coordinated strategies per category.

title: Prioritizing Accounting Conservatism Strategies under Financial Constraints: An Integrated Fuzzy MCDM Framework for Enhancing Financial Reporting Quality
source: Knowledge and Decision Systems with Applications
summary: Conservative accounting strategies are essential for businesses to enhance the quality of their financial reporting. However, businesses with limited managerial and financial resources cannot implement all these strategies simultaneously; t
content: Conservative accounting strategies are essential for businesses to enhance the quality of their financial reporting. However, businesses with limited managerial and financial resources cannot implement all these strategies simultaneously; therefore, it is necessary to determine which conservative accounting strategies should be prioritized. The primary objective of this study is to identify the most suitable conservative accounting strategies for firms operating under resource constraints. To achieve this, an integrated multi-criteria decision-making model based on fuzzy logic is employed. First, expert evaluations are modeled using spherical fuzzy sets. Second, the LOPCOW technique is used to calculate the importance weights of the criteria. Third, conservative accounting strategies are prioritized using the CoCoFISo method. This study offers a distinct perspective to the literature by addressing conservative accounting not merely in terms of influencing factors, but as a strategy selection problem amidst limited resources. The findings demonstrate that an uncertainty-responsive conservative accounting framework is the optimal strategy for accounting conservatism, while stakeholder and creditor protection emerges as the most important criterion.

title: MILK SPOILAGE AND CONTAMINATION ACROSS THE DAIRY CHAIN: MICROBIAL CAUSES, SAFETY CONCERNS, QUALITY DETERIORATION, AND ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES, WITH REFERENCE TO INDIA
source: SRJ International Journal of Scientific Research
summary: Milk combines high nutritional value with a marked susceptibility to microbial deterioration. Its high water activity, near-neutral pH, and supply of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals favour microbial growth (Gaucheron,
content: Milk combines high nutritional value with a marked susceptibility to microbial deterioration. Its high water activity, near-neutral pH, and supply of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals favour microbial growth (Gaucheron, 2011), and contamination can enter at almost any point in the dairy chain, including milking, handling, storage, transport, and processing (Shuba et al., 2025; Washaya et al., 2022). Refrigeration and heat treatment improve keeping quality, but neither guarantees it. In raw and pasteurized fluid milk, cold-tolerant Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Pseudomonas spp., are major contributors to quality loss because they release extracellular proteases and lipases that can remain active after pasteurization (Machado et al., 2017; de Oliveira et al., 2015). Gram-positive spore-formers, especially Bacillus and Paenibacillus, pose a different challenge because their endospores withstand conventional heat treatment (Gopal et al., 2015). Lactic acid bacteria, Enterobacteriaceae, Clostridium spp., and spoilage fungi add product-specific defects such as souring, gas formation, and coagulation (Garnier et al., 2017; Ledenbach& Marshall, 2009). The resulting defects, which include off-flavours, rancidity, bitterness, coagulation, sediment, and shortened shelf life, carry substantial economic consequences: rejected raw milk, discarded product, lost saleable life, and higher spending on testing, cleaning, and sanitation. Global losses attributed to milk spoilage have been estimated at approximately USD 5–6 billion a year (Lu & Wang, 2017); in the United States, dairy accounted for about 17% of the value of food lost or wasted at retail and consumer level (Buzby et al., 2014; Gunders & Bloom, 2017). The issue is especially pertinent to India, the world’s largest milk producer (247.87 million tonnes in 2024–25), where about two-thirds of marketable milk passes through the unorganised sector. Reported post-harvest milk losses of roughly 0.5–1.4% of production correspond to an indicative ₹3,000–8,000 crore a year, before allowing for quality downgrading, mastitis, and spoilage that goes unrecorded in informal channels. This review traces the problem from contamination sources through microbial activity and product deterioration to economic and environmental costs, giving particular attention to psychrotrophic and spore-forming bacteria and to the Indian dairy chain.

title: URBAN TRANSITION AND RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY MANAGEMENTSTRATEGIES IN NIGERIA: ADDRESSING THE DILEMMAS OF ARAPIDLY EMERGING MIDSIZE CITY
summary: Nigeria’s rapidly emerging midsize cities are undergoing profound urban transitions that place new demands on residential property management practice. Using Osogbo as a case study, this paper examines how accelerated urban growth, changing
content: Nigeria’s rapidly emerging midsize cities are undergoing profound urban transitions that place new demands on residential property management practice. Using Osogbo as a case study, this paper examines how accelerated urban growth, changing socioeconomic dynamics, and evolving housing patterns are reshaping property management strategies. The study adopts a mixed-method approach, combining household surveys, key informant interviews, and spatial observations to assess prevailing management practices and the dilemmas faced by property managers and residents. 250 questionnaire was administered to respondents who are property owners, managers and tenants. The respondents were randomly selected. However, 225 of the retrieved questionnaires were adequately filled and considered good enough foranalysis. Findings reveal persistent gaps in maintenance planning, service delivery, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder coordination, largely driven by informal development patterns and institutional capacity as constraints. The paper argues that conventional property management models are increasingly becoming inadequate for transitional urban contexts. It therefore proposes context-responsive strategies that integrate digital tools, public governance structures, contemporary management standards, with adaptive service frameworks. The study therefore contributes to urban management discourse by offering practical insights for sustainable residential property management in Nigeria’s midsize cities.

title: Deterministic Noncontact Release and Transfer Through Programmable Interfacial Stress Reconfiguration
summary: Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro-LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact-mediated detachment, which conce
content: Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro-LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact-mediated detachment, which concentrates stress at the perimeter and causes slip and misalignment. Here, we report a diving beetle-inspired electroactive switchable adhesive (DESA) that achieves deterministic transfer through vibration-driven noncontact release enabled by interfacial stress reconfiguration. A perforated electrode couples a bioinspired adhesive layer to an electroactive PVC gel actuator, defining electrically contracting electrode-contact regions and mechanically linked gel-continuous hole regions. Under actuation, differential displacement between these regions deforms the adhesive layer and promotes partial peel-off at distributed interior sites rather than along a single perimeter front. At the 269 Hz resonance, vibration amplifies the displacement mismatch and spreads peel-off across the contact area, progressively reducing the load-bearing area. The resulting inertial stress completes noncontact separation, suppressing misalignment. The adhesive layer provides > 20 kPa dry and > 42 kPa wet adhesion across diverse substrates and retains stable performance over 1000 attachment-detachment cycles. On a robotic platform, the device transfers microcomponents with a lateral placement error of 318 ± 155 µm (≈99.5% placement accuracy). This interfacial stress reconfiguration offers a route to deterministic placement beyond adhesion-strength control.

title: Decoding Electro‐Chemo‐Mechanical Coupled Failure in Silicon Monoxide‐Based Anodes via Operando Pressure Monitoring for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) require high‐energy‐density anodes that operate under practical low stack pressures. Although silicon‐based anodes are promising, most studies rely on stack pressures exceeding 50 MPa. Here, operan
content: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) require high‐energy‐density anodes that operate under practical low stack pressures. Although silicon‐based anodes are promising, most studies rely on stack pressures exceeding 50 MPa. Here, operando pressiometry reveals that areal‐capacity‐normalized stress serves as a comparative indicator of reaction uniformity in silicon monoxide (SiO)‐based anodes. While incorporating solid electrolyte (SE) and conductive carbon improves percolation pathways, SE content paradoxically promotes severe side reactions or lithium plating. Based on insights into the electro‐chemo‐mechanical behavior of SiO‐based anodes, a mixed ionic‐electronic conductor (MIEC) composite architecture combining low‐volume‐expansion SiO with a prelithiated Li 21 Si 5 phase (SiO/PreLiSi) is introduced. The SiO/PreLiSi anode provides continuous ionic and electronic pathways, reduces irreversible capacity loss, and enhances interfacial contact through plastic deformation, enabling uniform lithiation under low stack pressure without external SE and carbon additives. Compared to Si/PreLiSi counterparts, the SiO/PreLiSi composite forms stable buffering phases that mitigate volume changes and suppress stress accumulation. Consequently, the SiO/PreLiSi anode demonstrates reduced pressure variation, improved capacity retention, and prolonged cycling stability under low stack pressure. This work provides a fundamental design principle for next‐generation ASSB anodes capable of practical low‐pressure operation.

title: Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 Cathodes for Sodium‐Ion Batteries: From Fundamental Research to Practical Application
summary: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are highly promising for large‐scale energy storage applications due to the abundance and low cost of sodium. Among cathode candidates, the mixed phosphate Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) stands out f
content: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are highly promising for large‐scale energy storage applications due to the abundance and low cost of sodium. Among cathode candidates, the mixed phosphate Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) stands out for its balanced capacity, voltage, cost, and structural stability. However, its industrial deployment is still limited by intrinsic material bottlenecks. This review provides a unique integrated perspective that links fundamental mechanisms to industrial application. The crystal structure and sodium storage mechanism are first clarified, and then the core challenges limiting its electrochemical performance are systematically analyzed. On this basis, the representative modification strategies are comprehensively reviewed with detailed discussions on their regulatory effects on band structure, ion migration, and phase stability. More importantly, the industrial progress of NFPP is collected and elucidated from material production, cell manufacturing to energy system deployment, along with the key challenges. Finally, future research directions are outlined. This review aims to bridge the gap between fundamental research and industrial application of NFPP, thereby accelerating the adoption of low‐cost, long‐life SIBs.

title: Local Government Implicit Debt and Corporate AI Technology Level: Evidence From China
summary: ABSTRACT This paper uses data from listed companies from 2011 to 2023 to examine the impact of local government implicit debt (LGID) on the level of corporate artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The results show that LGID significantly
content: ABSTRACT This paper uses data from listed companies from 2011 to 2023 to examine the impact of local government implicit debt (LGID) on the level of corporate artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The results show that LGID significantly reduces the level of corporate AI technology. Moderation analysis reveals that this inhibitory effect is more pronounced in firms facing financing constraints and those with high levels of financialization. Meanwhile, R&D investment mitigates the inhibitory effect of LGID on AI technology. Furthermore, the effect of LGID on corporate AI technology is more pronounced among firms operating in more competitive markets, non‐state‐owned firms, firms in non‐eastern regions, or high‐tech firms. These findings provide valuable insights for policymakers to develop smart technologies aimed at protecting against LGID risks and effectively protecting firms' intelligent technologies.

title: D is for deposit: model, data and code
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Model, data and code for Cavanagh, Fishbein and Haszeldine, ‘D is for deposit: extending Europe’s carbon storage obligation to account for all hydrocarbons’, submitted to the International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control. The paper propos
content: Model, data and code for Cavanagh, Fishbein and Haszeldine, ‘D is for deposit: extending Europe’s carbon storage obligation to account for all hydrocarbons’, submitted to the International Journal of Greenhouse Gas Control. The paper proposes a redeemable deposit on oil and gas at first sale onto the EU market, paid by domestic and imported supply alike and redeemed against verified, permanently stored tonnes of CO₂. The workbook evaluates the identity S = D × V × I × M year by year to 2050. It covers three volume scenarios (IEA WEO-2024 STEPS and APS, plus a faster exit), two storage pathways, three carbon-intensity bases, and storage lags of 0, 5 or 10 years. It also tracks the fund: deposits paid in, redeemed, forfeited and outstanding. Every input is sourced, and every formula is live. The record also contains the Eurostat data series, the scripts that draw the paper’s figures, Table 1 and graphical abstract, and the Supplementary Information methods note. This version accompanies the submitted manuscript and will be updated with a link to the published article.

title: Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 as a Programmable Bridge Chassis for Biomanufacturing and Host‐Responsive Living Systems
summary: Microbial biomanufacturing and engineered probiotics increasingly use related microbial lineages across distinct product architectures, but the associated engineering and evidence requirements are rarely compared. Here, Escherichia coli Nis
content: Microbial biomanufacturing and engineered probiotics increasingly use related microbial lineages across distinct product architectures, but the associated engineering and evidence requirements are rarely compared. Here, Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) is evaluated as a programmable bridge chassis across four alternative deployment modes: purified molecule, cell-derived architecture/material, living-cell product, and host-state-responsive living system. The review links carbon-nitrogen-energy-redox allocation and global regulation to cellular-state trajectories, interface capacity, safety refactoring, materials-assisted protection, containment, and mode-specific qualification. Direct evidence includes 100-L heparosan fermentation, antibiotic-free β-alanine production, engineered outer-membrane-vesicle delivery, human studies of phenylalanine-consuming EcN, and glucose-responsive GLP-1 delivery in diabetic mice and non-human primates. The terminated SYNB1934 Phase 3 program is considered alongside positive studies to distinguish proof of function, pharmacodynamic activity, tolerability, manufacturing readiness, and late-stage efficacy. Operational criteria for bridge-chassis designation, explicit rules for boundary cases, and a prospective design-build-test-learn agenda are proposed. As functional embodiment changes, engineering priorities shift among flux, state, interface, formulation, containment, and evidence-not necessarily toward a more advanced mode.

title: Synthesis of eggshell‐based hydroxyapatite with trisodium citrate chelating agent
summary: Hydroxyapatite is a calcium phosphate ceramic similar to the mineral phase of bone and teeth, is widely used in biomedical implants due to its excellent biocompatibility. This study synthesizes hydroxyapatite from eggshell waste using triso
content: Hydroxyapatite is a calcium phosphate ceramic similar to the mineral phase of bone and teeth, is widely used in biomedical implants due to its excellent biocompatibility. This study synthesizes hydroxyapatite from eggshell waste using trisodium citrate as a modifier through hydrothermal and microwave‐assisted methods. Characterization is performed using x‐ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy‐dispersive spectroscopy, and Vickers hardness testing. High‐purity and crystalline hydroxyapatite are obtained at 180 °C (hydrothermal) and 120 °C (microwave). Sintered ceramics achieve hardness values of 3.98 GPa and 3.76 GPa, respectively. Trisodium citrate prevents agglomeration, produces rod‐like crystals, and promotes the formation of porous structures. After sintering, calcium/phosphorus ratios are close to 1.33, comparable to octacalcium phosphate. However, x‐ray diffraction analysis confirms that the dominant phase after sintering is calcium‐deficient hydroxyapatite, with octacalcium phosphate present only as a transient precursor phase at lower synthesis temperatures. The novelty of this work lies in combining eggshell biowaste valorization with trisodium citrate chelation, enabling the synthesis of calcium‐deficient, rod‐like, and porous hydroxyapatite that closely mimics natural bone apatite. This sustainable approach offers a green alternative for engineering bioactive ceramics for bone repair applications.

title: Layer‐by‐Layer Solvent‐Free Additive Manufacturing Enabling Controllable Ultrathick Electrode Coating for Lithium‐Ion Battery
summary: ABSTRACT Dry electrode manufacturing is emerging as a transformative strategy for sustainable lithium‐ion battery production, yet achieving ultrathick electrodes with homogeneous microstructures, efficient electron transport, and high elect
content: ABSTRACT Dry electrode manufacturing is emerging as a transformative strategy for sustainable lithium‐ion battery production, yet achieving ultrathick electrodes with homogeneous microstructures, efficient electron transport, and high electrochemical utilization remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a solvent‐free, layer‐by‐layer additive manufacturing strategy that enables architecturally controlled ultrathick cathodes through molecular‐level coupling between reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and binder. During roll‐to‐roll hot pressing, molten binder infiltrates the rGO framework to form a continuous conductive binder network, uniformly bridging NMC811 particles to enhance particle adhesion, suppress binder aggregation, and establish efficient electronic percolation. This strategy enables precise control of electrode thickness (300–1000 µm) and areal loading (20–100 mg cm − 2 ) while eliminating solvent‐induced structural defects. The resulting multilayer cathodes, comprising up to five sequentially deposited layers, deliver a specific capacity of 230 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 C and an areal capacity of ∼10 mAh cm − 2 . The nearly linear increase in areal capacity with layer number demonstrates homogeneous conductive networks and efficient electrochemical utilization throughout the electrode thickness. Electrodes with ∼50 mg cm − 2 loading retain 9 mAh cm − 2 after 50 cycles. This work establishes a scalable platform for architecturally engineering ultrathick multilayer electrodes, overcoming heterogeneity of conventional thick electrodes and advancing next‐generation high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries.

title: Effects of trehalose, ascorbic acid, and citric acid osmosis on flavor formation and powder indices of freeze-dried jackfruit powders
summary: This study explored the effects of three permeating agents on flavor formation and powder properties of freeze-dried jackfruit powder (FDJP). Results indicated that lipoxygenase activity, esterase activity, and cysteine content significantl
content: This study explored the effects of three permeating agents on flavor formation and powder properties of freeze-dried jackfruit powder (FDJP). Results indicated that lipoxygenase activity, esterase activity, and cysteine content significantly regulated the flavor profile of FDJP. Trehalose formed a continuous covering layer on the surface of FDJP while maintaining a dense porous internal structure. This structural configuration likely facilitates the retention of esters, terpenes, and cysteine within FDJP, simultaneously resulting in reduced hygroscopicity (3.5%) and enhanced solubility (16.5%). Ascorbic acid inhibited oxidative degradation of short-chain esters via reduction effect, while citric acid lowered lipoxygenase activity to 432.84 U/g through protonation to slow down fatty acid hydroperoxide generation. Metabolomic analysis further confirmed that phenylalanine metabolism, cysteine metabolism, and methionine metabolism served as the predominant metabolic pathways responsible for flavor compound biosynthesis in FDJP. This work offers theoretical references for manufacturing high-quality FDJP with preferable flavor and powder properties.

title: Bacterial cellulose-indigoidine films from fermentation waste for active strawberry packaging: Formation, characterization, and functional assessment
summary: This study developed indigoidine-retained bacterial cellulose (BC) films using indigoidine fermentation waste as a dual-function medium. Mass-balance and structural analyses indicated that indigoidine was immobilized within the nanofibrous
content: This study developed indigoidine-retained bacterial cellulose (BC) films using indigoidine fermentation waste as a dual-function medium. Mass-balance and structural analyses indicated that indigoidine was immobilized within the nanofibrous BC matrix possibly through physical adsorption, mechanical entrapment, and hydrogen-bonding interactions, without disrupting the Cellulose I crystalline framework. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested decreased BC–water hydrogen bonding and local water coordination around BC oxygen atoms after indigoidine incorporation. BC-indigoidine films showed enhanced ultraviolet-visible light shielding, a decrease in water vapor permeability from 0.41 to 0.32 g·mm·m-2·h −1 ·kP −1 , and antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli , Staphylococcus aureus , and Candida albicans . After 5 d of strawberry storage at 30 °C, weight loss was 30.59 ± 1.92% for the BC-indigoidine group, compared with 50.22 ± 14.20% for the pristine BC group and 70.38 ± 11.06% for the unwrapped control. This approach integrates cellulose biosynthesis and active-compound retention to valorize fermentation waste into bio-based films for active packaging.

title: Predicting the current and future potential distributions and biotic interactions between an herbivorous insect and its host plants in southern Africa
summary: Climate change will have profound impacts on species distributions and persistence in the near future, however, biotic interactions may mitigate climate effects among interacting species. In this study, we fitted species distribution models
content: Climate change will have profound impacts on species distributions and persistence in the near future, however, biotic interactions may mitigate climate effects among interacting species. In this study, we fitted species distribution models (SDMs) to predict the current and future habitat suitability of Gonimbrasia belina, a culturally and economically significant insect in southern Africa, and 11 of its host plants. SDMs were fitted with four algorithms using publicly accessible species occurrence records and bioclimatic variables (1970-2000) at 1 km resolution, while predicted habitat suitability were generated using weighted model ensembles. Future predictions were generated using four shared socioeconomic pathways of the EC-Earth3-Veg general circulation model (2061-2080). We also quantified ecological niche overlap (Schoener’s D) between the insect and the host plants with equivalency tests (1,000 randomizations) to evaluate statistical significance. Results show strong contributions and constraints of predictors representing water availability and water-energy balance to the distributions of the 12 species.
