G. belina and seven host plants were predicted to lose portions of their future suitable habitats, while the remaining four hosts may experience range expansions under climate change. Niche overlap was significantly lower between G. belina and most of its host plants (D=0.06–0.65) indicating a generalist herbivorous relationship. Range losses may disrupt biotic interactions between G. belina and some of its host plants, but herbivorous relationships may be sustained in predicted climatic refugia and with climate-adapted host plants. Nonetheless, long-term persistence of G. belina will depend on sustainable harvesting and protection of host plant diversity.

title: Fruit juice impregnation versus dilute koh in the low temperature activation of moringa oleifera stem carbon: textural development, pore size distribution and inherited morphology
summary: Woody stems pruned from Moringa oleifera plantations are an abundant but rarely valorised West African residue. Converting this biomass into porous carbon without corrosive reagents could support decentralised production. This study compare
content: Woody stems pruned from Moringa oleifera plantations are an abundant but rarely valorised West African residue. Converting this biomass into porous carbon without corrosive reagents could support decentralised production. This study compared four food-grade or plant-derived impregnants (Moringa leaf extract, watermelon juice, lime juice and lemon juice) with dilute potassium hydroxide (0.5 M) for activating stem char produced at 500 °C. Char portions (10 g) were soaked in 40 mL of each activatin

title: The Nexus Among Competitiveness, Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility: Evidence from Real Estate Companies in CALABARZON
source: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
summary: This study examined the nexus among competitiveness, sustainability, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) among 21 Philippine Stock Exchange-listed real estate companies operating in CALABARZON during the last quarter of 2024 and first
content: This study examined the nexus among competitiveness, sustainability, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) among 21 Philippine Stock Exchange-listed real estate companies operating in CALABARZON during the last quarter of 2024 and first quarter of 2025. Using a descriptive research design, data were collected through questionnaire checklists and interviews involving 31 management representatives, 394 employees, and 124 external stakeholders. Findings indicated favorable perceptions of competitiveness across external market and policy factors and internal management, marketing, and financial dimensions. Management generally reported higher assessments than employees. Competitiveness did not differ significantly by location, years of operation, payment mode, or years conducting CSR, but significant differences emerged across selected indicators associated with capital, workforce size, client volume, products or services, and branches. Sustainability initiatives were widely implemented, particularly in energy efficiency, green building, water conservation, and eco-friendly design; comparatively weaker ratings concerned climate action, sustainable cities, and community collaboration. Sustainability implementation likewise varied by certain financial and organizational characteristics, but not by location, years of operation, products or services, payment mode, or years conducting CSR. Government policies were generally perceived as influential in integrating economic, social, and environmental CSR practices. Correlation analysis showed a strong positive relationship between competitiveness and sustainability and moderate positive relationships between competitiveness and CSR and between sustainability and CSR. Qualitative findings identified financial constraints, regulatory burdens, stakeholder coordination challenges, environmental concerns, and tensions between profitability and social responsibility. The study proposed a Nexus Model linking business operations, financial performance, sustainability practices, and community impact to guide integrated organizational strategies.

title: AI-Powered Cloud Ecosystems for Scalable Enterprise Operations: From Predictive Analytics to Autonomous Infrastructure Manage-ment
source: Journal of Integrated Science Technology and Management
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cloud computing have emerged as two of the most transformative tech-nologies shaping modern enterprise operations. The integration of AI into cloud ecosystems has ena-bled organizations to achieve unpreceden
content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cloud computing have emerged as two of the most transformative tech-nologies shaping modern enterprise operations. The integration of AI into cloud ecosystems has ena-bled organizations to achieve unprecedented levels of scalability, efficiency, agility, and innovation. AI-powered cloud ecosystems combine advanced machine learning algorithms, predictive analytics, au-tomation tools, and intelligent resource management capabilities to optimize enterprise processes and support data-driven decision-making. These ecosystems facilitate the analysis of large volumes of structured and unstructured data, enabling organizations to forecast demand, identify operational risks, enhance customer experiences, and improve business outcomes. Furthermore, the evolution of autonomous infrastructure management has introduced self-monitoring, self-healing, and self-optimizing capabilities that reduce human intervention while increasing system reliability and perfor-mance. Enterprises increasingly rely on intelligent cloud platforms to manage dynamic workloads, cybersecurity challenges, and resource allocation in real time. This essay explores the role of AI-powered cloud ecosystems in scalable enterprise operations, examining their technological founda-tions, benefits, challenges, and transformative impact. It reviews existing scholarly literature on pre-dictive analytics, cloud-native architectures, AI-driven automation, and autonomous infrastructure management. Additionally, the study presents a comprehensive research methodology designed to investigate the effectiveness of AI-enabled cloud ecosystems in enhancing operational scalability and organizational resilience. The findings contribute to understanding how enterprises can leverage AI and cloud integration to achieve sustainable growth, competitive advantage, and digital transformation in an increasingly complex business environment.

title: The Effect of High-Protein Supplement Pellet Supplementation on the Growth of Post-Weaning Ettawa Crossbred Kids in Majene Regency, Indonesia
source: Journal of Animal Health and Production
summary: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of high-protein supplement pellets (HPSP), formulated from a combination of fish waste and moringa leaf ( Moringa oleifera ) meal, on the growth performance and nutritional status of Ettawa crossbred
content: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of high-protein supplement pellets (HPSP), formulated from a combination of fish waste and moringa leaf ( Moringa oleifera ) meal, on the growth performance and nutritional status of Ettawa crossbred kids in Majene Regency. The research was conducted in two phases. Phase I established a baseline by observing 24 post-weaning kids (12 males, 12 females) under traditional management fed only Leucaena leucocephala . Phase II employed a 2 x 2 factorial arrangement (diet × sex) where 24 kids were assigned to a control (20% forage + 80% commercial concentrate) and a treatment diet, where 16% of the commercial concentrate was substituted with HPSP (20% forage + 64% commercial concentrate + 16% HPSP). Results from Phase I indicated suboptimal growth with no sexual dimorphism, likely due to protein-energy imbalance and anti-nutritional factors in Leucaena . In Phase II, HPSP supplementation significantly improved average daily gain (ADG) (162.21 vs 142.56 g/d; P < 0.01) and feed conversion ratio (FCR) (4.53 vs 5.14; P < 0.05). A significant diet × sex interaction was observed for ADG (P < 0.01), with males showing a more pronounced response to high-quality nutrition. Furthermore, HPSP significantly enhanced hip height gain (P < 0.05), indicating superior skeletal development. In conclusion, the synergistic use of fish waste and moringa leaves in HPSP effectively optimizes the early-stage growth of Ettawa crossbred kids, providing a sustainable, locally sourced solution for livestock development in coastal regions.

title: GREENWASHING AND CORPORATE LIABILITY IN INDIA: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THE EXISTING LEGAL AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORK
summary: Greenwashing is when a company makes false or exaggerated claims, or uses a vague, one-sided or weak or limited substantiation to communicate environmental benefits. It can lead to a misallocation of sustainable investments, affect consumer
content: Greenwashing is when a company makes false or exaggerated claims, or uses a vague, one-sided or weak or limited substantiation to communicate environmental benefits. It can lead to a misallocation of sustainable investments, affect consumer decision making and erode confidence in corporate environmental reporting. This paper critically considers the effectiveness of India's law and regulation in combating greenwashing and holding companies liable. Uses a doctrinal approach with reference to the official and self-regulatory information described, the legal position is up to 31 October 2026. The study is based on the following: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Greenwashing or Misleading Environmental Claims, 2024, by the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA); Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Guidelines on Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) and Green-debt safeguards; Companies Act, 2013; Advertising Standards Council of India (ASC) green-claims standards; and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, as amended. The quantitative data suggests that there is a material enforcement concern – while 211 advertisements were investigated in 211 of which 211 required modifications in 2024-25, only 34 were investigated in 2023-24 and all these 34 required modification for lack of substantiation. This is an administrative review sample, and not a population estimation of greenwashing in India. The analysis reveals that India has taken a step beyond a voluntary approach, notably with the 2024 CCPA Guidelines and SEBI's BRSR Core regime. But the framework still has a number of drawbacks, and is spread across consumer regulation, securities regulation, corporate regulation and environmental regulation. The main deficiencies include lack of consistency in assurance, small value-chain verification, poor transparency of enforcement results, and the lack of a cohesive taxonomy for green claims and uncertainty in measuring life-cycle claims. The paper suggests a risk-based approach to verifying independently, board-level claim governance, standardised disclosure processes, coordinated enforcement and transparent reporting of regulatory findings.

title: From three-phase olive mill by-products to a stabilized soil amendment: Windrow co-composting of olive pomace, green waste and olive mill wastewater in southern Morocco
summary: Olive oil production around the Mediterranean generates large volumes of olive pomace (OP) and olive mill wastewater (OMW) whose uncontrolled disposal degrades soils, waters and air quality. The first part of this series identified co-compo
content: Olive oil production around the Mediterranean generates large volumes of olive pomace (OP) and olive mill wastewater (OMW) whose uncontrolled disposal degrades soils, waters and air quality. The first part of this series identified co-composting as the most suitable route for the solid fraction of a three-phase mill in Taroudant Province, southern Morocco [1]. To test this route under real conditions, a single windrow of OP and green waste at 50:50 (w/w) was composted for 121 days on an impermeable platform, with stored raw OMW as the sole rewetting agent. Temperature, pH, moisture, organic matter (OM), C/N and two sanitary indicators were monitored at up to 32 dates. The windrow followed the four conventional phases, its core staying above 65 °C from days 25 to 31 and above 55 °C from days 21 to 35 (maximum 68.2 °C), consistent with three of the four sanitation criteria of Regulation (EU) 2019/1009. The pH rose steadily from 5.70 to 7.93 without alkaline excursion, and total Kjeldahl nitrogen rose from 1.32 to 2.17% of dry matter, although an ash balance suggests that about one third of the nitrogen was lost. Moisture never fell below 41.5%. OM decreased from 79.5 to 49.8% of dry matter and C/N from 30.1 to 11.5, reaching a plateau before day 121. Escherichia coli fell by 99.56%, and no viable helminth eggs were detected in 1.5 g. These indicators suggest a stabilized product, but Salmonella , trace metals and phytotoxicity were not determined, so agricultural suitability remains unconfirmed.

title: Food Quality and Safety Aspects of African Indigenous Vegetables
source: edoc Publication server (Humboldt University of Berlin)
summary: In dieser Arbeit wurden die Auswirkungen ernährungssensibler Anbaumethoden und Nacherntebehandlungen von AIVs auf die Lebensmittelqualität sowie auf Sicherheitsaspekte des Ernährungsumfelds untersucht. Das wichtigste Ergebnis dieser Studie
content: In dieser Arbeit wurden die Auswirkungen ernährungssensibler Anbaumethoden und Nacherntebehandlungen von AIVs auf die Lebensmittelqualität sowie auf Sicherheitsaspekte des Ernährungsumfelds untersucht. Das wichtigste Ergebnis dieser Studie war, dass der Anbau in Beuteln zu Gemüse mit einem hohen Gehalt an Mineralstoffen und sekundären Pflanzenstoffen führt, was auf das Potenzial hindeutet, die ganzjährige Verfügbarkeit und den Zugang zu Gemüse auf Haushaltsebene trotz begrenzter Anbauflächen zu verbessern. Es zeigte sich, dass die passive Solartrocknung die Qualität von AIVs bewahrt, was sich daran zeigt, dass der Gehalt an sekundären Pflanzenstoffen bei einer Lagerung bei Raumtemperatur über mindestens 30 Tage erhalten bleibt. Sowohl der Anbau von AIVs in Beutelbeeten als auch deren Trocknung mit passiven Solartrocknern führten zu Nitratgehalten unterhalb der empfohlenen Mindestgrenzwerte, was auf eine unbedenkliche Verzehrsicherheit hindeutet. Biopacks bewahrten die Qualität der AIVs bis zu einem gewissen Grad, was sich in einem geringeren Frischgewichtsverlust, dem Erhalt der Blattfarbe und der Beibehaltung des Gehalts an sekundären Pflanzenstoffen bei Lagerung unter Kühl- und Raumtemperaturbedingungen zeigte. Biopacks gingen jedoch mit einem Rückgang des Ascorbinsäuregehalts einher, wobei die Vermehrung von Mikroorganismen bei Lagerung unter Raumtemperatur kaum eingedämmt wurde. Die praktische Umsetzung der drei Ansätze (Anbau im Beutelgarten, passive Solartrocknung, Verpackung in biologisch abbaubaren Folien) bietet Möglichkeiten, die ganzjährige Verfügbarkeit und den Zugang zu hochwertigen und sicheren AIVs unabhängig von Ressourcenengpässen sicherzustellen – ein entscheidender Aspekt für die Verringerung der dreifachen Belastung durch Mangelernährung.

title: EscalNet: Learning Isotropic Representation Space for Biomolecular Dynamics Based on Effective Energy
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Deep learning has substantially advanced the analysis of biomolecular simulation data by providing compact yet informative representations that capture the essential dynamics of a system and expose the underlying mechanisms. Here w
content: Abstract Deep learning has substantially advanced the analysis of biomolecular simulation data by providing compact yet informative representations that capture the essential dynamics of a system and expose the underlying mechanisms. Here we combine a neural network with Fourier analysis of trajectory data toward two objectives: preserving the biologically relevant low-frequency components of the motion and constructing an isotropic representation space in which conformational transitions are described by a Markov model. Applied to two Chignolin folding trajectories, the EscalNet (Effective Energy rescale net) representation space consistently gives better clustering and produces a Markov transition matrix that passes a Chapman–Kolmogorov test. Saliency scores further identify the structural determinants that govern the effective-energy landscape underlying the dynamics. Coupling neural-network representations with physical order parameters thus offers a promising framework for biomolecular trajectory analysis.

title: Experimental evolution of yeast reveals trade-offs between early and late stationary phase
summary: Stationary phase in yeast and other microorganisms begins when a limiting nutrient in the environment is exhausted and cell division ceases. Most cells subsequently enter quiescence and then lose viability. However, even in spent media, met
content: Stationary phase in yeast and other microorganisms begins when a limiting nutrient in the environment is exhausted and cell division ceases. Most cells subsequently enter quiescence and then lose viability. However, even in spent media, metabolism continues, and the environment can change over time, causing the relative fitnesses of genotypes to differ over the course of stationary phase. For yeast, how such fitness varies and what genotypes might be favored at what points in stationary phase is largely unknown. In this work we experimentally evolve S. cerevisiae in batch culture, varying the time spent in stationary phase between growth cycles, and we isolate adaptive clones. We measure the relative fitness of these adaptive clones across a range of environments, characterized by different amounts of time in stationary phase and by two different carbon sources. By comparing the performance during a period of the growth cycle of a mutant to that of its ancestor, we can estimate the effects of each observed mutation on performance during various phases of the growth cycle. Here, we show that when an adaptive mutation emerges in growth cycles that include a stationary phase, its effect on stationary phase performance is largely independent of the type of carbon source provided. For the same group of mutants, mutational effects on performance in early stationary phase are negatively correlated with those effects in late stationary phase, suggesting a trade-off. We also show that increased intervals of stationary phase result in larger fitness effects of adaptive mutations and distinct routes of adaptation. Together, these results demonstrate that stationary phase consists of more than one distinct fitness-related phenotype, and that the phenotypes that allow for high performance in the first few days of stationary phase trade off with those that allow for high performance in later stationary phase.

title: The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling,
content: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI c 1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI c 1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.

title: Escaping a Snowball Earth: Volcanic Carbon Dioxide Accumulation, Required Pressure and Deglaciation Time
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: A frozen planet stops weathering its rocks, so volcanic carbon dioxide, normally consumed by that weathering, accumulates in the air year after year until its greenhouse forcing can defeat the ice's own brightness. Accumulation time equals
content: A frozen planet stops weathering its rocks, so volcanic carbon dioxide, normally consumed by that weathering, accumulates in the air year after year until its greenhouse forcing can defeat the ice's own brightness. Accumulation time equals the moles required for the exit concentration divided by the net outgassing rate, since the usual silicate sink is switched off by ice cover and cold. Headline values are exit outgassing mol per year adopted exit = 3000000000000; exit weathering sink under ice fraction exit = 0; exit accumulation years at 005 bar exit = 1.969e+06; exit accumulation myr at 005 bar exit = 1.969; exit forcing log term at 005 bar w m2 exit = 27.74; exit accumulation years at 010 bar exit = 3.938e+06. Reaching a tenth of a bar needs about four million years at the adopted net outgassing rate, and near eight million at half that rate, matching the stratigraphic longevity of the great glaciations, and the resulting forcing at a tenth of a bar is sufficient against a 0.6 albedo only when dust-darkened tropical ice is included.

title: The Dune Sink: Organic Sand Volume, Production Time and the Dune Fields as a Term in Titan's Carbon Ledger
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Titan's equatorial dune fields are usually treated as a wind problem. This paper treats them as a hydrological and carbon-budget problem: the dunes are made of organic solids manufactured in the atmosphere from destroyed methane, so their v
content: Titan's equatorial dune fields are usually treated as a wind problem. This paper treats them as a hydrological and carbon-budget problem: the dunes are made of organic solids manufactured in the atmosphere from destroyed methane, so their volume is a record of how much methane the sky has processed and where the solid share of the products came to rest. At the mapped area of about fourteen million square kilometres with an adopted mean equivalent thickness of thirty metres, the fields hold roughly 426 thousand cubic kilometres of organic sand, embodying more methane, through its carbon, than the present atmosphere contains. At an adopted photochemical solids production rate, accumulating that inventory takes about 96 million years, making the dune seas young features that record the recent operation of the cycle. The dunes are therefore a genuine sink term in Titan's methane ledger: not where most destroyed methane goes, but where its solid fraction is stored, at a scale the budget cannot ignore.

title: Response of vegetative growth, photosynthetic physiology, flowering traits, pod set and grain nutritional quality to red-blue light ratios in adzuki bean
summary: Precise light management is critical for enhancing pod set and grain quality in protected cultivation. However, optimal red-blue (R: B) parameters and underlying multi-scale regulatory mechanisms remain largely uncharacterized for full-grow
content: Precise light management is critical for enhancing pod set and grain quality in protected cultivation. However, optimal red-blue (R: B) parameters and underlying multi-scale regulatory mechanisms remain largely uncharacterized for full-growth-cycle adzuki bean (Vigna angularis), limiting protected cultivation of this legume. Two Northern Chinese cultivars with contrasting photosensitivity (light-sensitive JH16, light-adaptive BH8824) were grown under five R: B ratios at equal photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD; 1:1 as control). Morphology, photosynthesis, metabolism, pod set and grain quality were evaluated. R: B ratio of 3:2 was optimal for synergistically improving pod set and basic nutritional quality. It optimized leaf anatomy and chloroplast ultrastructure, increased total chlorophyll by 17.52% in JH16 and 35.69% in BH8824 vs. control, enhanced photosystem II (PSII) photochemical efficiency and net photosynthesis, maintained redox homeostasis, and strengthened leaf carbon sink strength. Compared with the 1:1 control, the 3:2 ratio advanced flowering by 3–5 days, produced 60–61 total pods per 12 plants at physiological maturity, and shortened the total growth period by 8–9 days. Grain starch and soluble protein increased by 21.32%–57.68% and 53.88%–92.32%, respectively, with optimized starch composition and elevated amylopectin proportion. The high-blue 2:3 ratio slightly reduced pod number but significantly promoted functional secondary metabolites (total phenolics, total flavonoids). The two cultivars showed broadly consistent responses, with stronger morphological responsiveness in the light-sensitive genotype and greater quality potential in the light-adaptive one. These findings reveal multi-scale physiological mechanisms underlying light-quality regulation of photosynthetic efficiency and grain quality in adzuki bean, providing theoretical basis and reference parameters for precise light management in artificial-light protected cultivation.

title: Biological carbon accumulation accelerates CO₂ outgassing after abrupt Bering Sea warming
summary: Abstract Each winter, deepening of the wintertime mixed layer renews subsurface waters in productive high-latitude seas, regulating duration of regenerated dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) stored below the surface. However, whether weakenin
content: Abstract Each winter, deepening of the wintertime mixed layer renews subsurface waters in productive high-latitude seas, regulating duration of regenerated dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) stored below the surface. However, whether weakening of this winter water-mass renewal allows sustained biological carbon supply to establish a long-term reservoir remains unclear. Here we identify multi-year accumulation of predominantly regenerated carbon in the main basin of the Bering Sea during subsurface warming after 2014, associated with weakened winter water-mass renewal. Repeated shipboard observations reveal a ~ 56.8 µmol⋅kg⁻¹ increase in DIC at 26.50 σ θ between 1993 and 2023, more than 70% of which is non-anthropogenic, dominated by regenerated biological carbon. Monthly DIC reconstruction indicates that weakened winter renewal accumulates DIC at ~ 3.5 µmol⋅kg⁻¹⋅year⁻¹ after 2014. Atmospheric reanalysis further shows that strengthened Ekman suction due to enhanced wind stress curl after 2018 shoaled carbon-rich density layers and make it intersecting with the wintertime mixed layer, coinciding with winter CO₂ outgassing rising to 1.75 times the pre-2014 mean. These results show that, under sustained biological carbon supply, the long-term regenerated-carbon reservoir established by weakened winter renewal is not necessarily permanent; it can become eruptive CO₂ outgassing source when surface–subsurface connectivity is restored by subsequent shorter-term changes in atmospheric forcing.

title: Global time series of annual nitrogen stable isotope maps derived from Landsat: 30m, 1984–2023
summary: Abstract. The lack of knowledge on how nitrogen cycles respond to environmental changes globally is a critical gap in assessing the sustainability of current terrestrial ecosystem services and projecting future carbon sink. The absence of s
content: Abstract. The lack of knowledge on how nitrogen cycles respond to environmental changes globally is a critical gap in assessing the sustainability of current terrestrial ecosystem services and projecting future carbon sink. The absence of spatiotemporal continuity in current nitrogen-cycle observations limits our understanding of how nitrogen cycles respond climate change. Plant nitrogen stable isotope (δ15N) serves as an integrator of nitrogen cycles, allowing quantification of how nitrogen cycles change. Existing on-ground data allow for estimation of δ15N based on the established relationship between δ15N and plant reflectance, providing the basis for large-scale long-term monitoring of δ15N with satellite-based surface spectra. Here we describe a novel method that calculates the annual δ15N globally based on Landsat reflectance from 1984 to 2023 with planned updates for coming years using Google Earth Engine. The resulting spatio-temporal data include four channels: (i) mean δ15N values; (ii) prediction uncertainty; (iii) the number of Landsat retrievals used; and (iv) a data quality assessment. We also demonstrate ways to access and visualise the maps and time series at various spatiotemporal scales with minimal requirements on programming skills and computational capacity. Finally, we show applications of the δ15N maps for identifying drivers of δ15N variation. The framework is open access on the cloud, providing all users easy access to nitrogen cycle monitoring. The dataset is available at DOI: https://doi.org/10.25919/zxvv-bj04 (Yang et al., 2026). A web-based application provides code-free access and visualisation to the dataset: https://tern-landscapes.earthengine.app/view/nitrogen-availability.

title: The effect of ocean separating boundaries on equilibrium and transient mid-depth stratification and overturning
summary: The global overturning circulation (GOC) transports heat, salt, and carbon between ocean basins. Its mid-depth component is characterized by sinking in the North Atlantic and compensating upwelling elsewhere. However, much of our understand
content: The global overturning circulation (GOC) transports heat, salt, and carbon between ocean basins. Its mid-depth component is characterized by sinking in the North Atlantic and compensating upwelling elsewhere. However, much of our understanding of the GOC is based on conceptual theories that represent the global ocean as a single basin connected to a circumpolar channel representing the Southern Ocean. Here, we compare a single-basin conceptual model with a two-basin model comprising an active basin, where sinking occurs, and a passive basin, where it does not. Both configurations have the same total zonal width. To leading order, the two configurations exhibit similar equilibrium mid-depth stratification and sinking strength. However, systematic differences emerge: mid-depth stratification is shallower in the active basin and deeper in the passive basin than in the single-basin configuration. Because the sinking strength scales with stratification in the active basin, it is weaker in the two-basin configuration. We also investigate the transient adjustment to a weakening of deep-water formation, as may occur under global warming. We find that the active basin initially deepens more rapidly, whereas the passive basin deepens more slowly, than in the single-basin configuration. This difference in transient adjustment enhances the initial recovery of the overturning circulation on decadal timescales in the two-basin configuration. It also suggests that mid-depth ocean warming is enhanced in the Atlantic and reduced in the Indo-Pacific relative to predictions from single-basin theory. We verify these predictions using a three-dimensional circulation model.

title: Climate Change, the Ocean, and Human Rights
summary: Abstract Climate change poses a significant risk to the world’s ocean, and consequently, to the enjoyment of human rights by millions of people worldwide. The ocean is a climate regulator due to its characteristics as a sink that facilitate
content: Abstract Climate change poses a significant risk to the world’s ocean, and consequently, to the enjoyment of human rights by millions of people worldwide. The ocean is a climate regulator due to its characteristics as a sink that facilitates the uptake and redistribution of anthropogenic carbon dioxide and heat, and it is a vital component of the hydrological cycle. Importantly, the ocean provides a myriad of services to people, including food and freshwater, renewable energy, health and well-being, cultural values, income, trade, and transport. The effects of emitting greenhouse gases into the atmosphere are complex and interdependent but generally manifest in four major stressors on the ocean, namely: ocean warming, ocean acidification, ocean deoxygenation, and sea-level rise. Changes in marine life, the increased frequency and severity of hurricanes, floods, and storm surges leading to the loss of habitable land due to climate change, pose risks to the food security of millions of people and to several human rights, such as the rights to life, health, safety, an adequate standard of living, and culture. This chapter addresses climate change and its impact on human rights at sea. It provides a brief scientific background to climate change impacts on the ocean before analysing how the various impact categories pose threats to human rights.

title: The Carbon Monoxide Audit: Photochemical Bookkeeping for the Methane Mars Destroys
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Methane destruction is not invisible. Photochemistry converts each methane molecule, through a short chain of intermediates, into carbon monoxide, and carbon monoxide is abundant and well measured on Mars. That makes the carbon monoxide bud
content: Methane destruction is not invisible. Photochemistry converts each methane molecule, through a short chain of intermediates, into carbon monoxide, and carbon monoxide is abundant and well measured on Mars. That makes the carbon monoxide budget an independent audit: the methane sink, whatever it is, must pay its carbon into a reservoir whose size and lifetime are known. This budget performs the audit for the standard lifetime and for the fast sink. Carbon monoxide production from methane equals the methane destruction rate molecule for molecule. The steady carbon monoxide contribution is that production times the carbon monoxide lifetime, expressed as a mixing ratio through the shared inventory conversion, and compared with the observed abundance dominated by carbon dioxide photolysis. Headline values are co steady inventory from ch4 tonnes co27 = 191.8; co mixing from ch4 background ppb co27 = 0.01271; co observed mixing ppb co27 = 700; co fraction of observed background co27 = 1.816e-05; co production high case tonnes per year co27 = 456.7; co mixing from ch4 high ppb co27 = 0.1816. The fraction entries, from about two thousandths of one percent up to under three percent, mark the full range of what methane destruction could ever write into this ledger.

title: Evaluation of feeding preferences in two heterotrophic temperate gorgonian species under controlled aquarium conditions
summary: Corals play an important role in ecosystems, and with the continued threats they are exposed to, there is a need to protect and restore them. Knowing the optimal conditions under which they can grow and reproduce in controlled environments
content: Corals play an important role in ecosystems, and with the continued threats they are exposed to, there is a need to protect and restore them. Knowing the optimal conditions under which they can grow and reproduce in controlled environments is fundamental, and understanding their feeding patterns is key to making them thrive in these conditions. In the present study, different types of food (live Artemia nauplii and frozen copepods, cyclops, red plankton, and rotifers) were tested in two species of heterotrophic gorgonians: Paramuricea grayi and Eunicella verrucosa kept at Oceanário de Lisboa, to determine their feeding preferences. The results showed that P. grayi is less reliant on food stimuli to open its polyps and shows fewer signs of disturbance ( e.g ., polyp closure) under routine maintenance, while E. verrucosa is more selective and requires specific food cues to promote polyp opening and feeding ( e.g ., cyclops and red plankton). E. verrucosa acts as a selective feeder with strong preferences for certain prey ( e.g ., rotifers and red plankton), whereas P. grayi specialises in 24 h old Artemia nauplii and copepods. These results underscore the importance of considering species-specific differences in coral biology and ecology when maintaining these species in controlled conditions for conservation, aquarium husbandry, and educational purposes.

title: Soil Microbial Carbon Fixation Capacity Across Contrasting Restoration Contexts in Yellow River Delta Wetlands: Associations with Soil Conditions and Carbon-Fixing Communities
summary: Microbial carbon fixation is important for soil carbon sequestration in coastal wetlands. Ecological restoration has been widely implemented to recover the structure and functioning of degraded coastal wetlands, yet its effects on microbial
content: Microbial carbon fixation is important for soil carbon sequestration in coastal wetlands. Ecological restoration has been widely implemented to recover the structure and functioning of degraded coastal wetlands, yet its effects on microbial carbon fixation remain insufficiently understood. To address this knowledge gap, we analyzed changes in soil physicochemical properties, carbon fractions, microbial carbon fixation potential, and carbon-fixing microbial community composition and functions in freshwater-restored wetlands (FRZ), Suaeda salsa -restored wetlands (SRZ), and natural Suaeda salsa zone used as the unrestored reference (NSZ) in the Yellow River Delta. Compared with NSZ, FRZ generally showed higher microbial carbon fixation rates, whereas microbial carbon fixation in SRZ was relatively constrained, particularly in autumn. The mean fixation rate across the four sampling seasons was 3.6 times higher in FRZ than in SRZ. Carbon-fixing community composition differed among restoration zones, with Ignavibacterium and Desulfatitalea enriched in FRZ and Candidatus Promineifilum and Nitrospira enriched in SRZ. The enrichment of the Calvin cycle and its key genes, cbbL and cbbM , in FRZ may be associated with reduced soil salinity and increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) content. The weakened Calvin cycle and relative enrichment of the 3-hydroxypropionate (3-HP) cycle in SRZ may be associated with reduced DOC availability and elevated nitrate concentrations. Overall, different restoration strategies may influence microbial carbon fixation potential in coastal wetland soils by altering key soil conditions, particularly salinity, DOC, and nitrate. These findings improve our understanding of how restoration-associated soil conditions are linked to microbially mediated carbon sequestration and provide insights for managing coastal wetland carbon sink functions.

title: UV-C Irradiation Modulates Carbon and Nitrogen Cycles in Nile Tilapia Recirculating Aquaculture Systems
summary: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RASs) continuously accumulate organic carbon and nitrogen, relying on microbial nutrient-reduction efficiency to support fish production performance. Previous UV-C studies in aquaculture have focused on di
content: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RASs) continuously accumulate organic carbon and nitrogen, relying on microbial nutrient-reduction efficiency to support fish production performance. Previous UV-C studies in aquaculture have focused on disinfection and pathogen control, with limited research on carbon–nitrogen dynamics. This study evaluated continuous UV-C irradiation in a RAS for 30 days using Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), comparing conventional and UV-C-treated systems with three replicates each (n = 3). Water quality, carbon and nitrogen dynamics, bacterial abundance, plankton density, and fish production were monitored throughout the experimental period. UV-C was associated with 59.1% and 59.2% reductions in estimated organic carbon and the carbon accumulation rate, respectively. Bacterial abundance and plankton density decreased by 69.1% and 26.7%, coinciding with reduced capacity of microbial and planktonic nutrient sinks within the system. UV-C irradiation was able to reduce NH4+, and NO3− up to 22.0% and 10.6%, respectively. Higher NO2− in UV-C was increased to 1.08 mg/L due to shifts in carbon availability and microbial community structure. Residual nitrogen increased by 17.7% because nitrogen fluxes shifted toward assimilative pathways. Consequently, nitrogen utilization efficiency improved, as reflected by higher nitrogen efficiency factor, nitrification ratio, and nitrogen–carbon transformation ratio. UV-C treatment increased final biomass by 14.1%, achieved 100% survival, and reduced FCR by 24.3% compared with Ct, suggesting its potential to modify carbon–nitrogen dynamics and improve resource-use efficiency in RAS.

title: Particle-associated microbial respiration, production, and community composition across ocean basins
summary: Microbes play a vital role in the turnover of particulate organic carbon (POC) as it sinks from surface waters to the deep ocean. Factors such as temperature, oxygen, substrate quality, and microbial community structure can influence the de
content: Microbes play a vital role in the turnover of particulate organic carbon (POC) as it sinks from surface waters to the deep ocean. Factors such as temperature, oxygen, substrate quality, and microbial community structure can influence the depths and rates at which microbes solubilize and respire POC. Establishing direct relationships between these variables could improve models of the ocean carbon cycle. Here, we determine the relationships between environmental conditions (temperature, oxygen concentration), net accumulation of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), shifts in microbial community structure, and measurements of POC-attached microbial production and in situ respiration rates in the mesopelagic zone of the Eastern Tropical Pacific, North Atlantic, North Pacific, Southern Ocean, and Santa Barbara Basin. We identified positive correlations between net DOC accumulation rates and particle-associated bacterial production, suggesting a coupling between microbes’ ability to hydrolyze available organic matter and the incorporation of that carbon into bacterial biomass. In contrast, there were no significant cross-basin relationships between temperature or oxygen and bacterial production, respiration, or bacterial growth efficiency (BGE). In regions with moderate to high C-specific respiration rates, we observed large increases in fast-growing copiotrophs during particle incubations, leading to strong negative relationships between community diversity and C-specific respiration. This trend demonstrates that life strategies of the dominant taxa in the particle-attached community (e.g. fast-growing copiotrophs) dictate basin-scale patterns of respiration on sinking particles. Our work provides insight into the complex interactions among microbial community structure, environmental conditions, and microbially mediated transformations of sinking POC.

title: Controls of Radiocarbon in Dissolved Organic Carbon in the Southwestern Indian Ocean
summary: Abstract The Southwestern Indian Ocean is a hydrographically and geologically complex area featuring prominent upwelling and deep basins separated by mid‐ocean ridges. Radiocarbon content (Δ 14 C) of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) was measu
content: Abstract The Southwestern Indian Ocean is a hydrographically and geologically complex area featuring prominent upwelling and deep basins separated by mid‐ocean ridges. Radiocarbon content (Δ 14 C) of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) was measured at three stations (24°S–3°S). In the intermediate layer (200–1,500 m), a multiple linear regression (MLR) model using salinity, temperature, and apparent oxygen utilization demonstrated that conservative water mass mixing predominantly controls DOC Δ 14 C variability. In the deep layer (>2,000 m), a northward decline in DOC Δ 14 C values was not reproduced by MLR predictions. This pattern may partly reflect varying contributions of Circumpolar Deep Water and Indian Deep Water, combined with addition of aged DOC or selective removal of younger DOC. Older radiocarbon signatures of DOC were associated with elevated δ 3 He, suggesting an influence from hydrothermal processes.

title: Micron-precision depth control in automated volumetric laser ablation with ultrashort laser pulses
summary: Abstract Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altere
content: Abstract Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altered laser-material coupling caused by the formation of Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS). This work presents an industrial-grade setup for closed-loop volumetric ablation that integrates an ultrafast laser, a galvanometer scanner, and coaxial Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for real-time depth control. To overcome measurement artifacts arising from the evolving surface morphology and local fluctuations of the OCT depth signal, two complementary correction strategies were implemented. First, a morphology-dependent initial OCT depth offset is determined by extrapolating the stabilized depth progression and subsequently compensated. Second, a pixel-wise moving average of the OCT depth measurements provides a robust termination criterion for local laser processing. The developed processing system with the advanced control software enabled precise and reproducible laser ablation of volumetric structures in AISI 304 stainless steel with a depth accuracy of 1 μm to 2 μm regardless of the investigated initial surface states and process parameters for target depths ranging from 50 μm to 500 μm.

title: Testing the effectiveness of loss vs. gain frames in climate change messaging: a multi-country study
summary: This study examines how gain-framed vs. loss-framed messages about climate change influence perceived severity of climate change impacts, self-reported information-seeking intentions (i.e., desire to learn more about climate change mitigati
content: This study examines how gain-framed vs. loss-framed messages about climate change influence perceived severity of climate change impacts, self-reported information-seeking intentions (i.e., desire to learn more about climate change mitigation), and information seeking behavior (i.e., clicking on a link to learn more about climate change mitigation) across 26 countries. In this online experiment, participants are randomly assigned to read either a loss-framed or a gain-framed message about climate change. We hypothesize that perceived severity of climate change impacts, self-reported desire to learn, and information seeking behavior will be higher in the loss frame condition than in the gain frame condition, even when controlling for baseline levels of these variables. Additionally, we will test whether the relationship between message framing and the outcome variables is mediated by climate emotions (namely, hope and anxiety).

title: Climate-Smart Irrigation: Multiple Perspectives for Better Decision-Making
summary: Climate-smart irrigation (CSI) links agricultural productivity and livelihoods with adaptation, resilience, and, where feasible, mitigation. Assessing CSI is complicated by the different purposes of irrigation decisions and the scales at wh
content: Climate-smart irrigation (CSI) links agricultural productivity and livelihoods with adaptation, resilience, and, where feasible, mitigation. Assessing CSI is complicated by the different purposes of irrigation decisions and the scales at which their consequences emerge. This focused integrative review distinguishes actors from the decision perspectives through which success is judged. It identifies six non-hierarchical perspectives: user/livelihood, service/operational, resource stewardship/allocation, public policy/societal, public/development investment, and commercial/market. Three decision situations illustrate their interactions. Irrigation efficiency may benefit farmers without increasing basin water availability; solar-powered irrigation may reduce operational emissions while changing groundwater-use incentives; and scarcity allocation involves competing needs, rights, and resource risks. These situations show why success in one decision context does not necessarily indicate climate-smart performance. The review examines the boundaries and strength of supporting evidence, distinguishing demonstrated outcomes from indirect evidence and enabling conditions. The six perspectives are not criteria that every irrigation decision must satisfy. Their value lies in revealing dependencies, consequences, and evidence beyond the immediate decision position. CSI can therefore be assessed more clearly by examining what irrigation decisions achieve, for whom, under what conditions, at what scale, and with what climate relevance.

title: Data for: Multicriteria Decision Analysis of Blue-Green Infrastructure based on Multifunctional Performance and Stakeholder Preferences
summary: **Abstract.** Blue-green infrastructure (BGI) has been widely recognized as a multifunctional solution for cities since it can simultaneously contribute to stormwater management, heat mitigation, and biodiversity conservation. However, deci
content: **Abstract.** Blue-green infrastructure (BGI) has been widely recognized as a multifunctional solution for cities since it can simultaneously contribute to stormwater management, heat mitigation, and biodiversity conservation. However, deciding on BGI elements, such as green roofs or ponds, which perform different functions, is complex. Elements are interconnected, can be combined, their performance is uncertain, and societal preferences about the desired function also vary. This study tackles the complexity and uncertainty of assessing BGI combinations with respect to 13 technical, social, environmental, and economic objectives using participatory multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA). We assessed 61 combinations of green roofs, bioretention cells, detention ponds, and pervious pavement at different implementation rates (10%, 25%, 50% and 100%) in a municipality near Zurich, Switzerland. Using multi-attribute utility theory (MAUT) and the concept of expected expected utility (EEU), we integrated probabilistic performance predictions from domain-specific models with expert judgement and elicited preferences of six local stakeholders. EEU provides a rationale to select options when predicted performance and preference data are probabilistic. Overall, bioretention cells combined with detention ponds performed well in face of heterogeneous stakeholder preferences, indicating potential consensus for our case. Lower spatial coverage performed better than higher coverage because fewer associated drawbacks, e.g., costs and potential for invasive species, outweighed marginal performance gains of higher coverage. We contribute a non-fully compensatory MAUT framework that propagates uncertainty in both performance predictions and elicited stakeholder preferences, enabling robust recommendations for planners and decision-makers.**Contents of this package.** The package contains the data and code required to reproduce the multicriteria decision analysis reported in the associated publication, including all figures and tables in the paper and its supplementary material. It comprises: (i) predicted performances of all 61 BGI options on the 13 attributes, derived from domain-specific models (EPA SWMM for combined sewer overflow and micropollutant discharge, Urban Tethys-Chloris for pedestrian-level thermal comfort, EnergyPlus for building energy demand, species accumulation and generalized additive models for biodiversity, a life-cycle-assessment meta-analysis for greenhouse gas emissions, and an equivalent-annual-cost model for life cycle costs), together with the probability distributions fitted to represent their uncertainty; (ii) the elicited preference data of six stakeholder representatives — feasible objective weight sets, the aggregation (compensation) parameter of the weighted power mean model, and risk attitude parameters of the single-attribute utility functions — in anonymized form; (iii) the R code implementing the sampling-based expected expected

title: What, when, and who? Unpacking policy coherence for the 2030 agenda and beyond
summary: Policy coherence is widely presented as central for achieving the United Nations 2030 Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Despite its prominence in academic literature and recommendations for better governance, the concept
content: Policy coherence is widely presented as central for achieving the United Nations 2030 Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Despite its prominence in academic literature and recommendations for better governance, the concept still faces challenges in its broad and diverse definition. Although an emerging strand of critical scholarship has highlighted the political nature of policy coherence and the need to include practitioners in the study of coherence, these findings are yet to be translated into practitioner guidance. At the same time, there is still a lack of discussion regarding the practice of ‘coherence-making’ and what practical governance implications this may have for the remaining years of the 2030 Agenda and beyond. In this perspective I unpack the concept of coherence through a simplified heuristic asking ‘what’, ‘when’ and ‘who’ of policy coherence. The discussion concludes the need to: (i) Address policy coherence beyond goal formulations and high-level political strategies; to bring it closer to implementation practices in terms of budget spending and planned activities. (ii) Address implicit understandings of policy sequencing; if current policy measures are framed to have a positive future effect on climate targets such implications should be made explicit, preferably with interim targets for follow-up. (iii) Place greater emphasis on the vertical aspects of policy coherence and respond to institutional fragmentation and uncertain mandates, as well as a focus on the actors responsible for policy implementation – to shed a light on the practices of ‘coherence-making’.

title: Actual Evapotranspiration During Contrasting Wet and Dry Years in a Grazed Grassland on Fen Peat With Restricted Drainage
summary: ABSTRACT Actual evapotranspiration (ET a ) is a key component of ecosystem water, energy and carbon cycling, yet field‐scale measurements from managed grasslands on fen peat remain limited, despite a growing interest in water table depth (W
content: ABSTRACT Actual evapotranspiration (ET a ) is a key component of ecosystem water, energy and carbon cycling, yet field‐scale measurements from managed grasslands on fen peat remain limited, despite a growing interest in water table depth (WTD) management as a greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation strategy. This study quantified ET a using eddy covariance over two climatically contrasting years (2023–2024) in an intensively managed grassland on fen peat in Ireland, which had a flume installed in field drains to limit the loss of water from the ecosystem. Annual ET a decreased by 29.6% from 373 ± 28.4 mm in 2023 to 263.0 ± 7.2 mm in 2024, despite similar air temperatures and available energy. Reference crop evapotranspiration (ET 0 ) calculated using FAO‐56 Penman–Monteith was comparable for both years (584 and 581 mm, respectively) while crop coefficient (Kc) also decreased from 0.63 to 0.45. Incoming shortwave radiation was the strongest predictor of ETa, while a tensor‐product smooth revealed a significant joint nonlinear effect of vapour pressure deficit (VPD) and water‐table depth (WTD) on ETa (EDF = 11.58, F = 27.95, p < 0.001), indicating that the influence of atmospheric demand varied with WTD. Maximum daily ET a occurred at intermediate WTD (50–70 cm below the surface), whereas near‐saturated or deeper WTDs (> 70 cm below the surface) reduced ET a . These findings indicate that WTD can influence ET a by modifying vegetation response to atmospheric demand, highlighting how hydrological management of agricultural fens may influence vegetation water use, productivity and GHG mitigation strategies.

title: From Qualitative to Quantitative: A Data‐Driven Error Budget for Satellite Water Vapor Product Bias
summary: Abstract Satellite‐derived precipitable water vapor (PWV) products are widely used for meteorological and climatological research, yet the relative contributions of environmental and observational variables to product uncertainties remain u
content: Abstract Satellite‐derived precipitable water vapor (PWV) products are widely used for meteorological and climatological research, yet the relative contributions of environmental and observational variables to product uncertainties remain unquantified. Here, we present an explainable machine‐learning framework that integrates extreme gradient boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to establish a data‐driven error budget for satellite PWV product bias. The model accurately characterizes nonlinear relationships between product bias and multiple influencing factors, with an R 2 of 0.70, an RMSE of 2.19 mm, and an MAE of 1.57 mm. The SHAP‐based error budget reveals that background atmospheric moisture is the dominant contributor (29.69%), followed by surface temperature (14.27%), latitude (11.35%), and longitude (9.34%). Moving beyond previous qualitative evaluations, this framework provides a quantitative decomposition of satellite PWV product bias into multiple environmental and observational variables. The approach can be adapted to other evaluation metrics and extended to other satellite‐derived water vapor and geophysical products.

title: A causal decision framework for selecting industry 4.0 technologies to overcome open innovation barriers in construction
summary: The construction industry has long struggled to embrace open innovation, not for lack of intent, but because of deeply embedded financial, organizational, and cultural barriers that resist change. This study responds to that challenge by bu
content: The construction industry has long struggled to embrace open innovation, not for lack of intent, but because of deeply embedded financial, organizational, and cultural barriers that resist change. This study responds to that challenge by building an integrated decision-support framework that identifies which Industry 4.0 technologies are best positioned to address these barriers. The research followed a three-stage design. Following a systematic literature review and expert content validation, 11 open innovation barriers and 7 technologies were retained. Then, a two-method analytical sequence combining Pythagorean Fuzzy DEMATEL (PF-DEMATEL) with Grey MABAC applied. PF-DEMATEL mapped the causal structure among the barriers, identifying inadequate support from top management and their risk attitude (C2; weight = 0.1119, D + R = 4.566) as the central systemic mediator, while difficulty in finding suitable human resources for R&D (C6; D − R = 1.730) and market uncertainty regarding innovative products (C4; D − R = 1.023) emerged as the dominant root causes driving the broader barrier network. Grey MABAC then ranked the seven technologies by their weighted mitigation potential, placing Building Information Modelling well ahead of the field, followed by the Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence. The findings offer construction practitioners a sequenced, evidence-based roadmap for digital transformation that targets the most influential barriers first and builds collaborative innovation capacity from the ground up.

title: Pathways for the Sustainable Development of Distributed Generation Under Key Influencing Factors: Integrating Circular Economy Principles—A Case Study of the Sverdlovsk Oblast
summary: The global energy sector, as the primary anthropogenic source of greenhouse gas emissions, is undergoing a profound eco-modernization driven by the “3D” concept of decarbonization, decentralization, and digitalization. However, fossil fuels
content: The global energy sector, as the primary anthropogenic source of greenhouse gas emissions, is undergoing a profound eco-modernization driven by the “3D” concept of decarbonization, decentralization, and digitalization. However, fossil fuels still account for a significant share of the energy mix, especially in fossil fuel-exporting countries. The development of decentralized energy could play an important role in mitigation of GHG emissions and comprehensive eco-modernization of the energy sector. This study aims to develop a scientifically grounded scenario-based model for the development of distributed generation in a region with dominance of centralized generation and grid. A distinctive feature of the proposed tool is its systematic consideration of factors and the magnitude of their influence, which allows the model to be more precisely adapted to a specific territory. In addition, the model enables the incorporation of circular economy principles into the formulation of a distributed generation development strategy, creating an additional driver for the energy transition. The methodological approach is tested using the energy complex of the Sverdlovsk oblast, which is part of Russia’s Unified Energy System, thereby confirming its viability and operationalizability.

title: Flipping Field Cores to Disentangle Drivers of Peat Decomposition in Drained Coastal Peatlands
summary: ABSTRACT Peatland drainage and rewetting trigger microbial and biogeochemical responses that impact carbon cycling and greenhouse gas emissions. The direction and magnitude of these responses depend on environmental factors and peat charact
content: ABSTRACT Peatland drainage and rewetting trigger microbial and biogeochemical responses that impact carbon cycling and greenhouse gas emissions. The direction and magnitude of these responses depend on environmental factors and peat characteristics. This study assessed how previously oxygen‐exposed peat responds to rewetting and how deeper anoxic layers respond to further drainage, using a flipped core field experiment as a proxy. We examined the role of site conditions, redox history, and substrate legacy on biogeochemical responses and microbial communities. A one‐year in situ field incubation was conducted in two drained coastal peatlands (Assendelft‐ASD & Rouveen‐ROU) in the Netherlands. Intact peat cores (25–125 cm depth from surface) were extracted and reinstalled either in their original orientation (controls) or flipped vertically (flipped treatments). Flipping simulated two redox transitions: surface oxic peat (25–45 cm depth from surface) shifting to anoxic conditions (rewetting) and deeper peat (105–125 cm from surface) becoming oxygenated (drainage). Harvested samples were analyzed in the laboratory for basal CO 2 and CH 4 respiration rates, microbial abundance and diversity, extracellular enzyme activities, carbon fractions, and pore‐water chemistry. Rewetting reduced CO 2 respiration rates but stimulated CH 4 production, particularly at the ROU site where methanogens were relatively more abundant. In contrast, oxygen intrusion into anoxic peat increased CO 2 emissions and shifted microbial communities toward aerobic decomposers at both sites. However, the magnitude of these effects was strongly site‐dependent, driven by differences in microbial metabolic activity. These differences in microbial activity between sites were influenced by pore‐water chemistry. ASD pore water is more brackish and richer in sulphur and dissolved organic matter in deeper layers, whereas ROU pore water has low electrical conductivity. These site‐specific responses provide useful insights into the roles of redox history, substrate quality, and microbial communities in regulating greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics. Rewetting degraded topsoil, a common restoration technique, has produced variable outcomes, underscoring both the promise and the uncertainty associated with peatland restoration efforts.

title: Marine Fuel Cell Hybrid Power Systems: Architectures, Energy Management Strategies, and Shipboard Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Maritime decarbonization has intensified interest in fuel cell hybrid power systems as a promising pathway toward low‐emission and eventually zero‐emission shipping. In such systems, the energy management strategy (EMS) plays a cru
content: ABSTRACT Maritime decarbonization has intensified interest in fuel cell hybrid power systems as a promising pathway toward low‐emission and eventually zero‐emission shipping. In such systems, the energy management strategy (EMS) plays a crucial role in coordinating fuel cells and energy storage devices, thereby shaping system efficiency, operational economy, dynamic performance, and component lifetime. However, the existing review studies remain largely automotive‐oriented or focus on isolated technologies, with limited attention to the specific operating profiles, architectural choices, and control requirements of marine applications. To address this gap, this paper presents a ship‐oriented review of fuel cell hybrid power systems and their EMSs from an optimal design perspective. First, the dynamic characteristics and operational constraints of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) and solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) relevant to shipboard applications are analyzed. Second, EMS hybrid architectures are reviewed from two complementary perspectives: energy‐unit composition (e.g., fuel cell–battery, fuel cell–battery–supercapacitor) and direct current (DC)/DC interface topology. Third, EMS approaches are classified and compared, including rule‐based, optimization‐based, learning‐based, and hybrid/hierarchical strategies. The review shows that PEMFC‐based systems and SOFC‐based systems impose fundamentally different EMS requirements. PEMFC‐oriented EMSs should focus on dynamic load allocation, transient suppression, and degradation mitigation, whereas SOFC‐oriented EMSs should emphasize steady baseload operation, hierarchical supervisory control, and thermal–electrical coordination. Based on these insights, a design‐oriented mapping logic linking fuel cell type, hybrid architecture, EMS form, and ship mission profile is synthesized. The analysis suggests that system design should follow a mission‐driven logic in which ship operating characteristics determine load profiles, which then guide the selection of fuel cell technology, energy storage configuration, and EMS hierarchy. Finally, the key research needs are discussed, including health‐aware EMS, multi‐timescale coordination, digital‐twin‐based validation, and lifecycle‐oriented design.

title: Atomic‐Level Modulation of Boron Sites via Cobalt Single Atoms on CO 2 ‐Derived Carbon for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
summary: Electrochemical two‐electron oxygen reduction (2e − ORR) is an attractive alternative route for the production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). Boron (B)‐doped carbon materials have been widely investigated for selective H 2 O 2 electrosynt
content: Electrochemical two‐electron oxygen reduction (2e − ORR) is an attractive alternative route for the production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). Boron (B)‐doped carbon materials have been widely investigated for selective H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis. However, the most stable and abundant B configuration in the carbon basal plane shows limited catalytic performance, requiring a strategy to tune it into highly active B sites. Herein, a cobalt (Co) single‐atom‐modulated B‐doped porous carbon (ZNCC‐0.015) is synthesized through a one‐pot CO 2 conversion process using NaBH 4 and ZIF‐67. The Co─N 4 configuration electronically modulates neighboring B sites by electron transfer from the less electronegative Co to B, thereby optimizing OOH* adsorption energy and enabling B to function as a more efficient active site. ZNCC‐0.015 exhibits highly active and selective (>80%) performance for H 2 O 2 production, achieving an onset potential of 0.780 V versus RHE and improved ORR kinetics. It maintains a Faradaic efficiency (FE) above 80% over a wide potential window in the H‐cell, with a maximum H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.98 mol g cat −1 h −1 under bulk electrolysis conditions. This work proposes that transition metals regulate the electronic structure of adjacent heteroatoms in carbon frameworks, thereby tuning them into active sites for efficient H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis.

title: Pushing the Limit of Multisite Cooperation via Long‐Distance Synergy Over Atomically Dispersed Catalysts
summary: ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have revolutionized heterogeneous catalysis through near‐unity metal utilization and precisely defined active sites. However, their intrinsic limitation—linear scaling relations governing intermediate b
content: ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have revolutionized heterogeneous catalysis through near‐unity metal utilization and precisely defined active sites. However, their intrinsic limitation—linear scaling relations governing intermediate binding energies on isolated metal centers—fundamentally impedes multifunctional performance in complex multi‐step reactions, including the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR), and nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR). This review systematically organizes and critically synthesizes an emerging research direction of long‐distance synergistic catalysis, wherein nanoscale spatial separation between functional metal species is reframed as a critical, independently tunable design dimension rather than a synthetic deficiency. We deconstruct this frontier mechanistically into two complementary pillars: static electronic synergy—encompassing support‐mediated orbital modulation, remote charge shuttling, and neighbor‐assisted stabilization without mass transport—and dynamic spillover synergy—involving kinetically facilitated intermediate migration (H * , OH * , NO 2 − ) that mimics enzymatic channeling across segregated sites. Critically underpinned by operando spectroscopy, atomic‐resolution microscopy, and first‐principles simulations, this framework establishes quantitative distance–performance relationships spanning renewable energy conversion, environmental remediation, and sustainable chemical synthesis. This work provides a mechanistically guided design framework, rather than a universal theory, for next‐generation cooperative catalytic architectures transcending single‐site constraints.

title: Effects of Ferric Nitrate-Modified Biochar on N2O Emissions from an Acidic Moso Bamboo Forest Soil
summary: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas, and acidic forest soils are major sources. Biochar can mitigate N2O emissions in some soils but its effectiveness is pH-dependent, and can vary with biochar modification. It is unclear whether
content: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas, and acidic forest soils are major sources. Biochar can mitigate N2O emissions in some soils but its effectiveness is pH-dependent, and can vary with biochar modification. It is unclear whether modified biochar reduces or increases N2O emissions in acidic forest soils. This study was designed primarily to evaluate ferric nitrate-modified biochar as an amendment for improving soil pH in acidic Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) forest soils, and to determine whether this pH improvement can be achieved without increasing N2O emissions. We investigated effects of modified biochar on N2O emissions and nitrogen transformation genes in acidic Moso bamboo forest soils. An incubation study (121 days; 5% w/w dose; four replicates per treatment) included seven treatments: control, pristine biochar (B), and ferric nitrate-modified biochars (MB1–MB5) prepared at different pH values. Cumulative N2O emissions were lowest in the control and 4.8–7.7-fold higher in all biochar variants than in the control, peaking at MB3 and declining at MB5. Soil pH was the main factor: the N2O emission rate peaked at pH ≈ 5.18, and the (nirK + nirS)/nosZ ratio showed a fitted maximum at pH 5.19, although this quadratic fit was not significantly better than a linear model. Bacterial amoA and nosZ abundances increased with pH. Under MB treatments, N2O emission rate was negatively correlated with pH and nosZ and positively correlated with ammonium nitrogen, nitrate nitrogen, and the (nirK + nirS)/nosZ ratio (all p < 0.05). Soil pH and the amount of added nitrate varied in tandem across treatments, so their effects could not be fully disentangled.

title: Analysis of Voltage Stability in Distribution System in Presence of Electric Vehicle and Distributed Generator
summary: Due to its advantages over fossil fuel-powered vehicles in terms of both economy and ecology, the employment of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased recently. As the market for EVs expands, the electric grid is facing more difficulties mee
content: Due to its advantages over fossil fuel-powered vehicles in terms of both economy and ecology, the employment of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased recently. As the market for EVs expands, the electric grid is facing more difficulties meeting the demand for EVs, particularly in the distribution networks. The negative effect of EV charging loads on the power system's operating parameters has been observed with the widespread revival of electric vehicles (EVs). Increased peak load demand, smaller reserve margins, voltage instability, and reliability issues are caused by the increase in charging station loads. The purpose of this work is to examine how the increase in loads from EV charging stations affects the distribution network's voltage stability and power losses along with integration of Distributed generator in the system. The complete analysis is carried out on the practical 39-bus radial distribution network for increase in load due to interconnection of electric vehicle to the grid for three different types of EV charger for various load conditions. The results indicates that with DG integration system can withstand the increase in load due to EV connection up to a certain load level, above which, the increase in EV load results in voltage stability problem and increase in system losses. Finally the results indicate that, the performance of Distribution system in terms of voltage and losses depends on placement of DG and electric vehicle in the system.

title: In vitro Gas Production Kinetics and Methane Output of Complete Feed Silage Supplemented with Chestnut Tannin
source: Journal of Animal Health and Production
summary: Chestnut tannin is a plant-derived polyphenolic compound that may modify ruminal fermentation and gas production during feed degradation. This study evaluated the effects of chestnut tannin supplementation on cumulative gas production, tota
content: Chestnut tannin is a plant-derived polyphenolic compound that may modify ruminal fermentation and gas production during feed degradation. This study evaluated the effects of chestnut tannin supplementation on cumulative gas production, total gas production, gas-production kinetics, and methane-related variables of complete-feed silage using an in vitro rumen fermentation system. Five treatments were evaluated: T0, complete-feed silage without chestnut tannin; T1, T0 supplemented with 0.50% chestnut tannin; T2, T0 supplemented with 1.00% chestnut tannin; T3, T0 supplemented with 1.50% chestnut tannin; and T4, T0 supplemented with 2.00% chestnut tannin on a dry-matter basis. After 30 days of ensiling, the samples were incubated with rumen fluid and McDougall’s buffer for 72 h. Gas-production kinetics were estimated using an exponential model, and methane concentration was analysed by gas chromatography. Data were analysed by analysis of variance followed by Duncan’s multiple range test when the treatment effect was significant. Chestnut tannin supplementation significantly affected total gas production, potential gas production, and the fractional gas-production rate constant (P<0.05). Mean total gas production ranged from 180 mL/g DM in T2 to 192 mL/g DM in T0, whereas potential gas production ranged from 145 mL in T4 to 161 mL in T3. Chestnut tannin did not significantly affect CH₄/total gas or CH₄/substrate; however, both variables showed a tendency to vary among treatments (0.05< P<0.10), with T3 having the lowest numerical means. It can be concluded that chestnut tannin supplementation altered the in vitro gas-production characteristics of complete-feed silage, although no single inclusion level was consistently optimal.

title: Data-driven pluvial flood modeling for urban regions: An investigation of spatial generalizability
summary: Accurate and rapid flood prediction is essential for effective urban flood risk management, yet physics-based hydrodynamic models are computationally prohibitive for real-time or ensemble simulations. This study presents a machine learning-
content: Accurate and rapid flood prediction is essential for effective urban flood risk management, yet physics-based hydrodynamic models are computationally prohibitive for real-time or ensemble simulations. This study presents a machine learning-based surrogate modeling framework leveraging Random Forest, XGBoost, and U-Net to provide fast and reliable predictions of pluvial flood depth and velocity with generalizability to unseen hyetographs and locations. A key innovation is the introduction of a physically consistent reference depth/velocity input, which embeds hydraulic context and enhances transferability. Using hydrodynamic simulations for Montreal Island as training, validation, and testing data, the U-Net model consistently outperformed other models, achieving the lowest RMSEs for flood depth (0.093 m) and velocity (0.130 m/s) in test regions, and maintaining robust performance (RMSEs of 0.114 m and 0.151 m/s) when transferred to an unseen city (Ottawa). The presented framework offers significant potential for integration into real-time pluvial flood warning systems and urban resilience planning.

title: Orthounimodal Distributionally Robust Optimization: Representation, Computation, and Multivariate Extreme Event Applications
summary: This paper studies a basic notion of distributional shape known as orthounimodality (OU) and its use in shape-constrained distributionally robust optimization (DRO). As a key motivation, we argue how such type of DRO is well suited to tackl
