content: This paper studies a basic notion of distributional shape known as orthounimodality (OU) and its use in shape-constrained distributionally robust optimization (DRO). As a key motivation, we argue how such type of DRO is well suited to tackle multivariate extreme event estimation by giving statistically valid confidence bounds on target extremal probabilities. In particular, we explain how our approach can alleviate the bias–variance trade-off and other technical complications in conventional extreme value theory, while gaining interpretability and robustness compared with existing distributional shape notions used in the DRO literature. We characterize the extreme points of the OU distribution class in terms of what we call OU sets and build a corresponding Choquet representation, which subsequently allows us to reduce DRO under OU constraints into moment problems over infinite-dimensional random variables. We then develop, in the bivariate setting, a geometric approach to reduce such moment problems into finite dimension via a specially constructed variational problem designed to eliminate suboptimal solutions. Numerical results illustrate how our approach gives rise to valid and competitive confidence bounds for extremal probabilities. Funding: This work was supported by the National Science Foundation [Grants CMMI-1834710 and IIS-1849280]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.2023.0143 .

title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
summary: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United N
content: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. After committing to responsible investing (via United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI)), fund managers increase private information acquisition activities, that is, corporate site visits, particularly focusing on environmental and social issues. These visits generate negligible private investment value for the visiting funds. However, the information environment at the stock level improves following these visits with lower consensus analyst forecast errors. In addition to the information production role of these visits, they also generate positive externalities for other stakeholders through incremental improvements in the sustainability practices of the firms receiving sustainability-focused site visits from UNPRI fund managers. Collectively, the paper highlights the private costs and social benefits of responsible investing. This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance. Funding: S. Agarwal and J. Sulaeman acknowledge research support from Sustainable and Green Finance Institute [Grant WBS A-0006413-00-00]. Y. Zhang acknowledges financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72402239] and China Scholarship Council. This work was supported by the Ministry of Education, Singapore [Social Science and Humanities Research Thematic Grant SSRC2024-SSHRTG-022]. Any opinions, findings and conclusions or recommendations expressed in this material are those of the author(s) and do not reflect the views of the Social Science Research Council (Singapore) and the Ministry of Education (Singapore). Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08443 .

title: Two-layer micromagnetic modeling of ferrimagnets: Temperature-driven compensation and skyrmion dynamics
summary: Ferrimagnets host unique compensation phenomena that enable ultrafast dynamics and efficient current-driven manipulation, but their micromagnetic modeling remains challenging due to the need to resolve coupled sublattices. Here, we introduc
content: Ferrimagnets host unique compensation phenomena that enable ultrafast dynamics and efficient current-driven manipulation, but their micromagnetic modeling remains challenging due to the need to resolve coupled sublattices. Here, we introduce an equivalent two-layer model implemented in the widely used MuMax3 framework that qualitatively reproduces the temperature-dependent magnetic and angular momentum compensation states of ferrimagnetic alloys, including thermally induced, sperimagnetic-like fanning of sublattice moments. By assigning different magnetic parameters and gyromagnetic ratios to the two layers, we demonstrate that the magnetic and angular momentum compensation temperatures can be separated. As a key application, we simulate current-induced skyrmion motion and find that, at the angular momentum compensation point, the skyrmion Hall effect vanishes while the longitudinal velocity reaches a maximum. Modeling distinct gyromagnetic ratios in the two layers requires a modified version of MuMax3 with region-dependent g-factors. Our approach provides an efficient framework for qualitative investigations of a broad range of ferrimagnetic phenomena, including composition-dependent compensation, domain-wall dynamics, and effects arising from nonuniform current or temperature distributions.

title: Use of infrared thermography and machine learning to predict the infectious etiology of subclinical bovine mastitis in a robotic milking system
summary: Abstract Mastitis is a major challenge for dairy production, and infrared thermography (IRT) is a promising non-invasive tool for monitoring udder health. This study evaluated whether thermal information obtained by IRT, combined with anima
content: Abstract Mastitis is a major challenge for dairy production, and infrared thermography (IRT) is a promising non-invasive tool for monitoring udder health. This study evaluated whether thermal information obtained by IRT, combined with animal, production, and environmental variables, could be used in supervised machine learning models to predict subclinical mastitis (SCM) and its most probable infectious etiology in pasture-raised cows managed under a voluntary milking system. Eighty-nine lactating cows from a single herd underwent thermographic evaluation over six months, and milk samples from 530 mammary quarters were analyzed, of which 61 (11.5%) were positive for SCM. Mean (TMED), minimum (TCOLD), and maximum (THOT) udder surface temperatures, somatic cell count (SCC), milk composition, animal characteristics, and environmental data were used to develop a multilevel binary logistic model and a multinomial logistic model. The binary model, including SCC and TCOLD, showed an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.96. However, using a ten-fold internal cross-validation, AUC decreased to 0.81 and sensitivity decreased from 0.90 to 0.33. The thermographic variables improved model fit modestly but significantly, whereas SCC accounted for most of the predictive information. In the multinomial model, apparent AUC values ranged from 0.78 to 0.99 across microorganism categories, but sensitivity was low for coagulase-negative staphylococci (0.03) and Staphylococcus aureus (0.30) and decreased further in leave-one-animal-out internal cross-validation. IRT-derived variables may be a complementary component of multivariable predictive models, but the validation of the present models in independent herds and under different management conditions is required previous its use for SCM diagnosis.

title: Personalized Causal Recourse: A Human-In-The-Loop Approach
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: Algorithmic recourse addresses the challenge of providing tailored recommendations to users affected by unfavorable machine learning decisions, in potentially high-stakes scenarios. Traditional approaches to recourse often rely on the close
content: Algorithmic recourse addresses the challenge of providing tailored recommendations to users affected by unfavorable machine learning decisions, in potentially high-stakes scenarios. Traditional approaches to recourse often rely on the closest counterfactual explanations or assume a priori knowledge of a user’s causal structure, resulting in interventions that overlook individual contexts and specific feature interactions. To overcome these limitations, we study a human-in-the-loop framework that iteratively approximates the user’s structural causal model through interactive queries via Bayesian inference before producing recourse recommendations. This framework exploits humans’ feedback to improve the identification of causal effects, allowing personalized recourse that is plausible, cost-effective, and aligned with the actual causal dependencies of each user. As a proof of concept, we evaluate this framework through simulated human responses. Our simulations across linear and non-linear causal models show promising results, though challenges remain in capturing complex, non-linear structures, emphasizing the importance of accurate approximations and robust noise distribution modeling.

title: Curvature‐matched 5‐axis CNC machining using non‐circular toroidal cutters
summary: Abstract Highly accurate 5‐axis CNC machining requires a good, ideally higher order, match between the cutting tool and the reference surface along a common tangent direction. It has been shown that one can apply this, so‐called curvature m
content: Abstract Highly accurate 5‐axis CNC machining requires a good, ideally higher order, match between the cutting tool and the reference surface along a common tangent direction. It has been shown that one can apply this, so‐called curvature matching, even to convex surfaces using circular toroidal tools, by exploiting their interior hyperbolic points [BBR*21]. However, such an approach typically requires a large tool and is very restrictive in terms of motion planning due to possible global collisions between the tool and the material block. In contrast, in this work we consider toroidal tools with non‐convex inserts, which allow us to bring the hyperbolic points to the exterior side of the toroidal cutters, and therefore enable curvature‐matched machining without requiring large tools or restricting tool movability. The proposed framework is compared against path‐ and motion‐planning using classical circular tori on several benchmark geometries and demonstrates the superior behavior of cutting tools that have both elliptic and hyperbolic points on the cutting edge.

title: The effect of being a poll worker on democratic attitudes in a post-conflict society: evidence from an experiment in Colombia
summary: This paper examines how citizens’ direct participation in democratic processes boosts attitudes toward democratic practices. Focusing on compulsory poll working, we argue that citizens selected to work at polling stations on Election Day ga
content: This paper examines how citizens’ direct participation in democratic processes boosts attitudes toward democratic practices. Focusing on compulsory poll working, we argue that citizens selected to work at polling stations on Election Day gain additional information about democratic procedures, and that this shapes their attitudes toward electoral integrity and democracy. We test our claims by leveraging a pre-registered large-scale experiment from the 2023 Colombian regional elections. Based on a unique survey dataset of over 25,000 poll workers matched with a sample of ordinary citizens, we identify a positive and robust causal effect of electoral task management on attitudes toward electoral integrity and democracy that operates mainly via a theory-based mechanism, but also via a practice-based mechanism. Moreover, we discover that this treatment effect is smaller in municipalities heavily affected by political violence during previous civil conflict.

title: Probing the origin of the LHAASO Peanut with a hidden central accelerator
summary: A highly asymmetric, giant peanut-shaped structure has been detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) in ultrahigh-energy gamma rays at a high Galactic latitude, b≈-17.5^̧irc, suggesting anisotropic particle transp
content: A highly asymmetric, giant peanut-shaped structure has been detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) in ultrahigh-energy gamma rays at a high Galactic latitude, b≈-17.5^̧irc, suggesting anisotropic particle transport around a Galactic accelerator. We investigate whether its spectrum and morphology can arise from a hidden central accelerator embedded in a projected anisotropic halo. The baseline model accounts for the diffuse strip and central excess, while a phenomenological prescription for a localized magnetic field reorientation toward the line of sight (LOS), together with a particle-conserved remapping of the electrons downstream of the far excess into an emitting column of prescribed transverse extent, enhances the emission at the far excess position. We explore various source ages, along with different combinations of ambient magnetic field strength and parallel diffusion coefficient, while accounting for radiative cooling when estimating the viewing geometry. The exploration reveals that relatively rapid parallel transport enhances the far component, while preserving a dominant diffuse strip. Representative configurations remain compatible with the observed spectral energy distribution, although the fit far component remains weaker than the central component above 100 TeV, even in cases where their component fluxes are comparable at 25-100 TeV. These results illustrate the plausibility of a hidden central accelerator as the origin of the LHAASO Peanut, while identifying the remaining difficulty in reproducing the relative brightness of its compact components within the adopted phenomenological framework.

title: Penguatan Kemandirian Usaha melalui Manajemen Keuangan dan Pembukuan Terpadu bagi KWT Berkah Makmur, Desa Pucungbedug, Kabupaten Banjarnegara
summary: The Berkah Makmur Women Farmers’ Group (KWT) in Pucungbedug Village relies on the potential of corn and cassava grown on dryland to produce gluten-free functional foods, namely instant corn rice and cassava rice, as well as processed produc
content: The Berkah Makmur Women Farmers’ Group (KWT) in Pucungbedug Village relies on the potential of corn and cassava grown on dryland to produce gluten-free functional foods, namely instant corn rice and cassava rice, as well as processed products such as corn sticks and corn “dawet”. Despite having broad market prospects, the group’s business development is hampered by weak managerial governance, financial records that are intermingled with household affairs, and low financial literacy. This research-based Community Service Program aims to improve the KWT members’ capacity in financial management and integrated bookkeeping. The implementation method uses a participatory approach involving 11 active members of the Berkah Makmur Women’s Group through training sessions, simulations on maintaining a daily cash journal, calculating the Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), and managing profit and loss. The evaluation, which used pre-tests and post-tests, was conducted through the completion of questionnaires, with the results showing substantial descriptive improvement across all indicators, with the proportion of participants in the “Strongly Understand” category increasing for all indicators (even the indicator for understanding financial separation increased by 46%), while the “Somewhat Understand” and “Do Not Understand” categories were completely eliminated (0%). These results demonstrate that structured training can transform the group’s mindset from conventional production to a transparent and accountable business orientation, thereby supporting the Women Farmers’ Group (KWT) 's business independence.

title: Dynamical Systems Modeling of Global Health Resource Allocation under Governance Constraints
summary: Abstract Global health financing decisions must balance competing priorities: directing resources toward settings where they can generate the greatest service delivery, limiting fiduciary exposure, and ensuring that benefits are distributed
content: Abstract Global health financing decisions must balance competing priorities: directing resources toward settings where they can generate the greatest service delivery, limiting fiduciary exposure, and ensuring that benefits are distributed equitably across populations. These objectives can conflict when implementation capacity differs across countries. A constrained multi-objective optimization model is developed to make these trade-offs explicit, linking financing flows to service delivery through country-specific efficiency parameters while incorporating fiduciary risk and inter-population inequality into the allocation problem. A social planner optimizes a weighted objective that balances effective service delivery, risk mitigation, and distributional equity, allowing policy priorities to be represented explicitly through adjustable weights. A three-country numerical experiment illustrates how alternative policy priorities translate into different allocation outcomes. An efficiency-oriented allocation produces higher aggregate output ($Y=79$), representing greater efficiency-adjusted service delivery, and lower fiduciary risk ($\mathcal{R}=21$), but generates substantial disparities in per-capita benefits. An equity-oriented allocation reduces aggregate output ($Y=69$) and increases fiduciary risk ($\mathcal{R}=31$), but produces a more balanced distribution of benefits. These numerical examples are illustrative rather than empirical and are intended to make the model's trade-offs transparent and interpretable beyond a purely technical setting. The results demonstrate that efficiency, fiduciary risk, and equity cannot generally be optimized simultaneously, highlighting the importance of making allocation preferences explicit. The formulation provides a tractable basis for examining these trade-offs and a starting point for future extensions incorporating uncertainty, richer governance constraints, and empirical calibration.

title: Women’s Empowerment and Sustainable Tourism Development: The Mediating Role of Entrepreneurial Resilience in Semarang
summary: This study examines how women’s empowerment contributes to the advancement of sustainable tourism development, with entrepreneurial resilience as a mediating variable among women-owned tourism small and medium-sized enterprises. Grounded in
content: This study examines how women’s empowerment contributes to the advancement of sustainable tourism development, with entrepreneurial resilience as a mediating variable among women-owned tourism small and medium-sized enterprises. Grounded in empowerment theory and resilience theory, this study explores how economic empowerment, social empowerment, and political empowerment shape sustainable outcomes. Primary data were collected from 150 female entrepreneurs active in the tourism industry in Semarang, Indonesia, and then analyzed using structural equation modeling. The results indicate that all empowerment dimensions significantly strengthen entrepreneurial resilience directly. Economic empowerment has a direct positive impact on sustainable tourism development, while social and political empowerment do not have a direct impact on sustainable tourism development. Nevertheless, entrepreneurial resilience emerges as a meaningful determinant of sustainable tourism development and serves as a mediating pathway between the empowerment dimensions and sustainability outcomes. More specifically, entrepreneurial resilience acts as a partial mediator in the relationship involving economic and political empowerment, whereas entrepreneurial resilience acts as a full mediator in the relationship involving social empowerment. Overall, these findings confirm that empowerment alone is not sufficient to achieve sustainability, unless it is directed toward developing adaptive entrepreneurial capacity. This study enriches the existing body of knowledge by integrating perspectives on empowerment and resilience into a more integrated conceptual framework for examining sustainable tourism development.

title: Environmental conditions associated with the occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in agricultural landscapes affected by intensive livestock production farming
summary: Intensive livestock production is associated with increased pressure on aquatic environments in agricultural landscapes. The occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in waters exposed to intensive livestock production was analysed in relation
content: Intensive livestock production is associated with increased pressure on aquatic environments in agricultural landscapes. The occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in waters exposed to intensive livestock production was analysed in relation to selected physicochemical parameters. The study was conducted at two locations characterized by high livestock density and included precipitation, surface, groundwater, and well waters. The alga was detected in surface and precipitation waters, but was absent from groundwater. The occurrence of H. pluvialis was associated with moderately nutrient-enriched waters characterized by elevated conductivity and slightly alkaline pH. Elevated nutrient concentrations were recorded in waters influenced by intensive livestock production. The results suggest that H. pluvialis may represent a potential candidate indicator of aquatic environments exposed to intensive agricultural pressure. However, the observed relationships are associative rather than direct causal effects, and further studies are required to evaluate the broader indicator potential of this species under different environmental conditions.

title: DATA SCIENCE IN INSURANCE: A BIBLIOMETRIC MAPPING OF RESEARCH ON MOTOR INSURANCE CLAIMS MANAGEMENT
source: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
summary: This paper examines the role of data science in transforming insurance through a bibliometric mapping of machine learning research on motor insurance claims management. Digitalization and technologies such as artificial intelligence, IoT an
content: This paper examines the role of data science in transforming insurance through a bibliometric mapping of machine learning research on motor insurance claims management. Digitalization and technologies such as artificial intelligence, IoT and telematics are reshaping underwriting, claims processing, pricing and fraud detection, and motor insurance is a particularly prominent field of application. The study combines a narrative literature review with a bibliometric analysis of 195 Scopus-indexed documents published between 1994 and 2026, conducted with the Bibliometrix R package and Biblioshiny. The corpus is a moderately sized, interdisciplinary and fragmented field: it grows by 6.27% annually, conference papers (105) outnumber journal articles (68), and about 87% of documents appeared between 2018 and 2024. Keyword co-occurrence and thematic mapping reveal three research communities: automated claims processing based on computer vision and deep learning, fraud detection using ensemble methods, and predictive analytics for pricing, risk assessment and customer-facing operations. Trend analysis shows a shift from a method-centric to an application- and safety-centric orientation, with growing attention to deployment, security and customer trust. Theoretically, the study provides a structured map of the field’s thematic evolution. Practically, it suggests that insurers should prioritize explainability infrastructure and bias supervision alongside predictive accuracy.

title: Dataset for Non-monotonic trade-off between carbon intensity and carbon payback period in demolition-and-reconstruction: evidence from Qingdao, China
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset underpins a study of the whole-life carbon trade-off in the demolition-and-reconstruction of an ageing residential community, using the Yuanyang Garden community in Qingdao, China, as the case study. The associated research add
content: This dataset underpins a study of the whole-life carbon trade-off in the demolition-and-reconstruction of an ageing residential community, using the Yuanyang Garden community in Qingdao, China, as the case study. The associated research addresses three linked objectives: unit-area carbon intensity (CI, kgCO2/(m²·a)), the carbon payback period of the embodied carbon investment (CPP, years), and a resident need satisfaction score (RSS) constructed from observed need-prevalence rates.The dataset comprises: Resident questionnaire data (215 valid responses) covering household structure, current housing and environmental satisfaction, attitudes toward demolition-and-reconstruction, parking and greening needs, preferred dwelling size, and willingness to pay. All records are de-identified and contain only categorical attributes (age band, gender, tenure band); no names, contact details or other directly identifying information were collected.Government-staff questionnaire data (30 valid responses) from municipal and district staff in housing, planning, natural-resource and sub-district departments, covering policy difficulties, expected planning parameters and financing arrangements.A field condition survey of 84 old residential communities recording year of construction, number of stories, land area, floor area ratio, greening ratio, parking provision and structural type.Parameter settings and computation data: the parameterised life-cycle carbon model inputs, the L50(5^12) orthogonal-array experiment, the NSGA-II multi-objective optimisation outputs (Pareto solution sets under three weighting scenarios), and the TOPSIS ranking data underlying all tables and figures of the associated manuscript. All questionnaire participation was voluntary and anonymous and was based on fully informed verbal consent; no intervention, no sensitive personal data and no monetary compensation were involved.The NSGA-II source code and the raw logs of the ten fixed-seed runs are archived in a separate Zenodo record (https://zenodo.org/records/24124025).Reuse potential: the data support replication of the three-objective optimisation and decision analysis, re-weighting of the resident need satisfaction score, transfer of the modelling workflow to other demolition-and-reconstruction cases, and comparative studies of resident needs and low-carbon urban renewal.

title: Framing and Mapping Climate Regulation and Financial Governance
summary: This chapter examines the Paris Agreement with a focus on the various regulatory changes which have shaped the global response in mitigating the adverse effects of climate change. The chapter draws on the Performance Mapping of Sovereign Gr
content: This chapter examines the Paris Agreement with a focus on the various regulatory changes which have shaped the global response in mitigating the adverse effects of climate change. The chapter draws on the Performance Mapping of Sovereign Green Bond framework to illustrate how key attributes of the Paris Agreement and sovereign green bonds such as legal and regulatory impetus, governance, green financing, and the objectives of the Paris Agreement among others contribute to the attainment of the overarching goal of the Paris Agreement. The chapter also discusses how the recent rulings of the International Court of Justice will impact climate change regulation and the discourse on the role of responsibility party in combating the adverse impact of climate change on low emitting countries.

title: What non-financial disclosure research can (and cannot) learn from financial disclosure research about impression management – a structured literature review
summary: Purpose This paper reviews the literature on impression management (IM) in corporate disclosures and systematically compares research on financial disclosures (FD) and non-financial disclosures (NFD), particularly sustainability reporting.
content: Purpose This paper reviews the literature on impression management (IM) in corporate disclosures and systematically compares research on financial disclosures (FD) and non-financial disclosures (NFD), particularly sustainability reporting. Given the maturity of IM research in FD and the recent acceleration of IM research in NFD driven by societal and regulatory pressures, the study aims to identify commonalities, differences, and research gaps between both streams, and to assess how insights from FD research can inform future IM research in NFD. Design/methodology/approach We conduct a structured review of 83 archival studies published since 2000 in leading accounting and sustainability journals. The review compares FD and NFD studies along key dimensions, including motivators of IM, disclosure instruments, sample characteristics, and econometric approaches, thereby enabling a systematic assessment of methodological and conceptual differences between the two research streams. Findings The review yields four main findings. First, theoretical frameworks in NFD research remain largely disconnected from capital-market considerations that anchor FD research. Second, NFD research focuses predominantly on sustainability performance as a motivator of IM, leaving other motivators – such as CSR contracting, investor sustainability preferences, and political influence – largely unexplored. Third, prior studies emphasize textual IM instruments, while visual and structural elements central to sustainability reporting remain underexamined. Fourth, NFD studies typically rely on smaller samples and less rigorous econometric designs than FD research, limiting robustness and replicability. Originality/value This study systematically compares archival IM research across FD and NFD. By synthesizing insights from the mature FD literature, it develops a research agenda that broadens the scope of IM motivators, advances the measurement of visual and structural disclosure practices, and strengthens methodological rigor in future NFD research.

title: Overconfident chief executive officers in capital structure decision-making – a systematic literature review
summary: Purpose This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises and integrates the growing body of research on CEO overconfidence and corporate capital structure decisions, with particular attention to how alternative measures of overconfidence
content: Purpose This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises and integrates the growing body of research on CEO overconfidence and corporate capital structure decisions, with particular attention to how alternative measures of overconfidence may contribute to divergent findings. Design/methodology/approach This review systematically searched EconLit, Scopus, Web of Science, Business Source Ultimate and Google Scholar using terms covering CEO overconfidence and capital structure. After screening and eligibility assessment, we reviewed 53 studies and coded them by overconfidence proxy, research method, treatment of endogeneity, identification strategy and findings. Findings The review finds substantial heterogeneity in the operationalisation of CEO overconfidence. These measures are not conceptually equivalent and differ in construct validity and susceptibility to endogeneity and measurement error. The apparent inconsistency in findings should be interpreted cautiously: differences may reflect measurement and identification choices as well as institutional and firm-level context. Originality/value This review clarifies how measurement heterogeneity and differences in empirical identification shape conclusions about CEO overconfidence and capital structure. It also identifies priorities for future research, including construct triangulation, stronger causal designs and transparent reporting of alternative measures.

title: From Symbolic Action to Substantive Outcomes: The Positive Relationship Between Ideologically Aligned CEO Activism and Employee Productivity
summary: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue CEO activism has become increasingly prevalent among top executives, yet we know little about whether it is associated with substantive effects on firm effectiveness and the conditions under which such effec
content: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue CEO activism has become increasingly prevalent among top executives, yet we know little about whether it is associated with substantive effects on firm effectiveness and the conditions under which such effects arise. Research Findings/Insights Using a panel of 1026 S&P 1500 CEOs observed between 2015 and 2019, we find that CEO activism alignment with employee ideology is positively associated with employee productivity. We further find that this positive relationship is amplified in highly polarized industries and firms. Supplemental mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with our proposed mechanism. Theoretical/Academic Implications The study integrates the stakeholder‐alignment view of CEO activism with the meaning‐making view of executive symbolism to theorize CEO activism as a symbolic action with substantive organizational consequences. Our findings suggest that CEO activism may extend beyond stakeholders' evaluations and attitudes to also relate to the contributions they make to the firm. We also identify ideological polarization as an important contextual condition under which these relationships are stronger, as it makes CEO activism more salient, distinctive, and meaningful to employees. In doing so, we connect CEO activism to a more relational view of stakeholder governance, suggesting that symbolic executive actions may eventually contribute to such governance insofar as they relate to stakeholders' willingness to cooperate with and contribute to the firm. Practitioner/Policy Implications CEOs' public stances on sociopolitical issues can be associated with firm effectiveness when those stances align with employees' prevailing ideological values. Ideologically aligned activism can be associated with more favorable employee attitudes and, in turn, is associated with greater employee productivity, particularly when firms operate in ideologically polarized industries or employ internally polarized workforces. CEOs should therefore consider not only the prevailing ideology of their employees but also the broader ideological context in which their activism will be interpreted.

title: YASHIL OBLIGATSIYALAR ORQALI EKOLOGIK LOYIHALARNI MOLIYALASHTIRISH
source: Pedagogy and Psychology in the Modern World
summary: Mazkur maqolada yashil obligatsiyalar orqali ekologik loyihalarni moliyalashtirishning iqtisodiy mohiyati, tashkiliy mexanizmlari va rivojlanish istiqbollari tadqiq etilgan. Shuningdek, O‘zbekistonda yashil iqtisodiyotga o‘tish jarayonida y
content: Mazkur maqolada yashil obligatsiyalar orqali ekologik loyihalarni moliyalashtirishning iqtisodiy mohiyati, tashkiliy mexanizmlari va rivojlanish istiqbollari tadqiq etilgan. Shuningdek, O‘zbekistonda yashil iqtisodiyotga o‘tish jarayonida yashil obligatsiyalarning investitsion resurslarni jalb qilishdagi o‘rni, qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalarini rivojlantirish, energiya samaradorligini oshirish, suv resurslarini tejash va atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishga qaratilgan loyihalarni moliyalashtirish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan. Mamlakatda yashil obligatsiyalar bozorini rivojlantirish bilan bog‘liq mavjud muammolar aniqlanib, xalqaro tajriba asosida moliyalashtirish mexanizmlarini takomillashtirish, xususiy investorlar ishtirokini kengaytirish va ekologik loyihalar samaradorligini baholash bo‘yicha ilmiy-amaliy takliflar ishlab chiqilgan.

title: Prioritising own mother's milk in the neonatal unit: need for standardised metrics that capture lactation and infant feeding
summary: Major disruptions to healthcare services often result in a decline in breastfeeding. One way to counteract these negative effects is to prioritise the use of own mother's milk (OMM), which is especially relevant for sick and preterm babies
content: Major disruptions to healthcare services often result in a decline in breastfeeding. One way to counteract these negative effects is to prioritise the use of own mother's milk (OMM), which is especially relevant for sick and preterm babies admitted to neonatal units (NNU). This article provides an overview of the importance of recording specific lactation and infant feeding metrics and explores potential barriers that need to be overcome in order to provide OMM to all babies. It draws upon the experience of the authors, who participated in a virtual Roundtable Meeting, facilitated by Medela, in October 2021. Several key metrics emerged as relevant, including the need to record feeding data for each infant by milk type: OMM, pasteurised or raw donor human milk, and formula, as well as infant age at first exposure to OMM/colostrum, and the need to calculate neonatal unit-based statistics such as percentage of infants in neonatal care receiving OMM and the percentage of NNU infants exclusively breastfed at discharge home. Furthermore, aspects pertaining to mothers’ lactation support (e.g., by hospital/NNU staff, partners, and families) were also discussed, from timing, to the type of information provided. We conclude that capturing standardised data about lactation and infant feeding in NNU and beyond, by all those involved with the promotion of breastfeeding, and deriving standardised metrics would be a significant step towards the development of universally accepted quality indicators, as well as a leap forward to incentivise the provision of OMM to all sick and preterm infants.

title: 20 years of the International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal: A bibliometric overview
summary: Abstract The International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal (IEMJ) is a leading international journal in the field of entrepreneurship. In 2025, the journal celebrates the 20th anniversary. Motivated by this event, this study present
content: Abstract The International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal (IEMJ) is a leading international journal in the field of entrepreneurship. In 2025, the journal celebrates the 20th anniversary. Motivated by this event, this study presents a bibliometric overview of the publications and citations of IEMJ between 2005 and 2024. The paper uses Scopus database to collect the bibliographic material although in some exceptional cases it also considers the Web of Science Core Collection. The work identifies a wide range of leading trends in the journal in terms of highly cited papers, keywords, influential authors, institutions and countries. The results indicate that Spain is the most productive country publishing in IEMJ closely followed by the USA, and the University of Valencia is by far the most productive institution in the journal.

title: Stated Choice Methods in Long-Acting and Extended-Release HIV Technologies: A Scoping Review of Methodological Practices and Translational Utility
summary: Abstract Purpose of Review Long-acting and extended-release (LA/ER) technologies are expanding options for HIV prevention and treatment, but their population impact will depend on whether products and delivery models align with the prioriti
content: Abstract Purpose of Review Long-acting and extended-release (LA/ER) technologies are expanding options for HIV prevention and treatment, but their population impact will depend on whether products and delivery models align with the priorities and constraints of intended users and providers. We reviewed how stated choice methods have been designed, analyzed, and used to generate implementation-relevant evidence for LA/ER technologies. Recent Findings Fifty peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2026 met inclusion criteria. Most examined HIV prevention (74%), enrolled end-users only (92%), and used discrete choice experiments or related variants (86%). Stakeholder-informed attribute sources were reported in 94%, but only 40% described dedicated, study-specific qualitative or advisory processes. Preference heterogeneity (94%), service-delivery attributes (80%), and structural access barriers (94%) were common. Only 22% included a respondent-specific status-quo comparator, 60% reported comprehension testing, and 4% achieved moderate-to-high representativeness. Although 84% examined pipeline-aligned attributes, reporting did not establish whether those attributes remained modifiable at the relevant product-lifecycle stage. Only four studies included providers, and treatment-preference research was concentrated in high-income settings. Summary Methodological sophistication does not ensure translational utility. Stated choice studies should align their attributes, sampling, and choice architecture with the decision-maker, the product’s lifecycle stage, and the decisions still open to change. As products mature, research should prioritize actionable delivery, access, and health-system decisions and validate preferences against product experience and observed behavior.

title: The Thematic Structure of China’s Green Finance Policies: An LDA-Based Analysis of Policy Texts, 2008–2024
summary: Green finance connected environmental objectives with financial regulation and investment governance, yet its thematic organization within China’s multi-level policy system remains insufficiently understood. This study applied Latent Dirich
content: Green finance connected environmental objectives with financial regulation and investment governance, yet its thematic organization within China’s multi-level policy system remains insufficiently understood. This study applied Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling to 1729 national, provincial, and municipal policy documents issued during 2008–2024. A theory-informed interpretive framework covering intervention mode, goal orientation, instrument type, and innovativeness was used to examine the governance functions of the identified topics. The retained nine-topic solution identified themes concerning project operation management, demonstration-oriented fiscal reform, policy coordination, cooperative investment, innovation support, urban–rural infrastructure, low-carbon technology transition, fund-risk guidance, and credit-information evaluation. Project management, fiscal reform, and policy coordination were the three largest themes in the reported topic distribution, highlighting the textual prominence of administrative and fiscal arrangements alongside financial instruments. Annual keyword patterns suggested overlapping shifts from credit and environmental-risk language during 2008–2013 toward cooperative investment and infrastructure financing during 2014–2018, with innovation, low-carbon development, and ESG-related language becoming more visible in later years. These periods provided a descriptive organization of the findings rather than statistically identified stages. Regional document counts showed uneven policy-document coverage within the retrieved corpus. Infrastructure-related concerns appeared across several topics, while transport was not identified as a separate theme. The study provided an exploratory, corpus-level account of recurring green finance policy themes and discussed their relevance to sustainable infrastructure governance. The findings characterized policy articulation rather than institutional coordination, financial resource allocation, implementation effectiveness, or environmental outcomes.

title: Exploring how AI knowledge management factors and AI-driven sustainability information renovate green finance investments
summary: This study examines how AI-provided sustainability information shapes green finance investment, trust, and greenwashing through AI knowledge management processes. Drawing on signaling and knowledge management theories, 605 valid online surv
content: This study examines how AI-provided sustainability information shapes green finance investment, trust, and greenwashing through AI knowledge management processes. Drawing on signaling and knowledge management theories, 605 valid online survey responses in Vietnam were analyzed using thePartial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results suggest that AI-provided environmental impact information and environmental comparisons positively relate to knowledge acquisition and application, while sustainability certification information enhances knowledge sharing. Knowledge acquisition and knowledge application significantly drive green finance investment and reduce greenwashing, while trust strengthens green finance investment and mitigates greenwashing. The research proposes insights for business managers, customers, policymakers as well as banks and financial institutions to leverage AI-driven transparency, enhance ESG accuracy, and implement strategies to combat greenwashing in sustainable finance.

title: Vulnerability and Resilience of Migrants During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Gendered Analysis of Women Informal Food Vendors in Nairobi’s Informal Settlements
summary: Based on a quantitative survey of 448 female vendors and a comparative sample of 130 male vendors, this chapter presents a gendered analysis of the vulnerability and resilience of women informal foodGender inclusive leadershipwomen informal
content: Based on a quantitative survey of 448 female vendors and a comparative sample of 130 male vendors, this chapter presents a gendered analysis of the vulnerability and resilience of women informal foodGender inclusive leadershipwomen informal food vendors, Nairobi vendors in Nairobi’s informal settlements during the COVID-19 pandemic. The findings reveal that COVID-19 containment measures significantly disrupted women vendors’ livelihoods, leading to increased costs of running business operations; spoilage of perishable products; and decreased demand, patronage, retail prices, sales, and profits. The vendors adopted a number of strategies to cushion their business enterprises, including price and stock adjustment; reliance on credit, loans, and savings; use of mobile phones for business transactions; enhanced public health and hygiene; temporary business closures and relocation to their rural homes; reduction of household consumption and expenditure; and reliance on household assets and additional sources of income. The study underscores the need for holistic and context-specific strategies that support sustainable urban food systems governance, business financing, organisation, and training opportunities for women informal food vendors, including building resilience to external shocks from global pandemics.

title: Managerial myopia, investment allocation, and corporate digital transformation: evidence from China
summary: Abstract Digital transformation requires substantial upfront commitments whose payoffs are delayed and uncertain, which makes it particularly exposed to the time horizons of top managers. Drawing on upper echelons and agency perspectives, t
content: Abstract Digital transformation requires substantial upfront commitments whose payoffs are delayed and uncertain, which makes it particularly exposed to the time horizons of top managers. Drawing on upper echelons and agency perspectives, this study examines whether, through which investment channels, and under which governance conditions managerial myopia affects firm-level digital transformation, using 18,495 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2022. Managerial myopia is measured by rule-based textual analysis of the Management Discussion and Analysis, and digital transformation by the share of digital assets in total intangible assets. Empirically, managerial myopia is significantly and negatively associated with digital transformation. This result holds under an Oster bounds test, a Bartik-type instrumental variable, system GMM, a Heckman selection correction, and alternative measures and fixed-effects structures. Mechanism tests show that myopia is not associated with lower investment. Instead, myopic managers expand total investment and capital expenditure and are more likely to overinvest; the capital-expenditure and, more weakly, overinvestment channels carry significant negative indirect effects, whereas the larger investment scale partly offsets them, pointing to misallocation rather than underinvestment. Higher cash compensation intensity and, contrary to the incentive-alignment prediction, greater managerial equity exposure intensify the negative effect. The effect is weaker in firms with medium than with low female executive representation, but continuous and threshold specifications provide no evidence of nonlinear moderation. The effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned and financially constrained firms.

title: Financial globalization and environmental pollution in ASEAN+5 countries
summary: As ASEAN economies increasingly integrate into global markets, understanding whether this financial globalization exacerbates environmental degradation is critical for sustainable development policy. This study examines the relationship bet
content: As ASEAN economies increasingly integrate into global markets, understanding whether this financial globalization exacerbates environmental degradation is critical for sustainable development policy. This study examines the relationship between financial globalization and per-capita CO2 emissions in five ASEAN countries (Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines, and Malaysia) from 1990 to 2024. Using Bayesian hierarchical regression, we assess the independent effects of foreign direct investment, trade openness, renewable energy, economic development, financial development, and technological innovation. Our findings reveal that trade openness is the largest contributor to emissions (β = 1.160), while renewable energy significantly reduces emissions (β = −0.057). Economic development shows a weak negative effect (β = −0.257), and foreign direct investment provides minimal evidence of pollution-haven effects (β = 0.063). Contrary to expectations, technological innovation exhibits a small positive association with emissions (β = 0.046). These results indicate that the environmental consequences of financial globalization are heterogeneous and context-dependent. We conclude that ASEAN policymakers should prioritize environmentally oriented trade frameworks, accelerate renewable energy adoption, and impose stronger environmental standards on foreign investment to achieve sustainable global integration.

title: Leveraging AI appraisal for sustainable property investment decisions
source: Journal of Financial Management of Property and Construction
summary: Purpose As sustainable considerations increasingly influence real estate finance, traditional property valuation methods face limitations in capturing environmental, social and governance value. This paper aims to critically evaluate the ro
content: Purpose As sustainable considerations increasingly influence real estate finance, traditional property valuation methods face limitations in capturing environmental, social and governance value. This paper aims to critically evaluate the role and potential of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven appraisal techniques in supporting informed and effective sustainable property investment decisions. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing contemporary research sourced from major academic databases. The review focused on identifying AI applications (including machine learning and deep learning) used for valuing sustainable property attributes, assessing green real estate financial performance and integrating ESG factors into investment frameworks. Identified benefits, challenges and future trends were synthesized. Findings AI-driven appraisal demonstrates significant potential to enhance sustainable investment through improved accuracy in valuing green features, increased efficiency in data analysis and portfolio management and greater objectivity compared to traditional methods. Explainable AI techniques are emerging as crucial for ensuring transparency. However, key challenges remain, including the availability and quality of standardized ESG data, mitigating algorithmic bias, ensuring model interpretability for complex sustainability metrics and the need for skilled human oversight. Originality/value This paper provides a focused synthesis of the current state-of-the-art regarding AI appraisal specifically for sustainable real estate investment. It bridges the gap between technical AI advancements in valuation and their practical application in sustainable finance, offering valuable insights for investors, financial institutions, appraisers and policymakers aiming to leverage AI for promoting responsible investment in the built environment.

title: Reassessing the ESG disclosure and firm value relationship: financial constraints and R&D investment in an emerging economy
summary: Introduction This study examines the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure and firm value among Vietnamese listed non-financial firms, focusing on financial constraints and heterogeneity across R&D inve
content: Introduction This study examines the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure and firm value among Vietnamese listed non-financial firms, focusing on financial constraints and heterogeneity across R&D investment levels. Methods The raw panel covers 2018–2025, while the complete-case core estimation sample is concentrated in 2018–2022 due to missing data. The study employs Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS) as the baseline estimator, supplemented by firm and year fixed-effects models with firm-clustered standard errors, cluster bootstrap mediation analysis, and dynamic System GMM. Results The baseline FGLS estimates indicate negative associations between ESG disclosure and both firm value and the adapted SA financial-constraint measure. However, these associations become statistically insignificant under firm fixed effects. The SA coefficient remains positive and statistically significant in the firm-value model under both estimators, contrary to H3. Bootstrap results indicate a negative indirect association, with percentile and bias-corrected confidence intervals excluding zero, whereas the normal-based interval includes zero. Dynamic System GMM yields a negative coefficient on lagged ESG disclosure. Although R&D subgroup estimates differ, the pooled fixed-effects interaction test does not identify statistically significant cross-group heterogeneity. Discussion The findings highlight the sensitivity of the ESG-financing-firm value relationship to estimator choice and unobserved firm heterogeneity. The results also emphasize the importance of distinguishing ESG disclosure from substantive sustainability expenditures and interpreting the observed relationships as associational rather than definitive causal effects.

title: Does Eco-Friendly Product Shape Purchase Decisions Among University Students in Sylhet, Bangladesh?
summary: This study investigates whether eco-friendly product positioning meaningfully shapes purchase decisions among university students in Sylhet, Bangladesh, and situates that local evidence within the broader global and national green-economy t
content: This study investigates whether eco-friendly product positioning meaningfully shapes purchase decisions among university students in Sylhet, Bangladesh, and situates that local evidence within the broader global and national green-economy trend. A mixed-methods design combined primary survey data from 320 valid student respondents, most heavily from Army IBA (Army Institute of Business Administration) and SUST (Shahjalal University of Science and Technology), with secondary evidence on global Gen Z sustainability spending, Bangladesh’s green finance and waste data, and ESG disclosure from three Bangladeshi consumer-goods companies. Multiple linear regression shows that label-checking behavior, willingness to pay a premium, and skepticism toward greenwashing are the strongest and only statistically significant predictors of purchase likelihood, while general familiarity, trust, and perceived compliance are not. Only 39% of this Sylhet sample express willingness to pay a premium, compared with 70–80% of global Gen Z consumers, indicating that the global ‘green Gen Z’ narrative applies only partially to Bangladeshi university students. The paper concludes that eco-friendly positioning does shape student purchase decisions in Sylhet, but the effect operates mainly through concrete, low-cost behavioral cues rather than through abstract environmental attitude, and is conditioned heavily by income and greenwashing distrust.

title: TUS OS: Great Britain Electricity 2030 — What's Holding Back Clean, Reliable and Affordable Power?
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: TUS OS is an implemented architecture for answerable AI-assisted reasoning, bringing mathematical foundations, deterministic computation, evidence governance and structured inquiry together within a unified research system. Its development
content: TUS OS is an implemented architecture for answerable AI-assisted reasoning, bringing mathematical foundations, deterministic computation, evidence governance and structured inquiry together within a unified research system. Its development is documented through a public corpus of approximately 35 publications, including formal technical specifications, computational foundations, realised receipts, applied investigations and the completed eleven-paper mathematical research programme culminating in A General Theory of Answerability. At its centre is a fundamental intellectual concern: how can complex reasoning produce substantive, consequential answers while preserving an inspectable account of what makes those answers supportable? TUS OS addresses this through an integrated architecture in which the question, formal structure, evidence, interpretation, analytical development and final conclusions remain connected through a governed chain of authority. Its mathematical research programme develops the formal foundations of Answerability, including relationships between inference, evidential obligations, lawful conclusions, computational resources and executable realisation. Its operational architecture brings these principles into applied AI-assisted investigation. This is an independent public-information research demonstration. It is not commissioned by, affiliated with or authorised on behalf of a government, regulator, electricity operator or named project. Policies and projects appear as documented cases for investigation. The reports do not constitute operational instructions, investment approvals or official policy advice. This release presents the most substantial TUS OS applied investigation to date: a multidisciplinary examination of the conditions required to achieve abundant, clean, reliable and affordable electricity in Great Britain by 2030. The governing question Under what conditions is abundant, clean, reliable and affordable electricity achievable in Great Britain by 2030; what materially prevents those conditions being realised; why do those constraints persist; and which feasible changes, individually or together, would deliver the greatest improvement against the declared objectives by that date? Electricity presents a demanding systems-level inquiry. Generation, networks, finance, construction, regulation, operating security and customer affordability form an interconnected system in which progress depends on the interaction of distinct technical, economic and institutional conditions. The investigation examines those relationships, bringing specialist evidence into a common analytical structure to establish what is achievable, which constraints matter under different conditions, why they persist and which feasible interventions could deliver the greatest improvement. The principal findings The 72-page Great Britain Electricity to 2030 — Evidence-Bounded Decision Review develops seven major findings from electricity-system data

title: From “What Can Artificial Intelligence Do?” to “Says Who?”: Examining the Epistemic, Social, Political, and Economic Power Dynamics Shaping AI in Healthcare
summary: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely portrayed as a transformative innovation poised to revolutionize healthcare. Heavily promoted by financial and industry actors, this forward‐looking narrative is often adopted uncritically by
content: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is widely portrayed as a transformative innovation poised to revolutionize healthcare. Heavily promoted by financial and industry actors, this forward‐looking narrative is often adopted uncritically by decision‐makers, despite limited evidence of AI's clinical effectiveness in real‐world contexts and the persistence of numerous regulatory, professional, organizational, economic, sociopolitical, ethical, and governance challenges. In healthcare systems, characterized by pluralism and complexity, the trajectory of AI solutions is shaped by the strategic decisions and actions of diverse stakeholders who mobilize their epistemic, social, political, and economic powers in an effort to influence technology development and deployment. Drawing from a curated multidisciplinary body of scholarship and several real‐life examples, this paper critically examines how such power dynamics come to shape which AI healthcare solutions are developed, how they impact care delivery, and for whom they provide care. Specifically, we focus on how market imperatives influence AI research and narratives, how quantification and statistical analysis shape care delivery, and how, together, these dynamics delimit who ultimately receives care by further marginalizing vulnerable groups. The paper ends with numerous policies and practices for equitable, just, and publicly accountable AI in healthcare.

title: Ethical Procurement Practices and Performance of Commercial State Corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya
source: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
summary: Purpose: The general objective of this study was to assess the influence of ethical procurement practices on performance of commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, the study sought to assess the influence
content: Purpose: The general objective of this study was to assess the influence of ethical procurement practices on performance of commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, the study sought to assess the influence of accountability on performance of commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya and to evaluate the effect of conflict-of-interest management on performance of commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya. This study was anchored on; Institutional Theory and Control Theory. Methodology: This study used a cross-sectional survey design. According to State Corporations Advisory Committee (SCAC) (2024), there is a total of 46 commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya. The study targeted a total of 92 respondents comprising of Procurement managers and their assistants. Due to small size of the target population, this study used census method hence the sample size was 92 respondents. This study used closed-ended questions to collect the data. The researcher collected questionnaires, coded them, and entered them into the Software Package for Social Sciences (SPSS version 26) for analysis. Data analysis was done through use of descriptive and inferential statistics. Pearson correlation coefficient was used for testing associations between the independent and the dependent variables. Findings: The study concludes that accountability has a positive and significant effect on performance of commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya. The study also concludes that conflict of interest management has a positive and significant effect on performance of commercial state corporations in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Based on the findings, the study recommends that commercial state corporations in Kenya should strengthen conflict of interest management by establishing and enforcing clear policies requiring board members, managers, and employees to disclose any personal or financial interests that may influence their official decisions.

title: Who Registers and What Changes? Evidence From a Local Government Sustainable Development Goals Registration System Among Construction Firms in Japan
summary: ABSTRACT Guided by institutional theory, this study examines who registers for a local government SDG registration system and which firm outcomes change after registration. In Kochi Prefecture, Japan, voluntary registration preceded SDG‐rel
content: ABSTRACT Guided by institutional theory, this study examines who registers for a local government SDG registration system and which firm outcomes change after registration. In Kochi Prefecture, Japan, voluntary registration preceded SDG‐related points in public procurement. Using Business Evaluation data on 1447 construction firms (2019–2025), registration prediction is combined with group‐time difference‐in‐differences. Registration is strongly predicted by pre‐registration characteristics, particularly among early registrants. Statistically significant positive changes are detected only for profitability and completed construction work value; the former is only weakly evident beforehand, whereas the latter tends to become larger afterward. Other outcomes show no statistically significant change. The originality of this study lies in examining selection, five outcome domains, and timing within one design. Implications: when reviewing SDG‐related points, local governments should assess targeted outcomes rather than registration status alone and monitor participation by smaller firms. Limitations: the focus on one prefecture and one industry limits generalizability.

title: Unlocking Social Value in Construction Projects: A Systematic Review of Drivers and Barriers
summary: ABSTRACT Social value (SV) in construction projects extends beyond cost, time, and quality to encompass wider social, economic, and environmental outcomes. Although SV is increasingly recognized in policy and practice, its effective deliver
content: ABSTRACT Social value (SV) in construction projects extends beyond cost, time, and quality to encompass wider social, economic, and environmental outcomes. Although SV is increasingly recognized in policy and practice, its effective delivery remains inconsistent due to limited consensus on enabling drivers and persistent structural barriers. This study systematically identifies the key drivers and barriers influencing SV creation in construction projects. A systematic literature review was conducted using Scopus and Web of Science as primary databases. Following PRISMA guidelines, 55 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2012 and 2025 were selected. Bibliometric analysis examined publication trends and collaboration patterns, while qualitative content analysis synthesized reported drivers and barriers. Results show a steady growth in SV research, with the United Kingdom and Australia leading contributions, but limited international collaboration. Five core drivers were identified: institutional and policy enablement; collaborative ecosystem development; inclusive supply‐chain and social enterprise participation; organizational capability and learning; and strategic embedding and organizational integration. Six principal barriers emerged: policy implementation and governance gaps; institutional inertia and commercial priorities; contractual and procurement rigidity; capability and knowledge deficits; fragmented accountability and risk allocation; and measurement and conceptual ambiguity. The findings provide evidence‐based guidance for policymakers and practitioners seeking to embed SV more systematically in construction projects and enhance long‐term community outcomes. This review offers a comprehensive synthesis of SV drivers and barriers, advancing conceptual clarity and supporting more effective integration of social value in construction practice.

title: Entrepreneurial Orientation and Debt Finance Uptake among the Micro, Small and Medium Enteprises in Kericho County, Kenya
source: Journal of Entrepreneurship and Project Management
summary: Purpose: This study examined the effect of innovativeness and competitive aggressiveness on debt finance uptake among SMEs in Kericho County. Methodology: The descriptive cross-sectional research design, the study targeted 1,079 SMEs operat
content: Purpose: This study examined the effect of innovativeness and competitive aggressiveness on debt finance uptake among SMEs in Kericho County. Methodology: The descriptive cross-sectional research design, the study targeted 1,079 SMEs operating within Kericho County with a sample size of 292 SMEs owners/managers/entrepreneurs. The study adopted a stratified random sampling design based on the different sectors. Data were collected via structured questionnaires, yielding a robust 69.5% response rate (n=203). The analytical framework employed descriptive statistics and inferential statistics. Findings: The study concluded that firm’s innovativeness has a positive and significant influence on uptake of debt finance among SMEs in Kericho County, Kenya. The study also concluded that firm’s competitive aggressiveness has a positive and significant influence on uptake of debt finance among SMEs in Kericho County, Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: Based on the findings, the study recommends that proprietors should develop clear, written competitive strategies including market positioning statements, customer retention protocols, and rapid response tactics—and maintain records of market share trends to substantiate claims of revenue stability during lender assessments.

title: Trustworthy Crisis Mental Health Care: Key Values and Features
summary: CONTEXT: Mental health crises are increasing in the United States. Local and national policy efforts have focused on increasing access to crisis services, but little attention has been given to the quality of services delivered, or their pe
content: CONTEXT: Mental health crises are increasing in the United States. Local and national policy efforts have focused on increasing access to crisis services, but little attention has been given to the quality of services delivered, or their perceived trustworthiness by people who use them. While trust in health care has been well studied in general health care settings, there has been a gap in the context of crisis mental health care. This gap exists despite the central role of relationships in mental health care, the vulnerability of people experiencing crises, and the use of practices known to erode trust (e.g., involuntary hospitalization). Our aim was to develop a framework for conceptualizing values and features of trustworthy crisis mental health care. METHODS: With ongoing consultation from an advisory board, we conducted seven semistructured 1.5-hour virtual focus groups with 27 adults with lived experience of crisis mental health care to understand how trust in services is shaped. Transcripts were analyzed abductively for emergent themes through a rigorous process of codebook development and validation. FINDINGS: We identified four core values underpinning beliefs in a trustworthy crisis mental health care system (human connection, autonomy, transparency, and respect), and four supporting values (personalization, benevolence, competence, and access). A trustworthy crisis mental health care system that expresses these values would exhibit a range of features across relational, organizational, systems, and societal levels. Participants emphasized the need to invest in non-medical, alternative crisis models. A central tension in current services emerged between risk management (e.g., concern over liability and physical safety) and therapeutic benefit, undermining trustworthiness at all levels. CONCLUSIONS: Beliefs in trustworthy crisis mental health care are unique to this setting. While we have outlined values and features of trustworthy crisis services, future work is needed to identify appropriate strategies to operationalize these values, as well as ways to address salient tension points that compromise trustworthiness.

title: Sustainability Factors Influencing Construction Supply Chain Management in North-Central Nigeria
summary: Purpose: This study examines the drivers of and barriers to sustainability in the supply chain management (SCM) of construction projects in North Central Nigeria and their influence on sustainability outcomes. Design/Methodology/Approach: A
content: Purpose: This study examines the drivers of and barriers to sustainability in the supply chain management (SCM) of construction projects in North Central Nigeria and their influence on sustainability outcomes. Design/Methodology/Approach: A concurrent mixed-methods design was adopted. A structured questionnaire was administered to 328 construction professionals in contracting, consulting and manufacturing firms across the North Central Geopolitical Zone, selected through stratified random sampling, and 234 valid responses (71.34%) were retrieved. Semi-structured key informant interviews were also held with twenty purposively selected professionals. Twenty-seven driver items and twenty-two barrier items were ranked using the Relative Importance Index (RII) and triangulated with a thematic analysis of the interviews, while the predictive influence of six composite sustainability factors was tested using multiple linear regression across five outcome models. Research Limitation: The cross-sectional, perception-based data and the restriction of the survey to one geopolitical zone constrain generalisability, and the regression models establish association rather than causation. Findings: Cost savings and economic benefits (RII = 0.917), social responsibility and stakeholder expectations (RII = 0.904) and construction waste management (RII = 0.880) were the most influential drivers, while the unavailability of environmental standards, the lack of an established sustainability framework and prohibitive cost were the most pressing barriers; findings were corroborated independently by the interviewees. The six factors jointly and significantly predicted between 45.8% and 60.0% of the variance across the five outcome constructs. Social Drivers and Social Barriers were each significant in four of the five models, while Environmental Drivers and Economic Barriers were never significant despite ranking highly in the descriptive analysis. Practical Implication: Construction firms and regulators should prioritise structured stakeholder engagement and institutional and managerial reform alongside cost-based incentives, and should expedite construction-specific environmental standards and certified sustainable supplier networks. Social Implication: Strengthening the social dimension of construction supply chains can improve stakeholder trust, community welfare and the uptake of sustainable practice across North Central Nigeria. Originality/Value: This study provides new evidence that the social dimension, through both its drivers and its barriers, is the only consistent predictor of sustainability outcomes in construction supply chains.

title: Enfoques y tendencias contemporáneas de la gestión financiera en la administración empresarial: una revisión de la literatura
summary: El objetivo de este artículo es integrar críticamente los enfoques y tendencias de la gestión financiera empresarial y examinar las condiciones en que se relacionan con el desempeño organizacional, con atención a su pertinencia para América
content: El objetivo de este artículo es integrar críticamente los enfoques y tendencias de la gestión financiera empresarial y examinar las condiciones en que se relacionan con el desempeño organizacional, con atención a su pertinencia para América Latina. Se realizó una revisión documental integradora mediante búsqueda dirigida y verificación bibliográfica. El corpus comprendió 34 artículos temáticos publicados entre 2014 y 2026 y cuatro referencias metodológicas. La información se organizó en una matriz y se contrastó en ocho ejes, distinguiendo investigaciones empíricas, revisiones y contribuciones conceptuales. Los resultados muestran relaciones condicionadas por las restricciones financieras, las capacidades gerenciales, la calidad de la información y el contexto institucional. La evidencia sobre capital de trabajo cuestiona su reducción indiscriminada; los estudios de digitalización destacan capacidades complementarias; y los hallazgos sobre sostenibilidad ambiental, social y de gobernanza son heterogéneos. El análisis diferencia rentabilidad, liquidez, crecimiento y continuidad, así como asociaciones estadísticas y efectos de intervenciones delimitadas. Se concluye que una gestión financiera estratégica requiere coordinar decisiones operativas, inversión, financiamiento y riesgo. Como aporte, se propone un marco conceptual de articulación entre capacidades, decisiones y resultados, cuya validación empírica queda pendiente, y una agenda de investigación para pymes latinoamericanas.

title: Procurement Automation and Performance of Milk Processing Companies in Kiambu County, Kenya
source: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
summary: Purpose: The general objective of the study is to assess the effect of procurement automation on performance of milk processing companies in Kiambu County, Kenya. Specifically, the study sought to explore the effect of e-tendering on perfor
content: Purpose: The general objective of the study is to assess the effect of procurement automation on performance of milk processing companies in Kiambu County, Kenya. Specifically, the study sought to explore the effect of e-tendering on performance of milk processing companies in Kiambu County, Kenya and to determine the effect of e-invoicing on performance of milk processing companies in Kiambu County, Kenya. This study was guided by Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Resource-Based View (RBV) Theory. Methodology: This study adopted a descriptive research design. The population consisted of 21 milk processing firms in Kiambu County. Kiambu County was selected as it hosts some of the largest dairy processing firms in Kenya such as Brookside and Fresha Dairies. The study targeted management employees thus forming a target population of 189 respondents. The study adopted Yamane (1957) to determine the appropriate sample size of 129 respondents. The study used questionnaires to collect primary data. Data analysis was done through use of descriptive and inferential statistics with the help of SPSS version 25. The study results were presented through tables and figures. Findings: The study concludes that e-tendering has a positive and significant effect on performance of milk processing companies in Kiambu County, Kenya.
