Further, the study concludes that e-invoicing has a positive and significant effect on performance of milk processing companies in Kiambu County, Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Based on the findings, the study recommends that milk processing companies in Kenya should strengthen the adoption of e-invoicing systems by training employees, integrating electronic invoicing platforms with accounting systems, and ensuring timely processing and verification of supplier invoices.

title: Capabilities Over Stakeholder Pressure: How Sustainable Learning and Green Dynamic Capabilities Drive Corporate Sustainability Performance
summary: ABSTRACT With the growing emphasis on sustainable development, corporate sustainability performance (CSP) has become an important indicator of organisations' environmental, social and governance commitments. This study examines the effects
content: ABSTRACT With the growing emphasis on sustainable development, corporate sustainability performance (CSP) has become an important indicator of organisations' environmental, social and governance commitments. This study examines the effects of sustainable learning capabilities (SLC) and green dynamic capabilities (GDC) on CSP, focusing on the mediating role of GDC in the SLC–CSP relationship and the moderating role of stakeholder pressure (SP). The proposed model was empirically tested using data collected from organisations in Brunei Darussalam and analysed using SmartPLS. The results reveal that both SLC and GDC have significant positive effects on CSP, whereas SLC also positively influences GDC. Furthermore, GDC partially mediates the relationship between SLC and CSP, suggesting that sustainability‐oriented learning contributes to improved sustainability performance both directly and through the development of green dynamic capabilities. However, SP does not significantly moderate the SLC–CSP relationship, indicating that its moderating effect was not supported in the study context. Drawing on the resource‐based view (RBV) and institutional theory, this study advances understanding of how organisational capabilities contribute to CSP. The findings also offer practical implications for managers seeking to integrate sustainability‐oriented learning and green dynamic capabilities into organisational strategies to strengthen long‐term sustainability performance.

title: Making Climate Change Adaptation Governable: Comparing State‐Level Adaptation Policy Architectures in Germany and Australia
summary: ABSTRACT In federated systems of government, state governments have become pivotal in steering climate change adaptation through a range of instruments. This includes legislation, regulation, policies, strategies, guidelines, and sector pla
content: ABSTRACT In federated systems of government, state governments have become pivotal in steering climate change adaptation through a range of instruments. This includes legislation, regulation, policies, strategies, guidelines, and sector plans that structure responsibilities and resource distribution, and provide direction within sub‐national systems. Yet, compared to research on national and local levels, state‐level adaptation governance remains under‐examined. Addressing this gap, we analyse adaptation policy architectures of Baden‐Württemberg (Germany) and Victoria (Australia) to examine how these architectures authorise, structure, and direct climate change adaptation across the wider sub‐national system. Using qualitative document analysis of key state‐level laws, strategies, and sector plans, contextualised by expert interviews, we undertake a frames analysis, using climate change adaptation policy frames of hazards, climate impacts, risk management, vulnerability, and resilience, to illustrate how climate change is problematised and how responsibilities and instrument mixes are assembled across both cases. By employing analytical frames, we find that middle‐tier policy architectures actively constitute sub‐national adaptation governance in three ways: they construct the scales at which adaptation becomes actionable; encode distinct coordination logics; and institutionalise adaptation through different combinations of rules, resources, and routines. Baden‐Württemberg primarily does this through territorially and vertically organised statutory planning, whereas Victoria predominantly relies on the horizontal orchestration of heterogeneous system (or sector‐based) adaptation plans. The comparison identifies the State middle tier as an important site of adaptation system design, where policy arrangements distribute the burdens of translation, capacity, and accountability across jurisdictions and sectors in context‐specific ways. These findings call for greater attention to the design of state‐level policy instruments when examining how adaptation becomes governable and actionable across sub‐national systems. For, rather than only “enabling” local action, state‐level adaptation efforts configure what becomes legible, governable and actionable in the first place.

title: Agile Supply Chain and Organizational Performance of Cable Manufacturing Firms in Nairobi City County, Kenya
source: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
summary: Purpose: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of agile supply chain on organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. Specifically, the study aimed to determine the effect of supply cha
content: Purpose: The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of agile supply chain on organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. Specifically, the study aimed to determine the effect of supply chain flexibility and information integration on organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. Methodology: The research utilized a descriptive cross-sectional research design. The target population therefore consisted of 264 staff members drawn from the supply chain/logistics, operations, finance, and ICT departments across the 7 cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. The research utilized a stratified random sampling in the selection of 159 respondents determined using Slovin's Formula. The research utilized primary data collected through semi-structured questionnaires. The questionnaires generated both quantitative and qualitative data. Qualitative data was analyzed using thematic analysis, with the findings presented narratively. Quantitative data was analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics with the help of SPSS version 28 statistical software. Descriptive statistics included mean, standard deviation, percentages, and frequency distribution. Inferential analysis was conducted using Pearson correlation coefficient and multivariate linear regression analysis. Findings: The study found that that supply chain flexibility has a positive and significant effect on the organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. The study established that information integration has a positive and significant effect on the organizational performance of cable manufacturing firms in Nairobi city county, Kenya. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: Therefore, the study recommends that firms should strengthen internal operational systems to enable rapid responses to changes in production schedules and support real-time decision-making. The study also recommends that cable manufacturing firms should strengthen employee training on digital supply chain systems to enhance technological skills and operational adaptability.

title: Pengaruh Lingkungan Kerja dan Kompensasi terhadap Kepuasan Kerja Karyawan di Pabrik Sapu Harmony Ca
summary: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh lingkungan kerja dan kompensasi terhadap kepuasan kerja karyawan Pabrik Sapu Harmony Ca di Semarang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan teknik sensus terhadap seluruh 100 k
content: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh lingkungan kerja dan kompensasi terhadap kepuasan kerja karyawan Pabrik Sapu Harmony Ca di Semarang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan teknik sensus terhadap seluruh 100 karyawan, yang terdiri atas 80 pekerja tetap dan 20 pekerja harian lepas. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert lima poin dan dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dengan SPSS 26. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh butir instrumen memenuhi kriteria validitas dan reliabilitas. Uji Kolmogorov Smirnov menunjukkan residual tidak berbeda secara signifikan dari distribusi normal (Asymp. Sig. = 0,200). Lingkungan kerja berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan kerja (B = 0,416; t = 8,765; p < 0,001), demikian pula kompensasi (B = 0,389; t = 7,169; p < 0,001). Secara simultan, kedua variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 80,812; p < 0,001). Nilai R² sebesar 0,625 menunjukkan bahwa model menjelaskan 62,5% variasi kepuasan kerja. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya perbaikan kondisi fisik tempat kerja serta penerapan kompensasi yang adil dan transparan pada lingkungan produksi padat karya.

title: Model Explanatory Competitive Advantage Based on Innovation Capability Culinary MSMEs in Jombang
summary: This study explains the effects of organizational learning and knowledge sharing on competitive advantage, with innovation capability as a mediator. A quantitative explanatory design was applied using a five-point Likert questionnaire compl
content: This study explains the effects of organizational learning and knowledge sharing on competitive advantage, with innovation capability as a mediator. A quantitative explanatory design was applied using a five-point Likert questionnaire completed by 140 owners/managers selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model was reliable (composite reliability 0.871–0.957), met convergent and discriminant validity criteria (AVE 0.629–0.726; maximum HTMT 0.670), and model fit was adequate (SRMR 0.054). All hypotheses were supported: organizational learning and knowledge sharing positively and significantly affect innovation capability (β = 0.424 and 0.351) and competitive advantage (β = 0.176 and 0.181), and innovation capability positively affects competitive advantage (β = 0.455). Innovation capability partially (complementarily) mediates the effects of organizational learning (β = 0.193) and knowledge sharing (β = 0.160) on competitive advantage. The model explains 46.0% of the variance in competitive advantage and 40.2% in innovation capability. The study extends entrepreneurial human resource management research by positioning learning and knowledge sharing as people-based capabilities that operate through innovation. Owner should build learning routines and knowledge-sharing forums directed at product, packaging, and digital marketing innovation.

title: Lattice and interfacial state modulation in low-Pd ZnO for metronidazole removal and acute toxicity assessment of treated water
summary: Abstract The functional role of Pd in ZnO-based materials depends on the wurtzite host response, the formation of Pd-containing secondary phases, and the evolution of surface and interfacial environments. Here, we investigated ZnO-based mat
content: Abstract The functional role of Pd in ZnO-based materials depends on the wurtzite host response, the formation of Pd-containing secondary phases, and the evolution of surface and interfacial environments. Here, we investigated ZnO-based materials with nominal Pd contents of 0, 1, and 5% to determine how this compositional evolution affects lattice response, surface electronic states, optical behavior, and metronidazole (MET) photocatalytic removal. Rietveld refinement showed a modest expansion of the ZnO lattice at 1% Pd, increasing the unit-cell volume from 47.30 to 47.53 Å 3 , whereas increasing the nominal Pd content to 5% primarily increased the PdO and Pd phase fractions without further expansion of the wurtzite cell. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed progressive changes in the near-surface Zn–O electronic environment, with the Zn 2p and lattice-oxygen core levels shifting to higher binding energies as the Pd content increased. Pd 3d components corresponding to metallic Pd 0 and Pd 2 ⁺ associated with PdO, together with an intermediate-binding-energy contribution consistent with electron-deficient Pdδ⁺ environments, were resolved. The relative fitted area of this intermediate Pd component increased from 58.3 to 73.7% between 1 and 5% Pd, while the relative area of the high-binding-energy O 1s component increased from 7.1 to 27.9%. Urbach energy increased from 62.7 to 79.7 meV with increasing Pd content, consistent with a broader distribution of localized electronic environments. Among the investigated compositions, the nominal 1% Pd sample showed the highest photocatalytic activity, reaching 86% apparent MET removal after 120 min, compared with 56% for pristine ZnO and 80% for 5% Pd. The corresponding k app was 1.65 × 10 −2 min⁻ 1 , approximately 2.3 and 1.2 times the values obtained for pristine ZnO and 5% Pd, respectively. The largest activity loss occurred under hole scavenging, with MET removal decreasing from 86 to 57%, while MeOH and CHCl 3 reduced the conversion to 63 and 70%, respectively. These results support the participation of hole-dependent oxidation, •OH-mediated chemistry, and electron-dependent O 2 reduction, with the strongest inhibition observed under hole scavenging. Reusability tests showed an initial decrease in MET removal from 86 to 42% after the first recovery, followed by a nearly stable response of 41% in the third cycle; post-use Raman spectroscopy and elemental mapping confirmed the persistence of ZnO and PdO signatures and dispersed Pd. Acute-toxicity assays using Artemia salina showed 100% survival after both 24 and 48 h for the aqueous phase treated with 1% Pd. Within the investigated series, the nominal 1% Pd composition provided the most favorable balance between lattice response, surface and interfacial environments, photocatalytic kinetics, and high Artemia salina survival after treatment.

title: SENSORY STIMULATION AND OVERSTIMULATION CONTROL AS THE CRITICAL THERAPEUTIC DESIGN DETERMINANTS IN PSYCHIATRIC WARD SETTINGS: EVIDENCE FROM NORTHERN NIGERIA
summary: Sensory regulation and environmental stimulation management are theorised as primary determinants of therapeutic quality in psychiatric ward design, yet the relative ranking of design elements and their independent contributions to patient
content: Sensory regulation and environmental stimulation management are theorised as primary determinants of therapeutic quality in psychiatric ward design, yet the relative ranking of design elements and their independent contributions to patient recovery has rarely been tested empirically, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. A mixed-methods design integrating quantitative ward-level assessment with qualitative behavioural-spatial mapping was applied across 12 wards in three Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospitals (FNPHs). Six elements were assessed using the content-validated Therapeutic Design Index (TDI): connection to nature, natural lighting, colour psychology, spatial geometry, sensory stimulation, and minimisation of overstimulation. ANOVA tested inter-hospital differences; Pearson correlation and multiple regression related design elements to general patient recovery (N = 275 patients; 12 ward-level units). The model explained 96.0% of outcome variance (R² = 0.960, adjusted R² = 0.912). Sensory stimulation (r = 0.876, β = 1.154, p = .008) and minimisation of overstimulation (r = 0.804, β = 0.716, p = .048) were the strongest positive predictors, whereas spatial geometry was a significant negative predictor (β = −1.347, p = .007). Hospitals differed significantly on all elements (all p ≤ .025) except connection to nature (F = 2.540, p = .088), reflecting uniformly low biophilic provision. Sensory stimulation and overstimulation control are the dominant therapeutic design determinants in Northern Nigerian psychiatric wards, while poorly configured spatial geometry acts as an anti-therapeutic constraint. This element-level evidence hierarchy, the first for any FNPH in Northern Nigeria, offers a resource-sensitive framework for prioritising ward design investment and reform.

title: Understanding Smartphone Purchase Behavior Through the Lens of Government Administrative Employees
summary: This study examines sustainable consumer behavior among 200 Malaysian government administrative employees regarding smartphone acquisition and usage within the framework of Sustainable Development Goal 12 (SDG 12): Responsible Consumption a
content: This study examines sustainable consumer behavior among 200 Malaysian government administrative employees regarding smartphone acquisition and usage within the framework of Sustainable Development Goal 12 (SDG 12): Responsible Consumption and Production. Despite the public sector's role in advancing sustainability, a significant attitude-behavior gap persists, with consumers often prioritizing product performance and brand reputation over environmental considerations. This study investigates the influence of price sensitivity, brand image, product features, and social influence on smartphone purchasing behavior and replacement cycles. A quantitative approach was employed, using survey data collected from employees across several government entities. Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that social influence is the only statistically significant predictor of smartphone purchasing behavior (β = 0.384, p < 0.01), highlighting the importance of peer recommendations, workplace social norms, and social conformity in shaping purchasing decisions. In contrast, price sensitivity, brand image, and product features demonstrate no statistically significant relationships with purchasing behavior. Despite respondents' awareness of smartphone costs, environmental considerations, particularly product longevity and energy efficiency, receive limited attention. These findings highlight the need to strengthen sustainable consumption awareness among public sector employees. Accordingly, this study recommends implementing green procurement nudges and internal behavioral awareness programs within government institutions. By encouraging longer product usage cycles and environmentally responsible purchasing decisions, the public workforce can contribute to promoting circular economy practices and advancing Malaysia's commitment to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Community Based Security and Crime Prevention: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Vigilante Groups in Gombe State, Nigeria (2013-2023)
source: Journal of Central and Eastern European African Studies
summary: The paper examined the effectiveness of vigilante groups in the prevention of criminality in Gombe State, Nigeria focusing on the activities and effectiveness of the vigilante groups between 2013-2023. Primary data were collected through a
content: The paper examined the effectiveness of vigilante groups in the prevention of criminality in Gombe State, Nigeria focusing on the activities and effectiveness of the vigilante groups between 2013-2023. Primary data were collected through a field survey conducted in 2024 with respondents providing experiences and perspectives relating to the study period. The study was guided by the following research objectives: reasons for the emergence of vigilante groups and their level of effectiveness in crime prevention in Gombe State. The Broken window theory was adopted which underscores the effectiveness of vigilante groups in Gombe State highlighting how their prompt response to minor offences helps prevent the escalation of crime and strengthens community-level social control. Primary and secondary data were sourced from the selected three Local Government Areas affected by criminality in the State. The study adopted Taro Yamane’s formula to determine the sample size and Bourley’s Proportional formula to allocate respondents across the Local Governments selected. Using multi-stage cluster sampling and purposive techniques, a sample size of 400 respondents was determined for the study, and questionnaires were administered to all 400 selected respondents. Of the 400 questionnaires administered, 371 were successfully retrieved and found valid for analysis, representing 92.75% response rate. Thus, the remaining 29 questionnaires were not returned. However, 24 Key Informant Interviews were conducted. The Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) version 23.0 was used to analyse the quantitative data using descriptive statistics and cross tabulations. The qualitative data were presented in themes and interpreted in a narrative form. Findings revealed that reasons for the emergence of vigilante groups were inadequacies of law enforcement agencies to prevent crime, increased rate of petty crimes, armed robbery and theft, cultural values that support community policing, and political interests of some elites. The study also revealed a predominantly positive perception of vigilante group effectiveness, with 76.28% of respondents rating their performance as effective to varying degrees (effective, fairly effective and very effective) compared with 23.72% who rated it as ineffective. However, the study concluded that modern equipment and logistics should be provided to address root causes of criminality in Gombe State. Vigilante groups should also adopt modern technology, sensitization, and collaborate with religious and community leaders in preventing criminality in the State.

title: Contemporary History of the Democratic Republic of the Congo with a Perspective on the Great Lakes Region
source: Journal of Central and Eastern European African Studies
summary: The Great Lakes region in Africa is an ethnic-geopolitical “hornet’s nest” burdened with serious problems at the meeting of several worlds. The three francophone countries that emerged in the former Belgian (or in the case of Rwanda and Bur
content: The Great Lakes region in Africa is an ethnic-geopolitical “hornet’s nest” burdened with serious problems at the meeting of several worlds. The three francophone countries that emerged in the former Belgian (or in the case of Rwanda and Burundi, German for a few decades before) colonial territories are usually classified by some divisions as part of the Central African region, which also includes Chad, the Central African Republic, Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. Other groupings – such as this analysis – refer to them as francophone states of the African Great Lakes subregion, alongside Anglo-Saxon Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. We are convinced that the common or similar historical past also justifies this latter division. In the Great Lakes region, we can speak of 3 historical and one artificial state formation: the conglomerate of provinces that make up the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Congo-Kinshasa, the former Zaire, and the Belgian Congo), Rwanda, and Burundi all have historical precedents, in a given core area. While Uganda was artificially created by the British colonialists in 1896 by separating it from Tanzania and adding several other territories.

title: Is the Farmer Really “Homo Economicus”? Bounded Rationality and Cropping Pattern Preferences in Çukurova
summary: Although agricultural policies worldwide seek to steer cropping patterns through subsidies, rising input costs and market volatility have increasingly called into question the effectiveness of these incentives in shaping producer behavior.
content: Although agricultural policies worldwide seek to steer cropping patterns through subsidies, rising input costs and market volatility have increasingly called into question the effectiveness of these incentives in shaping producer behavior. This study empirically analyzes, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), the dynamics influencing the cropping-pattern preferences of field-crop producers in Adana, the leading agricultural province of Çukurova—one of Türkiye’s strategic production basins—who have shifted predominantly toward maize in recent years. Evidence from a field survey of 101 producers in Adana reveals a pronounced divergence between agricultural policymakers’ profit-oriented “homo economicus” assumption and the risk-averse reality of producers in the field. The results show that agricultural support carries only a marginal weight of 1.78% in producer decisions, whereas yield stability (54.38%) and factors providing structural security emerge as the dominant determinants. Maize achieves an overall preference score of 0.645 and clearly outperforms its competitors because of its licensed-warehousing infrastructure and transparent market mechanisms, unlike alternatives such as groundnut, which promise high profitability but entail substantial transaction costs and moral-hazard risks. In addition, the farm succession gap, affecting 60.4% of producers, together with the deepening labor crisis, compels rather than merely encourages farmers to adopt fully mechanized maize production. The study concludes that agricultural sustainability requires policies that are not exclusively price-oriented; instead, they should mitigate input-cost volatility, extend institutional safeguards across marketing channels, and address the rural demographic crisis through structural reforms.

title: Judging architecture: The struggle to find winning design proposals
source: FormAkademisk - forskningstidsskrift for design og designdidaktikk
summary: This article critically reflects on how qualified jurors succeeded in identifying winning design proposals during two design developer competitions. Following the close reading and coding of transcribed field notes from jury room deliberati
content: This article critically reflects on how qualified jurors succeeded in identifying winning design proposals during two design developer competitions. Following the close reading and coding of transcribed field notes from jury room deliberations, a judging theory is suggested. The proposed judging model may be of general interest for jury work in architecture and urban design competitions. The underlying concept for this judging theory is that professionals who make qualified assessments must complete critical ethical steps, which are influenced by (a) context and policy, (b) design proposals for competition sites, (c) judging process and competition criteria, and (d) selecting winners and producing the related jury reports. This theory describes and explains how professionals may act in fulfilling their assignment to find a winner.

title: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
summary: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that c
content: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008). It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species. We tested this hypothesis by combining molecular and morphometric data. Sequence data were obtained from 38 L. gastrophysus individuals collected from Northern and Southern American populations. We also used a subset of 13 specimens for geometric morphometrics. Phylogenetic analyses and automatic species delimitation methods consistently distinguished Northern and Southern Atlantic L. gastrophysus as separate clades, and geometric morphometrics supported the same split. The congruence among geographic, molecular, and morphometric data indicates that L. gastrophysus harbours two distinct lineages, highlighting the need for a formal taxonomic revision and separate fisheries management of northern and southern Atlantic populations.

title: VERTICAL LAND CONSOLIDATION IN JAKARTA VERSUS LAND READJUSTMENT IN KOBE, JAPAN: CONCEPTS, AGREEMENTS, IMPLEMENTERS, AND STAGES
summary: Vertical land consolidation (VLC) in Jakarta and land readjustment in Kobe, Japan, both reorganize urban land but emerged from different contexts. This normative legal study uses a descriptive-comparative approach and a literature review to
content: Vertical land consolidation (VLC) in Jakarta and land readjustment in Kobe, Japan, both reorganize urban land but emerged from different contexts. This normative legal study uses a descriptive-comparative approach and a literature review to compare them on concept, consensus acquisition, implementing actors, and implementation stages. VLC reorganizes land and buildings vertically to renew dense settlements with shared land rights, whereas Kobe reorganized land parcels and infrastructure for reconstruction after the 1995 earthquake. VLC requires the approval of at least 60% of participants before the location is determined, whereas in Kobe the city set the planning framework first and residents’ proposals were developed through machizukuri councils. VLC is carried out by central and regional governments, private partners, and residents; in Kobe, by the city government or local unions with residents and consultants. VLC follows four formal stages, while Kobe followed two planning steps.

title: A Markov Chain Model for Learning-State Transitions in Outcome-based Education
source: Spectrum of Engineering and Management Sciences
summary: This study presents a cross-sectional management framework for classifying students' academic performance in the outcome-based education (OBE) context using publicly available school-level academic performance data. The framework incorporat
content: This study presents a cross-sectional management framework for classifying students' academic performance in the outcome-based education (OBE) context using publicly available school-level academic performance data. The framework incorporates academic and engagement-related indicators, including study time, absences, previous academic failures, and final academic achievement, to classify students into high-performing, satisfactory, and at-risk categories. The analysis uses the mathematics subset of the Student Performance dataset, comprising 395 student records. Under the adopted classification rules, 15 students (3.80%) are classified as high-performing, 243 (61.52%) as satisfactory, and 137 (34.68%) as at-risk. Correlation analysis indicates that previous failures have a negative association with final grade (r=-0.360), whereas study time and absences have weak positive associations (r=0.098 and r=0.034, respectively). A sensitivity analysis further shows that the category proportions vary with changes in the classification thresholds. The proposed framework provides a mathematically interpretable and educationally meaningful descriptive approach for identifying groups of students who may require further academic monitoring and support in an OBE environment. Because the dataset contains one record per student, the study does not estimate longitudinal transitions, stationary distributions, or the effects of interventions. The findings are therefore interpreted as cross-sectional results rather than evidence of student progression over time.

title: Illiberal gateways and hubs: Chinese push and European pull in Hungary and Serbia
summary: In this article, we examine how Chinese economic engagement positioned Hungary and Serbia within US–China network competition from 2013 to 2025. Drawing on the network-centrality thesis, we apply a push–pull framework across infrastructure,
content: In this article, we examine how Chinese economic engagement positioned Hungary and Serbia within US–China network competition from 2013 to 2025. Drawing on the network-centrality thesis, we apply a push–pull framework across infrastructure, digital technology, production and finance. On the push side, Chinese firms sought markets, production sites and natural resources, channelled domestic overcapacity outward and internationalised the renminbi. On the pull side, illiberal governance was a key factor, since weak legal and societal constraints reduced entry friction. Because a gateway controls the institutional access point to a larger regulated space while a hub concentrates flows, the two positions emerged bidirectionally, as third countries adapted to great-power competition and China selected partners that fitted its expansion logic. Hungary became a gateway, where tariff-jumping access to the Single Market, tax breaks and lax regulation met Chinese demand for cost-effective production. At the same time, Serbia became a hub, where sovereign-guaranteed borrowing and resource endowments offered sites beyond EU oversight. Most European states became neither, and illiberal government is what distinguished those that did. The gateway–hub distinction therefore illuminates how third countries position themselves under great-power competition.

title: Humanitarian Mine Clearance with the Involvement of African Giant Pouched Rats: Methods, Challenges and Future Directions
source: Journal of Central and Eastern European African Studies
summary: This study provides a comprehensive overview of humanitarian mine clearance, with particular emphasis on the use of African giant pouched rats (Cricetomys ansorgei) as an innovative biological detection tool. The analysis examines the histo
content: This study provides a comprehensive overview of humanitarian mine clearance, with particular emphasis on the use of African giant pouched rats (Cricetomys ansorgei) as an innovative biological detection tool. The analysis examines the historical development of anti-personnel landmine technology, the international legal framework governing mine action, and the full range of current clearance methods, including mechanical systems, technological innovations, detection dogs, and biological approaches. Drawing on published field data, organizational reports, and semi-structured interviews with humanitarian demining professionals, the study evaluates the comparative advantages and limitations of each method. Findings indicate that African giant pouched rats offer significant operational benefits in terms of cost-effectiveness, olfactory sensitivity, and safety, while also presenting specific challenges related to training investment, cultural acceptance, and environmental conditions. The study argues that the future of humanitarian mine clearance lies in biosensor-hybrid systems that integrate biological detection tools with AI-supported robotic platforms and advanced sensor technologies. Enhanced international cooperation, sustained investment in research, and genuine community engagement are identified as essential conditions for achieving a landmine-free world.

title: Assessing Norms Convergence and Divergence in EU–Latin American Trade Relations: The Cases of EU–Mexico and EU–Mercosur Negotiations
source: JCMS Journal of Common Market Studies
summary: Abstract This article aims to assess the normative aspects of European Union (EU) trade relations with Latin America, examining the role of norms divergence and convergence within EU–Mercosur and EU–Mexico trade negotiations. It argues that
content: Abstract This article aims to assess the normative aspects of European Union (EU) trade relations with Latin America, examining the role of norms divergence and convergence within EU–Mercosur and EU–Mexico trade negotiations. It argues that the distinct levels of normative convergence on the human rights and environmental principles of EU–Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) relations amongst European and Latin American actors over time explain why and when EU trade agreements with the region are concluded, even in a scenario of agreement on trade liberalisation commitments. By focusing on the role of environmental and human rights norms within these two major EU–LAC trade negotiations, this research aims to understand to what extent the normative clashes amongst the two sides of the Atlantic have affected the outcomes of trade talks, producing inconsistencies within the principles of EU–LAC interregional relations. First, the article goes over the debate of the normative standpoints of interregionalism more broadly and EU–LAC interregional relations more specifically, contributing to the conceptual reflections of the literature on interregionalism. Drawing on semi‐structured interviews with negotiators, diplomatic and parliamentary actors, it assesses the evolution of EU–Mexico and EU–Mercosur trade agreements over the past years, focusing on issues of normative divergence and convergence amongst the negotiating parties. In particular, it examines the latest negotiation dynamics in both cases, assessing how normative divergences have affected the progress of the two trade negotiations, especially with regard to the human rights and sustainable development parts of the agreements.

title: Unraveling the Factors of Sustainable Market Competitiveness: Strategies of Digitalization, Circular Economy, Green Finance, and Gender Equality
summary: ABSTRACT Despite the central role of digitalization, circular economy, green finance, and gender equality in the European Union (EU) sustainability and competitiveness agendas, the mechanisms through which these factors jointly shape sustai
content: ABSTRACT Despite the central role of digitalization, circular economy, green finance, and gender equality in the European Union (EU) sustainability and competitiveness agendas, the mechanisms through which these factors jointly shape sustainable market competitiveness remain insufficiently understood. Existing research has widely examined these factors in isolation, whereas rare attention has been given to their combined direct, mediating, and moderating relationships grounded in the dynamic capabilities view, ecological modernization, and feminist institutionalism theories across the EU member states. Hence, this study primarily aims to examine the direct association among the outlined factors. Secondly, it examines the mediating role of circular economy between digitalization and sustainable market competitiveness, the mediating role of circular economy between green finance and sustainable market competitiveness, and the mediating role of green finance between digitalization and circular economy. Third, it seeks the moderating role of gender equality between digitalization and circular economy, the moderating role of gender equality between digitalization and green finance, and the moderating role of gender equality between green finance and circular economy across the EU nations. To this end, the study extracted country‐year level data from Eurostat and the OECD for 2014–2023, with a sample size of 270, and analyzed the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‐SEM) to clarify hypothesized associations among constructs. The outcomes indicate that all the direct and mediating paths are positive and statistically significant in the defined settings. In addition, gender equality significantly moderates the relationship between digitalization and circular economy but does not significantly moderate the relationships between digitalization and green finance or between green finance and circular economy. These outcomes extend the existing literature by directing EU policymakers on how to leverage these factors in digital‐to‐green transition, clarify the conditional mechanism of gender equality, and offer evidence‐based guidance to achieve sustainable market competitiveness. The study also contributes by integrating the dynamic capabilities, ecological modernization, and feminist institutionalism theories to draw comprehensive theoretical map for the sustainable market competitiveness. Hence, this study is unique in aligning the outlined factors in a multitheoretical framework for digital‐to‐green transition to achieve sustainable market competitiveness across the EU nations.

title: Microwave Promotion of Homogeneous Guerbet Reaction Catalyzed by an N‐Heterocyclic Carbene Ruthenium Complex
summary: The catalytic homologation of ethanol to higher alcohols through the Guerbet reaction represents a powerful strategy for upgrading bioethanol into renewable advanced biofuels and valued-added chemicals. Given the complexity of the underlyin
content: The catalytic homologation of ethanol to higher alcohols through the Guerbet reaction represents a powerful strategy for upgrading bioethanol into renewable advanced biofuels and valued-added chemicals. Given the complexity of the underlying reaction network, homogeneous catalytic systems can provide more precise control over activity and selectivity than heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, a well-established ruthenium N-heterocyclic carbene (Ru-NHC) complex was combined with microwave irradiation, reducing the reaction time from 4 h to only 10 min while significantly lowering the overall energy demand. Furthermore, microwave heating enhanced the atom economy of the process by favoring the desired aldol-condensation pathway over the competing Cannizzaro reaction, thereby increasing higher-alcohol formation and limiting byproduct generation. This effect was further enhanced by the use of suitable additives and by employing different inorganic bases as cocatalysts, providing a versatile and efficient catalytic protocol. The methodology was successfully extended to the upgrading of n-butanol, enabling the selective production of 2-ethylhexanol, a high-value chemical widely used in the manufacture of plasticizers, lubricants, and surfactants. Finally, regression analysis allowed us to resolve and quantify the effects of the different process parameters, providing insights into the behavior of microwave-assisted homogeneous Guerbet catalysis and confirming the positive influence of microwave heating on catalytic performance.

title: Membranous Ezrin Expression Is Associated With Regional Lymph Node Involvement in Canine Mast Cell Tumours
summary: Canine mast cell tumours (MCTs) show variable biological behaviour, ranging from localized tumours to aggressive disease with regional lymph node involvement. Understanding cellular features associated with this variability may help charact
content: Canine mast cell tumours (MCTs) show variable biological behaviour, ranging from localized tumours to aggressive disease with regional lymph node involvement. Understanding cellular features associated with this variability may help characterize their biological behaviour. Ezrin, a member of the ERM protein family involved in cell motility, has been associated with tumour progression in several neoplasms. However, its role in canine MCT remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate ezrin immunoreactivity and its association with regional lymph node histological status in a retrospective series of 27 canine cutaneous and subcutaneous MCTs. Cytoplasmic and membranous immunolabelling were scored by intensity and percentage of positive neoplastic cells. Cytoplasmic positivity exceeded 50% in 26/27 tumours (96.3%) and membranous positivity exceeded 50% in 19/27 (70.4%). Histological lymph node categories (HN0-HN3) were documented for 26 tumours. The ordinal percentage score for membranous immunolabel correlated positively with HN category (Spearman's ρ = 0.418, two-sided p = 0.034; n = 26), whereas the combined membranous score did not (ρ = 0.259, p = 0.202). The diffuse immunolabelling pattern also showed no statistically significant correlation with HN category (ρ = 0.165, p = 0.430; n = 25). These findings suggest an association between the proportion of MCT cells showing membranous ezrin immunoreactivity and regional lymph node histological status. Further studies are required in order to enlighten ezrin's role in MCT disease evolution.

title: Giant conductance enhancement in graphene nanoscrolls via interlayer-coupled states
summary: Graphene nanoscrolls form a unique radial superlattice whose geometry enables transport behaviors distinct from their flat counterparts. We theoretically demonstrate that rolling a graphene nanoribbon into a few-turn nanoscroll (1.0–1.2 tur
content: Graphene nanoscrolls form a unique radial superlattice whose geometry enables transport behaviors distinct from their flat counterparts. We theoretically demonstrate that rolling a graphene nanoribbon into a few-turn nanoscroll (1.0–1.2 turns) triggers a giant enhancement in longitudinal conductance by an order of magnitude (nearly twentyfold). We show that this effect stems from interlayer hopping between open boundaries, which not only transforms localized edge states into one-dimensional-like conducting channels and also induces a significant Fermi energy shift. Our results reveal an inverse scaling of conductance with turn number, establishing GNSs as a platform for geometry-driven quantum transport and offering a tunable approach to engineering nanoarchitectural electronic states.

title: Establishing soil organic carbon baselines for land degradation neutrality
summary: Establishing reliable baseline measurements for soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks has emerged as a cornerstone for tracking long-term changes in terrestrial ecosystems, serving as a critical indicator within international frameworks such as
content: Establishing reliable baseline measurements for soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks has emerged as a cornerstone for tracking long-term changes in terrestrial ecosystems, serving as a critical indicator within international frameworks such as the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3. However, estimating accurate baseline dynamics remains an intensive, data-demanding challenge due to high spatial soil variability across landscapes. Traditional soil assessments are typically limited by high costs, extensive laboratory processing times, and fragmented regional data configurations. To overcome these constraints, this chapter provides a comprehensive roadmap for integrating Digital soil mapping (DSM) methodologies into land degradation neutrality (LDN) verification frameworks. Central to this synthesis is the empirical SCORPAN conceptual framework, which functions as a robust quantitative tool to predict distinct spatial soil classes and continuous structural chemical parameters across landscapes without necessitating complex, process-based simulations of pedogenic pathways. This predictive structure relies on the assimilation of ground-truth observation sets (e.g., legacy soil databases and horizon-specific profile data) alongside multisource environmental covariates. These covariates incorporate topographic variables derived from digital elevation models (DEMs), land cover matrices, vegetation health markers (e.g., NDVI), and optical satellite imagery captures from modern constellations like NASA’s Landsat or the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Sentinel arrays. Furthermore, we emphasize the capacity of machine learning algorithms (such as random forest, gradient boosting, and deep neural configurations) to interpret complex nonlinear covariate interactions and capture underlying spatial dependence patterns. By transitioning from traditional, subjective polygon partitioning to continuous, pixel-based geostatistical inference, the integration of DSM provides a cost-effective, scalable, and highly repeatable baseline system. Ultimately, this granular spatial data empowers environmental governance to transition from reactive land remediation to site-specific, proactive stewardship, directly supporting climate-smart agricultural interventions, verified carbon credit accounting, and long-term ecosystem preservation goals.

title: eHydrogenation: Pd/C-Catalyzed Reduction of Alkenes and Alkynes without an External H2 Supply
summary: Abstract Combining electrolysis with conventional hydrogenation catalysts offers an alternative to external H2 delivery. We report eHydrogenation, which couples commercial Pd/C with constant-current electrolysis to reduce alkenes and alkyne
content: Abstract Combining electrolysis with conventional hydrogenation catalysts offers an alternative to external H2 delivery. We report eHydrogenation, which couples commercial Pd/C with constant-current electrolysis to reduce alkenes and alkynes in ethanol at room temperature under air. Complementary batch protocols use 0.5 mol % Pd and tolerate halides, nitriles, benzyl ethers, and free alcohols. The method uses routine electrochemical equipment without hydrazine or a purpose-built electrocatalyst and extends to a continuous-flow proof of concept.
