title: An oloid-derived four-operation geometric grammar for architectural form-making: an exploratory analysis of four architectural precedents
summary: Architectural proportioning systems are predominantly based on planar ratios, linear modules, anthropometric calibration, or externally introduced numerical relationships, while comparatively limited attention has been given to operationali
content: Architectural proportioning systems are predominantly based on planar ratios, linear modules, anthropometric calibration, or externally introduced numerical relationships, while comparatively limited attention has been given to operationalizing the intrinsic geometry of three-dimensional ruled-surface solids as reproducible architectural proportioning systems. This study investigates whether established oloid geometric relationships can be synthesized into a three-dimensional proportioning framework for architectural form-making. A geometric-analytical and exploratory research design was adopted. Established oloid geometry was operationalized as a four-rule grammar comprising fold, reflect, translate, and scale; the geometric reproducibility of the rule set was examined through independent hand construction; and its architectural relevance was explored through four a priori criterion-selected precedents representing different geometric and physical form-generation procedures. Proportional correspondence and procedural correspondence were evaluated separately so that qualitative similarity could not override numerical comparison. The study shows that established oloid geometry can be translated into a finite, hand-constructible four-operation grammar through which spatial configurations remain traceable to a common generating geometry. The four-precedent analysis produced mixed rather than confirmatory evidence: it identified a strong case-specific proportional correspondence together with clear proportional non-correspondences, demonstrating that the comparison procedure is capable of distinguishing positive and negative cases. The results do not establish general or method-specific architectural convergence toward oloid-derived relationships. The principal contribution is therefore the architectural synthesis and operationalization of established oloid geometry as a reproducible three-dimensional proportioning grammar, while architectural convergence remains an exploratory and hypothesis-generating proposition requiring validation through a substantially larger, prospectively selected sample. Structural, material, fabrication, and environmental performance are outside the demonstrated scope of the present study.

title: Development and Microstructural Investigation of Ni– Mo–FeCrAl Modified 40H Steel for Furnace Roller Applications
summary: Abstract This study investigates the effect of complex alloying on the microstructure and mechanical behavior of modified 40H structural steel intended for metallurgical furnace rollers. The steel was modified with Ni, Mo, Al, and FeCrAl-ba
content: Abstract This study investigates the effect of complex alloying on the microstructure and mechanical behavior of modified 40H structural steel intended for metallurgical furnace rollers. The steel was modified with Ni, Mo, Al, and FeCrAl-based additives and subjected to normalization at 880°C, quenching at 860°C, and tempering at 550°C. Microstructural evolution was analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with EDS characterization, while hardness was evaluated using Rockwell (HRC), Brinell (HBW), and Vickers (HV) methods. The as-cast condition exhibited a heterogeneous cast microstructure characterized by pronounced dendritic segregation and significant hardness scatter (473–561 HB). After heat treatment, the microstructure developed a more uniform and refined appearance, accompanied by a reduction in hardness scatter. Hardness values stabilized in the range of 42–48 HRC, accompanied by a decrease in measurement dispersion. SEM/BSE observations indicated a more uniform morphology after heat treatment, while local SEM/EDS analysis was used only as a supplementary semi-quantitative tool to evaluate elemental distribution in selected regions. The combined alloying and heat-treatment strategy contributed to microstructural refinement and reduced hardness scatter after heat treatment. These findings suggest that the proposed processing route may be beneficial for the development of 40H steel components intended for furnace roller applications.

title: Fabrication of an acid-treated 3D-printed Perlite monolithic adsorbent for efficient removal of organic dyes from aqueous solution
summary: Abstract Three-dimensional Perlite-based monolithic adsorbents with different Perlite loadings (3D-Per5, 3D-Per10, and 3D-Per15) were fabricated via digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing for methylene blue (MB) removal from aqueous sol
content: Abstract Three-dimensional Perlite-based monolithic adsorbents with different Perlite loadings (3D-Per5, 3D-Per10, and 3D-Per15) were fabricated via digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing for methylene blue (MB) removal from aqueous solutions. The influence of Perlite loading on adsorption performance was systematically investigated, with 3D-Per15 exhibiting the highest adsorption capacity. To further improve its performance, the optimized monolith was subjected to acid treatment, which removed surface impurities, increased the exposure of accessible adsorption sites, and enhanced pore accessibility, thereby significantly promoting dye adsorption while preserving the structural integrity of the printed monolith. The adsorption behavior was evaluated under different operating conditions. The highest MB removal efficiency of 89% and a maximum adsorption capacity of 17.8 mg g − 1 were achieved at pH = 10 and 85°C after 100 min. Kinetic analysis yielded an activation energy of 27.14 kJ mol − 1 , while thermodynamic parameters confirmed that the adsorption process was endothermic (ΔH = 24.36 kJ mol − 1 ) with a negative entropy change (ΔS = − 179.91 J mol − 1 K − 1 ). These findings demonstrate that integrating DLP 3D printing with post-print acid activation is a simple and effective strategy for developing high-performance monolithic adsorbents for wastewater treatment.

title: Anomalous high-pressure phase transition from sp 3 to sp 2 hybridization in carbon materials
summary: D phase exhibits nonmonotonic lattice thermal conductivity with changing temperature. Unique infrared and Raman spectral fingerprints are presented to aid phase identification in future experiments. This study establishes a complete atomist
content: D phase exhibits nonmonotonic lattice thermal conductivity with changing temperature. Unique infrared and Raman spectral fingerprints are presented to aid phase identification in future experiments. This study establishes a complete atomistic picture of an anomalous high-pressure phase transition with reduced coordination number. More anomalous phase transitions might exist in low-density porous carbons as well as III-V group compounds.

title: Fermenting Hope: Penicillin Technology Aid and Sino–American Cooperation in the 1940s
summary: Abstract This study explores penicillin technology’s transmission and localization in 1940s China, mapping the transnational techno-scientific network linking U.S. aid agencies, military forces, and China’s regime-controlled regions. Drawin
content: Abstract This study explores penicillin technology’s transmission and localization in 1940s China, mapping the transnational techno-scientific network linking U.S. aid agencies, military forces, and China’s regime-controlled regions. Drawing on published historical data, unpublished archival documents, this paper compares KMT-CPC parallel trajectories: both accessed U.S. strains and documents, but resource disparities led to divergent models—laboratory standardization vs. guerrilla-style local innovation. By analyzing the Penicillin for China Project’s stagnation and Beiping Penicillin Factory’s adaptation challenges, it reveals transnational aid coordination failures and tensions between standardized technology and local material foundations. This paper thus argues that technology transfer in non-Western contexts is not a mere transplantation of equipment or importation of knowledge, but a localization process dependent on the constant restructuring of techno-social networks. The multiple trajectories of penicillin in China illustrate the possibilities and limitations of scientific and technological modernization in wartime East Asia, and provide a new analytical perspective for understanding how technologies move and transform amid aid, war and political conflicts, and resource asymmetry.

title: Groundwater evolution modeling using multiple dating methods in the Pacific coastal area of Shimokita Peninsula, Japan
summary: Abstract Groundwater age is a key constraint for understanding long-term groundwater flow and evaluating the safety of the geological disposal of radioactive waste. This study reassessed groundwater ages and reconstructed groundwater evolut
content: Abstract Groundwater age is a key constraint for understanding long-term groundwater flow and evaluating the safety of the geological disposal of radioactive waste. This study reassessed groundwater ages and reconstructed groundwater evolution in the coastal sedimentary sequence of the Rokkasho area, Shimokita Peninsula, northeastern Japan, using multiple environmental tracers. Groundwater samples were analyzed for major dissolved constituents, stable isotopes, 3 H, 14 C, 36 Cl/Cl, and dissolved noble gases. Corrected 14 C ages of fresh groundwater were evaluated using hydrogen isotope ratios and noble-gas recharge temperatures, whereas the residence time of deep saline groundwater was assessed using the 36 Cl/Cl method. Fresh groundwater occurs from the shallow subsurface to approximately 180 m below sea level. Corrected 14 C ages range from modern to about 35 ka and are consistent with paleoclimatic variations inferred from δ 2 H values and noble-gas recharge temperatures, supporting the reliability of the age correction. Deep saline groundwater exhibits 36 Cl/Cl ratios close to secular equilibrium, indicating residence times of at least 400 ka. In the upper part of the low-permeability formation, groundwater chemistry indicates mixing among freshwater, fossil seawater, and relatively younger seawater. These results suggest that seawater infiltrated into the shallow formations during marine transgression, whereas older fossil seawater was preserved in deeper, low-permeability strata. Subsequent uplift and sea-level regression promoted freshwater flushing of the shallow aquifer while preserving mixed saline groundwater at intermediate depths. The combined use of multiple groundwater-dating techniques provides a robust reconstruction of long-term groundwater evolution at the Rokkasho site.

title: Advances in Catalytic CO Oxidation: From Mechanistic Understanding to Rational Catalyst Design
summary: Catalytic carbon monoxide (CO) oxidation is essential for hydrogen purification, exhaust treatment, and air quality control, yet high activity under ideal conditions does not necessarily translate into durable performance in complex gas str
content: Catalytic carbon monoxide (CO) oxidation is essential for hydrogen purification, exhaust treatment, and air quality control, yet high activity under ideal conditions does not necessarily translate into durable performance in complex gas streams. This review examines recent advances in CO oxidation through the coupled perspectives of reaction pathways, active-site design, structural dynamics, and poisoning resistance. Experimental and theoretical evidence for Langmuir–Hinshelwood, Eley–Rideal, termolecular, Mars-van Krevelen, and carbonate-mediated pathways is assessed, with particular attention to the roles of lattice oxygen, surface hydroxyls, and water. Across noble metals, transition metal oxides, perovskites, high-entropy materials, and supported atomic catalysts, effective design depends on balancing CO adsorption with oxygen activation while maintaining accessible and stable reactive interfaces. Defect engineering, aliovalent doping, and atomic-scale coordination control provide complementary means of achieving this balance. Operando characterization and multiscale modeling further show that the active structure can differ from the as-prepared catalyst, while data-driven approaches offer emerging tools for interpreting spectra and identifying activity descriptors. Water, sulfur compounds, alkali species, and halogenated contaminants introduce competing adsorption and reconstruction processes that make catalyst performance strongly dependent on operating conditions. Sacrificial sites, interfacial anchoring, and control of local coordination can improve tolerance, but their effectiveness must be established under relevant combined exposures. Future progress requires stronger links between mechanistic evidence and realistic testing, comparable activity and durability metrics, and integration of catalyst chemistry with reactor design and sustainability assessment. These priorities provide a framework for developing CO oxidation catalysts that combine low-temperature activity, selectivity, and operational stability.

title: Simulation of Solidification Microstructure in F45MnVS Non‐Quenched and Tempered Steel Continuous Casting Billets Based on the CAFE Method
summary: To characterise the microstructural evolution during solidification of F45MnVS non‐quenched and tempered steel, a microstructure prediction model for continuous casting billets is developed using the cellular automaton–finite element (CAFE)
content: To characterise the microstructural evolution during solidification of F45MnVS non‐quenched and tempered steel, a microstructure prediction model for continuous casting billets is developed using the cellular automaton–finite element (CAFE) method. The effects of key process parameters, including inclusion characteristics, superheat, casting speed and cooling water flow rate, are systematically investigated. Increasing the inclusion distribution growth factor from 0.8 to 1.2 reduces the columnar grain fraction and promotes equiaxed grain formation. As the number of effective inclusions increases from 0 to 80 000, the average grain size decreases significantly. Higher superheat reduces shell thickness, slightly coarsens grains and decreases the equiaxed grain ratio, with an optimal value of 20 °C. Increasing casting speed raises billet temperatures and reduces the equiaxed grain ratio, with an optimal value of 1.5 m/min. Higher cooling water flow increases shell thickness with limited influence on grain size; the optimal flow rate is 35 L/min. Industrial trials conducted under optimised conditions show good agreement between simulated and measured macrostructures, confirming the reliability of the model. The optimised parameters effectively promote equiaxed grain formation and microstructure refinement.

title: Highly Stable and Practical Sodium-Ion Batteries: Key Materials, Electrode Engineering, Manufacturing, and Prospects
summary: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to abundant sodium resources, low cost, and good manufacturing compatibility. However, their practical application remains limited by the structural stability of
content: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to abundant sodium resources, low cost, and good manufacturing compatibility. However, their practical application remains limited by the structural stability of key materials, interfacial side reactions, cycle life, and safety. This review focuses on highly stable and practical SIBs and systematically summarizes the main failure mechanisms and stabilization strategies of cathode materials, anode materials, and electrolyte/electrode interfaces. Particular attention is paid to phase-transition suppression in layered oxides, framework strengthening of polyanionic compounds, defect regulation in Prussian blue/white materials, closed-pore structure optimization of hard carbon, solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation, and interfacial stability of solid-state electrolytes. In addition, engineering strategies such as thick-electrode design, dry electrode manufacturing, thermal management, adaptive binders, and digital twin technologies are discussed from the perspective of material–electrode–device integration. Distinct from reviews centered on individual material classes, this work connects key-material failure mechanisms with electrode architecture, manufacturing, safety management, and industrialization, providing a full-chain materials–electrode–device–manufacturing perspective. Future efforts should focus on interfacial controllability, manufacturing consistency, and recycling sustainability to accelerate the large-scale application of SIBs.

title: CO2 reductive amination-enabled stereodivergent hydrocyanation of alkynes
summary: Stereoselective catalytic hydrocyanation of alkynes to access high-value nitriles constitutes an important transformation in synthetic chemistry. The key challenge lies in reliance on toxic cyanide reagents, and the inherent strong-field co
content: Stereoselective catalytic hydrocyanation of alkynes to access high-value nitriles constitutes an important transformation in synthetic chemistry. The key challenge lies in reliance on toxic cyanide reagents, and the inherent strong-field coordination of cyanide anions severely compromises both the reactivity and selectivity. By employing amidate intermediates instead, we have developed a cyanide-free pathway for stereodivergent and direct hydrocyanation of alkynes via nickel catalysis using readily available CO 2 /NH 3 . When KF is used as the additive, up to 95% Z -selectivity is achieved, while switching the additive to LiF enables efficient reversal to E -configuration (selectivity up to 90%). Experimental studies combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the formation of nickel(I)-amidate species is the rate-determining step. And the favorable transition state in this step is stabilized by cation-amidate interactions, which serve as the driving force for achieving precise control of stereoselectivity. This work efficiently constructs C-C bond and CN moiety via a step-economical strategy, providing safe and stereodivergent synthesis of alkenyl nitriles.

title: Identifying Early Ecological Disturbance Signals through Functional Shifts in Freshwater Microbial Communities
summary: Freshwater systems face multiple coexisting stressors, but typical monitoring programs will not identify degradation until water chemistry falls outside set standards or changes have occurred in macroinvertebrate and fish communities. The m
content: Freshwater systems face multiple coexisting stressors, but typical monitoring programs will not identify degradation until water chemistry falls outside set standards or changes have occurred in macroinvertebrate and fish communities. The microbes respond quickly (from hours to weeks) to environmental disturbances and facilitate key biogeochemical processes in freshwaters. This makes them promising indicators for early warning assessments. The current study investigates whether changes in functional attributes of freshwater microbial communities may act as an early signal of ecological disturbance before any structural and taxonomic change takes place. A systematic review of the literature on microbial resistance, resilience, functional redundancy, community assembly, and critical transition theories was coupled with a comparison of eight different functional indicators, from functional genes and enzymes to predicted metagenomic functionality. A simple simulation of indicator response to disturbance intensity was done afterwards. The synthesis shows that functional traits, especially the relative abundance of genes associated with nitrogen cycling and stress responses and the proportion of enzymes for acquisition of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus, respond more quickly and consistently to nutrient addition, pollution, warming, and changes in water flow regimes compared to taxonomic composition. In this experiment, functional gene indicators reached the level of detection 8.5 weeks prior to the macroinvertebrate indicator and four weeks prior to taxonomic community changes. Functional redundancy may obscure disturbances; therefore, increases in variation and delay in the recovery of functional indicators should be considered along with average values. A hierarchical approach to monitoring is suggested, which includes microbial functional assessment together with traditional biomonitoring.

title: PSGRNet: Multi-scale spectral–frequency representation learning with gated residual fusion for coastal wetland classification using UAV hyperspectral imagery
source: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
summary: Coastal wetlands are characterized by diverse vegetation, high spectral similarity, fragmented spatial distributions, and dynamic environmental conditions, posing significant challenges for accurate hyperspectral image classification. Altho
content: Coastal wetlands are characterized by diverse vegetation, high spectral similarity, fragmented spatial distributions, and dynamic environmental conditions, posing significant challenges for accurate hyperspectral image classification. Although UAV hyperspectral imagery provides fine-grained spatial and spectral observations that can help capture such complex and fragmented features, effectively leveraging this information to distinguish spectrally similar and spatially intermixed vegetation types remains an open problem. Therefore, we propose a Progressive Spectral Gated Residual Network (PSGRNet). Specifically, a spectral enhancement and multi-scale sequence modeling strategy is first introduced to strengthen discriminative spectral representations and capture multi-scale spectral dependencies. Building on these enhanced representations, a frequency-aware module further exploits global frequency-domain characteristics to aggregate informative spectral features adaptively. To effectively integrate both spectral and frequency-domain representations, a GRF strategy is developed to improve the robustness of the network in heterogeneous and fragmented coastal wetland scenes. We have collected three UAV-based hyperspectral datasets covering representative coastal wetland scenarios, including reed-dominated natural wetlands (NT-YK), highly fragmented landscapes with dynamic land-cover transitions (YC-YS), and human-influenced estuarine environments (LYG-LH). Experimental results on these three datasets demonstrate that PSGRNet outperforms 9 representative methods, achieving macro F1 scores of 89.25%, 81.99%, and 81.29%, respectively. These results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for accurate coastal wetland classification and demonstrate the value of the released datasets. The datasets will be publicly available at https://github.com/HAPPYFST/Wetland-HSI-Data .

title: Enhancing Plurigaussian simulation through neural truncation rules
source: Machine Learning and Data Science in Geotechnics
summary: Purpose Plurigaussian simulation (PGS) is a powerful approach in generating discrete stochastic structures of complex multiphase systems across a range of scales. Originating as an extension of truncated Gaussian simulation, PGS allows for
content: Purpose Plurigaussian simulation (PGS) is a powerful approach in generating discrete stochastic structures of complex multiphase systems across a range of scales. Originating as an extension of truncated Gaussian simulation, PGS allows for the detailed representation of phase relationships and connectivity. A key element of PGS is the identification of truncation rules to dictate the geometric and facies relationships and traditionally involves a trial-and-error approach based on the physical characteristics of the modelled structures. The purpose of this study is to present an approach to learning such rules. Design/methodology/approach This study introduces the use of generative adversarial networks, specifically using the Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty architecture, to automate and enhance the selection of truncation rules through a neural truncation rule. Findings By learning directly from the characteristics of the training data, this approach aims to bypass the limitations of manual truncation rule selection, offering a more efficient and precise method to replicate the desired structural features. Originality/value This study highlights the efficacy of generative machine learning in identifying suitable truncation rules for PGS, significantly reducing the uncertainty in truncation rule choice and enabling the accurate realisation of complex structural characteristics without the ill-informed trial-and-error process traditionally undertaken.

title: Waste-to- Metal–Organic Frameworks (MOFs): A green design and circular sustainability architecture for MOF-assisted bioenergy systems
summary: Green design and circular bioeconomy concepts are increasingly applied to sustainable waste-to-energy systems to improve renewable energy recovery, waste valorization, and resource circularity. In this transition, metal-organic-frameworks (
content: Green design and circular bioeconomy concepts are increasingly applied to sustainable waste-to-energy systems to improve renewable energy recovery, waste valorization, and resource circularity. In this transition, metal-organic-frameworks (MOFs) have been developed as promising multifunctional materials to improve anaerobic digestion and upgrade low-carbon biogas. This success is attributable to their tunable physicochemical features, adsorption capabilities, catalytic activities as well as selective gas separation. Notably, waste-derived MOFs, such as those from plastic waste and metal scrap, hold great promise for integrating waste management, renewable bioenergy production, enhanced nutrient recovery, and eco-friendly biofertilizer synthesis in sustainable bioresource systems. This PRISMA review covers waste-derived MOF synthesis, anaerobic digestion, biogas purification, digestate management, and agricultural reuse. It concludes that research is patchy, mainly quantitatively centered on technical performance, while generally addressing environmental, economic, governance, and social sustainability factors such as ecotoxicity, digestate safety, and circular reuse in a qualitative manner. Therefore, a stage-gated Waste-to-MOFs Technical-Environmental-Governance-Economic-and-Social (WA2MOF–TEGES) framework is proposed as a holistic circular-green design for integrated waste-to-bioenergy systems. It establishes sustainability monitoring through measurable, stage-specific parameters/indicators and adaptive decision-progression gates, from waste collection, precursor recovery, sustainable MOF synthesis, integrated anaerobic digestion, biogas upgrading, digestate evaluation, and nutrient recovery to biomass regeneration paths. The WA2MOF–TEGES framework provides a structured and transferable conceptual foundation for lifecycle-oriented sustainability governance, circular resource accounting, bio-friendly fertilizer recovery optimization, and low-carbon circular bioeconomy transitions. Future studies should aim to conduct experimental validation, standardize digestate safety, integrate into the lifecycle, and implement intelligent sustainability monitoring to enable scalable application.

title: Multiphysics-guided design of black phosphorus–carbon anodes through coupled transport, alloying, and chemo-mechanical evolution
summary: Black phosphorus–carbon (BP–C) anodes offer substantial potential for high-capacity sodium-ion storage, yet their performance is governed by tightly coupled ionic transport, electronic connectivity, alloying-induced deformation, pore evolut
content: Black phosphorus–carbon (BP–C) anodes offer substantial potential for high-capacity sodium-ion storage, yet their performance is governed by tightly coupled ionic transport, electronic connectivity, alloying-induced deformation, pore evolution, and mechanical degradation. A two-dimensional electro-chemo-mechanical framework is developed to establish quantitative relationships between electrode architecture, operating conditions, and the evolving stability of BP–C composites. The model integrates electrolyte transport, carbon-network percolation, particle-scale Na diffusion, sequential P→NaₓP→Na₃P transformation, finite chemical deformation, conservation-based porosity evolution, and damage-dependent conductivity loss. Validation against independent BP/CBP capacity and expansion data yielded a mean error of 5.94%, while experimental constraints on Na diffusivity, interfacial kinetics, mechanical modulus, and pressure-dependent porosity produced a mean deviation of 5.68%. The coupled analysis reveals a non-monotonic architecture–performance relationship: a balanced configuration with a carbon fraction of 0.50 and an initial porosity of 0.40 achieved a stability metric of approximately 0.56, whereas additional carbon did not provide continuous improvement. The predicted instability-transition rate reached approximately 2.8 C for 0.20 μm BP particles under 0.50 MPa confinement but decreased to about 1.5 C for 0.80 μm particles at 1.50 MPa. Moreover, the favorable carbon fraction shifted from approximately 0.30–0.42 at low rates to 0.47–0.60 under faster operation. The balanced architecture retained the highest stability ranking in seven of eight uncertainty perturbations, demonstrating that favorable electrode configurations emerge from the simultaneous balance of electronic percolation, ionic accessibility, Na redistribution, expansion accommodation, and stress localization rather than optimization of any single material parameter. These results establish an operating-dependent multidimensional design framework for mechanically resilient, transport-efficient phosphorus-based sodium-ion anodes.

title: Numerical modelling of mixed convection over slender cylinders: a critical review of transport mechanisms, computational methods and advanced nanofluids
source: International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat &amp Fluid Flow
summary: Purpose This critical study aims to offer a mechanistic assessment of numerical studies on mixed-convection heat and mass transfer over slender cylinders and related thin geometries. It aims to establish a coherent framework for classifying
content: Purpose This critical study aims to offer a mechanistic assessment of numerical studies on mixed-convection heat and mass transfer over slender cylinders and related thin geometries. It aims to establish a coherent framework for classifying the literature by dominant transport mechanisms, modelling assumptions and computational practices, and to explain the origins of apparently conflicting trends in surface drag, heat and mass transfer and entropy generation. Design/methodology/approach The review uses a mechanism-based synthesis to classify and critically interrogate studies of single, double and multiple diffusion; buoyancy-assisting and buoyancy-opposing flows; suction and injection; rotation; nonlinear stretching; porous resistance; radiation; viscous dissipation; chemical reaction; surface roughness; non-Newtonian rheology; and mono-, hybrid-, ternary- and tetra-hybrid nanofluids. Within each category, it systematically examines the governing assumptions, boundary and far-field conditions, constitutive and effective-property models, nondimensionalisation, parameter regimes and numerical treatments. Particular attention is given to the suitability, verification, convergence and validation of finite-difference, Keller-box, quasilinearisation, shooting, boundary-value, collocation, homotopy and spectral methods. Findings Transverse curvature enters the leading-order transport balance when the boundary-layer thickness is comparable to the cylinder radius; neglecting it can therefore compromise predictions of wall shear, heat transfer and mass transfer. Apparent contradictions in the literature arise predominantly from differences in buoyancy orientation, curvature magnitude, wall thermal and species conditions, constitutive and effective-property correlations, parameter ranges, nondimensionalisation and numerical treatment, rather than from genuine physical inconsistency. Iterative convergence alone does not establish numerical credibility. Reliable solutions also require grid- or collocation-point independence, residual assessment, far-field truncation tests, benchmark comparisons, branch-continuation and stability analyses where multiple solutions occur and, whenever feasible, validation against experiments or independent high-fidelity simulations. Advanced nanofluids may improve heat transfer, but the reported gains are strongly model-dependent and may be offset by increased viscosity, wall shear, pressure-drop demands, entropy generation, suspension-instability constraints and uncertainty in thermophysical property correlations. Originality/value Unlike conventional chronological surveys, this review offers a unified, mechanism-based and numerically rigorous synthesis of mixed convection over slender cylinders. title: Rødhals Man: a life at the end of the Mesolithic world
summary: Found buried within a shell midden on the Sejerø archipelago, the skeleton designated as Rødhals Man is here identified as belonging to the most recent individual in Denmark (who died c . 3800 cal BC) with unadmixed Mesolithic genetic ances
content: Found buried within a shell midden on the Sejerø archipelago, the skeleton designated as Rødhals Man is here identified as belonging to the most recent individual in Denmark (who died c . 3800 cal BC) with unadmixed Mesolithic genetic ancestry and a marine-dependent diet. However, through incremental sampling of dentine, the authors show that the diet of this individual was increasingly supplemented, from adolescence onwards, with terrestrial products and argue that these resources were probably farmed. They position Rødhals Man at the end of the Mesolithic world, providing a glimpse into the Neolithic transition at the scale of an individual life.

title: New meets the old: how plant tissue culture can assist cutting-edge methods in plant biotechnology
summary: Abstract Plant tissue culture supports many plant biotechnology workflows, bridging classical micropropagation with cutting-edge molecular tools. While advanced genome editing systems, such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindrom
content: Abstract Plant tissue culture supports many plant biotechnology workflows, bridging classical micropropagation with cutting-edge molecular tools. While advanced genome editing systems, such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and CRISPR-associated protein (CRISPR-Cas) systems, base editing, and prime editing, offer precise molecular modifications, their practical application in many crops is limited by the efficiency of plant regeneration. This review combines a bibliometric analysis of 2,389 publications from 2016 to 2026 with a narrative examination of the relationship between tissue culture and modern plant biotechnology. The bibliometric analysis maps publication trends, scientific collaboration, and research topics within a corpus selected for its coverage of this interface. We examine how cellular reprogramming, organogenesis, and somatic embryogenesis affect the recovery of plants following genetic interventions. We also discuss the integration of tissue culture with metabolic engineering, synthetic biology, and emerging technologies, including tissue-culture-independent editing, speed breeding, high-throughput phenotyping, and artificial intelligence-driven optimization. Together, the bibliometric and narrative analyses show how tissue culture contributes to many current applications while identifying regeneration bottlenecks and approaches that may reduce reliance on conventional culture procedures.

title: Nutrient Recovery Efficiency of Constructed Wetland Systems Treating Small-Scale Aquaculture Wastewater
summary: Nitrogen and phosphorus found in aquaculture wastewater have been cited to be a source of eutrophication and ecologically detrimental. The current study seeks to analyze the effectiveness of constructed wetland systems in removing these nut
content: Nitrogen and phosphorus found in aquaculture wastewater have been cited to be a source of eutrophication and ecologically detrimental. The current study seeks to analyze the effectiveness of constructed wetland systems in removing these nutrients and the suitability of constructed wetlands for small-scale aquaculture wastewater treatment. Quantitative secondary data analysis based on experimental results from pilot-scale constructed wetlands with Salicornia bigelovii for marine aquaculture effluents at low, medium, and high total ammonia nitrogen loadings was performed. The removal efficiencies of ammonia nitrogen, nitrite nitrogen, nitrate nitrogen, and phosphate phosphorus have been analyzed to observe the specific response of nutrients to treatments. It was found that the removal efficiency of ammonia nitrogen has reduced from 58.51% at low loading to 26.21% at high loading. The removal efficiency of nitrite nitrogen has reduced from 96.07% to 27.93%, showing a decrease of 68.14 percentage points. The removal efficiency of nitrate nitrogen has reduced from 52.03% to 29.69%, while that of phosphate phosphorus has been observed to be very limited, i.e., between 1.87% and 8.20%. It can be inferred that with an increase in nutrient loading, nitrogen treatment efficiency decreases significantly, especially for nitrite. Constructed wetlands are a sustainable method of wastewater treatment; however, better hydraulic design, vegetation, substrate, and additional phosphorus removal are required.

title: Ligand-Free Ni2+ Immobilization on Poly(acrylic acid)-Functionalized Magnetic Nanoparticles for His-Tagged Protein Purification
summary: Abstract The development of simplified, ligand-free magnetic affinity platforms holds promise for advancing future recombinant protein purification technologies. Purification of His6-tagged proteins, essential in biotechnology and biopharma
content: Abstract The development of simplified, ligand-free magnetic affinity platforms holds promise for advancing future recombinant protein purification technologies. Purification of His6-tagged proteins, essential in biotechnology and biopharmaceutical production, is commonly achieved via immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography (IMAC). However, magnetic IMAC systems commonly require additional chelating ligands for Ni2+ immobilization, increasing surface functionalization complexity. Developing a ligand-free magnetic platform for direct Ni2+ immobilization could therefore simplify this purification process. Poly(acrylic acid) (PAA)-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were developed as a simple ligand-free platform for direct Ni2+ immobilization and selective purification of His6-tagged proteins, exploiting the intrinsic metal-coordination capability of surface carboxylate groups. MNPs were synthesized by chemical coprecipitation and subsequently coated with PAA of two molecular weights (2 and 100 kDa) to systematically investigate the influence of polymer chain length on physicochemical properties, Ni2+ immobilization efficiency, and bioseparation performance. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy revealed a decrease in the free carboxylic acid stretching band and a concurrent increase in the carboxylate coordination band upon Ni2+ immobilization, supporting the involvement of PAA carboxylate groups in Ni2+ immobilization, consistent with a proposed carboxylate–metal interaction at the nanoparticle surface. Complementarily, zeta potential analysis demonstrated progressive surface charge evolution from bare MNPs to PAA-coated and Ni2+-loaded states, consistent with PAA adsorption and subsequent Ni2+ immobilization. The purification performance of both systems was then evaluated using His6-tagged Plasmodium falciparum serine hydroxymethyltransferase (His6-tagged PfSHMT) as a model protein. Despite both systems achieving near-complete adsorption, MNPs–PAA(2 kDa)–Ni2+ exhibited significantly higher desorption efficiency (63.5 ± 6.7%) than MNPs–PAA(100 kDa)–Ni2+ (37.8 ± 6.1%), demonstrating different protein recovery between the two PAA formulations investigated. The optimized MNPs–PAA(2 kDa)–Ni2+ system achieved rapid protein capture within 15 min and selective purification over nontagged proteins (BSA and lysozyme). Further application to crude E. coli cell lysate demonstrated enrichment of His6-tagged PfSHMT with retained enzymatic activity and a 326-fold purification. These findings establish PAA-functionalized MNPs as a simple and effective ligand-free nanoplatform for selective affinity-based bioseparation of His6-tagged proteins.

title: Facet-dependent anion adsorption for electrolyte-Cu interfacial stability in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries
summary: Initially anode-free Li-metal batteries, in which Li-metal is constructed in-situ during charging, enable increased energy density. However, interfacial degradation reactions between the electrolyte and lithiophobic Cu prevent stable solid
content: Initially anode-free Li-metal batteries, in which Li-metal is constructed in-situ during charging, enable increased energy density. However, interfacial degradation reactions between the electrolyte and lithiophobic Cu prevent stable solid electrolyte interphase formation on the negative electrode. Here, we elucidate a time-evolving interfacial mechanism in which adsorption of electrolyte components contributes to initial interfacial layer formation and solid electrolyte interphase stability. Most organic solvents adsorb more strongly than Li-salt compounds on Cu through van der Waals dispersion interactions. This preferential adsorption produces a solvent-dominated interfacial layer that undergoes rapid compositional reconstruction during Cu oxide reduction upon initial charging. In contrast, lithium tetrafluoroborate possesses a tetrahedral anion with isotropic charge distribution that binds strongly to the Cu (111)/(100) surfaces and native Cu oxides, producing a tetrafluoroborate-driven interfacial layer that electronically passivates the Cu interface and promotes homogeneous Li nucleation. Consequently, lithium tetrafluoroborate-containing cells achieve 62% capacity retention after 300 cycles at an areal capacity of 4.1 mAh cm−2 and electrolyte conditions of 1.5 g Ah−1 and 4 μL cm−2, establishing a mechanistic basis for adsorption-driven interfacial design in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries. Initially anode-free lithium-metal batteries are limited by unstable interfacial reactions at Cu current collectors. Here, authors show that preferential anion adsorption can stabilize the copper interface and improve long-term cycling.

title: Aero-eutectic graphite from gray cast iron as a current collector-free anode for lithium-ion batteries
source: Journal of Materials Science Materials in Energy
summary: Aero-Eutectic Graphite (AEG) is introduced as a novel metal-free, self-supported anode architecture for lithium-ion batteries, in which the graphitic framework simultaneously functions as both the electrochemically active material and the c
content: Aero-Eutectic Graphite (AEG) is introduced as a novel metal-free, self-supported anode architecture for lithium-ion batteries, in which the graphitic framework simultaneously functions as both the electrochemically active material and the current collector, eliminating the need for conventional metallic substrates and binders. AEG was prepared from gray cast iron containing type-A lamellar graphite through a selective extraction process, yielding a highly porous graphitic network with a specific surface area of 87.3 m2 g− 1. Structural characterization confirmed the preservation of the graphitic framework, as evidenced by the characteristic (002) reflection in X-ray diffraction and the typical G, D, and G′ bands in Raman spectroscopy, while semiquantitative EDS analysis revealed a predominantly carbonaceous matrix with minor detectable metallic species (< 1.25 wt%). Electrochemical measurements demonstrated reversible lithium intercalation/deintercalation below 0.5 V, characteristic of graphitic carbon. Under galvanostatic cycling at C/10, the self-supported electrode delivered a stable reversible capacity of approximately 300 mAh g⁻¹ over prolonged cycling. Furthermore, rate capability tests from C/50 to 1 C demonstrated stable cycling under varied currents, recovering 97.4% of the initial C/10 capacity. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed a progressive decrease in interfacial resistance and enhanced charge-transfer kinetics with cycling, indicating gradual electrode activation and electrochemical stabilization after approximately 50 cycles. These results demonstrate that AEG provides a robust, lightweight, and binder-free electrode architecture that integrates current collection and lithium storage within a single graphitic framework, offering a promising strategy for simplifying electrode design while maintaining competitive electrochemical performance.

title: Cellulose‐Derived Poly(Ionic Liquid)s With Cooperative Hydroxyl/Iodide Sites for Atmospheric‐Pressure CO 2 Cycloaddition
summary: ABSTRACT A cellulose‐derived poly(ionic liquid) (CLPI) is constructed by grafting imidazolium‐containing ionic polymer segments onto a renewable cellulose framework. The resulting material combines residual cellulose hydroxyl groups with gr
content: ABSTRACT A cellulose‐derived poly(ionic liquid) (CLPI) is constructed by grafting imidazolium‐containing ionic polymer segments onto a renewable cellulose framework. The resulting material combines residual cellulose hydroxyl groups with grafted imidazolium sites and associated iodide counterions, creating a heterogeneous polymer microenvironment for cooperative epoxide activation and nucleophilic ring opening. CLPI contains 11.93 wt% iodide, and shows greater CO 2 uptake than the cellulose precursor. Without metals, solvent, or external cocatalysts, CLPI catalyzes atmospheric‐pressure CO 2 cycloaddition with epoxides, affording 86% yield of 4‐(chloromethyl)‐1,3‐dioxolan‐2‐one at 100°C in 12 h. Hot‐filtration and post‐reaction analyses support predominantly heterogeneous catalysis and retention of the ionic polymer framework. A 10 g epichlorohydrin experiment affords 89% yield, demonstrating the scale‐up potential of the cellulose‐derived catalytic polymer.

title: Flexible Ultralow‐Power IGZO Multimodal Synaptic Transistors for Thermally Robust Neuromorphic Vision and Wearable Heatstroke Monitoring
summary: ABSTRACT Multimodal synaptic devices are increasingly required to enable more reliable and informed decision‐making in next‐generation neuromorphic systems. A wafer‐scale, energy‐efficient flexible optoelectronic synaptic transistor based o
content: ABSTRACT Multimodal synaptic devices are increasingly required to enable more reliable and informed decision‐making in next‐generation neuromorphic systems. A wafer‐scale, energy‐efficient flexible optoelectronic synaptic transistor based on an a‐IGZO channel and ALD‐deposited HfO 2 gate dielectric is demonstrated. The device is fabricated on a rigid silicon substrate and subsequently transformed into a flexible form, maintaining stable electrical characteristics under repeated bending (radius ∼3 cm). The device enables multimodal sensing by responding to optical stimulus and a wide temperature range (10‐75°C), capturing signals such as body temperature, ambient conditions, and sunlight. Under optical stimulation, the transistor emulates key synaptic functions, including EPSC, PPF, and the transition from STM to LTM, as well as learning‐forgetting‐relearning behavior. Reliable synaptic responses are achieved at a low drain voltage of 0.01 V, with an energy consumption of 1.6 fJ per synaptic event. The behavior is governed by defect‐mediated carrier trapping and detrapping in IGZO. System‐level applications include heatstroke risk classification (99.6% accuracy, within the physiological temperature range 37°C–42°C) and neuromorphic vision sensing enabled by persistent photoconductivity. These multimodal capabilities enable both heatstroke monitoring and thermally robust vision processing within a unified platform. The results present a scalable platform for low‐power neuromorphic and wearable healthcare applications.

title: Novel Protective Role of Nucleic Acid Binding With Sucrose‐Phosphate Synthase in Cyanobacterial Salt Stress Response
summary: Many cyanobacteria synthesise and accumulate large amounts of sucrose as a compatible solute in the cell to maintain osmotic balance under salt stress. This provides a novel strategy for simple sugar production that complements traditional
content: Many cyanobacteria synthesise and accumulate large amounts of sucrose as a compatible solute in the cell to maintain osmotic balance under salt stress. This provides a novel strategy for simple sugar production that complements traditional plant-based manufacturing routes. Although metabolic engineering has greatly improved sucrose biosynthesis in cyanobacteria, our limited understanding of relevant regulatory mechanisms severely hinders further progress in applied biotechnology. Previous studies have revealed that the freshwater cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942 adopts an ion-mediated enzymatic regulatory mechanism targeting sucrose-phosphate synthase (SPS), the rate-limiting enzyme in sucrose biosynthesis, to regulate sucrose production. Nevertheless, the details of this process remain elusive. Through subcellular localisation assays and biochemical characterisation, we demonstrate the direct physical interaction between SPS and intracellular nucleic acids in this cyanobacterium. This observation resembles that reported for glucosylglycerol-phosphate synthase (GGPS), the enzyme catalysing the key step in the biosynthesis of compatible solute glucosylglycerol in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. However, unlike the GGPS-nucleic acid interaction that modulates enzymatic activity, the binding of nucleic acids to SPS does not reshape the ion-dependent activation pattern of SPS. Instead, it enhances SPS protein stability against thermal and proteolytic degradation. This property enables cells to maintain a steady basal pool of the enzyme, thereby facilitating a rapid adaptive response to fluctuating salinity. Therefore, despite sharing similar physiological phenotypes regarding salt-induced compatible solute accumulation, various cyanobacteria have evolved differential molecular mechanisms for salt stress response.

title: MEC‐BioSense: Material‐Encoded Capillary Biointerface for Autonomous Whole‐Blood Biomarker Sensing
summary: ABSTRACT Bioelectronic sensing in complex biological fluids is often constrained not by molecular recognition, but by poor coordination of transport, separation, and interfacial interactions at the material level. Here, we present a materia
content: ABSTRACT Bioelectronic sensing in complex biological fluids is often constrained not by molecular recognition, but by poor coordination of transport, separation, and interfacial interactions at the material level. Here, we present a material‐encoded capillary biointerface that integrates microporous media, microfluidic geometry, and a hydrophilic graphene/poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate)/Prussian Blue bioelectronic interface into a unified, self‐regulated architecture. Capillary forces generated within a microfiber network are redistributed through vent‐regulated pathways and stabilized at a hydrophilic mixed ionic–electronic interface, enabling controlled plasma extraction, transport, and analyte delivery without external actuation. System performance is governed by the balance between capillary driving pressure and distributed hydrodynamic resistance, defining an operating regime that simultaneously achieves >99% cellular exclusion, ∼80–93% protein recovery, and stable interfacial wetting. Within this regime, undiluted whole blood is autonomously converted into a reproducible electrochemical signal. Using glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) as a model biomarker, the platform enables direct sample‐to‐answer detection within ∼9 min, spanning 0.02 pg mL −1 to 200 ng mL −1 with an ultralow detection limit (∼0.01 fg mL −1 ) and reduced pre‐analytical loss relative to centrifugation. These results establish that analytical performance is governed primarily by pre‐analytical transport and interfacial regulation and introduce a generalizable nano/micro‐engineered framework for autonomous, scalable point‐of‐care biointerfaces.

title: Two‐dimensional optoelectronic synaptic materials for emerging neuromorphic devices
summary: Abstract The exponential growth of global data and the fundamental energy efficiency limits of the traditional von Neumann architecture have driven an urgent need for novel computing paradigms. Neuromorphic computing, inspired by the highly
content: Abstract The exponential growth of global data and the fundamental energy efficiency limits of the traditional von Neumann architecture have driven an urgent need for novel computing paradigms. Neuromorphic computing, inspired by the highly efficient and parallel processing capabilities of the human brain, offers a promising solution. Among various hardware candidates, artificial optoelectronic synaptic devices based on two‐dimensional (2D) materials have attracted immense attention due to their atomic‐level thickness, excellent optoelectronic response, and ultra‐low power consumption. This comprehensive review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in 2D optoelectronic synaptic devices, focusing on six core operating mechanisms: defect‐mediated charge trapping, floating‐gate charge storage, van der Waals heterojunction interface engineering, ferroelectric polarization, ion migration, and phase‐change mechanisms. By leveraging these physical mechanisms, 2D optoelectronic synapses successfully emulate fundamental biological synaptic functions, including short‐term and long‐term plasticity, thereby realizing the integration of in‐sensor and in‐memory computing. Furthermore, we highlight the state‐of‐the‐art applications of these devices in brain‐inspired vision and neuromorphic computing systems. Despite significant laboratory‐scale achievements, transitioning from proof‐of‐concept to system‐level applications remains challenging. Finally, we outline critical engineering hurdles and future research trajectories, emphasizing the necessity for high‐quality wafer‐scale material growth, high‐density integration to minimize crosstalk, algorithm‐hardware co‐design, and the development of biocompatible platforms for advanced wearable technologies and brain‐computer interfaces.

title: Decoding the Dopant‐Dependent Catalytic Activity of Spinel Co 3 O 4 Nanocatalysts for the Alkaline Oxygen Evolution Reaction
summary: ABSTRACT The identification of structure–activity correlations is crucial for the rational design of high‐performance water splitting catalysts. Herein, we systematically elucidate the role of metal dopants in the intrinsic activity of coba
content: ABSTRACT The identification of structure–activity correlations is crucial for the rational design of high‐performance water splitting catalysts. Herein, we systematically elucidate the role of metal dopants in the intrinsic activity of cobalt spinel (M 0.1 Co 2.9 O 4 ) for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), based on experimental findings and density functional theory (DFT+ U ) simulations. The dopant effect within spherical, phase‐pure M 0.1 Co 2.9 O 4 nanoparticles is studied via the controlled variation of the metal dopant (3.3 at.% M = V, Cr, and Mn) while other particle parameters including shape and size, which may affect their catalytic activity, are maintained. Both experimental and DFT+ U studies demonstrate a direct dopant‐dependent OER activity with a strong promoting effect in terms of lower overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 , reduced charge transfer resistance, and higher TOF in the case of vanadium and chromium, whereas a detrimental effect is observed for manganese. The metal dopant strongly influences the surface transformation into CoOOH, the active species during OER. DFT+ U calculations identify the * OH→ * O deprotonation step as the potential‐determining step (PDS) for both pristine and M‐doped Co 3 O 4 (111) surfaces, and establish a correlation between dopant‐induced changes in oxidation state and spin configuration at the active site, the subsurface sites, PDS energetics and overpotential.

title: Adsorption-assisted plasmonic enhancement of flutamide detection using AuNPs@rGOPANI nanocomposite films
summary: Sensitive detection of flutamide (FLT) in aqueous samples remains important for pharmaceutical and environmental monitoring. Here, we developed a label-free surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor based on gold nanoparticles integrated with
content: Sensitive detection of flutamide (FLT) in aqueous samples remains important for pharmaceutical and environmental monitoring. Here, we developed a label-free surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor based on gold nanoparticles integrated with a reduced graphene oxide–polyaniline film (AuNPs@rGOPANI). The rGOPANI layer provides a chemically diverse interface that can retain FLT through aromatic and polar interactions, while the AuNP-containing structure may strengthen the optical response to changes in the near-surface dielectric environment. FE-SEM analysis of 232 distinguishable nanoparticle features gave an apparent mean diameter of 24.20 ± 3.07 nm. The sensor showed a concentration-dependent, nonlinear resonance-angle shift over the investigated interval of 0.02–200 μM, with a practical detection threshold of 0.02 μM (20 nM) under the tested conditions. Eight mean calibration responses were fitted to Langmuir, Sips, and Freundlich models. The Sips equation provided the lowest root mean square error (0.03047°) and highest coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.99090), whereas the Freundlich model was favored by the corrected Akaike information criterion, indicating that no single adsorption model could be selected unambiguously from the available data. The sensor responded more strongly to FLT than to the tested inorganic ions, carbohydrates, and beclamide as a structurally related pharmaceutical interferent, retained approximately 78% of its initial response after 30 days, and showed promising performance in river-water spike-recovery experiments. These findings support the potential of AuNPs@rGOPANI as an adsorption-assisted SPR interface for FLT sensing, while emphasizing the need for further replicate-based validation of quantitative performance across the full concentration interval.

title: Mycorrhizal fungi colonization of Artemisia californica roots in response to experimental nitrogen addition and Brassica nigra invasion
summary: Artemisia californica is a dominant shrub species found in Southern California coastal sage scrub (CSS) that is known to form relationships with mycorrhizal fungi for nutrient acquisition and water uptake. Root samples of A. californica wer
content: Artemisia californica is a dominant shrub species found in Southern California coastal sage scrub (CSS) that is known to form relationships with mycorrhizal fungi for nutrient acquisition and water uptake. Root samples of A. californica were collected during the spring for 3 years (2022-24) from a long-term (19-21 year) nitrogen (N) addition experiment at the Santa Margarita Ecological Reserve (SMER) in northern San Diego County. Root samples were collected from plots that received N at a rate of 50 kgN ha -1 y -1 (added N) or no additional N (control), and from patches within each experimental plot that were either free or covered with the invasive annual Brassica nigra . Nitrogen addition and B. nigra invasion significantly reduced vesicular arbuscular mycorrhizae (VAM) fungal structures, including arbuscule and vesicle counts per cm of sample and hyphal length, with the most severe decline occurring when both stressors were present. These changes may also be influenced by environmental soil properties such as soil moisture and pH. Soil pH was consistently lower in N-treated plots, while interannual increases in precipitation led to higher soil moisture that improved VAM colonization during the study’s wettest year (2024). Further research should be done to identify the mycorrhizal taxa affected by N inputs and B. nigra invasion to understand how these global change agents affect plant species diversity and ecosystem carbon and nutrient cycles, which could help inform efforts for conservation of this fragile ecosystem and preserve what is left of California’s iconic semiarid shrublands.

title: Distributionally Robust Low Carbon Dispatch of CCUS-Integrated Renewable Power Systems Considering Source-Load Bilateral Carbon-Quota Shortfall Risk
summary: Integrating renewable generation with carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) can facilitate power-sector decarbonization but also introduces coupled operational and carbon-quota shortfall risks under renewable uncertainty. Wind-pow
content: Integrating renewable generation with carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) can facilitate power-sector decarbonization but also introduces coupled operational and carbon-quota shortfall risks under renewable uncertainty. Wind-power forecast errors induce generator redispatch and adjustments in carbon capture, thereby reshaping network power and carbon flows. Consequently, the realized carbon responsibilities of generators and loads may exceed the quotas allocated before uncertainty is realized. To address this issue, this paper proposes a distributionally robust low-carbon dispatch framework that explicitly accounts for source-load bilateral carbon-quota shortfall risk. Carbon emission flow is employed to trace residual generator emissions to individual loads, after which carbon responsibility is allocated between the source and load sides. A Sinkhorn-distance-based ambiguity set and distributionally robust chance constraints are adopted to characterize wind-power uncertainty and control carbon-quota shortfall risk, respectively. A tractable solution method is further developed for the resulting optimization problem. Case studies on a modified IEEE 24-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in balancing economic performance, emission reduction, and carbon-risk control.

title: Digital Twin Synchronization Strategies for Real-Time Control of Distributed Production Networks
summary: Digital twin synchronization is central to reliable real-time control in distributed production networks, yet current implementations remain constrained by latency, state inconsistency, heterogeneous data structures, limited scalability, cy
content: Digital twin synchronization is central to reliable real-time control in distributed production networks, yet current implementations remain constrained by latency, state inconsistency, heterogeneous data structures, limited scalability, cybersecurity exposure, and weak industrial validation. This review critically examines the conceptual foundations, architectures, performance metrics, synchronization strategies, control mechanisms, applications, and research gaps associated with physical–virtual alignment across geographically dispersed manufacturing systems. The reviewed strategies comprise time-driven, event-driven, hybrid, edge–cloud coordinated, AI-driven predictive, and blockchain-based synchronization. Their suitability depends on the required balance among update frequency, state accuracy, communication delay, computational burden, data consistency, security, and control criticality. Evidence from manufacturing, robotics, logistics, energy-aware production, and multi-plant coordination shows that effective synchronization can support closed-loop control, adaptive scheduling, predictive maintenance, resource allocation, energy optimisation, and disturbance response. However, no single strategy performs optimally under all operating conditions. Fixed updates may waste resources, event-triggered methods may overlook gradual drift, predictive approaches remain vulnerable to model error, and secure consensus mechanisms may introduce unacceptable delay. The review therefore positions synchronization as a first-class control and systems-engineering problem rather than a secondary data-management function. Future research should prioritise self-adaptive and uncertainty-aware synchronization, deterministic low-latency communication, causal and federated twin architectures, energy-efficient computing, secure governance, standardised metrics, shared benchmarks, and long-term industrial field validation. These advances are required to move digital twins from passive monitoring tools to dependable operational intelligence systems for distributed manufacturing.

title: Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for brain diseases: Processing, membrane-derived functions and translational challenges
summary: Brain diseases such as glioblastoma (GBM), Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and ischemic stroke remain difficult to treat in part because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts and spatially controls the entry of many therapeutic
content: Brain diseases such as glioblastoma (GBM), Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and ischemic stroke remain difficult to treat in part because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts and spatially controls the entry of many therapeutic agents. Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) integrate cell-derived membrane shells with nanoparticle cores made of polymeric, lipid-based, or inorganic materials, offering promising biomimetic platforms for brain drug delivery. This review summarizes CNP fabrication and characterization methods and discusses how molecules associated with specific membrane sources and disease-specific delivery barriers inform platform design. Major membrane sources, including red blood cells, immune cells, stem cells, cancer cells, and platelets, are compared in terms of their relevant surface molecules, recognition mechanisms, potential delivery functions, and limitations. We further discuss how preparation and functionalization affect coating integrity, membrane-protein accessibility, and payload retention, and outline key challenges in reproducible manufacturing, biosafety, and clinical translation. This review provides a framework for evaluating CNP design and for assessing the evidence supporting brain-targeted delivery.

title: Field‐Free Brightening of Dark Excitons in a Two‐Dimensional Perovskite by Organic Spacer Fluorination
summary: ABSTRACT Modifying the organic spacer is a powerful way to tune the excitonic properties of two‐dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (R–P) hybrid halide perovskites. Here, fluorination of the spacer, replacing phenylethylammonium (PEA) with 4
content: ABSTRACT Modifying the organic spacer is a powerful way to tune the excitonic properties of two‐dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (R–P) hybrid halide perovskites. Here, fluorination of the spacer, replacing phenylethylammonium (PEA) with 4‐fluorophenylethylammonium (4‐FPEA), is shown to brighten dark excitons in (4‐FPEA) 2 PbI 4 without an external magnetic field. Below 30 K, (4‐FPEA) 2 PbI 4 exhibits a sharp photoluminescence (PL) signal 7.8 meV below the bright exciton that is absent in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 . Its long lifetime, strong linear polarization, and quadratic magnetic‐field dependence identify this signal as dark‐exciton emission. A magnetic field of up to 0.7 T changes this emission only weakly, whereas it strongly brightens dark excitons in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 . The response is also asymmetric, with its minimum displaced from the zero field. This offset, absent in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 , points to a built‐in mixing of dark and bright states that acts as an internal field. Under two‐photon excitation, which generates excitons deep inside the crystal, the dark‐exciton emission persists. The brightening, therefore, originates in the bulk, unlike the surface‐related brightening reported for other 2D R–P perovskites. These results identify spacer fluorination as a simple chemical route to access spin‐forbidden excitonic states in 2D R–P perovskites.

title: A Resistive Random‐Access Memory With Reduced Current–Voltage Nonlinearity for Reliable Analog Vector–Matrix Multiplication
summary: Suppressing current–voltage ( I – V ) nonlinearity in resistive random‐access memory (RRAM) is essential for minimizing computational errors in hardware neural networks. In this study, we propose a Pt/Al/TiO x /Al 2 O 3 /AlN/Pt RRAM with re
content: Suppressing current–voltage ( I – V ) nonlinearity in resistive random‐access memory (RRAM) is essential for minimizing computational errors in hardware neural networks. In this study, we propose a Pt/Al/TiO x /Al 2 O 3 /AlN/Pt RRAM with reduced nonlinearity in both high‐ and low‐resistance states (HRS and LRS). While the fabricated device maintains reliable multilevel memory characteristics, including pulse endurance over 6 × 10 5 individual programming pulses and multilevel retention for 10 5 s at 120 °C, it exhibits enhanced linearity within the analog read voltage range owing to trap‐assisted tunneling in the HRS and ohmic behavior in the LRS. Extended to the array level, the impact of the proposed device on analog vector–matrix multiplication (VMM) operations was experimentally measured. By incorporating the measurement data into system‐level simulations of fully‐connected network and VGGNet‐11 architectures, the hardware system achieved performance close to the ideal software baseline. Furthermore, comparative simulations based on different conduction mechanisms demonstrate the importance of device I – V linearity for accurate VMM operations. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed device for reliable hardware neural‐network implementation.

title: Reverse Sintering of Supported Metal Catalysts: Mechanisms and Applications
summary: Abstract Metal nanoparticle sintering severely compromises catalyst longevity and atom efficiency in heterogeneous thermocatalysis. To counteract sintering, structural dynamics can be harnessed through surface redispersion and, in suitable
content: Abstract Metal nanoparticle sintering severely compromises catalyst longevity and atom efficiency in heterogeneous thermocatalysis. To counteract sintering, structural dynamics can be harnessed through surface redispersion and, in suitable exsolution systems, oxidative redissolution followed by re-exsolution to recover metal dispersion. This review establishes a comprehensive framework bridging these two phenomena through dynamic structural evolution and chemical potential variations. We systematically analyze their thermodynamic descriptors and kinetic variables, dissecting four redispersion pathways alongside advanced exsolution support architectures. Crucially, we highlight opportunities for cross-fertilization, discussing how redispersion protocols simplify exsolution catalyst regeneration and how exsolution principles inspire support defect engineering to construct stable, semi-embedded crater structures. To unlock these mechanisms, we evaluate how advanced in situ characterization and multiscale theoretical calculations quantitatively describe and predict these dynamic pathways and regulatory factors. Ultimately, scaling these dynamic reconstructions up to realistic industrial conditions coordinates a conceptual pivot toward engineering operational self-healing catalytic systems, unlocking novel frontiers for sintering mitigation.

title: Real-Time Air Quality Detection and Prediction System
source: International Research Journal of Innovation in Science and Technology
summary: Air pollution is a growing environmental concern that affects human health and the environment. This paper presents a low-cost Real-Time Air Quality Detection and Prediction System using an Arduino Uno, MQ135 gas sensor, and DHT11 temperatu
content: Air pollution is a growing environmental concern that affects human health and the environment. This paper presents a low-cost Real-Time Air Quality Detection and Prediction System using an Arduino Uno, MQ135 gas sensor, and DHT11 temperature sensor. The system collects and processes sensor readings to generate indicative PPM and AQI-style values. A multiple linear regression model is used to predict air-quality trends for the next ten time steps. A Flask-based web dashboard displays real-time readings, temperature, air-quality categories, graphs, and predicted values. Tests conducted in indoor, outdoor, and smoke-exposed environments demonstrated the system's response to changing environmental conditions. Approximately 70–75% of predicted readings were reported within the study's accuracy tolerance. The proposed system provides a low-cost approach to local air-quality awareness and short-term prediction.

title: EXPRESS: An Exploratory Analysis of Variation in Payback Periods of Emissions Reduction Projects Using CDP Disclosures
summary: Firms continue to engage in projects to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. Based on their disclosures to CDP, many such projects have relatively short payback periods of 2-3 years. Earlier work by Blanco et al. (2020) found that payback
content: Firms continue to engage in projects to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. Based on their disclosures to CDP, many such projects have relatively short payback periods of 2-3 years. Earlier work by Blanco et al. (2020) found that payback periods appeared stable over time between 2010-2016. The current paper extends that work in several directions: by using a substantially longer time horizon, and exploring several factors that contribute to the variation in payback periods and trends. With the longer horizon of data now available, we find that paybacks are lengthening slowly but significantly over 2010-2024, by an average of about 2 weeks per year, or approximately one half year over our 14-year horizon. Firms with greater liabilities relative to their assets report faster payback, though the effect is only marginally significant. Firms in Europe that are subject to a carbon tax or an emissions trading scheme report shorter paybacks than in the US or elsewhere. Firms that are more consumer-facing report lengthening payback periods, while upstream firms do not. This analysis is exploratory, but prior firm-level research on these effects is mixed and surprisingly limited.

title: Terahertz Carrier Dynamics in Two‐Dimensional Materials Probed by Time‐Domain Spectroscopy
summary: ABSTRACT Precise modulation of carrier dynamics in two‐dimensional (2D) materials is pivotal for the advancement of ultrafast optoelectronics and terahertz (THz) technologies. THz spectroscopy, with its ability to probe photoconductivity on
content: ABSTRACT Precise modulation of carrier dynamics in two‐dimensional (2D) materials is pivotal for the advancement of ultrafast optoelectronics and terahertz (THz) technologies. THz spectroscopy, with its ability to probe photoconductivity on ultrashort timescales without contact effects, serves as a typical tool for this purpose. With particular emphasis on terahertz time‐domain spectroscopy (THz‐TDS) and optical pump–THz probe (OPTP) spectroscopy, this article reviews carrier transport and ultrafast dynamics in representative 2D material systems, including graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), MXenes, and other material classes with extensive THz studies. Special attention is devoted to the regulation of carrier dynamics, interfacial charge‐transfer mechanisms in heterostructures, and their correlations with device performance. Rather than attempting an exhaustive survey of all 2D material families or all THz spectroscopic methodologies, this review adopts a focused perspective on how THz spectroscopy can connect microscopic carrier processes with tunable optoelectronic properties and device functionalities. By synthesizing these insights, this review aims to provide a focused framework for understanding and exploiting the THz optoelectronic properties of 2D materials.

title: IP-C-PDL: A chaos-embedded trust-region interior-point framework for constrained economic dispatch in large-scale power systems
source: An International Journal of Optimization and Control Theories & Applications (IJOCTA)
summary: Constrained economic dispatch (ED)—the classical, single-bus, active-poweronly dispatch problem for thermal generation, not an optimal power flow or unit-commitment problem—in large-scale interconnected power systems such as the Java–Madura
content: Constrained economic dispatch (ED)—the classical, single-bus, active-poweronly dispatch problem for thermal generation, not an optimal power flow or unit-commitment problem—in large-scale interconnected power systems such as the Java–Madura–Bali (Jamali) network is non-convex and ramprate-coupled: deterministic solvers stall at local optima, while stochastic solvers incur unacceptable run-to-run variance. This paper proposes IP-C-PDL (Interior-Point Chaotic Powell’s Dog-Leg), which, within a single interior-point iteration, couples a Powell’s Dog-Leg trust-region step (Cauchy/quasi-Newton selection via accumulated SR1/BFGS curvature) with a stall-adaptive tentmap chaotic perturbation for ergodic basin escape; a multi-start pool, elite archive, and periodic SQP refinement complete the framework using only three user-specified parameters. On twelve CEC benchmark functions (30 runs, 12 methods), IP-C-PDL ranks 1 in 1 of 12 and top-3 in 7 of 12. On six ED scenarios spanning 5-, 16-, and 42-unit systems (50 runs, 10 methods, single-period and 24-hour horizons), it ranks 1 in 4 of 6 (mean rank 2.17/10) with zero constraint violations, yielding USD 22,239.29/day (σ = USD 0.41) on the 42-unit 24-hour case—0.16% better than the second-ranked comparator (t = −48.26, p < 10−42) and 4.67% better than the worst (t = −180.85, p < 10−70)—confirmed by Friedman, ANOVA, and Wilcoxon–Holm–Bonferroni tests. A five-factor sensitivity analysis identifies multi-start pool size as the dominant factor—with a cliff-edge improvement at just two starts—while the framework is insensitive to the remaining four hyperparameters and stabilises by 400 iterations. A policy sensitivity analysis further links dispatch quality to fiscal savings, Biaya Pokok Penyediaan (BPP) subsidy reduction, and avoided carbon emissions in the Indonesian power sector.
