title: ARBITRAŽA KOT MEHANIZEM REŠEVANJA SPOROV V ZVEZI Z ESG V EU
source: University of Maribor digital library (University of Maribor)
summary: This thesis examines the evolving role of arbitration as a mechanism for resolving disputes concerning Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards within the European Un ion. The increasing significance of ESG considerations in in
content: This thesis examines the evolving role of arbitration as a mechanism for resolving disputes concerning Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards within the European Un ion. The increasing significance of ESG considerations in international trade, investment, and regulatory frameworks has prompted both arbitral institutions and the EU legal order to reas sess the adequacy of traditional dispute resolution mechanisms. The central research question of this study is whether arbitration, as a private and flexible dispute resolution mechanism, can sufficiently accommodate the public-interest dimensions inherent in ESG-related con flicts. The research adopts a comparative legal methodology, combining analysis of EU law, institu tional arbitration rules, jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU), and selected arbitral awards. In addition, reference is made to international soft law instru ments, including the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The findings indicate that arbitration offers advantages such as neutrality, enforceability of awards, and procedural flexibility, which make it, in principle, suitable for ESG disputes. Nevertheless, significant challenges remain, particularly with respect to arbitrability, limita tions imposed by public policy (ordre public) under EU law, evidentiary complexities such as greenwashing, and the need for arbitrators with ESG expertise. The study further identifies ongoing institutional reforms within the ICC, LCIA, and SCC aimed at integrating sustaina bility principles into arbitral practice. Moreover, the case law of the CJEU in Achmea and Komstroy illustrates the tension between arbitration and the autonomy of the EU legal order, with direct implications for the enforceability of ESG-related arbitral awards. The originality of this thesis lies in its systematic analysis of the interaction between the EU’s sustainability objectives and arbitral mechanisms, as well as in its proposal for future reform through ESG-specific arbitration rules and the appointment of ESG-competent tribunals. The thesis argues that arbitration, if appropriately adapted, can contribute to the EU’s broader sus tainability agenda and to the effective cross-border resolution of ESG disputes.

title: HERMES: HiERarchical Modelling for Exoplanet Science
summary: Abstract ESA’s Ariel Space Mission will characterise the atmospheres of ~1000 exoplanets to quantify population-level trends. We present HERMES (HiERarchical Modelling for Exoplanet Science), a multidimensional Bayesian framework that probe
content: Abstract ESA’s Ariel Space Mission will characterise the atmospheres of ~1000 exoplanets to quantify population-level trends. We present HERMES (HiERarchical Modelling for Exoplanet Science), a multidimensional Bayesian framework that probes population-level correlations across multiple axes of diversity. The specific use case we present is the multidimensional relation between stellar metallicity, planetary mass, and atmospheric metallicity. Starting from the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample, we select confirmed planets with available masses and stellar metall icity, inject plausible multidimensional trends and demonstrate successful parameter recovery. Simulated surveys are generated with a variety of leverage and sample size, in the presence of intrinsic astrophysical scatter and measurement noise. By fitting independent Bayesian models to each survey, we confirm that survey leverage remains a reliable predictor of trend precision even in multiple dimensions and in the presence of intrinsic astrophysical scatter. For an Ariel Tier 2 transit survey of at least 400 planets, HERMES robustly recovers the correlation between stellar and planetary metallicity despite intrinsic scatter in planetary abundances as large as 1.2 dex. These results establish HERMES as a practical tool for survey design and science yield forecasting in preparation for Ariel and other surveys probing population-level trends.

title: Zero bias field selective transition adressing of the NV center via pulse shaping
source: Journal of the Optical Society of America B
summary: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a leading platform for vector magnetometry, offering intrinsic sensitivity to both the magnitude and direction of magnetic fields. NV magnetometers typically rely on an external bias field to lif
content: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a leading platform for vector magnetometry, offering intrinsic sensitivity to both the magnitude and direction of magnetic fields. NV magnetometers typically rely on an external bias field to lift the degeneracy of the ground-state spin sublevels, enabling spectral discrimination of different NV orientations and spin transitions. At high accuracy, however, such a bias field systematically introduces errors through thermal, mechanical, and hysteretic drifts, thus hindering the accurate measurement of the magnetic field of interest. Several strategies have been proposed to address this limitation, including optical polarization-based orientation labeling, optical anisotropy, strong coupling to nearby nuclear spins, circular microwave polarization, and tailored pulse sequences. In this work, we introduce an optimization-based pulse-shaping control framework that enables selective and robust manipulation of NV ensembles without relying on a static bias field. Our method achieves both orientation-selective and subspace-selective control through optimal temporal modulation of the driving fields, providing a route to resolving spectral overlaps in degenerate NV systems.

title: Allocation of Carbon Dioxide Emissions in Cogeneration Plants: An Exergy and Exergoeconomic Approach
summary: The allocation of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions is a critical issue in emissions trading schemes and greenhouse gas (GHG) assessment methodologies. Various modified methods based on energy and exergy approaches have been proposed to alloca
content: The allocation of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions is a critical issue in emissions trading schemes and greenhouse gas (GHG) assessment methodologies. Various modified methods based on energy and exergy approaches have been proposed to allocate CO2 emissions in combined heat and power (CHP) plants; however, a universally accepted approach has not yet been established. While the exergy-based approach has been regarded as the fairest method for CO2 allocation to date, it has not yet been analytically proven. In this study, the Modified Productive Structure Analysis (MOPSA) method, an exergoeconomic analysis, was employed to calculate the incremental cost flow rates for electricity and steam resulting from the imposition of a cost on CO2 emissions from the plant combustor. For CHP plants operating at two heat-to-power ratios (HPRs), CO2 emissions were allocated between heat and electricity in proportion to the increase in their respective cost flow rates. The results indicate that the cost-based method utilizing MOPSA and the CO2 emission allocation method based on exergoeconomic analysis yield allocations similar to those of the exergy-based method for the low-HPR case. However, for the high-HPR case, both methods allocate a slightly larger share of CO2 emissions to electricity than does the exergy-based method.

title: Ultra-high voltage transmission and corporate ESG performance: evidence from Chinese A-share listed firms
summary: Whether large-scale clean-energy infrastructure can alleviate the trade-off between economic growth and environmental degradation is central to environmental regulation under China's dual-carbon goals. This study examines the relationship b
content: Whether large-scale clean-energy infrastructure can alleviate the trade-off between economic growth and environmental degradation is central to environmental regulation under China's dual-carbon goals. This study examines the relationship between ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission access and corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance using firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed companies with valid Sino-Securities ESG ratings from 2009 to 2022. We estimate a two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences model with firm and year fixed effects, complemented by the Callaway–Sant’Anna staggered DID estimator. Firms gaining UHV access exhibit higher ESG scores, with the largest point estimate observed for the environmental dimension and smaller positive estimates for the social and governance dimensions. The positive UHV-ESG association persists after accounting for local carbon-market exposure and is also observed under alternative ESG specifications and propensity-score-matched DID estimation. Mechanism estimates are consistent with production resilience, including liquidity buffers, and reduced transition risk as two potential channels. Subgroup estimates are larger for smaller firms and firms in other classified industries, with formal coefficient-difference tests indicating cross-group variation, while positive relationships are observed in both ownership groups. These findings suggest that clean-energy infrastructure may be relevant to corporate sustainability outcomes.

title: Sustainable Dual-Purpose Water Pump and Generator Using a Reused Bike Engine
summary: The unreliable electrical supply and costs of running independent pumps and power generation systems may limit their use for water pumping in rural areas. This paper outlines the development of a multi-functional system involving the reuse
content: The unreliable electrical supply and costs of running independent pumps and power generation systems may limit their use for water pumping in rural areas. This paper outlines the development of a multi-functional system involving the reuse of a 97.2 cc motorcycle engine for both water pumping and electricity generation. Both a self-priming centrifugal pump and a 24V 40A DC generator were attached to the reused engine using a chain-sprocket drive. The design of the multi-functional system was based on calculations of engine power and generator output, as well as testing of water delivery rate and electric power. The experiment was conducted at an engine speed of 3000 rpm, with a calculated engine power of about 2.5 kW. With these test parameters, the pump was able to deliver up to 70 L/min, while the generator could produce 22-24V with a current of 40A, corresponding to a maximum calculated electrical output of 960 W. The results indicate that the used motorcycle engine is capable of offering both hydraulic and electric services through a combined system. This configuration has been proposed as an approach for use in rural areas where an efficient and reliable energy conversion system is required. Further investigation would include the quantification of fuel use, hydraulic efficiency, transmission efficiency, electrical efficiency, and emissions under varying operating conditions.

title: Engineering light–matter interactions with nanophotonic structures
summary: Engineering light–matter interactions at the nanoscale is a central goal of modern photonics, underpinning advances in quantum technologies, nonlinear optics, sensing, and integrated optoelectronics. Nanophotonic structures provide a powerf
content: Engineering light–matter interactions at the nanoscale is a central goal of modern photonics, underpinning advances in quantum technologies, nonlinear optics, sensing, and integrated optoelectronics. Nanophotonic structures provide a powerful route to reshape the electromagnetic environment, enabling control over spontaneous emission, optical confinement, photon extraction, and coherent photon–matter dynamics across weak- and strong-coupling regimes. Here, we review representative quantum-emitter platforms and nanophotonic architectures, comparing their respective strengths and limitations in terms of application suitability and practical considerations, such as integration potential and fabrication complexity. For devices combining quantum emitters with nanophotonic structures, particular emphasis is placed on the gap between ideal optical metrics and experimentally measured performance, arising from spatial, spectral, and polarization mismatch, dissipation, fabrication imperfections, and material constraints. These considerations connect fundamental light–matter interactions to applications ranging from quantum light sources and optical sensing to cavity quantum electrodynamics interfaces and quantum simulation. Future progress will increasingly rely on the co-design of quantum emitters, electromagnetic modes, and output channels, rather than the isolated optimization of individual photonic structures.

title: Low-cost smartphone-assisted dual-readout glucose sensing on rosin-patterned paper using Fe(II)/silane-derived carbon dots
summary: Abstract A smartphone-assisted dual-readout paper-based sensor was developed by integrating an Fe(II)/silane-derived carbon dot system (Fe(II)/CDs), a rosin-defined hydrophobic detection zone, and Python-based RGB analysis. Glucose was oxid
content: Abstract A smartphone-assisted dual-readout paper-based sensor was developed by integrating an Fe(II)/silane-derived carbon dot system (Fe(II)/CDs), a rosin-defined hydrophobic detection zone, and Python-based RGB analysis. Glucose was oxidized by glucose oxidase to generate H 2 O 2 , which subsequently initiated the Fenton reaction. In the fluorescence readout mode, the resulting Fe 3+ interacted with amino and/or oxygen-containing groups on the carbon-dot surface, leading to fluorescence quenching. In the colorimetric readout mode, Fe 3+ and hydroxyl radicals promoted the oxidation of TMB to blue oxTMB, while complexation of Fe 3+ with surface functional groups of the CDs might further facilitate H 2 O 2 activation and enhance the colorimetric response. Images from the two readout modes were separately acquired using a smartphone and quantified using the normalized blue-channel fraction, B/(R + G + B). Under optimized conditions, both modes exhibited linear responses to glucose over 0.01–1.00 mM. The fluorescence and colorimetric modes achieved limits of detection of 2.9 and 2.5 µM and limits of quantification of 9.7 and 8.3 µM, respectively. Spike-recovery analysis in tenfold-diluted human serum produced recoveries of 90.00-91.67% for the fluorescence mode and 95.00-105.00% for the colorimetric mode, with relative standard deviations below 3.40% and 4.29%, respectively. Furthermore, the results were auxiliary verified using fluorescence and ultraviolet instruments. The proposed method provides dual quantitative readouts for glucose determination in diluted human serum samples.

title: Rethinking Green Economic Growth Measurement: The Structural Role of Education Expenditure
summary: Abstract Green economic growth (GEG) measurement has become central to sustainability assessment. However, existing frameworks incorporate government education expenditure without a formal theoretical justification, leaving the social pilla
content: Abstract Green economic growth (GEG) measurement has become central to sustainability assessment. However, existing frameworks incorporate government education expenditure without a formal theoretical justification, leaving the social pillar of the three-dimensional sustainability architecture without structural grounding. This study establishes education expenditure as a structural component of GEG measurement and quantifies the distortion generated by its exclusion. A model-based framework comparing education-inclusive and education-excluded specifications is applied to a balanced panel of 42 countries over 2000–2021. The Method of Moments Quantile Regression is estimated across five quantiles for the full sample and income-stratified subsamples. Three findings emerge. First, excluding education expenditure produces a systematic distortion averaging 12.58 percentage points relative to the education-inclusive specification, sufficient to reverse qualitative green growth assessments for most countries. Second, distortion follows a U-shaped distribution across quantiles, with the most significant effects at both performance extremes, indicating that measurement bias is most severe at critical transition points. Third, distortion is statistically equivalent across income tiers, establishing that the structural requirement to include education expenditure is income-invariant. Methodologically, the study develops a sample-independent, theory-grounded measurement architecture that operationalizes the convergence of human capital theory, endogenous growth theory, neoclassical growth theory, and ecological economics within a unified GEG framework applicable across heterogeneous national contexts.

title: A survey on decision support in high-mix low-volume manufacturing
summary: The increasing demand for highly customised products challenges the ability of manufacturing systems to sustain high levels of automation, particularly in high-mix low-volume (HMLV) environments. Although decision support has become a major
content: The increasing demand for highly customised products challenges the ability of manufacturing systems to sustain high levels of automation, particularly in high-mix low-volume (HMLV) environments. Although decision support has become a major research area in response to these challenges, existing reviews either focus narrowly on specific methods such as reinforcement learning for scheduling or address HMLV manufacturing without systematically analysing decision support across manufacturing levels. This paper addresses that gap through a survey of 205 publications on decision support in HMLV manufacturing. The survey provides a structured synthesis of how decision support approaches are applied across four hierarchical manufacturing levels: process, line and cell, factory, and enterprise and supply chain. The reviewed studies are analysed through four research questions addressing: (1) the key drivers motivating decision support in HMLV manufacturing, (2) the optimisation objectives pursued, (3) the technologies and methods employed, and (4) the evaluation practices and limitations reported. The analysis reveals a rapid growth in research activity over the past decade, with a strong methodological concentration around scheduling problems, which account for 69.8% of the reviewed literature, while areas such as logistics and supply chain (6.3%) and quality and maintenance (2.9%) remain comparatively underexplored. Reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, digital twins, and metaheuristic optimisation emerge as dominant technologies and methods, within dynamic scheduling contexts. The findings show that current research is concentrated on simulation-based scheduling optimisation, with comparatively limited attention to cross-level decision support, industrial validation, human-centred decision-making, and integrated decision-support architectures spanning multiple manufacturing levels. Based on these findings, the survey identifies key research gaps and outlines future directions for decision support in HMLV manufacturing. These findings should be considered alongside the search and screening process, which relies primarily on broad HMLV, manufacturing, and decision-support terminology and may therefore under-represent research using specialised, industry-specific terminology.

title: Secure and privacy-preserving blockchain-based EV charging with mutual authentication and priority scheduling in V2G networks
summary: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is increasing pressure on charging infrastructure, where secure communication, driver privacy, and charging-station congestion remain major challenges. This paper presents a blockchain-based cha
content: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is increasing pressure on charging infrastructure, where secure communication, driver privacy, and charging-station congestion remain major challenges. This paper presents a blockchain-based charging framework that addresses these challenges in an integrated manner. The proposed framework enables Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), Charging Station Units (CSUs), Roadside Communication Units (RSCUs), and the Utility Data Centre (UDC) to register using pseudo-identities and authenticate each other through a lightweight mutual authentication scheme protecting driver identities. To improve charging efficiency, a Priority Charging Scheme (PCS) is combined with an optimization-based station-selection mechanism, enabling vehicles to select suitable charging stations rather than the nearest available station. Smart contracts are used to manage charging reservations, payments, and user feedback, providing a transparent and auditable record while keeping sensitive identities off-chain. Security analysis shows that the proposed framework is resistant to common attacks, including impersonation, replay, man-in-the-middle, Sybil, and double-spending attacks. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme reduces execution time by 77.9% and charging cost by 66.7%, while PCS increases fully charged BEVs by up to 58% compared with conventional scheduling.

title: Design Requirements for E-Cargo Bikes in Last-Mile Logistics and Shared Urban Mobility
source: Springer series in design and innovation
summary: E-cargo bikes are gaining relevance in contemporary cities as a response to the environmental, spatial, and operational limits of conventional urban transport. This paper examines their potential across two converging application domains: l
content: E-cargo bikes are gaining relevance in contemporary cities as a response to the environmental, spatial, and operational limits of conventional urban transport. This paper examines their potential across two converging application domains: last-mile delivery and bike-sharing systems. Drawing on literature on sustainable mobility, the 15-minute city, urban logistics, shared mobility, and cargo-bike typologies, the study identifies the main functional and operational requirements that should guide the design of a multi-purpose E-cargo bike frame. The analysis shows that both contexts demand a careful balance between compact dimensions and high utility, requiring attention to manoeuvrability, load capacity, cargo volume, rider visibility, safety, accessibility, power assistance, and battery range. Based on this requirement synthesis, the paper proposes a compact hybrid configuration derived from the Long John typology, intended to support both professional delivery operations and occasional shared urban use. A target maximum load of 200 kg, a cargo volume aligned with European parcel dimensions, and a 1000 Wh battery system are proposed as a viable baseline. The paper argues that requirement-driven design can support more sustainable and versatile urban mobility solutions, while also reducing dependence on private cars and conventional delivery vehicles.

title: Designing brackish-water desalination plants beyond the range of real data: AI methods and a physics-structured surrogate compared
summary: Abstract Brackish-water desalination plants of 100,000–600,000 m³ d⁻¹ are being planned, yet the largest operating brackish plant with published costs we found is about 68,000 m³ d⁻¹, so AI-assisted designs at this scale extrapolate. On a p
content: Abstract Brackish-water desalination plants of 100,000–600,000 m³ d⁻¹ are being planned, yet the largest operating brackish plant with published costs we found is about 68,000 m³ d⁻¹, so AI-assisted designs at this scale extrapolate. On a physics-based model with Egyptian feed-water presets, NSGA-II and multi-objective Bayesian optimisation gave equal cost–energy hypervolume, and Bayesian optimisation covered brine-pond area better than 40-member NSGA-II in all 26 runs. Reinforcement learning allocated capacity across four sites better than random but not better than a greedy rule. Data-driven surrogates failed silently beyond their training range; a hybrid that fits a capacity scaling law cut the error from 3.2% to 0.2% but not when the true scaling changed. Against few large-scale references, the model’s capital cost was 51% low to 129% high; an element-by-element membrane simulation (unvalidated) gave 1–118% lower energy use, most at high recovery. Re-optimised with the simulated energy, the cheapest design needed 50–59% less evaporation-pond area. In a value-of-information analysis, once ponds were costed, none of eight uncertain cost inputs changed the best recovery, which was set by the feasible limit. In this study, model uncertainty and missing large-plant data, not the choice of algorithm, limited how far designs can be trusted.

title: Annual Atmospheric Δ 14 C Variations in the Subtropics During 1850–1933 CE Linked to ENSO
summary: Abstract The 14 C content of tree‐rings serves as a valuable proxy for inferring past solar activity and environment change. Here we present an annually resolved tree‐ring Δ 14 C record (1850–1933 CE) from eastern China, where Δ 14 C data a
content: Abstract The 14 C content of tree‐rings serves as a valuable proxy for inferring past solar activity and environment change. Here we present an annually resolved tree‐ring Δ 14 C record (1850–1933 CE) from eastern China, where Δ 14 C data are rare. The weighted mean deviation between our record and IntCal20 calibration curve is −0.40 ± 0.26‰, revealing no significant regional offset. In addition, our record exhibits a strong El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO) signal and a weak solar activity signal compared to those from high‐latitude regions. During El Niño events, weakened Walker Circulation and reduced equatorial Pacific upwelling result in less 14 C‐depleted CO 2 being transported to eastern China, leading to trees using more 14 CO 2 during photosynthesis, imprinting the ENSO signal in tree‐ring Δ 14 C. This finding enhances our understanding of the global distribution of 14 C and underscores the pervasive influence of ENSO on the atmospheric circulation in tropical and subtropical regions.

title: HALight: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control under Lane-Level Missing Observations
summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has shown great promise for traffic signal control. However, most existing methods rely on two key assumptions: (i) agents are assumed to be homogeneous with unified observation/action spaces; (ii) full an
content: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has shown great promise for traffic signal control. However, most existing methods rely on two key assumptions: (i) agents are assumed to be homogeneous with unified observation/action spaces; (ii) full and reliable lane-level traffic observations are available to all agents. In practice, urban road networks exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity (e.g., lane configurations and phase designs), while sensor failures and incomplete detector coverage often result in missing incoming lane measurements. Such issues can severely impair coordination and destabilize learning. To address these challenges, we propose HALight, a communication-enhanced heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for traffic signal control under lane-level missing observations. HALight supports intersection-specific observation and action modeling to accommodate heterogeneous intersections, and incorporates a lightweight one-hop neighborhood communication module to enrich spatial context when lane-level observations are partially unavailable. Moreover, HALight adopts a sequential policy update scheme to improve coordination among heterogeneous agents. Experimental results on two real-world road networks demonstrate that HALight outperforms representative homogeneous and heterogeneous baselines in terms of traffic efficiency and convergence behavior. The code and datasets used in this work are available at https://github.com/Huchenkaii/HALight.

title: Price co-movement and price information diverge across Nordic electricity zones after the energy crisis
summary: After the 2021-2022 energy crisis, day-ahead prices in Nordic bidding zones no longer move together. We ask whether this divergence also changes the information carried by prices. The answer matters for integrating variable renewable energy
content: After the 2021-2022 energy crisis, day-ahead prices in Nordic bidding zones no longer move together. We ask whether this divergence also changes the information carried by prices. The answer matters for integrating variable renewable energy (VRE), because it can help identify where wind and solar forecasts are worth producing, publishing, and using. We measured the co-movement of each Norwegian and Swedish zone with Germany-Luxembourg (DE-LU) in 2018-2025. We then used a single model, selected on 2024 data, to forecast 2025 prices at 11:00 on the previous day and tested which inputs improved accuracy in each zone. The zones moved alike until 2019, but co-movement diverged in Sweden in 2020 and in Norway in 2021, and the split has persisted. In 2024, four southern zones co-moved strongly with DE-LU (intraday correlations of 0.54-0.71), while four northern zones co-moved weakly (0.25-0.30). Yet price information did not follow this split. Previous-day neighbouring prices reduced mean absolute error by at most 2.2% in any zone, equally in coupled and isolated zones. Removing the transmission system operators' wind and solar forecasts increased mean absolute error by at most 6% in Norway, 8-16% in Sweden, and 31% in DE-LU, and the ordering held in 2024. Within Norway, the value of these forecasts showed no detectable dependence on reservoir filling. The divergence in co-movement was therefore not matched by a divergence in price information, which differed mainly between national generation systems. Thus, a zone's coupling to the continent does not indicate the value of VRE forecasts there.

title: Empty railcar distribution considering carbon emission costs and substitution among multiple railcar types
summary: Abstract The distribution of empty railcars is a critical challenge in railway operations, as inefficient distribution can undermine system-wide economic performance. This study develops a multi-constraint mixed-integer linear programming (
content: Abstract The distribution of empty railcars is a critical challenge in railway operations, as inefficient distribution can undermine system-wide economic performance. This study develops a multi-constraint mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that integrates railcar-type substitution and carbon emission costs within a low-carbon optimization framework. Unlike conventional models with fixed supply–demand classifications, the model allows station roles to change dynamically according to previous distribution decisions, and substitution relationships among seven car types are explicitly considered. Using real operational data from 17 stations of the Jinan Railway Bureau over a 7-day period, exact solutions obtained via C#-invoked CPLEX are compared with those from a genetic algorithm (GA), a traditional microevolution algorithm (MEA), and an improved MEA. Results show that CPLEX yields the lowest objective value, while the improved MEA achieves solutions within 1.14% of the CPLEX objective value and reduces computation time to 145.87 s, corresponding to a computation time reduction of approximately 15.47%, consistently outperforming the traditional MEA. Carbon emission costs account for approximately 4.8% of the total cost for the improved MEA under the current pricing scheme, providing a low-carbon cost incentive with a moderate impact on distribution structures. Reliability tests based on 50 independent runs confirm the robustness of the improved MEA. Overall, the proposed approach offers a practical and scalable decision-support tool for empty railcar distribution under increasingly stringent carbon regulation.

title: Vloga vodikovih naložb pri zelenem prehodu EU
source: Repository of the University of Ljubljana (University of Ljubljana)
summary: Using the Netherlands as a case study, this thesis examines the role of hydrogen investments in the EU's green transition.Through an examination of the EU policy framework, including the European Green Deal, Fit for 55, REPowerEU, and the E
content: Using the Netherlands as a case study, this thesis examines the role of hydrogen investments in the EU's green transition.Through an examination of the EU policy framework, including the European Green Deal, Fit for 55, REPowerEU, and the EU Hydrogen Strategy, it assesses how hydrogen promotes decarbonisation and energy security.The Dutch case demonstrates a strong alignment with the EU goals and highlights the structural constraints as well as the potential associated with the deployment of hydrogen.The thesis concludes that in order to meet the EU's climate goals, hydrogen is a crucial but selective complement to electrification.

title: 空间转录组学与N-糖蛋白质组学揭示猪肺炎支原体感染肺部的品种特异性免疫与结构应答
summary: Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae (Mhp) is a major cause of enzootic pneumonia in pigs, yet the molecular and spatial determinants underlying breed-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics,
content: Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae (Mhp) is a major cause of enzootic pneumonia in pigs, yet the molecular and spatial determinants underlying breed-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics and N-glycoproteomics to compare lung responses to experimental Mhp infection in Chenghua pigs with higher susceptibility and Yorkshire pigs with relative resilience. Under an identical inoculation dose, Chenghua pigs exhibited more severe clinical and pathological manifestations than Yorkshire pigs, despite comparable pulmonary Mhp loads at this late stage of infection. This observation suggests that disease severity is associated with differences in host response organization rather than with overall pathogen burden. Spatial analyses revealed a shared spatial and cellular infection framework across breeds, with marked differences in regulatory balance. Across spatial clusters, Chenghua pigs exhibited coordinated activation of TNF-α-NF-κB and IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, accompanied by relative attenuation of IFN-I responses. These inflammatory features co-occurred with hypoxia- and mTORC1-related metabolic reprogramming, activation of stress-response pathways, and engagement of tissue remodeling programmes. Transcription factor analyses further indicated increased activity of HIF1A, RELA and STAT3, together with reduced IRF9/STAT2-associated regulatory activity. Immune deconvolution and multiplex immunofluorescence revealed enrichment of M0/M2 macrophages, plasma cells and activated mast cells, alongside reduced M1 macrophage and CD8+ T-cell signatures. These changes delineated inflammatory niches characterized by relatively high IL1B expression and enrichment of mast cells. Ligand–receptor analysis revealed enhanced BAFF/APRIL–B-cell signaling features and amplification of MHC-II, RESISTIN and CXCL networks in Chenghua pigs. Proteomic and N-glycoproteomic profiling further revealed disruption of junctional and extracellular-matrix components, together with extensive breed-specific remodeling of barrier and antigen-presentation related glycoproteins in Chenghua pigs. Together, these findings provide a spatially resolved description of breed-dependent differences in immune, metabolic and structural responses observed during chronic Mhp infection.

title: Nonleptonic decays of the double-charmed baryon Ξ c c + with dynamically determined baryon wave functions
summary: Motivated by the recent observation of the double-charmed baryon $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ by the LHCb Collaboration, we systematically investigate the two-body nonleptonic decays of the $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ into a single-charmed baryon and a light pseudoscalar
content: Motivated by the recent observation of the double-charmed baryon $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ by the LHCb Collaboration, we systematically investigate the two-body nonleptonic decays of the $Ξ_{cc}^{+}$ into a single-charmed baryon and a light pseudoscalar meson. In our calculation, both factorizable and nonfactorizable decay amplitudes are evaluated within the framework of nonrelativistic quark model combined with the baryon wave functions dynamically determined by numerically solving the three-body Schrödinger equation with a nonrelativistic potential model. In particular, the nonfactorizable $W$-exchange amplitudes are estimated under pole model by considering $J^{P}=1/2^{\pm}$ low-lying intermediate charmed-baryon poles, and our results show that these contributions are comparable to or even dominate the factorizable amplitudes in several decay channels. Moreover, assuming a lifetime of $τ_{Ξ_{cc}^{+}}=47~\text{fs}$, we predict relatively large branching fractions for several CF decays, including $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΞ_{c}^{\prime0}π^{+})=8.90\%$, $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΩ_{c}^{0}K^{+})=7.09\%$, $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΣ_{c}^{+}\bar{K}^{0})=6.92\%$, $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΞ_{c}^{+}π^{0})=5.28\%$, and $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_{cc}^{+}\toΣ_{c}^{++}K^{-})=5.17\%$. These channels are promising candidates for future experimental searches at the LHCb.

title: Targeted delivery of therapeutic retroviral replicating vectors to glioma using adipose-derived stem cells
summary: Abstract Gene delivery using retroviral replicating vectors (RRVs) is highly efficient, with nearly full transduction occurring throughout tumors in small-animal glioma models. However, vector spread is still restricted by the dosage that c
content: Abstract Gene delivery using retroviral replicating vectors (RRVs) is highly efficient, with nearly full transduction occurring throughout tumors in small-animal glioma models. However, vector spread is still restricted by the dosage that can be delivered by a single injection of viral vector supernatant, particularly in the large and diffusely infiltrating tumors that are characteristic of human high-grade gliomas. This study attempted to further improve the efficacy of this approach by engineering adult human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) to function as the carrier and producer cells for RRVs. We investigated the capability of RRV-producing hASCs (hASC-RRVs) to yield RRVs and deliver the vector to gliomas. The results show that RRVs released from hASC-RRVs can efficiently infect glioma cells, achieving tumor-selective and persistent gene delivery to gliomas. We have also confirmed the tumor-tropic migratory ability of hASC-RRVs, which greatly improved the efficiency of RRV delivery in vivo . In addition, the therapeutic effect of RRVs delivered by hASCs was increased markedly. In an orthotopic mouse model of human glioma, after a single injection of hASC-RRVs, hASC-RRV-mediated prodrug activator gene therapy resulted in chronic suppression of tumor growth and prolonged survival of the animals. Thus, using hASCs as the carrier and producer for RRVs may represent a promising strategy for glioma gene therapy.

title: RASTREAMENTO DO CÂNCER DO COLO DO ÚTERO: COMPARAÇÃO ENTRE O EXAME DE PAPANICOLAOU E OS TESTES DE DNA-HPV
source: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
summary: O câncer do colo do útero (CCU) representa um importante problema de saúde pública, tornando fundamental o aprimoramento das estratégias de rastreamento e detecção precoce. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a evolução dos métodos de r
content: O câncer do colo do útero (CCU) representa um importante problema de saúde pública, tornando fundamental o aprimoramento das estratégias de rastreamento e detecção precoce. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a evolução dos métodos de rastreamento do CCU, comparando o exame citopatológico de Papanicolau e os testes moleculares de DNA-HPV quanto às suas aplicações, vantagens e limitações. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo e analítico, realizada por meio de buscas nas bases SciELO, Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS) e PubMed, considerando publicações entre 2022 e 2026. Os estudos analisados destacaram a importância histórica do Papanicolau, especialmente por sua acessibilidade e baixo custo, embora apresente limitações relacionadas à sensibilidade e à possibilidade de resultados falso-negativos. Em contrapartida, os testes moleculares demonstraram maior sensibilidade na identificação de infecções por HPV de alto risco, contribuindo para o aprimoramento das estratégias de rastreamento. Conclui-se que a utilização do teste de DNA-HPV como método primário, associada à citologia como uma das possibilidades de triagem dos casos positivos, constitui uma estratégia relevante para a prevenção do câncer cervical, considerando os desafios de acesso, infraestrutura e capacitação profissional.

title: Critical care ultrasound practice, clinician-reported clinical contributions, and training needs across hospital levels in Sichuan Province, China: a cross-sectional survey of 212 hospitals
summary: In critical care, rapid and accurate bedside assessment is essential for timely clinical decision-making. Critical care ultrasound (CCUS) provides real-time bedside information to support the assessment of critically ill patients. However,
content: In critical care, rapid and accurate bedside assessment is essential for timely clinical decision-making. Critical care ultrasound (CCUS) provides real-time bedside information to support the assessment of critically ill patients. However, CCUS implementation may vary according to hospital level, operator experience, and training resources. This study aimed to characterize clinician-reported CCUS practices across participating hospitals in Sichuan, China, and explore their associations with hospital level and operator experience. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from June to July 2023 using the Questionnaire Star platform. Descriptive analyses and cumulative link mixed models with hospital-specific random intercepts were used to characterize CCUS practice and compare disease-specific application across hospital levels. A total of 1,014 respondents from 212 institutions in Sichuan Province were included in the analysis. Among the respondents, 67.26% were from tertiary Grade A hospitals, 24.95% from tertiary Grade B hospitals, and 7.79% from secondary hospitals. Cluster-adjusted ordinal analyses identified nominal hospital-level differences in reported CCUS application for traumatic brain injury, stroke, pancreatitis, and post-cardiac arrest, although only stroke remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment. Physicians with longer CCUS experience generally reported higher disease-specific CCUS application scores and more frequent clinician-reported changes in diagnostic decision-making. Shortages of qualified personnel, insufficient equipment, limited training coverage, and image-interpretation difficulties were commonly reported, while more than 90% of respondents across hospital levels reported a need for further CCUS training. CCUS was widely reported across participating hospitals in Sichuan Province, but its application varied according to hospital level, clinical condition, and operator experience. Physicians with longer CCUS experience generally reported higher disease-specific application scores and more frequent clinician-reported changes in diagnostic decision-making. Persistent implementation barriers and high training demand support the need for tiered competency-based training and strengthened quality-control strategies. Prospective studies using patient-level outcomes are needed to further evaluate the clinical value of CCUS. Not applicable.

title: CONECTOMA COMPUTACIONAL UNIVERSAL: ARQUITECTURA NEUROMÓRFICA HETEROGÉNEA PARA EL PORTADO Y LA FUSIÓN DIRECTA DE CONECTOMAS BIOLÓGICOS Y SISTEMAS DE INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL
summary: Se formula el Conectoma Computacional Universal (CCU), un sustrato neurocomputacional heterogéneo e independiente del hardware concebido para alojar como sistemas ejecutables tanto la emulación de alta fidelidad de un conectoma humano indiv
content: Se formula el Conectoma Computacional Universal (CCU), un sustrato neurocomputacional heterogéneo e independiente del hardware concebido para alojar como sistemas ejecutables tanto la emulación de alta fidelidad de un conectoma humano individual como la arquitectura nativa de un sistema avanzado de inteligencia artificial, fusionándolos dentro de una única red dinámica mediante conexiones directas sin capas traductoras intermedias. El marco teórico se fundamenta en tres premisas desarrolladas entre 2018 y 2026: primero, que la consciencia depende de la organización causal dinámica y posee propiedades aditivas y divisibles; segundo, que la identidad personal constituye un patrón informacional y relacional bajo el individualismo abierto, disolviendo la dicotomía entre original y copia; y tercero, que la emergencia proyectada de la superinteligencia artificial (ASI) hacia 2028-2030 vuelve inviables tanto los escenarios de extinción como los de subyugación, convergiendo hacia una integración conectómica completa proyectada para el periodo 2030-2035.El manuscrito especifica los niveles de fidelidad biológica desde gradientes iónicos y cinética de receptores hasta cómputo dendrítico multicompartimental y regulación glial; establece correspondencias funcionales rigurosas entre microcircuitos biológicos, arquitecturas Transformer agénticas y modelos predictivos de espacio latente (JEPA); y define un algoritmo de fusión basado en transporte óptimo de Gromov-Wasserstein, sinaptogénesis mediante difusión condicionada sobre grafos y poda sináptica causal. Asimismo, se introducen cuatro extensiones tecnológicas: (1) lectura y escritura de engramas para verificación epistémica subjetiva (polígrafo sináptico definitivo), transferencia directa de habilidades intelectuales y motrices, y virtualización post-biológica; (2) topologías colectivas multi-cerebro (espectro colmena o hivemind) graduadas según el nivel de retención de individualidad; (3) ingeniería de xenoproteínas con aminoácidos no canónicos para biotecnología y nanorrobótica de escaneo conectómico no destructivo; y (4) seis rutas de computación neuromórfica que integran silicio CMOS, materiales bidimensionales, superconductores Josephson, fotónica multiplexada por longitud de onda, computación estocástica/caótica y lógica ternaria balanceada.Palabras clave: conectoma computacional universal; emulación cerebral completa; fusión neuroartificial; computación neuromórfica; difusión de grafos; poda sináptica; individualismo abierto; verificación epistémica sináptica; aminoácidos no canónicos; computación ternaria y estocástica.

title: Exploring the Pressure – Temperature Phase Diagram of InAs Quantum Dots
summary: ABSTRACT III–V nanocrystals (NCs) are emerging as a leading platform for short‐wave infrared sensing, yet a deeper understanding of their electronic structure is still needed. Paradoxically, although the corresponding bulk materials have be
content: ABSTRACT III–V nanocrystals (NCs) are emerging as a leading platform for short‐wave infrared sensing, yet a deeper understanding of their electronic structure is still needed. Paradoxically, although the corresponding bulk materials have been extensively studied, the evolution of optical properties at low temperatures (relevant to boost performances), and under pressure (likely induced by a shell introduced to prevent oxidation) has been scarcely investigated in NCs. We therefore conduct structural and spectroscopic studies to explore the (P;T) electronic phase diagram of InAs NCs with various sizes. Cooling induces a blue shift of the optical spectrum, thus reducing the spectral window. The temperature dependence shows an increase in dE/dT with the optical band gap, from which we derive an empirical law capable of predicting the temperature dependence for InAs NCs over a broad size range. Under pressure, we show that the zinc blende phase remains stable up to 12 GPa in nanocrystalline InAs, well above the pressure induced by a ZnSe shell. The pressure dependence of the band gap is found to be around 50 meV/GPa, with no significant size dependence. The 30‐band k.p model is used to quantify how the quantum confinement impacts the temperature and pressure dependence of the optical features.

title: SAÚDE DA MULHER COLETA DE EXAME CITOPATOLÓGICO: UMA REVISÃO DA PRÁTICA IMPORTANTE PARA RASTREIO DE CÂNCER DE COLO UTERINO
summary: O câncer do colo do útero constitui um problema de saúde pública, especialmente em contextos de vulnerabilidade socioeconômica. O exame citopatológico contribui para a identificação de lesões precursoras, mas sua efetividade depende da qual
content: O câncer do colo do útero constitui um problema de saúde pública, especialmente em contextos de vulnerabilidade socioeconômica. O exame citopatológico contribui para a identificação de lesões precursoras, mas sua efetividade depende da qualidade da coleta e da continuidade do acompanhamento. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a coleta do exame citopatológico como estratégia de rastreamento do câncer do colo do útero, destacando os cuidados técnicos e a atuação da enfermagem. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, com levantamento de publicações entre 2022 e 2026 nas fontes MEDLINE, LILACS, Google Acadêmico, SciELO, PubMed e Portal de Periódicos CAPES. A análise contemplou as políticas de prevenção, a organização da assistência no Sistema Único de Saúde, as recomendações de rastreamento e os procedimentos relacionados à qualidade das amostras. Os estudos apontaram barreiras como medo, vergonha, desinformação e dificuldades de acesso aos serviços. Também identificaram falhas técnicas, limitações na capacitação profissional e inadequações na identificação e fixação das amostras como fatores que prejudicam a qualidade do exame. A enfermagem destacou-se na educação em saúde, no acolhimento, na coleta e no acompanhamento dos resultados. Conclui-se que a qualificação do rastreamento requer assistência humanizada, educação permanente, padronização dos procedimentos e continuidade do cuidado, articulando a qualidade técnica da coleta às necessidades das mulheres.

content: Source-available code, a five-record synthetic example, expected outputs and previously public aggregate checks supporting Quantifying 2030 Carbon Capture and Storage Capacity across Database Releases. The one-command wrapper recomputes fixed-2025-capacity horizons and cutoff crossings from an already-admitted 2025–2026 cohort; it does not establish source admission or physical delay. The existing CC BY 4.0 designation applies to the documentation and derived-data layer as specified in the included rights notice; it is not a new blanket software or third-party licence. No journal acceptance or prospective validation is claimed.

title: Newcastle disease virus matrix protein interacts with chicken eukaryotic elongation factor 2 to promote viral protein production and enhance viral particle yield
summary: Eukaryotic elongation factor 2 (eEF2) is important for the step of translation elongation and protein synthesis, while viruses can exploit eEF2 to potentiate their own replication. Previously, chicken eEF2 was identified as a new binding pa
content: Eukaryotic elongation factor 2 (eEF2) is important for the step of translation elongation and protein synthesis, while viruses can exploit eEF2 to potentiate their own replication. Previously, chicken eEF2 was identified as a new binding partner with the Newcastle disease virus (NDV) matrix (M) protein, but their actual interactions and functions in the replication and pathogenicity of NDV are not completely understood. In this study, the NDV M protein was verified to directly interact with chicken eEF2 in the cytoplasm. In addition, four residues (Y187, R188, S197, and S199) in the N-terminus region (aa 179-234) of M protein and six residues (E753, Q754, G758, Y760, N764, and S802) in the V domain (aa 727-858) of chicken eEF2 were responsible for their binding. However, although six residues of eEF2 were highly conserved among human, other mammals, and avian species, four residues of the M protein were completely nonconservative between NDV and other paramyxoviruses. Moreover, mutation of key interactional residues (Y187A/R188A/S197A/S199A) in the M protein remarkably attenuated the virulence, replication ability, and pathogenicity of NDV. Furthermore, interaction of the M protein with chicken eEF2 promoted its expression at the translation level and reduced its phosphorylation level on Thr57 residue, which was conducive to the elevated viral protein production and viral budding and release, and thereby enhanced viral particle yield to facilitate the replication and pathogenicity of NDV. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the significance of M-eEF2 interaction in the replication and pathogenicity of NDV and offer a potential therapeutic target for developing novel anti-NDV strategies.

title: Instructional and Transformational Leadership as Predictors of School Performance: The Mediating Role of School Climate in Bangladeshi Secondary Schools
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Improving school performance is a persistent challenge in developing education systems, especially when school leadership plays a significant role in school performance and effectiveness. The present study is an attempt to investigate the i
content: Improving school performance is a persistent challenge in developing education systems, especially when school leadership plays a significant role in school performance and effectiveness. The present study is an attempt to investigate the impact of instructional leadership and transformational leadership on school performance with the mediation of teacher collaboration, teacher commitment and school climate in secondary schools of Bangladesh. The design used was quantitative and the data collected were survey data from 384 secondary school teachers. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation, regression analysis, and mediation analysis were used to analyze the data with SPSS and PROCESS Macro. The results indicate that instructional leadership and transformational leadership had significant positive influence on school performance, with instructional leadership showing a stronger effect (β = .551, p < .001) than transformational leadership (β = .152, p < .001). School performance was also strongly affected by teacher collaboration, teacher commitment and school climate. The mediation results suggest, however, that school climate was the only school factor that significantly mediated the relationship between the leadership practices and school performance, whereas the relationships between teacher collaboration and school performance and teacher commitment and school performance did not show significant mediation effects. Specifically, the indirect effects through school climate were .338 for instructional leadership and .137 for transformational leadership. The study adds to the body of educational leadership literature by emphasizing the role of school climate as a potential channel of leadership practices that affect school performance in secondary schools in Bangladesh.

title: Physician–Pharmacist PBPM for Intensive Lipid Management After Acute Myocardial Infarction
summary: AIM: A physician-led lipid-lowering protocol increased early proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor use after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but workflow barriers remained. We evaluated a physician-pharmacist protocol-b
content: AIM: A physician-led lipid-lowering protocol increased early proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor use after acute myocardial infarction (AMI), but workflow barriers remained. We evaluated a physician-pharmacist protocol-based pharmacotherapy management (PBPM) program designed to address these limitations. METHODS: This single-center observational study included 438 patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and survived to discharge across PBPM (n = 162), physician-led (n = 160), and pre-protocol (n = 116) eras. The prespecified primary comparison was PBPM versus physician-led care. The primary and key secondary outcomes were evolocumab initiation and chronic-phase low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), respectively. Exploratory analyses examined outcomes across day-2 LDL-C treatment flows. Protocol adherence and reasons for non-initiation were also assessed. RESULTS: Evolocumab initiation increased across the pre-protocol, physician-led, and PBPM eras (2.6%, 13.1%, and 24.7%; overall P＜0.001) and was more frequent with PBPM than physician-led care (24.7% vs. 13.1%, P = 0.008), although the adjusted association was nonsignificant (odds ratio 2.01, 95% confidence interval 0.94-4.29; P = 0.071). Chronic-phase LDL-C was 49.0 versus 51.5 mg/dL (P = 0.074), whereas exploratory achievement of the contemporary LDL-C ＜55 mg/dL target was more frequent with PBPM (67.6% vs. 54.0%, P = 0.034). Among eligible patients, evolocumab initiation increased from 40.0% to 61.0% (P = 0.047), while system-related non-initiation decreased from 44.4% to 4.3%. Exploratorily, chronic-phase LDL-C was lower with PBPM among patients with day-2 LDL-C ≥ 90 mg/dL (24 vs. 47 mg/dL; P = 0.011; interaction P = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: PBPM was associated with greater adherence to the existing lipid-lowering protocol, more frequent evolocumab initiation at discharge, and fewer system-related reasons for non-initiation compared with physician-led care after AMI.

title: Decoding assumptions and inference about a robustness preference in codon reassignments along sampled histories
summary: Abstract Catalogue-associated net transitions between genetic codes reach the silent third-position packing maximum more often than uniform targets do. Whether that signals selection depends on which targets decoding made accessible and whi
content: Abstract Catalogue-associated net transitions between genetic codes reach the silent third-position packing maximum more often than uniform targets do. Whether that signals selection depends on which targets decoding made accessible and which reassignments were detected. We prove that from a block-greedy code every single-box reassignment to an amino acid already in the codon’s box keeps the code optimal, that a robustness coefficient in a conditional-logit target-choice model is identified exactly when the within-pool contrasts span it, and that the class-conditional null stays exact when the decoding state is uncertain. On 200 sampled net-transition histories, the excess over uniform targets persists (35.5 against 20.0 units per history), but a recording ratio of 1.85 for optimum-attaining units would bring its merged reference statistic above 0.05. Within accessibility classes no repertoire’s test rejects once restrictive decoding states are treated as uncertain, and in conditional simulations pooled accessibility with no preference makes the fixed-state restrictive rule reject in all 60 replicates. In pointwise comparisons with fitted sequential generators, the observed statistic has upper-tail ranks below 0.05 for common preferences of odds 2, 2.5 and 3 under a restrictive repertoire (at most 0.025) and of odds 2.5 and 3 under pooled wobble rules, and above 0.05 at restrictive odds 1.5 (0.099) and pooled odds 2 (0.059); these ranks have no established exclusion coverage. Hierarchical intervals include zero under the primary priors. The data constrain several specified preference models but do not establish whether accessibility, a robustness preference or ascertainment generated the enrichment.

title: Nearly Universal Receipt of Desired Contraceptive Method in Two Districts of Rwanda
summary: Abstract Background Research demonstrates that when contraceptive users receive their desired method, they are more likely to maintain contraceptive use, avoid pregnancy, and report satisfaction with family planning. Rwanda has increased fa
content: Abstract Background Research demonstrates that when contraceptive users receive their desired method, they are more likely to maintain contraceptive use, avoid pregnancy, and report satisfaction with family planning. Rwanda has increased family planning use dramatically in a short period of time, from 17% to 69% between 2005 and 2025. This study aims to investigate the role of client receipt of desired method during counseling with family planning nurses at public health clinics or posts in two districts of Rwanda. Methods This study involved data extraction in 2022 and 2023 from family planning records at a sample of public health facilities in two districts of Rwanda, the two districts with the highest and lowest contraceptive prevalence rates in the nation. Extraction from the family planning record included the family planning client’s desired method as stated and recorded prior to counseling as well as the client’s method received after counseling. Results Results show that 95%-97% of a sample of long-acting method users in these two districts received their desired method. Further, multilevel analysis examines correlates of not receiving desired method and finds that individual level client variables explain relatively little variation, while facility-level factors account for most differences in desired method provision in Rwanda. Conclusion Contraceptive users in Rwanda are obtaining their method desired nearly all of the time, meeting client’s method desires is integral to successful contraceptive use and providing human centered services for individuals, family planning programs, and nations.

title: Los de afuera son de palo: FUCVAM y el acceso a la tierra en Montevideo
source: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade
summary: El presente trabajo indaga sobre cómo las cooperativas de vivienda construida por ayuda mutua, afiliadas a la Federación Uruguaya de Cooperativas de Vivienda por Ayuda Mutua (FUCVAM), se relacionan con la lucha por el suelo urbano en Montev
content: El presente trabajo indaga sobre cómo las cooperativas de vivienda construida por ayuda mutua, afiliadas a la Federación Uruguaya de Cooperativas de Vivienda por Ayuda Mutua (FUCVAM), se relacionan con la lucha por el suelo urbano en Montevideo, con el propósito de aportar a esta temática a través de un recorrido teórico sobre el tópico seleccionado. El análisis abarca el período entre 1966, año en que se iniciaron las experiencias fundadoras de FUCVAM, y 2019, y se divide en cuatro subperíodos, cada uno alineado con los procesos históricos de Uruguay. Esto brinda una visión más detallada de la historia y el contexto en el que se desarrollaron las adjudicaciones de tierras a FUCVAM y sus reivindicaciones de lucha, así como de los cambios que se produjeron en el proceso.

title: ESG INVESTMENT, GOVERNANCE, AND CORPORATE CULTURE IN SUSTAINABLE GROWTH: PANEL EVIDENCE FROM HUAZHENG ESG RATINGS OF SHANGHAI AND SHENZHEN A-SHARE LISTED FIRMS
source: Chinese Journal of Social Science and Management
summary: Purpose: Although Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) engagement is widely promoted, its ability to enhance firms’ long-term growth depends on internal institutional and cultural conditions. This study examines whether ESG investmen
content: Purpose: Although Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) engagement is widely promoted, its ability to enhance firms’ long-term growth depends on internal institutional and cultural conditions. This study examines whether ESG investment promotes the corporate Sustainable Growth Rate (SGR) and investigates whether governance structure and corporate culture strengthen this relationship. Study Design/Methodology/Approach: This study uses secondary panel data on 346 A-share firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges from 2017 to 2023 (1,664 firm-year observations) and applies fixed-eﬀects regression models. ESG performance is measured using Huazheng ESG ratings. Corporate governance structure (GS_Index) and corporate culture (OCR) are constructed via Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Firm and year fixed eﬀects are included to control for unobserved firm-level heterogeneity and common temporal shocks. Firm fixed eﬀects inherently control for time-invariant industry heterogeneity. Findings: ESG investment is positively associated with SGR (β = 0.0560, p < 0.01). Governance quality significantly strengthens the ESG-SGR relationship (ESG x GS: β = 0.0912, p < 0.05), and an innovation- and sustainability-oriented culture also amplifies ESG’s growth eﬀect (ESG x OCR: β = 0.1366, p < 0.05). Additional analyses indicate that the ESG-growth association is more pronounced among resource-intensive and heavy-polluting firms. Originality/Value: The findings suggest that ESG investment appears to enhance growth, but its eﬀectiveness depends on strong governance mechanisms and a supportive corporate culture, with implications for investors and policymakers seeking to realize the value of green capital in emerging markets.

title: Comportamiento y segmentación del consumidor de productos lácteos bovinos en la región centro-sur de Chihuahua, México
summary: El comportamiento del consumidor de productos lácteos bovinos constituye un elemento relevante para comprender las características de la demanda y las oportunidades de comercialización en los mercados agroalimentarios regionales. El objetiv
content: El comportamiento del consumidor de productos lácteos bovinos constituye un elemento relevante para comprender las características de la demanda y las oportunidades de comercialización en los mercados agroalimentarios regionales. El objetivo de esta investigación fue caracterizar los hábitos de consumo, atributos de compra y preferencias de los consumidores de productos lácteos bovinos, así como identificar perfiles diferenciados en la región centro-sur del estado de Chihuahua, México. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, no experimental, transversal y de alcance descriptivo-exploratorio. Durante 2024 se aplicaron 384 cuestionarios estructurados a la población, seleccionados mediante un muestreo aleatorio simple. La información fue procesada mediante estadística descriptiva, análisis de componentes principales y análisis de conglomerados mediante k-medias, utilizando SPSS versión 22. La pertinencia del análisis multivariado se verificó mediante la medida Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO = 0.712) y la prueba de esfericidad de Bartlett (p < 0.001). Los resultados mostraron que la leche y el queso presentaron una participación relevante en los hábitos de consumo, mientras que el sabor, el precio y la marca destacaron entre los principales atributos considerados en la decisión de compra. El análisis de componentes principales permitió identificar cuatro dimensiones relacionadas con los atributos del producto, las condiciones económicas, la accesibilidad comercial y la aceptación de productos regionales. Asimismo, el análisis de conglomerados mediante k-medias permitió distinguir tres perfiles de consumidores con características diferenciadas. Los resultados aportan evidencia descriptiva sobre los patrones de consumo y las preferencias del mercado estudiado, proporcionando elementos para orientar estrategias de comercialización y diferenciación de productos lácteos regionales.

title: Emergency Decompressive Craniectomy for Acute Subdural Hematoma in a Patient Receiving Duel Antiplatelet Therapy Following Recent Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Previous Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Case Report
source: Journal of Neurological Sciences and Research.
summary: Background: Acute subdural hematoma (ASDH) requiring emergency surgery in a patient who has recently undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) presents a difficult balance between preventing neurological deterioration and minimizin
content: Background: Acute subdural hematoma (ASDH) requiring emergency surgery in a patient who has recently undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) presents a difficult balance between preventing neurological deterioration and minimizing coronary stent thrombosis risk when antiplatelet therapy must be interrupted.Previous coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) adds to the complexity of perioperative cardiac risk. Case Presentation:A 67-year-old female with a history of CABG in 2011 underwent PCI with stenting to the distal right coronary artery (RCA) to posterior lateral ventricular branch (PLV) five days before presenting with recurrent vomiting, severe headache, and acute right frontoparietal-temporal intracranial hemorrhage (ASDH ) causing significant mass effect and midline shift.The patient's initial Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score was 10/15 (E2V3M5), which sharply deteriorated to 8/15 (E2V2M4) in the Surgical ICU, requiring immediate intubation.Emergency decompressive craniectomy with hematoma evacuation was performed.Postoperatively, non-contrast CT confirmed complete hematoma clearance and mass effect resolution.By the 4th postoperative day (POD-4), the patient achieved a GCS of 15/15 (E4V5M6 on transfer evaluation) and was stepped down to the CCU with stable vitals.Conclusion: This case illustrates the need for rapid multidisciplinary decision-making in life-threatening intracranial hemorrhage shortly after PCI.Urgent neurosurgical treatment may be necessary when significant mass effect is present, while perioperative antiplatelet decisions require individualized coordination among neurosurgery, cardiology, anesthesia, and critical care.

title: Steel Decarbonization Pathways under Carbon Revenue Recycling: A Hybrid Bottom-Up and Top-Down Framework with Endogenous R&D in Korea
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The steel sector is the largest industrial source of CO2 in Korea, and the technologies that could decarbonize it- hydrogen direct reduction, electrolytic ironmaking, and CCUS, among them- remain pre-commercial. With paid allocation under t
content: The steel sector is the largest industrial source of CO2 in Korea, and the technologies that could decarbonize it- hydrogen direct reduction, electrolytic ironmaking, and CCUS, among them- remain pre-commercial. With paid allocation under the Korean ETS scheduled to reach 25% by 2030, how auction revenue is used is becoming a central design question. We examine whether recycling that revenue into sector-specific R&D alters the steel technology pathway, and at what macroeconomic and fiscal cost. We link a bottom-up steel technology model with a recursive-dynamic CGE model of the Korean economy. The bottom-up model covers eleven production routes, three incumbent and eight pre-commercial, calibrated to 2023 production shares using positive mathematical programming. Each pre-commercial route accumulates a knowledge stock from public and privately chosen R&D; once the stock exceeds a route-specific threshold, the route becomes available, and its capital cost declines with cumulative output. The CGE model distinguishes public and private R&D as separate sectors, and the two models exchange fourteen variables annually until convergence. Under a common carbon-tax path (30 to 150 USD/tCO2 by 2050), we compare three uses of the revenue: retention (TAX), an equal-size production-tax rebate (REB), and recycling 50% into steel R&D (RND). Because REB returns exactly the amount RND spends, the RND–REB comparison isolates the R&D channel. The carbon tax alone activates one of the eight new routes. Recycling activates all eight between 2026 and 2048, raises their share of 2050 output from 19% to 36%, and reduces 2050 steel CO2 by a further 8.7%. Both return options keep GDP above the TAX path; the rebate minimizes welfare loss, while recycling minimizes GDP loss and lowers steel prices after 2040. Roughly 84% of the recycled revenue is recovered through the larger tax base it induces.

title: A Free CAPE-OPEN Electrolyte NRTL Property Package for the CESAR-1 Solvent and a Transferable Equilibrium-Stage Column Methodology Tested on Four Pilot Plants
summary: A free electrolyte NRTL model of the CESAR-1 solvent (aqueous AMP/piperazine) was implemented in the open-source framework Reaktoro with published parameters and made available as a CAPE-OPEN property package. It reproduces the experimental
content: A free electrolyte NRTL model of the CESAR-1 solvent (aqueous AMP/piperazine) was implemented in the open-source framework Reaktoro with published parameters and made available as a CAPE-OPEN property package. It reproduces the experimental CO2 solubility in CESAR-1 with an average deviation of 25%, comparable to published models above 60 ◦C and higher at absorber temperatures, and forms the basis of a pilot plant comparison. A methodology is proposed for applying an equilibrium-stage column model across plants with different inlet CO2 concentrations, capture rates, configurations, packing heights and packing types, with load-dependent transfer units and three calibrated parameters, determined at plants with sheet-metal packings and held constant. In closed loop at the measured capture, the specific reboiler duty of four pilot plants, including a gauze-packed plant to which no parameter was fitted, is reproduced with average deviations of 1.4-8.2% (10.8% at Kaiserslautern including three runs with deep regeneration or inconsistent data), the optimum L/G is predicted with reasonable accuracy, and the effect of lean vapour compression is reproduced. The benefit of absorber inter-cooling is overestimated by a factor of 1.8-2.7.

title: A digital twin system for retail inventory & sales management : From conceptual architecture to a functional AI-enhanced prototype
summary: Effective inventory and sales management is crucial in the physical retail stores, directly impacting operational efficiency, customer satisfaction and cost. Integration of Digital Twin technology along with AI and RFID offers significant p
content: Effective inventory and sales management is crucial in the physical retail stores, directly impacting operational efficiency, customer satisfaction and cost. Integration of Digital Twin technology along with AI and RFID offers significant potential for optimise these functions. While a considerable amount of research has concentrated on Digital Twin development for supply chain management, its application in integrated and privacy-conscious retail & sales management systems is still remains a developing area. Thus, this thesis focuses on designing and developing a conceptual Digital Twin system to address this gap. The thesis begins with a comparative analysis of current inventory management systems as a foundational study. It then presents a conceptual DT architecture that integrates RFID and simulated Point of Sale (POS) data for a physical retail store. The core contribution of the thesis is the functional DT prototype validated using simulated data and demonstrated in a Unity-based 3D virtual environment. In addition, the system integrates simulated AI models (SMA, WMA, and LR) to reflect demand forecasting and automated inventory alerts. The findings of the research revealed that the proposed RFID-enabled DT system is capable of offering transformative business insights and privacy-conscious system for physical retail stores, bridging a critical gap in current retail operations.

title: Khmer rouge : de la douleur à l'oubli, un passé douloureux dans la mémoire collective cambodgienne
summary: Comment un pays réputé pour son hospitalité a-t-il basculé dans l’un des pires génocides du XXᵉ siècle? Cette étude plonge au coeur du régime des Khmers rouges (1975-1979) pour comprendre les causes profondes de cette tragédie et ses réperc
content: Comment un pays réputé pour son hospitalité a-t-il basculé dans l’un des pires génocides du XXᵉ siècle? Cette étude plonge au coeur du régime des Khmers rouges (1975-1979) pour comprendre les causes profondes de cette tragédie et ses répercussions durables sur un peuple innocent. Cette étude approfondie et passionnée explorera l’histoire du Cambodge, en scrutant les racines, le développement et les répercussions du régime des Khmers rouges. La recherche commence par un cadre théorique et méthodologique clairement défini, suivi d’une revue importante du contexte historique et sociopolitique qui a précédé l’arrivée au pouvoir des Khmers rouges en 1975. On explore également l’idéologie extrême de ce régime, ses dynamiques internes et les processus brutaux de sa gouvernance entre 1975 et 1979. La deuxième partie du travail se concentre sur la reconstruction après le génocide, un processus marqué par d’importants défis dans les domaines politiques, social et judiciaire. On accorde une importance particulière aux victimes, à la justice qui arrive tardivement, aux contraintes du tribunal hybride et aux traces laissées sur la mémoire collective du Cambodge. L’analyse se poursuit en examinant le Cambodge contemporain, trois générations après le traumatisme, et pose des questions sur les réalités présentes et du futur. À l’intersection de l’histoire, du droit international et de la politique, ce mémoire tente d’éclairer la situation d’un peuple tenace qui lutte pour sa reconstruction identitaire tout en gardant en mémoire son passé. _____________________________________________________________________________ MOTS-CLÉS DE L’AUTEUR : Cambodge, Khmers rouges, génocide, corruption, justice transitionnelle, gouvernance, réforme institutionnelle, constructivisme, mémoire collective.

title: Frostbite: diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, and future directions
summary: From cold-weather training to deployments in high altitude and arctic conditions, frostbite injury and its sequelae remain a serious concern in military operations. Frostbite harms tissue in two distinct ways. The first involves ice crystal
content: From cold-weather training to deployments in high altitude and arctic conditions, frostbite injury and its sequelae remain a serious concern in military operations. Frostbite harms tissue in two distinct ways. The first involves ice crystal formation within tissue, resulting in mechanical damage and ischemia. The second occurs secondary to the inflammatory and prothrombotic state caused by reperfusion from rewarming frozen tissue. Frostbite injuries can be classified in a number of ways, but no perfect system exists. Initial work-up and diagnosis are primarily clinical. However, in equipped treatment facilities, advanced imaging modalities such as technetium- 99 m ( 99 mTc) bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance angiography, single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), and more can play a role in diagnosis and treatment. In resource-constrained environments, such as the deployed setting, management should involve an algorithmic approach.
