After concurrent hypothermia and/or trauma have been evaluated for and treated, active rewarming should take place so long as there is no risk of refreezing. During re-warming, surgical consultation and evacuation considerations should be considered. Once evacuated to a definitive treatment facility, thrombolytic as well as other therapies may be indicated. Unless there is evidence of severe damage or infection, surgical management is typically delayed until injury margins are fully demarcated. Longer-term prognosis is dependent on severity, with deeper injuries often resulting in longer hospital stays, more amputations, and chronic disability. Looking forward, future frostbite research should aim to bridge field and hospital care with the goal of minimizing tissue loss and accelerating functional recovery.

title: Perceptions of College Readiness Among African American High School Students in Urban Areas of Montgomery County in Ohio
source: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
summary: The purpose of this qualitative interpretative phenomenological study was to explore how African American high school seniors from urban public schools in Montgomery County, Ohio, perceived their college readiness and how advanced coursewor
content: The purpose of this qualitative interpretative phenomenological study was to explore how African American high school seniors from urban public schools in Montgomery County, Ohio, perceived their college readiness and how advanced coursework, academic counseling, school leaders and school culture, and their own academic achievement shaped their preparation for college. The objective was to help African American students from urban high schools view their experiences and college preparation and inform educational leaders about specific areas for improvement. Twelve African American seniors (six female, six male) from two urban public high schools in Dayton and Trotwood, Ohio, who had applied to or been admitted to college for Fall 2026, took part in semi structured Zoom interviews analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes emerged: academic challenge and adjustment in advanced coursework, counselor support and access to college information, school culture and a college-like environment, and academic self-confidence and college-going identity. The results uncovered that students’ perception of college readiness varies among both female and male African American high school seniors. Although students have been introduced to rigorous courses such as honors, AP, or College Credit Plus (CCP) courses, some participants expressed that the experience created negative self-doubt about their ability to succeed in college-level coursework. Also, student interpretation of college readiness was found to be linked to information provided primarily through academic counseling; however, the findings revealed some students either did not seek guidance or were provided inadequate information. The students reported that educational leaders are essential to developing school culture for learning and student development. The relationships that are formed with leaders through trust, respect, and support, produce an atmosphere that students feel creates a fulfilling experience. Also, the findings showed most students identified their family as their primary influence to pursue college, as opposed to their school influencing their decision to attend college. Some students revealed their high school experience led them to consider not furthering their education due to their experience.

title: Creative Storytelling in Environmental Science
source: Journal of the Arkansas Academy of Science
summary: Storytelling in the environmental sciences provides a creative method of scientific dissemination, contrasting with traditional formats such as research papers, news articles, and journal articles. Though traditional methods of scientific d
content: Storytelling in the environmental sciences provides a creative method of scientific dissemination, contrasting with traditional formats such as research papers, news articles, and journal articles. Though traditional methods of scientific dissemination are valuable, creative storytelling offers another path to improve knowledge retention and consciousness toward the planet, particularly in elementary education. The objective of this creative project was to produce an elementary-level children’s fiction manuscript as an example of how environmental education can be integrated with storytelling. The writing process treated reading level, conceptual comprehension, and the avoidance of oversimplification as constraints equal to character creation, setting, plot, and fantastical elements. Set in a fictional town and written within the magical realism genre, the story follows a young female protagonist and her friends as they confront an environmental issue in their local community and work alongside city environmentalists and analysts. Educational content is distributed across the plot to allow scientific ideas to emerge as the kids investigate. The project resulted in a 13,143-word manuscript, supported by an interdisciplinary review of storytelling in scientific communication, environmental studies, psychology, and education, as well as a reflection on process, peer and professional edits/critiques, and future action. The creative project and study, through demonstration, argues that children’s literature can function well as a means of scientific dissemination, holding both education and storytelling in equal measure.

title: Analisis Teknologi Cryptocurrency Bitcoin Dalam Transaksi Bisnis: Perspektif Hukum Islam Dan Peraturan Mata Uang Di Indonesia
summary: Abstrak. Penelitian ini menganalisis penggunaan Bitcoin dalam transaksi bisnis berdasarkan hukum Islam dan ketentuan mata uang di Indonesia. Fokus kajian meliputi karakteristik teknologi cryptocurrency, praktik transaksi, unsur yang dapat m
content: Abstrak. Penelitian ini menganalisis penggunaan Bitcoin dalam transaksi bisnis berdasarkan hukum Islam dan ketentuan mata uang di Indonesia. Fokus kajian meliputi karakteristik teknologi cryptocurrency, praktik transaksi, unsur yang dapat menyebabkan transaksi dibenarkan atau dilarang menurut fikih muamalah, serta kedudukan Bitcoin berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 7 Tahun 2011 tentang Mata Uang dan Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 18/40/PBI/2016. Penelitian menggunakan metode penelitian hukum normatif dengan pendekatan kepustakaan. Data dikumpulkan melalui penelaahan buku, artikel ilmiah, penelitian terdahulu, dan peraturan yang dibahas dalam naskah, kemudian dianalisis secara kualitatif. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa teknologi blockchain memungkinkan pencatatan transaksi secara terdistribusi dan transaksi antarpengguna, tetapi karakteristik tersebut tidak dengan sendirinya menjadikan Bitcoin sebagai alat pembayaran yang sah di Indonesia. Dari perspektif hukum Islam, penilaian transaksi perlu mempertimbangkan objek dan tujuan transaksi, kejelasan akad, unsur kerelaan para pihak, serta ada tidaknya gharar, maysir, riba, dan penipuan. Penggunaan yang dominan spekulatif berisiko menimbulkan ketidakpastian dan kerugian. Kajian ini merekomendasikan agar pengguna memahami risiko dan status hukum yang berlaku, sedangkan penelitian selanjutnya perlu menelaah perkembangan regulasi dan praktik perdagangan aset kripto secara lebih mutakhir.

title: Rethinking water availability : Integrated approaches and tools for assessing water availability in a changing world
summary: Today, numerous countries face a dire situation, with insufficient and diminishing water resources affecting billions of people and ecosystems worldwide. One place where this can be seen is in southern Sweden. While historically largely exe
content: Today, numerous countries face a dire situation, with insufficient and diminishing water resources affecting billions of people and ecosystems worldwide. One place where this can be seen is in southern Sweden. While historically largely exempt from severe water shortages, recently an increasing number of areas have started experiencing periods of water scarcity. Despite the importance of understanding these changes, accurately quantifying the availability of clean freshwater remains a challenge. This is partly due to the complexity of defining which components that should be considered when assessing water availability, but also the lack of suitable tools to provide stakeholders and decision makers with information regarding current water storage capacity. This raises several important questions. How much water is currently stored? How much of this water is available? And how might its availability change in the future? To address these challenges, a series of new models and approaches were developed. These included a new method for assessing surface saturation, a modified and reconfigured version of AWRA-L (an Australian water balance model previously not tested outside Australia), a structural framework for assessing water availability, and a climate application compatible with AWRA-L for assessing lake storage dynamics under changing climate conditions. The results demonstrate the potential of these approaches to improve the assessment and understanding of water availability. The new surface saturation method, based on normalized topography and hypsometric curves, performed comparably to existing high-resolution maps while requiring only a fraction of the input data. The modified AWRA-L model successfully captured changes in water storage dynamics and eliminated the need for streamflow data required by the original configuration, increasing its applicability in data-limited settings. The structural framework provided a transparent means of assessing water availability across multiple levels and a broad range of influencing factors. Finally, the climate application successfully captured changes in lake storage dynamics under future climate conditions. Though major changes to overall storage volume were undetected across all but the most extreme scenario, changes in seasonal storage volume were observed across all scenarios, highlighting the need for strategies that can support water management under changing seasonal conditions.Overall, the results of this thesis contribute to increased knowledge of the complex aspects that influence water availability while at the same time providing managers in Sweden and abroad with flexible tools to facilitate its assessment.

title: Multi-fidelity predictive model for shock response of energetic materials using conditional U-Net
summary: Mapping microstructure to properties is central to materials science. Perhaps most famously, the Hall-Petch relationship relates average grain size to strength. More challenging has been deriving relationships for properties that depend on
content: Mapping microstructure to properties is central to materials science. Perhaps most famously, the Hall-Petch relationship relates average grain size to strength. More challenging has been deriving relationships for properties that depend on subtle microstructural features and not average properties. One such example is the initiation of energetic materials under dynamical loading, dominated by energy localization on microstructural features such as pores, cracks, and interfaces. We propose a conditional convolutional neural network to predict the shock-induced temperature field as a function of shock strength, for a wide range of microstructures, and obtained via two different simulation methods. The proposed model, denoted MISTnet2, significantly extends prior work that was limited to a single shock strength, model, and type of microstructure. MISTnet2 can contribute to bridging atomistics with coarse-grain simulations and enable first principles predictions of detonation initiation and safety of this class of materials.

title: A deep learning and TOPSIS framework for predictive maintenance scheduling in smart manufacturing: an Industry 4.0 approach
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Abstract Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance
content: Abstract Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design. The scheduling evaluation demonstrates near-perfect discrimination, capturing all failure-proximate assets by targeting less than one-third of the fleet, with a 3.70-fold efficiency improvement over random allocation, an AUPRC of 0.9923, and tier discrimination significant at p < 10⁻¹¹. Cross-domain validation on CWRU Bearing Fault rotating machinery confirms perfect discrimination (AUPRC = 1.000) and a Spearman correlation of ρ = 0.803 between the closeness coefficient and physical fault severity, thereby supporting physically grounded scheduling without explicit severity supervision. These findings establish that coupling accurate deep-learning-based prognosis with principled multi-criteria decision-making yields high-confidence intervention decisions and quantifiable gains in resource efficiency in Industry 4.0 smart manufacturing environments.

title: ODS 7, narrativas de co-creación y gobernanza ambiental: El caso de Ejido Solar
source: Esfera Pública Revista en Gobernanza y Sociedad
summary: In the context of Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 13, renewable energy and just energy transition initiatives have proliferated across the Global South in recent years at multiple scales. Most of these initiatives are designed at the ma
content: In the context of Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 13, renewable energy and just energy transition initiatives have proliferated across the Global South in recent years at multiple scales. Most of these initiatives are designed at the macro level, often linked to large-scale territorial projects. Relatively less attention has been paid to the potential of community-level renewable energy projects for just energy transitions, and to the factors determining their scalability and replicability. This article examines the experience of Mexico’s Ejido Solar initiative to illustrate the mobilization —primarily, though not exclusively— of Sustainable Development Goal 7. It highlights the initiative's potential and flexibility to incorporate context-specific “threshold” or “Scope 3” metrics without compromising its high potential for scaling and replication from a public policy perspective. To this aim, the study employs the “green transitions” methodology developed by the Go Green project at Roskilde University (Ansell, Sorensen & Torfing, 2023), focusing specifically on two of the 16 governance factors that play a key role in the co-creation stage of just energy transitions at the local level: 1. The definition of local problems associated with the environmental biosphere, where the narratives of multiple actors converge; and 2. The role of Sustainable Development Goals as potential facilitators of local public agendas centered on just energy transitions. The central argument is that narratives, the adoption of language, translation, and problem framing play a pivotal role in the success or failure of adopting initiatives aligned with the SDGs –specifically SDG 7 and the just energy transition. This process unfolds through the roles of three key actors –bureaucrats and policymakers, community beneficiaries, and international agencies– within deliberative arenas where narratives serve as an analytical tool (Bates et al., 1998) within the disciplines of political science and public policy (Rhodes, 2006).

title: Unsupervised reward-driven image segmentation in automated scanning transmission electron microscopy experiments
summary: Abstract Automated experiments in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) require rapid image segmentation to optimize the data representation for human interpretation, decision-making, site-selective spectroscopy, and atomic manip
content: Abstract Automated experiments in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) require rapid image segmentation to optimize the data representation for human interpretation, decision-making, site-selective spectroscopy, and atomic manipulation. Currently, segmentation tasks are typically performed using supervised machine learning methods, which require human-labeled data and are sensitive to out-of-distribution drift effects caused by changes in resolution, sampling, or beam shape. Here, we operationalize and benchmark a recently proposed reward-driven optimization workflow for on-the-fly image analysis in STEM. This unsupervised approach is much more robust because it does not rely on human labels and is fully explainable. The explanatory feedback can help humans verify the decision-making and potentially tune the model by selecting the position along the Pareto frontier of the reward functions. We established the timing and effectiveness of this method and demonstrated its capability for real-time performance in highthroughput and dynamic automated STEM experiments. The reward-driven approach allows for the construction of explainable robust analysis workflows and can be generalized to a broad range of image analysis tasks in electron and scanning probe microscopy and chemical imaging.

title: MatSKRAFT: A framework for large-scale materials knowledge extraction from scientific tables
summary: Scientific progress increasingly depends on synthesizing knowledge across vast literature, yet most experimental data remains trapped in semi-structured formats that resist systematic extraction and analysis. Here, we present MatSKRAFT, a c
content: Scientific progress increasingly depends on synthesizing knowledge across vast literature, yet most experimental data remains trapped in semi-structured formats that resist systematic extraction and analysis. Here, we present MatSKRAFT, a computational framework that automatically extracts and integrates materials science knowledge from tabular data at unprecedented scale. Our approach transforms tables into graph-based representations processed by constraint-driven GNNs that encode scientific principles directly into model architecture. MatSKRAFT significantly outperforms contemporary frontier large language models, achieving F1 scores of 89.33% for property extraction and 71.35% for composition extraction, while processing data 6-496 × faster—compared to the fastest and the slowest models, respectively—with modest hardware requirements. Applied to 66,267 tables from more than 45,500 research publications, we construct a comprehensive database containing 509,281 entries, including 104,000 compositions and a broad range of material properties that expand coverage beyond major existing databases. This systematic approach reveals previously overlooked materials with distinct property combinations and enables data-driven discovery of composition-property relationships forming the cornerstone of materials and scientific discovery.

title: Review Article: A Systematic Review of Acquisition and Processing Approaches for Earth Observations of Arctic Sea Ice Melt Ponds
summary: Melt ponds (MPs) are pools of meltwater that form on the ice surface during late spring and summer. By reducing surface albedo, they amplify the ice-albedo feedback and alter the sea-ice surface energy budget, exerting a strong influence on
content: Melt ponds (MPs) are pools of meltwater that form on the ice surface during late spring and summer. By reducing surface albedo, they amplify the ice-albedo feedback and alter the sea-ice surface energy budget, exerting a strong influence on the Arctic climate system. Melt pond parameterizations, often included in major Global Circulation Models (GCMs), can substantially affect simulated sea-ice state variables. However, observational constraints on MP processes remain limited, introducing uncertainty into climate projections, even as expanding observational capabilities offer increasing opportunities to strengthen MP representation in models. A consolidated knowledge of current methods for acquiring and processing Earth observation (EO) data relevant to melt ponds is required to support parameterization advancement, observational dataset development, algorithm design, field-campaign planning, and improved physical understanding of processes. To address these needs, we review the main EO methods used in MP studies: active and passive optical sensors (multispectral and LiDAR) and microwave instruments (synthetic aperture radar, radiometers, radar altimeters and scatterometers). We synthesize MP signatures across the electromagnetic spectrum, distill the underlying physical mechanisms governing sensor responses, and examine in detail each sensor's strengths and limitations, discussing in situ observations, processing techniques, and available MP datasets. We find that optical systems currently dominate pan-Arctic melt pond fraction (MPF) products despite cloud and light limitations, while microwave systems, though all-weather capable, face persistent challenges in discriminating melt ponds from other surface types, hampering equivalent product development. Data processing has evolved from statistical approaches to spectral unmixing, physics-based algorithms, and machine-learning techniques. Pan-Arctic and regional datasets are complementary, trading coarse continuous coverage for spatial detail. High-resolution products are largely derived from field campaigns and inherit their spatial limitations, being concentrated in coastal areas and first-year ice, leaving the central Arctic and multiyear ice zones under-represented. Temporal limitations hinder the capture of rapid melt transitions, while the lack of standardized classification and validation datasets limits algorithm development and intercomparison. This systematic side-by-side assessment of melt pond datasets, EO approaches, and field campaigns enables direct evaluation of coverage, uncertainties, and accessibility, providing a state-of-the-art synthesis of MP observations to support parameterization refinement and multimodal modeling aimed at reducing observational gaps and improving Arctic predictions.

title: Enhanced lemurs optimizer for multi-objective task scheduling in heterogeneous fog–cloud architectures
source: Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications
summary: Task scheduling in heterogeneous fog–cloud systems is an NP-hard multi-objective problem requiring simultaneous minimization of makespan, energy consumption, and processing cost, objectives that inherently conflict as workloads scale. Exist
content: Task scheduling in heterogeneous fog–cloud systems is an NP-hard multi-objective problem requiring simultaneous minimization of makespan, energy consumption, and processing cost, objectives that inherently conflict as workloads scale. Existing metaheuristics often converge prematurely due to poor initialization and fixed exploration–exploitation dynamics. This paper proposes an Enhanced Lemurs Optimizer (ELO) that seeds the exploration–exploitation refinement of the original Lemurs Optimizer (LO) with a problem-aware heuristic schedule under a weighted-sum scalarization framework. Simulations with 100–400 tasks in a heterogeneous fog–cloud environment, using 30 paired runs on shared instances and an equal evaluation budget for all metaheuristics, show that ELO achieves the highest weighted fitness for 200–400 tasks, improving on the original LO by 15.9–19.6% and reducing makespan and energy consumption by up to 24.2% and 21.8%, respectively; for 100 tasks, simulated annealing is marginally but consistently better (by 0.5% in mean fitness). Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirm that ELO significantly outperforms LO, GA, P2C, and Random at every task size and simulated annealing for 200–400 tasks, and ELO also outperforms NSGA-II when a single schedule is selected with the same weighted-sum rule; an ablation study identifies the heuristic initialization as the main source of the improvement. These results establish ELO as an effective weighted-sum scheduling framework for heterogeneous fog–cloud architectures, with an advantage that grows with problem size.

title: Constrained scenario adaptation in flight simulator training using conceptualized state spaces
summary: Abstract The EASA AI Roadmap 2.0 establishes trustworthiness as the backbone of AI readiness in aviation, requiring that machine learning is not only accurate, but also deterministic, traceable to formally defined concepts, bounded by expli
content: Abstract The EASA AI Roadmap 2.0 establishes trustworthiness as the backbone of AI readiness in aviation, requiring that machine learning is not only accurate, but also deterministic, traceable to formally defined concepts, bounded by explicit safety constraints, and reconstructable post-hoc. Existing approaches treat machine learning as an unconstrained predictor over a latent feature space and apply constraints only as post-hoc filters. The central methodological problem remains open: a formal mapping from heterogeneous subsymbolic training evidence to admissible scenario adaptations that preserves these properties by construction. This paper formulates and realizes such a mapping, decomposable into formally defined substeps that satisfy four structural properties: determinism, semantic grounding, constraint compliance, and reconstructability. A realization for cyber-physical scenario-based flight training is presented. Its core is a deterministic conceptualized state space based on Deep-Linking Keywords that links theory-based assessment and simulator-based performance. A deterministic finite automaton governs instructional progression. Scenario adaptation is approximated by a constrained machine learning policy within an admissible action space enforced by monotonicity constraints, phase gating, and a projection operator that clips outputs to the admissible action space. The architecture is analytically verified by construction against the four properties and demonstrated empirically on $$N{ = }160$$ policy cases using $$k{ = }5$$ group-wise cross-validation. The constrained machine learning component approximates the deterministic baseline policy with a profile Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of $$0.126 \pm 0.024$$ and a $$+0.344$$ improvement in scenario-focus classification accuracy over the majority-class baseline. Statistical generalization beyond this proof-of-concept scope is identified as the next step.

title: Physical activity and sedentary behavior are longitudinally associated with diurnal cortisol rhythms up to 1 year after colorectal cancer treatment
summary: Less robust diurnal cortisol rhythms are hypothesized to be associated with fatigue, depressive symptoms, psychological distress, sleep disturbances and poorer quality of life. Sedentary behavior and physical activity may influence cortisol
content: Less robust diurnal cortisol rhythms are hypothesized to be associated with fatigue, depressive symptoms, psychological distress, sleep disturbances and poorer quality of life. Sedentary behavior and physical activity may influence cortisol rhythmicity, providing mechanistic leads for intervention strategies. We examined longitudinal associations of accelerometer-assessed sedentary behavior and physical activity with diurnal cortisol patterns among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) up to 12 months post-treatment. Among 74 CRC survivors, total and prolonged sedentary time (in bouts ≥30 min), total physical activity (TPA), and relative amplitude of physical activity reflecting day-night contrast in activity were determined with 7-day thigh-worn accelerometry at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after cancer treatment. Salivary cortisol was sampled five times daily over two consecutive days at each follow-up timepoint. As a comprehensive assessment of diurnal cortisol rhythms, the relative amplitude of cortisol concentration (RA_cort), diurnal slope, area under the curve and cortisol awakening response (CAR) were derived as comprehensive measures of diurnal cortisol rhythms. We used confounder-adjusted linear mixed models to estimate overall longitudinal associations, with coefficients (β) reflecting differences in SD units of the cortisol parameters per 2 h/day of sedentary time, per 1 hour/day of physical activity, or per 1 SD of the RA of physical activity. More total sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a weaker decline in cortisol over time and thus a flatter slope (β = 0.19; 95% CI = 0.06,0.33). More prolonged sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a lower RA_cort (β = − 0.12; 95% CI = − 0.23, − 0.01) and flatter cortisol slope (β = 0.16; 95% CI = 0.04,0.27). More TPA (per 1 h/day: β = 0.23; 95% CI = 0.03,0.43) and a higher relative amplitude of physical activity (per SD: β = 0.15; 95% CI = 0.00, 0.29) were associated with a higher RA_cort. More total sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a higher CAR (β = 0.14; 95% CI = 0.01, 0.27). Higher physical activity levels, a larger RA of physical activity, and less sedentary time were associated with more robust diurnal cortisol rhythms, mainly driven by inter-individual associations. Intervention studies are needed to determine whether modifying these behaviors may improve cortisol rhythmicity after CRC. Registration : EnCoRe study ( https://www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl/ ).

title: CP-Agent: A harness-engineered agent for crystal plasticity simulation workflows
summary: Crystal plasticity (CP) simulations predict the mechanical behavior of polycrystalline metals, yet their routine use is hindered by the manual effort of configuring heterogeneous tools, orchestrating multi-step data pipelines, and calibrati
content: Crystal plasticity (CP) simulations predict the mechanical behavior of polycrystalline metals, yet their routine use is hindered by the manual effort of configuring heterogeneous tools, orchestrating multi-step data pipelines, and calibrating constitutive parameters against experiments. These bottlenecks impede productivity in systematic parameter studies, motivating interest in automated workflows. This study presents CP-Agent, a harness-engineered LLM-based agent that autonomously executes complete CP modeling workflows from natural-language tasks. Operating under the ReAct paradigm, the agent reasons about tool selection and sequencing while delegating numerical search to established optimizers. The harness comprises a minimal system prompt, typed tool definitions, a dispatcher, and a safety-bounded iteration loop, encoding domain knowledge through tool schemas rather than hard-coded logic. CP-Agent is demonstrated on four case studies: calibrating four slip parameters of additively manufactured stainless steel 316L against tensile data; validating the workflow against published copper benchmarks, reproducing stress-strain and texture evolution; recovering the initial crystallographic texture of copper, where the agent correctly identifies a diffuse initial texture; and reproducing the multi-pass rolling texture evolution of a Mg-Zn-Ca alloy, where the agent chains five deformation passes and recovers the experimentally observed weakened, split basal texture. In all cases, the agent inferred the correct execution sequence from the task statement, robustly across repeated runs, and delivered physically interpretable results. This work establishes harness engineering as a systematic approach to automating CP modeling workflows while maintaining physical interpretability and auditability through visible reasoning traces.

title: Time‐bound: Entanglements of digitalization and urbanization across global peripheries †
summary: This paper addresses lacunae in critically thinking about temporal entanglements between digitalization and urbanization in global peripheries. It proposes the concept of the time‐bound as a critical lens to unpack the temporal power of dig
content: This paper addresses lacunae in critically thinking about temporal entanglements between digitalization and urbanization in global peripheries. It proposes the concept of the time‐bound as a critical lens to unpack the temporal power of digitalization and urbanization. Bringing together scholarship from postcolonial science and technology studies (STS), new materialities and the global periphery to examine the time‐bound entanglements of digitalization and urbanization, it will anchor the analysis in three temporally and geographically differentiated cases from Kenya, India and Taiwan. All three are subject to projects of land digitalization within locations that are produced through complex historical, political and structural inequalities. Drawing upon these cases, this paper argues that while digitalization flattens the periphery as a space of ‘timeless time,’ communities experience anticipation, interruption, waiting and expulsion. By tracing temporal entanglements across a diversity of spaces, scales and materialities, this paper examines the temporal boundary un/making project of digitalizing states, produced through the entanglements between digitalization and urbanization within marginal and vulnerable populations.

title: Foreign Loan Financing for Indonesia’s Defense Modernization: Fiscal and Strategic Risks, Procurement Governance, and Industrial Self-Reliance
summary: Indonesia’s defense modernization requires substantial and sustained financing, yet fiscal constraints limit the government’s capacity to fund large-scale major weapons systems (MWS) procurement through annual budget allocations alone. This
content: Indonesia’s defense modernization requires substantial and sustained financing, yet fiscal constraints limit the government’s capacity to fund large-scale major weapons systems (MWS) procurement through annual budget allocations alone. This study examines the opportunities, risks, and policy implications of foreign loan financing for defense modernization and the strengthening of national defense-industrial self-reliance. Using a qualitative literature-review approach, the study applies content analysis to academic publications, regulations, policy documents, official institutional data, and selected international experiences. The findings show that foreign loans can improve financing certainty for long-term defense acquisitions and create opportunities to support technology transfer, offsets, domestic content requirements (TKDN), and the development of national industrial capabilities. However, these benefits are accompanied by significant risks, including debt-sustainability pressures, exchange-rate exposure, long-term fiscal commitments, supplier dependence, and potential technological reliance on foreign partners. The analysis further indicates that the effectiveness of foreign financing depends on procurement design, bargaining capacity, institutional coordination, contractual enforcement, and domestic absorptive capacity. Accordingly, this study proposes an integrated policy framework built on four interrelated pillars: fiscal sustainability, institutional strengthening, optimization of TKDN and offset mechanisms, and comprehensive debt-risk management. Foreign loans should therefore be treated not merely as financing instruments, but as strategic defense-economic policy tools capable of simultaneously supporting military modernization and strengthening Indonesia’s defense-industrial independence. The evidence base combines peer-reviewed scholarship with official Indonesian budget, planning, regulatory, and procurement documents available through September 2026.

title: Reclaiming The City of Gold’s story through graphic design as narrative infrastructure for inclusive and circular placemaking in Johannesburg
source: Journal of Place Management and Development
summary: Purpose This paper aims to explore how collaborative graphic design pedagogy may contribute conceptually to inclusive and circular placemaking in a contested Johannesburg heritage precinct. It interprets speculative visual communication pro
content: Purpose This paper aims to explore how collaborative graphic design pedagogy may contribute conceptually to inclusive and circular placemaking in a contested Johannesburg heritage precinct. It interprets speculative visual communication proposals as potential narrative infrastructure and develops symbolic circularity as a cultural and communicative complement to material circularity. Design/methodology/approach The research uses an interpretive, research-through-design case of an honours service-learning unit conducted with a local non-profit organisation. The corpus comprises student design artefacts, studio observations, walking-based visual documentation and formative feedback. Artefacts were interpreted through three propositions: gathering multiple narratives, continuity rather than replacement and collective authorship. The proposals were not implemented or evaluated with everyday precinct users. Findings The proposals most clearly support continuity rather than replacement through the reuse and recoding of Art Deco geometry and inherited visual references. They show conceptual potential for gathering multiple narratives through adaptable identity, wayfinding and projected-content systems. Collective authorship is least substantiated because participation was limited to the partner organisation and final design control remained with student teams. Digital access, curation, governance, maintenance and long-term stewardship remain unresolved. Originality/value The paper offers an exploratory theoretical contribution by defining symbolic circularity as the intentional reuse, recoding and circulation of inherited cultural meanings through graphic and narrative intervention. It positions narrative infrastructure as a potential basis for future participatory placemaking, while distinguishing speculative design capacity from enacted participation, environmental performance and realised urban impact.

title: Weather-aware contrastive state-space learning for probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasting under high irradiance variability
summary: Accurate probabilistic photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential to reliable operation of power systems with high renewable penetration. The rapid changes in the weather lead to strong non-stationarity in PV generation and degrade bo
content: Accurate probabilistic photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential to reliable operation of power systems with high renewable penetration. The rapid changes in the weather lead to strong non-stationarity in PV generation and degrade both prediction accuracy and uncertainty estimation. We propose a weather-aware contrastive state-space learning framework for probabilistic forecasting of PV power. Our framework integrates a selective state-space encoder for efficient long-range temporal modeling, a contrastive learning module that structures representations according to irradiance-ramp-based weather regimes, and a quantile forecasting head for direct uncertainty estimation. This design does not explicitly generate weather scenarios but adapts the learned representations to varying atmospheric conditions. The framework was validated using 118,865 operational measurements collected from a 350 kWp grid-connected photovoltaic system under real operating conditions. The experimental task is formulated as a short-term one-step-ahead PV power forecasting problem using a historical input window of 24 consecutive observations. On the full evaluation set, the proposed model achieved an RMSE of 0.318, an MAE of 0.251, a MAPE of 11.02%, and a CRPS of 0.244 on the original PV power scale after inverse transformation from the normalized training representation, outperforming the persistence, recurrent, Transformer-based, and state-space baselines that were evaluated. Under high irradiance-variability conditions on the evaluated photovoltaic installation, the RMSE was 36% lower than that of LSTM and 17% lower than that of the independent Mamba baseline. Ablation experiments also showed the complementary contributions of selective state-space modeling and weather aware contrastive learning. These results demonstrate the potential of weather-aware state-space representation learning for efficient probabilistic PV forecasting under non-stationary operating conditions.

title: Craniofacial Growth Transformer: A Growth-Aware Framework for Longitudinal Craniofacial Analysis and Forecasting
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of craniofacial growth is important for orthodontic planning, craniofacial assessment, and long-term monitoring of facial development. Most existing methods rely on sparse or cross-sectional data. As a res
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of craniofacial growth is important for orthodontic planning, craniofacial assessment, and long-term monitoring of facial development. Most existing methods rely on sparse or cross-sectional data. As a result, they do not fully capture how facial structures change over time or how different facial regions develop together.This study presents a growth-aware framework for longitudinal craniofacial analysis and forecasting. The framework is based on a dense longitudinal dataset containing nearly ten years of near-daily facial observations from three individuals. Using this dataset, we analyze temporal dependencies, age-related differences, developmental consistency across individuals, and relationships among craniofacial measurements.The results show that several craniofacial measurements follow similar developmental trajectories across individuals. This finding suggests the presence of shared growth patterns despite individual differences. The analysis also identifies stable relationships between anatomically related regions, including bilateral ocular structures and mandibular-facial dimensions. These findings indicate that craniofacial growth follows a coordinated process rather than independent changes in individual features.Based on these findings, we propose a Long Short-Term Memory–Temporal–Spatial Transformer (LSTM-TS-TF) model. The model captures temporal continuity, long-range developmental dependencies, and spatial interactions between facial measurements. Experimental results show that the proposed model improves forecasting accuracy and reduces prediction error by approximately 63--72% compared with conventional LSTM models.These findings show that dense longitudinal modeling can identify interpretable growth descriptors and coordinated developmental patterns. The results also support the use of growth-aware deep learning models for data-driven craniofacial analysis and predictive modeling in biomedical applications.

title: Trauma-Informed Care for Perinatal Psychological Trauma: Application Progress and Public Health Strategies
source: Journal of Public Health and Preventive Medicine
summary: Perinatal psychological trauma has emerged as a critical public health concern with profound implications for maternal and child health as well as intergenerational trauma transmission. Trauma-Informed Care (TIC), operating as a universal p
content: Perinatal psychological trauma has emerged as a critical public health concern with profound implications for maternal and child health as well as intergenerational trauma transmission. Trauma-Informed Care (TIC), operating as a universal prevention-oriented healthcare management framework, shows significant promise in restoring a sense of safety, mitigating perinatal post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and advancing health equity. This narrative review synthesizes current research progress on the multidimensional characteristics and population-level burden of perinatal trauma, analyzes the core concepts and implementation frameworks of TIC, summarizes validated screening and assessment instruments, and thoroughly examines practical bottlenecks—including primary healthcare workforce shortages, socio-cultural stigma, and cross-sectoral referral fragmentation—along with corresponding coping strategies. Ultimately, this review aims to clarify the conceptual boundaries and theoretical foundations of TIC, providing an evidence-based framework to accelerate the translation of TIC principles from micro-level clinical operations into standardized, integrated public health systems.

title: The Unseen Shift: A Phenomenological Study of Mothering Experiences in Nurses During COVID-19
summary: Abstract Background Infectious disease outbreaks and pandemics constitute a major global public health challenge, exerting profound adverse effects on healthcare workers who are mothers and on their children. This study aimed to describe an
content: Abstract Background Infectious disease outbreaks and pandemics constitute a major global public health challenge, exerting profound adverse effects on healthcare workers who are mothers and on their children. This study aimed to describe and interpret the lived experiences of mothering among nurses caring for young children during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods This qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of 12 female nurses caring for infants or toddlers, purposively recruited in 2025 from hospitals affiliated with Ardabil University of Medical Sciences in Iran. Individual semi-structured interviews (40–60 minutes each) were conducted by the principal investigator via telephone or videoconference to explore participants' experiences of caring for young children during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data collection continued until saturation was reached. Data were analyzed using Diekelmann's hermeneutic phenomenological method. Results Thematic analysis of the qualitative data revealed four main themes: 1) role conflict and existential exhaustion, (2) motherhood behind masks and infection control measures, (3) social isolation and the collapse of support networks, and (4) the lifeworld of fear, guilt, and resilience. Conclusions The findings revealed that participating nurses experienced motherhood through the formidable barriers of alcohol-based disinfectants, double-layered masks, hospital corridors, and isolation rooms, all while enduring profound social isolation. Despite these overwhelming challenges, they demonstrated remarkable self-sacrifice and resilience, persistently striving to safeguard their families' health and well-being.

title: Associations of dry period length with subsequent milk production, pregnancy, postpartum health, and early culling in Chinese Holstein cows
summary: Objective: Evidence from large commercial dairy populations in China remains limited on how associations between dry period length (DPL) and subsequent performance vary across outcomes, postpartum time, and lactation transitions.This study
content: Objective: Evidence from large commercial dairy populations in China remains limited on how associations between dry period length (DPL) and subsequent performance vary across outcomes, postpartum time, and lactation transitions.This study aimed to characterize these associations for milk production, pregnancy, postpartum health, and early herd exit in Chinese Holstein cows.Methods: This retrospective observational study used records from 10 commercial dairy farms collected between January 2018 and May 2026.The initial dataset contained 66 421 dry-period records from 34 565 cows; after quality control, 44 894 records from 17 975 cows were included in the analysis.DPL was modeled continuously using restricted cubic splines in outcomespecific multivariable models, with cow-level clustered inference.Time-varying associations and interactions with lactation transition were also evaluated.Results: Median DPL was 58 d.Adjusted 60-DIM cumulative milk yield and predicted 305-d milk yield peaked near 55-56 d.Relative to 58 d, DPL values of 30 and 120 d were associated with 894.9 and 600.0 kg lower predicted 305-d milk yield, respectively.Metritis, retained placenta, and live culling showed nonlinear associations with DPL.Pregnancy and ketosis associations varied over postpartum time, whereas, each 10-d increase in DPL was associated A c c e p t e d A r t i c l ewith a higher hazard of displaced abomasum (HR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.09-1.20).Several associations differed by lactation transition; no significant overall association was detected for mastitis, or death.Conclusion: Intermediate DPL values were associated with higher subsequent milk yield and more favorable estimates for selected health and live-culling outcomes.Time-varying and lactation-transition-specific associations precluded identification of a single DPL target across outcomes.These observational findings inform hypotheses for tailored dry-period management rather than establish an optimal management policy.

title: Structural Complementarity, Bottlenecks, and Total Factor Productivity in Mexico (2000–2025): A Matrix and Critical Political Economy Approach
summary: Abstract Traditional modeling of regional economic growth and Total Factor Productivity (TFP) in emerging economies has relied on continuous neoclassical specifications assuming unitary elasticity of substitution. This paper demonstrates th
content: Abstract Traditional modeling of regional economic growth and Total Factor Productivity (TFP) in emerging economies has relied on continuous neoclassical specifications assuming unitary elasticity of substitution. This paper demonstrates the analytical insufficiency of such frameworks to explain persistent subnational divergence across Mexico, where localized human capital accumulation fails to mechanically translate into proportional technical efficiency gains. Engaging in critical dialogue with evolutionary and radical political economy, we examine the fundamental epistemological tensions underlying aggregate capital and TFP accounting, formalizing a multidimensional matrix architecture that synthesizes Kremer’s (1993) O-Ring production theory, Liebig’s Law of the Minimum, input-output shock propagation through intersectoral networks (Acemoglu et al., 2012), and power asymmetries across Global Value Chains (Kapeller et al., 2024; Durand & Milberg, 2020). Utilizing the Adjusted Mazziotta-Pareto Index (AMPI), internal horizontal disparities across complex labor skills and critical infrastructure vectors are penalized non-compensatorily. Coupled Leontief inverse matrices derive sector-specific co-requirement structures, projecting realized factor absorption. Furthermore, applying local projections (Jordà, 2005) across five historical macroeconomic disruptions, we derive normative resilience matrices via Moore-Penrose pseudoinverses, auditing spatial mismatch through Mahalanobis distances and cosine similarity. Panel threshold regressions (Hansen, 1999) empirically validate the bottleneck hypothesis: the marginal return on technical skills is statistically indistinguishable from zero in states below the critical infrastructure threshold (γ 1 = 92.40), switching to a highly significant regime once surpassed (θ 2 = 0.428, p < 0.001). Two-step System GMM dynamic panel estimations with Windmeijer (2005) correction confirm structural supermodularity (β 3 = 0.015, p < 0.001) and significant penalties from Mahalanobis mismatch (β 4 = -0.142, p < 0.001). We deconstruct the nearshoring phenomenon through the lenses of capital’s spatial fix (Harvey, 2001), the maquiladora regime and labor market segmentation (Delgado Wise & Cypher, 2007; Marini, 1973), as well as biophysical boundaries and ecologically unequal exchange (Althouse et al., 2023; Obeng-Odoom, 2025). Finally, we categorize Mexico’s 32 states into four operational quadrants, contrasting conventional technocratic policy prescriptions with sovereign planning strategies for regional development. JEL Classification : O47, R11, C23, D57, B51.

title: Italian Political Climate Discourse at COP Summits (2010-2024): An English-Language Speech Corpus
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This corpus comprises ten speeches delivered in English by Italian political representatives at the Conferences of the Parties (COP) between 2010 and 2024. It includes interventions by six speakers: Stefania Prestigiacomo, Corrado Clini, An
content: This corpus comprises ten speeches delivered in English by Italian political representatives at the Conferences of the Parties (COP) between 2010 and 2024. It includes interventions by six speakers: Stefania Prestigiacomo, Corrado Clini, Andrea Orlando, Gian Luca Galletti, Mario Draghi, and Giorgia Meloni. The corpus contains 5,787 words before computational preprocessing. The texts were collected from official documents of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), publicly available video recordings, and previously documented sources. Where necessary, speeches were manually transcribed. Nine documents are provided in plain-text (.txt) format and one in Rich Text Format (.rtf). Word counts were calculated in R before undergo regex cleaning, numeric/date removal, dictionary-based lemmatisation, and stopword filtering. The ten documents are arranged chronologically and assigned identifiers from Doc. 1 to Doc. 10. The accompanying metadata provide information on the speaker, institutional role, COP edition, date, word count, source format, original source, and last access date. Two documents contain separate speeches delivered by Giorgia Meloni at COP28 in December 2023. The selection includes only speeches originally delivered in English that address climate policy, environmental responsibility, mitigation, adaptation, international cooperation, energy transition, or climate finance. Speeches delivered in Italian, translations, interviews, and journalistic paraphrases were excluded. The corpus was compiled to examine how Italian political representatives communicate environmental and climate issues in English as a lingua franca of international political communication. The collection builds on research originally conducted for Anna Raimo's doctoral thesis (2025) and was subsequently prepared for this release by Anna Raimo and Caterina Giachino. The analytical tools and computational pipeline used in this study are available in the associated GitHub repository: https://github.com/KatGia/Algorithmic-Ecologies.

title: Developing web-based decision-making support system for renewable energy prioritisation toward sustainable development in Indonesia
summary: Indonesia’s renewable energy transition is constrained not only by fragmented policy frameworks but also by limited availability of a practical and structured mechanism for prioritising renewable energy options. This study developed a web-b
content: Indonesia’s renewable energy transition is constrained not only by fragmented policy frameworks but also by limited availability of a practical and structured mechanism for prioritising renewable energy options. This study developed a web-based decision-making support system (DSS) that operationalises a multi-criteria framework for renewable energy planning toward sustainable development in Indonesia. The system combines AHP weights previously derived from 53 renewable-energy experts with independent TOPSIS ratings provided by 10 senior MEMR policymakers. The study results indicate solar and hydropower as consistently preferred technologies under the applied criteria, whereas wind and geothermal ranked lower. The same 10 policymakers interacted with the online prototype, viewed the real-time results, and provided preliminary usability feedback. The findings showed that the system provides a transparent and structured approach to renewable energy prioritisation. Preliminary user feedback was favourable, with an average score of 4.9 out of 5.0, indicating that the policymakers perceived the prototype as intuitive, useful, and relevant to planning needs. The study contributes a context-sensitive and policy-adaptable sustainable engineering tool for renewable energy planning in Indonesia.

title: Evaluating the Multilevel Impacts of the Waste-to-Energy Plant Through the Sustainable Development Framework in Putri Cempo Surakarta, Indonesia
summary: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) development has increasingly been promoted as a strategic solution for addressing urban waste challenges while supporting renewable energy transition initiatives. The Waste-to-Energy Plant in Putri Cempo, Surakarta, re
content: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) development has increasingly been promoted as a strategic solution for addressing urban waste challenges while supporting renewable energy transition initiatives. The Waste-to-Energy Plant in Putri Cempo, Surakarta, represents one of Indonesia’s efforts to integrate waste management with sustainable energy production. Nevertheless, the implementation of such infrastructure projects may also generate complex environmental, economic, and social implications for surrounding communities. This study aims to evaluate the multilevel impacts of the Putri Cempo WtE project through the sustainable development framework. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach, the research draws upon in-depth interviews, field observations, and document analysis involving five key informants. The findings indicate that the operation of the WtE facility has produced significant socio-environmental consequences. Environmentally, local residents reported persistent air pollution, dust exposure, and unpleasant odors associated with plant operations. Economically, informal waste workers experienced declining income opportunities due to restricted access to waste collection areas. Socially, community participation and institutional engagement between local residents and plant operators remain limited. The study further reveals that the unequal distribution of environmental risks and socio-economic burdens experienced by marginalized communities reflects broader tensions within green energy transition policies. In this context, the implementation of WtE infrastructure may reproduce tendencies associated with green colonialism, where sustainabilityoriented development disproportionately transfers environmental and economic burdens onto vulnerable local communities. Therefore, strengthening environmental governance and inclusive community engagement is essential to ensure that WtE development aligns with broader sustainable development and environmental justice principles.

title: Shaking Table Test of RC Framed Building Strengthened by e-CLT System
summary: The main part of the European residential building stock dates back to the second half of the 20 th century and is largely composed of RC framed structures that do not fulfill current seismic design requirements. Furthermore, they often pro
content: The main part of the European residential building stock dates back to the second half of the 20 th century and is largely composed of RC framed structures that do not fulfill current seismic design requirements. Furthermore, they often provide energy performance that is far from the required current energy standards. Based on this background. The multidisciplinary Horizon 2020 innovation research project e-SAFE (energy and Seismic AFfordable rEnovation solutions) has proposed and developed an innovative integrated seismic and energy retrofit system, named e-CLT. This system is composed of Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT) panels and friction dampers clamped to the exterior facades of the building. The impact of the e-CLT system on the structural response has been investigated by a shaking table test carried out within the RE-SAFE research project, performed at LNEC laboratories within the framework of the ERIES project. The goal of this paper is to show the structural performance provided by a RC framed structure equipped with e-CLT, considering increasing input magnitude and different e-CLT configurations.

title: NONLINEAR INFLATION-GROWTH DYNAMICS IN TANZANIA: TURNING-POINT EVIDENCE AND POLICY IMPLICATIONS
source: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
summary: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between inflation and longrun economic growth in Tanzania over the period 1970–2023 using an autoregressive distributed lag model with a quadratic inflation specification. The results indicate
content: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between inflation and longrun economic growth in Tanzania over the period 1970–2023 using an autoregressive distributed lag model with a quadratic inflation specification. The results indicate a statistically significant inverted U-shaped relationship, with an estimated inflation turning point of about 5.8 per cent. This estimate is lower than several thresholds reported in the cross-country literature and below the East African Monetary Union convergence ceiling of 8 per cent. The error-correction term is negative and statistically significant at the 5 per cent level, suggesting that approximately 19.5 per cent of disequilibrium is corrected each year. None of the control variables is statistically significant in the reported level component, although contemporaneous investment and the second lag of government expenditure exhibit significant short-run effects at the 5 per cent level. Overall, the estimated relationship suggests that moderate single-digit inflation is associated with more favourable long-run economic performance than higher inflation within the sample. Our findings suggest that regional convergence ceilings may exceed the inflation range associated with the estimated turning point, reflecting the fact that convergence criteria are designed primarily as macroeconomic stability bounds rather than growth-maximising targets. These findings highlight the value of country-specific estimates alongside cross-country evidence. The study contributes updated country-specific evidence on the inflation–growth nexus in Tanzania and highlights the value of country-specific estimates alongside cross-country evidence.

title: EUROPE'S NEXT AI SECURITY CHALLENGE: WHO CONTROLS THE FINAL ACTION? — From EU AI Act and NIS2 to 6G, the Digital Euro, Industrial AI and Critical Infrastructure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Technical Subtitle: A Patent-Pending Protected Execution-Finality Architecture for European AI Sovereignty, Autonomous AI Agents, Zero Trust Security, 6G Networks, Confidential Computing, Digital Payments, Enterprise Automation and Conseque
content: Technical Subtitle: A Patent-Pending Protected Execution-Finality Architecture for European AI Sovereignty, Autonomous AI Agents, Zero Trust Security, 6G Networks, Confidential Computing, Digital Payments, Enterprise Automation and Consequence-Bound Enforcement. ABSTRACT Europe is entering a new phase of artificial intelligence in which autonomous systems no longer merely generate information—they increasingly initiate real-world consequences. AI agents can modify enterprise databases, operate cloud infrastructure, authorize financial transactions, control connected devices, manage industrial processes, change telecommunications configurations and coordinate multiple autonomous systems. For European critical infrastructure, the fundamental security question is therefore evolving: Who independently verifies that the operation actually about to take effect is still the operation that was authorized—and who has the technical power to prevent an unauthorized consequence? This patent-pending technical disclosure introduces a broad Protected Execution-Finality and Consequence-Bound Authorization Architecture, developed within the DAS Protocols research programme, for independently controlling consequential operations across autonomous AI, distributed computing, telecommunications, financial infrastructure and cyber-physical systems. The central technical distinction is between permission to compute, propose, prepare or request an operation and permission to produce its actual digital, financial, informational, computational or physical consequence. Conventional authentication, identity management, role-based access control, API security, AI governance, cryptographic verification, hardware isolation and audit logging provide essential protections. However, authorization obtained at an earlier processing stage does not necessarily establish that a subsequently transformed, delegated, accelerated or externally executed operation remains within the same authorized scope. The disclosed architecture represents a proposed operation as a Candidate Act, maintains the relevant consequence in a Non-Effective State, reconstructs the Actual Pending Operation, and independently validates current source authority, operation identity, material dependencies, execution context, evidence sufficiency, policy conditions, revocation state and consequence-specific constraints. When the applicable requirements are satisfied, the architecture establishes narrowly scoped execution authorization. A protected Finality Sink, implemented through suitable software, firmware, hardware, isolated services or hybrid mechanisms, controls whether the consequential effect may actually occur. The architecture may additionally employ authenticated execution evidence, bounded-effect staging, protected authority continuity, source-to-destination fencing, cumulative-effect accounting, transaction reconciliation and conditional continuation authorization. European Industry Relevance: Ericsson ·

title: Not to be served but to serve: cumulative employment precarity and later-life agency among older Chinese migrants in the United Kingdom
summary: Population ageing has led governments to seek ways to encourage older people to delay retirement using policy instruments such as increasing state pension ages, prohibiting workplace discrimination, and encouraging employers to recognise ol
content: Population ageing has led governments to seek ways to encourage older people to delay retirement using policy instruments such as increasing state pension ages, prohibiting workplace discrimination, and encouraging employers to recognise older workers as a source of skilled labour. Capacity to delay retirement is unevenly distributed and concerns have been raised about the impact of the Extended Working Life agenda on older people whose careers have been characterised by precarious work. This article explores the experiences of one such community: older migrants who have faced lifetimes of discrimination, language barriers, and institutional barriers to formal employment. This 2022 study examines how cumulative migration-related employment precarity shapes later-life work and retirement choices among older Chinese migrants in Manchester, United Kingdom, most of whom have spent their careers self-employed, running catering businesses. Drawing on Life-course Theory, we explore how factors such as migration timing, labour market structures, health, and economic, business and social relationships across time shape agency in later life as it relates to work and employment. Using a participatory qualitative design, researchers worked with the community radio programme Dragons Voice to conduct three four-hour workshops with seventeen Chinese migrants aged 60+ to discuss their experiences in paid employment and their perceptions of the United Kingdom government’s Extended Working Life agenda. Discussions took place in English, Cantonese and Mandarin. Findings show that while business opportunities in the catering sector provided vital access to income and stability, they also resulted in occupational confinement. Participants discussed their sense of loss regarding earlier careers and their desire to follow new vocations. Further, they discussed the impact that catering had on their mental and physical health and their scepticism about being able to continue in the sector into their sixties. However, they also described later life as an opportunity to contribute economically and socially through family care, volunteering, cultural participation, community support, and collectively organised economic activity, drawing on the ways they found work in the past as a blueprint for economic engagement in later life. We discuss the implications of the UK government’s policy agenda on older migrants.

title: What Do Australian Children and Adolescents Eat? A Systematic Review of Dietary Patterns and Adverse Health and Cognitive Outcomes
summary: Abstract Purpose of Review Dietary patterns during childhood and adolescence play a crucial role in health outcomes, yet evidence from Australian populations is limited. This systematic review aimed to synthesise available evidence on dieta
content: Abstract Purpose of Review Dietary patterns during childhood and adolescence play a crucial role in health outcomes, yet evidence from Australian populations is limited. This systematic review aimed to synthesise available evidence on dietary patterns and their impact on health- and cognition-related outcomes among Australian children and adolescents. Scopus, Medline, CINAHL, EmCare, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 6 December 2024, with an updated search on 21 November 2025. Studies examining dietary patterns in relation to health or cognitive outcomes were eligible. Findings were reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Recent Findings Seventeen studies were included (age range: 1–19 years). Eight studies (47.1%) drew on the same Western Australian Raine Study cohort, so sample sizes cannot be meaningfully summed across studies. The nine remaining studies were drawn from independent Australian cohorts. This reliance on a single cohort limits the generalisability of the findings to the broader Australian population. Factor or principal component analysis and reduced rank regression were used to derive dietary patterns. The 39 reported dietary patterns were grouped into two broad categories: a healthy pattern (high intake of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and fish) and an unhealthy pattern (high consumption of processed and energy-dense foods). A healthy dietary pattern was linked to better mental health and cognitive and academic performance. In contrast, an unhealthy dietary pattern was associated with poorer mental health and lower cognitive and academic outcomes. Associations with cardiometabolic outcomes were inconsistent. Eleven of the 17 studies were rated as high methodological quality and six as medium quality; no study was rated as low quality. Summary Across a small and methodologically heterogeneous body of Australian evidence, unhealthy dietary patterns were consistently associated with poorer mental health, cognitive, and academic outcomes, whereas evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes was inconsistent and did not support a firm conclusion in either direction. Because most studies (9 of 17, 52.9%) were cross-sectional and almost half (8, 47.1%) derived from a single cohort, these associations are suggestive rather than causal. Within these limitations, the findings add to the case for dietary interventions and public health strategies that promote healthy eating from early life, and highlight the need for stronger evidence from longitudinal studies. Systematic Review Registration PROSPERO registration no. CRD42025649056

title: The cultural impact of global digitalization on health promotion research
summary: Culture in contemporary health promotion research is characterized by hybridization, in which the economic, political, and technological forces of global digitalization continually interact with local contexts. Building on the theoretical p
content: Culture in contemporary health promotion research is characterized by hybridization, in which the economic, political, and technological forces of global digitalization continually interact with local contexts. Building on the theoretical perspective laid out in the seminal work Culture as a Variable in Health Research: Perspectives and Caveats and the subsequent decade of scholarship, this paper argues that health promotion research within globally digitalized ecosystems requires a reconceptualization of culture that is systematically operationalized throughout the entire research process. The argument is developed by discussing this new reconceptualization of culture and analyzing how it systematically shapes every stage of the research process, operationalized through the integrative lenses of cultural humility and cultural safety and illustrated by examples, from inception, including problem formulation, to methodological applications in sampling, recruitment, surveys, and interviews. The resulting synthesized perspective redefines culture in health promotion research as an evolving, dynamic, and ecological process. This reconceptualization reveals that the global–local interplay influences how individuals and communities perceive and enact health within their living contexts, which necessitates the integration of social determinants of health in the research process, as culture operates inextricably from emerging social structures. The paper introduces a novel operational framework that bridges contemporary cultural theory with rigorous methodological application, offering pathways that empower individuals and communities to achieve sustainable healthy lifestyles within globally digitalized ecosystems.

title: REGIME-SWITCHING SUSTAINABILITY STATISTICS (RSSS): DEFINITION,ARCHITECTURE AND APPLICATIONS TO PENSION AND CLIMATE SYSTEMS Unifying Multivariate Regime-Switching Stochastic Differential Equations, Markov Chain Transition Dynamics, Behavioral Survey Calibration, and Large-Scale Monte Carlo Simulation for Sustainable Development
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper defines and formalizes Regime-Switching Sustaianability Statistics (RSSS) as a new methodological field for the stochastic modeling of climate-resilient environmental,energy and pension sustainability systems under regime shifts.
content: This paper defines and formalizes Regime-Switching Sustaianability Statistics (RSSS) as a new methodological field for the stochastic modeling of climate-resilient environmental,energy and pension sustainability systems under regime shifts. Complex socio-economic, environmental, and actuarial systems are fundamentally characterized by deep structural uncertainty, volatility clustering, and abrupt regime transitions. Traditional deterministic models and single-regime stationary processes fail to capture these non-stationary realities, leading to severe underestimation of tail risks, solvency shortfalls, and sustainability failures. This foundational concept paper formally establishes Regime-Switching Sustainability Statistics (RSSS) as a novel methodological and philosophical paradigm pioneered by Daniel Kamaru Adamu (Adamu, 2025; Adamu, 2026). By defining RSSS as the overarching statistical framework that couples Multivariate Regime-Switching Stochastic Differential Equations (RS-SDE), Markov Chain state-transition dynamics, behavioral survey calibration (n = 673 respondents), and large-scale Monte Carlo simulation with long-term sustainability goals, this paper bridges theoretical stochastic calculus and applied sustainable development. Grounded in verified empirical datasets specifically the 1980–2022 and 2016–2025 historical macroeconomic/climate calibration windows and primary survey data RSSS provides robust, policy-relevant decision support across actuarial science, pension system reform, and environmental risk management. Keywords: Regime-Switching Sustainability Statistics (RSSS), Multivariate RS-SDE, Markov Chain Dynamics, Hybrid Pension Sustainability, Behavioral Calibration, Tail-Risk Quantification, Sustainable Development Planning

title: Targeting trimeric SOD1 with Amisodin mitigates TDP-43-associated ALS pathology
summary: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor neuron loss. Although TDP-43 and SOD1 aggregation are major molecular features of ALS, their mechanistic relationship rema
content: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor neuron loss. Although TDP-43 and SOD1 aggregation are major molecular features of ALS, their mechanistic relationship remains unclear. Here, we show that cytoplasmic TDP-43 induced by overexpression or cellular stress promotes SOD1 aggregation and preferentially interacts with trimer-associated SOD1 species. Destabilization of trimeric SOD1 disrupts the SOD1–TDP-43 interaction and reduces TDP-43 aggregation. Genetic depletion of SOD1 ameliorated motor dysfunction and neuronal loss in hTDP-43(+/+) mice, supporting a functional contribution of SOD1 to TDP-43 neurotoxicity. Pharmacological targeting of trimeric SOD1 with Amisodin reduced cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation, preserved neurons, improved motor function, and prolonged survival. Amisodin also reduced insoluble SOD1 and TDP-43 and their association in spinal cord tissue. These findings identify trimer-associated SOD1 as a functional modulator of TDP-43 proteotoxicity and support its selective targeting as a therapeutically actionable strategy for molecularly defined forms of TDP-43-associated ALS.

title: COVID‑19, Governance Quality, and FDI in Emerging Markets: A Panel Quantile Analysis
source: Journal of Accounting Business and Management (JABM)
summary: The paper investigates how governance quality shaped FDI inflows in emerging markets and how this relationship changed during the COVID‑19 pandemic. Drawing on data from 20 countries, covering both the pre‑COVID period (2010–2019) and the p
content: The paper investigates how governance quality shaped FDI inflows in emerging markets and how this relationship changed during the COVID‑19 pandemic. Drawing on data from 20 countries, covering both the pre‑COVID period (2010–2019) and the post‑COVID period (2020–2022), the study uses a non‑parametric panel quantile regression to assess distributional impacts. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of this method to governance and FDI dynamics in emerging markets during the pandemic.
