title: Spectral diffusion of phosphorous donors in silicon at high magnetic field
summary: We study the central spin physics of a phosphorus donor electron in silicon interacting with a silicon-29 bath at high magnetic field (8.59 T). We find that the spectral diffusion time is shorter and exhibits a larger anisotropy with respec
content: We study the central spin physics of a phosphorus donor electron in silicon interacting with a silicon-29 bath at high magnetic field (8.59 T). We find that the spectral diffusion time is shorter and exhibits a larger anisotropy with respect to crystal orientation in the magnetic field than in previous measurements at 0.35 T. The increased anisotropy suggests a modification of the hyperfine interactions at high field. The 1.2 THz cyclotron energy is a significant fraction of the 10.8 THz Rydberg energy of the bound donor, which can result in a non-trivial magnetic perturbation of the hydrogenic donor wavefunction. Low-power, above-bandgap optical excitation is seen to increase the spectral diffusion time, recovering the low-field spectral diffusion time at most crystal orientations. Understanding such perturbations to the spatial wavefunction of donor electron spins could be key to engineering their high-fidelity control.

title: Candidate gene prioritization through integration of public transcriptomic data and network analysis in sugarcane under water deficit
summary: Climate change-induced water deficit significantly threatens sugarcane ( Saccharum spp.) yields, yet breeding for drought tolerance remains challenging due to its complex polyploid genome. Here, we demonstrate the value of reusing publicly
content: Climate change-induced water deficit significantly threatens sugarcane ( Saccharum spp.) yields, yet breeding for drought tolerance remains challenging due to its complex polyploid genome. Here, we demonstrate the value of reusing publicly available sugarcane transcriptomic data to explore gene expression profiles under drought. We propose a candidate gene prioritization framework, combining the integration of public transcriptome data and biological network mapping. Sixteen RNA-seq BioProjects of sugarcane grown under contrasting water conditions were retrieved from the SRA-NCBI repository. The 352 libraries were processed through a standardized analytical pipeline, and differential expression analyses were performed independently for each BioProject. The aggregated differentially expressed transcripts were subjected to functional enrichment analyses, revealing highly represented functional categories and candidate genes associated with stress-responsive pathways, notably involving abscisic acid signaling, raffinose biosynthesis, and key transcription factor families. The list of candidate genes was consolidated into 342 functionally coherent categories representing biologically related processes. Among these, 109 categories were associated with pathways responsive to water deficit conditions. Despite the inherent biological and experimental variability across studies, integrative analyses enabled the identification of conserved functional responses and recurrent candidate regulators associated with water deficit. This study demonstrates the utility of large-scale transcriptomic data reuse combined with network analysis to prioritize candidate genes and explore core molecular mechanisms, providing valuable targets for improving sugarcane drought tolerance through molecular breeding or biotechnological interventions.

title: The effects and toxicological responses of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate on the gill tissue of bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis)
summary: Abstract This study evaluated the acute and subchronic toxicity of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) on gill tissue of bighead carp ( Hypophthalmichthys nobilis ). The 96-h LC₅₀ was 9.43mg/L. Fish were exposed to 0, 0.47, 0.95, and 1.89
content: Abstract This study evaluated the acute and subchronic toxicity of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) on gill tissue of bighead carp ( Hypophthalmichthys nobilis ). The 96-h LC₅₀ was 9.43mg/L. Fish were exposed to 0, 0.47, 0.95, and 1.89 mg/L (0, 1/20, 1/10, 1/5 of LC₅₀) for 7, 14, and 21 days. SDBS caused dose- and time-dependent gill histopathology (lamellar fusion, epithelial lifting, mucous/chloride cell changes, inflammation). Biochemical assays showed increased MDA and reduced SOD, CAT, GPx activities, indicating severe oxidative stress. Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity was significantly suppressed. qPCR revealed downregulation of sod , ca t, gpx , nkaα1 , and upregulation of hsp70 , il-1β , tnf-α , and * bax/bcl-2 * ratio. Correlation analyses confirmed oxidative stress as the primary mechanism. These findings demonstrate that SDBS causes substantial gill damage via oxidative pathways, posing ecological risks to local freshwater ecosystems.

title: Unveiling the Dark Matter Nature with Reionization Relics
summary: Abstract Dark matter constitutes roughly one-fourth of the Universe, yet its physical nature remains unknown. Warm dark matter (WDM), a class of dark matter candidates, has nonnegligible velocity dispersion that suppresses the formation of
content: Abstract Dark matter constitutes roughly one-fourth of the Universe, yet its physical nature remains unknown. Warm dark matter (WDM), a class of dark matter candidates, has nonnegligible velocity dispersion that suppresses the formation of small-scale cosmic structures. Current constraints therefore rely mainly on small-scale probes such as the Ly α forest and Milky Way observations of satellite galaxies and stellar streams. We propose a novel large-scale probe based on long-lived “reionization relics”: because the thermal and dynamical evolution of the intergalactic medium depends on the local reionization redshift, patchy reionization imprints additional large-scale fluctuations in Ly α forest opacity and post-reionization H I traced by 21 cm intensity mapping. The strength of these imprints depends on WDM through both small-scale gas evolution and WDM-driven changes in the reionization history. For example, the Ly α (21 cm) power spectrum in 3 keV WDM differs from cold dark matter by ≃19% (≃19%) at k = 0.05 Mpc −1 at z = 4 ( z = 5.5) when reionization relics are included. Using Ly α forest with a covariance model designed to mimic the capabilities of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we forecast a constraint of m WDM > 5.0 keV (95%), which improves to m WDM > 7.1 keV when combined with 21 cm intensity-mapping observations from the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). The next-generation surveys can further strengthen the current best lower bounds from 9.7 to 39 keV.

title: Photoelectrical readout and Ramsey interferometry of single shallowly implanted NV centers in diamond
summary: Photoelectrical readout of the electronic spin state of the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is attracting significant interest due to the numerous advantages it possesses compared with conventional fluorescence readout. The higher c
content: Photoelectrical readout of the electronic spin state of the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is attracting significant interest due to the numerous advantages it possesses compared with conventional fluorescence readout. The higher charge carrier rate compared to the photon rate and the integration of the detection scheme on a chip can significantly advance quantum sensing and computing with color centers in diamond. Until now, photoelectric readout has been performed on ensembles of NV centers or single NV centers deep in ultrapure diamond substrates. However, many applications require the artificial creation and precise placement of shallow NV centers, and photoelectric detection of such centers has been challenging. Here we demonstrate photoelectrical readout and coherent control of the electronic spin of implanted shallow ($\sim$10 nm) NV centers buried by diamond overgrowth. The photoelectrically measured Ramsey $T_2^*$ agrees with conventional fluorescence readout and shows no measurable dependence on the readout photocurrent, for both shallow implanted and deep ingrown NV centers. We further find that overgrowth improves photoelectric readout by suppressing the background photocurrent. These results establish photoelectric readout as a viable route to chip-integrated, electrically detected nanoscale sensing and to spin registers based on engineered shallow NV centers.

title: Label-free diagnosis of colorectal cancer using a SERS platform based on a modified glass fiber filter membrane combined with machine learning
summary: Abstract Non-invasive screening is critically important for the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer (CRC). Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has shown great potential in liquid biopsy, yet it still faces the challenge of poor signal
content: Abstract Non-invasive screening is critically important for the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer (CRC). Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has shown great potential in liquid biopsy, yet it still faces the challenge of poor signal reproducibility in complex serum matrices. In this study, a flexible three-dimensional SERS platform based on a 4-mercaptophenol (4-MP)-modified glass fiber filter membrane (GFF@4MP) was developed and combined with machine learning for label-free discrimination of CRC serum. Through sodium chloride modification, silver nanoparticles were uniformly immobilized onto the three-dimensional porous scaffold. Crucially, 4-MP, serving as a surface functionalization modifier, was able to modulate the interfacial physicochemical microenvironment and provide specific binding sites. This optimized the ordered adsorption of serum targets within SERS “hot spots”, significantly reduced non-specific interference, and improved spatial uniformity (relative standard deviation of 7.63%). In the analysis of clinical serum samples (30 CRC cases and 30 healthy controls), the substrate modified with 4-MP functional groups yielded SERS spectra with superior intergroup discrimination. Combined with principal component analysis (PCA), the support vector machine (SVM) model achieved the best classification performance on an independent test set, with a prediction accuracy of 93.33% and an area under the ROC curve (AUC) as high as 0.988. This study effectively enhanced the stability of SERS detection in complex biological samples through interfacial chemical modification, thereby providing a reliable methodological strategy for non-invasive clinical screening of colorectal cancer.

title: A multi-scale investigation of aqueous foams stabilised by PNIPAM microgels
summary: Aqueous foams possess multiple structural motifs across different length scales: macroscopic foam, bubbles, foam films and the air/water interface. In this study, macroscopic foams are generated by sparging gas through an aqueous dispersion
content: Aqueous foams possess multiple structural motifs across different length scales: macroscopic foam, bubbles, foam films and the air/water interface. In this study, macroscopic foams are generated by sparging gas through an aqueous dispersion of PNIPAM microgels which act as foam stabilisers due to their surface activity. The stiffness of the microgels and thus their interfacial activity are tuned by variation of the cross-linker density. The effect of the cross-linker density and the microgel concentration on the resulting foam formation properties (foamability) and the foam stability are investigated. A lower cross-linker density and a higher microgel concentration enhance the foamability, generate foams with smaller bubbles and higher liquid fractions, and increase the foam stability. These observations are correlated with the microgel behavior at the single air/water interface examined by pendant drop tensiometry, Langmuir compression and atomic force microscopy as well as the mobility in single free-standing foam films determined using a thin film pressure balance. Our findings highlight good agreement across all length scales: increased foamability correlates with a faster decrease in surface tension, and higher foam stability with reduced mobility in foam films. In addition, differences in foamability alter the macroscopic foam structure (bubble size and liquid fraction), which also influences the foam stability in our systems.

title: VortexChat: Autonomous design of photonic devices from natural language
summary: Abstract The advancement of modern photonics is frequently bottlenecked by device design workflows that rely heavily on manual simulation and expert intuition. Although existing photonic inverse-design methods have largely automated paramet
content: Abstract The advancement of modern photonics is frequently bottlenecked by device design workflows that rely heavily on manual simulation and expert intuition. Although existing photonic inverse-design methods have largely automated parameter optimization, they still rely on researchers to formulate optimization objectives, construct predefined workflows, and diagnose or recover from unsuccessful optimization trajectories. To address these issues, we introduce VortexChat, an agentic framework that translates natural-language specifications into photonic designs. VortexChat autonomously orchestrates generative models, gradient-based optimization, and automated full-wave electromagnetic simulations, updating design strategies based on feedback. We demonstrate VortexChat through the autonomous design of a broadband terahertz perfect vortex beam multiplexer, a challenging task for conventional manual design approaches. Evaluated on the Vortex100 Benchmark, VortexChat achieves a 71% overall success rate under the simultaneous constraints of efficiency, mode purity, and broadband performance. Experimental measurements validate the resulting device, demonstrating mode purity exceeding 84% across the operating band, together with high efficiency and low inter-channel crosstalk. By reducing reliance on expert intervention, VortexChat offers a route toward more accessible and autonomous development of complex photonic devices.

title: Accelerating systems as probes of Lorentz violation
summary: We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for
content: We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for Lorentz violation. The dispersion relation, Hamiltonian, and massless and massive Wightman functions are obtained. We determine the conditions under which the scalar dynamics preserves boost symmetry and distinguish these from the weaker conditions required for stationarity along a single accelerated worldline. The Wightman functions are used to construct the finite-time Unruh-DeWitt response for a uniformly accelerated detector. For generic coefficients the response is nonstationary and depends on both the duration and temporal location of the measurement. The spectrum, which is the resulting excitation rate as a function of the energy level difference in the detector, is obtained numerically. It shows discernable differences with the usual massive thermal spectrum for dimensionless coefficients on the order of 10^{-7}. Experimental implications of the result are discussed. As an alternative viewpoint, we place Lorentz violation in the point-particle sector, derive the exact trajectory generated by a constant electric field, and study the proper-time Fourier response of a conventional scalar wave along the modified trajectory.

title: Anomalous Pressure‐Dependent Viscosity of Basaltic Melts and Its Role in Asthenosphere Melt Accumulation
summary: Abstract The asthenosphere's mechanical weakness enables plate tectonics, but its origin is debated. Partial melt has been proposed to cause this softening, yet recent studies suggest that the measured viscosity minimum in basaltic melts—an
content: Abstract The asthenosphere's mechanical weakness enables plate tectonics, but its origin is debated. Partial melt has been proposed to cause this softening, yet recent studies suggest that the measured viscosity minimum in basaltic melts—an essential control on melt mobility—is an experimental artifact. Using quantum mechanics‐based, machine learning‐accelerated molecular dynamics, we extend simulation timescales by >10 3 and achieve percent‐level precision. We show that basaltic melt exhibits a robust viscosity minimum (∼20% below 1‐bar values) at ∼3 GPa, driven by pressure‐induced reorganization of aluminum coordination that facilitates shear relaxation while silicon–oxygen polyhedra remain structurally rigid. Our results reveal a depth‐dependent rheological transition: melt mobility peaks below ∼150 km, promoting efficient extraction, but declines sharply during ascent, causing melt to stagnate beneath the lithosphere. This mechanism provides a physical basis for the dual seismic signatures of a melt‐depleted deep asthenosphere and a melt‐enriched layer near the lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary.

title: Velocity-resolved Ionization Mapping of the Broad-line Region. II. Signatures of Eccentric Broad-line Regions from a Quantitative Photoionization-based Model
summary: Abstract Velocity-resolved reverberation mapping (RM) is one of the most powerful tools for probing the geometry and kinematics of the broad-line region (BLR) in active galactic nuclei (AGNs). However, its interpretation may be nonunique, a
content: Abstract Velocity-resolved reverberation mapping (RM) is one of the most powerful tools for probing the geometry and kinematics of the broad-line region (BLR) in active galactic nuclei (AGNs). However, its interpretation may be nonunique, as similar velocity-delay signatures can arise from different combinations of BLR geometry and kinematics. To address this degeneracy, this series of studies develops velocity-resolved ionization mapping (IM) as a complementary technique. In this second paper of the series, we construct photoionization-based BLR models to quantitatively demonstrate the diagnostic power of the joint RM+IM framework. We calculate local H α and H β emissivities with C loudy , couple them with disk-like BLR models, and generate synthetic velocity-dependent line fluxes, lags, and Balmer decrements (BDs). The model reproduces the observed anticorrelation between the integrated BD and the incident ionizing continuum, with scatter naturally introduced by reverberation delays. We show that a virialized elliptical BLR can produce diverse velocity-delay maps and velocity-resolved lags that mimic RM signatures commonly attributed to virialized motion, inflow, or outflow. In contrast, the velocity-resolved BD is sensitive to the symmetry of the BLR gas distribution, providing a key diagnostic for distinguishing eccentric geometry from nonvirial motions. Through proof-of-concept comparisons with one double-peaked and one single-peaked AGN, we show that an elliptical-disk BLR can simultaneously reproduce the observed line profiles, velocity-resolved lags, and velocity-resolved BDs. These results provide a quantitative basis for IM, support the presence of eccentric BLR structures in AGNs, and demonstrate the potential of joint RM+IM analyses to break the BLR geometry-kinematics degeneracy. This framework has important implications for identifying geometry-induced biases and improving reverberation-based black hole mass measurements.

title: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries. I. the effects of stellar evolution
summary: Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. Wide binary companions can influence the delivery of planetary material onto white dwarfs, making it essent
content: Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. Wide binary companions can influence the delivery of planetary material onto white dwarfs, making it essential to understand the interplay between stellar evolution and binary perturbations. We investigate how uncertainties in stellar mass-loss histories affect the dynamical evolution of remnant planetary systems in wide binaries, and assess their relative importance compared with binary perturbations in driving the accretion of rocky material onto white dwarfs. We performed N-body simulations incorporating time-dependent stellar parameters interpolated from evolutionary tracks and tidal interactions, following the dynamical evolution up to the white dwarf stage. We explored two stellar-evolution models with distinct mass-loss histories for wide binary systems hosting a Jupiter-mass planet and a planetesimal disc, spanning a range of binary architectures. REBOUND MESA The adopted stellar-evolution model has only a minor effect on the survival of the planet, mainly affecting the timing and efficiency of planetesimal delivery during the white dwarf stage. Instead, the architecture of the binary primarily controls the pollution outcome: wider binaries produce the highest rates of accretion onto the white dwarf, consistent with the observed prevalence of polluted white dwarfs in wide binaries. Moreover, planetesimal reservoirs remain long-lived, with survival times increasing with binary separation, enabling gigayear-long metal pollution. Our results suggest that the architecture of wide binaries, rather than uncertainties in stellar evolution, is the dominant factor controlling the dynamical delivery of rocky material onto white dwarfs.

title: Salpyran ligands at the interface of copper chemistry and biology: structure–function relationships, metal selectivity, redox control, and biological interactions
summary: Cu radiolabelling shows PET imaging compatibility, though Fe(III) competition requires framework refinement. Cytotoxicity studies reveal context-dependent antiproliferative activity: copper coordination enhances potency in most cancer lines
content: Cu radiolabelling shows PET imaging compatibility, though Fe(III) competition requires framework refinement. Cytotoxicity studies reveal context-dependent antiproliferative activity: copper coordination enhances potency in most cancer lines but reduces it in carboplatin-resistant NSCLC models, without cross-resistance. This work establishes Salpyran as a versatile platform and provides design principles linking ligand structure, metal selectivity, redox behaviour, and biological activity.

title: TIPE2 suppresses adipogenesis via METTL14-mediated m6A methylation and represents a potential therapeutic target for obesity
summary: Abstract Despite conserved mechanisms maintaining energy homeostasis, the global obesity epidemic continues to rise. Tumor necrosis factor-α-induced protein 8-like 2 (TIPE2) is an anti-inflammatory regulator essential for immune homeostasis
content: Abstract Despite conserved mechanisms maintaining energy homeostasis, the global obesity epidemic continues to rise. Tumor necrosis factor-α-induced protein 8-like 2 (TIPE2) is an anti-inflammatory regulator essential for immune homeostasis, yet its role in adipogenesis remains unclear. Here, we show that TIPE2 expression in human adipose tissue is inversely correlated with body mass index (BMI) and metabolic dysfunction. In mice, Tipe2 deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity, hyperglycaemia, and insulin resistance, whereas systemic AAV-mediated TIPE2 overexpression alleviates these phenotypes. In vitro, TIPE2 suppresses adipogenic differentiation in primary preadipocytes. Mechanistically, TIPE2 regulates N6-methyladenosine (m6A) via m6A methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14). Loss of TIPE2 reduces m6A levels and METTL14 expression, whereas METTL14 restoration reverses the pro-adipogenic effects. Furthermore, TIPE2 modulates adipogenesis through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) signaling. Together, these findings identify TIPE2 as a suppressor of adipogenesis via coordinated regulation of METTL14-dependent m6A modification and PPAR-γ signaling.

title: Self-Healable Solid Polymer Electrolytes Produced by Photopolymerization of Zinc Ion-Based Deep Eutectic Monomers
summary: Abstract Zinc ion batteries are promising alternatives to lithium-ion systems because of their abundance, intrinsic safety, and high volumetric capacity; however, their development is hindered by the lack of compatible electrolytes. In this
content: Abstract Zinc ion batteries are promising alternatives to lithium-ion systems because of their abundance, intrinsic safety, and high volumetric capacity; however, their development is hindered by the lack of compatible electrolytes. In this study, an alternative strategy is reported for fabricating ion-conductive and self-healable solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on zinc ion deep eutectic monomers (DEMs), aiming to create zinc ion-based SPEs applicable for zinc ion batteries with green chemistry concept. Binary and ternary DEMs were prepared from the biocompatible cyclic amide N-vinylcaprolactam (NVCL) and zinc salts (Zn(TFSI)2 and Zn(OTf)2), with succinonitrile (SN) serving as a flexible crystalline additive. Liquid DEM formation was driven by specific Zn2+–amide interactions, enabling hydrogen-bond-donor-free eutectics that underwent near-quantitative photopolymerization within 60–180 s under ambient conditions. The optimized P(NVCL/Zn(TFSI)2/SN) solid electrolyte exhibited an ionic conductivity of 2.96 × 10–4 and 2.25 × 10–6 S cm–1 at 90 and 55 °C, a stable electrochemical window of up to 3.0 V vs Zn2+/Zn, and rapid self-healing (>50% recovery within 5 min at room temperature). The P(NVCL/Zn(TFSI)2/SN)s exhibited relatively high Young’s moduli of 654–659 MPa and remained thermally stable above 170 °C. These findings provide insights into the potential of NVCL/zinc ion-based DEMs as nonaqueous electrolytes for the production of self-healable, ion-conductive SPEs and pave the way for solvent-free, atom-economical, and sustainable zinc ion-based batteries.

title: ELECTROSPUN NANOFIBER-BASED THERAPEUTIC SYSTEMS FOR SKIN CANCER MANAGEMENT
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Skin cancer represents a growing global health burden with limited efficacy from conventional treatment approaches. Electrospun nanofibers have emerged as promising drug delivery platforms for localized skin cancer therapy, offering advanta
content: Skin cancer represents a growing global health burden with limited efficacy from conventional treatment approaches. Electrospun nanofibers have emerged as promising drug delivery platforms for localized skin cancer therapy, offering advantages including large surface area, tunable porosity, and capacity to maintain drug levels at the tumor site while minimizing systemic exposure. This review consolidates recent advances in electrospinning-based systems for dermatological malignancies, emphasizing material selection, therapeutic incorporation strategies, and functional modifications that enhance treatment effectiveness and skin penetration. Clinical translation challenges and regulatory considerations are addressed to provide a comprehensive overview of electrospun nanofiber technology for future clinical applications in skin cancer management. Additionally, clinical translation challenges, regulatory considerations, and future perspectives encompassing stimuli-responsive systems, targeted delivery, and scalable manufacturing are addressed. Overall, electrospun nanofibers hold significant potential as next-generation, patientfriendly platforms for effective and safe localized skin cancer therapy.

title: Novel Triple-action Pt(IV) prodrugs with carbocyanine and chalcone in axial position: photoactivation, tumor targeting, fluorescent tumor visualization, and high therapeutic efficacy
summary: Pt(IV) prodrugs are highly promising platform for anticancer agents due to the ability to fine-tune the structure and properties of the prodrug by varying the axial ligand conjugated with the Pt(IV) core. In this study, we have synthesized
content: Pt(IV) prodrugs are highly promising platform for anticancer agents due to the ability to fine-tune the structure and properties of the prodrug by varying the axial ligand conjugated with the Pt(IV) core. In this study, we have synthesized photoactivated Pt(IV) prodrugs with NIR-absorbing cyanine and chalcone in axial positions, which combine the advantages of dual-target chemotherapy, controlled photoactivation, photodynamic therapy, and fluorescent NIR bioimaging. The cyanine-chalcone-based prodrug Pt-4 demonstrated the ability to generate ROS, release carboplatin intracellularly and promote p53 expression under 660 nm light. Pt-4 prodrug demonstrated superior pharmacokinetic properties to carboplatin and excellent fluorescent imaging of CT-26 tumors. In vivo, Pt-4 prodrug + 660 nm light stimulated adaptive immune response in LLC tumors and significantly inhibited tumor growth of homograft CT-26 tumor. Our findings demonstrate excellent potential of Pt(IV)-carbocyanine light-activatable platform for tumor imaging, drug delivery and tumor eradication.

title: Synergistic hydrogen sulfide mitigation in sour crude oil using green‐synthesized copper nanoparticles and chemical scavengers
summary: Abstract Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) in sour crude oil poses significant operational, environmental, and safety challenges due to its toxicity and corrosive properties. This study examined the preliminary performance of green‐synthesized coppe
content: Abstract Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) in sour crude oil poses significant operational, environmental, and safety challenges due to its toxicity and corrosive properties. This study examined the preliminary performance of green‐synthesized copper nanoparticles (CuNPs), prepared using Biebersteinia multifida root extract, as an additional treatment alongside the commercial H 2 S scavenger MAKS 9185. Laboratory batch experiments used 250 mL crude‐oil samples with an initial estimated H 2 S concentration of 915 ppm. The commercial scavenger was applied at a fixed nominal dosage, while the CuNP preparation was added at volumetric ratios of 0.8% to 12.8% relative to the initial crude‐oil volume. Residual H 2 S concentrations were estimated using a Dräger‐based measurement procedure after a prescribed 30‐min settling period. Treatment with the scavenger alone reduced the estimated H 2 S concentration to 15 ppm, yielding a calculated removal efficiency of 98.36%. Adding the CuNP preparation at a nominal dosage of 4.8% resulted in a lower reported residual concentration of 3 ppm, equivalent to a calculated removal efficiency of 99.67%. This was an 80% reduction in residual H 2 S compared with the scavenger‐only treatment. Increasing the nominal CuNP preparation dosage to 12.8% produced no further measurable improvement. These findings offer preliminary evidence that combining plant‐mediated copper nanoparticle preparations with a commercial chemical scavenger may further reduce residual H 2 S under laboratory conditions. However, independent experimental replication, analytical validation, component‐specific controls, and quantitative evaluation of copper recovery and process feasibility are needed before the treatment's reproducibility, mechanisms, and practical advantages can be confirmed.

title: System-Level Analysis of a DCMD and PEMWE Integrated System for Hydrogen and Water Cogeneration
summary: The integration of desalination and hydrogen production offers a promising pathway to simultaneously address water scarcity and clean energy demands. This study evaluated the feasibility and performance of coupled direct contact membrane di
content: The integration of desalination and hydrogen production offers a promising pathway to simultaneously address water scarcity and clean energy demands. This study evaluated the feasibility and performance of coupled direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) and proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) systems for water–hydrogen cogeneration. A validated steady-state model was developed, incorporating coupled heat and mass transfer in DCMD and electrochemical, thermal, and hydrogen production models for PEMWE. A parametric analysis was conducted under two operational scenarios: (i) full coupling with zero net water output, and (ii) cogeneration of freshwater and hydrogen. The results indicate that system operation is constrained by the balance between DCMD production and PEMWE consumption, yielding a maximum current density of 2.29 A/cm² for a 50 cm² (1–2 kW) electrolyzer supported by a 200 cm² DCMD membrane. The net water production decreased from approximately 0.70 kg/h at zero current density to zero at this limit. The system efficiency decreased with increasing current density owing to rising activation and ohmic losses, as well as higher cooling requirements. By contrast, increasing stack temperature from 50 to 80 °C reduced cell voltage and improved overall efficiency, while lowering cooling demand. The feed temperature strongly enhanced the DCMD productivity, enabling higher feasible operating current densities. In the cogeneration mode, increasing the membrane area to 0.5 m² enabled simultaneous operation, with more than 95% of the produced water remaining available as useful output. These findings provide design insights for the development of water-efficient green hydrogen systems, particularly for deployment in water-limited regions

title: LDN 1622: Anomalous Emission in a Dark Cloud and the Small-Grain Survival Budget
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: LDN 1622, a cold dark cloud with dust temperatures near 12 kelvin, shows anomalous microwave emission near 30 gigahertz at a flux density near 12 janskys in published Green Bank Telescope measurements, weaker per unit dust column than in wa
content: LDN 1622, a cold dark cloud with dust temperatures near 12 kelvin, shows anomalous microwave emission near 30 gigahertz at a flux density near 12 janskys in published Green Bank Telescope measurements, weaker per unit dust column than in warmer clouds, testing whether the smallest grains survive or are depleted where starlight barely penetrates. The budget converts the adopted anomalous flux into an emissivity normalised by hydrogen column and by 100-micron brightness for direct comparison with the Perseus and rho Ophiuchi budgets, bounds the free-free share from the absence of ionised-gas tracers, and expresses the measured emissivity as a fraction of the warm-cloud value to size the small-grain depletion the dark environment implies. Headline values are ldn1622 ame flux 30ghz jy ldn1622 = 12; ldn1622 hydrogen column per cm2 ldn1622 = 2.5e+22; ldn1622 ame emissivity column units ldn1622 = 1.024e-18; ldn1622 perseus emissivity reference ldn1622 = 9.8; ldn1622 depletion factor vs perseus ldn1622 = 1.045e-19; ldn1622 dust temperature k ldn1622 = 12. Stating the result as a surviving fraction rather than a bare emissivity is what connects a flux measurement to the grain-evolution question the cloud was chosen to answer.

title: A novel role of NOX2 in enhancing HBV replication through ROS‑mediated autophagy activation
summary: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NO
content: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NOX2 affects HBV infection remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the potential role of NOX2 in HBV replication was investigated in cell models. First, it was demonstrated that NOX2 is highly expressed in transiently and stably HBV‑infected cells. Second, by employing inhibitor, RNA interference technique and plasmid overexpression, it was revealed that NOX2 plays an essential role in promoting HBV replication. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of how NOX2 affects HBV replication was illustrated. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication. These results suggested a previously unrecognized role of NOX2 in HBV replication. Taken together, NOX2 may serve as a novel target for developing treatment strategies against HBV‑related disorders.

title: Comparison of aluminum and iron electrodes for electrocoagulation of automotive cataphoresis wastewater: removal performance and operating cost
summary: This study investigated the applicability of the electrocoagulation (EC) process to wastewater generated by the electrocoating (cataphoresis) process used in the painting of vehicle bodies. Samples were obtained from an automotive factory i
content: This study investigated the applicability of the electrocoagulation (EC) process to wastewater generated by the electrocoating (cataphoresis) process used in the painting of vehicle bodies. Samples were obtained from an automotive factory in Bursa, Türkiye. In a laboratory-scale EC reactor equipped with Al–Al or Fe–Fe electrodes, the operating parameters that govern the removal of chemical oxygen demand (COD) and total phosphorus (TP) — inter-electrode distance, current density, and reaction time — were optimized. A Box–Behnken response surface design (Design-Expert 12.0) was used to construct mathematical models, whose adequacy was assessed by analysis of variance (ANOVA). Under the optimum conditions for Al electrodes, removal efficiencies of 74.88% (COD) and 95.37% (TP) were achieved individually, and 74.72% (COD) and 79.28% (TP) simultaneously. With Fe electrodes, the highest measured COD removal was 83.3%, and the TP removal was 61.42% individually and 83.30% (COD) and 46.20% (TP) simultaneously; the quadratic model fitted to the Fe–COD data was not statistically significant and was therefore used only descriptively. Operating costs at current (July 2026) unit prices were 63.8 TL/m³ (US$ 1.35) for Al electrodes and 72.6 TL/m³ (US$ 1.54) for Fe electrodes.

title: Effect of plant-based compost on the growth and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage under salt stress in peat-based growing media
summary: Soil salinity is one of the major abiotic stress factors limiting the growth, ornamental quality, and performance of ornamental plants. This study investigated the effects of different compost application rates on plant growth, morphologica
content: Soil salinity is one of the major abiotic stress factors limiting the growth, ornamental quality, and performance of ornamental plants. This study investigated the effects of different compost application rates on plant growth, morphological characteristics, phytochemical composition, and antioxidant defense mechanisms in ornamental cabbage ( Brassica oleracea var. acephala ‘Pigeon Red F1’) under salt stress. The experiment was conducted as a two-factor factorial design consisting of three compost rates (0, 20, and 40%) and four NaCl concentrations (0, 25, 50, and 75 mM). Morphological traits, chlorophyll content (SPAD), root characteristics, antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, POD, and SOD), oxidative stress indicators (MDA and H₂O₂), total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, DPPH radical scavenging activity, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) were evaluated. Compost significantly affected plant height, plant diameter, leaf number, plant fresh weight, root length, root fresh weight, and root dry weight. Increasing compost rates generally reduced plant height, plant diameter, and leaf number, whereas mean root length increased. Salinity significantly affected plant height, leaf number, and SPAD values. Compost × salinity interactions were significant for plant height, leaf length, SPAD values, and catalase activity, indicating that responses to salinity depended on the compost rate. Neither compost nor salinity nor their interaction significantly affected plant dry weight or central coloration diameter. The 20% compost treatment improved maintenance of total flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity under moderate salinity conditions, while the 40% compost treatment increased total phenolic content under non-saline conditions. Salinity significantly altered antioxidant enzyme activities and oxidative stress markers, whereas catalase activity, root length, root dry weight, and central coloration diameter were not significantly affected. Overall, compost application modified the physiological and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage to salt stress in a dose-dependent manner. These findings indicate that compost application may help maintain ornamental quality and improve stress tolerance under saline cultivation conditions, providing a sustainable strategy for ornamental cabbage production.

title: Constructing Ultra-Stable NiFe LDH Catalysts to Achieve Adaptability of Industrial-Level Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis for Fluctuating Power Supply
summary: Abstract Water electrolysis powered by renewable energy is a promising approach toward sustainable and clean energy. However, such devices demand catalytic electrodes that can stably and swiftly adapt to fluctuating renewable energy. Herein
content: Abstract Water electrolysis powered by renewable energy is a promising approach toward sustainable and clean energy. However, such devices demand catalytic electrodes that can stably and swiftly adapt to fluctuating renewable energy. Herein, the NiFe LDH electrode is fabricated by magnetron sputtering coupled with a chemical route, which enables efficient and stable water electrolysis under fluctuating electricity owing to its strong interfacial bonding and abundant active sites. The morphology and performance of NiFe LDH materials are controlled by regulating the Al content in the precursor. Importantly, NiFe LDH-3 displays excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance with an overpotential of 292 mV at 100 mA cm–2 and 335 mV at 300 mA cm–2. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), this catalyst achieves a low cell voltage of 1.71 V at 1 A cm–2 and maintains stability for over 300 h in 1 M KOH at 80 °C, with a voltage degradation rate of 0.035 mV h–1. Notably, the electrolyzer shows excellent adaptability to fluctuating renewable power, exhibiting a voltage degradation of only 0.186 mV per cycle over 430 cycles in start–stop experiments. This work presents a catalyst designed by combining magnetron sputtering with a chemical method, achieving the adaptability of the AEMWE to fluctuating power, which will accelerate the coupling of AEMWE technology with fluctuating renewable energy to realize green hydrogen production.

title: Fixed-Demand Multifidelity Modeling and Capacity–Energy Design of Industrial Alkaline Water Electrolysis for Green Ammonia
summary: Abstract Industrial alkaline water electrolysis for green ammonia requires capacity–energy decisions across model fidelities at the same hydrogen duty. A fixed-demand multifidelity framework combines 200 Shortcut simulations with 24 nested
content: Abstract Industrial alkaline water electrolysis for green ammonia requires capacity–energy decisions across model fidelities at the same hydrogen duty. A fixed-demand multifidelity framework combines 200 Shortcut simulations with 24 nested Rigorous training cases and 16 held-out Rigorous test cases at 11.12 t h–1 net H2. Fixed-demand fidelity matching removes throughput as a source of apparent performance differences, while response-specific fidelity selection retains low-fidelity information only when it improves prediction. Shortcut information does not preserve the Rigorous specific electricity consumption (SEC) ranking, whereas current density retains a cross-fidelity relationship. The final SEC representation uses Rigorous training data alone and gives a held-out root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.068 kWh kg–1 H2. Direct Rigorous calculations confirm minimum-area, knee, and minimum-energy alternatives spanning 52,800–93,600 m2 and 65.28–57.14 kWh kg–1 H2. Within this domain, fixed-demand electrification design requires joint consideration of electricity use and installed electrochemical capacity, with model fidelity selected by response.

title: Combined Action of Plasma-driven Co-generated Hydrated Electrons and Persulfate Radicals for mineralization via Reduction/Oxidation of Perfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)
source: Journal of Technological and Space Plasmas
summary: Plasma water treatment, in recent years, has outperformed other technologies in its capability to abate perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in water matrices. Recent computational experiements (J. Technol. Space Plasmas, vol. 6, no. 1, pp. 202
content: Plasma water treatment, in recent years, has outperformed other technologies in its capability to abate perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in water matrices. Recent computational experiements (J. Technol. Space Plasmas, vol. 6, no. 1, pp. 202–217, May 2025, doi: 10.31281/vab52w73) with Chemical Reaction Network (CRN) suggestes that plasma-phase H-radical are the direct couse of PFAS reduction and abatment when employing an electrified plasma/liquid interface (EPLI), a hypothesis that has not yet been experimentally validated. The same study demonstrates that EPLI-induced hydrated electrons ( ) reduce PFAS with poor extension (low Faradaic efficiency) due to low PFOA concentration. In the present contribution, CRN computational experiments were performed to demonstrate how EPLI-induced can activate , enabling the local production of additional radicals instead of sollelly allowing to reduce water. The CRN computational results allowed us to demonstrate the combined action of and radicals as a strategy for PFAS mineralization (convertion into CO2). Without optimizations, PFAS mineralization and abatment reached 13% due to the action of (5 mM of S2O8− and 8mA) and 90% due to the action of , respectively. The use of EPLI-induzed to activated radicals is proposed here for the very first time, while the corresponding bench-scale proof remains to be experimentally demonstrated.

title: Neuropharmacological and hypoglycemic activities of methanolic tubers extract of Pachyrhizus tuberosus: integrated in vivo and in silico evaluation
source: Beni-Suef University Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences
summary: Background Pachyrhizus tuberosus (Amazonian yam bean) is an edible tuberous legume that has long been used in tropical South America to treat pyrexia, skin diseases, itching, and gastrointestinal and stomach issues. Despite its ethnomedicin
content: Background Pachyrhizus tuberosus (Amazonian yam bean) is an edible tuberous legume that has long been used in tropical South America to treat pyrexia, skin diseases, itching, and gastrointestinal and stomach issues. Despite its ethnomedicinal significance, its potential neuropharmacological and hypoglycemic effects have not been well studied. The purpose of this work was to assess the anxiolytic, antidepressant-like, sedative, and hypoglycemic properties of the methanolic extract of P. tuberosus tubers (MTPT) utilizing experimental animal models, supplemented by computer analysis. Methods Pharmacological evaluation was done in Swiss albino mice. Anxiolytic activity was evaluated by Hole-Board Test (HBT) and Elevated Plus Maze (EPM). The antidepressant activity was assessed by the Forced Swimming Test (FST) and Tail Suspension Test (TST). Sedative activities were evaluated by Open Field Test (OFT) and Hole-Cross Test (HCT), and hypoglycemic activity was measured by Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT). GC–MS analysis was performed for identification of phytochemical constituents of MTPT. The pharmacological potential of the identified secondary metabolites was validated through in silico studies including molecular docking (AutoDock Vina and Discovery Studio 2021), PASS prediction and ADME/T profiling. Results MTPT showed significant dose-dependent anxiolytic, antidepressant, sedative and hypoglycemic activities. The extract administration at 400 mg/kg (p < 0.001) significantly improved the anxiolytic effects in HBT and EPM, reduced the immobility time in FST and TST (p < 0.001), and greatly inhibited locomotor activity in OFT and HCT, indicating strong sedative effects (p < 0.001). The same dose also significantly decreased blood glucose levels within two hours in the OGTT (p < 0.05). GC-MS/MS identified many bioactive compounds, and molecular docking showed a good binding affinity with docking scores of − 3.1 to − 7.5 kcal/mol, which supports the biological activities observed. Conclusion The methanol extract of P. tuberosus tubers exhibits promising anxiolytic, antidepressant, sedative, and hypoglycemic effects in experimental models. Both in vivo and in silico findings endorse that P. tuberosus is a potential natural source of bioactive compounds such as (Phthalic acid, Gorlic acid, Benzenepropanoic acid, 2,4-Di-tert-butylphenol3,5-bis(1,1-dimethylethyl)-4-hydroxy-, methyl ester) for developing therapeutic agents against anxiety, depression, insomnia, and hyperglycemia. title: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA)-mediated amplification of MMP2 is associated with UV-induced photoaging of human skin
summary: Abstract UVB radiation induces skin photoaging through ROS-mediated activation of MMPs and subsequent collagen degradation. Although extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) drives oncogene amplification in cancer, its involvement in non-neoplastic agi
content: Abstract UVB radiation induces skin photoaging through ROS-mediated activation of MMPs and subsequent collagen degradation. Although extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) drives oncogene amplification in cancer, its involvement in non-neoplastic aging processes remains unknown. Here, paired eyelid and medial upper arm skin specimens from three individuals are analyzed by histology, immunohistochemistry, and Circle-seq. Eyelid skin exhibits classic photoaging features and significantly higher ecDNA abundance. Circle-seq and FISH reveal enrichment of MMP2-carrying ecDNA in photoaged tissues and UVB-irradiated HaCaT cells, with circular junctions confirmed by Sanger sequencing. UVB exposure time-dependently increases ecDNA formation and MMP2 expression in vitro. In normal human epidermal keratinocytes (NHEK, p53-wildtype), UVB irradiation similarly induces ecDNA accumulation, confirming this phenomenon is not restricted to transformed cells. Pharmacological rescue experiments using Anisomycin demonstrate that olaparib-mediated MMP2 suppression is independent of p38/EGFR signaling, consistent with an ecDNA-dependent mechanism. Notably, the PARP inhibitor olaparib suppresses UVB-induced ecDNA amplification and reverses MMP2 upregulation at both mRNA and protein levels. These findings demonstrate that ecDNA-mediated MMP2 amplification contributes to UV-induced photoaging in human skin and reveal ecDNA formation as a mechanistic vulnerability in photoaging.

title: Dual Electric-Field Coupling in a Mo2TiC2/ZnIn2S4 Schottky Heterojunction Enables Efficient Piezo-Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
summary: Abstract Developing efficient and sustainable strategies for hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis is highly desirable for green energy conversion and environmental applications. Herein, a tightly integrated Mo2TiC2/ZnIn2S4 Schottky heterojunc
content: Abstract Developing efficient and sustainable strategies for hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis is highly desirable for green energy conversion and environmental applications. Herein, a tightly integrated Mo2TiC2/ZnIn2S4 Schottky heterojunction was successfully fabricated via a one-step hydrothermal method. Benefiting from the synergistic coupling of ultrasonic vibration and light irradiation, the optimized Mo2TiC2/ZnIn2S4-2 catalyst achieves an impressive H2O2 production rate of 6.67 mmol·g–1·h–1, which is 4.95 and 4.07 times higher than those of pristine Mo2TiC2 (1.35 mmol·g–1·h–1) and ZnIn2S4 (1.64 mmol·g–1·h–1), respectively, in a mixed solution of deionized water and ethanol. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the superior piezo-photocatalytic activity originates from the dual-electric-field coupling effect between the piezoelectric polarization field and the Schottky built-in electric field. This unique interfacial configuration not only promotes directional charge separation and migration but also accelerates the coupled oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and water oxidation reaction (WOR) pathways for H2O2 generation. In particular, Mo2TiC2 serves as an efficient electron sink and an ORR active platform, while ZnIn2S4 functions as a hole-enriched center to facilitate WOR. Radical trapping experiments confirm that superoxide radicals (·O2–) are the dominant reactive intermediates during H2O2 formation. Furthermore, the composite exhibits excellent cycling stability and structural robustness without obvious activity decay after five consecutive cycles. This work demonstrates an effective dual-electric-field engineering strategy for efficient piezo-photocatalytic H2O2 production and provides new insights into the design of MXene-based piezo-photocatalysts for sustainable energy and environmental applications.

title: Influence of Halogen Incorporation on the Structural and Electrocatalytic Properties of Co-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks
summary: Developing efficient electrocatalysts is essential for producing green hydrogen via water splitting. In this study, halogen-doped cobalt benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate (Co-BDC) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) were synthesized by incorporating F,
content: Developing efficient electrocatalysts is essential for producing green hydrogen via water splitting. In this study, halogen-doped cobalt benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate (Co-BDC) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) were synthesized by incorporating F, Br, and I. Structural characterization through X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and transmission electron microscopy confirmed that the halogens were successfully incorporated while preserving the crystalline framework. Electrochemical measurements showed that incorporating the halogenss (F, Br and I) significantly enhanced the catalytic performance compared with that of the pristine Co-BDC. Notably, the Br-doped Co-MOF exhibited the highest water-splitting activity, with a lower overpotential and improved charge-transfer kinetics. This improvement is attributed to the structural and surface modifications of the Co centers, which facilitate the reaction intermediate adsorption. These findings demonstrate that halogen functionalization is an effective strategy for engineering high-performance MOF-based electrocatalysts.

title: The nicotine–Parkinson paradox and molecular hydrogen from the gut microbiome
summary: The inverse association between tobacco smoking and Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, known as the smoking paradox, is one of the most consistent yet unexplained findings in neuroepidemiology. We propose that it may originate from the gut micr
content: The inverse association between tobacco smoking and Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, known as the smoking paradox, is one of the most consistent yet unexplained findings in neuroepidemiology. We propose that it may originate from the gut microbiome, specifically from the modulation of endogenous molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) production and its downstream signaling along the gut-brain axis, which could explain why transdermal nicotine fails where smoking protects. Despite robust evidence showing 32%–60% risk reduction in smokers, clinical trials with nicotine replacement therapy have failed to demonstrate disease-modifying effects. While preclinical studies have identified direct neuroprotective mechanisms of nicotine via nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) suppression, and anti-inflammatory pathways, these mechanisms alone cannot explain the differences between transdermal nicotine and smoking, including passive exposure. A key distinction is that smoking delivers nicotine and smoke condensates via the oropharyngeal and gastrointestinal route, directly contacting the intestinal mucosa and its resident microbiota, whereas transdermal patches bypass the gut entirely. PD patients consistently exhibit depletion of butyrate-producing and H 2 -generating bacteria alongside enrichment of hydrogen sulfide-producing Desulfovibrio species. Smokers, conversely, harbor increased abundance of Prevotella and Bacteroides , taxa equipped with group B [FeFe]-hydrogenases capable of substantial H 2 production. Endogenous H 2 is thought to promote butyrate synthesis, stabilize intestinal barrier function, and reduce systemic inflammation via the gut-brain axis. Molecular hydrogen has anti-inflammatory and mitochondria-protective effects, although the selective antioxidant mechanism originally proposed for it remains debated. We suggest that the application of exogenous molecular hydrogen, deliverable via hydrogen-enriched water, inhalation, or oral formulations designed for colonic release, may offer a novel preventive strategy without tobacco's toxicity. Such a strategy could simultaneously engage direct neuroprotective pathways and microbiome-mediated gut-brain signaling during the critical presymptomatic window of neurodegeneration.

title: Ebselen impairs biofilm-associated infections by targeting ArgR and disrupting arginine homeostasis in Gram-positive pathogens
summary: Biofilm-associated infections, particularly those caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), pose a major clinical challenge due to enhanced antibiotic resistance and metabolic adaptability. Here, we show that Ebselen, a
content: Biofilm-associated infections, particularly those caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), pose a major clinical challenge due to enhanced antibiotic resistance and metabolic adaptability. Here, we show that Ebselen, a small organoselenium compound, effectively disrupts mature MRSA biofilms and exhibits broad activity against biofilms formed by diverse Gram-positive pathogens. Using clinically relevant in vivo models, including implant-associated osteomyelitis and catheter-associated urinary tract infection, Ebselen significantly reduced bacterial burden and disease progression. Integrated multi-omics and structural analyses identified ArgR, a conserved regulator of arginine metabolism, as the direct molecular target of Ebselen. Mechanistically, Ebselen competitively binds the C-terminal domain of ArgR, suppressing arc operon expression, inhibiting arginine catabolism, and promoting intracellular arginine accumulation, ultimately destabilizing biofilm integrity. Together, these findings establish metabolic disruption of arginine homeostasis as a promising strategy to dismantle multidrug-resistant biofilm-associated infections.

title: Lusophone Strategic Potential in Energy Geopolitics
summary: The member states of the Community of Portuguese-speaking countries (CPLP) began, in 2014, their cooperation in the field of energy. Brazil is in the top 10 of the largest oil producers, and Angola is the second largest producer in sub-Saha
content: The member states of the Community of Portuguese-speaking countries (CPLP) began, in 2014, their cooperation in the field of energy. Brazil is in the top 10 of the largest oil producers, and Angola is the second largest producer in sub-Saharan Africa after Nigeria. Equatorial Guinea is member of the OPEC, and Mozambique has appreciable deposits of natural gas, already under exploration, in areas that have been affected by terrorist acts. East Timor also has hydrocarbons as its main source of revenue. Although not a producer, Portugal is a refiner and gateway to Europe for liquefied natural gas, taking advantage of its deep-water port located in Sines and the logistics and distribution infrastructure created there, having negotiated with Spain and France the interconnection with European energy network. Founded in 1996 with the Portuguese language as a link, the CPLP, made up of nine States spread across four continents and coastal in three oceans, has emphasized the need to deepen cooperation in economic terms, including energy. The entry of Equatorial Guinea in 2014, controversy for linguistic and political reasons, accentuated the energetic potential of the organization which, in addition to Lusophony, became “Petrophony”. This is a study in the domain of geopolitics, and using a qualitative methodology, this chapter analyses the strategic potential of the CPLP in the field of energy, evaluating its contribution to regional and global energy security. Given the circumstances marked by climate change and measures aimed at the transition from fossil energy to clean energy, this issue is analysed considering ongoing projects, mainly Brazil’s hydrographic potential and Portugal’s investments in renewable energy and hydrogen green.

title: The ethylene-dependent effects of α-pinene on plant defence responses
summary: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) play a role in plant defence responses and could be promising, environmentally friendly allochemicals for sustainable agriculture. This study aimed to clarify the interaction between α-pinene and ethylene (
content: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) play a role in plant defence responses and could be promising, environmentally friendly allochemicals for sustainable agriculture. This study aimed to clarify the interaction between α-pinene and ethylene (ET) amongst VOCs, and the function of ET in α-pinene-induced defence mechanisms in tomato plants. In this study, wild-type (WT) and Never ripe ( Nr ) tomato plants impaired in ET perception were treated with α-pinene. Defence-related responses were then monitored over 24–72 hours, revealing that α-pinene increased ET production. Distinct reactive oxygen species (ROS) responses were observed between genotypes: WT plants displayed increased superoxide after 48 hours, whereas Nr leaves showed significantly higher H 2 O 2 accumulation in response to α-pinene without exhibiting increased oxidative membrane damage. In parallel, superoxide dismutase activity increased in WT, but not in Nr leaves; meanwhile, catalase and ascorbate peroxidase activity remained unaffected. The level of non-enzymatic antioxidants declined during the first days, although ascorbate levels were recovered in WT after 72 hours and Nr plants showed no change in reduced glutathione levels. α-Pinene enhanced nitric oxide production in WT but not in Nr plants. Expression of hormonal marker genes revealed strong SA-related responses in WT, whereas Nr plants primarily showed JA-related gene expression. Pathogen assays showed that pre-treatment with α-pinene enhanced the resistance of WT to Pseudomonas syringae , whilst reduced the size of Botrytis cinerea -induced lesions only in Nr . Overall, the results demonstrate that ET fine-tunes α-pinene-induced priming by regulating ROS metabolism and hormonal signalling, thereby influencing the efficacy of defence against various pathogens.

title: From Lab to Industrial Scale‐Up: Rapid Joule Heating Synthesis of Electrocatalysts Towards Water Electrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Large‐scale green hydrogen production via renewable energy‐driven exchange membrane water electrolysis is highly dependent on the development of high‐performance and low‐cost electrocatalysts. Traditional catalyst synthesis strateg
content: ABSTRACT Large‐scale green hydrogen production via renewable energy‐driven exchange membrane water electrolysis is highly dependent on the development of high‐performance and low‐cost electrocatalysts. Traditional catalyst synthesis strategies suffer from lengthy fabrication procedures, limited structural modulation capability, and poor scalability for industrial deployment. As an emerging and transformative synthesis technology, rapid Joule heating (RJH) features transient ultra‐high temperatures, ultrafast heating/cooling rates, and direct energy input modes, enabling the construction of non‐equilibrium catalyst architectures with outstanding time and energy efficiency. Herein, this review comprehensively elaborates on the versatile and high‐efficiency applications of RJH in fabricating advanced electrocatalysts for proton and anion exchange membrane water electrolysis. We first systematically illustrate the fundamental working principles, typical reactor configurations, and unique synthesis superiority of the RJH technique. On this basis, we thoroughly summarize the state‐of‐the‐art RJH‐synthesized electrocatalysts toward the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER), covering atomic‐level catalysts, alloy catalysts, transition‐metal X‐ides, as well as defect‐ and interface‐engineered catalytic materials. Furthermore, special emphasis is placed on the advances in RJH‐assisted high‐throughput catalyst screening and roll‐to‐roll scalable manufacturing. Finally, the current challenges restricting the RJH‐based synthesis of water electrolysis catalysts are highlighted, and prospective research directions for future development are proposed.

title: Des extraits de plantes dans l’alimentation des bovins pour réduire leurs émissions de méthane entérique
summary: L'agriculture est le troisième secteur d'émissions de gaz à effet de serre (GES) en France. Le méthane entérique (eCH4), issu des processus digestifs naturels chez les ruminants, représente près de 5 % des GES en France. Au regard de son fo
content: L'agriculture est le troisième secteur d'émissions de gaz à effet de serre (GES) en France. Le méthane entérique (eCH4), issu des processus digestifs naturels chez les ruminants, représente près de 5 % des GES en France. Au regard de son fort pouvoir réchauffant, une réduction de ces émissions aurait un effet important sur la limitation du réchauffement climatique. L'utilisation de certains extraits de plantes (EP) dans la ration des bovins permettrait de réduire la production d'eCH4. Les effets de 5 EP sur les performances zootechniques et les émissions d'eCH4 de bovins (4 EP en vaches laitières (VL), 1 EP en vaches allaitantes (VA)) ont été évalués au cours de 5 essais réalisés dans le cadre du projet Méthane 2030. Pour chaque essai, quarante à cinquante animaux étaient répartis en 2 lots homogènes et équilibrés en termes de stade de lactation, production laitière et composition du lait pour les VL (Fermes expérimentales des Trinottières et de Trévarez) et en termes de parité, âge, date de vêlage, poids vif, note d'état corporel et sexe ratio de leur veau pour les VA (Ferm'inov). Durant 8 à 17 semaines, toutes les vaches recevaient la même ration de base. Les vaches des lots expérimentaux étaient supplémentées en suivant la recommandation des fabricants soit 50g par jour d'EP mélangés à la ration de base en VL ou incorporés dans un granulé et ajoutés séparément en VA. Les EP testés en VL étaient : Biochar (B), Tannins de châtaigniers (TC), Tannins et Saponines (TS), Monolaurate de glycérol et Isothiocyanate d'allyle (MP-AITC) et l'EP testé en VA était un mélange d'Huiles Essentielles et de Poudre de Plantes (HEPP). Dans tous les essais, l'ingestion de matière sèche (MSI) quotidienne a été enregistrée par lot (Ferm'inov, Trévarez) ou de façon individuelle à l'aide d'un dispositif d'auges peseuses (Trinottières) et les émissions individuelles d'eCH4 ont été mesurées quotidiennement grâce au système GreenFeed®. Les données d'eCH4 ont été calculées en g/j en VL et VA, et en g/kg de lait corrigé et g/kg MSI en VL ou en g/kg de poids métabolique (poids vif0,75) en VA. Les données des essais ont été analysées statistiquement avec un modèle linéaire mixte à l'aide du logiciel R, incluant les effets de la période d'essai, du traitement et de la parité. Les utilisations de B, TC, et HEPP n'ont pas eu d'effet significatif sur les performances zootechniques des VL et VA. En revanche, la distribution de TS a augmenté significativement l'ingestion des VL de 1,0 kg de MSI sans effet significatif sur les autres performances zootechniques. Aucune réduction significative des émissions d'eCH4 n'a été observée quelle que soit l'unité utilisée. Le MP-AITC est en cours de test et ses résultats seront ajoutés ultérieurement. Les teneurs en principes actifs des EP testés semblent avoir été insuffisantes dans ces essais pour obtenir une réduction significative des émissions d'eCH4 malgré le respect de la dose recommandée par les fabricants. title: Methane removal efficiency and pore gas concentration data from a landfill soil column experiment under cyclic precipitation conditions
summary: This dataset presents results from a controlled laboratory soil column experiment designed to investigate methane (CH₄) consumption efficiency and gas concentration dynamics in landfill cover soil under imposed cyclic precipitation. The stu
content: This dataset presents results from a controlled laboratory soil column experiment designed to investigate methane (CH₄) consumption efficiency and gas concentration dynamics in landfill cover soil under imposed cyclic precipitation. The study was conducted between November 18 and December 20, 2024, at the Ecohydrology Research Group laboratory, University of Waterloo (Ontario, Canada), as part of a broader project on the Mitigation of Methane Emission Hot-Spots from Municipal Landfills. We include CH₄ removal efficiency (MRE) data and CH₄ and CO₂ fluxes measured from three soil columns over time, including inflow/outflow rates, gas concentrations in the headspace, and computed flux values. In addition, we provide depth-specific gas concentration profiles (CH₄, CO₂, O₂) within the soil columns across multiple timepoints and depths, supporting analysis of vertical gas gradients under variable saturation conditions. We analyzed gas samples using a GC-2014 Shimadzu Gas Chromatograph with a flame ionization detector and methanizer, and calculated CH₄ removal by comparing inflow and outflow fluxes. The dataset enables investigations into landfill soil biogeochemistry, gas transport processes, and the effects of precipitation cycling on methane oxidation potential.
