title: Excess of rumen-degradable protein does not improve the performance of growing Zebu heifers on tropical pasture
summary: Abstract Although concentrations exceeding theoretical requirements may enhance microbial activity, the effects of such concentrations on cattle grazing tropical pastures remain unclear. This study assessed the influence of excess rumen-deg
content: Abstract Although concentrations exceeding theoretical requirements may enhance microbial activity, the effects of such concentrations on cattle grazing tropical pastures remain unclear. This study assessed the influence of excess rumen-degradable protein (RDP) on feed intake, digestibility, and weight gain in heifers grazing tropical pastures. Forty crossbred Zebu heifers (1/2 Nellore x 1/2 Brahman), 12 ± 2 months old and 210 ± 27.8 kg of body weight, were used in a completely randomized design. The heifers were allocated to eight 1-hectare Urochloa brizantha cv. Xaraés paddocks (5 heifers per paddock). The treatment consisted of concentrate supplementation [0.6% body weight (BW)] formulated to provide 100% (RDP100) or 150% (RDP150) of the RDP requirement. Increasing the RDP supply to 150% of the requirement did not affect ( p > 0.05) dry matter intake (6.21 vs. 6.49 kg/d) or digestibility (70.02 vs. 72.72%). Rumen ammonia nitrogen, serum urea nitrogen, and urine urea were higher ( p < 0.05) in RDP150 than in RDP100. However, average daily gain did not differ ( p > 0.05) between RDP100 (0.440 kg/d) and RDP150 (0.420 kg/d). Increasing RDP above the requirement did not enhance feed intake, digestibility, or weight gain in heifers grazing tropical pastures during the rainy season.

title: The Global Lakes Explorer: a basin-to-global scale data visualisation application for the assessment of nutrient emissions to lakes
summary: Phosphorus and nitrogen are critical plant nutrients, essential for fertiliser production and global food security. However, poor management of anthropogenic nutrient cycles leads to losses associated with pollution of water bodies, driving
content: Phosphorus and nitrogen are critical plant nutrients, essential for fertiliser production and global food security. However, poor management of anthropogenic nutrient cycles leads to losses associated with pollution of water bodies, driving eutrophication, biodiversity loss, and methane emissions. Addressing these interconnected challenges requires a sustainable, integrated, and, where possible, circular approach across the entire nutrient cycle. However, data on phosphorus and nitrogen emissions and impacts are fragmented across sectors and lack standardisation. Here, we introduce a new open-access web-based application: the “Global Lakes Explorer”, which harmonises phosphorus and nitrogen catchment export and emissions data alongside socio-economic and biodiversity risk factors spanning over 50 variables from multiple open data sources, covering more than 40,000 lake catchments worldwide. It enables users to visualise and download information on nutrient emissions across sectors, including agriculture, aquaculture, and wastewater, alongside socio-economic and environmental indicators. The app supports integrated governance on sustainable nutrient management in lake catchments by providing hindcasted emission data (1970–2015) in addition to future scenarios relating to shared socio-economic pathways (2015–2070) under various development projections. In this paper, we present several potential use cases for the app, including scenarios in which stakeholders can visualise and download forecasted nutrient emissions for their lake catchment of choice. We present ground-truthing analysis against phosphorus inputs from two lake catchments across natural and anthropogenic sources, in addition to model-to-model validation against total phosphorus estimations in the world’s 100 largest lakes. This open access tool is intended to help identify potential nutrient pollution risk areas, serve as a data source to support national governments in targeting efforts where they can have the greatest impact, and provide a tool that can help policymakers design informed, collaborative, and context-specific nutrient management strategies.

title: SoPlasmaFoam: An OpenFOAM-based solver for streamer and dielectric barrier discharges with adaptive mesh refinement
summary: This work presents SoPlasmaFoam , an open-source, multi-region plasma–dielectric solver built on OpenFOAM and integrated with the PETSc linear-algebra suite (with CPU and GPU back-ends), the blastAMR adaptive-mesh-refinement library (which,
content: This work presents SoPlasmaFoam , an open-source, multi-region plasma–dielectric solver built on OpenFOAM and integrated with the PETSc linear-algebra suite (with CPU and GPU back-ends), the blastAMR adaptive-mesh-refinement library (which, unlike Cartesian-only AMR frameworks, operates on hexahedral and arbitrary polyhedral meshes and can therefore conform to curved surfaces and complex geometries), and the ROUND family of high-resolution convective schemes. It solves the drift-diffusion-reaction transport equations for charged species, coupled self-consistently to the Poisson equation through either an explicit or a semi-implicit coupling treatment of the charge density, with plasma and dielectric regions joined by a monolithic multi-domain coupling that supports an arbitrary number of curved dielectric interfaces. Beyond presenting the solver, this work makes three contributions of broader use to plasma modeling. First, a systematic assessment of convective flux schemes on a stiff scalar-advection problem and on the positive-streamer benchmark shows that the Scharfetter-Gummel scheme is highly stable but excessively diffusive, over-predicting the field and propagation speed on coarse meshes, while the ROUNDF scheme outperforms all tested TVD limiters and is recommended for streamer transport. Second, an analysis of the Poisson-transport coupling demonstrates that the number of fixed-point correction loops per time step critically controls coupling error, that a semi-implicit Poisson formulation does not by itself remove this requirement, that the coupling must be tightened even when the convective Courant number and the dielectric-relaxation ratio are well below unity and that outer corrector looping is a necessary although not sufficient condition for retaining the temporal order of accuracy of any underlying discretization scheme. Third, we identify the limitations of the mixed-type wall boundary condition commonly used for the transport equations of charged species in OpenFOAM plasma solvers, which assumes a linear density profile between the cell centre and the wall face and, on coarse meshes, suppresses the ion flux to the wall and can lead to divergent or negative electron densities at the face. We propose an alternative based on the exponential Scharfetter-Gummel profile, which remains well behaved for drift-dominated transport. The solver is validated against a low-pressure DC glow discharge and the positive-streamer benchmark, and its multi-region capability is demonstrated on a nanosecond surface dielectric barrier discharge actuator, capturing streamer propagation and surface charging along the dielectric. A performance analysis confirms the expected memory-bound behavior of a finite-volume code, with good single-node scaling, and shows that with adaptive mesh refinement the solver is competitive with the fastest reported plasma codes on the streamer benchmark. The framework provides a modular foundation for future multiphysics simu

title: Feeding a microencapsulated blend of essential oils and capsaicin affects growth performance, carcass traits, and beef quality of feedlot-finished Nellore bulls
summary: Abstract This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of a microencapsulated blend of essential oils and capsaicin (BEO) on the performance, carcass traits, and meat quality of feedlot-finished cattle. Forty-seven Nellore bulls (360 ± 1
content: Abstract This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of a microencapsulated blend of essential oils and capsaicin (BEO) on the performance, carcass traits, and meat quality of feedlot-finished cattle. Forty-seven Nellore bulls (360 ± 15 kg; ~19 months old) were assigned to two treatments: a control diet without EO ( n = 24) or a diet supplemented with 150 mg/kg DM of BEO ( n = 23). All diets contained sodium monensin. Animal performance was assessed during the 94-day finishing period, and carcass and meat quality traits were evaluated after slaughter. Cattle fed BEO tended to have greater average daily gain (+ 130 g/day; P = 0.077), resulting in increased final body weight (+ 9.2 kg; P = 0.014) and carcass weight (+ 5.0 kg; P = 0.014). Subcutaneous fat thickness was also increased (+ 1.0 mm; P = 0.036), whereas dry matter intake, feed efficiency, dressing percentage, and loin muscle area were not affected. Meat from BEO-fed bulls had lower cooking loss (− 1.6% points; P = 0.005) and improved tenderness (− 3.2 N in shear force; P = 0.050), whereas pH, sarcomere length, and lipid content were unchanged. During retail display, BEO feeding was associated with lower meat lightness (L*) and yellowness (b*). No clear overall effect of BEO feeding was supported for lipid oxidation or any of the microbial groups evaluated, whereas microbial counts increased progressively during postmortem storage. In conclusion, dietary supplementation with a microencapsulated BEO combined with monensin, improved selected performance, carcass, and meat quality traits but did not provide clear evidence of improved microbial stability during retail display.

title: 2MASS J04151954-0935066: Radius, Gravity and Cooling Mass Budget for the T8 Spectral Standard
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The T8 dwarf 2MASS J04151954-0935066 anchors the late-T spectral sequence: its temperature near 740 kelvin and luminosity near two millionths of the Sun's make it cold enough for strong methane and water absorption yet warm enough that ammo
content: The T8 dwarf 2MASS J04151954-0935066 anchors the late-T spectral sequence: its temperature near 740 kelvin and luminosity near two millionths of the Sun's make it cold enough for strong methane and water absorption yet warm enough that ammonia remains a trace species rather than a defining one. Starting from temperature and luminosity, the budget obtains the radius by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, inverts the stated cooling relation at three field ages for the mass, derives gravity and mean density at the middle age, and locates the thermal emission peak that explains why this dwarf is characterised almost entirely in the infrared. Headline values are t8dwarf log luminosity solar t8dwarf = -5.67; t8dwarf luminosity watts t8dwarf = 8.184e+20; t8dwarf effective temperature k t8dwarf = 740; t8dwarf radius jupiter radii t8dwarf = 0.8657; t8dwarf cooling mass at 1gyr jupiter t8dwarf = 19.7; t8dwarf cooling mass at 3gyr jupiter t8dwarf = 33.84. Comparison with the warmer Gliese 229B budget is invited by the shared normalisation; the temperature ratio of the two dwarfs is carried as an explicit entry.

title: Effects of Ethylene Promoters and Inhibitors on Canola Growth, Endogenous Ethylene, and Plant-Derived Methane
summary: Earlier studies have shown that plants produce methane under aerobic conditions. However, the mechanisms of methane synthesis and its potential precursors in plants are not fully understood. Researchers have suggested several methane precur
content: Earlier studies have shown that plants produce methane under aerobic conditions. However, the mechanisms of methane synthesis and its potential precursors in plants are not fully understood. Researchers have suggested several methane precursors, including the amino acid L-methionine—a precursor of ethylene; however, the role of endogenous ethylene in plant-derived methane has not been investigated. The effects of four ethylene- promoting and two ethylene-inhibiting treatments on growth, physiological traits, and methane and ethylene emissions in canola (Brassica napus) were studied. Plants were grown under a temperature regime of 22/18 °C (16 h light/8 h dark) for one week and then subjected to three concentrations (low, medium, high) of each of the four ethylene-promoting treatments—methyl jasmonate (MeJA), ethephon (Eth), kinetin (Kin), and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA)—or two ethylene-inhibiting treatments—2,4-dinitrophenol (2,4-DNP) and silver nitrate (SN)—for three weeks. Overall, MeJA decreased stem diameter, plant dry mass, effective quantum yield of PSII, and photosynthetic pigments. Eth increased endogenous ethylene and stem height but decreased leaf and total plant dry mass. Kin and IAA decreased plant dry mass and specific leaf mass. 2,4-DNP decreased plant dry mass and shoot–root mass ratio. SN increased stem height and diameter, leaf area, growth rate and leaf area ratio, but it decreased specific leaf mass and shoot–root mass ratio. All the chemical treatments decreased leaf moisture. In conclusion, most plant traits were affected by MeJA and the fewest plant traits were affected by Kin. Further studies are needed to understand the effects of other ethylene-promoting and ethylene-inhibiting treatments on plant-derived methane, endogenous ethylene, and other plant traits.

title: Quantum Sensing as an Optimization-Inference Stack
summary: Every data science pipeline begins with a measurement. When that measurement is made by a quantum mechanical system—exploiting superposition, entanglement, and coherence—the sensor can in principle surpass the classical shot-noise precision
content: Every data science pipeline begins with a measurement. When that measurement is made by a quantum mechanical system—exploiting superposition, entanglement, and coherence—the sensor can in principle surpass the classical shot-noise precision limit. Atomic clocks already underpin GPS; magnetometers inform epilepsy-surgery planning; single-photon LiDAR systems detect methane leaks at parts-per-million-meter (ppm[Formula: see text]m) path-integrated concentration from ranges up to about 200 meters. This article has two purposes. The first is to serve as a primer for the INFORMS data science community; the author argues that the two central design problems in quantum sensing—what state should the probe be in? and what measurement should be performed?—can often be formulated or bounded using semidefinite programs (SDPs), develops both design problems from first principles, and shows how the resulting bounds constrain every other quantity in the sensing pipeline. The second purpose is to map a research agenda connecting the quantum layer to familiar data science tools: adaptive bandits, reinforcement learning, inverse problems, stochastic programming, and ML surrogates. An end-to-end methane emissions case study traces the complete stack from photon physics through SDP design to operational crew dispatch, providing the paper’s running quantum-versus-classical benchmark. History: Yu Ding served as the senior editor for this article.

title: Deep Unmixing-Classifier for Gas Detection Using Hyperspectral Images via a 3D-CNN Autoencoder
summary: An environmentally sustainable and healthy future relies on the identification of gas emissions that pose a potential hazard. Hyper spectral imaging technology, particularly in the Long Wave InfraRed (LWIR) region, is a highly capable means
content: An environmentally sustainable and healthy future relies on the identification of gas emissions that pose a potential hazard. Hyper spectral imaging technology, particularly in the Long Wave InfraRed (LWIR) region, is a highly capable means of detecting hazardous gases without being in their vicinity. Nevertheless, current work neglects a critical step in the process—disentangling the radiance contributions from the background and the target gases—before detection can take place which greatly reduces reliability. The goal of this paper, therefore, is to present new architecture that incorporates hyper spectral unmixing and gas classification through deep learning. We first presented raw radiance measurements as luminance-temperature data to standardize the inputs. Then, we utilize a specially designed 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) in conjunction with an autoencoder that retrieves endmember spectra plus their respective abundance values for each pixel. In addition, the CNN and BiGRU models employed in the unmixing capture both space and time dependencies for optimal feature representation. Finally, we identify target gases based on the unmixed spectral data and abundance information, using a three-layer fully connected neural network. Our proposed approach and framework are validated by quantitatively comparing experimental results from hyperspectral LWIR datasets of methane and sulfur dioxide to traditional methodologies including Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM) and Adaptive Cosine Estimator (ACE). Results show considerable improvement using the proposed method. The unmixing-classification framework provides a robust accurate option for gas detection. Other gases can be implemented into the system with no change to system parameters.

title: Completely Emptied Rumen After Rumen Evacuation in A Norwegian Red Dairy Cow
summary: This video shows the completely emptied rumen of a Norwegian Red dairy cow immediately after full rumen evacuation and omasal rinsing performed during a rumen content exchange experiment. The footage illustrates the appearance of the rumina
content: This video shows the completely emptied rumen of a Norwegian Red dairy cow immediately after full rumen evacuation and omasal rinsing performed during a rumen content exchange experiment. The footage illustrates the appearance of the ruminal wall after manual removal of solid and liquid digesta and rinsing with warm water. This procedure was part of a study investigating rumen microbial reconstitution and methane emission phenotypes following total rumen content exchange between low- and high-methane-yielding cows. All animal procedures were approved by the Norwegian Food Safety Authority (FOTS ID: 24379)

title: GRIDWELL Atlas: a self-updating screen to find the abandoned oil and gas wells best placed to add Enhanced Geothermal System electricity to the U.S. grid
summary: Drilling is the largest single cost of geothermal electricity, and the United States already has about 4.1 million abandoned oil and gas wells. However, the potential of these wells for Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) has been screened at
content: Drilling is the largest single cost of geothermal electricity, and the United States already has about 4.1 million abandoned oil and gas wells. However, the potential of these wells for Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) has been screened at each well's own depth only for documented orphaned wells. Earlier screens treated orphaned wells as a separate population, although an orphaned well is an abandoned well that no operator can be required to plug. This paper presents GRIDWELL Atlas, a self-updating screen that places orphaned wells and all other abandoned wells in one inventory. GRIDWELL Atlas assembles 948,992 abandoned wells from six state registries (Oklahoma, Kansas, California, New York, Colorado and North Dakota) and the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) list of documented orphaned wells for 26 states. Each well is assigned one of four abandonment types: 1) inactive and unplugged with an operator of record (57,765 wells); 2) orphaned and unplugged (130,813); 3) plugged and abandoned (518,750); and 4) dry and abandoned (241,664). Formation temperature is then estimated at the 382,424 wells that report a usable vertical depth, using a depth-matched bottom-hole temperature field. On 20,000 held-out measurements deeper than 8,202 ft (2,500 m), the median error of the depth-matched field is 14 °F (7.8 °C), compared to 16 °F (9.1 °C) for the all-depth interpolation it replaces. The results show that only 1,869 graded wells (0.49%) reach 302 °F (150 °C) at total depth. Inactive, unplugged wells are the most accessible type and also the type most often hot, with 1.3% of the graded wells of this type reaching EGS temperature. The 300 inactive, unplugged wells that reach EGS temperature are the best-fit wells. They are located in the Piceance Basin of Colorado and the Williston Basin of North Dakota, at a median depth of 12,108 ft (3,690 m) and a median temperature of 319 °F (160 °C). Only 7 of these wells are within 6.2 mi (10 km) of a grid interconnection at 69 kV or higher, and none is in a county that is a 2026 energy community. This paper also documents the wellbore, thermal, seismic and legal barriers that apply to each abandonment type, with the evidence for each barrier. The atlas downloads the state registries again every month, so wells are added as agencies record them as abandoned.

title: A Seasonal Analysis of Marine Inorganic Aerosol Chemical Composition Across the Atlantic‐Sector of the Southern Ocean
summary: Abstract Marine aerosols are the most important source of natural aerosols globally and play an important role in marine biogeochemical cycling as well as climate. Marine aerosols are chemically diverse and can originate from a combination
content: Abstract Marine aerosols are the most important source of natural aerosols globally and play an important role in marine biogeochemical cycling as well as climate. Marine aerosols are chemically diverse and can originate from a combination of primary and secondary sources. The overall aim of this work was to improve our understanding of the processes that control ocean emissions of aerosols including the role of sea ice, particularly outside of the frequently sampled summer season in the Southern Ocean. This work presents a seasonally resolved data set of coarse (>1 μm) and fine mode (<1 μm) inorganic aerosol concentrations (Na + , Cl − , K + , Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ , NH 4 + , NO 3 − , and SO 4 2− ) measured across the Southern Ocean between Cape Town, South Africa and the marginal ice zone. Primary sea salt aerosol concentrations were correlated with local wind speed in summer, but not in winter or spring. Blowing snow from sea ice was identified as an additional source of sea salt aerosols, but only in winter. Nitrate was present predominantly in the coarse mode and displayed strong seasonality with the highest concentrations in summer and spring. In contrast, ammonium and non sea salt sulfate were present in the fine mode, with the lowest concentrations observed in winter when ocean biogeochemisty is at a minimum. The presence of sea ice influenced sea salt aerosols through blowing snow, but also influenced secondary aerosol species due to increased biological activity as revealed by chlorophyll‐a concentrations.

title: Non-autonomous PMK-1/p38 MAPK signaling ensures homeostatic downregulation of germline stem cell proliferation in C. elegans
summary: Stem cell underproliferation leads to tissue loss, while overproliferation can induce tumorigenesis. Stem and progenitor proliferation rates are therefore coupled to the needs for differentiated cells in the tissues they maintain, yet these
content: Stem cell underproliferation leads to tissue loss, while overproliferation can induce tumorigenesis. Stem and progenitor proliferation rates are therefore coupled to the needs for differentiated cells in the tissues they maintain, yet these homeostatic mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we used the C. elegans hermaphrodite reproductive system to understand how germline stem cell (GSC) proliferation is linked to sperm availability and oocyte usage. We designed a forward genetic screening strategy to identify germline homeostasis-defective ( ghd ) mutants that grow benign, differentiated germline tumors akin to hamartomas. We provide evidence that the TIR-1/sterile alpha and TIR-motif containing 1 (SARM1) metabolic sensor works together with the NIPI-3/TRIB1 pseudokinase to activate a canonical PMK-1/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling cascade in the somatic gonadal sheath, where it shuts down the oncogenic extracellular signal-regulated kinase MPK-1/ERK to cell non-autonomously couple GSC proliferation with oocyte needs. Similar PMK-1/p38-dependent inter-tissue signaling modules could underlie stem cell homeostasis in other systems and prevent differentiated tumors.

title: Impact of Methane Gas Emission from Livestock Cumulative Density on the Environment using Computational Method
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
summary: The impact of methane emission on the environment due to livestock cumulative density was studied computationally using MATLAB ODE45 numerical scheme for a time interval of 0(30)720 days. The study revealed that on the based day of our expe
content: The impact of methane emission on the environment due to livestock cumulative density was studied computationally using MATLAB ODE45 numerical scheme for a time interval of 0(30)720 days. The study revealed that on the based day of our experimental time here called the initial condition, the relative abundance of the livestock cumulative density relative N1 is recorded as two hundred (200) in size whereas the methane gas emission N2 records two hundred and fifty (250) unit emitted. Furthermore, from the thirtieth (30th) day up to the seven hundred and tweenth (720 th) day, the data base result shows a monotonic increasing pattern in the relative abundance of both coordinates which converges to a saturating value of 992 sizes for the livestock cumulative density and 897 units as the methane gas emitted into the environment. From the result obtained, we observed further in this time interval that as the livestock cumulative density increases, the methane gas emitted into the environment increases, which indicates a direct proportion in terms of their interactions.The full detailed results and discussion is presented in this study

title: A geometry-tunable MWIR multispectral plasmonic filter based on a Dy-doped cadmium oxide bull’s-eye structure
summary: We propose a compact bull’s-eye plasmonic filter based on Dy-doped cadmium oxide (Dy: CdO), an ENZ-capable transparent conducting oxide with low optical losses in the mid-wave infrared (MWIR). The design combines the plasmonic response of D
content: We propose a compact bull’s-eye plasmonic filter based on Dy-doped cadmium oxide (Dy: CdO), an ENZ-capable transparent conducting oxide with low optical losses in the mid-wave infrared (MWIR). The design combines the plasmonic response of Dy: CdO beyond its ENZ wavelength with extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) enabled by the concentric bull’s-eye geometry. Two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations performed at a carrier concentration of 3.7 × 10²⁰ cm⁻³ demonstrate that systematic tuning of the corrugation period enables geometry-controlled multispectral resonances covering the 3–5 μm MWIR atmospheric window. To further tailor the spectral response, a SiO₂ dielectric encapsulation is incorporated to modify the local dielectric environment, while the geometrical parameters are systematically optimized to enhance resonant transmission and spectral selectivity. The encapsulated structure achieves a maximum transmission of 58% with a minimum FWHM of 400 nm, while increasing the average peak transmittance from approximately 45% to 50% and the average quality factor from 7.85 to about 9 (≈ 15%) compared with the unencapsulated design. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the proposed Dy: CdO bull’s-eye architecture outperforms its conventional Au-based counterpart in terms of transmission efficiency and spectral selectivity, providing a promising low-loss platform for compact MWIR multispectral filters. The proposed design offers significant potential applications in MWIR multispectral imaging and infrared spectroscopy.

title: Low-abundance taxa are associated with a refined rumen microbiome–resistome interplay in high-yielding dairy cows: an absolute abundance-based metagenomic perspective
summary: Abstract Background The rumen microbiota undergoes dynamic shifts in response to fluctuations in physiological stages and host-related factors, and has been associated with productive traits including milk yield, feed efficiency, and methan
content: Abstract Background The rumen microbiota undergoes dynamic shifts in response to fluctuations in physiological stages and host-related factors, and has been associated with productive traits including milk yield, feed efficiency, and methane emissions. However, the ecological mechanisms underlying the relationship between microbial relative abundance, absolute abundance, and shifts in microbiota structure, and their connection to host production performance, remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the rumen microecological features across cows with divergent lactation performance, with particular emphasis on linking microbial absolute abundance, mobile genetic elements, and antibiotic resistance genes to productivity in high-yielding cows. In this study, rumen fluid was collected from 8 high-yielding cows and 8 low-yielding cows selected from 90 mid-lactation Holstein cows. Shotgun metagenomics with spike-in-based absolute quantification and untargeted metabolomics were employed to investigate the characteristics and potential associations and transmission patterns of rumen microbial communities and ARGs in cows with different milk yields. Results We observed that high-yielding cows exhibited stronger carbohydrate metabolism capacity, higher Chao1 and ACE indices, and lower total microbial absolute abundance. Moreover, high-yielding cows displayed reduced absolute abundances of bacteria and viruses, increased relative abundances of archaea and eukaryotes, and a more intricate microbial network architecture. These shifts were accompanied by a reduction in ARGs prevalence, particularly within peptide, elfamycin, and fluoroquinolone antibiotic categories, and were accompanied by a streamlined ARGs interaction network. Furthermore, the attenuation of ARGs was associated with reduced levels of MGEs, especially those linked to replication, phage activity, genetic transfer, and defense functions. These findings suggest potential associations among microbial structure, MGEs, and ARGs in the rumen ecosystem. Conclusion These findings indicate that complex microbial networks involving low-abundance taxa, together with a streamlined ARGs ecosystem, are associated with high milk yield in dairy cows. This perspective offers valuable implications for mitigating antibiotic resistance risks in intensive livestock systems and advancing efficient, healthy dairy production.

title: WRF-Chem fields for the INFLUX aircraft mass balance flights, 2011 to 2016
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Subset of the WRF-Chem (version 3.6.1) simulations used in Balashov, Barkley, Davis and Shepson (2026), "Evaluation of aircraft-based methane emissions estimates and estimation methodologies with six years of data from Indianapolis", Journa
content: Subset of the WRF-Chem (version 3.6.1) simulations used in Balashov, Barkley, Davis and Shepson (2026), "Evaluation of aircraft-based methane emissions estimates and estimation methodologies with six years of data from Indianapolis", Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres. One MATLAB (HDF5) file per flight day, 37 files, holds the fields the analyses of the paper use: earth-relative wind, potential temperature, height, pressure and boundary layer height on the lowest 25 levels of the 3 km domain within 160 km of Indianapolis (the whole 3 km domain on 11/19/2014), every hour from 8 h before the first aircraft transect to 1 h after the last one, and the eight CH4 tracers (five regional source categories of the EPA gridded inventory and three Marion County tracers) during the flight hours. WRF_configuration.txt documents the complete model configuration of both domains; WRF_subsets_README.txt describes every variable and gives reading examples for MATLAB and Python. The analysis code that reads these files is archived separately (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24184834).

title: Conjugation Continuity in Donor–Acceptor Crown Ether Covalent Organic Frameworks Boosts Photocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
summary: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production using covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is constrained by inefficient charge separation and discontinuous electron transport. While donor–acceptor (D–A) configura
content: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production using covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is constrained by inefficient charge separation and discontinuous electron transport. While donor–acceptor (D–A) configurations can enhance internal electric fields, conjugation continuity within the acceptor moiety determines whether the separated charges can undergo long‐range migration to surface active sites,a factor often overlooked. Herein, we compare three crown‐ether (CE)‐based COFs: non‐D–A (CE‐BD‐COF), D–A non‐conjugated (CE‐BS‐COF), and D–A with a conjugation bypass (CE‐SA‐COF). CE‐BS‐COF exhibits a large dipole moment (8.92 D), but conjugation interruption localizes its LUMO, yielding a low surface photovoltage (34.0 mV). Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals ultrafast initial charge transfer (τ 1 = 1.98 ps) and fast charge‐separation stabilization (τ 2 = 41.65 ps) in CE‐SA‐COF, together with a long‐lived charge‐separated state (>7 ns). Consequently, CE‐SA‐COF achieves a H 2 O 2 production rate of 2800.00 µmol g − 1 h − 1 under air in pure water, which is 3.5 times that of CE‐BD‐COF and 1.6 times that of CE‐BS‐COF. This work clarifies the distinct roles of D–A configuration and conjugation continuity, demonstrating that conjugation continuity, rather than polarization strength alone, governs electron transport to surface active sites and offering a design principle for COF photocatalysts.

title: Effect of Feeding Red Seaweed Kappaphycus alvarezii on Nutrient Digestibility, Enteric Methane Emissions, and Rumen Metatranscriptome in Growing Sheep
summary: A 126-day study was conducted in growing male sheep to investigate the effect of feeding Kappaphycus alvarezii on nutrient utilisation, enteric methane emissions, and rumen microbiota. Control sheep (C, n = 15) were fed a basal diet consist
content: A 126-day study was conducted in growing male sheep to investigate the effect of feeding Kappaphycus alvarezii on nutrient utilisation, enteric methane emissions, and rumen microbiota. Control sheep (C, n = 15) were fed a basal diet consisting of wheat straw and concentrate mixture (35:65, DM basis), whereas the experimental group (Ka, n = 15) received the basal diet, with 5% K. alvarezii replacing an equal amount of the wheat straw on a dry matter (w/w) basis. A 16% reduction was observed in daily enteric methane emission (g/d) (p = 0.0001) in the Ka group compared with the C group. Dry matter digestibility (p = 0.0062) and average daily body weight gain (p = 0.0239) were adversely affected by K. alvarezii supplementation. However, there was no significant (p = 0.2379) difference in the TVFA production (mmol/L) between the C and Ka groups. Total protozoal counts, as well as populations of Entodiniomorphs and Holotrichs, were significantly reduced in the Ka group (p < 0.05). The metatranscriptome profiles of both groups revealed Bacillota and Bacteroidota as the most active bacterial phyla, while the transcript abundance of Thermodesulfobacteriota and Pseudomonadota increased marginally (p = 0.128) following K. alvarezii supplementation. Methanobacteriota was the single most dominant archaeal phylum. At the genus level, Desulfovibrio (p = 0.001) and Succinivibrio (p = 0.014) significantly increased in the Ka-supplemented group. Supplementation of K. alvarezii led to a targeted reduction in the minor methanogen community like Methanobacterium and Methanothermobacter. The fundamental housekeeping and metabolic COG categories, particularly carbohydrate transport and metabolism (FDR = 0.769) and energy production and conversion (FDR = 0.970), exhibited functional stability between the control and Ka groups. Dietary supplementation of K. alvarezii significantly upregulated pathways related to xenobiotic degradation, co-factors, and amino acid catabolism. Conversely, it suppressed lysine biosynthesis and nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism. Acetate concentration correlated positively with key fibrolytic Firmicutes (Butyrivibrio, Blautia, Roseburia) and negatively with Chloroflexota, whereas propionate and branched-chain VFAs showed distinct associations with taxa such as Xylanibacter, Synergistota, and Treponema, indicating suppressed crude protein digestibility.

title: Aircraft observations suggest large cattle-driven underestimates of springtime ammonia emissions in the U.S. Corn Belt
source: DOE Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) Repository
summary: This dataset presents airborne observations of atmospheric ammonia, water vapor, and methane collected across four U.S. Midwest regions: northwestern Iowa and southeastern South Dakota (NW-IA), northeastern Nebraska (NE-NE), central Minneso
content: This dataset presents airborne observations of atmospheric ammonia, water vapor, and methane collected across four U.S. Midwest regions: northwestern Iowa and southeastern South Dakota (NW-IA), northeastern Nebraska (NE-NE), central Minnesota (C-MN), and southern Minnesota (S-MN). Data were gathered to estimate surface emissions in key hot spot areas. Six research flights were conducted May 9–18, 2021, by Scientific Aviation (Boulder, CO) using a 2004 Mooney Ovation 2 aircraft. Concentrations were measured via cavity ring-down spectroscopy at altitudes from 250 to 3,500 m. Archived in Excel and CSV files, these data are easily imported into MATLAB to support regional trace gas studies.

title: Public Service Innovation in Transforming Waste Management into Green Economy-Based Assets through a Quadruple Helix Approach: A Collaborative Study of Waste Bank–Pegadaian
source: Greenation International Journal of Law and Social Sciences
summary: This study examines public service innovation in transforming household waste management into green economy-based assets through The Gade Clean & Gold program, a collaborative initiative involving Bank Sampah Rukmi, PT Pegadaian, local gove
content: This study examines public service innovation in transforming household waste management into green economy-based assets through The Gade Clean & Gold program, a collaborative initiative involving Bank Sampah Rukmi, PT Pegadaian, local government actors, community participants, and academics within a Quadruple Helix framework in Gunung Anyar, Surabaya. The background problem centers on the limitations of conventional final-disposal-oriented waste governance, the fragile sustainability of community waste banks when economic incentives are weak, and the absence of an integrated coordination platform among public, business, community, and academic actors. This research aims to analyze multi-stakeholder collaboration dynamics, evaluate the quality of waste-to-gold service innovation, and clarify the differentiated contributions of each Quadruple Helix pillar. A qualitative case-study design was applied through in-depth interviews with seven purposively selected informants, field observation, and document analysis. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldana, while validity was strengthened through source triangulation, technique triangulation, member checking, and saturation-based verification. The findings show that the collaboration has produced measurable outcomes, including 847 active customers and 12.4 tons of managed waste per year, exceeding the annual target by 55%. However, the program still faces capacity imbalance, limited rapid-response communication, digital literacy gaps, and weak formal institutionalization. The study concludes that The Gade Clean & Gold program has generated a promising green-economy service model, yet its sustainability depends on formal regulation, an integrated monitoring dashboard, and a stronger multi-actor coordination mechanism.

title: Microbiological Mechanisms of Bokashi Composting from Fermentation to Soil Ecological Effects
source: Transactions on Environment Energy and Earth Sciences
summary: Bokashi composting is a small-scale anaerobic fermentation technology that uses Effective Microorganisms (EM) to treat organic waste. This paper will systematically study the microbial mechanisms of Bokashi from fermentation to soil applica
content: Bokashi composting is a small-scale anaerobic fermentation technology that uses Effective Microorganisms (EM) to treat organic waste. This paper will systematically study the microbial mechanisms of Bokashi from fermentation to soil application. Lactic acid bacteria are the most numerous organisms in the community during fermentation, and they produce organic acids. Therefore, a self-limiting acidic environment is generated to inhibit pathogens and putrefactive organisms. A low Substrate Carbon-to-Nitrogen Ratio is also a reason for low-efficiency or poor-quality fermentation. Bokashi is aerobically aged a second time after soil incorporation to improve soil structure and water-holding capacity, reduce compaction, and supply nutrients for plants. In addition, the bioactive substances and organic acids produced in fermentation are generally antimicrobial and therefore meet the conditions for biosafety and crop growth. However, the functional advantages of EM inoculation over indigenous microbiota and the mechanistic connections between community structure and ecological function have not been fully revealed. Provide a theoretical basis for standardising household Bokashi protocols and promoting urban organic waste utilisation in this review.

title: Fostering Scientific Judgment in LLM-Assisted Catalyst Development
summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can provide plausible synthesis methods and reaction conditions for catalysis experiments in response to simple prompts, but the validity and accuracy of the responses are not necessarily reliable. We e
content: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can provide plausible synthesis methods and reaction conditions for catalysis experiments in response to simple prompts, but the validity and accuracy of the responses are not necessarily reliable. We evaluated a zero-shot GPT-5 proposal for a trimetallic, precious metal-free reverse water–gas shift catalyst. The output initially appeared chemically plausible, but we identified errors by tasking students to verify the model’s claims against the primary literature, thermodynamic constraints, and control experiments. We then fed our observations and experimental results back into the model with a second prompt to determine whether the model would converge on a more scientifically grounded and experimentally testable catalyst candidate. Although the revised catalyst did not improve performance, the process revealed unexpected findings about catalyst stability and generated new hypotheses. Ultimately, our results show that iterative model verification can transform plausible but unreliable LLM outputs into a useful framework for student-driven catalyst preparation, hypothesis generation, and scientific training.

title: Cu-Sn-Bi ternary liquid metal catalyst for methane pyrolysis to hydrogen and carbon
summary: Methane pyrolysis using liquid metal catalysts provides a promising pathway for low-emission hydrogen production. To synergistically optimize both reaction kinetics and hydrodynamics, this study introduces a novel Cu-Sn-Bi ternary catalyst
content: Methane pyrolysis using liquid metal catalysts provides a promising pathway for low-emission hydrogen production. To synergistically optimize both reaction kinetics and hydrodynamics, this study introduces a novel Cu-Sn-Bi ternary catalyst system. Within this ternary system, Cu contributes intrinsic catalytic activity toward methane pyrolysis, while Sn serves primarily as the liquid-metal solvent and Bi acts mainly as a hydrodynamic modifier. At 1050°C and a CH4 flow rate of 20 mL·min−1, the optimal Cu0.375Sn0.250Bi0.375 system achieved a CH4 conversion of 63.28% and an H2 selectivity of 98.57%. Experimental kinetic analyses indicate that while Bi exhibits limited intrinsic catalytic activity, it functions effectively as a physical hydrodynamic modifier. Specifically, by lowering the surface tension and increasing the melt density, Bi may favor smaller bubbles and a larger gas-liquid interfacial area. Furthermore, the incorporation of Bi mitigates the conversion decline typically observed at high gas flow rates. The accumulated carbon-metal “slurry-like” layer may contribute to this behavior by increasing the resistance to bubble motion and prolonging the effective gas residence time, although this effect was not directly measured. However, the low surface tension and high vapor pressure of Bi promote interfacial enrichment and evaporation, contributing to metal contamination in the solid carbon by-products. Additionally, operating above 1000°C with a Bi content exceeding 37.5 at.% results in pronounced accumulation of the surface carbon-metal layer, posing a critical risk of reactor clogging. These findings provide experimental insights into the trade-offs in liquid metal catalyst design and the formation and evolution mechanisms of carbon by-products.

title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM 2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
summary: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but
content: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but few have focused on the most recent wildfire-intensive years, and jointly estimated both to quantify wildfire contributions to total PM2.5 exposure. This study developed a high-resolution machine learning framework to estimate daily 1-km concentrations of total and wildfire-related PM2.5 across the CONUS from 2018 to 2024. This framework incorporates chemical precursors and wildfire smoke density as predictors and relies on publicly accessible data sources enabling future updates. The model achieved high performance with cross-validated R2 of 0.72 and 0.89 for daily and annual estimates, respectively. Elevated total PM2.5 concentrations were observed along the west coast and in several metropolitan areas across the CONUS. Wildfire smoke contributed substantially to total PM2.5 concentrations during major wildfire years, accounting for approximately 35% of PM2.5 along the west coast in 2020, and over 25% in the eastern U.S. in 2023. Wildfire-related PM2.5 mortality accounted for 20% of PM2.5-attributable deaths along the west coast in 2020 (30 times that in 2019), and 24% in the northeastern U.S. in 2023 (14 times that in 2019). These findings highlight the growing role of wildfire smoke as a major driver of total PM2.5 exposure and associated health risks in both western and eastern U.S., underscoring the need for sustained nationwide public health interventions to reduce wildfire smoke exposure.

title: INFLUX aircraft mass balance analysis: code and per-transect results
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: MATLAB and Python scripts and per-transect results for the aircraft mass balance analysis of methane emissions from Indianapolis (Marion County, Indiana) with 37 flights of the Indianapolis Flux Experiment (INFLUX), 2011 to 2016. The script
content: MATLAB and Python scripts and per-transect results for the aircraft mass balance analysis of methane emissions from Indianapolis (Marion County, Indiana) with 37 flights of the Indianapolis Flux Experiment (INFLUX), 2011 to 2016. The scripts compute the emission rates with four definitions of the background (Downwind Edge, Upwind, Adjusted ABL Upwind, Upwind Edge) and the emission rates of the South Side Landfill, run the sensitivity analyses of the Supporting Information, and draw the figures of the paper. The data folder holds Table S1 and Data Sets S1 to S4 of the paper. The README describes the inputs each script needs and the order in which to run them.

title: Integrating whole-genome sequencing and metagenomics improves phenotype prediction of fat deposition traits in pigs
summary: BACKGROUND: Fat deposition is a key economic trait affecting production efficiency and carcass quality in pigs and is influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. Although increasing evidence indicates that the gut microbiome contr
content: BACKGROUND: Fat deposition is a key economic trait affecting production efficiency and carcass quality in pigs and is influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. Although increasing evidence indicates that the gut microbiome contributes to host phenotypic variation, current genomic evaluation and prediction models largely rely on host genotype information and rarely account for microbiome effects. This study aimed to quantify the contribution of the gut microbiome to fat deposition traits and to evaluate whether incorporating microbiome information could improve phenotypic prediction in pigs. RESULTS: We collected phenotypic characteristics of six fat deposition traits including the shoulder backfat thickness, the 6th-7th rib backfat thickness, the last rib backfat thickness, waist backfat thickness, the 3rd-4th last rib backfat thickness, and the average backfat thickness from 478 Duroc × Landrace × Yorkshire pigs. Using whole-genome resequencing and metagenomic sequencing, we identified 21 million single nucleotide variants and quantified the abundances of 20,336 gut microbial species across 478 pigs. Distinct fecal microbial community structures were observed between pigs with high- and low-fat deposition, and 27 bacterial species were identified as potential biomarkers associated with fat deposition. Microbiability estimates for the six backfat thickness traits ranged from 0.17 to 0.44, indicating that the gut microbiome accounted for a considerable proportion of phenotypic variance beyond host genetic contributions. In contrast, the interaction effects between the host genome and gut microbiome accounted for only a negligible proportion of phenotypic variance across the six traits. Incorporating overall microbiome information into genomic prediction models resulted in mean phenotypic predictive abilities ranging from 0.082 to 0.292, representing increases in predictive ability of 0.023 to 0.084 across traits and reductions in the mean squared error of prediction of 0.001 to 0.009 compared with the additive genetic model. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that the gut microbiome makes a substantial contribution to variation in fat deposition traits in pigs. Integrating host whole-genome resequencing and gut metagenomic information yielded modest absolute gains in phenotypic predictive ability, suggesting that the gut microbiome may provide complementary information for prediction models of complex traits in pigs.

title: The Effect of Superhigh Organic Sulfur Content on Bituminous Coal Properties: Insights from Petrology, Chemical Composition, and Molecular Structure
summary: Abstract In order to study the influence of superabundant organic sulfur on bituminous coals, four coal samples were collected for comparative analysis: two superhigh-organic-sulfur (SHOS) coals of different ranks from the Chenxi and Heshan
content: Abstract In order to study the influence of superabundant organic sulfur on bituminous coals, four coal samples were collected for comparative analysis: two superhigh-organic-sulfur (SHOS) coals of different ranks from the Chenxi and Heshan coalfields and two low-organic-sulfur coals of different ranks from the Datong and Xishan coalfields. The two SHOS coals and their corresponding low-organic-sulfur coals of the same rank were high-volatile bituminous coals and low-volatile bituminous coals, respectively. Through conventional analysis, coal petrology analysis, X-ray diffraction analysis (XRD), and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) investigations, it was revealed that for these samples, superabundant organic sulfur in coal exerted profound alterations on the properties of chemical composition, petrology, and molecular structure. First of all, the superhigh content of organic sulfur changes the evolutionary regularity of oxygen content in the process of coal maturation, where the oxygen content is less than half of that in low-organic-sulfur coals. Because of the special origin of SHOS coals, the vitrinite content in the examined SHOS coals is nearly double that in low-organic-sulfur coals. Petrological indices show evidence that SHOS coal has experienced a strong oxidizing environment or aqueous transportation. In high-volatile bituminous coals with a mean random vitrinite reflectance (Ro,ran) of approximately 0.7%, XRD analysis shows that the examined SHOS coals exhibit a 37% increase in crystallite diameter (La) compared to that of low-organic-sulfur coals. In addition, at the same rank, HRTEM analysis shows that the examined SHOS coals exhibit a 67% higher relative molecular weight compared with low-organic-sulfur coals. Meanwhile, the XRD results show that the crystallite height (Lc) and average number of aromatic layers per carbon crystallite (Nave) of SHOS coals are significantly lower than those of the low-organic-sulfur coals in both ranks, and this differential becomes more pronounced in low-volatile bituminous coals. This study found that at different stages of coalification, the SHOS coals examined showed quite significant structural differences.

title: Combined Crossed Molecular Beams, Kinetics, and Theoretical Studies of the Multichannel N(2D) + C6H5CH3 (Toluene) Reaction: Rate Constants, Primary Product Channels, and Branching Fractions
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
summary: Abstract The elementary reaction N(2D) + C6H5CH3 (toluene), of potential relevance in the atmospheric chemistry of Titan, has been investigated using a combined experimental/theoretical approach. CMB (crossed-molecular-beam) experiments emp
content: Abstract The elementary reaction N(2D) + C6H5CH3 (toluene), of potential relevance in the atmospheric chemistry of Titan, has been investigated using a combined experimental/theoretical approach. CMB (crossed-molecular-beam) experiments employing mass-spectrometric detection and TOF (time-of-flight) analysis at collision energy of 34.3 kJ/mol were used for exploring primary products, branching fractions (BFs), and reaction micromechanism. Kinetic experiments in a continuous supersonic flow reactor were used for determining rate constants as a function of temperature (50, 75, 127, 177, and 296 K). Synergistically, electronic structure computations of the C7H8N PES (potential energy surface) and related statistical (Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus/Master-Equation, RRKM/ME) calculations of product BFs were carried out to facilitate interpretation of experiments and elucidate the reaction micromechanism. It is found that barrierless “bridge” additions of N(2D) to the different positions of the aromatic ring form seven-, six-, and five-membered ring isomeric C7H8N intermediates that lead to a variety of product channels. Rate constants are fast, ranging between 2.1 and 2.4 × 10–10 cm3 s–1 over the 50–296 K range. The BFs of channels leading to “ring-contraction” via HCN/C2H2/H eliminations and to “ring-expansion” via CH3 elimination were quantified. Statistical simulations of isomeric product BFs on the computed PES were performed in CMB conditions and at 94, 175, and 296 K. Agreement is noted between experimental and theoretical BFs. The results are expected to be useful for improved modeling of Titan’s atmosphere and to provide molecular-level insight into N-incorporation at methyl-substituted aromatic carbon sites, with potential relevance to plasma-assisted functionalization of carbon nanomaterials.

title: Model code and figure data for "Northern peatland methane emissions tripled during a century of warming"
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This record accompanies the manuscript “Northern peatland methane emissions tripled during a century of warming” and contains two ZIP archives. Authors: Liyang Liu*, Philippe Ciais, Yi Xi, Elodie Salmon, Lei Zhu, Gustaf Hugelius, Biqing Zhu
content: This record accompanies the manuscript “Northern peatland methane emissions tripled during a century of warming” and contains two ZIP archives. Authors: Liyang Liu*, Philippe Ciais, Yi Xi, Elodie Salmon, Lei Zhu, Gustaf Hugelius, Biqing Zhu, Xin Lin, Christina Biasi, Juliette Bernard, Gang Liu, Yuxing Sang, Pierre Friedlingstein, Nan Meng, Chunjing Qiu Correspondence to: Liyang Liu (liyang.liu@lsce.ipsl.fr) - ORCHIDEE-PEAT v3.1 model source code. This archive contains the model version used for the historical simulations reported in the manuscript. The source code is distributed under the CeCILL (CEA CNRS INRIA Logiciel Libre) license. - Figure data and plotting scripts. This archive contains Python scripts and the processed data they read, including gridded fields for maps and precomputed means and bounds for curves with shaded ranges. The accompanying README lists the figures included and explains how to run the scripts. External datasets used in the study - Climate forcing. The observation-based GSWP3–W5E5 forcing used for model calibration is available from [ISIMIP3a](https://data.isimip.org/search/tree/ISIMIP3a/InputData/climate/atmosphere/gswp3-w5e5/). The historical forcing used for the simulation ensemble is available from [ISIMIP3b](https://data.isimip.org/search/tree/ISIMIP3b/InputData/climate/atmosphere/). - Methane flux data. The [UpCH₄ v1.0 gridded wetland methane flux product](https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2253) was used for model calibration. Site-level methane flux observations from [ABCFlux v2](https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2448) were used for independent model evaluation. Both datasets are archived at ORNL DAAC. - Peatland spatial data. The peatland distribution and classification used in the simulations were based on the [Boreal–Arctic Wetland and Lake Dataset (BAWLD)](https://doi.org/10.18739/A2C824F9X) and the [northern peatland maps of Hugelius et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.17043/hugelius-2020).

title: Fermented Feeds and Enteric Methane Emissions: Mechanisms, Evidence Evaluation, and Opportunities and Limitations for Feed Resource Valorization in China
summary: Feed fermentation can alter ruminal methane production, but lower daily methane output does not necessarily indicate lower methane yield or effective mitigation, because it may result from reduced feed intake or impaired digestion. This cri
content: Feed fermentation can alter ruminal methane production, but lower daily methane output does not necessarily indicate lower methane yield or effective mitigation, because it may result from reduced feed intake or impaired digestion. This critical narrative review draws on searches of the Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed for publications dated from 1 June 2010 to 1 June 2026. Title, abstract, and full-text screening yielded 157 candidate publications as the primary literature pool. These included 30 original studies reporting direct methane measurements, of which 13 evaluated fermented-feed interventions. Methane was assessed primarily through in vitro rumen simulations and direct measurements in animals. Methane responses varied in both direction and magnitude. Across four verified studies in dairy cows that reported reductions, daily methane production decreased by 10.7–17.2%. A 24-h in vitro trial with fermented total mixed ration reported a 13.7% reduction in methane production. These values describe specific comparisons. Other interventions increased methane or produced responses that were not statistically significant, and some reductions coincided with poorer animal performance. Across this heterogeneous evidence base, no common mechanism has been established that consistently explains methane responses across feedstocks and fermentation processes. Ingredient substitution and changes in substrate utilization further limit attribution to fermentation itself. We recommend evaluating methane production, methane yield, product-based methane intensity, and methane production per unit of degraded dry matter alongside feed intake, digestibility, animal performance, and health. We also assess the potential of crop straws, agro-industrial by-products, and traditional Chinese medicine residues as substrates for fermented feeds in China. Long-term animal trials with appropriate controls are needed to determine whether sustained methane mitigation can be achieved without compromising nutrient utilization or animal performance.
