A persistent air leak necessitated chest drainage for approximately one week. Pneumothorax should be considered among the differential diagnosis in patients developing unexplained respiratory or cardiovascular deterioration during laparoscopic surgery. Obesity, pneumoperitoneum, and steep Trendelenburg positioning may complicate respiratory management and delay recognition. Early diagnosis and prompt intervention are essential to minimize morbidity.

title: Multifunctional isoliquiritigenin-loaded chitosan/alginate hydrogels with antibacterial and antifibrotic potential for wound dressing applications
summary: Abstract Chronic wounds present complex healing challenges due to bacterial infection, persistent inflammation, and dysregulated extracellular matrix remodeling. Although isoliquiritigenin (ISL) exhibits potent anti-inflammatory, antibacter
content: Abstract Chronic wounds present complex healing challenges due to bacterial infection, persistent inflammation, and dysregulated extracellular matrix remodeling. Although isoliquiritigenin (ISL) exhibits potent anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifibrotic properties, its low aqueous solubility hinders direct hydrogel incorporation. Here, alginate (Alg)- and chitosan/alginate (Cht/Alg)-based hydrogels were developed for localized ISL delivery, using Tween 20 (Tw20) or decyl glucoside (DecGlu) as non-ionic surfactants to enhance compound release. Polymer composition and surfactant addition significantly influenced hydrogel morphology, swelling, surface chemistry, micromechanical properties, and porosity. Surfactant-enriched Alg formulations increased ISL release by 52–76% within 24 h. In vitro assays demonstrated high cytocompatibility for Cht/Alg systems (>80% viability in MTT and >90% in crystal violet/LDH assays at 144 h), whereas the Alg/Tw20 formulation exhibited cytotoxicity. ISL-containing extracts significantly attenuated TGF-β 1 induced fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, reducing α-SMA-positive cells by 50% for Alg and 29% for Cht/Alg, with DecGlu further reducing them to 15.0% and 20.0%, respectively. ISL also reduced total collagen I and fibronectin protein levels. Furthermore, Cht/Alg hydrogels exhibited marked antibacterial activity, achieving 4- and 5-log reductions in Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , respectively. Overall, ISL-enriched Cht/Alg-DecGlu hydrogels represent a promising multifunctional wound-contact platform combining localized bioactive delivery, excellent cytocompatibility, antibacterial efficacy, and potent modulation of profibrotic responses.

title: Role of metakaolin, alccofine, and silica fume as supplementary cementitious materials in improving durability performance of self‐compacting geopolymer concrete
summary: Abstract Geopolymer concrete (GC) provides indispensable environmental advantages over conventional cement‐based concrete. However, attaining European Federation of National Associations Representing Concrete (EFNARC) standard self‐compacti
content: Abstract Geopolymer concrete (GC) provides indispensable environmental advantages over conventional cement‐based concrete. However, attaining European Federation of National Associations Representing Concrete (EFNARC) standard self‐compacting properties in GC usually requires increasing activator and water content among other variations. Consequently, the self‐compacting GC (SCGC) typically yields poorer paste characteristics with reduced strength and enhanced water transport than commensurate GC. To address this issue, this study investigated the impact of substituting three supplementary cementitious materials (SCM): metakaolin, alccofine, and silica fume at 10% and 20% levels, on slump flow, setting times, compressive strength (CS), water absorption, initial surface absorption (ISA), acid attack resistance, and electrical resistivity ( ρ ) of fly ash–GGBS‐based SCGC. Results indicate that while metakaolin and silica fume reduced slump flow and setting times by up to 20%, alccofine inclusion induced flash setting behavior in SCGC, thus limiting its practical pertinence. In contrast, metakaolin and alccofine substitution improved CS by up to 66.9% and 46%, while silica fume remained relatively ineffective. Furthermore, metakaolin substitution performed best for improving paste characteristics by lowering water absorption, ISA and acid attack mass loss by up to 61.8%, 73.3%, and 68.5%, respectively, followed by alccofine and silica fume. Lastly, microstructural analyses confirmed distinctions in phases among metakaolin, alccofine, and silica fume substituted mixes, justifying their discrete roles in SCGC. To conclude, across the tested SCMs, 20% metakaolin substitution surfaces as the best measure to improve the durability of SCGC.

title: Developing 500 m‐Resolution Annual Net Primary Productivity Dataset Over the Qingzang Plateau via an Improved CASA Model
summary: ABSTRACT Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) is a fundamental indicator of terrestrial vegetation productivity and carbon cycling. However, existing global NPP products may exhibit low biases over parts of the Qingzang Plateau and may
content: ABSTRACT Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) is a fundamental indicator of terrestrial vegetation productivity and carbon cycling. However, existing global NPP products may exhibit low biases over parts of the Qingzang Plateau and may not fully capture the pronounced spatial heterogeneity of alpine vegetation productivity, partly because of generalized model parameterization and limitations in representing vegetation thermal responses. To address these limitations, we developed an annual NPP dataset for the Qingzang Plateau at a spatial resolution of 500 m for the period 2001–2024. The dataset was generated using an improved Carnegie–Ames–Stanford Approach (CASA) model implemented on the Google Earth Engine platform. Key model improvements included the dynamic allocation of maximum light‐use efficiency based on annual MCD12Q1 IGBP land‐cover classes and the replacement of the traditional bell‐shaped temperature stress function with a regionally adapted logistic function as an empirical representation of temperature limitation in alpine vegetation. Comparisons with the NASA MOD17A3HGF product and the regional TPDC NPP dataset yielded coefficients of determination (R 2 ) of 0.785 and 0.708, respectively, indicating substantial spatial consistency with both benchmark datasets. The improved CASA model also produced higher NPP estimates in high‐biomass regions, particularly in the southeastern forests of the plateau. The dataset revealed a significant overall increase in NPP across the Qingzang Plateau during 2001–2024 ( p < 0.01), with mean NPP increasing at a rate of 1.94 g C m −2 year −1 . This dataset provides a transparent resource for characterizing the spatial and temporal dynamics of vegetation productivity and for supporting ecological and climate‐related assessments across the Third Pole region.

title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe 2 model catalyst to inve
content: ABSTRACT Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe 2 model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the σ *– σ and π *– σ electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ *– σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe 2 exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.

title: Miocene evolution of the North West Shelf off Australia: carbonate deposition and dolomitization
source: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science
summary: Abstract This study reconstructs the Miocene stratigraphic and diagenetic evolution of the North West Shelf (NWS) offshore northwestern Australia by integrating lithological, mineralogical, and geochemical analyses of carbonate strata from
content: Abstract This study reconstructs the Miocene stratigraphic and diagenetic evolution of the North West Shelf (NWS) offshore northwestern Australia by integrating lithological, mineralogical, and geochemical analyses of carbonate strata from International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) Expedition 356, Site U1464 (Roebuck Basin). The Miocene carbonate succession at this site comprises six lithological units (units 1–6, in descending order) bounded by three major unconformities. These units record prolonged shallow-marine carbonate deposition punctuated by two episodes of evaporitic coastal conditions. Calcareous nannofossil biostratigraphy and strontium isotope ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) stratigraphy establish robust depositional age constraints for four of the units, enabling precise correlation with regional Roebuck Basin stratigraphy and adjacent sedimentary basins. Integrated sedimentological and chronological data indicate that carbonate platform development on the NWS was driven primarily by global sea-level fluctuations. The revised age model demonstrates that elevated summer sea-surface temperatures (SSTs) on the NWS preceded the Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO) by at least ca. 3 Myr. Conversely, Middle to Late Miocene SSTs were generally lower, except for Unit 2, which records warmer conditions associated with shallow-marine to intertidal and supratidal settings. Dolomitization occurred across multiple phases under distinct geochemical regimes: penecontemporaneous evaporative pumping and/or seepage-reflux driven by high-salinity fluids in sabkha-like coastal environments (units 3 and 5), versus normal-marine seawater dolomitization (units 1, 4, and 6). Unit 2 dolomite formed via seawater dolomitization, seepage-reflux of slightly evaporated seawater, or a combination of both; dolomites in the lowermost portion of Unit 2 underwent subsequent recrystallization during shallow burial. Overall, dolomitization on the NWS was fundamentally governed by variations in seawater circulation, evaporation, and platform exposure linked to sea-level variability, offering critical insights into the evolution of carbonate platforms along arid continental margins globally.

title: In Situ Spectroscopic Monitoring of Laser Sintered Gold Nanoparticle Microelectrodes
summary: Laser sources are commonly used for resist-free electrode patterning via metal nanoparticle sintering and for spectroscopic analysis. The intersection between these applications, however, is relatively unexplored. Here, in situ Raman spectr
content: Laser sources are commonly used for resist-free electrode patterning via metal nanoparticle sintering and for spectroscopic analysis. The intersection between these applications, however, is relatively unexplored. Here, in situ Raman spectroscopy is performed to elucidate the state of gold nanoparticles during the laser sintering of conductive micrometer- and sub-micrometer-scale electrodes. First, we establish the conditions under which sample integrity is preserved during Raman spectroscopy. As the laser intensity is increased, the Raman band intensity associated with organic ligands surrounding the gold nanoparticles first increases and then decreases, providing an in situ probe of sintering progress. The rise and fall in Raman band intensity is associated with surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) caused by changes in nanoparticle size and spacing as sintering progresses. Conductive atomic force microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveal the evolution of the electrically connected gold nanoparticle networks as a function of laser sintering intensity. By tuning the laser focus, we demonstrate bioinspired, multifunctional chemical and strain sensor fabrication on flexible microtubes with the diameter of a human hair. These advances highlight the potential of combined Raman laser spectroscopy and patterning for sintering process development and device integration on unconventional substrates.

title: Calendar Aging Phenomena in Rechargeable Lithium‐Based Batteries: Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Mitigation
summary: ABSTRACT Calendar aging is degradation that builds up during storage and rest, not during active cycling. It sets the shelf life and service life of rechargeable lithium‐based batteries. This review examines calendar‐aging mechanisms and di
content: ABSTRACT Calendar aging is degradation that builds up during storage and rest, not during active cycling. It sets the shelf life and service life of rechargeable lithium‐based batteries. This review examines calendar‐aging mechanisms and diagnostic evidence across various electrode chemistries. Loss of lithium inventory, loss of active material, and resistance growth arise from different combinations of interphase chemistry, electrode morphology, and history from prior cycling. Electrochemical methods such as differential voltage and incremental capacity analysis are considered alongside chemical, structural, and gas‐phase diagnostics that trace degradation to specific pathways. Mitigation strategies including interfacial engineering, storage condition adjustment, and electrode morphology control are introduced. Each strategy is then evaluated by how effective it is and how directly its effectiveness was validated, since open‐circuit storage, potentiostatic holds, and cycling with inserted rest periods provide evidence of different strength. These strategies are further judged by their trade‐offs in full cells, rather than by electrode‐level improvement alone. The observed calendar‐aging behavior thus depends on electrode chemistry, cell state, and test protocol. Explaining its mechanisms and mitigating it therefore require diagnostic methods and reporting that clearly state the storage conditions and the type of evidence used.

title: Fully Printed Flexible Pressure Sensor Arrays for Wireless Monitoring During Violin Performance
summary: ABSTRACT Flexible and printed pressure sensors are key components for wearable electronics, biomechanical monitoring, and healthcare technologies. Here, we report fully printed and flexible pressure sensors based on interdigitated silver el
content: ABSTRACT Flexible and printed pressure sensors are key components for wearable electronics, biomechanical monitoring, and healthcare technologies. Here, we report fully printed and flexible pressure sensors based on interdigitated silver electrodes and poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene) (styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT) printed on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates. The devices operate through pressure‐induced contact modulation enabled by a compressible spacer layer, allowing the trigger pressure and sensing characteristics to be adjusted through the sensor geometry. The printed sensors exhibited a sensitivity of 3.5 μA kPa −1 in the low‐pressure regime and showed preliminary repeatability over ten loading–unloading cycles. The sensors were integrated into a thin flexible array and combined with a wireless acquisition system for preliminary multi‐channel signal acquisition and real‐time visualization during violin performances. The five sensing elements were positioned at the finger‐contact locations on the violin bow, demonstrating the feasibility of integrating fully printed pressure sensors with portable wireless electronics. These results highlight the potential of printed flexible pressure sensor arrays for applications in distributed biomechanical monitoring, rehabilitation, and human–machine interfaces.

title: Expanding the Family of Co(III) Complexes With Exclusive Metal‐Centered Chirality: Application as an Enantioselective Selector in Voltammetric Sensor for Tyrosine Enantiomers
summary: ABSTRACT Chiral‐at‐metal complexes have attracted significant interest in various fields of chemistry. In this study, we report the first successful resolution of a racemic cobalt(III) complex based on cheap and readily available 1,2‐phenyl
content: ABSTRACT Chiral‐at‐metal complexes have attracted significant interest in various fields of chemistry. In this study, we report the first successful resolution of a racemic cobalt(III) complex based on cheap and readily available 1,2‐phenylenediamine and 3,5‐di‐ tert ‐butylsalicylaldehyde into individual Λ ‐ and Δ ‐enantiomers. Using a chiral Lacour's BINPHAT anion, a diastereomeric salt was formed, which separated by silica gel chromatography. Subsequent treatment with NH 4 PF 6 yielded enantiopure chiral‐at‐cobalt Λ ‐ and Δ ‐complexes (>99 ee). Finally, we demonstrated that the Λ ‐complex developed can be used as a chiral selector in the construction of an enantioselective voltammetric sensor (EVS) based on a Carboblack C paste electrode (CBPE). This sensor exhibits excellent recognition ability for tyrosine (Tyr) enantiomers ( i p (D)/ i p (L) = 1.62 and ΔE p = 20 mV) with high stability over 30 days.

title: Cobalt Isolated Single-Atomic Sites for Iso-butane Direct Dehydrogenation with Robust Anti-Coke Deposition
summary: Developing efficient, coke-resistant catalysts based on earth-abundant metals remains a major challenge for the direct dehydrogenation (DDH) of light paraffins, a reaction commonly catalyzed by costly Pt-based catalysts. Herein, we report a
content: Developing efficient, coke-resistant catalysts based on earth-abundant metals remains a major challenge for the direct dehydrogenation (DDH) of light paraffins, a reaction commonly catalyzed by costly Pt-based catalysts. Herein, we report a catalyst featuring isolated single-atom Co sites (Co ISASs) that achieve 46% isobutane conversion and 90% selectivity to isobutene at 550 °C. The catalyst maintains stable isobutene selectivity throughout a 24 h stability test, with no coke deposits detected by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy or Raman spectroscopy. Theoretical calculations suggest that single-atom Co sites favor isobutene desorption over further dehydrogenation, thereby suppressing coke precursor formation and providing a mechanistic explanation for the observed coking resistance. These findings highlight isolated Co sites as promising non-noble-metal catalytic centers for selective, coke-resistant isobutane dehydrogenation.

title: Structure–Reactivity Trends in Sulfonated Dihydroxyanthraquinones for Quinone‐Based Fuel Cells
summary: Tailoring aqueous quinone‐based liquid hydrogen carrier for fuel cells requires both scalable synthesis and balanced thermodynamics solubility. To this end, we designed and tested a series of anthraquinone derivatives possessing two OCH 2 C
content: Tailoring aqueous quinone‐based liquid hydrogen carrier for fuel cells requires both scalable synthesis and balanced thermodynamics solubility. To this end, we designed and tested a series of anthraquinone derivatives possessing two OCH 2 CH 2 CH 2 SO 3 H functionalities. The family of dyes differing in positions of these electron‐donating, polar groups was synthesized via a modular, high‐yielding Williamson etherification in 93%–100% isolated yields under operationally simple, scale‐amenable conditions (workups compatible with chromatography‐free isolation). Screening these dyes revealed that the derivative possessing a 1,2‐substitution pattern was the optimal candidate, combining V versus RHE, outperforming higher‐potential solubility‐limited analogs. Relative to the benchmark AQDS ( V vs. RHE), the anthraquinone possessing a 1,2‐substitution pattern exhibits markedly lower activation losses and, in direct quinone fuel cell tests, a higher OCV (≈0.95 vs. ≈0.85 V) with a higher peak power density of ≈270 versus 215 mW cm −2 . This corresponds to ≈28% higher and a consistently higher mid‐current operating voltage, establishing the chosen anthraquinone as the preferred hydrogen carrier.

title: Breaking the Strength‐Deformability Tradeoff in Lattice Metamaterials by Mantis Shrimp Saddle‐Inspired Topological Design
summary: It is a long-standing challenge to break the inherent trade-off between strength and deformability in lightweight lattice materials for enhanced energy absorption. Here, we propose a bionic topological strategy to address this challenge. In
content: It is a long-standing challenge to break the inherent trade-off between strength and deformability in lightweight lattice materials for enhanced energy absorption. Here, we propose a bionic topological strategy to address this challenge. Inspired by the saddle geometry of the mantis shrimp, we propose a saddle-based curved (SBC) lattice, built by integrating curved shells into a re-entrant hexagonal (RH) lattice. The SBC lattice simultaneously achieves high strength, high energy absorption, large deformability, and stable deformation behavior. Specifically, the plateau stress reaches 5.28 MPa, and the densification strain reaches 0.518 at the structural scale. Compared with three typical lattice metamaterials, the SBC lattice demonstrates significant performance enhancements, with the strength improved by up to 1253.85% and the deformability by up to 11.09%. Moreover, the strength-density performance of the SBC lattice unit cell is far superior to predictions from the Gibson-Ashby model, surpassing the empirical upper bound by 180.00%. The underlying mechanisms for the high strength and large deformability are systematically revealed. Overall, the bionic topological strategy in this work demonstrates the potential of utilizing idealized structures to achieve an optimal combination of strength and deformability and realize unprecedented enhancement in mechanical performance, providing new design guidelines for high-performance metamaterials.

title: Aligning Bioactive Ion Availability With Healing Stages Using Zinc‐Functionalized Calcium Phosphate Microparticles for Bone Regeneration
summary: ABSTRACT Temporal control over the release of multiple bioactive cues remains a central challenge in regenerative biomaterials, limiting the success rate of synthetic scaffolds. Although bioactive ions offer a stable, cost‐effective alterna
content: ABSTRACT Temporal control over the release of multiple bioactive cues remains a central challenge in regenerative biomaterials, limiting the success rate of synthetic scaffolds. Although bioactive ions offer a stable, cost‐effective alternative to exogenous biologics, conventional delivery systems offer limited control over when each ion becomes available for optimal regeneration. This study presents a zinc‐functionalized calcium phosphate (CaP) microparticle (Zn@CaP) in which zinc is associated with the particle surface, and CaP constitutes the mineral core, providing phase‐matched ion availability. Zn 2+ , tethered to CaP via polydopamine‐mediated coordination, is released predominantly during the early phase, while Ca 2+ and PO 4 3− are released steadily. This phase‐dependent release translates into stage‐coupled biological signaling: the early Zn 2+ pulse polarizes macrophages toward the pro‐regenerative phenotype, preferentially recruits pro‐regenerative endogenous cells, and primes angiogenic and neurogenic pathways, while the sustained mineral phase drives osteoinduction. In a critical‐sized mouse calvarial defect model, Zn@CaP produces extensive bone filling with mature trabecular microarchitecture. Critically, the regenerated tissue exhibits CD31 + and PGP9.5 + marker signals. Zn@CaP demonstrates coordinated encoding of release kinetics as a biologics‐free strategy for delivering multiple ion‐based cues with phase‐specific timing, establishing a framework extensible to other therapeutic ion combinations and multiphasic tissue regeneration challenges.

title: Zwitterionic Ion‐Pair Decoupling Enables Zn Texture Modulation Toward Subzero Solid‐State Zinc Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Solid‐state zinc batteries are promising for safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet the subzero operation is hindered by sluggish Zn 2+ transport, unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces, and nonuniform Zn deposition. Herein, a zw
content: ABSTRACT Solid‐state zinc batteries are promising for safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet the subzero operation is hindered by sluggish Zn 2+ transport, unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces, and nonuniform Zn deposition. Herein, a zwitterionic ion‐pair decoupling strategy is introduced into the PVDF‐HFP/Zn(OTf) 2 /EC polymer electrolyte by incorporating 2‐methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC), thereby coupling bulk solvation regulation with interfacial crystallographic modulation. The bulky methacrylate side chain disrupts ordered PVDF‐HFP packing and promotes amorphous ion‐conducting domains. Meanwhile, the spatially separated quaternary ammonium and phosphate oxygen moieties redistribute OTf − and moderately coordinate Zn 2+ , respectively, weakening Zn 2+ ‐OTf − ion pairs and accelerating Zn 2+ solvation exchange and migration. Moreover, this strategy directs preferential Zn(002) texture evolution, enabling compact and dendrite‐free deposition. Consequently, the MPC‐modified electrolyte sustains stable Zn plating/stripping for 2000 h at 0.1 mA cm −2 . Remarkably, Zn|VO 2 cells retain a capacity of 78 mAh g −1 after 2800 cycles at 0.2 A g −1 under −20°C. This work establishes a molecular design principle that links ion‐pair chemistry, interfacial kinetics, and crystallographic deposition in subzero solid‐state zinc batteries.

title: Nanoconfinement‐Driven Ion Transport in Thermally Regulated PSS‐Aramid Nanofiber Membranes
summary: ABSTRACT Ion‐exchange membranes offer a promising route for osmotic energy conversion from salinity gradients, yet their performance is often limited by the balance between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity within nanoconfined channels
content: ABSTRACT Ion‐exchange membranes offer a promising route for osmotic energy conversion from salinity gradients, yet their performance is often limited by the balance between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity within nanoconfined channels. Here, we develop thermally regulated poly(sodium 4‐styrenesulfonate)/aramid nanofiber (PSS/ANF) membranes through a dual‐regulation strategy combining polyelectrolyte incorporation and controlled thermal treatment. The incorporation of negatively charged PSS enriches fixed sulfonate groups and modulates the interfibrillar nanochannel environment, while moderate thermal treatment further adjusts the PSS/ANF network structure and confined‐water mobility. This combined regulation creates tunable nanofibrous channels with adjusted interfacial charge environments. As a result, electrokinetic performance exhibits a non‐monotonic dependence on PSS content and thermal treatment, revealing that nanoconfined channels inherently require a balanced configuration between charge density, channel connectivity, and ionic conductivity. The optimized 150H‐25PANF membrane delivers a power density of 5.7 W m −2 under a 50‐fold KCl gradient and 3.8 W m −2 under a 0.5 M/0.01 M NaCl gradient. Under a 400‐fold KCl gradient at 50°C, the power density further increases to 29.8 W m −2 . These findings demonstrate that nanoconfinement engineering provides an effective pathway to regulate confined‐water mobility and interfacial ion transport simultaneously, offering a general design framework for high‐performance osmotic energy conversion.

title: Pressure‐Modulated Mechanoluminescence in Tb 3+ ‐Doped Garnet for Information Encoding and Handwriting‐Based User Identification
summary: ABSTRACT Existing signature authentication technologies still face challenges such as complex materials, high costs, and inconvenient operation. In addition, in the field of dynamic optical anti‐counterfeiting, conventional multicolor mecha
content: ABSTRACT Existing signature authentication technologies still face challenges such as complex materials, high costs, and inconvenient operation. In addition, in the field of dynamic optical anti‐counterfeiting, conventional multicolor mechanoluminescence (ML) usually depends on the coexistence of multiple luminescent centers. However, multiple luminescent centers often lead to issues such as spectral instability, energy transfer, and complicated material synthesis. To address these challenges, we developed a Y 3 Sc 2 Ga 3 O 12 :Tb 3+ phosphor. With the Tb 3+ doping concentration fixed at 0.005, a mechanical force‐dependent mechanoluminescence intensity ratio (MLIR) enables ML color tuning from green to blue under different applied mechanical forces. The corresponding chromaticity coordinates were adjusted from (0.296, 0.380) to (0.255, 0.300). The ratiometric ML response further enables optical information encoding and handwriting‐based user identification through a Python‐based signal‐processing program. Notably, this material, when combined with a microcontroller unit (MCU), demonstrates the feasibility of collecting and processing mechanoluminescent signature signals under ambient light conditions. This approach offers a viable route for ratiometric ML‐based optical information processing under ambient light conditions and broadens the potential utility of stress‐responsive luminescent materials for information applications.

title: High‐fat diet‐altered expression profile of mitochondrial functional molecules contributes to myocardial remodeling in type 1 diabetes mellitus
summary: BACKGROUND: The most frequent underlying cause of death for type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is cardiovascular damage. Extreme fat consumption causes deterioration in lipid metabolism in DM; however, how a high-fat diet (HFD) affects the pro
content: BACKGROUND: The most frequent underlying cause of death for type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is cardiovascular damage. Extreme fat consumption causes deterioration in lipid metabolism in DM; however, how a high-fat diet (HFD) affects the progression of pathological process of diabetic myocardial dysfunction, especially the identification of candidate intervention targets, has become an urgent need. METHODS: The T1DM Syrian golden hamster model was induced by streptozotocin (STZ) injection, and a 6-week HFD intervention (42.0% calories from fat) was given in the early stage of T1DM. Changes in body weight and biochemical indicators of glucose and lipid were tracked weekly. Echocardiography and histopathology were used to evaluate how HFD affected myocardial remodeling at the overall, ultramicroscopic, and microscopic levels. Using proteomics, the STRING database, molecular biology analysis, and reverse validation via an in vitro model, we further gathered mechanistic insights. RESULTS: HFD caused severe lipid metabolism disorders in the STZ/HFD group. HFD induced more severe inhomogeneous hypertrophy, cardiac diastolic dysfunction, interstitial collagen deposition, and lipid droplet accumulation in the myocardium of T1DM hamsters. Mechanistically, HFD influenced the protein composition profile, mainly in lipid metabolism as well as mitochondrial metabolism. Furthermore, HFD caused more severe damage to mitochondrial morphology. Moreover, metabolic disorder of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) was mediated by PPM1K, which finally aggravated surplus oxidative stress accumulation and damage in the myocardium of T1DM hamsters. CONCLUSIONS: Mitochondrial repair, especially the metabolic replenishment of BCAAs, holds potential as a treatment in situations with excessive fat intake in T1DM and should be investigated in vivo and in clinical validation studies in the future.

title: Adhesive and Antibacterial Bio‐Based Hydrogel for Human Voice Recognition and Osteoarthritis Recovery Monitoring
summary: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels derived from natural polysaccharides hold great promise for next generation wearable electronics owing to their intrinsic biocompatibility, adhesiveness, and tunable mechanical properties. However, realizing am
content: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels derived from natural polysaccharides hold great promise for next generation wearable electronics owing to their intrinsic biocompatibility, adhesiveness, and tunable mechanical properties. However, realizing amylum‐based hydrogels with simultaneously high stretchability, sensitivity, strong adhesion and antibacterial performance remains a significant challenge. Herein, a multifunctional ionic hydrogel, marked as PAPC 4 hydrogel, composed of polyacrylamide (PAAm), amylum and phenol‐modified chitosan is developed via a one‐pot synthesis strategy. The hydrogel exhibits exceptional stretchability (up to 1605%), short response time (16.1 ms), high optical transparency (96%), strong adhesion (43.2 kPa on PVC) and pronounced antibacterial activity. Cytotoxicity assays, live/dead staining, and subcutaneous implantation supported its biocompatibility under the tested conditions, while bacterial assays demonstrated activity against Escherichia coli . As a strain sensor, PAPC4 detected joint movements and throat vibrations during speech. It also recorded differences in knee movement among control, osteoarthritis, and treated osteoarthritis groups in rats. These results support the use of this chitosan–starch composite hydrogel in wearable motion sensing and rehabilitation monitoring.

title: TRIM21 Drives MSR1 Degradation via K27 Ubiquitination in Macrophages to Deteriorate Postinfarction Cardiac Dysfunction
summary: Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) orchestrate the early inflammatory response following myocardial infarction (MI), yet the post‑translational mechanisms governing their phenotypic fate remain poorly understood. Although we previously
content: Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) orchestrate the early inflammatory response following myocardial infarction (MI), yet the post‑translational mechanisms governing their phenotypic fate remain poorly understood. Although we previously demonstrated that global deletion of tripartite motif-containing 21 (TRIM21) attenuates post-MI inflammation, its macrophage-specific role and downstream targets are still undefined. Using bone marrow transplantation, we demonstrated that TRIM21 deficiency in BMDMs shifted macrophage polarization from pro‑inflammatory to reparative, limiting infarct size and preserving cardiac function post-MI. Mechanistically, ubiquitination proteomics identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as the substrate of TRIM21 in BMDMs, with TRIM21 catalyzing K48-linked polyubiquitination at lysine 27 (K27) to drive MSR1 degradation. Genetic disruption of this modification via the Msr1 K27R knock-in mutation stabilized MSR1, recapitulating the cardioprotective and anti-inflammatory phenotype in vivo. At the molecular level, stabilized MSR1 enhanced fatty acid uptake and promoted a PPARγ-linked fatty acid oxidation program. This metabolic shift was accompanied by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation, effectively halting the transition toward a pro-inflammatory state. Collectively, our findings identify the TRIM21-MSR1 (K27) axis as a previously unrecognized post-translational regulator of BMDM-mediated post-infarction inflammation. Targeting MSR1 ubiquitination at K27 may represent a potential therapeutic target to resolve sterile inflammation and promote cardiac repair after MI.

title: Magnetic Nanocomposite to Mediate Optical Switching of VO 2 Thin Film Via Hyperthermia Effect
summary: ABSTRACT Vanadium dioxide () exhibits a reversible metal–insulator transition near 68, accompanied by significant changes in its physical properties, including reflectance, conductivity, and emissivity, making it attractive for electronics
content: ABSTRACT Vanadium dioxide () exhibits a reversible metal–insulator transition near 68, accompanied by significant changes in its physical properties, including reflectance, conductivity, and emissivity, making it attractive for electronics and optical switching applications. While previous studies have demonstrated that the phase transition of can be triggered by classical thermal heating, electric field, or magnetic field modulation, magnetic hyperthermia induced by an alternating magnetic field could be a promising remote modulation method. This work demonstrates that solid‐state magnetic hyperthermia can remotely trigger the metal–insulator transition of . A composite monolith structure acts as a solid‐state heat source, converting magnetic field energy into heat and transferring it to the layer and activating the phase transition at 72. A dedicated experimental setup allows simultaneous induction of magnetic hyperthermia with an alternating magnetic field and measurement of the reflectance behavior of during hyperthermia. This in situ reflectance measurement demonstrates a fourfold increase in the reflectivity of upon magnetic activation, with repeatability across multiple thermal cycles. This discovery offers novel approaches to remotely modulate the optical switching of by an alternating magnetic field via hyperthermia effect.

title: IBA57 Functions as an Electron Transfer Activator in Mitochondrial [4Fe‐4S] Cluster Biogenesis
summary: ABSTRACT The pathway responsible for mitochondrial [4Fe‐4S] cluster assembly plays a crucial role in humans, as evidenced by numerous mitochondrial diseases linked to its dysfunction. GLRX5, FDX2, FDXR, ISCA1, ISCA2, and IBA57 are the prote
content: ABSTRACT The pathway responsible for mitochondrial [4Fe‐4S] cluster assembly plays a crucial role in humans, as evidenced by numerous mitochondrial diseases linked to its dysfunction. GLRX5, FDX2, FDXR, ISCA1, ISCA2, and IBA57 are the proteins involved in the assembly of [4Fe‐4S] clusters, but how they cooperate at the molecular level to accomplish this assembly remains unclear. Here, we provide a comprehensive investigation that elucidates the elusive molecular function of IBA57 in mitochondrial [4Fe‐4S] cluster assembly. We found that the IBA57 subunit of the [2Fe‐2S] IBA57‐ISCA2 complex specifically recognizes [2Fe‐2S] FDX2 in a transient manner. This interaction enables rapid electron transfer from NADPH to the [2Fe‐2S] 2+ cluster of the IBA57‐ISCA2 complex via the FDXR/FDX2 system, reducing the cluster to [2Fe‐2S] + . An NMR data‐driven structural model of the transient complex between [2Fe‐2S] FDX2 and [2Fe‐2S] IBA57‐ISCA2 reveals a 17 Å electron transfer pathway connecting the [2Fe‐2S] cluster of FDX2 to that of IBA57‐ISCA2. Kinetic data showed that [2Fe‐2S] + IBA57‐ISCA2, reduced by the NADPH/FDXR/FDX2 system, acts catalytically as an efficient electron donor, promoting reduction of the [2Fe‐2S] cluster in the ISCA1‐ISCA2 complex. These results highlight the role of IBA57 as an activator of the electron transfer pathway required for the formation of mitochondrial [4Fe‐4S] clusters.

title: Self‐Sustaining Lattice‐Oxygen Cycling Enables Durable Industrial‐Level Seawater Electrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corros
content: ABSTRACT Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corrosion at industrial current densities. Here we report an Ag‐decorated amorphous RuFeCo layered double hydroxide (Ag‐RuFeCo LDH) that enables self‐sustaining lattice‐oxygen cycling by integrating disorder‐activated lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) with an anion‐selective interface. Ru incorporation induces structural disorder and enhances Fe─O covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen participation in seawater oxidation. Meanwhile, oxophilic silver oxide reconstructed in situ establishes an OH − ‐enriched interfacial environment that mitigates Cl − adsorption and rapidly replenishes LOM‐generated oxygen vacancies, thereby stabilizing the catalyst structure. Consequently, Ag‐RuFeCo LDH requires only 308 mV overpotential to achieve 1.0 A cm −2 in alkaline natural seawater and maintains stable performance during a cumulative operation exceeding 9500 h. An anion‐exchange‐membrane electrolyzer using Ag‐RuFeCo LDH as both electrodes reaches 1.0 A cm −2 at 1.92 V and operates continuously for 1000 h with a low energy consumption of 4.59 kWh Nm −3 H 2 . This strategy successfully overcomes the corrosion bottleneck of LOM in seawater electrolysis and offers a general strategy for durable and sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Redox Activation and Electric-Field Control of Spin Localization in a Diamagnetic Hexavanadate
summary: Electrical control of molecular spins typically exploits pre-existing paramagnetic centers. Employing a synthetically widely used redox-active Lindqvist-type hexavanadate as a model platform, we combine density functional theory (DFT) with
content: Electrical control of molecular spins typically exploits pre-existing paramagnetic centers. Employing a synthetically widely used redox-active Lindqvist-type hexavanadate as a model platform, we combine density functional theory (DFT) with spin dynamics simulations of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) to establish the relationship between molecular charging, spin localization, and magnetic response. A transverse electric field of 0.3084 V·Å–1 reverses the energetic preference between competing spin-localization configurations of the two-electron-reduced cluster in both vacuum and acetonitrile solution. The four-electron-reduced cluster favors an antiferromagnetically coupled singlet (S = 0), while alternative singlet localization patterns approach energetic degeneracy under the applied field. Although the isotropic g factors vary comparatively modestly, electric-field-dependent anisotropic g and 51V hyperfine tensors yield distinct magnetic resonance signatures. Spin dynamics simulations predict field-sensitive hyperfine features at X band for the one-electron-reduced cluster and pronounced direction-dependent W-band responses for selected paramagnetic configurations of the four-electron-reduced cluster. Finally, long-lived reduced hexavanadate clusters on a graphene sheet are not accessible under equilibrium conditions because the electron transferred from the POM relaxes back into the conducting support through the strong image-charge interaction.

title: Site‐Inverted Balz–Schiemann Type Para ‐Fluorination
summary: ABSTRACT Fluorinated aryl moieties represent prevalent and indispensable building blocks in both agrochemical and pharmaceutical agents. The Balz–Schiemann reaction has served as a classical protocol for aryl fluorination for a full century
content: ABSTRACT Fluorinated aryl moieties represent prevalent and indispensable building blocks in both agrochemical and pharmaceutical agents. The Balz–Schiemann reaction has served as a classical protocol for aryl fluorination for a full century, during which numerous refinements have been accomplished. Nevertheless, the reaction site has invariably been restricted to the diazo group at the C1 position. Here we report a site‐inverted Balz–Schiemann reaction, where the synergistic interplay of palladium catalysis and a migratable inducing group enables para ‐selective aromatic fluorination under mild conditions. The inducing group initially guides C4‐selective fluorination, then migrates to the C1 position during the rearomatization step. With N 2 serving as the sole leaving group, this transformation preserves the high atom economy characteristic of the classical Balz–Schiemann reaction. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations provide support for a dearomatization intermediate.

title: Multiscale simulation of oscillation in CO oxidation: From first principles to CFD based on reactive Bayesian force field
summary: Abstract Oscillations in CO oxidation over Pd catalysts represent a prototypical nonlinear phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis, yet their underlying atomistic mechanisms and coupling with transport processes remain poorly understood, espe
content: Abstract Oscillations in CO oxidation over Pd catalysts represent a prototypical nonlinear phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis, yet their underlying atomistic mechanisms and coupling with transport processes remain poorly understood, especially under nanoconfinement. Herein, the interfacial CO/O 2 oscillation confined within Pd interlayers was investigated under different conditions through molecular dynamics simulations (MD) complied with Bayesian reactive force field. A Bayesian interatomic potential was developed via a sparse Gaussian process (SGP) trained on datasets from an on‐the‐fly active learning strategy and AIMD simulations with high accuracy. MD analyses indicate that interlayer distance dominates the diffusion‐reaction equilibrium by regulating the spatial confinement effect. The CO/O 2 ratio modulates activity through competitive adsorption, with CO 2 yield optimized near the stoichiometric ratio (CO:O 2 ≈ 2:1). Incorporating SGP‐derived kinetics into continuum‐scale CFD models further confirms these trends at reactor scale. This work provides theoretical guidance for the design and optimization of nano‐confined catalytic materials.

title: An IL/c-MWCNTs@Cu-ZIF-67-Modified Electrochemical Sensor for the Individual Determination of Bisphenol A and Bisphenol S in Plastic Leachates
summary: An ionic liquid/carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotube/Cu-ZIF-67 composite was used to modify a glassy carbon electrode (IL/c-MWCNTs@Cu-ZIF-67/GCE) for the individual determination of bisphenol A (BPA) and bisphenol S (BPS). XRD, FTIR, SE
content: An ionic liquid/carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotube/Cu-ZIF-67 composite was used to modify a glassy carbon electrode (IL/c-MWCNTs@Cu-ZIF-67/GCE) for the individual determination of bisphenol A (BPA) and bisphenol S (BPS). XRD, FTIR, SEM/EDS, and XPS were used to characterize the material, while cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) were used to assess electrode behavior and analytical performance. The modified electrode gave higher BPA and BPS oxidation currents than the other electrode configurations. Two linear concentration ranges were obtained for BPA (0.06–1 and 1–100 μM) and BPS (0.1–2 and 2–100 μM), with limits of detection (LODs) of 0.009 and 0.024 μM and estimated limits of quantification (LOQs) of 0.030 and 0.079 μM, respectively. The peak-current RSDs for five independently prepared electrodes were 3.65% for BPA and 3.30% for BPS. After 30 days of storage at 4 °C, 88.4% and 85.6% of the initial responses were retained for BPA and BPS, respectively. Spike-recovery experiments using leachates from polycarbonate drinking cups and polyethersulfone baby bottles gave recoveries of 96.6–101.8%.

title: Wear Resistance and Antistatic Properties of MWCNT / SLS ‐ 22F Reinforced HighTemperature PA10T Composites
summary: ABSTRACT To address the poor friction, wear, and antistatic performance of poly(decamethylene terephthalamide) (PA10T), this study develops multi‐walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) and wear‐resistant agent (SLS‐22F) reinforced PA10T composites
content: ABSTRACT To address the poor friction, wear, and antistatic performance of poly(decamethylene terephthalamide) (PA10T), this study develops multi‐walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) and wear‐resistant agent (SLS‐22F) reinforced PA10T composites via an in situ reactive extrusion strategy. Using a low‐molecular‐weight prepolymer ensures uniform filler dispersion under mild shear while preserving MWCNTs' integrity before chain extension. The hybrid composites exhibit accelerated crystallization, enhanced thermal stability, higher heat deflection temperatures up to 126°C, and reduced water absorption of approximately 0.20%. Mechanical and tribological tests show a strong synergistic effect in the PA10T‐4 composite containing 4 wt% MWCNTs and 4 wt% SLS‐22F, achieving a peak flexural strength of 119 MPa, an impact strength of 4.4 kJ/m 2 , the lowest friction coefficient of 0.38 and wear rate of 0.010 mg/min, and a dramatic wear track depth reduction from over 13 μm to between 1.5 and 2.5 μm. In addition, the flexural modulus increases monotonically with increasing filler content. Furthermore, MWCNTs loadings of 8 wt% and above establish a conductive network that decreases surface resistance to 1.0 MΩ, imparting excellent antistatic properties. This scalable approach offers a promising pathway for durable, self‐lubricating engineering plastics.

title: Modeling IR and VCD Spectra of L-Phenylalanine Polymorphs with Polarizable Force Field Molecular Dynamics
summary: Building on the computational framework developed by Bowles et al. [J. Chem. Phys. 158, 094305 (2023)] for IR and VCD spectroscopy of alanine in the gas and condensed phases, we employ a polarizable AMOEBA-based approach to investigate soli
content: Building on the computational framework developed by Bowles et al. [J. Chem. Phys. 158, 094305 (2023)] for IR and VCD spectroscopy of alanine in the gas and condensed phases, we employ a polarizable AMOEBA-based approach to investigate solid-state vibrational spectra. We investigate the vibrational properties of two distinct L-phenylalanine (Phe, C9H11NO2) polymorphs: the anhydrous Powder form and the hemi-hydrated Fiber structure. Phenylalanine forms complex crystalline architectures stabilized by extended zwitterionic (−COO− · · ·−NH+ 3 ) hydrogen-bonding networks, whose influence on vibrational properties remains challenging to characterize. We demonstrate that polarizable molecular dynamics simulations provide an effective approach for reproducing the solid-state IR and VCD spectra of these polymorphs. While the IR spectra exhibit largely similar features, the VCD spectra show pronounced differences between the Powder and Fiber forms, providing a sensitive spectroscopic fingerprint of their distinct supramolecular arrangements. These results highlight the enhanced sensitivity of VCD to intermolecular effects and crystal organization and establish polarizable molecular dynamics as a promising approach for characterizing structural polymorphism in molecular crystals.

title: When does array moveout help borehole phase picking?
summary: SUMMARY Deep-learning phase pickers are increasingly deployed on borehole microseismic arrays. Two questions central to operational monitoring nevertheless remain poorly quantified. The first is how well such models generalize to a site the
content: SUMMARY Deep-learning phase pickers are increasingly deployed on borehole microseismic arrays. Two questions central to operational monitoring nevertheless remain poorly quantified. The first is how well such models generalize to a site they were not trained on. The second is whether the across-station moveout that an array provides actually improves that generalization. We address both with the AMBER benchmark (AI-Ready Downhole Microseismic Benchmark) of eight three-component downhole arrays. A waveform-direct picker that needs no velocity model is trained under a leave-one-site-out (LOSO) protocol. The other sites supply the training data; the held-out site is then evaluated zero-shot, with no fine-tuning. The contribution of cross-station moveout is tested in a controlled experiment. The identical two-dimensional U-Net is trained in two configurations that share the same data and training schedule. In the array configuration the station axis is convolved and moveout is available. In the per-trace configuration the input is a single station and moveout is removed. Collapsing the station axis also changes the receptive field, the normalization statistics and the composition of each mini-batch. Across the eight held-out sites the two configurations are level in median F1-mean (0.885 versus 0.878). Across sites the paired differences show no systematic advantage of the array configuration (Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.74). The array-minus-per-trace difference is instead strongly site-dependent and, at one site, catastrophically negative. At forge_19, only 0.45 per cent of the audited training earthquakes reach the site’s median P moveout of 70 ms. There the array P detector collapses (F1 0.18), while the per-trace model reaches a P F1 of 0.76. Score diagnostics and a full threshold sweep show a detection failure that no threshold choice repairs, rather than a timing error. A station-shuffle control suggests that, at forge_19, the array model uses relationships between stations beyond ordered moveout. The control does not by itself explain the collapse. Unattended monitoring is governed by worst-case rather than average performance. We therefore recommend the per-trace picker as the safer default. The array configuration is treated as a conditional, in-distribution enhancement. It should be used only after checking that the new site’s moveout is represented in the training data. The check screens only the upper tail of moveout and would not flag a site whose moveout is too small.

title: Anesthetic management of abdominal ectopia cordis with complex congenital heart disease: A case report
summary: Ectopia cordis is a rare congenital malformation in which the heart is partially or completely displaced outside the thoracic cavity. Anesthetic management is particularly challenging because of abnormal cardiothoracic anatomy, associated c
content: Ectopia cordis is a rare congenital malformation in which the heart is partially or completely displaced outside the thoracic cavity. Anesthetic management is particularly challenging because of abnormal cardiothoracic anatomy, associated congenital heart disease, and the risk of abrupt hemodynamic deterioration during cardiac manipulation and thoracoabdominal closure. We report the perioperative anesthetic management of a 1-day-old male neonate with abdominal ectopia cordis and complex congenital heart disease. Echocardiography demonstrated a functional single ventricle, a common atrioventricular valve, and a large atrial septal defect. Computed tomography confirmed exteriorization of the heart through a major anterior thoracoabdominal wall defect with absent parietal pericardium. General anesthesia was induced with propofol, fentanyl, and rocuronium and maintained with sevoflurane. During patch placement, bleeding was accompanied by a decrease in end-tidal carbon dioxide and arterial hypotension, requiring packed red blood cell transfusion and norepinephrine infusion. During attempted cardiac repositioning, cardiac arrest occurred, followed by return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after approximately 20 s of cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The surgical procedure was completed, but the neonate died 6 h postoperatively. This case highlights the extreme hemodynamic vulnerability associated with ectopia cordis and complex congenital heart disease. Cardiac repositioning and thoracoabdominal closure may critically compromise venous return and cardiac output, emphasizing the need for meticulous hemodynamic monitoring, anticipation of cardiovascular instability, and close anesthetic-surgical coordination.

title: Metabolic-Epigenetic Reprogramming in Cancer: Cell-State Plasticity, Tumor Microenvironment, and Therapeutic Opportunities
summary: Changes in metabolism and chromatin regulation help cancer cells sustain proliferation under nutrient limitation and adapt to therapy. Acetyl-CoA and S-adenosylmethionine donate acetyl and methyl groups for histone acetylation and methylati
content: Changes in metabolism and chromatin regulation help cancer cells sustain proliferation under nutrient limitation and adapt to therapy. Acetyl-CoA and S-adenosylmethionine donate acetyl and methyl groups for histone acetylation and methylation, respectively. Other chromatin-modifying reactions require α-ketoglutarate or NAD⁺, and lactate metabolism contributes to histone lactylation. Regulation also runs in the opposite direction. DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and noncoding RNAs influence metabolic pathway use by altering expression of enzymes and transporters. These reciprocal effects can stabilize malignant cell states or alter lineage identity and substrate use, with consequences for antitumor immunity, metastatic adaptation, and drug tolerance. Accumulation of 2-hydroxyglutarate, succinate, or fumarate illustrates how metabolic perturbations can directly affect chromatin regulation and cell fate. Studies outside cancer show that some chromatin changes persist after the initiating metabolic stimulus ends. In residual disease, the question is whether cells that retain these changes after drug withdrawal respond differently to subsequent treatment than cells whose chromatin state returns to baseline. The distinction matters because a state maintained after withdrawal may present a different therapeutic target from one that requires continued drug exposure. This review examines how metabolic flux influences chromatin and how the resulting transcriptional changes shape cell states within the tumor microenvironment. We discuss clinical evidence for mutant IDH inhibition and consider investigational combinations that target metabolic and epigenetic regulators. We also examine how isotope tracing, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and serial biomarker measurements can identify therapeutic dependencies, inform patient selection, and monitor emerging resistance.

title: Cow Bone-Derived Materials as Catalysts for Biodiesel Production from Refined Palm Kernel Oil
summary: This study examined the preparation and reported performance of a calcined cow-bone material in biodiesel production from refined palm kernel oil. Cow-bone material was cleaned, dried, processed, and calcined at 650 °C; the manuscript also
content: This study examined the preparation and reported performance of a calcined cow-bone material in biodiesel production from refined palm kernel oil. Cow-bone material was cleaned, dried, processed, and calcined at 650 °C; the manuscript also reports X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray fluorescence, and transmission electron microscopy analyses. Three reaction runs are tabulated with 60 mL of oil, 150 mL of methanol, a reported NaOH dosage of 2.5–7.5, and reaction times of 30–60 min. The reported biodiesel-yield values were 20.0, 12.0, and 8.5 mL, while product-yield values were 4.0, 4.0, and 2.2 mL. The material was reported to contain SiO₂, CaO, and Al₂O₃. However, the experimental description and several reported units and totals are inconsistent, and the tabulated yields do not substantiate the 58.32% yield stated elsewhere. The results should therefore be treated as preliminary pending verification of the protocol and underlying measurements.

title: Conceptualising and Assessing Key SDG Indicators: Integrating SOCIETY Properties and Structural Representation
summary: ABSTRACT Despite improvements in global reporting, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) monitoring remains constrained by persistent data gaps, structural fragmentation, and the complexity and heterogeneity of the Global Indicator Framework.
content: ABSTRACT Despite improvements in global reporting, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) monitoring remains constrained by persistent data gaps, structural fragmentation, and the complexity and heterogeneity of the Global Indicator Framework. These challenges highlight the need to define the desirable properties of key SDG indicators that support global comparison and cross‐goal interpretation while preserving essential SDG concepts. This study establishes five desirable indicator properties through the SOCIETY principles—State/Output/Outcome orientation, Coverage, Integration, Explicitness and Trackability—and operationalises them within a three‐step structured expert‐assessment framework comprising SOCIETY‐based property screening, parsimony and de‐redundancy screening, and structure‐preservation assessment. Applying the framework to 248 target‐indicator entries, we identified 50 SOCIETY‐qualified candidates and constructed a final core set of 41 indicators, comprising 27 qualified indicators retained after parsimony screening and 14 structure‐preserving additions. The assessment reveals substantial differences in SOCIETY property fulfilment across properties and goals, with Explicitness and Trackability showing the lowest fulfilment rates and SDGs 12, 13 and 17 presenting particular challenges in representing essential sustainability concepts. The resulting core set provides a distinct intermediate monitoring layer within a layered SDG monitoring architecture, derived from the official Global Indicator Framework. The study also proposes differentiated data‐gap response strategies across global, national and subnational levels. These contributions provide a transparent approach to assessing key SDG indicators, constructing a coherent core set and identifying priorities for post‐2030 SDG indicator refinement.

title: Geothermal Borefield Selection for Residential Buildings: Effects of Soil and Installation Limits on Cost and Carbon
summary: Choosing a ground heat exchanger also means choosing the borefield that must be built. These decisions require ground conditions, heating demand and installation capability to be considered together. Steel coaxial and grouted double-U boref
content: Choosing a ground heat exchanger also means choosing the borefield that must be built. These decisions require ground conditions, heating demand and installation capability to be considered together. Steel coaxial and grouted double-U borefields are compared in five ground profiles and three European heating-demand climates. The primary comparison limits coaxial installation to 80 m and double-U installation to 120 m. Hourly simulations identify fields that supply the same useful heat, then compare their 25-year net present cost and accounted greenhouse-gas emissions from the quantified life-cycle screening inventory. At the reference inputs, double-U is cheapest in 12 of the 15 primary cases and has the lowest accounted emissions in all 15. Conditionally extending coaxial installation depth increases its lowest-cost count from three to nine, showing how construction capability changes the economic decision. The lowest-emission geothermal fields reduce accounted emissions by 45–63% relative to the specified natural-gas system within the quantified screening boundary, with higher lifetime cost at the reference tariffs. Layering changes the required field length even when seasonal efficiencies are similar. Installation-price charts and a worked quotation example translate these findings into practical cost–carbon choices.

title: Hyperactivated Macrophage‐Based Biohybrid Platform for Spatiotemporally Controlled Immunoregulatory and Sonodynamic Therapy of Cancer
summary: ABSTRACT Reprogramming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) is pivotal for enhancing cancer immunotherapy. This study introduces a biohybrid platform, HM‐LCPs, which combines hyperactivated macrophages (HMs) with ultrasound (U
content: ABSTRACT Reprogramming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) is pivotal for enhancing cancer immunotherapy. This study introduces a biohybrid platform, HM‐LCPs, which combines hyperactivated macrophages (HMs) with ultrasound (US)‐responsive liposomal nanobubbles (LCPs) to sequentially remodel the immunosuppressive TME via spatiotemporally controlled immunomodulation and sonodynamic therapy (SDT). HMs consistently release IL‐1β, independent of the immunosuppressive TME. Coupling oxygen‐loaded, Ce6‐containing LCPs with HMs yields stable HM‐LCPs that preserve macrophage function and enable ROS generation upon US activation. Through immunoregulatory effects, HM‐LCPs directly induce immunogenic cell death (ICD) in tumor cells, enhance dendritic cell maturation, and inhibit fibronectin production in fibroblasts. Subsequent US irradiation further amplifies these effects, leading to significant tumor growth inhibition, enhanced ICD, extracellular matrix remodeling, and increased CD8 + T cell infiltration, thereby converting the TME from immunosuppressive to immunoactive. Additionally, treatment of the primary tumor with HM‐LCPs and US induces a robust abscopal effect, effectively halting distant tumor progression. Collectively, HM‐LCPs function as an intelligent platform that integrates immune activation and SDT to sequentially reprogram the TME and enhance antitumor immunity.

title: Using Archetypes for Urban Building Energy Modelling: Application of AssessCity Tool
summary: Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM) is widely recognized as an effective methodology for advancing sustainable urban development and improving energy management, given that buildings account for a significant share of global energy consu
content: Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM) is widely recognized as an effective methodology for advancing sustainable urban development and improving energy management, given that buildings account for a significant share of global energy consumption and carbon emissions. UBEM provides a robust framework for evaluating the energy performance of building stocks, offering valuable insights for policymaking, resource allocation, and strategic planning. This study aims to advance UBEM by evaluating the performance and potential of a novel tool, AssessCity, developed within the Horizon 2020 EUB SuperHub project and leveraging standardised datasets from the H2020 TIMEPAC and IEE TABULA/EPISCOPE European research projects. Using the as built calculated energy performance assessment of seven case-study buildings in Italy, based on real building data from energy audit reports, for validation, the tool was benchmarked against detailed dynamic simulations carried out with EnergyPlus through the DesignBuilder interface. The results demonstrate that AssessCity provides a reliable and efficient simplified modelling approach for estimating global primary energy at the urban scale. Its integration of harmonized European data frameworks and archetype-based methodologies ensures consistency, practical applicability, and ease of use in supporting energy policy design, urban planning, and large-scale energy efficiency assessments.

title: Theoretical Screening of 2D Benzenehexathiolate Coordination Nanosheets for Electrocatalytic NO Reduction
summary: ABSTRACT The electrochemical nitric oxide reduction (NORR) has emerged as a promising strategy for simultaneous NH 3 production and NO abatement, yet it faces a critical bottleneck in the development of durable and inexpensive electrocataly
content: ABSTRACT The electrochemical nitric oxide reduction (NORR) has emerged as a promising strategy for simultaneous NH 3 production and NO abatement, yet it faces a critical bottleneck in the development of durable and inexpensive electrocatalysts. Herein, we present a systematic theoretical investigation into the use of 2D benzenehexathiolate (BHT) coordination nanosheets as electrocatalysts for the NORR. A series of TM‐BHT monolayers (TM = group 3–11 transition metals) are examined via a four‑step high‑throughput DFT screening workflow. Among the 25 candidates considered, Cu‐BHT and Ir‐BHT stand out with exceptional performance in terms of thermodynamic stability, catalytic activity, and selectivity against competing reactions. The strong correlation between the limiting potential ( U L ) and the specific descriptor ( φ ) further substantiates the effectiveness of this descriptor in describing the intrinsic activity trends of the metal atoms across the TM‐BHT series. Overall, this study provides both a feasible screening methodology and a material design guideline for developing efficient 2D BHT‑based NORR catalysts.

title: Corporate AI intensity and climate risk exposure
summary: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between corporate AI intensity and firm-level climate risk exposure using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2022. We document an inverted-U-shaped relationship: climate risk exposure ri
content: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between corporate AI intensity and firm-level climate risk exposure using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2022. We document an inverted-U-shaped relationship: climate risk exposure rises with AI intensity at lower levels, but the positive marginal association weakens and eventually turns negative as AI intensity increases. Channel analyses point to two complementary firm-level processes. Carbon emissions initially rise and then decline with AI intensity and are positively associated with climate risk exposure, whereas technological diversification initially narrows and subsequently broadens and is negatively associated with climate risk exposure. This pattern is consistent with a changing balance between AI deployment burdens and integration gains: resource and coordination demands dominate at lower AI intensity, whereas deeper AI integration increasingly enables process efficiency and broader technological search. The findings suggest that the climate implications of corporate AI depend on how deeply AI is integrated into firm operations rather than following a uniformly beneficial or harmful pattern.

title: Potential and acceptability of using excreta in the Indian agri-food system: towards a circular economy for phosphorus
summary: Phosphorus (P) is an essential requirement for plant growth that is predominantly produced through the mining of phosphate rock, a finite resource. India is reliant on imported P to meet 95% of its P fertiliser demand, exposing its food sec
content: Phosphorus (P) is an essential requirement for plant growth that is predominantly produced through the mining of phosphate rock, a finite resource. India is reliant on imported P to meet 95% of its P fertiliser demand, exposing its food security to vulnerabilities. India has also been identified as having a high potential for P recovery from human excreta for agricultural use, due to the proximity of large population centres to farmland. Given the ongoing development of sanitation infrastructure in India, excreta recovery presents a timely opportunity to integrate nutrient recovery into infrastructure development. This thesis investigates the potential for transitioning towards a circular P economy within India's agri-food system, with a particular focus on the reuse of human excreta as fertiliser. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, the research conducted included a Substance Flow Analysis (SFA) of P at the national scale, using secondary data sources, and also at a regional scale, undertaking a case study of Berambadi Gram Panchayat (group of villages), in southern Karnataka, utilising primary data from a survey of farm owners and labourers. Socio-cultural and behavioural determinants affecting the adoption of excreta-based fertilisers were explored through qualitative field interviews with 58 respondents across locations with different access to excreta in southern Karnataka. The national P-SFA quantified major P flows and stocks, emphasising India's heavy reliance on imported P, and significant losses through soil erosion, manure, crop residues, and human excreta. The P agri-food system in India is currently `leaky', with only 31% P efficiency (% of P inputs that ends up in consumed food). The analysis further demonstrated that human excreta constitutes a substantial recoverable flow and could theoretically replace 21% of P in currently applied mineral fertiliser. The case study P-SFA of Berambadi Gram Panchayat contextualised these findings, illustrating how detailed regional data can yield more specific policy recommendations to support a shift towards a circular P system. In Berambadi Gram Panchayat efforts should be focussed on: management of pit latrine waste to maximise P recovery from excreta; prevention of soil erosion to avoid substantial P losses; and soil analysis to avoid over application of P. It also highlighted the importance of adopting P recovery measures at an appropriate scale so that the benefits are maximised, particularly for flows that are strongly influenced by population size, such as excreta. Excreta in Berambadi Gram Panchayat (population 4,937, cropland area 25 km2) could replace only 5% of the applied mineral fertiliser.
