title: Advances in green and low-energy carbon capture key technologies toward engineering applications
summary: Within the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework, green and low-energy CO2 capture technologies are essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and achieve carbon neutrality. As global carbon capture, utilization, a
content: Within the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework, green and low-energy CO2 capture technologies are essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and achieve carbon neutrality. As global carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) demonstration scales continue to expand, chemical absorption using amine solvents has emerged as the industrial benchmark. However, high energy consumption and poor solvent stability hinder large-scale deployment, while secondary pollution from solvent degradation and amine emissions poses a critical barrier to the green and sustainable development of this technology. To overcome these limitations, research efforts in the CO2 capture field have increasingly focused on the synergistic integration of process intensification and materials innovation. This review summarizes recent advances in green and low-energy CO2 capture technologies for engineering applications. The review first presents mainstream process optimization strategies currently adopted in the CO2 capture industry. Building on this, the development and application of novel green and low-energy CO2 capture systems are discussed in detail, encompassing enzymatic absorption and phase-change absorption systems. Furthermore, catalytic desorption technology is identified as a critical enabler for driving the green transformation of conventional amine-based CO2 capture processes. By analyzing the underlying mechanisms, material selection, and process compatibility, future research directions are briefly discussed. This review aims to guide research, development, and engineering deployment of green, low-energy CO2 capture technologies.

title: Capacitance-Engineered Threshold Switching Transistors with 4 mV/dec Subthreshold Swing
summary: Abstract The subthreshold swing (SS) of conventional field-effect transistors (FETs) is fundamentally constrained by the thermionic emission governed by the Boltzmann distribution, imposing a theoretical minimum of 60 mV/dec at room tempera
content: Abstract The subthreshold swing (SS) of conventional field-effect transistors (FETs) is fundamentally constrained by the thermionic emission governed by the Boltzmann distribution, imposing a theoretical minimum of 60 mV/dec at room temperature. Here, we report an aligned carbon nanotube transistor (A-CNT FET) that achieves an exceptionally steep SS. By integrating an HfO2-based threshold-switching (TS) device in series with the gate of the A-CNT FET, we realize steep-slope switching behavior. The fabricated device exhibits an SS as low as 4 mV/dec and an on/off ratio of 3 × 105. Notably, the short-channel device (Lch = 50 nm) delivers an on-state current of 1 mA/μm while maintaining an SS of 12 mV/dec. Furthermore, scaling the capacitance of the TS device optimizes the voltage division between the TS device and the transistor, yielding synergistic improvements in both the on/off ratio and SS. This work establishes an effective strategy for high-performance steep-switching carbon nanotube transistors.

title: Lake hydrochemistry and aquatic plant diversity across permafrost landscapes of Yakutia, Eastern Siberia
summary: Central Yakutia in eastern Siberia is characterized by abundant lakes in permafrost-thaw depressions, named alaas. They constitute the traditional cultural landscape that is home to the indigenous Sakha people, providing critical ecosystem
content: Central Yakutia in eastern Siberia is characterized by abundant lakes in permafrost-thaw depressions, named alaas. They constitute the traditional cultural landscape that is home to the indigenous Sakha people, providing critical ecosystem services. This study aims at assessing present-day lake characteristics and exploring their drivers based on lake hydrochemistry and aquatic and terrestrial plant diversity derived from sedimentary DNA in surface sediments. Macrophyte diversity reflects different lake types distinguished using both lake morphology and hydrochemistry. It also reveals a dominance of brackish water-tolerant cosmopolitan submerged macrophytes across all lakes, particularly Stuckenia and Potamogeton . In contrast, Myriophyllum and M. verticillatum are exclusively found in mountain lakes and freshwater lakes in the lowlands. The hydrochemical analysis reveals a clear distinction between low-mineralised mountain lakes and the highly variable hydrochemistry of the lowland lakes with much higher mineral content. Mountain lake hydrochemistry seems to be mainly determined by climate, whereas environmental drivers of hydrochemistry in lowland thermokarst lakes are more diverse. New thermokarst lakes are characterised by high dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and mainly located in forests. In contrast, connected alaas lakes, typically located in large alaas systems with settlements and active land use, display lower DOC and mineralisation, despite their location close to anthropogenic influence. We assume that temporary high discharge, such as during snowmelts, enables dilution, thus lowering organic and mineral contents. Future warming may lead to prolonged exposure to evaporation, but also to increased hydrological connectivity and increase in the number of connected alaas lakes, thereby potentially providing more freshwater to the region.

title: Optimal Path for Orbital Debris
summary: Abstract This paper introduces the Dynamic Integrated Space-Economy (DISE-2024) model, a general equilibrium integrated assessment model (IAM) designed to analyze the long-run optimal dynamics of orbital debris. The model combines an optima
content: Abstract This paper introduces the Dynamic Integrated Space-Economy (DISE-2024) model, a general equilibrium integrated assessment model (IAM) designed to analyze the long-run optimal dynamics of orbital debris. The model combines an optimal economic growth framework with a physical representation of the Earth’s orbital environment, capturing the dynamics of orbital debris accumulation, collision risks, and the resulting destruction of space-based capital assets. The economic module determines optimal consumption paths and investment decisions across two capital stocks: terrestrial capital and space capital (i.e., satellites). The physical module endogenously models the generation of orbital debris, accounting for launch activities, in-orbit breakups, and collisions. The model is simulated over a 200-year horizon for a centralized economy, allowing the computation of optimal trajectories for key variables and the quantification of the output costs associated with orbital debris accumulation. (JEL Classification: D62; E21; E22; Q53; Q58).

title: Click-Functionalizable Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). Compared to light in the visible and NIR-I regions, NIR-II ligh
content: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). Compared to light in the visible and NIR-I regions, NIR-II light undergoes less absorption and scattering by biological tissues, enabling deeper tissue penetration and higher imaging resolution. Tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate (TTFtt)-bridged bimetallic diradicaloid complexes exhibit bright NIR-II emission with high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) relative to other NIR-II fluorophores. These complexes are also particularly modular, as the capping ligands on the metal centers can be substituted to impart desired properties. Here, azide-functionalized bis(imino)acenaphthene (BIAN) capping ligands are introduced to leverage and expand this modularity. BIAN-capped TTFtt complexes exhibit chemical and photophysical properties comparable to previously reported TTFtt complexes. BIAN backbones functionalized with an azide group further enable Huisgen cycloaddition “click” chemistry for the attachment of diverse functional moieties while preserving the intrinsic NIR-II photophysical properties of the TTFtt core. As one example, a sulfonate-clicked TTFtt complex (1-C3) displays enhanced solubility and increased photoluminescence (PL) intensity in aqueous solutions compared to other TTFtt complexes. Notably, 1-C3 also exhibits pH-dependent PL intensity, suggesting its potential utility as an NIR-II-emitting pH sensor. Furthermore, the enhanced water solubility of 1-C3 enabled us to obtain in vivo gastrointestinal imaging in murine models. Overall, these results demonstrate the dramatically expanded modularity of TTFtt complexes through the use of clickable-BIAN ligands.

title: Dynamic mathematical model of a non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) absorption spectroscopy measurement system for transient gas analysis
summary: Abstract Non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) absorption spectroscopy is widely used for quantitative gas analysis; however, the steady-state use of the Beer–Lambert law alone does not describe transient signals and temperature dependent behavior
content: Abstract Non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) absorption spectroscopy is widely used for quantitative gas analysis; however, the steady-state use of the Beer–Lambert law alone does not describe transient signals and temperature dependent behavior frequently encountered under practical flow conditions. Here, the effects of flow rate and cell temperature on transient NDIR responses are experimentally characterized, and a unified dynamic formulation is presented. The detection cell is modeled as a linear time-invariant system with a characteristic time constant τ = V/v (V: cell volume, v: volumetric flow rate), and, under isothermal operation, absorbance is expressed as the convolution of the input concentration with the instrumental impulse response. This representation accounts for response delays and waveform asymmetry under time-varying composition and flow, and it provides implementation-ready procedures for response correction and calibration in dynamic measurements. The formulation offers specification-level guidance beyond instrument-specific fixed settings and is expected to improve quantitative reliability for challenging sample matrices (e.g., powders, concrete, and liquids), thereby broadening NDIR applicability beyond conventional steel analysis.

title: A Label-Free Method to Quantify Early Stage Amyloid Aggregation via Intrinsic Phenylalanine Fluorescence
summary: Abstract The aggregation of amyloid-forming peptides is a dynamic, complex process that underlies their diverse biological activities, from physiological functions to disease-associated dysfunctions. While the structure of fibrillar end-pro
content: Abstract The aggregation of amyloid-forming peptides is a dynamic, complex process that underlies their diverse biological activities, from physiological functions to disease-associated dysfunctions. While the structure of fibrillar end-products is well-characterized for most amyloids, the heterogeneous and often transient oligomers, likely key in cytotoxicity, remain poorly investigated, especially for peptides with low-yield aromatic residues. Here, by exploiting and developing flow induced dispersion analysis in both peak and front modes, we demonstrate that intrinsic phenylalanine fluorescence can be harnessed to quantify the conversion of diffusing monomers into nondiffusing oligomers and fibrils. This approach is validated using PSMα3, a tryptophan- and tyrosine-free peptide from S. aureus, known for its fast amyloid fibrillation and key roles in bacterial virulence. We indeed characterize its low-molecular-weight oligomers, and size evolution from 2 to 10 nm over time. Importantly, to further validate the robustness of our front-mode approach, we apply it to hIAPP, a tyrosine-containing, tryptophan-free peptide, with critical outcome in type 2 diabetes. Our results overcome the limitations of traditional biochemical and biophysical amyloid assays by extending analysis from large oligomers and fibrils to small heterogeneous oligomers, under near-physiological conditions. This study thus offers a new analytical framework, thereby filling a critical gap in amyloid research, to probe the early stages of aggregation, key in the design of alternative therapeutics for amyloid-diseases.

title: Ultrafast kilowatt-range microwave pulsing for enhanced CO₂ conversion in atmospheric-pressure plasmas
summary: Ultrafast microwave power pulsation is demonstrated as an effective strategy to enhance CO2 conversion in atmospheric-pressure plasma reactors. While initial experiments at several hundred watts in a compact coaxial plasma torch showed impr
content: Ultrafast microwave power pulsation is demonstrated as an effective strategy to enhance CO2 conversion in atmospheric-pressure plasma reactors. While initial experiments at several hundred watts in a compact coaxial plasma torch showed improved performance, the present study investigates the scalability of this approach to kilowatt-range microwave power. Conversion and energy efficiency were examined in two reactor configurations: a Surfaguide-based system (KIT) and a cavity-based plasma torch (IPP), and benchmarked against the compact coaxial torch. Both kilowatt-scale setups share similar microwave coupling schemes, power levels, reactor tubes, and gas injection geometries, but differ in afterglow treatment. The torch at IPP employs rapid nozzle-based quenching, whereas the Surfaguide-based reactor relies on slower cooling along an extended quartz tube. Stable plasma operation was achieved at pulsation peak powers of ~4 kW and pulse durations from sub-microseconds to microseconds, with stability limited to inter-pulse times of ~10 us (cavity-based torch) and ~12 us (Surfaguide-based reactor). In contrast to the coaxial torch, no plasma reignition regime was observed in either kilowatt-scale reactor, resulting in weaker plasma temperature modulation. Notably, the period-averaged gas temperature in the Surfaguide-based reactor exceeded that under continuous-wave operation. Under these conditions, relative enhancements of <40% in CO2 conversion and <20% in energy efficiency were measured compared with continuous-wave operation. These improvements were largely suppressed in the torch at IPP, presumably due to rapid afterglow quenching. Finally, analysis of the instantaneous reflected microwave power provided qualitative insights into electron density dynamics during the power-OFF and power-ON phases.

title: MaterialCities: mapping building material stocks and floor area of the world’s 1.8 million settlements by structures and functions
summary: Abstract MaterialCities is a dataset of the gross floor area and the mass of eight construction materials of the world’s buildings in high resolution and detail. It differentiates floor area and material stocks by three building functions a
content: Abstract MaterialCities is a dataset of the gross floor area and the mass of eight construction materials of the world’s buildings in high resolution and detail. It differentiates floor area and material stocks by three building functions and five load-bearing structural types with region-specific construction archetypes using variant material intensity ranges that capture building materials’ inherent uncertainties and variabilities. The data is available in seven spatial resolutions, from its native data-driven delineation of individual settlements, towns, and cities, through Urban Centres polygons, to two levels of subnational administrative boundaries, individual countries, and two levels of global regional aggregations. It is the first global-scale high-resolution dataset of its kind to provide floor-area derived material stock estimates for detailed building archetypes. The data are provided in the GeoPackage format for use in geographic information systems (GIS) and as comma-separated value (CSV) tables to be easily filtered and recombined for ease of use. MaterialCities has many use cases including comparative assessments of buildings’ service provisioning, material requirements, energy consumption, and environmental impacts, quantifying the urban mine of secondary materials or building stocks at risk from disasters, and as baselines for future development scenarios.

title: NEFERTITI : Linking Early Galaxy Formation to the Assembly of the Milky Way
summary: Abstract We use a new implementation of the NEFERTITI galaxy formation model, coupled to ∼30 high-resolution Caterpillar dark-matter simulations of Milky Way (MW) analogs, to connect early galaxy formation with the MW's assembly down to z =
content: Abstract We use a new implementation of the NEFERTITI galaxy formation model, coupled to ∼30 high-resolution Caterpillar dark-matter simulations of Milky Way (MW) analogs, to connect early galaxy formation with the MW's assembly down to z = 0. Our locally constrained model resolves minihalos hosting the first Population III (Pop III) stars and self-consistently tracks inhomogeneous ionization and chemical enrichment. Pop III star formation begins at z ≃ 27, peaks at z ≃ 10–15, and persists down to z ≲ 5, producing Pop III systems with M * ∼ 10–5 × 10 5 M ⊙ . The present-day descendants of Pop III stars span [Fe/H] < −9 to ≈−1, with the most metal-poor stars typically enriched by a few (1–4) low-energy supernova progenitors. Pair-instability supernova descendants more commonly form in massive halos ( M vir > 10 8 M ⊙ ), often externally enriched, reflecting the strong feedback and delayed recovery following energetic explosions. These early systems serve as building blocks for the present-day Galaxy’s metal-poor component: although 90% of the total stellar mass formed in situ, the accreted component dominates at [Fe/H] < −1 and accounts for nearly all stars with [Fe/H] < −2.5. This accreted population is largely built by a few (∼5) massive ( M * > 10 8 M ⊙ ) destroyed dwarfs, but lower-mass systems become increasingly important at low metallicities, with ultrafaint and classical dwarf spheroidal analogs contributing ∼25% at [Fe/H] < −3. Our model simultaneously reproduces the properties of metal-poor MW stars and the JWST “Hebe” galaxy at z ∼ 11, supporting its identification as a pure Pop III system. Ultimately, NEFERTITI is a key tool to interpret upcoming local and high- z observations linking the near- and far-field cosmology.

title: Global consumption-based deforestation carbon emissions and regional hotspots: 2001–2020
summary: The consumption-based carbon emissions dataset for deforestation provides an important perspective for developing effective emission mitigation policies. However, existing datasets are largely limited to national-scale and lack spatially ex
content: The consumption-based carbon emissions dataset for deforestation provides an important perspective for developing effective emission mitigation policies. However, existing datasets are largely limited to national-scale and lack spatially explicit, high-resolution data at the global level. Here, we present a global, gridded dataset of consumption-based deforestation carbon emissions at 1 km resolution for 2001–2020. The dataset integrates spatial information on road networks, deforestation, and forest carbon fluxes with country-level global trade statistics. Our dataset shows that trade-related deforestation emissions amount to 39.6 Gt CO 2 e, constituting 31.8 % of global deforestation emissions. This new dataset fills a critical gap in spatially explicit consumption-based deforestation emissions data, and supports the development of targeted mitigation strategies from the consumer perspective. It also provides a valuable input for climate and carbon cycle models to assess the contribution of consumption-driven deforestation to global warming. Datasets are available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28091879 (Tang et al., 2024).

title: Addressing systematic underestimation in a global ship emission inventory through improved fleet representation and fuel compliance characterization
summary: As a sector with high energy demand, long-lived assets, and limited near-term low-carbon alternatives, global shipping is considered difficult to decarbonize and is subject to stringent emission controls. To evaluate emission control effect
content: As a sector with high energy demand, long-lived assets, and limited near-term low-carbon alternatives, global shipping is considered difficult to decarbonize and is subject to stringent emission controls. To evaluate emission control effects and conduct rapid response air quality simulations, accurate and timely ship emission inventories are indispensable. However, existing inventories face challenges from incomplete fleet representation and large uncertainties in PM 2.5 emissions after the global sulfur regulation. Here, we updated the Ship Emission Inventory Model to SEIMv2.3 by introducing an improved representation of post-2020 fuel sulfur compliance pathways and enabling near-real-time emission calculation within 3 d of AIS data acquisition. Ship activity and technical database are updated daily instead of yearly to obtain a more complete and rapid description of the global ship fleet. Fleet's multiple choices to comply with fuel sulfur regulation were considered, including switching to very low sulfur fuel and utilizing scrubbers to keep consuming heavy fuel oil. The daily expansion of ship technical database uncovered 8 % and 6.2 % of the total gross tonnage of active bulk carrier and container fleets, unveiling up to 5.4 % of global ship CO 2 emissions. The resulting emission discrepancies gradually accumulated over 2024, indicating that delayed fleet information updates remain an important source of uncertainty in ship emission estimates. Meanwhile, assuming that all ships switch to low-sulfur fuels after 2020 would lead to underestimation of PM 2.5 and BC emissions by approximately 43 % and 15 %. Although South China Ocean had the most absolute underestimation, the Indian Ocean had the highest underestimated portion, reaching 56 % and 15 % of its total PM 2.5 and BC emissions.

title: Carbamylome analysis reveals regulatory roles for lysine carbamylation in β-cell glycolytic and insulin-processing enzymes
summary: In type 1 diabetes (T1D), insulin-producing β cells are destroyed by an autoimmune response driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines. The signaling of these cytokines is partially mediated by post-translational modifications, such as phosphoryl
content: In type 1 diabetes (T1D), insulin-producing β cells are destroyed by an autoimmune response driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines. The signaling of these cytokines is partially mediated by post-translational modifications, such as phosphorylation and acetylation. However, the role of other post-translational modifications in β-cell cytokine signaling represents an important knowledge gap. In the context of autoimmune diseases, lysine carbamylation has gained attention for its role in pathogenesis. Here, we investigate possible roles of carbamylation in T1D. We found that pancreata from the T1D model, non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice, at pre-diabetic stage (8-9 weeks old) exhibit 11% carbamylation-positive β cells, whereas non-diabetic CD1 mice have only 5%. Proteomics analysis of the MIN6 insulin-producing cell line treated with a cocktail of three pro-inflammatory cytokines IFNγ + IL-1β + TNFα identified 284 carbamylated peptides from 222 proteins regulated by the cytokine treatment. Integration of carbamylation and acetylation provided a deep view of the cytokine-regulated PTMs and potential points of interplay. A functional-enrichment analysis revealed that carbamylation was enriched in pathways related to autoimmune diseases, metabolism, DNA replication, and protein translation. Moreover, functional testing demonstrated that carbamylation inhibits the glycolytic enzyme aldolase A and the insulin-processing enzyme carboxypeptidase E, identifying a possible role for cytokine-induced β-cell dysfunction. In summary, NOD mice have more carbamylated β cells than CD1 mice, and pro-inflammatory cytokine treatment regulates protein carbamylation in MIN6 cells. These data identified carbamylation as a potential regulatory mechanism for β-cell metabolism and insulin production in insulitis.

title: Roughness-controlled tribocharging governs friction in dry glass contacts
summary: Surface roughness can either increase or decrease friction depending on the dominant mechanism: smoothing reduces friction by suppressing asperity-induced deformation, but can increase friction by enhancing interfacial adhesion. Here, we sh
content: Surface roughness can either increase or decrease friction depending on the dominant mechanism: smoothing reduces friction by suppressing asperity-induced deformation, but can increase friction by enhancing interfacial adhesion. Here, we show that, for dry glass–glass contacts, increasing nanoscale roughness can reduce friction because it suppresses triboelectric adhesion. As the root-mean-square surface slope h’rms of the glass ball is increased from 0.01 to 0.09, the friction coefficient drops by about 30%, despite a threefold increase in the average contact pressure. Using rheometer-based friction measurements in dry nitrogen, super-resolution imaging of the real contact area, soft X-ray discharge, and Faraday-cup electrometry, we show that increasing roughness reduces both the real contact area and retained tribocharge, thereby weakening the electrostatic contribution to friction. Discharging the interface with soft X-rays largely removes the roughness dependence of friction. Our results establish tribocharging as an adhesion mechanism through which nanoscale roughness controls friction in dry dielectric contacts.

title: Stellar Population Spectra Incorporating Detailed Binary Evolution Using POSYDON
summary: Abstract The accuracy of stellar population properties inferred through spectral energy distribution fitting hinges on the reliability of the underlying spectral models. Binary interactions are fundamental for massive star evolution, and ig
content: Abstract The accuracy of stellar population properties inferred through spectral energy distribution fitting hinges on the reliability of the underlying spectral models. Binary interactions are fundamental for massive star evolution, and ignoring their spectral contribution can lead to incorrect results. We use the POSYDON binary population synthesis code to generate spectral models of stellar populations that include binaries at solar metallicity. Our framework incorporates a collection of spectral libraries that is designed to address key outcomes of binary stellar evolution like wind-stripped Wolf–Rayet (WR) stars, binary-stripped helium (He) stars, and a treatment for stellar mergers. Our starburst spectral models confirm previous results showing that the inclusion of binary interactions has a significant effect on the ultraviolet (UV) and ionizing regime of the integrated spectrum. In particular we find that WR stars and other massive main-sequence stars dominate the production of ionizing radiation at earlier times, but after ≃16 Myr binary-stripped stars produced through mass transfer begin to dominate. Furthermore, we show that the production of ionizing He + photons is especially sensitive to the underlying population of binary-stripped stars. While our results currently focus on high-mass stars (≥4 M ⊙ ) at solar metallicity, they provide the framework for binary spectral synthesis across a range of metallicities and masses and lay the foundation for calculations of the emergent emission-line spectra in the UV, optical, and infrared regimes. We make the spectral models from this work publicly available for use in a format that can be integrated into fitting codes.

title: Tau Disaggregation by a CNS-Permeable Small Molecule Reduces Fibril and Oligomer Burden and Preserves Proteostasis and Behavior
summary: Abstract Pathological aggregates of the microtubule-associated protein, tau, drive neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related tauopathies. Yet, strategies to slow or eliminate progressive accumulation of misfolded tau prot
content: Abstract Pathological aggregates of the microtubule-associated protein, tau, drive neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related tauopathies. Yet, strategies to slow or eliminate progressive accumulation of misfolded tau protein in the brain remain underdeveloped relative to upstream therapeutic approaches, such as amyloid-beta (Aβ) immunotherapy. Here, we explore a coumarin-based series of brain-permeable small molecules that disaggregate tau. Structure–activity relationships (SAR) identified nitrile-containing analogs as potential leads from the series and suggest a stacking-driven disassembly mechanism. Small molecules from this series disaggregated tau from AD brain-derived matter, reducing aggregate burden measured in vitro across both fibrillar and oligomeric tau species, two principal pathological aggregate species implicated in disease. Mechanistic studies demonstrate that disaggregation does not generate soluble oligomeric intermediates, addressing a central question in the field. Inhibitor treatment reduces prion-like seeding, a disease-related mechanism by which tau aggregation pathology spreads in the brain. The lead candidate from this series is well tolerated in vivo, which enabled efficacy testing in a tauopathy mouse model. Treatment reduced tau pathology while preserving behavioral function, proteasome capacity, and synaptic integrity. These findings establish small-molecule tau disaggregation as a viable therapeutic strategy and provide a mechanistic framework for the design of aggregate-directed therapeutics in neurodegeneration.

title: Field testing of floating mat systems for grass cultivation and biochar generation under variable weather conditions
summary: Variable weather conditions can substantially affect the stability and performance of a floating treatment wetland used to cultivate aquatic plants. This study evaluates the field performance and ecological potential of a floating foam mat
content: Variable weather conditions can substantially affect the stability and performance of a floating treatment wetland used to cultivate aquatic plants. This study evaluates the field performance and ecological potential of a floating foam mat designed to support aquatic plant growth and provide multiple benefits, including accumulation of nitrogen and phosphorus in plant biomass, atmospheric carbon sequestration, heavy metal removal, and biochar production. Plant growth trials were conducted in a watershed using 10 modular floating mats containing two aquatic macrophytes, common rush ( Juncus effusus ) and Switchgrass ( Panicum virgatum ), from mid-June to December 2025 (6 months) to assess vegetation growth, biomass composition, and pyrolysis product yields. Biomass monitoring showed that J. effusus had a root length of 64 cm (2′1″) and a stem length of 67 cm (2′2″), while P. virgatum had the highest root length of 97.5 cm (3′2″) and a stem length of 128 cm (4′2″) over a five-month period. The plant survival rate for each mat ranged from 90 to 92% by the end of harvesting. The Carbon, Hydrogen, Nitrogen, and Sulfur (CHNS) analysis revealed that P. virgatum roots had the highest concentrations of nitrogen (2.2%) and sulfur (0.3%). The J. effusus stem had higher concentrations of carbon (~ 45%) and hydrogen (~ 6%), like P. virgatum . Elemental concentrations showed high potassium (K) levels (> 10,000 ppm) in both biomasses. Furthermore, the highest biochar yields were obtained from pyrolyzed J. effusus root collected from the pool (JE-PR; 0.48 g/g) and P. virgatum root collected from the watershed (PV-WR; 0.42 g/g). The lowest yields were observed for J. effusus combined samples from the watershed (JE-WC; 0.35 g/g) and P. virgatum stems from the watershed (PV-WS; 0.39 g/g). These variations in the amounts of pyrolysis products and elemental compositions highlight differences in biomass chemical composition among plant parts. This study provides practical insights into the performance of a floating mat under variable weather conditions and explores the potential to combine aquatic plant cultivation with biomass valorization through pyrolysis.

title: A quick appraisal of machine learning techniques in different aspects of rice cultivation
summary: Rice is the most important cereal crop in the world, consumed by more than half of the global population. With the projected world population reaching around 9 billion by 2050, the cultivation of the rice crop becomes important for the food
content: Rice is the most important cereal crop in the world, consumed by more than half of the global population. With the projected world population reaching around 9 billion by 2050, the cultivation of the rice crop becomes important for the food security of the world. Machine learning methods are playing a crucial role in optimising technologies related to rice cultivation. This paper is a quick appraisal of 343 research articles for the comparative utilisation of Machine Learning methods pertaining to different aspects of rice cultivation viz crop improvement, crop monitoring, crop mapping, irrigation management, weed management, disease management, etc. The study indicated that ML methods are used unevenly in different aspects of rice cultivation, where the aspects like disease management, yield forecasting, post-harvest, crop mapping, crop monitoring lead in the utilization of ML methods in comparison to the other aspects like weed management, irrigation management, fertilizer management, etc. both in terms of the quantity and quality of methods utilized.

title: Enhancing the therapeutic ratio in prostate LDR brachytherapy: A TOPAS Monte Carlo investigation of nanoparticle radiosensitization
summary: Abstract This Monte Carlo study evaluates and compares the radiosensitization potential of gold (Au) and platinum (Pt) nanoparticles (NPs) in prostate low-dose-rate (LDR) brachytherapy using 125 I and 103 Pd sources. Using the TOPAS Monte C
content: Abstract This Monte Carlo study evaluates and compares the radiosensitization potential of gold (Au) and platinum (Pt) nanoparticles (NPs) in prostate low-dose-rate (LDR) brachytherapy using 125 I and 103 Pd sources. Using the TOPAS Monte Carlo software, Au and Pt NPs (30 and 100 nm) were uniformly distributed within a tumor volume at concentrations of 7, 18, and 30 mg/g within a modified MIRD male phantom. Dose enhancement factors (DEFs) and dose volume histograms (DVHs) were calculated for both source types. Au NPs consistently outperformed Pt NPs, with maximum DEFs of 2.58 for Au versus 2.53 for Pt ( 125 I, 30 mg/g, 100 nm). DEF increased with concentration and NP size, with 125 I yielding greater enhancement than ¹⁰³Pd due to its lower photon energy. DVH analysis demonstrated selective tumor dose escalation (tumor Dmean increased from 239.8 Gy to 282.2 Gy for Pt with 103 Pd) with negligible impact on organs at risk. Photoelectric energy deposition increased by up to 20.7-fold with NP addition, correlating with observed DEF trends. In conclusions both Au and Pt NPs significantly enhance tumor dose in LDR brachytherapy while sparing adjacent organs, supporting an improved therapeutic ratio. The near-equivalence of Au and Pt NP performance suggests Pt may represent a viable, cost-effective alternative for clinical translation. These findings provide a dosimetric foundation for future experimental and clinical investigations.

title: Naphthalene-Fused Meta-Dual-Boron Compounds Enable an 80 nm Red Shift with Concurrently Narrowed Full Widths at Half Maximum
summary: Multiple resonance emitters are highly sought after for their intrinsically narrowband emission, yet achieving long-wavelength emission without spectral broadening remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a naphthalene-fused rigid π-
content: Multiple resonance emitters are highly sought after for their intrinsically narrowband emission, yet achieving long-wavelength emission without spectral broadening remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a naphthalene-fused rigid π-extension strategy based on the meta-positioned dual boron framework BBCz-DB by replacing its peripheral carbazole units with naphthalene fragments to develop the yellow MR emitter DB-CzNa. This molecular design leverages the dual aromaticity of naphthalene: while the global π-delocalization effectively narrows the energy gap, the preserved local aromaticity maintains a highly rigid molecular framework, which significantly suppresses excited-state vibronic coupling. This synergistic effect allows the MR emitters to achieve a pronounced emission red shift without sacrificing their narrow emission characteristics. Consequently, DB-CzNa achieves an 80 nm red shift relative to BBCz-DB, delivering yellow emission at 546 nm with an ultra-narrow full width at half maximum of 16 nm (0.07 eV) in toluene. A sensitized fluorescence organic light emitting diode device based on DB-CzNa affords a yellow electroluminescence at 556 nm with a full widths at half maximum of 24 nm and a maximum external quantum efficiency of 26.9%. This work demonstrates that judicious naphthalene fusion on meta-dual boron frameworks provides a powerful strategy to overcome the trade-off between spectral redshift and broadening.

title: Detection of Escaping Magnesium in the Upper Atmosphere of WASP-76b
summary: Abstract Near-ultraviolet (NUV) observations can uniquely probe low-density, high-altitude gas in ultrahot Jupiters (UHJs) via strong resonance lines of metals. WASP-76b is a well-studied UHJ with prior detections of refractory metals and c
content: Abstract Near-ultraviolet (NUV) observations can uniquely probe low-density, high-altitude gas in ultrahot Jupiters (UHJs) via strong resonance lines of metals. WASP-76b is a well-studied UHJ with prior detections of refractory metals and complex day–night chemistry, making it a prime target for atmospheric escape diagnostics in the NUV. We present Hubble Space Telescope (HST)/STIS E230M (2274–3119 Å) transmission spectroscopy of WASP-76b. While broadband (∼200 Å) and narrowband (4 Å) transmission spectra do not show spectral features, a velocity-resolved single-line analysis reveals clear excess absorption in both components of the Mg ii doublet (2796 Å and 2803 Å, k and h lines). The Mg ii signal is localized to the blue wing (Doppler velocities [−50, −10] km s −1 ) and is recovered with narrower 0.5 Å bins; the inferred absorption exceeds both the optical continuum radius and the Roche-lobe scale, suggesting a highly extended upper atmosphere. We estimate a mass-loss rate of M ̇ ∼ 1 0 12.14 g s − 1 from ATES. The present NUV data do not improve constraints on lower-atmosphere properties, and a comparison with upper-atmosphere forward models disfavors scenarios with extreme Mg enrichment. Together with the near-solar metallicity inferred from optical+IR spectra, this suggests that the Mg ii absorption can arise in an escaping upper atmosphere without requiring extreme Mg enrichment, qualitatively consistent with hydrodynamic escape. Ongoing HST programs expanding the sample of UHJs focused on NUV observations will enable comparative tests of composition and kinematics in escaping atmospheres.

title: Global probabilistic forecasting of air pollution at the kilometre scale
summary: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) refers to particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 µm or less. It comes from human activities, such as traffic and industry, and from wildfires, desert dust and gases emitted by vegetat
content: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) refers to particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 µm or less. It comes from human activities, such as traffic and industry, and from wildfires, desert dust and gases emitted by vegetation. Short-term exposure to it accounts for about a million deaths a year. Operational forecasts run on grids tens of kilometres wide, which hide the pollution breathed by nearly two hundred million people a day. Machine learning has transformed weather forecasting, but data-driven forecasts of air pollution still blur extremes and lose skill as the air travels. Here we introduce Foehn, a generative model that learns from global kilometre-scale estimates of PM2.5 and computes where the air comes from. Over a year of retrospective forecasts, it outperforms the operational forecast at three stations in four and forecasts at the scale of this hidden exposure. Its ensembles are calibrated, and their mean detects local pollution extremes four days ahead as well as the operational forecast does one day ahead. Such forecasts could warn the millions whom coarse maps miss, once kilometre-scale data are available in real time.

title: On the Development of Membrane Reactor Technology for Ammonia Synthesis
summary: The rapid expansion of renewable electricity has renewed interest in hydrogen as a versatile energy carrier. However, large scale deployment remains constrained by challenges associated with hydrogen storage and transport. Consequently, alt
content: The rapid expansion of renewable electricity has renewed interest in hydrogen as a versatile energy carrier. However, large scale deployment remains constrained by challenges associated with hydrogen storage and transport. Consequently, alternative energy carriers capable of storing hydrogen in chemically bound form are attracting increasing attention. Ammonia (NH3) is one of the most promising candidates owing to its high hydrogen content, established infrastructure for storage and transport, relatively simple liquefaction, and potential for reconversion to hydrogen or direct use as a fuel. These features make ammonia attractive for both international energy trade and decentralised energy systems, where locally produced ammonia can link renewable electricity generation with distributed energy demand. Today, ammonia is produced almost exclusively through the Haber Bosch process, which relies on fossil based hydrogen and operates at high temperatures and pressures. This process is energy intensive, carbon intensive, and most suitable for large scale continuous production. Furthermore, ammonia synthesis is thermodynamically limited, requiring extensive recycling and severe operating conditions to achieve high yields. Membrane reactors offer an attractive alternative by integrating reaction and separation within a single unit. Continuous removal of ammonia shifts the reaction equilibrium, enabling higher conversions at milder conditions while reducing energy consumption and CO2 emissions. Their modular design also makes them well suited for decentralised ammonia production coupled to renewable electricity and electrolytic hydrogen. This thesis investigates membrane reactor technology for ammonia synthesis across multiple scales, from membrane material development and reactor proof of concept to scale up and techno economic assessment. Chapter 1 introduces the energy transition context, the role of hydrogen and ammonia as energy carriers, and the limitations of conventional Haber Bosch synthesis. It presents membrane reactors as a promising route toward intensified and decentralised ammonia production. Chapter 2 develops a non isothermal one dimensional packed bed membrane reactor (PBMR) model integrating in situ ammonia removal through NH3 selective membranes and sweep gas operation. Parametric studies identify membrane performance targets and optimal operating conditions. The results demonstrate that membrane reactors can significantly exceed the performance of conventional packed bed reactors under milder operating conditions. Carbon molecular sieve (CMS) membranes are identified as particularly promising candidates. Chapter 3 investigates phenolic resin derived, metal doped CMS membranes for ammonia separation. Membranes are fabricated and characterised experimentally, while gas transport is analysed through a model combining molecular sieving, surface diffusion, and Knudsen diffusion. title: Pyrene-based double helicenes to zigzag-edge enriched nanographenes
summary: Two isomeric zigzag-edged nanographenes with identical molecular formulae but distinct edge topologies were synthesised using a modular solution-phase strategy. The nanographenes exhibit green-to-orange fluorescence, with emission maxima at
content: Two isomeric zigzag-edged nanographenes with identical molecular formulae but distinct edge topologies were synthesised using a modular solution-phase strategy. The nanographenes exhibit green-to-orange fluorescence, with emission maxima at 517 and 575 nm for zz-NG 2 and zz-NG 1, respectively. Despite their identical molecular formulae, they show markedly different fluorescence quantum yields of 29% and 55%, respectively, and distinct radiative decay rates. These findings demonstrate that zigzag-edge connectivity can be used to tune the excited-state dynamics and fluorescence of nanographenes.

title: Acoustically optimized swarm of micro-drones in concert halls: from aeroacoustics to active acoustic masking
summary: This review paper examines recent advances in acoustic sensing, localization, noise mitigation, and decentralized swarm control of micro-drones operating in enclosed performance spaces, with a focus on concert-hall applications. We argue th
content: This review paper examines recent advances in acoustic sensing, localization, noise mitigation, and decentralized swarm control of micro-drones operating in enclosed performance spaces, with a focus on concert-hall applications. We argue that an acoustically optimized swarm of micro-drones can act as a distributed, reconfigurable acoustic element of the hall itself (augmenting early reflections, masking residual self-noise, and providing real-time acoustic mapping) without permanent electroacoustic installations. We synthesize evidence from digital-twin-based adaptive concert halls, acoustic shells, onboard spectral analysis, acoustic localization systems (MicNest, AIM, GCC-PHAT arrays), acoustic drone-to-drone communication (HUM), passive and active noise reduction, and resource-constrained multi-robot formation control. We conclude that decentralized, AI-driven swarm control can sustain low-latency, reliable formation behavior on resource-constrained platforms in enclosed spaces, provided that localization accuracy, acoustic side-channel reliability, and perceptually motivated noise budgets are jointly engineered.

title: Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
summary: Abstract Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off b
content: Abstract Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off between achieving spatial charge separation, which is necessary for dipole formation, and maintaining sufficient wavefunction overlap to ensure efficient radiative recombination. Here, we overcome this trade-off in the two-dimensional perovskite (AE3T)PbI 4 by leveraging organic-inorganic band-edge engineering to induce frontier-state hybridization, thereby forming bright hybridized dipolar excitons with spatially indirect character and appreciable optical transition strength. These excitons combine an out-of-plane permanent electric-dipole component, room-temperature nonlinear transport consistent with long-range dipole–dipole repulsion, and finite optical transition dipole moments. Beyond addressing a key constraint in dipolar-exciton design, this work establishes frontier-state hybridization as a molecular design principle for constructing optically active, electrically polarized excitons in low-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Anaerobic gut fungi enhance bioplastic degradability under anaerobic digestion conditions
summary: Abstract Background Biodegradable bio-based plastics (BPs) were developed to mitigate environmental plastic pollution, but they generally degrade more readily under aerobic than anaerobic conditions. Aerobic composting produces carbon dioxi
content: Abstract Background Biodegradable bio-based plastics (BPs) were developed to mitigate environmental plastic pollution, but they generally degrade more readily under aerobic than anaerobic conditions. Aerobic composting produces carbon dioxide, while anaerobic digestion (AD) generates both CO 2 and methane. Because CH 4 is a valuable energy source, enhancing plastic biodegradation under AD conditions could both reduce plastic waste and support fuel production. This study investigates anaerobic gut fungi (AGF) as a biological pretreatment enhancing the biodegradability of different bioplastic designs within AD sludge microbiomes. Results Three AGF-BP pairings were chosen to evaluate the efficacy of AGF pretreatment in improving BP biodegradability in anaerobic sludge. A polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) straw was pretreated with Neocallimastix californiae , while cellulose acetate (CA) and polylactic acid (PLA) films were pretreated with Neocallimastix lanati . Measurements of biogas production, BP weight loss, and surface characterization demonstrated that N. californiae enhanced the biodegradability of PHA and N. lanati enhanced the biodegradability of CA, whereas N. lanati did not significantly improve PLA biodegradability under AD conditions. 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metatranscriptomic analyses showed that the AGF-pretreated PHA and CA induced significant, BP-specific shifts in the relative abundance of microbial taxa, carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) transcripts, and other functional genes within the AD microbiome. Furthermore, biogas measurements revealed that N. lanati could partially metabolize CA during the pretreatment phase, but N. californiae could not metabolize PHA. These findings suggest that N. lanati acts through both enzymatic and mechanical mechanisms on CA, while N. californiae likely functions primarily through mechanical disruption of PHA. Transcriptomic analysis of N. lanati during the pretreatment phase further revealed upregulation of cellulolytic CAZymes and adhesion-related genes when grown on CA, suggesting that these factors likely contribute to CA degradation. Conclusions Our findings show for the first time that AGF pretreatment enhances biodegradability of BPs under AD conditions, likely through a synergistic effect of enzymatic hydrolysis and mechanical disruption of the polymer structure. These results highlight AGF as a promising biological pretreatment strategy for enhancing energy recovery and carbon valorization from bioplastic waste streams.

title: Integrating radiomics into multimodal artificial intelligence for lung cancer: a narrative review of digital health applications and clinical translation
summary: Abstract This narrative review examines radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for lung cancer diagnosis, staging, treatment response and prognosis. Evidence is organized by clinical decision points, validation maturity and implem
content: Abstract This narrative review examines radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for lung cancer diagnosis, staging, treatment response and prognosis. Evidence is organized by clinical decision points, validation maturity and implementation requirements. Clinical translation requires reproducible workflows, independent validation, calibration and demonstrated clinical utility. Current evidence remains predominantly retrospective and concentrated in non-small cell lung cancer, positioning radiomics as a potential complementary decision-support tool.

title: Electronically active Sn nanosheets enable Sn-to-Pt interfacial charge redistribution for acidic and alkaline hydrogen evolution
summary: Regulating Pt-support electronic coupling is crucial for improving the activity, durability, and Pt utilization of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. However, the weak electronic interaction between Pt nanoparticles and con
content: Regulating Pt-support electronic coupling is crucial for improving the activity, durability, and Pt utilization of hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. However, the weak electronic interaction between Pt nanoparticles and conventional carbon supports in commercial platinum-on-carbon (Pt/C) limits further performance enhancement. Herein, we report a two-dimensional Sn nanosheet-supported Pt nanoparticle catalyst (Pt/Sn NSs) constructed by liquid-phase exfoliation and atomic layer deposition. Structural and surface chemical analyses reveal pronounced interfacial electronic coupling between Pt nanoparticles and the Sn-based support. Combined with density functional theory calculations, the results demonstrate Sn-to-Pt interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced Pt stabilization on Sn nanosheets. Benefiting from this strengthened Pt-support electronic interaction, Pt/Sn NSs exhibit superior HER performance compared to commercial Pt/C in both acidic and alkaline media, requiring only 28 mV in 0.5 M H2SO4 and 37 mV in 1.0 M KOH to reach 10 mA cm-2, with Tafel slopes of 13.5 and 35.7 mV dec-1, respectively. The calculations further show support-induced modulation of the Pt electronic structure, a more nearly thermoneutral H* adsorption state, and more favorable reaction thermodynamics for the key HER steps. This work demonstrates that electronically interactive Sn nanosheets provide an effective support-engineering platform for regulating Pt-based HER electrocatalysis.

title: Teaching Children to Repair: Repair Interventions Impact on Children’s Attitudes, Perceived Behavioural Control, and Behavioural Intentions
summary: In the current throw-away society it is central to teach children sustainable approaches, such as repair, as their environmental attitudes develop in these years. Guided by the Theory of Planned Behaviour, we examine children’s repair-relat
content: In the current throw-away society it is central to teach children sustainable approaches, such as repair, as their environmental attitudes develop in these years. Guided by the Theory of Planned Behaviour, we examine children’s repair-related attitudes, perceived behavioural control, subjective norms, and repair intentions in relation to participation in repair-focused educational activities through two studies. Study 1 (repair events) involved 662 children (ages 8–18) at a public science event and used an observational design to examine associations with participation in brief hands-on repair activities. Study 2 (repair camps) employed a pre-test/post-test design with 70 sixth-grade students (ages 12–13), comparing an intervention school participating in classroom-based repair education and a Repair Camp with a control school. Across both studies, attitudes toward repair became more positive. Study 1 linked participation to more positive attitudes, Study 2 showed stronger pre-post attitude improvements. Neither study found corresponding differences in repair intentions. However, study 2 showed gains in perceived behavioural control, study 1 associated subjective norms with repair intentions. Study 1 also revealed age-related differences, with younger children reporting more positive attitudes and older children higher perceived behavioural control. Overall, the findings suggest that attitudes toward repair, perceived capability to repair, and intentions to repair are related but empirically distinct outcomes.

title: Четвертичный сектор как источник экологического замещения: межотраслевая оценка вклада инноваций в снижение «экологической стоимости» промышленного роста
summary: Обеспечение технологического суверенитета предполагает опережающий рост обрабатывающей промышленности, тогда как климатическое и экологическое регулирование выступает по отношению к этому росту ограничением. Инновации традиционно рассматрив
content: Обеспечение технологического суверенитета предполагает опережающий рост обрабатывающей промышленности, тогда как климатическое и экологическое регулирование выступает по отношению к этому росту ограничением. Инновации традиционно рассматриваются как средство разрешения данного противоречия, однако утверждение о том, что та или иная технологическая инновация снижает экологическую нагрузку, остается качественным и не позволяет ранжировать экологическую эффективность новых технологий. В статье предложен инструмент количественной оценки вклада инновационной деятельности в снижение экологических издержек промышленного роста. На базе эколого-расширенной модели «затраты — выпуск» вводится показатель «экологической стоимости» — совокупного прироста экологической нагрузки, приходящегося на один процент роста выпуска отрасли с учетом переноса эффектов по производственной цепочке. Учитываются три вида экстерналий: выбросы загрязняющих веществ в атмосферу, баланс отходов производства и забор пресной воды, приводимые к сопоставимому виду через систему экологических единиц. Расчеты выполнены по тридцати трем видам экономической деятельности на данных таблиц «затраты — выпуск» и форм федерального статистического наблюдения за охраной окружающей среды. Установлено, что перенос экологических эффектов сопоставим с прямым эффектом отрасли, а в первичном секторе превосходит его в полтора раза: нагрузка, возникающая вследствие развития спроса смежных секторов, составляет около 109 тысяч экологических единиц, или 143,4% от эффекта роста только самого первичного сектора. Четвертичный сектор, объединяющий виды деятельности по устранению экологических экстерналий, обеспечивает снижение нагрузки примерно на 115 тысяч экологических единиц, что позволяет говорить об экологическом замещении, однако не перекрывает совокупного эффекта роста: сохранение неизменного уровня экстерналий требует 3,05% прироста четвертичного сектора на каждый процент прироста остальных секторов. Сформулированы следствия для отбора приоритетов инновационной политики, для выбора индикаторов ее результативности и для оценки экологических эффектов промышленной кооперации в рамках Евразийского экономического союза.

title: Day-ahead economic dispatch of electro-thermal coupled virtual power plants toward zero-carbon airports
summary: Addressing the high energy consumption and carbon emission characteristics of airports, this paper proposes a day-ahead economic dispatch strategy for a zero-carbon airport virtual power plant (VPP) considering electro-thermal coupling. An
content: Addressing the high energy consumption and carbon emission characteristics of airports, this paper proposes a day-ahead economic dispatch strategy for a zero-carbon airport virtual power plant (VPP) considering electro-thermal coupling. An electro-thermal coupled VPP system model is established, incorporating wind power, photovoltaics (PV), electrical energy storage (ES), air source heat pumps (ASHP), ground source heat pumps (GSHP), and borehole thermal energy storage (BTES). To minimize the total operating cost, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model integrating the Chinese Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) carbon trading mechanism is formulated. The free carbon allowance is benchmarked against the purchased-electricity emissions of a no-carbon-cost baseline case, and the carbon trading cost is accounted for through net emission settlement between purchased emissions and sold emission reductions. A four-scenario case study based on a typical winter heating day at Ordos Airport demonstrates that: the CCER settlement mechanism reduces the accounting-based total operating cost by 20.52% mainly through monetizing surplus carbon credits; the GSHP-BTES electro-thermal coupling scheme decreases the total operating cost by 77.11% and net carbon emissions by 77.62% compared to a pure ASHP heating configuration; and the BTES storage capacity serves as a critical threshold determining whether the system operates as a net CCER seller or buyer.

title: A province-year dataset of carbon emissions and driving variables in China from 1980 to 2023
summary: This dataset provides province-year panel data for 30 provincial-level regions in mainland China from 1980 to 2023. It includes calibrated provincial CO2 emissions and 29 associated variables covering demographics, economic structure and in
content: This dataset provides province-year panel data for 30 provincial-level regions in mainland China from 1980 to 2023. It includes calibrated provincial CO2 emissions and 29 associated variables covering demographics, economic structure and industrialisation, energy consumption and efficiency, natural environment, transportation activity, technological development, and external economic factors. The package includes province-level CSV files before missing-value reconstruction, finalized province-level CSV files after reconstruction, a combined province-year panel CSV file, codebook files with variable definitions and source information, license information, environment files, and code for data processing and imputation.

title: ESGF-NG CMIP7.CMIP.ACCESS-Consortium.ACCESS-ESM1-6.historical version 1
summary: Project: CMIP7 CMIP core common experiments i.e. the DECK (Diagnostic, Evaluation and Characterization of Klima). Produced by: The ACCESS Consortium brings together Australian institutions contributing to the Australian Community Climate an
content: Project: CMIP7 CMIP core common experiments i.e. the DECK (Diagnostic, Evaluation and Characterization of Klima). Produced by: The ACCESS Consortium brings together Australian institutions contributing to the Australian Community Climate and Earth System Simulator (ACCESS) and its submissions to the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP). Participating organisations contribute to different ACCESS models and scientific activities, supported through a combination of institutional investment and Australian Government research infrastructure and research programs, together with international collaborations. (Using Model/Source: ACCESS-ESM1-6 with Experiment historical) The model is an updated version of ACCESS-ESM1-5, as used for CMIP6 (Ziehn et al., 2020). Its dynamic components are the UK Met Office Unified Model atmosphere (v7.3) in a configuration similar to HadGEM2 including CLASSIC aerosols, with the CABLE land surface model (v3) including land biogeochemistry. The atmosphere is coupled to the MOM5 ocean with WOMBATlite biogeochemistry and CICE5 sea-ice using the OASIS-MCT coupler. Chemistry is prescribed including monthly mean, zonally-averaged ozone. Volcano forcing is prescribed as stratospheric optical depth as monthly means in four equal area latitude bands. Land-ice is represented by an ice tile in the land surface model. A grid-cell is either completely ice or ice-free and the ice tile distribution does not change in time. The main differences from ACCESS-ESM1.5 include corrections to how convective momentum transport had been applied in the atmosphere, a change to ocean albedo to better match observations, a correction to the passing of ocean carbon fluxes into the atmosphere, updates to improve energy and water conservation across the land and atmosphere, inclusion of 3 new plant functional types (c4 crops and two Australian tree types), improvements to the treatment of land-use change, updates to some of the land parameterisations or parameter values, the inclusion of a pseudo-iceberg scheme for distributing runoff from Antarctica and Greenland and a substantial update to ocean-biogeochemistry. Many aspects of the model infrastructure have also been improved to ensure greater provenance, better support for users and enhanced model throughput. A manuscript describing ACCESS-ESM1.6 is in preparation (Ziehn et al.). Experiment: Simulation of the climate of the recent past (typically meaning 1850 to present-day) with prescribed carbon dioxide concentrations (for prescribed carbon dioxide emissions, see `esm-hist`). CMIP7 is a project of the [World Climate Research Programme (WCRP)](https://www.wcrp-climate.org/), providing climate projections to understand past, present, and future climate changes. It is part of the [WCRP Earth System Modelling and Observations (ESMO) Core Project](https://wcrp-esmo.org/), which was formed to coordinate all modelling, data, and observation activities across WCRP and its key partners.
