content: This study investigates the impact of complex liquid fertilizers on soil properties, nutrient absorption, and crop yield. The results demonstrate that liquid fertilizers significantly enhance soil fertility, increasing pH from 6.1 to 6.5, organic matter from 2.4% to 3.2%, nitrate by 90-92%, phosphorus by 78-80%, and potassium by 30%. Compared to traditional fertilizers, liquid fertilizers showed 82-88% nutrient absorption efficiency, leading to a 14-22% yield increase. Additionally, they posed lower environmental risks due to reduced nutrient leaching. The findings highlight the potential of liquid fertilizers in sustainable agriculture, improving productivity while minimizing environmental impact. Further research is recommended to explore long-term effects on soil health and diverse climatic conditions.

title: How effective is blockchain in developing trust-centric contract farming models
summary: Today, smart agriculture has emerged as a key domain for sustainable development, involving multiple stakeholders such as farmers, industrialists, government agencies, and others. However, contracts established among these entities often co
content: Today, smart agriculture has emerged as a key domain for sustainable development, involving multiple stakeholders such as farmers, industrialists, government agencies, and others. However, contracts established among these entities often come with high expectations, and failure to fulfil agreed terms can result in significant financial losses for the parties involved. Considering the increasing evidence of smart agriculture adaptation and its correlation with traditional contract farming practices. The research used a trust score analysis methodology, drawing on case studies of contract farming across many nations, including Open Agri-Food Blockchain Platforms, FAO Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS), AgriDigital Blockchain Platforms, and on-chain data. We subsequently utilized the Ricardian approach for contract authentication and the Ethereum adaptation for systems trust score analysis. This system guarantees contract integrity by overseeing and authenticating the actions of both parties concerned. The findings indicate that trust is significantly enhanced, rising by 80% to 100% based on counterpart evaluations. The findings indicate that an increase in trust scores and the use of Ricardian principles in contract farming enhance the likelihood of adopting contract farming, resulting in increased yields, lower input costs, and improved sustainability in rural and marginal areas. This study offers a novel framework on contract farming by encrypting the contract agreement and monitoring smart agriculture’s sustainable behaviors during contract farming. Smart triggers and penalty induction of 0.01 to 0.2 ETH reduce payment delays from the buyer side. The increase in trust is 80–100% based on equivalent ratings.The prototype shows how Ricardian contracts can combine off-chain plain language agreements with on-chain enforcement on Ethereum while maintaining efficiency, transparency, and verifiability.

title: Dragon fruit peel waste-derived iron nanozyme with peroxidase-like activity for smartphone-assisted colorimetric detection of urinary uric acid
summary: Uric acid monitoring is important for the early identification and management of hyperuricemia, which is linked to gout and an increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Turning agricultural and food-processing waste into use
content: Uric acid monitoring is important for the early identification and management of hyperuricemia, which is linked to gout and an increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Turning agricultural and food-processing waste into useful functional materials also offers a more sustainable path for developing low-cost analytical tools. Here, we developed a simple colorimetric method for detecting uric acid using a nanozyme made from dragon fruit peel, an abundant agricultural waste material. This nanozyme mimics the activity of natural peroxidase enzymes, converting a colorless substrate into a blue-colored product in the presence of hydrogen peroxide. Uric acid was found to inhibit this colorimetric reaction, with the intensity of the blue color decreasing as uric acid concentration increased. The colorimetric assay exhibited a linear response over a uric acid concentration range of 0–100 µM, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.49 µM. The method was applied to uric acid detection in rat urine samples using a smartphone camera for colorimetric readout. High concentration of calcium and magnesium ions were found to cause some interference with uric acid detection. These findings support the use of dragon fruit peel-derived nanozymes as a practical platform for affordable, point-of-care uric acid monitoring.

title: Eco-friendly preparation and characterization of avocado waste-derived silver nanoparticles-embedded alginate films for potential wound dressing use
source: Journal of Metals Materials and Minerals
summary: The ever-increasing volume of waste generated in the avocado industry poses an environmental problem; however, thanks to the valuable bio-components contained within this waste, this situation presents a potential to be transformed from a p
content: The ever-increasing volume of waste generated in the avocado industry poses an environmental problem; however, thanks to the valuable bio-components contained within this waste, this situation presents a potential to be transformed from a problem into an opportunity. In this study, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized using a green method with avocado peel extract as a biogenic reducing and stabilizing agent; the synthesized AgNPs were embedded into sodium alginate (SA) films to obtain functional biomaterials for wound dressing applications. The changes in physicochemical properties (Water resistance, swelling index, gel fraction, degradation behavior, and water vapor transmission rate (WVTR)) of the prepared AgNPs@SA films were investigated by varying the amounts of their components (alginate amount, AgNO3 concentration, and extract concentration). In terms of the obtained physicochemical properties, the film formulation using 2.0 g alginate, 2.0 mM AgNO3, and 0.20 g·mL‒1 extract was selected as optimum. The film synthesized with the determined optimum formulation was found to have an average thickness of 0.351 mm, a suitable WVTR value, and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Mechanical analysis results show that AgNPs@SA films exhibit a ductile and viscoelastic structure characterized by high elongation and sufficient tensile strength, indicating potential for use as a flexible and stable wound dressing. Characterization studies (SEM, EDX, FTIR, XRD, and XPS) supported the successful green synthesis of AgNPs and provided evidence consistent with their incorporation into the alginate films, while indicating the involvement of plant-derived components in nanoparticle synthesis. The findings indicate that avocado peel waste can be transformed into a value-added product for environmentally friendly wound dressing applications.

title: Analysis of policy networks in fisheries cultivation village program development: evidence from Kampar regency, Riau Province, Indonesia
summary: This study examines the relational and interpretive dimensions of policy-network implementation in the Fisheries Cultivation Village Program in XIII Koto Kampar District, Riau Province, Indonesia. The study employed a qualitative approach b
content: This study examines the relational and interpretive dimensions of policy-network implementation in the Fisheries Cultivation Village Program in XIII Koto Kampar District, Riau Province, Indonesia. The study employed a qualitative approach based on 15 semi-structured interviews conducted between April and May 2026, with interview data analysed thematically using NVivo 12 Plus. The findings show that program implementation involved differentiated actor roles, information flow, liaison and brokerage functions, trust relationships, and resource interdependence across organizational boundaries. Actors also demonstrated varying degrees of similarity in their definitions of implementation problems, particularly regarding feed/raw materials, market access, and capital, while identifying related solution areas including technical guidance, institutional strengthening, market access and downstreaming, and infrastructure improvement. These findings indicate that policy-network implementation involves both relational patterns and actors’ interpretations of problems and possible responses. The study contributes a relational–interpretive perspective that combines analysis of how actors interact with how they understand implementation challenges and formulate solution options. Rather than treating network positions, trust, interdependence, or shared problem definitions as indicators of implementation effectiveness, the study conceptualizes them as analytical features of how the policy network is organized, experienced, and interpreted.

title: Pathways for Standardising Low Carbon Concrete for Infrastructure Applications
summary: Abstract The European Green Deal requires that EU member states place ambitions reduction targets for the way in which we build and manage our transport infrastructure. Central to this is the need for innovative concrete products with signi
content: Abstract The European Green Deal requires that EU member states place ambitions reduction targets for the way in which we build and manage our transport infrastructure. Central to this is the need for innovative concrete products with significantly reduced embodied carbon. The traditional role of harmonised standards within the EU is that they play a key role in opening up markets, while also offering assurances over safety and quality. There is however a concern that they can also be conservative, prescriptive and slow to evolve, and that this can create barriers for low-carbon solutions such as geopolymer concretes or low-clinker cement concrete. Some countries have however made progress in this regard, and a good example is the UK introduction of BSI Flex 350, a flexible, performance-based guidance document developed by the British Standards Institution, as a blueprint for adopting alternative binders to facilitate innovation. While not yet applied in live infrastructure projects, it offers a forward-looking model grounded in whole-life carbon assessment, circular economy principles, and material-neutral performance criteria. This paper discusses the potential for a similar approach to be adopted within the EU and considers the implications for procurement reform, policy alignment and standard harmonisation.

title: Analysis on Application of Reverse Logistics on Global Supply Chains
source: International Journal of Applied Mathematics Computational Science and Systems Engineering
summary: The research focuses on the analysis of the role of reverse logistics in supply chain management operations. Reverse logistics can be regarded as an essential process of supply chain management that is associated with the movement of goods
content: The research focuses on the analysis of the role of reverse logistics in supply chain management operations. Reverse logistics can be regarded as an essential process of supply chain management that is associated with the movement of goods from the customers to the sellers or the manufacturers. It is associated with the return and recycling of the products. It is an essential part of supply chain operations to maintain an efficient flow of goods that is also associated with the cost-saving, value creation, and risk mitigation of the companies associated with the supply chain operations. The current study also examines the factors influencing the implementation of reverse logistics within a company, the current trends and technologies used in the reverse logistics process, the profitability aspect of this process to the company, and finally, finding the ways to improve the process. Secondary method and the quantitative method were adopted within the research, that enabled acquiring required outcomes from this research work. In addition, the deductive approach and the inductive approach have been applied for intermingling self-generated and pre-existing concepts and theories. The descriptive design has been applied for linking the different segments of the research topic. The positivism research philosophy has been applied for the purpose of shedding light on the positive impacts of reverse logistics on the management of supply chain operations.

title: Cathode Materials for Sodium-Ion Batteries: Limitations and Optimisation Strategies
summary: Sodium-ion batteries are expected to be used in place of lithium-ion batteries because sodium resources are abundant, inexpensive and structurally compatible with aluminium current collectors. However, the main deficiencies in cell-level en
content: Sodium-ion batteries are expected to be used in place of lithium-ion batteries because sodium resources are abundant, inexpensive and structurally compatible with aluminium current collectors. However, the main deficiencies in cell-level energy density, cycle life and interface stability are still with cathode materials. Layered transition metal oxides undergo irreversible phase transitions and are sensitive to the atmosphere of water and CO2. Polyanion compounds have a stable structure but are electronically insulating and lack capacity. Prussian blue analogues have open diffusion channels, but interstitial water and cyanide-derived precursors lead to side reactions and safety problems. The two most common ways to address the above problems are surface coating and elemental doping. Carbon, oxide and conductive polymer coatings promote interfacial charge transfer and mechanical buffering; sodium-site doping and transition-metal-site substitution stabilize the host lattice and suppress irreversible structural evolution. Systematically study the above deficiencies and optimisation paths in this paper, and discuss the remaining problems from the perspectives of energy density, scalable production, and compatibility with solid-state electrolytes.

title: Agentic AI-Enabled Smart Microgrid for Green Hydrogen Production in Rural Communities: Opportunity, Challenges and Future Outlook
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: In this paper, an agentic AI-driven smart micro-grid architecture for the generation and distribution of green hydrogen in rural communities is presented as a solution to the needs of sustainable, decentralised and intelligent energy system
content: In this paper, an agentic AI-driven smart micro-grid architecture for the generation and distribution of green hydrogen in rural communities is presented as a solution to the needs of sustainable, decentralised and intelligent energy systems. The current AI based microgrids are still lacking in autonomy, ineffective coordination of distributed energy resources (DERs) and integration of hydrogen production processes. The proposed study aims to overcome such disadvantages by developing a multi-layered cyber-physical architecture, which includes renewable energy resources, communication networks, and an agentic layer of AI that will be capable of making autonomous decisions, learning adaptively, and optimizing in real-time. The study applies the strategy of conceptual and system level design and provides a well-structured overview of the technologies involved in the integration of AI, smart grid, and hydrogen. The new approaches included in the framework are proposed to improve energy prediction, electrolysis system control and efficiency with reinforcement learning, digital twins and explainable AI as well as decentralized multi-agent coordination. It also does not depend on energy supply as it includes rural green hydrogen value chains to be utilized in clean cooking, transportation, agro-processing and small-scale industries. The results indicate that the value of agentic AI in delivering system flexibility, efficiency, resilience, and scalability is significant, and much greater than the value of the conventional AI-powered strategies. The paper presents a novel concept for an independently functioning energy structure and proposes the future research direction including federated learning, multi-agent systems, and decentralized energy markets. The proposed framework can provide a viable pathway to achieve energy Independence and reduce Carbon emissions and socio-economic sustainable development of the rural communities.

title: The Migration of Chemical Contaminants from Polyethylene Terephthalate Bottles Into Shani Soft Drink
summary: Conducted a comparison between the effect of different storage conditions and durations on the migration of polyethylene terephthalate contaminants to Shani soft drink (SH) to refer to the most suitable condition for storing this drink. A s
content: Conducted a comparison between the effect of different storage conditions and durations on the migration of polyethylene terephthalate contaminants to Shani soft drink (SH) to refer to the most suitable condition for storing this drink. A sample of the drink under study was obtained immediately after filling into 1-liter PET-bottles and stored at varying conditions including -18, 0, 4, 25°C, shade and the sun, at beginning of the storage, GC-MS was employed to identify potential chemical contaminants, during storage concentrations of identified contaminants were monitored by using HPLC. Also FTIR-spectra of drinks stored at the three worst conditions (-18, 0 and the sun) were compared and the inner surfaces of the same bottles were electron-microscopically scanned before and after storage to assess the morphological changes caused by each of them. The findings stated that cooling is the most suitable condition while the sun storage was the most detrimental among the other conditions, since the sample stored in the sun for 180 days was recorded the lowest value of pH and the highest concentrations of detected contaminants, as well comparison of FTIR-spectra revealed the presence of esters and carbonyl compounds at the highest concentration in the sample stored in the sun for 30 days. Similarly, comparison of captured SEM-images confirmed that PET-bottles stored at the sun were the most damaged compared to their counterparts stored at freezing temperatures, -18 and 0 °C.

title: Comprehensive system-level assessments of the carbon value chain: CO2 capture, storage, and utilization
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Deep decarbonization of carbon-intensive energy industries requires a consistent assessment framework that explicitly represents CO2 capture, conditioning, compression, transport, and storage or utilization, independent of the final product
content: Deep decarbonization of carbon-intensive energy industries requires a consistent assessment framework that explicitly represents CO2 capture, conditioning, compression, transport, and storage or utilization, independent of the final product. This thesis develops and applies a harmonized, modular framework using hydrogen and methanol as representative applications central to industrial decarbonization. Hydrogen is examined because it is both a key energy carrier and a major source of industrial CO2 emissions when produced from natural gas. This makes it a critical case for evaluation of how capture configuration, electricity supply, and CO2 handling affect cost, emissions, and efficiency. Methanol is assessed as a representative CO2 utilization pathway because it enables conversion of captured CO2 into a marketable product, requires large hydrogen inputs, and is widely discussed as a scalable platform chemical and energy carrier. Although many studies report techno-economic or life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) results for individual technologies, comparisons across pathways are often not decision-relevant due to inconsistent system boundaries, assumptions, and performance metrics. CO2 handling steps such as drying, multi-stage compression, transport, and storage are frequently simplified or omitted. In parallel, emerging sustainability constraints, particularly water use and electricity-source dependence, are inconsistently quantified, limiting robust technology selection in regions with carbon-intensive grids and evolving policy environments. To address these gaps, this thesis integrates bottom-up process modeling, cradle-to-gate GHG estimation, and techno-economic analysis under consistent system boundaries. Sensitivity and uncertainty analyses are used to identify dominant drivers and quantify outcome ranges. Multiple carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) enabled hydrogen and methanol pathways relevant to Alberta and other fossil-intensive regions are evaluated to determine how capture configuration, electricity supply, and process integration jointly influence cost, energy performance, GHG emissions, and water intensity. For blue hydrogen production at 607 t-H2/day capacity, steam methane reforming (SMR), autothermal reforming (ATR), and natural gas decomposition (NGD) are assessed using consistent assumptions. Levelized hydrogen costs without carbon capture and storage (CCS) are $1.22/kg-H2 (SMR), $1.23/kg-H2 (ATR), and $2.12/kg-H2 (NGD), increasing to $1.69/kg-H2 (SMR–52% CCS), $2.36/kg-H2 (SMR–85% CCS), $1.66/kg-H2 (ATR–CCS), and $2.55/kg-H2 (NGD–CCS). Under identical capacity and boundaries, ATR–CCS achieves the lowest life-cycle GHG intensity (3.91 kg- CO2e/kg-H2), followed by NGD–CCS (4.54), SMR–85% (6.66), and SMR–52% (8.20). These results demonstrate that concentrating CO2 into fewer, higher-pressure capture points reduces compression burdens and overall GHG emissions. Water withdrawal and consumption are quantified for grey and

title: Pedogenic factors associated with soil fertility constraints in the Northern Guinea Savanna of Nigeria and their implications for soil management
summary: Introduction Soil fertility constraints in the Northern Guinea Savanna of Nigeria were evaluated in relation to slope position, parent material, and World Reference Base (WRB) Reference Soil Groups (RSGs) using 157 georeferenced legacy soil
content: Introduction Soil fertility constraints in the Northern Guinea Savanna of Nigeria were evaluated in relation to slope position, parent material, and World Reference Base (WRB) Reference Soil Groups (RSGs) using 157 georeferenced legacy soil profile pits. Methods Descriptive statistics, Moran's I, Pearson correlation, principal component analysis (PCA), general linear models (GLMs) with and without interaction terms, and a Fertility Deviation Index (FDI) referenced to high-fertility benchmarks were applied. Results All 11 soil properties showed significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.14 -0.47). Organic carbon (OC) correlated positively with total exchangeable bases (TEB, r = 0.348), cation exchange capacity (CEC, r = 0.272), and base saturation percentage (BSP, r = 0.233), while clay correlated with CEC (r = 0.329). Four principal components explained 61.5% of the total variance. Parent material was associated with exchangeable potassium (F = 5.40, p < 0.001) and pH (F = 5.72, p = 0.002), slope position with particle-size fractions and total nitrogen (TN), and WRB RSGs with CEC (F = 7.35, p = 0.001) and clay (F = 3.49, p = 0.003). Models explained 3 -27% of the variance. Valley-bottom soils had higher OC, TN and available phosphorus (av. P), while Gleysols had the highest OC and BSP. FDI values were negative across all indicators and groups, with the largest deviations for OC (−50.3 to −91.8%), CEC (−52.4 to −75.3%) and av. P (−43.8 to −68.9%). Discussion Fertility constraints reflect the combined influence of slope position, parent material and soil class. Low OC and CEC were the most pronounced constraints relative to high-fertility benchmarks. FDI values indicate benchmark deviations, not temporal depletion, and management implications require field validation.

title: Analysis of the Current Development Status, Causes, Dilemmas, and Governance Paths of Price Wars in the New Energy Vehicle Industry
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: China's new energy vehicle (NEV) industry, after rapid expansion, is confronted with the predicament of growing output alongside squeezed profits. Its industrial profit margin dropped to 4.1% in 2025, a ten-year low, while vehicle manufactu
content: China's new energy vehicle (NEV) industry, after rapid expansion, is confronted with the predicament of growing output alongside squeezed profits. Its industrial profit margin dropped to 4.1% in 2025, a ten-year low, while vehicle manufacturing margins shrank to 1.5% in H1 2026. Price cuts launched by leading enterprises set off a chain reaction, trapping the sector in a prisoner's dilemma. This paper reviews NEV price competition and identifies its regional, continuous, transmissive and multi-dimensional evolutionary features. Drawing on the prisoner's dilemma game model and the "policy-technology-market" triple lock-in mechanism, it argues that the price war arises from firm gaming and institutional lock-in rather than supply-demand imbalance. A three-stage governance framework is put forward: short-term market regulation, medium-term unlocking of development paths, and long-term shift toward value-based competition. The study concludes that the industry can escape the price competition trap only by replacing price competition with value competition, supported by technological innovation, institutional improvement and global layout.

title: Essays on financial markets: aquaculture finance, energy transition, and intangible governance
summary: This doctoral dissertation investigates the pricing, management, and mitigation of risk in modern financial markets, traversing the domains of natural resource economics, energy transition finance, and corporate governance. As the global ec
content: This doctoral dissertation investigates the pricing, management, and mitigation of risk in modern financial markets, traversing the domains of natural resource economics, energy transition finance, and corporate governance. As the global economy enters an era of polycrisis defined by accelerating climate change, structural policy shifts, and complex agency conflicts, traditional valuation frameworks, which are often predicated on assumptions of linearity, stationarity, and limited dimensions, are increasingly insufficient. This research proposes and validates a unified computational and empirical framework to address these challenges, comprising four independent but thematically integrated essays. The first essay addresses the curse of dimensionality in natural resource valuation by applying Deep Q-Learning to the optimal harvesting problem in aquaculture. Treating the harvesting decision as a real option, the study evaluates Deep Reinforcement Learning as a scalable, nonparametric alternative to regression-based methods such as Least-Squares Monte Carlo. In the baseline setting, the DQN policy produces harvesting times that are broadly comparable with the LSMC benchmark, although the estimated option values remain lower. The main advantage of the framework is therefore its capacity to accommodate richer state spaces without requiring a rapidly expanding set of manually specified basis functions. The second essay bridges biological modeling and financial engineering to value a novel hedging instrument: the biomass futures contract. By integrating a stochastic biological growth model, which accounts for thermal stress, mortality shocks, and growth rates contingent on temperature, with a Schwartz dual factor pricing model, the study quantifies the hedging demand against production risks driven by climate change. The findings reveal that the economic value of biomass futures is highly dependent on the underlying state. These contracts offer substantial downside protection and fundamentally alter optimal harvesting strategies, primarily under scenarios of extreme environmental volatility. The third essay develops a physics-informed real options framework for evaluating nuclear power investment over extended horizons under climate-policy uncertainty. A key innovation is the incorporation of a climate tipping point that introduces a structural break into the natural carbon-decay mechanism and, in turn, the carbon-pricing function. Comparing alternative continuation-value approximators shows that tree-based methods, particularly Random Forest and XGBoost, are well suited to representing non-smooth exercise boundaries and can produce economically meaningful differences at the margin relative to global polynomial smoothing. The model interprets the additional value associated with the anticipated crisis regime as a "fear premium", reflecting ambiguity about a potentially irreversible environmental regime shift before the physical threshold is actually cro

title: When substitution benefits drift: prospectively assessing what keeps a biomass commitment environmentally justified
summary: Abstract A biomass commitment is made once, but its environmental benefit is not fixed. Chips committed to power, fuels or chemicals are unavailable to other uses, yet each is usually defended by an isolated substitution benefit that ignore
content: Abstract A biomass commitment is made once, but its environmental benefit is not fixed. Chips committed to power, fuels or chemicals are unavailable to other uses, yet each is usually defended by an isolated substitution benefit that ignores the uses forgone, the capacity that resists redirection and the decarbonizing energy system. Here we prospectively follow wood-chip allocation in Japan and its 47 prefectures through 2120, assessing greenhouse-gas reduction, avoided fossil demand and useful-product exergy, the work potential retained in products. The strongest sectoral target for mitigation, a 2030 fuel target, captures 44% of what climate-mitigation-guided allocation achieves. Prioritizing fossil displacement retains at most 24.3% of its mitigation, and prioritizing exergy at least 87.2%. Implementation inertia, resistance to moving chips from incumbent use, removes 26 to 30% when redirection is easy and 45 to 56% when it is not. Low-inertia allocation delivers more mitigation than any sectoral target across the tested coefficient range. An identical allocation delivers 79 to 119 Mt CO 2 e depending only on the decarbonization path. These results suggest that, where redirection is easy, commitments able to follow their changing benefit keep more of it than targets set once and held.

title: Low-emission hydrogen in Uruguay and Argentina: policy making under conditions of high technological and systemic uncertainty - Final Report
source: German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS)
summary: This report analyses how Argentina and Uruguay are navigating the early stages of developing a low-emission hydrogen (LEH2) economy under conditions of high technological, economic and political uncertainty. Based on extensive fieldwork con
content: This report analyses how Argentina and Uruguay are navigating the early stages of developing a low-emission hydrogen (LEH2) economy under conditions of high technological, economic and political uncertainty. Based on extensive fieldwork conducted in early 2024 – including 75 expert interviews and a focus group – the study examines stakeholder perceptions, national strategies, governance challenges and opportunities for value creation in both countries. The research “focuses on the question of how the main actors and stakeholders in the hydrogen economy perceive the uncertainties related to it” and how policy and international cooperation can support constructive action. As the landscape for the international roll-out of hydrogen has changed significantly – with support measures also being adapted – it is important to better understand how stakeholders in the Global South view their prospects and what concerns they have. This study can make an important contribution in this regard. The interviews were prepared, conducted and analysed by a trilateral research team. The three institutional partners were the Universidad Nacional de Quilmes in Argentina, Universidad de la República in Uruguay and the German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS). Senior researchers from Universidad Nacional de Quilmes and IDOS led the project, and the core research team comprised junior researchers from the partner institutions. The partners jointly designed the research project, arranged and conducted the interviews, and evaluated the findings and developed policy recommendations. Globally, hydrogen demand is rising, yet the ramp-up of LEH2 remains slow. Only 1% of global hydrogen is currently low-emission, and “the overall proportion of projects with final investment decision reached not more than 7%” of the expected production volumes by 2023. Persistently high producer prices and complex regulations (mainly at the level of the European Union) are seen as major obstacles to accelerating the roll-out of the hydrogen economy. This could change as a result of new technologies and regulatory reforms, but it is still unclear whether and when this will happen. Both Argentina and Uruguay therefore face a shifting environment: uncertain international markets, evolving certification rules and volatile investment conditions. Argentina possesses substantial natural resources and industrial capabilities – excellent wind and solar resources for green hydrogen, major gas reserves for blue hydrogen and an established nuclear sector that could support pink hydrogen production. Its 2023 National Hydrogen Strategy envisioned integrated value chains, export markets and up to 82,000 jobs by 2050. However, the political shift in 2023 introduced institutional instability. The new government prioritises deregulation and an investment regime that offers incentives “without conditionality” and removes local content requirements. Stakeholders highlighted macro-economic volatilit

title: Comparative Determination of Reducing Sugar in Commercial Tea Beverages and Carbonated Drinks
summary: Commercial beverages can contribute substantial dietary sugar, but the reducing sugar content measured under laboratory conditions can vary across products. This study compared reducing sugar characteristics of 10 commonly consumed commerci
content: Commercial beverages can contribute substantial dietary sugar, but the reducing sugar content measured under laboratory conditions can vary across products. This study compared reducing sugar characteristics of 10 commonly consumed commercial beverages, comprising five tea beverages and five carbonated drinks. Samples were pretreated with zinc acetate, potassium ferrocyanide, and activated carbon before analysis with an alkaline copper tartrate system and methylene blue endpoint detection. Two sample addition volumes, 4.5 mL and 1 mL, were tested to improve discrimination across high-sugar products. Several samples reached the brick-red endpoint after heating, indicating concentrations beyond the measurement range of the initial condition. In the 1 mL group, glucose titration volumes varied across both beverage categories, while jasmine tea and green grape-flavored tea produced the highest values among the tea samples. The experiment showed substantial variability in reducing sugar among commercial beverages and better differentiation after dilution. The results highlight the need for careful analytical control, transparent nutrition labeling, and moderation of sugar-sweetened beverages among adolescents. Larger sample sets, replicate measurements, and improved pretreatment procedures are needed to strengthen measurement accuracy and the reliability of comparisons between beverage categories.

title: Utilizing ultralow-dose hierarchical carbon nanocages to reduce tar and main hazardous substances of cigarette mainstream smoke
summary: Reducing tar content and minimizing toxic effects are the main tasks for the sustainable development of the tobacco industry. Adding adsorbents into cigarette filter tips is a convenient way to reduce tar content in mainstream smoke. Here,
content: Reducing tar content and minimizing toxic effects are the main tasks for the sustainable development of the tobacco industry. Adding adsorbents into cigarette filter tips is a convenient way to reduce tar content in mainstream smoke. Here, hierarchical carbon nanocages (CNC) were, for the first time, introduced into the filter tips as tar adsorbent, and the influences of specific surface area (SSA) and heteroatom doping on the adsorption capacity of wet tar components were systematically studied. The pure CNC with an optimized SSA of 1,000–1,400 m 2 /g and interconnecting macro-, meso- and micropores can achieve a high adsorption efficiency of over 85% for wet tar at an ultralow dose of 0.6–1.0 mg/cig. The high removal efficiency of >80% was realized for the main hazardous substances such as benzo [a]pyrene, phenolic compounds, and carbonyl compounds, which is mainly attributed to the van der Waals interactions as revealed by theoretical calculations. This performance surpasses that of conventional carbon nanotubes and activated carbon adsorbents reported in the literature, despite requiring only 1/15 to 1/50 of their typical doses. The hydrophobic nature of CNC ensures the stable adsorption of wet tar components under humid conditions. The biosafety tests demonstrate that the CNC has negligible toxicity at cellular, tissue, and animal levels in mice, confirming excellent biocompatibility. This study demonstrates a promising application scenario of CNC as a highly efficient and biocompatible adsorbent for removing the tar and hazardous substances from cigarette mainstream smoke.

title: Energy and Emissions Trade-offs of Electric Vehicle Charging and Vehicle Fuel Consumption in the United States
summary: Abstract While electric vehicles (EVs) produce no tailpipe emissions, their upstream emissions increase with the growing electricity demand from the power grid for battery charging. This research investigates how the growth in electric vehi
content: Abstract While electric vehicles (EVs) produce no tailpipe emissions, their upstream emissions increase with the growing electricity demand from the power grid for battery charging. This research investigates how the growth in electric vehicle (EV) adoption and travel demand over time affects overall vehicle fuel consumption and emissions, as well as electricity demand for EV battery charging and the resulting upstream emissions from power generation through a predictive analysis across four major U.S. cities: Atlanta, Los Angeles, New York, and Seattle. Our results highlight the trade-off between reductions in vehicle tailpipe emissions from increased EV adoption and the corresponding increases in upstream emissions from EV charging. Although increasing EV adoption generally has a positive impact on reducing vehicle emissions, even after accounting for the upstream emissions from EV battery charging in regions that rely heavily on fossil fuels for power generation, such as Atlanta, Georgia, these environmental benefits are substantially greater in regions where renewable energy contributes a larger share of the electricity mix, such as Seattle, Washington, and Los Angeles, California. The comparison across these U.S. cities highlights the importance of clean electricity generation in maximizing the environmental benefits of transportation electrification.

title: The Impact of Growth Environment and Economic Conditions on College Students' Irrational Consumption Behavior
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Irrational consumption has become a prevalent issue among contemporary Chinese college students, yet its integrated environmental and economic determinants lack systematic empirical clarification. This study aims to explore how multi-dimens
content: Irrational consumption has become a prevalent issue among contemporary Chinese college students, yet its integrated environmental and economic determinants lack systematic empirical clarification. This study aims to explore how multi-dimensional growth environment and economic conditions influence college students' irrational consumption, defined as excessive borrowing and overspending. Based on the 2021 China College Student Consumption and Credit Behavior Survey (CSCFS) data of 261 valid samples, this research adopts the Probit model for quantitative analysis. The results indicate that family and school environments significantly inhibit irrational consumption, while the direct effect of social environment is insignificant. Students' disposable income positively predicts irrational consumption tendencies, whereas financial literacy effectively restrains risky and excessive consumption behaviors. This study clarifies the dual influencing mechanism of external growth environment and individual economic competence, providing empirical evidence for family-school joint consumption education and youth financial risk governance.

title: What Does the Environmental Phillips Curve Measure? Okun’s Law, Trends and Cyclical Emissions in the G7, 1975–2024
summary: Abstract The Environmental Phillips Curve (EPC) posits a trade-off between unemployment and environmental pressure. This paper asks what the EPC measures once trends are removed and Okun’s law is taken into account. Using G7 data for 1975–2
content: Abstract The Environmental Phillips Curve (EPC) posits a trade-off between unemployment and environmental pressure. This paper asks what the EPC measures once trends are removed and Okun’s law is taken into account. Using G7 data for 1975–2024, we recast the EPC as a chain linking Okun’s law and the cyclical emissions–output relationship, estimate every link in levels and in deviations from trend with fixed-effects, mean-group, common-correlated-effects, panel ARDL (pooled mean group) and CS-ARDL estimators, and test the restriction implied by Okun’s law with a joint moving-block bootstrap. In deviations from trend, unemployment 10% above trend is associated with CO₂ emissions per capita 1.1% below trend. Okun’s law and the emissions–output elasticity account for 83% of this relationship with fixed effects, with a 95% bootstrap interval of 0.62–0.98, and for all of it with the mean-group estimator. The relationship is essentially contemporaneous and robust to the HP, Hamilton and boosted HP filters and to the sample period: across four filters and three periods, the fixed-effects EPC ranges from − 0.115 to − 0.072 and Okun’s law accounts for 83–108% of it. In levels, the EPC is fragile, sensitive to the sample window and absent from both PMG and CS-ARDL estimates in every period. The EPC is therefore best understood as the environmental image of Okun’s law, and cyclical emission reductions should not be counted as progress towards decarbonisation targets. JEL classification: Q43; Q54; Q56; E24; E32; C22; C23

title: Vitrimerization Routes for Waste PET Upcycling
summary: The accumulation of massive post-consumer poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste poses severe ecological hazards. Conventional mechanical recycling induces irreversible chain scission and severe property depreciation, while chemical depol
content: The accumulation of massive post-consumer poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste poses severe ecological hazards. Conventional mechanical recycling induces irreversible chain scission and severe property depreciation, while chemical depolymerization consumes excessive energy and toxic solvents, creating a performance-cost downcycling bottleneck limiting high-value PET reuse. This comprehensive critical review highlights vitrimer chemistry based on associative dynamic exchange as a transformative upcycling solution. The field is organized around two fabrication routes—depolymerization-reconstruction and in-situ/direct network construction while preserving the PET backbone—together with a cross-cutting transesterification catalytic dimension covering externally catalyzed, self-catalytic, and metal-free, no-added-catalyst (including residual-catalyst-assisted), and fully catalyst-free designs. Solvolysis-derived oligomers afford vitrimers with tunable glass transition temperature (Tg) (38~240 °C) and tensile strength up to 117 MPa; solvent-free extrusion fits continuous industrial lines, and metal-free designs may reduce heavy-metal contamination. Several optimized systems retain over 80% mechanical performance after cyclic reprocessing, although significant variations exist; for example, the bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET)/pyromellitic dianhydride (PMDA)/trimethylolpropane (TMP) vitrimer decreases from approximately 30 MPa to 16 MPa after two compression-molding cycles. These technologies show potential for closed-loop recycling and reprocessability, may reduce virgin resin demand, and may reduce carbon footprints, pending full life-cycle assessment. Major industrial barriers include insufficient creep resistance, incomplete monomer recovery, and non-uniform testing standards. This work delivers integrated theoretical and engineering guidance for scalable PET vitrimer circular-material development.

title: Real-World Performance of the eHighway System: Evidence from a Field Trial in Germany
summary: Abstract Electric Road Systems (ERS) represent a promising innovation for enabling carbon-neutral road freight transport. By electrifying segments of highways, these systems allow heavy-duty trucks to operate and charge electric energy whil
content: Abstract Electric Road Systems (ERS) represent a promising innovation for enabling carbon-neutral road freight transport. By electrifying segments of highways, these systems allow heavy-duty trucks to operate and charge electric energy while driving. An ERS solution, the dynamic charging of heavy-duty trucks via overhead lines on highways (eHighway system) has been developed and tested in Germany between 2019 and 2024. In this study, we present results from the real-world deployment of the system and provide a comprehensive analysis of its operational performance. Our results demonstrate that both overhead line trucks and the associated infrastructure have significant potential for the dynamic electrification of road freight transport. Despite experiencing unplanned outages, particularly during the early stages of operation, system performance improved over time, showing the technological feasibility and scalability of the eHighway system.

title: Role of Electric Mobility Projects on Urban Transport Efficiency: A Case of Key E-mobility Interventions in Nyarugenge District, Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the role of Electric Mobility Projects on Urban Transport Efficiency in Nyarugenge District, Rwanda.Specifically, the study assessed the role of Electric Two-Wheeler Initiatives in Urban Transport Efficiency.The study ad
content: This study examined the role of Electric Mobility Projects on Urban Transport Efficiency in Nyarugenge District, Rwanda.Specifically, the study assessed the role of Electric Two-Wheeler Initiatives in Urban Transport Efficiency.The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design using a mixed-methods approach.The target population comprised 1,966 respondents, from which a sample size of 333 respondents was selected.Data were collected using structured questionnaires and semi-structured interviews and analyzed using SPSS.Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and simple linear regression analysis were used to examine the relationship and influence of Electric Two-Wheeler Initiatives on Urban Transport Efficiency.The findings showed that electric motorcycles were widely available, frequently used for daily commuting, reliable, and accessible, while also reducing commuter waiting time and travel time.Correlation analysis indicated a strong positive relationship between Electric Two-Wheeler Initiatives and Urban Transport Efficiency (r = .766,p < .001).Regression analysis further showed that Electric Two-Wheeler Initiatives significantly influenced Urban Transport Efficiency, explaining 60.2% of its variation.The study concluded that Electric Two-Wheeler Initiatives play an important role in improving Urban Transport Efficiency.The study recommends increasing the availability and accessibility of electric motorcycles, strengthening their reliability and continuous operation, and supporting their wider adoption through appropriate policies and stakeholder interventions.

title: ARBOK-ZBGra: Replacing the Water in a Zinc-Bromine Battery with a Graphene-Like TEGA Electrolyte
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Zinc-bromine batteries pair two cheap materials and an electrolyte that does not burn, and grid-scale systems already exist, yet the chemistry has not become mass-market. Recent reviews trace the limits to the aqueous electrolyte: bromine c
content: Zinc-bromine batteries pair two cheap materials and an electrolyte that does not burn, and grid-scale systems already exist, yet the chemistry has not become mass-market. Recent reviews trace the limits to the aqueous electrolyte: bromine crosses from the cathode to the zinc anode, corrodes it and causes self-discharge; zinc grows dendrites that can puncture the separator; complexing agents are needed to hold bromine in a polybromide phase; energy density is about 70 Wh/kg, below 20% of the theoretical value; and the power per electrode area is low. We describe ARBOK-ZBGra, a concept in which the aqueous electrolyte with additives is replaced by thermally expanded graphite ARBOK (TEGA), a graphene-like carbon material with a specific surface of 2,400 m2/g. The porous framework is expected to hold bromine in its pores next to the electrode and to conduct the charge, so that zinc and bromine stay while water and complexing agents leave. World bromine output is about 430,000 t per year at about 3 USD/kg, almost 25 times cheaper than iodine, and bromine can be recovered from oil and gas produced water in the same pass as iodine by the ARBOK-Iodine module. The concept is at the stage of design: no ZBGra cell has been measured.

title: Drivers of household food insecurity in Brazilian Amazonian riverine communities
summary: Abstract The Amazon Basin faces mounting socio-environmental pressures that threaten both ecological integrity and food security. In this study, we examine socio-environmental, economic and cultural factors that may drive household food ins
content: Abstract The Amazon Basin faces mounting socio-environmental pressures that threaten both ecological integrity and food security. In this study, we examine socio-environmental, economic and cultural factors that may drive household food insecurity among ribeirinho (riverine) communities in the middle Juruá region of the Brazilian Amazon. We conducted 563 surveys with 348 women across 33 communities near the end of low-water (2023) and high-water (2024) seasons, assessing food insecurity using the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale, and analysing socio-demographic and income-related predictors. Our findings reveal that food insecurity is widespread and seasonally variable: 80% of households reported moderate or severe food insecurity during the low-water season, decreasing slightly to 74% in the high-water season. Significant predictors of food insecurity were low-water season, and absence of a cantina (small community store). This study highlights the mismatch between abundance and food access in Amazonian territories and underscores the importance of culturally appropriate, locally embedded strategies to promote food security. Our results demonstrate the importance of community-based initiatives and targeted public policies to promote dietary resilience and support food sovereignty in the face of environmental and community vulnerability.

title: Practical Time Series Forecasting: From Accurate Forecasts to High-Quality Decisions
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Accurate time series forecasting is the cornerstone of informed decision-making in domains ranging from energy systems and financial markets to climate science and infrastructure management. This thesis investigates how explicit modeling of
content: Accurate time series forecasting is the cornerstone of informed decision-making in domains ranging from energy systems and financial markets to climate science and infrastructure management. This thesis investigates how explicit modeling of temporal structure can improve the performance and practical value of time series driven systems. First, a decomposition-based univariate forecasting approach is proposed that separates a time series into interpretable components using multi-seasonal decomposition and forecasts each independently. The method achieves substantial improvements over recent state-of-the-art models, demonstrating that careful temporal structure extraction can be more effective than architectural complexity alone. Second, decomposition-derived representations are used for similarity analysis and relation discovery across time series, showing that temporal structure can expose meaningful cross-series relationships beyond univariate forecasting. Third, these ideas are extended to multivariate spatio-temporal forecasting, where component-specific latent dependency graphs are learned for trend, seasonal, and residual components, yielding consistent gains over strong transformer, linear, state-space, and foundation-model baselines. Finally, forecasting is integrated with downstream decision-making through a decision-aware framework for carbon-aware data center scheduling, where the forecasting and optimization modules are trained jointly to minimize carbon-emissions regret rather than prediction error alone. The central argument is that effective forecasting systems should do more than minimizing prediction error. They should identify meaningful temporal structure, exploit it to capture inter-variate dependencies, and align predictions with downstream operational objectives. Across the thesis, this perspective is developed through a sequence of studies on decomposition, similarity learning, graph-based forecasting architectures, and end-to-end decision-focused learning of a forecasting model.

title: Collaborative multidevice visual detection for violation monitoring in carbon emission trading markets
source: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering (AOPR)
summary: This paper presents an innovative method, the Multi-Device Collaborative Visual Detection (MDCVD) algorithm, aimed at addressing the challenge of monitoring violations in carbon emission trading markets within complex industrial environment
content: This paper presents an innovative method, the Multi-Device Collaborative Visual Detection (MDCVD) algorithm, aimed at addressing the challenge of monitoring violations in carbon emission trading markets within complex industrial environments. By combining multi-layer feature extraction, collaborative detection across devices, and lightweight model design, MDCVD achieves efficient real-time violation detection. We evaluated MDCVD on open datasets including VisDrone, UAVDT, and OpenStreetCam. The results show that MDCVD outperforms state-of-the-art detection algorithms in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and real-time performance. Specifically, the collaborative mechanism in MDCVD effectively reduces false positives and false negatives, enhancing detection robustness. This work contributes to providing an efficient monitoring solution suitable for large-scale carbon emission scenarios. Future work will focus on optimizing the collaborative mechanism and exploring the potential of applying the model to other industrial environments.

title: Where Digitalisation Supports Sustainability: Environmental Gains in the Agrifood Sector
summary: Abstract This paper investigates the role of digital technologies in enhancing environmental sustainability in the agricultural sector. Using microdata from the Italian Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) and counterfactual methods for pol
content: Abstract This paper investigates the role of digital technologies in enhancing environmental sustainability in the agricultural sector. Using microdata from the Italian Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) and counterfactual methods for policy evaluation, we find that digitalised farms exhibit lower GHG emissions. By contrast, we find no significant effects on water use. The potential impact on non-digitalised farms, had they been treated, is estimated to be even larger. The digitalisation of agricultural systems, therefore, holds significant potential for reducing emissions while promoting more effective, sustainable strategies. The paper offers novel and significant policy insights into promoting digitalisation to enhance environmental sustainability across the sector and to support economic actors in making more sustainable decisions.

title: From Leader to Laggard: Reflections on Food Provisioning at the University of Toronto during the COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: This paper investigates the significant shifts in food provisioning at the University of Toronto during COVID-19 and throughout subsequent years. The institutional response to the pandemic challenged, and in some cases, dismantled the funda
content: This paper investigates the significant shifts in food provisioning at the University of Toronto during COVID-19 and throughout subsequent years. The institutional response to the pandemic challenged, and in some cases, dismantled the fundamental undergirding of progressive food policies which have long been celebrated and promoted by university administrators. Campus dining halls are important: they directly influence the mental and physical health of millions of students each year throughout Canada, impart dietary practices which shape health outcomes in future, and generate significant environmental impacts. Changes to these dining halls have been executed through a hasty reordering and reorganization of the ideological, material, and spatial dimensions of food across campus. Data collection methods include ethnographic observations, documents accessed through FIPPA requests, digital media and university communications, internal and external reports, and meeting minutes. My findings contest the notion of ‘in-house’ food provisioning as a more progressive, sustainable, and ethical model. Further, they illustrate the potential for public institutions to implement foodservice models that increasingly converge with those of multinational corporations. These new dining hall spaces feature a growing encroachment of corporations into campus spaces and represent a shift in which students are remade into neoliberal consumers. Correspondingly, these changes appear to have negative outcomes on issues ranging from food security, employee precarity, affordability, sustainability, and nutrition. As a food activist and scholar directly impacted by these transitions, I reflect on multiple years of working in residence, discussing modes of resistance, contestations, and institutional responses throughout my tenure.

title: Remote sensing capabilities of detecting spatio-temporal dynamics in unregulated gold mining hotspots in Ecuador
summary: Degradation of the Amazon rainforest is increasing by expanding human activities, especially unregulated gold mining. These pressures have intensified over the past decade due to rising global gold prices and changes in political and regula
content: Degradation of the Amazon rainforest is increasing by expanding human activities, especially unregulated gold mining. These pressures have intensified over the past decade due to rising global gold prices and changes in political and regulatory-related developments affecting the mining sector. Given the sensitivity of the topic and the need for transparent and reproducible information, this study assesses the suitability of remote sensing datasets, including Sentinel-1 (S-1) Synthetic Aperture Radar data, PlanetScope (PS) optical imagery, as well as the Satellite Embedding Dataset V1 (SED), for detecting unregulated mining and investigating the spatio-temporal dynamics of mining expansion. Datasets are processed mainly in Google Earth Engine with dataset-specific methodologies applied. Supervised quantitative classification approaches were used for the SED and PS imagery, covering the period from 2017 to 2024. For S-1 data, a Sequential Change Detection (SCD) approach was implemented. The analysis focuses on three mining hotspots in eastern Ecuador, where unregulated activities have been reported. The results show a significant increase in the extent of mining and associated deforestation across all study areas, particularly during 2023 and 2024, with increase of extractivism ranging from 109 % to 1445 % across different AOIs compared to the initial year of the study, 2017. Comparison of classification results indicates that persistent cloud cover and temporal inconsistencies limit the effectiveness of optical PS data, whereas the SED dataset provides a reliable and efficient alternative for annual assessments with minimal preprocessing requirements. The SCD analysis revealed detailed expansion dynamics, demonstrating that mining typically initiates along major rivers and progressively expands toward tributaries and surrounding forest areas. This multi-method approach further enables cross-validation of results, which are consistent with independent reports documenting similar spatial patterns and trends. The severe environmental consequences of unregulated mining and threats to local communities emphasize the importance of systematic and transferable remote sensing-based monitoring frameworks to support environmental protection and enable timely, accessible reporting for environmental governance and decision-making.

title: Thermo-hydraulic optimization of deep geothermal systems: computational methods and classification
summary: Abstract Deep geothermal energy forms an important part of a sustainable energy portfolio, providing baseload power and heat. A significant global expansion of deep geothermal systems (DGSs) is projected for the coming decades, thereby incr
content: Abstract Deep geothermal energy forms an important part of a sustainable energy portfolio, providing baseload power and heat. A significant global expansion of deep geothermal systems (DGSs) is projected for the coming decades, thereby increasing use of local geothermal resources. This, together with a competitive energy market, creates an incentive to optimize DGSs with respect to large-scale design and operational control variables. In particular, simulation-based optimization can enhance both the sustainability and economic viability of geothermal projects. Key decisions include well placement, well spacing, flow rates, and reinjection temperatures, all of which interact through the coupled thermo-hydraulic behavior of the reservoir. This review provides an overview of thermo-hydraulic optimization methods for DGSs, with a focus on computational simulation-optimization pipelines. The reviewed literature is organized according to a newly proposed classification scheme; for each study, the underlying model, optimization methodology, and objective functions are reported. Finally, open challenges and research directions in the field are identified.

title: Host communities in corporate governance normative hierarchy: custodianship and surrogate responsibility for sustainable development in Africa
summary: This article develops a governance model that places African host communities at the centre of corporate decision-making by advancing custodianship and surrogate responsibility as normative foundations for ex ante protection. It begins by d
content: This article develops a governance model that places African host communities at the centre of corporate decision-making by advancing custodianship and surrogate responsibility as normative foundations for ex ante protection. It begins by demonstrating that existing corporate governance paradigms, shareholder primacy, enlightened shareholder value in its United Kingdom and Nigeria variants, and conventional corporate social responsibility offer little more than symbolic or discretionary recognition of communities, leaving them structurally unprotected despite being profoundly affected by corporate activity. Drawing on African communitarian philosophies and customary traditions, the article argues that the Western neoliberal emphasis on individualism, ownership and profit maximisation is misaligned with African sociocultural realities in which community constitutes a moral, political, and ontological anchor of social life. It shows that conceptions of community in Yorùbá, Igbo, and Hausa thought frame responsibility as relational, intergenerational and restorative, providing a culturally coherent basis for embedding community-centred obligations in corporate governance. Building on this foundation, the article redefines the role of directors and corporate actors as custodians and surrogate representatives of host communities, tasked with protecting communal welfare in the same way that existing governance frameworks protect shareholders, creditors, employees, and consumers. This approach introduces actionable institutional logics capable of bridging the gap between corporate purpose and stakeholder inclusion, transforming communities from discretionary beneficiaries into recognised constituents of corporate legitimacy. By proposing a framework that integrates custodianship and surrogate responsibility into directors’ duties, the article offers a pragmatic and contextually grounded pathway for aligning corporate governance with sustainable development in Africa.

title: TRANSIÇÃO ENERGÉTICA E DESENVOLVIMENTO SUSTENTÁVEL: TECNOLOGIAS RENOVÁVEIS E DESCARBONIZAÇÃO SEGUNDO AS REVISÕES DA LITERATURA RECENTE
summary: Este artigo examina o que as revisões recentes da literatura afirmam sobre transição energética, tecnologias renováveis e descarbonização em sua relação com o desenvolvimento sustentável. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa de revisões, de ab
content: Este artigo examina o que as revisões recentes da literatura afirmam sobre transição energética, tecnologias renováveis e descarbonização em sua relação com o desenvolvimento sustentável. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa de revisões, de abordagem qualitativa, que reuniu vinte sínteses publicadas entre 2024 e 2026: catorze revisões sistemáticas, uma revisão realista, uma revisão de escopo, uma revisão temática e três revisões de método narrativo ou não descrito. A análise foi organizada em cinco eixos: trajetórias e barreiras no Sul Global, Brasil e América Latina, integração à rede e armazenamento, hidrogênio verde, e bem-estar, objetivos de desenvolvimento sustentável e justiça. Os resultados indicam que barreiras institucionais, de financiamento e de planejamento pesam tanto quanto as tecnológicas, que nenhuma tecnologia isolada resolve os desafios de rede e que o hidrogênio verde só se sustenta em aplicações selecionadas. Os benefícios sociais das renováveis são reais, mas condicionais, e a participação de trabalhadores e comunidades segue pouco deliberativa. Conclui-se que a descarbonização depende de arranjos de política, financiamento e participação tanto quanto de engenharia, e que a evidência disponível é desigual entre regiões e tecnologias.

title: Managing safety, functionality, and sustainability of fire-protective clothing: balancing burn prevention, physiological burden, and lifecycle safety
summary: Workers in firefighting, emergency response, aviation, welding, metal processing, and petrochemical operations may be exposed to flame, radiant or convective heat, hot surfaces, molten materials, smoke, and chemical contaminants. Fire-prote
content: Workers in firefighting, emergency response, aviation, welding, metal processing, and petrochemical operations may be exposed to flame, radiant or convective heat, hot surfaces, molten materials, smoke, and chemical contaminants. Fire-protective clothing is needed when these hazards cannot be fully controlled at source. However, dense multilayer assemblies and chemical treatments can limit heat and moisture loss, increase cardiovascular and metabolic strain, restrict movement, and make cleaning and disposal more difficult. This critical narrative review focuses on structural firefighting and examines research on protective materials, garment engineering, occupational hygiene, ergonomics, thermophysiology, maintenance, and life-cycle management. Studies were selected purposively through a targeted literature update and synthesized across heterogeneous methods and endpoints. Flame resistance at the material level is only one determinant of protection in use. Outcomes also depend on the complete ensemble, wearer, task, environment, and service history. Added insulation can slow external heat transfer while limiting dissipation of metabolic heat; cleaning can remove contaminants but reduce mechanical, barrier, or heat-loss performance; and renewable or recycled content may have limited value if it shortens service life or creates additional chemical and recovery problems. The review proposes a two-stage evaluation approach: first, apply minimum safety requirements that cannot be offset by benefits in other domains; second, compare compliant systems in terms of physiological load, mobility, chemical safety, durability, maintainability, cost, and environmental effects. The synthesis informs condition-based inspection, validated decontamination, representative wear trials, worker input, chemical disclosure, and product-level service records. The framework and proposed service-based sustainability measure require prospective validation; laboratory performance and acute wearer responses do not establish reduced injury or disease incidence.

title: Graph foundation models for intelligent monitoring and control of renewable energy networks
summary: The rapid expansion of renewable energy resources has transformed modern power systems into highly interconnected and dynamic networks that require intelligent monitoring and adaptive control. Existing graph-based approaches mainly learn st
content: The rapid expansion of renewable energy resources has transformed modern power systems into highly interconnected and dynamic networks that require intelligent monitoring and adaptive control. Existing graph-based approaches mainly learn structural relationships from historical data and do not explicitly respect the electrical laws of the network. This paper proposes a physics-informed graph foundation model (PI-GFM) coupled with a digital twin (DT) for monitoring and control of renewable energy networks. PI-GFM is an impedance-aware graph encoder that is pre-trained in a self-supervised manner on pooled heterogeneous network data and then adapted through task heads for fault classification, bus-voltage estimation and one-hour-ahead DT forecasting. Electrical knowledge enters as soft penalties on nodal active and reactive power balance and on the linearised (LinDistFlow) branch voltage drop; the full nonlinear AC power flow is not enforced, and this scope is stated explicitly. The DT synchronises a latent network state over a four-hour window through a learned fusion, under explicitly defined operating limits, and its voltage estimates drive a reactive-power support controller. The framework is evaluated on a fully specified simulation of the IEEE 33-bus feeder with photovoltaic, wind and battery resources, solved with AC power flow and subjected to inverter faults, high-impedance line faults, voltage-instability events and reconfigurations, using chronological splits, 5 random seeds and DNN, LSTM, GCN, GAT and GraphSAGE baselines. On the unseen test season, PI-GFM attains a bus-voltage MAE of 3.31 × 10 −3 p.u., 17% lower than the best baseline (3.96 × 10 −3 p.u.), and a DT synchronisation accuracy of 84.9% of bus-hours within 0.005 p.u. (best baseline 75.9%). Its four-class accuracy is 96.39% (best baseline 97.12%), with a fault-detection false-alarm rate of 1.29%. Used as controller input, it keeps all buses within 0.95–1.05 p.u. in 88.2% of test hours, against 85.8% without control and 96.9% with perfect state knowledge. The ablation shows that both the physics terms and the DT reduce the estimation error, and pre-training improves low-label performance. The results are obtained on simulated data, on one feeder family, on a single CPU platform.

title: Fertilizer Subsidy Regulatory Coherence, Institutional Capacity, and Sustainable Agricultural Performance in Indonesia
summary: Indonesia’s fertilizer subsidy governance reforms introduced through a series of regulations enacted in 2025–2026 have strengthened certainty in procurement, distribution, raw material availability, subsidy payments, and production continui
content: Indonesia’s fertilizer subsidy governance reforms introduced through a series of regulations enacted in 2025–2026 have strengthened certainty in procurement, distribution, raw material availability, subsidy payments, and production continuity. However, previous studies have examined economic impacts, distribution, institutional capacity, and sustainability separately, leaving the ability of the latest regulatory architecture to produce sustainable agricultural performance insufficiently understood. This study is essential to prevent subsidy performance from being assessed solely through budget absorption, transactions, and distribution volumes. It aims to analyze regulatory evolution and coherence, contributions to institutional capacity, alignment with economic, social, and environmental dimensions, and a results-based regulatory improvement framework. The study employs an integrative qualitative approach combining content analysis of five principal regulations with a systematic literature review guided by PRISMA 2020. The findings show that the regulations have strengthened legal certainty, regulatory capacity, and supply resilience. Nevertheless, fragmented coordination, unequal regional capacity, unintegrated data, digital exclusion, and inadequate indicators of nutrient-use efficiency and soil health persist. The study recommends regulatory consolidation, a dynamic integrated data system, crop-calendar-based coordination, integration of subsidies with agricultural extension and soil management, and evaluation based on an input–process–output–outcome–impact framework

title: Structural Strengthening and Reinforcement Using Grid Composites
summary: This book provides a comprehensive introduction to the theoretical foundations, key technologies, and engineering applications of fiber‑reinforced polymer (FRP) grids for strengthening and reinforcing concrete structures. Currently, many ex
content: This book provides a comprehensive introduction to the theoretical foundations, key technologies, and engineering applications of fiber‑reinforced polymer (FRP) grids for strengthening and reinforcing concrete structures. Currently, many existing reinforced concrete structures have experienced performance deterioration, creating an urgent need for effective strengthening solutions. Owing to their high strength‑to‑weight ratio, excellent durability, and ease of construction, FRP grids have emerged as a promising material for structural strengthening. Drawing upon experimental investigations, theoretical analyses, and numerical simulations, this book systematically presents the interfacial behavior, flexural performance, shear performance, seismic performance, and design methods of FRP grid‑strengthened structures. In addition, it introduces the use of FRP grids as reinforcing materials in new concrete structures. Covering applications in bridges, tunnels, buildings, and underwater constructions, this book is a valuable resource for engineers, researchers, and graduate students in civil, structural, and materials engineering, as well as professionals involved in structural design, manufacturing, and rehabilitation. Key Features • Provides a detailed exploration of FRP grids, including constituent materials, manufacturing processes, mechanical properties, and structural behavior. • Features comprehensive discussions on bond characteristics, debonding mechanisms, and stress transfer at the grid–concrete interface, supported by experimental, analytical, and numerical investigations to enhance the understanding of failure modes and interfacial behavior. • Covers a wide range of applications, including flexural, shear, and seismic strengthening, spalling resistance, and the use of FRP grids as reinforcement for new structures, offering practical solutions for both retrofitting and new construction projects.

title: In vitro reduction of mineral oil hydrocarbons by Lacticaseibacillus casei DSM 20011
summary: Mineral oil hydrocarbons (MOH) are food contaminants of increasing concern due to their widespread occurrence in food and potential health risks. Although various physicochemical and biological strategies have been investigated to reduce ch
content: Mineral oil hydrocarbons (MOH) are food contaminants of increasing concern due to their widespread occurrence in food and potential health risks. Although various physicochemical and biological strategies have been investigated to reduce chemical contaminants in food, the ability of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to remove MOH has not previously been explored. The present study aimed to evaluate the in vitro removal of MOH by Lacticaseibacillus casei DSM 20011 under incubation 0for 4 h with shaking at 100 rpm. Following the screening of different LAB strains, L. casei DSM 20011 was selected for in vitro evaluation of MOH removal using a representative mineral oil mixture, followed by the determination of MOH by on-line LC GC-FID. L. casei DSM 20011 reduced MOH concentrations by up to approximately 80% (p < 0.05), with comparable reductions observed for the MOSH and MOAH fractions and no clear evidence of preferential removal of either fraction. Cell wall adsorption has been proposed as a mechanism contributing to PAH removal by LAB. Given the structural similarity between PAH and the MOAH fraction of MOH, together with the lack of recognized hydrocarbon-degrading enzymes in LAB, adsorption to the bacterial cell wall may also explain the observed MOH removal, although this hypothesis requires experimental confirmation. These findings identify the food-derived L. casei DSM 20011 as a promising candidate for the biological reduction of MOH contamination and provide a foundation for future studies investigating the mechanisms underlying MOH removal and validating its effectiveness in complex food matrices.

title: Utilizing UV-Sensitive Camera for UV-Reflectance-Imaging-Based Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient Content Prediction
