summary: This study presents a proof-of-concept monochrome camera system featuring a UV-sensitive sensor, enabling direct UV detection for non-destructive quantification of active pharmaceutical ingredient content in two-component canrenone-microcry
content: This study presents a proof-of-concept monochrome camera system featuring a UV-sensitive sensor, enabling direct UV detection for non-destructive quantification of active pharmaceutical ingredient content in two-component canrenone-microcrystalline cellulose tablets. Differences in UV absorption between API and excipient resulted in distinct grayscale intensity distributions on the tablet surface, enabling active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) quantification. Tablets were prepared with API contents ranging from 0 to 6 w/w% and imaged in-line on a conveyor belt under 365 nm UV illumination. Acquired images were pre-processed through background elimination, and illumination correction, then grayscale intensity histograms were extracted. These histograms served as inputs for partial least squares regression, producing a linear correlation between predicted and nominal API content, with a root mean square error of calibration 0.20 w/w%, root mean square error of cross-validation 0.24 w/w%, root mean square error of prediction 0.27 w/w%. The obtained relative prediction error was 6.78% at a target of 4 w/w%. The approach demonstrates rapid, non-destructive assessment of API content without sample preparation. By combining a cost-effective direct UV-imaging method with multivariate analysis, the system shows potential for real-time monitoring of API content in continuous tablet manufacturing.

title: Eco-Friendly Mineral Scale Inhibitors for Geothermal Systems: Recent Advances in Green Chemistry and Sustainable Energy Production
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Geothermal energy is a low-carbon, baseload renewable resource, yet its reliability and economics are repeatedly undermined by mineral scaling.As hot brines are produced, cooled, and re-injected, changes in temperature, pressure, pH, and di
content: Geothermal energy is a low-carbon, baseload renewable resource, yet its reliability and economics are repeatedly undermined by mineral scaling.As hot brines are produced, cooled, and re-injected, changes in temperature, pressure, pH, and dissolved gas content push the fluid beyond the solubility limits of calcium carbonate, amorphous silica, sulfates, and metal sulfides.The resulting deposits restrict flow in wells, plug heat exchangers, reduce injectivity, and force costly shutdowns.For decades, scale control relied on phosphonates, polyacrylates, and acidification, chemicals that raise concerns about persistence, eutrophication, and toxicity toward aquatic life.This review summarizes the main scale types encountered in geothermal systems, explains the mechanisms by which inhibitors act, and critically examines recent progress in eco-friendly alternatives, including polyaspartic acid, polyepoxysuccinic acid, carboxymethyl inulin, plant-derived polysaccharides and extracts, and biodegradable silica antiscalants.Performance data, environmental profiles, and testing methodologies are compared, and key obstacles are identified: high temperature stability, performance in high-salinity brines, cost, and the lack of standardized field validation.Finally, a research outlook is proposed that links green chemistry design principles with digital monitoring and circular resource recovery, so that geothermal plants can operate with minimal chemical footprints.

title: Dry anaerobic digestion of organic waste: operational determinants, reactor configurations, economics and process control
source: Journal of Energy and Environmental Sustainability
summary: Dry anaerobic digestion is a high-solids bioconversion route for stabilizing organic wastes while recovering biogas and nutrient-rich digestate. This mini-review synthesizes operational factors that determine the performance of dry anaerobi
content: Dry anaerobic digestion is a high-solids bioconversion route for stabilizing organic wastes while recovering biogas and nutrient-rich digestate. This mini-review synthesizes operational factors that determine the performance of dry anaerobic digestion of municipal, agricultural and industrial organic wastes, with emphasis on inoculum management, substrate composition, total solids content, co-digestion, reactor configuration, process instability and economics. Dry systems can reduce water demand, reactor volume and digestate-handling burdens relative to wet digestion, but they are more sensitive to mass-transfer limitations, heterogeneous feedstocks, localized acidification and ammonia or hydrogen sulfide accumulation. The literature indicates that stable operation requires active and acclimatized inoculum, appropriate substrate pre-processing, balanced carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, controlled moisture and total solids, and reactor designs that maintain effective contact between microorganisms and substrate. Co-digestion, digestate recirculation, micro-nutrient supplementation and careful start-up can improve process robustness, but these strategies must be optimized to avoid volatile fatty acid accumulation or nutrient depletion. Economic feasibility is strongly site-specific and depends on plant scale, retention time, feedstock logistics, energy use, digestate outlets, biogas valorization pathway and policy incentives.

title: Bio-Based Materials for a Circular Economy: A Review of Advances, Barriers, and Pathways to Scalable Adoption
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: The shift from a linear "take-make-dispose" industrial model toward a circular economy has made bio-based materials a central focus of sustainability research and policy.This paper presents a narrative literature review of recent advances i

title: Forecasting Regional Economic Effects of the Bien Hoa–Vung Tau Expressway
source: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
summary: Abstract: The Bien Hoa to Vung Tau Expressway is a 53-kilometre route in southern Vietnam connecting the industrial base of Dong Nai to the deep-water port area of Vung Tau, with an estimated investment of 17.8 trillion VND. Economic foreca
content: Abstract: The Bien Hoa to Vung Tau Expressway is a 53-kilometre route in southern Vietnam connecting the industrial base of Dong Nai to the deep-water port area of Vung Tau, with an estimated investment of 17.8 trillion VND. Economic forecasts for the project were prepared before 2018, and the regional context has changed substantially since then. This study re-assesses the expected economic effects using current data and an integrated analytical framework with five components: accessibility analysis based on a gravity potential model, regional interaction modelling incorporating observed traffic counts on National Highway 51, industrial development potential assessment, economic corridor centrality analysis, and GRDP growth forecasting under a range of agglomeration elasticities. The analysis covers the four principal localities on the corridor, Bien Hoa, Long Thanh, Phu My and Vung Tau, together with Ho Chi Minh City, Phu My Port and Long Thanh Airport as connecting nodes, and uses 2024 as the base year. The set of nodes constitutes the complete corridor rather than a sample drawn from it. Three findings emerge. First, the expressway moves the primary node of the corridor northward: Bien Hoa overtakes Phu My in economic centrality, rising 104 per cent against 62 per cent. Second, industrial development potential rises most in Long Thanh, which combines a 5,033-hectare industrial land reserve with the largest accessibility gain. Third, growth distributes across the corridor rather than concentrating in one centre, with Long Thanh recording the largest percentage gain from the smallest economic base. Estimated GRDP growth ranges from 1.2 per cent under a conservative elasticity of 0.03 to 26.8 per cent under a strong elasticity of 0.4. For sustainable development the results point in two directions. Journey distances on the corridor fall 22.8 per cent in aggregate, and diverting through traffic from National Highway 51 relieves congestion that currently generates avoidable emissions. Freight movement to the region’s principal port becomes shorter and more predictable. Against this, the project strengthens pressure to convert agricultural land, will generate induced traffic, and delivers benefits unevenly within each locality. Infrastructure of this scale shapes conditions for sustainable outcomes without securing them; the accompanying land use policy determines which outcome follows. Keywords: Accessibility analysis, Economic corridor, Regional economic impact, Sustainable development

title: The Brown Economy: Material use, emissions, and the role of agriculture
summary: This study examines the “brown economy” of Bulgaria, understood as patterns of economic activity associated with intensive resource use, environmental degradation, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Using economy-wide material flow account
content: This study examines the “brown economy” of Bulgaria, understood as patterns of economic activity associated with intensive resource use, environmental degradation, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Using economy-wide material flow accounts and emissions data, the analysis assesses the scale, structure, and evolution of material use and environmental pressures, situating Bulgaria in a comparative European Union context. Particular attention is paid to biomass extraction and agricultural activities, given their importance for material flows, land use, and non-CO₂ emissions. The results show that Bulgaria remains characterised by high reliance on domestic material extraction, limited circularity, and a material footprint above the EU average. Despite notable long-term reductions in GHG emissions, progress has been uneven across sectors, with persistent challenges in energy production, transport, and agriculture. Agricultural activities contribute structurally to emissions through livestock production, agricultural soils, and fertiliser use, while low circularity reflects limited reintegration of organic waste and residues into production cycles. The findings highlight that further progress in transitioning towards a greener economic model requires not only continued decarbonisation of energy and transport, but also targeted measures addressing material use, waste management, and emissions in agriculture. Strengthening circular practices and improving resource efficiency across sectors are essential for reducing the environmental footprint of the Bulgarian economy.

title: Effect of Cycling Protocol on the Stress and Mechanical Degradation of Hard Carbon Electrodes
summary: Abstract Maximum stress experienced by an electrode during cycling is shown to cause mechanical degradation and capacity fade, but the effect of potential window and stress range (Δσ) on cycling behavior was not investigated. Here, stresses
content: Abstract Maximum stress experienced by an electrode during cycling is shown to cause mechanical degradation and capacity fade, but the effect of potential window and stress range (Δσ) on cycling behavior was not investigated. Here, stresses generated in hard carbon (HC)-based porous composite electrodes were measured in situ while cycling under three different potential windows: (i) full window (2-0.0005 V vs Na/Na+), (ii) sloping (2-0.1 V vs Na/Na+), and plateau (0.1-0.0005 V vs Na/Na+) regions and three different C-rates. The stress range (Δσ), capacity, and mechanical hysteresis during sloping region were nearly rate-independent, while they showed significant rate dependence in the plateau region, suggesting two different ion-storage mechanisms. Both the stress range and mechanical hysteresis (indicator of irreversible deformation) increased at lower current densities during the plateau region, indicating higher irreversible mechanical work and degradation. During extended cycling, capacity continued to decrease even after the maximum stress saturated, indicating that Δσ and hysteresis are important to explain electrode degradation. Based on these observations, an optimized cycling protocol was used which reduced stress range and mechanical hysteresis while increasing specific capacity at faster rate, demonstrating the importance of coupled electro-chemomechanical responses for optimizing cycling protocols to improve capacity utilization and mechanical durability.

title: A coupled experimental-modeling framework for evaluating the electrochemical performance of lithium-ion battery electrodes remanufactured with recycled LiFePO 4
summary: The rapid growth of electric vehicle and electronics markets is generating a rising volume of endof-life batteries, making recycling essential to recover critical materials and reduce environmental impact. The electrochemical performance of
content: The rapid growth of electric vehicle and electronics markets is generating a rising volume of endof-life batteries, making recycling essential to recover critical materials and reduce environmental impact. The electrochemical performance of future recycled batteries needs to be optimized by identifying the best remanufacturing parameters. Here, we propose a coupled experimental and computational framework that moves towards this objective by using the recycling of LiFePO 4 (LFP) as a proof-of-concept. We first characterized a spent LFP material, subsequently we used direct recycling to obtain a regenerated active material to remanufacture recycled LFP electrodes. We also fabricated a pristine LFP electrode reference, and blended electrode (50:50 recycled-to-pristine ratio). The three samples were characterized by various experimental techniques, including electrochemical testing, microscopy, granulometry, etc. The experimental determinations were then used as inputs to generate representative 3D electrode microstructures and parameterize a 3D-resolved electrochemical model for each sample. The models managed to simulate the galvanostatic discharge curve of the three electrode samples, capturing the experimental trends with high accuracy at C/50 and C/20 C-rates. Furthermore, we analyzed the microstructural bottlenecks and benchmarked the three LFP electrode types. Our framework introduces a chemistry-agnostic approach to optimize blend ratios in blend electrodes containing recycled materials.

title: Study of reinforcement in gypsum and cement mortar matrices using polymer fibers from recycling processes
summary: Over the past few decades many studies have explored reinforcing gypsum or cement mortar matrices with various fibers. This study focuses on using recycled polymer fibers to improve the ductility, tensile strength, and flexural strength of
content: Over the past few decades many studies have explored reinforcing gypsum or cement mortar matrices with various fibers. This study focuses on using recycled polymer fibers to improve the ductility, tensile strength, and flexural strength of these materials, promoting the reuse of plastic waste. It also analyzes the feasibility of using recycled plastic flakes or fibers as reinforcement. The research analyzes the interface between these recycled polymers and the gypsum/cement matrices. To find the optimal conditions for mechanical reinforcement, different polymer types, geometries, and embedding depths are tested. Pull-out tests on specimens with embedded fibers are conducted and monitored with a digital image correlation (DIC) system. This study shows that fiber length and geometry are key factors to ensure good fibre reinforcement, with very short lengths leading to negligible reinforcement and with wavy shapes allowing better fibre performance.

title: From Tin Crisis to Thorium Transition: Energy Justice, Youth Acceptance, and Participation in Bangka Belitung’s Nuclear Future
summary: Bangka Belitung, Indonesia’s tin heartland, entered a compound crisis in 2024: provincial economic growth slowed to 0.77% after a crackdown on corruption in the tin trade, while about 167,000 hectares of land remain critically degraded. In
content: Bangka Belitung, Indonesia’s tin heartland, entered a compound crisis in 2024: provincial economic growth slowed to 0.77% after a crackdown on corruption in the tin trade, while about 167,000 hectares of land remain critically degraded. In 2025 the province also received Indonesia’s first regulatory approval for a nuclear power project, a site-evaluation program for a 500-megawatt thorium molten salt reactor on Kelasa Island. This study asks under what conditions youth acceptance of the project would be just and how acceptance could become participation in its governance. Using a qualitative explanatory case study that combines an integrative literature review with document analysis of regulatory, statistical, industry, and media sources, it evaluates four theoretical propositions through pattern matching. The evidence shows that the regulator has demonstrated technical rigor but procedural inclusion remains thin; that local support is driven mainly by expected economic benefits under conditions of crisis; that benefit-sharing arrangements remain undefined; and that the only site-specific acceptance survey predates the crisis and was co-authored by developer staff. The youth research team therefore designed a Youth Energy Justice Lab linking project benefits to ex-mining land restoration and youth-led monitoring.

title: Golden economy and agriculture – Renewable energy or digitalisation and high-tech innovation
summary: Sustainable and resilient agricultural systems play a key role in global growth and development. In the context of globalisation and Industry 5.0, the concept of "golden economy" is viewed from two perspectives. On the one hand, it is linke
content: Sustainable and resilient agricultural systems play a key role in global growth and development. In the context of globalisation and Industry 5.0, the concept of "golden economy" is viewed from two perspectives. On the one hand, it is linked to the development of the use of renewable sources, and on the other, it is associated with digitalisation, innovation, and artificial intelligence. This study aims to analyse how the elements of the golden economy, namely renewable energy, digitalisation, and innovation, impact agriculture and to identify the challenges facing the sector. The connections between the individual elements have been deduced. An analysis of the cost-effectiveness of golden economy and its impact on agriculture has been made. The results obtained show that new and emerging technologies and their applications in the agricultural sector have the potential to impact multiple aspects of farming, including new business models and product designs, competition, operational efficiency and accessibility.

title: Adsorption of dyes using Al2O3-bio-based nanosorbent: kinetic and thermodynamic studies
source: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: The continuous discharge of wastewater containing synthetic dyes presents serious environmental and health challenges due to its toxicity, chemical stability, and difficulty in degradation. This calls for concern and therefore, necessitatin
content: The continuous discharge of wastewater containing synthetic dyes presents serious environmental and health challenges due to its toxicity, chemical stability, and difficulty in degradation. This calls for concern and therefore, necessitating the development of a sustainable and efficient biosorbent. This study prepared a sustainable nanoadsorbent from snail shell wastes impregnated with aluminum chloride to produce a biomass-alumina (Al 2 O 3 –CaO) nanosorbent for removing methylene blue (MB) and thymol blue (TB) from wastewater. The prepared material was characterized using FTIR, XRD, SEM, EDX, and pH pzc analysis, followed by batch adsorption studies. The adsorption data were fitted to the Freundlich, Sips, and Temkin isotherms and to pseudo-first- and second-order kinetic models. The FTIR analysis shows Me–O stretches at 550 and 838 cm −1 . XRD confirmed its crystalline structure with an average particle size of 24.73 ± 2.90 nm. SEM micrographs showed uniformly dispersed spherical nanostructures, while EDX analysis confirmed the presence of Al, Ca, and O, confirming composite formation, with a pH pzc value of 6.35. The adsorption equilibrium data were best fitted by the Freundlich model, with R 2 values of 0.98 and 0.94 for MB and TB, with corresponding K F values of 366.46 and 208.84 mg/g, respectively. The kinetic results followed the pseudo-first-order model. Thermodynamic analysis recorded positive ΔS° value and ΔG° < 0, for both dyes, while ΔH° = + 68.24 and − 2.98 kJ mol⁻ 1 for MB and TB, respectively. Al 2 O 3 -CaO showed remarkable stability and reusability during four consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. This study shows the nanosorbent as a probable material for the remediation dye-laden wastewater.

title: Green Research, Energy, and Environmental Networking: A Critical Review of Trends and Opportunities
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology

title: Economic Literacy: Measurement, Expectations, and Policy Views
summary: How important is economic literacy – the understanding of basic economic concepts – for the formation of economic expectations and policy views? We design, implement, and psychometrically validate a survey module to measure economic literac
content: How important is economic literacy – the understanding of basic economic concepts – for the formation of economic expectations and policy views? We design, implement, and psychometrically validate a survey module to measure economic literacy in a representative adult population. Economic literacy is associated with education and intelligence but captures a distinct skill. While unrelated to ideological orientation, individuals with higher economic literacy (1) hold better-anchored economic expectations, (2) are more responsive to experimentally provided information on policy trade-offs, and (3) show a closer alignment between preferences, policy views, and party support. The results are consistent with economic literacy enabling voters to better process information and form policy views more consistent with their underlying preferences.

title: OECD metropolitan scan of Milan, Italy
summary: Twenty years after the 2006 OECD Territorial Review, Milan has strengthened its position as Italy's leading metropolitan economy and a major centre for investment and innovation. The transition from the Province of Milan to the Metropolitan
content: Twenty years after the 2006 OECD Territorial Review, Milan has strengthened its position as Italy's leading metropolitan economy and a major centre for investment and innovation. The transition from the Province of Milan to the Metropolitan City in 2015 created a new institutional framework for planning development at the metropolitan scale. Yet Milan's functional economy extends well beyond its administrative boundaries, while the benefits and pressures associated with its strong performance remain unevenly distributed across the metropolitan territory. This OECD scan assesses the metropolitan area's performance, strengths and pressures, and examines how Milan can sustain its international competitiveness while fostering more inclusive and territorially balanced development. It highlights growing pressures related to housing affordability, accessibility, demographic ageing, labour shortages and skills mismatches, alongside significant assets in innovation, investment and talent attraction. Many of these opportunities and challenges transcend municipal and provincial boundaries, underscoring the need for effective metropolitan co-ordination. The Scan identifies three strategic priorities: promoting more balanced metropolitan competitiveness by better connecting housing, transport, and innovation policies; reinforcing human capital and skills; and strengthening metropolitan governance and implementation. Adopting a more integrated, territorially balanced and implementation-oriented governance approach, could help Milan strengthen its international competitiveness while advancing social cohesion, resilience and sustainable long-term growth.

title: A data envelopment analysis alkalmazásának bibliometriai elemzése a szálláshely-szolgáltató szektorban
summary: A vállalkozásoknak a működésük során az erőforrásaikat hatékonyan kell felhasználniuk a pénzügyi eredményességük és a versenyképességük fenntartásához. Alábbi kutatásunk bibliometriai elemzéssel vizsgálja a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) a
content: A vállalkozásoknak a működésük során az erőforrásaikat hatékonyan kell felhasználniuk a pénzügyi eredményességük és a versenyképességük fenntartásához. Alábbi kutatásunk bibliometriai elemzéssel vizsgálja a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) alkalmazását a szálláshely-szolgáltató szektorban. A vizsgálat célja publikációs trendek, kutatási fókuszterületek, együttműködési hálózatok feltárása, a legaktívabb szerzők azonosítása, a DEA módszer intellektuális „magjának” meghatározása. A publikációk kiválasztása a PRISMA 2020 irányelveinek megfelelő, átlátható szűrési és dokumentálási folyamat szerint történt. Az elemzés során 204 angol nyelvű tanulmányt vizsgáltunk az 1996-2025 év időszakból, amelyek a Web of Science (WoS) adatbázisból kerültek kiválasztásra. Az elemzéshez és vizualizálásához a Bibliometrix R csomag webes felületét a Biblioshinyt, valamint VOSviewer szoftvereket használtuk. Az eredmények alapján megállapításra került, hogy a szálláshely-szolgáltató szektorban széles körben alkalmazzák a DEA módszert - a klasszikus DEA-tól a fejlettebb, Hybrid DEA-ig - a hatékonyság, Benchmarking elemzésére. A publikációkban a klasszikus (CCR/BCC)-modellek a leggyakoribbak (75,8%), a további megközelítések SBM (6,8%), Network/dinamikus (5,8%), speciális DEA (10,0%). Orientáció szerint az inputorientált (33,7%) és outputorientált (26,8%) megoldások mellett jelentős az orientáció nélküli modellek aránya (37,9%). A kutatások fő fókuszterületei az ázsiai térségek, az országok közül kiemelkedik Taiwan, Kína, az európai országok közül pedig Spanyolország, Olaszország. A társhivatkozási (co-citation) elemzés alapján 4 tudományos irány került azonosításra az irodalomban: (1) szállodai hatékonyság és versenyképesség, (2) menedzsment- és operatív hatékonyság Frontier-alapú elemzése, (3) strukturális és technológiai különbségeket kezelő Frontier-modellek, (4) Benchmarking-orientált hatékonysági modellek. A szerzői kulcsszavak együttes előfordulásának (co-occurence) elemzése során tíz tematikus klasztert azonosítottunk, amelyek a kutatások fő irányát mutatják.

title: Coffee biotechnology from yeast-assisted fermentation to spent coffee grounds valorization
summary: Coffee fermentation plays a central role in determining coffee quality through the generation of flavor-related metabolites, whereas spent coffee grounds (SCG), the major byproduct of coffee consumption, have emerged as promising renewable
content: Coffee fermentation plays a central role in determining coffee quality through the generation of flavor-related metabolites, whereas spent coffee grounds (SCG), the major byproduct of coffee consumption, have emerged as promising renewable feedstocks for sustainable biorefineries. Although controlled coffee fermentation and SCG valorization have attracted increasing attention, these fields have largely evolved independently. This review presents an integrated perspective on coffee biomass utilization by connecting flavor-oriented yeast-assisted coffee fermentation with the post-consumption biological valorization of spent coffee grounds. Particular emphasis is placed on the biochemical mechanisms by which yeasts degrade coffee mucilage and convert mucilage-derived substrates into flavor-related compounds and how fermentation-induced changes may influence coffee aroma after roasting. This mechanistic understanding provides a scientific foundation for the rational development of starter cultures capable of generating targeted sensory profiles tailored to consumer preferences. In addition, recent advances in the microbial and enzymatic valorization of SCG are summarized, including pretreatment-based strategies and the direct biological conversion of untreated SCG. Although these processes occur at distinct stages, shared yeast metabolic pathways provide a biochemical foundation for developing complementary biotechnological applications. By extending coffee biotechnology across the production and consumption chain, this review highlights strategies for increasing coffee value while maximizing the utilization of coffee-derived biomass.

title: Nutrient profiles govern organic-mineral fertilizer interactions on maize yield in Kenya
summary: Abstract Co-applying mineral and organic nutrient inputs is widely recommended to enhance maize yields and soil fertility in sub-Saharan Africa. However, long-term on-farm evaluations that assess how input combinations, baseline soil fertil
content: Abstract Co-applying mineral and organic nutrient inputs is widely recommended to enhance maize yields and soil fertility in sub-Saharan Africa. However, long-term on-farm evaluations that assess how input combinations, baseline soil fertility, and climatic conditions affect yield trajectories remain scarce. Over 10 seasons (5 years), this study investigated maize yield and agronomic nitrogen- and phosphorus use efficiencies (AEN; AEP) across 20 farms in two Kenyan counties (Vihiga and Siaya, ~ 48% and 64% clay content, respectively), comparing high- and low-fertility fields. Treatments evaluated local versus improved maize varieties (IR maize) and the addition of multi-component fertilizer (MCF), farmyard manure, and calcium-ammonium-nitrate (CAN) top-dressing in an additive split-plot design (only to IR maize). While combining all three inputs (MCF, manure, and CAN) achieved the highest overall yields, no treatment could significantly increase yields over time, highlighting the challenge of achieving positive temporal trends in continuous maize monoculture at realistic input rates. A significant negative interaction between MCF and manure negated ~ 70% of manure’s positive effect, potentially due to overlapping nutrient profiles. MCF significantly outperformed manure, showing higher yields and AEN values (39–43 kg yield kg − 1 N); AEP was highest under manure combined with CAN (52–62 kg yield kg − 1 P). CAN provided a modest yield benefit (+ 141 kg ha − 1 season − 1 ), showing no negative interactions with MCF or manure. Our findings suggest that effective plant nutrition in smallholder systems should focus on complementing nutrient profiles and consider both current yield and yield trajectories.

title: Linking Dilution, Evaporation Energy, and Operating Economics in Lithium Recovery from LFP Batteries
summary: The rapid growth in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery demand is expected to generate increasing amounts of end-of-life material, while recycling remains economically challenging due to low intrinsic material value and high processing cos
content: The rapid growth in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery demand is expected to generate increasing amounts of end-of-life material, while recycling remains economically challenging due to low intrinsic material value and high processing costs. This study evaluates lithium recovery from LFP black mass using an integrated process and operating-economic framework combining experimentally calibrated mass balances, first-principles evaporation-energy modelling, thermodynamic Li 2 CO 3 precipitation, and uncertainty analysis. Approximately 88% solvent evaporation was required to reach a precipitation-relevant lithium concentration of 28 g L −1 , corresponding to 62.2 kWh kg −1 Li 2 CO 3 using conventional single-effect evaporation without heat recovery. An illustrative mechanical vapor recompression (MVR)-inspired heat-recovery scenario reduced this requirement to 27.3 kWh kg −1 Li 2 CO 3 . Cumulative process losses resulted in an overall lithium recovery of approximately 58.4%. Sensitivity and Monte Carlo analyses identified Li 2 CO 3 and electricity prices as the dominant economic uncertainties under the single-effect reference, while heat recovery substantially reduced energy-related sensitivities. The need to concentrate dilute lithium-bearing solutions remained an inherent process constraint, but its economic penalty depended strongly on the evaporation-energy configuration. The fraction of the evaluated operating domain satisfying predefined yield and economic-risk criteria increased from approximately 0.8% under the single-effect reference to 30.9% under the heat-recovery scenario, shifting the active constraint toward precipitation yield. The results demonstrate the importance of integrating mass recovery, dilution, thermodynamics, and energy demand when evaluating the operating economics of LFP battery recycling.

title: Understanding Circular Economy Adoption in Agriculture: An Integrative and Configurational Perspective on Farm-Level Practices
summary: Circular Economy is increasingly promoted as a strategy to improve the sustainability of agricultural food systems, yet its implementation at the farm level remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how Circular Economy pra
content: Circular Economy is increasingly promoted as a strategy to improve the sustainability of agricultural food systems, yet its implementation at the farm level remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates how Circular Economy practices are adopted in agriculture, analysing whether and how regenerative practices aimed at restoring ecological functions are combined with Standard Circular Economy practices related to Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. Building on a multiple case study of 16 Italian fruit and vegetable farms, the analysis employs cross-case comparison to identify recurring bundles of circular practices, and the configurational Qualitative Comparative Analysis to unveil the conditions associated with the adoption of Regenerative practices in circular farms. The findings show that Circular Economy implementation is best understood as the outcome of bundles of interdependent practices rather than isolated actions. Three distinct recurring practice bundles are identified, i.e. Efficiency-oriented, Hybrid, and Systemic Bundles, reflecting different degrees of integration between standard circular economy practices and regenerative practices. Secondly, the configurational analysis associates regenerative practices adoption among standard circular practices adopters with a combination of institutional, internal, and market-related drivers. Exploratory second-order analyses highlight knowledge and coordination networks and price differentiation and quality segmentation as recurrent lower-order features within their respective models. Barrier configurations indicate that adoption can coexist with heterogeneous constraints. Overall, the study advances an integrative and configurational understanding of Circular Economy in agriculture, emphasizing the importance of practices combinations and contextual conditions in shaping farm-level adoption.

title: Real–world considerations on algae biochar
source: Journal of Energy and Environmental Sustainability
summary: Algae–derived biochar has gained interest because of its distinctive physicochemical characteristics, particularly its high porosity and substantial content of macro– and micronutrients. However, much of the published literature remains ove
content: Algae–derived biochar has gained interest because of its distinctive physicochemical characteristics, particularly its high porosity and substantial content of macro– and micronutrients. However, much of the published literature remains overly optimistic, often neglecting the economic realities of large–scale implementation. This review critically synthesizes research mainly from the past decade to evaluate the progress, challenges, and future prospects of algae–derived biochar. The principal achievement has been the translation of biological knowledge into increasingly efficient mass–cultivation systems, particularly those integrated with wastewater treatment. The major bottleneck remains algae harvesting, as even the latest technologies require substantial material and energy inputs, limiting economic viability. Emerging trends include the use of precipitation–based harvesting strategies to reduce biomass recovery costs and the subsequent thermochemical conversion of algal biomass into functionalized biochar products. Future progress will depend on prioritizing techno–economic feasibility, resource efficiency, and real–world scalability alongside improvements in biochar functionality and environmental performance.

title: Association of food consumption patterns with height growth of children and adolescents: A population-based observational study over four decades of food transitions in China
summary: BACKGROUND: Height is a key marker of early-life nutrition and health. China's four-decade food transition provides an opportunity to examine associations between food consumption and child/adolescent height. We aimed to identify food consu
content: BACKGROUND: Height is a key marker of early-life nutrition and health. China's four-decade food transition provides an opportunity to examine associations between food consumption and child/adolescent height. We aimed to identify food consumption patterns associated with greater height and favorable sustainability profiles and develop a score quantifying food-height associations. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted an observational study using height data from ~1.7 million Chinese students aged 7-18 years in the Chinese National Survey on Students' Constitution and Health (1985-2019) and provincial food consumption data from the National Bureau of Statistics (1985-2023). Temporal trends were examined across three socioeconomic transition phases (1985-1999, 2000-2010, and 2011-2023). Elastic net regression, weighted quantile sum regression, and principal component analysis were used to identify food groups and consumption patterns associated with height, followed by assessments of environmental and economic profiles. Associations were adjusted for provincial socioeconomic and environmental factors, including per capita gross domestic product, educational attainment, sunshine duration, and temperature. A Food Consumption-Height (FCH) score was developed using machine-learning models and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-derived food-group weights to quantify each food consumption associated with height and preliminarily validated in an independent observational sample from Guangzhou. From the 1980s to the 2020s, China's food consumption became more diverse alongside increasing height. Eggs and seafood showed stable associations with height across periods, while milk and fruits became increasingly important after 2000. Nine food consumption patterns were identified across the three periods. A pattern characterized by higher consumption of fruits, nuts, eggs, and milk (FUEL) showed the strongest and most consistent association with greater height in the most recent period (ρ = 0.518, 95% CI [0.453, 0.580]; p < 0.001) and was linked to lower environmental and economic burdens. Height-associated food consumption patterns generally exhibited more favorable nutritional profiles, particularly higher calcium density and calcium-to-phosphorus ratios. Further nutrient-level analyses showed positive associations of protein, calcium, and zinc densities with height and an inverse association for carbohydrate density across all three periods. The FCH score was positively associated with height (β = 0.075, 95% CI [0.069, 0.082]; p < 0.001), and this association showed preliminary consistency in 3,917 participants aged 10-16 years from the Guangzhou Student Nutrition and Health Survey. The main limitations of this study are the observational design and reliance on population-level food consumption data, which limit causal inference between dietary patterns and height outcomes.
