title: Temporal aggregation and the identification and stability of high-quality development configurations in agricultural enterprises
summary: To compare high-quality development configurations in agricultural enterprises under firm-mean static and annual panel fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, this study constructs a 15-indicator high-quality development index (HD) thro
content: To compare high-quality development configurations in agricultural enterprises under firm-mean static and annual panel fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, this study constructs a 15-indicator high-quality development index (HD) through principal component analysis (PCA), using 306 firm-year observations from 26 Chinese listed agricultural enterprises during 2010-2022. Multiyear means summarize long-term levels, whereas annual records preserve combinations within the same year. The baseline identifies four static and six annual paths, including one shared configuration of high environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, non-strong financing constraints, state ownership, and non-pollution-intensive industry status. Opposite ESG and financing-constraint (SA) states suggest complementarity at the configurational level. Annual D2, comprising non-high ESG, high SA, non-state ownership, and pollution-intensive industry status, is retained exactly under equal and entropy weighting and a separate PCA check raising the proportional reduction in inconsistency (PRI) cutoff to 0.65. Its identification is robust across these settings; outcome-direction checks and case evidence further support its correspondence with high HD. Under baseline rules, the annual solution has higher consistency on common annual data, while the static solution has slightly broader coverage. Relative performance changes with screening rules, and the complete baseline shared configuration is measurement-sensitive. The findings reveal configuration differences under temporal aggregation and inform enterprise assessment combining long-term types with annual states.

title: How does the digital economy empower new quality productive forces: evidence from China
summary: This study proposes a more comprehensive and reasonable measurement framework for new quality productive forces that incorporates two core dimensions, new quality input factors and new quality output efficiency, and further analyzes their t
content: This study proposes a more comprehensive and reasonable measurement framework for new quality productive forces that incorporates two core dimensions, new quality input factors and new quality output efficiency, and further analyzes their temporal evolution and spatial distribution. On this basis, the study investigates both the direct impact of the digital economy on new quality productive forces and the mediating pathways through which this impact occurs. The research findings indicate that while China’s new quality productive forces have shown a steady upward trend over the years, issues of insufficient development and spatial imbalance persist. The digital economy plays a crucial role in promoting the growth of new quality productive forces, with notable heterogeneity across different geographic locations, levels of economic development, and policy environments. Furthermore, the mechanism analysis confirms that the digital economy can drive micro-enterprise innovation, promote meso- industry upgrading, and optimize macro-economy resource allocation. Overall, the findings provide both theoretical insights and empirical evidence for promoting new quality productive forces in alignment with regional characteristics and accelerating the modernization of the industrial system.

title: Evaluating Tree Diversity and Carbon Sequestration in Kandyan Home Gardens: Implications for Climate-Smart Agroforestry and Carbon Mitigation
source: Journal of Environmental Professionals Sri Lanka
summary: Agroforestry systems are increasingly recognized for their dual capacity to sequester carbon and sustain biodiversity, yet fine-scale assessments of tropical home gardens remain limited. This study quantified species composition, above- and
content: Agroforestry systems are increasingly recognized for their dual capacity to sequester carbon and sustain biodiversity, yet fine-scale assessments of tropical home gardens remain limited. This study quantified species composition, above- and below-ground biomass, and carbon storage across four Kandyan home garden sites in Sri Lanka, encompassing 500 trees from 21 species. Total carbon (TC) ranged from 25,629 to 33,030 kg C per site. Smaller, structurally complex gardens (Bothota and Pallepola) exhibited higher carbon density (256–262 tC ha⁻¹) than larger, sparsely vegetated sites. Myristica fragrans (Nutmeg) dominated carbon stocks, contributing up to 9698.58 kg C per site, followed by Artocarpus altilis, Artocarpus heterophyllus, and Mangifera indica. Biodiversity indices indicated moderate to high diversity (H′ = 2.736–2.973) and evenness (E = 0.91–0.98). Findings highlight the importance of integrating high-carbon species with diverse vegetation structures to support carbon storage, biodiversity, and sustainable home-garden management.

title: Bisphenol A removal from wastewater in moving bed biofilm reactors using different carriers and impact on performance
source: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: Abstract Bisphenol A, a widely used plasticizer, is a xenoestrogen that disrupts endocrine systems in humans and other species. Therefore, its removal is a key priority for wastewater treatment. This study evaluated the effect of different
content: Abstract Bisphenol A, a widely used plasticizer, is a xenoestrogen that disrupts endocrine systems in humans and other species. Therefore, its removal is a key priority for wastewater treatment. This study evaluated the effect of different carrier materials in three bench-scale aerobic Moving Bed Biofilm Reactors operated in continuous flow. The reactors (Reactor 1: high density polyethylene, Reactor 2: polypropylene structure stuffed with polyurethane foam, Reactor 3: polypropylene structure stuffed with Luffa cylindrica biomass) were fed with synthetic wastewater, first without Bisphenol A and later spiked with 100 µg L −1 of the substance. The following Bisphenol A removal rates were observed: 92.1 ± 1.7% (Reactor 1), 91.9 ± 1.7% (Reactor 2), and 93.0 ± 1.0% (Reactor 3), with no statistically significant difference among them ( p -value = 0.22). Principal component analysis confirmed the similarity among reactors regardless of carrier material. After two weeks of acclimation, Bisphenol A did not affect the reduction of organic matter (> 80%) or ammoniacal nitrogen (> 85%). Although nitrite-oxidizing bacteria exhibited some sensitivity, with nitrite increasing between 1.5 and 2.0 mg L −1 across reactors, the overall treatment performance remained stable, highlighting Moving Bed Biofilm Reactors as a promising technology for Bisphenol A removal.

title: ESG performance, tone of earnings calls, and market reaction during an economic crisis
source: Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting
summary: Abstract This study explores the relationship between firms’ environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, the tone of earnings calls, and market reaction during the COVID-19 outbreak. Using a comprehensive sample of European lis
content: Abstract This study explores the relationship between firms’ environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, the tone of earnings calls, and market reaction during the COVID-19 outbreak. Using a comprehensive sample of European listed firms and a robust methodology, our findings show a less optimistic tone of the earnings calls during COVID-19 and a negative relationship between ESG and tone, wherein firms with lower ESG project a more positive outlook in their earnings calls to reassure stakeholders. We find a positive market reaction to the tone of earnings calls, which is more pronounced for firms that seek to reassure with an inflated tone, even in presence of lower ESG. This study offers new evidence on the value relevance of non-financial information as a driver of managerial tone and the effectiveness of companies’ communication strategies in reassuring stakeholders and market participants during an economic crisis; it provides insights into how companies could respond to manage stakeholders’ expectations when dealing with significant large-scale disruptions.

title: Capturing circular value for building sector actors
summary: Environmental and life-cycle cost assessments of two renovation case studies in Montreal, Canada—a single-detached house and a triplex—investigated three different renovation scenarios: business-as-usual, recycling, and reuse. Results indic
content: Environmental and life-cycle cost assessments of two renovation case studies in Montreal, Canada—a single-detached house and a triplex—investigated three different renovation scenarios: business-as-usual, recycling, and reuse. Results indicate that incorporating circular reuse principles offers the highest potential to reduce environmental impacts while lowering costs. Higher upfront costs and labour requirements for selective deconstruction are subsequently offset by savings via the use of secondary materials. As contractors typically prioritise initial budget considerations within project-based delivery frameworks, these redistributed gains may remain insufficiently visible at the decision-making stage, leaving longer term economic and environmental benefits partially obscured for contractors and clients. A structural mismatch exists between academic evaluations (often framed from cradle to cradle) and industry perspectives focused on project completion. Addressing this misalignment requires rethinking how value is assessed in the building sector, moving beyond upfront costs towards incorporating longer term environmental and economic considerations. By grounding life-cycle assessments in real renovation contexts and translating them into contractor-focused guidance, this study contributes practice-based evidence to support circular renovation decision-making and policy discussions. PRACTICE RELEVANCE This study outlines how circular renovation of a single-detached house and a triplex can achieve economic and environmental reductions if fully implemented. This includes a two-phase construction process: phase 1 (selective deconstruction) and phase 2 (renovation with secondary materials). If only phase 1 is followed, costs for the project rise as this phase is more costly than demolition. However, when both construction phases are followed, net negative greenhouse gas emissions can be achieved, representing a 123% reduction relative to a linear renovation (demolition and the use of primary materials). This significant reduction is due to the avoided burden approach which generates environmental credits that exceed gross impacts, resulting in negative net emissions. Project costs can also be reduced by up to 19%. A deconstruction guide produced for contractors showcases the best practices in selective deconstruction and reuse, and highlights the potential environmental and economic savings.

title: Adapting marketing mix strategies to cultural dimensions: a comparative study of Iraq and selected MENA economies
summary: This research aims to evaluate the impact of cultural criteria, as described in G. Hofstede’s model, on the elements of the marketing mix (7Ps) in Iraq and their differences from similar parameters in countries within the MENA region. To ac
content: This research aims to evaluate the impact of cultural criteria, as described in G. Hofstede’s model, on the elements of the marketing mix (7Ps) in Iraq and their differences from similar parameters in countries within the MENA region. To achieve the research objectives, semi-structured interviews were conducted with experts in the field of marketing, as well as surveys of respondents working at companies in Iraq, the UAE, Egypt, Jordan, and Kuwait, who are involved in making marketing decisions within their organizations. Data processing was carried out using cluster analysis and analysis of variance (ANOVA). The interpretation of the obtained data led to the following conclusions: successful marketing strategies that have proven effective in the Iraqi market are often focused on collective values and the social significance of brands, and are implemented through traditional communication channels. Significant differences were also identified between Iraq and neighboring countries, particularly that most successful marketing solutions in the UAE and Kuwait are based on the transmission of individualistic values and are oriented toward the demonstration of high social status.

title: Tea waste-extract-assisted fabrication of ZnO and TiO2 nanoparticles for photo catalysis application
summary: The increasing generation of bio-waste and the need for sustainable environmental technologies have encouraged the development of green nanotechnology. Tea waste is an abundant and renewable biomass resource containing polyphenols, flavonoi
content: The increasing generation of bio-waste and the need for sustainable environmental technologies have encouraged the development of green nanotechnology. Tea waste is an abundant and renewable biomass resource containing polyphenols, flavonoids, catechins, tannins, and other phytochemicals that can act as reducing, stabilizing, and capping agents during nanoparticle synthesis. This review summarizes recent advances in tea-waste-assisted green synthesis of ZnO and TiO 2 nanoparticles and evaluates their application in photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants. Particular emphasis is placed on the influence of tea-waste composition, extraction conditions, synthesis parameters, nanoparticle morphology, and surface properties on photocatalytic performance. Reported degradation efficiencies and experimental conditions are critically compared to identify key factors governing pollutant removal. Major challenges related to reproducibility, standardization, catalyst recovery, reusability, nanoparticle stability, leaching, environmental safety, real wastewater treatment, and large-scale implementation are also discussed. Finally, future research directions are proposed to facilitate scalable and sustainable applications of tea-waste-derived photocatalysts.

title: Cosmetic Packaging’s Green Transition: Trends, Gaps, and the Complex Cosmetic Macroplastic Packaging Waste Definition
summary: As the global cosmetic products market continues its rapid expansion, the industry faces an escalating waste management crisis driven by the massive annual production of packaging units used by the industry. This study investigates the stra
content: As the global cosmetic products market continues its rapid expansion, the industry faces an escalating waste management crisis driven by the massive annual production of packaging units used by the industry. This study investigates the strategic shift in scientific research and regulatory frameworks regarding cosmetic packaging waste. Using bibliometric analysis via the bibliometrix R-package and VOSviewer (v.1.6.20), a dataset of 352 Web of Science publications (2005–2025) was analyzed. The results reveal a significant thematic evolution: research has transitioned from "reactive" environmental remediation (e.g., wastewater treatment) toward "proactive" circular economy strategies, such as valorization and green synthesis. Despite these advancements, a critical gap remains in the lack of a specialized definition for complex cosmetic waste. To address this, the study introduces and defines Complex Cosmetic Macroplastic Packaging Waste (CCMPW). This category describes multi-material, predominantly plastic-based units with irregular geometries, high surface-to-volume ratios, and insufficient emptiability, which render them technically and economically challenging for standard municipal recycling streams. The findings suggest that distinguishing CCMPW from general plastic waste is a prerequisite for operationalizing proactive circular strategies and aligning with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes. By bridging the gap between structural packaging design and environmental impact, this research provides a conceptual framework for targeted interventions in the cosmetic industry’s green transition.

title: Teachers’ Perceptions about Digitalization of Teaching and its Influence on Students’ Engagement at GS Kagugu, Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: The digitalization of teaching has become a global educational priority aimed at enhancing student engagement and promoting learner-centered instruction.In Rwanda, national initiatives such as the ICT in Education Policy and Smart Classroom
content: The digitalization of teaching has become a global educational priority aimed at enhancing student engagement and promoting learner-centered instruction.In Rwanda, national initiatives such as the ICT in Education Policy and Smart Classroom Project seek to integrate digital technologies into classroom practices.However, limited evidence exists regarding teachers' perceptions of digitalization and its influence on student engagement at the school level.This qualitative case study explored secondary school teachers' perceptions of the digitalization of teaching and its influence on students' behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement at GS Kagugu in Gasabo District, Rwanda.Guided by Constructivist Learning Theory and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the study employed an interpretivist paradigm using semi-structured interviews and document analysis.Five purposively selected teachers from different subject areas participated in the study.Thematic analysis revealed that teachers conceptualize digitalization either as the substitution of traditional instructional tools or as a pedagogical transformation that promotes learner-centered and interactive learning.The findings indicated that digital teaching practices positively influence student motivation, participation, attention, and conceptual understanding when effectively integrated.However, challenges including unstable internet connectivity, power interruptions, limited digital competencies, and inadequate professional development constrain meaningful technology integration.The study recommends continuous school-based professional development, peer-led mentoring initiatives, equitable access to digital resources, and the provision of localized offline-capable digital learning materials.Educational digitalization should therefore prioritize teacher capacity building alongside technological investments to maximize student engagement and learning outcomes.

title: Turismo de bienestar y salud: producción científica entre 2020 y 2024 y agenda de investigación para América Latina
summary: El turismo de bienestar y salud constituye un nicho emergente del turismo mundial, pero la producción científica sobre el tema y su relevancia para América Latina han sido poco examinadas. El objetivo fue analizar la evolución y las tendenc
content: El turismo de bienestar y salud constituye un nicho emergente del turismo mundial, pero la producción científica sobre el tema y su relevancia para América Latina han sido poco examinadas. El objetivo fue analizar la evolución y las tendencias temáticas de las publicaciones científicas sobre turismo de bienestar y salud entre 2020 y 2024, para proponer una agenda de investigación orientada a la región. Se realizó una revisión sistemática con análisis bibliométrico, conforme a las directrices PRISMA 2020, en ScienceDirect, Scopus y SciELO; de 4847 registros identificados se seleccionaron 547 publicaciones, y el análisis bibliométrico detallado se efectuó sobre 153 artículos indexados en Scopus, con VOSviewer. La producción anual fue estable entre 2020 y 2023 (entre 32 y 37 artículos) y en el primer semestre de 2024 se registraron 16; la proyección lineal descendente hacia 2029 depende de este dato parcial y presenta un ajuste modesto (R² = 0.41). Las áreas temáticas predominantes fueron ciencias ambientales (23.2%), ciencias sociales (19.1%), ciencias de la tierra (8.9%) y energía (8.9%), con énfasis en la gestión del agua, el cambio climático y la sostenibilidad. La producción se concentra en Europa, encabezada por España e Italia, y la presencia latinoamericana es reducida; los artículos más citados abordan temas hidrogeológicos y de sostenibilidad. Se concluye que el campo requiere mayor colaboración interdisciplinaria y regional, y una agenda de investigación que vincule el turismo de bienestar con el desarrollo sostenible, la gobernanza del agua y los saberes ancestrales de América Latina.

title: The Living Building Challenge: Examining Practical Barriers to Circular and Regenerative Design
summary: Abstract Since its inception in 2006, the Living Building Challenge (LBC) has become a leading framework for sustainable building design. However, uptake remains limited, with only 35 projects achieving full certification globally as of 202
content: Abstract Since its inception in 2006, the Living Building Challenge (LBC) has become a leading framework for sustainable building design. However, uptake remains limited, with only 35 projects achieving full certification globally as of 2026. These rare examples offer insights into the systemic constraints to circular and regenerative construction. This study examines Australian LBC projects to identify potential support mechanisms that could facilitate wider adoption of circular construction practices. A mixed-methods approach combined a review of previous LBC projects with thematic analysis of 12 semi-structured interviews involving members of the National Circularity Centre Building (NCCB) delivery team, as well as external professionals with LBC experience. Located in Bega, New South Wales, the NCCB is the third Australian project to pursue full LBC certification. Although the LBC’s stringent requirements are frequently associated with increased project time and cost, the findings indicate that these impacts may be symptoms of broader industry constraints and project management complexity. Key barriers include inadequate team composition at initiation, delayed integration of LBC in the design process, and difficulties meeting strict material procurement criteria. Procurement challenges are further exacerbated by limited support and transparency in the manufacturing sector. These findings suggest that stronger early-project support, earlier integration of LBC requirements, and increased uptake of material passport (MP) databases (e.g., Declare Label and Product Aware), could improve the feasibility and scalability of high-performance circular and regenerative building outcomes.

title: Red economy (Fordism and Socialism): Characteristics and peculiarities in agriculture
summary: The article presents two main interpretations of the red economy, understood either as based on the Fordist principle of technological standardisation, mass production, and mass consumption, or as referring to the socialist economic system.
content: The article presents two main interpretations of the red economy, understood either as based on the Fordist principle of technological standardisation, mass production, and mass consumption, or as referring to the socialist economic system. It aims to analyse the main characteristics of these types of economy and provide comments on their specific implications in agriculture. The environmental limitations of Fordist principles are examined, indicating that the logic of intensified production and consumption generates systematic pressure on the environment not only in industry, but also in agriculture. Through an empirical analysis of consumption patterns in Bulgaria and the European Union, the compatibility of the Fordist economic system with the requirements of long-term sustainability is called into question. A revision of the Fordist model is considered necessary because ecological constraints increasingly restrict its contemporary applicability. In examining the socialist economy, the traditional socialist system is first considered, followed by its contemporary modification in China. The development of the socialist economy, and agriculture in particular, is discussed, and the processes of consolidation within the sector are described. It is demonstrated that the share of agriculture in the total production of the Bulgarian economy under socialism experienced a steady decline – from nearly 50% in the late 1940s to 10% of total social product and 11.1% of GDP in 1989 – a trend which, after the 1970s, was also accompanied by a slowdown in economic growth. The contemporary challenges facing China’s economy and agricultural sector are identified, and the reforms undertaken to address them are described.

title: High-mix low-volume production specificity – A case study of formula 1 power units
source: Central European Review of Economics & Finance
summary: This article addresses the issue of High-Mix Low-Volume (HMLV) production, with particular emphasis on its application in the Formula 1 environment. The aim of the study is to present the specific characteristics of low-volume, high-mix pro
content: This article addresses the issue of High-Mix Low-Volume (HMLV) production, with particular emphasis on its application in the Formula 1 environment. The aim of the study is to present the specific characteristics of low-volume, high-mix production and identify the factors influencing its effectiveness, using the example of Formula 1 Power Unit production. The theoretical section characterizes the HMLV model, highlighting, among other things, the importance of process flexibility, technology, digitalization, and Industry 4.0 solutions. The practical section analyzes the specifics of Formula 1 Power Unit production, taking into account the production tools used, inventory and spare parts management, material and operational constraints, and the impact of technical and financial regulations on the organization of research and development processes. The study utilized desk research, a case study, and secondary data analysis. The analysis indicates that Formula 1 Power Unit production exhibits key characteristics of the HMLV environment: small production scale, high technological complexity, significant component diversity, the need for rapid response to change, and strong integration of design, production, and research and development processes. The results also indicate that regulatory and financial constraints can foster more efficient resource use, increased reliability, and the development of innovative solutions. Formula 1 can therefore provide a valuable source of best practices for other high-tech sectors utilizing high-mix, low-volume production.

title: Foliar phenylalanine application modulates biochemical traits and antioxidant enzyme activities in strawberry under reduced nutrient solution supply
summary: Strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) productivity and biochemical fruit attributes can be adversely affected by reduced water and nutrient solution supply. Phenylalanine (Phe), a precursor of the phenylpropanoid pathway, may modify these
content: Strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) productivity and biochemical fruit attributes can be adversely affected by reduced water and nutrient solution supply. Phenylalanine (Phe), a precursor of the phenylpropanoid pathway, may modify these responses. This study investigated foliar Phe effects on fruit yield, biochemical attributes, and antioxidant-related responses of strawberry cv. ‘Sabrina’ under greenhouse soilless conditions. The experiment used a factorial completely randomized design with three Phe concentrations (0, 500, and 1000 µM) and two nutrient solution regimes (200 and 160 mL plant − 1 every other day), with three biological replicates. The interaction between Phe and nutrient solution regime significantly affected several biochemical and antioxidant traits. The highest total phenolic content (4.75 mg GAE g − 1 FW), total flavonoid content (2.22 mg QE g − 1 FW), DPPH radical-scavenging activity (82.25%), and FRAP value (27.44 mg Fe 2+ g − 1 FW) occurred at 500 µM Phe under 200 mL. In contrast, the highest total anthocyanin content (0.797 mg C3G g − 1 FW) occurred at 1000 µM Phe under 160 mL. Phe and nutrient solution regime independently affected fruit yield: the highest mean yield was at 1000 µM Phe (650.19 g plant − 1 ), and yield under 160 mL was 560.14 g plant − 1 versus 620.30 g plant − 1 under 200 mL (9.7% lower). PPO activity was lowest (0.035 U g − 1 FW) at 500 µM Phe under 200 mL and highest (0.15 U g − 1 FW) in untreated plants under 160 mL. SOD activity was affected independently by Phe and nutrient solution regime, whereas CAT, APX, and POD depended on their interaction. Overall, foliar Phe modified biochemical traits and antioxidant-related responses, but effects varied with trait, Phe concentration, and nutrient solution regime. Under the tested conditions, 500 µM Phe was associated with the highest values for several biochemical traits, whereas 1000 µM Phe produced the highest mean yield. These findings suggest potential applications of Phe in soilless strawberry production under reduced nutrient solution supply. However, the study was limited to one cultivar and one greenhouse environment, and mechanisms were not directly measured; therefore, validation across cultivars and growing conditions is required.

title: Radical housing and environmental struggles
summary: In organising this Special Issue, we intentionally begin from what we pose as the inseparability of a radical conception of housing and environmental struggle. Following the Radical Housing Journal’s understanding of housing as a fundamenta
content: In organising this Special Issue, we intentionally begin from what we pose as the inseparability of a radical conception of housing and environmental struggle. Following the Radical Housing Journal’s understanding of housing as a fundamentally political question, ‘inseparable from implicated, everyday practices of inhabiting space and challenging the forces that make the world unhomely and uninhabitable’ (RHJ Editorial Collective, 2019: i), we approach environmental and climate crises as housing questions, and housing struggles as increasingly ecological struggles. Across the contributions collected here, this relationship manifests itself in multiple forms: tenants confront the costs and power relations embedded in decarbonisation and retrofit; precariously housed communities endure intensifying heat, pollution and environmental risk; climate adaptation and ‘sustainable’ redevelopment are contested when they become rationales for displacement; and residents, activists and scholar-activists develop situated practices of repair, commoning, care, resistance and knowledge production. These contributions suggest that radical housing in a climate-changed world cannot be reduced to making the existing housing system greener, but is instead central to questions of just transitions. This raises the more difficult political question of how the places in which people live might be repaired, adapted and transformed without reproducing the property relations, inequalities and forms of dispossession that have made both housing and environmental crises so profoundly uneven in the first place. In a way, the main argument of this issue is to draw attention to the fact that the conditions that make housing precarious and the conditions that make environments uninhabitable are often produced through the same political-economic and ecological relations.

title: Agro-ecosystem Characterization and Climate Change Adaptation in Smallholder Systems in the Gidabo Sub-basin, Southern Ethiopia
summary: Climate, soils and topography are central determinants of agro‑ecosystem sustainability. This study investigated the Gidabo sub‑basin in southern Ethiopia using a mixed‑methods design, combining quantitative data from 384 households across
content: Climate, soils and topography are central determinants of agro‑ecosystem sustainability. This study investigated the Gidabo sub‑basin in southern Ethiopia using a mixed‑methods design, combining quantitative data from 384 households across five districts with qualitative insights from focus groups, interviews, and field observations. Results showed household concentration in the midlands (67.2%, 64.6% area), where biodiversity was highest (Shannon 2.81-3.85, richness 42-84) and farming centered on enset-coffee homegarden agroforestry. The highlands (14.3%, 14.2% area) exhibited Cambisols, mixed cereal-livestock systems, and moderate biodiversity (Shannon 2.54-2.68), while the lowlands (18.5%, 21.2% area) were dominated by Pellic Vertisols, agro‑pastoralism, and species such as Acacia, Moringa and Balanites spp. (Shannon 2.21-2.45). Agro‑ecosystems face soil degradation (acidity, erosion, poor fertility), climatic stresses (frost, drought), biotic pressures (fall armyworm, trypanosomiasis), and anthropogenic drivers (deforestation, cultural practices, population growth), all exacerbated by climate change. The findings highlight the limitations of indigenous adaptation strategies and underscore the need for agroecology-based interventions, strengthened extension services, improved credit and market access, and investment in soil and water conservation to enhance resilience and ensure agricultural sustainability.

title: Impact of nicotine concentration, form, and stereoisomer ratio on oral nicotine pouch pharmacokinetics and abuse liability: Protocol for a randomized crossover study in adults who use tobacco
summary: OBJECTIVES: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are tobacco-free products placed between the lip and gum to deliver nicotine. Sales have grown rapidly in the United States (U.S.), yet independent data on how nicotine characteristics shape ONP appe
content: OBJECTIVES: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are tobacco-free products placed between the lip and gum to deliver nicotine. Sales have grown rapidly in the United States (U.S.), yet independent data on how nicotine characteristics shape ONP appeal and addiction potential are lacking. Three nicotine characteristics vary across ONPs: concentration (mass of nicotine per pouch), form (the fraction of freebase, or unprotonated, nicotine), and stereoisomer (the proportion of S- to R-nicotine). This study will determine how these characteristics independently and jointly affect ONP nicotine pharmacokinetics and user experience among adults who smoke cigarettes or use moist snuff. DESIGN AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, double-blind, crossover trial will enroll 160 adults who smoke cigarettes or use moist snuff at a single U.S. site. INTERVENTIONS AND OUTCOMES: Participants will be randomized 1:1 to a lower (3 mg) or higher (6 mg) nicotine concentration arm. Within each arm, participants will complete five laboratory sessions in balanced, randomized order: four standardized ONP sessions (30 minutes, with the pouch placed between lip and gum) varying by nicotine form (30% vs. 70% freebase) and stereoisomer ratio (racemic [50% R- and 50% S-nicotine] vs. > 99% S-nicotine), plus one session using their usual tobacco product. Sessions will be separated by at least 48 hours. The primary outcome is maximum plasma nicotine concentration (Cmax). Secondary outcomes include time to maximum concentration (Tmax), total nicotine absorbed over 90 minutes (AUC), subjective effects, and behavioral economic demand indices. CONCLUSIONS: This will be the first study to systematically examine how nicotine concentration, form, and stereoisomer ratio interact to influence ONP abuse liability. Findings will identify which product characteristics drive ONP addiction potential and will inform FDA regulation aimed at maximizing the potential for ONPs to serve as a harm reduction alternative to cigarettes and moist snuff. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06315881; registered February 14, 2024.

title: Aerogel-based antimicrobial innovations: strategic development, mechanistic actions, and advanced applications in food safety and biomedical fields
source: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology
summary: The rising challenge of microbial resistance and contamination necessitates innovative materials with superior antimicrobial properties. Aerogels, characterized by ultra-low density, extensive porosity, and large surface area, have emerged
content: The rising challenge of microbial resistance and contamination necessitates innovative materials with superior antimicrobial properties. Aerogels, characterized by ultra-low density, extensive porosity, and large surface area, have emerged as promising matrices for incorporating various antimicrobial agents, including metallic nanoparticles, organic compounds, and natural bioactive materials. This review systematically discusses different aerogel types-silica-based, polymeric, bio-based, and hybrid aerogels and their unique potential as antimicrobial agents. It also highlights key mechanisms underlying their antimicrobial activities, such as reactive oxygen species generation, disruption of microbial membranes, sustained release of embedded agents, and physical adsorption of pathogens. Extensive applications are explored, emphasizing their roles in food packaging to enhance shelf life and safety, as well as in advanced biomedical applications like drug delivery systems, wound dressings, and tissue engineering scaffolds. Furthermore, this article addresses current challenges, including optimization of stability, cost-effectiveness, biocompatibility, and environmental sustainability, and provides insights into regulatory considerations crucial for their safe implementation. Finally, future research directions are proposed to facilitate broader utilization and technological advancement of aerogel-based antimicrobial solutions, significantly contributing to improved public health, food safety, and therapeutic outcomes.

title: Journal of Global Political Transformations
summary: The purpose of the study was to determine the functional purpose, mechanisms, and consequences of diplomatic silence in international crises.The work employed typologisation to classify the functions of silence, case study analysis to exami
content: The purpose of the study was to determine the functional purpose, mechanisms, and consequences of diplomatic silence in international crises.The work employed typologisation to classify the functions of silence, case study analysis to examine diplomatic cases, comparative analysis to compare models of silence, as well as discursive and politicalcommunicative analysis to interpret political consequences.The analysis allowed for the consideration of diplomatic silence as an independent form of political communication.A classification of the main functions was formulated, which included deterrence, signalling, crisis management, protection of the negotiation process, demonstration of position, and creation of strategic uncertainty.The comparison of relations between China and the United States of America and between China and Taiwan revealed a distinction between the crisis-regulatory and status-symbolic models of the use of silence.The study of Russia's war with Ukraine showed that the restriction of public information was used to enhance operational security and preserve uncertainty regarding the intentions and capabilities of the parties.The analysis of sanction conflicts around Russia and Iran demonstrated the use of silence as an instrument of strategic insurance aimed at minimizing political risks.The examination of India's diplomatic behaviour demonstrated the use of silence for balancing between competing centres of power without losing foreign policy flexibility.The advantages of silence are manifested through reducing the risk of escalation, maintaining negotiation channels, and protecting sensitive information, while the main threats remain the misinterpretation of intentions, the growth of distrust, and the accumulation of informational uncertainty.The results can be used by diplomatic agencies and specialists in international relations to assess the feasibility of using silence in crisis communications, negotiation processes, and the development of foreign policy strategies

title: Carbonized rice husk–peat substrate improves irrigation water productivity in greenhouse tomato under reduced irrigation–fertigation
source: Journal of the Saudi Society of Agricultural Sciences
summary: Abstract This study evaluated how cultivar and substrate modify greenhouse tomato responses to simultaneous reductions in irrigation water and nutrient supply. ‘Rambo F1’ and ‘Río Grande’ were grown under 100% or 50% crop evapotranspiration
content: Abstract This study evaluated how cultivar and substrate modify greenhouse tomato responses to simultaneous reductions in irrigation water and nutrient supply. ‘Rambo F1’ and ‘Río Grande’ were grown under 100% or 50% crop evapotranspiration (ETc) in carbonized rice husk + peat, cattle-manure compost + peat, or vermiculite + peat (1:1, v/v). The factorial experiment lasted 212 days, with six biological replicates per treatment combination for most variables and three for proline. Nutrient-solution concentrations were identical between irrigation regimes within each developmental stage; therefore, 50% ETc halved both water and cumulative nutrient delivery, rather than imposing water deficit alone. Growth, physiological, biomass, reproductive, and fruit-quality responses depended on cultivar and substrate. ‘Rambo F1’ under compost + peat achieved the highest marketable yield at 100% ETc (45.0 kg m⁻²), declining to 21.9 kg m⁻² under 50% ETc (Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). Under carbonized rice husk + peat, no significant marketable-yield difference was detected between 100% and 50% ETc in ‘Rambo F1’ (30.5 versus 25.9 kg m⁻²) or ‘Río Grande’ (20.9 versus 18.4 kg m⁻²; Holm-adjusted P = 0.312 for both). These contrasts do not establish yield equivalence. In this substrate, reduced supply increased irrigation water productivity 1.70-fold and 1.75-fold, respectively (Holm-adjusted P < 0.01 for both). Fruit-quality responses were selective, with no uniform improvement under reduced supply. These findings support evaluating cultivar–substrate combinations to improve irrigation water productivity under reduced irrigation–fertigation, with validation across commercial conditions and growing seasons required before recommending broader adoption.

title: Türkiye'de Lojistik Köylerin Sermaye Birikim Sürecindeki Yeri
source: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’deki lojistik köyleri teknik verimlilik ve maliyet minimizasyonu ekseninden çıkararak, kapitalist sermaye birikim rejiminin mekânsal ve toplumsal mantığı çerçevesinde tartışmayı amaçlamaktadır. Böylece lojistik, kapitali
content: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’deki lojistik köyleri teknik verimlilik ve maliyet minimizasyonu ekseninden çıkararak, kapitalist sermaye birikim rejiminin mekânsal ve toplumsal mantığı çerçevesinde tartışmayı amaçlamaktadır. Böylece lojistik, kapitalist sermaye birikim süreci ve lojistik köy arasındaki ilişkileri çözümlemeyi hedeflemektedir. Çalışma, tarihsel materyalist bir kuramsal çerçeveye dayanmaktadır ve nitel bir araştırma tasarımı izlemektedir. Yöntem olarak doküman analizi kullanılmış; kalkınma planları, ulaştırma ve lojistik strateji belgeleri, TCDD ve bakanlık raporları ile ulusal/uluslararası akademik literatür bütüncül biçimde incelenmiştir. Analizde, lojistik köylerin mekânsal yer seçimi mantığı, küresel üretim ve değer zincirleriyle kurduğu ilişkiler ve emek, mekân ile çevre üzerindeki etkileri, eleştirel mekânsal kuramlar ve küresel değer zinciri literatürü eşliğinde değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, Türkiye’de lojistik köylerin resmî söylemde rekabetçilik ve bölgesel kalkınma araçları olarak sunulmasına karşın, fiiliyatta sermayenin zaten yoğunlaştığı koridorları tahkim eden seçici mekânsal sabitlemeler olduğunu göstermektedir. Ayrıca bu yatırımlar, Türkiye’nin küresel değer zincirlerine bağımlı entegrasyonunu derinleştirirken, lojistik emek üzerinde yeni disiplin biçimleri ve kentsel çeperlerde mekânsal adaletsizlikler üretmektedir. Çalışma, lojistik köylerin planlanmasında mekânsal adalet, emek hakları ve çevresel etkilerin merkezî ölçütler olarak ele alınmasını; katılımcı yönetişim ve emek odaklı politikalarla desteklenmesini önermektedir.

title: Climate-Smart Food Systems and Sustainable Nutrition: Integrating Advanced Processing Technologies, Nutritional Bioavailability, Human Health, and Environmental Sustainability
summary: Background: Global food systems face a dual crisis of environmental degradation and malnutrition, a challenge acutely felt in climate-vulnerable nations like Pakistan. Transitioning to climate-smart food systems requires optimizing downstre
content: Background: Global food systems face a dual crisis of environmental degradation and malnutrition, a challenge acutely felt in climate-vulnerable nations like Pakistan. Transitioning to climate-smart food systems requires optimizing downstream processing to preserve nutritional quality while minimizing ecological footprints. Objective: This study investigates the integration of advanced non-thermal processing technologies to simultaneously enhance nutritional bioavailability, improve human health outcomes, and reduce environmental impacts, while evaluating consumer acceptance in urban Pakistan. Methods: Employing a mixed-methods design, the research combined experimental optimization with consumer behavior analysis in Islamabad. Phase 1 utilized 125 experimental runs to compare Response Surface Methodology (RSM) against machine learning algorithms (Artificial Neural Networks [ANN] and Random Forest) for optimizing Pulsed Electric Fields (PEF). Phase 2 administered a structured survey to 450 urban residents, analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: Experimental results demonstrated that ANN significantly outperformed RSM ( vs. ; RMSE = 0.082), identifying a global optimum (PEF at 25 kV/cm for 150 ) that maximized *in-vitro* mineral bioavailability while minimizing specific energy consumption. The PLS-SEM analysis validated the structural pathways, revealing that Advanced Processing Technology strongly enhances Nutritional Bioavailability (beta = 0.64, which subsequently acts as a critical mediator for improved Health Outcomes (). Furthermore, Environmental Awareness () and Perceived Nutritional Adequacy () significantly drove consumers' Willingness to Pay, with the model demonstrating robust out-of-sample predictive relevance (). Conclusion: AI-driven multi-objective optimization effectively resolves the complex trade-offs between ecological sustainability and nutrient retention.
