title: The agrobiodiversity functional types of shagras (Indigenous home gardens) in the Cumbal Indigenous Reserve, Nariño, Colombia
summary: Abstract Background Shagras, the traditional diversified home gardens of the Pastos Indigenous people, are important for the in situ conservation of Andean agrobiodiversity. However, the internal structure of their diversity and the factors
content: Abstract Background Shagras, the traditional diversified home gardens of the Pastos Indigenous people, are important for the in situ conservation of Andean agrobiodiversity. However, the internal structure of their diversity and the factors that sustain it remain poorly documented. Methods The agrobiodiversity of 262 shagras belonging to 202 households located between 3,077 and 3,522 m a.s.l. in the Cumbal Indigenous Reserve (Nariño, Colombia) was characterised through household surveys, GIS-measured areas, species inventories and associated practices. Shagra types were identified by hierarchical clustering (Ward.D2) of the proportion of species in each of 12 use groups. Results A total of 236 species or local names were recorded, with a median of 29 species per shagra distributed over 12 use groups; native trees are the richest group (mean of 8.0 species per shagra, present in 84.7% of shagras) and 48.7% of names appear in five shagras or fewer. Species richness increased with shagra area (about 70% more species per tenfold increase in area) and varied more among veredas than with altitude (no linear effect). Within each vereda, the number of tuber varieties per household increased by about 40% per 100 m of altitude. Four shagra types were identified that form a continuum: single-purpose Andean (T1; 28 shagras, median of 4 species from a single use group, almost only tubers and faba bean), dual-purpose (T2; 33 shagras, 15 species from three groups, mainly native trees and cold-climate crops), domestic multipurpose (T3; 96 shagras, 25 species from seven groups) and multipurpose with pastures (T4; 105 shagras, 40 species from ten groups, with the largest area, median 1,021 m²). Household characteristics were weakly associated with shagra type. Moreover, 42 of 46 households with several shagras have them of different types, so type reflects the role of the shagra rather than the household. More than 94% of households reported having lost varieties of potato, oca and ulluco, and 11 (5.4%) have a profile compatible with agrobiodiversity custodians. Conclusions These non-causal results and associations point to the need to strengthen in situ conservation at the plot and community scales, for which concrete measures are proposed.

title: Innovation Activity and Green Business Practices in European Firms: The Role of Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how innovation activity relates to green business practices among European firms and considers, rather than directly tests, the implications of these practices for sustainability communication. Using establishme
content: ABSTRACT This study examines how innovation activity relates to green business practices among European firms and considers, rather than directly tests, the implications of these practices for sustainability communication. Using establishment‐level data from 4666 firms across Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, Germany and Ireland drawn from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys, the study employs survey‐weighted logistic and fractional‐response models to account for complex survey design, firm characteristics, country effects and industry heterogeneity. Green business practices are measured through CO 2 emissions monitoring, energy management, on‐site solar adoption and solar electricity intensity. The findings reveal that broader innovation activity is positively associated with CO 2 monitoring and, more strongly, energy‐management adoption. However, innovation does not significantly predict on‐site solar adoption, indicating a boundary between general innovativeness and capital‐intensive renewable‐energy investment. Disaggregated results further show that R&D activity primarily drives CO 2 monitoring, whereas process innovation is particularly important for energy management. Importantly, energy management is associated with an approximately 13–14 percentage‐point higher probability of solar adoption, suggesting that organisational environmental readiness is more closely associated with renewable‐energy investment than innovation breadth alone. The study concludes by recommending that firms strengthen their environmental management systems to translate innovation into measurable green practices and renewable energy investments.

title: Political Influence as Strategic Substitution: Carbon Performance and Corporate Lobbying in US Climate Policy
summary: ABSTRACT Firms facing environmental regulation can respond through both operational adjustment and political engagement, yet existing research provides limited insight into how these strategies interact. This study addresses the theoretical
content: ABSTRACT Firms facing environmental regulation can respond through both operational adjustment and political engagement, yet existing research provides limited insight into how these strategies interact. This study addresses the theoretical question of how firms allocate resources between market and nonmarket strategies and whether corporate lobbying functions as a complement to, or a substitute for, environmental abatement. Drawing on public choice theory, we argue that firms allocate resources across alternative strategies based on relative costs and expected benefits, such that firms with poor carbon performance, facing higher compliance costs, are more likely to substitute towards lobbying. We further propose that this relationship is contingent on the credibility of the regulatory environment. We test these arguments using panel data on US firms' carbon emissions and lobbying expenditures from 2010 to 2020, exploiting the US withdrawal from the COP21 Paris Agreement as an empirical setting capturing a broader class of deregulatory shocks. The results show that firms with higher emissions systematically engage in more lobbying and that this relationship weakens following the decline in climate accountability. This study contributes to the literature by conceptualising corporate lobbying as part of a strategic allocation between market and nonmarket responses, by identifying carbon performance as a key driver of firms' strategic behaviour and by demonstrating how changes in regulatory credibility shape the interaction between environmental performance and corporate political activity.

title: Task-level assessment of robotic solutions in warehouses: a human-centric framework
summary: Technological advancements are transforming warehouse operations, as robotic solutions are increasingly deployed to enhance efficiency and productivity. Although these technologies reduce physical strain and automate repetitive tasks, their
content: Technological advancements are transforming warehouse operations, as robotic solutions are increasingly deployed to enhance efficiency and productivity. Although these technologies reduce physical strain and automate repetitive tasks, their broader effects on human factors (HFs), including perceptual, mental, physical, and psychosocial dimensions, remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, explicit links between specific robotic capabilities and task-level effects on workers remain limited. To address this gap, this study develops a human-centric, task-level framework for evaluating how different robotic solutions influence HFs in warehouse operations. Using an exploratory, qualitative, multi-method approach, the study triangulates insights from literature, practitioner discussions, robotics solution providers, and end users to classify robotic solutions according to interaction level, task-execution roles, and adaptability. Application of the framework to the key warehouse task of order picking shows that robotic solutions reduce physical workload while introducing mixed mental and perceptual demands related to supervision and monitoring, and psychosocial challenges associated with shared-space interaction and job engagement. These findings highlight the importance of early human-centric evaluation during technology selection and implementation, enabling organisations to anticipate potential benefits and challenges prior to deployment. The framework supports human-centric decision-making in warehouse robotics and provides a basis for future empirical research on task-level human–robot interaction (HRI).

title: Talk Without Substance? Institutional Pressures, the Rule of Law, and the Symbolic Decoupling of Corporate Green Innovation After the Paris Agreement
summary: ABSTRACT International climate agreements are widely presumed to push firms toward substantive environmental change, a presumption that hardens where domestic institutions are expected to hold firms to their word. Drawing on institutional t
content: ABSTRACT International climate agreements are widely presumed to push firms toward substantive environmental change, a presumption that hardens where domestic institutions are expected to hold firms to their word. Drawing on institutional theory, namely, legitimacy‐seeking, isomorphic pressure, and decoupling, this study interrogates that presumption, asking whether the Paris Agreement produced substantive corporate green innovation or chiefly symbolic environmental disclosure and how the rule of law conditions the response. Using 174,056 firm‐year observations across 51 countries and economies from 2007 to 2025 and a difference‐in‐differences design that interacts a common post‐treaty indicator with time‐invariant institutional characteristics while absorbing firm and year fixed effects, the analysis finds no robust average effect of the Paris Agreement on substantive green innovation once firm characteristics and ESG controls are absorbed. Rather than amplifying disclosure, the institutional setting separates the two channels: the post‐Paris interaction with a strong rule of law registers on environmental disclosure yet is indistinguishable from zero for real innovation. The sharpest evidence comes from legal origin, where common‐law firms raise environmental disclosure after Paris without any matching gain in substantive innovation, a pattern read here as institutional decoupling operating at the level of the international treaty. The study offers a large‐scale, cross‐country quasi‐experimental test distinguishing environmental talk from environmental action and cautions investors, boards, and policymakers against reading disclosure intensity as evidence of genuine innovation.

title: Enhancing Water and Sanitation Through Innovation and Collaboration Amid Global Conflicts: A Perspective on Sustainable Development Goal 6
summary: ABSTRACT This article is a “Perspective” piece, synthesizing and interpreting existing literature to offer a viewpoint on the challenges and opportunities related to SDG 6. Failure to advance toward Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6)—un
content: ABSTRACT This article is a “Perspective” piece, synthesizing and interpreting existing literature to offer a viewpoint on the challenges and opportunities related to SDG 6. Failure to advance toward Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6)—universal access to safe water and sanitation—threatens global public health, safety, and socioeconomic development. Without progress, communities face higher risks of waterborne diseases, reduced quality of life, and limited educational and economic opportunities, especially for vulnerable groups. Meeting SDG 6 requires increased investment, innovation, and collaboration. However, this perspective argues that global conflicts, exacerbated by contemporary geopolitical dimensions of globalization, are a primary barrier to progress. These conflicts obstruct SDG 6 by disrupting water supply chains, destroying infrastructure, and diverting resources from crucial projects. We systematically review the evidence quantifying the impacts of conflict on water and sanitation, demonstrating that conflict‐affected countries have, on average, 20% lower rates of access to safely managed drinking water than stable countries. We explore innovative technological solutions and sustainable practices, such as smart water management, water recycling, and nature‐based solutions, alongside successful collaborative case studies from post‐conflict Rwanda, Singapore, India, and China. We also address the specific challenges of implementing water technologies in conflict‐affected settings and recommend conflict‐sensitive, low‐tech solutions where appropriate. We conclude that peace is not merely a parallel goal but an essential prerequisite for effective resource allocation and the successful implementation of water and sanitation solutions. While progress can occur even in the absence of complete peace, a stable and cooperative international environment is critical for accelerating progress toward SDG 6, ensuring that improvements in water and sanitation contribute to broader objectives of health, equality, and economic prosperity.

title: A Study on the Current Status and Optimization Strategies for Exports in Hebei Province's Steel Industry
source: Frontiers in Business Economics and Management
summary: The international steel market has become increasingly volatile, with fluctuating demand, trade protectionism, and tighter environmental requirements reshaping export competition. As China's largest steel-producing province, Hebei plays a c
content: The international steel market has become increasingly volatile, with fluctuating demand, trade protectionism, and tighter environmental requirements reshaping export competition. As China's largest steel-producing province, Hebei plays a central role in national steel production and exports, yet its export structure still reflects the legacy of an extensive development model. Using customs and provincial data for 2020–2024, this paper examines the scale, trade modes, product structure, and destination markets of Hebei's steel exports. The results show that export value recovered after the pandemic but remained concentrated in general trade and in flat-rolled and long products, while high-value-added products accounted for a small share. Asia remained the dominant market, followed by Latin America, Europe, and Africa. Four constraints are identified: a one-dimensional product structure, insufficient technical standards, rising environmental costs, and cutthroat price competition. The paper proposes four optimization strategies: market monitoring and diversification, technology benchmarking, green supply chain development, and brand differentiation.

title: Screening of residual solvents in cocaine seizures by HS ‐ SPME ‐ GC ‐ MS : Application to multi‐class solvent profiling
summary: Abstract A headspace solid‐phase microextraction coupled to gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS‐SPME‐GC‐MS) method was developed for the screening of 50 residual solvents (RS), including alcohols, ethers, esters, ketones, aliphatics, a
content: Abstract A headspace solid‐phase microextraction coupled to gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS‐SPME‐GC‐MS) method was developed for the screening of 50 residual solvents (RS), including alcohols, ethers, esters, ketones, aliphatics, aromatics, and chlorinated solvents. Given the chemical diversity of the compounds, a diluent selection step was critically addressed to ensure analyte compatibility. Some key GC parameters were optimized using a one‐variable‐at‐a‐time (OVAT) approach, whereas HS‐SPME extraction parameters (extraction time, temperature, desorption time) were optimized using a design of experiments (DoE) strategy. A semi‐quantitative assessment using model solvent mixtures supported method optimization and characterization of the target compounds. Quantitative validation was performed for the most frequently encountered residual solvents, demonstrating good selectivity, coefficients of determination ( R 2 = 0.981–0.998), low detection limits (0.07–0.29 mg L −1 ), satisfactory recoveries (70.2%–117.4%), and acceptable intra‐ and inter‐day precision (RSD <15%). The proposed approach shows adequate performance for screening volatile residues in complex drug matrices such as cocaine hydrochloride. However, because the extraction strategy is based on saturated aqueous NaCl and does not require organic solvents, it can potentially be extended to other drug matrices that are soluble in aqueous media. This characteristic makes the approach particularly suitable for routine forensic applications. A kinetic study further revealed compound‐dependent profiles, with rapid initial sorption followed by stabilization (e.g., aliphatics and ethers), whereas aromatics and several ketones showed a more progressive increase, indicating that equilibrium was not generally reached under the evaluated HS‐SPME conditions.

title: Efektywność ekonomiczna branży wodociągowo-kanalizacyjnej w aspekcie zrównoważonego rozwoju
source: Zarządzanie Innowacyjne w Gospodarce i Biznesie
summary: Celem pracy było przedstawienie analizy efektywności ekonomicznej wprowadzenia rozwiązania technologicznego w pełnej skali technicznej, służącego do redukcji metali ciężkich ze ścieków, na przykładzie sektora wodociągowo-kanalizacyjnego w k
content: Celem pracy było przedstawienie analizy efektywności ekonomicznej wprowadzenia rozwiązania technologicznego w pełnej skali technicznej, służącego do redukcji metali ciężkich ze ścieków, na przykładzie sektora wodociągowo-kanalizacyjnego w kontekście koncepcji zrównoważonego rozwoju. W artykule przedstawiono specyfikę branży, metody oceny efektywności inwestycji oraz zależności między efektywnością ekonomiczną, społeczną i środowiskową. Wykazano, że współczesne podejście do efektywności ekonomicznej wykracza poza klasyczne wskaźniki finansowe i obejmuje także długookresowe efekty ekologiczne oraz społeczne. Przedstawiona analiza kosztów i korzyści zawiera symulację kosztochłonności oraz możliwego zwrotu inwestycji dotyczącej redukcji metali ciężkich ze ścieków przemysłowych w funkcjonującej stacji utylizacji emulsji olejowych. Przedstawiona analiza przeprowadzona na podstawie danych technologicznych i ekonomicznych (wycena inwestycji oraz koszt eksploatacji) wskazuje, że projekt ten należy traktować nie tylko jako modernizację technologiczną, lecz jako instrument zarządzania efektywnością ekonomiczną, ryzykiem środowiskowym oraz wartością strategiczną przedsiębiorstwa. Uwzględniając koszt inwestycyjny, analiza wykazała, że zwrot z inwestycji będzie możliwy po okresie pięciu lat.

title: Recombinant protein expression platforms based on Drosophila : Advances in S2 cells, glycoengineering, and whole‐fly biomanufacturing
summary: Among the various expression hosts available for the heterologous production of recombinant proteins, insect systems combine eukaryotic protein-processing capacity, genetic tractability, and scalable cultivation. This review provides an ove
content: Among the various expression hosts available for the heterologous production of recombinant proteins, insect systems combine eukaryotic protein-processing capacity, genetic tractability, and scalable cultivation. This review provides an overview of recombinant protein expression and manufacturing technologies based on Drosophila melanogaster, focusing on the established Schneider 2 cell system and the emerging transgenic whole-fly platform. By systematically examining stable expression, secretory production, serum-free suspension culture, bioreactor scale-up, downstream purification, and quality control, we demonstrate that Schneider 2 cells have developed into a relatively mature production platform. We further emphasize that glycosylation is a major determinant of product suitability and a central target of host engineering. In the whole-fly platform, site-specific transgenesis together with tissue-specific or inducible regulation enables protein expression to be coordinated with tissue function and developmental stage, providing a foundation for establishing a whole-fly production platform. In addition, evaluation of clinical-stage antigens produced in Schneider 2 cells and recent whole-fly production cases defines the current maturity of Drosophila-based recombinant protein process development and platform construction and identifies the associated developmental challenges. Overall, although Drosophila-based recombinant protein expression has not yet achieved commercial production, relatively mature and operational process workflows have been established. Future efforts should therefore focus on developing targeted production platforms for product areas in which Drosophila has advantages, rather than pursuing a universal platform applicable to all recombinant proteins.

title: The Cost of Congestion: How Increased Travel Time Raises Fuel Expenditure and Air Pollution in Patna City
source: American Scholarly Journal for Scientific Research
summary: Traffic congestion is often regarded primarily as an inconvenience: commuters spend more time travelling, arrive late at work or school, and experience greater stress. However, the economic and environmental consequences of congestion exten
content: Traffic congestion is often regarded primarily as an inconvenience: commuters spend more time travelling, arrive late at work or school, and experience greater stress. However, the economic and environmental consequences of congestion extend far beyond lost time. When vehicles move slowly, repeatedly accelerate and decelerate, or remain stationary with their engines running, they continue consuming fuel while covering relatively little distance. The result is an increase in petrol and diesel expenditure for households as well as greater vehicular emissions. This study examines the relationship between increasing travel time, fuel expenditure and air pollution in Patna, Bihar. Patna provides a particularly important case study because rapid urbanisation, mixed traffic, roadside commercial activity, limited road capacity and growing vehicle use have placed pressure on the city's transport network. A 2026 study of nine Patna corridors reported a mean traffic speed of 21.16 kilometres per hour, with average speeds falling to 15.85 kilometres per hour during the evening peak period. Commercial corridors recorded lower speeds and much higher passenger-car-unit flows than residential areas (Kumar et al., 2026). Government and environmental studies also show that transport is an important contributor to pollution in Patna. A source-apportionment study estimated transport's contribution to ambient PM2.5 concentration at approximately 19%, while transport contributed substantially to carbon monoxide and volatile organic compound emissions (The Energy and Resources Institute [TERI], 2021). This paper combines secondary evidence from government reports, academic studies and pollution assessments with an survey dataset of 100 Patna commuters. In the simulated survey model, 74% of respondents reported that their journeys frequently or very frequently took longer because of congestion, 69% believed that congestion had noticeably increased their monthly fuel expenditure, and 83% considered traffic to be an important contributor to Patna's air pollution. Among regular users of private motor vehicles, respondents experiencing the greatest reported delays also tended to report larger monthly fuel expenses. The study concludes that congestion imposes three interconnected costs on Patna: a time cost, a financial cost through additional fuel consumption, and an environmental cost through increased emissions. It recommends improved public transport, traffic-signal optimisation, stricter parking and encroachment management, better intersection design, walking and cycling infrastructure, behavioural interventions and continued transition toward cleaner vehicles. However, the paper argues that electrification alone cannot solve congestion because a zero-emission vehicle still occupies road space and contributes to travel delay. Sustainable mobility therefore requires reducing unnecessary vehicle kilometres and improving the efficiency with which limited urban road space i

title: Effects of the Graphene Oxide/Nano‐ SiO 2 Ratio on the Engineering Performance of Oil‐Based Polyurethane Grouting Materials
summary: ABSTRACT Water leakage threatens underground infrastructure, yet conventional oil‐based polyurethane grouts face a trade‐off between slurry fluidity and cured‐material strength and water resistance. Graphene oxide (GO) and nano‐SiO 2 were s
content: ABSTRACT Water leakage threatens underground infrastructure, yet conventional oil‐based polyurethane grouts face a trade‐off between slurry fluidity and cured‐material strength and water resistance. Graphene oxide (GO) and nano‐SiO 2 were surface‐modified with 3‐aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES, commercially designated KH‐550), washed, vacuum‐dried, and dispersed into the polyol component before reaction with polymethylene polyphenyl isocyanate (PAPI). The total modified filler loading was fixed at 4 g while the GO/nano‐SiO 2 ratio was varied. The 2 g/2 g formulation increased compressive strength by 64.8% to 4.22 MPa and retained 4.09 MPa after 7‐day immersion. The 1 g/3 g formulation provided the highest tensile strength and lowest water uptake among the tested compositions, with higher Component A apparent viscosity as a trade‐off. A two‐dimensional plane‐strain finite element model evaluated the mechanical response of a cured plug prepared from the 2 g/2 g formulation under hydraulic loading. Compression dominated the calculated body‐failure tendency; longer plugs reduced failure risk, whereas wider fractures reduced pressure‐bearing capacity. These findings support application‐specific formulation screening and comparative assessment of plug geometry. Direct injectability, permeability, and field performance require further validation.

title: When harm doesn’t count: How organizations learn not to see irresponsibility
summary: Research on corporate social irresponsibility and business ethics has yielded important insights into how organizational harm is evaluated, attributed, contested, and remembered. Much of this research, however, begins from the assumption th
content: Research on corporate social irresponsibility and business ethics has yielded important insights into how organizational harm is evaluated, attributed, contested, and remembered. Much of this research, however, begins from the assumption that harmful organizational consequences have already entered moral awareness. We challenge this assumption by distinguishing the occurrence of harm from its recognition as morally significant. We conceptualize moral visibility as the extent to which harmful organizational consequences become recognizable to particular actors as potentially morally significant and, therefore, available for ethical evaluation. Drawing on institutional theory, we develop the concept of selective moral attention to explain how institutional logics differentially organize this moral visibility. We argue that institutional logics become instantiated through organizational routines, categories, reporting practices, and decision processes that foreground some harmful consequences while backgrounding others. As these patterns of attention become routinized and reproduced, organizations may learn what warrants moral attention—and what does not. Thus, moral visibility is neither uniform nor fixed: it varies across harms, actors, and institutional contexts and can be reproduced, contested, and transformed. By theorizing moral visibility as an institutionally patterned outcome and selective moral attention as the mechanism through which it is produced, this work extends research on corporate social irresponsibility, institutional theory, and organizational ethics. It redirects attention from how organizations respond to recognized harm toward the prior institutional processes through which harm becomes available for moral concern in the first place.

title: Managerial Ability and Employee Workplace Health and Safety
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between managerial ability to efficiently convert capital into revenue (which we refer to as “managerial ability”) and employee workplace health and safety violations. We document a positive
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between managerial ability to efficiently convert capital into revenue (which we refer to as “managerial ability”) and employee workplace health and safety violations. We document a positive association between managerial ability and employee workplace health and safety violations. This relation is more pronounced in firm environments with weaker labor unionization, and becomes weaker in more innovative firm environments, when executive compensation includes stronger employee workplace health and safety incentives and when CEOs have longer horizons. Collectively, these findings suggest that while higher managerial ability is associated with greater employee workplace health and safety violations, firm environments that emphasize stakeholder protections and longer‐term managerial horizons attenuate this relation. Finally, while employee workplace health and safety violations do not significantly affect short‐ to medium‐term financial performance, they appear to harm long‐term financial performance in firms led by high‐ability managers.

title: Navigating Stormy Waters: Strategic Responses to Regulatory Uncertainty in Sustainability Reporting
summary: ABSTRACT Regulatory uncertainty poses complex strategic challenges, but firms' responses to it are often reduced to a binary choice between compliance and noncompliance. This study examines how companies manage regulatory uncertainty when f
content: ABSTRACT Regulatory uncertainty poses complex strategic challenges, but firms' responses to it are often reduced to a binary choice between compliance and noncompliance. This study examines how companies manage regulatory uncertainty when facing changing sustainability reporting requirements, focusing on the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and its partial reversal under the Omnibus I package. Through a multiple‐case study of 35 German companies, we combine regulatory uncertainty with a dynamic capabilities lens to develop a typology of four strategic responses. We advance three arguments. First, firms' responses extend beyond compliance and noncompliance. Second, regulatory uncertainty is partly self‐induced, as the firms shaping the rules generate the uncertainty others must navigate. Third, regulatory relief falls unevenly, unsettling firms without prior reporting experience while others facing release continue building capabilities they may no longer need.

title: H-Beta supported molybdenum catalyst for the conversion of DME to LPG
summary: Molybdenum supported on a H-Beta 150 zeolite was studied in the conversion of dimethyl ether (DME) to a sustainable chemical equivalent for conventional liquified petroleum gas (LPG). Catalysts with varying Mo loadings (1 to 20 wt.-%) were
content: Molybdenum supported on a H-Beta 150 zeolite was studied in the conversion of dimethyl ether (DME) to a sustainable chemical equivalent for conventional liquified petroleum gas (LPG). Catalysts with varying Mo loadings (1 to 20 wt.-%) were compared to the bare zeolite and an Pd/H-Beta 150 catalyst. Low Mo loadings (1 and 5 wt.-%) enhance LPG selectivity and hydrogenation activity, while the higher loadings (10 and 20 wt.-%) induce pore blockage and reduce activity significantly. The 5 wt.-% Mo species/H-Beta 150 catalyst exhibit the best balance of high selectivity and moderate olefin to paraffin ratio. Operating conditions were evaluated and revealed that higher temperatures increase DME conversion but favoured CO, CO 2 , and methane formation. These findings suggest that Mo/H-Beta 150 catalysts provide a viable, cost-effective alternative to platinum group metal-based catalysts for the selective production of LPG from DME.

title: The modal tax wedge: credit denial, fuel exclusion and freight cost asymmetry in India
summary: India has invested heavily in rail freight capacity, including two dedicated freight corridors, yet road still carries two thirds of surface freight. This study aims to determine whether India’s indirect tax architecture is neutral across f
content: India has invested heavily in rail freight capacity, including two dedicated freight corridors, yet road still carries two thirds of surface freight. This study aims to determine whether India’s indirect tax architecture is neutral across freight modes, consignors and consignments, and on whom any departure from neutrality falls. The architecture is examined as an implicit modal policy operating through three channels: the rate and credit treatment of freight services, for carrier and consignor alike; the exclusion of diesel from the goods and services tax (GST); and the compliance burden of the e-way bill and detention regime. A modal tax wedge is derived and calibrated, and a mixed methods design combines a state-month panel of 3,588 observations from official e-way bill statistics (July 2018 to May 2026) with four documentary corpora and a spatial layer. Because e-way bills cover rail, air and vessel as well as road movement, the panel measures documented goods movement rather than road freight. The calibrated wedge is positive, at Rs 0.55 to 0.79 per tonne kilometre, so the architecture raises road costs relative to rail rather than favouring road; sensitivity analysis leaves its sign intact in all plausible configurations. The compliance burden ratio is regressive by construction, falling sevenfold between consignment values of Rs 60,000 and Rs 50 lakh at central parameters. Event-window estimates show documented movement growth concentrated in states with smaller average consignments but remain descriptive. The study establishes differential tax incidence but does not identify modal responses; the instruments involved are administratively adjustable.

title: Next-generation multifunctional silica-based nanocomposite films: Recent advances in fabrication, surface functionalization, emerging healthcare and environmental applications through AI/ML-driven design
summary: Multifunctional silica-based nanocomposite films are increasingly utilized in healthcare and environmental fields due to their high surface area, adjustable porosity, chemical stability, biocompatibility, and versatile surface chemistry. Th
content: Multifunctional silica-based nanocomposite films are increasingly utilized in healthcare and environmental fields due to their high surface area, adjustable porosity, chemical stability, biocompatibility, and versatile surface chemistry. These properties allow a single platform to perform diverse functions such as antimicrobial action, controlled drug delivery, biosensing, photocatalysis, pollutant adsorption, self-cleaning, and environmental monitoring. This review examines recent developments by analyzing the relationships among material design, fabrication methods, functionalization techniques, and application performance. It covers mesoporous silica nanoparticles, silica aerogels, core–shell structures, and hybrid silica systems, alongside polymeric and inorganic matrices that improve mechanical, biological, and catalytic properties. Major synthesis approaches, including sol–gel processing, electrospinning, dip coating, spin coating, layer-by-layer assembly, hydrothermal techniques, and green synthesis, are evaluated based on their ability to control structure, scale production, ensure reproducibility, and address sustainability. The review also considers surface functionalization, nanoparticle doping, composite formation, and stimuli-responsive design for governing adsorption, antimicrobial activity, photocatalytic efficiency, drug loading, and targeted therapeutic effects. Healthcare applications include drug delivery, wound healing, tissue engineering, antimicrobial coatings, biosensors, and cancer treatment. Environmental uses involve water purification, heavy-metal removal, organic pollutant degradation, air purification, food packaging, and environmental sensing. Persistent challenges pertain to nanoparticle aggregation, long-term stability, cytotoxicity, environmental risks, scalability, reproducibility, and regulatory issues. Other topics include biosafety, green and additive fabrication, and AI/ML-assisted design. Published models of silica-shell morphology and drug–silica affinity are used to identify the validation required for complete films.

title: Equivalent reconstruction and nonlinear contact mechanics of particle-adhered rough sealing interfaces
summary: Abstract Solid-particle adhesion is an important factor contributing to the degradation of sealing interfaces, particularly in particle-laden operating environments such as subsea pressure-retaining coring, offshore oil and gas drilling and
content: Abstract Solid-particle adhesion is an important factor contributing to the degradation of sealing interfaces, particularly in particle-laden operating environments such as subsea pressure-retaining coring, offshore oil and gas drilling and production, and pipeline transportation. In this study, an equivalent rough-surface reconstruction model incorporating particle adhesion and a three-dimensional finite-element method (FEM) contact model between the seal ring and the reconstructed particle-adhered surface are established. The effects of particle size and coverage on equivalent stress, contact pressure, real contact area, normal contact force, and sealing safety margin are investigated. The results show that the dominant asperities of the original rough surface primarily determine the locations of contact-pressure and equivalent-stress concentrations. Particle adhesion intensifies these local concentrations and results in a more nonuniform load distribution across the sealing interface. Particle size has a markedly greater influence on the interfacial contact state than particle coverage. For a particle size of 1.25 µm, the variations in both real contact area and normal contact force remain within 5%. When the particle size increases to 2.5 µm, the real contact area increases by approximately 9%, while the normal contact force increases by 8–14%. At 5 µm, both the normal contact force and average contact pressure increase by 15–25%. At a coverage of 10%, the safety-margin deviation generally remains below 0.03. For 2.5 µm particles, this deviation increases to approximately 0.09 with increasing coverage, whereas the 5 µm cases exhibit larger overall deviations. This study proposes a particle-adhered equivalent rough-surface reconstruction method that preserves the characteristics of the original rough surface and quantitatively evaluates the effects of particle size and coverage on the sealing contact state, providing a methodological basis for performance evaluation and structural optimization of sealing interfaces operating in particle-laden environments.

title: Single-cell mass accumulation reveals copiotrophic bacterial growth rates in native seawater
summary: A bstract The growth of marine microbial communities drives biogeochemical cycling of carbon and other elements, yet the growth rates of individual species within complex ocean ecosystems remain poorly understood. In particular, the coexist
content: A bstract The growth of marine microbial communities drives biogeochemical cycling of carbon and other elements, yet the growth rates of individual species within complex ocean ecosystems remain poorly understood. In particular, the coexistence of a large diversity of copiotrophic bacteria, which are capable of fast growth but typically remain at low abundance, has been interpreted as a feast or famine existence. Here we show that contrary to the notion of infrequent growth, Vibrio bacteria exhibited consistent growth rates in coastal ocean samples, despite representing only a small fraction of the total community. These observations were enabled by a suspended microchannel resonator (SMR), which we adapted to function as a single-cell chemostat. By maintaining a continuous supply of native seawater around each trapped cell, we prevented nutrient depletion and used the SMR’s high mass precision to resolve growth rates that are otherwise undetectable. Vibrio species displayed significantly larger cell mass and faster growth than other community members across samples collected at different temporal intervals from days to years. Surprisingly, their growth was consistently limited by carbon, contrary to the expectation that heterotrophic bacteria in the euphotic zone would be limited by nitrogen and phosphorus due to competition with algae. The correlation between cell mass and growth rate of Vibrionaceae in seawater followed established growth laws derived from laboratory conditions, suggesting that growth physiology observed in pure cultures is applicable to wild bacterial populations. Overall, our findings suggest that rare species may play a disproportionately large role in the marine carbon cycle, with rapid biomass turnover driven by a combination of high growth rates balanced by intense predation.

title: Agentic reinforcement learning empowers next-generation chemical language models for molecular design and synthesis
summary: Abstract Language models are revolutionizing the biochemistry domain, assisting scientists in drug design and chemical synthesis with high efficiency. Yet current approaches struggle between small language models prone to hallucination and
content: Abstract Language models are revolutionizing the biochemistry domain, assisting scientists in drug design and chemical synthesis with high efficiency. Yet current approaches struggle between small language models prone to hallucination and limited knowledge retention, and large cloud-based language models plagued by privacy risks and high inference costs. To bridge this gap, we introduce ChemCRAFT, a novel framework leveraging agentic reinforcement learning to decouple chemical reasoning from knowledge storage. Instead of forcing the model to memorize vast chemical data, our approach empowers the language model to interact with a sandbox for precise information retrieval. This externalization of knowledge allows a locally deployable small model to achieve superior performance while being highly token-efficient compared to traditional multi-agent systems. To enable small language models for agent-calling ability, we build an agentic trajectory construction pipeline and a comprehensive chemical-agent sandbox. Based on sandbox interactions, we constructed ChemToolDataset, the first large-scale chemical tool trajectory dataset. Simultaneously, we propose SMILES-GRPO to build a dense chemical reward function, promoting the model's ability to call chemical agents. Evaluations across diverse aspects of drug design show that ChemCRAFT outperforms current cloud-based LLMs in molecular structure analysis, molecular optimization, and synthesis pathway prediction, demonstrating that scientific reasoning is not solely an emergent ability of model scale, but a learnable policy of tool orchestration. Furthermore, assessments in real-world drug optimization scenarios, including fentanyl analog optimization and pro-inflammatory GSTO1 inhibitors optimization, reveal that ChemCRAFT generates optimization trajectories mirroring human experts, confirming its reliability as a scientific assistant. This work establishes a cost-effective and privacy-preserving paradigm for AI-aided chemistry, opening new avenues for accelerating molecular discovery with locally deployable agents.

title: Synthetic Data in MR Spectroscopy: Current Practices, Applications, and Considerations
summary: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inacces
content: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. This review provides a structured overview of current practices in synthetic MRS data generation, with emphasis on the physical, biochemical, and computational assumptions that underpin commonly used models. A decomposition of synthetic MRS data is presented in terms of core building blocks, including basis sets, signal formation models, and metabolite parameter distributions such as concentration and relaxation properties. This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics. Beyond single-voxel modeling, synthetic data generation across multiple MRS modalities is discussed, including functional MRS, diffusion-weighted MRS, and spectroscopic imaging, with emphasis on modality-specific challenges such as physiological variability, motion, and confounding signal contributions. The role of synthetic data in clinical and preclinical research, acquisition optimization, software validation, and emerging artificial intelligence applications is further examined, with particular attention to domain shift and representational realism. Current practices in validation, reporting standards, and data accessibility are also reviewed, and key gaps limiting reproducibility and interoperability across studies are identified. Overall, this work provides a unified conceptual framework for synthetic MRS data generation, clarifies underlying assumptions across modeling choices, and outlines open challenges toward improving realism, standardization, and utility in both methodological and translational applications. Conducted by the MRS Synthetic Data Working Group under the Code & Data Sharing Committee of the MRS Study Group of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine (ISMRM), this review encompasses the existing literature, supplemented by the collective experience and in-house methodologies of its contributors, providing a community perspective that extends beyond the published record.

title: Interplay of valley, orbital, spin, and layer degrees of freedom in Ta 2 CS 2 MXene
summary: We show that the MXene Ta$_2$CS$_2$ provides an excellent platform for hosting multiple coupled degrees of freedom, viz., valley, spin, orbital, and layer. The interplay among these degrees of freedom gives rise to a range of intriguing pro
content: We show that the MXene Ta$_2$CS$_2$ provides an excellent platform for hosting multiple coupled degrees of freedom, viz., valley, spin, orbital, and layer. The interplay among these degrees of freedom gives rise to a range of intriguing properties in reciprocal space, including valley-orbital and orbital-layer coupling. In the presence of spin-orbit interaction, these couplings lead to valley-dependent and layer-dependent spin splitting of the electronic bands. We further show that the intrinsic electric polarization in Ta$_2$CS$_2$ introduces an additional tuning parameter, enabling control over these coupled degrees of freedom and resulting in switchable valley-dependent orbital moments and Zeeman-like spin splitting. We demonstrate that these nontrivial orbital and spin textures manifest in the orbital and spin Hall effects, respectively. Our results establish noncentrosymmetric MXenes as a promising platform for exploring the interplay among multiple degrees of freedom, their tunability, and the resulting orbital and spin transport phenomena in these two-dimensional materials, thereby paving the way for next-generation spin-orbitronic devices.

title: Tunable electronic and transport properties of biphenylene via fluorination and disorder
summary: Biphenylene (BPN) network is a newly synthesized 2D carbon allotrope hosting anisotropic Dirac electronic states. Here, we investigate how fluorination and correlated chemical disorder modify the electronic structure and charge transport of
content: Biphenylene (BPN) network is a newly synthesized 2D carbon allotrope hosting anisotropic Dirac electronic states. Here, we investigate how fluorination and correlated chemical disorder modify the electronic structure and charge transport of fluorinated biphenylene (F/BPN) using density functional theory, Wannier-based tight-biding Hamiltonian, and quantum transport simulations. We show that fluorination reshapes the transport response of BPN, producing concentration-dependent anisotropic conduction regimes. For pristine and ordered fluorinated systems, we identified the emergence of negative differential resistance (NDR) and a bias-induced inversion of the preferred transport direction, from armchair to zigzag and vice versa. In contrast, disorder suppresses the NDR, driving the system toward an approximately Ohmic transport regime. At high fluorine coverage, we further observed a nonmonotonic dependence of the armchair current on adatom concentration, which we attribute to the formation of correlated quasi-linear fluor conformation that promote armchair-oriented C-$π$ transport channels while simultaneously suppressing transport along the zigzag direction. Our results demonstrate that correlated fluorination can be used as an active mechanism to engineer electronic transport.

title: Dispersionless Range-Separated Hybrid Meta-GGA Functional
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Abstract We present a new (nearly) dispersionless, range-separated hybrid meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) density-functional theory (DFT) approach, dlωB97M, augmented with theDas20-mod dispersion function (a modification
content: Abstract We present a new (nearly) dispersionless, range-separated hybrid meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) density-functional theory (DFT) approach, dlωB97M, augmented with theDas20-mod dispersion function (a modification of Das20 [J. Phys. Chem. A, 125:1787, 2021]), resulting in the dlωB97M+Das20-mod method. The novelty of the new method is the introduction of a multiplicative factor gradually switching off Das20 at intermolecular separations shorter than the van der Waals (vdW) minimum, the region where semilocal density-functional approximations (DFAs) start to recover dispersion interactions.Das20-mod still accurately approximates the true dispersion energies of most dimers at vdW minima and larger separations so that dlωB97M is dispersionless in this region, but not for shorter separations. We have tested the performance of dlωB97M+Das20-mod against a suite of published DFT+D methods across a diverse set of benchmark intermolecular interaction energies. Our results demonstrate that dlωB97M+Das20-mod delivers consistently reliable predictions, with accuracy superior to that of the best published DFT+D methods. Since the dlωB97M contribution includes only the physical components of interaction energy that a semilocal DFA can recover and Das20-mod approximates true dispersion energy except at very short separations, dlωB97M+Das20-mod is more appealing from a physical point of view than most DFT+D approaches. It also allows meaningful energy decomposition analysis, as the fraction of dispersion energy recovered by dlωB97M is known at all intermolecular separations. Thus, taking into account its accuracy, dlωB97M+Das20-mod can be recommended for modeling intermolecular interactions between closed-shell molecules (note that it is not designed to model reactive processes).

title: Cannibalism-inspired biomimetic nanovesicles achieve boosted tumor targeting capacity via senescence-induced membrane remodeling
summary: Conventional biomimetic tumor-targeting carriers are hindered by insufficient target molecule density, unstable intercellular adhesion, and complex modification requirements. Inspired by cell cannibalism phenotype of senescent tumor cells,
content: Conventional biomimetic tumor-targeting carriers are hindered by insufficient target molecule density, unstable intercellular adhesion, and complex modification requirements. Inspired by cell cannibalism phenotype of senescent tumor cells, we developed senescent tumor cell membrane nanovesicles (STCM-NVs) that utilize senescence-induced cell membrane remodeling strategy to amplify native targeting capacity. We found that senescence induction achieves dual remodeling of tumor cell membranes: molecularly, it upregulates the expression of cell adhesion molecules and exposes multiple targeting sites to enhance STCM-NVs tumor recognition; morphologically, it promotes the formation of dense filopodia to stabilize STCM-NVs-target cells adhesion and prevent shear stress-mediated off-target detachment during systemic circulation. In vitro, STCM-NVs showed a 3.3-fold higher targeting affinity index than non-senescent tumor cell membrane-NVs (HTCM-NVs). In vivo, based on tumor-to-liver fluorescence intensity ratios, STCM-NVs achieved more than 6-fold improvement in tumor-targeting capacity relative to HTCM-NVs. Moreover, STCM-NVs also exhibited superior tumor-accumulation kinetics featuring more rapid tumor uptake, an earlier accumulation peak, and prolonged intratumoral retention. After loading with a therapeutic agent, STCM-NVs significantly increased the tumor inhibition rate from 71.68% (for HTCM-NVs) to 90.74% in an orthotopic breast cancer mouse model. Further mechanistic studies revealed that Fibronectin-1 and Collagens serve as the core targeting molecule and internalization mediators, respectively, which promote efficient caveolae-dependent cellular uptake through F-actin reorganization. Overall, this study establishes a mechanistic foundation for using cellular physiological phenotypes to enhance innate biological processes and offers a translatable strategy for targeted therapies. Tumor cell membrane targeting is dynamically modulated by cellular phenotype, instead of a static property. Senescence‑induced membrane remodeling upregulates adhesion molecules and induces filopodia formation. Senescent breast tumor cell membrane nanovesicles retain remodeling phenotypes with superior tumor targeting, enhanced cell adhesion, and efficient internalization. Fibronectin-1, Collagen, and F‑actin cooperate to mediate tumor recognition, internalization, and trafficking for effective drug delivery.

title: Accelerating Periodic Coupled Cluster and Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theories With Frozen Natural Orbitals
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Abstract We present a unified frozen natural orbital (FNO) framework for periodic Gaussian-orbital post-Hartree–Fock calculations with explicit k-point sampling. The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-speci
content: Abstract We present a unified frozen natural orbital (FNO) framework for periodic Gaussian-orbital post-Hartree–Fock calculations with explicit k-point sampling. The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-specific (SS-FNO) and state-averaged (SA-FNO) variants constructed from perturbative one-particle density matrices. We implement these approximations for periodic Möller–Plesset perturbation theory, algebraic diagrammatic construction, and equation-of-motion coupled cluster methods in the PySCF software package and benchmark them for correlation energies, equations of state, fundamental band gaps, and quasiparticle band structures of semiconductors and insulators. FNO truncation reproduces canonical results with small errors while substantially reducing computational cost. SS-FNO enables accurate large-basis band gap calculations, including quadruple-ζ results, whereas SA-FNO efficiently compresses the virtual space for multistate band-structure calculations. Combined with basis-set and thermodynamic-limit extrapolations, the framework provides a practical route to high-accuracy correlated calculations in periodic systems.

title: Flash Communication: On-Complex Assembly of Organic Azide Ligands
summary: Abstract Organic azides can serve as precursors to reactive metal nitrenes. Transition metal complexes of organic azide ligands are typically prepared by coordination of presynthesized organic azides to appropriate metal complexes. Here, we
content: Abstract Organic azides can serve as precursors to reactive metal nitrenes. Transition metal complexes of organic azide ligands are typically prepared by coordination of presynthesized organic azides to appropriate metal complexes. Here, we report on-complex assembly of organic azides by alkylation of metal complexes featuring inorganic azide ligands. This strategy, which we demonstrate in the context of Rh2 complexes, avoids isolation and handling of organic azides and thus provides access to complexes of volatile, potentially explosive organic azide ligands.

title: Heteroepitaxial single-crystal diamond on sapphire: a review
summary: Abstract Heteroepitaxial growth of single-crystal diamond on sapphire substrates is a key technical route toward large-size, high-quality diamond wafers. This paper systematically reviews the recent research progress in the preparation of I
content: Abstract Heteroepitaxial growth of single-crystal diamond on sapphire substrates is a key technical route toward large-size, high-quality diamond wafers. This paper systematically reviews the recent research progress in the preparation of Ir/sapphire composite substrates, heteroepitaxial growth of (001) and (111) oriented diamond, stress and defect control strategies, and device applications. Studies have shown that by optimizing the off-cut angle of sapphire substrates, annealing processes, and Ir deposition conditions, the crystal orientation of Ir films can be effectively regulated, thereby achieving the epitaxial growth of high-quality diamond. In particular, methods such as microneedle structures, Pd buffer layers, and SiO 2 nanosphere interlayers have significantly reduced the thermal mismatch stress and dislocation density, and free-standing single-crystal diamond films with a size of 2 inch or even larger have been successfully obtained. In terms of device applications, MOSFETs and Schottky barrier diodes based on heteroepitaxial diamond have demonstrated high breakdown voltage and high current density, proving their potential in the fields of power electronics and ultraviolet detection. Despite this progress, the control of twinning in (111)-oriented diamond, the alleviation of interfacial stress, and the uniformity over large dimensions remain central challenges for future research.

title: Hyper-cross-linked microporous polymers (HCPs): preparation and methane storage applications
summary: Global warming, pollution, energy shortages and depletion are major threats facing the world today. A critical step in addressing these environmental and energy challenges is the transition from conventional fossil fuels, such as oil and co
content: Global warming, pollution, energy shortages and depletion are major threats facing the world today. A critical step in addressing these environmental and energy challenges is the transition from conventional fossil fuels, such as oil and coal, to clean and sustainable green energy sources. Natural gas, composed primarily of methane, stands out as an economical, efficient and low-carbon transition fuel. However, storage and transportation of natural gas pose cost and safety concerns. To address these issues, adsorbed natural gas (ANG) technology has emerged as a highly desirable alternative for methane storage. Hyper-cross-linked polymers (HCPs) offer significant advantages such as high porosity, tunable pore size, diverse synthetic strategies, and robust structural stability, making them promising for practical applications in methane storage. This review discusses the current progress in structural design and preparation of HCPs, driven by the need for improved methane storage capacities. The discussion not only highlights recent research advances but also looks ahead to the remaining challenges and future directions for the development of HCPs in the pursuit of practical methane storage.

title: Energy Conserving Variational Dynamics with Gaussian Wavepackets in the Nonadiabatic Regime
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract We present a theoretical framework for a “trajectory”-driven nonadiabatic dynamics that generalizes the variational Gaussian wavepacket approach to dynamics on multiple diabatic states. By applying the time-dependent variational pr
content: Abstract We present a theoretical framework for a “trajectory”-driven nonadiabatic dynamics that generalizes the variational Gaussian wavepacket approach to dynamics on multiple diabatic states. By applying the time-dependent variational principle to a single Gaussian wavepacket per state, we obtain a set of coupled equations for the Gaussian center and width parameters that include terms arising from the coupling potential. We investigate the role of these terms as they change the Gaussian time evolution and of the initial conditions on the wave function for several standard benchmarks of nonadiabatic dynamics, including a three-state and a two-dimensional model. The state populations obtained with the fully variational Gaussian dynamics is found in close agreement with exact quantum results. Finally, we demonstrate that the use of the Gaussian wave function in nonadiabatic dynamics preserves the symplecticity of the variational space, which ensures the energy conservation and minimization of error when solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.

title: Good's buffers accelerate interfacial proton transfer kinetics
summary: The Good's buffers HEPES, TAPSO, and Tris are shown to increase proton transfer (PT) kinetics in a broadly important and benchmark model reaction: the protonation of a metal hydroxo to yield the aquo complex, Ru II -OH + H + → Ru II -OH 2 .
content: The Good's buffers HEPES, TAPSO, and Tris are shown to increase proton transfer (PT) kinetics in a broadly important and benchmark model reaction: the protonation of a metal hydroxo to yield the aquo complex, Ru II -OH + H + → Ru II -OH 2 .

title: Fringing electric fields probe shear-induced electrical anisotropy in carbon black suspensions
summary: Probing electronic transport in dense suspensions of metallic or semiconducting nanoparticles in flow is an emergent field of soft matter where there is strong coupling between flow-induced microstructure and electronic behaviour. In carbon
content: Probing electronic transport in dense suspensions of metallic or semiconducting nanoparticles in flow is an emergent field of soft matter where there is strong coupling between flow-induced microstructure and electronic behaviour. In carbon black suspensions, shear induces microstructural anisotropy in the weak flow regime due to strong attractive potential between particles that causes secondary structures to form and, under certain conditions, form vorticity aligned flocs. These structures can be reorganized by tuning the imposed stress through a change in shear. Using electrodes designed to exploit fringing field effects, we probe the electrical transport of carbon black secondary structures along all three flow directions across different flow regimes. We find enhanced conductivity in the vorticity direction and evidence of a metal-insulator transition with decreasing shear rate, indicating secondary structures aligning along this orientation.

title: Innovative contactless dual-coupled microwave sensor for non-invasive blood glucose monitoring
summary: Abstract In this paper, a novel non-invasive blood glucose monitoring system based on microwave sensing using a compact, contactless and sensitive dual-coupled sensor configuration is proposed. The proposed sensor consists of two electromag
content: Abstract In this paper, a novel non-invasive blood glucose monitoring system based on microwave sensing using a compact, contactless and sensitive dual-coupled sensor configuration is proposed. The proposed sensor consists of two electromagnetically coupled resonators, configured as a bandpass filter centered around 2.2 GHz. The sensor is fabricated on a 40 × 40 mm 2 Rogers RO3003C substrate with a 20 mm gap between the resonators to accommodate different finger sizes and incorporates a dedicated mechanical isolation structure to minimize measurement variability caused by direct contact, applied pressure, and positioning uncertainty. The operation of the sensor is based on near-field electromagnetic coupling between the resonators and biological tissue, enabling detection of glucose-correlated variations in dielectric properties without direct skin contact. The experimental trials for glucose concentrations from 76 to 201 mg/dL showed a monotonic decrease in the transmission coefficient with increasing glucose concentration with a sensitivity of 0.031 dB/mg/dL and frequency shift sensitivity of 0.41 MHz/mg/dL. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed sensor and indicate the feasibility of sensitive contactless glucose monitoring using a microwave-based sensor.

title: Coupled carbon-nitrogen dynamics and soil stabilization under perennial alley cover cropping in raspberry planting
summary: Agriculture faces the dual challenge of sustaining productivity and mitigating climate change through soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. The current management practice in perennial raspberry production in the Fraser Valley, British C
content: Agriculture faces the dual challenge of sustaining productivity and mitigating climate change through soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. The current management practice in perennial raspberry production in the Fraser Valley, British Columbia, Canada, pre-disposes the soil to continual degradation via incessant tillage of the alleys with no C input. Therefore, a regenerative approach is critical for restoring SOC and structural stability. The objective of this study was to determine how specific cover crops and selected mixtures influence the reorganization of soil organic matter fractions and the distribution of C and nitrogen (N) across water-stable aggregates and Silt+Clay size fraction after eight years of production. Five cover crop treatments including Red Clover (RCl, Trifolium pratense ), Ryegrass (RG, Lolium multiflorum ), RCl+RG mixture, Mustard+RCl+RG (Mustard, Mu, Brassica juncea ) mixture, and Radish+RCl+RG (Radish, Ra, Raphanus sativus ) mixture were compared with a tilled Control treatment. Results showed that alley cover cropping significantly improved soil structural stability by increasing the macroaggregates (2000-250 µm) from 24.67% in the tilled Control to 38.61% under RG monoculture and RCl+RG mixture. Conversely, mesoaggregates (250-53 µm) decreased from 51.72% in the tilled Control to 41.56% under RCl+RG, but the effect was not significant. The mean weight diameter (MWD) improved from 360.01 µm in the tilled Control to a peak of 507.14 µm in the RCl+RG mixture. This mixture also achieved the highest concentration of C (24.23 g kg⁻¹) and N (2.09 g kg⁻¹) when compared to other treatments. Soil C stabilization pathways were highly treatment-specific: RCl+RG primarily enhanced water-stable aggregate associated C concentration (2.02%) compared with the tilled Control (1.49%). In contrast, only RG improved C content, exhibiting the highest C and N concentrations associated with Silt+Clay size fraction (3.92% C and 0.41% N). In conclusion, eight years of alley cover cropping effectively changed soil structure and established diverse C stabilization pathways. These findings underscore the importance of functional species complementarity of cover crops for enhancing soil C concentrations, providing a mechanistic framework to climate-resilient perennial agroecosystems in cool-temperate regions.

title: Surface Hardness Improvement of SUS430 Stainless Steel by Solution Nitriding and Nitrocarburizing
source: Journal of Metals Materials and Minerals
summary: This research aims to study the effect of the gas nitrocarburizing process on surface hardness and microstructural changes of ferritic stainless steel SUS430 (0.09% C and 16.44% Cr). The specimens were initially prepared by a solution nitri
content: This research aims to study the effect of the gas nitrocarburizing process on surface hardness and microstructural changes of ferritic stainless steel SUS430 (0.09% C and 16.44% Cr). The specimens were initially prepared by a solution nitriding process at 1050 °C for 90 minutes, followed by cooling with nitrogen gas. After that, they were subjected to a gas nitrocarburizing process at 570 °C for 180 minutes. The results show that this process can significantly improve the surface hardness, to a maximum hardness of 1341 HV, which is an increase of 774 HV compared to the specimen treated only by solution nitriding. The treatment at 1050 °C led to the formation of a martensitic structure near the surface, which has high hardness and enhances the diffusion ability of nitrogen and carbon during the subsequent process. This diffusion resulted in the formation of a compound layer, including Fe2-3N, Fe4N, and CrN, along with a uniform diffusion zone. These are the key mechanisms responsible for the significant increase in surface hardness. The study indicates that the combination of solution nitriding and gas nitrocarburizing is an effective approach to improve the surface hardness of SUS430 stainless steel and shows high potential for industrial applications requiring wear and friction resistance.

title: Skin microbiota–T-cell immune crosstalk and disease progression in stasis dermatitis: from chronic inflammation to venous ulceration
summary: Stasis dermatitis (SD) is an inflammatory skin disorder associated with chronic venous disease, and some patients progress to venous leg ulcers (VLUs). In addition to persistent venous hypertension, interactions among the skin microbiota, T
content: Stasis dermatitis (SD) is an inflammatory skin disorder associated with chronic venous disease, and some patients progress to venous leg ulcers (VLUs). In addition to persistent venous hypertension, interactions among the skin microbiota, T-cell immunity, barrier injury, and the tissue microenvironment may be involved in disease chronicity. This review integrates evidence from SD, chronic venous disease, VLU, and related skin and wound studies, focusing on bidirectional crosstalk between the skin microbiota and T-cell immunity. Microbial antigens, virulence factors, metabolites, and extracellular vesicles can regulate local T-cell responses, while T cells can reciprocally shape the microbial niche by influencing antimicrobial defense, the skin barrier, and tissue repair. Based on current evidence, we further propose a stage-specific model of progression from SD to VLU, in which venous hypertension and barrier injury, chronic inflammation and tissue remodeling, and persistent microbial colonization, biofilms, and repair failure successively become predominant. Future longitudinal and multi-omics studies are needed to clarify the causal roles of microbe–immune interactions and inform patient stratification and precision interventions.

title: Patterns of soil organic carbon, nutrients, and vegetation traits along a tidal elevation gradient in subtropical artificial mangroves
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Tidal elevation is a key environmental factor influencing planted mangrove growth and soil processes. However, many previous studies have focused on surface soil organic carbon (SOC) or single nutrient indicators, and it remains unclear whe
content: Tidal elevation is a key environmental factor influencing planted mangrove growth and soil processes. However, many previous studies have focused on surface soil organic carbon (SOC) or single nutrient indicators, and it remains unclear whether tidal elevation is consistently associated with soil carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) concentrations and stocks throughout the 0–100 cm profile in young Kandelia obovata plantations, especially across multiple coastal bays. This study examined vegetation attributes and soil C, N, and P concentrations and stocks along a tidal elevation gradient in approximately 8-year-old K. obovata plantations across three coastal bays in Wenzhou, Zhejiang, China. Vegetation attributes, soil physicochemical properties, and SOC, total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) concentrations and stocks were quantified within the 0–100 cm soil profile. In models accounting for non-independence at the plot scale and variability at the sampling point scale, elevation and soil depth were significantly correlated with soil organic carbon (SOC), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) concentrations ( P < 0.05). Across the 0–100 cm profile, SOC stocks were significantly higher at high elevation (HE) than at low elevation (LE) ( P < 0.05), whereas middle elevation (ME) showed intermediate values and did not differ significantly from HE or LE. TN and TP stocks did not differ significantly among elevation groups, indicating contrasting patterns between soil carbon and nutrient pools along the elevation gradient. Higher elevation plots were also associated with greater vegetation biomass and larger root C and N pools. Overall, tidal elevation was more strongly associated with vegetation and carbon-related soil variables than with TN and TP stocks in these 8-year-old plantations. These findings suggest that soil carbon indicators may be useful for monitoring planted mangrove dynamics and for informing site selection in high-latitude coastal ecosystems.

title: An adaptive spatio-temporal framework for carbon-aware and privacy-preserving DNN partitioning
summary: Introduction Choosing where to split a deep neural network (DNN) between device and cloud requires balancing latency, carbon emissions, privacy and device thermal state, which existing partitioning methods rarely address jointly. Methods We
content: Introduction Choosing where to split a deep neural network (DNN) between device and cloud requires balancing latency, carbon emissions, privacy and device thermal state, which existing partitioning methods rarely address jointly. Methods We propose GreenSplit, an adaptive spatio-temporal framework that selects the split layer and cloud region by minimising a normalised four-term cost under a hard privacy exclusion zone, with an Adaptive Weight Controller (AWC), current and forecast carbon intensity, Laplace noise on transmitted activations, a thermal-battery model, and a dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) safeguard. We evaluated it in simulation on MobileNetV2 across three cloud regions (200 sustained-load trials), extended the decision model to ResNet-50, ViT-Base and the CLIP ViT-B/32 image encoder, and tested the noise mechanism on a pretrained ImageNet MobileNetV2 with 1,000 real images. Results Under our assumed energy constants, offloading a lightweight CNN is carbon-costly (5.8–6.7 × on-device carbon), so the framework keeps MobileNetV2 local; it then behaves as local execution with DVFS, emitting 66.0% of the carbon of unmanaged local execution with no privacy-zone violations (4% for baselines without the zone). Its 32.5% throttle rate at nominal thermal parameters is not robust (0–100% over plausible parameters), although DVFS lowers throttling in every draw. Laplace noise at operating budgets (ϵ r ≤ 10 leaves the cloud classifying at chance, while accuracy-preserving budgets ( ϵ r ≈ 3 × 1 0 4 –3 × 10 5 ) allow perfect re-identification among 1,000 images and give a vacuous differential-privacy bound. The AWC's benefit in its original scenario does not transfer to unseen disturbances in its original min–max form; a fixed-scale variant is stable but gives only a modest gain and no thermal benefit. Discussion The hard exclusion zone, not the noise, provides utility-preserving protection. All results are simulated; validation on physical devices is required.

title: Glyphosate residues in forest plantation soils: distribution, persistence, and environmental risk in Thathe Vondo, South Africa
summary: Abstract Glyphosate-based herbicides are widely used in commercial forest plantations to suppress competing vegetation, yet concerns persist regarding their persistence in soil, environmental contamination, and potential risks to human heal
content: Abstract Glyphosate-based herbicides are widely used in commercial forest plantations to suppress competing vegetation, yet concerns persist regarding their persistence in soil, environmental contamination, and potential risks to human health. This study assessed the spatial distribution, seasonal variation, and associated human health risk of glyphosate and its main metabolite, aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA), in soils adjacent to water bodies in the Thathe Vondo Forest Plantation, Limpopo Province, South Africa. Soils were collected from 16 sampling sites in the wet and dry seasons at distances of 0, 50, 100, and 150 m from surface waters. Glyphosate and AMPA were determined by gas chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (GC–MS/MS) after solid-phase extraction and derivatization with trifluoroacetic anhydride and 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol. Glyphosate was detected at all sites, with site mean concentrations ranging from 2.22 to 3.94 µg g −1 , whereas AMPA was below the limit of detection (< 0.1 µg g −1 ) in all samples, suggesting limited degradation and persistence of the parent compound in plantation soils. A three-way factorial analysis of variance (ANOVA) showed a significant effect of sampling site on glyphosate concentrations ( F 15,128 = 2.306, p = 0.006), whereas season, distance, and all interaction effects were not significant ( p > 0.05). Tukey’s honestly significant difference (HSD) test showed that concentrations at the Tshirovha River were significantly higher than those at the lowest-ranked sites, while most sites had statistically similar intermediate concentrations. Mean seasonal concentrations were similar (~ 3.1 µg g −1 in the dry season and ~ 3.0 µg g −1 in the wet season), although variability was higher in the wet season. A human health risk assessment based on standard US EPA exposure models indicated negligible non-carcinogenic risk for both adults and children: hazard indices combining incidental soil ingestion and dermal contact ranged from 3.78 × 10 −5 to 6.72 × 10 −5 for adults and from 3.51 × 10 −4 to 6.23 × 10 −4 for children, far below the threshold of 1, with ingestion as the dominant pathway and children having approximately nine-fold higher indices than adults. These findings indicate that site-specific spatial variability is the primary driver of glyphosate distribution in plantation soils and highlight the need for routine soil monitoring, assessment of effects on forest biota, and careful management of herbicide use.

title: Coupled Mechanisms of Surrounding Rock Stability and Spontaneous Combustion Control in Gob-Side Entry Retaining under Fully Mechanized Top Coal Caving
