Comparing the SHP with different CR mixtures provided direct information on how CR concentration modifies water retention and conductivity, comparing pre- and post-incubation measurements provided information about the temporal dynamics of CR effects on SHP. Compared to the control, water retention increased systematically by 2 vol % to 5 vol % across the CR-soil mixtures from saturation to field capacity while the unsaturated hydraulic conductivity was slightly reduced. However, biodegradation of CR started immediately after harvest especially for shoot residues, simultaneously altering residue carbon and nitrogen concentrations. During the experimental time of 31 d for CR-soil mixtures and of 48 d for 100 % CR layers, carbon mass exponentially decreased about 46 %–50 % in 100 % CR layers, 7 %–15 % in root-soil mixtures and 21 %–27 % in shoot–soil mixtures. Despite this degradation, a positive effect on the soil water retention curve persisted, with water content increasing on average by 1.5 vol % per gram of carbon in a kilogram of soil at satu

title: A climatological description of atmospheric CO 2 concentrations
summary: At regional scales, atmospheric CO 2 concentrations show (i) a global trend, (ii) a seasonal cycle that varies with location and altitude and (iii) inter-annual and synoptic variability. The CO 2 atmospheric inversion of the Copernicus Atmo
content: At regional scales, atmospheric CO 2 concentrations show (i) a global trend, (ii) a seasonal cycle that varies with location and altitude and (iii) inter-annual and synoptic variability. The CO 2 atmospheric inversion of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) constrained by surface measurements of the gas concentration provides a 4D (spatial+time) description of the CO 2 mixing ratio. A comparison of the CAMS modelling against AirCore profiles acquired over France and the USA indicates an accuracy on the order of 1 ppm (CO 2 ) at most levels in the atmosphere with larger errors close to the surface. Evaluation of the total column against the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) observations shows a standard deviation of less than 1 ppm over most sites. In this paper, we attempt a simple description of the concentration time series where the trend is provided by the Mauna Loa measurement dataset and the seasonal cycle is adjusted using annual and semi-annual harmonics. Most of the atmospheric concentration variability is captured by this simple modelling. Over France, the differences between simulated concentrations and in-situ (AirCore) measurements are on the order of 1.5 ppm over the free troposphere and higher. The evaluation against column concentration retrievals from TCCON indicates typical errors on the order of 1 ppm for the climatological fit. The climatological product is updated in near-real time with the Mauna Loa measurements and may therefore be used as prior information for ground-based and satellite-based remote sensing of the CO 2 profile or the column-averaged dry air mole fraction of CO 2 (XCO 2 ). Besides, the deviations between the full CAMS modelling and the climatological fit are used to compute realistic vertical variance-covariance matrices for each of the model grid cells.

title: Photochemical mechanism–dependent ozone formation and precursor sensitivity under varying NO x conditions
summary: Photochemical mechanisms are core components of air quality models, yet differences among them can introduce substantial uncertainty in tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) simulations. We compared three mechanisms (CB06, SAPRC07, and RACM2) using CMA
content: Photochemical mechanisms are core components of air quality models, yet differences among them can introduce substantial uncertainty in tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) simulations. We compared three mechanisms (CB06, SAPRC07, and RACM2) using CMAQ during an O 3 pollution episode in Chengdu, China. A customized volatile organic compound (VOC) emission inventory was developed for RACM2. RACM2 and SAPRC07 produced comparable O 3 levels (94.8–96.1 ppbv) with better performance at high-NO x urban site, whereas CB06 simulated lower O 3 (∼80 ppbv) and performed better at low-NO x site. Inter-mechanistic differences in O 3 formation were mainly associated with RO 2 +NO reactions, consistent with larger variability in RO 2 than in HO 2 , while O 3 loss differences mainly arose from OH+NO 2 and O 3 +alkene reactions. Differences in primary RO x production were most evident in carbonyl photolysis, whereas termination differences mainly involved RONO 2 formation and peroxy-radical self- and cross-reactions. Mechanism-dependent discrepancies were more pronounced at high-NO x urban site. Despite these discrepancies, the three mechanisms exhibited a broadly consistent photochemical framework, with O 3 formation dominated by RO 2 +NO and RO x termination shifting from NO x -dependent pathways at high-NO x urban site toward peroxy-radical reactions at low-NO x suburban site. Sensitivity analysis showed O 3 was most sensitive to anthropogenic aromatics and alkenes at urban site and relatively more sensitive to biogenic VOCs at suburban site, although response magnitudes remained mechanism dependent. These findings demonstrate that mechanism choice substantially affects O 3 formation and precursor sensitivities, emphasizing the need for multi-mechanism approaches to improve model reliability and support emission control strategies.

title: UCLCHEM 4.0: An open source gas-grain astrochemistry simulation framework
summary: Abstract Astrochemical modelling is a key tool for interpreting the formation and destruction of molecules in the interstellar medium, complementing the increasingly detailed observations from modern facilities. UCLCHEM is a gas-grain astro
content: Abstract Astrochemical modelling is a key tool for interpreting the formation and destruction of molecules in the interstellar medium, complementing the increasingly detailed observations from modern facilities. UCLCHEM is a gas-grain astrochemical modelling framework that computes the chemical evolution of a parcel of gas and dust under a time-dependent physical description. This description can be user-defined, for example when post-processing hydrodynamical simulations, or one of the included parametrizations of cloud collapse, protostellar cores and shocks, covering scenarios ranging from from extragalactic environments to protoplanetary disks. The chemistry is solved with a rate-equation formalism in three phases (gas, surface and bulk ice), which are coupled through freeze-out, thermal and non-thermal desorption, and a geometrical treatment of the growth and shrinkage of the ice surface and bulk. This release adds an object-oriented Python interface, a description of the upgrade from two to three phases, and expanded support for post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and user-defined parametrizations. We give an overview of the physics and chemistry included in UCLCHEM, the inner workings of the solver, and the programming interface.

title: Anchoring Sites for Gold in Zeolites and Ethanol Selective Oxidation Over Zeolite‐Supported Gold Catalysts
summary: ABSTRACT Anchoring sites for gold in zeolites and selective oxidation of ethanol with gas‐phase oxygen over zeolite‐supported Au catalysts were studied experimentally and computationally by evaluating effects of the Au loading, zeolite Si/A
content: ABSTRACT Anchoring sites for gold in zeolites and selective oxidation of ethanol with gas‐phase oxygen over zeolite‐supported Au catalysts were studied experimentally and computationally by evaluating effects of the Au loading, zeolite Si/Al ratio and zeolite topology for ZSM‐5, mordenite and faujasite. Additional comparisons were made with silicalite‐1, silica and silica‐alumina. Anchoring structures and stability of Au particles on various surface sites were determined. Although Au particles anchor similarly by displacing H atoms from either Al sites in the zeolite framework or from silanol groups on the external surface of zeolites and amorphous materials, Au particles are more stable on Al sites in the zeolite framework, resulting in a higher Au dispersion and greater stability. Moreover, Au particles are more stable by anchoring on double Al‐atom framework sites, which become more abundant at lower Si/Al zeolite ratios, than on single Al‐atom framework sites. The reaction rate for Au supported on ZSM‐5 is 6 times higher than that on silicalite‐1 without Al sites and 29 times higher than that on amorphous silica. The zeolite Al sites unoccupied by Au adsorb ethanol but do not serve as oxidation catalytic sites. Therefore, Au and Al do not act as two separate active sites.

title: Polymorph Engineering of the Layered Rare‐Earth Magnet GdAlGe
summary: ABSTRACT The recent advances in research on layered magnets have established them as invaluable materials for spintronic applications and precursors to 2D magnets. The problem is that the number of such materials available for experimentati
content: ABSTRACT The recent advances in research on layered magnets have established them as invaluable materials for spintronic applications and precursors to 2D magnets. The problem is that the number of such materials available for experimentation is still low. To tackle the problem, one may employ phase engineering; in particular, the interplay between the phase stability and dimensionality provides great opportunities for design of layered magnets. Here, this interrelation is harnessed to produce epitaxial films of an overlooked layered polymorph of GdAlGe. The compound is formed by alternating triangular Gd and honeycomb AlGe lattices. It is stable in ultrathin films, up to 5 monolayers. In thicker films, an additional unwanted phase emerges. The structural quality of the ultrathin films is witnessed by electron and X‐ray diffraction as well as electron microscopy. Magnetization measurements detect an anisotropic ferromagnetic state. The GdAlGe magnetism is corroborated by a study of electron transport revealing the anomalous Hall effect and negative magnetoresistance. The present study can serve as a blueprint for design of layered magnets via polymorph engineering.

title: Yarrowia lipolytica as a phosphate-solubilizing yeast for plant growth promotion
summary: Phosphorus (P) availability is a major constraint to crop production in highly weathered tropical soils, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to improve P use efficiency. This study evaluated the plant growth-promoting potenti
content: Phosphorus (P) availability is a major constraint to crop production in highly weathered tropical soils, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to improve P use efficiency. This study evaluated the plant growth-promoting potential of Yarrowia lipolytica through in vitro characterization and greenhouse experiments. The yeast exhibited high calcium phosphate solubilization (70.18%), lower solubilization of iron and aluminum phosphates, and the ability to release soluble P in phytate-containing medium (6.75 mg P L − 1 ). Culture medium acidification and acid and alkaline phosphatase activities were observed in vitro, although their contributions to P mobilization were not directly established. Indolic compounds were also detected colorimetrically in tryptophan-supplemented cultures, although their identities and involvement in plant growth promotion were not established. Under greenhouse conditions, increasing inoculum volume significantly increased plant height, fruit number, and total fruit weight of Micro-Tom tomato, with the greatest responses observed at the highest inoculation dose. In maize, inoculation increased plant height at 50 days after sowing from 40.85 to 46.50 cm, representing a 13.8% increase. No significant effects on plant height were detected in rice or common bean. Overall, Y. lipolytica exhibits multiple plant growth-promoting traits, particularly those related to phosphorus mobilization and the production of indolic compounds, demonstrating its potential as an agricultural bioinput. Growth responses varied between the experiments, but the contributions of substrate fertility, plant species, and inoculation regime could not be separated. Not applicable.

title: Formate, hydrogen, and acetate shape the morphology, physiology and lifestyles of the host-associated methanogen Methanobrevibacter smithii
summary: Methane-producing archaea (methanogens) are increasingly linked to gastrointestinal, neuropsychiatric, and neurodevelopmental disorders. These conditions are often associated with altered microbial metabolism that changes the availability o
content: Methane-producing archaea (methanogens) are increasingly linked to gastrointestinal, neuropsychiatric, and neurodevelopmental disorders. These conditions are often associated with altered microbial metabolism that changes the availability of acetate, formate, hydrogen, carbon dioxide, and methane in the gut. However, the physiological importance of formate and acetate in host-associated methanogens remains poorly understood, limiting our ability to interpret microbiome data and infer functions and cross-domain interactions of methanogens in health and disease. Here, we investigated the physiological and metabolic capabilities of Methanobrevibacter smithii , the predominant methanogen of the human gut. Formate limitation altered growth, morphology, extracellular pH, gas metabolism, and cellular organization, and induced the formation of cell aggregates. Although acetate was consumed only in small quantities (nmol), its availability significantly influenced growth, gas metabolism, extracellular pH, and formate utilization, indicating functions that extend beyond its role as a biosynthetic precursor. Conversely, nutrient excess promoted a transition to a biofilm lifestyle, suggesting that biofilm formation may function as a carbon sink. We further developed Msm_MEP, an experimentally refined genome-scale metabolic model based on the AGORA2 reconstruction, which captures the metabolic capabilities of M. smithii , quantifies ATP allocation across cellular processes, and predicts the phenotypic consequences of gene deletions. Together, our findings identify formate, hydrogen, and acetate as interacting determinants of M. smithii physiology and suggest metabolite-dependent transitions between planktonic growth, cell aggregation, and biofilm formation. Our results establish a framework for interpreting microbiome data and understanding how environmental metabolites shape archaea physiology and cross-domain interactions within the human microbiome.

title: Low organic matter degradation rates and decoupled benthic nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in the deeper North Sea (Norwegian Trench)
source: Data Portal of the Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research
summary: Shelf seas such as the North Sea play a significant role in global marine carbon and nutrient cycling. Carbon and other nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) are released at the seafloor by degradation of organic matter (OM), after which they
content: Shelf seas such as the North Sea play a significant role in global marine carbon and nutrient cycling. Carbon and other nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) are released at the seafloor by degradation of organic matter (OM), after which they are returned to the water column or sequestered in the sediment. This balance affects nutrient bioavailability in coastal ecosystems. For the North Sea, the deep Norwegian Trench is the main OM accumulation area, but benthic biogeochemical cycling and fluxes are poorly constrained. To determine rates of OM degradation and elucidate the fate of the released nutrients, benthic nutrient and oxygen fluxes were measured in whole-core incubation experiments in two consecutive years across depositional environments in the Norwegian Trench. A biogeochemical mass balance model was applied to account for nitrogen and phosphorus biogeochemical pathways from the whole-core incubation data. In addition, the surface sediment was analysed for key physicochemical properties. Total organic carbon (TOC) content showed a strong correlation with the sediment grain size: organic-rich and fine-grained sediment accumulated in the deep, central trench (1.2 to 2.1 wt% TOC) while slope areas were characterized by organic-poor, coarse-grained sediment (0.1 to 1.2 wt% TOC). Benthic oxygen (O2) consumption rates were similar across depositional environments (-6.0 ± -2.0 mmol m-2 d-1) and relatively low compared to global and regional rates. Low effluxes and high removal efficiencies for dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN: 0.1 ± 0.2 mmol m-2 d-1 and 93 ± 23 % retention efficiency) and phosphorus (DIP: 0.02 ± 0.03 mmol m-2 d-1 and 74 ± 42 % retention efficiency) at most sites in the study area show that trench sediments are an efficient sink for N and P released during OM mineralization. Combined, our results provide much-needed, process-based constraint on benthic fluxes in a key coastal OM accumulation area and show that Norwegian Trench sediments impact North Sea biogeochemical budgets by serving as an efficient sink for carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus.

title: Forest pest prediction using a hybrid Random Forest–LSTM model
summary: Introduction Forest pest outbreaks can substantially affect forest ecosystem stability and pose challenges to forest health monitoring and risk management. However, forest pest monitoring datasets commonly contain a high proportion of zero
content: Introduction Forest pest outbreaks can substantially affect forest ecosystem stability and pose challenges to forest health monitoring and risk management. However, forest pest monitoring datasets commonly contain a high proportion of zero observations and exhibit pronounced temporal variability, which can limit the predictive performance of conventional machine learning approaches. To address these challenges, this study developed a hybrid RF-LSTM framework incorporating Zero-Inflated Poisson (ZIP) features and LSTM-derived temporal features to evaluate the effects of these feature enhancements on Random Forest (RF) model performance. Methods Multi-station daily monitoring data for Coleoptera and Lepidoptera in Rui’an City, Zhejiang Province, China, were used to evaluate the proposed framework. The ZIP model was first employed to characterize the zero inflation structure of pest occurrence data, while the LSTM network was used to extract temporal representations from sequences of meteorological, seasonal, and ZIP-derived features. The ZIP-derived and LSTM-derived features were then incorporated into the RF model for evaluation. Results Compared with the conventional RF model, incorporating ZIP features increased R2 from 0.69 to 0.71 for Coleoptera and from 0.79 to 0.81 for Lepidoptera. Further integration of LSTM-derived temporal features increased R2 to 0.85 and 0.87, respectively. The proposed framework was also evaluated under different training sample ratios. R2 increased with the training sample ratio for both pest groups, although MAE and RMSE did not decrease consistently. Discussion These results indicate that ZIP based feature enhancement and LSTM-derived temporal features can improve RF model performance, although the extent of improvement varies between pest groups and training sample sizes.

title: Canopy Management and Supplemental Fertilization Improve Cayenne Pepper (Capsicum frutescens L.) Yield in Sandy Dryland Conditions
summary: Cayenne pepper cultivation in sandy dryland areas often faces suboptimal conditions that limit productivity. This study aimed to assess the impact of canopy management through pruning of lateral branches, combined with supplemental fertiliz
content: Cayenne pepper cultivation in sandy dryland areas often faces suboptimal conditions that limit productivity. This study aimed to assess the impact of canopy management through pruning of lateral branches, combined with supplemental fertilization, on the growth and yield of cayenne pepper. A field experiment was conducted in Gumantar Village, North Lombok Regency, Indonesia, utilizing a factorial randomized complete block design with three replications. Pruning treatments included: no pruning, complete pruning, pruning at three weeks after planting, and pruning at five weeks. Fertilization treatments included: no supplemental fertilizer, monopotassium phosphate (MKP), and potassium-silicate-humic acid. Results showed significant interaction effects of pruning and supplemental fertilization on yield and its components, including fruit weight per plant, number of fruits per plant, and fruit-set percentage. The highest yield, 5.2 kg per plot (approximately 6.9 t/ha), was achieved with complete pruning combined with MKP treatment, while the lowest yield, approximately 5.2 t/ha, occurred in the control. Both pruning and fertilization treatments significantly affected vegetative growth parameters, including plant height, leaf number, and stem diameter. Plants without pruning produced the shortest plants but had the highest leaf number and stem diameter. Meanwhile, plants treated with MKP showed the greatest improvement in vegetative growth. The findings highlight that canopy management, combined with MKP supplementation, is strongly recommended for maximizing cayenne pepper yield in sandy, dryland environments.

title: Non-exhaust Emissions from the Tyre and Road Surface Interface – The Life-NEEVE State-of-the-art and Project Progress
summary: Abstract Non-exhaust emissions (NEE) from the interaction between road surface and vehicle tyres are a growing, yet unregulated, source of particles contributing to air pollution in traffic environments. The source is complex and the factor
content: Abstract Non-exhaust emissions (NEE) from the interaction between road surface and vehicle tyres are a growing, yet unregulated, source of particles contributing to air pollution in traffic environments. The source is complex and the factors affecting emissions and particle properties numerous. Abrasion of road surfaces depends on construction and material properties but also on tyres trafficking the surface. In countries where studded tyres are used, road surfaces abrade faster, and abrasion resistance is crucial. Tyre abrasion depends on tyre properties, road surface texture, vehicle properties (torque, weight) and driving behaviour. The emitted particles from tyre–road interaction are often heterogeneous aggregates where road surface wear particles are mixed into a tyre material matrix. Additionally, road dust is resuspended in tyre–road contact, a major air quality issue when road dust sources are strong and accumulation high. The Life-NEEVE project aims to reduce NEE by developing innovative road and brake materials and defining essential low-emitting tyre properties. This paper presents a road and tyre NEE state-of-the-art and ongoing Life-NEEVE progress.

title: Methane-derived carbon black as a biochar alternative: Assessing long-term stability using accelerated ageing methods
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Methane pyrolysis is an emerging technology for producing hydrogen without direct carbon dioxide emissions because methane is converted into hydrogen and solid carbon. However, at present the solid carbon co-product has limited value and ma
content: Methane pyrolysis is an emerging technology for producing hydrogen without direct carbon dioxide emissions because methane is converted into hydrogen and solid carbon. However, at present the solid carbon co-product has limited value and may otherwise require landfilling. One potential value-added pathway is to co-pyrolyze this solid carbon with woody biomass to create composite materials with biochar-like properties. By combining the carbon-rich and recalcitrant character of methane-derived carbon black (CB) with the porosity and surface functionality of woody biochar (WBC), these composites may provide useful properties for soil applications while also functioning as a carbon sink. To investigate their long-term stability and environmental reactivity, CB, WBC, and WBC-CB composites were exposed to accelerated freeze-thaw (FT), wet-dry (WD), and chemical ageing with H2O2. Changes in morphology, elemental composition, specific surface area (SSA), and surface chemistry were evaluated using SEM/EDS, BET, and FTIR spectroscopy, and potentiometric titrations with surface complexation models (SCMs) were used to evaluate changes in acid-base behavior and reactive surface sites. The results showed that ageing affected the physical and chemical properties of the materials differently depending on their composition and the ageing treatment. WBC and composites with lower CB contents showed greater structural degradation but maintained a high relative C content, whereas CB and a WBC-26%CB (the composite with the highest concentration of CB, 26%) were more physically stable. Chemical ageing produced morphological degradation and changes in surface chemistry of biochar-based materials, increasing the intensity of the C=O stretching band at ~1700 cm-1 associated with carbonyl-containing functionalities. FT ageing mainly comprised physical degradation, including pore destruction and cracking, together with a decrease in the relative contribution of aliphatic C–H groups at ~2920 cm-1 in the composites. The relative contribution of C–O functionalities remained nearly unchanged after FT ageing. WD ageing produced a different response, exposing smaller pore spaces and increasing the specific surface area of WBC-3%CB (from 2.1 to 8.3 m2/g) and WBC-14%CB (from 3.1 to 6.0 m2/g). It also increased oxygen-containing functionalities in WBC, particularly groups with C–O bonds (~1160 cm-1), which may include phenolic, carboxylic, ether, and ester groups. These changes were also reflected in the potentiometric titrations. WD ageing increased the relative concentration of the second acidic site, attributed to phenolic hydroxyl groups, in the biochar-based materials. In WBC and WBC-14%CB, the pKa of this site also shifted toward ~7 (from 8.5 to 7.3 and from 8.7 to 7.0, respectively), indicating easier deprotonation and greater surface reactivity near neutral pH, which may be important in soils affected by acid rain or repeated fertilizer application. Overall, the results show

title: AfriCCS: Carbon capture and storage readiness atlas for Africa, evidence register and data
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: AfriCCS is an evidence-graded register of readiness for geological carbon capture and storage (CCS) in 55 African countries and territories, published by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Techn
content: AfriCCS is an evidence-graded register of readiness for geological carbon capture and storage (CCS) in 55 African countries and territories, published by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). It covers eight dimensions: storage geology, source-sink proximity, infrastructure, policy, legal, institutions, finance and public acceptance. This deposit contains the evidence register v2 (528 records, evidence accessed to 21 October 2026), the coding of each scored record against a 0 to 5 rubric, cell levels under four evidence sets with explicit absence states, London Protocol status, rank ranges and SMAA results for entries that pass the A/B evidence gate, and the summary tables. Every field is described in CODEBOOK.csv. Missing evidence is never imputed and no league table is produced. Web application: https://africcs.ncelknust.org Provisional status: Provisional research output. Single-analyst coding; second-reviewer checks are pending; missing evidence is never imputed; no league table is produced. Not peer reviewed. Contact: ncel@knust.edu.gh

title: The debt burden of tropical cyclones and climate change
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Addressing climate change through mitigation and adaptation is expected to require more than $6 trillion in global investment annually by 2035. Yet many countries face significant barriers to accessing this finance, including low or absent
content: Addressing climate change through mitigation and adaptation is expected to require more than $6 trillion in global investment annually by 2035. Yet many countries face significant barriers to accessing this finance, including low or absent credit ratings, large debt burdens, and high borrowing costs. Climate change may further amplify these barriers, creating a “vicious cycle” in which mounting economic losses reduce the capacity of countries to invest in adaptation and mitigation. We provide evidence that the cost and availability of capital for many countries have already been shaped by both historical exposure to naturally-occurring tropical cyclones (TCs) and anthropogenic warming. Our empirical estimates suggest that, on average across TC-exposed countries, 20% of debt-to-GDP ratios are attributable to TCs from 1980 to 2019. Across all countries, GDP levels are on average 12% lower due to the combined impacts of baseline naturally-occurring TCs and anthropogenic warming. In a separate correlational machine-learning analysis, we estimate that these macroeconomic impacts are associated with an increased likelihood of hotter countries receiving credit ratings below investment grade ( < BBB–), as well as persistent credit risk premiums of at least 1 basis point in 64 countries and 5 basis points in highly exposed countries. We provide estimates for 181 countries, including many TC-affected and/or hot countries that do not have bond yield data. Future increases in temperature and TC activity may further worsen sovereign credit conditions, potentially undermining climate resilience and long-run development prospects.

title: Ação climática estagna e mundo caminha para 2,7°C até 2100
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Impact on Infrastructure of Connected and Automated Traffic
summary: Abstract This paper examines the structural challenges posed by the projected increase in road freight and the introduction of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAV) on European infrastructure through 2050. While automation aims to reduce c
content: Abstract This paper examines the structural challenges posed by the projected increase in road freight and the introduction of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAV) on European infrastructure through 2050. While automation aims to reduce costs and decarbonize transport, it introduces technical phenomena that could accelerate the deterioration of roads and bridges. A primary concern is reduced lateral wandering: Unlike human drivers who naturally vary their position within a lane, CAVs follow precise, synchronized trajectories. This “rail-type” loading concentrates stress, potentially increasing pavement rutting by 30% to 56% and reducing the service life of flexible pavements by half to two-thirds. Furthermore, truck platooning, where vehicles travel with short inter-truck gaps, can create vertical loads that exceed current bridge design standards. The study also highlights the impact of Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEV), which may require increasing driving axle loads from 11.5 to 12.5 t. According to the fourth power law, this one-ton increase results in a 40%-increase in stress on some existing pavements. These effects are further exacerbated by higher temperatures, which make elastic pavements more susceptible to fatigue. To mitigate these risks, the authors make several suggestions.

title: Transport Infrastructure in Germany: Review and Evaluation of Guidelines, Regulations and Design Values Regarding Climate Change and Resilience
summary: Abstract Climate change poses increasing challenges to transport infrastructure, necessitating adaptation in planning, construction, and maintenance. Regulations play a central role in anchoring climate resilience within transport systems.
content: Abstract Climate change poses increasing challenges to transport infrastructure, necessitating adaptation in planning, construction, and maintenance. Regulations play a central role in anchoring climate resilience within transport systems. The research project “Review and evaluation of guidelines and regulations regarding climate change” aims to create a cross-modal approach for assessing the relevance and adaptability of regulatory frameworks considering projected climate conditions. Building on prior investigations by the German Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV) Research Network, this study addresses identified research needs from earlier assessments. The aim of this project is to provide an overview of regulations of transport infrastructure for which it would be useful to consider potential adjustments due to the consequences of climate change. A uniform approach to assess these impacts of climate change is applied for all modes of transport. The focus is on the regulations regarding infrastructure. Selected regulations for rail and road transport infrastructure are being examined in detail and recommendations for action to adapt regulations are formulated. Based on the investigations, a strategy for implementing potential climate adaptation measures in regulations is developed. This contribution offers insights for policymakers, researchers, and practitioners working towards future-ready transport systems. The research is being conducted since February 2025.

title: High-temperature performance of asphalt binder mastic with biochar as a sustainable filler
summary: Abstract Asphalt pavement durability relies critically on the rheological consistency and thermal stability of the mastic matrix. However, these critical properties are increasingly susceptible to degradation under growing traffic demands a
content: Abstract Asphalt pavement durability relies critically on the rheological consistency and thermal stability of the mastic matrix. However, these critical properties are increasingly susceptible to degradation under growing traffic demands and severe climatic fluctuations. By substituting conventional fillers such as crusher dust with biochar, this research aims to evaluate how this porous material enhances the physical and rheological properties of the mastic. The mastic was prepared using filler/binder ratios of 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0, and the effects on the physical and rheological properties of the mastic were evaluated. The results show that, across these filler/binder ratios, the behaviour of biochar mastic is more similar to that of conventional mastic. Specifically, at a filler/binder ratio of 1.0, biochar as filler improved mastic performance by an average of 111.12%, 119.61%, and 64.40% for non-recoverable rate at stress levels of 0.1 ( Jnr 0.1 ) and 3.2 ( Jnr 3.2 ), and stress sensitivity ( Jnr slope ), respectively. Grey relational analysis (GRA) shows that biochar-mastic was ranked higher than the conventional mastic. This study shows that biochar, a bio-based by-product, has potential as an alternative filler to conventional mineral filler based on mastic-scale rheological properties.

title: Investigating Methanol Metabolism Bottlenecks and the Effects of Carbon Dioxide on Alphaproteobacterial Methanotrophs
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Methane emissions are a crucial topic of concern within the scope of the climate crisis. As the second most abundant greenhouse gas, methane has a global warming potential of 27-30 over 100 years compared to carbon dioxide, absorbing more e
content: Methane emissions are a crucial topic of concern within the scope of the climate crisis. As the second most abundant greenhouse gas, methane has a global warming potential of 27-30 over 100 years compared to carbon dioxide, absorbing more energy by comparison (USEPA, 2025). As such, innovative strategies are required in order for the most detrimental consequences of climate change to be mitigated. One popular strategy is utilizing methanotrophs, a diverse group of bacteria that utilize single carbon compounds as their sole energy source. Aerobic methanotrophs fall under a wide breadth of phyla, including Gammaproteobacteria, Alphaproteobacteria, and Verrucomicrobia (Dave et al. 2025). Each possess different metabolic strategies to assimilate formaldehyde, formate, and carbon dioxide, possessing the ribulose monophosphate cycle, serine cycle, and Calvin-Benson-Bassham cycle respectfully. While Gammaproteobacteria and Alphaproteobacteria both possess the ability to oxidize methane and methanol, Alphaproteobacteria exhibit poorer growth on methanol compared to Gammaproteobacteria. A potential reasoning to this phenomenon was that alphaproteobacterial methanotrophs were accumulating high concentrations of formaldehyde, a toxic metabolite, when cultured on methanol. In addition to this, despite much research on methanotrophs being conducted over the past century, there are still fundamental gaps in our understanding of their metabolism. Unlike Gammaproteobacteria, alphaproteobacterial methanotrophs can also utilize another greenhouse gas as a source of energy: carbon dioxide. Despite this knowledge being long-known, little is understood to whether carbon dioxide assimilation is a bottleneck for formaldehyde oxidation in alphaproteobacterial methanotrophs. In this work, Methylosinus trichosporium OB3b, Methylocystis sp. Rockwell, and Methylocystis sp. WRRC1 were grown under methane or methanol as primary carbon sources, and supplemented with carbon dioxide. Their growth was compared across treatment conditions, and assessed for extracellular concentrations of formaldehyde through a colorimetric assay. Methylosinus trichosporium OB3b was the sole strain that significantly improved in growth when carbon dioxide was added to methanol. In addition, all three strains were found to be accumulating high concentrations of formaldehyde only when methanol was used as the carbon source. In addition to this, no formaldehyde was detected when Methylosinus trichosporium OB3b was cultured with carbon dioxide and methanol. Transcriptomic analysis of differentially expressed genes for Methylosinus trichosporium OB3b was conducted for methane with carbon dioxide and methanol with carbon dioxide, using methane with dinitrogen as the reference condition. The differentially expressed genes between conditions provided insights into how the cells metabolically regulate in the presence of carbon dioxide, with some hypothesized strategies such as the upregulation of a glycine

title: Chitosan in Mitigating Saline Stress in the Morphophysiology and Production of Solanum melongena L. in a Semi-Arid Area
source: Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
summary: Abstract Objective: Evaluate the effect of foliar application of chitosan on mitigating the deleterious effects of irrigation water salinity on the gas exchange, growth and production of eggplant cv. Preta Comprida grown under semiarid cond
content: Abstract Objective: Evaluate the effect of foliar application of chitosan on mitigating the deleterious effects of irrigation water salinity on the gas exchange, growth and production of eggplant cv. Preta Comprida grown under semiarid conditions. Methods: The experiment was conducted in a greenhouse using a randomized block design in a 5 × 2 factorial scheme, consisting of five levels of electrical conductivity of the irrigation water (ECwi) - (0.4, 1.4, 2.4, 3.4, and 4.4 dS m -1 ) and two chitosan concentrations (0 and 0.50 g L -1 ), with four replicates. Results: Foliar application of chitosan improved the growth and physiology of eggplant plants under irrigation water salinity levels up to 1.0 dS m -1 . However, the application of 0.50 g L -1 of chitosan was not sufficient to mitigate the effects of salinity above level of ECwi. On the other hand, chitosan application increased water use efficiency at all evaluated salinity levels. Conclusion: In this sense, foliar application of chitosan improves the morphophysiology of eggplant plants when irrigated with water up to 1.0 dS m -1 , but it is not effective in mitigating the effects of salt stress at higher levels of irrigation water salinity. Thus, chitosan represents a promising strategy for sustainable management of saline waters under semi-arid conditions. However, further studies are required to elucidate how chitosan attenuates the deleterious effects of irrigation water salinity.

title: Carbon and economic implications of promoting preventive care: A case study of Japan's community gathering place
summary: Abstract This study examines the supply-chain greenhouse gas emissions (carbon footprint) and economic impacts of preventive care policies. As a case study, we focus on community gathering places named “kayoinoba”, where older residents mee
content: Abstract This study examines the supply-chain greenhouse gas emissions (carbon footprint) and economic impacts of preventive care policies. As a case study, we focus on community gathering places named “kayoinoba”, where older residents meet at least once a week, for group exercise and social activities as a part of the national long-term care prevention system. While preventive care is widely recognized to suppress long-term care demand, the financial and environmental impacts remain unexplored. To address this knowledge gap, this study employs an environmental input-output analysis paired with detailed operational and expenditure data obtained through interviews with 102 local organizations across nine municipalities in Japan. By quantifying the carbon footprint from preventive care activities, this study sets future scenarios based on participation rates and the subsequent reduction in the need for lower level long-term care. Findings demonstrate that net economic costs between the promotion of community gathering places and reduction in the long-term care demand are expected to decrease, and this impact will intensify over time as the population ages (339 billion Japanese yen in 2050). In addition, without rebound effects on the carbon footprint resulting from behavioral changes among older adults who have become healthier due to preventive care measures, preventive care reduces net emission within the health care system by 2.97 gCO2eq/Japanese yen. Furthermore, the study found preventive measures’ impact varies by prefecture owing to differences in of older adult numbers and certified care needs rates. Additionally, we conducted scenario analysis group with the lowest cost or carbon footprint intensity. These results suggest that each municipality can reduce the carbon footprint intensity of the health system by emulating these groups’ activities. Incorporating environmental considerations into municipal preventive care offers a pathway to achieving sustainable health systems and climate change mitigation, that is, global planetary health priorities.

title: Unifying biomedical knowledge in a modern multimodal graph
summary: Abstract Biomedical knowledge graphs (KGs) are widely used in the life sciences, yet many are derived from unstructured documents and therefore lack schema-level constraints, whereas graphs assembled from structured resources are difficult
content: Abstract Biomedical knowledge graphs (KGs) are widely used in the life sciences, yet many are derived from unstructured documents and therefore lack schema-level constraints, whereas graphs assembled from structured resources are difficult to harmonize into a unified representation. We present O ptimus KG, a multimodal biomedical labeled property graph (LPG) built from structured and semi-structured resources to preserve factual, type-specific metadata across molecular, anatomical, clinical, and environmental domains. O ptimus KG contains 190,939 nodes across 10 entity types, 21,818,752 edges across 27 edge types, and 67,070,490 property instances encoding 109,665,797 values across 145 distinct property keys, derived from 18 ontologies and controlled vocabularies. The graph enforces a top-level schema for nodes and edges and retains granular, type-specific properties, cross-references, and provenance. We assessed the validity of O ptimus KG by evaluating whether graph relationships are supported by evidence from the scientific literature using a multimodal agent, PaperQA3. PaperQA3 identified supporting evidence for 70.0% of sampled edges, whereas 83.4% of sampled false edges received no supporting evidence. Edges without literature support were concentrated in associations derived from experimental and functional genomics resources, suggesting that O ptimus KG captures biomedical knowledge that may precede synthesis in the scientific literature. O ptimus KG is distributed as Apache Parquet files, providing a standardized resource for graph-based machine learning, knowledge-grounded retrieval with large language models, and biomedical discovery use cases such as hypothesis generation.

title: Long-term environmental risks, monitoring gaps, and intergenerational responsibility in CO2 geological storage: a critical review and conceptual framework
summary: The climate value of Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) hinges on the assumption that CO 2 can be stored permanently. Yet this assumption rests on evidence gathered over decades, while the storage commitment extends across centu
content: The climate value of Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) hinges on the assumption that CO 2 can be stored permanently. Yet this assumption rests on evidence gathered over decades, while the storage commitment extends across centuries to millennia. This paper critically synthesizes available evidence across three dimensions. For long-term environmental risks, the four trapping mechanisms operate on different timescales, and the uncertainties associated with leakage pathways through abandoned wells, caprock heterogeneity, and injection-induced geomechanical responses cannot be fully resolved by short-term monitoring records. For monitoring, existing technologies involve trade-offs among sensitivity, spatial coverage, duration, and cost, with no viable solutions for centennial-scale stewardship, and the attribution of anomalous signals remains methodologically underdeveloped. For liability, the United States and the European Union limit operator obligations to 20–50 years, creating a temporal mismatch with the risk horizon, while China has yet to enact dedicated legislation for long-term liability. Drawing on millennial-scale precedents from the nuclear industry, specifically the Yucca Mountain disposal standards and the OECD/NEA Records, Knowledge and Memory (RK&M) project, this paper proposes a conceptual framework for intergenerational environmental responsibility based on three pillars: technical verifiability, institutional continuity, and epistemic humility. Given the structural feature of CCUS in which benefits accrue now while risks are deferred, institutional design needs to be in place before large-scale deployment locks in irreversible commitments.

title: Techno-Economic Modeling, CCUS and Energy Management Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy and Hydrogen Production Systems in Alberta
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Alberta has been reported to have a significant carbon footprint. According to the Government of Canada's report, Alberta was responsible for over 40% of Canada’s total Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, releasing over 256.5 million tonnes of
content: Alberta has been reported to have a significant carbon footprint. According to the Government of Canada's report, Alberta was responsible for over 40% of Canada’s total Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, releasing over 256.5 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2020. A major chunk of this came from the oil and gas extraction, accounting for 20.7% of Canada's total GHG emissions in 2019. The combination of hydrogen production, Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) and CO₂-Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) can be a promising pathway to achieving Canada’s Net-Zero targets while decarbonizing the upstream sector. The objective of this paper is to establish the techno-economic readiness of Alberta as a blue hydrogen hub, including CO2 EOR, not only for emissions management but also as a carbon utilization method to support a broader, more realistic energy transition strategy. This study presents a combined techno-economic and life-cycle analysis of blue hydrogen production using steam methane reforming, with storage into viable oil & gas reservoirs. The key focus is to analyze the cradle-to-grave cycle of blue hydrogen production and CCUS, considering available technology, feasibility, and carbon emissions. This study adopts a life-cycle approach to evaluate the environmental impact of Steam Methane Reforming (SMR) based hydrogen production coupled with CCUS at a capture rate of 95%. The system boundaries of LCA include natural gas extraction and transportation, hydrogen production, CO2 capture, compression & transportation, and geological sequestration through CO2 EOR. To identify reservoir suitability for CO2 EOR, a reservoir screening methodology established by Bachu (2016) was applied to Alberta’s pool database of over 15,000 reservoirs, from which 79 pools were identified as suitable for CO2 EOR and carbon sequestration. For permanent sequestration, calculations have been performed to determine the CO2 retention percentage as a function of the Hydrocarbon Pore Volume HCPV% of CO2 injected into the reservoir. A thorough techno-economic analysis was conducted to compare the tax incentives available for CCUS pathways. The economic evaluation is conducted using a discounted cash flow model with a plant life of 20 years across three policy scenarios: a base case, Canada’s Investment Tax Credit (ITC), and the United States Section 45Q tax credit. Finally, 4 major hydrogen production hubs were proposed near Alberta’s carbon emission-intensive industrial clusters. Results show that SMR with 95% CCUS is a competitive production pathway across all hub locations, ranging from $1.96/kg H₂ at Hub 3 (Calgary) to $2.42/kg H₂ at Hub 1 (Fort McKay), with CO₂ transport distance being the primary cost differentiator. Under the base case, in which revenue was considered only from hydrogen and crude oil sales, a small positive NPV is observed for Hubs 1, 2, and 3, and even a negative NPV for Hub 4. title: Influence of Halide Type and Concentration on the Corrosion Resistance of Cr-Alloyed Steels in Supercritical CO2-Saturated Aqueous Environments
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: The deployment of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) and CO2-enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) increasingly relies on the safe transport and injection of dense-phase supercritical CO2 (s-CO2). While dry CO2 is generally non-corro
content: The deployment of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) and CO2-enhanced oil recovery (CO2-EOR) increasingly relies on the safe transport and injection of dense-phase supercritical CO2 (s-CO2). While dry CO2 is generally non-corrosive to engineering steels, water condensation or the presence of formation brine in operational systems triggers CO2 dissolution, carbonic acid (H2CO3) formation, and accelerated corrosion of pipelines and surface equipment. Notably, halide ions (Cl-, Br-, I-) inherently present in subsurface brines further exacerbate integrity risks by destabilizing corrosion-product films and passive layers—with their effects strongly dependent on both concentration and ionic identity. To address these critical challenges, this thesis systematically evaluates the corrosion behavior of three representative engineering alloys (X70 carbon steel, P91 (9Cr) martensitic steel, and 316L austenitic stainless steel) under simulated CCUS/CO2-EOR operating conditions. Corrosion exposure tests were conducted in s-CO2-saturated brines at 45 °C and 10 MPa for 120 hours, with comprehensive characterization via weight-loss measurements, scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM/EDS), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). First, the influence of NaCl concentration (0.01–1.00 mol·L-1) on corrosion performance was quantified: X70 exhibited the highest susceptibility, with corrosion rates ranging from ~3.31 to 5.22 mm·y-1, attributed to the formation of loose, porous iron oxide/carbonate corrosion products that fail to inhibit anodic dissolution. P91 showed substantially improved resistance compared to X70, with corrosion rates spanning ~0.03 to 0.07 mm·y-1 and a local minimum near 0.10 mol·L-1 NaCl—indicating a potential stability window for the formation of a compact, Cr-enriched corrosion-product film that temporarily mitigates attack. 316L demonstrated the best overall performance, maintaining consistently low corrosion rates (~0.01–0.02 mm·y-1) across the full salinity range, owing to the synergistic effects of Cr, Ni, and Mo in stabilizing a dense, impermeable passive film resistant to chloride-induced breakdown. Second, at a fixed ionic strength (0.10 mol·L-1 NaX, X = Cl-, Br-, I-), the role of halide identity was clarified to establish relative corrosiveness and guide alloy selection. Chloride ions were identified as the most aggressive, inducing the highest corrosion rates for both P91 and 316L, while bromide and iodide exhibited reduced corrosivity—with iodide showing a unique tendency to promote localized oxidation (e.g., FeO, Fe2O3) on P91 but negligible impact on 316L. Collectively, the findings provide quantitative corrosion rate data, mechanistic insights into halide-induced degradation, and practical guidance for materials screening, corrosion risk management, and engineering design in CCUS and CO2-EOR environments.

title: Survival Strategies of Unicellular Microorganisms: Substance Acquisition and Energy Metabolism
summary: Unicellular microorganisms are widespread in almost all natural ecosystems and face environmental stresses. Analyzing their adaptation process has a significant influence on microbial ecology. These microorganisms deeply affect chemical rec
content: Unicellular microorganisms are widespread in almost all natural ecosystems and face environmental stresses. Analyzing their adaptation process has a significant influence on microbial ecology. These microorganisms deeply affect chemical recycling in the global ecosystem. This research analyzes the survival strategies of three types of unicellular microorganisms: autotrophs, heterotrophs, mixotrophs, and explains the different metabolic ways under long‑term lack of resources. Result shows that microorganisms use structural and physiological rebuilding to survive in resource-limited conditions, but long-term resource consumption may limit their recovery. Autotrophic microorganisms fix inorganic carbon to make organic compounds, and this process may consume a lot of energy. Mixotrophic organisms combine these two metabolisms, but this may bring an extra energy burden. The research suggests that no strategy has absolute advantages, and all these adaptations may bring metabolic costs. This conclusion can explain how microorganisms in natural environments adapt to fluctuations in nutrient conditions.

title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
summary: Abstract Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase trans
content: Abstract Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A 2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A 2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

title: Comparative mitochondrial DNA barcoding for the molecular authentication of Greek Thunnus alalunga and Thunnus thynnus products
source: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
summary: Introduction Seafood mislabeling and species substitution are very frequent and have become a concerning issue in global seafood markets. Different tunas species, and their processed products, can be morphologically identical, often making
content: Introduction Seafood mislabeling and species substitution are very frequent and have become a concerning issue in global seafood markets. Different tunas species, and their processed products, can be morphologically identical, often making their identification challenging. This can compromise market transparency, consumers' confidence and fisheries management, highlighting the need for reliable authentication methods. In Greece, both Thunnus thynnus and Thunnus alalunga are marketed as premium tuna products and hold significant cultural and economic importance, supporting traditional small‐scale fisheries. Therefore, their accurate species identification and traceability are of great importance. Methods In the present study, DNA barcoding was used for the genetic identification and authenticity evaluation of Greek tuna products labeled as T. alalunga or T. thynnus , examining three mitochondrial markers (CYTB, COI, and 16SrRNA). Phylogenetic analysis, haplotype characterization, genetic distance analysis, and identification of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were performed to evaluate species discrimination and genetic diversity among Thunnus species. Results Although, the three mitochondrial markers exhibited different levels of interspecific differentiation among the examined Thunnus species, T. alalunga and T. thynnus generally formed distinct phylogenetic clades. Among all markers, CYTB exhibited the highest discriminatory power, producing the highest number of SNPs and haplotypes and providing the clearest separation between intra‐ and interspecific variation. Our findings, furthermore, revealed notable levels of species substitution, as several products labeled as T. alalunga were genetically identified as T. thynnus . Conclusion Overall, this research provides a valuable genetic reference data to support species identification, seafood traceability and authentication in tuna supply chains.

title: Optimal grid connection capacity of a hybrid renewable microgrid: an energy management and economic optimisation model
summary: Microgrids are usually assessed with the grid connection taken as given, although its power limits import and export and its cost is paid before operation starts. Choosing this power is therefore a trade-off between the connection cost and
content: Microgrids are usually assessed with the grid connection taken as given, although its power limits import and export and its cost is paid before operation starts. Choosing this power is therefore a trade-off between the connection cost and the costs of imported energy, backup generation and unserved load, which the reviewed levelized-cost formulations do not capture. This paper presents a model for determining the optimal power of connection to the electric grid, which limits import and export, to minimise the levelized cost of the microgrid. Unlike the reviewed formulations, the connection power is a decision variable and its cost is part of the objective. The objective combines the costs of generation and battery storage, the import costs, export revenues and fuel costs, the penalties for lost load, and the daily cost of the connection. A cost-based source-selection strategy compares the day-ahead market price with the fuel cost of the backup gas generator in every hour. For a microgrid with a 60 kW solar plant, a 20 kW wind plant, a 40 kW backup gas generator and a 50 kW / 200 kWh battery, and critical and non-critical consumers whose maximum load ranges from 40 to 240 kW across six scenarios, the optimal connection power grows almost proportionally with the load, from 17.9 kW up to the 170 kW limit, equal to the maximum possible export. The levelized cost decreases by 2.8% at the lowest load (40 kW) compared with a connection sized for the maximum possible export.

title: The optical colors of hidden spiral-like features in nine Virgo early-type dwarfs
summary: Dwarf early-type galaxies (ETGs) are abundant in nearby clusters, offering a key laboratory for studying environmentally driven galaxy transformation. Although dwarf ETGs were once considered structurally simple, deep imaging has revealed e
content: Dwarf early-type galaxies (ETGs) are abundant in nearby clusters, offering a key laboratory for studying environmentally driven galaxy transformation. Although dwarf ETGs were once considered structurally simple, deep imaging has revealed embedded spiral-like features (e.g., bars and spiral arms) in some of them, contributing only a small fraction of the total galaxy light. The origin of these features at dwarf scales remains uncertain. As a pilot study, we investigated the nature of spiral-like features in nine Virgo dwarf ETGs with clear embedded arms. Our goal is to use optical colors to test whether these features differ from the surrounding diffuse component, which would constrain their formation pathways. In doing so, we established the methodology on a well-characterized sample, ahead of a future analysis of the much larger NGVS dwarf sample. Using deep (g)- and (i)-band images from the NGVS, we applied a residual-based image analysis method to separate excess light associated with the spiral-like component from the diffuse host. The residual images are used to define the arm and interarm regions, enabling direct measurements of light fractions and (g-i) colors for the spiral-like feature and the diffuse component in which they are embedded. The spiral-like features contribute only a few percent of the total galaxy light (approximately ( 1.5%!-!5.5%) in (i) and ( 1.7%!-!3.7%) in (g)). We find a diverse range of stellar colors across the sample: four galaxies host spiral-like features that are redder than their interarm regions, four show no robust color difference between the arm and interarm regions, and one exhibits a distinctly bluer spiral-like component. The latter is consistent with a recently quenched transition object, while the redder and color-uniform features are consistent with an older or more metal-rich stellar population. Spiral-like features in Virgo dwarf ETGs exhibit a surprising diversity in their photometric properties, implying that there are multiple evolutionary channels at work, rather than a single one. This pilot analysis also demonstrates the readiness for the much larger NGVS sample of dwarfs with potential spiral-like features.

title: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and Sustainable Business Practices in Indonesia: A Systematic Literature Review
source: Journal of Social Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice
summary: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are central to Indonesia’s economy, yet their contributions to employment and output do not automatically translate into sustainable business practices. Recent evidence also indicates substantial
content: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are central to Indonesia’s economy, yet their contributions to employment and output do not automatically translate into sustainable business practices. Recent evidence also indicates substantial barriers to adopting green practices. This review synthesizes research on environmental, social, and economic sustainability among Indonesian MSMEs and identifies the internal capabilities and external conditions that enable or constrain implementation. The study is designed as a qualitative systematic literature review of peer-reviewed journal articles on Indonesian MSMEs published during 2021–2026. The revised protocol specifies a Scopus search across title, abstract, and keyword fields using terms for MSMEs, sustainability, and Indonesia. The final search date and study-selection counts must be inserted from the actual Scopus search history and screening log: ("MSMEs" and "Sustainability Business"). The evidence is organized into three sustainability dimensions—environmental, social, and economic—while financial capability, leadership, technology, governance, and stakeholder networks are treated as enabling conditions. The candidate literature gives comparatively greater attention to environmental and economic practices, whereas the social dimension is less consistently operationalized. The review integrates the Triple Bottom Line with resource-based and stakeholder perspectives to explain how internal capabilities and external pressures shape sustainability practices and business outcomes in Indonesian MSMEs. The final synthesis depends on completion of the Scopus search verification and PRISMA screening record; the review also relies on secondary literature and does not provide primary empirical validation.

title: Hubungan Literasi Keuangan terhadap Minat Investasi Mahasiswa Universitas PGRI Palembang
summary: Financial literacy is a crucial component that helps students understand financial management and consider investment decisions. This study aims to examine the relationship between financial literacy and investment interest among students a
content: Financial literacy is a crucial component that helps students understand financial management and consider investment decisions. This study aims to examine the relationship between financial literacy and investment interest among students at Universitas PGRI Palembang. A quantitative, associative research approach was employed. Convenience sampling a type of non-probability sampling was used to select a sample of 50 active students from Universitas PGRI Palembang. Data were collected via a Google Forms questionnaire, consisting of eight questions regarding financial knowledge and eight statements concerning investment interest. Financial literacy was measured based on the number of correct answers, while investment interest was assessed using a five-point Likert scale. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression. The results indicate a correlation coefficient of 0.546, a regression coefficient of 1.955, a significance value of less than 0.001, and a coefficient of determination of 29.8%. These findings demonstrate a positive and significant relationship between financial literacy and investment interest among students at Universitas PGRI Palembang. Consequently, higher levels of financial literacy among students are associated with a greater inclination toward investment.

title: Measurement and statistical evaluation of industrial synergy and new productive forces in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Region: from the perspective of modern capital metropolitan area construction
source: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
summary: After the implementation of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei coordinated development strategy, industrial synergy has become the focus of the earliest breakthrough. In 2023, the modernization plan of the metropolitan area with the capital as the c
content: After the implementation of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei coordinated development strategy, industrial synergy has become the focus of the earliest breakthrough. In 2023, the modernization plan of the metropolitan area with the capital as the core was introduced, which made the industrial synergy of Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei have the dual significance of collaborative innovation and double chain integration. Most of the research on industrial transfer or regional division of labor is qualitative thinking, lacking statistical measurement standards or methods designed according to metropolitan areas. In this paper, industrial synergy and new productivity are combined to investigate, and statistical indicators are given for the subsystems involved in the two. The entropy weight-CRITIC model and the coupling coordination method are used as analytical tools. Due to the limitations of public data, this paper does not make specific numerical calculations. The relevant conclusions are a methodological inspiration for the subsequent quantitative analysis. Qualitative analysis under this framework reveals that the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region has achieved phased progress in non-capital function relocation, industrial structure optimization, and the integration of innovation and industrial chains. A preliminary pattern featuring "R&D in Beijing, achievement transformation in Tianjin, and manufacturing in Hebei" has taken shape. Nevertheless, the synergistic performance of the two systems is still constrained by several challenges, including the gradient gap in regional development, uneven distribution of innovation resources, inadequate benefit-sharing and cost-sharing mechanisms, and restricted mobility of production factors.

title: Green Bonds and Financing Costs: A Case Study of CATL
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: There is broad agreement in the literature that if a company's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance is better, the cost of its debt financing will be lower. Because Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) is the wo
content: There is broad agreement in the literature that if a company's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance is better, the cost of its debt financing will be lower. Because Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) is the world's leading power battery enterprise, its green bond issuance has been highly active, and its relevant information is publicly and freely available, this company was selected as the case to compare the coupon rates of green bonds and conventional bonds. It was found that the average rate of CATL's 2026 green bonds is 1.56%, clearly below the 3.655% average for conventional bonds issued between 2019 and 2020. The mean spread is about 210 basis points. This substantial difference suggests that green bonds may indeed enjoy a pricing advantage over conventional bonds. The conclusion is that green bonds can generate substantial interest savings. Firms should value ESG disclosure, and regulators should support small and medium-sized enterprises in improving ESG capabilities and regulate green bonds to prevent greenwashing.

title: Market Liberalization, Labour Relations and Maize Production Efficiency in Trans-Nzoia County, Kenya
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: Market liberalization has reshaped agricultural production by transforming farming practices, labour relations, and institutional arrangements that influence smallholder productivity.However, empirical evidence on how these interconnected t
content: Market liberalization has reshaped agricultural production by transforming farming practices, labour relations, and institutional arrangements that influence smallholder productivity.However, empirical evidence on how these interconnected transformations affect maize production efficiency remains limited, particularly in Kenya.This study examined the influence of changing farming practices and labour relations on maize production efficiency among smallholder farmers in Trans-Nzoia County, Kenya.A convergent mixed-methods design was employed involving 385 randomly selected maize farmers, complemented by focus group discussions and key informant interviews.Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data were analysed thematically.The findings reveal a selective modernization process characterized by relatively high adoption of certified seed (63%) but limited uptake of mechanization (42%), agrochemicals (33%), agricultural credit (26%), and irrigation (18%).Labour relations have shifted from traditional reciprocal arrangements towards hired labour, with high labour costs (82%), inadequate labour skills (72%), and labour shortages (69%) emerging as major production constraints.Drawing on these findings, the study proposes Fragmented Agrarian Modernization (FAM), an empirically grounded framework describing an asynchronous process in which technological innovation outpaces institutional, financial, and labour systems.The study concludes that maize production efficiency depends on synchronized technological and institutional transformation rather than technology adoption alone.It recommends strengthening rural finance, mechanization services, irrigation, agricultural extension, labour skills development, and farmer organizations to promote efficient, resilient, and sustainable smallholder agricultural systems under market liberalization.

title: Effect of Working Environment on Employee Performance in the Hospitality Industry in Rwanda: A Case of Lemigo Hotel
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of the working environment on employee performance in the hospitality industry in Rwanda, using Lemigo Hotel as a case study.Specifically, it assessed the effect of physical ergonomics and safety, open communi
content: This study examined the effect of the working environment on employee performance in the hospitality industry in Rwanda, using Lemigo Hotel as a case study.Specifically, it assessed the effect of physical ergonomics and safety, open communication, professional growth and development, and work-life balance on employee performance.A mixed-methods descriptive research design was adopted, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches.Data were collected from a census of 198 employees using structured questionnaires, interview guides, and documentary review, and were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression in SPSS, while qualitative data were analysed thematically.The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between the combined working-environment factors and employee performance (R = 0.799), with the four predictors jointly explaining 67.4% of the variance (R² = 0.674; adjusted R² = 0.641).The regression coefficients showed that physical ergonomics and safety (B = 0.353, p = 0.025), open communication (B = 0.472, p = 0.003), professional growth and development (B = 0.676, p = 0.001), and work-life balance (B = 0.353, p = 0.009) each had a significant positive effect on employee performance, with no multicollinearity (VIF = 1.246-2.491).All four null hypotheses were rejected.The study concludes that a safe, communicative, developmental, and balanced working environment is a fundamental determinant of employee performance in the hospitality industry.It recommends that Lemigo Hotel invest in ergonomic and safety upgrades, institutionalize transparent communication channels, expand career-development pathways, and strengthen work-life balance policies to sustain and improve employee performance.

title: ІНВЕСТИІЙНЕ ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННЯ ІННОВАЦІЙНОГО РОЗВИТКУ ТУРИСТИЧНИХ ТЕРИТОРІЙ УКРАЇНИ В УМОВАХ ЄВРОІНТЕГРАЦІЇ
summary: The study is devoted to a comprehensive analysis of investment support for the innovative development of Ukraine’s tourist territories in the context of European integration processes and post-war recovery. The article reveals the theoretic
content: The study is devoted to a comprehensive analysis of investment support for the innovative development of Ukraine’s tourist territories in the context of European integration processes and post-war recovery. The article reveals the theoretical and methodological foundations of the innovative development of tourist destinations, characterizes current trends and challenges, and highlights the need to establish a stable and diversified system for attracting investments. Particular attention is paid to assessing the dynamics of investment in tourism innovations in 2019–2024, which demonstrates significant fluctuations under the influence of pandemic and wartime crises, while also illustrating the sector’s ability to gradually recover. Based on an analysis of recent scientific works, the study identifies key academic approaches to the modernization of the tourism sector, examines innovative technologies that shape competitive advantages in the hospitality industry, and outlines regional features of tourism development in Ukraine. The research identifies several barriers that hinder innovation, including institutional instability, limited access to finance, low investment attractiveness of certain regions, and high security risks. The article systematizes the main tools of investment support, including public-private partnerships, EU grant programs, local development funds, bank lending, and crowdfunding. It substantiates the importance of strengthening institutional infrastructure for supporting innovations, including cluster models, tourist information centers, and digital service ecosystems. Drawing on European best practices, the study emphasizes the need to adapt national tourism policy to the standards of sustainable destination management, the green economy, and integrated territorial planning. The article proposes several directions for increasing investment activity, such as improving the regulatory environment, developing partnerships between government, business, and local communities, implementing green financing instruments, and accelerating the digitalization of tourism products.

title: Green finance, agricultural expansion, and the measurement of water-use performance: evidence from Chinese provinces
summary: In China, green finance is increasingly used to support sustainable agriculture, and evaluations often judge its water outcomes by the ratio of output to water withdrawn. That ratio can rise because farmers use less water or because they pr
content: In China, green finance is increasingly used to support sustainable agriculture, and evaluations often judge its water outcomes by the ratio of output to water withdrawn. That ratio can rise because farmers use less water or because they produce more while withdrawal stays roughly constant. We distinguish the two with an annual panel of all 31 mainland provinces from 2004 to 2023, estimating grain output, agricultural withdrawal, and crop water productivity on a common sample so that the estimates obey their accounting identity. Nationally, grain output rose by 48% and effective irrigated area by 32% over the period, while agricultural withdrawal rose by 2%. A 10% rise in a province’s green finance index is associated with approximately 2.4% more grain output and 2.1% more total sown area, and more than 90% of the output association runs through grain sown area.
