Agricultural withdrawal shows no detectable change, and an equivalence test limits its response to less than 1.5% in either direction, so measured water productivity rises. These associations reflect long-run provincial development paths and remain nearly unchanged when provincial agricultural spending and water policy pilots are controlled for. Agricultural green total factor productivity, which lies outside the accounting identity, shows no corresponding improvement. Total withdrawal, reported alongside production, is therefore essential to judging whether a financing policy relieves water scarcity.

title: Beyond screen time: how screen use context is associated with developmental outcomes in early childhood
summary: Background Excessive screen time is a leading parental health concern, reflecting its potential negative impact on child development. Although substantial evidence links higher screen exposure to adverse developmental outcomes in early chil
content: Background Excessive screen time is a leading parental health concern, reflecting its potential negative impact on child development. Although substantial evidence links higher screen exposure to adverse developmental outcomes in early childhood, much less is known about the independent contribution of the context of use to developmental outcomes. The objective of this longitudinal study was to examine whether screen time and context of use at 18 months predicted developmental outcomes at age 3. Methods The sample comprised participants from the Cohort'18 Growing Up in Hungary study ( n = 2,569; 52.0% boys). All analyzed data were based on maternal report. Outcomes were assessed using the Ages & Stages Questionnaires-3. Context of use was operationalized as a count of non-recommended screen-use situations (during household chores, meals, at bedtime, or for soothing). Associations were examined using bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression models. Results Mean daily screen time at 18 months was 85.7 minutes, and only 14.0% had no screen exposure on an average day. Higher levels of screen time at 18 months were associated with increased odds of delays in communication, fine motor, problem-solving, and personal-social skills, but not gross motor skills, at age 3 in both bivariate analyses and multivariable models adjusted for the child's sex and baseline delay in the same domain. After accounting for socioeconomic characteristics (maternal educational attainment, partnership status, and difficulties covering household expenses), associations were modestly attenuated. Context of use was an independent predictor of developmental delays, with the most consistent evidence observed for fine motor and problem-solving skills. Conclusions The findings indicate that screen use is already widespread at 18 months, both in terms of duration and its use across different everyday contexts. Higher levels of screen time and screen use in a greater number of non-recommended contexts were associated with less favorable developmental outcomes, suggesting the importance of promoting moderate and developmentally appropriate screen-use practices in early childhood.

title: Strengthening Students’ Personal Financial Planning through Budgeting Education at SMAN 10 Pandeglang: A Community Service Report
summary: Financial literacy is an essential life skill that helps adolescents make informed decisions about limited resources. On 22 October 2026, Universitas Pamulang PSDKU Serang conducted a community-service activity at SMAN 10 Pandeglang to stre
content: Financial literacy is an essential life skill that helps adolescents make informed decisions about limited resources. On 22 October 2026, Universitas Pamulang PSDKU Serang conducted a community-service activity at SMAN 10 Pandeglang to strengthen students’ personal financial planning skills through budgeting education. A total of 200 students participated. The activity addressed pocket-money management, distinguishing needs from wants, allocating expenses, prioritizing spending, and setting savings goals through explanations, guided budgeting exercises, and prioritization scenarios. This article presents a descriptive account based on program materials, event documentation, information from the organizing team, and contemporaneous media coverage. The percentage improvement in students’ financial-planning competence and the number and quality of completed budget worksheets and personal financial plans require further evaluation. Accordingly, the article reports the implementation and learning focus without making numerical claims about competency gains or student outputs.

title: БАНКЛАРНИ УЗОҚ МУДДАТЛИ МОЛИЯЛАШТИРИШ ТАРКИБИНИ ОПТИМАЛЛАШТИРИШ
summary: The article studies the issue of optimizing the structure of long-term financing of Uzbek commercial banks, excluding deposits, in the context of bank business models. A linear programming model is proposed that simultaneously takes into ac
content: The article studies the issue of optimizing the structure of long-term financing of Uzbek commercial banks, excluding deposits, in the context of bank business models. A linear programming model is proposed that simultaneously takes into account the full annual value, maturity, currency openness, stability, refinancing risk and impact on capital of credit lines of international financial institutions, syndicated loans, domestic and international bonds, subordinated loans, green bonds, sukuk and hybrid instruments. The model was tested on the basis of separate restrictions for a large state-owned bank, a large private bank, a medium-sized universal bank and a bank specializing in financing small and medium-sized businesses. In the baseline scenario, the weighted average full value was formed within 13.33-15.25 percent, and the average term was 4.92-5.96 years. The results of the stress scenario showed that the stabilizing importance of domestic bonds and Islamic instruments increases when external resources become more expensive

title: Sex and gender differences in the effects of the Serious Accidents Punishment Act on construction injury rates by company size in South Korea: an interrupted time-series analysis
summary: Background: Occupational injury remains a major public health concern in South Korea's construction industry. The Serious Accidents Punishment Act (SAPA), which holds employers criminally liable for serious workplace accidents, was enforced
content: Background: Occupational injury remains a major public health concern in South Korea's construction industry. The Serious Accidents Punishment Act (SAPA), which holds employers criminally liable for serious workplace accidents, was enforced in January 2022 for businesses with 50 or more employees; however, its effects on construction injuries, particularly by sex and company size, remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate changes in injury rates among construction workers following SAPA enforcement by company size, sex, and injury type. Methods Monthly National Health Insurance Service cohort data from January 2011 to December 2024 were used to calculate age- and sex-standardized injury rates (ASR; ICD-10 codes S00–T88) per 100,000 construction workers. An interrupted time-series design with a generalized additive mixed model, incorporating a cyclic cubic spline for seasonal variation and an autoregressive error structure, was applied to estimate the acute (level) and gradual (slope) effects of the SAPA for companies with ≥50 and < 50 employees, stratified by sex and injury type (inpatient and outpatient). Results Following SAPA enforcement, men in companies with ≥50 employees showed nonsignificant immediate increases in inpatient ASR [19.88 per 100,000; 95% confidence interval (CI): −28.63 to 68.38] and outpatient ASR (463.61; 95% CI: −197.95 to 1,125.16), whereas women showed immediate decreases in both company size groups. Female inpatient ASR in companies with < 50 employees decreased significantly (−92.42 per 100,000; 95% CI: −174.96 to −9.88), which was the only statistically significant finding. Male outpatient ASR in ≥50-employee companies declined after the initial increase, whereas male inpatient ASR showed gradually increasing trends in both company size groups. Conclusions The changes in construction injury rates following SAPA enforcement differed by sex and company size. The immediate increases among men in larger companies may partly reflect changes in injury reporting, and the decrease among women in smaller companies suggests a possible spillover effect on firms not yet subject to the law. These findings underscore the need for targeted occupational safety interventions addressing subcontracting structures and sex-specific occupational hazards in the construction industry.

title: Social finance practices at credit institutions in Vietnam: Descriptive survey-based research
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstract This study is an exploratory empirical investigation of perceived factors and barriers associated with social finance in mobilizing resources for Vietnam's sustainable development goals, given t
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstract This study is an exploratory empirical investigation of perceived factors and barriers associated with social finance in mobilizing resources for Vietnam's sustainable development goals, given the constrained public budget. A comprehensive survey is circulated among staff and managers who are directly involved in sustainable and social finance initiatives and activities within various credit institutions in Vietnam. Their positions provide them with both operational and managerial perspectives, enabling the study to capture informed assessments of current practices, implementation challenges, and future development opportunities for social finance in Vietnam. Using a descriptive, survey-based analysis, the study evaluates credit institutions' awareness, implementation, and reported readiness perceptions toward social finance. The findings indicate: low and uneven awareness of social finance; implementation activities primarily focus on green credit and agricultural lending, with inadequate outreach to vulnerable groups. Although policy-oriented institutions such as the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies and People’s credit funds demonstrate clearer alignment with social finance objectives, the study’s respondent-level evidence has revealed that most surveyed commercial banks have not yet formally integrated these practices into their strategies. Major barriers include a lack of a comprehensive legal framework, limited guiding policies, resource constraints, and insufficient expertise in social finance. Research findings provide a firm foundation for formulating appropriate, feasible policy recommendations to enhance the role of credit institutions in promoting social finance in Vietnam.

title: The Role of Banking Development and Renewable Energy in Shaping Environmental Sustainability in Saudi Arabia: Evidence from a Bootstrap ARDL Approach
source: Journal of Administrative and Economic Sciences
summary: Objectives Environmental sustainability remains a central policy concern for economies undergoing structural diversification, particularly in carbon-intensive nations such as Saudi Arabia, yet the influence of banking-sector development rem
content: Objectives Environmental sustainability remains a central policy concern for economies undergoing structural diversification, particularly in carbon-intensive nations such as Saudi Arabia, yet the influence of banking-sector development remains comparatively under-examined. This study investigates how banking development, renewable energy consumption, and economic growth shape environmental sustainability in Saudi Arabia using both carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and the load capacity factor (LCF). Material and Methods LCF provides a composite measure that integrates ecological footprint and bio-capacity, thereby enabling an assessment of environmental sustainability beyond conventional single-dimensional measures. Using an annual dataset covering 1980–2024, we estimate two environmental models employing the bootstrap autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) framework. Results Findings indicate long-run co-integration among the variables. Banking-sector development significantly reduces CO₂ emissions and enhances LCF in the long run, demonstrating the potential for green financial intermediation to support national sustainability goals. Renewable energy consumption consistently improves environmental indicators, while economic growth displays an inverted U-shaped association with both CO₂ and LCF, supporting the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC). CUSUM and CUSUMSQ tests confirm parameter stability. Conclusion The study concludes with policy implications aligned with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, emphasising the strategic importance of green finance, renewable energy expansion, environmental risk assessment, and sustainable growth pathways.

title: Determinants of MSME/SME Export Readiness: Systematic Literature Review 2016-2026
source: Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Export readiness determines whether micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and small and medium industries (SMEs) are able to enter foreign markets in a planned manner, but the determining factors are scattered and the methods of meas
content: Export readiness determines whether micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and small and medium industries (SMEs) are able to enter foreign markets in a planned manner, but the determining factors are scattered and the methods of measuring them vary. This study aims to map the internal and external determinants of MSME/IKM export readiness based on journal articles published in 2016–2026 through a systematic literature review that follows the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Searches on Scopus and Google Scholar yielded 266 records, and 57 articles that met the criteria, including the existence of a Digital Object Identifier (DOI), were synthesized thematically with a descriptive calculation of the direction of the findings. Only 15 studies made export readiness the focus of the study, while the other studies used export propensity, intentions, or barriers as approaches. The most consistent internal factors were resources and managerial orientation (15 out of 23 studies reported positive influences), followed by technology and digital, financial capacity, and quality standards and certifications. The external factors that most often proved important were government support and business networks, while institutions and regulations were most often reported as barriers. Eleven studies originated in Indonesia and were mostly limited to one region or one sector. These findings demonstrate the need for multidimensional export readiness instruments validated in Indonesian MSMEs/SMEs.

title: The impact of tax blacklisting
summary: Abstract This paper estimates the policy and economic impacts of a European Union-led effort to review and “blacklist” jurisdictions based on their noncompliance with international standards designed to curb corporate profit shifting and pr
content: Abstract This paper estimates the policy and economic impacts of a European Union-led effort to review and “blacklist” jurisdictions based on their noncompliance with international standards designed to curb corporate profit shifting and private tax evasion. Using a combination of regression discontinuity and difference-and-difference methods, I find evidence of improvements in tax governance four years after the inception of the list. However, despite evidence that some jurisdiction raised their tax rates in response to the listing exercise, there no clear evidence that listing had a significant impact on offshore wealth or shifted profits, largely because the bulk of jurisdictions that host both of these were not targeted by the EU. The results suggest that “coercive” efforts to reduce global tax evasion and avoidance will struggle without better targeting and enforcement.

title: Digital Payments and Formal Savings as Robust Within-Country Correlates of Account Ownership: Evidence from the Global Findex Panel
summary: Abstract Financial inclusion sits at the heart of global development policy, yet cross-country evidence on what is associated with account ownership over time remains scattered across survey waves and shifting indicator definitions. This st
content: Abstract Financial inclusion sits at the heart of global development policy, yet cross-country evidence on what is associated with account ownership over time remains scattered across survey waves and shifting indicator definitions. This study draws on six waves (2011–2024) of the World Bank Global Findex Database, covering up to 145 economies per wave, to document global and regional trends in account ownership and to identify which usage-dimension behaviors are most robustly associated with it in a country-year panel of 294 observations from the 2014, 2017, 2021, and 2024 waves covering 95 mostly low- and middle-income economies. Population-weighted global account ownership rose from 50.6% in 2011 to 78.7% in 2024, with the largest absolute gains in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Averaged across surveyed countries, the gender gap remained broadly unchanged at roughly 6 percentage points and the within-country income gap narrowed only modestly (14.1 to 11.7 percentage points). A two-way fixed-effects panel regression shows that digital payment use ( β = 0.552, p < 0.01) and formal savings ( β = 0.418, p < 0.01) remain statistically significant correlates of account ownership within countries over time, whereas the associations with mobile money (negative in the pooled specifications) and formal borrowing, which are significant in the pooled and wave-fixed-effects models, shrink toward zero once country fixed effects are included. Median regressions, with and without country effects, suggest that the results are not driven by outlier countries. The study contributes a consistent comparison of pooled and within-country associations across the four Findex waves in which all four usage indicators are available, with descriptive trends from 2011. Because the usage indicators overlap conceptually with account ownership and the design is observational, the estimates are descriptive correlates, not causal effects. They suggest that digital payment ecosystems and formal savings deserve policy attention alongside, rather than instead of, account-ownership efforts.

title: Intrinsic Motivation Strategies and Employee Performance in Five-Star Hotels: Evidence from Radisson Blu Kigali, Rwanda
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: This article examined the influence of intrinsic motivation strategies on employee performance at Radisson Blu Hotel and Convention Centre in Kigali, Rwanda. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study used structured questionnaires with a strati
content: This article examined the influence of intrinsic motivation strategies on employee performance at Radisson Blu Hotel and Convention Centre in Kigali, Rwanda. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study used structured questionnaires with a stratified employee sample; descriptive statistics and simple linear regression were used for analysis.

title: Effect of Real Estate Investment Strategies on Social Welfare Outcomes of Members in Professional Associations: A Case of Rwanda Bar Association’s Advocates Investment Company
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of real estate investment strategies on social welfare outcomes among members of the Rwanda Bar Association's Advocates Investment Company.It assessed property acquisition, rental income, and property developm
content: This study examined the effect of real estate investment strategies on social welfare outcomes among members of the Rwanda Bar Association's Advocates Investment Company.It assessed property acquisition, rental income, and property development in relation to income security, housing access, savings capacity, living conditions, and asset ownership.Guided by Modern Portfolio Theory, Income Capitalization Theory, and Theory of Change, the study adopted a descriptive and correlational mixed-methods design.The target population comprised 320 members and staff, from whom 178 respondents were selected using Slovin's formula, stratified sampling, and simple random sampling.Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and documentary review.Of the 178 questionnaires distributed, 164 were returned, representing a 92.1% response rate.The instrument demonstrated strong validity (CVI = 0.83) and reliability, with Cronbach's alpha values ranging from 0.834 to 0.861.Descriptive results indicated high ratings for property acquisition (M = 4.10), rental income (M = 4.16), property development (M = 4.156), and social welfare outcomes (M = 4.160).Significant positive correlations existed between social welfare and property acquisition (r = .772),rental income (r = .719),and property development (r = .725),all p < .001.Regression results showed that the strategies jointly explained 68.4% of the variance in social welfare outcomes (R² = .684,p < .001),with property acquisition being the strongest predictor (B = .527).The study recommends enhanced due diligence, professional rental management, and disciplined project governance to strengthen welfare outcomes.

title: Alternative materials for sustainable buildings in developing countries: a systematic review (2020–2026)
summary: This systematic review (PRISMA 2020) examines the economic, environmental, regulatory, and social factors influencing the adoption of alternative building materials (e.g., bamboo, earth-based, bio-based) in developing countries between 2020
content: This systematic review (PRISMA 2020) examines the economic, environmental, regulatory, and social factors influencing the adoption of alternative building materials (e.g., bamboo, earth-based, bio-based) in developing countries between 2020 and 2026. It aims to identify material typologies and categorize implementation barriers. Expected results will highlight that adoption is primarily constrained by institutional factors—such as limited green finance, unclear certification frameworks, and fragmented supply chains—rather than technical performance. The findings will provide evidence-based policy recommendations for mainstreaming sustainable materials.

title: From multi-level governance to adoption: co-producing policy recommendations for climate adaptation in seven European regions within an EU-funded project
summary: European countries are developing ambitious climate adaptation strategies, yet implementation remains fragmented, underfunded and frequently misaligned with multi-level governance capacities. Developed within the Horizon 2020 IMPETUS projec
content: European countries are developing ambitious climate adaptation strategies, yet implementation remains fragmented, underfunded and frequently misaligned with multi-level governance capacities. Developed within the Horizon 2020 IMPETUS project, this study presents a multi-method, co-production-oriented approach that connects the assessment of governance, policy and financing barriers with the development of actionable policy recommendations across seven European regions. The approach combined stakeholder mapping and analysis, Theory of Change application, multi-level governance assessment and structured policy mapping with (i) seven regional policy-and-finance workshops, (ii) targeted semi-structured interviews with public-administration representatives and decision-makers from industry and finance, and (iii) a policy-recommendation co-creation session involving regional representatives. The methodology developed supports action-oriented knowledge co-production, cross-regional comparison and the integration of perspectives across the Quintuple Helix, including public authorities, industry and finance stakeholders, academic and research organizations, and civil society, with the natural environment treated as a cross-cutting dimension. The process resulted in 34 co-produced, regionally grounded policy recommendations organized in five areas: governance, policy, funding, legislation, and awareness. Five recurrent implementation barriers were identified across the regions: fragmented governance and unclear responsibilities; limited and uncertain financing; weak integration of adaptation into policy and legislation; insufficient administrative and technical capacity; and uneven stakeholder awareness, participation and ownership. Uptake of co-produced outputs followed a continuum, from stakeholder validation and policy-ready plans to operational use, rather than formal policy adoption. By linking multi-level governance analysis with policy co-production, the study shows how shared and context-specific barriers can be translated into feasible regional implementation pathways. The IMPETUS approach therefore contributes to moving climate adaptation from strategic commitment toward actionable adoption that is regionally anchored and responsive to different institutional contexts.

title: Restoring agricultural ecosystems under the Nature Restoration Regulation: promises, pitfalls and pathways towards sustainable food systems
summary: The EU Nature Restoration Regulation may mark a turning point in European environmental law. It seeks to respond to accelerating biodiversity loss, habitat degradation, and growing climate vulnerability by recognising that ecosystem integri
content: The EU Nature Restoration Regulation may mark a turning point in European environmental law. It seeks to respond to accelerating biodiversity loss, habitat degradation, and growing climate vulnerability by recognising that ecosystem integrity and resilience are indispensable to the sustainable transition promoted by the Green Deal and its vision of a transition towards sustainable food systems. Crucially, the NRR brings agricultural ecosystems, and thus agricultural production, within the scope and logic of restoration in a context where agricultural pressures remain the leading drivers of habitat loss and ecosystem deterioration across the Union. This article builds up from the hypothesis that, although Regulation (EU) 2024/1991 introduces an unprecedented legal features and charcteristics for the restoration of degraded ecosystems, the political and legal compromises embedded in its final text may constrain its capacity to produce transformative change, particularly in agricultural ecosystems. The hypothesis is assessed by examining whether the Regulation is capable of altering the objectives, institutional arrangements, implementation mechanisms and policy relationships that have traditionally shaped the governance of agricultural ecosystems under EU biodiversity and agricultural law.. To answer this question, the article develops a legal and governance framework for assessing the Regulation’s transformative capacity. It first identifies the principal innovations through which the NRR seeks to move forward from the current Nature Directive Framework. It then evaluates whether these innovations are supported by the legal and institutional conditions necessary to produce more than incremental regulatory change. In particular, the analysis considers the binding force and substantive precision of restoration obligations, the capacity of the Regulation to address the structural drivers of agricultural ecosystem degradation, the integration of restoration objectives across biodiversity and agricultural governance, the allocation of responsibilities between the Union and the Member States, and the adequacy of planning, financing, monitoring and accountability mechanisms.

title: From tenants to real estate: the redistributive nature of “renovictions” in Switzerland
summary: In Switzerland, displacement due to renovation or demolition of the existing housing stock is often framed in public and academic discourse as an individual hardship for affected tenants. This paper argues that displacement resulting from s
content: In Switzerland, displacement due to renovation or demolition of the existing housing stock is often framed in public and academic discourse as an individual hardship for affected tenants. This paper argues that displacement resulting from so-called “renovictions” constitutes a process of value appropriation, through which tenants and the public bear a substantial share of the costs of gains accruing to landowners and housing-asset holders. My argument builds on the case of renovictions in estates held by for-profit investors in Basel and Zurich, where, due to the specificities of Swiss tenant law, redevelopment often takes the form of lease terminations affecting entire tenant populations. Drawing on expert interviews with developers, real estate analysts, public authorities, social service providers, and tenants living in such estates, this paper examines three central mechanisms of value appropriation. First, it traces the extraction of reproduction-based housing and land values from both displaced and incoming tenants. Second, it examines how gains generated by publicly financed infrastructure and services are redistributed toward landowners and housing-asset holders, externalizing costs onto the public and undermining public investment in turn. These gains are sustained both by the taxes paid by the municipalities' working populations, who are, in both cases, disproportionately tenants, and by the low-paid labour through which urban improvements are (re-)produced. Third, the paper examines the exploitation of low-paid labour, including in the construction sector, whose work underpins the profits of the real estate industry. Renovictions thus expose a compounding extraction from working-class tenants, who contribute to the creation and financing of rising property values through their labour and taxes only to face higher rents and displacement as those same values are appropriated. This capturing of collectively produced value in the for-profit real estate market helps explain the deepening precarity of lower- and middle-income tenants in Switzerland, while renovictions further drive up asking rents and create pressing challenges for both tenants and public institutions.

title: Effect of Integration of Supply Chain Practices on the Operational Efficiency of Distribution Firms in Rwanda: A Case of Sulfo Rwanda Industries
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study assessed the effect of supply chain integration practices on the operational efficiency of distribution firms in Rwanda, focusing on Sulfo Rwanda Industries.Specifically, the study examined the effect of internal integration on o
content: This study assessed the effect of supply chain integration practices on the operational efficiency of distribution firms in Rwanda, focusing on Sulfo Rwanda Industries.Specifically, the study examined the effect of internal integration on operational efficiency.A mixed-methods approach and descriptive correlational research design were adopted.The target population comprised 567 employees involved in supply chain and operational activities, from which a sample of 235 respondents was determined using Yamane's formula.Stratified and simple random sampling techniques were used.Data were collected through structured questionnaires and interviews and analyzed using SPSS version 26.Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression were employed.The findings revealed that internal integration positively contributes to operational efficiency.Respondents reported that sharing workflow systems, coordinating production, procurement and inventory schedules, conducting regular departmental meetings, improving information sharing, and reducing operational errors enhance organizational efficiency.Pearson correlation analysis showed a strong positive and statistically significant relationship between internal integration and operational efficiency (r = 0.813, p < 0.001).Regression analysis indicated that internal integration significantly predicted operational efficiency, explaining 77.4% of its variation (R² = 0.774).The study concluded that effective internal integration improves coordination, resource utilization, decision-making, and operational performance at Sulfo Rwanda Industries.The study recommends strengthening interdepartmental coordination, investing in integrated information systems, promoting collaborative planning, and improving communication mechanisms to enhance operational efficiency and competitiveness among distribution firms in Rwanda.

title: Green bond issuance by corporates and governments (2014-2025)
source: Publications Office of the European Union
summary: This indicator measures the green bonds which are issued specifically to finance green projects (i.e. the proceeds from green bonds are earmarked for green projects), as a share of all bonds issued by corporates and governments in Europe. T
content: This indicator measures the green bonds which are issued specifically to finance green projects (i.e. the proceeds from green bonds are earmarked for green projects), as a share of all bonds issued by corporates and governments in Europe. The use of proceeds is typically guided by a set of criteria or green bond frameworks. Only bonds classified as green bonds by the data provider are included; social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bonds are excluded. The values include the issuance of all bonds issued by corporates and governments in the calendar year that were issued in a country of the European Union. To be included in the calculation, the bond must be listed with the data provider. Corporates refers to private-sector issuers (including financial institutions) and governments refers to public-sector issuers, as classified by the data provider. Similar content: [EU SDG 13_70] Green bond issuance by type of issuer. The shares per type of issuer are expressed as a percentage of all bonds issued by corporates and governments combined, so the shares for corporates and governments add up to the share for all issuers. Data source restrictions: Data from the commercial data provider London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG). Data are not publicly available.

title: Disease control potential of Mentha longifolia L. Hór-1 chemotype essential oil demonstrated against grapevine grey rot
summary: Introduction Mint essential oils are promising agricultural antifungals as natural alternatives to chemical pest management. However, their phytotoxicity and volatility are challenging their application, which can be overcome by the use of
content: Introduction Mint essential oils are promising agricultural antifungals as natural alternatives to chemical pest management. However, their phytotoxicity and volatility are challenging their application, which can be overcome by the use of adjuvants. In addition to formulation, the investigation of lesser-studied mint chemotypes may also lead to the development of novel and efficient fungicides due to the diversity of secondary metabolites of mint species. Materials and methods The antifungal and phytotoxic effects of the essential oil of Mentha longifolia L. Hó́r-1 chemotype were investigated in the present study using Vitis vinifera as a plant host and the grey rot causal fungus Botrytis cinerea as a pathogen. In addition, the effects of adjuvants on the above traits, as well as the essential oil-fungus interactions, were investigated in detail. Results The previously shown rare composition of M. longifolia L. Hór-1 essential oil was reinforced by the study, which detected significant amounts of thymol and carvacrol. The essential oil showed both fungistatic and fungicidal effects against B. cinerea in vitro . The fungicidal activity and the phytotoxicity of the essential oil against V. vinifera foliar disks were enhanced by the application of pine terpene-based or dioctyl sulfosuccinate emulsifiers. Fine-tuning of the formulation showed that 0.055% (v/v) essential oil in the presence of either adjuvant has no phytotoxic effect on grapevine, has >90% in vitro fungicidal activity, and decreases grey rot symptom severity by ~50% in artificially infected berries. Detailed microscopic analysis suggests that the adjuvants aid the penetration of the essential oil through the fungal cell wall. Discussion The results suggest that 0.055% (v/v) essential oil amended with 0.1% (v/v) pine terpen-based adjuvant can be applied to control grey rot; however, this should be reinforced by field studies. In addition, results reinforce the widely accepted theory that adhesion-promoting adjuvants facilitate the essential oil uptake of target cells.

title: Financial Resilience as a Mediator of the Relationship between Cost of Living, Financial Literacy, Debt Management and Financial Well-Being among M40 Households in Malaysia
source: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
summary: This conceptual paper develops a model in which cost of living, financial literacy, and debt management are theorized as antecedents of financial well-being among M40 households, with financial resilience positioned as the mediating mechani
content: This conceptual paper develops a model in which cost of living, financial literacy, and debt management are theorized as antecedents of financial well-being among M40 households, with financial resilience positioned as the mediating mechanism linking these antecedents to the ultimate outcome. This study develops eights propositions describing the expected direct and indirect relationships among these constructs, which derived from Brüggen’s conceptualization of financial well-being, Salignac’s multidimensional framework of financial resilience and a substantially recent body of literature on financial literacy and household debt behavior. This study is expected to highlight the negative effect of cost of living on financial resilience and through it, on financial well-being. Whereas financial literacy and debt management are expected to exert positive effects on resilience and well-being. As a conceptual contribution, this paper does not report primary data collection. It synthesizes the literature into a coherent, testable framework and proposes a methodology for future empirical validation among Malaysian M40 households. The paper concludes by discussing the theoretical contribution of this model, its practical relevance to household financial planning together with the limitations.

title: Green capital flows: how CSR-driven environmental management influences foreign direct investment in G20 economies
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how corporate social responsibility (CSR)-driven environmental management influences foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in G20 nations over 2005–2024, overcoming limitations and policy implications fo
content: Purpose This study aims to examine how corporate social responsibility (CSR)-driven environmental management influences foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in G20 nations over 2005–2024, overcoming limitations and policy implications for existing literature. Design/methodology/approach This study develops a new Green CSR index (GCI) originally designed to measure environmental management in its entirety and grouped within four pillars: quality of environmental disclosure, reduction in carbon intensity, compliance and good practices toward stakeholders. Based on an unbalanced sample of 19 G20 countries (N = 380), the empirical investigation uses fixed effects, system GMM (to control for endogeneity), spatial Durbin models (to reflect spillovers) and threshold regression (to verify nonlinearity) to provide robust estimates of relationships between GCI and FDI. Findings An increment of one standard deviation in GCI is associated with a 7.2% increase in FDI inflows. This effect is much stronger for emerging (9.7) than for advanced economies (4.1), suggesting a catch-up effect. The effectiveness decreases after a quality threshold for institution (Rule of Law = 0.78). Spatial analysis shows competition bias: gains by one country draw FDI away from neighbors. Policy simulations indicate G20-wide CSR harmonization could result in a US$187bn increase in annual FDI, with high-return interventions (granting mandates for CSR which yield an ROI of 27.5) particularly strong for emerging economies. Originality/value Research presents dynamic multidimensional GCI extending beyond a binary or emission-only CSR. It offers causal, spatially aware and policy-relevant insights about the relationship between environmental CSR and FDI that connects international finance, sustainability strategy and institutional economics for G20 economies.

title: Strengthening Inclusive Economic Development through Mango-Based Green Entrepreneurship: Cross-Border Mentoring of Women MSMEs in Indonesia and Malaysia
source: American Journal of Economic and Management Business (AJEMB)
summary: Women operating mango-based micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) face challenges related to limited product diversification, access to finance, market reach, and adoption of sustainable production practices, which constrain th
content: Women operating mango-based micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) face challenges related to limited product diversification, access to finance, market reach, and adoption of sustainable production practices, which constrain their potential contribution to inclusive economic development. This study evaluated an integrated green entrepreneurship mentoring program implemented through an academic partnership between Indonesia and Malaysia. Using a participatory action research (PAR) approach, the study involved 25 purposively selected women entrepreneurs in North Sumatra, Indonesia, from May to October 2026. Participants completed 90 hours of training covering green entrepreneurship, mango processing, digital marketing, sustainable packaging, and financial literacy. Program outcomes were assessed through pre- and post-training competency assessments, direct observation, focus group discussions, document reviews, and participatory capacity scoring. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and normalized gain (N-gain) calculations. Mean competency scores increased from 40.3 to 72.4, corresponding to a moderate normalized gain of 0.54. The average number of product varieties increased from 1.6 to 4.2, while mango byproduct utilization rose from 12% to 76%. The proportion of participants holding formal business bank accounts increased from 40% to 92%, and marketplace participation reached 88%. The proportion of participants using nonrecyclable plastic packaging decreased from 88% to 28%. These findings suggested that integrated mentoring could support improvements in product innovation, financial inclusion, digital market participation, and environmentally sustainable business practices. The program demonstrated potential as an approach to strengthening women-led MSMEs and supporting inclusive regional economic development. However, the absence of a comparison group limited causal attribution, highlighting the need for longitudinal evaluation to determine whether the observed improvements translated into sustained business performance and environmental benefits.

title: Edible oil microencapsulation for food fortification: technologies, encapsulating systems, and functional applications
source: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
summary: Food fortification with edible oils improves diet quality, but presents limitations of oxidative instability, off-flavors, and reduced shelf life, which can be overcome by microencapsulation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive over
content: Food fortification with edible oils improves diet quality, but presents limitations of oxidative instability, off-flavors, and reduced shelf life, which can be overcome by microencapsulation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in edible oil microencapsulation for food fortification. It evaluates core encapsulation techniques, materials, emulsifiers, and microcapsule properties, highlighting their effects on efficiency, morphology, particle size, and process yield. Furthermore, it synthesizes current evidence on the physicochemical, microbiological, sensory, and nutritional impacts of incorporating microencapsulated edible oils into meat, bakery, dairy, and beverage matrices. Studies indicate that microencapsulation can enhance the nutritional profile of fortified foods, oxidative stability, reducing peroxide values, and increasing sensory acceptance through off-flavor masking. Despite these advances, knowledge gaps remain regarding long-term stability, interactions with food matrices, and validation through in vivo models.

title: Unlocking green finance in developing economies: a grey rational and best-worst multi-criteria approach to barrier assessment and strategic pathways
source: Journal of economic and administrative sciences.
summary: Purpose Green finance, while relatively new, is quickly becoming crucial in sustainable finance. Experts hail it as one of the most effective ways to achieve environmental goals. This study investigates current research to measure barriers
content: Purpose Green finance, while relatively new, is quickly becoming crucial in sustainable finance. Experts hail it as one of the most effective ways to achieve environmental goals. This study investigates current research to measure barriers preventing developing countries from fully embracing a green finance system. Design/methodology/approach Twenty barriers were identified through a literature review and reduced to nine via interviews with financial, economic and environmental experts. These barriers were evaluated using grey rational analysis and the best-worst method. Findings The findings show that developing countries' inability to build green finance systems stems from misalignment between green finance and economic policy, poor business climate, and banks' limited capacity to handle green projects. This study suggests pathways for regulators to systematically overcome these barriers. Practical implications The findings of this study provide strong implications for the regulators of developing countries in identifying the barriers to adopting green finance, and the suggested pathways will aid in formulating more effective plans to advance sustainability in their country. Originality/value This paper examines green finance growth and presents issues based on prior research. We demonstrated barriers to green finance in developing countries through expert opinions and provided adoption pathways.

title: Community Involvement and Performance of Environmental Project: A Case of Green Amayaga Project in Ruhango District, Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: The general objective of this study was to assess the effect of community involvement on the performance of environmental projects, with specific reference to the Green Amayaga Project in Ruhango District.The reliability of the research ins
content: The general objective of this study was to assess the effect of community involvement on the performance of environmental projects, with specific reference to the Green Amayaga Project in Ruhango District.The reliability of the research instrument was assessed using Cronbach's Alpha, while validity was determined through the Content Validity Index (CVI).Data analysis was conducted using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), employing descriptive statistics such as frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations, as well as inferential statistics including correlation and regression analysis at a significance level of 0.05.Multiple regression analysis revealed that all three phases of community involvement have a statistically significant positive effect on project performance (p = 0.000 < 0.05).The implementation phase emerged as the most influential predictor with an unstandardized coefficient (β=0.415,t = 7.830), followed by the monitoring and evaluation phase (β=0.278,t = 5.451) and the initial phase (β=0.233,t = 5.178).The overall model yielded an R-square of 0.747, indicating that these three dimensions of community involvement explain 74.7% of the variance in the performance of the Green Amayaga Project in Ruhango District.The study concludes that active community involvement throughout all project phases is a primary driver of performance of the Green Amayaga Project in Ruhango District.Project managers should institutionalize clear task-specific coordination and role communication during the implementation phase to maximize the environmental performance and beneficiary satisfaction of the Green Amayaga Project.

title: Islamic finance meets climate action: a conceptual exploration of challenges and solutions
summary: Purpose This study aims to explore the strategic alignment between Islamic financial principles and climate action, aiming to advance understanding of how Shariah-compliant instruments can contribute to sustainability goals. It highlights t
content: Purpose This study aims to explore the strategic alignment between Islamic financial principles and climate action, aiming to advance understanding of how Shariah-compliant instruments can contribute to sustainability goals. It highlights the pivotal role of corporate governance in mobilising Islamic finance for climate mitigation and adaptation, offering insights into the opportunities and challenges of integrating ethical finance with global environmental imperatives. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a structured literature review combined with expert interviews to explore the intersection of Islamic finance and climate action. The review systematically synthesises peer-reviewed academic research to identify conceptual linkages and thematic trends. In addition, semi-structured interviews with domain experts were conducted to complement the literature and provide practical insights, enhancing the findings’ theoretical grounding and real-world relevance. Findings This study reveals that Islamic finance offers distinct ethical and structural advantages for supporting climate action, particularly through instruments like green sukuk and social finance. While challenges exist – such as standardisation and governance alignment – Islamic finance demonstrates strong potential to drive sustainable development. Corporate governance emerges as a critical enabler in ensuring accountability, transparency and Shariah alignment in climate-related financial strategies. Research limitations/implications This study contributes to the growing body of knowledge at the intersection of Islamic finance and climate action by offering a practice-informed perspective. Integrating expert interviews enhances the depth of conceptual analysis and provides a valuable foundation for future empirical research and model development in ethical and sustainable finance. Practical implications This study provides strategic insights for Islamic financial institutions, policymakers and corporate leaders on leveraging Shariah-compliant instruments to support climate resilience and sustainable development. By highlighting governance, ethical alignment and innovation pathways, the findings inform policy design, investment strategies and institutional practices aligned with long-term environmental goals. Originality/value This study makes an original contribution by examining the Islamic finance–climate action nexus through an integrated framework that brings together multi-stakeholder perspectives. It advances prior work by foregrounding corporate governance as a central mechanism for mobilising Islamic finance towards sustainable investment. This study also offers practical guidance for Islamic financial institutions, policymakers and corporate leaders, while highlighting how Islamic finance can influence societal sustainability norms and strengthen community resilience.

title: Total Quality Management Practices and Performance of Construction Projects in Rwanda: A Case of ECOMECO Ltd
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: Rwanda's construction sector continues to face recurring quality deficiencies, schedule delays, and cost overruns, linked to inconsistent adoption of Total Quality Management (TQM) practices.This study examined the influence of quality plan
content: Rwanda's construction sector continues to face recurring quality deficiencies, schedule delays, and cost overruns, linked to inconsistent adoption of Total Quality Management (TQM) practices.This study examined the influence of quality planning, quality assurance, quality control, and quality improvement on overall project performance at ECOMECO Ltd, focusing on quality, scope, cost, time, and client satisfaction.A quantitative research design was employed, using a Likertscale questionnaire administered to 109 stratified respondents, of whom 106 provided responses, representing a 97.2% response rate.The instrument demonstrated high content validity (CVI = 0.937) and good reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.826).Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25.0 through descriptive statistics, normality testing, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and ANOVA.Findings showed that quality assurance (mean = 4.83) and quality improvement (mean = 4.41) very strong, while quality planning (mean = 3.64) and control (mean = 3.76) were generally high but lacked formal plans.Project performance was strong in scope compliance but weak in budget and schedule adherence.TQM practices predicted project performance (R = 0.818, R² = 0.669, F = 50.974,p < 0.001).Quality planning had the strongest effect (β = 0.482), followed by quality control (β = 0.385) and quality assurance (β = 0.192), while quality improvement showed a negative effect (β = -0.165).The study concludes that planning and control are pivotal and recommends formalizing TQM frameworks, institutionalizing audits, adopting improvement cycles, and integrating quality management with cost and schedule controls.

title: Streaming into Selfhood: Parasocial Dynamics and Self-pleasing Congruence in Green Repurchase Intentions
summary: Abstract In the live streaming shopping context, this study extends the Expectation Confirmation Theory model by proposing three constructs, including Customer Experience Quality, Parasocial Interaction and Self-Pleasing Experience. These c
content: Abstract In the live streaming shopping context, this study extends the Expectation Confirmation Theory model by proposing three constructs, including Customer Experience Quality, Parasocial Interaction and Self-Pleasing Experience. These constructs are identified as critical drivers of green products repurchase intention, with self-pleasing experience replacing satisfaction to emphasize pleasing value in green consumption. Survey data were collected from 588 respondents regarding their perceptions of green products usage, which were subsequently analyzed using Partial least square-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to investigate its impact on the repurchase intention of green products. The results indicate that customer experience quality and parasocial interaction are significant factors influencing customers’ confirmation of expectations related to live streaming shopping. The findings also confirm that confirmation and perceived performance serve as important mediators in facilitating the generation of self-pleasing experience. Additionally, both perceived performance and self-pleasing experience exhibit a positive relationship with the repurchase intention of customers.

title: Japan’s Decarbonisation Strategy in Southeast Asia: State Developmentalism and Institutional Mechanisms for Regional Energy Transition
summary: Climate change mitigation and the pursuit of net-zero emissions have become central priorities in global governance following the Paris Agreement. Japan faces mounting pressure to transform its energy systems and promote green transformatio
content: Climate change mitigation and the pursuit of net-zero emissions have become central priorities in global governance following the Paris Agreement. Japan faces mounting pressure to transform its energy systems and promote green transformation both domestically and regionally. Southeast Asia, a region undergoing continuous industrialisation and increased energy demand, has been a focal point of Japan’s decarbonisation strategy. Existing literature has examined Japan’s regional energy engagement, including overseas coal financing, strategic competition with China, and the promotion of emerging technologies such as hydrogen and ammonia. However, much of this research lacks a clear political-economic framework and offers limited analysis of the institutional mechanisms through which Japan operationalises its energy transition policies. This article asks two key questions: how has Japan engaged in carbon neutrality strategies toward Southeast Asia, and how can its decarbonisation diplomacy be explained using theoretical tools derived from state developmentalism? It advances two principal arguments. First, Japan has constructed regional institutional frameworks to promote decarbonisation and energy transition in Southeast Asia. Second, Japan’s decarbonisation diplomacy reflects developmentalist policy preferences – securing domestic industrial interests and regional economic presence – supported by institutional capacities that mobilise state agencies and private-sector actors.

title: Capability Conversion and SME Outcomes in Europe: Innovation, Digitalization, and Green Technology
summary: This study examines whether entrepreneurship education, finance, enterprise training, and environmental technology are associated with innovation sales, digital commercialization, and resource-efficiency adoption in European SME ecosystems.
content: This study examines whether entrepreneurship education, finance, enterprise training, and environmental technology are associated with innovation sales, digital commercialization, and resource-efficiency adoption in European SME ecosystems. We analyze unbalanced country–year samples over 2008–2023 using fixed-effect specifications, exploratory indirect-association tests, and moderation models. The original mediation pathways and prespecified interaction tests do not reach conventional 5% statistical significance; these findings do not establish zero effects. Environmental technology is positively associated with resource-efficiency adoption in a limited green-technology specification, subject to country- and year-exclusion sensitivity. In supplementary innovation-sales analyses, the university-education × R&D-transfer interaction is negative in the contemporaneous two-way fixed-effects model (157 observations, 27 countries; β = −4.958, clustered p = 0.016; wild-cluster bootstrap p = 0.0377) but is not statistically significant in the one-year-lagged common-sample specification (wild p = 0.2616) or after excluding 2020 (wild p = 0.1354). A separate cleaner-technology-investment association is likewise sensitive to sample restrictions. Declining complete-case coverage, short effective panels, measurement heterogeneity, and aggregate-level identification preclude firm-level causal conclusions. The evidence supports cautious, context-dependent assessment of capability conversion rather than claims that nonsignificant mechanisms are absent.

title: PROBLEMS IN ORGANISING EDUCATION ON THE "GREEN ECONOMY" AND INTRODUCING RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES
summary: Uzbekistan's green economy requires graduates capable of planning, financing and implementing low-carbon projects; however, the curricula designed to prepare such specialists have not been systematically compared. This article classifies 61
content: Uzbekistan's green economy requires graduates capable of planning, financing and implementing low-carbon projects; however, the curricula designed to prepare such specialists have not been systematically compared. This article classifies 61 study programmes from eight Uzbek universities according to the extent of sustainability integration in their curricula, using three indicators derived from an audit of 1,773 courses: the proportion of sustainability-focused courses, the proportion of courses incorporating sustainability-related topics and the proportion of courses linked to the green economy goals (SDGs 7, 12 and 13). Ward's hierarchical clustering and k-means demonstrated a high level of agreement (adjusted Rand index: 0.78), identifying three groups: nine highly integrated programmes, all at Green University; 19 programmes with medium integration; and 29 programmes with low integration. DBSCAN distinguished only the specialised programmes and placed the remaining programmes along a continuum, indicating that the mediumand low-integration groups differ in degree rather than in kind. Even a renewable energy programme was classified in the low-integration group because its energy-related courses were not complemented by sustainability content across the rest of the curriculum. The scientific novelty of the study lies in classifying individual study programmes rather than universities as a whole, thereby highlighting the importance of establishing programme-level targets for green economy education.

title: Do Alternative Indicators of Overeducation Converge? Evidence from Job Analysis, Realized Matches, and Self-Assessment
summary: Abstract Overeducation is commonly measured using job analysis (JA), realized matches (RM), and self-assessment (SA). Although these approaches are frequently treated as alternative operationalizations of the same phenomenon, questions rema
content: Abstract Overeducation is commonly measured using job analysis (JA), realized matches (RM), and self-assessment (SA). Although these approaches are frequently treated as alternative operationalizations of the same phenomenon, questions remain​ about the extent to which they identify the same workers and reflect a common underlying construct. Using data from the Czech Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC 2022–2023; N = 2,742), this study systematically compares the prevalence, overlap, latent structure, and validity of alternative overeducation indicators. JA benchmarks were derived from the Czech National System of Occupations, while RM benchmarks were constructed from Czech Labour Force Survey data. Results reveal substantial variation in prevalence estimates across measures and only moderate agreement in individual classifications. The strongest convergence is observed between JA and RM, whereas subjective overeducation exhibits considerably weaker alignment with both objective indicators. Latent-structure analyses provide limited support for a single overeducation construct underlying all three measures. Instead, JA and RM form a highly overlapping pair of objective indicators, while SA captures a partially distinct dimension of educational mismatch. Validation analyses show that objective mismatch indicators significantly predict subjective overeducation but explain only a limited share of variation in workers’ subjective assessments. Profile analyses further demonstrate that workers identified by different combinations of indicators differ systematically in their characteristics. The findings challenge the common practice of treating alternative overeducation indicators as interchangeable and suggest that the principal distinction lies between objective and subjective approaches to measuring educational mismatch.

title: Efficient Trading With Price Impact
summary: ABSTRACT This paper studies how to compute trading strategies that trade off expected returns, risk, and the trading costs generated by price impact in an efficient manner. For a general model where impact is nonlinear and decays gradually,
content: ABSTRACT This paper studies how to compute trading strategies that trade off expected returns, risk, and the trading costs generated by price impact in an efficient manner. For a general model where impact is nonlinear and decays gradually, we show that the performance of linear feedback policies can still be computed in closed form. These are optimal for linear impact and linear decay dynamics only. However, when the linear impact parameters are optimized for the nonlinear impact model at hand, then the performance of the resulting policy is competitive with state‐of‐the‐art machine‐learning methods. The gap in performance becomes significant only when the market is so illiquid that neither of the strategies is attractive net of trading costs.

title: The Evolution of Hours Worked and the Gender Wage Gap: Evidence From Four Countries
summary: ABSTRACT We examine the contribution of the intensive margin of labor supply (hours worked above zero) to the gender wage gap over a long time‐horizon across four high‐income economies: France, Germany, the UK, and the US. We do so by bridg
content: ABSTRACT We examine the contribution of the intensive margin of labor supply (hours worked above zero) to the gender wage gap over a long time‐horizon across four high‐income economies: France, Germany, the UK, and the US. We do so by bridging a recent literature on gender differences in high‐paying, high‐hour jobs with traditional wage gap decomposition methods. We first build a model in which firms offer two wage contracts—one that pays a fixed wage but allows workers to choose their preferred number of hours up to “full time,” and a second in which wages are determined by imperfectly observable productivity and can require working more than standard hours. The former includes part‐ and full‐time work, while the latter requires workers to supply long hours but allows them to earn a higher remuneration. We then decompose the hourly wage gap separately for part‐, full‐, and overtime workers to observe the relative contribution of sorting and remuneration across these “hours regimes” over time and across countries. We show that while female employment in overtime work has increased and the gender wage gap has decreased in most countries and hours regimes, this was not driven by increasing selection on observables but rather by a decline over time of the unexplained component of the wage gap—a pattern that holds for most countries and hours regimes. We conclude by considering the contribution of the institutional framework (unions, labor market flexibility, parental leaves) to these cross‐country differences.

title: PENGARUH KARAKTER LABA TERHADAP MARKET VALUE PERUSAHAAN PADA SEKTOR ENERGI YANG TERDAFTAR DI BURSA EFEK INDONESIA
summary: ABSTRACT This study aims to analyze the effect of earnings characteristics on the Market Value of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2016–2025 period. This research employs a quantitative approac
content: ABSTRACT This study aims to analyze the effect of earnings characteristics on the Market Value of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2016–2025 period. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative research design. The study uses secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports and year-end closing stock prices. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 687 firm-year observations. Earnings characteristics are classified based on the relationship among Net Income, Cash Flow from Operations, and Total Accruals, which are represented by dummy variables. Data analysis was conducted using the Weighted Least Squares (WLS) regression method with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics. The results indicate that earnings characteristics in categories D1 and D2 have negative and statistically significant effects on Market Value compared to the reference category, with regression coefficients of -0.335 (sig. 0.028) and -0.472 (sig. 0.030), respectively. In contrast, Net Income and Cash Flow from Operations have positive and statistically significant effects on Market Value. Simultaneously, all independent variables significantly affect Market Value, with a significance level of less than 0.001. The Adjusted R-squared value of 0.267 indicates that the research model explains 26.7% of the variation in companies' Market Value. This study concludes that earnings characteristics, net income, and operating cash flows constitute relevant financial information in relation to market valuation of energy sector companies. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh karakter laba terhadap Market Value perusahaan pada sektor energi yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2016–2025. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian asosiatif kausal. Data yang digunakan merupakan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan tahunan perusahaan dan harga saham penutupan akhir tahun. Sampel ditentukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling dengan total 687 observasi perusahaan-tahun. Karakter laba diklasifikasikan berdasarkan hubungan antara laba bersih (Net Income), arus kas operasi (Cash Flow from Operations), dan total akrual (Total Accruals) yang direpresentasikan melalui variabel dummy. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan regresi Weighted Least Squares (WLS) dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa karakter laba kategori D1 dan D2 berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap Market Value dibandingkan dengan kategori referensi, masing-masing dengan koefisien regresi sebesar -0,335 (sig. 0,028) dan -0,472 (sig. 0,030). Sebaliknya, Net Income dan Cash Flow from Operations berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Market Value.
