title: ОКРЕМІ ПРОБЛЕМИ РЕАЛІЗАЦІЇ ПРАВ ТА ІНТЕРЕСІВ ВЛАСНИКІВ ЗЕЛЕНИХ ОБЛІГАЦІЙ ТА СПОСОБИ ЇХ ВИРІШЕННЯ
summary: У статті досліджено окремі проблеми реалізації прав та інтересів власників зелених облігацій в Україні. Виокремлено та проаналізовано чотири взаємопов’язані проблеми, а саме: (а) неефективність існуючих законодавчих механізмів реагування на
content: У статті досліджено окремі проблеми реалізації прав та інтересів власників зелених облігацій в Україні. Виокремлено та проаналізовано чотири взаємопов’язані проблеми, а саме: (а) неефективність існуючих законодавчих механізмів реагування на порушення емітентами зелених облігацій обов’язків щодо цільового використання коштів, залучених від розміщення зелених облігацій; (б) правову невизначеність щодо тлумачення терміну «грінвошинг» та юридичної відповідальності за вчинення грінвошингу; (в) відсутність законодавчо закріпленої таксономії, зокрема метрики зелених проєктів відповідно до міжнародних критеріїв та стандартів; та (г) відсутність належних процедур нагляду та контролю за діяльністю верифікаторів (незалежних експертів) та юридичної відповідальності перед регулятором та власниками зелених облігацій. Також досліджено чинне правове регулювання зелених облігацій в Україні, зокрема релевантні положення законодавства, які встановлюють вимоги до річної звітності емітентів зелених облігацій в частині цільового використання коштів від розміщення зелених облігацій, положення, які регулюють можливі підстави дефолту за зеленими облігаціями та правові наслідки такого дефолту. Встановлено, що чинне правове регулювання зелених облігацій не адаптоване до специфіки цих фінансових інструментів, зокрема через відсутність вимог щодо обов’язкової незалежної перевірки звітності емітентів, оціночний характер можливої підстави дефолту емітента, яка може застосовуватись у зв’язку із порушенням вимоги про цільове використання коштів від розміщення зелених облігацій, наявність обов’язку власника зелених облігацій довести наявність істотної шкоди для того, щоб обґрунтувати існування обставини дефолту за зеленими облігаціями, а також через обумовленість реалізації права вимоги дострокового погашення зелених облігацій 25-відсотковим порогом голосів усіх власників зелених облігацій. Проаналізовано відповідний досвід правового регулювання зелених облігацій в Європейському Союзі у acquis ЄС, яке регламентує, зокрема, розміщення європейських зелених облігацій та встановлює таксономію сталих інвестицій. Сформульовано пропозиції щодо законодавчого запровадження інституту «зеленого дефолту», зниження кількісного порогу для пред’явлення власниками зелених облігацій вимог про їх дострокове погашення у разі «зеленого дефолту», обов’язкової верифікації звітності про цільове використання коштів, визначення поняття грінвошингу на рівні закону, впровадження таксономії зелених проєктів, а також встановлення юридичної відповідальності верифікаторів перед регулятором та власниками зелених облігацій.

title: Purple economy – Symbiosis between care economy, gender equality, cultural diversity, and sustainable development, and its implementation in agriculture
summary: The text presents purple economy as a dynamic interaction and a unique synergy between social care and vulnerable human capital on the one hand, and cultural diversity and cultural realities as a key component of sustainable development. Pu
content: The text presents purple economy as a dynamic interaction and a unique synergy between social care and vulnerable human capital on the one hand, and cultural diversity and cultural realities as a key component of sustainable development. Purple economy is an alliance of economy, culture and social care trying to link economic development with sustainability. The text also reveals that when applied to agriculture, the purple economy emphasises how cultural values, traditions, creative industries, and identity can enhance agricultural development. In agriculture, purple economy means using cultural and creative assets to add economic, social, and ecological value to farming systems. It links culture, sustainability, creativity and agriculture to boost rural development, protect heritage, and create unique market opportunities.

title: Ozone and Thermal Comfort Responses in Signature Urban Microenvironments under Non-typical Weather
summary: Urban street microenvironments exhibit pronounced heterogeneity in both physical morphology and anthropogenic activity, but ozone pollution and heat stress during non-typical meteorological periods remain poorly understood in these microenv
content: Urban street microenvironments exhibit pronounced heterogeneity in both physical morphology and anthropogenic activity, but ozone pollution and heat stress during non-typical meteorological periods remain poorly understood in these microenvironments. To address this research gap, this study focused on the representativeness of thermal environment and pollution effects, for which two contrasting microenvironments were selected: (Ⅰ) an “urban desertification” area dominated by impervious surfaces, and (Ⅱ) a “traffic-dining” composite pollution belt. Using KZ filtering, regression, and GAM, we found that short-term fluctuations account for over 77% of total O₃ variance in both areas, with wind speed emerging as a key suppressor of O₃ at sub-hourly scales. At longer timescales, solar radiation and temperature positively correlate with O₃, while humidity exerts a negative influence ‒ effects more pronounced in the traffic-dining zone. GAM analysis reveals strong nonlinear relationships between meteorological factors and O₃. The meteorological factors exhibit varying degrees of correlation and jointly regulate both O₃ and Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT), thereby revealing for the first time a compensatory mechanism between the two indices. This study highlights the need for fine-scale, high-frequency monitoring to improve microenvironment management and urban livability.

title: Game Changers or Coincidences? Analyzing Bitcoin's and FBToken's Influence on Fenerbahce Assets
source: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Today's financial markets are shaped by the interaction of traditional instruments and digital assets such as cryptocurrencies. This study examines the short- and long-term relationships between the financial assets of Fenerbahçe Sports Clu
content: Today's financial markets are shaped by the interaction of traditional instruments and digital assets such as cryptocurrencies. This study examines the short- and long-term relationships between the financial assets of Fenerbahçe Sports Club—specifically its stock price (FBS) and fan token (FBT)—Google Trends search interest (FBG), and Bitcoin (BTC). The analysis is based on weekly data covering the period from November 22, 2022, to November 30, 2023. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model was employed to investigate both short- and long-term dynamics. The empirical results reveal no significant long-term relationship between Bitcoin and the other variables. However, Fenerbahçe’s stock price and fan token value have a statistically significant and positive impact on search interest, indicating that the club’s financial performance influences public attention and fan engagement. In the short run, lagged Bitcoin prices negatively affect Fenerbahçe-related financial assets, suggesting delayed investor reactions to cryptocurrency market movements. Additionally, lagged values of Google Trends have a positive and significant effect, underlining the role of digital attention in shaping asset fluctuations. The findings contribute to the growing literature on sports finance and behavioral economics, demonstrating that sports-related assets are influenced by both market fundamentals and public sentiment indicators such as search trends.

title: The orange economy and agriculture
summary: This study explores the relationship between the Orange Economy (creative and cultural industries) and the agricultural sector using Robert Pirsig’s Metaphysics of Quality (MOQ) and Joel Mokyr’s theory of technological progress. While initi
content: This study explores the relationship between the Orange Economy (creative and cultural industries) and the agricultural sector using Robert Pirsig’s Metaphysics of Quality (MOQ) and Joel Mokyr’s theory of technological progress. While initially appearing opposed – one innovative, the other traditional – the two sectors are revealed to interact in a positive feedback loop that drives economic growth. Technological advances in agriculture, stemming from creative scientific breakthroughs (Dynamic Quality events), freed labor for service sector employment, including research and cultural production, which in turn stimulated further agricultural innovation. By analysing the Orange Economy through MOQ’s framework of quality patterns rather than conventional industry categories, this study shows that creativity and artistic values permeate all sectors. Intellectual patterns (scientific knowledge) combined with social patterns (knowledge institutions) are fundamental drivers of sustained economic growth, including in agriculture. Historical data from Sweden and the United States illustrate parallel growth in agricultural productivity and overall economic development. The findings suggest that the Orange Economy’s influence extends beyond measurable creative industries, shaping the entire innovation ecosystem that has transformed human civilization since the Industrial Revolution.

title: Pedological classification as a key determinant of arable soil microbial communities and effects of cash-crop management
summary: Abstract. Climate and soil-related variables, along with soil management practices, have been identified as key determinants of soil microbial composition and, consequently, soil ecosystem functioning. While numerous biogeographic studies a
content: Abstract. Climate and soil-related variables, along with soil management practices, have been identified as key determinants of soil microbial composition and, consequently, soil ecosystem functioning. While numerous biogeographic studies at local to continental scales have identified several variables such as pH, soil carbon quality and quantity and total precipitation as important predictors of microbial composition and diversity, these observations have not been validated by similar biogeographic research within agricultural systems, limiting our ability to compare microbiomes from cultivated sites. This observational study of topsoil microbial composition in Quebec's cash crop fields is one of the rare biogeographical studies conducted in arable land that investigates a wide range of soil, climate, and farming-related variables. In this study, the taxonomic and predictive carbon-related functional composition of microbial communities was investigated in 80 cultivated mineral topsoils across 38,000 km2 in Quebec, Canada. Using multivariate statistics, we examined how two climatic variables (precipitation and growing degree-days), 9 soil-related variables (pedological classification, soil texture and structure, pH, carbon and nutrient concentrations), and 6 agricultural management practices (crop diversity indexes, tillage intensities, organic fertilization type and compaction risk) influenced community variation (represented by the robust Aitchison beta diversity). Pedological classification, based on the Canadian System of Soil Classification, emerged as one of the strongest and most consistent predictors of prokaryotic and fungal community structure and of the structure of inferred prokaryotic carbon-cycling functional potential, whereas farming practices showed little relative influence. All six climate- and soil-related variables that significantly explained microbial variance in the biogeographic analyses were also significantly different between pedological soil classifications. We also hypothesized that the strong predictive power of soil classification indicates that it serves as a proxy for additional key variables. Further taxonomic analyses revealed that stratifying samples by pedological groups provided a more nuanced understanding of the specific effects of organic fertilizer type and soil tillage intensity, with distinct taxonomic families responding within each soil classification and some soils showing distinct sensitivities to specific farming practices. This evidence supports integrating soil classification as a foundational framework for assessing microbial responses to farming practices across soil types and for monitoring the soil microbiome at large geographic scales.

title: High-density planting as an effective strategy for early sugarcane selection
summary: Abstract The initial stage of sugarcane breeding involves evaluating seedlings derived from biparental or polycrosses, which are subsequently assessed through vegetative propagation. In this context, the use of high-density planting may ena
content: Abstract The initial stage of sugarcane breeding involves evaluating seedlings derived from biparental or polycrosses, which are subsequently assessed through vegetative propagation. In this context, the use of high-density planting may enable evaluation of more plants per family or more families within smaller areas, thereby optimizing experimental area and resources during the early stages of the breeding program. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of sugarcane genotypes selected within families under a high-density planting (HDP) system during the initial phase of genetic improvement. Two experiments were conducted at the Sugarcane Research Center of the Federal University of Viçosa. In Experiment I, 98 half-sib families were evaluated in a randomized block design with planting densities of 0.12 m within rows and 1.40 m between rows. Families were ranked based on average values of total soluble solids (Brix) and tons of cane per hectare (TCH). The ten highest-performing and ten lowest-performing families for each trait were identified. Due to overlap between groups, 34 families were ultimately selected. In Experiment II, the two most vigorous stalks per plot from these 34 families were evaluated using an augmented block design. The results showed that family classification was more consistent between experiments for Brix than for TCH. Chi-square tests confirmed a significant association between family classification in Experiment I and individual performance in Experiment II for both characteristics. Individuals selected within superior families under an HDP system maintained their performance in subsequent evaluations, contributing to more efficient resource use and optimizing the evaluation of large populations in limited areas during the early stages of sugarcane breeding.

title: Economic Impact of Implementing a PDCA-Based Traveler Sheet for Cost Reduction in a CNC Machining Area
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Manufacturing companies continuously seek strategies that improve operational efficiency while reducing production costs and increasing profitability. However, the absence of standardized production control mechanisms limits process traceab
content: Manufacturing companies continuously seek strategies that improve operational efficiency while reducing production costs and increasing profitability. However, the absence of standardized production control mechanisms limits process traceability, increases rework, generates material waste, and negatively affects financial performance. This applied research evaluates the economic and operational impact of implementing a traveler sheet (HV-CNC-001) under the Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) methodology in the CNC. A mixed-method approach with a predominantly quantitative design was employed using a pretest–posttest experimental comparison over six months. The implementation was evaluated through six key performance indicators related to production control, traceability, setup time, rework, and information management. Statistical analyses included Student's t-test and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The results showed significant improvements across all evaluated indicators, including a 50.0% reduction in information search time, a 39.6% reduction in traceability-related defects, a 45.5% decrease in specification rework, and an 18.8% reduction in total production cycle time. From an economic perspective, these operational improvements generated estimated annual savings of MXN $706,920, demonstrating that standardized production control contributes directly to cost reduction, productivity improvement, and enhanced manufacturing competitiveness. The findings confirm that integrating PDCA with standardized production documentation not only strengthens operational management but also creates measurable financial value, supporting decision-making aimed at continuous improvement and sustainable industrial competitiveness.

title: MATLAB® for Scientific Computing and Artificial Intelligence
summary: MATLAB ® for Scientific Computing and Artificial Intelligence is divided into three parts: in Section I, the reader is introduced to the MATLAB programming language and shown how MATLAB can aid in the understanding of advanced High School M
content: MATLAB ® for Scientific Computing and Artificial Intelligence is divided into three parts: in Section I, the reader is introduced to the MATLAB programming language and shown how MATLAB can aid in the understanding of advanced High School Mathematics. In Section II, the reader is shown how MATLAB can be used to solve real-world problems from a broad range of scientific disciplines. The end of Section II introduces Simulink. Finally, in Section III, the reader is introduced to neuron oscillator computing, neural networks, and shown how the Deep Learning Toolbox can be used to solve a large array of problems in Artificial Intelligence (AI). This book was developed from a series of national and international workshops that the author has been delivering for over twenty-five years. The book is beginner friendly and has a strong practical emphasis on programming and computational modelling. Features: No prior experience of programming is required. Online GitHub repository available with codes for readers to practice. Covers applications and examples from biology, chemistry, computer science, data science, earth sciences, economics, electrical and mechanical engineering, mathematics, physics, psychology, sports science, statistics, and neuron oscillator computing. Full solutions to exercises are available on the Web. Support Material: GitHub Repository of MATLAB/Simulink files, data files, and Solutions to Exercises: https://github.com/proflynch/MATLAB-for-Scientific-Computing-and-AI/ MATLAB Central File Exchange: https://mathworks.com/matlabcentral/profile/authors/63144/

title: Assess land use changes and the impact on population change across the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Greater Bay Area Urban Clusters
summary: Abstract Hong Kong, Zhuhai, and Macao Greater Bay Area Urban Clusters (HZM-GBAUC) collectively constitute one of the world's most densely populated and institutionally diverse cross-boundary metropolitan clusters. This study systematically
content: Abstract Hong Kong, Zhuhai, and Macao Greater Bay Area Urban Clusters (HZM-GBAUC) collectively constitute one of the world's most densely populated and institutionally diverse cross-boundary metropolitan clusters. This study systematically evaluates land use conditions across the HZM-GBAUC at four discrete time points spanning 2016 to 2025, integrating four corresponding periods of population density data. Employing a land use transfer matrix, a spatial center-of-gravity migration model, and the Getis-Ord Gi* hot spot analysis, this study conducts a quantitative analysis of multi-source remote sensing land use data and demographic statistics through the ArcGIS 10.7 platform. The findings indicate that Zhuhai displays high-intensity population agglomeration across its entire territory; Hong Kong's population distribution is redistributing outward from the urban core toward the peripheral New Territories; and Macao's Cotai reclamation area has facilitated directed population transfer into newly developed built zones. The hot-cold patterns of population growth align broadly with the spatial trajectories of built-up land expansion across the HZM-GBAUC. For the first time, under a unified conceptual framework, the spatio-temporal mechanisms governing land–population linkages across Hong Kong, Zhuhai, and Macao are examined, offering suggestions for the global governance of high-density cross-boundary urban agglomerations in integrating diversified residential land supply.

title: Multiplicity and asymptotic behavior for a biharmonic equation with mixed Neumann-Steklov boundary conditions
source: Nonlinear Differential Equations and Applications NoDEA
summary: Abstract This paper investigates a system with mixed Neumann and nonlinear Steklov boundary conditions, motivated by the elasticity theory of thin plates. By means of the inversion reduction method, the system is rigorously transformed into
content: Abstract This paper investigates a system with mixed Neumann and nonlinear Steklov boundary conditions, motivated by the elasticity theory of thin plates. By means of the inversion reduction method, the system is rigorously transformed into a single biharmonic equation exhibiting a concave-convex structure. More precisely, we study the case in which the interior exponent satisfies $$2<p<2_*$$ 2 < p < 2 ∗ and the boundary exponent satisfies $$1<q<2$$ 1 < q < 2 , under the influence of a parameter $$\lambda >0$$ λ > 0 and a sign-changing weight function $$b(x)$$ b ( x ) . According to whether the boundary integral of the weight function is strictly negative or equal to zero, variational methods are used to establish the existence of at least two solutions or of one guaranteed solution, respectively. In each case, at least one component of the corresponding solution pair changes sign. In addition, a detailed asymptotic analysis as $$\lambda \rightarrow 0^+$$ λ → 0 + is developed, proving strong convergence of the solution pairs and identifying the limits of suitable rescaled families through associated limiting equations.

title: Trade Determinants and Export Potential of Senegalese Vegetable Products
source: Revue Française d'Economie et de Gestion
summary: This paper aims to identify the key factors and export potential of Senegalese vegetables to 33 partners for the period 2000-2021. We apply the Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood method (PPML) to the structural gravity model using WITS, CEPI
content: This paper aims to identify the key factors and export potential of Senegalese vegetables to 33 partners for the period 2000-2021. We apply the Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood method (PPML) to the structural gravity model using WITS, CEPII, WDI and WDG databases. The results suggest that Senegalese exports of horticultural products can be boosted both by strengthening macroeconomic competitiveness and by targeting importers with high GDP, strong institutional robustness, a shared colonial past, and preferential trade agreements. Conversely, administrative costs and procedures, as well as the language barrier, considerably reduce trade flows. The assessment of export potential revealed substantial untapped commercial potential. Indeed, all of Senegal's partners represent only the tip of the iceberg (0 to 30%). It also highlights a high concentration of trade flows towards a few European partners, while African partner countries remain marginal in the export structure.

title: Femuna: designing an integrated digital ecosystem for women across life domains
summary: Background Despite the proliferation of mobile health (mHealth) applications, women continue to manage reproductive health, mental wellness, financial planning, and caregiving responsibilities across disconnected, single-purpose tools—a fra
content: Background Despite the proliferation of mobile health (mHealth) applications, women continue to manage reproductive health, mental wellness, financial planning, and caregiving responsibilities across disconnected, single-purpose tools—a fragmentation that increases cognitive load, reduces long-term engagement, and remains underexplored in the mHealth literature. Objectives This work presents Femuna, an integrated cross-platform application designed around the principle of functional interdependence, and evaluates whether coherence-centered design measurably improves the user experience of women managing multiple life domains. Methods Femuna was implemented in Flutter and Firebase, combining task management, menstrual and pregnancy tracking, emotion monitoring, financial planning, educational content, and peer community support over a shared data layer through which features inform one another and drive adaptive notifications, and an AI mental-wellness chatbot deployed via a prompt-engineered Mistral 7B (BERTScore F1 = 0.8406). Usability was assessed through a mixed-methods design combining a concurrent think-aloud protocol with a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire, administered to a purposive sample of 185 women (ages 18–50) across diverse occupational and family contexts. Results Questionnaire responses yielded an aggregate mean usability score of 4.2 on the five-point scale, indicating consistently high satisfaction across all evaluated dimensions, and thematic analysis of session transcripts showed that participants particularly valued functional integration, reporting reduced task-switching burden and an interface organization aligned with the relational structure of their daily responsibilities. Conclusions The findings support coherence-centered design as a measurable quality criterion in mHealth development and ground a replicable framework for gender-responsive applications based on feminist HCI principles, integrated systems architecture, and participatory usability evaluation.

title: Mindset-signaling teacher practices: a revised conceptual framework
summary: Research on teacher practices that communicate mindset-related messages has expanded in recent years, yet the literature remains conceptually fragmented because similar practices are described with different terminology and varying levels o
content: Research on teacher practices that communicate mindset-related messages has expanded in recent years, yet the literature remains conceptually fragmented because similar practices are described with different terminology and varying levels of specificity. This narrative mini review revisits Sun's conceptual framework of mindset-signaling teacher practices, drawing on empirical research to refine and extend its categorization of teacher practices. Relevant studies were identified through literature searches in Scopus, Web of Science, and ERIC, together with backward reference searching. Eleven empirical studies informed the revision of the original framework. The revised framework comprises five categories (sorting, norm setting, value placement, instructional support, and emotional responses to difficulty) with subcategories that organize mindset-signaling teacher practices while integrating conceptually similar practices previously described with different terminology across studies. By providing a common conceptual language, the framework offers a basis for measurement development, empirical research, and the translation of mindset theory into evidence-informed classroom practice.

title: Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: A field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals
summary: Leak detection on pumped transmission mains that cross steep terrain relies on hydraulic signals whose response to a small leak may be comparable to sensor noise. We evaluated five unsupervised methods (PELT with Bayesian and Akaike penalti
content: Leak detection on pumped transmission mains that cross steep terrain relies on hydraulic signals whose response to a small leak may be comparable to sensor noise. We evaluated five unsupervised methods (PELT with Bayesian and Akaike penalties, Bayesian online changepoint detection [BOCD], an OLS-CUSUM structural-break procedure and a moving-average ±3σ chart) on flow and pressure series recorded every 30 s during seven controlled leak trials (valve setting 3-5% of nominal flow) in two field campaigns on an Andean transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. Detections were compared with a chance-level reference obtained by placing the same number of changepoints at random. Relative to the preceding leak-free observations, flow decreased in all seven trials (mean -0.50%; sign test p = 0.016; placebo test p = 0.003), whereas pressure, recorded at 0.1-m resolution, showed no change (placebo p = 0.99). No single event exceeded its per-event detection threshold; the flow change was resolvable only as a seven-event mean (signal-to-noise ratio -3.3). None of the five detectors located leak onsets more often than chance (pooled p > 0.40 for every method-signal pair). The PELT variants flagged six of seven events on pressure, but at 560-960 false alarms per day and 13-33% precision. Although BOCD on pressure reached the highest average precision (0.54), its excess over the chance reference was not significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.14). A CUSUM tuned to the observed flow change, the optimal sequential detector for a persistent shift, would need 12-29 min to detect it at one false-alarm per day, 8-20 times the trial duration. Chance-level performance is therefore the expected outcome for 90-120-s leaks at 30-s sampling, whereas a persistent leak producing the same flow change would be detectable within tens of minutes.

title: L'impact du secteur informel sur la croissance économique et la réduction de la pauvreté dans les pays de l'UEMOA
source: Revue Française d'Economie et de Gestion
summary: L’objectif principal de cette étude consiste à analyser le rôle du secteur informel dans le développement économique des pays de l’UEMOA en mettant en évidence ses effets à la fois sur la croissance économique et sur la pauvreté. Sa contrib
content: L’objectif principal de cette étude consiste à analyser le rôle du secteur informel dans le développement économique des pays de l’UEMOA en mettant en évidence ses effets à la fois sur la croissance économique et sur la pauvreté. Sa contribution réside dans le fait qu’elle apporte un éclairage nouveau sur l’importance du secteur informel dans les économies de l’UEMOA. Les données employées proviennent de la base de données de la Banque Mondiale et de celle de l’Organisation Internationale du Travail. L’approche méthodologique utilise des modèles de panel, notamment les modèles à effets fixes. Les résultats obtenus révèlent que le secteur informel exerce un impact globalement positif sur la croissance économique et qu’il participe de façon substantielle à la réduction de la pauvreté dans les pays de l’UEMOA. Sur le plan de la croissance, le secteur informel contribue de manière significative à l’activité économique en absorbant une large part de la main-d’œuvre et en générant une production réelle. En ce qui concerne la réduction de la pauvreté, le secteur informel joue un rôle essentiel en créant des opportunités d’emploi pour les populations exclues du marché du travail formel.

title: Legal Obligations for AI Explainability: Open Questions on Technical Methods
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: In this paper, we connect legal scholarship on transparency, reason-giving, and justification in algorithmic decision-making systems (ADMS) with the technical literature on AI Explainabilitypose an organisational decision-making architectur
content: In this paper, we connect legal scholarship on transparency, reason-giving, and justification in algorithmic decision-making systems (ADMS) with the technical literature on AI Explainabilitypose an organisational decision-making architecture to situate technical explanations within their institutional and legal context, and use this framework to analyse the explainability obligations arising under European Union law. The paper discusses where AI Explainability approaches may be useful in satisfying legal obligations, alongside their limitations. Drawing on examples of ADMS, we illustrate how technical explanations may support, and where they may fail to support, legally meaningful reason-giving in practice. Building on this analysis, the paper identifies a set of open interdisciplinary research questions concerning the conditions under which technical approaches to explaining ADMS can satisfy legal obligations, contributing to a more precise and productive dialogue between legal and technical communities on legally meaningful AI explainability.

title: Understanding Leadership in Theory and Practice: Developing the Reflective Leader
summary: This book provides a critical but accessible introduction to leadership theory, encouraging readers to question, compare, and apply new perspectives in relation to their own experiences and practice. Beginning with a discussion about what g
content: This book provides a critical but accessible introduction to leadership theory, encouraging readers to question, compare, and apply new perspectives in relation to their own experiences and practice. Beginning with a discussion about what good and bad leadership looks like, the book then guides the reader through a dozen prominent leadership theories, using a novel typology organised around sociological, psychological or methodological perspectives. It then considers how leadership is shaped by circumstance through the Organisational Context Matrix. A central theme of the book is the importance of reflection and reflexivity in leadership learning. Readers are encouraged not only to consider what leadership theory tells us but also how their own experiences, assumptions and behaviours shape their understanding and practice of leadership. Case studies, vignettes, historical examples and reflective questions encourage critical engagement, enabling students to bridge between theory and practice. Combining theoretical depth with practical application, this book offers a distinctive approach to understanding leadership and developing a lifelong orientation towards leadership learning. Novel in its applied approach, and rich in both theory and practice Understanding Leadership in Theory and Practice should be core reading for advanced undergraduate, postgraduate and professional students of leadership, in addition to practicing and aspiring leaders.

title: The Charge as You Drive Project. Full Scale Testing of a Solution for Dynamic Charging of Electric Vehicles by Induction
summary: Abstract Electric Road Systems (ERS) are a promising solution for charging electric vehicles, increasing their range while reducing battery size. However, their reliability must be validated under real operating conditions. In France, withi
content: Abstract Electric Road Systems (ERS) are a promising solution for charging electric vehicles, increasing their range while reducing battery size. However, their reliability must be validated under real operating conditions. In France, within the Charge as You Drive (CAYD) project funded by the government, a 1.5 km dynamic inductive charging demonstrator was built on the A10 motorway near Paris and is currently under evaluation. This article presents studies conducted in the CAYD project to characterize the mechanical response of pavements with embedded inductive coils and assess their durability under heavy traffic. A full-scale accelerated pavement test (APT) was performed to compare seven integration solutions, instrumented and subjected to 200,000 heavy vehicle load cycles. The most durable solution was selected for the A10 demonstrator. The instrumented A10 section has been open to traffic since April 2025, and charging tests with three types of vehicles have started. Initial results show satisfactory performance, with an average charging power of 200 kW for heavy-duty vehicles.

title: Influence of Soil Transverse Isotropy on the Thermo‐Mechanical Response of Energy Piles
source: International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics
summary: ABSTRACT Driven by carbon neutrality goals, energy piles have emerged as a sustainable technology integrating structural support with geothermal energy harvesting. However, the complex thermo‐mechanical interactions within the pile–soil sys
content: ABSTRACT Driven by carbon neutrality goals, energy piles have emerged as a sustainable technology integrating structural support with geothermal energy harvesting. However, the complex thermo‐mechanical interactions within the pile–soil system, especially considering the transverse isotropy inherent in natural sedimentary soils, remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a rigorous three‐dimensional continuum‐based analytical method for energy piles embedded in transversely isotropic soil. By introducing two displacement potential functions, the governing thermoelastic equations are decoupled, and closed‐form solutions are derived by satisfying continuity conditions at the pile–soil interface. The accuracy of the proposed method is validated against centrifuge tests and full‐scale field measurements. Parametric analyses reveal that the transverse isotropy of the soil modulates the stress field. Specifically, increasing the horizontal‐to‐vertical stiffness ratio and thermal expansion ratios enhances the soil restraint on the pile, leading to an increase in additional thermal stress of the soil. In contrast, the transverse isotropy of thermal conductivity has a marginal effect on the mechanical response. The proposed method provides a basis for assessing the influence of soil transverse isotropy on the thermo‐mechanical response of energy piles.

title: Higher Education Resource Agglomeration and Urban Low-Carbon Green Innovation: A Nonlinear Perspective in the Context of Carbon Neutrality
summary: As a key part of urban innovation systems, higher education resources shape cities’ capacity for low-carbon green innovation through knowledge production, technology diffusion, talent cultivation, and entrepreneurial activity. Using panel d
content: As a key part of urban innovation systems, higher education resources shape cities’ capacity for low-carbon green innovation through knowledge production, technology diffusion, talent cultivation, and entrepreneurial activity. Using panel data from 288 Chinese cities, this study applies a quantile-on-quantile regression framework to examine how different dimensions of higher education resource agglomeration are associated with the distributional and nonlinear patterns of urban low-carbon green innovation. The results show that: (1) The associations between higher education resource agglomeration and urban low-carbon green innovation differ across resource dimensions. In the baseline model with city and year fixed effects, university and student agglomeration have positive coefficients at the 10% and 5% levels, respectively, using conventional standard errors, whereas the faculty coefficient is not statistically significant. (2) The association between higher education resource agglomeration and low-carbon green innovation exhibits a nonlinear distributional pattern. Positive associations at some quantile combinations coexist with negative associations at others. (3) The interaction between economic density and faculty agglomeration is negative and significant using conventional standard errors, whereas the environmental-policy-attention interactions are not statistically significant. City-clustered inference does not support statistical significance for the baseline coefficients or the faculty–economic-density interaction. These results suggest that efforts to strengthen urban low-carbon green innovation should focus on optimizing rather than simply expanding higher education resource agglomeration and should adopt differentiated strategies that reflect local educational endowments, innovation capacity, and education–industry alignment.

title: Deep generative design and structure-based evaluation of celecoxib-inspired PTGS2/COX-2 ligands: a computational study in the context of adenomyosis-associated inflammation
summary: Adenomyosis is a chronic inflammatory gynecological disorder in which cyclooxygenase-2 (PTGS2/COX-2)-derived prostaglandin signaling contributes to inflammation. This study asked whether deep learning-based generative modification of the ce
content: Adenomyosis is a chronic inflammatory gynecological disorder in which cyclooxygenase-2 (PTGS2/COX-2)-derived prostaglandin signaling contributes to inflammation. This study asked whether deep learning-based generative modification of the celecoxib scaffold yields compounds with a more favorable predicted interaction profile at PTGS2. A generative platform combining a three-dimensional convolutional neural network with a conditional variational autoencoder returned twelve analogues, all carried forward without post hoc selection and examined by substructure analysis, docking at the experimentally defined ligand-binding site, pharmacophore comparison, ADMET and toxicity prediction, density functional theory, and 200 ns molecular dynamics with MM/GBSA estimation. The benzenesulfonamide group of celecoxib was retained in five of twelve analogues and the trifluoromethyl-pyrazole core in none, so the compounds are better described as scaffold-hopped analogues than as close derivatives. AI Analogue 2 returned the most favorable predicted binding energy (− 10.024 kcal/mol; celecoxib − 7.748 kcal/mol) and formed a persistent complex with an effective binding energy of − 51.89 kcal/mol. Its predicted pose lies along the main cyclooxygenase channel rather than the COX-2 side pocket occupied by celecoxib, so the two energies are not comparable as affinities. Redocking of the co-crystallized ligand gave a deviation of 1.924 Å and the celecoxib trajectory did not converge, indicating a rigid-receptor starting-pose artifact rather than a property of the generated compounds. Predicted blood–brain barrier permeability coincided with an active neurotoxicity call, identifying central exposure as the principal predicted liability. The study does not establish COX-2 inhibition, selectivity over COX-1, improved safety, or therapeutic activity in adenomyosis .

title: From Possibility to Probability: Population-Genetic Accessibility of Enzyme Specialization After Gene Duplication Original Article
summary: Abstract Promiscuous enzymes catalyze more than one reaction, creating opportunities for new functions but also trade-offs when improving one reaction reduces another. Gene duplication may resolve this conflict by allowing the two copies to
content: Abstract Promiscuous enzymes catalyze more than one reaction, creating opportunities for new functions but also trade-offs when improving one reaction reduces another. Gene duplication may resolve this conflict by allowing the two copies to specialize, but only if the new copy survives long enough to diverge. We combined a constraint-based model of enzyme activity with forward-time simulations in SLiM to separate what happens after a duplicate is retained from whether a new duplicate can reach that state. Under dosage compensation, persistent specialization evolved in 56 of 300 populations in which duplication was imposed, but in none of 5,700 simulations that began with one new duplicate. Including additive dosage increased establishment from 51 to 2,421 of 5,700 origins, increased near-fixation from 1 to 2,421, and produced 102 persistent specialists. However, dosage did not change specialization after population-wide retention: 61 of 1,140 compensated populations and 60 of 1,140 additive populations specialized. Once every individual carried the duplicate, the shared dosage benefit no longer changed which genotypes were favored. All specialists arising from a single origin occurred under strong catalytic antagonism and high mutation supply. Thus, dosage primarily determined whether a new duplicate survived and spread, whereas catalytic conflict and mutation supply determined whether retained copies later specialized.

title: Glauconitic Greensand as a Sedimentary Source of Natural Hydrogen Generation: Experimental Insights and Implications for Basin Screening
summary: Natural hydrogen has been increasingly discussed as a low-carbon energy resource; however, most exploration concepts have focused on ultramafic rocks. This study conducted a screening case study of glauconitic sand from the Arnager Formatio
content: Natural hydrogen has been increasingly discussed as a low-carbon energy resource; however, most exploration concepts have focused on ultramafic rocks. This study conducted a screening case study of glauconitic sand from the Arnager Formation (Bornholm, Denmark) to assess its potential to generate natural hydrogen. The starting material was reacted with deionized water in sealed batch reactors for 24 h while varying the temperature (50–80 °C) and solid–liquid ratio (0.3–2) as a proxy for water– rock interaction. Gas chromatography showed that the gas produced was H2-dominant, with minor amounts of H2S and CO that varied with experimental conditions. The post-reaction mineralogy and bulk chemistry indicated a quartz-dominated framework that remained largely intact, whereas the Fe-bearing component showed evidence of selective modification: glauconite abundance decreased relative to the starting material, bulk Fe was depleted, and K was broadly retained in the solids. Together, these observations support a transferable concept: quartz-rich sands can act as redox-active substrates for hydrogen generation if they contain a reactive Fe-bearing fraction and are in contact with water at a favorable temperature and water–rock ratio.

title: Thermal-regulating smart windows for a sustainable future
summary: Thermal-regulating smart windows are emerging as key technologies for improving building energy efficiency while preserving daylight access and visibility. Conventional windows allow excessive solar heat gain, heat loss, condensation, and f
content: Thermal-regulating smart windows are emerging as key technologies for improving building energy efficiency while preserving daylight access and visibility. Conventional windows allow excessive solar heat gain, heat loss, condensation, and frost, which increase energy demand. This review examines thermal-regulating smart windows from an integrated perspective, focusing on the coordinated combination of heating, cooling, and dynamic optical modulation under changing seasonal conditions. Active approaches, including Joule heating, dielectric heating, and thermoelectric cooling, provide controllable surface heating or cooling. Conversely, passive strategies, including low-emissivity coating, solar-thermal conversion, radiative cooling, and evaporative cooling, regulate heat exchange without continuous energy input. Chromic technologies, including electrochromic, mechanochromic, thermochromic, and photochromic systems, enable adaptive control of solar and thermal radiation. By comparing these mechanisms based on their complementary seasonal roles, spectral selectivity, energy requirements, and integration potential, this review differentiates multifunctional thermal management from single-function smart-window concepts. Applications in buildings, vehicles, greenhouses, and wearable or flexible devices are also discussed. Finally, we identify key perspectives for next-generation windows, including multifunctional integration, independent spectral control, climate-responsive operation, scalable manufacturing, long-term durability, life-cycle sustainability, and real-building validation. These advances could enable adaptive glazing platforms that simultaneously manage heat, light, comfort, and energy under dynamic environmental and seasonal conditions. This Review differentiates multifunctional thermal management from single-function smart-window concepts. Applications in buildings, vehicles, greenhouses, and wearable or flexible devices are discussed.

title: Un orden de magnitud menos: 0,13–0,32 t C/ha/año arbitrados, no las 2,5–9 prometidas
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Ninguna variable ambiental del pastoreo ha generado más promesas por unidad de evidencia que el carbono del suelo. Este artículo ordena las cifras que el libro «Manejo de pastos y forrajes» imprime en sus capítulos 26 y 3, afirmación por af
content: Ninguna variable ambiental del pastoreo ha generado más promesas por unidad de evidencia que el carbono del suelo. Este artículo ordena las cifras que el libro «Manejo de pastos y forrajes» imprime en sus capítulos 26 y 3, afirmación por afirmación y con su estatuto, y muestra que entre la literatura arbitrada y la no arbitrada hay un orden de magnitud de diferencia. La síntesis de Garnett et al. (2017), del Food Climate Research Network de la Universidad de Oxford [gris institucional, síntesis], estima el potencial global del mejor manejo de pastizales en 0,3–0,8 Gt CO₂/año, suficiente para compensar solo entre el 20 y el 60 % de las emisiones de los propios animales en pastoreo, con una ganancia que se satura hacia los ~40 años y es reversible si el manejo se revierte: ninguna promesa de neutralidad sale de esa cifra. A escala de finca, los siete estudios arbitrados de la revisión resumida por el Leverhulme Centre dan tasas de 0,13–0,32 t C/ha/año, frente a las 2,5–9 t C/ha/año que circulan en la literatura no arbitrada. Y la afirmación mayor —bajar el CO₂ atmosférico a niveles preindustriales con el manejo del pastoreo— está refutada en su propia aritmética por Briske et al. (2013) [arbitrada]: exigiría 2 t C/ha/año adicionales y sostenidas en unas 5.000 millones de hectáreas, cuando las tierras de pastoreo son sumideros muy débiles a esa escala. La conclusión práctica es la doctrina del libro: el carbono del buen manejo se cuenta como co-beneficio ambiental probable y como argumento de permanencia del sistema, nunca como flujo de caja proyectado sin comprador y contrato reales, y nunca como promesa de neutralidad.

title: Retrofitting Existing Housing with Sustainable Construction Materials in Greater Manchester, UK and Lagos, Nigeria: A Comparative Study Protocol
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Applied Science
summary: Buildings account for approximately 37% of global energy- and process-related CO2 emissions, making retrofitting of existing housing stock a significant lever for climate mitigation. This paper is a study protocol, not a report of completed
content: Buildings account for approximately 37% of global energy- and process-related CO2 emissions, making retrofitting of existing housing stock a significant lever for climate mitigation. This paper is a study protocol, not a report of completed research: it sets out the rationale, research questions, study area, and a proposed mixed-methods design, including a multi-criteria material evaluation framework and a structured cross-case comparison matrix, for a planned comparative study of housing retrofit practice in Greater Manchester, UK, and Lagos, Nigeria. Greater Manchester has an estimated 880,000 homes requiring some form of energy retrofit by 2038, with a current regional target to retrofit at least 60,000 homes between 2025 and 2030; Lagos State's own housing deficit is separately estimated at approximately 3.3 to 3.4 million units, distinct from Nigeria's national housing deficit of approximately 15 million officially, or up to 28 million when structurally substandard homes are included. The protocol proposes purposive sampling of practitioners in each city, case study review of completed retrofit projects against an explicit multi-criteria evaluation matrix, and thematic analysis of interview and survey data, with the explicit aim of identifying which UK retrofit materials and practices could transfer to Lagos's tropical climate and weaker regulatory environment, and which cannot. No data collection has yet occurred; the contribution of this paper is the verified background and a proposed, reviewable, and now more fully specified method.

title: Boosting electrochemical CO2 capture using hybrid electrode configurations in supercapacitive swing adsorption
summary: Abstract This work investigates the effect of electrode configuration on CO2 capture in supercapacitive swing adsorption (SSA), with a battery-type electrochemical CO2-capture system included for comparison. Three systems with distinct elec
content: Abstract This work investigates the effect of electrode configuration on CO2 capture in supercapacitive swing adsorption (SSA), with a battery-type electrochemical CO2-capture system included for comparison. Three systems with distinct electrode configurations were studied: a symmetric supercapacitor with two identical activated carbon electrodes (AC//AC), an asymmetric supercapacitor with a manganese dioxide positive electrode and an activated carbon negative electrode (MnO2//AC), and a comparative battery-type electrochemical CO2-capture system with a manganese dioxide positive electrode and a zinc foil negative electrode (MnO2//Zn). The net CO2 response depended on electrode configuration and gas-facing orientation. When the MnO2//Zn battery-type system was employed with ZnSO4 electrolyte, the CO2 adsorption capacity reached 768.85 mmol kg-1, significantly higher than the 190.87 mmol kg-1 achieved by the conventional AC//AC symmetric system. This study provides insight into how electrode configuration and charge-storage behaviour affect SSA and related electrochemical CO2-capture systems.

title: Lightweight and Hydrophobic Bamboo‐Plastic Porous Composites With Enhanced EMI Shielding Performance
summary: ABSTRACT Rapid 5G and smart electronics development makes electromagnetic interference (EMI) a critical threat to stability, security, and health. Conventional polymer‐based shields, however, suffer from insufficient conductivity, weak adhe
content: ABSTRACT Rapid 5G and smart electronics development makes electromagnetic interference (EMI) a critical threat to stability, security, and health. Conventional polymer‐based shields, however, suffer from insufficient conductivity, weak adhesion, and non‐degradability, limiting advanced applications. Herein, a high‐performance bamboo‐plastic composite was rationally designed using renewable copper‐plated bamboo fiber (MBF, via acid‐alkali pretreatment and dual‐step electroless plating) as the scaffold and biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) with 11.9 wt% CNTs as the conductive matrix. The as‐prepared MBF/CNTs/PLA composite formed a uniform and dense conductive network, achieving a high electrical conductivity of 18.2 S/cm and exhibiting an outstanding electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness (EMI SE) of 67.2 dB in the X‐band at a thickness of 2 mm. The shielding was achieved via a combined reflection‐absorption mechanism, where absorption dominated the penetrated energy attenuation ( SE A / SE T ≈ 87%), thereby mitigating secondary electromagnetic pollution. Additionally, the composite exhibited excellent overall performance, including a tensile strength of 15.0 MPa and superhydrophobicity (water contact angle of 150.2°). This lightweight biomass composite provides a sustainable strategy for efficient EMI shielding and holds promising prospects for 5G electronics, flexible electromagnetic protection, and lightweight packaging.

title: From Green Innovation to Legitimacy: The Roles of ESG Engagement and Institutional Context in China
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental innovation does not automatically confer legitimacy: firms must also persuade institutional audiences that their actions merit recognition. This distinction matters in state‐capitalist economies, where the state evalu
content: ABSTRACT Environmental innovation does not automatically confer legitimacy: firms must also persuade institutional audiences that their actions merit recognition. This distinction matters in state‐capitalist economies, where the state evaluates firms alongside investors and communities. Using panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we examine the association between green innovation and state‐oriented legitimacy (SOL), the mediating role of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) engagement, and the moderating role of regional institutional quality. We distinguish green innovation as a substantive activity, ESG engagement as a potential signal, and SOL as a state‐oriented legitimacy measure. Green innovation is positively associated with SOL, partly through ESG engagement. Institutional quality appears to strengthen this indirect relationship mainly through the link between innovation and ESG engagement. The findings extend research on how institutional context shapes the relationship between environmental activity, corporate signalling, and legitimacy.

title: From digital drive to green breakthrough: How supply chain digitalization expands firms’ green innovation boundaries
summary: In the current digital economy era, supply chain digitalization is a pivotal catalyst of enterprise transformation and development. It also is an indispensable foundation upon which to address imbalances between the quantity and quality of
content: In the current digital economy era, supply chain digitalization is a pivotal catalyst of enterprise transformation and development. It also is an indispensable foundation upon which to address imbalances between the quantity and quality of green innovation. Using data from China’s A-share listed companies and leveraging its Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Policy as a quasi-natural experiment, this paper examines how policy-induced supply chain digitalization affects firms’ green innovation boundaries. Empirical evidence suggests that the policy-induced advancement of supply chain digitalization significantly promotes the expansion of firms’ green innovation boundaries, primarily through two mechanisms: enhanced digital knowledge absorption capacity and reduced knowledge application costs. Moreover, the boundary-expanding effect associated with policy-induced supply chain digitalization is more pronounced in firms with executives holding environmental backgrounds and in digital-intensive industries. Furthermore, the expansion of green innovation boundaries associated with policy-induced supply chain digitalization exhibits distinct characteristics. Firstly, content-wise, it emphasizes design and production. Secondly, in depth, it favors technological invention. Thirdly and finally, in position, it displays both upstream and downstream orientation. The findings of this study highlight the importance of policy initiatives that facilitate supply chain digitalization, promoting efficient flows of digital knowledge and elements of green innovation, and reducing the costs of knowledge application to promote green innovation breakthroughs along value chains.

title: Surface chemistry governs early redox and cytokine responses to superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles across hepatic-relevant cell models
summary: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) are increasingly utilised in biomedical and nanomedicine applications, raising important questions regarding early interactions with hepatic cellular systems. This study investigated how s
content: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) are increasingly utilised in biomedical and nanomedicine applications, raising important questions regarding early interactions with hepatic cellular systems. This study investigated how surface chemistry influences the biological behaviour of SPIONs across hepatic-relevant cell models through integrated physicochemical characterisation and response screening. Carboxyl (CAR), amine (AMI), and polyethylene glycol (PEG)-coated SPIONs were characterised in biologically relevant media, revealing coating-dependent agglomeration. SPION exposure (2-24h) was conducted in THP-1 (macrophage-like), Hep G2 (hepatocyte), EA.hy926 (endothelial), and HMC-1.1 (mast cell) models to assess cytotoxicity, redox balance and inflammatory signalling. SPION-induced reactive oxygen species generation and reduced glutathione depletion occurred in a coating- and cell-type-dependent manner, with THP-1 cells showing the greatest sensitivity. Cytokine profiling revealed different responses across models. THP-1 cells demonstrated pronounced pro-inflammatory activation, including increased IL-8, IL-1β and IL-18 secretion, with PEG-SPIONs driving the strongest effects. Conversely, Hep G2 cells exhibited a largely suppressive phenotype characterised by reduced cytokine secretion, while EA.hy926 and HMC-1.1 cells displayed temporally and ligand-dependent responses. Across models, biological responses were associated with nanoparticle dispersion behaviour, supporting agglomeration as an important determinant of early nanoparticle-cell interactions. he association between altered dispersion, redox perturbation and inflammatory responses supports a model in which SPION surface chemistry influences nanoparticle behaviour in biological media, thereby modulating oxidative stress and inflammatory signalling in a cell-dependent manner. Notably, these responses occurred in the absence of overt cytotoxicity, highlighting early perturbations in redox and inflammatory signalling as sensitive indicators of nanoparticle biological activity that may precede overt cellular damage.

title: Elevational Patterns of Carbon Fixation in Spring Ephemeral Wildflowers
source: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
summary: Understory plant phenology varies across elevation, constrained by frost and shade, limiting fitness and demography as a function of growing season length. However, growing season length could also trade-off with photosynthetic efficiency a
content: Understory plant phenology varies across elevation, constrained by frost and shade, limiting fitness and demography as a function of growing season length. However, growing season length could also trade-off with photosynthetic efficiency across elevations so that plants with short seasons can maintain positive carbon budgets because of more acquisitive photosynthetic strategies. To test this possibility, I quantified phenology and photosynthetic efficiency for a spring ephemeral (Erythronium umbilicatum) and a spring-active summer-green species (Trillium erectum) at different elevations and constructed agent-based carbon budget models for both. I found significant differences in annual carbon gain strategies between high and low populations of both species that were equally dependent on differences in both intrinsic photosynthetic efficiency and phenology, highlighting that phenological escape success can only be assessed when both are evaluated and providing new insight into the ecophysiological processes determining where these species are able to persist across the landscape.

title: Evaluation of strength properties of bio-remediated crude oil contaminated soil using Bacillus pumilus as liner and cover material in municipal solid waste containment applications
summary: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of Bacillus pumilus -induced calcite precipitate to enhance the engineering performance of bio-remediated crude oil-contaminated soils for waste containment applications. Remediated soil sampl
content: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of Bacillus pumilus -induced calcite precipitate to enhance the engineering performance of bio-remediated crude oil-contaminated soils for waste containment applications. Remediated soil samples were bio-treated with Bacillus pumilus (B) – cementation reagent (C) mixtures. Trial mix ratios of 75% B – 25% C, 50% B – 50% C, and 25% B – 75% C with B. pumilus suspension densities in the range 1.5 × 10⁸ − 2.4 × 10⁹ cells/ml and a fixed cementation reagent concentration. The 50% B – 50% C ratio yielded optimum improvement and was adopted in this study. The cementation reagent was prepared and applied to soil samples compacted using three energy levels namely, British Standard light (BSL), West African Standard (WAS), and British Standard heavy (BSH). The bio-cementation with B. pumilus (1.5 × 10⁸ to 2.4 × 10⁹ cells/ml) cementation solutions under gravity infiltration on the post-remediated soil specimens showed slight improvements with liquid limit reducing from 43.8% to 41.1%, plastic limit increased from 36.3% to 37.5%, and the plasticity index increased from 7.3% to 7.4%. UCS values reached 225.4, 264.4, and 385.1 kN/m² for BSL, WAS, and BSH compaction, respectively, recorded exceeded the minimum requirement of 200 kN/m². The findings confirm that bio-cementation using B. pumilus can effectively enhance the strength and plasticity characteristics of bioremediated oil-contaminated soils, supporting their suitability as liner and cover materials in waste containment systems.

title: Intrinsic linewidths of confined phonons in few-layer hBN
summary: Understanding lattice vibrations in two-dimensional (2D) materials is essential for controlling thermal transport, mechanical response, and energy dissipation in nanoscale devices. However, the intrinsic lifetimes of low-energy phonon modes
content: Understanding lattice vibrations in two-dimensional (2D) materials is essential for controlling thermal transport, mechanical response, and energy dissipation in nanoscale devices. However, the intrinsic lifetimes of low-energy phonon modes, particularly those that are optically silent, remain largely unexplored. Here we use helium-3 spin-echo spectroscopy to resolve low-energy phonons at the surface of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and measure their intrinsic linewidths. We report the simultaneous observation of multiple surface-confined interlayer shear modes whose energies agree closely with linear-chain model predictions. By resolving their intrinsic linewidths, we demonstrate a strong confinement-dependent reduction in phonon lifetimes, with a near order-of-magnitude increase in linewidth between the four- and two-layer modes, substantially exceeding simple inverse-layer-number scaling. The three- and four-layer linewidths show no statistically resolved temperature dependence over the measurement range, consistent with a substantial temperature-independent contribution. We also observe the flexural and Rayleigh wave modes and extract the bending rigidity of a quasi-freestanding hBN monolayer. The systematic broadening with decreasing effective layer number suggests that confinement strongly influences phonon decay. These results reveal how reduced dimensionality affects the decay of interlayer shearing modes in hBN, providing direct insight into the phonon lifetimes, confinement effects, and dissipation pathways that govern the dynamical behaviour of two-dimensional materials.

title: Evaluating the Capability of Activated Carbon Nanoparticles-Incorporated PLA Nanofibrous Structure as Hemodialysis Supplement for Uremic Toxins Removal
source: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
summary: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an expanding condition affecting a large population worldwide, with a significant proportion of these patients progressing to kidney failure and requiring considerations such as hemodialysis (HD). HD
content: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an expanding condition affecting a large population worldwide, with a significant proportion of these patients progressing to kidney failure and requiring considerations such as hemodialysis (HD). HD presents several challenges, such as an inflexible treatment regimen and limited toxin removal. Recent advancements have confirmed the use of adsorbents to increase the efficiency of the dialysis process. In the present research, adsorbents composed of polylactic acid (PLA) nanofibers containing activated carbon nanoparticles (AC NPs) were designed. Formation of uniform PLA nanofibers and presence of AC NPs on the surface of PLA nanofibers were evidenced. According to roughness evaluation, surface roughness of the prepared adsorbent was beyond the threshold of hemolysis, platelet and protein adhesion, and activation of the coagulation cascade. In addition, despite the enhanced surface hydrophilicity of the nanofibrous structure containing AC NPs, according to partial thromboplastin time test, the prepared adsorbent did not accelerate the clot formation. Evaluation of the fabricated nanostructural adsorbents for uremic toxin removal revealed high equilibrium adsorption and significant removal percentage. PLA nanofibrous mat containing 10 wt% AC NPs (possessing total weight of 3.5 mg), removed 31% of hippuric acid content and 90.5% of urea from the exposed solution and provided equilibrium adsorption capacity of 0.2 and 2.41 for the mentioned toxins, respectively. Adsorbents composition together with their unique microstructure providing high surface area and dual size porosity would account for the observed efficiency in uremic toxin removal.

title: Easy access to the geminal coupling between unresolved prochiral methylene protons
summary: For NMR analysis of molecular configuration and conformation, scalar and, especially, residual dipolar couplings between prochiral methylene protons are highly valuable. Yet, their measurement is often hindered by strong coupling. We presen
content: For NMR analysis of molecular configuration and conformation, scalar and, especially, residual dipolar couplings between prochiral methylene protons are highly valuable. Yet, their measurement is often hindered by strong coupling. We present a new method, inverse PSYCHEDELIC, that overcomes this issue. Demonstrations are given on steroids and the neuropeptide proctolin.

title: Knockout of RAG complex genes in chicken reveals distinct dosage effects on avian B cell development after V(D)J recombination
summary: Introduction In chickens, B cell receptor (BCR) diversity is generated primarily through gene conversion rather than V(D)J recombination. Unlike in mammals, RAG1 haploinsufficiency impairs chicken B cell development and subsequent gene conv
content: Introduction In chickens, B cell receptor (BCR) diversity is generated primarily through gene conversion rather than V(D)J recombination. Unlike in mammals, RAG1 haploinsufficiency impairs chicken B cell development and subsequent gene conversion, indicating an avian-specific dosage requirement. However, the precise contribution of RAG2 to this developmental process remains unclear. Methods To address this, we generated RAG2 -disrupted chickens using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing in primordial germ cells. Results and discussion At 1-week of age, V(D)J recombination was not detected under the conditions used in RAG2 homozygous knockout ( RAG2 -/- ) chickens, whereas wild-type and heterozygous knockout ( RAG2 +/- ) birds showed comparable activity. Histological analysis revealed impairment of bursal, thymic and splenic development in RAG2 -/- chickens. Consequently, B and T cell populations were severely reduced, indicating that complete RAG2 loss blocks mature lymphocyte development, mirroring RAG1 deficiency. However, unlike RAG1 +/- chickens, RAG2 +/- chickens displayed non-significant alteration of BCR downstream signaling and antibody diversification through gene conversion. This is attributed to RAG1 ’s dosage-dependent role in maintaining gene expression associated with B cell identity, and subsequent chromatin regulators essential for gene conversion, a function not shared by RAG2 . These findings reveal a unique, asymmetric dosage requirement for RAG1 and RAG2 during avian B cell development that fundamentally diverges from the mammalian paradigm.

title: GREEN EDUCATION AND THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS IN THE SCHOOL CURRICULUM
source: EPRA International Journal of Research & Development (IJRD)
summary: Sustainable development requires a generation of learners who understand environmental challenges and are equipped to transform societies. Green education embeds environmental awareness, climate change literacy, and sustainable practices ac
content: Sustainable development requires a generation of learners who understand environmental challenges and are equipped to transform societies. Green education embeds environmental awareness, climate change literacy, and sustainable practices across school curricula, aligning classroom learning with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This chapter examines the theoretical foundations of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), surveys global and Indian initiatives, and proposes strategies for integrating sustainability into various subjects. Drawing on cases from Finland’s cross-curricular theme, Ontario’s Eco Schools, Australia’s Resource Smart program, New Jersey’s climate-change standards, and India’s National Curriculum Framework and eco-club movement, it illustrates how schools can move beyond isolated environmental lessons to achieve systemic change. The chapter discusses pedagogical approaches, such as project-based learning, fieldwork, and community partnerships, highlights teacher training needs, and analyses challenges related to time, resources, and assessment. It concludes by offering policy recommendations and a framework for evaluating impact.

title: Distinct interfacial effects of a CNT-AuNPs nanocomposite on commercial and lab-made screen-printed carbon electrodes
summary: The electrochemical performance of nanostructure-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) is strongly influenced by the physicochemical characteristics of the underlying electrode architecture. In this work, a cystamine-mediated ca
content: The electrochemical performance of nanostructure-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes (SPCEs) is strongly influenced by the physicochemical characteristics of the underlying electrode architecture. In this work, a cystamine-mediated carbon nanotube/gold nanoparticle nanocomposite (CNT-AuNPs) was synthesized and applied to commercial and lab-made SPCEs to investigate how an identical nanostructured modifier affects distinct electrode substrates. Structural and morphological characterization confirmed the successful anchoring of AuNPs, with an average particle size of 21.03 ± 6.82 nm and homogeneously distributed throughout the CNT network. Electrochemical characterization revealed pronounced substrate-dependent effects. For the commercial SPCE, CNT-AuNPs modification decreased the charge-transfer resistance ( R ct ) by 45.22% and increased the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) by 64.36%. In contrast, for the lab-made SPCE, R ct decreased by 75.86% and peak-to-peak separation (Δ E p ) decreased from 0.77 to 0.59 V, while the ECSA increased by only 5.11%. Using dopamine, epinephrine, ascorbic acid, and uric acid as model electroactive probes, the modified electrodes exhibited enhanced anodic responses, lower oxidation potentials, and improved discrimination of overlapping redox processes. These findings demonstrate that CNT-AuNPs induce distinct substrate-dependent electrochemical effects at the interface, highlighting electrode architecture as a critical parameter in the design of electrochemical platforms.

title: Functioning and Limitations of Mineral Coverage in Drained Peatlands – How Parent Material Shapes Carbon Dynamics and Soil Development
source: Zurich Open Repository and Archive (University of Zurich)
summary: As Switzerland moves towards its Climate Strategy for Agriculture 2050, the management of drained peatlands—major sources of CO₂ emissions—has become a national priority. Mineral cover, which involves applying a 30–50 cm layer of mineral so
content: As Switzerland moves towards its Climate Strategy for Agriculture 2050, the management of drained peatlands—major sources of CO₂ emissions—has become a national priority. Mineral cover, which involves applying a 30–50 cm layer of mineral soil over organic soil, is an intermediate management strategy that aims to maintain agricultural productivity while mitigating carbon losses. However, its long-term effectiveness as well as the role of organo-mineral interactions remain poorly understood. This research, therefore, assesses the sustainability of mineral cover in the Bernese Seeland region using a four-chapter framework. The success of mineral coverage in organic soils depends primarily on locally available mineral material. It was therefore essential to establish a robust method for determining the region's geological composition (Manuscript I). Using the FingerPro elemental tracing approach, this study demonstrates that the parent material of the Bernese Seeland is characterised by a hybrid alpine–molasse composition (>75%). This material mainly originates from two regional sources: siliceous granite associated with moraines and calcareous sandstone derived from molasse. Establishing this geological baseline provides a necessary framework for understanding how different mineral inputs influence the long-term chemical environment of mineral-covered peatlands. Building on this classification, the second phase of the research examined how these parent materials influence pedogenesis (Manuscript II). The results highlight a clear pedogenic hierarchy, with siliceous morainic deposits significantly more favourable for soil development than calcareous molasse. Haplic Luvisols typically develop on siliceous moraines, whereas haplic Calcisols form on calcareous molasse. Two main factors explain the superiority of siliceous material. First, the more abundant, better-connected macroporosity observed in silica-bearing soils enhances water and air infiltration. Second, higher geochemical reactivity promotes the formation of clays and hydroxides of iron, aluminium, and manganese. These reactive constituents are essential for the formation of organo-mineral associations, which in turn increase the long-term stabilisation potential of underlying organic matter. Beyond material compatibility, studying soil development on these substrates also provides valuable insight into their long-term evolution when used as mineral covers. While the composition of the mineral layer is critical, the initial condition of the buried organic soil is equally important. An analysis of the carbon cycle in these systems is therefore essential to identify potential sources of CO₂ emissions linked to peat degradation (Manuscript III). Although mineral cover is intended to protect organic soils, its mitigation potential is constrained by the buried peat's inherent vulnerability.
