We measured its gas-phase infrared absorption cross-section (ACS) by Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy and calculated its radiative efficiency (RE). We monitored its decay in near-anhydrous and humid gas matrices. The spectrum was dominated by the 1167–1305 cm−1 absorption band. Its integrated ACS over 833.5–3000 cm−1 was 1.25 × 10−16 cm molecule−1, and weighting with the stratospheric-adjusted Pinnock curve yielded a mixing-ratio-based RE of 0.108 W m−2 ppb−1. The CF3OF e-folding decay time was 3451 min in near-anhydrous synthetic air and 2704 min in 40 % O2/60 % Ar. In ambient air, it decreased from 2448 to 168 min as the absolute humidity increased from 3.8 to 22.2 g m−3, demonstrating that water vapor strongly accelerated CF3OF removal. In near-anhydrous synthetic air, the CO2 rise time of 3591 min agreed with the CF3OF decay time to within 4.1 %, supporting a kinetic association between CF3OF loss and CO2 formation. Using the condition-specific decay times and the mass-based RE adjusted by a lifetime-dependent atmospheric-distribution factor, we calculated direct 100-year GWP (GWP100) values ranging from 3.44 × 10⁻⁵ to 1.15 × 10⁻². Its short persistence limits cumulative direct radiative forcing under the investigated conditions. Together with its reported plasma-processing capability, these findings provide experimental support for CF3OF as a low-GWP alternative to conventional high-GWP fluorinated process gases.

title: High-temperature thermal performance of ceramic-array load bearing multi- layer insulation for radioisotope thermophotovoltaic system
summary: Abstract A hollow ZrO 2 ceramic array Load Bearing multi-layer insulation (LBMLI) is proposed for the radioactive thermophotovoltaic system (RTPV). Two theoretical models including the finite element model and layer-by-layer model are compa
content: Abstract A hollow ZrO 2 ceramic array Load Bearing multi-layer insulation (LBMLI) is proposed for the radioactive thermophotovoltaic system (RTPV). Two theoretical models including the finite element model and layer-by-layer model are compared to analyze the thermal insulation performance. The number of layers, spacing, ceramic array quantity, thermal conductivity of spacing material, and reflective screen emissivity on heat loss are analyzed. At the LBMLI of 9 dots’ ceramic array, as the quantity of layers increased from 15 to 20, the heat power loss significantly decreased from 22.5 W to 17 W. By reducing the emissivity from 0.1 to 0.025, the heat loss is almost linearly reduce to 8.5 W. For mechanical stability, a 15-layer-screen ceramic array LBMLI is designed for the present RTPV, with 25 ceramic arrays in each layer. When the input power is 250 W, if not considering insulation frame heat loss of the ceramic array LBMLI, the temperature at heat source center could reach 1106.3 ℃, and the thermal efficiency of ceramic array LBMLI is 69.5%. When it is considered, the temperature of the heat source is 1079.4 ℃, and ŋ thermal is 57.0%. Moreover, considering optical cavity size, when reducing the lateral two dimensions of ceramic array LBMLI by 8 cm each, the temperature at heat source center changes to 1159.9 ℃ when considering insulation frame heat loss, with ŋ thermal being 60.2%. Results show that hollow ZrO 2 ceramic array LBMLI is expected to reduce the heat leakage.

title: Mineralized hydrogels for bone defect repair: advances, mechanisms, and challenges
summary: Mineralized hydrogels have emerged as promising biomaterials for bone defect repair. Recent advances in biomimetic mineralization have enabled precise regulation of mineral nucleation, growth, phase transformation, and spatial organization
content: Mineralized hydrogels have emerged as promising biomaterials for bone defect repair. Recent advances in biomimetic mineralization have enabled precise regulation of mineral nucleation, growth, phase transformation, and spatial organization within hydrogel matrices. This review comprehensively summarizes preformed-mineral incorporation, in situ mineralization, and externally regulated mineralization strategies, comparing their underlying mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and translational potential. In situ mineralization generally provides improved matrix–mineral integration and biological responsiveness, whereas externally regulated approaches introduce spatiotemporal control over mineral formation while enabling multifunctional regulation of osteogenesis, angiogenesis, immunomodulation, and antimicrobial activity. Despite encouraging preclinical progress, clinical translation remains limited by challenges including degradation–regeneration synchronization, mechanical matching, biosafety, and scalable manufacturing. Future development should emphasize programmable biomimetic mineralization, multiscale structural design, and coordinated regulation of immune–vascular–osteogenic crosstalk to facilitate the clinical translation of next-generation mineralized hydrogels for bone regeneration.

title: Green Research, Sustainable Technologies and Green Chemistry for Environmental Protection: Strategies, Applications and Future Perspectives
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Environmental degradation caused by industrialisation, urbanisation, intensive agriculture, fossil fuel consumption and waste accumulation is a major global challenge.Green research, sustainable technologies and green chemistry provide prev
content: Environmental degradation caused by industrialisation, urbanisation, intensive agriculture, fossil fuel consumption and waste accumulation is a major global challenge.Green research, sustainable technologies and green chemistry provide preventive approaches to reduce pollution, conserve resources and protect ecosystems.Green chemistry focuses on waste prevention, safer chemicals, renewable raw materials, energy efficiency, catalysis and biodegradable products.Sustainable technologies include renewable energy, wastewater treatment, green materials, carbon management, recycling and resource recovery.This paper reviews their role in environmental protection, highlighting green solvents, biocatalysis, biodegradable polymers, nanotechnology and circular economy practices.It also discusses environmental assessment tools, including the E-factor and life-cycle assessment, along with challenges such as high costs, technological limitations and inadequate infrastructure.The study emphasises integrating scientific research, technological innovation, sustainable policies and circular economy principles to achieve effective environmental protection and sustainable development.

title: CO 2 carbonation and wave properties in mixtures of basalt and red mud
summary: Abstract. Red mud is a highly industrial by-product with potential for CO₂ mineralization, while basalt provides reactive minerals and further enhances carbonation. This work investigates the CO₂ carbonation of a mixture of basalt and red m
content: Abstract. Red mud is a highly industrial by-product with potential for CO₂ mineralization, while basalt provides reactive minerals and further enhances carbonation. This work investigates the CO₂ carbonation of a mixture of basalt and red mud (in powder form). The study aims to propose a theoretical methodology to evaluate the weight of CO₂ in the mixture as a function of reaction time. In addition, we propose a model to obtain the P- and S-wave velocities before and after carbonation of the mixture, which is partially saturated with water. The model considers the mineral composition of the basalt and red mud grains, compaction, temperature, water saturation, and grain size. Velocities and mass density increase with compaction, while porosity decreases. Carbonation and velocities are enhanced by higher temperature and smaller grain sizes, while compaction slightly decreases CO₂ absorption.

title: Unsupervised neural clustering and seismic attribute analysis for gas channel delineation in the Scarab field
summary: Abstract The western offshore Nile Delta of Egypt represents a significant hydrocarbon province, characterized by complex stratigraphy and challenging reservoir connectivity. This study investigates two vertically stacked, unconnected chann
content: Abstract The western offshore Nile Delta of Egypt represents a significant hydrocarbon province, characterized by complex stratigraphy and challenging reservoir connectivity. This study investigates two vertically stacked, unconnected channel systems, Channels 1 and 2, which serve as the primary reservoirs in the Scarab Field. Conventional seismic interpretation techniques often fall short in delineating subtle stratigraphic features and reservoir architecture. To overcome these limitations, we employed an integrated machine learning workflow combining Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to enhance reservoir characterization. After data conditioning and the calculation of seismic attributes, PCA was applied to reduce dimensionality and extract the most informative seismic attributes. The resulting principal components were input into SOMs, an unsupervised neural network approach used to classify seismic meta-attributes into meaningful lithological facies. The SOM successfully identified six distinct facies classes: siltstone, clayey sand, clayey limestone, gas-bearing sandstone, water-bearing sandstone, and interbedded siltstone, validated through well log calibration. In particular, the technique delineated gas-water contacts and subtle stratigraphic trends that are critical for both exploration and development planning. The results and quantitative analysis through classification accuracy and GWC misfit assessments using different data types demonstrate that unsupervised machine learning, supported by multi-attribute seismic analysis, offers important improvements over traditional interpretation methods in detecting Direct Hydrocarbon Indicators (DHIs), refining stratigraphic resolution, and reducing exploration risk.

title: Schizophrenia-Linked 3q29 Deletion Produces Hyperdopaminergic Signaling in the Dorsal Striatum
summary: Dopamine dysregulation has long been recognized as a central feature of schizophrenia (SZ), yet the mechanisms linking genetic risk to dopaminergic dysfunction remain poorly understood. While pharmacological models have historically been us
content: Dopamine dysregulation has long been recognized as a central feature of schizophrenia (SZ), yet the mechanisms linking genetic risk to dopaminergic dysfunction remain poorly understood. While pharmacological models have historically been used to induce hyperdopaminergic states and recapitulate select clinical features of SZ, these approaches do not model the underlying disease biology. In contrast, genetically informed models enable investigation of dopaminergic abnormalities as emergent consequences of bona fide disease-associated mechanisms. Here, we examined a mouse model of the 3q29 deletion. In humans, this 1.6 Mb deletion is typically de novo and confers a greater than 40-fold increased risk for SZ, representing the single largest known molecular risk factor for the disorder. Using this model, we identified a robust hyperdopaminergic phenotype characterized by elevated evoked dopamine release selectively within the dorsal striatum. Mechanistically, this phenotype appears to arise from a PKC-mediated reduction in dopamine transporter (DAT) availability, impairing dopamine clearance and prolonging dopaminergic signaling. Together, these results establish a direct link between a high-risk SZ mutation and striatal dopamine dysfunction, while also highlighting PKC-DAT signaling as a potential therapeutic target for treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric symptoms associated with 3q29 deletion.

title: Ionic Liquids in Sustainable Development: Applications, Environmental Challenges & Future Perspectives
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Ionic liquids (ILs) are designer salts composed of organic or inorganic ions that melt below 100 °C and offer a distinctive combination of negligible vapour pressure, high thermal stability, ionic conductivity, broad electrochemical windows
content: Ionic liquids (ILs) are designer salts composed of organic or inorganic ions that melt below 100 °C and offer a distinctive combination of negligible vapour pressure, high thermal stability, ionic conductivity, broad electrochemical windows and highly tunable salvation behavior.These properties have stimulated their use in catalysis, biomass processing, carbon dioxide capture, separations, electrochemical energy storage, environmental remediation and pharmaceutical technologies.However, the designation of ILs as inherently "green" solvents is not justified by low volatility alone.Their synthesis, purification, toxicity, biodegradability, persistence, recovery requirements and life-cycle energy demand can substantially influence overall sustainability.This review critically discusses the contribution of ILs to sustainable development, emphasizing the relationship between molecular structure, physicochemical performance and environmental safety.Recent advances in bio-based and biodegradable ILs, recyclable process systems, COSMO-RS/QSPR-assisted screening and data-driven molecular design are highlighted.Particular attention is given to biomass valorisation, CO2 management, energy technologies, separation processes and environmental applications.Major research gaps include incomplete long-term ecotoxicity data, limited industrial-scale life-cycle inventories, high viscosity and cost, imperfect recovery, and insufficient consideration of transformation products and mixture toxicity.Future development should therefore follow a Safe-and-Sustainable-by-Design framework in which functionality, toxicity, biodegradability, resource efficiency; recyclability and techno-economic feasibility are optimized simultaneously.ILs has strong potential to support sustainable development, but their environmental credentials must be demonstrated through whole-life assessment rather than assumed from physicochemical properties alone.

title: Sustainable weed management under changing agroecosystems: ecological impacts, allelochemicals, molecular and biotechnological innovations
summary: Weeds impose major constraints on agricultural productivity by reducing crop yield, intensifying crop-weed interference, and altering ecological processes within agroecosystems. Their persistence is driven by diverse adaptive traits, includ
content: Weeds impose major constraints on agricultural productivity by reducing crop yield, intensifying crop-weed interference, and altering ecological processes within agroecosystems. Their persistence is driven by diverse adaptive traits, including rapid reproduction, physiological plasticity, invasiveness, genetic variability, metabolic flexibility, and herbicide-resistance evolution, all of which may be further reinforced under changing agroecosystem conditions associated with rising temperatures, altered precipitation patterns, and increasing atmospheric CO 2 . Although conventional weed control practices, particularly herbicide-based approaches, have improved short-term management efficiency, their long-term effectiveness is increasingly challenged by environmental concerns and the widespread emergence of resistant weed populations. This study synthesizes current knowledge on the ecological impacts of weeds, their roles in crop infestation and yield loss, invasion success, and the principal strategies used for sustainable weed management. Particular emphasis is placed on allelopathic interactions and the growing potential of allelopathic aqueous extracts, crop residues, and plant-derived metabolites as biologically derived tools with potential environmental advantages for weed suppression. The study further highlights molecular and biotechnological advances that are reshaping weed science, including the identification of allelopathy-associated genes and metabolic pathways, marker-assisted and genomic approaches, transgenic strategies, CRISPR/Cas-mediated genome editing, RNA interference, plant tissue culture, metabolic engineering, microbial production systems, synthetic biology, bioprospecting, gene mining, and fermentation-based technologies. These molecular biology- and biotechnology-based approaches provide new opportunities to enhance crop competitiveness, manipulate weed-suppressive traits, improve allelochemical production, and develop more targeted, biologically informed weed-control strategies. Overall, the evidence indicates that sustainable weed management should move beyond exclusive reliance on synthetic herbicides and instead integrate ecological understanding, allelopathy, molecular biology, and biotechnology into diversified, field-relevant, and long-term adaptive management strategies.

title: Dynamic multi-omics analysis of Adenovirus-induced rAAV-producing stable cell lines reveals the interplay between adenoviral infection and host cell metabolism
summary: Recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAV) are invaluable delivery vehicles for gene therapy. However, to make rAAV-based therapies more accessible, there is a need to increase rAAV titers. Here we analyze the phenotypic variation among 30
content: Recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAV) are invaluable delivery vehicles for gene therapy. However, to make rAAV-based therapies more accessible, there is a need to increase rAAV titers. Here we analyze the phenotypic variation among 30 Adenovirus-induced stably-transfected human producer cell clones to identify metabolic signatures associated with high vs low rAAV production. Exometabolomic characterization revealed decreased amino acid consumption in higher producers. Analysis of RNA-Seq data in the context of a genome-scale metabolic model identified upregulated carnosine biosynthesis-associated pathways during the first 6 hours post infection with adenovirus, relative to uninfected growth. Meanwhile, late infection timepoints exhibited increased amino acid release and de novo biosynthesis of serine, glycine, and arginine. Moreover, high producers decreased expression of genes linked with cholesterol biosynthesis and increased HMG-CoA degradation via HMGCL. Furthermore, sphingosine and ceramide biosynthesis genes were altered in high-producers in directions previously reported to resist cell death and suppress immune signaling. Overall, these findings elucidate the metabolic modulation upon adenoviral infection in a helper virus-induced AAV production process using stably transfected human cell lines.

title: Distributed photovoltaic access openable capacity assessment and overload risk prediction method for smart grid
summary: As the penetration ratio of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems continues to rise, the uncertainty in power generation and load during grid operation has increased. Moreover, the coupling of multiple operational constraints makes traditio
content: As the penetration ratio of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems continues to rise, the uncertainty in power generation and load during grid operation has increased. Moreover, the coupling of multiple operational constraints makes traditional capacity assessment methods inadequate for accurately characterizing PV integration capacity and associated operational risks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a method for assessing the openable capacity of PV systems and predicting overload risks by integrating multi-source measurement data. First, a two-layer capacity assessment optimization model is constructed, and the variation particle swarm optimization algorithm is employed to solve for the PV integration capacity boundary. Subsequently, a deep time-series prediction model is developed, incorporating a convolutional neural network, a convolutional block attention module, and a bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), assessing operational risks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a capacity gain rate of 6.8% on the test dataset, an F1-score for risk prediction of 0.935, and maintains an average absolute percentage error below 6.1% under noisy interference conditions. When the PV penetration rate reaches 60%, the method can still maintain an openable capacity of 768.5 kW and reduce the maximum voltage deviation at the terminal node from 0.045 to 0.022 p.u. The findings indicate that the proposed method enhances both the accuracy of PV integration capacity assessment and the capability for operational risk prediction, thereby providing effective support for the safe operation of distribution networks under high PV penetration scenarios.

title: Semantic Translation of User Intent into Kubernetes Placement Constraints for AI Workflows
summary: Abstract Modern AI applications are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous cloud–edge infrastructures, where each microservice in a workflow may require different resources and has different performance characteristics. Traditional cont
content: Abstract Modern AI applications are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous cloud–edge infrastructures, where each microservice in a workflow may require different resources and has different performance characteristics. Traditional container orchestration systems (e.g., Kubernetes) do not natively support either expressing high-level user goals or automatically translating them into concrete resource-aware deployment decisions. This paper presents CorMOS, a lightweight, intent-driven orchestration mechanism that enriches container deployment descriptors using ontology-based semantic knowledge. CorMOS introduces an OWL ontology for modelling workload types and user goals and applies semantic reasoning together with ML techniques to infer missing resource specifications and placement preferences. These inferred constraints are automatically injected into Helm charts and Argo Workflows, enabling Kubernetes to schedule microservices on the most appropriate cluster nodes. CorMOS was developed and evaluated both on a heterogeneous k3s testbed and within the NEMO Open Call 1 environment, where it was integrated into the NEMO orchestration pipeline. Experimental results show that CorMOS can autonomously complete incomplete workload descriptors, infer values for up to 50% of missing resource parameters while achieving 80% estimation accuracy, and incur low processing overhead while sustaining a throughput of approximately 20 charts/min. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of semantic enrichment in reducing manual configuration effort while enabling intent-driven deployment with low computational overhead.

title: Feasibility of Using Solar Photovoltaics to Decarbonize the Natural Gas Compressor Station Along the East–West Pipeline in Saudi Arabia
summary: This study evaluates the techno-economic and environmental feasibility of integrating a grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) system to decarbonize natural gas compressor stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline. The objective of t
content: This study evaluates the techno-economic and environmental feasibility of integrating a grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) system to decarbonize natural gas compressor stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline. The objective of this study is to assess whether solar PV can reliably offset the station’s annual electricity demand of 23,520 MWh while maintaining economic viability. The System Advisor Model (SAM) software was utilized to simulate two representative locations, Abqaiq and Al-Duwadimi, under fixed tilt and single-axis tracking configurations. All systems were sized to meet and slightly exceed the required demand over a 25-year lifetime, while exporting the excess energy produced to the grid. Results show that single-axis tracking delivers similar Year-1 AC energy with a smaller DC array, and under equal PV module capacity, it produces higher annual AC output than fixed-tilt systems. Seasonality variability leads to higher grid-imported energy during low-irradiance periods, while a 0.5%/year DC degradation causes a gradual decline in PV generation over time. Financial analysis under a net-zero billing framework illustrates a reduction of approximately 50% in payback time compared to conventional billing, with 1st year significant savings of $ 1.78–1.83 M and additional export revenues of $ 0.33–0.36 M. The calculated LCOE ranges from 2.94–3.62 (¢/kWh), with the Abqaiq single-axis scenario offering superior performance. Environmentally, displacing grid electricity with solar PV avoids 670,729–688,292 tons of CO₂ over the entire project’s lifecycle, while lifetime PV emissions represent only 1–1.5% of the avoided grid emissions, confirming a substantial net environmental benefit.

title: Carbon Capture Applications of Plant-Mediated Nanoparticles
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Anthropogenic CO₂ emissions necessitate innovative mitigation strategies combining environmental sustainability with technological efficiency.This review examines plant-mediated synthesis of nanoparticles for CO₂ capture, representing a dua
content: Anthropogenic CO₂ emissions necessitate innovative mitigation strategies combining environmental sustainability with technological efficiency.This review examines plant-mediated synthesis of nanoparticles for CO₂ capture, representing a dual sustainability approach addressing both production and application.Phytosynthesis utilizes biochemicals from plant extracts to reduce metal ions and form nanostructures, eliminating hazardous chemicals and energy-intensive processes characteristic of conventional synthesis.We analyze diverse nanomaterial categories including metal oxides, biosynthesized carbons, and cellulosic nanostructures, evaluating their CO₂ capture mechanisms, performance parameters, and practical implementation challenges.Plant-derived nanoparticles demonstrate multiple advantages: renewable resource utilization, reduced production footprint, cost-effectiveness, and functional properties suitable for carbon sequestration.Despite promising laboratory results, significant challenges remain regarding performance optimization, reproducibility, and industrial scalability.Future research must focus on mechanistic understanding, standardized synthesis protocols, performance enhancement through surface modification, and comprehensive techno-economic assessment.This integrated approach positions plant-derived nanomaterials as potential contributors to global carbon management strategies.

title: A marine worm oxygen carrier to improve the quality of preserved tumor samples
summary: Biobanked tissue samples are essential for cancer research, yet pre-analytical ischemia-hypoxia during tissue handling can compromise tissue or derived models quality, limiting their value for translational research. Here, we investigated w
content: Biobanked tissue samples are essential for cancer research, yet pre-analytical ischemia-hypoxia during tissue handling can compromise tissue or derived models quality, limiting their value for translational research. Here, we investigated whether M101, an extracellular hemoglobin from Arenicola marina, could mitigate, indirectly by providing oxygen, handling-induced ischemia-hypoxia in cancer tissues and subsequent live 3D models. Using prostate cancer PC3 and ovarian cancer TOV-21G XG preserved ex vivo, M101 reduced the emergence of hypoxia-associated markers, including the hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha, and attenuated metabolic stress. In XG-derived micro-dissected 3D tumor models cultured for 8 days, M101 improved tissue morphology, reduced fragmentation, and was associated with higher proliferative activity and lower inflammatory interleukin-6 release. Together, these findings suggest that M101 helps preserve structural and functional features of biobanked tumor models during ex vivo handling. Thus, oxygen carriers could represent a bio-compatible strategy to improve the fidelity of biobanked samples and patient-derived tumor models for precision oncology applications.

title: Enzyme-like catalysis in nanozyme-integrated electrochemical sensors for drug analysis
summary: Nanozymes have emerged as promising alternatives or complementary catalysts to natural enzymes in electrochemical sensing owing to their high catalytic activity, tunable structures, and excellent stability. This review focuses on their appl
content: Nanozymes have emerged as promising alternatives or complementary catalysts to natural enzymes in electrochemical sensing owing to their high catalytic activity, tunable structures, and excellent stability. This review focuses on their applications in drug analysis, highlighting recent advances in nanozyme-enabled electrochemical sensing strategies for pharmaceutical detection. It first covers nanozyme types, catalytic mechanisms, and differences from natural enzymes. Sensor construction strategies are then discussed, including surface functionalization, interface optimization, and multifunctional integration. Applications are summarized by drug class, including anticancer agents, cardiovascular drugs, antibiotics, narcotic drugs and controlled substances. Existing research indicates that nanozymes improve detection sensitivity and selectivity, and some platforms have already demonstrated the potential for on-site or real-time monitoring. However, challenges remain. Catalytic mechanisms are not fully understood, selectivity is limited in complex samples, batch-to-batch reproducibility is poor, device integration is low, and clinical validation is lacking. Future work should focus on better design, standardized preparation, intelligent system integration, and multicenter clinical studies to promote their practical application in precision medicine, therapeutic drug monitoring, and public health.

title: Current Prospective of Electrochemical Oxidation for the Removal of Pharmaceutically Active Compounds from Wastewater: Current Issues, Environmental Risks, and Future Strategies
source: Journal of Energy and Environmental Sustainability
summary: Pharmaceutical active compounds (PhACs) are emerging contaminants in aquatic environments due to their extensive use and persistence, posing ecological risks and potential threats to human health. Conventional wastewater treatment plants of
content: Pharmaceutical active compounds (PhACs) are emerging contaminants in aquatic environments due to their extensive use and persistence, posing ecological risks and potential threats to human health. Conventional wastewater treatment plants often fail to completely remove these micropollutants, necessitating advanced treatment technologies. Electrochemical oxidation (EO) has gained significant attention as a sustainable and effective tertiary treatment for degradation of PhACs due to its operational simplicity, minimal chemical addition, and potential for complete mineralization. Recent advancements in anode materials−including boron-doped diamond (BDD), dimensionally stable anodes (DSA), and novel nanostructured electrodes−have enhanced oxidation kinetics and broadened the spectrum of treatable compounds. Coupling EO with auxiliary processes such as photoelectrochemical oxidation, sonoelectrochemical treatment, and membrane filtration demonstrates further improvements in removal efficiency and energy performance. Current research trends also focus on understanding reaction mechanisms, identifying transformation products, optimizing energy consumption, and scaling up reactor designs for real-world applications. Despite challenges related to cost, electrode fouling, and by-product formation, EO represents a promising technology for mitigating PhAC contamination in wastewater streams. This paper reviews the state-of-the-art developments, practical limitations, and future directions for EO as a key strategy toward sustainable pharmaceutical removal in water treatment.

title: Soil quality index as a predictor of wetting-front dynamics under surface drip irrigation
summary: Efficient soil water movement is essential for improving crop water-use efficiency under drip irrigation, yet the role of Soil Quality Index (SQI) in predicting wetting-front under surface drip irrigation has not been comprehensively studie
content: Efficient soil water movement is essential for improving crop water-use efficiency under drip irrigation, yet the role of Soil Quality Index (SQI) in predicting wetting-front under surface drip irrigation has not been comprehensively studied. This study investigated five land-use systems—bare fallowing for 2 years (BF2), bare fallowing for 3 years (BF3), monocropping (MOC), crop rotation (CR), and fallowing with vegetation (FV)—on soil quality and wetting-front development under surface drip irrigation. Soil hydro-physical and chemical properties at 0–30 cm depth were assessed, including bulk density (BD), water-holding capacity (WHC), pH, effective cation exchange capacity (ECEC), available phosphorus (P) and potassium (K), organic carbon (OC), total nitrogen (N), and base saturation (Bsat). Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to derive the Soil Quality Index (SQI), while wetting width and depth were measured after 15, 30, and 60 min of irrigation. Land-use management significantly (P < 0.05) affected soil properties and wetting-front dimensions. SQI ranged from 0.33 (bad) under BF3 to 0.99 (very good) under FV, while values of 0.43 (fair), 0.83 (very good), and 0.89 (very good) were obtained at BF2, MOC and CR, respectively. FV produced the greatest wetting width and depth, followed by CR, whereas BF3 recorded the lowest values. Strong positive relationships occurred between SQI and wetting dimensions, with correlation coefficients generally > 0.70 and reaching 0.984 between SQI and wetting depth at 60 min. The principal component regression model explained 92.75% of SQI variability. These findings demonstrate that vegetation-based fallowing and crop rotation enhance soil quality and water movement, supporting sustainable irrigation water management.

title: Composite approach to quantifying regulating soil-based ecosystem services using multiple indicators
summary: Abstract The spatial evaluation of soil functions and soil-based ecosystem services (SES) is a key challenge and demand nowadays. SES can provide a scientific background to the decision and policy-making. We define them as benefits that hum
content: Abstract The spatial evaluation of soil functions and soil-based ecosystem services (SES) is a key challenge and demand nowadays. SES can provide a scientific background to the decision and policy-making. We define them as benefits that humans and the environment derive from soils and their functions. In our studies we presented the first maps of SES on a national scale for Poland. The research was focused on evaluation of regulating SES, which plays a crucial role in the crop production and circulation of matter and processes in the entire environment. Regulating SES contribute to CO 2 fluxes and sequestration, nutrient cycling, water cycle regulation, control of erosion and mass movements, among others. In this research we develop the multi-indicators index, grouping four SES and 11 separate indicators. For this reason, we used geometric means for calculating regulating SES and their final integrated index. For the nutrients provision, and carbon sequestration we used digital soil mapping approach with quantile regression forest algorithm, while for the water regulation and erosion control, mechanistic and empirical models were applied. Our results showed that regulating SES in Polish agricultural areas is relatively low, indicating serious limitations for Polish agriculture. In particular, 84% agricultural soils were classified as having very low or low status of regulating SES especially due to natural limitations, whereas only 2% showed high status, mainly due to the limited capacity for erosion control and high water retention capacity. This is an important step in the agricultural studies indicating the main soil health problems and areas of improvement to increase the natural potential of soils. The presented approach, due to the applied statistical and point bonitation methods, can be applied to other SES evaluation, and also allows to implement different indicators that may be more important for different regions in the world.

title: Contour Based Ecological Landscape Restoration in the Torhasan Pond Micro Watershed
summary: Global climate change and land-use alterations induce hydro-ecological challenges such as increased surface runoff and soil erosion at the watershed scale. This study proposes a contour-based ecological restoration model centered on nature-
content: Global climate change and land-use alterations induce hydro-ecological challenges such as increased surface runoff and soil erosion at the watershed scale. This study proposes a contour-based ecological restoration model centered on nature-based solutions for the Torhasan Pond micro-watershed in Çanakkale, Türkiye. Micro-topographic adjustments, vegetative buffer strips, and bioswales were integrated within a holistic landscape framework. Hydrological analyses indicate that the proposed hybrid model reduces the existing surface runoff coefficient (C=0.45) to 0.20–0.25, significantly decreasing the annual runoff volume. Furthermore, spatial revegetation based on hydro-functional criteria aims to control erosion, improve water quality, and foster habitat continuity.

title: Exploration of Carbon Quantum Dot Composites for Environmental Remediation
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Background & Objective: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) used for environmental remediation and sensing, distinguished by their quasispherical morphology (typically 2-10 nm in diameter), sp² and sp³ hybridized carbon cores, and abundant surface f
content: Background & Objective: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) used for environmental remediation and sensing, distinguished by their quasispherical morphology (typically 2-10 nm in diameter), sp² and sp³ hybridized carbon cores, and abundant surface functional groups (carboxyl, hydroxyl, amino, carbonyl) that enable versatile interactions with environmental pollutants.CQDs have attractive features such as ease of synthesis, good water solubility, high photostability, high photo response, low cytotoxicity, facile surface functionalization.Materials and Methods: This article critically examines CQD structure and properties, top-down and bottom-up synthesis, biomass-derived precursors, heteroatom doping, and composite formation, with emphasis on adsorption, photocatalytic remediation.Results: CQDs act as adsorptive interfaces, photosensitizers, electron reservoirs, charge-transfer bridges, conductive additives, and defectengineering agents.CQDs can improve charge separation and interfacial kinetics when their electronic structure is matched to a host semiconductor or electrode; however, apparent benefits can be confounded by differences in precursor purification, CQD loading, particle size, surface passivation, illumination, electrolyte composition, and normalization procedures.Conclusion: The crucial repurposing of plentiful biomass waste as a source of CQDs is essential to meet the pressing demands of a more sustainable future.Future perspectives in environmental remediation involve improving the characteristics and stability of CQDs.

title: Rare taxa are associated with resource use efficiency in a highly disturbed aquatic ecosystem
summary: A central goal in ecology is to understand the distribution of abundance and species roles in ecosystem functioning among species in communities. The mass ratio hypothesis emphasizes the importance of common taxa, and the diversity insuranc
content: A central goal in ecology is to understand the distribution of abundance and species roles in ecosystem functioning among species in communities. The mass ratio hypothesis emphasizes the importance of common taxa, and the diversity insurance hypothesis highlights the potential role of rare taxa. However, it remains unclear whether common and rare taxa differ in their associations with chlorophyll‐based resource use efficiency (RUE) in disturbed aquatic ecosystems. Here, we investigated diatom communities across a cascade dam system in the Yellow River during a spring normal flow period and linked the diversity and network complexity of common and rare taxa to chlorophyll‐based RUE for phosphate, ammonium and turbidity. Spatial patterns and phylogenetic null models showed that common taxa had relatively stable alpha diversity along the river and a larger inferred contribution of dispersal limitation. Rare taxa declined markedly in the inter‐dam zone and showed a larger inferred contribution of heterogeneous selection. Co‐occurrence network analyses and random forest models showed that the chlorophyll‐a (Chl‐a) to phosphate and Chl‐a to ammonium ratios were mainly associated with turbidity and common taxa network complexity. The Chl‐a to turbidity ratio was mainly associated with rare taxon network complexity. Together, these results suggest that common and rare diatom taxa are linked to chlorophyll‐based RUE through different aspects of community organization in a highly disturbed river ecosystem.

title: Photoisomerization Triggered Temporal Control in Invertase Activity Through pH Modulation
summary: ABSTRACT The pH modulation in response to environmental stimuli is crucial for several biomolecular processes and functions within the human physiological system. Inspired by such complex biomachinery, remote control of pH in a light‐respon
content: ABSTRACT The pH modulation in response to environmental stimuli is crucial for several biomolecular processes and functions within the human physiological system. Inspired by such complex biomachinery, remote control of pH in a light‐responsive manner using photoswitches has shown widespread applications. However, maximizing pH modulation, bistability of photoswitches over a wider pH range, improving thermal stability of the metastable state at different pH and tolerance toward aqueous buffered systems are some of the important challenges. In this study, we report an azoheteroarene‐based molecular photoswitch that shows excellent photoswitching even in enzyme‐containing aqueous phosphate buffer with excellent Z isomer stability, pH variation (ΔpH) up to 1.3 units, and Δp K a of 1.74 units. Besides structural elucidation of E and Z isomers using single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction, we have also achieved temporal control of the activity of invertase toward sucrose hydrolysis through reversible photoisomerization of the photoswitch by light. Herein, we report the proof‐of‐concept on transduction of molecular‐level E / Z photoisomerization in activation and inhibition of invertase activity via pH modulation in a cascade manner, which can be useful to the food industry and pharmaceutical applications.

title: Proton‐Pump Engineering in Photo‐Responsive TiCo‐MOFs for Efficient Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
summary: ABSTRACT The current industrial anthraquinone route to hydrogen peroxide is energy‐intensive, hazardous, environmentally unfriendly and has spurred a quest for greener synthetic methods. Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production using water and oxy
content: ABSTRACT The current industrial anthraquinone route to hydrogen peroxide is energy‐intensive, hazardous, environmentally unfriendly and has spurred a quest for greener synthetic methods. Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production using water and oxygen is an attractive alternative, but its efficiency is often limited by the slow kinetics of water oxidation, which in turn restricts the proton supply needed for the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we report a proton‐pump engineering strategy that precisely tailors the proton‐donating capability of a stable photo‐responsive TiCo 2 ‐based metal–organic framework (MOF) without altering its underlying framework topology. By incorporating functional groups with distinct pK a values, ‐NH 2 and ‐OH, onto the terephthalate linkers, we achieve controlled modulation of the local proton transfer kinetics. The TiCo 2 ‐OH MOF exhibits significantly enhanced proton conductivity, superior charge separation efficiency, and a markedly stabilized *OOH intermediate. As a result, this material delivers a high H 2 O 2 production rate of 20 525 µmol g −1 h −1 in pure water under visible light irradiation without any sacrificial agents, exceeding the best previously reported MOF‐based photocatalysts under comparable conditions. This work establishes pore engineering as a generalizable, non‐destructive strategy for overcoming the proton supply bottleneck in photocatalytic proton‐coupled reactions, offering a sustainable platform for green H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Bond response and auxetic performance of helical auxetic fibers in mortar matrix
summary: This study proposes a design method for helical auxetic fiber (HAF) fabricated from stainless-steel wire and flexible fibers. The HAF feature a stable initial state and remarkable auxetic performance and are promising for concrete engineeri
content: This study proposes a design method for helical auxetic fiber (HAF) fabricated from stainless-steel wire and flexible fibers. The HAF feature a stable initial state and remarkable auxetic performance and are promising for concrete engineering applications. First, a self-developed manufacturing system was employed to fabricate HAF by winding stainless-steel wires around core fibers. Second, the auxetic behavior of HAF with various core fiber types, wrapping angles, and diameter ratios between the core fiber and the wrapping fiber are determined and quantified as the maximum negative Poisson’s ratio. Furthermore, the bond performance of HAF in mortar matrix is investigated by pull-out tests, where the influences of the water-cement ratio of mortar, embedment length of HAF, and types of HAF on interfacial bond properties are systematically discussed. Last but not least, the auxetic behavior of HAF in mortar matrix is captured by an in-situ 4 dimensional microfocus X-ray computed tomography (X-ray μCT) system during interfacial pull‑out testing, which further clarifies its reinforcement and toughening mechanism in mortar matrix. Test results revealed that HAF fabricated from stainless-steel wire and Polypropylene (PP) fiber, with a diameter ratio of 2 and a wrapping angle of 15 ° , exhibited the maximum negative Poisson’s ratio. Moreover, compared with traditional steel fiber and PP fiber, the average interfacial bond strength of this HAF in mortar was improved by 42.2% and 103.9%, the pull-out absorbed energy increased by 162% and 151%, respectively. In-situ X-ray μCT results demonstrated that HAF exhibits a distinct auxetic behavior in mortar matrix at the partial debonding stage during pull‑out testing. This behavior effectively strengthens the interfacial mechanical interlock between HAF and mortar matrix, thereby enhancing the overall interfacial bond performance.

title: Impact of steam blanching on the fatty acid stability in chloroplast-rich fraction (CRF) obtained from post-harvest residues of pea vine
summary: Post-harvest residues of pea vine were steam blanched to deactivate the endogenous enzymes, followed by the extraction of chloroplast-rich fraction (CRF) enriched with sources of micronutrients and fatty acids. This study aimed to evaluate
content: Post-harvest residues of pea vine were steam blanched to deactivate the endogenous enzymes, followed by the extraction of chloroplast-rich fraction (CRF) enriched with sources of micronutrients and fatty acids. This study aimed to evaluate the correlation between packaging variables (oxygen and light presence or absence) and storage temperatures (-20°C, 4°C, 25°C, and 40°C) regarding the stability of fatty acids in freeze-dried pea vine CRF throughout a duration of 91 days. The degradation rates of palmitic acid, palmitoleic acid, stearic acid, oleic acid, linoleic acid, and α-linolenic acid demonstrated first-order reaction kinetics with associated activation energies. All fatty acids in CRF were stable when preserved at low temperatures (-20°C and 4°C), in spite of exposure to air; this stability was undermined at elevated temperatures with air exposure. Furthermore, upon exposure to light, all detected fatty acids in CRF had significant degradation during storage at 25°C or 40°C, regardless of air exposure.

title: Extraction method shapes the physicochemical quality, oxidative stability, and food-grade application of Seje (Oenocarpus bataua Mart.) oil in alginate-stabilized reduced-fat mayonnaise
summary: ABSTRACT Oenocarpus bataua (seje) is an underutilized Amazonian palm whose oil, rich in oleic acid and α-tocopherol, remains largely unexplored for food applications. This study evaluated the influence of four extraction methods — Soxhlet w
content: ABSTRACT Oenocarpus bataua (seje) is an underutilized Amazonian palm whose oil, rich in oleic acid and α-tocopherol, remains largely unexplored for food applications. This study evaluated the influence of four extraction methods — Soxhlet with cyclohexane (SOX-Cy) and n-heptane (SOX-hp), supercritical fluid extraction (SFE), and hot pressing (HP) — on the yield, fatty acid composition, nutritional indices, minor constituents, and oxidative stability of seje oil, using multivariate analysis to select the most suitable oil for a reduced-fat mayonnaise stabilized with sodium alginate. The extraction technique markedly determined oil quality: yield ranged from 31.70% (HP) to 47.70% (SOX-hp), oleic acid from 63.98% to 74.99%, and α-tocopherol from 313.67 to 1201.80 mg/kg, the latter strongly correlated with oxidative stability (r = 0.95). Principal component analysis of eleven physicochemical and compositional variables (90.4% of variance) discriminated the four methods and identified SOX-Cy oil as the most suitable, combining the highest α-tocopherol content and monounsaturated fatty acid proportion, the lowest acidity, and the greatest oxidative stability (induction period 8.53 h vs. 5.50 h for refined sunflower oil). Among three formulations with decreasing alginate concentration, RFM-2 (25% alginate) reproduced the weak-gel, shear-thinning behaviour and structural recovery of commercial mayonnaise. However, its colour and taste differed significantly from the sunflower-oil control (p < 0.01), and consumption intention was lower (54% vs. 90%). Overall, the extraction method is decisive for seje oil quality, and SOX-Cy oil enables a reduced-fat mayonnaise with commercial-like texture, whose acceptance is limited by colour and flavour rather than by structure, supporting the valorization of this Amazonian resource.

title: Advances in microfluidic platforms for phenotypic microbial analysis and digital-twin-oriented modeling: A comprehensive and critical review
summary: Microfluidics has revolutionized experimental microbial analysis by enabling precise, high-throughput phenotypic measurements of growth, inhibition, and stress responses in microscale environments that replicate natural and industrial condi
content: Microfluidics has revolutionized experimental microbial analysis by enabling precise, high-throughput phenotypic measurements of growth, inhibition, and stress responses in microscale environments that replicate natural and industrial conditions. This article provides a comprehensive and critical review of recent advances in microfluidic platforms for phenotypic manifestations of microbial metabolic activity and digital twinning. It begins by situating microfluidics within classical microbial culture strategies and explaining how miniaturization enables precise environmental control with reduced resource use. The architecture and operation of microfluidic chips are examined: microcolonies-based, droplet-based, biofilm-oriented, and single-cell systems, together with flow control, nutrient delivery, and CFD-assisted design. Using extensive literature data, a cross-comparison with conventional culture highlights reproducibility and scaling challenges where applications for growth and toxicity screening are compared through three quantitative performance metrics: Fold Speed Increase (FSI), Fold Resource Saving (FRS), and Microfluidic Performance Gain (MPG), providing scenario-dependent estimates of screening-time and liquid-volume efficiency under explicitly stated comparison assumptions. The review critically analyzes microscopy-based detection methods, including optical, fluorescence, and time-lapse imaging, which underpin most microfluidic studies, outlining their analytical power and current limitations in quantitative, in situ metabolic sensing. Finally, perspectives are offered on coupling microfluidics with integrated sensing, AI, and mechanistic modeling to enable digital twins for predictive and sustainable microbial biotechnologies.

title: A predictive-prescriptive analytics framework for resilient blood supply chain network design
summary: The blood supply chain is complex due to its perishable nature, time criticality, dependence on voluntary donations, and vulnerability to demand fluctuations, particularly during crises such as natural disasters and pandemics. This study pr
content: The blood supply chain is complex due to its perishable nature, time criticality, dependence on voluntary donations, and vulnerability to demand fluctuations, particularly during crises such as natural disasters and pandemics. This study proposes a decision making framework for sustainable and resilient BSC network design by combining fuzzy demand forecasting with multi objective robust optimization. The framework operates in two stages. First, a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural network forecasts blood demand across five transfusion centers in Fars province, Iran, generating triangular fuzzy numbers for optimistic, baseline, and pessimistic scenarios. The forecasting model achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 4.42% across the five transfusion centers. Second, these fuzzy outputs are incorporated into a multi-objective, fuzzy-informed optimization framework that captures demand variability through scenarios and adopts a conservative upper-bound treatment of temporary-center disruption rates and environmental emission coefficients. The model integrates decisions on permanent and temporary center locations, donor allocation, and blood flow management while minimizing total cost, blood shortage, and environmental emissions. The model is solved using the Non dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA II), producing a converged (GD = 0.07) and uniformly distributed (Spread = 0.08) Pareto front with seven non dominated solutions. Validation against CPLEX and MOPSO on small scale instances confirms the reliability of NSGA II, with an optimality gap below 0.5%. Sensitivity and resilience analyses show that the designed network maintains a 99.3% demand fulfillment rate under severe disruption scenarios while allowing temporary center locations and resource allocations to adapt to changing conditions. The framework provides a data driven decision support tool for healthcare policymakers and offers a transferable approach for resilient healthcare network planning. By preserving uncertainty throughout the forecasting and optimization pipeline, the study strengthens the connection between data driven prediction and real world network design.

title: Attributing future urban ecosystem-service supply–demand imbalances to climate, land-use, and population drivers: A spatial diagnostic framework for semi-arid metropolitan regions
summary: Urban ecosystem-service assessments increasingly quantify mismatches between ecological supply and social demand, yet they less often diagnose how different social–ecological drivers separately shape future imbalances across supply, demand,
content: Urban ecosystem-service assessments increasingly quantify mismatches between ecological supply and social demand, yet they less often diagnose how different social–ecological drivers separately shape future imbalances across supply, demand, and supply–demand balance. This study develops a spatial diagnostic framework for attributing future urban ecosystem-service supply–demand imbalances to climate change, land-use change, and population growth in western Tehran, a semi-arid metropolitan region experiencing rapid urban expansion and water-resource pressure. Six urban ecosystem services, Water Provision, Carbon Storage, Food Provision, Energy Provision, Soil Conservation, and Recreational Spaces, were assessed for a baseline period (2013–2022) and a future period (2023–2040). The framework integrates InVEST-based ecosystem-service modeling, GIS-based spatial analysis, groundwater mass-balance simulation, crop-yield regression, the Ecosystem Service Supply–Demand Ratio (ESSDR), full-factorial scenario simulation, variance-based driver attribution, and driver-conditioned Spearman trade-off analysis. In the baseline period, balance was observed for services such as Water Provision, Soil Conservation, and Recreational Spaces, whereas imbalance was observed for services such as Carbon Storage, Food Provision, and Energy Provision. The future period was simulated under three climate scenarios, four land-use change scenarios, and three population scenarios. It was observed that under all scenarios, the overall supply-demand index decreases. However, with green space expansion, this index decreases by 78% by the end of the simulation period, indicating a more favorable outcome compared to the urban land expansion scenario (166% decrease). The results indicated that population was the dominant driver of ecosystem service demand, with a variance-based contribution rate of 67.4%. In contrast, ecosystem service supply was primarily influenced by land-use change and climate, which contributed 58.8% and 38% of the explained variance, respectively. The results of this study provide urban managers with insights into how urban ecosystems change in response to variations in social-ecological factors and help them prioritize spatial and temporal planning efforts.

title: Moving Compute Into Orbit: The Political Economy of AI Infrastructure
summary: Terrestrial siting restrictions can make orbital computing attractive even when its engineering costs are higher. We develop a public choice model in which a local government chooses terrestrial restrictions and a national sponsor chooses o
content: Terrestrial siting restrictions can make orbital computing attractive even when its engineering costs are higher. We develop a public choice model in which a local government chooses terrestrial restrictions and a national sponsor chooses orbital subsidies and safety requirements. Firms allocate heterogeneous workloads between Earth and orbit. In an interior equilibrium with uniformly distributed workload-specific cost differences, a one-unit increase in terrestrial restrictions reduces the preferred subsidy by one-half unit while increasing orbital deployment. Safety effort falls below its conditional social optimum when the sponsor gives insufficient relative weight to damage borne by other space users. Orbital relocation can improve welfare under existing restrictions while remaining inferior to feasible terrestrial reform. Public opinion surveys, election results, and fiscal reports describe the local burdens and benefits relevant to these choices. Engineering calculations quantify ideal radiator requirements and the launch expenditure that avoided electricity spending could finance, including sensitivity to utilization. We recommend comparing orbital subsidies with feasible terrestrial reform, coordinating satellite and launch licensing, tying public funding to measurable performance and knowledge spillovers, and aligning launch and reentry fees with administrative costs and external risks.

title: Robotic search and rescue in earthquake-collapsed buildings: capabilities, evidence gaps, and a roadmap for human-multi-robot rescue
summary: Following an earthquake, rescue robots must search for and assist trapped individuals in complex environments characterized by unstable rubble, narrow cavities, darkness, dust, and unreliable communications. This paper reviews the technical
content: Following an earthquake, rescue robots must search for and assist trapped individuals in complex environments characterized by unstable rubble, narrow cavities, darkness, dust, and unreliable communications. This paper reviews the technical evidence for seven categories of robots within the seven-stage mission chain of search and rescue (SAR) in building collapse scenarios, covering unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs); tracked, wheeled, and reconfigurable robots; quadrupedal robots; snake-like and continuum robots; humanoid and hybrid robots; heavy-duty engineering robots; and casualty evacuation and medical transport robots. This paper evaluates representative “platform-sensor-mission” capabilities across two independent dimensions: validation maturity (E0–E4) and relevance to collapse rescue scenarios (S0–S4). The study clearly distinguishes between signals indicating the possible presence of trapped individuals, 3D positioning information usable to guide excavation operations, and the actual execution of subsequent rescue operations. Currently, evidence of field applications is primarily concentrated on tasks such as site entry, reconnaissance, mapping, visual search, and the detection of vital signs through rubble. In contrast, evidence regarding sustained communication, supply delivery, close-range manipulation of casualties, casualty management, evacuation, and mission handoffs is significantly lacking. This leads to the identification of three major gaps: the transition from search and detection to rescue operations; the coordinated transition between different platforms; and the assurance of safe deployment. The roadmap proposed in this paper emphasizes that human-supervised robot teams should share rescue information while preserving its uncertainty; maintain communication links where feasible; hand off tasks to appropriately equipped robots; and obtain authorization before performing critical operations involving safety. End-to-end evaluations should quantify information loss during task handoffs, positioning uncertainty, resilience following team failures, and the level of protection provided to trapped individuals.

title: Spatial Electrochemical Potential Encoding Decouples Information Storage From Optical Display for Water‐Triggered Hidden Multicolor Information Decoding
summary: ABSTRACT Water‐triggered optical materials hold promise for optical information storage, smart labels, and anti‐counterfeiting owing to their mild activation conditions and operational simplicity. However, existing systems typically encode
content: ABSTRACT Water‐triggered optical materials hold promise for optical information storage, smart labels, and anti‐counterfeiting owing to their mild activation conditions and operational simplicity. However, existing systems typically encode hidden information in the composition or structure of optical materials, coupling information storage with optical output and limiting information‐carrier design flexibility. Herein, a printed spatial electrochemical potential‐encoding strategy is proposed, integrating potential‐encoding units with distinct redox capabilities and a composite electrochromic layer to decouple information storage from optical output by pre‐storing hidden information in a spatial electrochemical potential distribution. The device exhibits high visual concealment before activation, with a color difference (Δ E * ) of less than 1 between different potential‐encoding regions. Upon water‐triggered activation, transient ionic pathways facilitate potential‐driven electron transfer and ion migration, inducing localized redox reactions that decode the stored electrochemical information into spatially independent, nonvolatile green, blue, and magenta optical outputs. Electrochemical analyses and simulations reveal the potential‐gradient‐regulated charge‐transfer mechanism. Enabled by fully printed fabrication, this platform supports ternary information encoding, dynamic pattern anti‐counterfeiting, physical‐digital authentication, and smart‐packaging applications. This strategy establishes spatial electrochemical potentials as an independent information‐encoding dimension, offering a new paradigm for passive optical storage, secure identification, and intelligent interactive systems.

title: International transport corridors and entrepreneurial dynamics: A quasi-natural experiment on the China Railway Express
summary: A central question for transport policy is whether major transnational infrastructure can generate transformative economic impacts beyond its core logistics function. This paper examines the China-Europe Railway Express (CERE) as a quasi-na
content: A central question for transport policy is whether major transnational infrastructure can generate transformative economic impacts beyond its core logistics function. This paper examines the China-Europe Railway Express (CERE) as a quasi-natural experiment to assess its role as an external enabler of urban entrepreneurship. Employing a multi-period difference-in-differences model on a panel of 280 Chinese prefecture-level cities covering the period 2007-2024, we estimate the causal effect of the CERE on regional entrepreneurial activity. The study found that the CERE has significantly improved the entrepreneurial activity of cities along the route, with the result consistently holding under replacing the explanatory variables, instrumental variable estimation, propensity score matching and placebo tests. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the entrepreneurial dividend of CERE is most pronounced in eastern and western regions, as well as in cities with higher administrative status, indicating that the local realization of infrastructure benefits depends critically on regional conditions. Mechanism analyses identify four primary transmission channels: trade openness, employment and talent agglomeration, industrial expansion, and industrial upgrading. This study empirically validates the external enabler theory within the context of a major national infrastructure strategy, advancing our understanding of the micro-entrepreneurial mechanisms through which strategic transport investment drives local economic development.

title: The Hidden Footprint of Hydrogel Adsorbents: Residual Monomer, Crosslinker and Nanofiller Leaching and the Ecotoxicity of Treated Water – A Critical Review
summary: Hydrogel adsorbents are currently among the most investigated materials for the removal of colours, metals and medicines from water. Most articles evaluate them by capacity, speed and number of reusecycles . Hardly anybody asks what the gel
content: Hydrogel adsorbents are currently among the most investigated materials for the removal of colours, metals and medicines from water. Most articles evaluate them by capacity, speed and number of reusecycles . Hardly anybody asks what the gel leaves in the water that it has just cleansed. This review tackles that hidden footprint. We collect the evidence for three kinds of leachable species: leftover monomers such as acrylamide and acrylic acid, unreacted crosslinkers with initiator residues and nanofillers that shed particles or ions, principally Ag, ZnO, Fe3O4 and graphene oxide. Release routes are traced over the whole service life, from initial wash after manufacture to regeneration in acid or base and eventually disposal. Analytical approaches for the detection of these species at regulatory levels are discussed; acrylamide can be detected at low ng L−1 by LC-MS/MS and dissolved and particulate metal are separated by ICP-MS after ultrafiltration. The toxicity data are grossly inconsistent. Acute effects of acrylamide on algae, daphnids and fish occur only at mg L−1, although drinking-water limitations are 0.1–0.5 µg L−1 and dissolved silver is active below 1 µg L−1. However, most research on the environmental safety of hydrogels are based on a single seed germination test. We suggest a tiered approach combining leachate chemistry with multi-trophic bioassays and safe-by-design steps: cleaner starting and cross-linking chemistry, confirmed purification and solid anchoring of nanofillers. Proposed minimal reporting standard will verify claims of clean water.

title: Core–periphery patterns in sustainable development: Heterogeneous associations between core-city SDG performance and new-town development
summary: Metropolitan areas (MAs) are important spatial units for regional coordination and sustainable urban development. Guided by Core–Periphery theory and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework, this study examines cross-sectional as
content: Metropolitan areas (MAs) are important spatial units for regional coordination and sustainable urban development. Guided by Core–Periphery theory and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework, this study examines cross-sectional associations between the SDG performance of 29 Chinese core cities and the development of 100 new towns across Industry, City, Employment, and Integration. Entropy weighting was used to calculate core-city SDG scores and new-town development scores. The mean new-town scores were 79.93 for Industry, 85.84 for City, 85.31 for Employment, and 73.21 for Integration. K-means clustering identified four new-town profiles. The Random Forest Algorithm (RFA) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were then used to characterize nonlinear predictive associations and quantify the relative contribution of each SDG to model predictions. SDG 9 contributed prominently to predictions of Industry, whereas SDGs 15 and 9 were prominent in predictions of City. The Integration model exhibited weaker and more heterogeneous predictive performance. The four clusters also showed distinct development profiles and heterogeneous associations with core-city SDG performance. These findings represent model-based associations rather than causal effects or directly identified spatial spillovers. The study extends Core–Periphery theory to sustainable-development assessment and provides a conditional empirical basis for differentiated new-town planning and metropolitan coordination.

title: A novel quantile-weighted ridge parameter for the Weibull regression model: Theory, simulation, and real-data application from Saudi Arabia
summary: The Weibull regression model constitutes a flexible and widely applied framework for the analysis of positive, right-skewed data in reliability, survival, environmental, and engineering research. In its standard formulation, one parameter g
content: The Weibull regression model constitutes a flexible and widely applied framework for the analysis of positive, right-skewed data in reliability, survival, environmental, and engineering research. In its standard formulation, one parameter governs the mean of the response distribution, while a second controls its dispersion and shape, thereby affording the model considerable flexibility for regression-based inference. However, when the explanatory variables are highly correlated, maximum likelihood estimation becomes unstable, resulting in inflated variances and unreliable coefficient estimates. This paper proposes a novel class of ridge estimators with a quantile-weighted ridge parameter for the Weibull regression model to mitigate this problem. The theoretical properties of the proposed estimator are derived, and conditions under which it outperforms the maximum likelihood estimator are established. A Monte Carlo simulation study is conducted to assess the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimator relative to competing methods, with results indicating that it achieves lower mean squared error across all conditions considered. The proposed method is further illustrated through an application to groundwater quality data, in which several physicochemical variables exhibit pronounced multicollinearity, as confirmed by variance inflation factors and the condition number. The empirical results corroborate the simulation findings, demonstrating that the quantile-weighted ridge estimator yields more stable and reliable parameter estimates than conventional alternatives under conditions of multicollinearity.

title: Use of Digital Tools and Environmental Practices Among Informal Caregivers of Older Adults in the European Union Embracing the Triple Transition: Cross-Sectional Study
summary: Background: The European Union is currently facing a demographic, digital, and environmental transition collectively known as the triple transition. Although these trends significantly impact long-term care services, they have typically bee
content: Background: The European Union is currently facing a demographic, digital, and environmental transition collectively known as the triple transition. Although these trends significantly impact long-term care services, they have typically been studied in isolation, overlooking potential synergies between the adoption of digital tools and environmental practices among informal caregivers of older adults. This study uniquely bridges this gap by applying an integrative social-ecological-infrastructural systems framework to examine how these transitions interact in everyday caregiving contexts. Objective: This study examined the relationship between the use of digital tools and eco-friendly practices among informal caregivers of older adults across the European Union and whether the adoption of digital solutions related differently to specific types of eco-friendly behaviors. Unlike previous research focusing on isolated aspects of each transition, we examined their interconnections, providing empirical evidence for developing integrated policy approaches. Methods: Using data from the Survey of Gender Gaps in Unpaid Care, Individual and Social Activities project (n=5761 informal caregivers of adults aged ≥65 years), we analyzed the association between frequency of use of digital tools for caregiving and environmental practices. We used the social-ecological-infrastructural systems conceptual framework and the theory of planned behavior (TPB) to interpret findings. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and multilevel mixed-effects regression models. Results: >.99). Respondents using digital tools daily had scores of environmentally sustainable behavior (SESBs) 22% higher than nonusers. Demographic patterns revealed higher use of digital tools among younger, more educated, and employed caregivers, indicating that any potential digital-environmental co-occurrence may be unevenly distributed across the caregiver population. Conclusions: The use of digital tools may be related to environmental behavior through improved access to information, peer norms, and a greater perceived ability to act, though these mechanisms were not directly tested. The stronger associations with consumption-related behaviors indicate that digital platforms may be particularly relevant to caregivers' access to eco-friendly products, second-hand goods, fair-trade options, and sustainable local services. By contrast, the lack of statistically significant correlations with recycling and resource conservation suggests that digital solutions alone may be insufficient to address behaviors that depend on structural conditions, physical infrastructure, local service availability, or established household routines. Policies should consider digital inclusion, caregiver support, and green infrastructure as interconnected areas while ensuring that older, less educated, and more burdened caregivers are not excluded from these potential co-benefits.
