title: Predicting cardiac conduction block in anti-SSA/Ro antibody-positive adults: development of a risk stratification model
summary: Background Anti-SSA/Ro antibody positivity has been increasingly linked to cardiac conduction block (CCB), yet the clinical features and risk factors for conduction abnormalities in this population remain unclear. Unlike degenerative conduc
content: Background Anti-SSA/Ro antibody positivity has been increasingly linked to cardiac conduction block (CCB), yet the clinical features and risk factors for conduction abnormalities in this population remain unclear. Unlike degenerative conduction disease, antibody-mediated conduction dysfunction may be reversible at an early stage. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for prevalent CCB at admission in anti-SSA/Ro antibody-positive patients and to develop an individualized risk-stratification model. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 869 adult patients with anti-SSA/Ro antibody positivity were enrolled, of whom 174 had CCB at admission, and were randomly divided into a training set ( n = 608) and an internal validation set ( n = 261) at a 7:3 ratio. Lasso regression, univariate and multivariable logistic regression were used for variable selection and model development. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis. Based on the regression coefficients of the multivariable logistic regression model, the coefficients were simplified into an simplified risk score, and patients were stratified into low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups by the tertiles of the total score in the training set, missing values imputed separately within each set and all model parameters derived from the training set. Results Twelve variables were selected by Lasso regression, and multivariable logistic regression identified Gender (OR = 2.12, 95% CI 1.41–3.21, P < 0.001), Age (per 1-year increase: OR = 1.03, 95% CI 1.02–1.05, P < 0.001) and Heart rate (per 1-beat/min increase: OR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.97–0.99, P = 0.045) as independent predictors of prevalent CCB at admission. The AUC was 0.68 (95% CI 0.63–0.74) and 0.70 (95% CI 0.62–0.78) in the training and internal validation sets, respectively, and the corresponding Hosmer-Lemeshow P values were 0.9676 and 0.7584.In the internal validation set, the calibration intercept was −0.04 (95% CI −0.35 to 0.28) and the calibration slope 1.12 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.63). The odds of CCB increased stepwise across the low-, intermediate- and high-risk strata in both sets (intermediate risk: OR 2.54 and 2.80; high risk: OR 4.73 and 6.56, respectively). Conclusion Female Gender, Age and Heart rate were independent predictors of prevalent CCB at admission in anti-SSA/Ro antibody-positive patients. A risk score based on these three predictors stratified patients into low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups, with a stepwise increase in the odds of CCB that was reproduced in the internal validation set. Discrimination was nevertheless modest and, pending external validation, the score should serve as an adjunctive tool for preliminary risk stratification rather than for individual prediction or diagnosis.

title: Dynamic Socio‐Technical Simulation of CCU Adoption Under Uncertainty: Integrating Multi‐Criteria Decision Analysis and Agent‐Based Modeling
summary: ABSTRACT The large‐scale deployment of carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies requires decision‐making under technological uncertainty, evolving policy environments, economic constraints, and societal influence. Conventional tech
content: ABSTRACT The large‐scale deployment of carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies requires decision‐making under technological uncertainty, evolving policy environments, economic constraints, and societal influence. Conventional techno‐economic and multi‐criteria assessments provide valuable insights but do not, by themselves, represent the dynamic interactions among facility adoption, regulatory responses, community conditions, and technological learning. This study develops an integrated socio‐technical simulation framework combining multi‐criteria decision analysis with agent‐based modeling and simulation to explore CCU adoption under alternative sustainability‐oriented decision priorities. The framework represents heterogeneous industrial facilities, nine sustainability‐related evaluation criteria, and feedback mechanisms involving regulatory incentives, social acceptance, and technology maturity. Five decision‐priority scenarios—climate, economy, energy, social, and infrastructure—are compared over a 30‐step simulation horizon. The results show substantial differences in adoption and system‐level performance. The climate scenario achieves the highest deployment, with 22 adopted facilities, and the greatest cumulative net avoidance (38 981.4 t) but also the highest cumulative hydrogen consumption and operating costs. Other scenarios exhibit different combinations of deployment, mitigation, and expenditure, indicating that no single scenario performs best across all assessed indicators. The framework therefore provides an exploratory approach for examining socio‐technical feedback and system‐level trade‐offs in CCU deployment. Its results are conditional on the specified model structure and baseline assumptions, rather than predictions of real‐world industrial adoption.

title: Second primary malignancies after CAR T-cell therapy: causal attribution, clonal evolution, and risk-adapted surveillance
summary: Background Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy can produce durable remission in refractory hematologic malignancies, but the expanding survivor population has focused attention on second primary malignancies (SPMs). Interpretatio
content: Background Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy can produce durable remission in refractory hematologic malignancies, but the expanding survivor population has focused attention on second primary malignancies (SPMs). Interpretation is difficult because recipients already carry substantial age-, disease-, and treatment-related cancer risk; follow-up is often short; outcome definitions vary; and competing mortality is high. Main body This critical review integrates epidemiologic, genomic, mechanistic, and regulatory evidence into a causal framework. Available evidence is consistent with a multistep clonal-evolution model: pre-existing clonal hematopoiesis and cumulative genotoxic injury establish the substrate; lymphodepletion, marrow inflammation, regenerative stress, and altered immune surveillance modify clonal fitness; and additional events permit transformation. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms are the most actionable subgroup. By contrast, T-cell malignancies derived from CAR-modified cells are exceptionally rare and require direct lineage and vector analysis because detection of a CAR sequence alone does not prove insertional oncogenesis. We propose a graded attribution ladder and a risk-adapted surveillance pathway centered on serial blood counts, prompt evaluation of unexplained cytopenias or lymphoid abnormalities, age-appropriate cancer screening, and mechanism-specific molecular testing. Conclusion Temporal association should not be equated with causation. Prospective denominator-based cohorts, matched comparators, paired biospecimens, integration-site mapping, and single-cell lineage reconstruction are needed to distinguish background risk, treatment-associated clonal selection, and true product-related oncogenesis.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Surgery in the Pre-Conflict Era: A Retrospective Analysis of the Surgical patterns and outcomes Medani Heart Center, Sudan (2019–2022)
summary: Abstract Background Pediatric cardiac care in sub-Saharan Africa is characterized by a significant surgical-medical gap, where late referrals and infrastructural limitations complicate outcomes for congenital and acquired heart disease. Whi
content: Abstract Background Pediatric cardiac care in sub-Saharan Africa is characterized by a significant surgical-medical gap, where late referrals and infrastructural limitations complicate outcomes for congenital and acquired heart disease. While Medani Heart Center (MHC) emerged as a critical tertiary referral hub in Sudan to address these geographic and systemic barriers, the 2023 conflict has fundamentally disrupted these specialized services. Documenting the clinical and procedural patterns established prior to this crisis is essential to providing a baseline for assessing current survival gaps and guiding future service restoration. This study evaluates the surgical patterns, patient demographics, and perioperative outcomes of pediatric cardiac patients managed at the MHC between 2019 and 2022. Methods We conducted a retrospective, observational cohort study of pediatric patients aged under 18 years who underwent cardiac surgical intervention at the Medani Heart Center (MHC), Sudan, between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2022. Data were retrieved from the center’s official registry for 250 patients who met the inclusion criteria. Although the study was intended to extend into 2023, data from January 2023 onward were lost due to the destruction of the center's infrastructure during the national conflict. This analysis represents the final, verified clinical record of the MHC’s pediatric cardiac services prior to the suspension of operations. Results Among the 250 pediatric cardiac surgical patients analyzed, the majority were males (54.8%) and predominantly school-age children (54.0%). Procedures comprised structural congenital repairs (ventricular septal defect [VSD] 24.4%, atrial septal defect [ASD] 10.0%, patent ductus arteriosus [PDA] 9.2%), complex cyanotic anomaly corrections (Tetralogy of Fallot 18.8%), and valvular interventions (23.6%). Surgical volume peaked in 2021 (38.4%) before stabilizing in 2022. Post-operative outcomes were largely favorable, with 83.6% of patients experiencing an uneventful recovery and 87.2% requiring an intensive care unit (ICU) stay of 5 days or fewer. The overall mortality rate was 4.0%. Conclusion This study confirms that a high-volume regional pediatric cardiac surgical program can deliver efficient, high-quality care, evidenced by an 83.6% complication-free recovery rate and streamlined ICU management. The surge and subsequent stabilization of procedural volumes indicate a maturing clinical workflow capable of managing complex congenital and valvular cases. These findings validate the effectiveness of past clinical protocols while highlighting an essential baseline for future cardiovascular care reconstruction in the region. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Small Effects, Big Noise: A Methodological Audit of Module Evaluation in Small-Scale Crack Instance Segmentation
summary: Abstract Crack instance segmentation papers built on YOLO-seg routinely claim gains by contrasting a baseline against the same model plus a proposed module, yet their statistical reliability is rarely examined. We audit a representative mod
content: Abstract Crack instance segmentation papers built on YOLO-seg routinely claim gains by contrasting a baseline against the same model plus a proposed module, yet their statistical reliability is rarely examined. We audit a representative module, a skeleton-aware label assigner (STAL), across three epoch budgets, three seeds, three calibers, and eight metrics, and replicate on a second dataset and a second, structurally different module. Sweeping its tolerance proves the module is not inert; yet no gain is usable. The paired effect stays below 0.9 pt and flips sign with budget and caliber; the cross-seed correlation flips sign on identical runs; and the minimum detectable effect exceeds the observed one by 2.7–13.3×. All seven domain metrics are undecidable, one quantised to 11.1 pt by its 9 crossing pairs, and with three seeds exact Wilcoxon cannot return p < 0.25 at any effect size. Both replications reproduce the resolution ceiling, not the effect. From these results we derive an eight-rule minimum discernible protocol: effect-size floor, fixed caliber, verified pairing, MDE beside every difference, per-seed dispersion, fixed budgets, computed seed budget; every rule checkable from a single per-seed table.

title: Complete chloroplast genome of Ethiopian endemic Aloe weloensis: comparative genomics and phylogenetic placement
summary: Abstract Aloe weloensis is a narrowly distributed, habitat-threatened endemic species of the Ethiopian Welo highlands. This species has been utilized as a source of medicine for treating diverse ailments, such as ear infections, headaches,
content: Abstract Aloe weloensis is a narrowly distributed, habitat-threatened endemic species of the Ethiopian Welo highlands. This species has been utilized as a source of medicine for treating diverse ailments, such as ear infections, headaches, rheumatism, stomachaches, wounds, and malaria. However, lack of molecular data has prevented the accurate identification and refinement of taxonomic relationships within Aloe L. In this study, we sequenced, assembled and annotated the chloroplast genome of A. weloensis. The plastome was 153,001 bp in size, and exhibited a typical quadripartite structure with a Large Single-Copy region (LSC = 83,613 bp), a Small Single-Copy region (SSC = 16,192 bp), and a pair of Inverted Repeats (IR = 26,598 bp). The genome encoded 130 genes encompassing (84 protein-coding genes, 38 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs). Comparative analysis within the ten studied Aloe species revealed a highly conserved plastome architecture. The highest divergence was observed in three coding genes ( matK, psbM, and rpl22 ) and three non-coding intergenic regions ( petN_psbM, petD_rpoA, and trnQ-UUG_psbK ), which are proposed as candidate markers for species identification and population studies. In addition, analysis of Simple Sequence Repeats (SSRs) and Long Sequence Repeats (LSRs) revealed 1,022 and 540 repeats, respectively, which also serve as valuable genetic markers that promote genomic variation and rearrangements. The RNA editing prediction identified 734 candidate C-to-U and U-to-C events across 62 sites, most often shifting residues from hydrophilic to hydrophobic. Phylogenomic reconstruction based on 64 protein-coding genes across 21 taxa placed A. weloensis within a well-supported clade (BS = 94, PP = 1) alongside A. perfoliata and A. marlothii , consistent with monophyletic Aloe . This study provides valuable genomic resources and candidate molecular markers for conservation genetics, future evolutionary studies, development of molecular markers, and breeding programs.

title: Consciousness as the Self Reflection of Cosmic Laws

content: Academic and philosophical circles have long lacked a self consistent physical explanation for the origin essence and diversity of products of consciousness. Most existing studies are limited to descriptions of neuroscience phenomena or philosophical speculations. They often deify and particularize human consciousness, overemphasize the subjective experience of carbon based life, and separate the homology of biological cognition and silicon based system cognition. Few explain why the same conscious system can produce completely different ideological achievements such as science shamanism theology religion and agnosticism. When touching on ultimate questions related to consciousness many researchers in scientific research finally turn to the standpoint of agnosticism. Based on the theory of the origin of light this paper establishes a unified model of signal coding and law cognition for consciousness and puts forward the core proposition. Consciousness is essentially the response and summary of complex material systems to the underlying cosmic signals and the self reflection of cosmic laws. Consciousness is not a mysterious innate gift. It emerges after material structures become increasingly complex and develop the capabilities of signal collection memory induction and feedback. Simple substances such as stones can only passively bear external effects. They cannot retain signals nor extract laws. Shamanism theology and religion are projective reflections shaped by information conditions cultural backgrounds and individual spiritual pursuits. title: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, a
content: Abstract Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.

title: Ecological change in the native Scottish pinewoods since 1971 – data from the Bunce 2018–2022 re-survey
summary: The native pinewoods of Scotland are acknowledged to be an important ecological resource, both for their biodiversity value and as a cultural and amenity resource. Due to the unique nature of the habitat and its limited range, it plays a cr
content: The native pinewoods of Scotland are acknowledged to be an important ecological resource, both for their biodiversity value and as a cultural and amenity resource. Due to the unique nature of the habitat and its limited range, it plays a critical role as an early warning system for broader environmental issues. In the late 1960s and 70s, increased concern was expressed regarding a decline in the status and management of the pinewoods. In response to the concerns, an ecological monitoring survey was initiated by R. G. H. Bunce of the Nature Conservancy in 1971, recording ground flora, tree information, soils and other descriptive attributes. Since that time, interest in the pinewoods has increased further, and there is a general consensus that the habitat is more vulnerable than ever. Thanks to a recent repeat survey between 2018 and 2022, questions addressing the threats and changes occurring in the pinewoods can now be explored in a statistically robust way. These questions include issues surrounding the impacts of deer grazing, regeneration, the balance between native and exotic species, local disturbances, trends in ground flora species occurrences, climate change and recovery from acidification. The new data from the 2018–2022 survey are now publicly available via the following DOI: https://doi.org/10.5285/5e268e86-4a4f-4112-bf2d-c3b0179c915c (Smart et al., 2023). Change data are available at: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34574874 (Wood et al., 2026).

title: High-intensity wave vortices in the beam-optics domain: 3D spatial structure, single-plane models, and their propagation properties
source: Journal of the Optical Society of America A
summary: Typically, vortices in wave fields are associated with amplitude zeros. In contrast, recently described high-intensity (Type II) wave vortices appear near amplitude poles and can exist only in disconnected space. We attempt to extend the co
content: Typically, vortices in wave fields are associated with amplitude zeros. In contrast, recently described high-intensity (Type II) wave vortices appear near amplitude poles and can exist only in disconnected space. We attempt to extend the concept of a Type II optical vortex (OV) to paraxial beam-like optical fields. It is shown that "true" Type II OV fields can exist only in a multiply connected three-dimensional space, where spatial "holes" impenetrable to the electromagnetic field are formed by purposefully created filamentary inclusions of material. However, the cross-section of a "true" Type II OV can be reproduced in a specific plane of ordinary "free" space, where the hole is designated by a region with zero amplitude. Methods for the practical creation of the discussed field structures are proposed, including methods using programmable light modulators and computer-synthesized holograms. The results of computer simulations demonstrate reasonable agreement with experimental data.

title: Comparison of direct and indirect epiglottis lifting techniques using the McGRATH™ MAC video laryngoscope on the incidence of intubation-related complications: a randomized controlled trial
summary: Abstract Background During video laryngoscopy (VL), the epiglottis can be lifted either indirectly from the vallecula or directly by placing the blade beneath it. Although direct lifting improves vocal cord visualization, whether these tech
content: Abstract Background During video laryngoscopy (VL), the epiglottis can be lifted either indirectly from the vallecula or directly by placing the blade beneath it. Although direct lifting improves vocal cord visualization, whether these techniques differ in intubation-related complications remains unclear. This multicenter randomized controlled trial investigated whether direct epiglottis lifting using the McGRATH™ MAC VL increases intubation-related complications compared with indirect lifting. Methods This multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial was conducted at two hospitals in Japan. Adult patients scheduled for elective surgery requiring tracheal intubation were screened; after exclusion of 96 patients, 938 were randomized to direct ( n = 464) or indirect lifting ( n = 474). Thirty-nine patients (direct, n = 19; indirect, n = 20) had unavailable primary outcome data and were not included in the modified intention-to-treat population, which comprised 899 patients (direct, n = 445; indirect, n = 454). The primary outcome was a composite of hoarseness, postoperative sore throat, hypoxemia, aspiration, dental injury, and epiglottal displacement. Secondary outcomes included individual complications, intubation conditions, and hemodynamic responses. Subgroup analyses by anesthesiologist experience were performed. Results The primary composite outcome did not differ between groups (direct 42.9% vs. indirect 41.9%; P = 0.787). Other individual complications (hoarseness, sore throat, hypoxemia, aspiration, dental injury) were comparable. Epiglottal displacement occurred exclusively in the direct group (4.5% vs. 0%). External laryngeal manipulation (backward upward rightward pressure [BURP]) was required less frequently in the direct group (6.3% vs. 10.4%; P = 0.030). Intubation time, number of attempts, and hemodynamic responses did not differ between groups. No significant difference between techniques was found within any experience group, whereas the interaction between lifting technique and anesthesiologist experience was significant (P for interaction = 0.025; exploratory). Conclusion This superiority trial did not demonstrate a significant difference in intubation-related complications between direct and indirect epiglottis lifting, although their comparative safety remains uncertain. Direct lifting required less frequent BURP use, but epiglottal displacement occurred exclusively with this technique. Trial registration UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (Registration No UMIN000055803). Date of registration 10/10/2024.

title: GreenScapes: Optimized Vegetation Configurations in Cities
summary: Vegetation plays a central role in cities, serving functional roles such as balancing shade and sky exposure, shaping the microclimate, carbon sequestration, and providing acoustic screening. Furthermore, aesthetic choices in landscape styl
content: Vegetation plays a central role in cities, serving functional roles such as balancing shade and sky exposure, shaping the microclimate, carbon sequestration, and providing acoustic screening. Furthermore, aesthetic choices in landscape styles (formal, modernist, picturesque) are important for citizens' well-being and should be considered in the design of urban landscapes. In this paper, we present a novel method for placing vegetation, ranging from shrubs to large trees, in 3D urban scenes. Our method uses individual lots as input and employs a conditioned Vision-Language Model (VLM) to generate a top-down rendering of vegetation, placing large trees, small trees, and shrubs on lawn areas. This rendering is then converted into a 3D scene by detecting individual plants and selecting appropriate 3D assets. To refine the proposed configurations, we define an optimization loop that keeps the VLM-generated positions fixed after a deterministic feasibility repair and uses CMA-ES to optimize per-instance scale transformations along with discrete vegetation asset substitutions. To define the objective function for the optimization, we evaluate the generated 3D scenes with efficient surrogate models of shade and path-based acoustic exposure. Furthermore, we render in-scene views at each optimization step to compute view-dependent perceptual descriptors, enabling the generation of both aesthetic and functional vegetation layouts for urban scenes.

title: HyperGenie: A method for predicting enzymatic gene essentiality using hypergraph neural networks and genome-scale metabolic models
summary: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant st
content: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant strains optimize for maximum growth. Recent machine learning approaches circumvent this limitation using random forests or graph neural networks on mass flow graphs (MFGs). However, data-driven tools like random forests discard network topology, while graph-based tools like MFGs decompose multi-component biochemical reactions into pairwise interactions, misrepresenting complex stoichiometry and limiting interpretability. Furthermore, existing methods remain largely uncharacterised in data-scarce regimes and cross-environmental conditions. Here, we introduce HyperGenie, a framework that integrates genome-scale metabolic models with directed hypergraph neural networks by representing metabolites as nodes and reactions as hyperedges. Operating directly on wild-type flux features, HyperGenie eliminates post-knockout optimality assumptions, achieves a 13% PR-AUC improvement over prior objective-dependent methods, and matches computationally demanding, state-of-the-art flux-sampling baselines. Using HyperGenie to guide targeted growth curve assays, we identified latent essentiality misannotations across three genes in the benchmark iML1515 dataset, which we then reconciled and validated experimentally via PCR. In data-scarce regimes, HyperGenie retained robust predictive performance (> 90% PR-AUC) when trained on as little as 40% of the data. To isolate the value of hypergraph message passing, we benchmarked HyperGenie against an independent-reaction multilayer perceptron (MLPGenie) across diverse nutrient environments and uptake rates, where HyperGenie's hypergraph inductive bias yielded consistent accuracy gains (> 2% in glucose; > 4% across six alternative carbon sources). Notably, HyperGenie exhibits robust zero-shot cross-nutrient generalization, accurately forecasting gain-of-essentiality phenotypes on novel carbon sources, though loss-of-essentiality remains challenging. Finally, coupling hypergraph representations with SHAP attribution provides actionable mechanistic insights into metabolic rewiring, establishing a data-efficient, interpretable platform for discovering novel antibiotic targets.

title: Risk assessment and strategic decision support to enhance preparedness and minimize human and economic losses in managing natural disasters
summary: Abstract Accurate prediction of the impacts of natural disasters is essential for effective risk management, emergency response, and policy planning. However, the complex, nonlinear, and highly irregular nature of disaster-related data pose
content: Abstract Accurate prediction of the impacts of natural disasters is essential for effective risk management, emergency response, and policy planning. However, the complex, nonlinear, and highly irregular nature of disaster-related data poses significant challenges for traditional modeling approaches. This study proposes a comprehensive machine learning and deep learning framework for economic loss prediction, integrating advanced preprocessing, optimization, and validation strategies to enhance predictive accuracy and robustness. Multiple predictive models, including deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks, and gradient boosting, are systematically evaluated and optimized using a Turbulent Flow of Water-based Optimization algorithm. To address data irregularities, Isolation Forest is used for outlier detection, and statistical tests are applied to assess distributional assumptions before normalization. Model performance is rigorously assessed using 5-fold cross-validation and a diverse set of evaluation metrics that capture accuracy, bias, and agreement. In addition, ensemble learning is employed to improve predictive reliability further, while runtime analysis provides insights into computational efficiency. The statistical significance of performance differences is verified using ANOVA and the Wilcoxon test, and an ablation study is conducted to examine model stability and sensitivity. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust, statistically significant improvements in predictive performance, highlighting its suitability for reliable economic loss modeling. This study contributes a validated, generalizable, and decision-oriented modeling approach that can support data-driven disaster risk reduction and management strategies.

title: Effects of meteorological factors and air pollutants on hospital admissions for type 2 diabetes mellitus in Urumqi: a time-stratified case-crossover study
summary: Background The joint effects of meteorological conditions and air pollutants on the risk of hospitalization for diabetes remain insufficiently understood, particularly due to the limited availability of large-scale time-series studies in no
content: Background The joint effects of meteorological conditions and air pollutants on the risk of hospitalization for diabetes remain insufficiently understood, particularly due to the limited availability of large-scale time-series studies in northern China. Methods Daily hospitalization records of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in Urumqi City from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2025, were collected, along with corresponding daily air pollutant concentrations and meteorological data. A time-stratified case-crossover design combined with a distributed lag nonlinear model (DLNM) was applied to assess nonlinear exposure-response relationships and lagged effects. Two-pollutant models, seasonal stratification analyses, and interaction analyses involving extreme weather events were conducted to evaluate the robustness of exposure effects. Results During the study period, the mean daily number of type 2 diabetes admissions was 18.96, ranging from 0 to 102. Low-temperature exposure was associated with an increased risk of admission over intermediate cumulative lag periods, but the association attenuated over the full lag period. Relative to the median daily mean temperature (10.60 °C), the cumulative relative risk (RR) at the 5th percentile (−13.08 °C) was 1.470 (95% CI: 1.141–1.895) over lag 0–21 days and 0.986 (95% CI: 0.753–1.292) over the lag 0–31 day lag. At the 1st percentile (−17.69 °C), the corresponding RRs were 1.487 (95% CI: 1.068–2.073) and 1.027 (95% CI: 0.695–1.516), respectively. Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) was positively associated with admissions in the same-day analyses and remained positively associated in selected two-pollutant models adjusted for sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) or the daily maximum 8-h average ozone concentration (O 3 -8h). Positive associations for NO 2 and ozone (O 3 ) were mainly observed in the warm season, whereas an inverse statistical association with particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM 2.5 ) was mainly observed in the cold season. Cold spells may have modified the association between O 3 and admissions (interaction RR = 1.683, 95% CI: 1.049–2.699); however, the 95% confidence intervals for all additive synergy indices included the null value. Conclusion Low temperature and short-term NO2 exposure were associated with T2DM hospital admissions in Urumqi, although the low-temperature association attenuated over the full cumulative lag period. The associations with air pollutants also exhibited distinct seasonal patterns. Cold-wave events may amplify the association between O 3 exposure and T2DM hospitalization risk on the multiplicative scale, although evidence of additive interaction was lacking. Conversely, the observed inverse association between PM 2.5 and hospitalization highlights the need to consider potential ecological biases, including those potentially related to behavioral avoidance and changes in healthcare utilization, when interpreting environmental epidemiological findings.

title: Soil Aggregate Associated Carbon, Biological Pools and Wheat Yield Under Contrasting Mechanized Rice Residue Management Practices with Varying Nitrogen Application in North-Western India
source: Communications in Soil Science and Plant Analysis
summary: Soil aggregation plays an important role in organic carbon stabilization and protection. However, the effects of rice residue management and nitrogen (N) application on aggregate-associated carbon fractions and biological properties are not
content: Soil aggregation plays an important role in organic carbon stabilization and protection. However, the effects of rice residue management and nitrogen (N) application on aggregate-associated carbon fractions and biological properties are not always studied together. This study evaluated eight rice residue management practices under three N levels (0, 75, and 100% of the recommended dose) in an irrigated rice–wheat system of north-western India. The study examined soil aggregate distribution and stability, different organic carbon fractions, biological carbon pools, and wheat productivity. No significant interaction between N application and residue management was observed for the measured yield, carbon, and biological parameters and therefore, their main effects were assessed separately. Compared with no N application (N0), the recommended N dose (N100) increased total water-stable aggregates by ~7.34%, macro-aggregates by ~13.0%, mineral-associated carbon by ~42.0%, and sodium hypochlorite-oxidizable carbon by ~73.8%. Compared with residue burning (CT-RB), zero tillage with complete residue retention (ZT+R100) increased total water-stable aggregates, macro-aggregates, and micro-aggregates by ~19.5%, ~22.9%, and ~16.6%, respectively. It also improved water-soluble organic carbon (~15.3–38.4 mg kg–1), carbohydrate carbon (~2.5–5.9 g kg–1), microbial biomass carbon (~146.4–244.2 µg g−1soil), basal soil respiration (~12.2–32.7 µg CO2 g−1hr–1), glomalin-related soil proteins (~5.1 to 9.6 g kg–1), and fungal biomass (~480–689 µg n-acetyl glucosamine g–1 soil). Macro-aggregates generally contained higher concentrations of labile carbon and biologically active pools than meso and micro-aggregates. Wheat grain yield under ZT+R100 was ~15.4% higher than residue removal (CT-R0) and ~17.3% higher than CT-RB. In nutshell, these findings indicate that rice residue management influences not only soil aggregation but also the distribution of carbon fractions and biological pools among different aggregate sizes. Under the conditions of this study, ZT+R100 and residue retention with rice straw compost incorporation (CT+R100+C) emerged as the most beneficial residue-management practices, while N100 generally produced the highest values, but mostly was comparable with N75 for the measured parameters. However, the absence of a significant interaction indicates that the combined effects of residue management and N application did not establish a statistically distinct optimum treatment.

title: The Effects of Low Earth Orbit Thermal Cycling on the Mechanical Performance and Structural Integrity of 2-D Aramid/Epoxy Tubular Braided Composites
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Satellites are an essential component of modern technology responsible for upholding much of the world’s information infrastructure. Their use has provided global positioning, Earth and deep space imaging, weather forecasting, and long-rang
content: Satellites are an essential component of modern technology responsible for upholding much of the world’s information infrastructure. Their use has provided global positioning, Earth and deep space imaging, weather forecasting, and long-range communications. Most satellites are situated in a region of space known as low Earth orbit (LEO) which contains several environmental hazards including but not limited to ionizing radiation, space debris impacts, and large temperature fluctuations. Ambient temperatures in LEO range between -65℃ and 125℃, and satellites in LEO fluctuate between these temperature ranges frequently as they enter and exit the region of orbit with direct sunlight. With these fluctuating temperatures, cyclical expansion and contraction of materials within satellites occur, which can cause stress development in homogeneous materials and at points of connection with dissimilar materials. This fluctuation in temperature is called thermal cycling. To minimize the potential damage incurred by thermal cycling, the design of a material with a near zero coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) is ideal. Tubular braided composites (TBCs) are a highly customizable class of textile composites bearing a cylindrical structure optimal for use in structural reinforcement applications. Their composition with high-strength fibers coupled with polymer matrices allow for the creation of structures with high-specific strength and near zero CTEs. As a result, they may be able to resist the potential risks posed by thermal cycling if used in satellites. However, TBCs have seen limited use in satellite structures, with much of the currently used components being made with carbon fiber. Aramid fiber TBCs may be a viable alternative due to their lower density, which may serve to improve the overall deployment process of a satellite. Additionally, they still provide high specific strength and a relatively small, negative CTE necessary to design a near-zero CTE TBC. To verify the suitability of aramid based TBCs in satellite structures, this work investigated the effects of relatively low amounts of thermal cycling on 2-D Kevlar®/Epoxy TBCs. This was completed through the use of mechanical testing to identify any potential changes in their mechanical performance, and with scanning electron microscopy (SEM) to identify structural changes induced by thermal cycling. These TBCs were manufactured at one of three braid angles (35°,45°, and 55°) and were exposed to either zero, five, or ten thermal cycles. From the mechanical tests, it was found that thermal cycling decreased the average elastic modulus and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of the 35-degree TBCs by 6.6% and 13.8% after five cycles, and 17.0% and 33.5% after ten cycles respectively. title: A shifted gamma–logistic transmuted distribution with properties and applications to process monitoring via CUSUM control charts
summary: We introduce the shifted gamma–logistic transmuted (SGLT) distribution, obtained by applying the quadratic rank transmutation map (QRTM) to a shifted, power-transformed logistic baseline that coincides with the power half-logistic law. Clos
content: We introduce the shifted gamma–logistic transmuted (SGLT) distribution, obtained by applying the quadratic rank transmutation map (QRTM) to a shifted, power-transformed logistic baseline that coincides with the power half-logistic law. Closed-form expressions are derived for the cdf, pdf, reliability and hazard functions, quantile function, moments, moment generating function and order statistics. The three parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood; the score equations were re-derived and checked against finite differences, and standard errors come from the observed information. A Monte Carlo study ( N = 1000 replications) shows that mean squared errors decrease with the sample size, but that the transmutation parameter is poorly determined for n ≤ 100. A two-sided likelihood-ratio CUSUM chart for SGLT observations is constructed, with the decision interval calibrated by simulation to an in-control average run length of 370. On two industrial datasets the SGLT attains the lowest AIC and BIC among the eight models of the original comparison (Tables 2 and 3), but its λ = 0 sub-model attains lower values still, the likelihood-ratio test does not reject λ = 0, and bootstrap-calibrated KS, CvM and AD tests reject the SGLT fit for the glass-fibre data while not rejecting it for the carbon-fibre data. The results delimit what the added transmutation parameter does and does not contribute.

title: Risk analysis of hearing loss in workplace populations due to combined exposure to benzene compounds and occupational noise
summary: Objective Occupational noise-induced hearing loss has emerged as the second most common occupational disease in China. Combined exposure to benzene compounds and noise is common in workplaces, and there is an urgent need to clarify the asso
content: Objective Occupational noise-induced hearing loss has emerged as the second most common occupational disease in China. Combined exposure to benzene compounds and noise is common in workplaces, and there is an urgent need to clarify the association of hearing damage associated with this combination. Methods Judgment sampling was used to recruit 155 employees from four typical enterprises, who were assigned to a control group, an organic solvent-exposure group, a noise-exposure group, and a combined-exposure group. Questionnaires, environmental monitoring, biological sample analyses, and pure-tone audiometry were conducted, along with SPSS statistical analysis, to investigate hearing damage resulting from exposure to these two factors, both individually and in combination. Results Multiple benzene compounds were detected in both the organic-solvent-exposure group and the combined-exposure group; ambient toluene concentrations were weakly to moderately positively correlated with PGA, and xylene concentrations were weakly to moderately positively correlated with 2-MHA, 3-MHA, and 4-MHA. Hearing loss in the noise-exposure group was concentrated at the high-frequency range, whereas the organic solvent-exposure group affected mid- to high-frequency ranges. In the combined-exposure group, hearing loss spanned the entire frequency range, with an abnormality rate significantly higher than those of the single exposure groups. Concentrations of benzene metabolites were weakly to moderately positively correlated with hearing-threshold levels. Conclusion Benzene compounds and noise each exert independent ototoxic effects; combined-exposure is associated with auditory health hazards, providing a scientific basis for protecting workers’ hearing health and managing associated risks.

title: Arithmetic Geometry, Spectral Zeta Theory, and Non-Commutative Geometry of the Chrysene Formalism: The (9, 8) Hermitian Curve over GF(4), Genus-1 Goppa Codes, the Ihara–Bass Zeta Function, and Connes’ Spectral Triple
summary: This paper develops four mathematical constructions associated with finite graph and quaternary structures in the Chrysene Formalism. The smooth projective Hermitian curve Y^2 Z + Y Z^2 = X^3 over GF(4) has genus one and attains the Hasse-W
content: This paper develops four mathematical constructions associated with finite graph and quaternary structures in the Chrysene Formalism. The smooth projective Hermitian curve Y^2 Z + Y Z^2 = X^3 over GF(4) has genus one and attains the Hasse-Weil bound with nine rational points: eight affine points and one point at infinity. Its rational-point group is (Z/3)^2. The numerical correspondence with the two nine-vertex parts and eight perfect matchings of the chrysene graph is distinguished from a canonical structural identification. Evaluation of the Riemann-Roch spaces L(4P_infinity) and L(3P_infinity) on the eight affine points gives, respectively, a Euclidean self-dual [8,4,4] quaternary code and a [8,3,5] quaternary code correcting up to two errors. Exact computations for the supplied chrysene and tetracene graph models establish that both each have 1189 spanning trees and Ihara-Bass derivative +7134 at one, while their degree-shift invariants, three-matching counts, adjacency characteristic coefficients, and non-backtracking closed-walk counts distinguish them. In particular, the length-14 non-backtracking traces are 168 and 56. Finite even spectral data are separated from the stronger real-spectral-triple requirements: the natural inversion exchanges the bipartition, and the full diagonal algebra fails the order-one condition for adjacency hopping. For a path with nearest-neighbor hopping strength t, an explicit admissible observable gives the spectral-distance lower bound (N-1)/(2t), without asserting equality. At t=1 this yields 2.5 and 26.5 for paths of lengths six and fifty-four vertices. These results are mathematical constructions and conditional model interpretations, not empirical validation of molecular coding, transport, or biogenesis.

title: Temporally partitioned wind power forecasting with validation-calibrated residual diagnostics for PHM-oriented interpretation
summary: Introduction Accurate wind-power forecasting is critical for the reliable integration of renewable energy into power grids, but reproducible evaluation requires explicit temporal partitioning and clearly defined feature-availability assumpt
content: Introduction Accurate wind-power forecasting is critical for the reliable integration of renewable energy into power grids, but reproducible evaluation requires explicit temporal partitioning and clearly defined feature-availability assumptions. This study presents a temporally partitioned, forecasting-first workflow utilizing the DaKS/Kassel synthetic wind-power dataset. Methods The canonical tabular benchmark establishes a target-time-aligned baseline by combining DaKS day-ahead numerical weather prediction covariates with recent observed-power history constructed relative to target valid time. Preprocessing parameters are fitted on the training partition, model and warning-threshold selection use validation data, and the test partition is reserved for final evaluation. For comparison, controlled subset experiments on four parks evaluated several advanced neural and sequential architectures, including a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a gated recurrent unit (GRU), a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, a temporal convolutional network (TCN), and PatchTST-Lite (Patch Time Series Transformer). Furthermore, we developed a validation-calibrated residual diagnostic layer that analyzes prediction errors across spatial, temporal, and operating-regime dimensions. Results Within the canonical comparable full-dataset benchmark, XGBoost achieved the lowest test mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0657, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.1134, and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.860. The strong-model diagnostic run achieved a test MAE of 0.0662 while retaining structured candidate warning episodes. Discussion These residual patterns are interpreted as structured deviations in forecast behavior rather than as confirmed physical equipment faults. This framework provides a reproducible forecasting and residual-screening foundation for future research in wind-energy digital twins and prognostics and health management (PHM).

title: Routine vitamin B12, folate and thyroid biomarkers, cognitive trajectory and mortality in older adults with neurocognitive disorders: a retrospective cohort study
summary: Background Vitamin B12, folate and thyroid-function testing are routinely included in dementia workups, but their prognostic significance after a neurocognitive-disorder diagnosis remains uncertain. Methods We analyzed a deidentified Taiwan
content: Background Vitamin B12, folate and thyroid-function testing are routinely included in dementia workups, but their prognostic significance after a neurocognitive-disorder diagnosis remains uncertain. Methods We analyzed a deidentified Taiwanese tertiary-hospital cohort of patients aged ≥65 years with neurocognitive disorders (dementia or mild cognitive impairment; n = 7,969). The prespecified primary analyses were mixed-effects models of annual MMSE and CDR-SB trajectories in which baseline vitamin B12, folate, TSH and free thyroxine were entered jointly, restricted to patients with all four biomarkers and at least two assessments (MMSE n = 818; CDR-SB n = 1,009). CDR progression and all-cause mortality were secondary outcomes, and prescription-record analyses were exploratory. Sensitivity analyses addressed missing data, selection into the analysis sets, competing risks, confounding, laboratory timing and prior treatment. Results Biomarker testing and repeated cognitive assessment were clinically driven, so all estimates apply to a selected tested-and-followed subgroup that was younger, less impaired and less likely to die than untested or unfollowed patients. Higher baseline vitamin B12 was associated with slower MMSE decline (β +0.146 points/year per SD, 95% CI +0.038 to +0.255; FDR q = 0.017), an association retained after multiple imputation and selection weighting but attenuated after excluding patients treated before baseline. The full-range association of higher TSH with slower decline on both scales was not robust: it depended on a few patients with TSH > 10 mIU/L and was absent within the euthyroid range. Folate deficiency was associated with faster CDR progression (HR 1.57, 95% CI 1.13–2.19, p = 0.008), including in competing-risk models; the estimate for vitamin B12 deficiency was imprecise (HR 1.22, 95% CI 0.88–1.69, p = 0.23) and does not exclude a clinically relevant increase. Higher vitamin B12 was associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.035 per 100 pg/mL, 95% CI 1.016–1.055), but this was attenuated after flexible adjustment for renal function. Documented vitamin B12 supplementation showed no detectable association with CDR-SB trajectory in a small exploratory matched analysis. Conclusion In patients who underwent biomarker testing and repeated cognitive assessment, routine biomarkers from workups for reversible causes provided modest, context-dependent prognostic information. We interpret these associations as possible indicators of clinical state rather than evidence that the biomarkers, or their correction, influence the progression of neurocognitive disorders.

title: Nonlinear Associations of Carbon Density and Habitat Quality with Climate, Vegetation and Topography in the Qilian Mountains
summary: Habitat quality and carbon density showed contrasting environmental associations, with several SHAP zero crossings recurring across three boosting models. Background and Objectives: Nonlinear ecosystem-service relationships can reveal spati
content: Habitat quality and carbon density showed contrasting environmental associations, with several SHAP zero crossings recurring across three boosting models. Background and Objectives: Nonlinear ecosystem-service relationships can reveal spatial heterogeneity relevant to conservation, but their sensitivity to model choice remains an important source of uncertainty. Materials and Methods: We combined the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model, 12 machine-learning algorithms, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Model fitting and SHAP interpretation used five historical snapshots from 2000 to 2020; extrapolated estimates for 2025 were used only for illustrative temporal comparison. Results: Both indicators were generally higher in the southeastern than northwestern Qilian Mountains. Mean annual temperature and elevation ranked highest for habitat quality, with zero crossings near −4 °C and 3.84 km. Normalized difference vegetation index ranked highest for carbon density, with zero crossings at 0.16–0.17; evapotranspiration crossings occurred around 147–150 mm. Precipitation boundaries varied more among models. Conclusions: The contrasting associations identify candidate environmental gradients for monitoring and restoration assessment. Agreement among boosting models supports consistency within this model family, while the crossings remain statistical descriptors of model-derived indicators rather than demonstrated ecological tipping points.

title: Powertrain Systems Design for Heavy-Duty Trucks: Integrating Hybrid Electric Technologies with Low- and Zero-Carbon Fuel Engines to Reduce Fuel Consumption and Greenhouse Gas Emissions
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Class 8 heavy-duty (HD) trucks are major contributors to global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, accounting for 50%, 40%, and 25% of transportation-sector emissions in the United States, Canada, and Europe, respectively. This thesis proposes
content: Class 8 heavy-duty (HD) trucks are major contributors to global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, accounting for 50%, 40%, and 25% of transportation-sector emissions in the United States, Canada, and Europe, respectively. This thesis proposes new powertrain architectures and creates a vehicle-level design framework to evaluate the combined effect of hybridization and the use of natural gas (NG) or Hydrogen (H2) compression ignition (CI) engines on reducing fuel consumption and GHG emissions in Class 8 HD trucks. First, a conventional Class 8 diesel truck model is created and validated against on-road test data collected from a Peterbilt 579 truck operating over a real-world regional-haul drive cycle. The validated baseline model is then modified by replacing the diesel engine with HPDI NG and HPDI H2 engines, along with the required changes to the onboard fuel storage and delivery systems. These HPDI engines use a small amount of diesel fuel as an ignition pilot while maintaining brake thermal efficiencies comparable to modern diesel engines. The results show that the conventional HPDI NG truck reduces tailpipe CO2 emissions by 20.3% to 21.1%, while the conventional HPDI H₂ truck reduces tailpipe CO2 emissions by 97.4% to 98.5% relative to the baseline diesel configuration over the real-world regional-haul drive cycle. Second, three hybrid electric powertrain configurations are modeled and evaluated for Class 8 HD truck applications: a pre-transmission parallel (P2) hybrid, a complex power-split hybrid, and a series plug-in hybrid. Energy management strategies are developed for each architecture, and a multi-stage component sizing framework is created to optimize the primary powertrain components and key control-related variables. The framework minimizes net powertrain energy consumption while maintaining propulsion system performance comparable to the validated conventional baseline model. Third, the propulsion system performance criteria traditionally used for conventional HD trucks are revised to better address hybridized Class 8 trucks equipped with downsized engines. Real-world grade profiles of 15 steep highways frequently used by HD trucks are derived and applied as gradeability criteria. The results demonstrate that engine downsizing is feasible in the P2 hybrid configuration while maintaining performance comparable to the conventional baseline and reducing net powertrain energy consumption by 3.4% to 8.9% over a real-world regional-haul drive cycle. Fourth, the hybrid powertrains are optimized for integration with different NG-CI engines, including a diesel-pilot premixed NG engine and downsized or full-size technology-enhanced HPDI NG engines. Engine technology packages, including turbo-compounding and increased compression ratio, are applied to improve brake thermal efficiency in the mid-to-high torque regions where hybridized engines operate most frequently. title: AfriBuild: Building materials carbon atlas for Africa, catalogue and evidence data
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: AfriBuild is an evidence map and tiered emission-factor catalogue for building materials in Africa, published by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). This deposit (catalogue ve
content: AfriBuild is an evidence map and tiered emission-factor catalogue for building materials in Africa, published by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). This deposit (catalogue version 0.3.2) contains the catalogue of 1,134 material and country combinations (21 materials in 54 countries) with evidence tiers T1 to T4 and T0 gaps, values, 95% intervals and sources; the evidence database of 79 included studies and values read from full texts; a data-readiness index; cement-related CO2 embodied in national consumption; national cement screening factors; grid carbon intensity; household floor materials; and a Ghana detail set with clinker imports, cement scenarios and the GhaBuild-EF factor table with pedigree scores. title: Transient thermoviscoelastic stresses in AISI 4340 steel cylinders: fractional-memory modeling, experimental benchmarking and design implications
summary: Abstract The fractional heat equation of Hendy et al. (2019) is replaced by a fractional Green–Naghdi heat transport law with a memory-dependent derivative, whose fractional order is bounded by a harmonic passivity condition. The model is a
content: Abstract The fractional heat equation of Hendy et al. (2019) is replaced by a fractional Green–Naghdi heat transport law with a memory-dependent derivative, whose fractional order is bounded by a harmonic passivity condition. The model is applied to a finite solid cylinder of AISI 4340 alloy steel, heated over a central disk of its top face and clamped at its base. Laplace transformation and a finite Hankel series reduce the problem to a two-point boundary-value problem, solved analytically by the state-space approach with growing and decaying axial modes, so that base reflections are represented. The solution is verified against independent finite-difference solutions, Chebyshev collocation, convergence tests and an exact quasi-static solution for a 20 mm cylinder. In an experimental benchmarking against published measurements on AISI 4340, the predicted thermoelastic coefficient, −1.01 K/GPa, agrees with the measured release heating, −1.2 ± 0.3 K/GPa, and the predicted longitudinal wave speed differs from the measured ultrasonic velocity by 3.7%. The tensile-bar data exclude the illustrative fractional-memory parameters at the structural scale and bound the memory time from below, but a calibration–validation test shows that they cannot identify it. For design, the allowable temperature rise under slow heating is 135–331 K across the yield-strength range of the steel. Rapid heating of short cylinders over a large part of the end face amplifies the peak von Mises stress by up to a factor of two and can make the clamped base critical, while the heat-transport law changes the peak by up to 29%.

title: From Agro-Waste to Adsorbent: Ziziphus spina-christi Seed-Derived Materials for the Removal of Malachite Green from Water – A Mini-Review
source: Al-Noor Journal of Engineering Management and Computer Science
summary: Malachite green (MG) is a cationic triphenylmethane dye that is still used in textile dyeing and, illegally in many countries, in aquaculture. Because of its toxicity, its persistence and the accumulation of its reduced metabolite, leucomal
content: Malachite green (MG) is a cationic triphenylmethane dye that is still used in textile dyeing and, illegally in many countries, in aquaculture. Because of its toxicity, its persistence and the accumulation of its reduced metabolite, leucomalachite green, in fish tissue, its removal from water is of great importance. Adsorption is the most practical treatment option for MG, but the high cost of commercial activated carbon has led researchers to develop low-cost adsorbents from agricultural wastes. This mini-review discusses the use of the seeds and stones of Sidr (Ziziphus spina-christi), an abundant agricultural waste in Iraq and the Middle East, as a precursor for MG adsorbents. The properties and regulation of MG are first described, followed by the composition of Sidr seeds and the methods used to prepare raw, chemically modified and carbon-based adsorbents from them. The reported adsorption capacities are then compared with those of other adsorbents used for MG, and the adsorption mechanisms, the role of pH and the energy and cost of the preparation steps are discussed. However, the number of studies is still limited, and most of them are based on single-dye batch experiments, linear model fitting and incomplete characterisation. Future studies should focus on nonlinear modelling, determination of the point of zero charge, tests in real effluents, regeneration studies and a comparison between simple and chemically intensive preparation methods.

title: Scretching–Planck Quantum Thermodynamics
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Scretching–Planck Ab Initio Theory of Statistical Thermodynamics: Partition Functions, Entropy, Heat Capacity, and Molecular Reaction Energetics This research presents a comprehensive application of the Scretching–Planck (SP) density–ph
content: The Scretching–Planck Ab Initio Theory of Statistical Thermodynamics: Partition Functions, Entropy, Heat Capacity, and Molecular Reaction Energetics This research presents a comprehensive application of the Scretching–Planck (SP) density–phase action to statistical thermodynamics, demonstrating how macroscopic thermodynamic properties can be calculated from microscopic atomic and molecular energy levels. Using independently developed computational code, the study constructs partition functions directly from ab initio SP energy spectra, connecting quantum-level electronic structure, molecular rotation, vibration, and nuclear-spin symmetry with measurable entropy, heat capacity, and reaction enthalpy. The investigation begins with atomic systems and extends to seven diatomic molecules and molecular ions: H₂, HD, D₂, HeH⁺, He₂⁺, LiH, and LiD. Their bound rovibrational energy levels are calculated on SP potential-energy curves and incorporated into molecular partition functions. This approach accounts for the contributions of electronic, rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom to temperature-dependent thermodynamic properties. The SP formulation is further applied to six polyatomic molecules: water (H₂O), ammonia (NH₃), methane (CH₄), hydrogen cyanide (HCN), acetylene (C₂H₂), and carbon dioxide (CO₂). Molecular equilibrium structures and harmonic vibrational frequencies are obtained using the proposed SP-2 computational approach and incorporated into statistical-mechanical calculations of entropy and heat capacity. A principal numerical benchmark is the thermodynamics of normal molecular hydrogen at 298.15 K. The study reports an SP molar entropy of: S° = 130.681 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, compared with a tabulated value of 130.680 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. The calculated constant-pressure molar heat capacity is: Cₚ = 28.834 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, compared with the reference value of 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. These reported results correspond to absolute differences of 0.001 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ in entropy and 0.002 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ in heat capacity, illustrating the precision targeted by the SP partition-function calculations. The investigation also examines deuterium (D₂) and atomic S-state systems, reporting agreement with tabulated thermodynamic quantities to the displayed precision. These comparisons provide additional tests of molecular isotope effects, quantum energy-level spacing, and the statistical populations of atomic and molecular states. An important component of the research concerns ortho–para nuclear-spin statistics in molecular hydrogen. The SP treatment incorporates the antisymmetry requirements associated with identical fermionic nuclei, determining the allowed rotational states and their statistical weights. Temperature-dependent ortho–para heat-capacity curves are then constructed from the corresponding SP rovibrational levels. title: Carbon Nanomaterials in Silicon Anodes of Lithium-Ion Batteries: Structural Design from Zero to Three Dimensions
summary: Silicon is the most promising anode candidate for next-generation lithium-ion batteries owing to its theoretical capacity of 4200 mAh/g, which is approximately ten times that of commercial graphite. Its practical application, however, is se
content: Silicon is the most promising anode candidate for next-generation lithium-ion batteries owing to its theoretical capacity of 4200 mAh/g, which is approximately ten times that of commercial graphite. Its practical application, however, is severely hindered by a large volume expansion of about 300% during lithiation, which causes particle pulverization, an unstable solid electrolyte interphase, and poor electronic conductivity. Carbon nanomaterials have proven to be the most effective components for addressing these challenges. Based on the structural dimensionality of the carbon component, this review classifies carbon nanomaterials in silicon anodes into five categories: zero-dimensional carbon coatings, one-dimensional carbon nanotubes and nanofibers, two-dimensional graphene-based sheets, three-dimensional porous carbon matrices, and hierarchical architectures that integrate components across these dimensions. For each category, the structural features, working mechanisms, representative performance, and remaining limitations are analyzed, and the failure mechanism–structural function–carbon architecture relationship is emphasized throughout. Zero-dimensional coatings provide interfacial protection, one- and two-dimensional carbons construct conductive networks, three-dimensional porous matrices reserve expansion space, and hierarchical structures integrate these functions synergistically. Current challenges and future directions, including initial Coulombic efficiency, cost, and scalable production, are also discussed.

title: Unconditional Energy Stable Hybrid IEQ-FEMs for the Cahn–Hilliard–Navier–Stokes Equations
source: International Journal of Numerical Analysis and Modeling
summary: We investigate two unconditionally energy stable invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) finite element methods (FEMs) [Chen et al. Numerical Algorithms, 99:1161-1202, 2025] for solving the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes (CHNS) equations. The ti
content: We investigate two unconditionally energy stable invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) finite element methods (FEMs) [Chen et al. Numerical Algorithms, 99:1161-1202, 2025] for solving the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes (CHNS) equations. The time discretization of these IEQ-FEMs is based on the first- and second-order backward differentiation methods. The auxiliary energy function introduced by the IEQ approach, modeling the square root of the nonlinear part of the energy, does not belong to the finite element space used for the spatial discretization. These methods offer distinct advantages. Consequently, we propose a new hybrid IEQ-FEM that combines the strengths of both schemes, offering computational efficiency and unconditional energy stability in the finite element space. We provide rigorous proofs of mass conservation and energy dissipation for the proposed IEQ-FEMs. Several numerical experiments are presented to validate the accuracy, efficiency, and solution properties of the proposed method.

title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
summary: Abstract Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by
content: Abstract Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

title: Controlling chemoselectivity of heterogeneous Pt catalysts via a support induced effect
