content: calculations indicate that the observed differences in selectivity could be because of support-dependent interactions at Pt-support interfacial sites, which modify the local electronic environment and adsorption behaviour of the substrate. These results suggest that the support-metal interfacial sites could potentially play a key role in controlling and switching chemoselectivity during 3-nitrostyrene hydrogenation. These results demonstrate that, in addition to modifying the metallic sites, the chemoselectivity of supported Pt nanoparticles can also be tuned by changing the support, offering an additional approach for designing new chemoselective supported metal catalysts for 3-nitrostyrene hydrogenation.

title: Estimation of individual-tree DBH and allometry-derived biomass of Korean red pine using mask-based multimodal deep learning from UAV imagery
summary: Accurate estimation of individual-tree biomass is important for forest inventory, carbon assessment, and fuel management. In this study, we proposed a mask-based multimodal deep learning framework for estimating diameter at breast height (D
content: Accurate estimation of individual-tree biomass is important for forest inventory, carbon assessment, and fuel management. In this study, we proposed a mask-based multimodal deep learning framework for estimating diameter at breast height (DBH) and allometry-derived tree biomass (TB) using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. Field measurements and UAV imagery were collected from two Korean red pine plots in South Korea. Crown metrics obtained from Mask R-CNN delineation were combined with crown-specific image features in a fully connected prediction head. Leave-one-plot-out evaluation was used to compare the framework with image-only and metric-only neural networks, least squares regression, random forest, and XGBoost. In the baseline comparison, the multimodal model showed the lowest test relative root mean square error (rRMSE) in both evaluation directions: 10.93% and 11.09% for DBH and 26.24% and 25.90% for allometry-derived TB. However, paired comparisons did not consistently support lower multimodal error against every model. Model performance also varied with image resizing and alternative masks. These results support combining crown metrics and image features for individual-tree estimation within the conditions examined. Further evaluation is required for other forest conditions.

title: Nanochannel-stabilized Donnan–water-state coupling enables stable solar evaporation of hypersaline brines
summary: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporators provide a promising pathway for sustainable desalination and resource recovery from hypersaline brines, yet their performance is often limited by inefficient interfacial energy utilization and s
content: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporators provide a promising pathway for sustainable desalination and resource recovery from hypersaline brines, yet their performance is often limited by inefficient interfacial energy utilization and salt crystallization fouling. Although interfacial water-state regulation and charged-interface-mediated salt management have been explored separately, their coupled physicochemical interactions remain insufficiently understood. Multiscale channels were fabricated by in situ Schiff-base polymerization of electrospun membranes to increase the fraction of intermediate water and immobilize sulfonate groups for Donnan-effect-mediated ion regulation. This coupled structure–charge design promotes vapor generation while alleviating interfacial salt accumulation at the evaporation surface. The resulting evaporator achieves stable evaporation rates exceeding 1.30 kg m −2 h −1 in 15 wt% brines over nine consecutive 12 h cycles under 1 sun irradiation, reaching 2.04 kg m −2 h −1 under reduced pressure. This work provides a mechanistic bridge between nanoconfinement, water-state regulation and Donnan-effect-mediated ion redistribution, providing a design principle for durable solar desalination and brine concentration under hypersaline conditions.

title: Short-circuit-resistant sulfide solid-state batteries through lithium dewetting
summary: In sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries, lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte indiscriminately through grain boundaries, interparticle voids and pores, causing internal short circuits that accelerate degradation and terminat
content: In sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries, lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte indiscriminately through grain boundaries, interparticle voids and pores, causing internal short circuits that accelerate degradation and terminate cell life. This penetration has been understood largely in mechanical terms, and mitigation has focused on suppressing cracks. Here we show that chemical wetting, governed by the lithium/electrolyte interfacial energy, is a decisive factor in lithium penetration. Even when crack pathways were mechanically suppressed, short circuits persisted, because the negative interfacial energy renders sulfide electrolytes lithium-wetting, drawing lithium into their pores. Incorporating a small amount of tungsten, which strongly repels lithium, induced lithium dewetting and suppressed infiltration. The resulting electrolyte sustained lithium plating and stripping for more than two years without short circuiting and enabled long-lived high-rate full cells and anode-less pouch cells under low stack pressure. These findings establish interfacial energy as a key design parameter for durable all-solid-state batteries.

title: A New Nakagami–Zero-Truncated Poisson Distribution: Properties, Estimation, and Applications
summary: This paper introduces the Nakagami zero-truncated Poisson (NZTP) distribution, a new three-parameter lifetime model obtained by compounding the Nakagami distribution with the zero-truncated Poisson distribution through the maximum operator.
content: This paper introduces the Nakagami zero-truncated Poisson (NZTP) distribution, a new three-parameter lifetime model obtained by compounding the Nakagami distribution with the zero-truncated Poisson distribution through the maximum operator. The construction is motivated by parallel-system reliability settings, where the system lifetime is determined by the maximum of a random number of component lifetimes. The probability density function, cumulative distribution function, survival function, and hazard rate function of the proposed distribution are derived in closed form. Fundamental statistical properties are established, including raw moments, the moment generating function, quantile function, Shannon entropy, Rényi entropy, and order statistics. Parameter estimation is carried out via maximum likelihood, and the score equations are derived explicitly. A Monte Carlo simulation study is conducted to assess the finite-sample performance of the estimators under three parameter configurations and four sample sizes. The bias and RMSE decrease as the sample size increases. The practical applicability of the proposed distribution is demonstrated through an application to carbon fibre strength data, where the NZTP model fits the data as well as the gamma zero-truncated Poisson (GZTP) model.

title: Executable Certification: Verification Code and Machine-Checked Proof as Accretive Layers in Orthogonal Review
summary: A previous paper in this journal established orthogonal review: a procedure in which review stages are assigned deliberately different validity questions rather than collapsed into a single judgment. This editorial announces an accretive ex
content: A previous paper in this journal established orthogonal review: a procedure in which review stages are assigned deliberately different validity questions rather than collapsed into a single judgment. This editorial announces an accretive extension of that procedure. Two artifacts are now published beside qualifying papers — a verification-code dossier, in which declared quantitative claims within scope are recomputed by a program that asserts rather than prints, and a formal-proof dossier, in which declared discrete content of the paper is machine-checked by the Lean 4 kernel. The methodological claim is that these layers supply a second kind of orthogonality. The three review disciplines of the earlier architecture are independent in the question they ask but identical in how they fail, namely by forming a wrong opinion; a verification harness and a proof kernel have no opinion to be wrong, and signal detected disagreement by a failed check. Their reliability remains conditional on correct encodings, adequate checks, and the trusted implementation. The two new layers are partial rather than total predicates on a manuscript, and their domains are fixed by status labels together with the declared checking scope; we state those domains precisely and show that neither contains the other. We report the defects the layers have found in two published papers and in one unpublished dossier — the last caught in pre-production by an independent checking system — and we grade those findings, since several are conservative and one was not. We also report one false positive generated by the review layer itself. For a journal that applies mathematical rigour to questions such as biogenesis, where the experimental loop is slow and in places not yet runnable, machine-checked internal consistency is the external constraint available before experiment, and its principal value is that it converts a falsification register into quantities an experiment can measure. The layers do not establish empirical chemical claims; numerical checks reach declared real-valued quantities, while the present Core Lean tier is limited to its stated discrete domain. They do not substitute for adversarial review; what they replace is testimony, by an artifact the reader can execute.

title: Open Well Data: a catalogue of public subsurface data sources with a verification status per record, standardized well-data collections and a channel dictionary
summary: Public subsurface data from wells (wireline logs, drilling records, production, core and seismic) is published by many regulators, geological surveys and research programmes, each with its own formats, units and licence terms. Open Well Dat
content: Public subsurface data from wells (wireline logs, drilling records, production, core and seismic) is published by many regulators, geological surveys and research programmes, each with its own formats, units and licence terms. Open Well Data (OWD) indexes these sources and standardizes selected collections. Its catalogue lists 507 public data sources in 79 countries and territories; each record states the access route, the licence as the source writes it, a verification status and the date of the last check. A dated attempt to re-read the landing pages of 503 records, between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-08, found 388 readable pages; of these, 238 (61 %) state no licence and 115 (30 %) do not state the access conditions. One hundred and sixteen standardized collections of versions 1.1.0 to 1.6.0, deposited progressively as versioned Zenodo records (48,901 files, 868,615,377 rows, from 32 data providers in 13 countries), use standard names and declared standard units, with the original names and units kept alongside; since version 1.4.0, every value of every collection is compared with an independent reader, with the exceptions listed in the catalogue (data/known-issues.tsv), and every file is rebuilt byte for byte before release. A channel dictionary of 8,045 mnemonics (6,602 seen in source files) maps 2,451 of them to 147 of its 185 standard variables; 1,853 of these mappings are checked against data values. A plausibility screen of the coverage tables flagged 7 unit inconsistencies in 6 source files. A benchmark with a fixed split by well gives reference baselines for compressional slowness prediction (test RMSE 12.2–29.3 µs/ft).

title: The ADAPT Map: circuit rewrites and over-conjugated states in ADAPT-VQE
summary: Variational quantum circuits are usually judged by the energy they reach. We ask by what route ADAPTVQE reaches the ground state, and follow both the optimized angles of all its circuits, tabulated as the ADAPT Map, and the bond orders of t
content: Variational quantum circuits are usually judged by the energy they reach. We ask by what route ADAPTVQE reaches the ground state, and follow both the optimized angles of all its circuits, tabulated as the ADAPT Map, and the bond orders of the state optimized at each depth. In three polyenes, an H6 chain, and benzene, re-optimization hardly changes the earlier angles up to a system-dependent depth. At that depth the change jumps by an order of magnitude and a generator already in the circuit is selected again with the opposite sign, while the convergence curve shows at most a change of pace. In a replay of this circuit, the first copy of the generator carries probability out of the Hartree–Fock determinant and the second carries it back. The partly applied circuit passes through states up to about 1 Eh above the Hartree–Fock energy, although the final state hardly changes. In the polyenes and the H6 chain, the operations between the copies act as spectator excitations (a single excitation plus the hop of a second electron), absent from the singles-and-doubles pool. In these four systems the double bonds are corrected early. The single bonds follow only after about 99% of the correlation energy has been recovered, once single excitations enter. In between, the states are over-conjugated, with a bond-order alternation smaller than the exact value. When chemical accuracy is first reached, it is still too small by a fifth to a quarter of its Hartree–Fock error. Benzene shows no such stage.

title: Unification Study of General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics Based on Spiral-Dimension Unified-Field Tensor Equation
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: As two cornerstones of modern physics, general relativity (GR) and quantum mechanics suffer from fundamental incompatibility of underlying axioms, fragmented mathematical frameworks, and the inability to derive each other, which constitutes
tags: Introduction to the mathematics of general relativity
content: As two cornerstones of modern physics, general relativity (GR) and quantum mechanics suffer from fundamental incompatibility of underlying axioms, fragmented mathematical frameworks, and the inability to derive each other, which constitutes a long-standing grand challenge in fundamental physics. Based on the original spiral-dimension unified-field tensor equation, this paper establishes a full-domain dynamical system containing radial spacetime-curvature degrees of freedom, material angular-phase torsion degrees of freedom, and tensor-trace scalar degrees of freedom. Through covariant-gradient lifting, the primitive second-order tensor dynamical equation is obtained. Angular torsion dynamics act as an inter-layer coupling channel; the spiral rotation from higher-dimensional layers injects energy into the local layer via torsion coupling and generates the scalar source term Jk . When the angular torsion is switched off by taking the limit ωk → 0 , the inter-layer coupling source Jk → 0 . Further freezing the tensor-trace degrees of freedom (scalar waves, scalar fields, and spacetime expansion-contraction modes), the unified-field equation degenerates into the Einstein field equation of general relativity and fully recovers macroscopic gravitational spacetime geometry dynamics. When radial-curvature degrees of freedom approach zero, the unified-field equation sequentially degenerates into the Klein-Gordon relativistic wave equation, the Helmholtz equation, and the non-relativistic Schrödinger equation. Meanwhile, the explicit expression of the Coulomb potential is derived from first principles based on the nuclear spiral torsion-field, which completely covers the microscopic quantum-mechanics and electromagnetic-interaction system. This study demonstrates that general relativity represents an approximate theory for a closed single-layer spacetime. To guarantee automatic energy-momentum conservation, GR discards the scalar dynamical degrees of freedom corresponding to tensor trace. Within the spiral layered-manifold framework, the local layer forms an open system, and torsion introduces cross-dimensional energy input, rendering the dynamics of scalar waves and spacetime expansion-contraction physically self-consistent. General relativity and quantum mechanics are not independent axiomatic physical systems; instead, they are approximate solutions of thespiral-dimension unified-field equation under different degree-of-freedom limits, achieving strict unification at both mathematical and physical-mechanism levels. Several long-standing theoretical puzzles within general-relativity framework, including the cosmological-constant vacuum-energy catastrophe, dark-matter problem, dark-energy origin, spacetime singularities, and the physical origin of early-universe inflation, can be explained endogenously by the present unified-field theory without introducing ad-hoc hypothetical fields or new particles. title: Effects of synthetic and natural hydro-retainers on germination, seedling growth, and biochemical responses of barley (Hordeum vulgare L.)
summary: Abstract Climate change has increased water demand while increasing water resources. To enhance water absorption and nutrient retention in soil, hydro-retainers are widely used in agriculture; however, most are synthetic, non-biodegradable
content: Abstract Climate change has increased water demand while increasing water resources. To enhance water absorption and nutrient retention in soil, hydro-retainers are widely used in agriculture; however, most are synthetic, non-biodegradable acrylate-based products. This research was conducted to evaluate the impact of a hydro-retentive synthetic potassium polyacrylate and natural cladode powder from Opuntia ficus-indica , on germination of three barley ( Hordeum vulgare ) varieties Kounouz, Artorio and Rihane. Using natural cladode powder, potassium polyacrylate, and their combination at different concentrations (0.2%, 0.5%, and 1%), to test the germination of Kounouz and Artorio in vitro over a 15-day treatment period and Rihane in vivo over a one-month treatment period. This work focuses on the physiological and biochemical behaviour of the barley varieties in response to the application of synthetic hydrogel and natural cladode powder and their combination. The measurements included germination rate, plant height, root length, total protein, chlorophyll content, oxidative stress markers, and hydrogen peroxide levels. The findings reveal varietal-specific responses to hydro-retentive treatments, with potassium polyacrylate significantly enhancing germination rates, especially at higher concentrations. Conversely, Opuntia ficus-indica cladode powder showed positive effects at lower concentrations but inhibited germination at higher doses. Improvements in chlorophyll content and antioxidant enzyme activities at specific concentrations suggest an optimization pathway for stress resilience in barley seedlings. Mixed hydrogel treatments, particularly at a 0.5% concentration, affected positively the evaluated parameters.

title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype–phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive
content: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype–phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype–phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar “frequency matching” results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the “replicated genotype–phenotype map” for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for mutational robustness. Last, our theory suggests a possible mathematical definition for evolvability with predictive power that can be tested in evolutionary simulations and, ultimately, in comparative genetics studies.

title: ImpCresst: a versatile simulation tool focusing on solid-state detectors at keV energies
summary: Abstract We present Imp Cresst , a Geant4 -based Monte Carlo tool to simulate backgrounds from natural and cosmogenic radionuclides, and calibration signals in solid-state detectors and their response to it. It is tuned for a fast-evolving
content: Abstract We present Imp Cresst , a Geant4 -based Monte Carlo tool to simulate backgrounds from natural and cosmogenic radionuclides, and calibration signals in solid-state detectors and their response to it. It is tuned for a fast-evolving and heterogeneous detector environment with a focus on physics at the keV range. This tool was originally developed and validated by the CRESST collaboration; however, its flexibility and configurability make it suitable for other experiments with similar requirements. Key features of Imp Cresst include the dynamic geometry implementation directly from CAD files, ROOT-based data persistency of the whole event topology and automatic metadata annotation for data provenance, and interfaces to various particle generators, particularly for radiogenic and cosmogenic radionuclides. It includes also a newly developed particle generator for radioactive bulk and surface contaminations which is completely independent of any user defined confinement volumes. The auxiliary tool CresstDS applies detector-specific energy and time resolution based on a user-provided data set of empirical parameterization. We discuss also how to manage an Imp Cresst based workflow in an HPC environment based on Apptainer and nextflow.

title: Enhanced Multiphase Circumgalactic Medium and Gas Cycling in Galaxy Mergers
summary: Abstract We investigate the impact of galaxy mergers on the circumgalactic medium (CGM) using the FIREbox cosmological hydrodynamic simulation. By comparing matched samples of merging and isolated galaxies with stellar masses M ⋆ ∼ 10 10 –1
content: Abstract We investigate the impact of galaxy mergers on the circumgalactic medium (CGM) using the FIREbox cosmological hydrodynamic simulation. By comparing matched samples of merging and isolated galaxies with stellar masses M ⋆ ∼ 10 10 –10 11 M ⊙ at z = 0 and merger mass ratios larger than 1: 10, we find that mergers significantly alter CGM properties. Merging systems exhibit enhanced radiative cooling, leading to shorter cooling times than free–fall times across large CGM volumes. This results in amplified multiphase structure and increased cool/cold gas content ( T ∼ 10 4 K) compared to isolated galaxies. Both inflow and outflow mass fluxes are elevated across a wide range, and the enhancement is mostly pronounced in cool (∼10 4 K) and hot (∼10 6 K) phases by at least ∼1 dex in mergers, with cool gas primarily generated in situ via radiative cooling rather than from pre-existing streams. Gas cycling analysis reveals that mergers fundamentally accelerate CGM processing, amplifying the effective transfer rate from cold/cool cosmic inflow to galaxy inflow by factors of ∼27 through rapid cycling of inflowing gas through intermediate CGM phases, efficiently fueling the interstellar medium and star formation. The enhanced cool gas content in mergers produces elevated column densities for low- and intermediate-temperature ion species in the inner CGM, while high-temperature species remain largely unaffected.

title: COP1 attenuates secondary thalamic neuroinflammation via degrading c/EBPβ after cortical infarction
summary: Neuroinflammation is a critical driver of secondary thalamic damage after cortical infarction. The E3 ubiquitin ligase constitutive photomorphogenic 1 (COP1) has been known as an important negative regulator of the transcription factor CCAA
content: Neuroinflammation is a critical driver of secondary thalamic damage after cortical infarction. The E3 ubiquitin ligase constitutive photomorphogenic 1 (COP1) has been known as an important negative regulator of the transcription factor CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein beta (c/EBPβ). However, the important role of COP1-c/EBPβ axis in secondary thalamic neuroinflammation after distal middle cerebral artery occlusion (dMCAO) remains unexplored. Herein, we investigated whether COP1 mitigates secondary thalamic neuroinflammation by ubiquitin-mediated degradation of c/EBPβ in microglia after dMCAO. Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent Sham or dMCAO surgery. Inflammatory factors, c/EBPβ, COP1 and microglial polarization were assessed by transcriptomics, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, western blotting, immunohistochemistry and single-cell RNA sequencing. short hairpin RNA and lentivirus were used to achieve c/EBPβ knockdown or overexpression and COP1 overexpression, respectively. K48-linked ubiquitination of c/EBPβ was examined. The neurological functions of rats were evaluated. We found that dMCAO triggered a pro-inflammatory milieu in the ipsilateral VPN, characterized by M1 microglial polarization and up-regulations of interleukin (IL)-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). What is worth noting that c/EBPβ was upregulated and shifted its expression from neurons to microglia, thus aggravating inflammation and neuronal loss in ipsilateral VPN after dMCAO. Nevertheless, with c/EBPβ knockdown the opposite results was observed. Crucially, COP1 expression was downregulated in ipsilateral VPN after dMCAO, while COP1 overexpression promoted K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of c/EBPβ, thereby reducing microglial activation and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and consequently conferring neuroprotection against secondary thalamic damage. Importantly, c/EBPβ re-expression reversed the protective effects of COP1 overexpression, manifested by increased IL-1β, TNF-α, and iNOS expressions, enhanced microglial activation, and aggravated neuronal damage and impaired neurological function. Our findings elucidate a previously unexplored mechanism by which COP1 alleviated secondary ipsilateral thalamic neuroinflammation after cortical infarction through ubiquitin-dependent degradation of c/EBPβ. Moreover, the restoration of c/EBPβ expression reversed the protection of COP1 overexpression. This study highlights the COP1-c/EBPβ axis as a promising therapeutic target for mitigating secondary thalamic damage after ischemic stroke.

title: Reexamination of collisional ionization cross sections including double photoionization processes
summary: Collisional ionization (CI) cross sections in dense plasmas remain difficult to constrain due to uncertainties in plasma conditions and the overlapping spectral signatures of competing atomic processes. The use of x-ray free electron lasers
content: Collisional ionization (CI) cross sections in dense plasmas remain difficult to constrain due to uncertainties in plasma conditions and the overlapping spectral signatures of competing atomic processes. The use of x-ray free electron lasers (XFELs) to both heat and probe solid-density targets has significantly advanced the field by eliminating assumptions about ion density. However, questions remain regarding collisional cross sections, suprathermal electron evolution and competing atomic processes. In this work, we revisit experimental data from XFEL-heated aluminum, previously analyzed using collisional radiative models that did not treat the degenerate electron distribution and atomic processes self consistently. We present a new analysis using BibBarT which dynamically evolves non-thermal electron populations and explicitly includes degeneracy effects. Furthermore, we incorporate an important atomic process recently observed in plasma state that mimic signatures of CI, shake-off. Our results show that including shake-off processes improves agreement with observed emission features, and lowering recombination rates further improves the agreement with data -- indicating a possible overestimate of three-body recombination in these conditions.

title: Non-Hermitian Dirac vortex: Minimal theory for topological-cavity surface-emitting laser
summary: We construct a non-Hermitian Dirac-vortex model that combines a complex-mass winding with an infinite-imaginary-potential boundary, extending the Jackiw-Rossi and neutrino-billiard models to the dissipative regime. Moreover, this model serv
content: We construct a non-Hermitian Dirac-vortex model that combines a complex-mass winding with an infinite-imaginary-potential boundary, extending the Jackiw-Rossi and neutrino-billiard models to the dissipative regime. Moreover, this model serves as a minimal theory for the recently proposed topological-cavity surfaceemitting laser (TCSEL): the imaginary mass encodes vertical radiation loss and the absorbing boundary defines the active region. We derive closed-form expressions for the modal frequencies, thresholds, and tunable vectorbeam polarizations, which are validated experimentally. Our work provides a rare example in which an analytical non-Hermitian topological theory captures the essential physics for engineering practical optoelectronic devices.

title: Isotope-based age scale with multi-month precision for the SE-Dome II ice core from Southeast Greenland over the past 150 years
summary: Precise age scales are essential for reconstructing past climate variability at high temporal resolution. Here, we present a new oxygen-isotope record for the SE-Dome II ice core from southeast Greenland and construct a multi-month-resoluti
content: Precise age scales are essential for reconstructing past climate variability at high temporal resolution. Here, we present a new oxygen-isotope record for the SE-Dome II ice core from southeast Greenland and construct a multi-month-resolution age scale spanning 1871–2020 CE. The chronology, named SE2025iso, was developed by aligning oxygen-isotope variations in the ice core with isotope-enabled climate-model simulations. High snow accumulation at the SE-Dome site preserved multi-month variations of oxygen isotopes, allowing age determination beyond seasonal extremes. Although absolute validation at the monthly scale is challenging, the chronology has an estimated mean uncertainty of 2.0 months and is supported by multiple consistency evaluations, including melt and tritium horizons, seasonal accumulation comparisons, and volcanic reference layers. The reconstructed snow accumulation rates correlate well with climate reanalysis data, except in summer. The reconstructed accumulation record shows that the weak seasonality at SE-Dome persisted throughout the past 150 years. This persistence suggests that the balance near the boundary between summer- and winter-dominated accumulation regimes across Greenland remained broadly stable despite recent Arctic warming. Applying the SE2025iso age scale to chemical records shows that hydrogen peroxide concentrations peak approximately 2–3 weeks after the summer solstice and that volcanic sulfate records exhibit reproducible post-eruption peaks at multi-month resolution. Overall, the SE2025iso chronology highlights the potential of high-accumulation ice-core sites for investigating multi-month-scale climate variability and aerosol deposition processes.

title: The instantaneous mass accretion rate of novae in quiescence: - an archival ultraviolet optical spectral analysis
summary: We present the first results of our archival spectral analysis to derive the quiescent instantaneous mass transfer rates M ̇ in novae, using synthetic disk spectra generated with TLUSTY, white dwarf (WD) masses estimates from the literature
content: We present the first results of our archival spectral analysis to derive the quiescent instantaneous mass transfer rates M ̇ in novae, using synthetic disk spectra generated with TLUSTY, white dwarf (WD) masses estimates from the literature, Gaia parallax-derived distances, and updated color excess values. Our results for nine novae, based on ultraviolet spectra and on a number of optical spectra, yield mass accretion rates that are higher than those derived from simple integration of the UV and optical luminosity. Twenty one years after its eruption, HR Del, with a mass transfer rate of 4 × 10 − 7 M ⊙ /yr, must have been burning the H-rich material as it accreted onto the WD. V842 Cen, which was previously thought to be a low mass transfer system, happened to be on the other extreme with M ̇ of the order of 10 − 7 M ⊙ /yr. For both novae, the enhanced mass transfer rate must have been self-sustained by a feedback loop. RR Pic, with M ̇ ≈ 3 × 10 − 8 M ⊙ /yr, was better fitted with an accretion disk in which the outer disk is heated up to a temperature of 12,000 K, in agreement with H and He emission lines coming from the outer disk and a large emission region on the leading side of the disk. Such a disk, augmented with a heated outer disk, also gives a good fit to the spectra of CP Lac, and DI Lac with M ̇ ∼ 4.5 and 9 × 10 − 9 M ⊙ /yr. V1974 Cyg and V533 Her, with an accretion rate of ∼ 3 × 10 − 9 M ⊙ /yr, have an even flatter spectrum. As to V446 Her and BK Lyn, they were caught in a state of low accretion and have the lowest mass accretion rates in our sample: M ̇ ∼ 10 − 9 and ∼ 10 − 10 M ⊙ /yr respectively. title: Pro/Ala/Ser (PAS) peptides as an alternative to polyethylene glycol (PEG) for the surface shielding of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) carrying therapeutic mRNA
summary: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), comprising a mixture of cationic lipids, neutral phospholipids, cholesterol and, in particular, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-conjugated lipids on their surface, have emerged as a powerful technology to enca
content: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), comprising a mixture of cationic lipids, neutral phospholipids, cholesterol and, in particular, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-conjugated lipids on their surface, have emerged as a powerful technology to encapsulate and deliver protein-encoding mRNAs as modern vaccines or for therapeutic intervention. However, the common use of PEG for surface shielding of mRNA-LNPs has raised concerns, especially in the light of a growing prevalence of anti-PEG antibodies in the healthy population. PASylation offers a biological alternative to the chemical PEG polymer, employing recombinant or synthetic (poly)peptides made of the small natural L-amino acids Pro, Ala and Ser which, in contrast to PEG, are biodegradable. PAS sequences are conformationally disordered, fully uncharged but strongly solvated and, thus, closely match the biophysical properties of PEG chains. Based on this notion, we synthesized a novel PASylated lipid, Pga-PAS 40 -ditetradecylamine (PAS-DTA), by replacing the PEG moiety in a clinically approved PEG-lipid (ALC-0159) with a 40mer PAS peptide N-terminally protected with pyroglutamate (Pga). mRNA-LNPs were formulated with this PASylated lipid, adopting a published procedure for conventional LNPs, and their properties were compared with those prepared using common PEG-lipids. To this end, we designed template DNAs for the in vitro transcription (IVT) of mRNA encoding a PASylated murine interferon alpha-11 (mIFNα11) which, when systemically applied, is effective against hepatitis B infection of transgenic mice. mRNA-LNPs formulated with PASylated or PEGylated lipids showed practically identical RNA-encapsulation efficiencies (~ 50%), hydrodynamic diameters (85–120 nm) as well as Zeta potentials (− 4 to − 13 mV). In addition, cultured HepG2 and HEK293E cells transfected with the PASylated mRNA-LNPs encoding either enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) or PAS 200 -mIFNα11 showed robust expression of both recombinant proteins. Furthermore, in a side-by-side experiment with HepG2 cells transfected with mRNA-LNPs that were prepared using PAS-DTA or two different PEG-lipids, comparable or slightly higher amounts of secreted PAS 200 -mIFNα11 were detected in the culture supernatant both by western blotting and ELISA. Taken together, our in vitro data indicate that PAS-lipids offer a viable alternative to PEG-lipids for the preparation of mRNA-LNPs, without immunochemical cross-reactivity but with potentially better tolerability for the transfected target cells.

title: X-Ray to Mid-infrared Spectral Energy Distributions: A Catalog of X-Ray-selected Active Galactic Nuclei in the XMM-COSMOS Survey
summary: Abstract We present a component-resolved analysis of the IR–X-ray connection in a sample of 104 spectroscopically confirmed Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs). By combining XMM-Newton, Swift/UVOT, and new high-angular-resolution JWST/NIRC
content: Abstract We present a component-resolved analysis of the IR–X-ray connection in a sample of 104 spectroscopically confirmed Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs). By combining XMM-Newton, Swift/UVOT, and new high-angular-resolution JWST/NIRCam imaging for a subset of the sources, we constructed detailed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) in which the IR emission was explicitly decomposed into accretion-disk, torus, and polar-dust components. This approach enables us to isolate the intrinsic AGN IR luminosities with minimal host-galaxy contamination, providing a clean assessment of the physical relationship between the accretion flow, circumnuclear dust, and the X-ray corona. By incorporating JWST/NIRCam observations into our SED decomposition, we significantly reduce host-galaxy contamination and isolate the nuclear infrared emission with greater fidelity, particularly at near-infrared (NIR) wavelengths. This improvement is most apparent at 1 μ m, where sources with JWST coverage exhibit a markedly steeper relation between ν L ν (2 keV) and the NIR luminosity than those without JWST data. This behavior is naturally explained by starlight dilution, whereby host-galaxy emission dominates lower-resolution measurements.

title: Modulating Growth Conditions and Microenvironment to Boost Antimicrobial Efficacy of Probiotics Against Pathogens
summary: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm-associated infections highlights the need for alternative strategies to control pathogenic microorganisms. Probiotics have emerged as promising candidates due to their abilit
content: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm-associated infections highlights the need for alternative strategies to control pathogenic microorganisms. Probiotics have emerged as promising candidates due to their ability to inhibit pathogen growth. However, their potential ways of application in human medicine remain insufficiently understood. Here we investigate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of selected probiotic strains, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Fibro 1 and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus Fibro 2, against clinically relevant pathogens, with the aim of generating insights to support the design of improved probiotic-based systems for wound infection treatment. Probiotics were investigated for their growth, lactic acid production, and biofilm formation in different media. A range of in vitro antimicrobial activity assays were employed, including growth inhibition and antibiofilm assays. In addition to free probiotics, probiotics incorporated into electrospun fiber mats via microchip electrospinning were investigated in in vitro biofilm models. Probiotics exhibit strain- and condition-dependent inhibitory effects, influencing both planktonic growth and biofilm development of pathogens, while metabolic analysis showed marked medium-dependent glucose utilization and lactate production. Probiotics incorporated into fiber mats retain measurable metabolic activity after encapsulation and preserve their antibiofilm activity. Overall, this study provides a deeper understanding of probiotic effects on pathogens and identifies key factors influencing antimicrobial efficacy. These findings support the rational design of enhanced probiotic-based formulations for applications in infection control and wound care.

title: Simulating catalytic resonance with molecular dynamics
summary: Static heterogeneous catalysts are constrained by the Sabatier principle, where their overall turnover is limited by balancing the kinetics of reactant binding, surface reaction, and product unbinding. Modulating the surface binding energie
content: Static heterogeneous catalysts are constrained by the Sabatier principle, where their overall turnover is limited by balancing the kinetics of reactant binding, surface reaction, and product unbinding. Modulating the surface binding energies between a strong binding state and a weak binding state can overcome this limit. For such a dynamic catalyst, a maximum turnover is achieved at a catalytic resonance modulating frequency. Here, we demonstrate that classical molecular simulation approaches can be used to study this phenomenon. Our method introduces a generic classical model for a surface reaction with time-dependent surface binding energy. Using a non-equilibrium molecular simulation in which reactants tend to be added to the system and products tend to be removed, we can simulate many catalyst cycles. Our approach reproduces catalytic resonance, with the dynamic catalyst providing up to a three-order-of-magnitude boost in turnover compared to the static catalyst. We further demonstrate the presence of a second resonant frequency in the gas phase, associated with resonance of the reacting bond. The general approach outlined here can be extended to more detailed models and used to study the molecular-scale effects of surface modulation and to computationally test input frequency, amplitude, and waveform for programmable catalysts.

title: Planets Surviving Common-envelope Evolution Should Be Rare, Massive, and Orbit Very Close to Their Host Star
summary: Abstract The discovery of exoplanets around white dwarfs uniquely informs our understanding of planetary survival through stellar evolution. Common-envelope (CE) evolution is one of the proposed mechanisms that could shape the orbital archi
content: Abstract The discovery of exoplanets around white dwarfs uniquely informs our understanding of planetary survival through stellar evolution. Common-envelope (CE) evolution is one of the proposed mechanisms that could shape the orbital architecture of these planets around stellar remnants. In this work, we predict the occurrence rate and orbital-separation/planet-mass distributions for planets that could form around white dwarfs through CE evolution. We simulate populations of giant-planet systems, sampling initial conditions from observed mass and semimajor-axis distributions for main-sequence stars. We evolve the host star from main sequence to white dwarf to assess which planetary configurations could survive, and we predict the resulting post-CE planet population. Our results suggest that such planets should be rare, massive, and have very close orbital separations. We find that most of the surviving planets have masses of >10 M Jup and orbital separations <1.4 times the tidal-disruption radius, a disrupt (≲0.006 au, also called the Roche limit), which is in contrast to high-eccentricity migration, which produces planets with orbital separations >2 a disrupt . The properties of CE survivors from our simulations contrast with the known closely orbiting planet WD 1856+534 b, suggesting a different mechanism may be responsible for its formation.

title: The ALMA-QUARKS Survey: A Keplerian Circumbinary Disk Candidate in the High-mass Star-forming Region IRAS 08303–4303
summary: Abstract We present the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Band 6 continuum and molecular line observations of IRAS 08303–4303, a high-mass star-forming region, with an angular resolution of ∼0 . ″ 3 (∼700 au at the distanc
content: Abstract We present the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Band 6 continuum and molecular line observations of IRAS 08303–4303, a high-mass star-forming region, with an angular resolution of ∼0 . ″ 3 (∼700 au at the distance of 2.35 kpc). Six dense condensations are identified in the 1.3 mm continuum, and at least four of them are associated with molecular outflows. The estimated outflow parameters, particularly mass outflow rates ≥10 −4 M ⊙ yr −1 , suggest that the driving sources are high-mass young stellar objects. Two of the condensations are forming a wide protobinary system with a separation of ∼900 au. They reside within a single rotating structure, identified as a circumbinary disk that has a mass of about 2 M ⊙ . This structure is traced by multiple molecular lines and exhibits a Keplerian rotation pattern. Based on the Keplerian rotation assumption, the enclosed mass is derived to be between 32 and 61 M ⊙ : 22–43 M ⊙ for the primary and 10–18 M ⊙ for the secondary. The circumbinary disk is, on the whole, gravitationally stable; yet, some parts with Toomre Q < 2 indicate potential fragmentation. Various molecular lines reveal a streamer-like structure connecting to the circumbinary disk, suggesting transfer of material from the envelope to the protobinary system through it. Despite the observational rarity of such circumbinary disks around high-mass YSOs, the high binary fraction among massive stars underscores their significance. This source, therefore, serves as a key laboratory for understanding the formation of high-mass binary systems.

title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
summary: Abstract We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodyna
content: Abstract We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive ($\gtrsim$0.3\Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect --- a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model --- the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN~1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than $-$3 in the outer layers of about 0.9\Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass ($<$0.01\Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

title: Oxidation effect on the microwave properties of TPU/BAC nanocomposites
summary: Films of composite materials based on thermoplastic polyurethane with oxidized birch activated carbon (TPU/BAC-HNO3) were obtained with a filler concentration of 30 wt.%. Also before introduction into TPU, activated carbon was oxidized with
content: Films of composite materials based on thermoplastic polyurethane with oxidized birch activated carbon (TPU/BAC-HNO3) were obtained with a filler concentration of 30 wt.%. Also before introduction into TPU, activated carbon was oxidized with a 5% and 20% nitric acid solution. The morphology of composites was studied by the optical and FTIR methods. The films’ average thickness varied from 0.50 to 0.73 mm. The microwave properties of investigated composite films were evaluated in the X-band (8-12 GHz). It was found that all composites retain high radio-transparency across the measured frequency range, with reflection coefficient S11 ranging from -18.4 to -13.8 dB and transmission coefficient S21 values between -0.86 and -0.41 dB. Power absorption of loaded films slightly increased to 5.8-14.3% compared to pure TPU (5.5-8.8%). Attenuation constant (α) remains low both for the pure TPU and for all loaded samples containing pure and oxidized carbon filler, not exceeding 0.28 mm−1.

title: Quantifying building-related climate impacts in Hamburg through a digital twin [résumé]
summary: Urban areas are central to achieving global climate goals, yet cities face a core dilemma: demolishing and rebuilding cre-ates high embodied carbon, while older buildings often perform poorly in operation. Urban Digital Twins (UDTs) can hel
content: Urban areas are central to achieving global climate goals, yet cities face a core dilemma: demolishing and rebuilding cre-ates high embodied carbon, while older buildings often perform poorly in operation. Urban Digital Twins (UDTs) can helpnavigate these trade-offs, but their use in municipal governance is limited. This presentation introduces the Energy Twin, anAgent-Based simulation developed with Hamburg city stakeholders to assess long-term Global Warming Potential (GWP) indistrict-scale demolition-versus-retrofit scenarios, specifically on non-residential buildings. The model integrates embodiedand operational emissions at the building level, enabling comparison of policy pathways towards the city's 2040s carbon-neutrality targets. Scenarios are calibrated against empirical German renovation and demolition rates for non-residentialbuildings, and were co-designed through an iterative, four-phase consultative process with Hamburg's Authority for Environ-ment, Climate, Energy and Agriculture, translating planning knowledge into model parameters and decision rules.A demonstration for the Hammerbrook district compares five intervention strategies over a 25-year horizon - All Refit, AllDemolition, Worst-first, Old-first, and Random - highlighting the carbon payback period required for new construction tocompensate its embodied emissions. Results show that continuous retrofit consistently yields the lowest cumulative GWP,as the embodied-carbon debt of demolition cannot be repaid by operational savings within the available timeframe, evenaccounting for the greater efficiency of new construction. The targeted renewal of the worst-performing building stocknarrows this gap but does not outperform the retrofit scenario. The results also show that rapid intervention - renovation ratesabove roughly 2% per year, prioritized on the worst-performing buildings - is essential for meeting near-term climate goals.The Energy Twin provides a problem-driven UDT that links energy modeling to planning needs. It was implemented on theGAMA Platform as an interactive and decision-maker friendly tool, allowing stakeholders to inspect buildings and triggerinterventions in simulation. The presentation also outlines the consultative methodology used to co-develop the model withmunicipal authorities, showing how collaborative, transdisciplinary processes can support more sustainable urban transfor-mation, and discusses current limitations and pathways for e hing agent-level decision logics.

title: Optimization of vermicompost and water management for greenhouse tomato in Northeast China based on the CRITIC-VIKOR model
summary: Abstract Greenhouse agriculture is the main way of supplying vegetables in winter, but year-round continuous cropping in greenhouses can cause soil deterioration and lead to a decline in the quality of vegetable yields, and these conditions
content: Abstract Greenhouse agriculture is the main way of supplying vegetables in winter, but year-round continuous cropping in greenhouses can cause soil deterioration and lead to a decline in the quality of vegetable yields, and these conditions are not conducive to the development of greenhouse agriculture. How to improve the environmental conditions in greenhouses to ensure high yield and good quality of crops grown inside, while also achieving sustainable development in facility agriculture, is an important issue that remains to be addressed. Thus, we used a common horticultural crop-tomato, as a study subject and used \(\:{ET}_{gage}\) evaporator dish for controlled irrigation accompanied by application of different amounts of vermicompost for experimental study. The experimental design was a two-factor randomized block design with three levels of vermicompost application: 150 t•ha − 1 (V 1 ), 300 t•ha − 1 (V 2 ), 450 t•ha − 1 (V 3 ), and three levels of irrigation: 0.6\(\:{ET}_{gage}\) (W 1 ), 0.8\(\:{ET}_{gage}\) (W 2 ), and 1.0\(\:{ET}_{gage}\) (W 3 ). The results of the experiment showed that the application of vermicompost could significantly reduce soil bulk density and enhance the water holding capacity of the field, as well as promote the growth of the plant and finally realize the improvement of yield, quality and water productivity. In terms of irrigation impacts, appropriate reductions in irrigation can improve yield, quality, and water productivity of tomatoes, but can reduce the photosynthetic capacity of tomato leaves.The results of CRITIC-VIKOR evaluation model showed that V 3 W 1 was the best treatment in terms of overall benefits for greenhouse tomato, with maximum values of soluble sugars (SS), total soluble solids (TSS), sugar-acid ratio (SAR) and WP, as well as better yields and organic acids (OA) under this treatment. Compared to V 3 W 3 , the greenhouse management method using V 3 W 1 can save 40% of the irrigation amount, with a yield reduction of less than 12%, but the quality is greatly improved, and the economic benefit can also be increased by 0.8–1.4 RMB per kilogram. In addition, comparisons between models indicate that the CRITIC-VIKOR model exhibits better stability and universality compared to EWTOPSIS (Entropy Weight Method and TOPSIS). This study demonstrates that in the cold regions, using greenhouse cultivation of crops, applying 450 t•ha − 1 vermicompost and irrigating with 60% \(\:{ET}_{gage}\) of water can effectively improve the quality of continuous cropping soil and achieve sustainable development in facility agriculture.

title: Impacts of innovation policy on firm green technology innovation based on evidence from a natural experiment in China
summary: Abstract Can a national innovation-platform policy raise the quality of firms’ green innovation, and if so, through adding resources or by reallocating existing ones? We study China’s Demonstration Bases for Entrepreneurship and Innovation
content: Abstract Can a national innovation-platform policy raise the quality of firms’ green innovation, and if so, through adding resources or by reallocating existing ones? We study China’s Demonstration Bases for Entrepreneurship and Innovation (DBEI), a multi-actor platform policy rolled out in three staggered batches in 2016, 2017, and 2020. Using 41,600 firm-year observations from 4613 Chinese listed firms over 2010–2023, we estimate a staggered difference-in-differences design and corroborate the estimates with heterogeneity-robust estimators (Sun–Abraham and Callaway–Sant’Anna) and a randomization inference permutation test. We find that DBEI designation raises green invention patent grants by about 4.6%, and patent applications by about 3.6%; the effect emerges only from the fourth year after designation and accumulates thereafter, and it is larger for granted and forward-cited patents than for applications—indicating an improvement in innovation quality and direction rather than a mere increase in patent quantity. A distinctive pattern in the channels—digital transformation is significant, whereas human-capital structure and R&D investment are not—supports a reallocation mechanism: the platform lowers coordination and information costs and reorganizes existing factors rather than inducing additional factor inputs. Enterprise-affiliated bases are markedly more effective than university-affiliated and regional bases (an effect roughly eight times larger), which we interpret as evidence that ecosystem performance depends on a firm-centered orchestration mode rather than on the mere presence of complementary actors. The findings contribute to innovation ecosystem and policy-mix theory by distinguishing a reallocation from a resource-addition channel and by specifying the governance boundary conditions under which platform policy works, and they offer guidance for designing quality-oriented, enterprise-centered innovation policy.

title: Aggregation of porous organic cryptophane cages and xenon–aggregate interactions in aqueous media: implications for host–guest chemistry and hyperpolarized 129 Xe NMR biosensing
summary: Xe NMR biosensors (XBS). Despite the Cry structure being hydrophobic and aromatic, both of which promote aggregation, the XBS field has so far mostly considered monomeric (isolated) Xe@cage systems where two-site Xe exchange occurs only bet
content: Xe NMR biosensors (XBS). Despite the Cry structure being hydrophobic and aromatic, both of which promote aggregation, the XBS field has so far mostly considered monomeric (isolated) Xe@cage systems where two-site Xe exchange occurs only between the cage and the solvent environments. With this in mind, I have performed large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of water-soluble Cry cages and free Xe atoms in aqueous conditions to study Cry aggregation and Xe-aggregate interactions at the molecular level. The simulations predict aggregation that depends strongly on the number of hydrophilic groups on the cages, with cages having fewer such groups aggregating more. The aggregation trend is reproduced in three independent simulations per cage, with two different force fields, and at elevated salt concentration. Analysis of Xe interactions with the cages and their aggregates showed that Xe accumulates at the surface of the cages, increasingly so as the aggregate size grows. The analysis also revealed hitherto unreported solvent-exposed Xe binding sites in all three simulations of the most strongly aggregating cage, and in one of them a buried site with Xe residence times of more than a hundred nanoseconds. These findings suggest that aggregation of cryptophanes and other porous organic cages should be considered in their host-guest chemistry and applications. In particular, the validity of the commonly assumed two-site Xe exchange model in the XBS field should be carefully assessed in the presence of aggregation.

title: Structure, diffusion, and relaxation in a charge-neutral prothymosin α -histone H1 condensate
summary: Condensates formed by oppositely charged intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) provide model systems for understanding how transient electrostatic interactions govern structure and dynamics in biomolecular assemblies. Here, we develop a
content: Condensates formed by oppositely charged intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) provide model systems for understanding how transient electrostatic interactions govern structure and dynamics in biomolecular assemblies. Here, we develop a sequence-resolved coarse-grained framework for charge-complementary protein mixtures and apply it to a nearly charge-neutral system containing 50 prothymosin α (ProTα) and 40 histone H1 molecules. The single-bead-per-residue model combines a hydropathy-based description of disordered regions with a structure-based Gō-type native-contact potential of the folded domain of histone H1. Pressure-controlled equilibration over P = 2-12 bars is used to generate states of progressively increasing density, followed by NVT production simulations at the corresponding fixed volumes. Chain dimensions-the radius of gyration Rg, end-to-end distance RN, and their ratio R=⟨RN2⟩/⟨Rg2⟩-remain nearly unchanged across these states, whereas translational mobility and chain relaxation slow markedly with increasing density. Center-of-mass motion remains subdiffusive, with effective diffusion coefficients decreasing from ∼0.22 to 0.05-0.06 nm2/ns and substantial chain-to-chain dynamical heterogeneity. Chain relaxation is well described by a stretched exponential, C(t)=exp[-(t/τR)β], with β < 1. ProTα exhibits approximately Rouse-like mode scaling, whereas histone H1 deviates from Rouse behavior because of its composite globular-domain/disordered-tail architecture. Despite strong preferential ProTα-H1 association, individual intermolecular contacts remain short lived (τbind ≈ 0.4-0.7 ns) compared with global chain relaxation (τR ≈ 12-136 ns), establishing a fast-exchange regime in which local contacts continuously reorganize rather than form persistent cross-links. The framework provides a computationally tractable route for connecting sequence, molecular architecture, and collective dynamics in charge-complementary protein assemblies and can be extended, with appropriate reparameterization, to other IDP-rich systems.

title: Legal Aspects of Climate Adaptation and the Economics of Resilience
summary: Climate adaptation has moved from the margins of environmental policy to the centre of public law, economic gov ernance and human-rights protection. Mitigation determines the magnitude of future change; adaptation determines how institution
content: Climate adaptation has moved from the margins of environmental policy to the centre of public law, economic gov ernance and human-rights protection. Mitigation determines the magnitude of future change; adaptation determines how institutions, infrastructure, ecosystems and communities withstand change that can no longer be avoided. The legal challenge is distinctive because adaptation has no single metric equivalent to tonnes of greenhouse gases. Its effectiveness depends on place, timing, distribution, uncertainty and the avoidance of maladaptation. This study de velops an integrated account of international, European Union and comparative adaptation law through the analytical lens of resilience economics. It examines duties to assess risk, plan under uncertainty, climate-proof investment, pro tect life and health, manage water and coasts, preserve ecosystems, regulate insurance and finance, allocate loss and enable participation. It argues that a legally adequate adaptation regime requires binding processes and reviewable outcomes: recurrent risk assessment, quantified objectives, transparent priorities, minimum protection standards, eq uitable finance, robust data, independent monitoring and remedies. Economic appraisal remains essential, but it must recognise catastrophic risk, irreversibility, distribution and the limits of monetary substitution. Resilience is therefore not a licence to normalise harm. It is a legal obligation to reduce vulnerability while preserving rights, ecological integrity and the capacity of future generations to choose.

title: The Swedish carbon balance - A material flow account
summary: This report maps the fossil and biogenic carbon flows that entered and left the Swedish economy in 2023 and discusses the implications of the Swedish climate target and some EU regulations on future carbon flows. The carbon flows were mappe
content: This report maps the fossil and biogenic carbon flows that entered and left the Swedish economy in 2023 and discusses the implications of the Swedish climate target and some EU regulations on future carbon flows. The carbon flows were mapped according to Eurostat’s Economy Wide Material Flow Accounts (EW MFA) framework, focusing on anthropogenic carbon flows. The input flows in this framework consist of domestic extraction and import, while the output flows of export and domestic processed output, the latter of which is dominated by greenhouse gas emissions. Net additions to stock is the difference between output and input flows.Domestic extraction was dominated by biomass, amounting to about 24.2 Mton of biogenic carbon, roughly three quarters of which was forest biomass. Fossil carbon extraction amounted to about 1.1 Mton C and consisted mainly of limestone and peat. Sweden imported large quantities of fossil energy carriers (about 23.0 Mton C), primarily consisting of crude oil and petroleum fuels, while simultaneously exporting a considerable amount of petroleum products (10.7 Mton C). In addition, Sweden was a net importer of fossil based products such as organic chemicals and plastics. The biogenic carbon flows in trade was dominated by wood and wood-based products; the export (9.6 Mton C) mainly consisted of sawn wood, market pulp, and paper and paperboard, while the import (5.1 Mton C) consisted of industrial roundwood and wood fuels. In contrast, Sweden was a net importer of agricultural crops, food products, and biofuels, although the associated carbon flows were smaller than those in the forest sector. Domestic processed output consisted mainly of carbon dioxide emissions to air, which totalled 11.7 Mton of fossil C and 14.4 Mton of biogenic C. Net additions to stock, which describe the net accumulation of material in the economy, were estimated at about 7 Mton C in total, 3.8 Mton of which were biogenic C. This measure excludes the net accumulation of biogenic carbon related to land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF, which, for comparison, amounted to 11.5 Mton C when excluding harvested wood products.Achieving Sweden’s climate neutrality target by 2045, and complying with EU regulations on aviation and shipping, will require a substantial reduction in fossil carbon emissions and have implications on other carbon flows. This transition will reduce petroleum trade and affect biogenic carbon flows, partly within the economy through redirection of biomass towards production of renewable fuels, chemicals and materials, and partly through changes in the import and export of renewable fuels.
