title: Green Global Value Chains for Sustainable Development: Environmental Upgrading in a Fragmented Spatial Economy
summary: In a world facing environmental transformation, mobilising the capital, skills, and knowledge required for decarbonisation and wider sustainability remains a formidable challenge. We argue that Green Global Value Chains (GGVCs)-and the Gree
content: In a world facing environmental transformation, mobilising the capital, skills, and knowledge required for decarbonisation and wider sustainability remains a formidable challenge. We argue that Green Global Value Chains (GGVCs)-and the Green Foreign Direct Investment (GFDI) that helps to build and reconfigure them-are central to this shift and can support sustainable development across a fragmented spatial economy. We advance the concept of environmental upgrading, showing how participation in GGVCs can move firms, regions, and countries towards cleaner production and higher-value activities while reshaping natural capital. This work has three aims. First, it offers a unified conceptual perspective on how GVCs shape environmental and development outcomes, introducing the Green Smile Curve and a typology of green, brown, and ordinary value chains. Second, it provides new empirical evidence on the geography of GFDI. Third, it proposes a GGVCs-sensitive policy framework-centred on building, embedding, and reshaping value chains-to help governments leverage GGVCs. This title is also available as Open Access on Cambridge Core.

title: Delivered-cost competitiveness of green ammonia imports to Germany: An end-to-end techno-economic assessment of supply chains from Morocco, Chile, and Saudi Arabia
summary: Green ammonia is increasingly considered a low-carbon energy carrier for industrial demand centers. This study compares end-to-end supply chains from Casablanca (Morocco), Mejillones (Chile), and NEOM Oxagon (Saudi Arabia) to Brunsbüttel, G
content: Green ammonia is increasingly considered a low-carbon energy carrier for industrial demand centers. This study compares end-to-end supply chains from Casablanca (Morocco), Mejillones (Chile), and NEOM Oxagon (Saudi Arabia) to Brunsbüttel, Germany. The system boundary distinguishes renewable electricity, ammonia conversion (electrolysis, nitrogen separation, and Haber–Bosch synthesis), refrigerated storage, terminal handling, distance-based maritime freight, and route-specific charges. The assessment combines harmonized cost accounting, deterministic operating-condition stress tests, and screening-level probabilistic uncertainty analysis. Under the baseline assumptions, delivered costs are 1,178.93 USD/t NH₃ for Morocco, 1,242.13 USD/t NH₃ for Saudi Arabia/NEOM, and 1,341.63 USD/t NH₃ for Chile. The embedded desalination contributions are 1.60, 2.88, and 3.04 USD/t NH₃, respectively, and remain below 0.4% of the corresponding conversion benchmarks. A one-at-a-time ±20% sensitivity analysis identifies conversion cost as the dominant absolute cost driver, whereas freight differentiates route resilience. A 50,000-draw Monte Carlo screening analysis yields conditional P5–P95 delivered-cost intervals of 1,036.05–1,321.84 USD/t NH₃ for Morocco, 1,098.37–1,385.33 USD/t NH₃ for Saudi Arabia/NEOM, and 1,193.24–1,490.47 USD/t NH₃ for Chile. Conversion cost dominates the uncertainty ranking (Spearman ρ = 0.986–0.995). Under the adopted assumptions, the Casablanca route has the lowest delivered cost and the least exposure to maritime logistics among the three assessed routes. These findings remain conditional on the selected cost benchmarks and uncertainty bounds.

title: Can Small Modular Reactors Enable State-Specific Energy Portfolios for US AI Ambitions through 2035?
summary: Abstract The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure in the US is emerging as a major new source of electricity demand, raising concerns about fossil lock-in during accelerated grid expansion. Here, we assess the role of small modular reactors
content: Abstract The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure in the US is emerging as a major new source of electricity demand, raising concerns about fossil lock-in during accelerated grid expansion. Here, we assess the role of small modular reactors (SMRs) within portfolios that also include on-site solar and wind power, grid electricity, battery storage, and direct air capture. Using a state-resolved scenario analysis for 2028–2035, we compare nuclear-inclusive and non-nuclear portfolios across alternative AI load trajectories, SSP-RCP electricity mixes, and decarbonization constraints. Relative to a grid-only counterfactual, nuclear-inclusive portfolios that achieve carbon neutrality by 2035 require 2.4–47.2 GW of SMR capacity, avoid 0.3–1.3 GtCO2, reduce water consumption by an amount equivalent to the annual use of 28.3–50.5 million people, and deliver \$105.8–194.8 billion in cumulative energy-system cost savings across climate and efficiency pathways. The results show that SMRs can materially expand cost-effective decarbonization options for AI infrastructure, while their contribution depends on timely deployment, permitting, and coordination with state-level electricity planning.

title: How multidimensional urban spatial agglomeration shapes carbon balance in seven Chinese megacities: Nonlinear relationships and geographic variations
summary: Abstract Compact urban development has been widely considered a potential pathway for carbon mitigation, yet how different forms of urban spatial agglomeration influence urban carbon balance remains insufficiently understood. This study inv
content: Abstract Compact urban development has been widely considered a potential pathway for carbon mitigation, yet how different forms of urban spatial agglomeration influence urban carbon balance remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the effects of multidimensional spatial agglomeration on net carbon emissions (NCE) in seven Chinese megacities by integrating multi-source geospatial data, ensemble learning, and interpretable spatial analysis. A spatially explicit carbon balance framework was developed by combining anthropogenic carbon emissions with terrestrial ecosystem carbon sequestration. Urban spatial agglomeration was quantified from three dimensions, including physical morphology, functional organization, and socioeconomic concentration, and their nonlinear relationships with urban carbon balance were further examined. The results reveal a clear spatial decoupling between carbon sources and sinks, with carbon emissions concentrated in urban cores and carbon sequestration mainly supported by peripheral ecological spaces. The effects of spatial agglomeration on carbon balance were nonlinear, with carbon impacts increasing during early stages of urban concentration but gradually weakening as improvements in resource efficiency and infrastructure sharing emerged. Among the agglomeration dimensions, socioeconomic and functional clustering showed the strongest associations with NCE, whereas the carbon implications of urban morphology varied across geographic settings. Climate and topographic conditions further shaped these relationships by influencing energy demand, ecosystem productivity, and patterns of urban expansion. These findings suggest that the carbon implications of urban agglomeration depend on how urban activities, spatial structures, and ecological spaces are organized, rather than on compact development alone.

title: Conservative versus liberal oxygen therapy after cardiac arrest: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
summary: Background Optimal oxygen therapy after cardiac arrest remains uncertain, with concerns that both excessive and insufficient oxygen exposure may adversely affect outcomes. We evaluated the effects of conservative vs. liberal oxygen therapy
content: Background Optimal oxygen therapy after cardiac arrest remains uncertain, with concerns that both excessive and insufficient oxygen exposure may adversely affect outcomes. We evaluated the effects of conservative vs. liberal oxygen therapy after cardiac arrest using the contemporary randomized evidence. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from January 2023 through July 15, 2026 (updating a previous meta-analysis), for randomized controlled trials comparing conservative/restrictive vs. liberal oxygen therapy after cardiac arrest. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses (REML with Hartung–Knapp adjustment) were performed to estimate risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs), with adjustment for clustering and a sensitivity analysis restricted to dedicated cardiac arrest trials (Tier 1). Results Twelve reports from 11 randomized trials were included; 4,102 participants (4,051 after adjustment for clustering) contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis. Conservative oxygen therapy did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality (RR: 0.96, 95% CI: 0.84–1.11; low certainty) or improve favorable neurological outcomes (RR: 1.01, 95% CI: 0.91–1.13), and the estimate for 180-day mortality (two trials) was very imprecise (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.10–7.91). Results were similar in the analysis restricted to the three dedicated cardiac arrest trials (mortality RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.81–1.36). ICU length of stay was shorter with conservative oxygen therapy (MD: −4.54 h, 95% CI: −8.56 to −0.53), whereas hypoxemic episodes tended to be more frequent (RR: 1.75, 95% CI: 0.93–3.30; very low certainty). The apparent benefit in smaller, less direct trials was not seen in the large dedicated trials and is hypothesis-generating only. Conclusion Conservative oxygen therapy after cardiac arrest did not improve mortality or neurological outcomes, and no clinically important difference in all-cause mortality was detected (low certainty). Hypoxemic episodes tended to be more frequent. Apparent benefit in smaller, less direct trials was not confirmed by the large dedicated trials and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating; the evidence is insufficient to define an optimal oxygen target. Systematic Trial Registration identifier CRD420261462056.

title: Public opinion surveys with large language models: methodological opportunities and validity risks
summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being considered as tools for computational social science, yet their implications for survey and public-opinion research remain insufficiently understood. This study examines whether a
content: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being considered as tools for computational social science, yet their implications for survey and public-opinion research remain insufficiently understood. This study examines whether and how they can serve as methodological instruments for estimating aggregate public opinion under out-of-sample conditions. Across three studies, commercial and open-source LLMs are evaluated against recent Pew Research Centre surveys. Study 1 shows that GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 can approximate national-level response distributions more accurately than uniform, normal-distribution, and historical-average baselines, with GPT-4 achieving mean absolute errors of approximately 4–8.5%. However, the models also exhibit important threats to validity, including underrepresentation of Republican viewpoints, underestimation of uncertainty, and, in some cases, overly homogeneous response distributions. Study 2 extends the analysis to GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Llama 3.3, showing that aggregate predictive accuracy generalises across models but that partisan alignment and distributional fidelity are model- and topic-dependent. Study 3 demonstrates that collective-level estimation is more valid than aggregating persona-based individual simulations, which produce substantially higher error and stronger homogeneity bias. Ablation tests further indicate that predictions are relatively robust to role prompts and temperature settings but sensitive to survey-item context. These findings suggest that LLMs may be useful as exploratory and supplementary tools in public-opinion research. However, the responsible use of LLMs requires explicit validation against human data, attention to bias and uncertainty, and careful integration with established principles of survey design.

title: The Regenerative Nexus: Green Transition in Architectural Education (The “Incept” Model)
summary: The INCEPT project introduces a critical pedagogical shift to align European Architectural Education with urgent Climate-Neutrality goals, specifically addressing the vast challenge posed by the existing built environment.Recognizing that r
content: The INCEPT project introduces a critical pedagogical shift to align European Architectural Education with urgent Climate-Neutrality goals, specifically addressing the vast challenge posed by the existing built environment.Recognizing that regenerative design must fundamentally oppose linear "design and demolish" practices, INCEPT developed three interconnected intellectual outputs to cultivate a high-conscious and action-oriented professional generation.Firstly, the project produced a comprehensive Compendium on the Green Transition which systematized theoretical knowledge in key areas: circular economy principles, low-tech sustainable design, and life-cycle assessment (LCA).This resource provides a foundational knowledge base essential for transitioning architecture away from high-carbon materials and operational inefficiency.Secondly, the creation of an Online Training Course extended this essential knowledge-from zero-emission strategies and bioclimatic design to digital lifecycle management (BIM/Digital Twin)-to a wider professional and academic community, ensuring broad dissemination of current best practices across the European building stock.Thirdly, the innovative Climate-Neutral Building Design Atelier functioned as a "Living Lab" across Zagreb, Bucharest, and Sofia.This interdisciplinary studio centered its methodology on the adaptive reuse of complex urban sites, including heritage buildings and brownfield voids.By applying the learned principles to real-world interventions, students successfully integrated regenerative systems, low-carbon materials, and circular design details, validating an educational model focused on heritage respect and systemic environmental thinking.The collective results demonstrate the efficacy of making adaptive reuse the central, necessary skill for architects committed to a truly regenerative and circular future.

title: Craft Entrepreneurship at the Intersection of Management, Digitalization and Sustainability: A Bibliometric Mapping of Research Trends (1991-2025)
summary: Abstract The study aims to map the development and thematic structure of craft entrepreneurship research and to identify research directions relevant to the management and transformation of craft-based enterprises. The bibliometric analysis
content: Abstract The study aims to map the development and thematic structure of craft entrepreneurship research and to identify research directions relevant to the management and transformation of craft-based enterprises. The bibliometric analysis covers 460 publications indexed in the Scopus database in 1991-2025. Publication and citation performance and author-keyword co-occurrence have been analyzed using VOSviewer. The results show a marked increase in research activity, particularly after 2020, and reveal seven thematic clusters covering craft entrepreneurship and identity; social entrepreneurship, cultural heritage and local development; innovation and sustainability; digital entrepreneurship; creative economy; niche-market specialization; and management and organizational resources. Overlay analysis indicates that entrepreneurial skills, strategic management, family business, emerging economies, handicraft and artisan entrepreneurship represent some of the most recent research topics, while entrepreneurship, innovation, craft and social entrepreneurship retain central positions in the knowledge structure. The findings demonstrate that craft entrepreneurship is evolving from a niche research topic into an interdisciplinary field increasingly connected with digitalization, sustainability and the management of small craft-based enterprises. The study provides a structured knowledge map and identifies research directions relevant to management studies and the socio-economic dimensions of production engineering.

title: Spatiotemporal CNN LSTM Based Multi Class Stability Assessment of Renewable Integrated Power Systems Using PMU Measurements
summary: Abstract The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources and the resulting variability in power-system operating conditions have created significant challenges for reliable real-time stability monitoring and corrective control. Con
content: Abstract The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources and the resulting variability in power-system operating conditions have created significant challenges for reliable real-time stability monitoring and corrective control. Conventional stability assessment methods often require extensive computation and may not satisfy the low-latency requirements of Wide Area Monitoring Systems (WAMS). To address these challenges, this paper proposes a spatiotemporal deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for multi-class stability assessment using synchronized Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data streams. The CNN layers learn spatial correlations among measurements from different buses, while the LSTM layers capture the temporal evolution of disturbance dynamics. The proposed framework simultaneously classifies four stability conditions: Stable, Transient Instability, Voltage Instability, and Frequency Instability. The methodology is evaluated on the IEEE 9-bus, IEEE 39-bus, and IEEE 118-bus benchmark systems under diverse disturbances, including three-phase faults, generator disconnections, line contingencies, and sudden load changes. A total of 5,150 operating and disturbance cases are considered. The proposed CNN-LSTM model achieves an overall classification accuracy of 97.4%, with an average model inference latency of 17.3 ms for each 500 ms PMU observation window, outperforming standalone SVM, ANN, CNN, and LSTM models. Because the classifier requires a complete observation window, a stability decision becomes available 519.2 ms after disturbance onset, and the corrective action is applied at 0.649 s for STATCOM, 0.769 s for SVC, and 1.019 s for battery dispatch, excluding communication delay. All closed-loop results reported in this paper use these actuation instants. For transient instability on the IEEE 39-bus system, STATCOM support limits the critical generator to a peak rotor angle of 75.0 degrees, against loss of synchronism at 1.33 s without control, and synchronism is retained for communication delays up to approximately 334 ms. For voltage instability on the IEEE 118-bus system, SVC support limits the weak-bus voltage to 0.894 p.u. and the excursion below the 0.90 p.u. ANSI limit to 0.18 s, against collapse to 0.621 p.u. without control. For frequency instability following a 650 MW generator trip, the decision delay places the battery dispatch after the rate-of-change-of-frequency peak, so the maximum ROCOF is unchanged at 1.48 Hz/s and the nadir improves only from 48.79 Hz to 48.89 Hz; the measurable benefit is a shorter recovery, 4.3 s against 7.5 s to return above 49.8 Hz. The results therefore establish a mechanism-dependent latency limit: measurement-window-based deep-learning control is effective for rotor-angle and voltage mechanisms, which evolve over the first one to two seconds, and cannot act on the inertial phase of a frequency event. title: Long-Term Assessment of Electricity Recovery Relative to Wastewater COD Energy Potential in an Anaerobic Digestion and CHP System
summary: Abstract This paper assesses electricity recovery from biogas relative to the theoretical chemical energy potential of wastewater COD using long-term operational data from a municipal wastewater treatment plant collected between 2013 and 20
content: Abstract This paper assesses electricity recovery from biogas relative to the theoretical chemical energy potential of wastewater COD using long-term operational data from a municipal wastewater treatment plant collected between 2013 and 2024. The analysis covered biogas production and utilization pathways, electricity generation, HHV-based CHP electrical efficiency, operational availability and load, and the theoretical COD energy potential calculated using an energy equivalent of 3.9 kWh/kg COD. Biogas volumes were converted to normal conditions, and chemical energy was determined from methane content and the estimated higher heating value. Electricity recovery relative to the theoretical COD energy potential was decomposed into three components: the ratio of biogas chemical energy to COD energy potential, the share of biogas energy directed to CHP, and HHV-based CHP electrical efficiency. HHV-based CHP electrical efficiency remained relatively stable at 26.2-31.2%, whereas greater variability occurred at earlier stages of the conversion chain. Electricity recovery relative to COD energy potential ranged from 4.51% to 13.07%. In 2020, when the lowest recovery was recorded, approximately 44% of biogas chemical energy was directed to CHP and about 42% was flared. In contrast, in 2017 the lowest HHV-based CHP electrical efficiency coincided with a high share of biogas directed to cogeneration and substantially higher electricity recovery. The results show that reduced electricity recovery may arise at different stages of the COD-biogas-CHP-electricity chain and cannot be assessed solely from biogas production or HHV-based CHP electrical efficiency. The proposed decomposition may support operational management and modernization planning. Because continuous annual heat-use measurements were unavailable, the analysis concerns electricity recovery and does not represent total energy recovery from wastewater.

title: Analytical calculation method for symmetrical short-circuit current of grid-forming converter considering virtual internal potential and angular frequency transient process
summary: Grid-forming converters have become increasingly important in renewable-dominated power systems because of their capability to establish voltage and frequency references independently of the grid. Among various grid-forming approaches, virt
content: Grid-forming converters have become increasingly important in renewable-dominated power systems because of their capability to establish voltage and frequency references independently of the grid. Among various grid-forming approaches, virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control is widely utilized due to its ability to emulate the electromechanical behavior of synchronous machines. Nevertheless, severe current surges may arise when grid faults occur, posing considerable challenges to converter protection and operational reliability. To maintain current within permissible limits, virtual-impedance-based current-limiting schemes are frequently integrated into VSG-controlled converters. Although numerous studies have investigated current-limiting strategies and control enhancements, relatively little attention has been devoted to developing analytical models capable of accurately describing the fault-current evolution. In particular, the dynamic variations of the internal voltage source and frequency deviation are commonly simplified or neglected, which can lead to noticeable discrepancies between analytical predictions and actual transient responses. To address this issue, this paper develops a closed-form analytical framework for evaluating the short-circuit current behavior of a grid-connected VSG equipped with virtual-impedance current limiting during symmetrical three-phase faults. An analytical description of the internal voltage dynamics is first derived from the converter equivalent circuit together with the reactive power-voltage regulation mechanism. Subsequently, the interaction between the internal voltage and fault current introduced by the virtual impedance is incorporated into the model, enabling derivation of an explicit fault-current expression that accounts for both voltage and frequency transients throughout the fault process. The proposed formulation is validated through detailed MATLAB/Simulink studies under different operating conditions. Comparison results demonstrate that the developed approach provides accurate prediction of the dominant fault-current trajectories over the investigated operating conditions and offers useful theoretical support for protection assessment and transient analysis of converter-dominated power systems.

title: Halal Integrity in Heavy Industry: A Conceptual Governance–Leadership–Sustainability Framework for Ethical Industrial Operations
source: Journal of Halal Science Industry and Business
summary: While Halal governance is well-established in food and pharmaceuticals, its application to heavy industry remains largely unexplored, presenting distinctive challenges related to supply chain transparency, material integrity, and technical
content: While Halal governance is well-established in food and pharmaceuticals, its application to heavy industry remains largely unexplored, presenting distinctive challenges related to supply chain transparency, material integrity, and technical Shariah-compliance. This gap is particularly significant for petrochemical operations where high-volume production must reconcile religious principles with global industrial standards. This conceptual study develops a novel integrative framework—the Governance–Leadership–Sustainability (GLS) Model—to operationalise Halal integrity in heavy industry contexts. Using the Hengyi Petrochemical Complex as an illustrative case, the research proposes a benchmark framework for ethical industrial governance within ASEAN. The research employs a conceptual methodology, synthesising insights from Brunei's national Halal standards, peer-reviewed literature on Islamic ethics and sustainable operations, and global petrochemical industry reports. The resulting framework merges governance structures, leadership dynamics, and sustainability principles through a Halal-Tayyiban lens, emphasising amanah (trust), tayyib (wholesomeness), and maslahah (public good). The analysis suggests that robust Halal integrity in heavy industry depends upon a dual foundation of rigorous legal compliance and proactive, values-driven leadership. Practices observed at Hengyi—including supplier audits, Shariah-based contractual provisions, and ethics-oriented workforce development—illustrate this convergence. Furthermore, embedding sustainability principles may enhance corporate legitimacy and market positioning, aligning industrial outputs with both Islamic values and universal sustainability targets. This paper's primary contribution is a first-of-its-kind hybrid framework that systematically extends Halal governance into the non-consumer heavy industry sector. It provides a pioneering blueprint for policymakers and corporate leaders, positioning Brunei as a normative architect of ethical industrialisation in ASEAN. As a conceptual study, findings are derived from secondary data. Future research should empirically validate the framework through qualitative case studies and quantitative surveys to assess its practical efficacy across diverse industrial contexts

title: The Hydrogen Economy and its Social Implications: Workforce Transformation and Access Inequality
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: Hydrogen economy is accompanied by socio-economic factors, workforce transformation and access inequality in the emerging economies. Thus, the study anticipates social implication of hydrogen production and workforce transformation through
content: Hydrogen economy is accompanied by socio-economic factors, workforce transformation and access inequality in the emerging economies. Thus, the study anticipates social implication of hydrogen production and workforce transformation through the analyses of needed skill, measures of implementation as well as the integration of social justice. The literature study addressed some challenges by looking at the comparative framework that put hydrogen workforce planning at the centre of knowledge, training and labour market governance. Findings revealed that there is a need to develop a dynamic model for the planning of the hydrogen workforce, creation of the hydrogen skill structure for defining the difference in skills between the hydrogen roles and those in other industrial sectors. Also, there is a need to implement training programs for new roles within the hydrogen sector and adjustment in the level of apprenticeship to be able support the transition of workforce while it is significant to upskill the trainers to improve the capacity of the training providers. The study provides a robust insight for government, policymakers and other stakeholders that are interested in the transformation of renewable energy.

title: Low Carbon Clay-Based Plaster for Earthen Building Conservation
summary: Earthen heritage represents a cultural and environmental resource of considerable significance, particularly in regional contexts such as Piedmont, Italy, where numerous vernacular buildings using traditional materials are still preserved.H
content: Earthen heritage represents a cultural and environmental resource of considerable significance, particularly in regional contexts such as Piedmont, Italy, where numerous vernacular buildings using traditional materials are still preserved.However, the fragility of these structures and the limited availability of technical knowledge constitute significant challenges for their active conservation and valorisation.At the same time, the need for decarbonization in the construction sector calls for a reconsideration of traditional materials and techniques in response to current environmental challenges.This study is part of a research project conducted by Politecnico di Torino that aims at investigating the potential of earthen plasters for both the conservation of built heritage and new building applications.Several plaster formulations were experimentally tested and some of them were enriched with corn cob due to its insulating properties and regional availability.The paper focuses on the environmental impacts of six plasters assessed through a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), considering modules A1-A3 (cradle-to-gate) from raw material extraction to the packaging of the final product.Direct data were combined with secondary data from Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) and literature.The results shows that plasters containing hydrated lime exhibit the highest Global Warming Potential (GWP), while clay-based formulations have significantly lower impacts.Plasters stabilized with gypsum present intermediate GWP values and demonstrate the best environmental performance when considering both sustainability and potential mechanical improvements.Corn cob inclusion increases GWP but may enhance thermal performance, offering potential benefits during the building use phase in terms of energy efficiency and comfort.These findings highlight that combining agriculture by-products such as corn cob and clay allows traditional construction techniques to be reinterpreted through a circular economy perspective, strengthening the link between innovation, local identity, and sustainability.

title: Effect of Heterogeneous Austenite and Multiscale B2 Precipitates on the Strength–Ductility Balance of Fe–Mn–Al–C–Ni Lightweight Steel
summary: A Fe–29Mn–9Al–1C–6Ni (wt%) lightweight steel is processed by hot rolling followed by solution and aging treatments to obtain a heterogeneous austenitic microstructure containing NiAl‐type B2 precipitates. Microstructural characterization re
content: A Fe–29Mn–9Al–1C–6Ni (wt%) lightweight steel is processed by hot rolling followed by solution and aging treatments to obtain a heterogeneous austenitic microstructure containing NiAl‐type B2 precipitates. Microstructural characterization reveals the coexistence of coarse nonrecrystallized (NRX) and fine recrystallized (RX) austenite, together with two categories of B2 precipitates according to their spatial location: grain‐boundary B2 (GB‐B2) precipitates and intragranular B2 (IG‐B2) precipitates. Their formation is associated with the local recrystallization state, stored deformation energy, and solute redistribution. After solution treatment at 950 °C and subsequent aging at 550 °C, the steel exhibits the most favorable strength–ductility balance, with a yield strength of 1259 MPa, a tensile strength of 1459 MPa, and a total elongation of 33.8%. The corresponding specific yield strength reaches 189 MPa·cm 3 ·g −1 . Strengthening analysis indicates that conventional strengthening mechanisms, including solid‐solution, grain‐boundary, dislocation, and B2 precipitation strengthening, provide an estimated yield strength of approximately 1025 MPa, while the remaining contribution of approximately 234 MPa is attributed to heterogeneous deformation‐induced (HDI) strengthening. The favorable strength–ductility balance is therefore associated with the combined effects of heterogeneous recrystallization, B2 precipitation, and HDI‐assisted strain hardening.

title: Urban Transformations and Heritage Formation. The Case of the Train Stations in Valle Del Cauca, Colombia
summary: The construction of the railroad system in Colombia and its subsequent consolidation throughout the 20th century is one of the symbols of the transformations the country experienced during the last century.This was characterized by the gene
content: The construction of the railroad system in Colombia and its subsequent consolidation throughout the 20th century is one of the symbols of the transformations the country experienced during the last century.This was characterized by the generation of new building typologies adapted to the physical and spatial needs of Colombian society.In the region of Valle del Cauca, in the southwest of the country, one of these new typologies was the train stations, which were distributed throughout the territory, reaching 47 stations, forming a system that functioned as an integrating element of an area historically and geographically isolated by the geological characteristics of the territory.In this way, the stations can be categorized into three groups according to the degree of contextual modification they represent; the first group as town originators, since some show the emergence of populations as a process of consolidation of the buildings used for the railway function and later urban growth given the commercial and industrial activity that arose in their contexts.A second group can be called town transforming stations, where existing settlements benefited from the need to implement a station for passengers and cargo nearby, which promoted the modification of urban layouts, affecting land use and subsequently leading to significant geometric changes.Finally, there is a third group, which includes large and medium-sized cities which allowed the arrival of the train with specific modifications, but which were not as significant as the previous ones.Likewise, in this group there is evidence of the appearance of some minor stations that did not generate urban modifications in their surroundings.These modifications can be studied on the basis of geometric changes in the urban layouts made after the station appeared, or even based on commercial activities, the hierarchy of the station in the towns and the emergence of new squares or parks within historical or consolidated urban realities.Despite the enormous relevance of the railway system, it has been progressively dismantled since the second half of the 20th century, closing passenger transportation since 1980 and being currently relegated to an intermittent cargo system.From this moment on, the evident obsolescence of the system has meant a clear deterioration of the stations, which present phenomena of abandonment, unproper occupation and destruction, thus generating poles of insecurity and deterioration.For this reason, the following research seeks to understand the phenomenon of train stations in Valle del Cauca as an integrated system that is implanted in strategic places of the territory connecting important historical, social and environmental values.Thus, being an integral part of a landscape that can be understood under the parameters of the concept of cultural landscape, and for that reason be the object of future conservation and restoration projects that face the social title: Regional green growth coalitions and the eco-social-growth trilemma: the case of the automotive industry in West Sweden
summary: This study analyses how and why a regional green growth coalition is constructed in West Sweden, and how this coalition shapes the organisation and prioritisation of economic, ecological and social objectives in the green transition. Drawin
content: This study analyses how and why a regional green growth coalition is constructed in West Sweden, and how this coalition shapes the organisation and prioritisation of economic, ecological and social objectives in the green transition. Drawing on the transition of the region’s automotive industry, the analysis shows that while Sweden’s national growth model has shifted away from green export-oriented growth, regional actors continue to align around this trajectory. The coalition is sustained by perceived state withdrawal, intermunicipal collaboration and a framing of the transition as essential for regional competitiveness and welfare provision. Within this regional growth model, economic competitiveness takes precedence, while social objectives are largely treated as outcomes of successful green growth. The article contributes to growth model research by showing how regional coalitions can sustain growth trajectories that diverge from national strategies, and how this shapes the incorporation and prioritisation of social objectives in green growth.

title: Lca-Based Approach to Drive the Development of a Low-Emission Prefabricated Wall: A Combined Experience Between University and Enterprises
summary: The decarbonisation of the European construction sector requires a systematic transition towards low-emission building products and components.In this context, the updated Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD) introduces the mand
content: The decarbonisation of the European construction sector requires a systematic transition towards low-emission building products and components.In this context, the updated Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD) introduces the mandatory assessment of Whole Life Carbon (WLC), thereby extending the regulatory focus beyond Operational Energy to include Embodied Carbon (EC) emissions associated with material production, construction processes, maintenance, and end-of-life stages.This paper contributes to the growing body of research on WLC implementation by presenting a combined academic-industrial study aimed at reducing EC in prefabricated components.The collaboration involves the Department of Architecture and Design at the Politecnico di Torino, the Sarotto Group, and Ricehouse s.r.l.The research compares two technical solutions for prefabricated walls applied to a Sarotto Group's case study: the Klimasismico system, based on concrete and synthetic insulation, and an innovative RiceCycling Wall (RCW) prototype composed of rice husks, natural cement and geopolymeric foam.A WLC analysis was carried out according to the Life Cycle Assessment standards and the EU Level(s) framework, using generic datasets from OneClickLCA©.System boundaries encompass all the primary stages of the building life cycle: Production (A1-A3), Transport (A4), Construction (A5), Maintenance (B2), Repair (B3), Replacement (B4), Energy Use (B6), and End-of-Life (C1-C4).Results highlight a reduction of approximately 11,500 kg CO₂e when substituting Klimasismico with the RCW, driven primarily by lower emissions in the Production and Replacement stages.However, the bio-based prototype increases Transportation and End-of-Life impacts due to its higher mass.In the near future, additional activities should be undertaken to enhance the final version of the RCW.The study demonstrates that integrating bio-based materials and short supply-chain solutions can support the decarbonisation targets set by EPBD IV.It also highlights the importance of WLC studies in research as a guiding tool for innovation in construction systems.

title: Experimental thermal performance of a low-cost solar water heater with a serpentine CPVC collector under high-andean climatic conditions: A case study
source: Energy Sources Part A Recovery Utilization and Environmental Effects
summary: The search for accessible and efficient solar water heating systems is critical in rural and high-Andean areas with limited access to conventional energy sources. This study experimentally evaluates the thermal performance of a low-cost sol
content: The search for accessible and efficient solar water heating systems is critical in rural and high-Andean areas with limited access to conventional energy sources. This study experimentally evaluates the thermal performance of a low-cost solar water heater incorporating a 1.2596 m2 serpentine CPVC collector under high-Andean climatic conditions in Peru. A prototype featuring a 1.2596 m2 horizontal serpentine CPVC collector was designed and monitored over 30 consecutive days using an Arduino system with four temperature sensors. Thermal efficiency was evaluated under three usage scenarios: daytime use, nighttime use, and no use. When water was used during the day, average efficiency reached 27.71%, with a maximum of 40.53%, and an average temperature drop of 1.62 °C due to cold water entering the tank. In nighttime use, average efficiency was 26.22%, peaking at 44.71%; however, the instantaneous thermal effect of nighttime withdrawal was not directly monitored. When the water was not used, efficiency remained more stable, averaging 28.70% with a maximum of 34.50%, with no statistically significant differences among usage patterns (p > 0.05). Maximum outlet temperatures reached 43.4 °C, even under variable solar radiation (1.69 to 6.32 kWh/m2). Daily solar energy was strongly correlated with collector (r = 0.879, p < 0.001) and outlet temperatures (r = 0.868, p < 0.001), while a significant but lower correlation was observed with storage-tank temperature (r = 0.683, p < 0.001). The results provide experimental evidence on the feasibility and operational limitations of low-cost CPVC solar water heating systems under high-altitude and highly variable solar conditions.

title: Determinants of carbon intensity in large emerging economies and Japan
summary: Carbon intensity is a key indicator of progress towards decarbonisation in fast-growing economies. This study examines the long-run and short-run determinants of carbon intensity in ten large emerging economies and Japan over 1990-2023 (374
content: Carbon intensity is a key indicator of progress towards decarbonisation in fast-growing economies. This study examines the long-run and short-run determinants of carbon intensity in ten large emerging economies and Japan over 1990-2023 (374 annual observations). The variables show strong cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneous slopes, so we estimate a cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL) model with the dynamic common correlated effects mean group (DCCE-MG) estimator. We then test how sensitive the results are to the specification, the sample and the estimator. A Kaya decomposition separates the behavioural effects of income from its mechanical link with carbon intensity. The results show that per capita energy use and the renewable share of final energy consumption are the most robust determinants of carbon intensity across all specifications. The near-unit negative income coefficient largely reflects the Kaya identity: per capita emissions still rise with income, so decoupling is relative rather than absolute, and there is no evidence of an inverted-U relationship. Trade openness has a small positive effect that is not robust to excluding Japan, and FDI, urbanisation and population growth are not significant. Carbon intensity adjusts quickly to its long-run equilibrium, although adjustment speeds and elasticities differ across countries. The findings suggest that decarbonising the energy system, rather than relying on income growth, is the main policy lever for reducing carbon intensity in these economies.

title: Greening coloniality: carbon economy projects beyond Europe
summary: This paper examines carbon economy (CE) projects in Latin America, the Middle East and Africa. While CE projects perpetuate historical modes of exploitation rooted in European colonialism, new actors and dynamics beyond established colonial
content: This paper examines carbon economy (CE) projects in Latin America, the Middle East and Africa. While CE projects perpetuate historical modes of exploitation rooted in European colonialism, new actors and dynamics beyond established colonial power centres are emerging. The paper explores how Brazilian investments in sugarcane ethanol and Arab Gulf investments in carbon offset deals in Africa reconfigure rather than overcome Eurocentric notions of coloniality. It contributes to understanding how European colonial legacies, racial capitalism and relational extractivism shape CE development, while foregrounding the role of non-European actors and the entangled nature of extractive logics in the global carbon economy.

title: Unravelling Goods and Services Tax in India: An Analytical Study
source: Global Journal of Management and Business Research
summary: This study examines the rationale, evolution, and implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India. It traces the transition from GST 1.0 to GST 3.0, analyzes the institutional machinery underpinning its operation, and compares I
content: This study examines the rationale, evolution, and implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India. It traces the transition from GST 1.0 to GST 3.0, analyzes the institutional machinery underpinning its operation, and compares India’s GST framework with global counterparts. The paper highlights reforms that have shaped GST’s trajectory, identifies impediments to effective implementation, and proposes a forward-looking framework to strengthen its role as a “Good and Simple Tax.” Purpose The paper addresses the limitations of India’s pre-GST indirect taxation system, particularly the complexities associated with the interstate movement of goods and services and the distribution of tax revenues. It demonstrates how GST has progressively resolved these challenges through successive iterations. By benchmarking India’s GST against international models, the paper advances a policy framework to enhance its impact and sustainability. Design The analysis is grounded in Dalton’s Theory of Public Finance and a historical overview of tax reforms in India. Following this conceptual foundation, the paper explores the evolution of GST from its inception to GST 3.0, the institutional mechanisms supporting its implementation, comparative insights from other jurisdictions, and the bottlenecks encountered in practice. It concludes with a proposed framework for ensuring the long-term effectiveness of GST. Findings The study reveals that GST has eliminated the cascading effect of taxes, simplified compliance processes, enhanced revenue buoyancy, and reinforced fiscal federalism. Originality This paper situates the origin of GST within the inadequacies of India’s earlier indirect taxation regime and demonstrates how these shortcomings have been addressed. It evaluates India’s GST in a comparative perspective, and contributes to the discourse by proposing a framework for the next phase of reform, GST 3.0.

title: Exciton binding regulation in oxygen-independent tumor photooxidation enables synchronous photoluminescence for cancer theranostics
summary: Overcoming the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in light-driven cancer therapy remains a significant challenge for theranostics. Herein, we report a fullerene-loaded heptazine‒perylene (HP/C60) nanopolymer that enables the oxygen-independent o
content: Overcoming the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in light-driven cancer therapy remains a significant challenge for theranostics. Herein, we report a fullerene-loaded heptazine‒perylene (HP/C60) nanopolymer that enables the oxygen-independent oxidation of intracellular biomolecules via photogenerated hole transfer (+1.53 V vs. NHE). Concurrently, HP/C60 facilitates cancer theranostics through spatiotemporal fluorescence imaging with resistance to photobleaching. By precisely tuning the exciton binding energy through controlled interface-induced charge delocalization, we optimize the ratio of exciton recombination and dissociation pathways, enabling the rational allocation of photoluminescence for high-contrast bioimaging and photooxidation for efficient tumor elimination. A 20-minute red light irradiation of HP/C60 is sufficient to initiate the complete ablation of solid tumors of female mice, with the entire therapeutic process monitored via real-time fluorescence imaging. This work establishes exciton management as a universal design principle to synchronize photooxidation and photoluminescence and supports the development of organic semiconductors for cancer theranostics. Overcoming the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in light-driven cancer therapy is challenging for developing theranostic systems. Here, the authors report a fullerene-loaded heptazine‒perylene nanopolymer that facilitates cancer theranostics through the oxygen-independent oxidation of intracellular biomolecules, and through spatiotemporal fluorescence imaging with resistance to photobleaching.

title: High Voltage Hydrogen Storage and Transmission Systems: Electrical Safety and Design Consideration
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: The notable fact that renewable energy sources (RES) are cumulatively receiving universal prominence and preferential patronage in contrast to their fossil fuel counterparts which are characterized with notable challenge of greenhouse gas p
content: The notable fact that renewable energy sources (RES) are cumulatively receiving universal prominence and preferential patronage in contrast to their fossil fuel counterparts which are characterized with notable challenge of greenhouse gas pollution remains infinitely indelible. Consequent upon the expensive price and fast diminishing reserve of the latter, articulate research on the former has not only been accorded global attention but also granted progressively growing acceptability, in-depth study and thorough investigation day by day. Nevertheless, some unpleasant mitigating factors which include instability, fluctuation of output, inconsistency in annual weather pattern, intermittency, inadequacy of predictability and lots more militarize vehemently against the output of a renewable energy source (RES). Thus, the urgent necessity of an excellent storage system to mitigate these challenges is obviously necessitated which earns green hydrogen its pride of place as a suitable means of storage. Therefore, it could be inferred that renewable energy sources will certainly perform better when coupled with hydrogen storage systems. However, designing a high voltage hydrogen system require both careful and skillful integration of electrical technology, materials science and safety engineering. The amalgamation of high voltage and hydrogen’s inflammability promotes unique and serious risks that must be combatted via robust design. Hence, the significance of this research work which presents an X-ray analysis on high voltage hydrogen storage systems: electrical safety and design considerations. The first part of the methodology involves an analytical consideration of integration of safety facilities besides advanced design scheme to minimize the risk index while the second part includes a meticulous investigation of the potential electrical hazards and control layouts coupled with the electrical advancements that are needed for the proper incorporation of these technologies as a crucial factor to ensure safety during storage of electrical energy in the form of green hydrogen. The result reveals that a high voltage hydrogen storage system must make adequate provision for prevention of sparks, arcs and heat while facilities must be incorporated for instant detection and quick response to hydrogen leaks besides monumental compliance to global safety standards.

title: Consumers: The Climate’s Biggest Advocates or Most Fearsome Foes?
summary: In 2019, the nonprofit organization Change Climate set out to reduce carbon emissions by steering consumers toward less carbon-intensive goods.Change Climate began by helping businesses alter their work processes so that they absorbed as mu
content: In 2019, the nonprofit organization Change Climate set out to reduce carbon emissions by steering consumers toward less carbon-intensive goods.Change Climate began by helping businesses alter their work processes so that they absorbed as much carbon as they emitted.Companies who achieved carbon neutrality could emblazon their products with the "climate neutral" label.By connecting businesses seeking to decarbonize with consumers eager to support them, Change Climate aimed to accelerate investment in renewable energy.By 2024, goods as varied as bass guitars to yoga mats bore the words "climate neutral." 1 Change Climate's turn to consumers to propel social change drew upon a strategy familiar to me as an American historian writing in the US context.In no place has "the consumer" been accorded more power as an agent of change than in the United States.Some historians credit the very creation of an American nation to the rise of consumer consciousness, noting that shared resistance to taxes on British imports fomented the rebellion against British rule. 2 Consumer solidarity accelerated other social movements.Quaker abolitionists opened " free stores" to market sugar or coffee sourced from supply chains free of the taint of slavery.3 In the post-Second World War era, the United States became, in historian Lizabeth Cohen's words, "a consumer republic" where citizens increasingly measured the nation's promise of democracy by how well it ensured access to consumer goods.4 Change Climate taps into a long-standing tradition by viewing consumers as critical decision-makers.Environmental advocates' perspective on consumption is more ambiguous.On one hand, commercial spaces, such as food cooperatives and cata logs, proved critical to helping environmental activists articulate and enact their environmental agendas.5 Many of the environmental movement's strongest champions in the 1970s were Americans worried that pollution and deforestation might undermine the suburban way of life in 17 Consumers: The Climate's Biggest Advocates or Most Fearsome Foes?

title: Tail risk spillover effects of the technology market on Chinese new energy vehicle firms: A perspective of time-varying technological cycles
summary: This study investigates the dynamic tail-risk connectedness and spillover effects from the global technology market to the Chinese New Energy Vehicle (NEV) industry. Amidst the global energy transition and heightened financial volatility, w
content: This study investigates the dynamic tail-risk connectedness and spillover effects from the global technology market to the Chinese New Energy Vehicle (NEV) industry. Amidst the global energy transition and heightened financial volatility, we employ a Conditional Autoregressive Value at Risk (CAViaR) model to quantify marginal tail risks, coupled with a Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregression (TVP-VAR) framework to construct dynamic risk spillover networks. Using daily data from January 2015 to March 2025, our analysis captures structural shifts in connectedness driven by critical technological cycles (e.g., the battery revolution and the emergence of disruptive AI models like DeepSeek) as well as exogenous shocks (e.g., the COVID-19 pandemic). Empirical findings reveal that tail-risk spillovers are highly asymmetric and time-varying. Notably, global technology markets serve as consistent net sources of tail-risk spillovers to the NEV sector, with network connectedness intensifying sharply during technological breakthroughs and macro-crises. Frequency-domain decomposition further demonstrates that while short-term spillovers dominate during tranquil periods, long-term tail-risk connectedness escalates significantly during crises. Additionally, leading NEV firms act as pivotal hubs in shaping intra-industry network dynamics. These findings elucidate the evolutionary patterns of tail-risk connectedness across distinct technological phases, providing actionable insights for dynamic portfolio allocation and risk management in the green economy.

title: Frozen Electric Double Layers Enable Redox‐Window‐Unlimited Ultrahigh Current Injection in Monolayer Light‐Emitting Devices
summary: ABSTRACT Electrolyte‐gated transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) light‐emitting devices can reach the highest carrier densities among current‐driven monolayer emitters, but their operation is fundamentally capped by the electrochemical sta
content: ABSTRACT Electrolyte‐gated transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) light‐emitting devices can reach the highest carrier densities among current‐driven monolayer emitters, but their operation is fundamentally capped by the electrochemical stability window of the electrolyte. Access to ultrahigh current injection is important not only for bright electroluminescence, but also for high‐density excitonic, polaritonic, and laser‐relevant regimes. Here we show that this voltage ceiling can be removed by freezing the electric double layers after junction formation. A lateral PN junction is first created in a monolayer WSe 2 device by high‐density electric ‐double‐layer doping and then frozen at 10 K under bias, immobilizing the ionic configuration while preserving the accumulated carriers. This enables redox‐window‐unlimited high‐bias operation up to 20 V and yields an ultrahigh current density of 0.8 MA cm −2 . The frozen‐electric‐double‐layer concept decouples ultrahigh carrier accumulation from electrochemical breakdown and provides a simple route to redox‐window‐unlimited ultrahigh‐injection operation in atomically thin light emitters.

title: Borders, Empire, and Climate Catastrophe
summary: Amid incessant aerial bombings, civilian deaths, and destruction, including slain media and medical personnel-at least a hundred thousand tons of US-supplied bombs-the United Nations Secretary-General declared that the "living hell in Gaza"
content: Amid incessant aerial bombings, civilian deaths, and destruction, including slain media and medical personnel-at least a hundred thousand tons of US-supplied bombs-the United Nations Secretary-General declared that the "living hell in Gaza" was now suffering from a human-made famine as well. 1 The Gaza strip is a narrow strip of land about twentyfive kilo meters long and six to twelve kilo meters wide and populated by about two million people. 2 The violent and vis i ble erasure is an amplification of the long-term eco-genocide through dispossession, destruction, uprooting, and burning of Palestinian olive trees, desiccation of agricultural lands and water rights, and denial of fishing rights.3 Weaponized humanitarian aid sits idly across a militarized border in this orchestrated famine.4 The "toxic legacy" of this bombing will "last generations and extend beyond its borders." 5 Like the bombs, Palestinians did not choose their bound aries, nor did many postcolonial nation-states.The technological ambitions haunting us today as well as planetary change connect border formations in Turtle Island to Palestine, Kashmir, and Aboriginal Australia.The world's dependency on oil and fossil fuels has occurred through material pro cesses of settler state formations and imperial expansionism reliant on racialized economic systems, many that formed during early colonial expansion and slavery.Plainly put, slavery and wealth from slaveholding as well as extreme natu ral resource extraction drove Britain's Industrial Revolution.6 Drawing upon Britain's model, American industrialization and development followed a similar script.7 At its height, in 1914, before the Great War, European powers colonized about 84 percent of the world.8 Some of the few parts of the world uncontrolled by European powers were the non-European parts of the Ottoman Empire, including historic Palestine.At the end of the Great War, built on the twin imperatives of resource extraction and political expediency, Palestine's bound aries embodied 18 Borders, Empire, and Climate Catastrophe

title: Decarbonising the Built Environment: Retrofit Strategies and Whole Life Carbon Assessment in Early 20th-Century Multi-Family Houses
summary: Considering the climate urgency and the European Union's (EU) decarbonisation goals, the construction sector is one of the main contributors to greenhouse gas emissions.According to the European Commission, buildings account for approximate
content: Considering the climate urgency and the European Union's (EU) decarbonisation goals, the construction sector is one of the main contributors to greenhouse gas emissions.According to the European Commission, buildings account for approximately 40 per cent of the EU's final energy consumption and over a third of its energy-related greenhouse gas emissions.Such impact affects the lifecycle of buildings, from material production and construction to use, maintenance, and decommissioning.The International Energy Agency's forecasts estimate that over 85 per cent of existing buildings will still be in use by 2050, while the annual renewal rate of the European building stock is only about 1 per cent.In this scenario, renovating the existing buildings is key to achieving climate neutrality and avoiding new CO2eq emissions.The main purpose of the study, carried out by the Department of Architecture and Design (DAD) and Department of Energy (DENERG) at Politecnico di Torino, was to develop a simplified Whole Life Carbon (WLC) assessment over 19 case studies of multi-family houses built in Turin (Climate zone E) between the 1940s and 1970s.The study was divided into an analysis of climate parameters, building orientation, energy requirements, and building typologies.Then, some energy efficiency solutions were developed, including renovations of the building envelope, the addition of solar shading, and replacement services (primarily mechanical and electrical).The WLC assessment considered both Embodied Carbon (EC) and Operational Carbon (OC) emissions over a 50-year period.Consistent with UNI EN 15978 and RICS guidelines, the adopted methodology is based on the framework proposed within the #BuildingLife project led by Green Building Council Italia.A comparative analysis of advanced retrofit strategies demonstrates the potential of innovative, low-carbon renovations to support the decarbonisation of the building stock.Introduction.Unlike many European cities, which are characterised by relatively recent buildings, Italian cities have developed in layers, giving rise to a highly heterogeneous and recognisable architectural landscape (BPIE, 2011).It is home to compact historic districts, 19th-century neighbourhoods, and a vast post-World War II residential heritage, the latter often energy inefficient (ENEA, 2023) but now fully integrated into the urban identity.Today, it represents one of the most significant challenges for Italy's ecological transition.The redevelopment of these buildings is therefore not a simple technical intervention, but an action with profound repercussions on urban quality, the future of the built environment, and the ability to achieve national and European energy targets (Ruggieri et al., 2023).

title: MOF‐Based Photothermal Catalysts for Solar Energy Conversion: Design Principles, Mechanistic Insights, and Applications in CO 2 Conversion and Hydrogen Production
summary: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalysis, which couples solar energy harvesting and thermal‐driven surface reactions, has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable energy conversion. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs), with their structural tunab
content: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalysis, which couples solar energy harvesting and thermal‐driven surface reactions, has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable energy conversion. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs), with their structural tunability, high porosity, and capability of incorporating active metal sites, have become versatile platforms for constructing photothermal catalysts. This review mainly summarized the recent research progress in MOF‐based photothermal systems, focusing on their structural advantages, design strategies, and mechanistic features in energy‐related reactions. Key design approaches, including ligand engineering, metal‐node engineering, pore‐space and confinement modulation, interfacial hybridization, and MOF‐derived structural reconstruction, are discussed in terms of their roles in enhancing light harvesting, photothermal conversion, charge transfer, and catalytic bond activation. Representative applications in CO 2 hydrogenation and aqueous‐phase methanol reforming for hydrogen production are then highlighted to illustrate the advantages of MOF‐based systems on coupling confined active sites, defect chemistry, and multifunctional interfaces to improve catalytic activity and selectivity. Finally, the remaining challenges in structural stability, mechanistic understanding, selectivity control, and scale‐up are discussed, together with future opportunities for the rational design of next‐generation MOF‐based photothermal catalysts. This review aims to provide a comprehensive perspective of MOF chemistry in advancing photothermal catalysis for efficient carbon utilization and hydrogen production.

title: Multi-scale measurement of livestock greenhouse-gas emissions: framework, methods, and integration strategies
summary: Livestock production is a major source of greenhouse gases (GHGs). Methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O) account for a substantial share of agricultural emissions globally. Accurate quantification of these gases is essential for advancing m
content: Livestock production is a major source of greenhouse gases (GHGs). Methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O) account for a substantial share of agricultural emissions globally. Accurate quantification of these gases is essential for advancing mitigation strategies, verifying carbon credits, and supporting Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) frameworks. However, in livestock production systems, spatial heterogeneity, animal behavior variability, and dynamic environmental conditions make consistent and scalable measurement a persistent challenge. This review develops a unified framework for classifying and evaluating GHG measurement methods in livestock systems across spatial and methodological scales. Techniques are organized into three categories: animal-scale (e.g., respiration chambers, GreenFeed, and in vivo sensors), facility-scale (e.g., flux chambers, open-path lasers, and tunnel systems), and atmospheric-scale (e.g., micrometeorological and remote-sensing methods). For each category, principles of operation, precision, cost, and scalability are comparatively evaluated, along with calibration procedures, sensor drift, and environmental compensation. Emerging hybrid and data-fusion approaches integrate multi-sensor networks with Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity and machine-learning algorithms to enable continuous, high-resolution monitoring across scales. These technologies also support precision livestock farming through wireless sensor networks, automated decision-support systems, and real-time farm management. These integrated systems bridge the gap between high-accuracy laboratory instruments and large-scale observational platforms, providing a methodological roadmap for developing robust, scalable, and data-driven MRV frameworks.

title: A Two-Level Analysis of Regulatory Change in EU Sustainability Reporting and Its Implications for Company Reporting Systems
summary: Abstract The European Union has built the world’s most extensive corporate sustainability reporting framework and, within a decade, begun to scale it back, creating an environment of regulatory uncertainty for the companies that must report
content: Abstract The European Union has built the world’s most extensive corporate sustainability reporting framework and, within a decade, begun to scale it back, creating an environment of regulatory uncertainty for the companies that must report. This paper examines how that framework has evolved across three successive reforms: the Non-Financial Reporting Directive (NFRD), the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the 2026 Omnibus simplification package, and examines the implications of these changes for corporate reporting system design. Using a document-based comparative analysis of the legal instruments, the study codes the direction of change across a set of criteria at two levels - the directives and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). The findings are interpreted through the institutional theory and the dynamic capabilities perspective. Regulatory change proves to be asymmetric. The shift from the NFRD to the CSRD expanded the framework on every dimension, while the Omnibus package contracted it on almost all of them. The widely discussed simplification is therefore more accurately characterised as a recalibration of the framework’s scope, pace, and intensity rather than its dismantling. Against this background, the paper argues that companies should design their reporting systems around a stable regulatory core, with more changeable requirements incorporated as configurable components.

title: Citrate-Controlled Copper Electrodeposition in a Cu-Ni Single Electrolyte: Kinetics, Film Composition, and Mechanism
summary: Abstract Citrate-based Cu-Ni electrolytes are widely used for the electrodeposition of Cu-rich Ni1−xCux alloys and Cu/Ni multilayers, yet the influence of citrate speciation on copper deposition kinetics remains poorly understood. In this w
content: Abstract Citrate-based Cu-Ni electrolytes are widely used for the electrodeposition of Cu-rich Ni1−xCux alloys and Cu/Ni multilayers, yet the influence of citrate speciation on copper deposition kinetics remains poorly understood. In this work, copper electrodeposition from electrolytes containing 0.025 M CuSO₄, 0.7 M NiSO₄, and 0-0.5 M Na₃Cit was investigated using chemical speciation modelling, rotating-disk-electrode measurements, Koutecký-Levich analysis, and thin-film characterization. Increasing citrate concentration progressively converted free Cu²⁺ into Cu(II)-citrate complexes and significantly reduced the copper deposition current. Kinetic analysis revealed a transition from diffusion-limited deposition in citrate-free and low-citrate electrolytes to a mixed kinetic mass-transport regime at higher citrate concentrations, where the current plateau fell below the bulk diffusion limit. Copper films deposited from citrate-containing electrolytes exhibited smoother morphologies but also substantial incorporation of C, H, and O species throughout the film thickness. Depth profiling by SIMS and ToF-EERD showed a decrease in Cu purity from approximately 98 to 87 at.% with increasing citrate concentration. These findings support a mechanism in which Cu(I)-citrate intermediates form a gel-like Cu(I)-Cu(II)-Ni(II)-citrate interphase that regulates copper deposition through coupled kinetic and mass-transport limitations.

title: The Historical Value of Disaster-Resistant Building Districts and Pathways to Regional Revitalization: Challenges Facing the “Honichi Building” in the Yoshiwara Honcho Shopping District
