content: The Yoshiwara Honcho shopping district in Fuji city, Shizuoka prefecture, originated from "Yoshiwara-juku," which was one of the 53 stations along the Tōkaidō road.The Honichi building, completed in 1961, stands at the eastern end of the shopping district, and is an extremely important structure in Yoshiwara's history.

title: AI Capability and Sustainable Growth: Environmental Strategy Pathways and Institutional Contingencies
summary: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a potential driver of sustainable business transformation, yet its impact on firms' sustainable growth (SG) is not fully understood. This study explores the relationship be
content: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly recognized as a potential driver of sustainable business transformation, yet its impact on firms' sustainable growth (SG) is not fully understood. This study explores the relationship between AI capability (AIC) and SG, defined as the simultaneous enhancement of economic performance (ECP) and environmental sustainability (ENS), through firms' symbolic and substantive environmental strategies. It also examines how government regulatory pressure (GRP) and government policy support (GPS) influence these relationships. Grounded primarily in the dynamic capabilities perspective and supplemented by a contingency perspective, we test the proposed model using two‐wave survey data from 298 firms in South Korea, analyzing the data with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM). The results reveal that AIC positively influences both ECP and ENS. Additionally, AIC is linked to both symbolic and substantive environmental strategies, but only the substantive strategy significantly mediates the relationship between AIC and SG. Furthermore, GRP enhances the connection between AIC and symbolic environmental strategy, while GPS strengthens the link between AIC and substantive environmental strategy. These findings indicate that the sustainability value of AI is contingent on strategic deployment and the institutional conditions affecting firms.

title: Progress, ambition and gaps towards the 2030 EU27 climate and energy targets
summary: This study examines the alignment, progress, and ambition of EU27 Member States in meeting the 2030 targets for greenhouse gas reductions, renewable energy deployment, and energy efficiency improvements, as reported in their National Energy
content: This study examines the alignment, progress, and ambition of EU27 Member States in meeting the 2030 targets for greenhouse gas reductions, renewable energy deployment, and energy efficiency improvements, as reported in their National Energy and Climate Plans. The analysis applies a gap approach and is framed within debates on renewable energy securitisation, EU climate leadership, and the ‘energy efficiency first’ principle. Results show that most Member States display insufficient ambition across the three areas compared to EU benchmarks. The EU’s leadership-by-example approach is evident in Sweden, Romania, and Lithuania, which have achieved long-term GHG reductions, and in Greece and Hungary, which show progress under the Effort Sharing Regulation. The securitisation of renewables is clear in countries near Russia. In energy efficiency, the analysis highlights ongoing challenges. Only a few Member States are on track to fulfil 2030 commitments, while for most the targets appear overly ambitious given current performance.

title: Powering the Nordic transition: Electrifcation pathways for a net-zero future
summary: This report examines Nordic experiences with electrification as a pathway for transitioning away from fossil fuels, drawing on 14 cases across five countries and four sectors: electric vehicles, ferries, heating and industry. It analyses po
content: This report examines Nordic experiences with electrification as a pathway for transitioning away from fossil fuels, drawing on 14 cases across five countries and four sectors: electric vehicles, ferries, heating and industry. It analyses policy approaches, enabling conditions, barriers and just transition considerations to inform national and regional roadmaps under the global Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels (TAFF) process. The findings highlight the importance of coordinated electricity and infrastructure planning, long-term yet adaptable policies, sector-specific instruments and public support to reduce investment risks. As electrification scales, grid constraints, economic uncertainty and unequal access present growing challenges. The Nordic experiences offer transferable lessons for advancing electrification while ensuring a just and inclusive transition.

title: All it takes is political will? Political agency, cabinet governance and climate regulations
summary: Why do some governments adopt stringent climate policies despite the electoral risks? While existing research emphasises the role of institutions in enabling ambitious climate action, it often overlooks the agency of elected politicians in
content: Why do some governments adopt stringent climate policies despite the electoral risks? While existing research emphasises the role of institutions in enabling ambitious climate action, it often overlooks the agency of elected politicians in navigating intra-cabinet conflicts and how different modes of bargaining affect policy output. Taking the case of the housing sector, where climate policy costs can spark backlash, this article examines how cabinet governance, especially mechanisms of conflict resolution, shapes the adoption of stringent climate regulations. Applying process tracing to Germany’s heating law to phase out fossil fuel heating (2023) and France’s minimum energy performance standards for rentals (2021), the study finds two different pathways through which the agency of politicians enables stringent climate policy. The article contributes to the literature by providing a more granular account of how institutions such as cabinet governance shape policy outcomes by conditioning the strategies available to elected politicians.

title: ENACT 2026 state of Nature-based Solutions report: Global analysis of NbS commitments under the Rio Conventions
summary: This report presents the results of the application of a global, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment framework developed to examine the extent and depth of the integration of nature-based solutions (NbS) in national policy docu
content: This report presents the results of the application of a global, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment framework developed to examine the extent and depth of the integration of nature-based solutions (NbS) in national policy documents submitted under the three Rio Conventions. The country-level analysis covers 127 countries. Importantly, this report evaluates the integration of criteria of the IUCN Global Standard for NbS and additional criteria derived from academic literature into national policy frameworks. Based on the identified gaps, this report provides recommendations to strengthen NbS across policies and commitments, with the goal of achieving better Global Stocktake outcomes and stronger mid-term review of the Land Degradation Neutrality and Global Biodiversity Framework.

title: Equity, access, and intersectional pedagogies in STEM education: Proceedings of the1st International Conference «Gender and Minorities in Science Education - Globalperspectives and local practices»: Napoli, October 14, 2025
source: Directory of Open access Books (OAPEN Foundation)
summary: The first edition of the Gender and Minorities in Science Education conference aimed to enhance critical discussions on equity, access, and intersectional pedagogies in education—particularly STEM—for women and underrepresented minorities.
content: The first edition of the Gender and Minorities in Science Education conference aimed to enhance critical discussions on equity, access, and intersectional pedagogies in education—particularly STEM—for women and underrepresented minorities. Through an intercultural lens that helped compare experiences across different countries and disciplines, the initiative explored how science is defined, taught, and practiced and which obstacles prevent participation and representation. It also aimed to reflect on the current global context and its influence on educational landscapes. The contributions ranged from academic research to student-led perspectives, highlighting global patterns and local practices. By incorporating a diversity of viewpoints, the conference sought to challenge exclusionary paradigms and promote inclusive, transformative approaches to science education, ultimately amplifying the voices of those historically marginalized.

title: Just transition in the livestock sector under the frameworks of the Paris agreement and environmental, social, and governance: a review
source: Journal of Animal Science and Technology
summary: Countries are committed to reduce their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions under the Paris agreement (PA); yet, the livestock sector (LS) continues to encounter challenges in fully achieving PA goals. Key challenges include inconsistent governa
content: Countries are committed to reduce their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions under the Paris agreement (PA); yet, the livestock sector (LS) continues to encounter challenges in fully achieving PA goals. Key challenges include inconsistent governance, limited GHG emissions reporting, limited access to climate mitigation technology, and social and economic transition barriers. Current approaches often discuss mitigation, adaptation, and transparency in isolation rather than through integrated strategies. Therefore, this review examined how the LS can achieve a just transition (JT) toward climate sustainability by aligning these elements with the PA and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) frameworks. Existing literature, industry standards, and policy documents were synthesized to investigate how PA and ESG frameworks support JT in the LS, focusing on alignment of transparency systems, mitigation, and adaptation strategies to achieve nationally determined contributions (NDCs). This review followed a narrative approach. Key policy and technical documents were identified from major institutional sources, including the United Nations framework convention on climate change (UNFCCC), food and agriculture organization (FAO), and intergovernmental panel on climate change (IPCC) with citation chaining to identify related peer-reviewed literature. The review covers material published between 2015 and 2026. It also traces the institutional evolution of LS within the UNFCCC, from the Koronivia joint work on agriculture at the conference of parties (COP) 23 through the Sharm el-Sheikh joint work (SJWA) at COP 27 and the COP 28 UAE declaration, showing gradual but limited progress. ESG principles are increasingly aligned with national climate objectives and may offer indirect support for PA goals. Within LS, however, their integration remains limited, with persistent challenges including fragmented supply chains, animal welfare gaps, weak traceability, and smallholder vulnerability. Improved transparency systems place additional pressure on national reporting capacity, which may affect trust in collective climate action. JT in agriculture further requires addressing behavioral and socio-cultural dimensions, including dietary shifts and their implications for rural livelihoods and food system equity. In conclusion, merging the ESG frameworks and PA objectives may facilitate more transparent, socially equitable, and climate resilient LS, while supporting the transition toward a long-term sustainable future.

title: Strata movement and subsidence prediction for underground coal gasification in steeply dipping coal seams: a numerical study benchmarked against a near-horizontal UCG case
summary: Underground coal gasification (UCG) is a promising technology for clean and efficient coal utilization, especially in Xinjiang, China, where steeply dipping coal seams are common. However, the combined influence of coal seam inclination and
content: Underground coal gasification (UCG) is a promising technology for clean and efficient coal utilization, especially in Xinjiang, China, where steeply dipping coal seams are common. However, the combined influence of coal seam inclination and high-temperature on strata movement and surface subsidence is still unclear, restricting UCG application under such conditions. In this study, a three-dimensional thermal–mechanical coupled model was benchmarked against a near-horizontal UCG field case and subsequently used to investigate steeply dipping seam scenarios. Stress redistribution, strata deformation, plastic zone evolution, and surface subsidence were systematically analyzed for various dip angles. Results show that increasing dip angle modifies overburden load transfer, reduces subsidence magnitude and extent, and changes subsidence patterns from symmetric to asymmetric. The temperature amplification effect first decreases and then increases across the four investigated dip angles, potentially reflecting the combined influence of gravity-driven deformation and thermal–mechanical weakening. With increasing seam inclination, plastic deformation is increasingly restricted, resulting in elastic-dominated strata behavior and a highly localized plastic zone around the gasification cavity. Based on these mechanisms, a surface subsidence prediction method was also developed. The findings and the proposed prediction method, therefore, provide a useful reference for understanding UCG-induced strata movement in steeply dipping coal seams and for designing future site-specific studies in Xinjiang.

title: Public Bus Transport for urban sustainability : Framing within Global Sustainable Development Agendas
source: International Journal of Accounting, Finance, Auditing, Management and Economics
summary: Faced with the growing challenges of urban sustainability, public bus transport represents a strategic lever for achieving the sustainable development goals set by the United Nations Agenda 2030, in particular Goal 11 (SDG 11), which aims t
content: Faced with the growing challenges of urban sustainability, public bus transport represents a strategic lever for achieving the sustainable development goals set by the United Nations Agenda 2030, in particular Goal 11 (SDG 11), which aims to make cities inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable. While the international governance of the SDGs, Moroccan national mobility dynamics, and smart technologies applied to urban transport have each been widely studied, few works articulate these three levels jointly around the specific case of urban bus transport. This paper therefore addresses the following question: to what extent, and through which levers of action, does public bus transport contribute to the achievement of SDG 11 in Moroccan cities, between international orientations and local dynamics? Methodologically, the study is based on a literature review mobilizing a corpus of 34 scientific articles and 15 institutional reports, as well as a conceptual framework based on international policies and national strategies for sustainable mobility. It also draws on examples from Casablanca, Rabat and a special focus on the city of Agadir, to illustrate the diversity of local involvement and commitments, particularly in terms of raising awareness, mobilizing stakeholders and deploying intelligent technological solutions in mobility management, in the service of sustainable development. The results take the form of a conceptual reading grid structured around four thematic axes (smart technologies, dimensions of sustainable development, the SDG 11 normative framework, and Moroccan strategies). They highlight the growing contribution of the bus as an accessible structuring mode of transport with low environmental impact, as well as the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies in enhancing the quality of service and sustainability of bus transport services. This reflection opens up research perspectives around the integration of frugal innovations into mobility policies, the monitoring of SDG indicators at local level, and territorial governance in the implementation of sustainable transport solutions.

title: Life-cycle flow-induced vibration characteristics of nuclear fuel rods subject to multi-source uncertainties
summary: Flow-induced vibration (FIV) affects grid-to-rod fretting wear and the service life of nuclear fuel rods. During operation, irradiation and corrosion alter material properties and spacer-grid supports, while axial coolant turbulence and loc
content: Flow-induced vibration (FIV) affects grid-to-rod fretting wear and the service life of nuclear fuel rods. During operation, irradiation and corrosion alter material properties and spacer-grid supports, while axial coolant turbulence and local transverse disturbances generate stochastic excitation. Their combined effects on life-cycle nonlinear vibration and correlated uncertainties remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops a multi-span beam model incorporating axial and transverse flow excitation, burnup-dependent preload relaxation, grid-to-rod clearance, and unilateral contact. Stochastic time-domain integration is employed to predict the vibration response, while a non-probabilistic ellipsoidal model quantifies response bounds and parameter correlations. Including transverse-flow excitation increases the predicted root-mean-square (RMS) displacement by 19% at 3 m/s and reduces the experimental prediction error by 20.1%. The maximum RMS displacement increases from 4.92 μm at the beginning of life to 14.00 μm near 34.3 GW d/t, before decreasing to 9.11 μm at 50 GW d/t. The response bounds evolve non-monotonically, while positive correlation between transverse-flow parameters widens the uncertainty interval.

title: Digital–Green Coordination for Low-Carbon Industrial Chain Transfer: An Exploratory Case Study of Meizhou’s Integration into the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area
source: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
summary: Under China’s dual-carbon targets, less-developed regions face the challenge of undertaking industrial chain transfer without reinforcing low-end specialization or carbon lock-in. Taking Meizhou’s integration into the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Ma
content: Under China’s dual-carbon targets, less-developed regions face the challenge of undertaking industrial chain transfer without reinforcing low-end specialization or carbon lock-in. Taking Meizhou’s integration into the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area as an exploratory case, this paper develops a digital–green coordination framework linking industrial chain transfer with carbon reduction. The framework distinguishes the complementary roles of digitalization and greening. Digitalization improves information transparency, industrial matching, cross-regional coordination, and process monitoring, whereas greening guides project selection and low-carbon upgrading through entry standards, carbon-related constraints, and related incentives. Their relative importance varies across the transfer process. During project introduction, green screening plays a stronger gatekeeping role; during construction, digital coordination and green finance can reduce coordination and upgrading costs; and during operation, carbon accounting and low-carbon demonstration scenarios can support continuous carbon management and value conversion. Three mechanisms are identified: digital platforms embedded with green standards, data-enabled green finance for low-carbon upgrading, and carbon-accounting systems linked to low-carbon demonstration scenarios. The analysis suggests that Meizhou and comparable recipient regions should move from scale-oriented industrial reception toward more selective, traceable, and low-carbon integration. As an exploratory study, the framework clarifies possible mechanisms and generates propositions for future empirical testing.

title: Ultrasonic welding vs. reflow soldering: Reliability of Cu terminal joints on AMB substrates for EV power modules
summary: In this study, Cu terminal joints on Si 3 N 4 -based active metal brazing (AMB) substrates for electric vehicle power modules were investigated to compare ultrasonic welding and reflow soldering across three substrate conditions: Cu A (C102
content: In this study, Cu terminal joints on Si 3 N 4 -based active metal brazing (AMB) substrates for electric vehicle power modules were investigated to compare ultrasonic welding and reflow soldering across three substrate conditions: Cu A (C1020 oxygen-free Cu), Cu B (C1011 oxygen-free Cu), and electroless Ag-plated Cu B. The ultrasonic joints formed a continuous Cu–Cu direct bonding structure without a distinct interface, accompanied by severe interfacial plastic deformation and grain refinement. The Cu B substrate exhibited a broader HAGB distribution, suggesting more advanced recrystallization-related microstructural evolution compared with the Cu A and electroless Ag conditions. In contrast, soldered joints exhibited Cu 6 Sn 5 and Ag 3 Sn intermetallic compounds (IMCs), with coarsened Ag 3 Sn prominently formed on the electroless Ag substrate. Mechanically, the ultrasonic joints generally showed higher mean shear strength than the reflowed-soldered joints across all substrate conditions, with the highest strength observed for the Cu B substrate, associated with its higher interfacial HAGB fraction and twin-containing microstructure. Overall, ultrasonic welding eliminates solder-derived IMC formation by forming a direct Cu–Cu joint without a solder layer while maintaining a stable metallic current-conduction path, demonstrating strong potential as a terminal bonding technology for high-temperature, high-power EV power modules.

title: ‘When you keep having sleepless nights and suicidal thoughts … ' understanding the mental health impacts of climate change on smallholder farmers in Ghana
summary: ABSTRACT Climate change poses significant risks to the livelihoods and well-being of smallholder farmers, particularly in vulnerable regions such as Ghana. While earlier studies in northern Ghana have explored farmers’ coping strategies and
content: ABSTRACT Climate change poses significant risks to the livelihoods and well-being of smallholder farmers, particularly in vulnerable regions such as Ghana. While earlier studies in northern Ghana have explored farmers’ coping strategies and some of the emotional and socio-economic effects of climate-related challenges, less attention has been paid to how climate change risks interact with financial stress and coping mechanisms to influence farmers’ mental health in dryland farming systems. This study addressed this gap using a mixed-methods approach involving 300 smallholder farmers in the Nandom Municipality of northwest Ghana. Quantitative data were analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings show that farmers have experienced rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and more frequent droughts and floods, reflecting broader climate change trends observed locally and globally. These climate-related risks were found to negatively affect farmers’ mental health, contributing to anxiety, depression, hopelessness, and, in some cases, suicidal thoughts. The study further revealed that climate change intensifies financial stress, which in turn worsens mental health outcomes among farmers. At the same time, coping mechanisms played an important role in reducing the severity of these mental health effects. The study highlights the need for policies and interventions that not only strengthen climate adaptation and livelihood resilience, but also provide mental health and psychosocial support for smallholder farmers in dryland communities in Ghana and across sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Advances in hazardous waste disposal technologies: Environmental impacts, treatment efficiency, and sustainable strategies
source: South African Journal of Chemical Engineering
summary: Hazardous waste generation has increased rapidly due to industrialisation, urbanisation, and technological advancement, creating significant risks to human health, ecosystems, and sustainable development. Effective hazardous waste managemen
content: Hazardous waste generation has increased rapidly due to industrialisation, urbanisation, and technological advancement, creating significant risks to human health, ecosystems, and sustainable development. Effective hazardous waste management requires advanced treatment technologies, strong regulatory frameworks, and sustainability-focused strategies. This review evaluates current treatment and disposal methods, including physical, chemical, biological, and thermal technologies, emphasising their efficiency, environmental impacts, and sustainability. We conducted a systematic review of studies published between 2012 and 2026 using major scientific databases, focusing on destruction efficiency, emission control, residue management, and resource recovery potential. The findings show that thermal technologies such as incineration, pyrolysis, and plasma gasification effectively reduce waste volume and destroy organic contaminants. However, they are energy-intensive and may produce secondary emissions. Physicochemical and biological treatments offer cost-effective, environmentally friendly alternatives but are often limited by slower treatment rates, incomplete contaminant removal, and secondary residue generation. Developing regions, especially sub-Saharan Africa, require special attention because insufficient collection coverage, inadequate treatment facilities, substantial capital requirements, limited technical expertise, and weak regulatory enforcement can limit the scalability of advanced hazardous waste technologies. Therefore, technology selection should be based on treatment efficiency, affordability, infrastructure needs, local technical expertise, environmental hazards, resource-recovery potential, and regulatory viability. The study emphasises the need for integrated, context-specific waste management frameworks that combine technological innovation, environmental monitoring, and policy measures to reduce risks and enhance resource recovery, guiding future research and sustainable hazardous waste management.

title: DOCKET: A Pluralistic Benchmark for Evaluating AI-Assisted Policy Feedback in U.S. Rulemaking
summary: As AI models advance and impact deliberative democracies, there is a growing need to assess their support of pluralistic viewpoints. Most pluralism benchmarks are insufficient for this: they are not grounded in diversity (i.e., stakeholders
content: As AI models advance and impact deliberative democracies, there is a growing need to assess their support of pluralistic viewpoints. Most pluralism benchmarks are insufficient for this: they are not grounded in diversity (i.e., stakeholders across different frames, skills and needs), quality (i.e., rigorous and technical debates), and impact (i.e., invested deliberators and real-world outcomes). To address this, we first (i) curate DOCKET, the most comprehensive dataset of the U.S. Federal Notice & Comment process to date. DOCKET consists of 42.3M public comments on 22,400 regulations across 44 government agencies between 2016 and 2026 and contains millions of policy debates; we link public comments to particular policy items proposed by regulators to track the public's attention and the responsiveness of regulators to public input. (ii) Next, we demonstrate the pluralistic utility of DOCKET - we show that public commenters have a wide breadth of perspectives with significant depth in policy expertise and that regulators are often responsive. (iii) Finally, we present DOCKETBench, the first systematic evaluation of LLMs' ability to represent human policy perspectives in federal rulemaking. Only 18-30% of LLM-generated feedback aligns with real human comments. LLMs critique proposals broadly but generally, lacking the specific grounding, citations, and lived-experience arguments that humans bring to bear; in addition, most models we test systematically agree with government perspectives (overlapping with up to 68% of their claims) and agree least with labor unions (as little as 26% of their claims), demonstrating a fundamental skew in perspectives that even tools like persona modeling do not solve. Taken together, we reveal fundamental gaps in how language models navigate real policy issues, and DOCKETBench serves as a testbed for closing those gaps in a crucial real-world domain.

title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
summary: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different a
content: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. CGTransformer achieves high generation validity and the highest single shot crystal structure prediction (CSP) match rate among the compared MP-20 baselines (63.24%), while same backbone comparisons show improved structure recovery over coordinate-based ordering. Furthermore, we demonstrate property-conditioned inverse design for wide-bandgap semiconductors, where ESG achieves a much higher stable, unique and novel (S.U.N.) rate and stronger target-property alignment than the coordinate-based baseline. These results establish topology-guided sequence construction as an effective route to improving crystal generation and property-directed design at fixed model capacity.

title: Class actions against greenwashing: Legal approaches in the USA and Canada
source: Učënye zapiski Kazanskogo universiteta. Seriâ Gumanitarnye nauki/Učenye zapiski Kazanskogo gosudarstvennogo universiteta. Seriâ Gumanitarnye nauki/Učenye zapiski Kazanskogo universiteta. Seriâ Gumanitarnye nauki
summary: This article explores class actions as a tool for private enforcement against greenwashing in the legal systems of the USA and Canada. The substantive and procedural features of class actions challenging business entities for deceptive envi
content: This article explores class actions as a tool for private enforcement against greenwashing in the legal systems of the USA and Canada. The substantive and procedural features of class actions challenging business entities for deceptive environmental claims were identified. Based on the analysis of current legislation, court decisions, and foreign legal doctrines, the main categories of environmental claims that become the subject of class actions were singled out: claims about environmental properties of goods, claims about corporate environmental policies and practices, and climate-related claims about achieving carbon neutrality goals and emission reductions. The findings from this study suggest that the effectiveness of class actions is determined not only by the prohibition against misleading environmental claims but also by the procedural framework of collective protection, including the scope of applicable law and the territorial organization of the legal system.

title: Structural Spans, Material Quantities, and Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Interrelations in Intermediate Floors of Finnish Mid-Rise Timber Apartment Buildings
summary: ABSTRACT In Finland, timber-structured intermediate floors are recognised as complex and carbon-intensive components of timber apartment buildings due to their multi-layered composition. To better understand their material use and associate
content: ABSTRACT In Finland, timber-structured intermediate floors are recognised as complex and carbon-intensive components of timber apartment buildings due to their multi-layered composition. To better understand their material use and associated emissions, this study analyses 28 floor assemblies from Finnish timber apartment buildings constructed using 2D (panel) and 3D (volumetric) construction methods. From these, the longest structural span was identified, and the corresponding material quantities (in terms of volume and mass) and GHG emissions were calculated. By analysing the interrelations between structural span, material quantities, and GHG emissions, the study demonstrates how these relationships vary across different floor assemblies. The main findings are: (1) structural span alone did not consistently explain total assembly-level material volume, mass, or carbon footprint; (2) non-structural materials accounted for 64% and 58% of the carbon footprint in 2D and 3D assemblies, respectively, indicating that environmental performance is governed primarily by non-structural components; (3) for structural timber, the correlation between structural span and carbon footprint was moderate in 2D assemblies and weak in 3D assemblies; and (4) the average structural span was shorter in 3D assemblies (4.39 m) than in 2D assemblies (6.82 m), while the average floor thickness remained similar (540 mm in 3D vs. 536 mm in 2D). Although the average structural span of the 3D assemblies was 36% shorter than that of the 2D assemblies, their average material mass and carbon footprint were only 12% and 21% lower, respectively. This study helps compare 2D and 3D assemblies by highlighting differences in material quantities and associated emissions by product category.

title: Spatially optimized electrification accelerating sustainable methanol production
summary: China dominates global fossil-based methanol industry, so decarbonizing its methanol sector is important for climate mitigation. Electrification offers a promising option; however, spatiotemporal mismatches between intermittent renewable ge
content: China dominates global fossil-based methanol industry, so decarbonizing its methanol sector is important for climate mitigation. Electrification offers a promising option; however, spatiotemporal mismatches between intermittent renewable generation and continuous methanol production pose substantial challenges. Here, we develop an hourly-resolution, spatial optimization framework to assess how China’s fossil-based methanol production can be decarbonized through electrification. We analyze alternative electrification strategies and evaluate their economic feasibility and environmental impact. Using data from methanol plants across China, we show that nationally coordinated electrification reduces methanol production costs by up to 18.6% relative to isolated plant-level electrification. By 2040, coordinated electrification approaches cost parity with coal-based methanol, yielding production costs of 434–472 USD t -1 . By 2050, expanded renewable power coupled with enhanced national transmission enables electrified methanol production to achieve both cost and carbon superiority. Under full electrification, production costs reach 351 and 482 USD t -1 for the two electrolysis pathways based on proton exchange membrane electrolyzer (PEME) and solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) technologies, respectively, while delivering negative carbon abatement costs of -45.6 and -14.5 USD tCO 2 -1 , and reducing life-cycle emissions by 92% and 90%, respectively, relative to coal-based production. These findings indicate that spatially coordinated electrification can substantially lower the cost of decarbonizing China’s hard-to-abate methanol industry, thereby supporting the broader energy transitions towards low-carbon production.

title: Measurement and specification sensitivity of sustainability indicators for Nordic carbon emission monitoring
summary: Sustainability indicators can be conceptually relevant while yielding unstable associations with carbon emissions. This study examines how measurement, country composition and model specification change the interpretation of an indicator su
content: Sustainability indicators can be conceptually relevant while yielding unstable associations with carbon emissions. This study examines how measurement, country composition and model specification change the interpretation of an indicator suite for Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden. A source-audited panel contains 120 country-year records for 2001–2024. Private-sector credit measures financial depth, and constant-price resource productivity measures output per domestic material input. The primary analysis estimates within-country annual log-change associations with country and year effects using 115 observations for 2002–2024. Approximate time-score heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent intervals, synchronized time-block bootstraps and country omissions assess uncertainty. Levels regressions, alternative financial and resource measures, and explicitly qualified PMG and location–scale quantile calculations provide sensitivity checks. Energy intensity has a positive annual-change coefficient of 0.453, with an approximate 95% interval of 0.227–0.679. Its point estimate remains positive under all five country omissions, although excluding Iceland produces an interval spanning zero. The negative credit association in levels does not persist in annual changes. Resource productivity, tax-revenue shares and urbanization remain imprecisely estimated or specification-sensitive. A non-compensatory evidence matrix distinguishes directional consistency from precision and construct validity; no indicator meets a stringent interpretation requiring interval support across every assessed country omission. The contribution is an auditable assessment of indicator interpretability, not a universally validated reliability score. Nordic monitoring should combine energy intensity with energy composition, tax receipts with policy-design measures, and resource productivity with absolute material use. The results describe conditional associations rather than causal policy effects.

title: A rapid carbon footprint calculation method for contaminated site remediation: Model development and validation
summary: Contaminated site remediation is essential, yet the carbon emissions generated by remediation operations constitute a secondary environmental burden rarely quantified at the planning stage. Existing tools either require extensive engineerin
content: Contaminated site remediation is essential, yet the carbon emissions generated by remediation operations constitute a secondary environmental burden rarely quantified at the planning stage. Existing tools either require extensive engineering data or are calibrated to North American conditions. We developed a modular, parameter-light framework for rapid carbon emission screening, requiring only 5–7 core input parameters. The framework decomposes remediation systems into material, energy, and transport modules, applies technology-specific emission factors from a compiled database, and quantifying uncertainty via Monte Carlo simulation. Two distinct emission patterns were identified: energy-driven processes (e.g., thermal desorption) with energy shares exceeding 85%, and material-driven processes (e.g., solidification/stabilization) with material shares over 60%. Validation against 118 cleaned cases showed a median relative error of 61.40%. To ensure practical applicability, we established a three-tier reliability system with 95% prediction intervals, explicitly cautioning the low reliability of certain technologies. Material emission factors, remediation scale, and reagent dosage explained over 80% of output variance. Positioned as a rapid screening tool rather than a precision instrument, the framework proposes a dual-track strategy: static baseline estimation for data-scarce stages, and dynamic modular calculation for site-specific scenarios. This enables carbon considerations to enter remediation decision-making at the earliest stage, thereby supporting the selection of lower-carbon technologies and reducing the secondary environmental footprint of pollution cleanup activities.

title: Engineering built-in electric field in D–A-based covalent organic frameworks for efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
summary: Abstract The built-in electric field (BIEF) of photocatalysts plays an important role in the separation and transport efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers and hence governs the photocatalytic activity. Herein, we report the one-pot
content: Abstract The built-in electric field (BIEF) of photocatalysts plays an important role in the separation and transport efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers and hence governs the photocatalytic activity. Herein, we report the one-pot gram-scale synthesis of three isostructural donor–acceptor (D–A) based covalent organic frameworks with regulated BIEF using ethanol as a green solvent. Through engineering the asymmetric electronic configuration of the donor component without changing the main framework, promoted photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate from 2.3 to 31.8 mmol g-1 h-1 was achieved. Comprehensive mechanism studies reveal that the BIEF strength was significantly enhanced by the fine regulation of donor component, enabling efficient photogenerated charge carrier transport, and suppressing their recombination, thereby inducing a high hydrogen evolution rate. This work not only provides an efficient way for the green synthesis of D–A-based covalent organic frameworks, but also gains insight into the influence of BIEF based on uniformly arranged D–A components for the development of advanced photocatalysts.

title: Advancing a just and equitable climate transition: Modeling nuclear energy and COP30-driven sustainable development
summary: The COP30 agreement, as illustrated in the provided modeling, represents a critical shift toward a just and equitable transition, ensuring that climate action safeguards vulnerable populations while fostering sustainable development. This s
content: The COP30 agreement, as illustrated in the provided modeling, represents a critical shift toward a just and equitable transition, ensuring that climate action safeguards vulnerable populations while fostering sustainable development. This study analyzes the significance of nuclear energy in the systemic transition from a carbon-intensive system to a low-carbon future by evaluating energy development scenarios through logical weighting and stochastic modeling. By assigning variables such as Capital Expenditure and temporal weights to COP28, COP29, and COP30, the research quantifies how past international commitments influence future energy trajectories. The findings, derived from the comparative analysis of Scenarios 1, 2, and 3, highlight the urgent need for accelerated emissions reductions and expanded renewable energy deployment. At COP30, the scenarios show relatively similar values, as they follow the trends observed at COP28 and COP29. The fact that Scenario 3 exhibits the highest standard deviation indicates significant volatility in the production of industrial power, hydrogen, and heat using nuclear power plants. The modeling demonstrates that while past events provide a cumulative foundation, the specific weighting of COP30 variables including the Power Generation trends is essential for achieving long-term environmental resilience and green employment. Ultimately, this focuses on the necessity of aligning global development pathways with high-fidelity climate objectives to mitigate long-term risks.

title: Majority Filter For Enhancing Pixel-Based Random Forest Land Cover Classification In Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency
summary: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noi
content: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noise, which undermines map reliability. This study aimed to integrate Random Forest (RF) classification and majority filtering to enhance the quality of land cover mapping in Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency. RF was applied to Sentinel-2 image data with varying numbers of trees (ntree) to determine the optimal model performance. Subsequently, majority filtering was applied to each classification result to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence. The evaluation employed multiple accuracy metrics, including User’s Accuracy (UA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), F1-Score, Overall Accuracy (OA), and Kappa Coefficient (KC). Comprehensive accuracy increased with the ntree until reaching an optimal point. Beyond this point, additional ntree resulted in diminishing returns. Applying majority filtering as a post-processing procedure led to further improvements in classification accuracy. While majority filtering can reduce classification noise and improve the visual quality of land cover maps, it also carries the risk of removing small, accurately classified land cover patches. This consequence is rarely discussed in similar studies. These findings highlight the importance of integrating pixel-based machine learning classification with majority filtering in land cover classification workflows, while emphasising a trade-off that tends to favour visual accuracy over the preservation of spatial detail.

title: Effect of preheating palm oil biodiesel fuel on the performance and emissions of diesel engine common rail direct injection
source: Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science and Technology (JMEST)
summary: Fossil fuel consumption continues to increase while its reserves continue to decrease and produce high emissions that trigger global warming. Therefore, more environmentally friendly alternative energy is needed. Biodiesel is a sustainable
content: Fossil fuel consumption continues to increase while its reserves continue to decrease and produce high emissions that trigger global warming. Therefore, more environmentally friendly alternative energy is needed. Biodiesel is a sustainable choice because it is biodegradable, low in sulphur, and can replace fossil fuels. This study investigates the influence of biodiesel fuel preheating temperature on engine performance, fuel consumption, and emissions in a Common Rail Direct Injection (CRDI) diesel engine. The experimental method was carried out by heating B40 and B50 fuels at temperatures of 40°C to 60°C at intervals of 10 °C. Engine performance was evaluated using a chassis dynamometer at engine speeds of 1500 to 3000 rpm at intervals of 500 rpm, fuel consumption was measured with a digital scale, and exhaust emissions testing was carried out using an opacity smoke meter. Fuel preheating at 60°C in B40 and B50 blends improved engine performance, where power output increased by up to 1.03% (78.3 vs 77.5 HP), torque rose by up to 2.64% (178.6 vs 174 Nm), BSFC reduced by up to 7.30%, and opacity emissions decreased by up to 40% compared to fossil diesel. Fuel preheating improves atomization and promotes cleaner combustion in a diesel engine.

title: Bacillus cereus PHB CMST1: a potential Halophilic Bacterium for cost-effective and sustainable production of polyhydroxyalkanoates
summary: Abstract Bacteria can spontaneously produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a thermoplastic and biodegradable substance. PHA is the best polymer substitute for plastic made from petrochemicals. In this investigation, we isolated sixteen bacteri
content: Abstract Bacteria can spontaneously produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a thermoplastic and biodegradable substance. PHA is the best polymer substitute for plastic made from petrochemicals. In this investigation, we isolated sixteen bacterial strains from brine and sediment samples collected from a solar salt works facility. Among the sixteen bacterial strains screened for polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) production, two strains, Z6 and Z9, exhibited promising results based on Sudan Black B and Nile Blue A staining. Subsequent morphological, biochemical, and molecular characterization identified strain Z9 as Bacillus cereus PHB CMST1 through 16S rRNA sequencing, which demonstrated superior PHA production compared to the other strain. To optimize PHA production, we employed a one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) methodology, revealing optimal conditions of 35°C, pH 7, 2% salinity, and a 3-day incubation period, utilizing wheat bran as the carbon source and urea as the nitrogen source. Further optimization using Response Surface Methodology-Central Composite Design (RSM-CCD) indicated that B. cereus strain PHB CMST1 requires 5% wheat bran and 2% urea for enhanced PHA synthesis. The yellowish-green dots in the thin layer chromatography (TLC) plate indicated the presence of PHA. FT-IR analysis confirmed that, 𝛽-glycosidic linkages between the sugar monomers were found. The derivatives of polyhydroxybutyric acid confirmed the monomeric polymer by GC-MS analysis. PHA's XRD study showed wide peaks at 20° and 43°, indicating that the PHA had a semi-crystalline structure. Bacillus cereus shows considerable promise for cost-effective and large-scale production of PHA bioplastics, utilizing wheat bran as a non-expensive carbon source.

title: Post-processing strategies for generative design outcomes in a UAV tail boom
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Abstract Generative design produces structurally efficient but organically shaped geometries that require post-processing before Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) manufacturing. This paper compares two post-processing strategies applied to th
content: Abstract Generative design produces structurally efficient but organically shaped geometries that require post-processing before Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) manufacturing. This paper compares two post-processing strategies applied to the same generative design outcome for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) tail boom: a complex variant faithful to the raw topology, and a simplified variant with symmetric arms, self-supporting geometry, and uniform cross-sections oriented toward FDM manufacturability. Both variants were evaluated using linear static and buckling finite element analysis underidentical loading conditions. Scaled prototypes of the simplified variant were FDM-printed at two infill configurations and physically load-tested. The manufacturing-oriented simplification reduced both mass and print time while eliminating support structures; peak stress remained well below the material limit. FEA-predicted stress concentrations correlated with observed fracture locations in physical tests. For lightly loaded polymer FDM structures, these results suggest that manufacturing-oriented simplification of generative design outcomes incurs a negligible structural penalty while improving printability and reducing production cost.

title: The forgotten bright star: Theta Eridani as a millenary stellar transient observed by Hipparchus, Ptolemy and al-Sufi
summary: Theta Eridani is a V=2.9 star that was nonetheless reported as one of the thirteen brightest stars in the night sky by both Ptolemy in his Almagest (137 AD) and by al-Sufi in his The Book of Fixed Stars (964 AD), in addition to being previo
content: Theta Eridani is a V=2.9 star that was nonetheless reported as one of the thirteen brightest stars in the night sky by both Ptolemy in his Almagest (137 AD) and by al-Sufi in his The Book of Fixed Stars (964 AD), in addition to being previously referred by Hipparchus (129 BC) as a particularly bright star. The discrepancy between its historical and modern visual magnitude $ΔV \sim 2.7$ is the highest among the $\sim 1000$ stars in the Almagest. Theta Eridani is actually a triple star system, and here we combine interferometric data from VLTI/PIONIER and VLTI/GRAVITY, spectroscopic data from ESPaDOns and FEROS, and photometric data from TESS in order to solve for the orbital parameters, masses and radii of the close inner binary Theta Eridani Aa+Ab. We find that it is a tight eccentric binary ($a=0.083 \text{ au}$, $e=0.105$) of intermediate-mass stars ($M_{Aa}\simeq 2.3 M_{\odot}$, $M_{Ab}\simeq 2.2 M_{\odot}$) that are extended to $\sim 80\%$ of their Roche lobe radii ($R_{Aa}\simeq 4.3 R_{\odot}, R_{Ab} \simeq 4.0 R_{\odot}$), resulting in prominent ellipsoidal oscillations in the lightcurve. We also find that the primary is in a very special phase of its evolution in which it has just finished core hydrogen burning. The remarkable combination of orbital and stellar parameters hints that the historical brightening of Theta Eridani was due to a millenary transient phase powered by orbital energy extraction during a long-lived ``common envelope'' stage triggered by eccentric Roche lobe overflow in a previously more eccentric binary ($e\simeq0.6$). This strengthens the case that the apparent brightening was real and not due to an error by three different ancient observers, as has been commonly claimed in the past.

title: Detectability limits of Ce abundances in RVS Gaia
summary: Gaia DR3 provides medium-resolution Radial Velocity Spectrograph (RVS) spectra for millions of stars, but the extent to which they contain recoverable cerium (Ce) information across stellar parameter space remains unclear. We assess Ce dete
content: Gaia DR3 provides medium-resolution Radial Velocity Spectrograph (RVS) spectra for millions of stars, but the extent to which they contain recoverable cerium (Ce) information across stellar parameter space remains unclear. We assess Ce detectability in RVS spectra and the reliability of DR3 Ce abundances ahead of the larger DR4 catalog. Gaia We computed synthetic spectra across a stellar-parameter grid representative of the RVS sample. We combined the Cayrel equivalent-width criterion and the Cramér-Rao bound to map Ce detectability as a function of stellar parameters and signal-to-noise ratio (S/N). We also quantified continuum-placement errors and compared the predicted detectability boundary with the DR3 GSP-Spec catalog. Gaia Gaia Ce is reliably detectable primarily in cool giants at Fe/H ≳-0.5 dex and with at least Ce/Fe gtrsim0 at an average S/N of 50, and the detectability region expands toward higher gravities at increasing S/N. Continuum-placement errors of gtrsim1% become a significant source of bias, and at gtrsim2% they completely prevent Ce detection. The criterion we present identifies where RVS Ce abundances, including those from DR4, can be robustly exploited. Outside our detectability region, these abundances should be interpreted cautiously, whether derived by GSP-Spec or by supervised methods. Currently, depending on the assumed continuum-placement uncertainty, between ∼40% and ∼70% of the published DR3 Ce measurements fall within this region; however, the rest are not reliable. Our findings are particularly important for metal-poor stars, for which the Ce lines in the RVS range are simply not detectable.

title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaqu
content: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3 + microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1 + dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like proteins, supporting a role for this lectin in immune receptor regulation. Complementary in vivo transcriptomic profiling showed that Gal3 deletion suppresses type I interferon and microglial neurodegenerative transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings position Gal3 at the interface between Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and plaque-associated microglial responses in AD.

title: Pennycress population genomics reveals a complex global expansion history and local climate-adaptation targets for neodomestication
summary: Abstract Background Field pennycress ( Thlaspi arvense ) is an emerging winter oilseed crop whose life cycle fits between corn-soybean rotations, yielding animal feed and feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel. Results Here we analyze the
content: Abstract Background Field pennycress ( Thlaspi arvense ) is an emerging winter oilseed crop whose life cycle fits between corn-soybean rotations, yielding animal feed and feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel. Results Here we analyze the largest pennycress panel assembled to date, 739 natural accessions spanning four continents, combining genome-wide diversity analysis with multi-year field evaluation. Our genomic data support that pennycress originated in Eurasia and likely underwent a complex history involving multiple introductions and admixture. Scans for selective sweeps among populations between Eurasian and North American identify phenology-related genes, including the MADS-Affecting Flowering ( MAF ) transcription factors and the seed-dormancy gene DELAY OF GERMINATION 1 ( DOG1 ), suggesting possible targets of phenological adaptation. By cross-species climate genome-wide association studies, we detect 10 syntenic peaks, suggesting partly conserved molecular machinery underlying climate adaptation in Arabidopsis and pennycress. Multi-year, multi-location field trials of over 400 accessions in Illinois identify a significant locus associated with green canopy cover, a trait important for biomass, containing a tandem array of Mitochondrial Transcription Termination Factor ( mTERF5 ) genes. Finally, the field trials reveal significant genotype-by-environment interaction, underscoring the need for regional breeding programs. Conclusions Together, these results document worldwide patterns of genetic variation and candidate climate-adaptive genes that can accelerate the neodomestication of pennycress for cultivation in the midwestern United States.

title: Accelerating Iterative Data-Driven Hotspot Protein Engineering Using Annealed Oligos and Cell-Free Expression
summary: Abstract Protein engineering increasingly leverages data-driven strategies to navigate complex fitness landscapes, but conventional high-throughput screening workflows mainly capture sequence-function data for only high-performing variants,
content: Abstract Protein engineering increasingly leverages data-driven strategies to navigate complex fitness landscapes, but conventional high-throughput screening workflows mainly capture sequence-function data for only high-performing variants, producing limited datasets for learning. Recent approaches retaining full sequence-function information frequently rely on laborious cell-based cloning and expression or broad sequencing, which slows iterative design. This problem has been partly addressed through the rapid cell-free assembly and expression of predefined variants from gene fragments. However, gene fragments present limitations for hotspot engineering, where their size can prevent closely spaced mutations from being independently swapped, and the limited quantities typically supplied do not readily support multiple screening rounds. We extend this approach to hotspot engineering using short (∼20−40 bp) annealed oligo fragments to rapidly screen predefined variants in <9 h while preserving complete sequence-function data. Bulk-prepared oligos provide sufficient material for repeated screening rounds without cloning or amplification. Their small size also facilitates the independent swapping of hotspot mutations. This workflow is validated by screening 3 to 10 fragment assemblies for two proteins. Its utility for high-iteration protein engineering is demonstrated with an additive model-guided screening campaign, which identified variants with >100% increase in fitness.

title: Resilience-oriented energy management of renewable-rich networked microgrids with battery storage and peer-to-peer power sharing
summary: In the evolving landscape of smart grids and sustainable power systems, ensuring resilience and optimal energy management in interconnected microgrids is paramount. This study presents a rule-based energy management framework for managing e
content: In the evolving landscape of smart grids and sustainable power systems, ensuring resilience and optimal energy management in interconnected microgrids is paramount. This study presents a rule-based energy management framework for managing energy in a network of interconnected microgrids, each having both solar and hydro energy sources along with battery energy storage systems. It handles possible problems like frequency deviations, drops in generation and voltage spikes, in addition to managing the energy loads and shared energy of all microgrids. Important features in the system are the exchange of power between microgrids, battery management and controlling voltage and frequency with droop methods. A key part of the study involves creating and understanding a resilience index focused on supporting critical loads during disruptions. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in maintaining operational stability, minimizing carbon emissions, enhancing critical load coverage, and reducing voltage and frequency fluctuations. The graphical analytics provide intuitive understanding of energy dynamics and fault impacts across the network. This study provides a replicable, adjustable and practical approach for strengthening Networked Microgrids forming a base for the inclusion of AI controllers that offer better performance.

title: An extracellular contractile injection system for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells
summary: Protein delivery into plant cells remains a major barrier in plant biotechnology. The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system, a phage tail-like bacterial nanomachine that naturally delivers pr
content: Protein delivery into plant cells remains a major barrier in plant biotechnology. The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system, a phage tail-like bacterial nanomachine that naturally delivers proteins into insect host cells. Here we retargeted PVCs to plants by engineering their tail fibres to recognize the plant cell surface receptor FLAGELLIN SENSITIVE 2 (FLS2). We designed and characterized a library of FLS2-targeting PVCs and evaluated their ability to deliver native and non-native cargoes, including a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and R2 retroelement genome editor. Engineered PVCs delivered Cre into wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells with efficiencies up to 16%. Delivery was FLS2 dependent and scaled with receptor abundance, reaching 75% of leaf cells in FLS2-overexpressing Arabidopsis . We further demonstrated the PVC-mediated delivery of R2 protein, resulting in the targeted insertion of a reporter gene into the plant genome and the expression of the integrated gene. This work establishes PVCs as a platform for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells, laying the foundation for targeted and precise plant genetic engineering.

title: Functional -PO2-mediated asymmetric CuN3 site enabled synergistic acetylene hydrochlorination
summary: Symmetric metal-N 4 (MN 4 ) sites represented a common configuration in single-atom catalysts (SACs) but often limited catalytic activity due to inadequate substrate polarization and activation. Herein, we overcame this fundamental limitati
content: Symmetric metal-N 4 (MN 4 ) sites represented a common configuration in single-atom catalysts (SACs) but often limited catalytic activity due to inadequate substrate polarization and activation. Herein, we overcame this fundamental limitation by precisely engineering the microenvironment around copper single-atom using P-doping to introduce non-coordinating -PO 2 group, which induced the transformation of symmetric CuN 4 site into low-coordinated, asymmetric electron-rich CuN 3 configuration. Crucially, the CuN 3 site and proximal -PO 2 group, co-located at pore defect, created an enzyme-mimicking catalytic pocket. When applied for the model reaction of acetylene hydrochlorination, these biomimetic CuN 3 and -PO 2 catalytic units enabled the profound synergistic effect, dramatically enhancing the adsorption, activation and dissociation of HCl to form the active Cu-Cl δ- /P-O-H δ+ intermediates. Once C 2 H 2 approached these activated species, it became polarized due to the local micro-electric field arising from the electronegativity differences between Cu-Cl δ- and P-O-H δ+ , thus lowering the barrier of rate-limiting step for C 2 H 3 Cl formation. This process endowed the P-doped Cu SAC with the enhanced acetylene hydrochlorination activity reaching comparable performance with the previously reported Cu-based analogues. This enzyme-mimetic strategy of creating synergistic catalytic microenvironment offered a powerful paradigm for designing highly efficient SACs for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
summary: R-2-Hydroxyglutarate (R2HG), an oncometabolite predominantly produced by mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1/2 (IDH1/2) in various cancers, is known to drive cancer progression through noncovalent inhibition of α-ketoglutarate (αKG)-dependen
content: R-2-Hydroxyglutarate (R2HG), an oncometabolite predominantly produced by mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1/2 (IDH1/2) in various cancers, is known to drive cancer progression through noncovalent inhibition of α-ketoglutarate (αKG)-dependent enzymes. In this work, we propose an alternative mechanism wherein R2HG contributes to cancer development via covalent modification of biologically critical lysines, a process termed lysine-R2HGylation (KR2HG). We designed and synthesized R2HG-mimicking probes and demonstrated their effectiveness in facilitating KR2HG target profiling and site mapping. We identified KR2HG as a post-translational modification, confirmed its C5-linkage on GSTP1(K209), and demonstrated that SIRT5 functions as a deacylase for GSTP1-KR2HG in vitro. Furthermore, we found that R2HG slightly but significantly inhibits the enzymatic activity of GSTP1 through KR2HG and dramatically suppresses monocyte differentiation via this catalytically important lysine modification. Our findings provide an alternative perspective on the role of R2HG in leukemia progression and offer a practical tool for the clinical investigation of R2HG-elevated cancers. R-2-hydroxyglutarate is a cancer-linked metabolite whose mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, the authors identify and structurally characterize lysineR2HGylation as a protein modification and develop probes that reveal GSTP1 as a functional target in leukemia cells.

title: Methane and nitrous oxide concentrations and sea–air fluxes in western Long Island Sound, a eutrophic urban estuary: Hourly to seasonal variability
summary: Western Long Island Sound is a seasonally hypoxic urban estuary undergoing anthropogenic change, which may influence concentrations and emissions of the potent greenhouse gases methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O). To provide a benchmark o
content: Western Long Island Sound is a seasonally hypoxic urban estuary undergoing anthropogenic change, which may influence concentrations and emissions of the potent greenhouse gases methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O). To provide a benchmark of current gas distributions in this system, enabling detection of future changes and comparison with data from other estuaries worldwide, we obtained the first water column profiles of dissolved CH4 and N2O concentrations in western Long Island Sound. We collected samples at seven stations along an 18-km transect in August 2023, October 2023, and May 2024. CH4 concentrations and sea–air fluxes were highest in August (mean concentration of 101 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 154 μmol m−2 d−1) and lowest in May (mean concentration of 32 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 62 μmol m−2 d−1). Conversely, N2O concentrations and sea–air fluxes were highest in May (mean concentration of 12.0 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 4.8 μmol m−2 d−1) and lowest in August (mean concentration of 10.1 nmol kg−1 and mean sea–air flux of 2.5 μmol m−2 d−1). Surface concentrations and sea–air fluxes of CH4 and N2O were highest at the westernmost station (closest to New York City) in all three seasons, suggesting that there is a persistent source of surface water to western Long Island Sound with high concentrations of CH4 and N2O. To investigate short-term variability in CH4, N2O, and oxygen (O2), we collected samples every 4 h over 28 h at the middle station of the transect, in all three months. We concluded that there is measurable short-term variability in all three gases, and that the drivers of variability in these dissolved gases are complex and not dominated by tidal advection or light levels alone.

title: CbLDM: A diffusion model for recovering nanostructure from atomic pair distribution functions
summary: The nanostructure inverse problem is a compelling challenge that helps researchers to understand the structure–property relationships of nanomaterials. This work focuses on recovering a model system of monometallic nanoparticles from their
content: The nanostructure inverse problem is a compelling challenge that helps researchers to understand the structure–property relationships of nanomaterials. This work focuses on recovering a model system of monometallic nanoparticles from their pair distribution function (PDF) data, framing the task as a highly ill-posed conditional generation problem. We introduce a Condition-based Latent Diffusion Model as a practical solution. The model incorporates an accelerated sampling strategy that initializes generation from a conditional-prior sample rather than from pure Gaussian noise, allowing the sampler to skip a contiguous block of intermediate denoising steps, reducing inference time by 8% under the default conservative setting, with a maximum speedup of 27% achievable at the cost of marginal accuracy loss. In addition, we employ a Laplacian matrix in place of a conventional distance matrix to represent nanostructures, which enhances recovery stability. Our results demonstrate that a latent diffusion model with a conditional prior can generate physically meaningful nanostructures consistent with PDF observations, laying the groundwork for solving more complex inverse problems in the future work.

title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
summary: Abstract TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While co
content: Abstract TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While conceptually, higher-dimensional approaches such as 4D and 5D correlation spectra are capable of exceeding the established molecular-weight limitations by ameliorating signal overlap, their intrinsic implications for sensitivity and measurement times required have severely limited these important prospects in practice. Here we show that in high-dimensional experiments, the extensive use of dedicated transverse-mixing optimal control pulses (TROPs) can reduce the necessary measurement time by almost an order of magnitude. TROP’ed non-uniformly sampled experiments not only benefit from a multiplicative sensitivity enhancement in each complex time point due to concomitant transfer of both components of complex signals along multi-step magnetization transfer pathways, but additionally from facilitation of reconstruction with better raw data. Aided by the processing framework provided to future users here, the combination of an extensive use of TROPs with increased dimensionality hence presents itself as highly promising to ameliorate the conventional limitations of solid-state NMR.

title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
summary: Abstract Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic anal
content: Abstract Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/ . They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
summary: Abstract Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-sc
content: Abstract Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.

title: Process diagnostics of snowmelt runoff in global hydrological and land surface models – Part 2: Are more complex models better?
summary: The added value of increased process complexity has long been a central yet unresolved question in hydrological modeling, particularly for snowmelt runoff (SMR), where multiple physical processes interact in complex ways. In this study, we
content: The added value of increased process complexity has long been a central yet unresolved question in hydrological modeling, particularly for snowmelt runoff (SMR), where multiple physical processes interact in complex ways. In this study, we develop a Tree-Based Model Complexity Scoring (TBMCS) method to quantify the complexity of snow-related processes across 13 global hydrological and land surface models. We then systematically revisit the important linkage between model complexity and model performance in three distinct SMR characteristics, i.e., total runoff ( Q sum ), peak flow ( Q max ), and centroid timing (CTQ) of runoff in the snowmelt period. Further, we assess how the basin complexity (as delineated by 1455 snow-dominated basins), forcing difference and calibration status can modulate this linkage. Results show that (1) models differ substantially in their physical process representations, with the largest divergence in melting process treatments, followed by sublimation, interception and rainfall-snowfall partitioning processes. (2) Model performance for Q sum and Q max shows only weak associations with model complexity.
