Raman spectroscopy was employed to evaluate vibrational mode positions, line widths, and disorder-activated features across multiple growth conditions. Among all investigated metals, Fe-assisted growth at 650 °C yielded the narrowest full width at half-maximum (FWHM) for the A1g, B2g, and A2g phonon modes, accompanied by the suppression of oxide vibrational features near 900 cm–1 and the absence of low-wavenumber disorder-induced modes. In contrast, Cu-, Co-, and Ag-assisted growth exhibits broader line widths, increased spectral variability, and additional defect-related signatures, particularly at 600 and 700 °C. These results establish a comparative framework for metal-mediated CVT synthesis and identify Fe as an effective additive for improving BP structure and lattice coherence.

title: Pyrolysis-Side Study for a Proposed Integrated Heavy-Oil Pyrolysis and Coke-Gasification Process: Effects of Temperature and Initial Syngas Pressure
summary: Abstract A pyrolysis-side study was conducted to clarify how thermal severity and initial syngas pressure influence product redistribution and coke structure during heavy-oil conversion, providing experimental guidance for a proposed integr
content: Abstract A pyrolysis-side study was conducted to clarify how thermal severity and initial syngas pressure influence product redistribution and coke structure during heavy-oil conversion, providing experimental guidance for a proposed integrated pyrolysis–coke-gasification concept without claiming validation of the complete recycle process. Canadian oil-sands bitumen was pyrolyzed at 400–500 °C and initial syngas pressures of 0.5–5 MPa with a fixed CO/H2 volume ratio of 2:3. Pyrolysis temperature had the strongest effect on product distribution. As the temperature increased from 400 to 500 °C, the oil yield decreased from 46.67 to 22.13 wt %, while gas and coke yields increased. Approximately complete conversion was reached at 450 °C, whereas further heating mainly promoted secondary cracking and condensation. At 450 °C, increasing the initial syngas pressure from 0.5 to 5 MPa increased the oil yield from 29.86 to 35.53 wt % and reduced gas and coke yields by 3.62 and 2.05 wt %, respectively. The increase in liquid yield was mainly associated with an 11.72 wt % increase in VGO, accompanied by lower gasoline and diesel yields, indicating that higher pressure favored the retention of heavier liquid intermediates. Coke produced at higher temperatures was more condensed, more ordered, and less reactive, whereas higher syngas pressure resulted in a more disordered and functionalized carbon structure with higher oxidation reactivity. An exploratory composite structure–reactivity descriptor showed a strong within-data set association with the air-oxidation index (R2 = 0.9791; Q2LOO = 0.9498); however, the relationship is based on only eight unique operating conditions and requires external validation before predictive generalization. Considering conversion, product distribution, pressure severity, and coke reactivity, 450 °C and 1 MPa were retained as a reasonable bench-scale reference among the tested conditions, rather than as a temperature–pressure optimum.

title: Practice Design and Field Performance of a Continuous Gas Recirculation System for Liquid Unloading in High-Water-Production Gas Wells
summary: Abstract Liquid loading is a major operational challenge in gas wells with high water production, often resulting in reduced gas deliverability and premature well shut-in. To address this problem, this study investigates a continuous gas re
content: Abstract Liquid loading is a major operational challenge in gas wells with high water production, often resulting in reduced gas deliverability and premature well shut-in. To address this problem, this study investigates a continuous gas recirculation system that utilizes a portion of the produced natural gas as the lifting medium. The system compresses and reinjects the recycled gas through the tubing–casing annulus to enhance liquid transport and sustain gas production. The engineering design incorporates critical gas velocity calculations, gas injection parameter determination, wellbore pressure-loss analysis, and surface gathering-system considerations. The proposed configuration was implemented in the Y well group of the Yan'an Gas Field, Ordos Basin, China, to evaluate its field applicability.Field observations showed that Well Y1 maintained a daily gas production rate of 2.5–5.5 × 10⁴ m³/d and a daily water production rate of 180–250 m³/d, with a circulating gas injection rate of 2.5–5.0 × 10⁴ m³/d. Well Y0 achieved a relatively stable daily gas production rate of approximately 2.0 × 10⁴ m³/d. In addition, the study presents a 20-year production forecast comparing the continuous recirculation system with conventional drainage measures and a no-treatment scenario. The field results indicate that continuous gas recirculation can support liquid unloading and restore gas production in severely liquid-loaded wells. This study provides an engineering basis for the design and field application of continuous gas recirculation systems in gas wells with high water production.

title: Grassland legacy effects regulate nutrient leaching losses in cropland phases in long-term grassland-crop rotations
summary: Nutrient leaching from agricultural land threatens water quality and soil fertility. Grassland–crop rotations (GCR) are increasingly promoted as a sustainable strategy to build soil organic matter and enhance nutrient retention. However, th
content: Nutrient leaching from agricultural land threatens water quality and soil fertility. Grassland–crop rotations (GCR) are increasingly promoted as a sustainable strategy to build soil organic matter and enhance nutrient retention. However, the extent to which grassland management exerts legacy effects (LEs) on nutrient leaching during subsequent cropland phases remains poorly understood. Using a 15-year field experiment in a temperate agroecosystem (Lusignan, France), we quantified how grassland LEs influence the leaching of six nutrients (NO 3 -N, PO 4 -P, K + , Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , and SO 4 -S) during two GCR cycles. Three GCR management regimes differing in grassland duration and nitrogen fertilization were compared with continuous grassland and continuous cropland (CC). Repeated-measures mixed models were used to assess annual and period-specific LEs on nutrient concentrations, modelled drainage, and leaching loss. Grassland LEs reduced model-estimated nutrient leaching losses during subsequent cropland phases by up to 74% relative to CC, with the strongest and most consistent reductions observed for NO 3 -N, whereas reductions for the other nutrients were smaller and less certain. The LEs on nutrient concentrations were generally weak and variable across nutrients, while modelled drainage showed more consistent changes. Indeed, driver analyses revealed that LEs on nutrient leaching losses were more strongly associated with modelled drainage than with leachate concentrations, except for PO 4 -P. The effects of grassland duration and repeated GCR cycles were nutrient-specific, whereas reduced N fertilization generally weakened beneficial LEs across nutrients. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for drainage dynamics and nutrient-specific responses when assessing the environmental benefits of grassland–crop rotations.

title: Catalyst-Free Solid-State Dearomative Cycloaddition Driven by Pressure-Induced Proton-Gating
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Dearomative cycloadditions enable the transformation of flat, unreactive aromatic compounds into complex three-dimensional architectures characteristic of many successful drugs and natural products. However, these reactions typical
content: Abstract Dearomative cycloadditions enable the transformation of flat, unreactive aromatic compounds into complex three-dimensional architectures characteristic of many successful drugs and natural products. However, these reactions typically require harsh conditions or photocatalysts, limiting their synthetic scope. Here, a topochemical, self-catalyzed, and light-free dearomative cycloaddition reaction is reported that proceeds smoothly in the solid state under exceptionally mild, gigapascal-range pressures at room temperature. This reaction follows an inverse-electron-demand mechanism and is proton-gated, initiated by a pressure-induced proton transfer between a model electron-poor diene and a dienophile acting as a Brønsted–Lowry acid–base pair. Although the resulting sp3-rich product can be fully recovered at ambient pressure, it undergoes a spontaneous, dynamic, yet nondestructive retro-Diels–Alder reaction back to the starting materials over time. By establishing pressure and proton transfer as synergistic gating elements for solid-state reactivity, this study introduces a sustainable, solvent-free paradigm for molecular synthesis.

title: Penijavanicins A and B, Complex Polycyclic Polyketides Featuring a cis -Fused Dihydroisocoumarin-Tetrahydropyran Core with Anti-Neuroinflammatory Activity
summary: Abstract Chemical investigation of the soil-derived fungus Penicillium sp. 16F038 using the One Strain Many Compounds (OSMAC) strategy led to the discovery of penijavanicins A and B (1 and 2), two structurally novel aromatic polyketides. Co
content: Abstract Chemical investigation of the soil-derived fungus Penicillium sp. 16F038 using the One Strain Many Compounds (OSMAC) strategy led to the discovery of penijavanicins A and B (1 and 2), two structurally novel aromatic polyketides. Comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including 1,1-ADEQUATE NMR and HRESIMS, established their planar structures as an unprecedented 6/6/6/6/6 pentacyclic framework incorporating a cis-fused dihydroisocoumarin-tetrahydropyran architecture. The challenging stereochemical assignments, posed by the densely functionalized and conformationally constrained core, were successfully resolved through O-methylation derivatization, quantitative ROESY analysis, and TDDFT-ECD calculations. Biological evaluations revealed that compound 2 displayed significant antineuroinflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated BV-2 microglial cells by markedly suppressing nitric oxide (NO), TNF-α and IL-6 production without appreciable cytotoxicity. Furthermore, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and Western blot analyses suggested that 2 exerts its anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting the ERK/NF-κB signaling pathway.

title: Price-setting tipping points in decarbonising EU electricity markets
summary: Abstract The role of fossil fuels, particularly natural gas, in setting clearing prices on the European Union's integrated electricity market is at the forefront of energy policy debates. Identifying price-setting technologies in electricit
content: Abstract The role of fossil fuels, particularly natural gas, in setting clearing prices on the European Union's integrated electricity market is at the forefront of energy policy debates. Identifying price-setting technologies in electricity spot markets is, however, inherently complex due to cross-border trading, overlapping bidding strategies, and lack of granular plant-level operational data. Furthermore, empirical evidence remains limited on how the energy transition and the growing role of variable renewables may alter these price-setting dynamics. In this paper, we present an approach to reverse-engineer the most likely price-setting technology for each hour on the day-ahead market across EU bidding zones. Analysing a decade of data, our findings show distinct "tipping points" that indicate structural shifts in price-setting, moving from traditional fossil fuel dominance towards renewable-driven price-setting in highly nonlinear fashion.

title: Role of different types of algal EPS in combating the toxic effects tetrabromobisphenol-A and atrazine towards marine microalgae Chlorella sp.: cellular toxicity, uptake, and oxidative stress
summary: Introduction Tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA) and atrazine (ATZ) are aquatic pollutants that threaten primary producers. Algal extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) may reduce their toxicity by modifying pollutant-cell interactions. Methods
content: Introduction Tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA) and atrazine (ATZ) are aquatic pollutants that threaten primary producers. Algal extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) may reduce their toxicity by modifying pollutant-cell interactions. Methods This study compared the toxicity of TBBPA and ATZ in marine Chlorella sp. and evaluated the protective effects of loosely bound EPS (LB-EPS), tightly bound EPS (TB-EPS), and their combination (LB+TB-EPS). Growth, photosynthetic performance, oxidative stress, and antioxidant enzyme activities were assessed. UPLC, zeta potential, wettability, and three-dimensional excitation–emission matrix (3D-EEM) spectroscopy were used to investigate cellular pollutant accumulation, surface properties, and EPS characteristics. Results Both pollutants impaired algal growth and photosynthesis, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA), and altered superoxide dismutase and catalase activities. ATZ exhibited greater toxicity than TBBPA, potentially through interference with photosystem II. UPLC analysis revealed reduced cellular accumulation of both pollutants following EPS supplementation. Supporting analyses indicated modifications in cell-surface properties and pollutant-EPS interactions. TB-EPS provided the greatest protection, followed by LB+TB-EPS and LB-EPS. Discussion EPS mitigated pollutant-induced toxicity, potentially by modifying pollutant-cell interactions and reducing contaminant bioavailability and cellular uptake. The superior protective performance of TB-EPS highlights the importance of EPS fractions in regulating pollutant toxicity. These findings provide insights into EPS-mediated protection in marine primary producers and its implications for aquatic ecological risk assessment.

title: Full-range flexural modelling of hybrid-reinforced steel fibre recycled aggregate concrete beams
summary: Hybrid FRP-steel reinforcement and steel fibre-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (SFRAC) can improve crack control and deformation capacity, but the full-range flexural response of hybrid SFRAC beams remains insufficiently quantified.
content: Hybrid FRP-steel reinforcement and steel fibre-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (SFRAC) can improve crack control and deformation capacity, but the full-range flexural response of hybrid SFRAC beams remains insufficiently quantified. This study developed a four-stage semi-analytical model for the load-mid-span deflection response of hybrid FRP-steel-reinforced SFRAC beams. Nine beams, comprising eight hybrid specimens and one all-steel reference, underwent four-point bending. Parameters included steel-fibre volume fraction, lower-to-upper bottom-reinforcement area ratio and lower-layer reinforcement type. A nonlinear finite-element model with explicitly embedded steel fibres interpreted pre-peak response, reinforcement-strain development, and damage distribution. The semi-analytical model defines cracking, yielding, ultimate, and post-peak reference states through sectional equilibrium, strain compatibility, an equivalent fibre-bridging force, ultimate-curvature correction, and calibrated post-peak secant stiffness. Compared with the identically reinforced fibre-free beam, steel-fibre volume fractions of 0.5%, 1.0%, 1.5%, and 2.0% increased the ultimate load by 8.9%, 12.6%, 13.6%, and 16.4%. Increasing lower-layer BFRP bar diameter from 10 to 14 and 18 mm increased ultimate load by 4.9% and 13.8%, respectively. Lower-layer BFRP and CFRP beams exceeded the all-steel reference’s ultimate load by 15.5% and 21.1%, respectively. Lower-layer FRP bars’ sustained elastic tensile contribution governed post-yield hardening. The fibre-bridging coefficient, ultimate-curvature coefficient, and post-peak secant stiffness were calibrated using five identically reinforced hybrid beams with steel-fibre volume fractions of 0–2.0% and held fixed thereafter. Internal assessment using three held-out hybrid specimens gave MAPE values of 3.7%, 10.5%, 10.4%, and 8.2% for \(P_{{{\text{cr}}}}\) , \(P_{{\text{u}}}\) , \(\delta_{{\text{u}}}\) , and \(\delta_{{\text{f}}}\) respectively. An external literature assessment gave a 7.3% MAPE for \(P_{{\text{u}}}\) . The all-steel reference specimen identified the applicability boundary, indicating that the model is intended for beams with linearly elastic FRP reinforcement in the lower layer of bottom reinforcement. Further independent validation is needed before the calibrated coefficients are generalised.

title: Electrochemical Quantification of Salivary Amyloid-β1–42 Using Disposable Gold Screen-Printed Electrodes: Analytical Validation and Comparison with ELISA
summary: Abstract Sensitive quantification of low-abundance biomarkers in noninvasive biofluids is critical for advancing Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnostics. In this study, we developed an electrochemical immunosensor for the detection of amyloid
content: Abstract Sensitive quantification of low-abundance biomarkers in noninvasive biofluids is critical for advancing Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnostics. In this study, we developed an electrochemical immunosensor for the detection of amyloid β 1–42 (Aβ1–42) in human saliva using disposable gold screen-printed electrodes (AuSPEs). The sensing interface was fabricated through covalent antibody immobilization on a cysteamine-modified gold surface to enable selective electrochemical recognition of Aβ1–42. Under optimized conditions, the immunosensor exhibited a linear response over the concentration range of 10–40 pg/mL with a limit of detection of 5.39 pg/mL and good selectivity toward structurally related peptides. To reduce matrix-associated signal variability during saliva analysis, a simple PBS dilution protocol was applied, resulting in reduced intersubject signal variability compared with untreated saliva samples (SD ≤ 3.05 μA) and a strong correlation with PBS measurements (R2 = 0.9962). The developed platform demonstrated the feasibility of electrochemical detection of low-abundance Aβ1–42 in diluted human saliva using disposable electrodes. Furthermore, pilot application using 25 human saliva specimens demonstrated strong linear concordance with a commercial ELISA benchmark (R2 = 0.9817), supporting the analytical reliability and preliminary feasibility of this noninvasive platform for salivary Aβ1–42 measurement.

title: Workout intensity and structure affect breathing pattern dynamics during cycling
summary: Abstract Purpose The two main components of breathing pattern, respiratory frequency ( f R ) and tidal volume (V T ), respond to variable exercise intensity in distinct ways; little is known about how they respond to abrupt changes in workl
content: Abstract Purpose The two main components of breathing pattern, respiratory frequency ( f R ) and tidal volume (V T ), respond to variable exercise intensity in distinct ways; little is known about how they respond to abrupt changes in workload such as during intermittent workouts (e.g., high-intensity interval training [HIIT]). This study aimed to assess how breathing pattern changes between and within continuous and intermittent workouts in a large cohort varying in biological sex and fitness. Methods Participants (n = 92, 39 F) completed a ramp test and six individualized cycling workouts (four intermittent). Continuous breath-by-breath data were collected as well as ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) at fixed time points. Variables were normalized to % reserve and analyzed with linear-mixed models. For the intermittent workouts, the inflection point and response magnitude of each variable was estimated across the recovery to work transition. Results f R was particularly sensitive to between-workout differences, tracking time-on-task and RPE more closely than the other variables. During HIIT, f R typically responded first to the recovery to work transition, and it was the only variable whose response magnitude increased monotonically with the work-rate step. V T increased at work bout onset in 5x4 and SEP but fell in the shorter-recovery 15x1 and 30x30. Large sex and fitness differences mostly disappeared when adjusting to reserve values. Conclusion Since f R tracks RPE, time-on-task, abrupt work-rate changes, and generalizes across sex and fitness, it is a particularly valuable monitoring target when applied in the field alongside other variables.

title: Agaricus arvensis fairy rings link to enhanced Leymus chinensis productivity and potential microbial phosphorus mobilization in a typical steppe of Inner Mongolia
summary: Inroduction Fairy rings are concentric bands of vegetation that develop as soil fungi expand radially. Although fairy rings are known to enhance plant productivity, the mechanisms linking soil microorganisms, nutrient availability, and plan
content: Inroduction Fairy rings are concentric bands of vegetation that develop as soil fungi expand radially. Although fairy rings are known to enhance plant productivity, the mechanisms linking soil microorganisms, nutrient availability, and plant quality in grassland ecosystems remain insufficiently understood. Methods This study focuses on Agaricus arvensis fairy rings in Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia, with the aim of exploring whether fairy ring-associated changes in soil microorganisms and phosphorus availability are linked to the yield and quality of the dominant grass species Leymus chinensis . Vegetation characteristics, soil physicochemical properties, and high-throughput sequencing were integrated to resolve these mechanisms. Results Fairy rings significantly altered plant community composition by markedly increasing the importance value of L. chinensis . These changes were associated with shifts in soil microbial community structure, particularly bacterial communities in the 10-30 cm soil layer. Fairy ring soils exhibited elevated concentrations of organic acids, including oxalic, lactic, maleic and fumaric acids, which was positively correlated with the mobilization of soil phosphorus and higher soil AP. As a consequence, aboveground biomass and forage quality of L. chinensis were significantly improved, with crude protein content increasing by 24-43%. Correlation analyses showed that bacterial community variation was more closely associated with organic acid accumulation and phosphorus availability than fungal variation, suggesting that bacteria may contribute to the observed differences in plant yield and quality. Conclusion This study suggests a potential pathway in which fairy rings are associated with microbial shifts, organic acid accumulation, and increased phosphorus availability, which together may contribute to improved plant growth and forage quality. These findings deepen our understanding of microbe-plant interactions in grassland ecosystems and provides data to support the potential agricultural value of developing fairy rings.

title: Therapeutic effects of moxa smoke-derived carbon dots in experimental rheumatoid arthritis
summary: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. We isolated and purified moxa smoke-derived carbon dots (ACDs) using a smoldering-combustion aerosol-capture ro
content: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. We isolated and purified moxa smoke-derived carbon dots (ACDs) using a smoldering-combustion aerosol-capture route, characterized their physicochemical properties, and evaluated their anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic effects in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and a rat model of collagen-induced arthritis (CIA). ACDs were well-dispersed, quasi-spherical nanoparticles (1.9–4.0 nm; mean, 2.9 nm) containing locally ordered sp 2 -carbon domains and oxygen- and nitrogen-containing surface groups. At concentrations ≤150 μg/mL, ACDs did not compromise RAW264.7 cell viability and attenuated LPS-evoked nitric oxide (NO) generation and IL-6 release. In CIA rats, ACDs improved clinical and histological manifestations, including arthritis scores, ankle swelling, synovial hyperplasia, inflammatory infiltration, and cartilage injury, and decreased serum NO, PGE 2 , TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-18. ACD treatment was also associated with reduced p38 MAPK and NF-κB phosphorylation and decreased NLRP3, ASC, cleaved caspase-1, and GSDMD-NT expression. These findings demonstrate the anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity of ACDs and support further investigation of their biological effects in RA.

title: Beyond thermodynamic stability: oxygen penetration kinetics and oxide-scale integrity jointly govern the oxidation resistance of medium-entropy carbides
summary: Abstract Selection of medium-entropy carbide ceramics has long relied on empirical trial and error and on thermodynamic criteria, yet whether such criteria can predict the oxidation resistance of a material has rarely been examined. Here, t
content: Abstract Selection of medium-entropy carbide ceramics has long relied on empirical trial and error and on thermodynamic criteria, yet whether such criteria can predict the oxidation resistance of a material has rarely been examined. Here, ten Ti/Zr/Hf/Nb/Ta-based ternary carbide systems were screened by thermodynamic calculation, and three candidates were selected and oxidized. (TiZrHf)C, although the least stable of the three in thermodynamic terms, shows the best oxidation resistance, owing to its large surface-to-interstitial energy difference (5.927 eV) and to the dense oxide scale it develops. (TiHfTa)C has the most negative formation energy, but its multiphase scale accumulates pores and cracks at high temperature, which disrupt the continuity and density of the scale, may ease oxygen transport into the substrate, and eventually causes pronounced structural degradation. (ZrHfTa)C fails catastrophically through short-circuit diffusion along through-thickness cracks that form early in oxidation. Oxidation resistance is therefore not determined by thermodynamic stability alone, but by the interplay between oxygen penetration kinetics and the microstructure of the oxide scale. These results expose the limits of a single thermodynamic screening criterion and offer a combined framework for designing oxidation-resistant medium-entropy carbide ceramics.

title: Tailoring pore architecture and residual carbon ordering in vat-photopolymerized SiC ceramics via debinding temperature
summary: Abstract Vat photopolymerization (VPP) of SiC ceramics produces green bodies that contain about 45 vol% organic phase, so thermal debinding does not simply remove a fugitive binder but defines the pore architecture on which both the subsequ
content: Abstract Vat photopolymerization (VPP) of SiC ceramics produces green bodies that contain about 45 vol% organic phase, so thermal debinding does not simply remove a fugitive binder but defines the pore architecture on which both the subsequent solid-state sintering and the pore-related functionality depend. This work examines how the debinding temperature (450–650°C) governs the open pore structure, the structural ordering of the residual carbon and the porosity–strength relationship of pressureless-sintered SiC ceramics. Mercury intrusion porosimetry shows that the open porosity rises from 27.25% at 450°C to a maximum of 35.92% at 600°C, with a single pore-size peak between 100 and 300 nm, while the total pore area falls from 9.07 to 2.67 m² g⁻¹, indicating that a tortuous, high-surface-area pore network is replaced by a coarser and better-connected one. EDS and Raman spectroscopy show that the residual carbon is progressively enriched and reaches its highest structural order at 600°C (ID/IG = 0.63). The ceramic debound at 600°C combines a sintered porosity of 13.99%, a density of 2.77 g cm⁻³ and a flexural strength of 290.2 ± 24.3 MPa, and the strength–porosity data follow the Ryshkewitch–Duckworth relation (σ0 = 394.9 MPa, b = 2.36, R² = 0.949). The debinding temperature therefore provides a single processing lever for the design of porous VPP-SiC components with a controlled open pore fraction and load-bearing capacity.

title: SUSTAINABLE HVAC OPERATIONS AND ENERGYEFFICIENT MAINTENANCE FRAMEWORKS FOR SMART BUILDINGS IN SAUDI ARABIA UNDER VISION 2030
summary: Cooling-intensive buildings in Saudi Arabia face a linked operational challenge: reducing electricity consumption without compromising thermal comfort, ventilation, equipment reliability, or service continuity. This critical review examines
content: Cooling-intensive buildings in Saudi Arabia face a linked operational challenge: reducing electricity consumption without compromising thermal comfort, ventilation, equipment reliability, or service continuity. This critical review examines sustainable heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) operations and energy-efficient maintenance frameworks for existing and emerging smart buildings within the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030. Literature published during 2020–2025 is organized across climate-responsive operation, supervisory control, condition monitoring, fault detection, maintenance decision making, and implementation governance. The analysis distinguishes demonstrated technical capability from deployable facility management practice and avoids treating simulated savings as guaranteed field outcomes. It identifies weaknesses in cross-climate transferability, inadequate fault labels, uncalibrated energy baselines, limited lifecycle costing, and incomplete representation of occupant health. A staged operations-to-maintenance framework is proposed that combines reliable sensing, fault triage, human authorization, verified intervention, and continuous measurement. The central finding is that sustainable HVAC performance depends on institutionalizing verifiable operational routines alongside digital optimization. For Saudi portfolios, the priority is robust, climate-specific and maintainable integration rather than technology adoption alone. The review concludes with research priorities and measurable implementation indicators.

title: Deformation mechanism of a large-span small-clearance twin tunnel crossing a fault fracture zone
summary: This study investigates the deformation behavior of large-span small-clearance twin tunnels crossing a fault fracture zone, using the Nanxiangling Tunnel as a case study. A closed-loop framework integrating numerical prediction, monitoring
content: This study investigates the deformation behavior of large-span small-clearance twin tunnels crossing a fault fracture zone, using the Nanxiangling Tunnel as a case study. A closed-loop framework integrating numerical prediction, monitoring feedback, and model calibration is established. A three-dimensional FLAC3D model of sequential twin-tunnel excavation reproduces the spatial distribution of surrounding-rock displacement and support axial forces, while an integrated sensing–transmission distributed optical fiber monitoring system based on Brillouin optical time-domain reflectometry (BOTDR) synchronously captures crown settlement and horizontal convergence at four typical sections. Taking the measured displacement at the fault-core section as the target, pattern-search back analysis inverts the elastic modulus, cohesion, and internal friction angle of the fault-zone surrounding rock, yielding a coefficient of determination of 0.94 between simulated and measured crown settlements. Crown settlement at the fault core is amplified to 11.39 and 12.90 mm in the left and right tunnels, 75% and 66% larger than at the normal section. The longitudinal disturbance zone spans 405–545 m, with a strong-influence range of about 60 m (3.3 times the fault width). A three-level early-warning criterion with settlement-rate thresholds of 0.10, 0.30, and 0.38 mm/m (defined as the crown-settlement increment per metre of excavation advance) is established, providing a reference for deformation control of similar projects.

title: Evolution characteristics and ecological risk assessment of heavy metal pollution in sediments of Laizhou Bay over the past century
summary: Laizhou Bay is a typical semi-enclosed bay in the Bohai Sea, where heavy metal pollution has become a prominent issue due to industrial, agricultural, and shipping activities within its watershed. To reconstruct the centennial evolution of
content: Laizhou Bay is a typical semi-enclosed bay in the Bohai Sea, where heavy metal pollution has become a prominent issue due to industrial, agricultural, and shipping activities within its watershed. To reconstruct the centennial evolution of heavy metal pollution in this bay, this study conducted geochemical analyses of seven heavy metals (Cu, Pb, Zn, Cr, Cd, As, and Hg) on a sediment core, building upon an established chronostratigraphic and grain-size framework. By integrating the geo-accumulation index, potential ecological risk index (evaluated using multiple background values), element correlation analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA), we reconstructed the historical evolution of heavy metal pollution in Laizhou Bay over the past century, identified pollution sources, elucidated the controlling effects of grain size, and explored the response of pollution evolution to regional industrialization. The results indicate that: (1) With 1960 and 2000 as key transition boundaries, the centennial heavy metal evolution can be divided into three stages: 1930–1960, a natural background-dominated low-pollution and low-risk stage; 1960–2000, a transitional stage of intensifying anthropogenic pollution; and 2000–present, a high-pollution stage under partial emission-control implementation. Hg and Cd are the major pollution and risk contributors; Cu, Pb, Zn, and Cr are predominantly derived from natural inputs, while As exhibits an independent source signature. (2) The selection of background values significantly influences pollution and risk assessment results. Hg is most sensitive to background value selection; the Bohai Sea sediment background underestimates Hg pollution and ecological risk, whereas the Shandong Province soil background and the in-situ natural background of the core yield consistent assessment results. (3) Cu, Pb, Zn, Cr, Cd, and Hg are highly homologous and significantly controlled by mean grain size (Mz), preferentially enriching in fine-grained sediments; As shows weak correlations with other heavy metals and grain size, indicating an independent source. This study confirms that the heavy metal pollution evolution in Laizhou Bay corresponds well with the temporal sequence of regional industrialization, and that Hg and Cd are priority targets for sediment management and ecological remediation in the bay.

title: Temporal transcriptomic dynamics of pectoral muscle in Xianghuang chicken across embryonic and post-hatch stages
summary: Introduction Understanding the dynamic transcriptional regulation of pectoral muscle development from embryonic to post-hatching stages is crucial for improving meat production in native chickens. Methods In the present work, we profiled th
content: Introduction Understanding the dynamic transcriptional regulation of pectoral muscle development from embryonic to post-hatching stages is crucial for improving meat production in native chickens. Methods In the present work, we profiled the transcriptome of Xianghuang chicken pectoral muscle at five developmental milestones: embryonic days 13 (E13) and 17 (E17), as well as days 1 (D1), 14 (D14), and 35 (D35) post-hatching. Results Across these stages, we observed stage-dependent variations in body weight, pectoral muscle weight, and myofiber diameter and cross-sectional area. A total of 9,423 genes showing differential expression genes (DEGs) were resolved by STEM clustering into three temporal patterns: Cluster I (2,168 genes, declining expression), Cluster II (2,344 genes, rising expression), and Cluster III (794 genes, transiently peaking at D1). GO and KEGG analyses assigned Cluster I to cell-cycle and cytoskeletal categories, Cluster II to oxidative phosphorylation and energy-related pathways, and Cluster III to ribosome function and mitochondrial biogenesis terms. PPI network analysis pinpointed cluster-specific candidate hub genes: ACTB , SRC , ITGB3 , EGFR , and FN1 (Cluster I); NDUFS1 , NDUFS2 , NDUFS3 , NDUFS8 , and COX5A (Cluster II); RPS2 , RPS14 , RPS15 , RPL10A , RPL12 , RPL17 , RPL23 , RPL26L1 , and RPL35 (Cluster III). Transcription factor prediction identified SMAD5 and ZNF24 as shared regulators among several of these ribosomal genes. qRT-PCR validation confirmed the consistency of the RNA-seq data. Discussion Collectively, this work offers a detailed transcriptomic atlas of pectoral muscle development in a native chicken breed and highlights ribosomal proteins as key nodal regulators during the transition from embryonic to post-hatch growth.

title: Antagonist antibody to NPR1, REGN-NPR17544 (baloncibart), increases blood pressure and plasma volume
summary: Abstract Hypotension and hypovolemia cause morbidity across many clinical disorders, yet pharmacologic options are limited. REGN-NPR1 7544 (REGN7544/baloncibart), a first-in-class monoclonal antibody, allosterically antagonizes natriuretic
content: Abstract Hypotension and hypovolemia cause morbidity across many clinical disorders, yet pharmacologic options are limited. REGN-NPR1 7544 (REGN7544/baloncibart), a first-in-class monoclonal antibody, allosterically antagonizes natriuretic peptide receptor 1 (NPR1), a membrane guanylyl cyclase activated by atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) and brain natriuretic peptide to promote vasorelaxation and natriuresis. REGN-NPR1 7544 bound human and cynomolgus monkey NPR1 with nanomolar affinity, increased systolic blood pressure (SBP) in NPR1 Hu/Hu mice by 10–15 mmHg for up to 28 days, corrected severe hypotension in ANP-overexpressing mice, and inhibited ANP-induced mesenteric vessel relaxation. In monkeys, SBP increased by 15–20 mmHg, with biomarkers consistent with plasma volume expansion. In a randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 1 single-ascending-dose study in healthy adults (N = 80), doses ≥ 100 mg were generally well-tolerated, producing sustained 5–10 mmHg SBP increases and biomarker signals consistent with volume expansion. These data implicate tonic NPR1 signaling in human blood pressure and volume regulation, supporting REGN-NPR1 7544 as a candidate for hypotension and hypovolemia.

title: Bryophyte diversity and community turnover along an elevational gradient in the high-altitude region of Mila Mountain, Xizang, China
summary: Introduction Bryophyte diversity and community turnover remain insufficiently documented along high-altitude elevational gradients on the Xizang Plateau. We investigated these patterns on the eastern slope of Mila Mountain. Methods We surve
content: Introduction Bryophyte diversity and community turnover remain insufficiently documented along high-altitude elevational gradients on the Xizang Plateau. We investigated these patterns on the eastern slope of Mila Mountain. Methods We surveyed 146 quadrats (0.25 m² each) across seven sites (4,079–5,230 m a.s.l.), obtaining 1,085 specimen records. We standardized richness to 12 quadrats per site using incidence-based rarefaction and assessed sampling completeness using Chao2 and sample coverage. We evaluated turnover using pairwise Jaccard similarity and principal coordinates analysis. We also summarized substrate representation, conducted a soil-only rarefaction sensitivity analysis, and examined environmental covariation descriptively (n = 7 sites). Results We recorded 109 bryophyte taxa in 59 genera and 34 families, including 94 moss taxa and 15 liverwort taxa. Pottiaceae was the richest family (31 taxa), followed by Bryaceae (10) and Polytrichaceae (9). Observed richness ranged from 22 to 50 taxa and rarefied richness from 16.01 to 36.31 taxa. Rarefied richness generally increased toward lower elevations, with departures from a monotonic trend. Pairwise Jaccard similarity ranged from 0.146 to 0.469. Soil accounted for 94.1% of specimen records and supported 98 taxa. Soil-only rarefaction showed a similar non-monotonic pattern. Discussion These results provide a baseline for bryophyte diversity and turnover along the transect and highlight the need for replicated environmental measurements and substrate-stratified sampling.

title: Impacts of Residence Time and Temperature on CO Electrolysis to Acetate at the 100 cm2 Electrode Scale
summary: Abstract The electrochemical reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) to acetate offers a promising route to upgrade waste carbon into a valuable product, yet scale-up beyond laboratory-scale cells remains underexplored. Here, we develop a 100 cm2
content: Abstract The electrochemical reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) to acetate offers a promising route to upgrade waste carbon into a valuable product, yet scale-up beyond laboratory-scale cells remains underexplored. Here, we develop a 100 cm2 CO electrolyzer in a membrane–electrode assembly (MEA) configuration using a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-guided approach. An anode-side serpentine flow field increases electrolyte velocity and anolyte residence time, facilitating oxygen removal and promoting further anodic oxidation of crossover ethanol to acetate. Combined with controlled reactor temperature, these effects improve acetate selectivity and operational stability. At 200 mA cm–2, the electrolyzer achieves a peak acetate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65% and stable operation for 140 h. These results identify anolyte residence time and reactor temperature as important reactor-level parameters impacting product distribution and stability, providing practical design guidance for selective and scalable CO-to-acetate electrolysis at the 100 cm2 scale.

title: Effects of Bamboo and Cocopeat-Based Cellulose Fibers on the Properties of Low-Carbon Mortar Containing Recycled Brick Aggregates
summary: Abstract This study investigates a low-carbon mortar in which 60% of the Portland composite cement (PCC) was replaced by fly ash (40%), limestone powder (15%), and metakaolin (5%), reinforced with alkali-treated bamboo cellulose (CB) or coc
content: Abstract This study investigates a low-carbon mortar in which 60% of the Portland composite cement (PCC) was replaced by fly ash (40%), limestone powder (15%), and metakaolin (5%), reinforced with alkali-treated bamboo cellulose (CB) or cocopeat cellulose (CCP), and containing recycled brick aggregate (RA) as a 20% replacement for natural sand. First, the CB dosage was varied from 0.5% to 2% of binder mass in plain cement mortar; 1.5% gave the highest 28-day compressive strength (29.9 MPa versus 25.3 MPa for the control) and was adopted for the second stage. Compressive (7 and 28 days) and flexural (28 days) strengths were measured, and hydration and microstructure were examined by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). The pozzolanic binder and the cellulose reduced the 7-day compressive strength by up to 32%. XRD indicated that both celluloses retarded early clinker hydration but promoted carboaluminate formation by 28 days, when the fiber mixtures reached 17.2–17.4 MPa, versus 16.6 MPa for the plain pozzolan mortar and 20.0 MPa for the control. The fiber mixtures containing RA reached 20.0–20.1 MPa. Bamboo cellulose gave the highest flexural strength, 5.61 MPa, 31% above the control and 14% above the plain pozzolan mortar, and SEM showed intact bamboo fibers bridging pores, whereas cocopeat cellulose left it practically unchanged (4.98 versus 4.90 MPa). The load–displacement curves showed that bamboo cellulose raised both the peak load and the displacement at failure of the pozzolan mortar, consistent with microcrack bridging, although no mixture showed a post-peak softening branch. RA reduced the flexural strength of the bamboo and cocopeat mixtures by 33% and 28%, to 3.78 and 3.59 MPa, respectively, below that of the control. The bamboo cellulose mortar with RA therefore offers the best balance of clinker reduction, waste valorization, and strength, with flexural performance as the main limitation.

title: Parallel growth without equilibrium: FinTech and climate finance in India
summary: Introduction In India, the fields of financial technology (FinTech) and climate finance have experienced significant growth over the past decade (2016–2025). However, there is limited national-level evidence regarding these connections. Thi
content: Introduction In India, the fields of financial technology (FinTech) and climate finance have experienced significant growth over the past decade (2016–2025). However, there is limited national-level evidence regarding these connections. This study examines the development and correlation of six FinTech indicators-volume of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions, value of UPI transactions, total digital payment transactions, financial inclusion index, Internet penetration rate, and FinTech funding-alongside three climate finance indicators: climate finance flows, green bond issuances, and investments in renewable energy. Methods This study utilized secondary data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), World Bank, and Statista, with additional data from the International Energy Agency (IEA), Climate Policy Initiative (CPI), and Climate Bonds Initiative (CBI) for the climate finance series from 2016 to 2025. The methodologies applied included descriptive statistics, compound annual growth rate (CAGR), trend regression, Pearson's correlation, and bivariate and log-linear regression analyses. To address common trends, the correlations were recalculated using year-on-year growth rates. Furthermore, unit root tests, autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds tests, and Granger causality tests were performed, incorporating adjustments for the multiple tests. Results The value and volume of UPI transactions demonstrated the most substantial growth among digital payment metrics, with compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) of 185.11% and 181.22%, respectively. This growth coincided with significant advancements in Internet penetration, financial inclusion, and climate finance metrics. At the level of analysis, all FinTech indicators, except for FinTech funding, show strong and statistically significant correlations with climate finance indicators. However, these correlations weakened and, with one exception, became statistically insignificant after adjusting for the growth rates. No evidence of cointegration was identified, and the sole statistically significant Granger causality finding did not remain significant after applying corrections for multiple tests. Discussion Evidence indicates that the observed parallel growth aligns with common temporal trends rather than demonstrating a definitive causal or equilibrium relationship between the two variables. Given that the study relies on ten annual observations, the analysis lacks the power to identify weaker or delayed linkages. Future research should utilize higher-frequency and state-level data. The findings advocate for sustained investment in digital financial infrastructure and financial inclusion as foundational elements of sustainable finance. Additionally, they underscore the necessity of targeted mechanisms to effectively direct FinTech activities towards climate-related projects.

title: Effects of infill pattern and infill density on the mechanical and sensing performance of direct ink writing three-dimensional-printed flexible strain sensors
source: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part E Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering
summary: Direct ink writing three-dimensional printing provides a versatile platform for fabricating flexible multi-functional polymer materials, helping to balance the requirements of flexible strain sensors, including sensitivity, sensing range, a
content: Direct ink writing three-dimensional printing provides a versatile platform for fabricating flexible multi-functional polymer materials, helping to balance the requirements of flexible strain sensors, including sensitivity, sensing range, and printability. In this work, a polydimethylsiloxane/carbon nanotube composite flexible strain sensor is developed using direct ink writing three-dimensional printing. The effects of carbon nanotube content (2–10 wt.%) on rheology and printability are investigated, and the mechanical and sensing performances of three infill patterns (grid, spiral, and honeycomb) are evaluated at three infill densities (30%, 40%, and 50%). Combining finite element simulations with experiments, 6 wt.% carbon nanotubes are identified as the optimal composition, balancing conductivity and printability. The grid pattern shows the best mechanical performance (maximum force of 17.2 N and displacement of 47.46 mm), while the spiral structure provides the most stable resistance signal. The grid structure is most sensitive to infill density: increasing infill density from 30% to 50% expands the strain range from 25% to 80% and increases the relative resistance change from 30% to 150%. The spiral and honeycomb structures exhibit a decreasing gauge factor with increasing infill density, whereas the grid structure reaches a peak gauge factor of 4.05 at 40% infill density. This study provides theoretical and experimental support for tailoring the structure–property relationship of direct ink writing printed flexible sensors.

title: Extracorporeal norepinephrine filtration is associated with increasing norepinephrine requirements during percutaneous hepatic perfusion with melphalan
summary: Abstract Chemosaturation with percutaneous hepatic perfusion (CS-PHP) using melphalan is frequently associated with profound hypotension, necessitating high-dose norepinephrine support. We investigated the potential of the extracorporeal ch
content: Abstract Chemosaturation with percutaneous hepatic perfusion (CS-PHP) using melphalan is frequently associated with profound hypotension, necessitating high-dose norepinephrine support. We investigated the potential of the extracorporeal chemofilter to remove circulating norepinephrine. In this prospective observational study, paired blood samples were obtained upstream and downstream of the extracorporeal filter during CS-PHP at predefined procedural timepoints. Norepinephrine was quantified using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Transfilter concentration reduction was assessed in conjunction with temporal changes in norepinephrine administration during the procedure. A total of ten CS-PHP procedures in eight patients were analyzed. This included the main test, for which one procedure was performed on each patient (n = 8), as well as an additional test on one patient, for which two additional procedures were performed to enable an intra-individual assessment of three consecutive procedures. Circulating norepinephrine concentrations increased during treatment, peaking upstream of the filter during active filtration. The filter reduced norepinephrine concentrations by a median of 91.3% after bypass closure and 91.9% during melphalan perfusion (both p = 0.008). Norepinephrine infusion rates increased from a median of 0.2 μg/kg/min after inferior vena cava occlusion to 0.6 μg/kg/min immediately after filter activation ( p < 0.01). These rates remained elevated throughout filtration before decreasing after completion of the procedure. The temporal relationship between transfilter concentration reduction of norepinephrine and a significant increase in norepinephrine administration suggests an association with hemodynamic effects during CS-PHP.

title: Breaking Micropore Confinement: N,S‐Codoped Carbon Nanocages With Lewis Acid–Base Synergy for High‐Energy Zinc‐Ion Hybrid Capacitors
summary: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZICs) offer high safety, low cost, and environmental friendliness, yet their energy density is severely constrained by poor desolvation of hydrated [Zn(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+ ions in carbon cathodes, impo
content: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZICs) offer high safety, low cost, and environmental friendliness, yet their energy density is severely constrained by poor desolvation of hydrated [Zn(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+ ions in carbon cathodes, imposing a rigid ∼0.86 nm micropore barrier. Here, we overcome this limitation through a Lewis acid–base synergy. We design hierarchical N,S‐codoped carbon nanocages (NSCNCs) via a BaSO 4 template‐mediated carbothermal reduction of ZIF‐8. In this system, electron‐poor sulfur acts as a Lewis soft base, while electron‐rich nitrogen acts as a Lewis hard base. The delocalized electron cloud of sulfur mitigates charge accumulation arising from isolated nitrogen doping, thereby enhancing the adsorption of [Zn(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+ . Concurrently, the cooperative Lewis base sites promote desolvation of hydrated zinc ions, reducing the critical micropore constraint to 0.79 nm, with the pyridinic N‐S configuration plays a dominant role. As a result, flexible quasi‐solid‐state ZICs based on NSCNCs deliver a high specific capacity of 176.6 mAh g −1 , a peak energy density of 148.8 Wh kg −1 , and a maximum power density of 4 kW kg −1 , while retaining 91.6% capacity after 10 000 cycles. This work establishes a new design paradigm in which electronic modulation and pore engineering work synergistically to overcome the long‐standing pore‐size limitation in zinc‐ion storage.

title: Data-Intensive and Ai-Mediated Anticipatory Governance: A Functional Typology of Institutional Capacity, Decision-Making, and Governance of Expertise
summary: Abstract Anticipatory Governance (AG) has emerged as a strategic approach for addressing uncertainty, systemic risk, and complexity in contemporary socio-technical systems. Governments and universities increasingly rely on Big Data, Data Sc
content: Abstract Anticipatory Governance (AG) has emerged as a strategic approach for addressing uncertainty, systemic risk, and complexity in contemporary socio-technical systems. Governments and universities increasingly rely on Big Data, Data Science, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support future-oriented public decision-making, yet the institutional and societal implications of these technologies remain conceptually fragmented. This article addresses this gap through a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) that examines how data-intensive and AI-enabled capabilities become embedded across foresight, knowledge creation, policy design, and policy assessment. Rather than treating the generic technical differences among Big Data, Data Science, and AI as the principal contribution, the study develops a functional typology that distinguishes infrastructural observation and evidentiary integration, analytical modeling and interpretation, and AI-enabled decision mediation. The review analyzes how these functions respond to uncertainty, non-linearity, interdependence, and feedback; reshape informational, analytical, and decisional capacity; and redistribute epistemic and decisional authority. The findings indicate a cumulative but non-deterministic movement from expanded observability, to analytical structuring, to increasingly mediated action. We conceptualize this movement as decisional embedding: the degree to which technological systems enter the institutional production of alternatives, prioritization, recommendation, adjustment, or execution. The contribution lies in showing that technological integration in anticipatory governance is not merely an increase in computational capability, but a reconfiguration of knowledge, judgment, responsibility, and authority. The article concludes with implications for accountable, contestable, and human-governed hybrid decision architectures.

title: Paired Synthesis of Polycyclic Constitutional Isomers via Solvent-Controlled Skeletal Disproportionation
summary: Abstract The paired synthesis of skeletally distinct polycyclic isomers has traditionally relied on separate and tailored synthetic designs, whereas their direct interconversion ranks among the most challenging transformations even within t
content: Abstract The paired synthesis of skeletally distinct polycyclic isomers has traditionally relied on separate and tailored synthetic designs, whereas their direct interconversion ranks among the most challenging transformations even within the realm of skeletal editing. However, we introduce that solvent‑controlled skeletal disproportionation, despite its scarcity, offers a convenient means to formally achieve such atom‑conserving skeletal reorganization. We exemplify this strategy with the copper‑catalyzed aerobic oxidation of readily available diarylamines, arylglyoxals, and alkenes: the addition of a few drops of hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) to a 1,2-dichloroethane (DCE, 2.0 mL) suffice to trigger a complete selectivity flip in product skeletons. This “butterfly effect” leverages a switchable synthesis of two non-interconvertible, yet pharmaceutically privileged isomers—6/5/6/6 tetracyclic indolo[1,2- a ]quinolines and 6/6 semi-saturated 2-acyl-1,4-dihydroquinolines, whose structural divergence is quantified by an average Tanimoto coefficient of 0.45. DFT calculations reveal that HFIP resolves the inherent regioselectivity conundrum between electron-rich arylamines and dicarbonyl electrophiles by reshaping the ring-size of competing transition states through hydrogen bonding, thereby redirecting chemoselectivity at the onset of the domino process. Biological evaluation across three cancer cell lines shows that this solvent-controlled skeletal divergence directly yields pronounced bioactivity bifurcation between the two isomers. This strategy allows the parallel expansion of compound libraries and would accelerate biological evaluation through a single synthetic design.

title: An open-source, high-torque, and portable hip exoskeleton for physically demanding locomotion
summary: Abstract Physically demanding jobs such as emergency services, construction, and military operations often require people to overcome challenging inclined terrain that increases their risk of injury and fatigue. Although exoskeletons are a
content: Abstract Physically demanding jobs such as emergency services, construction, and military operations often require people to overcome challenging inclined terrain that increases their risk of injury and fatigue. Although exoskeletons are a promising tool for assisting human locomotion, few devices have demonstrated substantial reductions in energy expenditure during physically demanding activities. Here, we present the Open-source, High-torque, and Portable (OpenHi-P) hip exoskeleton that reduces the absolute metabolic cost of walking, compared to not wearing the exoskeleton, by approximately twice that of any portable lower-limb exoskeleton and three times that of any portable hip exoskeleton in studies of healthy adults that met our inclusion criteria. Healthy young adults completed a multi-day experiment where human-in-the-loop optimization identified personalized exoskeleton assistance for each user during treadmill walking at 1 m/s and a 10° incline. Personalized assistance reduced the metabolic cost of incline walking by 2.1 W/kg (22%) compared to not wearing the exoskeleton ( n = 8). In a preliminary experiment that emulated a physically demanding firefighter training protocol, personalized assistance also reduced the cost of transport by 2.6 J/(m·kg) (20%) compared to not wearing the exoskeleton ( n = 4) during repeated bouts of inclined and loaded walking. In a preliminary outdoor experiment on uneven and inclined terrain, personalized assistance reduced the cost of transport by 1.6 J/(m·kg) (20%) and increased speed by 9% compared to not wearing the exoskeleton ( n = 4). This open-source, portable hip exoskeleton can substantially reduce the energetic cost of physically demanding tasks and accelerate exoskeleton development.

title: Coastal-adapted RSEI: a zonal adaptation index for ecological environment quality assessment in coastal zones
summary: Coastal zones, as composite ecosystems with significant land_sea interactions, require accurate ecological environment quality assessments for effective management. The Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) offers a simple and feasible "ho
content: Coastal zones, as composite ecosystems with significant land_sea interactions, require accurate ecological environment quality assessments for effective management. The Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) offers a simple and feasible "holistic modeling" tool for large_scale terrestrial ecological environment quality assessments. However, its coastal application faces challenges including mismatched indicator systems, missing water environmental information, and distorted stress responses, leading to assessment blind spots and misjudgments. In this study, we constructed a Coastal_Adapted Remote Sensing Ecological Index (CARSEI) following a zonal_adaptation strategy. We optimized the indicator system through ecological zoning and indicator adaptation, integrating the Cyanobacteria and Macrophytes Index (CMI), Turbid Water Index (TWI), and Soil Salinity Index (SI_T) to capture water quality signals and salinization stress. A spatial integration strategy was further applied to combine zonal assessment results into a continuous, seamless ecological quality map. We tested and validated CARSEI in the Yellow River Delta coastal zone of China. The results showed that CARSEI can comprehensively characterize ecological environment quality across the whole coastal zone, with an average accuracy of 86.89%, substantially higher than the original RSEI (66.72%). CARSEI also yielded higher PC1 explained variance for input indicators and consistent indicator trends along ecological quality grades, and it better captured the spatial differentiation of ecological quality along the land_sea gradient with robust adaptability across different ecosystem types. This CARSEI overcomes the limitations of the conventional "holistic modeling" framework and provides a more reliable tool for precise monitoring and management of coastal zone ecological environments.

title: Fe 3 O 4 , MnO 2 , and Na 2 S 2 O 8 amendments steer bacterial succession, fecal indicator regrowth, and humification during sewage sludge composting
summary: Abstract Sewage sludge with a low carbon-to-nitrogen ratio often fails to reach the thermophilic phase that drives bacterial succession and pathogen reduction during composting. Redox-active amendments are added to intensify composting, but
content: Abstract Sewage sludge with a low carbon-to-nitrogen ratio often fails to reach the thermophilic phase that drives bacterial succession and pathogen reduction during composting. Redox-active amendments are added to intensify composting, but how each one reshapes the bacterial community, and with it fecal indicator regrowth and humification, has not been compared under identical conditions. Fe₃O₄, MnO₂, and Na₂S₂O₈ were each applied at 1% (w/w) to one dewatered sludge feedstock and compared with an unamended control over 42 days of reactor composting. Only Na₂S₂O₈ produced a thermophilic phase, peaking at 68°C and remaining at or above 55°C for four days, which meets the United States time–temperature condition for in-vessel sludge composting. It shifted the day-5 community toward Firmicutes (52.4%) and Actinobacteriota (16.5%), enriched the cellulose-degrading thermophile Thermobifida about 25-fold relative to the control, and prevented the early regrowth of Escherichia–Shigella , which reached 5.8 to 13.4% of the bacterial community in the other treatments. Fe₃O₄ and MnO₂ instead favored Proteobacteria and Bacteroidota, and Fe₃O₄ more than doubled the Escherichia–Shigella bloom relative to the control. All amendments raised humic acid and the humic-to-fulvic acid ratio relative to the control, yet total humic substances fell by 17 to 24% in every treatment, least under MnO₂ and Na₂S₂O₈. Ratio-based maturity indices therefore indicated progressive humification while humic carbon was being lost. Amendment choice determines which degrader and indicator populations develop, and maturity certification for land application should include an absolute humic measure.

title: Comparison of efficacy and recurrence between carbon dioxide laser ablation and conventional curettage for the treatment of molluscum contagiosum in children
summary: Objective To compare the clinical efficacy, postoperative bleeding, and recurrence between carbon dioxide (CO₂) laser ablation and conventional curettage in the treatment of pediatric molluscum contagiosum. Methods A retrospective analysis
content: Objective To compare the clinical efficacy, postoperative bleeding, and recurrence between carbon dioxide (CO₂) laser ablation and conventional curettage in the treatment of pediatric molluscum contagiosum. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 120 children with molluscum contagiosum who attended the Dermatology Department of our hospital from September 2022 to September 2024. Patients were divided according to treatment modality into an observation group (CO₂ laser ablation, n = 60) and a control group (conventional curettage, n = 60). In the observation group, there were 25 males (41.7%) and 35 females (58.3%), with a mean age of 5.17 ± 2.96 years; in the control group, there were 23 males (38.3%) and 37 females (61.7%), with a mean age of 5.81 ± 3.01 years. No topical anesthetic was used in either group. However, the observation group received local infiltration anesthesia with 2% lidocaine 2 min before the procedure, whereas the control group underwent treatment without local anesthesia. The two groups were compared in terms of lesion clearance rate at 4 weeks post-treatment, persistent bleeding requiring additional hemostatic measures, individual adverse events, and recurrence at 6 months. Results The 4-week lesion clearance rate was 91.7% (55/60) in the observation group and 93.3% (56/60) in the control group, with no statistically significant difference ( P > 0.05). The incidence of persistent bleeding requiring additional hemostatic measures was 0% (0/60) in the observation group and 18.3% (11/60) in the control group ( P < 0.05). At the 6-month follow-up, recurrence occurred in 8 of 55 patients who had achieved complete clearance in the observation group (14.5%) and in 7 of 56 patients in the control group (12.5%), with no statistically significant difference between the groups ( P > 0.05). After adjustment for age, sex, disease duration, number of lesions, lesion location, and staged treatment, CO₂ laser ablation remained associated with a lower likelihood of persistent bleeding requiring additional hemostatic measures (aOR=0.05, 95% CI: 0.01–0.45, P = 0.008), whereas no independent association was observed with 4-week complete clearance or 6-month recurrence. Conclusion There were no statistically significant differences in clearance or recurrence during six months of follow-up between CO₂ laser ablation performed under local infiltration anesthesia and conventional curettage performed without anesthesia. The CO₂ laser group showed a lower incidence of persistent bleeding requiring additional hemostatic measures, whereas no statistically significant between-group differences were observed in the other recorded adverse events. No conclusions regarding procedural pain or treatment tolerability were drawn because the anesthesia protocols differed between the groups and validated pediatric pain or behavioral assessment tools were not used.

title: Multi-Slotted Hexagonal-Core Resonant Architecture for an Ultra- Efficient Graphene THz MIMO Antenna with Exceptional Diversity for 6G Wireless Systems
summary: Abstract This paper presents a low-profile graphene-based hexagonal-core resonator 1×2 multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for future sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems operating in the terahertz (THz) band. The
content: Abstract This paper presents a low-profile graphene-based hexagonal-core resonator 1×2 multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for future sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems operating in the terahertz (THz) band. The antenna consists of a graphene radiating patch on a flexible polyimide substrate with an annealed copper ground plane. The designed antenna is optimized by evolving its geometry while simultaneously optimizing the feed, substrate thickness, and ground thickness to improve impedance matching, gain, bandwidth, efficiency, isolation, and diversity performance. The patch resonates at 2.61, 3.50, 4.4531, and 6.25 THz, with impedance bandwidths of 0.6156, 0.7822, 0.815, and 1.5226 THz, respectively, and a reduced pattern of 1.827λ₀ × 0.783λ₀. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 13.1076 dB and a radiating efficiency of 99.038%. The designed antenna achieves port isolation greater than − 30.668 dB and − 67.4517 dB due to its orthogonal, anti-parallel feeding configuration. The envelope correlation coefficient is found to be insignificant (0.012) and diversity gain is 10 dB which shows satisfactory MIMO multiplicity functionality. The graphene patch radiator is conductive enough for electricity, and the extensible polyimide base and reduced surface area for THz operation allows for a loss-free deployment. We created and verified an analogous RLC circuit for the designed antenna using CST full-wave and ADS circuit simulators. The simulation resonances match the proposed equivalent RLC circuit model well. The designed antenna can be used for 6G communication, THz sensing, imaging, spectroscopy, the Internet of Things (IoT), emerging industrial applications, and innovative wireless technologies. The electromagnetic and circuit-level simulations provide insight into the resonance mechanism, impedance behavior, and frequency-selective response.

title: CFRP-Confined Pre-Damaged Recycled Aggregate Concrete Square Columns Under Axial Compression
summary: This study investigates the axial compressive performance of carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP)-confined pre-damaged recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) square columns. A total of 90 square specimens (100 mm × 100 mm × 300 mm) were tested
content: This study investigates the axial compressive performance of carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP)-confined pre-damaged recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) square columns. A total of 90 square specimens (100 mm × 100 mm × 300 mm) were tested under monotonic axial compression. Three key variables were considered: pre-damage level (D1 slight, D2 moderate, D3 severe), number of CFRP layers (1, 2, 3), and recycled fine aggregate (RFA) replacement ratio (0%, 50%, 100%), with the recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) replacement ratio fixed at 50%. Pre-damage was induced by pre-loading specimens to 0.9 fco on the ascending branch, peak stress fco, and 0.9 fco on the descending branch, respectively. Failure modes, full stress–strain responses, peak strength, peak strain, and CFRP hoop rupture strain were analysed. Test results show that CFRP confinement effectively restores and enhances both load-carrying capacity and deformability of pre-damaged RAC columns. Higher pre-damage level reduces post-strengthening peak strength. Increasing RFA replacement ratio decreases peak strength yet generally improves ductility. More CFRP layers produce higher strength and better deformation capacity. The average effective hoop rupture strain coefficient of CFRP for square specimens is 0.60. Empirical formulas for predicting peak strength and peak strain are proposed and developed from the present test database. This work provides experimental baseline data for retrofitting of damaged RAC structures using CFRP.

title: Continuous and Episodic Metal Exposures Disrupt Aquatic Insect Drift, Emergence, and Larval Survival
summary: Abstract Metal contamination in streams occurs under both chronic and episodic exposures, yet the effects of varying exposure on invertebrate life-history processes are poorly understood. We conducted two 9-day mesocosm experiments with ben
content: Abstract Metal contamination in streams occurs under both chronic and episodic exposures, yet the effects of varying exposure on invertebrate life-history processes are poorly understood. We conducted two 9-day mesocosm experiments with benthic macroinvertebrate communities to compare the effects of continuous and pulsed exposures to dissolved copper and zinc on larval drift, adult emergence, and benthic survival. Our goal was to evaluate how different exposure regimes alter in situ survival relative to the downstream movement of invertebrate prey resources and their dispersal to terrestrial consumers. Both exposure regimes significantly increased total larval drift (29–52% above controls), with Baetidae (Ephemeroptera) and Hydropsychidae (Trichoptera) dominating the drift response. Cumulative daily drift increased rapidly after initial exposure, with Baetidae under continuous exposure showing 3-fold higher drift relative to controls. Total emergence was higher under continuous exposure and was primarily driven by stimulated emergence in Chironomidae (Diptera). Total benthic abundance declined by 24–33% across treatments and was similar between exposure regimes, suggesting responses were more strongly associated with peak concentrations than cumulative dose. Together, our results show that continuous and episodic metal exposures can reduce benthic abundance while simultaneously increasing emigration through drift and emergence, thereby altering critical ecosystem services provided by aquatic insects.

title: Evaluation of two different 3D electrodes in the electrogenerative removal of tin(II) from chloride solutions using a flow-through reactor
summary: Abstract This study investigates the electrogenerative removal of tin(II) from SnCl 2 /NaCl solutions using carbon felt (CF) and reticulated vitreous carbon (RVC) cathodes coupled to a sacrificial zinc anode in a flow-through reactor. Cycli
content: Abstract This study investigates the electrogenerative removal of tin(II) from SnCl 2 /NaCl solutions using carbon felt (CF) and reticulated vitreous carbon (RVC) cathodes coupled to a sacrificial zinc anode in a flow-through reactor. Cyclic voltammetry on CF showed a cathodic wave and an anodic stripping peak attributable to Sn(II)/Sn(0) deposition and dissolution, superimposed on hydrogen evolution at negative potentials. The influence of the cathode material, initial Sn(II) concentration, dissolved oxygen and pH were examined. With 500 mg L − 1 of Sn(II), CF and RVC removed 99.6% and 98.6% of the dissolved Sn(II) concentration, respectively, after 4 h. CF performed slightly better than RVC at all sampling times, but the differences (1–4 percentage points) were within the experimental scatter. Nitrogen purging increased the 4 h removal from 82.3% to 99.6%, and removal was faster at pH 7 than at pH 4 or 5. The concentration decay followed apparent pseudo-first-order rather than zero-order kinetics (k 1 = 1.35 h − 1 for CF and 1.07 h − 1 for RVC), but the strong dependence of the rate on dissolved oxygen and pH indicates that the process was not controlled by mass transport alone. Scanning electron microscopy showed a cracked deposit on the CF fibres. Because the cell current, the tin mass balance and the composition of the deposit were not determined, the results establish efficient removal of dissolved Sn(II) but not the faradaic efficiency or the purity of the recovered tin; these quantities are identified as priorities for further work.

title: Strengthening microbial carbon and phosphorus co-limitation during subtropical forest restoration
summary: Abstract Aims Subtropical forest restoration is expected to alter soil microbial nutrient limitation, yet the successional trajectory and underlying drivers remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how microbial carbon (C) a
content: Abstract Aims Subtropical forest restoration is expected to alter soil microbial nutrient limitation, yet the successional trajectory and underlying drivers remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how microbial carbon (C) and phosphorus (P) limitation shift along a typical restoration chronosequence and identified the key biotic and abiotic factors influencing these shifts. Methods We selected a restoration chronosequence in subtropical China, spanning early Pinus massoniana plantation (PM), mid-stage P. massoniana–Lithocarpus glaber mixed forest (PL) and Choerospondias axillaris deciduous broadleaf forest (CA), and late-stage L. glaber evergreen broadleaf forest (LG). Soil enzyme activities, litter properties, soil physicochemical traits, and microbial biomass were measured. Microbial C and P limitation were quantified using vector analysis and threshold elemental ratio modeling, with Random Forest and PLS-PM used to identify key drivers. Results β-D-glucosidase (BG), β-N-acetylglucosaminidase (NAG), and acid phosphatase (ACP) exhibited a unimodal pattern peaking at CA, while cellobiohydrolase (CBH) declined continuously. Microbial C-P co-limitation intensified along succession, with LG exhibiting the highest vector length (0.79) and angle (80.04°). Litter nitrogen and litter C:N ratio emerged as primary predictors of C limitation, while microbial biomass N:P and C:N predicted P limitation. Soil properties exerted the strongest positive effect on C limitation but the strongest negative effect on P limitation. Conclusions Vegetation restoration was accompanied by a shift from weak C and moderate P limitation in early P. massoniana forests to severe C-P co-limitation in late broadleaved forests, a transition likely influenced by increased litter recalcitrance, stoichiometric imbalances, and plant-microbe competition. Therefore, managing litter quality and nutrient stoichiometry may help alleviate microbial co-limitation and sustain soil carbon sequestration.

title: Evaluation of outer membrane vesicle conjugated with either Poly-(lactide-co-glycolide) Microparticles or Chitosan nanoparticles or polyanhydride nanoparticles as an oral vaccine against poultry salmonellosis.
summary: Abstract Salmonella infections are a major concern in poultry, impacting both animal health and food safety. Conventional vaccines, including live attenuated and inactivated bacterins, often exhibit limited efficacy and short-lived immunity
content: Abstract Salmonella infections are a major concern in poultry, impacting both animal health and food safety. Conventional vaccines, including live attenuated and inactivated bacterins, often exhibit limited efficacy and short-lived immunity. This study aims to develop and evaluate a novel oral vaccine formulation incorporating poly-lactide-co-glycolide (PLG) microparticles conjugated with Salmonella Typhimurium outer membrane vesicles (OMVs). PLG microparticles were synthesized using the solvent evaporation technique and characterized for size (3654 ± 914.6 nm) and zeta potential (-12.3 mV).
