title: Optimizing Laser Tattoo Removal: Combination Strategies Based on Laser Principles and Biological Mechanisms
source: Journal of Aesthetic Surgery and Laser Science
summary: Since the introduction of Q-switched lasers, they have been widely regarded as the gold standard for tattoo removal. However, clinically significant complications, including scarring and hypopigmentation, continue to occur, and some tattoos
content: Since the introduction of Q-switched lasers, they have been widely regarded as the gold standard for tattoo removal. However, clinically significant complications, including scarring and hypopigmentation, continue to occur, and some tattoos remain resistant to complete clearance. In addition, tattoo removal typically requires multiple treatment sessions over a prolonged period, creating a considerable burden for patients. To overcome these limitations, numerous novel tattoo removal strategies have recently been investigated, including optimization of laser parameters, optical-clearing agents, the glass-slide technique, fractional carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) lasers, the R20 and R0 methods, Rapid Acoustic Pulse devices, picosecond lasers, microencapsulated tattoo inks, and imiquimod. This review narratively examines these emerging modalities based on the principles of laser physics and the biological mechanisms of tattoo removal. Contemporary tattoo removal strategies can be categorized according to three fundamental mechanisms: reduction of tissue scattering (increased effective penetration depth [EPD]), fragmentation of tattoo pigments, and enhancement of inflammation-mediated lymphatic clearance. Accordingly, current therapeutic approaches are classified into laser parameter optimization, optical-clearing agents, physical enhancement of EPD, multipass techniques, peak tensile stress optimization, tattoo ink modification, and immunomodulation. Based on these mechanisms, we propose a combination strategy consisting of fractional CO 2 laser pretreatment followed by multipass picosecond laser treatment (e.g., the R20 method) using optimized laser parameters.

title: Successful Management of Acute SMV occlusion in Pancreatic Conversion Surgery After Carbon Ion Radiotherapy: A rare complication and surgical pitfall
summary: Abstract Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often locally advanced at diagnosis, and multimodal strategies including conversion therapy are used to increase the chance of margin-negative resection. Carbon-ion radiotherap
content: Abstract Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often locally advanced at diagnosis, and multimodal strategies including conversion therapy are used to increase the chance of margin-negative resection. Carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIRT) enables strong local tumor control. However, the side effect of CIRT toward local vasculature has not yet been fully understood. Literatures regarding the surgical pitfall of vessel reconstruction after CIRT have barely been reported. Case presentation: A 45-year-old female initially diagnosed with locally advanced PDAC underwent 14 cycles of systemic chemotherapy followed by CIRT. After conversion, she underwent distal pancreatectomy with common hepatic artery divestment. Superior mesenteric vein (SMV) was partially trimmed due to dense adhesion between pancreas, resulting in a 1.5cm defect. The defect was repaired primarily with 5 − 0 Prolene suture. On postoperative day2, she developed high fever and rapid deterioration of liver function. Urgent contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated critical narrowing/near-occlusion of portal vein/SMV without definite thrombus. Emergent exploratory laparotomy showed severe intimal fibrosis of SMV causing luminal compromise. The SMV defect was reconstructed using patch augmentation. The patient achieved an R0 resection with final pathological finding revealing residual ductal adenocarcinoma in a fibrotic background (pT1b pN0). Her Liver function rapidly recovered after the venous reconstruction. Conclusions: This case shows a rare post-CIRT vascular complication with SMV to portal vein fibrosis causing acute hepatic ischemia after pancreatic cancer conversion surgery, which was successfully rescued with prompt patch augmentation. To avoid such complications in conversion surgery for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC), it is of crucial importance to take radiation-related vasculopathy into consideration during the manipulation of vasculature nearby to the previously CIRT-radiated area.

title: A study of the gas sensing performance of copper oxide - polyaniline nanocomposite thin films
source: Journal of the Turkish Chemical Society Section A Chemistry
summary: Three different nanostructures of cupric oxide with various shapes and sizes were successfully achieved using the same reaction parameters (heat, time, and the same concentration of NaOH) but with different cupric salts (copper nitrate trih
content: Three different nanostructures of cupric oxide with various shapes and sizes were successfully achieved using the same reaction parameters (heat, time, and the same concentration of NaOH) but with different cupric salts (copper nitrate trihydrate, copper chloride dihydrate, and copper carbonate monohydrate). Polyaniline was prepared using an oxidation polymerization reaction, and then it was combined with the three nanostructures of CuO to prepare CuO-polyaniline nanocomposite thin films to measure their gas sensing performances in ambient conditions. The chemical structures of the prepared materials were examined using XRD, FTIR, and FE-SEM. The gas-sensing measurements were performed using gas-sensing equipment with two gases: ammonia (as a reducing gas) and CO2 (as an oxidizing gas). The CuOa sample that had a nano spherical shape had the highest sensing preperformance, 90.2% after 30 seconds for ammonia gas, and 80.9% for CO2 gas after 45 seconds.

title: On-Surface Synthesis of Silicon Phthalocyanines
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Phthalocyanines are macrocyclic compounds with exceptional optical and electronic properties, making them indispensable in fields from organic electronics to catalysis. A significant advancement in this family is the development of
content: Abstract Phthalocyanines are macrocyclic compounds with exceptional optical and electronic properties, making them indispensable in fields from organic electronics to catalysis. A significant advancement in this family is the development of silicon phthalocyanines (SiPcs), where axial ligands suppress aggregation and enhance solubility, boosting their utility in optoelectronics and biomedicine. However, despite their importance, the formation and characterization of SiPcs on surfaces at the molecular level have remained largely unexplored. Here, we report the synthesis of SiPc species on Au(111). Using a combination of scanning tunnelling microscopy, noncontact atomic force microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that depositing a silicon phthalocyanine dichloride (SiPcCl2) precursor yields dispersed, flat-lying monochlorinated silicon phthalocyanines (SiPcCl) and SiPc species. Subsequent annealing induces complete dechlorination, forming a scattered layer of unprecedented SiPc compounds. Electronic structure measurements reveal a HOMO–LUMO gap of ∼1.5 eV and a Si(III) oxidation state. Additionally, our theoretical calculations reveal the successful reduction of N2O upon adsorption on the SiPc species. Altogether, this work establishes a novel strategy for on-surface synthesis of well-defined SiPc monolayers, opening avenues for their integration into surface-based devices and nanomaterials for optoelectronics, sensing, and catalysis.

title: Photochemistry of Pyruvate Embedded in Sodium Chloride Clusters
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
summary: Abstract During the aging of sea-salt aerosols, they undergo acid displacement reactions with inorganic and organic acids, which lead to the enrichment of the conjugate bases in the aerosol. Pyruvate is among the most abundant organic conju
content: Abstract During the aging of sea-salt aerosols, they undergo acid displacement reactions with inorganic and organic acids, which lead to the enrichment of the conjugate bases in the aerosol. Pyruvate is among the most abundant organic conjugate bases found in aged sea-salt aerosols. Here we study the photochemistry of charged pyruvate-doped sodium chloride clusters to better understand and characterize the absorption spectra and photochemistry of pyruvate in the actinic region. Cationic sodium chloride clusters doped with pyruvate are generated by electrospray ionization, mass selected in the cell of an FT-ICR mass spectrometer and irradiated with tunable laser light. Photofragments are quantified by mass spectrometry. Quantum chemical calculations are employed to identify possible cluster structures and model the absorption spectra. We observe relatively small photodissociation cross sections <1.3 × 10–19 cm2. Fragmentation proceeds mostly by loss of neutral cluster building blocks NaxClx and NaxClx–1CH3COCOO. Traces of NaxClx–2CO2+ products result from C–C bond photolysis. The absorption proceeds via an n → π* transition at the pyruvate dopant. Compared to free pyruvate, coordination to sodium ions blue shifts the band position by about 0.4 eV. Distortions of the O–C–C–O dihedral angle induce an additional blue shift of up to 0.7 eV. The presence of multiple cluster isomers therefore leads to multiple absorption maxima in the photodissociation spectra over a wide wavelength range. Evidence for singlet–triplet transitions is found at wavelengths >360 nm.

title: Acid-Catalyzed Degradation of Murexide: An Accessible Experimental and Computational Approach
summary: Acid-catalyzed degradation limits the stability of many organic molecules, and its study often requires advanced instruments. This study shows how cyclic voltammetry, UV-vis spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, av
content: Acid-catalyzed degradation limits the stability of many organic molecules, and its study often requires advanced instruments. This study shows how cyclic voltammetry, UV-vis spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, available in most laboratories, can be combined to study such reactions, using murexide as a model system. The degradation of murexide, measured by the decrease in its cyclic voltammetric peak current, followed pseudo-first-order kinetics. The apparent rate constants were 0.0058, 0.0119, and 0.0343 min⁻¹, with half-lives of 119, 58, and 20 min at pH 4.9, 3.0, and 2.0, respectively. The UV-vis rate constant at pH 4.9 agreed with the electrochemical value. The large peak separation (730–742 mV) indicated slow electron transfer at the Pt electrode, with a transfer coefficient (α) of 0.32 and a heterogeneous electron transfer rate constant (k⁰) of (5.2 ± 0.2) × 10⁻4 cm s⁻¹. DFT calculations showed that protonation at the C5 carbon (calculated pKa ≈ 3.1) opens a low-energy hydrolysis pathway to alloxan and uramil. TDDFT analysis showed that the loss of the absorption at 510 nm is due to dis-ruption of the C5–N–C5 conjugation. This combined approach provides an accessible framework for studying acid-catalyzed degradation in research and teaching settings.

title: Heterostructured BiVO4/g-C3N4 Semiconductor Nanomaterials for Enhanced Visible-Light-Driven Degradation and Mineralization of Emerging Water Contaminants
summary: The persistence of emerging contaminants (ECs)—including pharmaceuticals, endocrine-disrupting compounds, and synthetic dyes—in aquatic ecosystems poses a critical threat to environmental and public health due to their resistance to convent
content: The persistence of emerging contaminants (ECs)—including pharmaceuticals, endocrine-disrupting compounds, and synthetic dyes—in aquatic ecosystems poses a critical threat to environmental and public health due to their resistance to conventional wastewater treatment processes. Semiconductor photocatalysis offers a sustainable, solar-driven pathway for complete pollutant mineralization, yet single-component photocatalysts suffer from rapid electron–hole recombination and limited visible-light utilization. In this study, we report the rational design and synthesis of a two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) Z-scheme heterostructured bismuth vanadate/graphitic carbon nitride (BiVO4/g-C3N4) nanocomposite via a facile hydrothermal–calcination coupling strategy. Structural and morphological characterization using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) confirms the intimate interfacial contact between monoclinic scheelite BiVO4 nanoparticles and ultrathin g-C3N4 nanosheets. Optical and photoelectrochemical analyses—including UV–Vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS), photoluminescence (PL), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)—demonstrate extended visible-light harvesting up to 540 nm, suppressed charge-carrier recombination, and accelerated interfacial charge transfer. Under simulated visible-light irradiation (λ ≥ 420 nm), the optimized 15 wt% BiVO4/g-C3N4 heterojunction achieved 96.4% degradation of tetracycline hydrochloride within 90 min, exhibiting an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant (k = 0.0368 min-1) that is 4.3-fold and 5.8-fold higher than pristine g-C3N4 and bare BiVO4, respectively. Total organic carbon (TOC) analysis confirmed 81.2% mineralization efficiency, while radical scavenging and electron spin resonance (ESR) experiments verified that superoxide (•O2-) and hydroxyl (•OH) radicals serve as the primary reactive oxidative species, substantiating a direct Z-scheme charge-transfer mechanism. Furthermore, the composite retained greater than 91% of its catalytic activity over five consecutive recycling runs, demonstrating strong structural stability for practical water remediation.

title: Maskless Femtosecond-Laser Micromachining of Recessed Gates in β-Ga2O3 MOSFETs
summary: Abstract Maskless patterning routes that enable rapid, flexible prototyping of ultra-wide-bandgap transistors are highly desirable for accelerating the development of beta-phase gallium oxide (β-Ga2O3) electronics. Here, we present the firs
content: Abstract Maskless patterning routes that enable rapid, flexible prototyping of ultra-wide-bandgap transistors are highly desirable for accelerating the development of beta-phase gallium oxide (β-Ga2O3) electronics. Here, we present the first demonstration of maskless femtosecond-laser micromachining (fs-LM) utilized as a lithography-free approach to fabricate recessed gates in β-Ga2O3 MOSFETs. Controlled gate-recess depths are realized directly within the epitaxial channel and incorporated into functional transistors. Cross-sectional HR-TEM and EDS depth profiling within the gate region confirm the structural integrity of the underlying layer stack and show conformal HfO2 gate dielectric deposition over the laser-processed surface. However, SEM and AFM analyses reveal void formation and surface roughness within the recesses, which contribute to an elevated drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL ≈ 716 mV/V) compared to a conventionally fabricated ICP-RIE reference device (DIBL ≈ 369 mV/V). While further optimization of the laser and post-processing parameters is required to mitigate laser-induced defects and match the electrical performance of plasma-etched controls, these results demonstrate maskless fs-laser micromachining as a prospective route for rapid device prototyping and low-volume fabrication of recessed-gate β-Ga2O3 MOSFETs.

title: Screening of benzoic acid degrading bacteria and their alleviating effects on tomato autotoxicity
summary: Abstract The autotoxicity stress resulting from the accumulation of benzoic acid significantly restricts the sustainable development of facility tomatoes. In this study, two high-efficiency benzoic acid-degrading strains, Peribacillus frigo
content: Abstract The autotoxicity stress resulting from the accumulation of benzoic acid significantly restricts the sustainable development of facility tomatoes. In this study, two high-efficiency benzoic acid-degrading strains, Peribacillus frigoritolerans FJAT-49528 and Peribacillus simplex FJAT-53808, were screened. Both of these strains can effectively degrade benzoic acid and exhibited broad-spectrum degradation capabilities for various phenolic acid autotoxic substances. Additionally, both strains exhibited plant growth-promoting functions, including IAA production, organic phosphorus solubilization, and siderophore production. Whole-genome analysis and annotation identified key genes involved in multiple phenolic acid degradation pathways in the two strains. These genes are involved in the catabolism of various phenolic acid substrates such as benzoic acid, protocatechuic acid and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid. Potted experiments showed that the two Bacillus strains significantly alleviated benzoic acid-induced stress in tomato plants. On the 10th day under benzoic acid stress, compared with the control group, the POD activity in the benzoic acid group decreased by 74.48%, while the T1 and T2 treatment groups showed increases of 13.38% and 11.30% respectively. The PPO activity in the T1 group reached 401.33 U/g at the same time, which was 36.2% higher than the benzoic acid group. By day 30, the MDA content in the T1 and T2 groups was reduced by 16.5% and 13.6% respectively compared to the control group, effectively suppressing membrane lipid peroxidation damage. Overall, these findings show that Peribacillus frigoritolerans FJAT-49528 and Peribacillus simplex FJAT-53808 are potential benzoic acid-degrading strains in continuous cropping application.

title: Unravelling bacteriochlorophyll biosynthesis in the uncultured Roseilinea
summary: Filamentous anoxygenic phototrophs (FAPs) of the Chloroflexota phylum are abundant members of microbial mat communities. All isolated and culturable FAPs are found in a single class within this phylum, but metagenomic studies of hot spring
content: Filamentous anoxygenic phototrophs (FAPs) of the Chloroflexota phylum are abundant members of microbial mat communities. All isolated and culturable FAPs are found in a single class within this phylum, but metagenomic studies of hot spring communities from around the world have indicated that phototrophic members of an additional class may exist, which have so far eluded cultivation for study in the laboratory. Metagenome-assemble genomes (MAGs) of these "Candidatus Roseilinea" species all lack genes encoding the central enzymes of bacteriochlorophyll biosynthesis common to all FAPs and to the seven other diverse phyla of anoxygenic phototrophs, which could indicate that these organisms are no longer phototrophic or that they employ a novel set of enzymes to generate chlorophyllide from magnesium protoporphyrin IX. Here we demonstrate that the five terminal enzymes of bacteriochlorophyll biosynthesis encoded in the MAG of Japanese hot spring-dwelling "Ca. Roseilinea sp. NK_OTU-006" are active and restore pigment production and phototrophic growth in a set of mutants of the model purple phototrophic bacterium Rhodobacter sphaeroides. While many organisms are known to require exogenous supply of metabolically costly modified tetrapyrroles such as vitamin B12 for growth, the retained function of the tested Roseilinea enzymes and the restriction of these species to dense microbial mats leads us to hypothesise that these organisms may be the first examples of bacteriochlorophyll auxotrophs. We suggest that Roseilinea scavenge pigment precursors and/or breakdown products excreted by other members of the mat to generate the mature bacteriochlorophyll they require to perform phototrophy, an exchange that we demonstrate can occur between Rhodobacter sphaeroides mutants. We further suggest that future attempts to isolate Roseilinea species should employ the exogenous supplementation of (bacterio)chlorophyllide into culture medium.

title: MoveChain: Real Implementation of Multi-Sensor Supply Chain Monitoring Using Move on Sui and IOTA
source: Distributed Ledger Technologies Research and Practice
summary: In the modern era, supply chain management faces challenges in ensuring product authenticity and preventing counterfeiting. Blockchain technology, combined with Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring, offers a promising approach through immuta
content: In the modern era, supply chain management faces challenges in ensuring product authenticity and preventing counterfeiting. Blockchain technology, combined with Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring, offers a promising approach through immutable tracking and real-time verification of product conditions. This paper presents MoveChain, a Move-based smart contract library for automated supply chain ownership management with multi-sensor IoT integration. We implement MoveChain on two Move-compatible blockchain platforms (Sui and IOTA) and validate the solution through real-world testing with physical hardware. The system supports simultaneous monitoring of multiple environmental parameters (temperature, humidity, GPS location) with configurable thresholds and automatic compliance verification. Evaluation follows a two-phase approach: laboratory testing with cross-platform deployment, and field validation on a 2-kilometer public delivery route with deliberate violation scenarios. Results demonstrate successful detection of environmental and routing anomalies within 30 seconds, with multi-channel alerting through blockchain recording, Telegram notifications, and local logging. Cross-platform analysis reveals cost, not scalability, as the primary trade-off: IOTA provides lower costs for most functions including sensor updates, making it more economical for IoT-intensive scenarios, while update latency showed no clear scaling trend with sensor count on either platform within the tested range (1–200 sensors per product). The GPS recording strategy reduces transaction overhead while maintaining complete audit trails. Field testing with physical IoT devices validates that Move's resource-oriented programming model can support supply chain applications under real-world conditions including vehicular transport, variable network connectivity, and GPS signal variability.

title: Thermocatalytic decomposition of R134a and structural characterization of ceramic CaO-CeO2 catalysts in a two-step reaction system
summary: In this study, a two-step thermocatalytic decomposition system using CaO-CeO 2 catalysts based on ceramic oxides was proposed for syngas production from the fluorocarbon refrigerant R134a. In Step-1, R134a and H 2 O reacted with CaO at high
content: In this study, a two-step thermocatalytic decomposition system using CaO-CeO 2 catalysts based on ceramic oxides was proposed for syngas production from the fluorocarbon refrigerant R134a. In Step-1, R134a and H 2 O reacted with CaO at high temperature to produce CO 2 , accompanied by the conversion of CaO into CaF 2 and CaCO 3 . In Step-2, the generated CO 2 further reacted with CeO2 and H 2 O to form CO and H 2 . Catalyst characterization revealed that CaO acted as a reactive center for fluorine capture, with the CaO-to-CaF 2 conversion-related intensity ratio reaching its highest value of 1.81 under the 0.001 SLPM/600°C condition. In contrast, CeO 2 maintained its mesoporous structure and structural stability, exhibiting only minimal crystallite growth of 0.1–3.1% at 400–600°C, while CaO showed substantial crystallite growth of 201–351% due to sintering. Furthermore, CeO 2 generated oxygen vacancies that facilitated CO 2 reduction, with the lattice parameter associated with Ce 3 + formation reaching 5.4232 Å. By translating these catalyst structural variations into mathematical kinetics, the numerical model of temperature-dependent syngas production behavior was developed. Consequently, this study clarifies the catalyst degradation behavior during thermocatalytic refrigerant decomposition and successfully predicts the syngas yield profiles, contributing to the optimized design of sustainable refrigerant resource recovery systems.

title: Incorporation of Spirulina and Moringa into Dark Chocolate: Physicochemical and Nutritional Properties, Activated Carbon Deodorization, Sensory Quality, And In Vitro Gut Microbiota Responses
source: Library, Museums and Press - UDSpace (University of Delaware)
summary: Dark chocolate bar is a confectionery widely consumed by a large population around the world. However, it is associated with a series of problems, including sustainability, supply chain, and climate change. These concerns are prompting inte
content: Dark chocolate bar is a confectionery widely consumed by a large population around the world. However, it is associated with a series of problems, including sustainability, supply chain, and climate change. These concerns are prompting interest in alternative ingredients. Spirulina and Moringa are novel food ingredients rich in protein, minerals, and antioxidant compounds. Besides the nutritional benefits, they are also more environmentally friendly compared to cacao trees. However, the strong off-flavor of Spirulina affects its sensory properties and limits consumer acceptance. This thesis investigated the development, sensory optimization, and potential gut health benefits of Spirulina and Moringa chocolate through three interconnected studies. In the first study, Spirulina and Moringa were used to replace cocoa powder at different concentrations to produce dark chocolate bars. The physicochemical and nutritional properties were evaluated. The result showed that the protein content increased (172%), and the carbohydrate content decreased (28%) when the Spirulina concentration increased from 0% to 100%, and led to a shift of the mineral profile. As Spirulina concentration increased, the potassium, magnesium, zinc, and copper content decreased, while phosphorus and iron content were elevated. For Moringa chocolate, the incorporation of Moringa decreased the protein content (12.73%) when the Moringa concentration increased from 0% to 75%, and the carbohydrate content was not affected. The chocolate with Spirulina and Moringa had a darker color compared to the regular dark chocolate. The hardness level of Spirulina chocolate also elevated from 25.06 to 33.28 kg, while the hardness of Moringa chocolate decreased to 13.77 kg. Both Spirulina and Moringa chocolates showed an increase in particle size when the substitution level increased. The total phenolic content gradually decreased from 24.33 to 1.07 mg GAE/g, and the DPPH quenching activity dropped from 234.42 to 28.22 mg TE/g as the Spirulina concentration increased from 0% to 100%. The rheological properties were also affected. The viscosity of the chocolate samples with Spirulina and Moringa was higher, and the yield stress also increased. A total of 31 volatiles were detected in Spirulina chocolate using SPME GC-MS. Aldehydes, alcohols, and hydrocarbons from Spirulina contributed to the grassy, fishy, earthy, and mushroom odor. The pre-treatment method with activated carbon (AC) effectively adsorbed some off-flavor compounds, lowered the peak area% of some targeted volatiles, and improved the chocolates’ sensory properties. To evaluate the effects of Spirulina and Moringa incorporated dark chocolate, In Vitro fecal fermentation was performed alongside raw ingredient powders and an inulin positive control. Fermented gut microbiota community composition was characterized by 16S rRNA sequencing. Alpha-diversity analysis showed that Shannon diversity and evenness were significantly higher in all ch

title: B‐Doped g‐C 3 N 4 /MgIn 2 S 4 S‐Scheme Heterojunction for Dual‐Functional Photocatalysis: Pollutant Degradation and CO 2 Reduction
summary: The rational design of heterojunction photocatalytic system with suppressed charge recombination and maximized solar energy utilization is critical for water purification and solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion. Herein, we report the ration
content: The rational design of heterojunction photocatalytic system with suppressed charge recombination and maximized solar energy utilization is critical for water purification and solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion. Herein, we report the rational construction of an S‐scheme heterojunction comprising B‐doped g‐C 3 N 4 (BCN) and MgIn 2 S 4 (MIS) via a facile self‐assembly strategy. Excellent bifunctional photocatalytic performance was achieved by the optimized BCN/MIS‐7 composite. Specifically, the RhB degradation efficiency reached 92.12% after 120 min of visible illumination, with a rate constant of 0.0715 min −1 —6.74‐fold higher than that of pristine CN. Meanwhile, the CO evolution from CO 2 reduction under the same light conditions was 26.48 μmol·h −1 ·g −1 , markedly outperforming the separate precursors. The integration of narrow‐bandgap MgIn 2 S 4 extended the spectral response via sub‐bandgap photon excitation, substantially enhancing visible‐light harvesting. The photoelectrochemical measurements and EPR spectroscopy revealed that the improved performance stems from the S‐scheme charge‐transfer mechanism, which exerted a dual function: it accelerated the interface separation of photo‐excited carriers and, at the same time, preserved the strong reductive capability of MIS and the pronounced oxidation activity of BCN. The findings of this work present a promising strategy toward the fabrication of high‐performance and stable S‐scheme heterojunctions derived from g‐C 3 N 4 .

title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
summary: Abstract Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies ag
content: Abstract Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). Here we present high-resolution neodymium isotope (ε Nd ) records from a depth transect in the equatorial Atlantic over the iNHG. We find a persistent latitudinal and depth gradient in neodymium isotope values in the deep Atlantic during the Late Pliocene, absent in the Early Pleistocene, indicating an expansion of NADW extent over the iNHG. In contrast, our reconstruction suggests very little glacial-interglacial variability in NADW extent during both the Late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene. These results suggest deep-water circulation was substantially different during a warm climate state, with implications for the role of NADW formation during major climate transitions and its future stability.

title: Minimalist catalyst for excellent tacticity: Stereocontrolled radical polymerization with Lewis acids
summary: Stereoregular vinyl polymers are made by coordination or anionic polymerization, whereas radical polymerization, the dominant industrial route, offers little stereocontrol. We report a simple Lewis acid–mediated reversible addition–fragment
content: Stereoregular vinyl polymers are made by coordination or anionic polymerization, whereas radical polymerization, the dominant industrial route, offers little stereocontrol. We report a simple Lewis acid–mediated reversible addition–fragmentation chaintransfer polymerization: with only 3.3 mol% samarium Lewis acid, polymerization of more than a dozen functionalized acrylamides reaches up to 97% m diad selectivity, the highest tacticity in homogeneous radical polymerization of a commodity monomer. A single samarium center coordinates the radical chain end and the incoming monomer, fixing its addition orientation. The isotactic polymer resists backbone degradation in acid and base, and in hydrogels, isotactic and atactic chains reinforce the networks differently. This method provides a minimalist route to diversify polymer properties from one monomer feedstock and offers a new strategy for stereocontrolled radical polymerization.

title: Valorization of Ivorian gold tailings as partial cement replacement in mortar: Mechanical performance and leaching behavior
summary: Gold mining is a key sector of the Ivorian economy but generates large quantities of tailings that raise important environmental, economic, and social challenges. This study explores their reuse as secondary raw materials in construction ma
content: Gold mining is a key sector of the Ivorian economy but generates large quantities of tailings that raise important environmental, economic, and social challenges. This study explores their reuse as secondary raw materials in construction materials. Four gold mining residues, differing by mine of origin and processing route (washing or cyanidation residues) were characterized and incorporated at 50% replacement in cement mortars. Their physicochemical, microstructural, mechanical, and environmental performance was assessed. The residues are mainly composed of fine quartz-rich particles (D 80 < 180 µm) and exhibit low reactivity, as confirmed by R3 and pozzolanic index methods. This limited reactivity leads to reduced formation of hydration products, as measured by Thermogravimetric analysis, particularly hydrates (< 6.5%), compared to the reference mortar (hydrate = 9.0%). Consequently, compressive strengths are lower for tailings-based mortars (about 21–14 MPa at 28 days) than for the reference (41 MPa). Leaching tests confirm compliance with Soil Quality Decree thresholds, indicating no major environmental restriction for reuse. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of gold mining tailings as secondary raw materials for use in construction applications.

title: Interfacial control of CO 2 mineralization and Ni recovery: the roles of silicate polymerization degree and nickel-bearing amount
summary: -pressure conditions. The results of carbonation-only control experiments revealed that increasing Ni content reduced the extent of carbonation in both Ni-bearing forsterite and Ni-bearing enstatite. Furthermore, Ni-bearing enstatite exhibi
content: -pressure conditions. The results of carbonation-only control experiments revealed that increasing Ni content reduced the extent of carbonation in both Ni-bearing forsterite and Ni-bearing enstatite. Furthermore, Ni-bearing enstatite exhibited a lower carbonation extent than Ni-bearing forsterite. This difference was attributed to the chain silicate structure of enstatite, which is more resistant to breakdown than the isolated tetrahedra structure of forsterite, causing slow dissolution and reducing carbonation. The concurrent carbonation-sulfidation results indicated that sulfidation partially decreased the extent of carbonation because Ni was converted to Ni-sulfide, which does not participate in carbonation. We found that in both minerals, the sulfidation extent decreased as the Ni content increased, and it was highest for 1.7 wt% Ni-bearing forsterite. Thus, a higher initial Ni content did not translate into a higher fractional Ni extraction by sulfidation. These findings highlight the intricate interplay between carbonation and sulfidation in ultramafic rocks and suggest that similar behaviors may occur in other ultramafic rocks with comparable structures.

title: Estimating agricultural development resilience against hunger in the 21 century
summary: Achieving the Sustainable Development Goal of Zero Hunger is becoming more difficult because of growing uncertainties such as climate change and geopolitical conflicts. This study develops a global index, Anti-Hunger Agricultural Developmen
content: Achieving the Sustainable Development Goal of Zero Hunger is becoming more difficult because of growing uncertainties such as climate change and geopolitical conflicts. This study develops a global index, Anti-Hunger Agricultural Development Resilience (AHADR), to measure the resilience of agricultural systems against hunger. AHADR fluctuated throughout 2001–2019 but improved overall, whereas regional inequality in AHADR increased. Most countries exhibit either low-AHADR agglomeration (11.32%) or high-AHADR agglomeration (59.41%). Countries categorized as having medium, high, or very high AHADR tend to experience more dynamic transitions between resilience states, whereas countries with low AHADR usually remain in stable, lower-level resilience states. Extreme droughts have a detrimental effect on AHADR, while the relationships of livestock and fertilizer use with AHADR may be nonlinear.

title: Resource Rich but Risky Patches: Primary Productivity Triggers Intraguild Predation of Insects by Livestock in Oak Savannas
summary: Theoretical models on intraguild predation (predation among organisms within the same trophic level, intraguild predation) assume a spatially heterogeneous primary productivity. Hence, resource-rich patches could attract both predators and
content: Theoretical models on intraguild predation (predation among organisms within the same trophic level, intraguild predation) assume a spatially heterogeneous primary productivity. Hence, resource-rich patches could attract both predators and prey, yet prey may suffer higher predation rates. This theoretical framework can be extended to antagonistic, size‑asymmetric interactions among herbivores in which negative effects arise not only from predation but also from other non‑trophic mechanisms. We analyzed antagonistic interactions driven by primary productivity among oak-defoliating Lepidoptera and livestock in Iberian oak savannas. Caterpillars defoliate oak canopies, but exclusion experiments have shown that free-range livestock predate/trample soil-pupating Lepidoptera. We used fine-scale multispectral imagery to assess the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) of oak canopies and surrounding pasture. Then, we tracked the visits of GPS-collared sheep in each tree of the study site, where we sampled oak-defoliating Lepidoptera caterpillars. NDVI of canopies and pasture were spatially correlated, and sheep grazed more often at more productive patches. Negative top-down effects (increased predation/trampling) outweighed positive bottom-up ones (increased food availability) in soil-pupating Lepidoptera, whose abundance was lower in productive pastures due to higher sheep activity. In contrast, species pupating in leaves/branches were more abundant in those trees, benefiting from increased productivity while avoiding predation, as their pupae were inaccessible to sheep. Irrespective of the underlying mechanisms (direct predation and/or trampling), our results show that assessments of antagonistic interactions between large herbivores and insects must incorporate landscape‑level variation in productivity and the movement abilities of both guilds.

title: Integrated placental metabolomic and lipidomic profiling reveals class-specific lipid remodelling in severe preeclampsia
summary: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity, yet the placental metabolic changes associated with disease severity remain poorly defined. We combined untargeted metabolite profiling with targeted quantification of 173
content: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity, yet the placental metabolic changes associated with disease severity remain poorly defined. We combined untargeted metabolite profiling with targeted quantification of 173 lipid species across 12 classes in placentas from normotensive ( n = 9), non-severe preeclamptic ( n = 5) and severe preeclamptic ( n = 7) pregnancies. Of 43 preselected metabolite features, four differed between control and severe preeclampsia, three of them lipid-related, whereas metabolites of central carbon metabolism were unchanged. In the lipidome, 87 species differed between control and severe preeclampsia after false-discovery-rate correction, but none between control and non-severe preeclampsia. The pattern was class-specific and bidirectional: all 42 membrane phospholipid species that differed were reduced, as were five of six ceramide species, whereas all 28 differing triacylglycerol and cholesteryl ester species were increased. Triacylglycerol was the most extensively affected class and the only class that also differed between non-severe and severe preeclampsia. Most class-level differences persisted after adjustment for gestational age at delivery. Severe preeclampsia is thus accompanied by a coordinated loss of membrane phospholipids and ceramide together with neutral lipid accumulation in the placenta; because severe disease and fetal growth restriction coincided, their contributions could not be separated.

title: Enhancement of ceramic surface insulating performance enabled by APPJ film deposition with different precursor feedthrough positions
summary: Abstract Ceramics has emerged as a critical material in electrical insulating parts due to its superior thermal conductivity and chemical stability, while further reducing its surface energy and improving insulating performance simultaneous
content: Abstract Ceramics has emerged as a critical material in electrical insulating parts due to its superior thermal conductivity and chemical stability, while further reducing its surface energy and improving insulating performance simultaneously remains a challenge. In this study, a silicon film is deposited on the ceramic surface by an Ar/HMDSO APPJ to reduce surface energy, enhance surface resistance and flashover voltage. The precursor HMDSO is injected into APPJ from two distinct positions around the grounded electrode: upstream injection (Injection Mode 1) and downstream injection (Injection Mode 2). The effects of the precursor feedthrough position on discharge characteristics, film performances and their stability are investigated. It is indicated that decrement of surface energy and increment of flashover voltage are achieved simultaneously for ceramics treated by two injection modes, with slight variations in the stability. Moreover, the surface resistance under Mode 1 is 27.6% higher than under Mode 2. It is revealed by optical emission spectroscopy (OES), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results, and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) that the species activity in DBD region for APPJ with Mode 1 is higher than Mode 2, resulting in the deposition of a denser cross-linking film. This study provides a reference for the design of APPJ electrode structure for film deposition.

title: Co-firing performance of pellets prepared from rice husk, rice straw, and lignite in a circulating fluidized bed combustor
summary: This study evaluates the co-firing performance of rice husk (RH) and rice straw (ST) pellets with and without 25% lignite addition in a 350 kWₜₕ circulating fluidized bed boiler. Four pellet formulations (RH100, RH75+CP25, ST100, and ST75+C
content: This study evaluates the co-firing performance of rice husk (RH) and rice straw (ST) pellets with and without 25% lignite addition in a 350 kWₜₕ circulating fluidized bed boiler. Four pellet formulations (RH100, RH75+CP25, ST100, and ST75+CP25) were investigated in terms of mechanical properties, thermal reactivity, and gaseous emissions. RH100 exhibited a higher vertical compressive strength than ST100 (21.55 vs 13.00 MPa), whereas ST100 showed higher abrasive resistance (98.02 vs 94.55%). The addition of 25% lignite caused modest reductions in compressive strength and abrasive resistance, while impact resistance remained high for all formulations (99.79-99.98%). Thermogravimetric analysis showed higher combustion reactivity for the pure biomass pellets than for the corresponding lignite-containing blends. Ignition temperatures increased from 221 to 245°C for the RH-based formulations and from 216 to 220°C for the ST-based formulations after lignite addition. ST100 exhibited the highest combustion indices, with Di = 0.044, S = 1.57 × 10⁻¹⁵, and C = 3.68 × 10⁻¹⁰. During CFBB combustion at 850±10°C, lignite addition increased CO concentrations from 1083.55 to 1803.96 mg/Nm³ for the RH-based fuels and from 1488.17 to 2832.42 mg/Nm³ for the ST-based fuels. SO₂ was not detected for the pure biomass pellets but reached 29.21 and 64.30 mg/Nm³ for RH75+CP25 and ST75+CP25, respectively, while NO emissions remained within 8.01–13.77 mg/Nm³. Overall, the results demonstrate a clear trade-off associated with 25% lignite incorporation: pellet mechanical integrity was largely retained, whereas combustion reactivity decreased and CO and SO₂ emissions increased. Among the tested formulations, the pure biomass pellets provided the most favorable overall balance of mechanical integrity, combustion reactivity, and gaseous emissions.

title: Cyclometalated Half‐Sandwich Iridium Complexes With NHC Ligand: Preparation, Structure, and Catalytic Activity in Amide Synthesis and Hydrogenation of Ketones
summary: ABSTRACT Four air‐stable cyclometalated half‐sandwich iridium complexes, based on N‐heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) and bearing the general formula [Cp*IrCl(C^C*)], were successfully synthesized with satisfactory yields. These stable iridium c
content: ABSTRACT Four air‐stable cyclometalated half‐sandwich iridium complexes, based on N‐heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) and bearing the general formula [Cp*IrCl(C^C*)], were successfully synthesized with satisfactory yields. These stable iridium complexes exhibited good catalytic performance in the hydrogenation of ketones and the synthesis of amides. Under the catalysis of complex 2b , a series of ketones and amides with diverse substituents were obtained in high yields through the hydrogenation of ketones and the amidation of aldehydes with NH 2 OH·HCl. The resulting cyclometalated half‐sandwich iridium complexes ( 1–2 ) were fully characterized by 1 H and 13 C NMR spectra, infrared spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry. In addition, the molecular structures of complexes 1b and 2a were unambiguously confirmed by single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction analysis.

title: Distinct Methane-Cycling Pathways Drive Variable Surface Flux in Freshwater Wetlands
summary: Abstract Freshwater wetlands are the largest natural source of methane (CH4), representing a third of global emissions. Both CH4 production and oxidation are microbially mediated, yet the metabolic controls governing CH4 cycling across wetl
content: Abstract Freshwater wetlands are the largest natural source of methane (CH4), representing a third of global emissions. Both CH4 production and oxidation are microbially mediated, yet the metabolic controls governing CH4 cycling across wetland types remain poorly resolved. Here, we investigated six hydrologically and geochemically distinct wetlands in the Prairie Pothole Region of North America. By integrating genome-resolved metatranscriptomic data with porewater geochemistry, dissolved CH4 profiles, and chamber-based flux measurements across these wetlands, we assessed how microbial gene expression associated with electron acceptor utilization corresponds to CH4 cycling and identified the dominant methanogenic pathways driving CH4 production. CH4 porewater concentration varied across seasons and sites, with higher concentrations later in the season under more reducing conditions. Wetlands with higher expression of denitrification and sulfate reduction genes exhibited lower methanogenesis and porewater CH4 concentrations. Sites with higher porewater CH4 showed elevated expression of all three methanogenic pathways. Methanogenic activity, however, was not predictive of surface flux. Instead, emissions were modulated by site-specific physical and geochemical controls on methanotrophic CH4 consumption. These findings demonstrate that equivalent CH4 production can emerge through distinct microbial pathways, and that production alone is a poor predictor of atmospheric emissions. This distinction carries important implications for modeling wetland contributions to global CH4 budgets.

title: High-risk HPV integration reprograms cis-regulatory architecture through HPV-specific stripe transcription factors
summary: Background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory pr
content: Background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory programs remain incompletely defined, limiting the identification of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.We aimed to characterize the regulatory architecture associated with hrHPV integration and evaluate its functional relevance in preclinical models.Methods: Human cervical epithelial organoids carrying integrated HPV16 upstream regulatory region-E6/E7 sequences and an HPV16-integrated mouse model (14 E2.2 HPV16-int ) were established.Viral integration mapping, motif enrichment analysis, chromatin accessibility and histone modification profiling, three-dimensional chromatin interaction analysis, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and patient-derived organoid/xenograft models were integrated to assess integration-associated regulatory changes and pharmacological perturbation.Results: Human epithelial organoids and mice with hrHPV integration recapitulated progressive malignant phenotypes in vitro and in vivo.Across cervical and head and neck cancer datasets, hrHPV integration hotspots were enriched for motifs of a defined subset of 25 HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs).Higher HSTF motif density was associated with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, enhanced super-enhancer-promoter interactions, and elevated HSTF regulatory activity along hrHPV-positive epithelial cancer trajectories.Spatial and single-cell multi-omic analyses further confirmed that HSTF activation was triggered by hrHPV integration, which could be blocked by HSTF inhibition in vivo.Conclusions: These findings reveal an hrHPV integration-associated cis-regulatory network that promotes chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation in HPVdriven carcinogenesis.Targeting HSTF-associated regulatory program may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for hrHPV-integrated precancerous lesions and cancers.

title: Luminescent and Stable Eu(III) Complex Nanocrystals: A Class of Eu(III) Emitters Toward Amine/Ammonia
summary: ABSTRACT Eu(III) complexes exhibit highly efficient luminescence, while their emissions are significantly sensitive to amine/ammonia‐induced quenching. Herein, we report a class of Eu(III) complex nanocrystals in which aliphatic amines serv
content: ABSTRACT Eu(III) complexes exhibit highly efficient luminescence, while their emissions are significantly sensitive to amine/ammonia‐induced quenching. Herein, we report a class of Eu(III) complex nanocrystals in which aliphatic amines serve as structural regulators to construct highly luminescent and stable ultrasmall Eu(III) emitters. The addition of aliphatic amines enables the originally insoluble complexes to be dissolved in n ‐hexane, producing Eu(III) complex nanocrystal solutions. The primary‐ and secondary‐amine based Eu(btfa) 3 PBI nanocrystal solutions showed photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) reaching 24%–36% and 30%–37%, respectively. In a sharp contrast, the complex's luminescence was completely or substantially quenched when dissolved directly in primary or secondary amine liquids, with PLQYs decreasing to 0 or 0.0%–1.2%. The significantly suppressed quenching upon nanocrystal formation originated from the substantial reduction of vibrationally induced nonradiative decays, which was further supported by the low quenching constants toward amines. The nanocrystal's emission was further enhanced upon using the tertiary amines. A remarkable PLQY of 64% was obtained for tri‐ n ‐decylamine based Eu(dbm) 3 dmbipy nanocrystals. The nanocrystal solutions exhibited excellent stability, with their PLQYs well retained after 10 h of ambient storage or continuous irradiation with 365 nm UV light. Furthermore, proof‐of‐concept experiments demonstrated the potential application of nanocrystal solids as amine/ammonia‐resistant warning labels.

title: Promoting effect of sulfated zirconia on the activity of Au catalysts for formic acid dehydrogenation mediated by amino acids
summary: ZrO 2 -SO 3 H promotes Au dispersion, enabling the design of a stable and active Au/ZrO 2 -SO 3 H catalyst for formic acid dehydrogenation, with a TOF of 1672 h −1 using conventional NEt 3 and 865 h −1 using l -arginine.
content: ZrO 2 -SO 3 H promotes Au dispersion, enabling the design of a stable and active Au/ZrO 2 -SO 3 H catalyst for formic acid dehydrogenation, with a TOF of 1672 h −1 using conventional NEt 3 and 865 h −1 using l -arginine.

title: Ligand-Mediated Long-Range Interactions Enable Selective Activation of H2O2 for Efficient Water Decontamination
summary: Steering hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) activation to selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2•−) offers a potent solution for water decontamination, especially under neutral or even alkaline conditions. However, the practical potential of th
content: Steering hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) activation to selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2•−) offers a potent solution for water decontamination, especially under neutral or even alkaline conditions. However, the practical potential of this approach has long been constrained by inefficient O2•− generation due to non-selective O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation. Here, we develop a biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) strategy to synthesize a meso-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin iron (TCPP-Fe) catalyst that directs heterolytic O–H bond cleavage during H2O2 activation, leading to predominant O2•− generation with an apparent O2•− generative selectivity of 90.3% among the quantified reactive oxygen species. The TCPP-Fe catalyst exhibits exceptional catalytic performance, achieving a normalized apparent rate constant of $$40.6\,{{{{\rm{L}}}}}^{2}\,{\min }^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{{\rm{H}}}}}_{2}{{{{\rm{O}}}}}_{2}}}^{-1}\,{{{{{\rm{g}}}}}_{{{{\rm{cat}}}}.}}^{-1}$$, which is approximately 2.1-fold higher than the next-highest value in the compiled dataset of representative Fe-based, Fe-alloy, and related catalysts. This remarkable reactivity and selectivity arise from BSCSE-induced modulation of the electronic structure of Fe sites, which facilitates efficient electron transfer between H2O2 and Fe centers while electrostatically stabilizing the Fe–*OOH intermediate to steer O2•− generation. Integrated into a continuous-flow catalytic membrane filtration system treating real secondary effluent, TCPP-Fe enables >96% bisphenol A removal with negligible Fe leaching and sustained removal performance during 120 h of operation. This work bridges biomimetic principles with heterogeneous catalysis, providing a generalizable design strategy for next-generation catalysts toward sustainable water decontamination. Biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) steers H2O2 activation toward superoxide generation, enabling efficient and durable contaminant removal in complex water matrices.

title: Influence of Road Types on Lifespan of Public Service Vehicle Coil Springs in Homa Bay County, Kenya
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: Public Service Vehicles (PSVs) in Homa Bay County rely heavily on helical coil springs to absorb dynamic shock loads, yet the county's heterogeneous road network ranging from paved bitumen highways to unpaved earth and murram tracks acceler
content: Public Service Vehicles (PSVs) in Homa Bay County rely heavily on helical coil springs to absorb dynamic shock loads, yet the county's heterogeneous road network ranging from paved bitumen highways to unpaved earth and murram tracks accelerates mechanical fatigue, causing premature spring sagging, cracking, and fracture, with attendant safety and financial costs for operators.This study sought to establish the influence of road types on the operational lifespan of coil springs in PSVs within Homa Bay County.The study was anchored on mechanical fatigue (stress-cycle) theory, which explains component failure as a function of repeated dynamic loading.A mixed-methods descriptive cross-sectional design was adopted, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches.The target population comprised PSV drivers/operators, SACCO fleet managers, and automotive mechanics operating within Homa Bay County's major routes, from which a sample of 133 respondents (100 drivers/operators, 18 fleet managers, and 15 mechanics) was drawn through stratified random and purposive sampling.Data were collected using questionnaires, interview guides, and observation checklists, whose validity was established through expert review and pilot testing, and reliability through Cronbach's Alpha and data triangulation.Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-Square tests, One-Way ANOVA, and thematic analysis.Findings revealed a marked lifespan reduction correlating with declining road surface quality: vehicles on bitumen roads averaged 100,000-120,000 km before spring replacement, compared to 35,000-50,000 km on gravel roads and 18,000-25,000 km on unpaved earth routes, with overloading further exacerbating failure rates.The study concluded that road surface type significantly influences coil spring lifespan and recommends targeted road infrastructure investment, stricter load-limit enforcement, and route-based preventive maintenance scheduling for PSV fleets.

title: The Renaissance That Wasn’t
summary: The Renaissance That Wasn'tMany nuclear boosters interpreted the global stagnation of nuclear power as a temporary phenomenon that would soon give way to renewed growth.Before the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, prominent visionaries such as Alvin
content: The Renaissance That Wasn'tMany nuclear boosters interpreted the global stagnation of nuclear power as a temporary phenomenon that would soon give way to renewed growth.Before the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, prominent visionaries such as Alvin Weinberg had already prophesized that a "second nuclear era" was inevitable and that the world could look forward to a "nuclear renaissance." 1 Such expectations grew more pronounced during the following decades.Several seemingly plausible arguments backed up the new optimism, ranging from the urgent need to phase out fossil fuels in an age of climate change to the assertion that a new generation of reactors would make nuclear power inherently safe.During the first decades of the twenty-first century, nuclear boosters were remarkably successful in garnering public and political support for their visions.Yet it proved difficult to turn the idea of a nuclear renaissance into a tangible real ity.Very few new reactors were built worldwide in the new millennium.At the same time, older ones nearing the end of their operational lives were shut down.As a result, the share of nuclear energy in the global electricity mix was cut in half during the first quarter of the twenty-first century (figure 6.1).To understand this outcome, we need to examine not only the political twists and turns surrounding nuclear power but also how the atom's expected revival clashed with the features of the nuclear steam engine, its envirotechnical entanglements, and a multitude of prob lems linked to the nuclear fuel cycle. Nuclear NewspeakFollowing the Chernobyl disaster, nuclear visionaries around the world pondered how to regain public and political acceptance of the atom.

title: Orthogonal Self‐Assembled Two‐Dimensional Charge‐Transfer Cocrystals With Superior Photothermal Stability for Low‐Loss NIR‐II Waveguiding and Epitaxial Heterostructure Fabrication
summary: Low-dimensional organic near-infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two-dimensional (2D) structural growth and low-loss waveguiding within the NIR-II region remains a fo
content: Low-dimensional organic near-infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two-dimensional (2D) structural growth and low-loss waveguiding within the NIR-II region remains a formidable challenge due to one-dimensional (1D) packing tendencies imposed by strong charge transfer (CT) interactions. In this study, we strategically choose the extended π-conjugated structure donor dithieno[2,3-d:2',3'-d']benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b']dithiophene and the strong electron-withdrawing acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, and report the first large-scale preparation of 2D organic CT cocrystal microsheets with NIR-II emission at 1050 nm via a gas-phase self-assembly. The strategically expanded conjugation framework not only further promotes the luminescence red-shift but also introduces an interaction network with orthogonal directions, counterbalancing the intrinsic 1D stacking constraints brought by the strong CT interactions and guiding the crystals into a thermodynamically stable 2D morphology. The compact network plays a crucial role in endowing the material with exceptional structural and photothermal stability, as well as low-loss optical waveguiding. Furthermore, attributed to the extremely low lattice-mismatch rate, 1D-2D branched heterostructures were constructed, which demonstrated efficient energy transfer (ET) and cross-band optical signal conversion over 600 nm. This work breaks new ground in extending 2D organic cocrystals into the NIR-II region and provides a promising material platform for low-loss, and integrated NIR optoelectronic devices.
