title: The Recruitment of Systemic-to-Pulmonary Arterial Collaterals in Chronic and Severe Precapillary Pulmonary Hypertension as an Adaptive or Misguided Mechanism
summary: BACKGROUND: The clinical impact of systemic-to-pulmonary arterial collaterals (SPCs) across pulmonary hypertension (PH) groups remains unclear. The authors evaluated the prevalence, clinical correlates, and prognostic relevance of SPCs in a
content: BACKGROUND: The clinical impact of systemic-to-pulmonary arterial collaterals (SPCs) across pulmonary hypertension (PH) groups remains unclear. The authors evaluated the prevalence, clinical correlates, and prognostic relevance of SPCs in a comprehensive PH cohort. METHODS: The authors retrospectively analyzed 434 adult PH patients diagnosed per European Society of Cardiology and European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) guidelines. Baseline risk was evaluated using multiparametric risk scores. All patients underwent diagnostic heart catheterization and angiography, with SPC recruitment semi-quantitatively graded from 0 (none) to 3 (severe, high grade: 2-3). RESULTS: Mean age was 51.9 ± 18.2 years (61.1% female; groups 1, 2, 3, and 4 comprised 51.6%, 3.4%, 10.1%, and 33.2%, respectively). High-grade SPCs were significantly more prevalent in group 4 (58.3%) compared to groups 1 (30.4%), 2 (20.0%), and 3 (6.8%) (P <.001). Higher SPC grade significantly correlated with PH severity across clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and risk score measures (P <.001). Although higher SPC grades were linked to clinical worsening requiring parenteral prostacyclins (P = .027), they were not associated with overall 5-year survival, regardless of pulmonary vascular resistance severity or non-CTEPH etiology (P = .920). Only the Registry to Evaluate Early and Long-Term PAH Disease Management 2.0 score independently predicted mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.19, P <.001, 95% CI: 1.13-1.26). CONCLUSION: Systemic-to-pulmonary arterial collaterals are recruited across all PH etiology groups beyond group 4. While SPC recruitment serves as a marker of advanced pulmonary vascular involvement and elevated risk status, it does not act as an independent driver of long-term mortality.

title: Engineering Tunable Helper Lipid Architecture to Improve Messenger RNA Lipid Nanoparticle Performance
summary: Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper
content: Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper lipid architecture as a major, largely unexplored design lever for optimizing LNP performance. Using a modular library of more than 80 rationally designed helper lipids, we show that systematic variation in headgroup chemistry, linker topology, and tail cardinality reshapes both LNP biophysical behavior and biological performance. Martini molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with multimodal structural analyses reveal that high-performing scaffolds undergo a pH-dependent transition into fusogenic inverse hexagonal-like ordering, substantially lowering the energetic barrier for endosomal escape. These performance gains persist across the clinically relevant ALC-0315 and DLin-MC3-DMA platforms, establishing helper lipid architecture as a transferable design parameter across distinct ionizable lipid chemistries. Translating these design principles into function, optimized helper lipid formulations restore hepatic protein expression in a mouse model of ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency and increase antigen expression and immunogenicity in both preclinical models and in the in vitro human MIMIC platform. Together, these findings establish helper lipids as tunable molecular actuators of potency, tolerability, and stability, offering an engineering framework for next-generation mRNA vaccines and therapeutics.

title: Photo-Induced Metallization and Nonthermal Melting of 4H-SiC under Femtosecond Laser Irradiation: A Real-Time TDDFT Study
summary: Abstract SiC as a representative third-generation wide-bandgap semiconductor, is of great importance for high-power electronics, high-frequency devices, and radiation-resistant applications. However, the microscopic mechanisms underlying fe
content: Abstract SiC as a representative third-generation wide-bandgap semiconductor, is of great importance for high-power electronics, high-frequency devices, and radiation-resistant applications. However, the microscopic mechanisms underlying femtosecond laser-induced nonthermal melting in SiC remain insufficiently understood. Herein, real-time time-dependent density functional theory is employed to investigate the electron dynamics of 4H-SiC under 800 nm femtosecond laser irradiation with intensities ranging from 10 10 to 10 14 W/cm 2 . The ionization mechanisms, energy absorption, current density dynamics and dielectric response are systematically analyzed. As the laser intensity increases, 4H-SiC undergoes a transition from multiphoton absorption (Keldysh parameter γ >> 1) to tunnel ionization ( γ<<1), with a crossover threshold at approximately 5\times10 12 W/cm 2 . The phase relationship between the induced current and the electric field evolves from in-phase (dielectric response) to quadrature (Drude metallic response), providing a dynamical signature of photo-induced metallization. Analysis of the density of states difference reveals continuous electron occupation filling in the conduction band and hole deepening in the valence band, culminating in bandgap collapse at intensities exceeding 10 13 W/cm 2 . The nonthermal melting threshold is determined to be approximately 2 eV/atom, corresponding to a laser intensity of approximately 10 13 W/cm 2 . Rate equations are used to estimate the total number of excited electrons and the corresponding plasma frequency, which reaches approximately 12 eV at laser intensity of 10 13 W/cm 2 , consistent with the observed optical breakdown behavior. These findings elucidate the complete microscopic physical picture of femtosecond laser-induced nonthermal melting in 4H-SiC and provide theoretical guidance for ultrafast laser precision processing of wide-bandgap semiconductors.

title: Effect of self-focusing of the laser beam on terahertz generation in anharmonic nanoparticles
summary: Abstract The present work investigates the influence of self-focusing of the amplitude-modulated laser beam on terahertz radiation generation from the interaction of the laser with anharmonic spherical nanoparticles. A detailed numerical an
content: Abstract The present work investigates the influence of self-focusing of the amplitude-modulated laser beam on terahertz radiation generation from the interaction of the laser with anharmonic spherical nanoparticles. A detailed numerical analysis was performed to study the evolution of the beam width parameter and the generated THz field amplitude. The results reveal that self-focusing significantly enhances the THz field due to the increase in laser intensity arising from transient beam contraction. Additionally, the effects of anharmonicity in electron motion, nanoparticle size, interparticle spacing, and laser intensity have been examined. The study shows that both the anharmonic restoring force and the spatial configuration of nanoparticles play crucial roles in modulating the amplitude of THz emission. The enhancement observed under self-focusing of the laser and optimized nanoparticle parameters highlights the importance of nonlinear optical and structural effects in tailoring strong THz sources for advanced photonic and biomedical applications.

title: Plant growth, biomass, and nitrogen utilization are impacted by mutations in C4 PEPCK1 in maize
summary: Efficient photosynthesis is crucial to agricultural productivity and can be constrained by the plant carbon-nitrogen balance, offering an opportunity for genetic improvement. Furthermore, soil N availability limits grain yields, and crops r
content: Efficient photosynthesis is crucial to agricultural productivity and can be constrained by the plant carbon-nitrogen balance, offering an opportunity for genetic improvement. Furthermore, soil N availability limits grain yields, and crops require substantial N fertilizer to be productive. In C4 plants, carbon-concentrating mechanisms respond to decreased soil nitrogen and share molecular intermediates with N metabolism. Maize, one of the most widely grown crops globally, uses a combination of two C4 photosynthetic pathways. Most carbon fixation occurs through the NADP-malic enzyme (NADP-ME) pathway, yet some fixation is also thought to occur via phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK). However, genetic evidence for the contribution of PEPCK is lacking. Here, we used a transposon-based mutagenesis approach to study the function of the C4 isoform of PEPCK1 in maize. The C4 pathway intermediate aspartate accumulated to high concentrations in the leaves of the pepck1-2::Ds knock-down mutant, providing genetic support for the PEPCK secondary pathway as a complement to the dominant NADP-ME shuttle in maize. Field experiments over multiple seasons in either N-limiting or N-sufficient soils demonstrated the pepck1::Ds mutants produced higher vegetative and grain biomass without changes in leaf photosynthetic rates or parameters. This study confirms that PEPCK1 catalyzes the decarboxylation of carbon shuttled as aspartate, as an alternative route to decarboxylation by NADP-ME in a nominally NADP-ME subtype C4 species maize, providing clear genetic support for two-pathway operation. Further, the greater resilience and N-responsiveness of mutant plants are valuable traits for sustainable and subsistence farming in the future.

title: Terrestrial precipitation seasonality and its redistribution through snow processes
summary: Precipitation controls ecosystem structure and function, governing plant growth, species distributions, nutrient and carbon cycling, and the water that sustains terrestrial and freshwater biodiversity. Across most of the globe, precipitatio
content: Precipitation controls ecosystem structure and function, governing plant growth, species distributions, nutrient and carbon cycling, and the water that sustains terrestrial and freshwater biodiversity. Across most of the globe, precipitation is strongly seasonal, and snowpacks further shape this seasonality by storing water and releasing it later as melt. Yet the global patterns of precipitation seasonality and the extent of its snow-driven redistribution remain poorly quantified. Current knowledge originates mainly from local studies or from climate indices that obscure much of the seasonal signal. Here, we use directional statistics, applied to global gridded Global Precipitation Climatology Centre and ERA5-Land data, to quantify the seasonality of terrestrial precipitation and of surface water inputs (rainfall plus snowmelt). Precipitation centers of mass cluster in summer or winter and rarely fall in spring or autumn. Strong bimodality is rare and largely confined to the Horn of Africa and to transition zones between winter- and summer-dominated regimes. Precipitation seasonality is relatively weak in most snow-influenced regions, yet snow consistently amplifies the seasonality of surface water inputs. In two example applications, we link precipitation seasonality to vegetation greening across Africa. Our quantification of terrestrial precipitation seasonality and its redistribution through snow storage and melt provides a benchmark for understanding how the seasonal timing of freshwater supply shapes ecosystems and environmental processes.

title: A tilted-cathode vacuum-channel transistor with staggered dual gates for suppressed gate interception and sub-THz operation
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract Vacuum-channel transistors (VCTs) are attractive for high-frequency and radiation-tolerant electronics because electron transport through the vacuum channel is largely ballistic. However, in conventional single-gate architectures,
content: Abstract Vacuum-channel transistors (VCTs) are attractive for high-frequency and radiation-tolerant electronics because electron transport through the vacuum channel is largely ballistic. However, in conventional single-gate architectures, the same gate field participates in both electron extraction and trajectory control, creating a trade-off between efficient anode collection, gate interception, and current saturation. These limitations can restrict their performance in high-frequency amplification. Here, we numerically investigate a VCT incorporating a 45°-tilted cathode and a staggered dual-gate geometry. The tilted emission surface redirects the initial electron trajectories toward the anode, while the staggered gate geometry provides spatially separated control of electron extraction and downstream transport. Under the selected operating conditions, the simulated device exhibits a low-current onset region, a rapid-growth region, and a high-Va reduced-slope transport regime together with a gate-interception ratio below 0.041% in the identified low-gate-interception operating region. Large-signal simulations further yield positive power gain at the investigated frequencies up to 500 GHz, including 7.6 dB at 50 GHz and 4.6 dB at 500 GHz. At 50 GHz, the calculated power-added efficiency (PAE) reaches 34.1%. The results show that cathode-angle engineering combined with spatially distributed gate control can reduce electron interception while retaining positive simulated power gain at sub-THz frequencies.

title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
summary: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measure
content: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

title: Seismic fragility of geopolymer concrete pile supported wharves under exposure zone dependent chloride deterioration and nonlinear soil pile interaction
summary: Abstract Pile supported wharves in seismic coastal regions experience earthquake loading while undergoing progressive chloride deterioration, yet the influence of spatially varying marine exposure on the seismic fragility of geopolymer conc
content: Abstract Pile supported wharves in seismic coastal regions experience earthquake loading while undergoing progressive chloride deterioration, yet the influence of spatially varying marine exposure on the seismic fragility of geopolymer concrete wharves remains insufficiently quantified. This study develops an exposure zone resolved framework linking chloride ingress, reinforcement corrosion, bond degradation, cyclic pile response, nonlinear soil pile interaction, and seismic fragility for geopolymer concrete and ordinary Portland cement concrete wharves. Marine exposure produced substantially lower deterioration in the investigated geopolymer concrete system. At 365 days, chloride penetration and reinforcement mass loss were 22.8% and 40.9% lower than the corresponding Portland cement concrete values, while displacement ductility was 24.6% greater. Service life analysis showed that the median DS3 seismic capacity at 60 years retained 81.2% of its initial value for geopolymer concrete compared with 71.2% for Portland cement concrete. Uniform deterioration assumptions overestimated the 60 year DS3 median capacity by 20.5% and 23.0%, respectively, and failed to identify the tidal zone as the governing response location. The results demonstrate that spatial marine deterioration can materially alter both seismic fragility and critical damage location, supporting exposure zone resolved assessment of aging pile supported wharves.

title: Multimodal nondestructive evaluation for structural assessment of composite wind turbine blades
summary: Composite wind turbine blades carry load through laminates, sandwich panels and adhesive joints, where damage can develop beneath an intact surface. Blade geometry, environmental exposure and offshore access constrain inspection. This revie
content: Composite wind turbine blades carry load through laminates, sandwich panels and adhesive joints, where damage can develop beneath an intact surface. Blade geometry, environmental exposure and offshore access constrain inspection. This review compares optical and thermal inspection, ultrasonic and acoustic methods, electromagnetic techniques, and strain and vibration monitoring through their measurement principles and practical limits. The comparison follows the information needed to locate damage, determine its geometry and assess its structural consequence. Optical imaging records surface morphology; thermography responds to heat transport; elastic waves interrogate internal features. Strain and vibration measurements track the loaded structure, while electromagnetic contrast depends on material composition. Combining these responses is useful only when the additional observation constrains an unresolved damage parameter under the relevant acquisition conditions. Published fusion results demonstrate improvements in some image-comparison metrics, with other metrics unchanged or degraded; these results do not establish general gains in blade sizing or residual-strength assessment. A spar-cap example relates delamination geometry to measured tensile capacity and illustrates the consequence of unresolved interface depth. Measurement variability is distinguished from non-unique damage inference, and laboratory feasibility is separated from blade-scale validation and field applicability. The main requirements are independent damage references, acquisition under realistic loading and environmental variation, and uncertainty carried into a mechanism-specific structural assessment. Maintenance benefit requires comparison with existing inspection practice.

title: Diterpenoid and Flavonol Glycosides from Sumatran Fern Selliguea feei Bory
source: Mindanao Journal of Science and Technology
summary: Selliguea feei Bory (Polypodiaceae) is a Sumatran fern whose rhizomes are traditionally used to treat rheumatism and hypertension. However, its fronds have not previously been chemically investigated, and none of its constituents have been
content: Selliguea feei Bory (Polypodiaceae) is a Sumatran fern whose rhizomes are traditionally used to treat rheumatism and hypertension. However, its fronds have not previously been chemically investigated, and none of its constituents have been evaluated against multidrug‑resistant bacteria. This study aimed to isolate and characterize secondary metabolites from the fronds of S. feei and to evaluate their antibacterial activity against clinical isolates of methicillin‑resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and multidrug‑resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (MDRPA). Fresh fronds were macerated with methanol and successively partitioned with n‑hexane, ethyl acetate, and n‑butanol. The ethyl acetate and n‑butanol fractions were separated using silica gel column chromatography and crystallization. Structures were elucidated using 1D and 2D NMR, UV–Vis, IR, and LC–MS analyses. Antibacterial activity was determined using the agar diffusion method at 60 µg/disc, with chloramphenicol (3 µg/disc) as the positive control. Four known compounds were isolated: the diterpenoid onychiol B (1) and three flavonol glycosides, kaempferol‑7‑O‑α‑L‑rhamnoside (2), kaempferol‑3,7‑O‑α‑L‑dirhamnoside (3), and kaempferol‑3‑O‑β‑D‑glucoside‑7‑O‑α‑L‑rhamnoside (4). Compounds 1–3 are reported for the first time from the genus Selliguea. Compound 2 showed moderate inhibition of MRSA (12.17 ± 0.88 mm) and limited inhibition of MDRPA (6.92 ± 0.14 mm).

title: Fabrication of Tannic Acid/ZIF‐8–Reinforced Chitosan/Corn Starch Composite Films and Their Application for Chilled Pork Preservation
summary: ABSTRACT Chilled pork suffers rapid quality deterioration during cold‐chain storage due to moisture loss, microbial proliferation and lipid oxidation, while conventional polyethylene (PE) packaging is nondegradable. Here, we engineered a fu
content: ABSTRACT Chilled pork suffers rapid quality deterioration during cold‐chain storage due to moisture loss, microbial proliferation and lipid oxidation, while conventional polyethylene (PE) packaging is nondegradable. Here, we engineered a fully biodegradable active packaging film by incorporating tannic acid (TA) and zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8) into a chitosan/corn starch matrix, forming a densified network via hydrogen bonding and Zn‐O/Zn‐N coordination. The optimised CSTZ‐8 film (20 wt% TA, 8 wt% ZIF‐8) achieved a tensile strength of 28.5 MPa, along with 42.7% and 18.8% reductions in WVP and OTR compared to CS/St film. Functionally, it integrated UV‐shielding, potent radical scavenging (DPPH > 94%; ABTS > 90%), and notable antibacterial efficacy (inhibition zone: 8.2 mm against E. coli and S. aureus ). Preservation studies revealed that CSTZ‐8 maintained total viable count below the spoilage threshold (6.0 log CFU/g) for 12 days, delaying the time to reach the total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB‐N) threshold of 15 mg/100 g by 5–6 days relative to PE film. These results establish CSTZ‐8 as a practical, scalable, food‐grade active packaging material that extends chilled pork shelf life by 5–6 days over conventional PE film, offering a fully biodegradable solution for real‐world cold‐chain meat distribution.

title: Repurposing a biosynthetic enzyme for imaging UDP-glucose dynamics in living systems
summary: Metabolite dynamics remain difficult to visualize in living systems, particularly for nucleotide sugars that link metabolism to glycosylation and signaling. Here we repurpose Helicobacter pylori UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase to develop UGlu
content: Metabolite dynamics remain difficult to visualize in living systems, particularly for nucleotide sugars that link metabolism to glycosylation and signaling. Here we repurpose Helicobacter pylori UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase to develop UGluS, a genetically encoded ratiometric fluorescent sensor for its biosynthetic product, UDP-glucose (UDP-Glc). Circularly permuted GFP insertion and directed evolution yield an approximately 18-fold excitation-ratio response and an apparent dissociation constant of 32.5 μM, with preferential responsiveness to UDP-Glc over related metabolites. Live-cell imaging and microplate assays reveal responses to metabolic, genetic and mechanosensitive perturbations in mammalian cells. In zebrafish larvae, UGluS reveals uridine-induced increases in UDP-Glc availability and fin-fold enrichment. In mouse liver slices and skeletal muscle in vivo, insulin- and glucose-induced decreases in UDP-Glc availability accompany increased glycogen content. These findings establish UGluS as a tool for imaging UDP-Glc dynamics across biological scales and extend the use of biosynthetic enzymes as fluorescent sensing scaffolds.

title: Screening and Characterization of Protease Producing Microorganisms from Traditional Fermented Foods for Enhanced Meat Tenderization
summary: Microbial proteases are vital for industrial applications; however, identifying cost-effective strains with robust catalytic performance under processing conditions remains challenging. Traditional African fermented foods represent an under
content: Microbial proteases are vital for industrial applications; however, identifying cost-effective strains with robust catalytic performance under processing conditions remains challenging. Traditional African fermented foods represent an underexplored niche for isolating biotechnologically valuable enzymes. This study aimed to screen and characterize protease producing microorganisms from traditional fermented foods for enhancing meat tenderization. Proteolytic strains were isolated from Nigerian fermented foods (ogi, nono, iru, fufu, and ogiri) and identified via 16S rRNA sequencing. Submerged fermentation parameters f or the top isolate, Bacillus subtilis, were optimized using a 45-run Central Composite Design. The enzyme underwent ammonium sulphate fractionation, biochemical characterization, and ex vivo beef tenderization testing. Bacillus subtilis exhibited the highest proteolytic index (1.20) and sequence identity (99.44%, GenBank: PZ306399.1). The response surface quadratic model was highly significant (F = 16.98, p < 0.0001), yielding a maximum protease activity of 297 U/mg under optimized parameters (35 °C, pH 7.0, 1.25 g carbon, 1.0 g nitrogen, 72 h). Ammonium sulfate salting-out at 80% saturation achieved a 2.78-fold purification fold (specific activity: 250.00 U/mg; 50% recovery). The enzyme showed peak activity at 50 °C and pH 8.0, with catalytic activation by Mn2+(118.90%) and Ca2+(118.74%), and marked PMSF sensitivity (55% residual activity), confirming a predominantly serine-type protease profile. Beef marination elevated cooking loss from 41.44% to 51.07% and marinade soluble protein from 17.61 to 24.53 U/mL over 60 minutes. B. subtilis protease is a robust biocatalyst for sustainable meat tenderization and food processing.

title: PVP/HPMC-stabilized silver nanoparticle coatings balance antibacterial activity, silver mobility, breathability, and cytocompatibility in commercial face masks
summary: Abstract Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are widely used to impart antibacterial activity to face masks; however, post-manufacturing finishes should not compromise breathing resistance or filtration, and the mobility and biological effects of
content: Abstract Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are widely used to impart antibacterial activity to face masks; however, post-manufacturing finishes should not compromise breathing resistance or filtration, and the mobility and biological effects of the incorporated silver need to be controlled. In this study, AgNPs were synthesized at room temperature by L-ascorbic acid reduction in an aqueous poly(vinylpyrrolidone)/hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (PVP/HPMC) matrix, which served as a stabilizing and film-forming medium, and were immobilized on commercial three-layer polypropylene medical masks by dip-coating at nominal Ag concentrations of 50 and 100 ppm (M50 and M100). The spherical, face-centered cubic AgNPs had a mean diameter of 24.8 ± 2.4 nm, and ICP-OES revealed Ag loadings of 8.63 ± 0.25 and 17.03 ± 0.32 µg cm − 2 for M50 and M100, respectively. Under limited-moisture conditions (1–2 µL PBS cm − 2 , 37 °C, 24 h), less than 10% of the loaded Ag was mobilized. Particle filtration efficiency was preserved (95.0% for the pristine mask versus 96.1% and 97.3% for M50 and M100) and was unaffected by moisture. M50 retained 93% of the original air permeability and remained within the EN 14683 Type I/II differential-pressure limit after moisture challenge, whereas M100 exceeded this limit. In direct-contact assays, viable counts of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus were reduced by 78.8–83.4% for M50 and 95.9–97.4% for M100 (log reductions of 0.68–1.59, below the 2-log efficacy threshold of standardized tests), whereas the silver-free coating showed no antibacterial activity. Both formulations were non-cytotoxic to L929 fibroblasts according to ISO 10993-5, although M100 induced a modest decrease in metabolic activity and a transient intracellular oxidative response. Increasing the Ag loading thus enhanced antibacterial activity at the expense of breathability and cellular compatibility, identifying M50 as the more balanced formulation.

title: Historical Patterns and Future Projections of Forest Fire Risk in China: Implications for Adaptive Fire Management Under Climate Change
summary: Forest fires are a major ecological disturbance that threatens biodiversity, carbon storage, and human safety, and quantifying their response to climate change is critical for adaptive management. In this study, we integrated 19,632 histori
content: Forest fires are a major ecological disturbance that threatens biodiversity, carbon storage, and human safety, and quantifying their response to climate change is critical for adaptive management. In this study, we integrated 19,632 historical fire records (2000–2024) across 985 Chinese counties with meteorological, forest, geographic, and socioeconomic covariates to develop multi-target machine learning models and to project county-level fire probability under four SSP scenarios (SSP1, SSP2, SSP3, and SSP5) for 2030–2060. For heterogeneous distributions of these fire-related outcomes, we adopted a task-specific heterogeneous ensemble framework in which fire occurrence, record count, burned area, and fire duration were each assigned a model, with selection based on temporally separated validation and outcome-appropriate metrics. The satellite-enhanced XGBoost burned-area model and LightGBM fire-duration model achieved R2 values of 0.767 and 0.696, respectively, whereas the count model showed limited point-prediction performance in the panel data. SHAP analysis identified seasonal cyclic variables, historical fire legacy, and geographic coordinates as the most influential predictors, indicating that the fitted model relied more strongly on seasonal rhythm and long-term fire-probability information than on transient meteorological fluctuations. These represent associative predictive contributions rather than causal relationships. Our projections showed a consistent decline in national mean fire probability by 13–30% from 2030 to 2060 across all scenarios, with SSP3 consistently yielding the highest fire probability. The spatial pattern remained stable, with southwestern mountainous areas persisting as high-risk hotspots, and March remained the peak fire month across all scenario–year combinations. Within the specified adjustment model, sensitivity analysis showed positive associations of temperature and population change with projected fire probability and a negative association of rainfall change, while baseline fire probability contributed most to cross-county variation. These findings provide scientific support for regionally differentiated, climate-adaptive forest fire management strategies, with priority resources allocated to persistent high-risk counties and the spring fire season.

title: Solvent-Directed Heat Shock for Engineering Emissive States in Nonconjugated Polymers: Towards Single-Component Cool-White Light Emission
summary: Non-conjugated polymers can be engineered into highly photoluminescent materials without conventional πconjugated chromophores by activating their through-space electronic states. However, the development of a low-energy cluster-state emitt
content: Non-conjugated polymers can be engineered into highly photoluminescent materials without conventional πconjugated chromophores by activating their through-space electronic states. However, the development of a low-energy cluster-state emitter from a simple polymer without chemical modification remains a fundamental challenge. We report here a solvent-directed heat-shock approach that reconfigures the excited-state landscape of the water-soluble, biocompatible, carbonyl-rich pharmaceutical binder polymer poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (weak high-energy emitter). Ethanol is used as a transient chain-mobilizing medium: rotary evaporation redistributes and pre-associates the pendant carbonyls within a viscous, solvent-dried film, and heating just above the ethanol boiling point removes the residual solvent and collapses the swollen matrix into a rigid cluster state. The rigid clusters display strong visible clusteroluminescence (350-750 nm) upon excitation with longwavelength UV and visible light, yielding single-component cool white emission (CIE 0.26, 0.33) under 405 nm excitation. The retained cool-white emission in aqueous media across the 1-30 mg mL-1 concentration range expands this approach beyond dry solids, linking nonconventional photophysics to water-processable soft materials.

title: A Venus Cloud-Level Aerostat Colony as a Superior Offworld Settlement Strategy to a Mars Surface Colony: A Monte Carlo and Neural Network Analysis
summary: Abstract This study tests the proposition that a crewed aerostat colony floating within the Venus cloud deck at 54 to 60 km altitude represents a superior offworld settlement strategy to a crewed surface colony on Mars. The author construct
content: Abstract This study tests the proposition that a crewed aerostat colony floating within the Venus cloud deck at 54 to 60 km altitude represents a superior offworld settlement strategy to a crewed surface colony on Mars. The author constructed first-principles physical and economic models of both colonies and propagated the uncertainty in 367 input parameters through Monte Carlo simulation of 20,000 draws per test. An H2O deep learning surrogate was refitted on bootstrap resamples of each response to produce per-prediction perturbation sensitivities, while a paired permuted-refit null arm supplied per-variable p-values alongside permutational multivariate analysis of variance. Five research questions were evaluated as ten one-sided tests against an alpha test statistic of 0.05. The null hypotheses were rejected for radiation (p = 0.00015; median Venus advantage 143.8 mSv per year) as well as for colony net present value in both habitat configurations (p = 0.024 and 0.022; median Venus advantage approximately USD 228 million per colonist). The null hypotheses for water and oxygen cost, for four export lines and for a gravity health benefit were not rejected. These findings suggest a possible systemic Venus advantage arising from several moderate benefits acting together rather than any single commodity.

title: Chemically specific NMR relaxation in thermally modified mesoporous materials
summary: Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation provides a non-invasive method for characterising solid–liquid interactions within porous materials. However, the influence of pore surface chemistry on the surface relaxivity of differe
content: Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation provides a non-invasive method for characterising solid–liquid interactions within porous materials. However, the influence of pore surface chemistry on the surface relaxivity of different liquid adsorbates remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the effects of thermal surface modification on eight liquid adsorbates (cyclohexane, acetone and six alcohols) confined within mesoporous silicas and γ-alumina using low-field (12.7 MHz) two-dimensional 1 H T 1 – T 2 relaxation measurements. Thermal treatment reduced the T 1 / T 2 ratios of the alkyl groups of confined alcohols, indicating reduced surface affinity, with the magnitude of this reduction dependent on alcohol structure. Furthermore, by examining cyclohexane, acetone and methanol confined within mesoporous silicas with nominal pore sizes between 6 and 50 nm, we quantify, for the first time, the influence of surface dehydroxylation on both longitudinal and transverse surface relaxivities. Silica pore surface dehydroxylation reduced the transverse surface relaxivities of acetone and both functional groups of methanol by approximately 40–60%, whereas that of cyclohexane remained nearly unchanged. Overall, these findings demonstrate the sensitivity of nuclear spin surface relaxivity to both adsorbate chemistry and pore surface functionalisation, and highlight the potential of low-field NMR relaxation for characterising surface chemistry changes in functional porous materials.

title: Exhausted ROS Accumulation and Attenuated Pyroptosis of Nucleus Pulposus Cells via Injectable Hydrogel for Ameliorating Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
summary: Intervertebral disc degeneration is one of the primary contributors to chronic low back pain, yet effective therapies remain limited owing to the persistent oxidative stress and inflammatory microenvironment within the nucleus pulposus. Exc
content: Intervertebral disc degeneration is one of the primary contributors to chronic low back pain, yet effective therapies remain limited owing to the persistent oxidative stress and inflammatory microenvironment within the nucleus pulposus. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation activates pyroptosis and amplifies inflammatory cascades, thereby accelerating disc degeneration. Herein, an injectable reactive oxygen species-responsive hydrogel (GCTD) is developed to simultaneously scavenge ROS and suppress pyroptosis for nucleus pulposus microenvironment remodeling and intervertebral disc degeneration treatment. The hydrogel is constructed by incorporating cyclodextrin-modified gelatin methacryloyl for effective delivery of disulfiram, a potent pyroptosis inhibitor, together with scavenging-ROS thioketal crosslinkers. In situ injection of GCTD into degenerated rat intervertebral discs retains disc height and maintains the structural integrity of nucleus pulposus tissue. These findings may provide a new therapy for intervertebral disc degeneration to remodel the inflammatory microenvironment of the nucleus pulposus.

title: Synthesis of Curved Nanoplatelet Graphite From Calcium Carbide and Amorphous Carbon at Low Temperature
summary: ABSTRACT Artificial graphite requires high temperature and high pressure conditions, which leads to high energy consumption and cost in its production. This study proposes a new low‐temperature oxidative‐reductive graphitization technology,
content: ABSTRACT Artificial graphite requires high temperature and high pressure conditions, which leads to high energy consumption and cost in its production. This study proposes a new low‐temperature oxidative‐reductive graphitization technology, which involves converting amorphous carbon and carbon elements in calcium carbide into graphite. Glucose hydrothermal carbon spheres (CS), citric acid pyrolysis carbon (CA) and biomass bamboo pyrolysis carbon (BB) have been converted into curved nanoplatelet graphite, and the potential graphitization mechanism has been discussed. The experimental results show that the samples prepared at 1100°C possess both a high degree of graphitization and excellent performance as lithium‐ion battery anodes. The graphitized carbon GC CS ‐3 prepared from calcium carbide and CS achieves 441 mA h g −1 at a current density of 0.1 A g −1 , remains at 183.3 mA h g −1 at 5 A g −1 , and the capacity reaches 412.1 mA h g −1 after 500 cycles at a current density of 1 A g −1 . This technology provides an efficient and simple solution for amorphous carbon graphitization and lithium anode material optimization.

title: Navigating the influence of climate and land use change on net primary production dynamics in China's vegetation ecosystems
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Introduction Vegetation productivity is shaped by climate and human activities. However, the relative contributions of climate change and land use change across China’s vegetation ecosystems remain insufficiently understood. Methods We used
content: Introduction Vegetation productivity is shaped by climate and human activities. However, the relative contributions of climate change and land use change across China’s vegetation ecosystems remain insufficiently understood. Methods We used the Carnegie–Ames–Stanford Approach (CASA) model to estimate net primary production (NPP), univariate linear regression and the Mann–Kendall test to assess trends, and a scenario framework to compare the relative contributions of climate change (Ctr. Clim), land use change (Ctr. Ccl), and a residual term (Ctr. Res). Results NPP in China’s cropland ecosystems (CES), forestland ecosystems (FES), and grassland ecosystems (GES) has shown a clear upward trend from 2000 to 2022, with the highest growth rate observed in FES. Results indicate that the influence of climate change has declined over time, while that of land use change has increased. Specifically, Ctr. Clim decreased by 37.57%, 29.18%, and 31.71% in CES, FES, and GES, respectively, whereas Ctr. Ccl increased by 18.29%, 13.15%, and 14.66%. Spatially, climate change had a positive impact on NPP in over 80% of the areas across all ecosystems. Discussion These findings highlight changes in the relative contributions associated with vegetation productivity and support consideration of land management and climate adaptation together.

title: Precursor-directed cerium–nickel hydroxide/MOF heterointerfaces for membraneless zinc–bromine batteries and oxygen evolution
summary: Precursor-directed coordination offers a route to electrochemical heterointerfaces whose constituent domains share a common metal source. Here, ligand-driven restructuring of a cerium–nickel hydroxide generates coordination hybrids with a n
content: Precursor-directed coordination offers a route to electrochemical heterointerfaces whose constituent domains share a common metal source. Here, ligand-driven restructuring of a cerium–nickel hydroxide generates coordination hybrids with a nonmonotonic electrochemical response. Combined diffraction, microscopy and spectroscopy support probable hydroxide/MOF-like heterointerfaces, with carboxylate-containing domains adjoining hydroxide-rich regions and changes consistent with interfacial electronic interactions. Intermediate ligand treatment improves bromine redox response, recovered discharge charge and cycling efficiencies in a membraneless zinc–bromine cell, whereas the highest dosage sharply suppresses discharge. Alkaline anodic polarization and capacitive measurements favor intermediate formulation. These trends suggest a preparation window in which coordination-driven restructuring benefits electrochemical function, while more extensive treatment compromises accessibility or connectivity.

title: Rewriting Copper-Catalyzed ATRA Reactions through a Cu(II)/Cu(III) Pathway
summary: Abstract Atom transfer radical addition (ATRA) reactions are typically mediated by photocatalytic Cu(I)/Cu(II) redox cycles, whereas Cu(II) complexes generally serve as precursors to the catalytically active Cu(I) species. Herein, we report
content: Abstract Atom transfer radical addition (ATRA) reactions are typically mediated by photocatalytic Cu(I)/Cu(II) redox cycles, whereas Cu(II) complexes generally serve as precursors to the catalytically active Cu(I) species. Herein, we report a Cu(II) complex supported by the rigid tridentate ligand 3,6-di-tert-butyl-1,8-di(pyridin-2-yl)-9H-carbazole (dpc) that displays an unexpected photocatalytic reactivity. While [Cu(dpc)OAc] exhibits low or no activity in established Cu(II)-mediated transformations, it efficiently catalyzes ATRA reactions, such as the chlorosulfonylation of alkenes, that are typical for Cu(I). Electrochemical and spectroscopic studies revealed that the rigid ligand framework suppresses conventional Cu(II)/Cu(I) photochemistry, instead enabling a Cu(II)/Cu(III) photocycle. Mechanistic investigations support the preassembly of a photoactive Cu(II)-sulfonyl chloride complex followed by light-induced radical generation and Cu(III)-mediated product formation. These findings establish a strategy for promoting ATRA reactivity through Cu(II)/Cu(III) catalysis and underline ligand design as a tool for controlling copper photochemistry.

title: Microscopic Neuromodulation with Locally Enhanced Electric Field
summary: Implantable neural stimulation devices play an important role in fundamental neuroscience research, clinical applications, and emerging technologies such as neuroprosthetics and brain machine interfaces, with increasing demand for spatially
content: Implantable neural stimulation devices play an important role in fundamental neuroscience research, clinical applications, and emerging technologies such as neuroprosthetics and brain machine interfaces, with increasing demand for spatially precise neuromodulation at cellular and circuit levels. Microelectrode based electrical stimulation relies on charge injection into neural tissue, where irreversible electrochemical reactions at the electrode electrolyte interface may lead to electrode degradation and tissue damage. Although microscale magnetic stimulation provides an alternative, it typically requires sophisticated microcoil architectures and complex fabrication processes. In this work, we introduce a novel neural stimulation mechanism based on localized electric field enhancement. The proposed device employs an electrically insulated sharp metallic tip to concentrate the electric field and generate localized displacement currents capable of activating nearby neurons. Finite element simulations were performed to investigate the underlying stimulation mechanism and establish design guidelines for device fabrication. MEMS based neural probes were subsequently fabricated and experimentally evaluated through in vivo animal studies, with neuronal activation observed at distances of less than 200 micrometers from the probe tip using two-photon imaging. By avoiding Faradaic charge transfer at the tissue interface while offering high spatial localization, orientation selectivity, and a compact device architecture, the proposed approach provides a promising alternative to existing stimulation technologies for chronic and high-density neural interfaces.

title: Scenario-Based Hybrid Differential Evolution for Local Energy Community Scheduling: A Multi-Objective Synthetic Benchmark with Shared Storage
summary: This study compares multi-objective search configurations for day-ahead scheduling of photovoltaic generation, shiftable loads, and a shared battery in a synthetic local energy community. The objectives are mean scenario cost, mean cost in
content: This study compares multi-objective search configurations for day-ahead scheduling of photovoltaic generation, shiftable loads, and a shared battery in a synthetic local energy community. The objectives are mean scenario cost, mean cost in the worst 10% of scenarios (empirical Conditional Value-at-Risk (CvaR) at confidence 0.90), and relative dispersion of a source-defined household score. That score credits exported net load at both retail and feed-in prices; it is a proxy, not household billing or an allocation of battery benefits. Scenario-based Hybrid Differential Evolution (S-HDE) combines Generalized Differential Evolution 3 (GDE3)-style selection, a scenario curriculum, and periodic battery pattern search. Ten 20-household instances, each with 30 scenarios, are compared across six configurations and five seeds (300 reported runs), with a common ceiling of 4,400 schedule evaluations but unequal attained counts. Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) has the best reported mean Hypervolume (HV) (0.2407 ± 0.0382; mean rank 1.30), followed by S-HDE (0.2298 ± 0.0261; rank 2.80). Printed per-instance means reproduce the Friedman result (χ² = 41.257, p = 8.32 × 10⁻⁸). Reported normal-approximation Wilcoxon comparisons favor NSGA-II over S-HDE (Holm-adjusted p = 0.02531); neither ablation differs detectably from S-HDE. The findings describe the reported in-sample benchmark. Original code, objective definitions, front archives, and evaluation ledgers are needed to verify computational provenance; corrected household billing would define a different optimization experiment.

title: Field Calibration of Low-Cost SHT20 and BH1750 Sensors for Microclimate Monitoring in a Tropical Greenhouse: Effects of Calibration Range and Transmission Interval
summary: Low-cost sensor nodes now drive climate control in many tropical greenhouses, yet their accuracy is usually taken from datasheets rather than tested across the conditions in which a controller acts. Here, three ESP32 nodes with SHT20 temper
content: Low-cost sensor nodes now drive climate control in many tropical greenhouses, yet their accuracy is usually taken from datasheets rather than tested across the conditions in which a controller acts. Here, three ESP32 nodes with SHT20 temperature and relative humidity (RH) sensors and BH1750 light sensors were calibrated and validated against reference instruments in a fan-and-pad cooled greenhouse in Indonesia and followed through 1458 paired readings per quantity at three times of day. The effect of the transmission interval was isolated by subsampling 1 min series at 5 and 10 min, which holds the weather constant between intervals. Before correction the sensors read up to 2.4 °C warm and 8.5 % RH wet, and a linear correction fitted on a two-hour late-afternoon window brought the validation root-mean-square error (RMSE) to 0.34 °C–0.75 °C and 1.1 %–2.6 % RH, within the stated accuracy of reference instruments that are not traceable; these figures measure agreement with that reference, not absolute accuracy. In the field, 83 % of temperature readings agreed with the reference to within ± 1 °C inside the calibrated range but 38 % above 39.3 °C, mostly at midday, and the share of humidity readings within ± 5 % RH fell from 92 % to 36 % above 65 % RH in the morning. In 18 hourly windows, a 10 min interval changed hourly means of temperature and humidity by no more than 0.22 °C and 0.91 % RH, but missed hourly illuminance peaks by up to 19.9 klx under rapidly varying light. In this greenhouse, most of the disagreement with the reference arose outside the calibration window, which suggests, though this was not tested, that field calibrations of low-cost nodes should span the midday heat and the morning humidity at which cooling decisions are made.

title: Production of the bioplastic precursor 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylic acid in sugarcane and sorghum
summary: Lignocellulosic biomass from bioenergy crops is a vast and largely untapped feedstock for biomanufacturing. Engineering these crops to synthesize high-value compounds directly in planta offers a promising strategy to establish new revenue s
content: Lignocellulosic biomass from bioenergy crops is a vast and largely untapped feedstock for biomanufacturing. Engineering these crops to synthesize high-value compounds directly in planta offers a promising strategy to establish new revenue streams. This study evaluated the production of the polyester precursor 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylic acid (PDC) in sugarcane and sorghum by expressing four plastid-targeted microbial enzymes (QsuB, PmdA, PmdB, PmdC) under constitutive promoters. PDC was effectively produced in both crop types and straightforwardly extracted from the biomass of transgenic lines using an aqueous methanol solvent. In sugarcane, PDC accumulated preferentially in leaves, reaching 318 μg/g dry weight in high-performing lines during a second harvest following regrowth. Engineered sorghum achieved substantially higher titers, with the top line accumulating 1.9 mg/g in leaves and 3.0 mg/g in stems of mature plants. This concentration in stems (ca. 0.3% dry weight) meets the threshold for cost-competitiveness with microbial synthesis. Unlike previous findings in woody poplar species, cell wall composition and agronomic traits in these grasses largely mirrored wild-type controls. Overall, these findings demonstrate that sorghum and sugarcane are viable platforms for dual-use bioproduction, preserving bioenergy potential while delivering commercially relevant titers of a valuable platform chemical.

title: TopoPPI: A geometry-aware platform for visualization and low-distortion mapping of protein-protein interaction interfaces
summary: Protein-protein interfaces encode molecular recognition through spatially organized contacts, yet their buried, curved surfaces are difficult to inspect as a whole. Flattening these surfaces can expose interface organization but introduces
content: Protein-protein interfaces encode molecular recognition through spatially organized contacts, yet their buried, curved surfaces are difficult to inspect as a whole. Flattening these surfaces can expose interface organization but introduces geometric distortion and may divide individual residues into disconnected regions. We present TopoPPI, a geometry-aware platform that converts interaction surfaces into low-distortion two-dimensional atlases while retaining links to source atoms, residues and contacts. TopoPPI extends OptCuts with a contact-weighted penalty for seam-induced fragmentation of residue footprints-the surface regions assigned to individual residues-jointly balancing continuity, seam length and distortion. In a leakage-controlled benchmark of 2,236 experimental complexes, the geometry-only OptCuts foundation achieved 88.39% lower family-weighted scale-fair distortion than the next-best tested parameterization across 2,209 complete comparable outputs. Across 2,204 exact-domain comparisons, TopoPPI reduced family-weighted residue-footprint fragmentation by 12.81% (95% confidence interval, 11.50-14.05%), with a 2.60% increase in normalized seam length and a 0.061% increase in scale-fair distortion. Continuity gains extended to 1,180 fixed-pose pairs of AlphaFold monomer models and 145 predicted complexes, with fragmentation reductions of 18.60% and 11.65%, respectively. Functionally annotated antibody and colicin-immunity interfaces demonstrated reconnection of the footprints of experimentally characterized binding and specificity residues. Further applications mapped published binding and folding free-energy estimates onto the KRAS-RAF1 interface and compared shared receptor residues across two growth-hormone recognition sites. Available through graphical and command-line interfaces, TopoPPI provides a residue-aware visualization framework for integrating structural contacts and functional annotations within geometrically controlled interface maps.

title: Gastronomy as a catalyst for the circular economy in tourism: a multi-case analysis of UNESCO Creative Cities in Brazil
summary: A economia circular (EC), aplicada aos sistemas alimentares, posiciona a gastronomia como um vetor estratégico. No turismo, essa abordagem valoriza produtos locais, reduz desperdícios e mitiga emissões de carbono. Nesse contexto, o artigo t
content: A economia circular (EC), aplicada aos sistemas alimentares, posiciona a gastronomia como um vetor estratégico. No turismo, essa abordagem valoriza produtos locais, reduz desperdícios e mitiga emissões de carbono. Nesse contexto, o artigo tem como objetivo analisar de que forma os princípios da EC podem ser integrados aos sistemas alimentares no contexto do turismo gastronômico, visando à promoção do turismo regenerativo por meio da valorização da cultura alimentar, dos produtos locais e da redução do desperdício. A pesquisa adotou a metassíntese como procedimento metodológico, caracterizada como um estudo qualitativo voltado à análise e à interpretação integradas de achados provenientes de pesquisas qualitativas sobre um tema comum. Alinhada ao conhecimento contemporâneo sobre EC, sistemas alimentares e turismo sustentável, a pesquisa também contemplou a análise das Cidades Criativas da Gastronomia da UNESCO no Brasil: Belém, Florianópolis, Belo Horizonte e Paraty. Os resultados indicam que a gastronomia é um caminho para a transição rumo a sistemas alimentares circulares, ao fortalecer circuitos curtos de comercialização, estimular a agricultura familiar e agroecológica, valorizar a sociobiodiversidade e fomentar práticas de prevenção e reaproveitamento de resíduos alimentares. Apesar dos desafios relacionados à governança, à infraestrutura e à capacitação profissional, as cidades analisadas demonstram elevado potencial transformador, funcionando como laboratórios vivos de inovação territorial. Conclui-se que a consolidação de sistemas alimentares circulares no turismo depende da articulação entre políticas públicas integradas, da cooperação entre produtores, chefs e gestores de destinos e do reconhecimento da gastronomia como elemento central para o desenvolvimento sustentável e de baixo carbono.

title: Particle size matters: Foliar-applied nano-silicon regulates C:N:P:K stoichiometry in Dendrocalamus brandisii seedling leaves under drought stress
summary: Bamboo is a vital forest resource in tropical and subtropical regions, where leaf elemental composition and stoichiometric balance critically mediate growth and stress adaptation. Nano-silica (SiO₂-NPs) can regulate plant stress responses,
content: Bamboo is a vital forest resource in tropical and subtropical regions, where leaf elemental composition and stoichiometric balance critically mediate growth and stress adaptation. Nano-silica (SiO₂-NPs) can regulate plant stress responses, yet its effects on silicon accumulation and elemental stoichiometry in bamboo leaves under drought stress remain unclear. This study investigated drought-stressed Dendrocalamus brandisii seedlings treated with SiO₂-NPs of five particle sizes (10, 20, 40, 60, and 80 nm). Leaf SiO₂ content, SPAD values, photosynthetic gas-exchange parameters and C, N, P, and K concentrations, stoichiometric ratios were assessed on days 3, 6, and 9 after foliar application. The results showed that responses varied with particle size and sampling time. T1 (10 nm) induced rapid early-stage responses, particularly in SiO₂ and K, whereas T2 (20 nm) sustained stable effects throughout the middle and later stages. T5 (80 nm) showed weaker or delayed responses. Correlation and plasticity analyses revealed that leaf SiO₂ was closely associated with SPAD, Pn, Gs, Tr, and Si-related ratios. PCA further identified SiO₂, SPAD, Pn, Tr and Si-related ratios as key drivers of treatment separation. Overall, 20 nm SiO₂-NPs optimally enhanced leaf elemental accumulation and stoichiometric balance under drought stress. These findings highlighted the importance of particle-size optimization for nano-silica application in bamboo seedlings’drought management.

title: Where Climate Change Lands: Spatial Framing and Domestication in South Korean Newspapers, 2000–2025
summary: This study analyzes 26 years of climate change coverage (2000–2025) across four major South Korean newspapers (n = 27,646) to examine how geographic framing varies across sub-national regions and shifts over time. Drawing on Olausson’s (201
content: This study analyzes 26 years of climate change coverage (2000–2025) across four major South Korean newspapers (n = 27,646) to examine how geographic framing varies across sub-national regions and shifts over time. Drawing on Olausson’s (2014, The diversified nature of “domesticated” news discourse: The case of climate change in national news media. Journalism Studies, 15(6), 711–725, https://doi.org/10.1080/1461670X.2013.837253) domestication typology and LLM-assisted classification, the analysis finds that extroverted domestication dominates Korean climate reporting but is historically unstable. Different triggering events are associated with different domestication modes, with introverted domestication peaking in 2010–2014, coinciding with the Low Carbon Green Growth policy period, and with climate disasters coinciding with a sharp introverted surge. Regional analysis of twelve sub-national locations reveals a structural asymmetry between metropolitan areas, imagined as sites of climate governance, and provincial regions, imagined as sites of climate consequence. These findings extend the domestication framework from the global-national to the national-sub-national scale and support a theoretical link between domestication and the production of place-based climate imaginaries.

title: Performance of an alkali-activated binder derived from recycled glass fiber reinforced plastic under high-pressure CO2 exposure
summary: This study investigates the durability of glass fiber reinforced plastic (GFRP) geopolymer cement exposed to high pressure CO 2 . The relationship between mechanical performance, microstructural evolution and leachate chemistry is studied i
content: This study investigates the durability of glass fiber reinforced plastic (GFRP) geopolymer cement exposed to high pressure CO 2 . The relationship between mechanical performance, microstructural evolution and leachate chemistry is studied in the setting of CO 2 storage. GFRP was produced from GFRP rebar production waste. The geopolymers were exposed to 1500 psi (10.3 MPa) of CO 2 saturated brine at 125 °F for 90 days and benchmarked against conventional Class G cement. The mechanics of the GFRP-derived binder are a key finding as it maintained mechanical performance for the duration of the study compared to the Class G cement which showed significant degradation. The scratch test results showed that the GFRP binder scratch-derived strength increased from 14.5 MPa at day 1 to 17.9 MPa at day 90, an increase of 23.4%, and the tensile strength remained stable at about 1.5 MPa. However, Class G cement lost 42.3% of its scratch-derived strength (from 12.3 to 7.1 MPa) with a minor loss in tensile strength. The non-destructive computed tomography (CT) analysis revealed a more homogenous internal damage of the GFRP binder in comparison to Class G cement. Brine chemistry after exposure showed moderate alkalinity (pH 8.0), a large increase in dissolved inorganic carbon and a significant leaching of potassium (from 19 to 12,690 ppm). These results suggest a potential for GFRP derived alkali-activated binders in CO 2 -rich wellbore applications.

title: Marine Exopolysaccharide Diabolican Enhances the Physical Properties of Collagen Hydrogels via a Temperature-Dependent Polyionic Complexation
summary: Collagens and glycosaminoglycans are essential components of the extracellular matrix, providing key biochemical and mechanical properties. Type I collagen and hyaluronan (HA) are therefore widely used in tissue engineering to mimic the cha
content: Collagens and glycosaminoglycans are essential components of the extracellular matrix, providing key biochemical and mechanical properties. Type I collagen and hyaluronan (HA) are therefore widely used in tissue engineering to mimic the characteristics of human tissues. However, native HA does not significantly improve the properties of collagen hydrogels when combined with this biopolymer. In this study, the marine exopolysaccharide diabolican (HE800 strain), which exhibits structural similarities to HA, was evaluated as an alternative glycosaminoglycan for combination with type I collagen. Mixing collagen with diabolican led to the formation of polyionic complexes (PICs), even under conditions of high osmotic strength. Complex formation depended on both the molecular weight of diabolican and temperature. Performing the mixing on ice slowed down complexation, enabling the preparation of homogeneous hydrogels. The interplay between PIC formation and collagen gelation generated composite hydrogels with significantly improved physical properties when high-molecular-weight (HMW) diabolican was used, doubling the mechanical strength compared to pure collagen. Encapsulated fibroblasts remained viable, adopted a spindle shaped morphology, proliferated, and did not induce hydrogel contraction until day seven. Importantly, these advantages were achieved without chemical functionalization or crosslinking. Overall, HMW diabolican represents a promising alternative to hyaluronan for tissue engineering applications.

title: Joint Inversion of Summertime Anthropogenic and Biogenic NO x and NMVOC Emissions over the Continental United States Using TEMPO and TROPOMI Observations
summary: Abstract. Nitrogen oxides (NOx) and non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) are major air pollutants and key precursors to tropospheric ozone. We constrain summertime US NOx and NMVOC emissions by assimilating midday TEMPO and TROPO
content: Abstract. Nitrogen oxides (NOx) and non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) are major air pollutants and key precursors to tropospheric ozone. We constrain summertime US NOx and NMVOC emissions by assimilating midday TEMPO and TROPOMI nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and formaldehyde (HCHO) observations to assess how joint emission inversions and daytime TEMPO observations improve top-down emission estimates. Satellite NO2 and HCHO retrievals evaluated against Pandora show negative biases; notably, TROPOMI HCHO is systematically lower than TEMPO HCHO by 30–40 % over the southeastern US, and a bias correction was applied to TROPOMI HCHO. Top-down NOx emissions derived from TEMPO and TROPOMI are 5–20 % lower than prior estimates. Posterior biogenic NMVOC emissions are reduced by 40–50 %, and top-down anthropogenic NMVOC emissions derived from both satellite datasets are also 20–40 % lower in urban areas. While overall top-down NOx emissions appear underestimated, TEMPO-derived emissions demonstrate better performance than TROPOMI-derived emissions. Updated NMVOC emissions mitigate the prior model overprediction of HCHO and other NMVOC species, with TEMPO data providing stronger constraints while TROPOMI-derived emissions are overcorrected. Joint NOx and NMVOC inversions yield the best O3 simulations compared to NMVOC-only inversions. Furthermore, NMVOC emission estimates are sensitive to the NOx emission inversion, resulting in a 10 % difference in posterior emissions due to complex NOx–hydroxyl radical (OH)–VOC chemical interactions. Our work demonstrates that TEMPO's better midday retrieval quality provides enhanced constraints for top-down emission estimation compared to TROPOMI, laying the groundwork for diurnal geostationary assimilation while highlighting the critical need for multi-species joint inversions.

title: Potential to modulate corneal epithelial repair via nitric oxide-releasing glycosaminoglycans
summary: barrier restoration. A derivative consisting of CS with prolonged NO release and low molecular weight HA with intermediate NO-release kinetics were identified as the most promising materials. The HA derivative enhanced epithelial migration
content: barrier restoration. A derivative consisting of CS with prolonged NO release and low molecular weight HA with intermediate NO-release kinetics were identified as the most promising materials. The HA derivative enhanced epithelial migration even during later timepoints of the migration assays. A carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) gel formulation containing the HA derivative further promoted cell migration. In corneal tissue models, treatment with both the free and CMC-formulated NO-releasing HA enhanced restoration. Barrier recovery, as measured by transepithelial electrical resistance, confirmed restoration of tissue integrity post-wounding, concomitant with a cytokine milieu associated with pro-wound healing. Overall, NO-releasing, low molecular weight HA in a CMC gel formulation represents a promising bioactive strategy for promoting corneal wound repair.

title: Evaluation of marginal and average sectorial GHGs emissions abatement costs using an open-source energy system optimization model: the Italian case study
source: Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change
summary: Abstract To achieve a carbon-neutral Europe by 2050, emission reduction efforts must be supported by quantitative tools that capture the interactions among sectors and technologies. This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate system-wide
content: Abstract To achieve a carbon-neutral Europe by 2050, emission reduction efforts must be supported by quantitative tools that capture the interactions among sectors and technologies. This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate system-wide marginal abatement costs and sectorial and sub-sectorial average abatement costs with a multi-sectoral energy system optimization model. The approach compares the total system cost and emissions of a sequence of whole-system optimizations under progressively stricter emission constraints. The constraints are applied along the entire decarbonization trajectory rather than to a single target year. The resulting marginal costs are then allocated to the sectors and technologies that deliver each emission reduction step. Since every point of the curve corresponds to a consistent system configuration, technology interactions and sector coupling are preserved, and each cost level can be traced back to the technology transitions and input assumptions that drive it. The methodology is demonstrated on the Italian energy system with the open-source TEMOA-Italy model, considering emission reduction targets of up to -90% in 2050. The results show that marginal abatement costs rise steeply as the targets become more ambitious, and that abatement costs vary widely across sectors. The power sector is the cheapest to decarbonize, thanks to mature renewable technologies. Transport shows intermediate costs, with marked differences across its sub-sectors. The industrial and residential sectors show the highest costs and contribute mainly at the most ambitious targets. The open-source framework allows the approach to be reproduced and transferred to other energy systems.

title: Regional artificial intelligence development and agricultural ecological efficiency: evidence from Chinese provinces
summary: Existing studies have primarily focused on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and carbon emission efficiency, while systematic evidence on whether and through which mechanisms AI improves agricultural ecological eff
content: Existing studies have primarily focused on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and carbon emission efficiency, while systematic evidence on whether and through which mechanisms AI improves agricultural ecological efficiency (AEE) remains relatively limited. Using provincial panel data from China for the period 2005 to 2023, this study employs the entropy weighting method to measure regional AI development and a slack-based measure (SBM) model incorporating undesirable outputs to evaluate AEE. A two-way fixed effects model is further constructed to examine the effects of AI on AEE and the underlying mechanisms. AI is conceptually distinct from general digitalization, automation, precision agriculture, and information technology development, as its defining feature lies in leveraging machine learning, intelligent sensing, and algorithmic decision-making to achieve more advanced data processing and intelligent decision-making capabilities. The results indicate that a 0.1-unit increase in regional AI development is associated with an average increase of 0.01078 units in AEE. Mechanism analysis suggests that AI can indirectly improve AEE by promoting green finance development and industrial structure upgrading. Furthermore, agricultural technological innovation exhibits a significant threshold effect, with higher levels of technological innovation strengthening the positive effect of AI on AEE. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the positive effect of AI on AEE is more pronounced in eastern regions, regions with lower levels of urbanization and agricultural modernization, and non-major grain-producing regions. Further analysis identifies positive spatial spillover effects of AI on AEE in neighboring regions, contributing to coordinated green agricultural development across local and neighboring regions. This study provides evidence on the effects, transmission mechanisms, and threshold conditions through which AI improves AEE, offering new empirical insights into the role of AI in facilitating the green transformation of agriculture and extending the analytical perspective of agricultural sustainability research.

title: Measures, Evolutions, and Determinants of Green Efficiency: Evidence from China
summary: This study measures urban green efficiency in 270 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022 using an output-oriented variable-returns to-scale (VRS) slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis model that incorporates carbon dioxide emissions as a
content: This study measures urban green efficiency in 270 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022 using an output-oriented variable-returns to-scale (VRS) slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis model that incorporates carbon dioxide emissions as an undesirable output. It then traces the temporal evolution and city-size distribution of green efficiency and examines the factors associated with its variation using two-way fixed-effects models. The analysis further tests whether the relationships of economic openness and economic development with green efficiency differ systematically across city-size tiers. The results show that the national mean VRS green-efficiency score is 0.736 and that efficiency follows a non-monotonic pattern across city sizes, with megacities recording the highest average level and large and medium-sized cities exhibiting relatively lower levels. Over time, green efficiency displays marked fluctuations rather than a sustained upward trajectory. The cross-tier pattern is also sensitive to returns-to-scale assumptions, as the relative VRS advantage of small cities disappears under the constant-returns-to-scale specification. In the second-stage analysis, economic openness is positively associated with green efficiency at the national level, while economic development shows no uniform independent association. Their interaction is positive and significant, indicating that the relationship between openness and green efficiency becomes more favorable as development increases. City-size heterogeneity is pronounced but structurally uneven: differences in the development–efficiency relationship are broad and statistically strong across city tiers, whereas openness-related heterogeneity is concentrated in specific inter-tier contrasts rather than being uniformly distributed across all city-size groups. These findings show that national averages conceal distinct urban trajectories and conditional relationships. Policy design should therefore account for differences in city size, development conditions, and the capacity of cities to translate external economic linkages and development gains into greener production performance.
