content: Early in-ovo sexing can support more efficient hatchery management by enabling sex determination before hatching.This study investigates a non-invasive framework for sexing Mojosari duck eggs at day 5 by integrating external morphological, embryonic vascular, and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM)-based textural features.External morphological measurements, including egg length and width, were obtained directly using a digital caliper, while egg weight was measured using a digital weighing scale; embryonic vascular and textural features were extracted from RGB candling images acquired with the eggshell intact.A total of 503 labeled eggs were analyzed.Statistical differences between female and male eggs were assessed using Welch's t-test with Holm adjustment and Hedges' g effect sizes, showing significant differences in Length, Width, Weight, and Sinus Terminalis Area.Four classifiers Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM-RBF, and XGBoost, were evaluated using Bayesian optimization and stratified cross-validation, with model configuration determined exclusively from training and validation data.On the independent test set of 100 eggs, Random Forest achieved 85.00% accuracy, 82.16% balanced accuracy, 83.41% Macro-F1, and 0.9285 ROC-AUC.Batch-held-out evaluation yielded 80.44% accuracy, 75.92% balanced accuracy, 77.22% Macro-F1, and 0.8795 ROC-AUC.The study provides application-level evidence for day-5 in-ovo sexing of Mojosari duck eggs using low-cost RGB candling, while characterizing sex-related features and contribution of feature groups (hybrid feature fusion).Future studies should validate the approach across broader duck populations, incubation stages, and imaging conditions.

title: COMPLEXITIES OF TEACHING AND LEARNING ENTREPRENEURSHIP IN THE SELECTED RURAL UNIVERSITY
source: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Economy
summary: In an era of rapidly growing recognition of entrepreneurship, understanding the complexities of teaching and learning entrepreneurship in rural South African universities is not just an academic endeavour; it is a strategy to build a sustai
content: In an era of rapidly growing recognition of entrepreneurship, understanding the complexities of teaching and learning entrepreneurship in rural South African universities is not just an academic endeavour; it is a strategy to build a sustainable, inclusive entrepreneurship development policy. Grounded on multiple theoretical lenses, cognitive development, critical, evolutionary and Schumpeterian theory, the study examines and critiques frameworks that guide entrepreneurship education, paying attention to rural universities. A qualitative research design was employed, using document analysis and Critical Discourse Analysis to explore policy documents and institutional reports from selected rural universities. The study revealed a persistent gap between theory and practice, and students struggle to transform abstract knowledge into real-world entrepreneurship. This is fuelled by weak entrepreneurship ecosystems, insufficient practical exposure, the digital divide and theoretically oriented lecturers. Overall, rural higher education remains constrained in structural, pedagogical and contextual challenges. The report recommends that universities transform their community challenges into business opportunities that students can use as a practical breeding ground for entrepreneurship development. In addition, the study endorses student-centred solutions such as project-based learning and work-integrated learning.

title: Does ESG Add Incremental Information to Multi-Factor Portfolios in China's A-Share Market? Evidence from CSI 300 Constituents
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: In recent years, more and more investors around the world have started to think about environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues when they invest, not just financial numbers. However, it is still not fully clear whether ESG adds rea
content: In recent years, more and more investors around the world have started to think about environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues when they invest, not just financial numbers. However, it is still not fully clear whether ESG adds real, extra information to a systematic, rule-based (quantitative) investment strategy, beyond what common risk factors already explain. This paper studies whether ESG shows incremental explanatory power in a quantitative stock portfolio, using stocks from the CSI 300 Index in China and ESG ratings from Huazheng ESG, one of the most widely used domestic ESG rating providers. Based on the Fama-French five-factor model plus a momentum factor, this study sorts stocks into an ESG long-short portfolio and uses a time-series regression to test whether this portfolio still earns a return that the other six factors cannot explain. This study expects the ESG portfolio to show a small but positive extra return (alpha) after controlling for size, value, profitability, investment, and momentum, though this result may partly overlap with these existing factors rather than being fully separate from them. The findings will help clarify how much new information ESG really adds to a standard quantitative portfolio in China's A-share market.

title: Epilogue: The Global Atom Between Past and Future
summary: In an era marked by climate change, political populism, geopo liti cal turmoil, and technological disruption, the future of nuclear power remains as contentious as ever.The debate about the atom in the 2020s is both heated and ambiguous.On
content: In an era marked by climate change, political populism, geopo liti cal turmoil, and technological disruption, the future of nuclear power remains as contentious as ever.The debate about the atom in the 2020s is both heated and ambiguous.On the one hand, we hear that nuclear power is seeing a revival, that numerous new reactors will soon be built worldwide, and that new, more advanced atom-splitting technologies are being worked out by creative teams of scientists and engineers.Power ful actors, from the White House to the International Energy Agency (IEA), view nuclear power as a vital component of solving vari ous prob lems.Without the atom, the enthusiasts tell us, complete decarbonization will never be pos si ble-especially in an age of artificial intelligence with its enormous electricity needs.Additionally, avoiding nuclear energy would increase our dependence on unreliable dictatorships for fossil fuel supplies.Alternatively, our electricity grids would suffer repeated breakdowns as they are overwhelmed by intermittent renewables.Many governments, including those of France, Britain, China, and India, are firmly committed to nuclear investment, regardless of the cost.The message is clear: Nuclear power's role will grow more prominent in the coming decades.On the other hand, the real-world trend, in terms of nuclear power's contribution to the global electricity mix, is a gradual and seemingly unstoppable decline.The downward trend has been more pronounced in some parts of the world than in others.In Europe, where about a third of the world's nuclear power plants were built, there were 178 reactors in operation in 1989.Since then, the number has dropped by 38 percent

title: Coal mine waste valorisation for soil fertility enhancement in Malawi: a critical review of processing technologies, agronomic potential, and environmental sustainability
source: Acta Agriculturae Scandinavica Section B - Soil & Plant Science
summary: Malawi's experience with coal mine waste offers a transferable regional case for evaluating safe and economically viable agricultural reuse in other resource-constrained mining regions. Coal mining produces heterogeneous residues that pose
content: Malawi's experience with coal mine waste offers a transferable regional case for evaluating safe and economically viable agricultural reuse in other resource-constrained mining regions. Coal mining produces heterogeneous residues that pose environmental challenges yet may improve soils when their properties and risks are characterised. This review evaluates the agronomic potential, processing options, environmental safeguards, economics and governance of coal-derived materials, drawing on official sources and studies from the Livingstonia Coalfield and Mchenga and Kaziwiziwi mines. These materials may supply silicon, potassium, calcium, iron, carbonaceous matter and soil-forming minerals, but their value is source-specific and cannot be inferred from total elemental concentrations. Although local evidence is limited, Mchenga waste contained nutrient-bearing elements alongside measurable potentially toxic elements, underscoring the need for screening before use. A preliminary matrix identifies northern Rumphi and Karonga as logical pilot sites. Direct application should be limited to demonstrably low-risk materials, while organic blending, targeted activation and engineered soil formulations are more controllable. A SWOT analysis and phased framework link characterisation, mineral-recovery screening, agronomic testing, economics, regulation and farmer adoption. Agricultural use should follow only if higher-value mineral recovery proves unsuitable. Priorities include site characterisation, logistics, multi-season field trials, contaminant bioavailability, techno-economic analysis and enforceable product specifications.

title: Decarbonizing Toward Justice: Sustaining Academic Community and Research in More Diverse Ways
summary: For many historians, travel for archival research or academic events is key to intellectual community, professionalization, and producing scholarship.Yet, the climate crisis and COVID-19 pandemic have underscored long-standing calls to crit
content: For many historians, travel for archival research or academic events is key to intellectual community, professionalization, and producing scholarship.Yet, the climate crisis and COVID-19 pandemic have underscored long-standing calls to critically reimagine the assumption of frequent air travel, the greatest source of emissions for most academics.Recent studies have demonstrated the urgency of this issue.For example, academic travel in the last few years from just one R1 US university generated annual emissions equivalent to a small city in the Philippines, and travel to a single academic conference in 2019 equaled the annual emissions of Edinburgh, UK. 1 Academia's emphasis on frequent travel incurs other burdens as well, especially for scholars at under-resourced universities or in rural areas, those working outside of the acad emy, and colleagues with caregiving responsibilities, mobility constraints, or neurodivergent conditions. 2 However, not traveling, especially to conferences where networking happens, can exact a high professional toll, particularly for gradu ate students, early career scholars, precariously employed academics, scholars at non-elite institutions, and those based in the Global South.Perhaps you are already nodding your head in agreement, fired up to rethink academic travel.In that case, skip ahead to the bullets, where we describe examples of academic conferences, organizations, and informal networks that are already doing just that.If you are on the fence, keep reading.Allow us to make the case that decarbonizing academic travel should be embraced as part of a larger proj ect of building more inclusive, equitable, and accessible academic communities.A growing body of research has documented the climate impacts of scholarly gatherings.This research demonstrates that not only is decarbonization of conferences pos si ble, but it is also not an either/or scenario of fully in person or fully remote.3 A range of alternative formats 31

title: An exploratory typology of regulatory conditions for autonomous, digital, and zero-emission freight innovations in Europe
summary: The EU′s concurrent policy initiatives toward decarbonisation, digitalisation, and automation of freight transport have generated a rapidly expanding body of regulations, technical standards, and emerging governance frameworks. However, the
content: The EU′s concurrent policy initiatives toward decarbonisation, digitalisation, and automation of freight transport have generated a rapidly expanding body of regulations, technical standards, and emerging governance frameworks. However, the regulatory landscape is not uniformly uncertain for multimodal freight innovators, as different domains, transport modes, and regulatory instruments create distinct deployment challenges that generic calls for regulatory clarity cannot address. This article presents an empirically grounded, cross-modal mapping of the EU multimodal freight regulatory landscape, developed through a workflow-based comparative methodology applied to the HOLOGISTICS Horizon Europe innovation portfolio. Assessing more than thirty regulatory instruments across 3 functional domains, comprising transport assets operations, digital data interoperability, and electrical charging systems, a typology of regulatory conditions structured along 2 dimensions is proposed: regulatory specificity and regulatory maturity. The typology yields 4 quadrants: Settled Prescription, Prescriptive Transition, Active Convergence, and Regulatory Vacuum, each associated with a distinct deployment risk profile and a targeted policy response. Applied to the HOLOGISTICS innovation portfolio – with particular analytical depth on autonomous Inland Water Way (IWW) operations and digital freight platforms, which represent the most regulatory-complexity cases the typology reveals that the most technologically ambitious innovations operate in the least settled regulatory environments. Consequently, we observe that current EU research and innovation funding frameworks often underproduce the explicit regulatory outputs necessary for these innovations to achieve real-world deployment. The article concludes with differentiated policy recommendations addressed to EU institutions, national regulators, and research programme designers.

title: Role of Spirulina and plant resins in sustainable edible packaging and smart food preservation systems
summary: As the world goes circular, there is a growing need for sustainable substitutes of petroleum-based food packaging. The present article explores the potential of biopolymers produced from Spirulina platensis for facilitating the development
content: As the world goes circular, there is a growing need for sustainable substitutes of petroleum-based food packaging. The present article explores the potential of biopolymers produced from Spirulina platensis for facilitating the development of novel bioactive packaging materials. Due to their inherent antibacterial and antioxidant properties, the issues discussed herein address the challenges of minimizing plastic waste generation and improving food safety at the same time. Spirulina platensis is a significant source of bioactive substances, including proteins, phycocyanin, polysaccharides, and other functional elements. These components contribute to the synthesis of a biopolymer matrix with promising film-forming capabilities, antioxidant and antibacterial potential, and the ability to promote the development of sustainable bioactive packaging materials. To overcome conventional constraints like moisture sensitivity and brittleness, the paper describes several formulation techniques, such as blend casting and nanotechnology integration. High production costs and inconsistent supply chains continue to impede commercial scaling, even while laboratory-scale results show notable increases in the shelf life of perishable goods (meat, dairy, and fruit products). In conclusion, Spirulina platensis-based bioactive packaging represents a promising and sustainable approach to the development of innovative active packaging materials. Its protein- and polysaccharide-rich composition, along with its antioxidant and antimicrobial potential, offers opportunities to improve packaging functionality and food preservation. However, further research is required to standardise formulation performance, enhance mechanical and barrier properties, ensure sensory acceptability, and establish scalable production strategies for successful commercial application.

title: Humpty Dumpty Epistocracies: Democratic Inclusion, Public Ignorance and the Structural Instability of Epistocracy
summary: Abstract Epistocrats argue that public ignorance justifies epistocratic interferences with our political decisions to protect and promote the common good. In response, this paper shows that inclusive democracy is a more structurally stable
content: Abstract Epistocrats argue that public ignorance justifies epistocratic interferences with our political decisions to protect and promote the common good. In response, this paper shows that inclusive democracy is a more structurally stable institutional response to public ignorance than exclusionary epistocracy, whether justified with instrumentalist, paternalistic or jury defences. A Robust Political Economy framework helps to show why epistocracy is fragile. Epistocrats see that informed knowers are competent, but overlook that they are highly unrepresentative, which makes empowering them structurally unstable. An ignorant public does not know that the knowers are competent and lacks a peaceful way to oust unrepresentative politicians from power. This creates a competence/stability dilemma: either epistocracy prioritises a competent politics that fails to represent ignorant citizens and compromises stability, or epistocracy prioritises a stable politics that represents ignorant citizens but compromises the competence that epistocracy promises. This turns the democracy/epistocracy debate away from competence and towards institutional stability and feasibility. The problem is not that the public is too ignorant for democracy, but that the public may be too ignorant for epistocracy.

title: Vietnam’s Economic Transformation: Institutional Opportunities and Challenges Toward the 2045 Vision
summary: Vietnam’s four-decade development trajectory from under $100 per capita in 1986 to the upper-middle-income threshold of $5,026 per capita in 2025, with gross domestic product (GDP) reaching $514 billion and growth of 8.02% (General Statisti
content: Vietnam’s four-decade development trajectory from under $100 per capita in 1986 to the upper-middle-income threshold of $5,026 per capita in 2025, with gross domestic product (GDP) reaching $514 billion and growth of 8.02% (General Statistics Office of Vietnam [GSO], 2026, Socio-economic Situation in the Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025), is one of the most compelling in post-war economic history. The 14th National Party Congress (19-23 January 2026) escalated ambitions dramatically, targeting annual GDP growth of at least 10% for 2026-2030 and achieving high-income status by 2045. However, the relationship between reform declarations and institutional outcomes in Vietnam is historically tenuous: only 25% of the Vietnam 2035 recommendations were reflected in policy documents by 2023 (World Bank, 2025a, Vietnam 2045: Breaking Through: Institutions for a High-income Future). This article employs a qualitative research design with systematic secondary data analysis to critically examine the institutional dimensions of Vietnam’s economic transformation, giving explicit attention to tensions and contradictions that official narratives understate. The article proposes two hypotheses: H1—institutional quality, measured through the Provincial Competitiveness Index (PCI), Worldwide Governance Indicators and Corruption Perceptions Index, mediates the translation of policy ambition into long-run growth outcomes; and H2—the Four Pillar Resolutions (57, 59, 66, 68) represent a structurally coherent reform package that is nonetheless vulnerable to the same state capture risks and implementation fragmentation that constrained earlier reform cycles. Synthesising evidence from World Bank (2025a, Vietnam 2045: Breaking Through: Institutions for a High-income Future, 2025b, Vietnam 2045: Growing Greener: Pathways to a Resilient and Sustainable Future), Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA) (2024, Vietnam 2045: Pathways to a High-income Future), GSO (2026, Socio-economic Situation in the Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025), PCI 2024 (Malesky et al., 2025, The Vietnam Provincial Competitiveness Index and Provincial Green Index Report 2024: Promoting a Business-enabling and Environmentally Friendly Investment Climate), ISEAS (2025, To Lam Prepares for Private Sector-led Growth in Vietnam) and CECODES, RTA, & UNDP (2025), the article identifies both genuine institutional opportunities and structural risks that require sober assessment. The study contributes an analytically balanced perspective to the India-Vietnam comparative literature.

title: A robust and interpretable hybrid SunAFNet framework for sunflower classification with adversarial resilience and mIoU-validated explainability
summary: Accurate and reliable monitoring of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) developmental phases and health status is fundamental for optimizing agricultural yields and ensuring global food security. Manual diagnostics are subjective and time-consumi
content: Accurate and reliable monitoring of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) developmental phases and health status is fundamental for optimizing agricultural yields and ensuring global food security. Manual diagnostics are subjective and time-consuming, and most stand-alone deep learning architectures are limited in their ability to accurately model the fine-grained spatial texture and long-range relationships between the various parts of the capitulum. For this study, we introduce a novel dual-stream hybrid framework: SunAFNet which combines a frozen DenseNet201 backbone with a selectively fine-tuned Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16). The key component of the architecture is a flexible Attention Fusion Module, which dynamically weights local spatial descriptors and global contextual features based on input complexity with an MLP-Softmax mechanism. SunAFNet has been evaluated on a large image dataset of 5,111 images of capitula of five growth and health classes and resulted in a diagnostic accuracy of 97.26%, which is better than the existing CNN and Transformer baselines. The framework showed very high generalization capability, achieving 94.26% accuracy on an independent secondary dataset, and remained very close to the optimal Robustness Index of 0.9899 despite various environmental and digital perturbations. A low value of the Expected Calibration Error (ECE 0.0675) was found, and the model achieved near-perfect selective prediction (accuracy 1.000) on clean data. Furthermore, SunAFNet demonstrated pronounced defensive resilience across a multi-level FGSM adversarial spectrum ( \(\:\epsilon\in\:\left\{0.01,0.05,0.10,0.20,0.30\right\}\) ), maintaining 71.71% accuracy at \(\:ϵ=0.10\:\) and retaining 42.35% diagnostic capability even under extreme perturbation ( \(\epsilon = 0.30\) ), well above stochastic chance. Moreover, a multi-layered Explainable AI (XAI) suite was validated empirically to ensure that the model’s logic is based on biologically relevant floral markers with a statistically significant mIoU of 0.7487 ( p = 0.0098), ensuring grounded diagnostic decisions. SunAFNet can provide a platform to support real-time precision agricultural monitoring, which is both fast and efficient in terms of both computing and inference speed, with an inference latency of merely 38.35 ms.

title: Live bass, fish heads, and bacalao: ethnic supermarkets increase seafood access and strengthen food system resilience in a US urban system
summary: Ethnic supermarkets serving specific cultural communities have long provided alternatives to mainstream food retail systems; however, their role in seafood diversity and supply chain structure is poorly understood. To characterize product d
content: Ethnic supermarkets serving specific cultural communities have long provided alternatives to mainstream food retail systems; however, their role in seafood diversity and supply chain structure is poorly understood. To characterize product diversity and pricing, we surveyed non-frozen seafood products at supermarkets serving Asian, Black/Latin American/Caribbean, Eastern European, and “mainstream” communities in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA, and conducted interviews with store staff to elucidate seafood procurement systems at different stores. The four types of stores offered significantly different product compositions from each other (i.e., different mixes of live organisms, whole finfish, fillets, and processed and packaged products). Asian supermarkets offered significantly greater diversity in seafood species (including higher proportions of wild-caught and domestic species) at significantly lower prices than other stores. Interviews suggested that seafood supply chains at the large chain businesses were typically highly centralized, while smaller and ethnic businesses tended to work with multiple and culturally specific providers, and in many cases put considerable effort into building a complex network of suppliers in order to obtain their desired seafood products. These results indicate that ethnic supermarkets provide critical access to culturally specific seafood products for a wide range of communities, in stark contrast to an increasingly homogenized mainstream seafood retail system. These ethnic markets further function as an established but in some ways underrecognized market for domestic seafood. They also provide an example of a non-corporate, alternative food system resilient to perturbations. Small-scale seafood harvesters and local seafood advocates could benefit from recognizing and building on these successful existing networks.

title: WCIP-based modeling and deep neural network–driven optimization of a terahertz sensor for IoT-enabled green hydrogen monitoring
summary: Reliable hydrogen monitoring is a critical requirement for the safe deployment of emerging green hydrogen infrastructures. In this work, a compact terahertz (THz) hydrogen sensor combining physics-based electromagnetic modeling and data-dri
content: Reliable hydrogen monitoring is a critical requirement for the safe deployment of emerging green hydrogen infrastructures. In this work, a compact terahertz (THz) hydrogen sensor combining physics-based electromagnetic modeling and data-driven optimization is proposed. The sensing platform consists of three laterally cascaded spiral resonators functionalized with graphene, black phosphorus (BP), and vanadium dioxide (VO \(_2\) ), enabling strong near-field confinement and tunable electromagnetic interaction with the surrounding gas medium. The device is analyzed using an extended Wave Concept Iterative Process (WCIP), which provides an efficient full-wave framework for modeling planar structures incorporating ultrathin conductive and anisotropic materials without volumetric discretization. Hydrogen sensing is evaluated through concentration-dependent resonance-frequency shifts associated with the modeled hydrogen-induced perturbation of the VO \(_2\) sensing region, while the intrinsic refractive-index sensitivity is evaluated separately. The investigated concentrations range from 500 ppm to 40 000 ppm H \(_2\) , covering ppm-level concentrations up to approximately the lower explosive limit (LEL). The optimized configuration achieves sensitivities ranging from 1.22 to 1.39 THz/RIU while maintaining sharp spectral responses and quality factors between 22.2 and 25.8. To accelerate the design exploration process, a deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model is developed to learn the nonlinear relationship between material parameters and sensing performance. Comparative evaluation against several machine-learning algorithms demonstrates the superior predictive accuracy of the proposed DNN, enabling rapid multi-parameter optimization beyond conventional full-wave simulations. Finally, the proposed sensing platform is discussed as a potential component of a 6G-enabled Internet-of-Things (IoT) monitoring architecture for distributed hydrogen-safety monitoring. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach for high-resolution THz hydrogen sensing in next-generation smart energy systems.

title: Nanozyme innovative drugs: characteristics and non-clinical development pathway
summary: Nanozymes integrate the tunable microstructure of nanomaterials with the catalytic activity of natural redox enzymes, positioning them as frontier candidates in catalytic medicine. Their catalytic stability, multi-enzyme synergy and low-cos
content: Nanozymes integrate the tunable microstructure of nanomaterials with the catalytic activity of natural redox enzymes, positioning them as frontier candidates in catalytic medicine. Their catalytic stability, multi-enzyme synergy and low-cost scalable synthesis are offset by nano-specific risks––accumulation, free metal leakage, protein-corona-driven immune disturbance and complement activation––that preclude direct application of conventional drug-evaluation guidelines. In this narrative review, evidence was retrieved from [PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI; January 2007–June 2026]. This review surveys the microstructure–activity relationships, standardized preparation and disease-intervention mechanisms of five representative nanozymes (Fe3O4, CeO2, noble-metal, single-atom carbon-based and metal-organic framework (MOF)-based). Benchmarking against the International Council for Harmonization (ICH) guideline suite and National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) nanomedicine-specific technical guidelines, it proposes an integrated non-clinical evaluation framework spanning quality control, absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME), multi-level toxicology and efficacy stratification, and outlines translational bridging through backbone cross-comparison and the ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-intercalated layered double hydroxide (LDH) paradigm. No nanozyme has yet been approved as a drug; translation hinges on quantifying structure–activity relationships, harmonizing nano-specific evaluation standards and generating early human data. Precision material design, standardized catalytic-activity assays and exploratory clinical studies are the near-term priorities.

title: Room temperature chemical upcycling of poly(bisphenol A carbonate) via solvent- and catalyst-free aminolysis
summary: amine-induced depolymerization under solvent- and catalyst-free conditions at room temperature. Under these mild conditions, PC polymer is rapidly cleaved to produce bisphenol A (BPA) with 94% yield and a high-value 2-imidazolidinone (IMD)
content: amine-induced depolymerization under solvent- and catalyst-free conditions at room temperature. Under these mild conditions, PC polymer is rapidly cleaved to produce bisphenol A (BPA) with 94% yield and a high-value 2-imidazolidinone (IMD) with 80% yield, through a practical isolation protocol. This method was applied to post-consumer PC plastics, such as safety goggles, bike helmet shields, and mobile phone cases, achieving good yields of BPA and IMD products. The structural characterization of BPA and IMD was confirmed by single-crystal XRD, NMR, and FT-IR techniques. In a co-valorization approach integrating plastic and biomass feedstocks, the reaction of shredded compact disc PC waste with biomass-derived furfurylamine was successfully scaled to a 15 g batch, affording BPA in 84% yield along with a 66% yield of the biomass-based urea derivative (1,3-bis(furan-2-ylmethyl)urea). Green chemistry metrics and technoeconomic analysis underscore the environmental and economic advantages of the developed recycling technology for the PC plastic industry. Overall, the study establishes a practical, room temperature, solvent- and catalyst-free platform for upcycling PC plastic waste into value-added building blocks, contributing to more sustainable management of PC plastics.

title: Sacrificial Nitrogen‐Rich Molecule‐Modified Resin for Fabricating Hard Carbon With Enhanced Plateau Sodium Storage
summary: ABSTRACT Closed pores in hard carbon are crucial for enhancing low‐voltage plateau Na + storage. However, their construction through precursor molecular engineering remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a molecular design stra
content: ABSTRACT Closed pores in hard carbon are crucial for enhancing low‐voltage plateau Na + storage. However, their construction through precursor molecular engineering remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a molecular design strategy by incorporating sacrificial nitrogen‐rich molecules into phenolic resin, enabling the one‐step construction of hard carbon (PMF‐HC) with enhanced plateau storage capability. Specifically, melamine participates in the resin network via co‐condensation and preferentially decomposes during pyrolysis, reconstructing the pyrolysis pathway. This process promotes defect and vacancy generation while inhibiting graphitic layer ordering, thereby constructing a highly disordered carbon architecture enriched with intrinsic closed pores favorable for Na + plateau storage. Consequently, PMF‐HC exhibits a high reversible capacity of 342 mAh g −1 with an initial Coulombic efficiency of 91.7%, dominated by an excellent plateau capacity of 256 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, PMF‐HC exhibits outstanding rate performance, retaining 72.4% capacity at 2000 mA g −1 , and outstanding cycling stability with a capacity decay of 0.0484% per cycle over 1200 cycles at 400 mA g −1 . PMF‐HC‖Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 full cell, with an energy density of 234 Wh kg −1 , verified its practical performance. This study highlights the importance of molecular design of polymer precursors in directing carbon structural evolution and provides a versatile strategy for constructing advanced hard carbon.

title: AI-enabled XR digital twins for integrated electric mobility and urban energy systems: A review and conceptual co-optimization framework
source: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
summary: This review critically synthesizes research at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, extended reality (XR), electric mobility, and urban energy systems, with two contributions: a structured evidence synthesis and
content: This review critically synthesizes research at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, extended reality (XR), electric mobility, and urban energy systems, with two contributions: a structured evidence synthesis and a conceptual Integrated Mobility-Energy Digital Twin (IMED) co-optimization framework. A PRISMA-informed workflow covers Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar from January 2020 to 15 September 2026, with thematic coding of AI prediction/control, EV-grid interaction, digital-twin maturity, XR decision support, validation, and deployment barriers. IMED is positioned as a conceptual architecture rather than a validated real-time platform. Its contribution is the joint specification of mobility and electrical decision variables and constraints, distinction among digital models, digital shadows, and bidirectionally synchronized twins, and a governed XR feedback pathway enabling authorized human input to modify bounded priorities, constraints, scenario approval, annotations, or safe overrides. A multi-objective formulation addresses charging cost, emissions, congestion, travel time, battery degradation, user inconvenience, and grid risk. Key gaps include city-scale validation, benchmark datasets, interoperability, cybersecurity, uncertainty quantification, and developing-country evidence. Proposed evaluation targets include grid conflicts, renewable-energy utilization, charging cost, accessibility, emissions, reliability, latency, constraint violations, and human decision quality.

title: Monitoreo comunitario en arrecifes coralinos: trayectoria de una brigada en el Parque Nacional Arrecife de Puerto Morelos
summary: Introduction: Community participation provides a mechanism to directly involve local populations in the monitoring, conservation, and management of protected natural areas linked to their territory. In reef ecosystems, where maintaining con
content: Introduction: Community participation provides a mechanism to directly involve local populations in the monitoring, conservation, and management of protected natural areas linked to their territory. In reef ecosystems, where maintaining continuous monitoring programs poses a significant logistical challenge, community monitoring teams can help generate ecological data and strengthen their connection to environmental management. In Mexico, this type of participation has been promoted by CONANP through subsidy programs. Objective: This study documents and analyzes the trajectory of a community monitoring team dedicated to reef monitoring in the Puerto Morelos Reef National Park, examining its organizational evolution, capacity development, and generated ecological data, as well as its contribution to the monitoring and management of the protected natural area. Methods: The study describes the path of formation, growth, and consolidation of the collective, its organizational practices, cooperation with authorities and other organizations, and the biological monitoring strategies sustained over a six-year period. Results: Between 2019 and 2025, the team evolved from an emergent response to Stony Coral Tissue Loss Disease into a platform for continuous observation and rapid environmental response. The monitoring efforts generated reliable data across 13 monitored sites, including eight historical priority sites. The team incorporated new indicators and post-disturbance assessment strategies for hurricanes, bleaching, and diseases, strengthening its technical capacity and networks with authorities, academia, and civil society organizations. The data generated directly influenced management decisions, including the temporary closure of subzones due to bleaching and the activation of post-hurricane restoration actions. Conclusions: This case study illustrates how a community brigade progressively became a space for participatory governance and knowledge co-production. Its trajectory documents the decisions, organizational adjustments, and renewal processes through which the brigade responded to changes, constraints, and emerging needs over time, reflecting the dynamic and adaptive nature of such initiatives within the context of Protected Natural Areas. Over a period marked by recurrent reef disturbances, the brigade managed to sustain monitoring continuity, expand its technical and organizational capacities, and generate information that contributed to the monitoring and decision-making processes within the PNAPM.

title: Are organisations expanding greenwashing to social and governance washing? A quantitative inquiry on ESG disclosure volumes in the Colombo Stock Exchange
summary: This study investigates whether greenwashing, involving intentional or unintentional false environmental assertions, has extended into the social and governance dimensions, resulting in what could be labelled as ESG-washing. Drawing on legi
content: This study investigates whether greenwashing, involving intentional or unintentional false environmental assertions, has extended into the social and governance dimensions, resulting in what could be labelled as ESG-washing. Drawing on legitimacy theory and impression management approaches, the research examines ESG disclosure volume patterns among 42 non-financial companies listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange during the period 2018/19–2022/23. The study considers disclosure breadth, rather than ESG performance, as a potential indicator of washing behaviour, examining whether patterns in disclosure growth are consistent with strategic impression management or true ESG commitment. By analysing the temporal, dimensional, and aggregate patterns of four indices, i.e. environmental, social, governance, and total ESG, the study identified three key findings. First, disclosure expansion is selective rather than parallel across all dimensions. Second, the social dimension is the dominant pattern of dimensional imbalance, suggesting emphasis on dimensions involving less verifiable claims. Third, non-linear environmental expansion patterns suggest a reactive response to external pressures rather than integration with sustainability. Overall, the findings indicate disclosure patterns consistent with potential washing beyond environmental claims, although materiality choices and contextual events in the emerging market setting offer equally plausible explanations.

title: Finite Element Simulation of the Polishing Process for Aluminum Workpieces in the LS-DYNA Software
summary: Abstract Finishing of long cylindrical aluminium components increasingly relies on abrasive belt machining, yet dependable guidelines for selecting its operating regimes remain scarce. To help close this gap, the present work applies explic
content: Abstract Finishing of long cylindrical aluminium components increasingly relies on abrasive belt machining, yet dependable guidelines for selecting its operating regimes remain scarce. To help close this gap, the present work applies explicit dynamic finite element modelling in LS-DYNA to reproduce, at the scale of a single abrasive grain, how the surface of a 6061-T6 alloy is generated during belt polishing. Two idealised grain geometries are contrasted: a truncated cone standing for a fresh abrasive and a half-ellipsoid approximating the same grain after wear. The material response is captured through the Johnson-Cook constitutive and fracture relations together with a Mie-Grüneisen equation of state, so that high strain rates, frictional heating and element erosion are reflected. For each geometry the resultant contact force, the total, sliding and workpiece-side energies, the actual contact area, the contact-zone temperature, the chip morphology and the residual groove profile were examined while the sliding velocity, the indentation depth and the friction coefficient were varied. The computations show that wear-driven rounding of the grain reduces the polishing force at low speeds but simultaneously raises the dissipated energy and the local heating, whereas the conical grain leaves a smoother groove under milder thermal loading. Near a practical belt speed of about 5 m/s the predicted temperature rise stays limited, and grain shape combined with cutting depth governs the attainable finish more strongly than speed alone. These findings offer a physically grounded basis for choosing rational polishing conditions and for deciding when a worn belt should be replaced.

title: Rearrangements of carbocations during isomerization and oligomerization of hydrocarbons: is it time to dot the ‘i’?
summary: The mechanisms of the rearrangements of carbocations, usually discussed within college courses in organic chemistry, are often superficial and incomplete.In this feature article, we discuss development of ideas about the reaction mechanisms
content: The mechanisms of the rearrangements of carbocations, usually discussed within college courses in organic chemistry, are often superficial and incomplete.In this feature article, we discuss development of ideas about the reaction mechanisms and up-todate understanding of the pathways of similar processes using high-level DFT modeling.Additionally, we present how fast DFT simulations (PRIRODA software) foster visualization and understanding of carbocation transformations.

title: Halal and Tayyiban Food Security: Towards an Ethical and Sustainable Global Food System
source: Journal of Halal Science Industry and Business
summary: This study aims to explore how Halal and Tayyiban principles can be integrated into the wider discourse on food security to promote a more sustainable, ethical, and spiritually conscious global food system. It seeks to identify the potentia
content: This study aims to explore how Halal and Tayyiban principles can be integrated into the wider discourse on food security to promote a more sustainable, ethical, and spiritually conscious global food system. It seeks to identify the potential of these principles to enhance resilience, trust, and inclusivity within food supply chains. This paper employs a systematic literature review, synthesising findings from peer-reviewed publications, institutional reports, and policy documents that address the intersections among halal assurance, sustainability, and food security. The review highlights key themes, conceptual relationships, and policy implications that emerge from the literature. The analysis shows that Halalan Tayyiban food security strengthens traditional food security models by incorporating ethical, environmental, and social justice dimensions. Upholding tayyiban standards encourages responsible production and consumption, boosts consumer confidence, and promotes sustainable resource management. The findings emphasise the importance of multi-stakeholder collaboration, effective halal governance, and transparency in ensuring that food systems remain both secure and spiritually meaningful. This study is based on secondary data and conceptual analysis. Future empirical research is necessary to test the implementation of Halalan Tayyiban principles across different cultural and institutional contexts. This paper contributes to the emerging global dialogue on Islamic perspectives in sustainable food systems. It offers a holistic conceptual framework that integrates Halal and Tayyiban values into the broader agenda of global food security, fostering an ethical, resilient, and spiritually aligned approach to feeding the world.

title: Sliding scales in the steel industry – an effective basis for comparison?
source: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
summary: Abstract Purpose The decarbonization of the steel industry is an important contributor to reaching net-zero by 2050. Increased circularity is expected to aid in this transition. However, the constrained nature of scrap supply is often not a
content: Abstract Purpose The decarbonization of the steel industry is an important contributor to reaching net-zero by 2050. Increased circularity is expected to aid in this transition. However, the constrained nature of scrap supply is often not accounted for, which could lead to unsustainable decision-making. A sliding scale framework could enable a more robust comparison between decarbonization measures. However, multiple frameworks have been developed, differing in their methodological approaches. Method A four step method was implemented to investigate three sliding scale frameworks. This consisted of a literature review, comparative analysis, life cycle assessment, and discussion and recommendation development. In the first two phases the method documents of sliding scale frameworks were studied and compared based on a selection of fundamental elements and modelling requirements. For each framework, nine life cycle assessment scenarios were developed, according to the different methodological requirements of the respective system. These scenarios depict varying stages of conventional and decarbonized production across major production pathways. Finally, the results of the comparative analysis and LCA have been discussed, to determine if sliding-scale frameworks offer a robust basis for comparison, and to provide recommendations for future harmonization efforts between different frameworks. Results The comparative analysis identified methodological differences for every investigated aspect. The influence of these differences on the LCA results is in the same order of magnitude as those brought on by technical decarbonization measures. While the sliding scale systems enable a comparison across different scenarios, different conclusions can be drawn depending on which system is chosen for the analysis. This is mainly due to how quantitative emission thresholds are derived, in addition to diverging definitions of low-emission steel production. Conclusions Harmonization is required for multiple elements of the sliding scale methodologies. Most importantly, the near-zero production definition should be refined to include additional quantitative criteria and a common definition of low-emission production is required. Furthermore, a uniform approach is required for determining quantitative emission thresholds. It is proposed that both near-zero and low-emission steel definitions be based on a reference installation threshold representing conventional production processes.

title: Solar Resource Clustering for Strategic Concentrating Solar Power Plant Siting in South Africa
summary: South Africa has abundant solar resources, creating significant opportunities to deploy solar energy technologies to support decarbonization and enhance energy security. Concentrating Solar Power (CSP), when coupled with thermal energy stor
content: South Africa has abundant solar resources, creating significant opportunities to deploy solar energy technologies to support decarbonization and enhance energy security. Concentrating Solar Power (CSP), when coupled with thermal energy storage, can deliver dispatchable generation, which makes it uniquely suited to enable higher renewable penetration and support the energy transition. However, adoption of the technology in South Africa remains limited. To support future CSP development, this study proposes a solar resource clustering methodology to characterize and facilitate the identification of regions for targeted CSP deployment. The methodology incorporates satellite-derived direct normal irradiance data, a feature derivation strategy, and unsupervised clustering to delineate diverse solar resource clusters. The proposed method is evaluated against two alternative approaches to deriving the clustering inputs to demonstrate the value of clustering locations based on feature profiles that characterize the solar resource with respect to CSP-relevant temporal attributes. Results show that the clusters produced by the proposed method exhibit greater spatial granularity and temporal cohesion with respect to features relevant to CSP performance, compared to those produced by the alternative methods. The clusters also reveal significant diversity in the available solar resources across South Africa, pointing to deployment opportunities beyond traditionally targeted locations. Overall, the methodology can be applied to characterize solar resources and improve the understanding of spatiotemporal DNI patterns in the context of CSP siting. It further offers insights that could support improved representation of CSP in energy system planning frameworks.

title: Risk-Oriented Perspectives on Halal Compliance in Plant-Based Food Ingredients: Origin Variability and Production System Control
source: Journal of Halal Science Industry and Business
summary: Plant-based food systems are frequently perceived as inherently permissible due to their non-animal origin. However, the increasing use of multi-origin additives, fermentation-derived ingredients, recombinant enzymes, and complex processing
content: Plant-based food systems are frequently perceived as inherently permissible due to their non-animal origin. However, the increasing use of multi-origin additives, fermentation-derived ingredients, recombinant enzymes, and complex processing technologies introduces new challenges for Halal compliance. This review provides a risk-oriented assessment of Halal considerations in plant-based food ingredients, focusing on origin variability, production pathways, and manufacturing system integrity. Particular attention is given to emulsifiers, hydrocolloids, fermentation-derived flavor enhancers, recombinant proteins, blood-related components, and processing aids, all of which may involve animal-derived inputs, fermentation substrates, or genetically engineered systems. Beyond ingredient-level evaluation, the review highlights the importance of cross-contamination control, segregation practices, and traceability across shared production facilities. A structured Halal Critical Control Point (HCCP) framework is proposed to operationalize compliance assessment across raw material sourcing, fermentation media, enzyme production, solvent usage, and manufacturing systems. As plant-based innovation advances through biotechnology and precision fermentation, a system-based and science-driven Halal governance approach is essential to ensure compliance, consumer trust, and regulatory coherence

title: Toward Regenerative Energy Optimization in Historic Hospitals: The Case of Colțea Clinical Hospital, Bucharest
summary: The methodology combines a high-resolution energy simulation of the baseline scenario with a proposed two-pronged intervention:(1) the sensitive integration of a rooftop photovoltaic (PV) array, invisible from the street to protect urban id
content: The methodology combines a high-resolution energy simulation of the baseline scenario with a proposed two-pronged intervention:(1) the sensitive integration of a rooftop photovoltaic (PV) array, invisible from the street to protect urban identity, and (2) upgrades to the internal thermal envelope, including high-performance insulation and glazing.The results show a significant reduction in energy demand, with heating consumption decreasing by 21% and cooling by 13%.Crucially, the 499 MWh of annual PV production offsets 44% of the building's post-retrofit electricity needs.This work provides a validated, replicable model for transforming energy-intensive heritage buildings-particularly 24/7 healthcare facilities-into more sustainable and resilient assets, proving that deep energy retrofits are feasible without compromising historical value.

title: The Movement for Green AI
summary: Artificial Intelligence Is Part of the Climate EmergencyCan artificial intelligence (AI) "supercharge climate action"?On July 18, 2023, the leader of the United Nations (UN), António Guterres, rallied a hall of experts with the proposal tha
content: Artificial Intelligence Is Part of the Climate EmergencyCan artificial intelligence (AI) "supercharge climate action"?On July 18, 2023, the leader of the United Nations (UN), António Guterres, rallied a hall of experts with the proposal that AI just might save us from planetary collapse.The group was assembled in New York City to debate the promises and pitfalls of AI.Meanwhile, in Phoenix, AZ, meteorologists announced on the same day that the city had set a new heat rec ord: for the number of consecutive days with temperatures above 110°F.Ultimately, the city would lift above 110°F for thirty-one days in a row.Residents fried eggs on sidewalks.1 In New York, Guterres continued, "We need a race to develop AI for good." 2 By that point, the AI industry was already sprinting to capture the market potential of the climate emergency.From tech giants to scrappy start-ups, firms capitalized on climate disaster.3 In 2023, Google (the parent com pany of DeepMind, a top AI firm) rolled out its Green Light Proj ect, which used AI to coordinate traffic lights and reduce vehicle emissions from drivers idling at stop lights.4 Like many industry efforts, Google may well be addressing climate concerns with the aid of AI technologies.But many such efforts, including Google's Green Light Proj ect, leave in place-and extend-the underlying growth economy that is driving the climate crisis.In this case, Google reduced drivers' idling time but did nothing to cut the number of cars on the road through structural changes such as support for public transportation.Unsustainable, extractive, and unequally experienced, the growth economy also allows AI to be commercialized largely by private industry rather than to be held as a public resource-sidestepping public input and accountability for climate action.5 Shifting the focus from how AI tools are used to how AI systems are designed in the first place 39The Movement for Green AI

title: An alcohol-solution combustion combining with gel calcination process for the preparation of NixCoyCu(1-x-y)Fe2O4 magnetic nanoparticles and their adsorption performances of Congo red from aqueous solution
summary: NixCoyCu(1-x-y)Fe2O4 magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were successfully prepared through a novel and economical strategy coupling alcohol solution combustion with gel calcination, and their physicochemical and magnetic performances were verifi
content: NixCoyCu(1-x-y)Fe2O4 magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were successfully prepared through a novel and economical strategy coupling alcohol solution combustion with gel calcination, and their physicochemical and magnetic performances were verified by XRD, TEM and VSM techniques. For larger specific surface area and saturation magnetization to apply, three key elements those affected the whole preparation process including element proportion, calcination temperature, and absolute alcohol amount, and different characterization technique were optimized, and for the adsorption of Congo red (CR) dye, Ni0.1Co0.8Cu0.1Fe2O4 MNPs were fabricated under the conditions of 400 °C calcination for 2 hours with 65 mL absolute alcohol, the obtained product exhibited a uniform particle size of 18.9 nm and a saturation magnetization value of 76.4 emu/g. The influencing factors on the adsorption, including adsorption time, concentration of CR solution, and pH, were systematically investigated, and the adsorption mechanism was revealed, further analysis revealed that the adsorption process for CR on the nanoparticles exhibited a high consistency with pseudo-second-order kinetic and Langmuir models, which revealed that the adsorption of CR on Ni0.1Co0.8Cu0.1Fe2O4 MNPs belonged to the single-layer chemisorption, the adsorption efficiency remained at 81.4% of their first adsorption even after undergoing 8 cycles, and the adsorption capacity maintained larger values when the pH of CR solution was not more than 9.

title: Rongalite‐Mediated C( sp 2 )─H Methylenation of Imidazoheterocycles: A Metal‐Free Route to Symmetric Bis(heteroaryl)Methanes
summary: An efficient and sustainable protocol has been developed for the methylenation of heteroarenes using rongalite as a convenient methylene source. The reaction proceeds through the in situ generation of formaldehyde, enabling a green one‐pot
content: An efficient and sustainable protocol has been developed for the methylenation of heteroarenes using rongalite as a convenient methylene source. The reaction proceeds through the in situ generation of formaldehyde, enabling a green one‐pot synthesis of methylene‐bridged bis(heteroaryl) derivatives. The protocol applies to a diverse range of heteroarenes, providing the corresponding products in good to excellent yields. Furthermore, a gram‐scale reaction demonstrated the practical applicability and scalability of this methodology.

title: Tourism Flow Governance and Government Role in Historical Heritage Sites along the Silk Road: The Dunhuang Model and Its Implications for Samarkand
source: Central Asian Journal of Innovations on Tourism Management and Finance
summary: Taking the Mogao Grottoes in Dunhuang as a typical reference case, this paper constructs a government-led governance mechanism for tourism flow regulation at archaeological and historical heritage sites, aiming to provide theoretical founda
content: Taking the Mogao Grottoes in Dunhuang as a typical reference case, this paper constructs a government-led governance mechanism for tourism flow regulation at archaeological and historical heritage sites, aiming to provide theoretical foundations and practical optimization schemes for heritage city governance along the Silk Road. Adopting a comparative case study approach, this study develops a multidimensional analytical framework covering institution, technology, spatial planning, and social participation, and combines descriptive statistical analysis and dimensional effectiveness evaluation to systematically compare heritage tourism governance practices between Dunhuang and Samarkand. The results reveal that Dunhuang has established a mature government-led tourism flow governance system. Centered on a unified administrative institution, supported by preventive monitoring and early warning technologies, empowered by digital diversion and intelligent reservation scheduling, and guaranteed by community participation and benefit sharing, this system achieves a virtuous cycle of heritage protection and sustainable tourism development. Statistical data show that from 2015 to 2024, Dunhuang maintained a tourism revenue growth rate 4.5 percentage points higher than its tourist arrival growth rate, verifying the efficiency of the government-led model. In contrast, Samarkand currently confronts prominent governance dilemmas stemming from fragmented administrative management, uncontrolled urban spatial expansion, insufficient community engagement, and backward technical governance tools, where heritage protection fails to occupy a prioritized position in urban development decision-making. From 2015 to 2024, the compound annual growth rate of international tourists in Samarkand reached 34.7%, but supporting governance capacity lags far behind the expansion speed of tourist flows. This study innovatively introduces the government-led governance framework into the research of Silk Road archaeological heritage governance and conducts a systematic Sino-Uzbek comparative analysis of tourism flow governance models at world heritage sites. It complements the theoretical research on heritage tourism governance in transitional countries and provides targeted, operable policy implications for Samarkand to optimize its tourism flow governance system and balance heritage protection and industrial development.

title: Real-time visual wrinkle segmentation during paper deep drawing
summary: Abstract Paper deep drawing, inspired by the metal forming technique, is investigated as sustainable alternative to plastic packaging, aiming to achieve airtight sealing and versatile design. However, paper’s inherent tendency to form wrink
content: Abstract Paper deep drawing, inspired by the metal forming technique, is investigated as sustainable alternative to plastic packaging, aiming to achieve airtight sealing and versatile design. However, paper’s inherent tendency to form wrinkles complicates the production process, making it difficult to achieve consistent quality. To effectively control the forming of wrinkles, a runtime-optimized algorithm capable of quickly detecting them for precise material flow manipulation is required. Related fields like facial wrinkle and concrete crack detection provide promising methodologies, particularly using Gabor filters due to their edge-detection capabilities. However, speed optimization has rarely been prioritized in existing studies. Addressing these challenges, this research introduces the Runtime Optimized Wrinkle Detection (ROWDe) algorithm, employing Gabor filters for high accuracy and speed. ROWDe significantly reduces computation time through GPU acceleration, optimized kernel selection, and streamlined pre-processing. Tests on 12-megapixel images yield processing times of under 40 ms, suggesting the method’s suitability for real-time processing. With an average precision of 0.9151 and a recall of 0.8157 on a manually annotated paper deep drawing dataset, the algorithm proves robust against variations in lighting, paper color, and die shape.

title: Electron Beam Hardening and Surface Modification – Possibilities and Applications of the Technology
summary: Abstract Electron beam (EB) hardening and surface modification are advanced surface-engineering technologies enabling precise, localized enhancement of material properties with minimal thermal effects on the bulk material. This review discu
content: Abstract Electron beam (EB) hardening and surface modification are advanced surface-engineering technologies enabling precise, localized enhancement of material properties with minimal thermal effects on the bulk material. This review discusses the fundamental principles, process parameters, material responses, and industrial applications of electron beam surface treatment. Rapid heating and self-quenching during EB processing promote microstructural refinement and the formation of martensitic, bainitic, metastable, and nanostructured phases, leading to significant improvements in surface hardness, wear resistance, fatigue performance, and, in selected materials, corrosion resistance. The effects of key processing parameters, including beam energy, current, energy density, scanning speed, interaction time, and beam deflection, are considered. Applications in the automotive, aerospace, tooling, and medical sectors are presented, together with the main advantages and limitations of the technology. Electron beam processing is also compared with laser, induction, conventional heat treatment, ion beam, and plasma-based surface modification methods. Recent developments include hybrid treatments combining electron beam processing with nitriding and PVD coatings, pulsed electron beam technologies, compact accelerator systems, and advanced process monitoring. Future developments are expected to focus on Industry 4.0 integration, new material systems, hybrid processes, micro- and nanoscale surface engineering, sustainability, and broader industrial adoption.

title: Reliability-Calibrated q-Rung Orthopair Fuzzy Decision Support for Uncertainty-Aware Crop Prioritisation
summary: Crop prioritisation requires simultaneous evaluation of productivity, production stability, input burden, soil condition, and irrigation dependence under uncertain evidence. This study proposes a Reliability-Calibrated q-Rung Orthopair Fuzz
content: Crop prioritisation requires simultaneous evaluation of productivity, production stability, input burden, soil condition, and irrigation dependence under uncertain evidence. This study proposes a Reliability-Calibrated q-Rung Orthopair Fuzzy Distance-to-Ideal method (RC-qROF-DI) for transparent, non-predictive agricultural decision support. Unlike conventional applications that elicit membership, non-membership, and hesitation independently, RC-qROF-DI transforms observed desirability and empirical reliability into an admissible orthopair representation in which unresolved evidence is determined by data quality. The method was evaluated using 10,000 complete observations covering six crops and 20 soil, climate, management, contextual, and yield variables. Six decision criteria were constructed: mean yield, yield variability, fertilizer use, pesticide use, organic carbon, and irrigation dependence. Entropy weights were combined with q-rung orthopair distance-to-ideal ranking. At the primary Fermatean setting, sugarcane ranked first with a closeness coefficient of 0.5747, followed by potato (0.5473), wheat (0.4341), maize (0.4241), cotton (0.4195), and rice (0.4096). The first three positions were preserved across the intuitionistic, Pythagorean, Fermatean, and higher-rung specifications; full-ranking Spearman agreement with the primary model ranged from 0.9429 to 1.0000. All ±10% weight perturbations preserved the ranking. Across 500 stratified bootstrap samples, sugarcane ranked first in 86.4% and potato in 13.4%. The framework provides an auditable link from numerical evidence to fuzzy support, opposition, indeterminacy, and ranking uncertainty. Its output is a within-dataset production-profile prioritisation, not a location-specific agronomic recommendation.

title: Robust district-scale siting of solar and wind: A synthetic convex-optimization study motivated by South Korea
summary: This study develops a linear programming framework for solar and wind capacity allocation under pooled national energy balance and district-level monthly self-sufficiency. Motivated by South Korea’s energy transition, it uses 228 hypothetic
content: This study develops a linear programming framework for solar and wind capacity allocation under pooled national energy balance and district-level monthly self-sufficiency. Motivated by South Korea’s energy transition, it uses 228 hypothetical nodes and twelve synthetic monthly periods rather than observed Korean district data. The model combines capacity costs, a linear land-related penalty, and monthly energy requirements. An explicit interval uncertainty set yields a lower-envelope robust counterpart, while demand multipliers quantify marginal supply costs. In the synthetic instance, local rather than pooled balance increases the objective by 37.3%. A uniform 30% availability contraction increases capacity and cost by 42.9%, as implied by model homogeneity. Robust designs have zero shortfall at the lower-bound realization used in optimization; this is a feasibility check, not independent reliability validation. Sensitivity analyses vary the availability contraction and monthly energy buffer. A budgeted-uncertainty extension permits adaptive dispatch, and supplementary calculations examine the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and a three-bus hourly storage and transmission model. The results illustrate relationships between local supply obligations, uncertainty assumptions, and cost, without establishing empirical Korean siting outcomes or operational reliability.

title: An Integrated Computer Vision–Digital Twin Framework for Structural Health Monitoring and Comparative Environmental Risk Assessment of Reinforced Concrete Bridges Toward Sustainable Urban Development
source: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
summary: The progressive deterioration of reinforced concrete (RC) bridges driven by aging, increasing traffic demands, and aggressive environmental exposure presents significant challenges to structural reliability, infrastructure resilience, and s
content: The progressive deterioration of reinforced concrete (RC) bridges driven by aging, increasing traffic demands, and aggressive environmental exposure presents significant challenges to structural reliability, infrastructure resilience, and sustainable urban development. This study presents an integrated computer vision–digital twin (CV–DT) framework incorporating Mask R-CNN with a ResNet-50 feature pyramid network (FPN) for automated defect segmentation, structural condition assessment, and comparative environmental risk evaluation. A dataset comprising 6,000 annotated images collected from 12 RC bridges was utilized, representing cracking, concrete spalling, exposed reinforcement, and intact concrete surfaces. The proposed deep learning model was trained and evaluated using a 70:15:15 dataset partition, enabling pixel-level defect localization and quantitative damage characterization. The model achieved a precision of 93.1%, recall of 90.4%, and mean average precision (mAP@0.5) of 94.2%, while image-based crack-width estimation demonstrated a mean absolute error of 0.18 mm. Subsequently, segmented defects and associated damage indicators were integrated into a bridge information modeling–enabled digital twin to facilitate spatial deterioration mapping, condition visualization, and risk-informed maintenance planning. Comparative environmental risk assessment was performed using a multi-criteria decision-making approach based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), incorporating chloride exposure, flood susceptibility, temperature variability, and traffic-related pollution. The assessment identified substantial environmental vulnerability differences, with high-exposure bridges exhibiting an average composite risk index of 0.76 compared with 0.39 for low-exposure bridges. Furthermore, a scenario-based life-cycle assessment indicated that preventive maintenance strategies informed by integrated structural and environmental risk indicators could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 18% relative to conventional reactive maintenance practices. Cross-bridge validation and sensitivity analyses were considered to evaluate model transferability and environmental risk-ranking robustness. The findings highlight the potential of combining instance segmentation, digital twin technology, and environmental risk modeling to improve structural deterioration assessment and infrastructure decision-making. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach for intelligent bridge asset management, optimized maintenance prioritization, reduced environmental impacts, and the long-term sustainability of urban transportation networks.

title: Mass balance and metabolite profiles in humans of ACT001, a novel sesquiterpene lactone derivative, using 14 C‐radiolabelled techniques
summary: AIMS: ACT001, a novel sesquiterpene lactone derivative, is effective against treating glioblastoma multiforme and other diseases. This study aims to investigate its metabolic and excretion characteristics. METHODS: C]ACT001 was administered
content: AIMS: ACT001, a novel sesquiterpene lactone derivative, is effective against treating glioblastoma multiforme and other diseases. This study aims to investigate its metabolic and excretion characteristics. METHODS: C]ACT001 was administered to six healthy subjects. Blood, urine and fecal samples were collected and measured for total radioactivity (TRA), ACT001 and its main metabolite (monomethylamine micheliolide, MA-MCL). The safety was also assessed. RESULTS: ) of TRA, of TRA, ACT001 and MA-MCL were 33.7 h, 3.16 h, and 8.45 h, respectively. ACT001 and MA-MCL accounted for 14.49% and 30.50% of TRA, respectively. In addition, radiochromatographic profiling confirmed no other individual metabolite exceeded 2% of total peak area. The individual ratios of total radioactivity in whole blood relative to plasma ranged from 0.330 to 0.827. The primary excretion route of ACT001 was urine (accounting for 90.08% ± 1.16% of dose), with a small amount excreted in faeces (accounting for 7.30% ± 0.66% of dose), resulting in a total excretion rate of 97.39% ± 0.93%. Metabolites represented more than 80% of urinary excretion. The main metabolic pathways involved demethylation, oxidation, and dealkylation to form micheliolide and glucuronidation or cysteine conjugation of related metabolites. CONCLUSIONS: of TRA (33.7 h) vs. ACT001 (3.16 h) and MA-MCL (8.45 h). The overall mass balance was nearly complete. ACT001 and MA-MCL were the primary circulating compounds. Demethylated metabolites were the primary substances excreted in urine and faeces.

title: Fuel efficiency gains, market restructuring and rising fuel consumption in global passenger aviation (1996–2025)
summary: Abstract Fuel or GHG emission efficiency improvements are a key part of aircraft manufacturers’ narratives about their commitment to climate mitigation. However, climate impact depends on absolute emissions, and therefore on the amount of f
content: Abstract Fuel or GHG emission efficiency improvements are a key part of aircraft manufacturers’ narratives about their commitment to climate mitigation. However, climate impact depends on absolute emissions, and therefore on the amount of fuel burnt. The latter depends on several parameters, including traffic volumes, distances flown, fleet mix and seat density aboard. This calls for a joint assessment of the combined effect of technological progress, fleet renewal, market restructuring and traffic growth on the fuel consumption. Considering the global provision of regular passenger air services in 1996 and 2025, we find that fuel efficiency improved by 44% (as fuel intensity declined by 31%, from 32 to 22 g/available seat- kilometre), thanks to the introduction of newer aircraft, as well as changes in aircraft size, distance flown and seat density. Meanwhile, air traffic tripled (+ 8,037 billion available seat-kilometres), mostly due to more second/latest-generation aircraft being operated on medium-/long-haul routes. Consequently, the modelled amount of fuel burned has doubled (+ 139 million tonnes). This suggests that fuel savings from the phase-out of older aircraft were more than offset by the traffic increase associated with the deployment of newer aircraft, a dynamic that is insufficient to reduce the climate impact of passenger aviation.

title: The Formation Mechanisms and Governance Paths of ESG Greenwashing in Listed Companies
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: ESG information disclosure provides an important basis for investors and the public to understand the fulfillment of responsibilities by listed companies, while the deviation between disclosed content and actual actions also affects market
content: ESG information disclosure provides an important basis for investors and the public to understand the fulfillment of responsibilities by listed companies, while the deviation between disclosed content and actual actions also affects market evaluation and governance effectiveness. A review of relevant studies reveals that ESG greenwashing in listed companies mainly manifests as the omission of material adverse matters in content selection, the disconnection between commitments and actions in expression, the concealment of adverse activities in accounting scopes, and strategic arrangements in disclosure timing. The pursuit of reputational benefits by enterprises leads to greenwashing, and reporting requirements, regulatory accountability, and the availability of verifiable information provide opportunities for such behaviour. Identify the corresponding material problems and reporting scope in the governance measures, coordinate regulatory investigations with inspections and judicial supervision, and connect financing and policy support to actual results. The above measures can be based on reliable internal records and independent external audits. Further research is needed to establish corresponding standards for the identification of greenwashing, investigate whether disclosures are consistent with changes in operations, and determine when governance measures lead to continuous improvements.

title: Residual Infrastructures as Regenerative Terrains: Climateadaptive and Culturally Situated Design in Post-Colonial Tanzania
summary: Begin Across sub-Saharan Africa, the transformation of colonial infrastructures presents a distinct set of challenges and opportunities that diverge from Eurocentric narratives of post-industrial redevelopment.Cities such as Iringa are shap
content: Begin Across sub-Saharan Africa, the transformation of colonial infrastructures presents a distinct set of challenges and opportunities that diverge from Eurocentric narratives of post-industrial redevelopment.Cities such as Iringa are shaped not by decommissioned factories, but by residual socio-productive architectures whose material logics, climatic intelligence, and symbolic weight continue to structure everyday life.These spaces are neither abandoned nor fully assimilated into the contemporary urban metabolism; rather, they occupy an intermediate condition where memory, identity, and environmental adaptation intersect in complex ways.This contribution emerges from a fifteen-year trajectory of field-based research conducted between universities, local
