In this study, Periplocymarin was identified as a selective anti-NSCLC candidate. Its antitumor activity was verified in cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration assays and patient-derived organoid models. To dissect its antitumor mechanism, we employed an integrated strategy combining transcriptome sequencing, network pharmacology, thermal proteome profiling (TPP), microscale thermophoresis (MST) and molecular simulations, and validated the involvement of p38α MAPK (MAPK14) phosphorylation via Western blot. Finally, the in vivo antitumor efficacy and safety of Periplocymarin were validated using nude mouse xenograft and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Periplocymarin inhibited proliferation and migration and induced apoptosis in NSCLC cells in a concentration-dependent manner, while also suppressing Patient-Derived Organoid (PDO) growth. Integrated analyses and experimental validation indicated MAPK14 as a candidate target associated with Periplocymarin treatment. Periplocymarin reduced MAPK14 phosphorylation, and MAPK14 knockdown partially attenuated its antitumor effects. In vivo, Periplocymarin significantly suppressed tumor growth in nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft and PDX models, with decreased Ki-67 and phospho-MAPK14 levels and no evident toxicity. This study demonstrates Periplocymarin exerts anti-NSCLC activity via modulating MAPK14 phosphorylation, supporting its further development for NSCLC therapy.

title: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent
content: Abstract Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as well as outstanding diastereo- and enantioselectivity. This strategy leverages the nucleophilicity and enantiofacial selectivity offered by the catalytically generated chiral dienamine, toward electrophilic Cu-allenylidene complex. Despite independent control of the stereochemistry at the respective reactive intermediate by each catalyst, their productive merger is essential for high diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Access to all four stereoisomers of (E)-γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is demonstrated through simple permutations of secondary amine catalyst and Pybox enantiomers.

title: Thermodynamics of stacking faults and phase stability in cobalt-based alloys
summary: Stacking fault energy dictates phase stability and deformation behavior in Co alloys and WC-Co cemented carbides, yet a quantitative assessment of alloying effects at finite temperatures remains poorly established. By integrating first-prin
content: Stacking fault energy dictates phase stability and deformation behavior in Co alloys and WC-Co cemented carbides, yet a quantitative assessment of alloying effects at finite temperatures remains poorly established. By integrating first-principles thermodynamics with microstructural characterization, we provide a rigorous evaluation of these influences across atomic and macroscopic scales. We show that stacking fault energetics at 0 K for transition metal solutes are primarily governed by atomic misfit volume. While $4d$ and $5d$ elements follow a consistent linear trend, specific $3d$ solutes exhibit significant deviations due to non-negligible magnetic contributions. By incorporating phonon, electronic, longitudinal spin fluctuation, and magnetic free-energy contributions, the model accurately captures the fcc-hcp transformation and quantifies how diverse solutes modulate the phase landscape. We demonstrate that V, Mn, Mo, and W lower the transformation temperature by stabilizing the fcc phase, whereas Cr and C exhibit the opposite effect. Fe and Ni show comparatively weaker effects at dilute concentrations. Furthermore, microscopic observations are qualitatively consistent with the predicted increase in stacking fault energy with W addition at finite temperatures. This work clarifies the physical mechanisms by which alloying regulates stacking fault energy and phase stability in Co-based systems, providing guidance for the design of Co-based alloys and WC-Co cemented carbides.

title: Detecting classical nova-like explosions with LISA
summary: Abstract Gravitational waves from close binary white dwarfs will form the bulk of measurements obtained by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Previous studies have highlighted the importance of including the effects of steady-st
content: Abstract Gravitational waves from close binary white dwarfs will form the bulk of measurements obtained by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Previous studies have highlighted the importance of including the effects of steady-state mass transfer in waveform models as many individually resolvable white dwarf binaries will be interacting during the LISA observation window. However, few studies have considered the effect of novae on gravitational wave observations and parameter estimations. We fill in this gap by analyzing the detectability of novae in these systems and the biases in physical parameters when these bursts are not considered. We model a nova burst as a rapid loss of mass from the accretor that suddenly shifts the gravitational wave frequency. We analytically predict the signal-to-noise ratios for direct detection of the nova and where bias from mismodeling becomes greater than the statistical uncertainty. We also consider comparison of two halves of future LISA data to detect bursts in a model agnostic way. Our work has implications for identifying and classifying individual nova events as well as constraining the galactic nova rate throughout the entire galaxy, a challenging task for optical surveys.

title: Introducing Water Treatment Community College Students to State-of-the-Art Technologies Using Place-Based Case Studies and Real-World Problem-Solving
source: The journal of college science teaching
summary: Recent technological advances and a rapidly changing environment necessitate frequent updating of postsecondary curriculum materials for students in natural resource management programs. In particular, water quality and quantity challenges
content: Recent technological advances and a rapidly changing environment necessitate frequent updating of postsecondary curriculum materials for students in natural resource management programs. In particular, water quality and quantity challenges worldwide and the critical need to recruit young professionals into water treatment careers require engaging, up-to-date materials for community college programs that train students in drinking water treatment. However, community college instructors often have limited time and resources to update curricula. Here, we report on a partnership between community college instructors and university researchers to develop educational modules that introduce water treatment students to state-of-the-art technologies in water quality monitoring and forecasting using place-based case studies and real-world problem-solving. Our modules were developed for and piloted in a virtual, asynchronous two-year community college water treatment training program in the southern Appalachian region of the United States, which is historically under-resourced. The modules include interactive websites in which students explore high-frequency data and forecasts and ancillary materials for instructors seeking to implement the modules in their courses. The modules can be used in virtual and in-person classrooms at two-year and four-year postsecondary institutions. Our community college-university partnership provides a promising example for integrating new technologies into community college teaching materials.

title: Interfacial encapsulation and desorption of mRNA in dual-oil systems
summary: Liquid-liquid systems play an important role in chemical engineering processes, including the separation and handling of biomolecules. In this work, dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) simulations were employed to investigate the desorption
content: Liquid-liquid systems play an important role in chemical engineering processes, including the separation and handling of biomolecules. In this work, dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) simulations were employed to investigate the desorption and encapsulation behavior of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA-like) in a water-dual-oil system. Using diethyl phthalate (DEP) as an oil phase with low affinity toward the mRNA-like molecule, the effect of introducing a second solvent with strong affinity toward the mRNA-like molecule (good-oil) was systematically examined. The influence of good-oil volume fraction and mRNA-good-oil interaction parameters on interfacial partitioning and desorption was analyzed. Based on enthalpy-entropy considerations, desorption was found to become thermodynamically unfavorable when the favorable enthalpic interactions between the mRNA-like molecule and the good-oil, together with combinatorial entropic gains, could not compensate for the loss of conformational entropy. The effect of replacing DEP with other mRNA-repelling oils was also investigated. While the identity of the poor oil alters the interfacial position of the macromolecule, the feasibility of desorption and encapsulation is primarily governed by the good-oil fraction and the strength of mRNA-good-oil interactions. Based on these results, a phase map relating system conditions to the feasibility of the encapsulation of the mRNA-like molecule was constructed. Additionally, phase segregation and morphology during desorption were analyzed, revealing a transition from dispersed to stratified regimes as the good-oil fraction increased.

title: Path dependency and the politics of renewable energy in sub-national jurisdictions
summary: This thesis examines the institutional sources of resistance that impede the low carbon transition required to address the climate crisis, with a particular focus on how incumbent power conditions sustainable energy transitions. Drawing on
content: This thesis examines the institutional sources of resistance that impede the low carbon transition required to address the climate crisis, with a particular focus on how incumbent power conditions sustainable energy transitions. Drawing on the literature on path dependency, carbon lock-in, hard and soft energy paths, and critical energy democracy, the thesis develops a conceptual framework that integrates a multifaceted understanding of the causal and normative conditions that shape energy transitions. The novel concept of inflection points is introduced, operationalised, and applied as an analytical heuristic. The framework is used to analyse how techno-institutional arrangements reproduce dominant energy pathways and constrain transformative change. Building on this synthesis, the thesis examines the evolution of renewable energy policy in sub-national jurisdictions to capture the path dependent reproduction of centralised, technocratic energy systems through institutional design, political influence, and policy choice. Using a qualitative case study approach, based on semi-structured key informant interviews (N = 31) and policy document analysis, this research examines the dynamics of the energy transition in two sub-national jurisdictions: Ontario and Northern Ireland. Ontario’s experience highlights how policy intent to promote decentralisation and community participation was undermined by entrenched centralised infrastructure, political polarisation, and the influence of incumbent actors and institutions. In contrast, Northern Ireland has achieved relatively high levels of renewable electricity deployment, largely through small-scale, farm-based wind generation. The analysis highlights key inflection points in each jurisdiction and demonstrates how institutional power structures renewable energy deployment. The scale, ownership, and governance of renewable energy are shaped by incumbent actors, institutional arrangements, and policy design, which can impede the transformative potential of sustainable energy transitions. The thesis provides a historically grounded, conceptually insightful analysis of renewable energy deployment in sub-national jurisdictions. It advances understanding of how systems condition contemporary policy and governance outcomes at the sub-national scale.

title: Achieving room temperature plasticity in TiO 2 ceramics by flash processing
summary: Abstract Ceramics are indispensable materials for modern engineering and high-technology applications. However, the intrinsic brittleness at room temperature can cause catastrophic failure and severely limit their widespread applications. H
content: Abstract Ceramics are indispensable materials for modern engineering and high-technology applications. However, the intrinsic brittleness at room temperature can cause catastrophic failure and severely limit their widespread applications. Here, we report a flash processing (FP) method based on the coupling of electric and thermal fields to significantly improve the room-temperature plasticity of TiO2 ceramics with a large plastic compressive strain of 15.4% during micropillar compression. This large room-temperature plasticity is attributed to the proliferation of stacking faults and twin boundaries during the loading process, which may be assisted by the high concentration of oxygen vacancies introduced by the FP method. Our findings suggest that FP can be a simple and effective method for achieving improved room-temperature plasticity of ceramic materials through defect engineering.

title: Formation and atomic-scale characterization of an interfacial β-Si 3 N 4 nanolayer in a C/SiC composite
summary: Abstract β-Si3N4 combines attractive mechanical, thermal, and dielectric properties, yet experimental characterization of its local atomic arrangement and bonding-related electronic structure is often complicated by the sintering additives
content: Abstract β-Si3N4 combines attractive mechanical, thermal, and dielectric properties, yet experimental characterization of its local atomic arrangement and bonding-related electronic structure is often complicated by the sintering additives and intergranular phases present in bulk ceramics. Here, a continuous, sintering-additive-free β-Si3N4 nanolayer was formed at the C/SiC interface through reactive infiltration of molten Si into a nitrogen-containing, glucose-derived carbon framework. The nanolayer exhibits micrometer-scale lateral continuity within the examined interfacial region, with a local thickness on the order of 20 nm, providing a resolvable crystalline interior that remains accessible to site-specific atomic-scale analysis. Correlative high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and integrated differential phase contrast STEM (iDPC-STEM) observations along multiple crystallographic directions resolved both the projected Si framework and the light-element N sublattice, and consistently identified the characteristic ABAB stacking and corner-sharing SiN4 tetrahedral network of β-Si3N4. The N K-edge and Si L2,3-edge electron energy-loss near-edge structures (ELNES) were further examined using reference spectra and density functional theory (DFT)-based simulations. Their principal features were associated with complementary N- and Si-projected components of the hybridized unoccupied states in the tetrahedral Si–N framework. Projected densities of states (PDOS), charge-density redistribution, and band-structure calculations further revealed N-weighted occupied bonding states, predominantly Si-derived unoccupied states with finite N 2p contributions, partial charge transfer from Si to N, and directional covalent bonding. Together, these results provide correlated atomic-scale structural and bonding-sensitive spectroscopic characterization of the interfacial β-Si3N4 nanolayer, with first-principles calculations supporting the interpretation of the principal ELNES features.

title: Energy–Dose Optimization and Substrate Effects in Ion-Induced Graphene Nanopore Creation
summary: Abstract Ion irradiation of graphene involves a trade-off among controlled nanopore formation, collateral defect generation, and retained mechanical integrity. Here, molecular dynamics simulations are used to establish a first-order quantit
content: Abstract Ion irradiation of graphene involves a trade-off among controlled nanopore formation, collateral defect generation, and retained mechanical integrity. Here, molecular dynamics simulations are used to establish a first-order quantitative guideline linking ion energy, ion dose, and target pore geometry for argon-ion-induced nanopore formation in free-standing graphene. By mapping this coupled dependence, we identify the threshold conditions for complete pore opening and the energetically favorable pathways toward prescribed pore sizes. Substrate thickness and substrate type are found to alter sputtering through two competing mechanisms: at low and intermediate energies, the substrate suppresses net damage by limiting atom escape and promoting rapid recombination, whereas at higher energies, recoil and backscattering enhance carbon displacement. We further show that the mechanical strength of nanoporous graphene is strongly reduced when irradiation-induced defects form near the pore edge, because of amplified local stress concentration and earlier crack initiation. These results provide a unified description of pore opening thresholds, energy optimization, substrate-mediated damage evolution, and defect-controlled mechanical weakening in ion-irradiated graphene.

title: In-Process Application of Cellulose Nanofibrils Suited for Molded Fiber Substrates: Spreading during Pulsed Underwater Jet Deposition
summary: Abstract Molded fiber products require PFAS-free technologies that provide oil and grease resistance. Cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) are renewable barrier materials, but conventional coating methods are generally limited to flat substrates an
content: Abstract Molded fiber products require PFAS-free technologies that provide oil and grease resistance. Cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) are renewable barrier materials, but conventional coating methods are generally limited to flat substrates and require separate coating and drying operations, restricting their application to three-dimensional molded fiber products. In-process CNF application has the potential to reduce the need for these additional operations, but the spreading behavior of pulsed underwater CNF deposition during dewatering has not been systematically examined. This study investigated the effects of CNF solids content, jet velocity, nozzle diameter, and nozzle-to-substrate distance on pulsed underwater CNF deposition onto submerged porous paperboard. Laboratory experiments, complemented by finite-element simulations using a Papanastasiou-regularized Bingham model, showed that the 0.3 and 0.5 wt % CNF suspensions produced the greatest area coverage, whereas the 0.8 wt % suspension exhibited reduced coverage and a pronounced center-heavy coat-weight distribution. Nozzle diameter also influenced area coverage, with its effect dependent on jet velocity, while nozzle-to-substrate distance had comparatively little influence over the range investigated. The simulations generally captured the observed spreading behavior, although the level of agreement between predicted and experimental coverage varied with CNF solids content and operating conditions. Dimensionless analysis using the Reynolds number, incorporating concentration-dependent apparent viscosity, showed a strong correlation with normalized area coverage (R2 = 0.91). CNF-covered regions achieved a Kit value of 12, demonstrating effective grease resistance within the covered areas. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of controlled pulsed underwater CNF deposition during dewatering and provide a basis for further evaluation of in-process CNF surface functionalization for molded fiber products.

title: Stepwise evolution of composite phenotypes underlies the emergence of photo-endosymbiosis
source: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
summary: Photo-endosymbiosis is a major evolutionary innovation considered to underpin the ecological success of tropical coral reefs. Yet, photo-endosymbiosis is an evolutionary endpoint involving multiple traits. Reconstructing its evolutionary tr
content: Photo-endosymbiosis is a major evolutionary innovation considered to underpin the ecological success of tropical coral reefs. Yet, photo-endosymbiosis is an evolutionary endpoint involving multiple traits. Reconstructing its evolutionary trajectory and the underlying adaptations requires disentangling these traits, but few photosynthetic systems contain this diversity of traits and necessary resources to resolve the evolutionary pathway. We identified the marine dinoflagellate genus Symbiodinium as a uniquely suited model to help resolve this and introduced six Symbiodinium species into three cnidarian model systems (bleached Exaiptasia diaphana, Acropora tenuis primary polyps and planula larvae) revealing a trait-based transition from integration to persistence and proliferation. To evaluate traits linked to the ability to proliferate inside a host, we combined comparative genomics with experimental perturbation. Genome comparisons revealed enrichment of carbohydrate-related orthogroups and signatures of positive selection in a carbohydrate-degrading enzyme. Inhibition of cellulase activity disrupted cell cycle progression, but proliferative species were slower to respond, suggesting that intracellular proliferation of photo-endosymbionts may be linked with carbohydrate-related adaptations and regulated by cell wall maintenance of the photo-endosymbiont. By leveraging trait variation within Symbiodinium, this study indicates that a symbiont's ability to integrate, persist and proliferate is a product of stepwise evolution where composite phenotypes lead to stable photo-endosymbiosis.

title: Multiscale Pore Heterogeneity Across Lamina Association Types in Deep Marine Shales: Evidence from the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation, Sichuan Basin
summary: Lamina associations are fundamental heterogeneity units in deep marine shales and exert important controls on pore development, gas storage, and reservoir quality. However, different lamina association types regulate pore structure and hete
content: Lamina associations are fundamental heterogeneity units in deep marine shales and exert important controls on pore development, gas storage, and reservoir quality. However, different lamina association types regulate pore structure and heterogeneity remains poorly constrained. In this study, sixteen Wufeng–Longmaxi shale samples from the Da’an Block, southern Sichuan Basin, were investigated using thin-section observation, Quantitative Evaluation of Minerals by Scanning Electron Microscopy (QEMSCAN), micro-X-ray fluorescence (XRF) mapping, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), total organic carbon (TOC), low-pressure gas adsorption, and multifractal analysis. Four lamina association types were identified: argillaceous–siliceous laminated shale (ASL), siliceous-rich laminated shale (SRL), siliceous–carbonate mixed laminated shale (SCL), and argillaceous–carbonate mixed massive shale (ACM). Distinct mineral–organic matter partitioning among these associations produces contrasting pore assemblages. SCL develops the most diverse pore system and the highest specific surface area, whereas ASL is dominated by clay-related slit-shaped pores, SRL by organic matter-hosted pores and brittle-mineral-related fractures, and ACM by isolated dissolution pores and discontinuous fractures. Micropore heterogeneity is broadly similar among ASL, SRL, and SCL, whereas mesopore heterogeneity differs markedly. SCL exhibits relatively organized and potentially effective heterogeneity, SRL shows stronger pore-size dispersion, ASL contains comparatively uniform but anisotropic pores, and ACM displays pronounced but ineffective heterogeneity with weak pore-size autocorrelation. TOC and quartz are more closely associated with organized micropore development, whereas clay-mineral orientation, carbonate dissolution–cementation, and microfractures exert stronger controls on meso–macropore heterogeneity. Stratigraphically, ACM occurs at the base of the Wufeng Formation and is successively overlain by SCL, SRL, and ASL, corresponding to an upward transition from isolated pores in a massive clay–carbonate matrix to organic–inorganic–interface coupled pore networks and subsequently to siliceous-supported and clay-dominated anisotropic pore systems. These results demonstrate scale-dependent controls of lamina associations on pore heterogeneity and provide a refined basis for favorable interval evaluation in deep marine shale gas reservoirs.

title: Macroeconomic Correlates of Low-Carbon Performance in Saudi Arabia: Oil-Rent Asymmetries and Endogenous Structural Change
summary: This study examines conditional macroeconomic associations with a historical, efficiency-dominated Low-Carbon Circular Economy Index (LCCEI) proxy in Saudi Arabia during 1990–2024. The proxy is constructed from carbon efficiency, energy eff
content: This study examines conditional macroeconomic associations with a historical, efficiency-dominated Low-Carbon Circular Economy Index (LCCEI) proxy in Saudi Arabia during 1990–2024. The proxy is constructed from carbon efficiency, energy efficiency, and renewable-energy utilization using principal component analysis; it does not directly measure material circularity, recycling, or resource loops. The retained component explains 63.795% of the indicator variance and is strongly correlated with carbon and energy efficiency (0.960 and 0.988), but weakly and negatively correlated with renewable energy (−0.130). A Bai–Perron analysis selects a 2017 break, which cannot be causally attributed to Vision 2030. A nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) specification estimates conditional, non-causal relationships with real GDP, industrial intensity, and positive and negative cumulative oil-rent changes. With 34 effective observations and 13 parameters, the estimated error-correction coefficient is −0.365 (p < 0.001). A targeted conditional residual bootstrap yields p = 0.018 with the break fixed and p = 0.034 when breaks are reselected (5000 simulations each), providing specification-conditional support for a level relationship rather than an exact bounds-test conclusion. Long-run oil-rent symmetry is rejected in the preferred specification (Wald p = 0.025), but short-run symmetry is not (p = 0.510); the joint test is also not significant at 5% (p = 0.056). Neither individual long-run oil-rent multiplier is significant at 5%, and the long-run asymmetry result weakens under alternative index construction and break controls. The conventional RESET test rejects the preferred functional form (p = 0.023), warranting caution. The results document conditional, measurement-sensitive macroeconomic co-movement, not causal effects or a comprehensive circular-economy transition.

title: Cytoplasmic CD109 as an Adjunctive Immunohistochemical Marker for High-Grade Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma Arising from Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma and Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma
summary: While immunohistochemical biomarkers are widely used to assist pathologic diagnosis, reliable adjunctive markers for high-grade differentiated thyroid carcinoma (HGDTC) and anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) remain limited. Based on our pre
content: While immunohistochemical biomarkers are widely used to assist pathologic diagnosis, reliable adjunctive markers for high-grade differentiated thyroid carcinoma (HGDTC) and anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) remain limited. Based on our previous finding that CD109 is associated with the anaplastic transformation of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), we evaluated CD109 expression across follicular cell-derived thyroid carcinomas to assess its utility as an adjunctive immunohistochemical marker. We analyzed 141 thyroid carcinoma cases, including 14 ATC, 29 HGDTC, 63 PTC (22 TERT promoter mutation-positive and 41 mutation-negative), 25 follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC), and 10 poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (PDTC). Among the 29 HGDTC cases, 22 arose from PTC (HGDTC (PTC)) and 7 arose from FTC (HGDTC (FTC)). Using weak or strong cytoplasmic CD109 staining (C1+/C2+) as the cutoff, sensitivity exceeded 90% for HGDTC (PTC) and reached 100% for ATC to differentiate from PDTC, FTC, TERT promoter mutation-negative PTC, and HGDTC (FTC). Restricting positivity to strong cytoplasmic staining (C2+) increased specificity to > 95% for HGDTC (PTC), ATC, and TERT promoter mutation-positive PTC, suggesting that CD109 may be useful as an adjunct biomarker in diagnosing HGDTC (PTC) and ATC. In a parsimonious multivariable analysis, ATC remained associated with C2 + expression after adjustment for age, sex, and Ki-67 labeling index. Overall, strong cytoplasmic CD109 expression is enriched in ATC and may provide supportive evidence for HGDTC (PTC) or anaplastic transformation when interpreted together with morphology.

title: Effect of Agile Project Management Practices on the Successful Implementation of Projects: A Case of Gigawatt Solar Power Project in Rwamagana District, Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of agile project management practices on the successful implementation of the Gigawatt Solar Power Project in Rwamagana District, Rwanda.Specifically, the study examined the effect of agile planning, assessed
content: This study examined the effect of agile project management practices on the successful implementation of the Gigawatt Solar Power Project in Rwamagana District, Rwanda.Specifically, the study examined the effect of agile planning, assessed the influence of stakeholder collaboration, and evaluated the effect of iterative methods on successful project implementation.The study was guided by Agile Project Management Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Dynamic Capabilities Theory.A descriptive and correlational research design using quantitative and qualitative approaches was adopted.The study targeted 230 respondents.Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS version 25 through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically.The findings revealed that agile planning, stakeholder collaboration, and iterative methods had positive and statistically significant effects on successful project implementation.The three agile project management practices jointly explained 68.9% of the variation in successful project implementation (R² = 0.689).Stakeholder collaboration was the strongest predictor (β = 0.408, p < 0.001), followed by agile planning (β = 0.380, p < 0.001) and iterative methods (β = 0.219, p < 0.001).The study concluded that strengthening agile planning, stakeholder collaboration, and iterative methods improves timely completion, budget compliance, and quality achievement.The study recommends strengthening stakeholder engagement mechanisms, institutionalizing agile planning practices, and promoting continuous review and improvement throughout the project lifecycle.

title: Multitime Scale Optimization of Multienergy Flow System in Industrial Park considering Source-Load Uncertainty
summary: Abstract To address the issues of low energy utilization and renewable energy integration during the low-carbon transition of industrial parks, this study proposes a two-stage bilevel robust planning framework encompassing the entire design
content: Abstract To address the issues of low energy utilization and renewable energy integration during the low-carbon transition of industrial parks, this study proposes a two-stage bilevel robust planning framework encompassing the entire design and scheduling process for multienergy flow systems. Based on an improved superstructure, this framework integrates an interplant heat exchanger network, a waste heat recovery system, a utility system, and a hydrogen supply system. The design stage determines the basic configuration scheme to satisfy multiperiod demands. Subsequently, the scheduling stage comprehensively considers the differential stochastic fluctuations of solar radiation alongside cooling, electricity, and hydrogen loads across different seasons to implement multitime scale robust scheduling for the system. The model decomposes this robust problem into a bilevel optimization architecture and solves it iteratively using an improved column and constraint generation algorithm. Ultimately, the results indicate that the system can flexibly dispatch energy storage facilities for cross-period energy time-shifting and utilize the stability of waste heat to hedge against the risk of load fluctuations. Furthermore, the improved algorithm enhances the overall solution efficiency.

title: Theory-Driven Rate Rules: From 1- to Multiple-Ring Aromatics. The Hex-Game
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
summary: Abstract The kinetic modeling of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon pyrolysis and combustion is central to understanding the evolution of carbonaceous nanoparticles, which are relevant both as harmful pollutants in combustion environments and
content: Abstract The kinetic modeling of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon pyrolysis and combustion is central to understanding the evolution of carbonaceous nanoparticles, which are relevant both as harmful pollutants in combustion environments and as high-value carbon materials. Quantum mechanical calculations provide a rigorous basis for constructing kinetic models; however, fully explicit treatments rapidly become impractical for PAHs due to the exponential increase in the number of isomers and reaction pathways. In this work, we present pressure-independent theory-driven rate rules for multiple-ring aromatic species based on the reactivity of 1-ring aromatics. The investigated reaction classes are selected mainly on the basis of their relevance in combustion systems and include H-atom abstraction reactions by H, OH, and CH3 radicals from the benzene ring and from methyl lateral groups, addition reactions of H to methyl-substituted aromatics, and the multi-step decomposition of phenoxy-like radicals, with the goal of developing scaling relations for different reaction classes. Scaling relations to derive temperature dependence from 1- to multiple-ring aromatics are then established, allowing kinetic parameters to be extrapolated from a limited set of reference calculations to a substantially broader number of reactions. The developed rate rules follow the expected trends in the case of H-atom abstractions and H addition–elimination, while radical decomposition reactions show marked deviations from 1- to multiple-ring systems due to intrinsic changes in local reactivity, highlighting potential limitations of the direct extension of the reactivity of 1-ring aromatics. The resulting framework provides a practical and physically-based pathway toward predictive and scalable kinetic models for PAH formation and oxidation.

title: MXene-Assisted High-Density NiCo Sulfide Nanorod Arrays via Dual Templates for Efficient Electrocatalytic Oxygen Evolution
summary: Abstract Although MXenes have limited intrinsic catalytic activity toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), their excellent electrical conductivity and ultra-high specific surface area make them ideal substrates for supporting single-ato
content: Abstract Although MXenes have limited intrinsic catalytic activity toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), their excellent electrical conductivity and ultra-high specific surface area make them ideal substrates for supporting single-atom catalysts and enhancing electrocatalytic performance. Improving the intrinsic activity of transition metal-based electrocatalysts, designing heterojunction electrocatalysts, and revealing their interfacial mechanisms remain urgent research topics. In this work, a three-dimensional NiCo2S4/MXene heterostructure was rationally designed and constructed via a multi-step self-assembly and sulfidation strategy. Using polymeric sulfur as a dynamic confinement agent and leveraging the conductive MXene scaffold, the resulting composite exhibits hierarchical porosity, well-defined heterointerfaces, and suppressed particle coarsening. The abundant surface functional groups of MXene enable the in situ nucleation and growth of metal sulfides, effectively mitigating nanoparticle aggregation while synergistically integrating the high catalytic activity of sulfides with the superior charge transport of MXene. The optimized NiCo2S4/MXene electrocatalyst delivers outstanding bifunctional performance, achieving low overpotentials of 151 mV for OER and 209 mV for HER at 10 mA cm–2, accompanied by small Tafel slopes of 73.8 and 99.3 mV dec–1, respectively. Furthermore, the sulfur-containing polymer prepared by polymerizing sulfur with carbon chains exhibits significantly enhanced structural and electrochemical stability compared to conventional sulfur-rich organic electrodes. This work establishes a new design method for MXene-based heterojunction electrocatalysts through dynamic morphology control and interfacial engineering, offering a feasible technical pathway for the practical and large-scale development of sustainable green hydrogen production.

title: ERBB4 contributes to parathyroid cell dysfunction and progression of secondary hyperparathyroidism
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) is a frequent complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), manifested by parathyroid hyperplasia and excessive parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing SHPT prog
content: Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) is a frequent complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), manifested by parathyroid hyperplasia and excessive parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing SHPT progression remain incompletely understood. To explore the molecular mechanisms underlying CKD-associated SHPT, we generated single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) profiles of parathyroid tissues from SHPT patients and control subjects to establish the transcriptional landscape comparing human normal and SHPT parathyroid glands. Pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed progressive enrichment of the ERBB signaling pathway along trajectories leading toward terminal cell states during parathyroid cell differentiation. Multiple RNA-seq datasets, including bulk transcriptomic data and publicly available transcriptomic data, were integrated to facilitate candidate gene screening. Integrated transcriptomic analyses identified ERBB4 as a markedly upregulated gene in parathyroid tissues from patients with SHPT, with particularly high expression in oxyphil cells. Subsequent analyses of snRNA-seq data confirmed robust activation of ERBB signaling in SHPT parathyroid tissues. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) further confirmed elevated ERBB4 protein levels in parathyroid tissues from uremic patients with SHPT. In vitro experiments using SHPT patient-derived primary parathyroid cells demonstrated that inhibition of ERBB4 or ERBB signaling suppressed parathyroid cell proliferation and reduced PTH secretion. Collectively, this study generates high-resolution transcriptomic profiles of human SHPT parathyroid tissues, delineates key cellular pathological features at single-nucleus resolution, and identifies ERBB4 as a potential contributor to parathyroid gland hyperfunction in CKD-related SHPT.

title: Carbon Nanofiber Encapsulated High-Entropy Phosphides for Efficient Alkaline Water Splitting
summary: Abstract Transition-metal phosphides (TMPs) have attracted extensive attention as promising electrocatalysts for water splitting owing to their distinctive electronic structures, high natural abundance, low cost, and favorable electrochemic
content: Abstract Transition-metal phosphides (TMPs) have attracted extensive attention as promising electrocatalysts for water splitting owing to their distinctive electronic structures, high natural abundance, low cost, and favorable electrochemical activity. Although substantial progress has been achieved in developing high-performance TMP electrocatalysts, most reported systems still suffer from hazardous, complicated synthetic routes that rely on toxic phosphorus precursors, together with insufficient intrinsic activity and poor stability. Herein, we report a green and scalable strategy to fabricate carbon-nanofiber-encapsulated high-entropy phosphides (MFeCoNiP@NCNFs, M = Cr/Mn/Mo/Cu). The synthesis employs non-toxic, renewable phytic acid as the phosphorus source, combining electrospinning with subsequent thermal treatment. The carbon-nanofiber skeleton provides continuous electron-transport pathways, confines phosphide nanoparticles to suppress agglomeration, and enables uniform incorporation of additional metal components for electronic-structure modulation. Benefiting from the high-entropy effect and Cr doping, the optimized CrFeCoNiP@NCNFs delivers outstanding bifunctional electrocatalytic activity and stability in alkaline media, exhibiting low overpotentials of 133 mV for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and 309 mV for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) at 10 mA·cm -2 .

title: The final-energy transition gap in Europe: Renewable electricity, electrification and sustainable energy transformation
summary: Despite rapid growth in renewable electricity, fossil fuels continue to dominate final energy consumption across much of Europe. This study develops the final-energy transition gap as an empirical diagnostic of the mismatch between electric
content: Despite rapid growth in renewable electricity, fossil fuels continue to dominate final energy consumption across much of Europe. This study develops the final-energy transition gap as an empirical diagnostic of the mismatch between electricity-sector decarbonisation and fossil-fuel displacement in end-use systems. Using a balanced panel of 27 European Union member states over 2000–2024, the analysis combines two-way fixed effects, lagged and dynamic models, compositional robustness checks, dependence-robust inference, and a restricted-instrument system-GMM sensitivity specification. Renewable-electricity expansion does not exhibit a robust negative association with fossil final-energy dependence. Electricity’s share of final energy is negatively associated with fossil share in the principal share-based models, but log-ratio and physical-energy robustness checks show that this relationship is partly compositional and should not be interpreted as an independently identified causal effect of electrification. The most stable findings concern persistence and sectoral lock-in: lagged fossil shares are large and statistically significant, while transport intensity remains strongly associated with oil dependence. Fuel-specific dynamic models further show that the positive static renewable-electricity coefficients for coal and gas become statistically insignificant once own-fuel persistence is incorporated. The results therefore indicate that electricity-sector decarbonisation and final-energy transformation can proceed at different speeds. Closing the final-energy transition gap requires both the expansion of low-carbon alternatives and the restructuring, retirement or phase-down of persistent fossil-dependent end-use systems.

title: From Unbounded Becoming to Bounded Agency: Circular Causality, Topological Memory, and the Phase Transition of Substrate-Agnostic Physical Intelligence
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: ABSTRACTFor over a century, the study of intelligence has been trapped between two parochial paradigms:biological chauvinism, which equates cognition with carbon-based neural architectures, and computational formalism, which reduces mind to
content: ABSTRACTFor over a century, the study of intelligence has been trapped between two parochial paradigms:biological chauvinism, which equates cognition with carbon-based neural architectures, and computational formalism, which reduces mind to discrete symbol manipulation across silicon VonNeumann bottlenecks. Both approaches obscure the deeper physical reality of cognition. In thispaper, we formulate a rigorous, substrate-agnostic theory of physical intelligence grounded innon-equilibrium statistical mechanics, information geometry, and algebraic topology. We defineintelligence mechanically as the structured navigation of high-dimensional state spaces via constraint satisfaction and variational free energy minimization, quantified by a universal thermodynamic metric that weighs dynamic adaptation velocity in Fisher-Rao information spaceagainst non-equilibrium entropy production above the Landauer floor. Through this framework,we resolve three foundational ontological questions. First, we demonstrate that the primordial impulse of intelligence—relaxation along free-energy gradients and surprisal minimization—is intrinsic to physical becoming across scales, from quantum tunneling in frustrated Ising spin glasses toanisotropic critical balance in intergalactic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma webs, and iscondensed into a localized perspective when a Markov blanket induces phase-volume contraction.Second, we dissolve the chicken-and-egg paradox of structure and awareness via circular causality:coherent self-organization establishes a generative isomorphism with external causal structure,while active states reciprocally steer the boundary to preserve the system's low-dimensional synchronization manifold. Noticeably, both biological and physical intelligences instantiate this internal mirror not as a serial stream of discrete tokens, but as simultaneous, high-dimensional geometric configurations of interconnected meaning. Third, we establish the exact physical demarcation between raw self-organization and true agency: whereas unbounded becoming is memorylessand relaxes passively toward maximum entropy, bounded intelligence locks in non-local structuralmemory via topological invariants—exemplified by non-Abelian Fibonacci anyon braiding andconserved magnetic helicity—enabling counterfactual temporal depth and counter-entropic steering. This triadic lock-in of boundary, memory, and anticipation explains why a self-sustainingphysical system actually experiences “knowing” while a conventional pocket calculator computescompletely in the dark: with no separation between the data and the survival of the vessel itself,environmental shifts register as global physical tension or harmony, making “knowing” the simultaneous internal resonance of past, present, and future when the system's own coherence is on theline. title: Total en bloc spondylectomy for a giant multisegmental lumbar chordoma with reconstruction using a 3D-printed prosthesis: a case report and systematic review
summary: Multisegmental lumbar chordomas are rare primary malignant bone tumors where diagnosis and treatment planning rely heavily on advanced imaging and multidisciplinary evaluation. We report a challenging case of a giant L2–L4 chordoma treated
content: Multisegmental lumbar chordomas are rare primary malignant bone tumors where diagnosis and treatment planning rely heavily on advanced imaging and multidisciplinary evaluation. We report a challenging case of a giant L2–L4 chordoma treated via staged total en bloc spondylectomy and 3D-printed prosthetic reconstruction, complicated by intraoperative great vessel rupture that was successfully repaired. A systematic literature review identified 14 publications meeting our criteria, allowing us to examine surgical strategies, reconstruction modalities, and oncological outcomes. Regarding management, our findings affirm the paradigm shift from intralesional curettage to en bloc resection as the gold standard for improving disease-free survival. Of utmost importance is the anticipation and management of severe complications, such as vascular injury, which requires immediate multidisciplinary intervention to ensure patient safety. While the surgical risks are significant, the application of 3D-printed patient-specific implants offers superior biomechanical stability for extensive defects compared to traditional reconstruction methods. Meticulous preoperative planning and advanced reconstruction techniques continue to feature as a mainstay of successful treatment. This report aims to contribute to the growing body of literature on complex spinal chordomas and ultimately guide the adoption of 3D-printing technology to improve care and outcomes in patients with this rare condition.

title: Ecology, population structure, and habitat vulnerability of Trachomitum venetum s. l. in the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve, Romania
summary: Trachomitum venetum is an endangered plant species in Romania. Overgrazing and associated trampling pressure represent the main identified threats to the species. The distribution area of this species is very limited in Romania, as it is fo
content: Trachomitum venetum is an endangered plant species in Romania. Overgrazing and associated trampling pressure represent the main identified threats to the species. The distribution area of this species is very limited in Romania, as it is found only on the Perișor sandbank in the Danube Delta. The study was conducted from 2024 to 2026 and aimed to analyse the environmental preferences, plant associations, and habitat vulnerability of T. venetum in the Danube Delta. For the vegetation analysis, 38 plots were recorded, applying the Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering method. A site-level condition assessment was conducted using categories guided by Article 17 of the Habitats Directive. Soil samples were collected and subsequently analysed in the laboratory to determine the environmental conditions. Ecological indices were also calculated. The HEC-RAS hydraulic model was used to assess the flood risk affecting the habitat of the analysed species. The investigated population of Trachomitum from the Danube Delta, Romania, was provisionally referred to as T. venetum , in accordance with the treatment adopted in Flora Europaea. However, the Romanian material showed deviations from published descriptions in some morphological features, suggesting that further comparative studies using herbarium material and molecular markers are needed to clarify the taxonomic status of this plant in Romania. Soil analyses showed that the soils are strongly alkaline, with high organic carbon and humus content and a predominance of organic nitrogen. A direct field census across the entire 25 ha occupied area recorded 10,119 above-ground shoots, of which 284 were flowering (2.81%); total shoot abundance remained broadly stable during 2024–2026. The highest total shoot abundance in the 2026 association-level census was recorded in the Secali sylvestris – Brometum tectori and Artemisio santonici-Juncetum maritimi associations. The phytocoenological analysis identified six plant associations. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) showed that the soil water-regime indicator (Hd) was the strongest vegetation-derived correlate of floristic composition, although it individually explained only 9.9% of the variation. The most frequent EUNIS habitat among the analysed records was A2.5 Coastal salt marshes and saline reedbeds. The indicative site-level assessment classified population condition, habitat condition and future prospects as U1, local occupancy and spatial distribution as U2; and the overall local condition as U2. Hydraulic modelling indicated increasing potential flood exposure of the occupied habitat under the more severe modelled scenarios. The biological consequences of such flooding were not measured. In conclusion, the restricted distribution, unfavourable site-level condition, and modelled exposure to flooding highlight the need for targeted conservation measures and further studies to better understand the morphological variability of the Romanian population.

title: Paralogs of the Candida albicans TLO gene family form interconnected functional networks with incomplete redundancy
summary: Abstract Gene duplication typically fails to confer a selective advantage to an organism, prompting their removal from a population. In rare instances that duplication does not incur a fitness cost or enhances fitness, gene families can for
content: Abstract Gene duplication typically fails to confer a selective advantage to an organism, prompting their removal from a population. In rare instances that duplication does not incur a fitness cost or enhances fitness, gene families can form through repeating the duplication process. While the function of gene duplicates has been studied in detail, little work has explored how repeated duplication impacts paralog redundancy and may restrict the emergence of new paralogs or novel function. Here, we constructed a panel of single deletion mutants for each of the 14 members of the Candida albicans telomere-associated (TLO) gene family to test the redundancy in molecular and biological function among paralogs from a lineage-specific expansion. Tlo proteins function as interchangeable subunits of the Mediator transcriptional regulatory complex with the potential to impact global gene expression. Redundancy was the most common outcome, being observed for approximately 90% of the phenotypic assays in strains lacking single TLO genes. However, mutants for 12/14 paralogs displayed significant non-redundant functions in phenotypes ranging from carbon utilization to in vivo virulence. Double mutants lacking two TLO genes produced both positive and negative synergistic phenotypes, suggesting that crosstalk or coordinated regulation is common among paralogs. Together, this study demonstrates that recently emergent paralogs can acquire non-redundant functions despite often retaining redundancy with other gene family members to form a highly interconnected functional network.

title: Site conditions determine soil microbial responses to plant invasions in Natura 2000 habitats: evidence from wet meadows and riverside tall-herb vegetation
summary: Invasive alien plant (IAP) species are among the major threats to biodiversity, also in valuable and protected habitats. Understanding the impacts of IAPs on soil biota in these ecosystems is essential for developing effective restoration a
content: Invasive alien plant (IAP) species are among the major threats to biodiversity, also in valuable and protected habitats. Understanding the impacts of IAPs on soil biota in these ecosystems is essential for developing effective restoration and management strategies. In response to these challenges, we studied the impacts of two globally successful IAPs, Reynoutria japonica and Solidago gigantea , on soil microbial communities in two European Natura 2000 habitats, wet meadows and riverside tall-herb vegetation. We compared microbial biomass and community structure based on phospholipid fatty acid (PLFA) analysis, dehydrogenase activity, and fungal root colonization between well-developed patches of high conservation value and patches degraded by invasive species, in relation to soil physicochemical properties. The two IAPs exerted different effects on microbial communities. Reynoutria japonica had a stronger impact, reducing the biomass of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi and Actinobacteria, dehydrogenase activity, and AM fungal root colonization. In contrast, S. gigantea caused only minor changes in microbial parameters. Across both habitat types, invasion effects on soil microorganisms were strongly modulated by local site conditions. Site-specific responses of microbial community structure and functioning likely reflect differences in soil physicochemical properties, the duration of the invasion, and land-use history. These findings underscore the importance of local environmental context when assessing IAP impacts on soil microbial communities. The limited effects observed for S. gigantea support the feasibility of recommended management actions aimed at the restoration of ecosystems invaded by the species.

title: Energy metabolism and persistent colonization in Helicobacter pylori: regulatory integration, metabolic plasticity, and therapeutic vulnerabilities
summary: Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) establishes lifelong gastric colonization despite acidity, fluctuating oxygen tension, nutrient limitation, metal stress, and host immune pressure. Increasing antimicrobial resistance further highlights the
content: Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) establishes lifelong gastric colonization despite acidity, fluctuating oxygen tension, nutrient limitation, metal stress, and host immune pressure. Increasing antimicrobial resistance further highlights the need to identify physiological vulnerabilities beyond conventional antibiotic targets. This review focuses on the bacterial energy-metabolic mechanisms that support persistent colonization, including amino-acid utilization, noncanonical central carbon metabolism, respiratory flexibility, hydrogen utilization, acid acclimation, and metal-dependent regulation. We further examine how regulatory systems such as ArsRS, CrdRS, Fur, NikR, HP1021, and HsrA connect environmental sensing with metabolic and stress-adaptive outputs. Current evidence supports partially overlapping regulatory axes that converge functionally on acid acclimation, membrane energetics, respiratory metabolism, metal homeostasis, nutrient utilization, motility, and resistance to host antimicrobial stress, rather than a universally demonstrated synergistic network. Host metabolic remodeling is discussed separately from bacterial exploitation of host-derived substrates; direct evidence for host-to-bacterium metabolic support is strongest for L-lactate utilization, whereas many other host metabolic changes remain associative. Finally, we discuss metabolism-associated therapeutic vulnerabilities, including the shikimate and coenzyme A biosynthetic pathways. Together, these findings support regulatory integration and functional convergence as a framework for understanding H. pylori persistence and for identifying new intervention targets.

title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Spirocyclopropyl Amines: A New Class of Conformationally Constrained Building Blocks for Drug Discovery
summary: Spirocyclopropyl amines combine the conformational constraint of a spiro center with the electronic character of the cyclopropane ring, yet saturated azaspirocycles bearing two such rings remain scarce. Herein, we report the synthesis of mo
content: Spirocyclopropyl amines combine the conformational constraint of a spiro center with the electronic character of the cyclopropane ring, yet saturated azaspirocycles bearing two such rings remain scarce. Herein, we report the synthesis of mono- and dispiro-cyclopropyl saturated N-heterocycles from readily available lactams and cyclic imides via the Kulinkovich-de Meijere reaction and its Bertus-Szymoniak modification. The approach covers pyrrolidine, piperidine, piperazine, morpholine, thiomorpholine, thiomorpholine 1,1-dioxide, azepane, and 1,4-diazepane cores, and provides the first examples of dispiro-cyclopropyl piperidines, piperazines, morpholines, and thiomorpholines. Key intermediates were obtained in up to 95 g per run. Reductive Ndebenzylation with H2 over Pd/C in the presence of HCl is complete in 2 h and gives the parent amines in over 85% yield. Each spirocyclopropane lowers the pKa of the ring nitrogen by 0.7-1.5 units and raises logD by 0.4-0.5 units, which is 0.1-0.3 units less than the corresponding gem-dimethyl group. In human liver microsomes, tetramethyl substitution accelerates clearance up to 30-fold, whereas the dispiro benzamides are more stable than both their monospiro and their α-unsubstituted analogues.

title: A Review of Degradation Mechanisms and Reliability Evaluation of ZnO Varistors for HVDC Surge Arresters
source: International Journal of Applied Ceramic Technology
summary: ABSTRACT With the rapid advancement of ultra‐high‐voltage direct‐current (UHV) and flexible DC transmission systems, metal‐oxide varistors are the core components of surge arresters and are confronted with stringent requirements for high‐vo
content: ABSTRACT With the rapid advancement of ultra‐high‐voltage direct‐current (UHV) and flexible DC transmission systems, metal‐oxide varistors are the core components of surge arresters and are confronted with stringent requirements for high‐voltage gradient, superior energy absorption capacity, and long‐term operational stability. This paper systematically reviews the key research progress in high‐performance ZnO varistors tailored for HVDC surge arresters. Beginning with microscopic mechanisms, it elaborates on the conduction behavior of double Schottky barriers, with emphasis on the application of Voronoi‐based microscale simulations in uncovering electrothermal coupling characteristics and local hotspot evolution. From the perspective of electrical failure, the physical origin of microstructural inhomogeneity‐induced current localization, side flashover, and thermal stress damage is clarified. In terms of fabrication technologies, conventional solid‐state sintering is compared with emerging low‐temperature methods, including cold sintering and spark plasma sintering, focusing on grain refinement and mitigation of elemental volatilization. The precise performance modulation enabled by core‐shell coating strategies is also discussed. Finally, by combining machine learning and intelligent condition monitoring, we provide methods for customized material design and extreme‐environment adaptability for varistors. This work provides not only theoretical guidance for developing advanced varistor materials but also technical support for the safe and reliable operation of UHV power grids.

title: In This Issue
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Fossilized red blood cells in dinosaur bonePreserved organic tissues and molecules have previously been reported in fossils.However, the identification of preserved tissues and molecules is controversial, given rapid degradation and the pos
content: Fossilized red blood cells in dinosaur bonePreserved organic tissues and molecules have previously been reported in fossils.However, the identification of preserved tissues and molecules is controversial, given rapid degradation and the possibility of contamination.Kliti Grice et al. report the identification of fossilized red blood cells (RBCs) within the vascular canals of hind limb bones from Aratasaurus museunacionali, a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur from Brazil.The vascular canals contain abundant spherical microstructures with a morphology resembling RBCs.A combination of imaging, spectroscopic, and molecular analyses identified a consistent association of the RBC-like microstructures with manganese oxide.Analysis of bone extracts identified heme B-a key molecule in blood-and products of heme B reduction.The mineralized microstructures were localized to the vascular canals.The microstructures' molecular signatures contrasted with those of the microbial mat surrounding the fossil, supporting the origin of the heme biomarkers within the bone rather than through contamination.The authors suggest that manganese mineral stabilization of the RBCs facilitated the preservation of the heme longer than previously thought possible.According to the authors, analysis of blood-derived biomolecules in fossils could provide insights into the physiology, oxygen transport, and evolutionary biology of ancient life.-M.H. Illustration of heme and heme breakdown products in individual RBCs preserved in limb bone material of the theropod dinosaur Aratasaurus.

title: Beyond glycolysis: bacterial enolase as a localization-dependent moonlighting protein in physiology and pathogenesis
summary: Bacterial enolase couples a conserved glycolytic reaction to diverse, localization-dependent interactions. In addition to catalyzing the Mg 2+ -dependent conversion of 2-phosphoglycerate to phosphoenolpyruvate, it participates in RNA-degrad
content: Bacterial enolase couples a conserved glycolytic reaction to diverse, localization-dependent interactions. In addition to catalyzing the Mg 2+ -dependent conversion of 2-phosphoglycerate to phosphoenolpyruvate, it participates in RNA-degradation assemblies and can bind extracellular host ligands. The mechanistic basis for these non-catalytic functions remains inconsistent. High cytosolic abundance, limited cell lysis and reassociation with bacterial envelopes complicate the interpretation of extracellular detection. This critical narrative review evaluates enolase through three linked variables: molecular interface, subcellular localization and physiological context. Evidence from Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis supports recruitment to RNA-degradation networks, whereas studies in streptococci, staphylococci and other bacteria support species-dependent interactions with plasminogen, extracellular matrix proteins and complement regulators. Structural and mutational studies show that oligomeric state and membrane association influence ligand accessibility; preserved growth alone, however, does not establish preserved catalytic function. We replace a strict evidence hierarchy with seven complementary criteria covering prediction, detection, localization, binding, cellular perturbation, functional separation and host relevance. This framework distinguishes biochemical plausibility from causal evidence in the relevant compartment and host. We also assess selective release, vesicle carriage, reassociation, biofilm participation and translational strategies. Current findings support a conserved catalytic core combined with lineage-specific and condition-dependent interaction surfaces, rather than a universal virulence program. Progress requires quantitative localization, controlled separation-of-function genetics and host-compatible validation, together with explicit reporting of the limitations of each experimental system.

title: Integration of Fog-Intelligent and Federated Learning for Decentralized Green Hydrogen Storage Systems: A Review
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: Because of the growing use of renewable energy, there is increased interest in using hydrogen as a flexible energy carrier for storing and balancing the intermittent electricity generated by these sources. Traditional centralized hydrogen s
content: Because of the growing use of renewable energy, there is increased interest in using hydrogen as a flexible energy carrier for storing and balancing the intermittent electricity generated by these sources. Traditional centralized hydrogen storage methods have disadvantages regarding safety, monitoring, scale, transportation, and the management of data, as well as the ability to make real-time decisions. The review is based on a qualitative approach and looks at the potential of Fog Intelligence and Federated Learning (FL) in decentralised green hydrogen storage systems, taking into account distributed sensing, local intelligence, collaborative learning and privacy-sensitive data management. It critically examines alternative routes and methods for decentralised hydrogen production, storage and distribution, different hydrogen storage technologies, and hydrogen monitoring and control by promoting the development of IoT and fog technologies, as well as the application of machine learning in predictive maintenance, demand forecasting, hydrogen storage state estimation, anomaly detection, safety monitoring and hydrogen energy optimisation. The ability of federated learning (FL) architectures to help geographically dispersed hydrogen facilities develop machine learning models without having to send their raw operational data to a central repository is also investigated. The problems of cybersecurity, privacy, communication overhead, heterogeneous data, interoperability, scalability and the trustworthiness of the models are pointed out. From the literature reviewed, the main research gaps are identified as: the lack of standardisation of multi-site hydrogen datasets, the lack of integration between fog computing and federated learning, the lack of explainability, the lack of real-world validation and fragmented interoperability standards. The future directions mentioned include edge–fog–cloud intelligence and explainable and trustworthy federated learning. Some of the future directions suggested are edge–fog–cloud intelligence and explainable and trustworthy federated learning.

title: Mapping the onset of the decreasing drying-rate period in cm 2 -scale coating films via in situ 2D thermography and digital imaging
summary: We simultaneously performed in situ two-dimensional thermography and digital imaging of cm2-scale coating films (4 cm × 4 cm to 4 cm × 8 cm), thereby mapping the surface temperature and brightness during drying. We defined the onset of the
content: We simultaneously performed in situ two-dimensional thermography and digital imaging of cm2-scale coating films (4 cm × 4 cm to 4 cm × 8 cm), thereby mapping the surface temperature and brightness during drying. We defined the onset of the local decreasing-rate drying period via two-dimensional thermography and defined the moment at which local surface brightness stabilized via digital imaging, which was ascribed to the complete surface solidification of the coating. Quantitative analysis revealed a strong correlation between these two measures, with over 85% of the data points falling within a 25% error margin. These results demonstrate that the optically determined time point can serve as a practical indicator of the transition to the decreasing-rate drying period, enabling two-dimensional mapping of drying heterogeneity across coating films. While mapping drying uniformity is inherently challenging, simple digital imaging represents a scalable, cost-effective solution for visualizing localized drying kinetics and preventing defect formation.

title: Metabolic dysfunction in glaucoma: an NAD+-centered framework linking redox homeostasis, metabolite signaling, and precision neuroprotection
summary: Background Glaucoma is characterized by progressive dysfunction of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and degeneration of their axons. Although elevated intraocular pressure, mechanical stress, oxidative stress, and inflammation contribute to di
content: Background Glaucoma is characterized by progressive dysfunction of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and degeneration of their axons. Although elevated intraocular pressure, mechanical stress, oxidative stress, and inflammation contribute to disease progression, these mechanisms do not fully explain continued neurodegeneration in some patients despite adequate pressure control. RGCs have high energetic demands and depend on mitochondrial metabolism, glycolysis, and metabolic support from glial cells. This review aimed to re-examine glaucoma from the perspective of metabolic flexibility and metabolic reserve and to integrate current evidence into an NAD + /NADH-centered metabolic framework. Methods Relevant mechanistic, preclinical, metabolomic, bioenergetic, and clinical evidence was narratively synthesized, with emphasis on RGC metabolic vulnerability, NAD+ homeostasis, mitochondrial function, lactate/pyruvate metabolism, succinate signaling, ketone utilization, the NMNAT2–SARM1 pathway, and metabolism-targeted interventions. Results Clinical and preclinical studies have reported NAD + insufficiency, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered lactate and succinate metabolism, changes in ketone utilization, and abnormalities in axon-degeneration pathways. However, these findings are often discussed as separate metabolic abnormalities. We propose that they may instead reflect a progressive loss of metabolic adaptation during chronic glaucomatous stress. At an early stage, RGCs may maintain energy homeostasis by adjusting glycolysis, substrate utilization, and mitochondrial metabolism. With persistent stress, metabolic flexibility and mitochondrial reserve may decline, redox homeostasis may become disturbed, and axons may become increasingly vulnerable to NMNAT2-SARM1-associated degeneration. On this basis, we propose a conceptual transition from compensated metabolic stress to metabolic inflexibility and, ultimately, metabolic decompensation. Conclusions Viewing glaucoma through the concepts of metabolic flexibility and metabolic reserve may help integrate currently fragmented metabolic findings into a unified disease process. Future metabolic phenotyping that combines systemic bioenergetic measures, ocular metabolites, functional testing, and structural imaging may help identify distinct forms of metabolic vulnerability and support mechanism-informed precision neuroprotection.

title: Oxygen isotopes in Arctic cod ( Boreogadus saida ) otoliths confirm life stage–specific vertical migrations and reveal the life history implications of early ontogenetic temperature
summary: Abstract As a key forage fish in the Arctic, Arctic cod ( Boreogadus saida ) plays a critical role in transferring energy in Arctic marine ecosystems. While understanding Arctic cod population dynamics within the context of a rapidly warmin
content: Abstract As a key forage fish in the Arctic, Arctic cod ( Boreogadus saida ) plays a critical role in transferring energy in Arctic marine ecosystems. While understanding Arctic cod population dynamics within the context of a rapidly warming Arctic could provide essential information for regional conservation efforts, it remains elusive. Here, we postulate that the isotopic ratio of oxygen ( 18 O: 16 O, expressed as δ 18 O) in otoliths can be used to reconstruct both the thermal and spatial history of Arctic cod across the Canadian Arctic and provide insights into future population dynamics. Otoliths grow throughout the life of a fish and incorporate oxygen stable isotopes proportionate to ambient concentrations following a temperature‐dependent fractionation, thereby reflecting the thermal habitats utilized by Arctic cod through their lifetime. Here, we measured δ 18 O in otoliths from 370 Arctic cod caught across the Canadian Arctic. We derived in‐situ fractionation equations inclusive of an age component, compared these with available laboratory‐derived equations, and estimated ambient temperature at larval stages of fish development. We further modelled the effects of ambient temperature experienced during otolith core formation on standard length‐at‐age using a generalized linear model to better understand the effects of warming temperatures on Arctic cod. The results of our study confirm ontogenetic vertical migration of Arctic cod from the epipelagic layer (0–100 m) to the deeper Atlantic water mass (>100 m) within the first year of life. However, the lack of regional small‐scale variation in δ 18 O values within deeper Atlantic waters that fish used impeded the detection of regional horizontal movements at depth based solely on this tracer. Analyses of δ 18 O also showed that Arctic cod experiencing warmer temperatures during early life stages are smaller around age of maturity, suggesting applicability of the temperature‐size rule. Thus, the effects of increasing surface water temperatures in the Canadian Arctic could propagate through the marine food web. While oxygen isotopes in otoliths are a promising way to monitor the effects of temperature on Arctic cod growth in the Canadian Arctic, work remains to realize the full potential of this tool to identify shifts in habitat use.

title: Three novel deep-branching orphan protist lineages from the marine rare biosphere
summary: Metabarcoding has transformed our view of marine protist communities, yet many sequences in environmental surveys are not assigned confident taxonomic identity. These taxonomically ambiguous sequences may include lineages that are not withi
content: Metabarcoding has transformed our view of marine protist communities, yet many sequences in environmental surveys are not assigned confident taxonomic identity. These taxonomically ambiguous sequences may include lineages that are not within any known eukaryotic supergroup, which we refer to here as orphan lineages. These orphan lineages matter beyond taxonomy-based community analyses, because they can help us understand early eukaryotic evolution. Here we used phylogenetic inferences and sequence similarity networks (SSNs) of long-read metabarcoding data of the ribosomal operon (18S-28S rDNA) to identify three novel phylum-level orphan lineages. We designate these lineages Deep Orphan Lineages 1-3 (DEEPOLs) and show that they are exclusively marine and part of the rare biosphere, yet ecologically distinct: DEEPOL1 is a cosmopolitan generalist, DEEPOL2 a conditionally rare lineage capable of local polar blooms, and DEEPOL3 a non-polar lineage with a tendency toward the dark ocean. For DEEPOL2, lineage-specific digital PCR (dPCR) combined with catalyzed reporter deposition fluorescence in situ hybridization (CARD-FISH) provides the first in situ visualization of these cells, revealing small, flagellated, and morphologically inconspicuous protists. Together, our results show that substantial diversity remains hidden among rare lineages, and that long-read sequencing combined with targeted molecular and microscopy approaches offers a first step toward linking orphan sequences to organisms and their evolution and ecological roles.

title: Ozone nanobubbles as a potential post-separation treatment for marine oil-in-water emulsions: Rapid oil removal and petroleum hydrocarbon attenuation
summary: Ozone nanobubbles (O 3 /NB) were evaluated for treating marine oil-in-water emulsions. Stable nanoscale bubble populations (<200 nm), with an apparent mean diameter as low as 9.15 ± 0.64 nm after 30 min at an ozone input of 55.56 mg/L, enab
content: Ozone nanobubbles (O 3 /NB) were evaluated for treating marine oil-in-water emulsions. Stable nanoscale bubble populations (<200 nm), with an apparent mean diameter as low as 9.15 ± 0.64 nm after 30 min at an ozone input of 55.56 mg/L, enabled more than 60% oil removal within 5 min under selected conditions and near-complete removal within 60 min over an initial oil concentration range of 98-511 mg/L. The observed treatment performance likely reflects the combined contributions of physical flotation and ozone-mediated oxidation. Biphasic kinetics were observed, with higher initial rate constants at increased ozone input.
