title: The Fundamentals and Applications of Graphdiyne‐Based Electrocatalysts in Water Electrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Green hydrogen production powered by renewable electricity is central to the transition toward a carbon‐neutral energy system, yet its large‐scale implementation remains constrained by the sluggish kinetics, high energy consumption
content: ABSTRACT Green hydrogen production powered by renewable electricity is central to the transition toward a carbon‐neutral energy system, yet its large‐scale implementation remains constrained by the sluggish kinetics, high energy consumption, and insufficient durability of electrocatalysts for water electrolysis. Graphdiyne (GDY), an emerging two‐dimensional carbon allotrope composed of sp ‐ and sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon atoms, provides a distinctive materials platform for electrocatalysis. The unique carbon‐bonding environment of GDY enables strong interactions with metal atoms, clusters, and heterogeneous phases, allowing atomic‐level regulation of active‐site coordination, charge redistribution, interfacial coupling, and reaction intermediates. This review systematically discusses the fundamental structural and electronic characteristics of GDY and establishes their relationships with electrocatalytic behavior in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and overall water splitting. Particular emphasis is placed on representative GDY‐based catalytic architectures, including atomically dispersed catalysts, metal quantum‐dot/GDY composites, hierarchical heterostructures, and metal‐free GDY derivatives. Their synthesis principles, active‐site configurations, catalytic mechanisms, and performance characteristics are discussed. The perspectives integrating operando characterization, multiscale theoretical modeling, emerging elemental regulation, and electrode engineering are proposed. This review aims to establish a structure–electronic state–catalytic function framework for GDY‐based electrocatalysts and to provide design principles for translating innovative carbon materials into efficient and durable water electrolysis technologies.

title: Learning Day-Ahead Electricity Price Dynamics in Renewable Power Systems: A Time-Adaptive Segmented Multi-Model Ensemble Forecasting Approach
summary: Climate change and energy security concerns are accelerating the shift from conventional generation to renewable power systems, where the variable output of wind and photovoltaic generation amplifies the volatility and complexity of day-ahe
content: Climate change and energy security concerns are accelerating the shift from conventional generation to renewable power systems, where the variable output of wind and photovoltaic generation amplifies the volatility and complexity of day-ahead electricity prices, making accurate price forecasting essential for energy saving, renewable energy integration and sustainable power system operation. This paper proposes an adaptive ensemble electricity price forecasting framework that integrates Random Forest, XGBoost and CNN-LSTM through a validation-based mixture selection strategy. A closed candidate space includes equal weighting, individual experts and non-negative least-squares combinations, with shrinkage towards equal weighting calibrated through forward-chaining cross-validation. State identification, gating, expert attention, similar-period correction and temporal consistency are implemented as optional modules and retained only when they improve validation performance. The framework is evaluated using seasonal rolling forecasts for the Shaanxi electricity spot market, with similarity retrieval restricted to historical observations to prevent future information leakage. The proposed ensemble achieves an overall mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 27.16%, against 30.14% for Random Forest, 32.80% for XGBoost and 32.02% for CNN-LSTM, and also better than six additional baseline methods. Comparative and ablation analyses indicate that the framework combines complementary expert predictions while allowing the contribution of each component to be assessed. These results support adaptive ensemble forecasting under varying electricity market conditions.

title: Solar Powered IoT Water Purification System
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: Access to clean water is essential, yet small water-treatment units often give the user no information about the condition of the water being processed, and many depend on a mains supply. This paper presents the design of a solar-powered, I
content: Access to clean water is essential, yet small water-treatment units often give the user no information about the condition of the water being processed, and many depend on a mains supply. This paper presents the design of a solar-powered, IoT-enabled water purification prototype. The treatment path consists of three stages in sequence: a 5-micron sediment filter, a 10-inch activated carbon (CTO) block filter and an ultraviolet (UV-C) chamber, followed by a clean-water storage tank. An ESP32 microcontroller acquires readings from an EC-0568 pH meter, a turbidity sensor, a TDS sensor, a water-temperature sensor and a tank water-level sensor, and sends them over Wi-Fi to a Blynk dashboard for remote observation. A solar panel, charge controller and 12 V rechargeable battery with a buck converter supply the system, demonstrating renewable-energy use at prototype scale. The selected 3 W panel is a demonstration-scale source and may not sustain continuous pump and UV operation, so the actual operating time will be measured and recorded. The prototype has no RO stage and is not intended to remove dissolved salts, and sensor readings alone do not certify water as safe to drink. The work serves as an educational platform that combines basic water treatment, embedded sensing, renewable energy and IoT monitoring

title: Load Forecasting and Energy Demand Prediction
summary: The transition towards decarbonized, decentralized, and digitalized energy systems has highlighted the importance of precise and adaptive load forecasting (LF). This chapter presents a detailed review of LF theory, techniques, and applicati
content: The transition towards decarbonized, decentralized, and digitalized energy systems has highlighted the importance of precise and adaptive load forecasting (LF). This chapter presents a detailed review of LF theory, techniques, and applications in modern power systems. It highlights the evolution from conventional statistical models to sophisticated artificial intelligence and hybrid models that can effectively address the nonlinear and dynamic behavior of energy demand. The chapter discusses the forecast horizon, ranging from very short- term to long-term forecasts, in the context of power system operation, planning, and policy formulation. The factors that impact LF, including weather, economic, demographic, and behavioral factors, are reviewed, and new challenges posed by the variability of renewable energy sources, electric vehicles, and demand participation are also discussed. The chapter highlights the importance of probabilistic and hybrid models of LF in managing uncertainties in power systems. Performance metrics and applications of LF in power system operation, markets, demand response, and renewable energy integration are also presented.

title: Reframing the AI Compute Continuum: Workload-Resource-Location Fit in Sustainable Platform Infrastructure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository provides the bibliometric dataset documentation and reproducibility materials associated with the research study entitled "Reframing the AI Compute Continuum: Workload–Resource-Location Fit in Sustainable Platform Infrastruc
content: This repository provides the bibliometric dataset documentation and reproducibility materials associated with the research study entitled "Reframing the AI Compute Continuum: Workload–Resource-Location Fit in Sustainable Platform Infrastructure." The study investigates the evolution of research on sustainable AI computing infrastructure through the interrelated dimensions of workload characteristics, computational and energy resources, and infrastructure location. It examines how workload scheduling, resource allocation, cloud–edge orchestration, data-center infrastructure, energy efficiency, renewable energy integration, cooling technologies, and carbon-aware computing contribute to the emerging AI compute continuum. Data sources and study coverage The bibliometric study covers publications dated 2010-2026 and draws on three bibliographic sources: Web of Science Scopus IEEE Xplore The identification and screening process comprised 1,604 retrieved records, 669 duplicate records removed, and 935 unique records screened. Following relevance-based exclusions, the final analytical corpus contains 830 publications. The final dataset reflects the inclusion of seven additional 2026 publications directly relevant to physical AI infrastructure, data-center power systems, cooling, and thermal management. Bibliometric analyses The research workflow includes: Scientific production and bibliometric performance analysis. Author-keyword co-occurrence and conceptual network analysis. Thematic evolution and strategic mapping. Document-level bibliographic coupling. Sensitivity and robustness analyses examining keyword occurrence thresholds, counting methods, and thesaurus-based terminological harmonization. The analytical workflow uses bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer, and SciMAT. Reproducibility and methodological transparency The repository is intended to support transparent documentation and reproducibility of the bibliometric workflow, including the study-selection process, analytical configurations, terminology harmonization, network outputs, and sensitivity analyses. The temporal analysis distinguishes between 2010-2024 (363 publications) and 2025-2026 (467 publications). The complete bibliometric corpus contains 830 publications. In the document-level bibliographic coupling analysis, the largest connected component comprises 595 documents; this network-visualization subset does not constitute a further exclusion from the bibliometric corpus. Data access and reuse The files included in this deposit are subject to the applicable licenses, intellectual-property rights, and database-provider conditions. Reuse permissions apply only to materials that the depositors are authorized to redistribute. title: Effect of Fraud Investigation Practice on Fraud Management in State Corporations in Kenya’s Energy Sector
summary: This study examined the relationship between financial fraud investigation practices and fraud management in state corporations within Kenya's energy sector. Despite internal audit functions, external oversight mechanisms, and financial acc
content: This study examined the relationship between financial fraud investigation practices and fraud management in state corporations within Kenya's energy sector. Despite internal audit functions, external oversight mechanisms, and financial accountability frameworks, concerns about procurement irregularities, contract mismanagement, and weaknesses in fraud detection and investigation persist in Kenya's energy-sector state corporations. These challenges reflect the broader problem of financial fraud in public institutions, where fraud undermines accountability, operational efficiency, and public trust. Anchored in Fraud Triangle Theory, the study used a cross-sectional survey design and targeted 77 finance, accounts, and audit professionals across seven state corporations. Eight participants from the Rural Electrification and Renewable Energy Corporation (REREC) participated in the pilot study and were excluded from the main survey, leaving 69 eligible respondents. Of these, 66 completed questionnaires were returned and analysed, representing a response rate of 95.65 per cent. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression with SPSS Version 28. Descriptive findings indicated that respondents perceived internal audit quality and the use of advanced data analytics as relatively strong fraud investigation practices, whereas whistleblower mechanisms were comparatively weak. Pearson correlation analysis found a strong, positive, and statistically significant association between financial fraud investigation practices and fraud management (r = 0.805, p < 0.001). Regression results showed that investigation practices accounted for 64.8 per cent of the variation in fraud management (R² = 0.648), and the regression coefficient (B = 0.865, p < 0.001) indicated a positive, statistically significant predictive relationship. The study concludes that systematic fraud investigation practices are positively associated with fraud management in state corporations within Kenya's energy sector. It recommends strengthening whistleblower protection and reporting mechanisms, investing in forensic data analytics, and enhancing collaboration between internal and external audit functions to improve institutional accountability and financial fraud management.

title: Biomass‐Based Hydrochar/NiFe‐MOF Composite Electrodes for Hydrogen Production Using Water Electrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Hydrogen (H 2 ) is regarded as a clean and abundant renewable energy source, and a particularly promising method for producing clean H 2 on a large scale without producing greenhouse gases is water electrolysis. Nevertheless, elect
content: ABSTRACT Hydrogen (H 2 ) is regarded as a clean and abundant renewable energy source, and a particularly promising method for producing clean H 2 on a large scale without producing greenhouse gases is water electrolysis. Nevertheless, electrode development is crucial in water electrolysis due to high overpotentials, limited stability, and high costs of current materials. Therefore, in this study, we developed a metal organic framework (MOF) composite integrated with coffee waste‐derived hydrochar (HC@NiFe‐MOF)‐Ni foam electrode as an effective electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in the water splitting process. The structural integrity and electrochemical performance of the developed electrode were greatly improved by combining NiFe‐MOFs with HC. The HC@NiFe‐MOF‐doped electrode demonstrated improved HER activity compared with bare Ni foam, achieving a Tafel slope of 117.2 mV/dec and an overpotential of 77 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 , along with stable electrochemical performance under the investigated operating conditions. Moreover, by avoiding MOF particles from aggregating together, the incorporation of HC enhances dispersion and provides a more consistent and readily available active surface area. Consequently, this study demonstrates the promise of HC@NiFe‐MOF‐doped electrode as a reliable, highly efficient electrocatalyst for the production of sustainable H 2 , providing a breakthrough in the development of cutting‐edge materials for energy production applications.

title: Synchrotron X-ray tomography and functional evaluations of lead-free piezoceramic-filled natural rubber composites
source: Journal of Metals Materials and Minerals
summary: Flexible piezoelectric composite materials have gained increasing attention due to their widespread applications in modern electronic devices such as energy harvesters, dielectric capacitors, or wearable sensors. In this work, flexible piez
content: Flexible piezoelectric composite materials have gained increasing attention due to their widespread applications in modern electronic devices such as energy harvesters, dielectric capacitors, or wearable sensors. In this work, flexible piezoelectric composites were developed by incorporating BCZT lead-free piezoceramic fillers into a flexible NR matrix (NR/BCZT composites) with BCZT content ranging from 0 phr to 60 phr (referred as 0BCZT to 60BCZT). Additionally, the structure-property relationships of the NR/BCZT composites were evaluated using synchrotron X-ray tomographic microscopy (SR-XTM), in conjunction with various materials characterization techniques. This work found that the addition of BCZT filler into NR reduced cure time from 14.01 min (0BCZT) to 11.18 min (60BCZT), whereas hardness of the NR/BCZT composites increased from 40.18±0.08 to 45.92±0.11 with increasing BCZT content from 0 phr to 60 phr, respectively. Conversely, the tensile strength of the NR/BCZT composites at all compositions was lower than that of pure NR (tensile strength of 0BCZT = 24.70±2.56 MPa), except for the 30BCZT composite, which exhibited strong adhesion between the BCZT filler and the NR matrix and resulted in the observed highest tensile strength of 26.88±0.90 MPa. Interestingly, no increase in dielectric permittivity occurred at a low BCZT loading of 15 phr, while a significant enhancement from 2.76±0.13 to 3.34±0.08 was observed when the BCZT content was further increased from 15 phr to 30 phr, respectively. The filler dispersion in the NR matrix was investigated using synchrotron X-ray tomographic microscopy (SR-XTM), combined with quantitative analysis of SEM images. The results showed that, the interparticle spacing decreased with increasing the BCZT content in the NR/BCZT composites. This reduction in the interparticle spacing play an important role in the observed electrical properties of the NR/BCZT composites. These findings help to provide a better understanding of the development of lead-free piezoceramic-filled natural rubber composites.

title: Applications of Cellulose Nanomaterials in Energy Storage Devices
summary: Cellulose nanomaterials (CNMs) represent highly promising sustainable materials for the next generation of energy storage devices such as batteries, supercapacitors, and fuel cells. Being produced from the most abundant biological polymer,
content: Cellulose nanomaterials (CNMs) represent highly promising sustainable materials for the next generation of energy storage devices such as batteries, supercapacitors, and fuel cells. Being produced from the most abundant biological polymer, cellulose nanofibrils, cellulose nanocrystals, and bacterial cellulose possess outstanding mechanical properties along with high specific surface area and tunable chemical composition of the surface. Functional roles for CNMs in these devices are diverse, ranging from flexible substrates and binders to host matrices for electrolytes and robust separators. High porosity and hydrophilicity of the nanomaterials are important for effective ion transport. Besides this, cellulosic nanostructures can be used in combination with various conductive materials such as carbon nanotubes and graphene to produce composite electrodes with high capacity, flexibility, and lightweight. Besides these technical advantages, biodegradable and renewable CNMs represent an opportunity to decrease the environmental impact and toxicity of energy storage devices. Despite existing challenges in production scalability and cost optimization, continued advancement in CNM research is vital for developing efficient, eco-friendly, and wearable energy solutions.

title: Role of Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Neural Grid
summary: Advancements in electrical power systems have moved much ahead of the old transmission and distribution networks. The idea of the neural grid shows a big change towards a more reliable, self-running, and well-organized electricity system. T
content: Advancements in electrical power systems have moved much ahead of the old transmission and distribution networks. The idea of the neural grid shows a big change towards a more reliable, self-running, and well-organized electricity system. The Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) play a major role in building the neural grid. IoT helps with real- time sensing, communication, and coordination between many devices in the grid. AI adds more power by giving analytical thinking, prediction, and automatic decision-making. We can imagine IoT as the nervous system and AI as the brain of the neural grid. This work explains neural grids and how IoT and AI work together in different ways, such as their basic technology, structure, operation, challenges, and future growth. It also highlights practical problems faced in our country, especially in renewable energy use, load management, and frequent failures in the distribution network.

title: Offshore Solar Photovoltaic Potential Around India: Evidence, Marine Constraints, and Deployment Pathways—A Critical Review
source: International journal of research and scientific innovation
summary: Offshore solar photovoltaic (PV) systems may broaden renewable-electricity options where coastal demand, land competition and maritime space intersect. India is a relevant case because of its extensive coastline, substantial solar resources
content: Offshore solar photovoltaic (PV) systems may broaden renewable-electricity options where coastal demand, land competition and maritime space intersect. India is a relevant case because of its extensive coastline, substantial solar resources and varied marine environments; however, offshore PV remains an emerging technology rather than an established commercial pathway. This critical review synthesises the India-specific resource evidence identified in the cited literature, evaluates the transferability of international marine-floating-PV research, and examines the engineering, environmental, social, economic and governance conditions that determine whether offshore resource can become deployable electricity. The principal India-focused baseline identified in the literature is the 2017 assessment by Solanki et al., which used ERA-Interim data for 2015–2016 and reported mean global horizontal irradiation (GHI) of 5.49 kWh/m²/day, with comparatively favourable radiation along Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. These are published historical findings, not new estimates produced by this review. Subsequent reviews highlight wave and wind loading, fatigue, corrosion, biofouling, mooring performance, maintenance access and extreme-weather survivability as central design concerns. Public resources such as the INCOIS Integrated Marine Energy Atlas, ERA5, the Global Solar Atlas and GEBCO can support future spatial screening, but their availability does not itself establish a validated national estimate of offshore-PV capacity. The review develops an evidence-to-siting framework that distinguishes theoretical solar resource, technology-specific technical potential, environmentally and socially constrained potential, and economically deployable potential. It also identifies a practical research pathway combining multi-source resource comparison, metocean characterisation, transparent exclusion mapping, uncertainty analysis, site validation and monitored demonstration projects. The available evidence supports the need and feasibility of further assessment, but does not justify a bankable national capacity figure or a claim that all Indian EEZ waters are suitable for development.

title: Perceived Uncertainty and Perceived Performance of Public-Private Partnerships in Kenya: A Project-Level Stakeholder Survey
source: Research Journal of Business and Finance
summary: Anchored in Transaction Cost Economics (TCE), this study examined the association between perceived uncertainty and perceived performance of public-private partnerships (PPPs) in Kenya. Uncertainty was measured as perceived exposure to forc
content: Anchored in Transaction Cost Economics (TCE), this study examined the association between perceived uncertainty and perceived performance of public-private partnerships (PPPs) in Kenya. Uncertainty was measured as perceived exposure to force majeure events, regulatory and policy change, and market volatility, and performance through project efficiency, financial viability, service delivery and stakeholder satisfaction. Adopting a positivist philosophy and an explanatory, cross-sectional survey design, the study collected primary data with structured five-point Likert questionnaires from respondents engaged in PPP implementation across six sectors. A design-stage target of 260 respondents was set from an estimated population of 400; 215 usable questionnaires (82.7% of the target) were returned and aggregated to 67 PPP projects. Data were analysed with descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple linear regression. Projects whose respondents reported more uncertainty also reported lower performance (r = −.66, p < .001; B = −0.34, 95% CI [−0.43, −0.24]), and the fitted line accounted for 43% of the sample variance in rated performance. The null hypothesis (H₀: β₁ = 0) was rejected in favour of H₁: β₁ < 0. The study concluded that perceived uncertainty and perceived performance are negatively associated across the projects studied.

title: Photovoltaic-Health-Monitoring-Adaptive-Control
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Health Monitoring and Adaptive Control of Photovoltaic Energy Materials Official repository for "Health Monitoring and Adaptive Control of Photovoltaic Energy Materials using Reinforcement Learning Guided Multimodal Large Language Models."
content: Health Monitoring and Adaptive Control of Photovoltaic Energy Materials Official repository for "Health Monitoring and Adaptive Control of Photovoltaic Energy Materials using Reinforcement Learning Guided Multimodal Large Language Models." This project presents a reinforcement learning guided multimodal framework for photovoltaic health monitoring and adaptive control. The proposed TemporalHierarchicalCompressive model integrates temporal dependency modeling, hierarchical feature learning, and compressive state representation to improve photovoltaic system assessment, energy optimization, and operational reliability. 1. Overview Photovoltaic systems operate under dynamic environmental conditions, material degradation, and changing energy demands. Conventional monitoring and control methods often struggle to integrate heterogeneous sensor information, capture long-term temporal dependencies, and balance energy production with material preservation. To address these challenges, this study proposes a unified framework combining domain pretraining, multimodal large language models, and reinforcement learning. The framework aims to: Capture temporal dependencies in photovoltaic operating conditions. Integrate heterogeneous material, electrical, environmental, and operational information. Identify photovoltaic health conditions and degradation patterns. Generate compact and informative multimodal state representations. Optimize adaptive control strategies through reinforcement learning. Improve energy yield, operational safety, and long-term system reliability. 2. Proposed Framework The proposed TemporalHierarchicalCompressive framework consists of three core components: 2.1 Temporal Recall Gate Captures dynamic temporal dependencies and selectively preserves relevant historical information for photovoltaic state estimation. 2.2 Hierarchical Feature Integrator Integrates multimodal information across different abstraction levels, establishing relationships among material properties, electrical measurements, environmental variables, and operational states. 2.3 Compressive State Encoder Transforms high-dimensional multimodal representations into compact state vectors while preserving important information for downstream monitoring and adaptive control. 2.4 Reinforcement Learning Optimization The framework incorporates Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) to optimize continuous adaptive control decisions. The reward function integrates three objectives: Task Reward: Energy yield, prediction accuracy, health-monitoring correctness, and operational safety. Quality Reward: Calibration, temporal consistency, cross-modal agreement, and output completeness. Robustness Reward: Stability under sensor noise, missing modalities, environmental shifts, and degradation perturbations. The reward weights are set to 0.5, 0.3, and 0.2, respectively. 3. Datasets Two photovoltaic datasets are used in the experimental framework. Dataset Purpose Photovoltaic Material Performance Dataset D

title: Introduction to floating solar photovoltaics
summary: The Paris Agreement, together with national commitments towards net-zero emissions, has marked a rare consensus within the international community: the future of the global energy system must be built upon renewable energy sources. Among th
content: The Paris Agreement, together with national commitments towards net-zero emissions, has marked a rare consensus within the international community: the future of the global energy system must be built upon renewable energy sources. Among these, solar photovoltaics (PV) have emerged as a central pillar, owing to their modular nature, flexible scalability and an unprecedented decline in costs in the history of energy technologies. In just over two decades, PV has evolved from an expensive, experimental option into one of the most competitive sources of electricity worldwide. Solar photovoltaics are no longer a peripheral renewable option; they have become one of the defining infrastructures of the global energy transition.

title: Source–Load Data-Driven Multi-Objective Siting and Sizing of Distributed Energy Storage in Islanded Microgrids
summary: The variability of renewable generation and load demand complicates energy storage planning for islanded microgrids, particularly when siting, sizing, operating reliability, and economic performance must be considered simultaneously. This p
content: The variability of renewable generation and load demand complicates energy storage planning for islanded microgrids, particularly when siting, sizing, operating reliability, and economic performance must be considered simultaneously. This paper proposes a source-load data-driven method for siting and sizing distributed energy storage in an islanded microgrid. An improved grey wolf optimiser-gated recurrent unit (IGWO-GRU) model was developed to forecast photovoltaic output and nodal loads under normal and adverse weather conditions. The forecasts were incorporated into a multi-objective planning model that maximised islanded supply reliability and capacity-normalised discharge throughput while minimising annualised planning and operating cost. Continuous state-of-charge evolution, transitions between grid-connected and islanded operation, nodal-voltage limits, line-loading limits, upstream-grid power exchange, and priority supply to critical loads were explicitly considered. NSGA-III was directly coupled with a pandapower full-chronology AC power-flow model so that every candidate configuration was evaluated from its simulated operating performance. In the synthetic PV–BESS IEEE 33-bus case study, the 1319 h chronological assessment yielded 640 feasible configurations, including 10 non-dominated solutions. For this synthetic case and predefined candidate buses, the results illustrate a chronological planning workflow and quantify conditional trade-offs among annualised cost, islanded supply reliability, and capacity utilisation. They do not establish universal forecasting or optimisation superiority.

title: Conceptual Architecture of a 30-Meter All-Electron Plasma-Wakefield γγ Higgs Factory with Galinstan Liquid-Metal Shielding, Beam Dump, and Multi- Stage Lateral Extraction
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: I present the foundational conceptual architecture of LumTechnionG (Apollo Project XXI Century), an ultra-compact (30 m linear footprint, ∼1,500 m3 total volume) multifunction linear collider designed to overcome the four classical volumetr
content: I present the foundational conceptual architecture of LumTechnionG (Apollo Project XXI Century), an ultra-compact (30 m linear footprint, ∼1,500 m3 total volume) multifunction linear collider designed to overcome the four classical volumetric bottlenecks of high-energy physics facilities. By combining symmetric multi-stage capillary Laser Wakefield Acceleration (LWFA, ∼50 GV/m blowout regime) of pure electron beams in both arms with coherent fiber-array laser drivers, renewable liquid/plasma mirrors, and millimeter-offset inverse Compton scattering, the system operates as a clean photon-photon (γγ → H) collider around the 125 GeV threshold, completely eliminating positron/muon production complexes and kilometer-scale rings. All ionizing interactions are confined within a central 4 m armored core (Phanes-in-Hephaestus Capsule) featuring an 18–20 T REBCO superconducting solenoid, silicon-tungsten calorimetry, dynamic Galinstan (Ga-In-Sn, vapor pressure < 10−8 Pa) liquid-metal curtains acting as non-degradable Compton electron beam dumps, and a multilayer liquid-metal/borated-polyethylene perimeter pool that suppresses electromagnetic pulses and photoneutrons. Adjacent control electronics (The Lyre) achieve sub-15 ns trigger latency via dual-skin dielectric immersion and sealed Galinstan microchannel cooling. Fast pulsed electromagnets (kickers) placed in the initial meters of acceleration enable three staged lateral extraction lines (Apollo's Three Endowments): 50–250 MeV for FLASH oncology, 0.5–1 GeV for clean medical radioisotopes and photofission, and 2–5 GeV for an X-ray Free-Electron Laser (XFEL) atomic scanner, enabling continuous industrial and medical self-financing alongside fundamental physics operations.

content: THE WORLD IN SYMBOLS 2027 is an annual global outlook published by PRMS Architecture Lab as part of the PRMS Working Papers series and the Renewable Horizons Collection. This special edition examines ten global transformations expected to shape 2027, covering energy security, financial markets, artificial intelligence, climate change, energy transition, future architecture, geopolitical transformations, urban resilience, human habitat and measurable architecture. The publication explores these developments from the perspective of buildings and cities, examining their implications for energy, water, materials, technology, environmental performance, human comfort and operational conditions. Drawing on institutional reports and documented trends available as of November 17, 2026, this outlook connects global developments with the evolving challenges of the built environment. The publication presents an editorial perspective and an agenda for observation and critical analysis, rather than a deterministic forecast. title: Pyrolysis Kinetics and Synergistic Interactions Between Biomass and Coking Coals During Co-pyrolysis
summary: Abstract Partial substitution of coking coal with renewable biomass offers a potential pathway to reduce fossil carbon consumption in integrated steelmaking and thereby contribute to decarbonization. While biomass is typically employed via
content: Abstract Partial substitution of coking coal with renewable biomass offers a potential pathway to reduce fossil carbon consumption in integrated steelmaking and thereby contribute to decarbonization. While biomass is typically employed via blast furnace (BF) injection replacing pulverized coal, its application in cokemaking has faced challenges, particularly in maintaining coke strength at high temperatures. Recent advances, however, have shown that microalgal biomass—specifically Chlorella vulgaris —can be incorporated at levels up to 10 wt% without significantly impairing coke quality. This study investigates the co-pyrolysis behavior of coal and microalgae (MA) to better understand their interactions during the cokemaking process. The objective was to examine how MA incorporation influences the apparent coal-associated thermal-decomposition response, product yields, and elemental distributions relative to torrefied lignocellulosic biomass. A custom fixed-bed pyrolysis rig was used to quantify char, tar, and gas yields from coal–MA and coal–TB blends, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) assessed changes in thermal behavior. The MA-containing blends exhibited lower apparent activation energies for the estimated coal-associated decomposition response and increased aliphatic contributions to the recovered tar; considered together with the H/C and evolved-gas data, these trends are consistent with a possible hydrogen-transfer and radical-stabilization mechanism.

title: Green Hydrogen as an Energy Vector for Renewable Energy Integration: Emerging Research Trends and Thematic Assessment
summary: Green hydrogen is increasingly positioned as an energy vector capable of linking variable renewable electricity with storage, conversion, transport, and end-use sectors. This study examines the recent evolution of this research field throug
content: Green hydrogen is increasingly positioned as an energy vector capable of linking variable renewable electricity with storage, conversion, transport, and end-use sectors. This study examines the recent evolution of this research field through a combined bibliometric and thematic assessment of 1339 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection for 2024–2026. VOSviewer was used to analyze publication dynamics, international co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and temporal thematic evolution. The bibliometric findings were further interpreted through a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis informed by representative publications and a Research Maturity versus Emerging Potential Matrix positioning 47 author keywords. The results reveal rapidly increasing scientific activity, a highly interconnected international collaboration structure, and six major thematic clusters spanning hydrogen production, storage, renewable energy integration, techno-economic assessment, decarbonization, infrastructure, and digital optimization. Mature themes such as hydrogen, electrolysis, storage, and renewable energy remain the scientific foundation of the field, while renewable energy integration, techno-economic analysis, hydrogen infrastructure, supply chains, advanced electrolysis, and data-driven approaches show stronger recent momentum. Overall, the findings indicate a transition from technology-centered research toward system-oriented integration, where the future role of green hydrogen depends increasingly on coordinated technical, economic, infrastructural, and operational development.

title: ThomasLloyd renewable energy reference projects
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Factual, open reference dataset of utility-scale renewable energy projects associated with ThomasLloyd: utility-scale solar in India, solar and biomass power plants in the Philippines and rooftop solar in Vietnam. Each record is a reference
content: Factual, open reference dataset of utility-scale renewable energy projects associated with ThomasLloyd: utility-scale solar in India, solar and biomass power plants in the Philippines and rooftop solar in Vietnam. Each record is a reference project and states its relationship to ThomasLloyd. Each record includes location, installed capacity, site area, gross annual generation, avoided CO2 emissions and jobs created, separated into construction and permanent jobs. Figures cover the year ending 31 December 2023. The two projects in Vietnam are the exception: their published project pages state no reference year, and they report no construction jobs. Avoided CO2 emissions are estimated in line with the International Financial Institutions Technical Working Group methodology for grid-connected renewable energy projects, using the 2022 harmonised combined-margin grid factors: 0.822 for solar in India, 0.482 for biomass in the Philippines, adjusted for the greenhouse gas footprint of biomass collection, 0.617 for solar in the Philippines and 0.493 for solar in Vietnam. Scope: this dataset covers the fifteen reference projects that have their own project page. The track record of the ThomasLloyd team is larger and comprises 115 projects in 20 countries with 27.6 GW of generating capacity, 10.3 GW of it renewable; that figure refers to the team, not to the group as a legal entity. Employment figures follow the definition used on the published project pages: staff hired for the construction phase of a plant and staff recruited for its operation. This dataset reports the two separately, as construction jobs and permanent jobs; the project pages show their combined total. Published as open reference data under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), with attribution to ThomasLloyd.

title: Effect of Green Procurement Practices in Enhancing Cold Supply Chain Performance: A Case of Rwanda Medical Supply
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of Green Procurement Practices in Enhancing Cold Supply Chain Performance at Rwanda Medical Supply.Specifically, the study sought to determine the effect of green training and monitoring practices on cold supp
content: This study examined the effect of Green Procurement Practices in Enhancing Cold Supply Chain Performance at Rwanda Medical Supply.Specifically, the study sought to determine the effect of green training and monitoring practices on cold supply chain performance at RMS.The study adopted a quantitative research approach using a cross-sectional research design.A total of 109 employees involved in procurement, warehouse and inventory management, logistics and distribution, quality assurance, and cold chain management were targeted and participated in the study.All 109 questionnaires were successfully completed and returned, representing a response rate of 100%.Primary data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to the selected employees.Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and simple linear regression analysis using SPSS Version 2.7.The findings revealed a strong positive and statistically significant relationship between green training and monitoring practices and cold supply chain performance (r = 0.761, p < 0.001).Regression results showed that green training and monitoring practices explained 57.9% of the variation in cold supply chain performance (R² = 0.579).The study concluded that regular employee training, environmental sustainability awareness, effective temperature monitoring, and timely correction of storage deviations were important for improving cold supply chain performance at RMS.The study recommended strengthening continuous employee training, improving environmental sustainability awareness, enhancing temperature monitoring systems, and establishing effective procedures for reporting and correcting storage deviations.

title: A High–Mid–Low Triangular Echo State Network with Attention and Improved Beaver Behavior Optimizer for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
summary: Proper photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting supports grid stability, efficient dispatch, and economic performance. While most forecasting models use rigid time smoothing, which eliminates multi-scale volatility, in this study, we propose a H
content: Proper photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting supports grid stability, efficient dispatch, and economic performance. While most forecasting models use rigid time smoothing, which eliminates multi-scale volatility, in this study, we propose a High–Mid–Low Triangular Echo State Network (HMLT-ESN) optimized by a Quasi-Oppositional Learning Cyclonic Foraging Beaver Behavior Optimizer (QCBBO). HMLT-ESN partitions photovoltaic sequences into high-, mid-, and low-frequency components using Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD). Each component is processed by a sub-reservoir, and each sub-reservoir uses different activation functions: TreX for transients, tanh for periodicities, and sigmoid for trends. Rather than using a fixed leakage rate, we introduce an attention-driven diagonal matrix that adjusts each timescale blockwise according to its instantaneous activation energy. Recurrent topology is restricted to an equilateral triangular lattice that provides an analytically tractable spectral radius. The circle map achieves better coverage over the normal input domain and feature discrimination, while the QCBBO runs autonomously to avoid local optima. Tested on a 20 MWp plant in northern China, the model predicts 15 min power at 15 min resolution using 90 min windows. The HMLT-ESN reduces Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 41.57% and Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) by 51.73% compared to ESN, acting as a robust dispatch tool for renewable-heavy power systems.

title: HERIT4AGES develops smart energy router prototype
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: A HERIT4AGES Smart Energy Router (SER) prototype was developed by project partner UNINOVA to support smarter energy management in heritage buildings. The SER integrates renewable energy generation, energy storage and intelligent control tec
content: A HERIT4AGES Smart Energy Router (SER) prototype was developed by project partner UNINOVA to support smarter energy management in heritage buildings. The SER integrates renewable energy generation, energy storage and intelligent control technologies to optimise energy flows, maximise photovoltaic self-consumption, reduce grid dependency and energy costs.

title: Mobilising Finance for Renewable, Reliable, Secure and Affordable Energy in the Philippines: The Case of Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
summary: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in the Philippines account for 99.6% of all enterprises and 66.6% of enterprise employment, yet face high electricity prices, reliability challenges and a persistent financing gap, having co
content: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in the Philippines account for 99.6% of all enterprises and 66.6% of enterprise employment, yet face high electricity prices, reliability challenges and a persistent financing gap, having consistently received less than 5% of total bank credit over the past decade. Expanding renewable energy and energy efficiency investment among these smaller businesses is therefore important for enterprise competitiveness and resilience, as well as to achieve the Philippines’ energy security goals and target of 50% renewable energy in the power mix by 2040. The report focuses on how the Philippines can strengthen access to finance for MSMEs in renewable, reliable, secure and affordable energy, including in renewable energy and energy efficiency. The report identifies the main barriers preventing viable renewable energy and energy efficiency investments from accessing finance. It proposes priority actions to strengthen project pipelines, establish common market foundations, and align finance and guarantees with MSME renewable, reliable, secure and affordable energy needs. It also recommends developing aggregation and fostering a domestic supply chain capable of reaching dispersed enterprises at scale.

title: A Two-Sided Quaternion Differential Equation Model for Power Balance Dynamics in Stand-Alone Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
summary: Hybrid renewable energy systems combine intermittent sources with storage, and their energy management rests on the power balance of a common bus. Existing models either describe the devices in detail or treat this balance as a static const
content: Hybrid renewable energy systems combine intermittent sources with storage, and their energy management rests on the power balance of a common bus. Existing models either describe the devices in detail or treat this balance as a static constraint. We model the power deviations of a stand-alone system phenomenologically by a two-sided quaternion differential equation, with the battery in the scalar part and the photovoltaic, wind and load deviations in the vector part. The quaternion product drives the battery by a weighted balance of the other deviations and rotates the vector part, while the two-sided form separates battery coupling from coupling among the other components. A fast buffer absorbs the transient mismatch of the bus, and a sustained residual requires a separate compensation channel. We prove well-posedness and a norm identity in which the decay of all deviations enters through one rate. A variation of constants formula in the quaternion algebra yields a modal decomposition in which the right coefficient splits one frequency into two, along with explicit equilibria and harmonic gains. The multistage Adomian decomposition method runs in the same algebra, and its error bound does not grow with time, both for the free response and for a piecewise smooth injection.

title: Symmetrical_Economy 3
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

content: Overview: "Symmetry-Based Field Theory of Sustainable Economic Rebalancing" by Masao Nanba (2026) [1]This paper presents a field-theoretic macroeconomic framework designed to address the structural instabilities of modern global capitalism. The author argues that contemporary economic crises—such as widening wealth inequality (\(r > g\)), financial bubbles, ecological depletion, and political instability—stem from an institutional obsession with linear, year-over-year (YoY) exponential growth. In this regime, the financial field (\(\psi _{F}\)) has detached from and overgrown the real productive economy (\(\psi _{R}\)), while extreme capital concentration erodes the foundational democratic and social support field (\(\psi _{D}\)) required to sustain the system. [1]To resolve these structural flaws, the paper proposes four core concepts and principles:1. Rotational Symmetry and Base Stock Protection: Instead of endless linear expansion, economic dynamics must adopt rotational symmetry, coupling periods of growth with cyclical regeneration, rest, and redistribution. Using the collapse of Japanese coastal fisheries as an example, the paper highlights how standard GDP accounting ignores the liquidation of foundational stocks (\(S_{\text{base}}\)), such as overharvesting juvenile fish or exhausting worker well-being. Sustainable cycles must ensure net-zero or positive regeneration of these ecological and social bases. [1]2. Unified Field Coupling: By modeling the real productive density, financial field, and democratic support density together, the author demonstrates that allowing democratic legitimacy and everyday livelihood stability (\(\psi _{D}\)) to fall below a critical threshold triggers institutional breakdown and systemic phase transitions. [1]3. Controlled Perturbations vs. Policy Delay: Drawing on shock-induced symmetry breaking and non-equilibrium inverted pendulum dynamics, the model shows that abrupt, large-scale policy shocks cause supply-chain fragmentation and social panic. Conversely, delaying reform incurs an exponentially growing crash penalty (\(E_{\text{crash}} \propto \exp(\sqrt{g/L}\,\tau)\)). Optimal governance therefore requires immediate, gradual, and iterative low-amplitude policy adjustments (\(\tau \to 0\)) that protect vulnerable populations. [1]4. Bifurcated National Survival Strategies: Because nations face different boundary conditions, transition paths must differ. Japan, facing demographic contraction and import vulnerabilities, should pursue structural decentralization by building resilient, multi-local hubs anchored in regional food, sustainable fisheries, and renewable energy (\(V_{\text{JP}}\)). In contrast, the United States must leverage its massive capital inertia and venture ecosystems to drive high-velocity technological innovation, continuously recharging global confidence in the US Dollar (\(V_{\text{US}}\)). title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Optimizing Energy Consumption in Power Distribution Networks
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Abstract With the continuous growth in electricity consumption and the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power distribution networks have become more complex in terms of both structure and dynamics. The operational efficie
content: Abstract With the continuous growth in electricity consumption and the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power distribution networks have become more complex in terms of both structure and dynamics. The operational efficiency of these networks plays a crucial role in ensuring a reliable and cost-effective energy supply. Traditional network control and management methods often lack the capability to respond promptly to fluctuations in demand and generation. This paper proposes a hybrid artificial intelligence-based framework for optimizing energy consumption in power distribution networks. In the proposed approach, the load demand at different network nodes is initially predicted using artificial neural networks. Subsequently, an optimization algorithm, such as a genetic algorithm or reinforcement learning, is employed to adjust the network configuration and schedule distributed energy resources. Simulation results on the IEEE test system demonstrate that applying this approach can significantly reduce power losses and improve voltage stability. The findings indicate that the proposed intelligent system, by improving load forecasting accuracy and optimizing network scheduling and configuration, can substantially reduce energy losses. Keywords :Artificial Intelligence, Power Distribution Network, Energy Consumption Optimization, Load Forecasting, Power Losses, Reinforcement Learning

title: A Critical Perspective of Energy Communities’ Development in Spain: Main Barriers and Facilitators
summary: The concepts of Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) and Citizen Energy Communities (CECs) have gained importance in recent years. Both concepts have been articulated and transposed in the regulations of several European Union (EU) Member St
content: The concepts of Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) and Citizen Energy Communities (CECs) have gained importance in recent years. Both concepts have been articulated and transposed in the regulations of several European Union (EU) Member States, and are commonly known under the umbrella term of energy communities (ECs). This study critically examines the development of ECs in Spain, together with the supporting regulatory mechanism for collective self-consumption (CSC). The study combines two complementary approaches: (i) a systematic literature review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology, based on research and implementation evidence on ECs in Spain and (ii) an analysis of selected real-world projects to identify barriers and facilitators. By combining a semi-quantitative assessment of the literature with qualitative evidence from real-world Spanish EC initiatives, the analysis synthesises the main technical, legal, economic and social factors shaping EC implementation, while also examining the role of business models, digital tools and governance arrangements in supporting scalability, participation and social impact. The findings highlight both the opportunities and the persistent barriers associated with the consolidation of ECs in Spain, particularly regarding regulatory complexity, financial sustainability and limited diversification beyond photovoltaic (PV) CSC.

title: Unified sliding-mode control of a flexible excitation system with lightweight stator/rotor dual-channel damping injection
summary: Abstract With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power systems are increasingly exposed to broadband and strongly coupled disturbances. Under large disturbances, parameter perturbations, and operating-point variations,
content: Abstract With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, power systems are increasingly exposed to broadband and strongly coupled disturbances. Under large disturbances, parameter perturbations, and operating-point variations, flexible excitation system (FES) may exhibit aggravated DC-link voltage fluctuations, sluggish excitation response, and insufficient damping of electromechanical oscillations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a unified sliding-mode control framework for a FES consisting of a three-level neutral-point-clamped voltage-source converter (NPC-VSC), a DC link, and a DC/DC excitation chopper. An adaptive-gain second-order sliding-mode (AG-SOSM) controller is introduced into the VSC outer loop to ensure finite-time convergence of the DC-link voltage and enhanced disturbance rejection. In the VSC current inner loop and the chopper control loop, band-pass-filter (BPF)-enhanced sliding surfaces are combined with the super-twisting algorithm (STA) to achieve fast tracking of the excitation variable with reduced chattering. In addition, lightweight stator-side reactive power damping and rotor-side damping-torque components are injected through the reference path, enabling coordinated dual-channel damping enhancement without modifying the main controller structure. Time-domain simulation results under network disturbances, mechanical-power perturbation, excitation-related parameter variations, and converter-current harmonic evaluation show that, compared with CES, PID-FES, and CSMC-FES benchmarks, the proposed strategy improves electromechanical damping, accelerates dynamic recovery, maintains DC-link voltage regulation, and reduces converter-current harmonic distortion.

title: Advancing floating solar photovoltaic (FSPV) development towards sustainable development goals: policy implications for Vietnam
summary: This chapter examines policy and regulatory frameworks not as administrative instruments, but as system-level stabilising mechanisms that shape the long-term technical, economic and environmental feasibility of FPV-hydropower integration Th
content: This chapter examines policy and regulatory frameworks not as administrative instruments, but as system-level stabilising mechanisms that shape the long-term technical, economic and environmental feasibility of FPV-hydropower integration The global energy landscape is entering a phase of profound transition, driven simultaneously by two systemic forces: the rapid growth in electricity demand to support economic expansion and urbanisation and the urgent need to mitigate environmental impacts, particularly greenhouse gas emissions and resource degradation. The convergence of these pressures is reshaping the way energy is produced, distributed and consumed worldwide, compelling countries to shift towards sustainable development pathways grounded in renewable energy and intelligent technologies.

title: Hydrogen Generation, Migration and Accumulation in Rock: A Comprehensive Review
source: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF PURE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
summary: In the pursuit of clean and sustainable energy solutions, the attention has shifted towards hydrogen, an emerging contender with vast potential. This comprehensive review delves into the promise of geological formations as reservoirs for hy
content: In the pursuit of clean and sustainable energy solutions, the attention has shifted towards hydrogen, an emerging contender with vast potential. This comprehensive review delves into the promise of geological formations as reservoirs for hydrogen, offering insights into the intricate processes governing its generation, migration, and accumulation. The article highlights the significance of this phenomenon within the renewable energy landscape, emphasizing its pivotal role in curtailing greenhouse gas emissions and fortifying energy security. This multidisciplinary analysis traverses the realms of geology, renewable energy, environmental science, and geography, providing a holistic comprehension of rocks' central role in the storage and release of hydrogen, thus contributing to the global endeavor to combat climate change and embrace sustainable energy sources.

title: The Perceived Role of Prosumer Energy in the Sustainable Energy Transition: Evidence from Rural Municipalities in Poland
summary: The energy transition requires not only the development of renewable energy sources but also the active participation of local communities in energy production and consumption processes. In this context, prosumer energy is increasingly reco
content: The energy transition requires not only the development of renewable energy sources but also the active participation of local communities in energy production and consumption processes. In this context, prosumer energy is increasingly recognised as a key component of the sustainable energy transition. Despite the growing body of research on prosumerism, relatively little attention has been devoted to how its significance is perceived by local authorities, particularly in rural areas. The aim of this article is to identify how representatives of rural municipalities in Poland perceive the role of prosumer energy in the sustainable energy transition. The study employed a survey-based research design involving representatives of 518 rural municipalities. The analysis encompassed five dimensions of the energy transition: (1) the achievement of environmental and climate objectives, (2) energy justice, (3) environmental responsibility, (4) value conflicts, and (5) local communities’ energy resilience. The findings indicate that prosumer energy is perceived as an important component of the sustainable energy transition in rural areas. Respondents attribute particular significance to its contribution to environmental protection, the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, the strengthening of energy security, and the enhancement of local communities’ resilience to energy crises. At the same time, the results reveal a clear asymmetry in perceptions of prosumer energy, with considerably greater importance attached to its environmental, energy-related and economic functions than to the social dimension of the energy transition. Respondents also recognise the risk of unequal access to the benefits of the energy transition, particularly for low-income households, older people, and residents of multi-family buildings. The article contributes to the literature on the energy transition by providing insights into the perspectives of representatives of rural municipalities and demonstrating that the social dimension of prosumer energy remains less prominent than its contribution to environmental objectives and energy security.

title: System design and engineering guidelines
summary: This chapter investigates advanced inverter architectures for hybrid renewable energy systems, highlighting the limitations of conventional topologies and explaining the emergence of three-level T-type boost inverters. Beginning with classi
content: This chapter investigates advanced inverter architectures for hybrid renewable energy systems, highlighting the limitations of conventional topologies and explaining the emergence of three-level T-type boost inverters. Beginning with classical configurations such as neutral-point-clamped (NPC) and flying-capacitor inverters, the chapter then introduces Z-source and quasi-Z-source topologies and analyses their advantages and drawbacks in grid-connected PV applications. Particular emphasis is placed on switching-based boost techniques capable of achieving high voltage gain, low current ripple and fault-tolerant operation - key requirements for the deployment of distributed PV systems, battery energy storage systems (BESS) and modern microgrids.

title: Internal Model Control-Based Time-Delay Compensation for Small-Signal Stability Improvement in Inverter-Fed Islanded Microgrids
summary: Inverter technology has emerged as a key enabler for renewable energy integration and power delivery in modern microgrids (MGs). Digital time delays associated with measurement, computation, and pulse-width modulation can significantly affe
content: Inverter technology has emerged as a key enabler for renewable energy integration and power delivery in modern microgrids (MGs). Digital time delays associated with measurement, computation, and pulse-width modulation can significantly affect the dynamic performance and stability of islanded inverter-fed microgrids. This paper presents an internal model control (IMC)-based current controller with explicit digital time-delay compensation to improve stability and dynamic performance by addressing delay-induced oscillatory interactions among different control layers. A comprehensive small-signal model is developed by incorporating power, voltage, and current control loops, digital time delay, LC filter, network, and load dynamics. The third-order Padé model of the delay is verified against the exact delay, and system stability is evaluated through eigenvalues, damping ratios and participation factors. At the nominal delay of 15 μs (1.5Ts, Ts=10μs), the current-loop modes of the IMC without compensation are almost undamped (ζ≈0.002) and become unstable beyond 15.25 μs, whereas the proposed controller damps the same modes with ζ=0.29 and remains stable up to 24.75 μs. The proposed design is also compared with a Smith predictor, its robustness to filter, line and load variations is assessed, and particle swarm optimization (PSO) with an explicit stability constraint raises the minimum damping ratio to 0.62. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified through comparison with a conventional IMC controller without delay compensation using the OPAL-RT OP4510 real-time simulator, where it reduces the frequency overshoot after load changes from about 30% to below 4% of the steady-state deviation.

title: Plasma-Enabled CO2 Utilization and Valorization: From Fundamentals to Polymer-Based Materials and Industrial Applications
summary: Converting CO2 into chemicals and materials with renewable electricity is a central goal of carbon utilization. Non-thermal plasma is a promising route: energetic electrons activate CO2 while the gas stays much cooler than in thermal proces
content: Converting CO2 into chemicals and materials with renewable electricity is a central goal of carbon utilization. Non-thermal plasma is a promising route: energetic electrons activate CO2 while the gas stays much cooler than in thermal processes, and the discharge can follow intermittent power. This review takes a polymer-science perspective, in which polymers play three roles. As membranes, sorbents and functional surfaces, they capture and separate CO2; in plasma catalysis, they act as packings, supports and precursors; and they are products of CO2 valorization, from CO2-derived polycarbonates to surfaces functionalized by CO2-containing plasmas. We outline CO2 plasma chemistry, compare dielectric barrier, microwave, gliding-arc and plasma-jet sources, and show how power, waveform, discharge mode, gas composition, humidity and exposure time control polymer surface chemistry, morphology and aging. A parameter–structure–property–performance framework links these effects to CO2 uptake and separation. We then appraise the consistency of the evidence, separate validated results from conceptual proposals and assess industrial prospects, including energy demand and scale-up. The main challenges are energy efficiency, polymer stability under plasma, syngas composition and inconsistent reporting. We close with a reporting checklist, a maturity assessment of the three roles and directions for future research.

title: A real-time explainable machine learning framework for wide-area fault detection and localization using optimally placed synchrophasor measurements
summary: Abstract Modern transmission networks face increasing protection challenges due to renewable energy integration, bidirectional power flows, high-impedance faults (HIFs), and potential failures of local protection devices, motivating the dev
content: Abstract Modern transmission networks face increasing protection challenges due to renewable energy integration, bidirectional power flows, high-impedance faults (HIFs), and potential failures of local protection devices, motivating the development of intelligent wide-area protection schemes. This paper presents a distributed real-time framework for wide-area fault detection and localization using synchrophasor measurements. Optimal Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) placement is achieved using Binary Integer Linear Programming (BILP) to ensure complete network observability with the minimum number of PMUs. A Virtual PMU implemented in the OPAL-RT HYPERSIM real-time simulator streams synchrophasor measurements via the IEEE C37.118 protocol over User Datagram Protocol (UDP) to a separate computer, where a multilayer Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) perform real-time inference for fault detection and faulted-line identification. The framework is evaluated on the IEEE 9-bus system under symmetrical, asymmetrical, and high-impedance fault conditions (up to 90 Ω in testing, 80 Ω in training). The ANN reaches 98.68 % ± 0.10 % test accuracy (mean ± SD, 5 training runs) with zero false positives; the SVM reaches 98.37 % ± 0.06 %. The estimated average inception-to-decision latency is ≈9.4 ms (8.33 ms average PMU frame-waiting time, ∼0.5 ms estimated communication/IEEE C37.118 processing, ∼0.5 ms estimated feature extraction, and 0.083 ms measured Artificial Neural Network (ANN) inference), with a worst-case PMU frame-waiting time of 16.67 ms at 60 frames/s well within the 50–150 ms fault duration range in the dataset. The trained models are not inherently topology-adaptive; however, topology-aware retraining on additional samples recovers both models to at least 98.7 % accuracy across all evaluated topology-change scenarios. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identifies current magnitude features at THE three PMU buses as the dominant fault-discriminating features, consistent with (though not an independent statistical proof of) the BILP placement strategy. These results demonstrate that combining optimized PMU placement, real-time synchrophasor communication, and explainable machine learning enables fast, accurate, and transparent wide-area protection suitable for next-generation transmission systems.

title: Neural Grids: Artificial Intelligence in Power and Energy Systems
summary: Master the future of energy by learning how to apply cutting-edge AI to solve the real-world complexity, intermittency, and security challenges of modern power grids and renewable systems. The convergence of artificial intelligence and powe
content: Master the future of energy by learning how to apply cutting-edge AI to solve the real-world complexity, intermittency, and security challenges of modern power grids and renewable systems. The convergence of artificial intelligence and power engineering represents one of the most significant developments in the modern energy landscape. Over the past two decades, the rapid expansion of renewable generation, electrification of transportation, distributed energy resources, and digitalization of power grids has fundamentally reshaped how electricity is produced, transmitted, and consumed. These advancements, while enabling sustainability and decarbonization, have introduced heightened levels of uncertainty, intermittency, and operational complexity. Traditional tools based on deterministic models, linear optimization, or rule-based control are increasingly insufficient for managing the nonlinear dynamics and real-time decision-making required in today’s energy systems. This book is an in-depth exploration of how modern artificial intelligence techniques can be systematically applied to the modeling, control, optimization, and forecasting challenges faced by power and energy networks. It covers a wide spectrum of AI methods, including machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary computation, and hybrid intelligent systems, focusing on their tailored applications in load forecasting, stability assessment, energy trading, fault detection, demand response, and grid security. Special emphasis is placed on smart grids, renewable energy integration, microgrids, and electric vehicle ecosystems, where conventional analytical methods often fall short due to the complexity and uncertainty of system dynamics. Balancing conceptual clarity with hands-on implementation, each chapter introduces the underlying AI methodology in a simplified and intuitive way, followed by detailed case studies, mathematical models, and simulation-based demonstrations. The integration of real-world datasets and benchmark problems ensures that readers can directly connect theoretical concepts with applied solutions in contemporary power and energy systems. By combining algorithmic insights with domain-specific energy applications, the book equips readers with the knowledge and skills necessary to design intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable energy systems for the future.
