title: Method for using spectral flow data to predict vortex-induced vibration onset of static structures
summary: Spectral representations of vortex-shedding behavior, such as airfoil data derived from computational fluid dynamics or experiment, can support the efficient identification of potential vortex-induced vibration onset. However, the use of su
content: Spectral representations of vortex-shedding behavior, such as airfoil data derived from computational fluid dynamics or experiment, can support the efficient identification of potential vortex-induced vibration onset. However, the use of such data is hindered by the myriad practical considerations required to scale, filter, and rank the risk of overlap between natural frequencies and shedding frequencies. This problem spans across Reynolds number, local angle of attack, and local skew angle, in addition to frequency harmonics, interpolation, and multi-body multi-element structures. The combinatorial scale of the problem additionally necessitates efficient numerical methods. This paper presents a reproducible, open-source framework with accompanying source code and a graphical user interface. With the improvements here, these problems can be addressed to enable the straightforward use of existing spectral datasets for arbitrary beam-type structures. We describe the methods, present a simple verification case, and exercise the method on a sample structure using a spectral airfoil dataset. The framework enables designers to readily navigate the complex space to identify, avoid, and include (via one-way coupling) the onset of vortex-induced vibration in their design workflows. Code, example datasets, and reproduction assets are openly released.

title: Cross-modal evidence conflict fusion for smart grid intrusion detection
summary: Smart-grid intrusion detection faces three coupled challenges: generalization to unseen events, unequal evidence quality across modalities, and false alarms caused by sensor perturbations. Random sample-level splitting can produce optimisti
content: Smart-grid intrusion detection faces three coupled challenges: generalization to unseen events, unequal evidence quality across modalities, and false alarms caused by sensor perturbations. Random sample-level splitting can produce optimistic estimates when neighboring samples from the same event occur in both the training and test sets. This paper presents the Cross-Modal Evidence Conflict Fusion model (CMECF), which combines modal credibility, pairwise evidence conflict, conflict-conditioned message passing, and encoder-level physics-consistency constraints over four synchronized evidence streams: PMU measurements, control-panel logs, protective-relay logs, and Snort alerts. On the MSU/ORNL binary dataset, Random Forest recorded macro-F1 of 0.896 under a random split and 0.564 under an event-level split. In the seed-42 event-level evaluation, CMECF recorded macro-F1 of 0.595, weighted-F1 of 0.623, and $$\textrm{FPR}_{\textrm{A}}$$ of 0.604; the corresponding Random Forest macro-F1 and $$\textrm{FPR}_{\textrm{A}}$$ were 0.564 and 0.722. Under the PMU Gaussian perturbation at $$\sigma =0.3$$ , macro-F1 was 0.523 for CMECF and 0.378 for Random Forest. CMECF has approximately $$105\,\textrm{K}$$ parameters and a model-forward latency of 1.5 ms per sample on the stated hardware. All comparative results come from a single seed-42 run and are reported descriptively. Within this evidence, CMECF records the highest observed macro-F1 and weighted-F1, the lowest measured false-positive rate, stronger performance retention under the evaluated PMU perturbation, and a compact millisecond-scale four-modality inference profile.

title: A two-stage MPPT controller with energy-regret coordination and transition memory for PV systems under complex partial shading conditions
summary: Partial shading creates multiple photovoltaic power peaks and makes online maximum power point tracking (MPPT) costly in harvested energy. ER-ISSA-IVY combines improved sparrow search (ISSA) with contracting Ivy (IVY) refinement. A best-so-
content: Partial shading creates multiple photovoltaic power peaks and makes online maximum power point tracking (MPPT) costly in harvested energy. ER-ISSA-IVY combines improved sparrow search (ISSA) with contracting Ivy (IVY) refinement. A best-so-far-referenced rule balances estimated exploration gains against measured probing costs; transition memory reuses measured peaks while retaining globally initialized alternatives. Simulations in Python with NumPy use a five-module engineering PV model and a time-domain PWM boost converter. For ER-ISSA-IVY, baseline static and step-irradiance efficiencies are \(100\%\) and \(94.35\%\) , respectively. The controller achieves \(99.99\%\) efficiency in the historical satellite-profile summary and \(99.911\%\) mean daily efficiency in a separate continuous 14-hour simulation. Its switching-level overshoot and ripple are \(0.77\%\) and \(0.07\%\) , respectively. ER-ISSA-IVY has the lowest mean number of first-hit evaluations in static scenarios S1–S3. ER-ISSA-IVY ranks highest or joint-highest in eleven of twelve combinations of array size and profile for ten- and twenty-module arrays. Memory improves whole-profile mean efficiency in all three mismatch tests. Comparisons with six hybrid algorithms show that ER-ISSA-IVY achieves higher mean dynamic efficiency and faster re-tracking under the tested protocols.

title: Dynamic Trust Network Analysis For Social Network-Based Consensus Decision-Making
source: International Journal of Information Technology & Decision Making
summary: This study addresses two critical challenges in social network-based consensus decision-making (SNCDM): dynamic trust network analysis and consensus development design. A novel dynamic trust network analysis method is proposed to integrate
content: This study addresses two critical challenges in social network-based consensus decision-making (SNCDM): dynamic trust network analysis and consensus development design. A novel dynamic trust network analysis method is proposed to integrate direct and indirect trust relationships by adjusting direct trust levels based on opinion similarities through trust compensation mechanisms and estimating indirect trust levels via position-weighted trust propagation and path aggregation. A spectral clustering method is developed to partition decision makers into manageable subgroups for enhancing consensus development. This leads to the proposition of a SNCDM framework, which effectively addresses trust decay, mitigates over-trust effect, and preserves trust information integrity. A case study on prioritizing barriers to the renewable energy transition in China is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SNCDM framework. A comparative analysis shows that the proposed framework performs better in trust information preservation and consensus acceleration than comparable approaches. Overall, this study offers a practical solution for SNCDM in which trust relationships embedded in social networks play a central role in consensus development.

title: Ensuring bedload transport to preserve trout spawning habitats and increase hydropower sustainability
summary: Hydropower operations in Alpine rivers modify the natural flow and sediment regimes, affecting aquatic habitat conditions. Bedload sediment transport is essential for renewing habitats that support trout reproduction in Alpine rivers. This
content: Hydropower operations in Alpine rivers modify the natural flow and sediment regimes, affecting aquatic habitat conditions. Bedload sediment transport is essential for renewing habitats that support trout reproduction in Alpine rivers. This study examined three streams in north-western Italy regulated by run-of-river (RoR) plants. We assessed active bedload conditions for grains with diameters ≤ 10 cm, corresponding to the substrate sizes typically used by trout for spawning. The conditions were estimated through the dimensionless critical shear stress approach proposed by Shields and a unit stream power criterion based on Bagnold’s framework, and subsequently evaluated in the field through sediment tracing using painted and unpainted clasts. Annual threshold exceedance was assessed over 14 years to determine the frequency of bedload transport. Sediment tracing proved effective in detecting active bedload conditions in all studied streams and demonstrated a clear relationship between discharge magnitude and the size of transported sediments. The thresholds were exceeded every year under both natural and altered regimes, although exceedance duration was reduced under altered conditions. The results indicate that sediment tracing can be used to assess the impact of hydropower regulation on the mobilization of bed materials and evaluate the occurrence of bedload transport relevant to fish spawning habitats.

title: Technological sustainability, entrepreneurial orientation, and firm performance: a reconfiguration perspective from the United Arab Emirates
summary: Purpose This study examines whether technological sustainability carries a positive indirect association between entrepreneurial orientation and firm performance and whether sustainability challenges weaken that association. Design/methodol
content: Purpose This study examines whether technological sustainability carries a positive indirect association between entrepreneurial orientation and firm performance and whether sustainability challenges weaken that association. Design/methodology/approach Cross-sectional survey responses from 545 informed organizational respondents in the United Arab Emirates were analyzed through Mode A composite modeling with 10,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. The respondent, not a verified unique firm, is the unit of observation. Hierarchical, robust, quantile, predictive, and sensitivity analyses assessed the stability of the associations. Findings Entrepreneurial orientation was positively associated with technological sustainability, which was positively associated with performance and formed a significant positive indirect association. H4 was not supported in the prespecified mean model. Negative interaction estimates at the lower and median performance quantiles and under Huber estimation remain exploratory follow-up evidence because no formal cross-quantile equality test is available. Research limitations/implications Cross-sectional common-source measurement, uncertain firm independence, incomplete archived instrument-development records, weak covariance fit, a significant reverse indirect model, and the absence of direct environmental outcomes restrict causal, measurement, firm-level, and environmental inference. Practical implications Managers can audit the sustainability-oriented technology portfolio by mapping current digital, circular, renewable-energy, data, analytics, and smart-system investments, identifying integration gaps, and tracking organizational performance separately from environmental outcomes. Originality/value The study positions technological sustainability as a sustainability-oriented technology portfolio interpreted through a reconfiguration lens. The data establish associations among entrepreneurial posture, the portfolio, and perceived organizational performance, not direct evidence of reconfiguration episodes or environmental improvement.

title: Next-generation high performance MXene–MgF2 based wideband solar absorber with artificial intelligent optimization for renewable energy mining applications
summary: Solar energy provides a promising and easily accessible renewable energy source when it comes to solving energy issues. Industries consume high amounts of energy for various uses. Thus, the concept of a solar absorber that absorbs wideband
content: Solar energy provides a promising and easily accessible renewable energy source when it comes to solving energy issues. Industries consume high amounts of energy for various uses. Thus, the concept of a solar absorber that absorbs wideband radiation is shown in this study. The absorber's configuration is MXene-Magnesium Fluoride-MXene. These structures create a novel geometry that traps the heat and absorbs a high amount of radiation. The proposed absorber's resonator layer geometry has a T-shape with a Nanodisk MXene-based resonator Solar Absorber, whose structure makes it polarization-insensitive. An average of 95.57% absorption was achieved within the range of 200-3000 nm, keeping absorptance above 96% over a bandwidth nm while exceeding 92% over a much wider bandwidth of around 2120 nm across the spectral spectrum under investigation. Moreover, this suggested absorber achieved 94.9% average absorption under AM 1.5. Examined several solar absorber structures and the findings. Optimized the design over several parameters and examined the outcome. Then, analyzed the Transverse Electric and magnetic fields with magnetic and electric colour-changing fields, which are described in the results section. The research presents clear engineering outcomes for solar thermal absorber design, with machine learning methods demonstrating the application of artificial intelligence in the study. The examination shows that the Machine Learning model's maximum achievable R 2 value of 0.93 for parameter change intends to minimize the simulation period by a quarter when compared with older methods, while minimizing other simulation needs. The high absorption rate with a unique resonator design is promising for applications as a renewable solar dryer for mining.

title: Designing for creative expression in sustainability education: A practice-based framework for active digital learning environments
summary: Sustainability education often begins from a shared problem, but students do not arrive at it through shared assumptions, experiences, disciplines, or professional ambitions. This concise paper presents Sustainability & Creativity, an inter
content: Sustainability education often begins from a shared problem, but students do not arrive at it through shared assumptions, experiences, disciplines, or professional ambitions. This concise paper presents Sustainability & Creativity, an interdisciplinary elective at a transnational university in Vietnam, as a case study in designing digital learning environments where creative expression functions as both subject and method: a mode of encountering sustainability rather than simply a topic within it. The course uses media-rich Canvas modules, low-stakes group discussion, formative knowledge checks, and client-informed assessment to scaffold creative engagement. Synthesising established learning design theories and sustainability competencies, the paper articulates a four-stage practice-based framework for operationalising Canvas as a creative learning environment. Evidence from learning analytics and course evaluation data across six deliveries suggests design supported preparation, participation and applied sustainability learning. The paper contributes a practice-based model for designing digital learning environments where creative expression functions as an essential mode of sustainability learning rather than a peripheral addition. In doing so, it offers scalable strategies for higher education practitioners seeking to activate learning management systems as collaborative, creative spaces.

title: Event-triggered distributed STW-RBFNN control of PV-battery DC microgrids under uncertainty and delays
summary: Voltage regulation in PV-battery DC microgrids is challenging because of nonlinear converter dynamics, uncertain operating conditions, changes in PV generation and load demand, and communication delays. This paper presents a distributed smo
content: Voltage regulation in PV-battery DC microgrids is challenging because of nonlinear converter dynamics, uncertain operating conditions, changes in PV generation and load demand, and communication delays. This paper presents a distributed smooth super-twisting radial basis function neural network (STW-RBFNN) controller for DC-link voltage regulation. The RBFNN estimates uncertain nonlinear dynamics online, while the super-twisting term deals with estimation errors and bounded disturbances. Directed pinned coordination is used for voltage regulation, and a two-stage event-triggered scheme reduces communication between units. The controller is tested on a six-node PV-battery DC microgrid under nominal conditions, 40 stochastic Monte Carlo runs, and communication delays. Under nominal conditions, the RMSE is 0.0089 V, the MAE is 0.0074 V, and the settling time is 0.601 s. The controller requires 3228 network-wide transmissions, 91.03% fewer than 1 ms periodic communication. Across the Monte Carlo runs, the mean RMSE is 0.00704 V with a standard deviation of 0.00027 V. Tests with delays from 0.5 to 10 ms show small changes in voltage error and communication. The analysis establishes conditional practical boundedness for the reduced continuous-time model. Simulations evaluate the complete digital implementation with sampling, saturation, and delayed communication; no analytical delay margin is established.

title: Transition metal oxides for oxygen electrocatalysis: Electronic structure engineering, benchmarking strategies, and advanced OER catalysis
summary: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a critical kinetic bottleneck in renewable energy conversion technologies, including water electrolyzers, metal–air batteries, and regenerative fuel cells. Although noble-metal-based catalysts such as
content: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a critical kinetic bottleneck in renewable energy conversion technologies, including water electrolyzers, metal–air batteries, and regenerative fuel cells. Although noble-metal-based catalysts such as IrO 2 and RuO 2 exhibit outstanding OER activity, their scarcity, high cost, and limited long-term stability hinder large-scale deployment. Transition metal oxides (TMOs) have emerged as promising alternatives owing to their compositional versatility, tunable electronic structures, rich redox chemistry, and structural robustness. Nevertheless, the relationships among crystal chemistry, electronic configuration, active-site evolution, reaction mechanism, and catalytic performance remain incompletely understood. This review examines the fundamental chemistry and electronic principles that govern TMO electrocatalysts, with an emphasis on the mechanistic distinctions among the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), lattice‑oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM), and oxide path mechanism (OPM), as well as the mechanism-dependent applicability of electronic, structural, and defect descriptors. Advanced synthesis routes, in situ/operando characterization, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and machine learning (ML)-assisted discovery are discussed as complementary tools for identifying active phases and guiding rational catalyst design. A benchmarking framework is outlined that covers activity normalization, reference electrode calibration, iR correction, Faradaic efficiency, durability testing, and practically relevant current densities. Performance enhancement strategies, including defect engineering, heteroatom doping, strain engineering, crystal-phase and morphology control, conductivity enhancement, interface engineering, and surface reconstruction, are critically evaluated, along with their synergistic and antagonistic coupling. The electrolyte-dependent requirements for catalysts operating in acidic and alkaline media are then compared to highlight the activity–stability trade-off. Finally, catalyst-level advances are linked to alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs), anion-exchange-membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs), and proton-exchange-membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) in terms of electrode architecture, catalyst loading, membrane/ionomer interactions, transport limitations, and device-level performance criteria. This integrated perspective provides a framework for developing efficient and durable TMO electrocatalysts for the OER.

title: Physics-interpretable topological machine learning identifies domain-wall contributors to high-frequency loss in a nanocrystalline soft magnet
summary: Abstract High-frequency core loss constrains efficiency and power density, yet loss models do not identify which parts of an evolving domain-wall network carry the dominant reversal resistance. We present a physics-interpretable topological
content: Abstract High-frequency core loss constrains efficiency and power density, yet loss models do not identify which parts of an evolving domain-wall network carry the dominant reversal resistance. We present a physics-interpretable topological machine-learning workflow combining micromagnetic simulations, persistent homology, principal component analysis and inverse mapping for an idealized nanocrystalline soft-magnet model driven at nominal frequencies of 100 kHz–10 MHz using α = 1.0 and frequency-specific integration. Because reversal here is dominated by domain-wall motion, we treat the shape and energy of the wall network, captured by persistent homology, as the governing factor of loss. The first coordinate tracks magnetization, whereas the second captures frequency-associated domain subdivision and correlates with the exchange contribution to domain-wall energy. Their feature-space gradient reveals a reversal barrier near coercivity that increases with frequency. Inverse mapping localizes the largest contributions to propagating reversed-domain tips and selected fine wall segments rather than uniformly across the wall network. Consistent structure–energy–mechanism relationships connect the representation to magnetic physics. Within this protocol, reversal resistance is associated not simply with wall amount, but with a spatially selective subset of high-energy wall configurations. The workflow provides testable spatial descriptors for low-loss materials screening and optimization.

title: Yeşil Nanoteknoloji: Sürdürülebilir Kimya ve Nanobilimin Kesişim Noktası
summary: Nanomalzemelerin üretim ve kullanımındaki hızlı artış, bu malzemelerin sentez süreçlerinin çevresel etkilerinin sistematik olarak değerlendirilmesini zorunlu kılmaktadır. Yeşil nanoteknoloji, yeşil kimyanın ilkelerini nanomalzemelerin tasar
content: Nanomalzemelerin üretim ve kullanımındaki hızlı artış, bu malzemelerin sentez süreçlerinin çevresel etkilerinin sistematik olarak değerlendirilmesini zorunlu kılmaktadır. Yeşil nanoteknoloji, yeşil kimyanın ilkelerini nanomalzemelerin tasarımı, sentezi ve kullanımına uyarlayarak tehlikeli reaktiflerin, enerji tüketiminin ve atık oluşumunun azaltılmasını hedefleyen disiplinler arası bir yaklaşımdır. Bu bölümde önce sürdürülebilirlik ve yeşil kimya kavramları, Anastas ve Warner tarafından tanımlanan on iki ilke ve Winterton’ın proses ölçeğine yönelik tamamlayıcı ilkeleri ele alınmakta; bu ilkelerin nanopartikül sentezindeki karşılıkları tartışılmaktadır. Ardından nanopartiküllerin bileşim ve boyutsallığa göre sınıflandırılması, yukarıdan aşağıya ve aşağıdan yukarıya sentez yaklaşımları ile bitki özütleri, mikroorganizmalar ve atık biyokütle kullanılarak yürütülen biyolojik sentez yöntemleri özetlenmektedir. Biyomoleküllerin hem indirgen hem de kararlaştırıcı olarak işlev gördüğü bu yöntemlerde pH, sıcaklık, öncül derişimi ve özüt bileşiminin ürün özelliklerine etkisi vurgulanmakta, temel karakterizasyon teknikleri tanıtılmaktadır. Son olarak yeşil nanopartiküllerin biyomedikal, tarım, gıda, çevresel iyileştirme, sensör ve enerji uygulamaları değerlendirilmekte; biyolojik kaynaklardaki değişkenlikten doğan tekrarlanabilirlik sorunları, standardizasyon, toksikolojik güvenlik ve ölçek büyütme gereksinimleri tartışılmaktadır.

title: Problems Facing Consultant Engineers and Integrated Solutions for Improved Project Performance in the Nigerian Construction Industry: A Survey of Professionals in Ibadan
summary: Consultant engineers are central to the delivery of construction projects, yet project failures in Nigeria are frequently linked to deficiencies in design, supervision and professional conduct. Existing studies have largely examined these d
content: Consultant engineers are central to the delivery of construction projects, yet project failures in Nigeria are frequently linked to deficiencies in design, supervision and professional conduct. Existing studies have largely examined these deficiencies in isolation. This study assessed fifteen consultant-related problems in terms of frequency and severity, examined their perceived effect on project cost, time, quality and safety, and evaluated fifteen technological, managerial and regulatory solutions among professionals who work with consultant engineers in Ibadan, Nigeria. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted using a structured questionnaire (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.86 in the pilot study) administered to 60 professionals with at least five years of field experience, comprising consultant engineers (n = 22), contractor site engineers (n = 17), client project managers (n = 17) and other professionals (n = 4). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, the Relative Importance Index (RII), a one-sample t-test and Friedman tests. Respondents rated the problems as low in frequency (overall mean = 2.22 out of 5) but high in severity (overall mean = 4.08). Inadequate geotechnical investigation was the most frequently reported problem (mean = 2.42), whereas lack of specialised building services expertise was the most severe (mean = 4.23). Respondents agreed strongly that these problems affect project performance (mean agreement = 4.27), and all fifteen solutions were strongly endorsed; however, the ranking items did not produce a valid priority order, and no significant differences were found within solution groups (Friedman test, p > 0.05). The findings indicate that consultant-related problems, although perceived as infrequent, carry serious consequences for project performance, and that technological, managerial and regulatory measures are supported as complementary remedies. The conclusions are limited by a small purposive sample drawn from one city and by the reliance on perception-based data.

title: Wave-to-water energy balance of an S-shaped buoy and ball-screw power take-off driving small-scale batch reverse osmosis
summary: Abstract Small wave energy converters can supply fresh water off the grid only if every link between the sea and the membrane is accounted for. This study couples a time-domain model of the S-shaped buoy SB-1.5 and its ball-screw power take
content: Abstract Small wave energy converters can supply fresh water off the grid only if every link between the sea and the membrane is accounted for. This study couples a time-domain model of the S-shaped buoy SB-1.5 and its ball-screw power take-off (PTO), both experimentally verified in earlier work, with a batch seawater reverse osmosis (RO) model based on solution–diffusion transport, film-theory concentration polarisation, and Pitzer osmotic pressure. The PTO law is anchored to the published bench power and to a mean-to-peak ratio of 0.26 measured from the oscilloscope records, and the buoy follows the Cummins equation calibrated to the published 22 W full-scale absorbed power. In the ShiDao wave climate (2.0 kW/m), the unit absorbs 54.0 W (capture width ratio 1.83%), delivers 19.2 W of electricity and passes 7.3 W of hydraulic power to a 0.6 m² membrane element. With a batch cycle at 30% recovery, this gives about 142 L/day (51.7 m³/yr) at 0.83 g/L, whereas a fixed-pressure once-through module on the same chain gives 10.5 L/day. The hydraulic energy of 1.23 kWh/m³ is about 1.4 times the least work of separation, and the motor–pump set, at 48% stage efficiency, is the weakest link. Monte Carlo and Sobol analyses bound the output at 115–171 L/day (5–95%), with motor–pump efficiency alone explaining 58% of the variance. The simulation is calibrated to published bench tests and full-scale values, and sea trials are the next step. An unconstrained linear damper would absorb 2.6 times more power than the rating-limited PTO, and a 100 W generator raises the annual permeate from 51.7 to 79.6 m³. One unit provides 15 L/day per person for about nine people (volume only, before post-treatment), and eleven units cover a village of one hundred.

title: Empirical evidence on the environmental impacts of pumped-storage hydropower projects and implications for early-stage planning: a systematic review protocol for environmental impact assessment documents.
summary: Abstract Pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) is increasingly important for renewable energy integration, but its development can result in significant environmental impacts requiring careful assessment. Comprehensive understanding of the enviro
content: Abstract Pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) is increasingly important for renewable energy integration, but its development can result in significant environmental impacts requiring careful assessment. Comprehensive understanding of the environmental impacts associated with PSH development is currently lacking in the scientific literature. Environmental impact assessments (EIAs) are mandated for many PSH projects and provide valuable project-level data across different environmental goods. However, available EIA reports have not yet been systematically synthesised. Hence, this protocol describes a systematic review to synthesise empirical evidence on environmental impacts of PSH projects from EIA reports, summaries, and authorisation decisions. A structured search will be conducted across major national and international repositories in English and German language that archive EIA and planning documents, supplemented by targeted Google searches. Documents will be screened for inclusion in the analysis in two steps: first for project and document type, then for comprehensiveness, technological detail, and environmental scope. Eligible documents will undergo structured data extraction. Project details will be coded deductively. Environmental impacts will be coded inductively. Analysis will combine narrative synthesis and descriptive statistics, such as vote counting and cross-tabulations, to identify recurring environmental impacts and assess their relevance against early-stage planning criteria. Ultimately, this review aims to provide a transparent and replicable synthesis of EIA evidence to bridge the gap between project-specific environmental knowledge and consideration of PSH in early planning stages to anticipate and mitigate impacts more effectively.

title: The Use of Genetic Algorithms in Urban-Scale Building Placement Optimization: The Case of Selçuklu District, Konya
summary: Building placement optimization in urban areas is a multidimensional and interdisciplinary process requiring the integrated evaluation of sustainability, energy efficiency, environmental performance, and zoning constraints. Due to the limit
content: Building placement optimization in urban areas is a multidimensional and interdisciplinary process requiring the integrated evaluation of sustainability, energy efficiency, environmental performance, and zoning constraints. Due to the limitations of conventional methods in addressing these complex and interrelated variables through a holistic and performance-based approach, computational design approaches—particularly genetic algorithms (GA)—have become effective and increasingly preferred decision-support tools. This study applies GA-based Building placement optimization to a selected sample parcel in the Selçuklu district of Konya. A three-dimensional model was developed in the Rhinoceros–Grasshopper environment, where detailed climate analyses were conducted using the Ladybug plugin, and alternative optimization scenarios were evaluated through the Galapagos plugin. The results indicate that the optimal solution is an angled placement at the parcel corner, improving solar gain while reducing shading effects caused by surrounding tall buildings. However, discrepancies between the optimized solution and existing zoning regulations highlight conflicts between computational outputs and planning constraints, emphasizing the need for integrative approaches.

title: Nonlinear Coupled Time-Domain Modeling of Hull Geometry Effects for Improved Dynamic Response of Floating Wind Platforms
summary: Abstract This study presents a fully coupled time-domain simulation framework—integrating aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, control, and structural dynamics—for the evaluation and parametric design of floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) semisubm
content: Abstract This study presents a fully coupled time-domain simulation framework—integrating aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, control, and structural dynamics—for the evaluation and parametric design of floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) semisubmersible platforms. Unlike conventional linear formulations or decoupled methodologies that systematically overlook second-order hydrodynamic drift and transient dynamics, the proposed approach incorporates nonlinear wave kinematics, viscous dissipation, and time-domain aerodynamic force interactions within a unified numerical solver. A genetic algorithm is employed as a systematic design space exploration tool across a multi-parameter geometric modification space—comprising column dimensions and heave plates—operating independently of the governing equations of motion. Evaluating candidate configurations under realistic irregular sea states reveals that geometric modification directly governs platform motion sensitivities. Specifically, refined configurations successfully shift the heave natural frequency below the primary wave energy spectrum to avoid high-energy first-order wave excitation bands, while pitch dynamics are effectively stabilized through platform-induced vortex shedding and rotor aerodynamic damping. Validation against established reference data confirms that the framework achieves substantial suppression of transient standard deviations in aerodynamic thrust and drivetrain torque, thereby enhancing power quality and alleviating fatigue loading without requiring overly complex active control mechanisms. Overall, the proposed methodology offers a viable and reliable analytical foundation to support the conceptual design and preliminary assessment of next-generation floating wind turbines under complex metocean conditions.

title: Durability Assessment of Precast Accropodes and Feasibility of Their Use as a Viable Alternative to Natural Resources in Coastal Engineering Applications: A Case Study
summary: Abstract The traditional approach to breakwater construction has long depended on the availability of locally quarried rock masses. However, due to the continued depletion of suitable geological resources and growing environmental restricti
content: Abstract The traditional approach to breakwater construction has long depended on the availability of locally quarried rock masses. However, due to the continued depletion of suitable geological resources and growing environmental restrictions, several coastal regions are now facing material shortages. In response, the use of precast concrete armor units, particularly accropodes has emerged as a viable alternative for coastal protection infrastructure. This study investigates the feasibility and long-term performance of using precast concrete accropodes in breakwater applications through a targeted case study. A series of concrete mix-designs were developed, considering both mechanical performance and exposure to aggressive marine environments. The study includes comprehensive quality control testing during production, including compressive strength tests at 7 and 28 days. Emphasis is placed on the durability of the concrete against carbonation, a key degradation mechanism in coastal environments that leads to the penetration of carbon dioxide and the onset of crack expansion. Experimental assessments were conducted to determine the carbonation depth of the different concrete compositions. The results inform optimal mix-design strategies to enhance service life and structural reliability. Findings are further discussed in the context of recent literature, in real-world coastal protection systems.

title: Cost Sensitivity-Assisted Net Load Forecast Correction for Day-Ahead Scheduling of Wind–Solar–Coal Systems with Molten Salt Storage
summary: Wind–solar–coal systems require flexible generation and storage operation to accommodate renewable variability while meeting regional demand and scheduled electricity exports. Coordinating coal-fired units with molten salt thermal energy st
content: Wind–solar–coal systems require flexible generation and storage operation to accommodate renewable variability while meeting regional demand and scheduled electricity exports. Coordinating coal-fired units with molten salt thermal energy storage can improve renewable integration and operating economy. However, day-ahead schedules depend on uncertain net load forecasts, and higher forecast accuracy does not necessarily yield lower operating costs. This paper proposes a cost sensitivity-assisted forecast correction framework to improve the economic value of net load predictions. Analysis of the scheduling model links forecast errors to asymmetric balancing costs, equipment state changes, and inter-temporal storage constraints. Starting from a temporal convolutional network forecast, the framework learns cost responses to signed forecast perturbations evaluated through the complete scheduling model. These responses supervise action value differences in the critics of a soft actor–critic agent, guiding joint correction of hourly forecasts to minimize realized daily cost. Tests on the Reliability Test System–Grid Modernization Laboratory Consortium benchmark show a 7.47% reduction in mean realized cost relative to the uncorrected temporal forecast, despite higher forecast error. With identical cost sensitivity inputs, auxiliary critic supervision reduces mean cost by 2.01% compared with ordinary critic training.

title: Estimating Venous Clinical Severity Score with the Aid of Support Vector Classification Approach
summary: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) affecting the lower limbs is a condition that significantly impacts quality of life and needs holistic management for its treatment. This condition affects those standing or sitting for prolonged periods,
content: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) affecting the lower limbs is a condition that significantly impacts quality of life and needs holistic management for its treatment. This condition affects those standing or sitting for prolonged periods, especially habitual sitters, and is worsened by obesity and high cholesterol.To predict the participants with Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS), machine learning (ML) techniques were used: Support Vector Classification (SVC). With the implementation of SVC, the prediction of VCSS-related outcomes was demonstrated, which shows the use of advanced analytical aspects in the estimation of VCSS. Additionally, to aid in maximizing the performance of the models, two optimization methods, namely SHO and ESMA, were used during refinement. This improvement illustrates that using more than one optimization technique in combination with SVC base is effective. The numbers are 0.829, 0.832 and 0.833, which show a definite beneficial effect on predicting accuracy. Such enhancement is critical in optimizing the reliability and accuracy of prediction, especially in cases of difficult conditions or the unavailability of target variables. This optimization process, where ESMA and SHO optimizers are used, illustrates the resilience and versatility of the model in different circumstances, resulting in a more accurate prediction system.

title: The Inner Life of Nature-Adapted Buildings: Integrating Form and Function Through Strategic Design
summary: Living organisms have evolved complex strategies to adapt and thrive in their environments, constantly balancing form and function to ensure survival, resilience, and efficiency.This evolutionary model offers a profound lesson for architect
content: Living organisms have evolved complex strategies to adapt and thrive in their environments, constantly balancing form and function to ensure survival, resilience, and efficiency.This evolutionary model offers a profound lesson for architecture, highlighting the potential of strategic design to create buildings and spaces that are not only functional but also regenerative, responsive, and comfortable for their inhabitants.This paper explores how architecture can draw inspiration from the adaptability and functionality of living organisms to integrate nature's principles into the built environment, with a particular focus on the processes of regenerative, bioclimatic, and biophilic design.

title: Climate-smart aquaponics model: source code, input data and outputs
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Accelerating climate change, population growth, and resource depletion severely threaten global food security, especially in vulnerable arid regions. These threats necessitate the development of sustainable agriculture like aquaponics, in w
content: Accelerating climate change, population growth, and resource depletion severely threaten global food security, especially in vulnerable arid regions. These threats necessitate the development of sustainable agriculture like aquaponics, in which fish and plants coexist, benefiting each other and forming a self-sustaining food system that enhances water, energy, and nutrient efficiency. This study developed and tested an integrated dynamic model to evaluate facility-scale water-energy-food interactions in aquaponics integrating anaerobic digestion, distillation desalination and climate control in desert environments. The model was compared with observations from pilot systems across three arid regions: Negev (Israel), Sonoran (USA), and Taklamakan (China) deserts. Out-of-sample errors were 10-28% for energy and water fluxes, whereas dissolved nutrient concentrations were not predicted reliably (negative Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency). The reference configuration (167 m2 hydroponics and a 0.1 m3/d distillation rate per 1 m3 aquaculture), selected from one-at-a-time response analyses and not a demonstrated global optimum, achieved 95% water use efficiency with an energy consumption of 0.27 kWh/day/m2. Integrating evaporative cooling, dynamic shading, and mechanical cooling energy-saving strategies into a climate-smart model reduced electricity use about fourfold and total energy use 2.4-fold relative to the pilot reference system. Grid independence was storage dependent, and off-grid operation potential was assessed as feasible through anaerobic digestion supplying about 1.95 MWh/day of methane bioenergy and solar systems contributing up to 9 MWh/day with adequate electrical and thermal storage. A screening cost assessment showed that the renewable supply and storage did not pay back at 2024 prices, with PV and battery electricity costing about 1.24 $/kWh, so economic feasibility was not established. The adaptability of systems to extreme weather and global warming ensures resilient and sustainable food production amid climate variability. These findings inform the design of energy-saving aquaponics with storage-dependent grid independence for sustainable food production under present and future climates.

title: Single‐Phase Inverter With Sensorless Observer Control and Multi‐Order Harmonic Compensation
source: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications
summary: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a sensorless control strategy for a single‐phase inverter based on a discrete‐time state observer. The proposed observer accurately reconstructs the AC‐side capacitor current, enabling capacitor current feedback
content: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a sensorless control strategy for a single‐phase inverter based on a discrete‐time state observer. The proposed observer accurately reconstructs the AC‐side capacitor current, enabling capacitor current feedback without the need for a physical current sensor. To enhance power quality, a proportional–resonant (PR) controller with multiharmonic compensation is employed to suppress dominant low‐order harmonics and reduce total harmonic distortion (THD). Additionally, a one‐step‐ahead prediction scheme is adopted to mitigate digital control delays and enhance system stability. The proposed method is validated on a 2‐kW hardware prototype. Experimental results show that the output voltage THD is reduced from 11.82% to 5.18% under nonlinear load conditions, demonstrating significant improvement in output waveform quality and confirming the effectiveness of the approach.

title: From Correlation to Prediction: Electroluminescence-based Indicators and Composite Health Scoring for Photovoltaic Power Loss Prediction in a 204-Panel Fleet
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Electroluminescence (EL) imaging is an established non-destructive technique for detecting cell cracks, hot spots, and edge damage in crystalline-silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules, but most fleet-scale studies stop at correlation analysis w
content: Electroluminescence (EL) imaging is an established non-destructive technique for detecting cell cracks, hot spots, and edge damage in crystalline-silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules, but most fleet-scale studies stop at correlation analysis without testing out-of-sample predictive power.This study analyses a 204-panel, 63.24 kWp rooftop PV fleet and develops a composite Health Score combining Power Performance, Crack Severity, and Thermal Risk dimensions with an edge-damage penalty as an operational prioritisation tool.Pearson/Spearman association, 5-fold crossvalidated Random Forest and linear-regression models, and a five-scenario weight-perturbation analysis separate association from prediction and test the Score's ranking stability.Crack count showed the strongest association with power loss (r = 0.96) and the highest cross-validated predictive performance (R² = 0.92), while crack area and hot-spot area showed weak, sometimes inverse, associations (r = -0.12 and -0.18), diverging from single-cell crack-hotspot coupling.Because the Health Score's Power Performance component is defined directly from Power_Loss, its principal interpretation is as a composite condition and maintenance-prioritisation index rather than as an independent predictor of Power_Loss; it showed substantial rank stability under ±5 percentage-point weight perturbation (Spearman ρ ≥ 0.98, top-20-worst overlap ≥ 85%).These findings offer an empirically evaluated, fleet-scale framework for EL-informed operations-and-maintenance prioritisation in tropical PV installations.

title: Beyond Resource Dependence: Human Ecological Perspectives on Angola’s Sustainable Development Challenges
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Human ecological concerns in Africa have become increasingly urgent as nations struggle to balance economic growth with environmental sustainability. Angola, a leading oil-producing country, presents a critical case for examining the comple
content: Human ecological concerns in Africa have become increasingly urgent as nations struggle to balance economic growth with environmental sustainability. Angola, a leading oil-producing country, presents a critical case for examining the complex interplay between natural resource exploitation, ecological degradation, and human well-being. Despite significant oil revenues, widespread pollution, deforestation, and the disruption of traditional livelihoods have exposed deep vulnerabilities in the human environment system. This paper explores how continued oil exploration along Angola’s coastal and inland regions has reshaped ecological relationships, intensified socio-economic inequalities, and hindered the realisation of sustainable development objectives. Through a human-ecological lens, the study highlights how the degradation of water sources, loss of biodiversity, and displacement of communities challenge both environmental justice and national development agendas. In the post-SDG context, the paper argues for a transition from extractive-centred growth to an inclusive ecological model that prioritises local participation, environmental restoration, and adaptive governance. Such a shift is essential to reframe Angola’s development trajectory toward resilience, sustainability, and human dignity

title: Capitals, Capacities, and Agency in Off-Grid Renewable Energy Projects in the Peruvian Amazonia
summary: Off-grid renewable energy technologies (RETs) are often introduced in rural communities to expand electricity access and support development. However, electricity access alone does not ensure reliable service. This is especially relevant in
content: Off-grid renewable energy technologies (RETs) are often introduced in rural communities to expand electricity access and support development. However, electricity access alone does not ensure reliable service. This is especially relevant in riverine Indigenous territories of the Peruvian Amazonia, where electricity provision is shaped by seasonal dynamics, environmental change, unclear responsibilities, weak institutional follow-up, and changing relations with external actors. This thesis analyzes these dynamics in two Shipibo-Konibo communities in the Ucayali Region: Panaillo and Junín Pablo. It asks how community capacities and agency are shaped over time in relation to community-based off-grid RET projects. The thesis develops a capital–capacity–agency framework to examine community capacity as function-specific and context-dependent. It analyzes how assets associated with capital domains are configured and applied in relation to the capacity needs of specific functions involved in organizing electricity service. The research combines a systematic literature review with mixed-method fieldwork: household surveys, focus groups, interviews, participant observation, and document analysis. Panaillo is analyzed through a 2019–2024 temporal reconstruction focused on a solar boat project. Junín Pablo is examined through 2024 fieldwork centered on a proposed river turbine project. Community capacity is not a single aggregate attribute. It is function-specific and depends on different combinations of assets that do not automatically substitute for one another. Both communities had cultural, organizational, and territorial capacities before and beyond the projects. However, these capacities were not always connected to RET-related functions such as maintenance, financing, custodianship, technical operation, repair access, or institutional follow-up. In Panaillo, residents redirected the solar boat toward territorial surveillance, connecting it with governance routines, adaptive knowledge, and operator learning, while broader transport expectations declined. In Junín Pablo, where the river turbine was not implemented, agency appeared through caution, procedural demands, partner evaluation, and conditional engagement. The thesis argues that project fragility cannot be explained by a lack of community capacities. It emerges when socio-technical arrangements remain incomplete: when responsibilities, rules, maintenance, financing, repair pathways, and external support are not organized. How these projects unfold over time depends not only on technology provision, but on how functions are organized, how capacity needs are addressed through configured and applied assets, and how community actors interpret and respond to changing capacity configurations.

title: Evaluation of Impact of Energy Sharing on Bidirectional Low-Temperature District Energy Systems in Vancouver
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Fifth-generation district heating and cooling (5GDHC) systems have emerged as a promising approach for reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in Canadian communities. These systems operate using low-temperature bidirection
content: Fifth-generation district heating and cooling (5GDHC) systems have emerged as a promising approach for reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in Canadian communities. These systems operate using low-temperature bidirectional networks that enable simultaneous heating and cooling, direct thermal energy exchange between buildings, and the integration of renewable and waste heat resources. Their performance depends largely on the ability to balance thermal demands within the district and maximize energy sharing among connected buildings. However, there remains limited understanding of how building demand composition influences energy-sharing potential and system operation, including total energy consumption and central plant capacity requirements. This thesis first reviews existing approaches for modelling building thermal demands and evaluating energy-sharing potential in district energy systems, with a particular focus on fifth-generation district heating and cooling networks. Building on the identified research needs, representative hourly heating and cooling demand profiles for residential, commercial, office, and healthcare buildings were generated using eQUEST 3.65 based on assumptions derived from the U.S. Department of Energy prototype building models. These demand profiles were then used as inputs to a dynamic simulation model of a bidirectional low-temperature district energy system developed in OpenModelica. The integrated modelling framework was used to investigate the relationship between building demand composition, energy sharing, and system performance. The framework is intended as an exploratory sandbox model rather than a calibrated representation of a specific operating district energy system; therefore, its numerical results should be interpreted only to assess the ability of the developed modelling approach to capture variations in system performance across the investigated scenarios. To quantify energy-sharing potential, district demand overlap coefficient (DOC) is used to represent the theoretical opportunity for energy sharing based on building demand profiles, while a network DOC is used to evaluate the actual energy sharing achieved during system operation. To assess the robustness of the system-level comparisons, the model behaviour was compared with a published 5GDHC reference case and interpreted as a system-level benchmark rather than full validation of a specific district. A local sensitivity analysis was then conducted for five key demand, heat-pump, and operating parameters, together with a coupled analysis of the network temperature limits. These analyses were used to determine whether the main conclusions remained consistent under changes in modelling assumptions and numerical settings. The results show that building demand composition is a key factor influencing energy-sharing performance. title: Left in the dark: understanding energy access for communities near the Lake Turkana Wind Power project, Kenya
summary: Global South countries juggle the energy justice imperatives of implementing universal electrification while also moving towards renewable energy. This article revisits the case of Lake Turkana Wind Power project, in the remote north of Ken
content: Global South countries juggle the energy justice imperatives of implementing universal electrification while also moving towards renewable energy. This article revisits the case of Lake Turkana Wind Power project, in the remote north of Kenya; this has already received much attention for procedural injustices, but not for energy access injustices. Nearby residents have not yet benefited from electrification although the project improves supply to areas under the national grid. This article explores the issue through an energy justice lens. It examines the barriers to electrification identifying technical, economic, political and governance challenges, and considers how these might be overcome.

title: Eco-Centric Jurisprudence: The Rise of India's Green Fundamental Right through the Expansion of Article 21 of the Constitution to Ensure Climate Justice
source: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
summary: Environmental degradation and climate change have emerged as critical challenges to constitutional governance, human dignity and sustainable development. In India, the constitutional recognition of environmental protection has progressively
content: Environmental degradation and climate change have emerged as critical challenges to constitutional governance, human dignity and sustainable development. In India, the constitutional recognition of environmental protection has progressively evolved through judicial interpretation, particularly by expanding the scope of Article 21 of the Constitution to encompass the right to a clean and healthy environment. This paper examines the emergence of eco-centric jurisprudence in India and analyses the transformation of environmental protection from a legislative and policy-oriented concern into an enforceable dimension of fundamental rights. It explores the contribution of constitutional provisions, particularly Articles 14, 21, 48A and 51A(g), in establishing environmental protection as a shared responsibility of the State and citizens. It further examines the role of environmental legislation, judicial activism and Public Interest Litigation in strengthening environmental governance. Through an analysis of landmark judicial pronouncements, the paper traces the evolution of environmental jurisprudence and the incorporation of fundamental environmental principles, including sustainable development, the Public Trust Doctrine, the Precautionary Principle, the Polluter Pays Principle, Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Intergenerational Equity. Particular attention is devoted to the Supreme Court’s evolving approach towards climate justice, especially its recognition in M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India of the constitutional right to be free from the adverse effects of climate change under Articles 14 and 21. The paper argues that climate-related harm disproportionately affects economically disadvantaged and vulnerable communities, thereby raising concerns of substantive equality, human dignity and constitutional accountability. It also identifies institutional weaknesses in environmental enforcement and the limitations of existing regulatory mechanisms. Finally, it advocates comprehensive climate change legislation, stronger institutional accountability, effective environmental adjudication and enforceable ecological safeguards. The paper concludes that India’s transition towards eco-centric constitutionalism requires a rights-based and intergenerational approach that reconciles developmental priorities with ecological preservation and advances substantive climate justice for present and future generations.

title: Modelo de planificación, evaluación y monitoreo ambiental mediante diagnóstico causal estructurado desde indicadores territoriales para El Salvador
summary: The objective of this study was to develop a model for environmental planning, assessment and monitoring through a structured causal diagnosis based on territorial indicators for El Salvador, by applying the Driving Forces-Pressure-State-Im
content: The objective of this study was to develop a model for environmental planning, assessment and monitoring through a structured causal diagnosis based on territorial indicators for El Salvador, by applying the Driving Forces-Pressure-State-Impact-Response framework to the period 2000-2024. The methodology adopted a quantitative approach with a descriptive-correlational scope; the universe was the national environmental system, represented by 89 indicators obtained through documentary analysis of secondary databases (World Bank, FAOSTAT, WHO/UNICEF, CEPALSTAT and MARN) and recorded in a time-series matrix, validated by cross-checking against the original reports of each source and by criteria of causal relevance and practical feasibility. Data were processed in R through ordinary least squares linear regression, using the coefficient of determination as a measure of robustness, the t test as the significance criterion (p < .05) and the annual relative rate of change as a measure of intensity, which allowed the indicators to be classified in a quadrant matrix. Among the results, 19 of the 21 core indicators showed significant trends; driving forces and basic-service responses displayed the most robust changes, whereas the biophysical state showed gradual and persistent deterioration in forest cover and water availability, and safely managed sanitation declined from 45.7 % to 36.0 %. The study concludes that the model links the empirical indicator base, the causal analytical core and the management cycle, and makes it possible to prioritize wastewater treatment, ecosystem restoration and transport decarbonization as the main axes of national environmental policy.

title: Reported Effects of Coprecipitation Synthesis on ZnO/Activated Carbon Nanocomposite Characteristics: A Systematic Review
summary: ZnO/activated carbon (ZnO/AC) nanocomposites are promising functional materials due to the combination of ZnO semiconducting properties and the high surface area and porosity of activated carbon. This study aims to systematically examine th
content: ZnO/activated carbon (ZnO/AC) nanocomposites are promising functional materials due to the combination of ZnO semiconducting properties and the high surface area and porosity of activated carbon. This study aims to systematically examine the effects of coprecipitation synthesis on the characteristics of ZnO/AC nanocomposites and their implications for various applications. A systematic review was conducted on research articles published between 2016 and 2026, following predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Six studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the final qualitative synthesis, comprising three studies on supercapacitor electrodes, two on water treatment and photocatalytic applications, and one on biomedical applications. The findings indicate that synthesis parameters, including precursor type, ZnO ratio, precipitating agent, pH, calcination temperature, activation method, and post-synthesis treatment, influence morphology, particle size, porosity, functional groups, crystal structure, and optical properties. The reviewed materials predominantly exhibit hexagonal wurtzite ZnO structures, nanoscale dimensions, and porous morphologies, with characteristic functional groups including O–H, C=O, and Zn–O. Recent studies demonstrate increasing interest in multicomponent composites to enhance material functionality. ZnO/AC nanocomposites show promising potential for biomedical, environmental, and energy storage applications. However, the limited number of eligible studies and variations in reported synthesis parameters highlight the need for further systematic experimental validation.

title: The Role of library and Information Services in Development of Blue Economy in Maritime Institutions in Southern Nigeria

summary: The study investigated the role of library and information services in the development of blue economy in maritime institution in Southern Nigeria. Five research questions and two hypotheses guided the study. The study adopted descriptive r
content: The study investigated the role of library and information services in the development of blue economy in maritime institution in Southern Nigeria. Five research questions and two hypotheses guided the study. The study adopted descriptive research methodology. Population of 104, comprises academic librarians and lecturers in maritime institutions in Sothern Nigeria. Questionnaire was used as instrument to elicited data. Data was analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics. The findings revealed promoting of education, research and development, facilitating access to information, etc. as the roles of library and information services in developing BE.

title: Geoeconomic risk and generation costs in Sri Lanka’s hydro-thermal power system
summary: Introduction: Regulated electricity systems in import-dependent economies face structural vulnerability when global energy crises transmit into domestic generation costs. This paper develops a cost decomposition framework that distinguishes
content: Introduction: Regulated electricity systems in import-dependent economies face structural vulnerability when global energy crises transmit into domestic generation costs. This paper develops a cost decomposition framework that distinguishes systematic geoeconomic risk driven by oil price, exchange rate, and freight cost shocks from structural risk arising from endogenous generation mix shifts, grounding the analysis in the systematic/unsystematic risk decomposition from Modern Portfolio Theory. Materials and methods: The geoeconomic multiplier is derived from the Cost–Insurance–Freight (CIF) import price identity, providing a theoretically grounded transmission mechanism with explicit pass-through coefficients. Applied to Sri Lanka’s regulated power system (Q2 2025–Q2 2026), the framework constructs a CIF-based multiplier calibrated to observe movements in global oil prices, the LKR/USD exchange rate, and the Baltic Dry Index. A Monte Carlo simulation ( N = 10,000) quantifies uncertainty across empirically bounded input distributions. Results: System-wide generation costs exceed the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) reported benchmark of Rs. 96.8 billion in 99.6% of simulations under both the PUCSL forecast mix (90% CI: Rs. 100.0–124.6 billion) and the independently derived dry-season analogue mix (90% Confidence Interval (CI): Rs. 108.0–170.1 billion). Oil price is the dominant systematic risk driver (r = 0.795), followed by freight dynamics (r = 0.572). The oil share of the generation mixes functions as the system’s geoeconomic beta, governing amplification of external shocks into domestic costs. Conclusions: Cost-reflective tariff frameworks in hydro-thermal systems face structural vulnerability to external shocks that cannot be addressed through operational efficiency alone. The findings suggest that reducing the system’s geoeconomic beta through investments in battery storage, wind energy, and demand response represents a promising structural hedge, though a full comparative cost–benefit assessment of these interventions lies beyond the scope of the present model. The framework is replicable across import-dependent regulated power systems in the Global South.

title: Bayesian optimization of exergy rate for multi-well injection schemes in carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems
summary: Carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems use captured carbon dioxide as a subsurface working fluid, coupling renewable energy production with long-term carbon dioxide utilization. Their decades-long sustainability hinges on how carbon dioxid
content: Carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems use captured carbon dioxide as a subsurface working fluid, coupling renewable energy production with long-term carbon dioxide utilization. Their decades-long sustainability hinges on how carbon dioxide injection rates are allocated across wells and operational stages, yet each candidate strategy demands a computationally prohibitive full-physics simulation. With the lifetime average reservoir exergy rate as the objective, Bayesian optimization is employed to make this search tractable, identifying interpretable interwell injection-rate allocations while matching the solution quality of an industry-standard optimizer at a lower computational cost. The framework is demonstrated on a geothermal reservoir with five injectors and two producers over a 30-year lifetime, comparing Uniform, Zonal, and Stepwise Injection Rate Schemes against the lifetime average reservoir exergy rate. The results demonstrate that the exergy optimization primarily navigates a fundamental trade-off between the quantity and the quality of the produced energy. Excessive injection greatly penalizes performance, reducing the lifetime average exergy rate to 429 kW at a tenfold-higher rate, below the 494 kW obtained under conservative injection, which nonetheless underutilizes the reservoir. Temporal flexibility in the injection-rate allocation resolves this tension. Relative to the Zonal Rate Scheme, the Stepwise Rate Scheme raises specific exergy by 15.6% and cuts carbon dioxide injection by 11% while still delivering a higher average exergy rate, thereby extracting more useful energy from less carbon dioxide circulation. Flow diagnostics and Proper Orthogonal Decomposition analyses further confirm the underlying mechanism. Guided by the well connectivity, optimized injection-rate allocations redirect injection spatially and temporally, extending fluid residence time, whereas the geologically anchored dominant mode of the flow field remains unchanged. This study contributes essential insights into advancing sustainable energy production techniques, and the framework is generalizable to other subsurface systems involving multiple injection and production wells.

title: Application of multiagent deep reinforcement learning in source-grid-load-storage coordinated scheduling
source: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering (AOPR)
summary: Source–grid–load–storage coordinated scheduling is becoming increasingly important in modern energy systems due to the growing penetration of renewable generation, flexible demand, and energy storage. However, the strong coupling and dynami
content: Source–grid–load–storage coordinated scheduling is becoming increasingly important in modern energy systems due to the growing penetration of renewable generation, flexible demand, and energy storage. However, the strong coupling and dynamic uncertainty among heterogeneous subsystems make conventional centralized or single-agent scheduling methods difficult to scale and adapt in real time. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for coordinated source–grid–load–storage scheduling. The method models source, grid, load, and storage units as interactive agents and integrates shared reward guidance, coordination message exchange, and attention-based policy learning to improve collaborative decision-making. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves lower operating cost, higher renewable utilization, better power balance, and stronger robustness under renewable and load uncertainty than representative baselines. These findings indicate that coordinationaware multi-agent learning is a promising direction for intelligent energy scheduling and can support more adaptive and efficient dispatch in future power systems.

title: Process Resilience, Microbial Adaptation, and Integrated Bioresource Recovery for Circular Bioeconomy Applications: A Systematic Review
summary: With increasing global energy demand and the need to mitigate climate change, anaerobic digestion (AD) has emerged as a promising waste-to-energy technology that produces renewable biogas and supports sustainable waste management. However,
content: With increasing global energy demand and the need to mitigate climate change, anaerobic digestion (AD) has emerged as a promising waste-to-energy technology that produces renewable biogas and supports sustainable waste management. However, the operation of AD systems under extreme environmental and operational conditions, including temperature extremes, salinity, ammonia toxicity, pH fluctuations, organic overloading, water scarcity, and emerging contaminants, threatens process stability and methane production. This systematic review aims to synthesize current evidence on the resilience of anaerobic digestion systems under extreme conditions, with particular emphasis on microbial adaptation mechanisms, process stability, and opportunities for bioresource recovery. Findings from the reviewed literature indicate that physiological adaptation, syntrophic interactions, direct interspecies electron transfer, and microbial community restructuring are key mechanisms that enhance system resilience. The review further identifies resource-recovery pathways, including biomethane upgrading, nutrient recycling, digestate valorization, volatile fatty acid production, biohydrogen generation, and carbon recovery, as important strategies for improving the sustainability of AD systems within circular bioeconomy frameworks. Drawing on the synthesized evidence, the paper proposes a conceptual resilience framework linking environmental stressors, microbial adaptation, engineering interventions, process management, and resource recovery. The review concludes by highlighting priority research areas, including synthetic microbial consortia, digital monitoring technologies, climate-resilient digester design, and artificial intelligence-based optimization, to advance sustainable renewable energy production and circular bioeconomy development.
