title: Extended Generalized Pareto Models for the Spatial Modeling of Extreme and Bulk Rainfall
summary: ABSTRACT The peaks‐over‐threshold (POT) approach to defining extreme observations is intuitive and less wasteful than other methods such as the block maxima approach. However, POT requires the selection of an appropriate high threshold to d
content: ABSTRACT The peaks‐over‐threshold (POT) approach to defining extreme observations is intuitive and less wasteful than other methods such as the block maxima approach. However, POT requires the selection of an appropriate high threshold to define an extreme observation. In spatial modeling problems, POT requires threshold selection at each location in the study. Threshold selection is usually performed using visual tools and therefore can be subjective and tedious when modeling data from many locations. Extended generalized Pareto (EGP) distributions, extensions of the standard POT model, are more robust to threshold selection and are suitable for modeling extremes using low thresholds, thereby incorporating more data in the analysis and potentially eliminating careful threshold selection by location. This work extends two EGP models spatially using Bayesian hierarchical models to predict rainfall return levels across the province of Nova Scotia, Canada. The spatial models incorporate a forecasting variable as a covariate to account for heterogeneous behavior of extreme rainfall across space and allow for interpolation of inference between stations.

title: Quantifying Thermal Inertia Effect of Permafrost in the Community Earth System Model Version 1.2
summary: Abstract Permafrost's thermal inertia causes permafrost thaw to lag behind climate warming. This is critical for understanding climate sensitivity of permafrost, but has not been well quantified. Using differences between stabilized and tra
content: Abstract Permafrost's thermal inertia causes permafrost thaw to lag behind climate warming. This is critical for understanding climate sensitivity of permafrost, but has not been well quantified. Using differences between stabilized and transient experiments from the CESM1.2, we quantified thermal inertia effect of permafrost in the Northern Hemisphere. The results show that thermal inertia's effect on ground temperature is not apparent in the shallow layers, but enhances with depth. Under the 1.5°C and 2.0°C global warming, thermal inertia reduces warming of ground temperature at 35 m depth by 0.60°C and 0.52°C. It also reduces loss of permafrost extent by 1.8 × 10 6 and 1.7 × 10 6 km 2 , and the corresponding delay times are approximately 19 and 18 years, respectively. Thermal inertia's effect on active layer is small because of its small effect on ground temperature in shallow layer. Magnitude of thermal inertia in different global warming period is related to warming rate in surface air temperature in the transient experiments, a higher warming rate in surface air temperature leading to a greater thermal inertia effect. These results provide important implications for understanding permafrost dynamics and associated thermal change in a warming world.

title: How Is Induced Demand Addressed in Road Infrastructure Planning? An Evaluation of the German Federal Transport Infrastructure Plan
summary: Abstract Given current climate protection targets, the expansion of highway networks has become the subject of a heated public debate. It has long been empirically demonstrated that network expansions induce demand and, in turn, CO2 emissio
content: Abstract Given current climate protection targets, the expansion of highway networks has become the subject of a heated public debate. It has long been empirically demonstrated that network expansions induce demand and, in turn, CO2 emissions, yet transport planning methods still fail to adequately account for these impacts. This paper examines how induced traffic demand is addressed in the German Federal Transport Infrastructure Plan 2030 (FTIP 2030), which has been the subject of ongoing critique in recent years. Based on a systematic literature review on induced demand, the methods used in the FTIP and the appraisal results for its 1,047 road projects were evaluated. The findings show that the FTIP methodology underestimates induced demand by up to a factor of eight and CO2 emissions by up to a factor of four (4.1 Mt/a vs. 1.0 Mt/a). The results highlight the need for integrated transport planning for sustainable mobility that goes beyond road capacity expansion to address accessibility and climate protection targets – particularly in metropolitan areas with high traffic volumes and limited space, yet significant potential to strengthen alternatives to road transport.

title: How far can a surrogate travel? Mapping cross-climate transferability of building energy surrogates considering limited data budget
summary: Machine learning (ML) surrogate models accelerate early-stage building energy prediction by replacing slow physics-based simulation, but a surrogate is often tied to the climate of its training data, and reusing it elsewhere normally requir
content: Machine learning (ML) surrogate models accelerate early-stage building energy prediction by replacing slow physics-based simulation, but a surrogate is often tied to the climate of its training data, and reusing it elsewhere normally requires regenerating datasets and retraining. Transfer learning (TL) offers a potential solution by reusing a surrogate trained in one city for another, yet its reliability under cross-climate weather domain shifts remains poorly understood, and practitioners lack guidance on when it is worthwhile. This study investigates how far an ML building energy surrogate can be transferred across climates under limited target domain data. An artificial neural network trained on Gothenburg data was transferred to five target cities spanning a range of weather domain distances, quantified from hourly EPW data using Maximum Mean Discrepancy. Three TL methods were evaluated through transfer gain, negative transfer rate, and equivalent target simulations saved, across multiple target-data regimes and transfer configurations and compared to multiple linear regression and XGBoost as baselines. The results indicate that TL offers a clear advantage when the source and target climates are similar, whereas for distant climates, a well-tuned XGBoost model trained on the target data alone performs better. The results are consolidated into practical, exploratory maps. By locating a target city on these maps, practitioners can judge when cross-climate transfer is reliable, when it requires validation, and when local retraining is preferable, providing evidence-based guidance for cross-climate surrogate reuse under early-stage design constraints.

title: Operational Resilience of Road Systems When Disruptions Arise
summary: Abstract Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly
content: Abstract Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly to emerging threats results in cascading risks across the interdependent services like emergency response and healthcare. This research adopts a systems thinking approach to investigate how operational resilience of the road systems can be enhanced during such disruptions. While previous studies have examined transport resilience to hazards, few have considered system interdependencies, especially in disaster scenarios. This research addresses this gap by placing roads within broader network of societal functions, where localised failures of critical components can lead to systemic breakdowns. Through comparative case studies from the UK and selected Global South countries, we analyse good practices and persistent limitations in resilience planning. The results highlight the importance of data-informed decision-making, inclusive governance and multi-level coordination in building resilient road networks. We propose a four-stage framework - sense, anticipate, adapt, and recover, creating greater adaptive capacity. This work contributes to growing calls urging transport professionals and policymakers to embrace whole system approaches amid pressing climatic, social, and infrastructure challenges.

title: Status loss or control gain?
summary: Die Klimapolitik richtet ihren Blick zunehmend darauf, wie viel konsumiert wird und nicht mehr nur darauf, wie produziert wird. Der Sechste Sachstandsbericht des IPCC beziffert das Potenzial nachfrageseitiger Maßnahmen in den Sektoren Gebäu
content: Die Klimapolitik richtet ihren Blick zunehmend darauf, wie viel konsumiert wird und nicht mehr nur darauf, wie produziert wird. Der Sechste Sachstandsbericht des IPCC beziffert das Potenzial nachfrageseitiger Maßnahmen in den Sektoren Gebäude, Landverkehr und Ernährung auf 40 bis 70 Prozent der Emissionen bis 2050. Ein großer Teil davon liegt nicht darin, anders zu kaufen, sondern weniger. Genau daran entsteht Widerstand und zwar auch bei Menschen, denen Umweltschutz wichtig ist. Diese Arbeit argumentiert, dass dieser Widerstand eine eigene soziale Logik hat: Er wird von zwei Kräften gleichzeitig geprägt, einer symbolischen Statusbedrohung, die daraus entsteht, mit weniger Besitz gesehen zu werden und einem Gefühl von Autonomie, das aus der selbst getroffenen Entscheidung wächst. Die Argumentation verbindet drei Literaturstränge: die Forschung zum Statussignalisieren, die Selbstbestimmungstheorie und die GLORCY-Taxonomie individueller Gewinne und Verluste bei Konsumreduktion. Daraus wurden vier Hypothesen abgeleitet und in einem 2 × 2 Zwischensubjekt-Onlineexperiment geprüft (N = 167). Die wahrgenommene Statusbedrohung wurde über eine kurze Rahmung des eigenen sozialen Umfelds variiert, die wahrgenommene Autonomie über die Bildunterschrift eines Instagram-ähnlichen Beitrags einer fiktiven Person, die keine neue Kleidung mehr kauft. Kleidung diente dabei als empirischer Anwendungsfall. Die Ergebnisse sind in den Hauptbefunden eindeutig. Statusbedrohung senkte die Akzeptanz von Konsumreduktion (H1), Autonomie erhöhte sie (H2). Beide Effekte waren statistisch signifikant aber von bescheidener Größe, was einer einzelnen kurzen Rahmung realistischerweise entspricht. Die vorhergesagte Pufferwirkung (H3) zeigte sich in der erwarteten Richtung. Autonomie half besonders dann, wenn eine Bedrohung vorlag, erreichte aber keine statistische Signifikanz. Die explorative Dreifachmoderation durch die Statusorientierung (H4) ergab keinen Effekt. Die soziale Bedeutung von weniger Konsum ist damit eine reale Barriere und keine Randfrage. Kampagnen, die sie übergehen, dürften an Wirkung verlieren. Das Gefühl der eigenen Wahl ist ein praktisch nutzbarer Hebel. Kommunikation kann beide Kräfte ansprechen, indem sie bewusste Reduktion sichtbar anerkennt und sie zugleich als eigene Entscheidung der Konsumentinnen und Konsumenten darstellt. Ob die Kombination beider Prinzipien wirksamer ist als jedes für sich, bleibt offen und muss in künftigen Studien direkt geprüft werden.

title: Ensemble-based assessment of projected hazard risk: Identification of regions exposed to extreme precipitation in North-Central Europe
summary: Abstract Accelerated transformations in the European hydrological cycle during the early 21st century call for a rethinking of approaches used to detect regions susceptible to precipitation extremes. This work provides a risk map for extrem
content: Abstract Accelerated transformations in the European hydrological cycle during the early 21st century call for a rethinking of approaches used to detect regions susceptible to precipitation extremes. This work provides a risk map for extreme precipitation events, categorizing areas into four risk levels: from no risk to high risk. These were defined based on the direction, magnitude, and statistical significance of trends in extreme precipitation indices, with the highest category representing significant positive trends within the upper percentiles of the precipitation distribution. The study includes 70 years of historical data from E-Obs (1951–2020) and 13 bias-adjusted CORDEX models under two future scenarios, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, for 80 years (2021–2100). To ensure reliable detection of long-term changes, the analysis employs the Mann-Kendall test with an iterative pre-whitening procedure. The historical risk assessment derived from seven decades of E-Obs observational data shows a heterogeneous pattern across Europe. Elevated risk zones are predominantly concentrated along the western coastal regions of Scandinavia, particularly in Norway’s Atlantic-facing territories. In contrast, continental interior regions (Central European lowlands) generally exhibit lower risk levels. Under the RCP4.5 scenario, some areas, particularly in Scandinavia, show increased risk, although model agreement remains variable. The RCP8.5 scenario presents a noticeable increase in risk levels, with widespread agreement among climate models. Almost the entire study domain transitions into medium to high-risk categories. This broadly shift represents not merely an intensification of existing patterns but a fundamental reorganization of the region’s extreme precipitation climatology. The changes are especially pronounced across the Scandinavian countries, with almost the entire region falling into the high-risk category. The contrast between the two emissions scenarios emphasizes the strong sensitivity of extreme precipitation patterns to greenhouse gas concentration pathways. Overall, the results emphasize the urgency of mitigation and inform adaptation planning in regions likely to face higher extreme precipitation risk.

title: Exogenous brassinolide at different concentrations modulates growth development and physiological indices in Capsicum annuum L. pepper
summary: Abstract Brassinolide (BR), as an emerging plant growth regulator, has shown significant effectiveness in promoting plant growth, enhancing stress resistance, and improving crop quality. This study used the seeds of the pepper variety ‘Chan
content: Abstract Brassinolide (BR), as an emerging plant growth regulator, has shown significant effectiveness in promoting plant growth, enhancing stress resistance, and improving crop quality. This study used the seeds of the pepper variety ‘Changxian Tianxia’ as experimental materials to investigate the effects of different concentrations of brassinolide on the growth and development of chili peppers. Five treatment groups were set up with brassinolide concentrations of 0 mg. L − 1 (CK), 0.1 mg. L − 1 , 0.2 mg. L − 1 , 0.3 mg. L − 1 , and 0.4 mg. L − 1 . Each treatment group had three replicates, and the growth and physiological indicators of the plants were measured to explore the effects of brassinolide on the growth and development of peppers. The experimental results showed that brassinolide can significantly enhance the growth vitality of pepper plants, effectively increase chlorophyll content, enhance peroxidase (POD) activity, and reduce malondialdehyde content; Among them, brassinolide at a concentration of 0.3 mg. L − 1 has the most outstanding effect in promoting pepper growth. This study explores the mechanism by which different concentrations of brassinolide affect the growth and development of peppers, providing a scientific basis for high-yield and high-quality cultivation of peppers and promoting the application of brassinolide in agricultural production.

title: A Two-Stage SARIMA–GARCH Approach to Forecasting Global Monthly Carbon Dioxide Emissions: Trend, Seasonality, and Mitigation Implications
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Accurate near-term projections of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions help governments gauge progress toward the Paris temperature goals and time demand-side mitigation. Most forecasts rely on annual figures, overlook the pronounced within-year
content: Accurate near-term projections of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions help governments gauge progress toward the Paris temperature goals and time demand-side mitigation. Most forecasts rely on annual figures, overlook the pronounced within-year movement of emissions and their reaction to sudden shocks, and rarely model the resulting volatility. Using the IEA–EDGAR v8.0 global monthly fossil CO₂ inventory (156 observations, January 2010–December 2022), this study builds a two-stage model: a seasonal autoregressive integrated moving-average (SARIMA) mean equation selected by an exhaustive search, followed by a GARCH(1,1) variance equation when an ARCH-LM test detects heteroskedasticity. STL decomposition shows a mild upward trend with a strong annual cycle—the seasonal component accounts for 73.9% of short-term fluctuation, with December–January peaks and August–September troughs. The selected mean model is SARIMA(1,0,0)(1,1,1)12 with drift (Ljung–Box p = 0.96), and the GARCH(1,1) removes the remaining ARCH effect (p = 0.27). With MAPE of 1.01% in sample and 2.55% in a held-out 2022 test set and Theil's U of 0.76, it projects 38.86 Gt in 2023 and 39.00 Gt in 2024, a rise of only 0.38% consistent with the Global Carbon Budget's near-plateau. A plateau is far from the rapid, sustained cuts needed for 1.5 °C, so the paper closes with season- and sector-targeted mitigation measures.

title: Aerodyne Lifting and Thrusting Bodies with >90% Decrease in Energy Intensity
summary: Current train, airplane, and motor vehicle transportation is 90- to 300- fold more energy intensity than the basic aerodynamic skin friction of a passenger fuselage. And as an additional consequence; it is possible to reduce energy intensit
content: Current train, airplane, and motor vehicle transportation is 90- to 300- fold more energy intensity than the basic aerodynamic skin friction of a passenger fuselage. And as an additional consequence; it is possible to reduce energy intensity of air and ground transit by more than 90% with substantial reductions in transit cost, time, energy, and environmental impact. A strategic technology for reducing transit energy on railway and highway corridors is ground-effect flight, which displaces most of wheel suspension with aerodynamic suspension and enables higher speeds and multi-modal vehicles capable of seamless highspeed transit between existing highway/railway/waterway/Airway corridors. The combination of highspeed multi-modal vehicles and advances in scheduling would substantially eliminate traffic congestion and favor land-based transit over vastly extended markets. The geopolitical and humanity implications include the ability to rapidly become fully independent of petroleum fuels and the respective funding of wars and other inhumanities with oil revenues. Implementation in a few years is possible because the technology is vehicle based and functional on existing infrastructure. Also, the technology can operate with a near-zero greenhouse gas footprint, which can expedite mitigation of emissions causing global warming.

title: Sustainability Strategies and Practices in the Management of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Narrative Review
summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 850 million people worldwide and is projected to become a leading cause of death by 2040. Kidney care is resource-intensive, contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water and energy consumpt
content: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 850 million people worldwide and is projected to become a leading cause of death by 2040. Kidney care is resource-intensive, contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water and energy consumption, and healthcare costs. Addressing sustainability in CKD management is critical for aligning kidney health delivery systems with global climate and health goals. A multidisciplinary narrative review was undertaken to qualitatively synthesize literature on CKD management, integrating clinical nephrology, environmental sustainability, and planetary-health perspectives. Studies examining dialysis, kidney transplantation (KT), and preventive kidney management (PKM) were analyzed through the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework, encompassing environmental, economic, and social dimensions. Dialysis, though life-sustaining for people with CKD G4-G5, is the least sustainable option due to its high ecological footprint and cost. KT often provides superior survival and long-term cost-effectiveness but faces barriers such as donor availability, inequitable access, and procedural and pharmaceutical emissions. PKM, including early detection, lifestyle improvements, appropriate virtual care, and optimized pharmacologic management, is important for slowing disease progression and may reduce the need for resource-intensive kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Although the environmental and economic effects of PKM have not been consistently quantified, avoiding or delaying progression to advanced CKD may reduce healthcare resource use, costs, and environmental impacts. Findings support a coordinated, value-based model of kidney care that aligns preventive, interventional, and supportive practices, while recognizing gaps in environmental and economic evidence. Embedding sustainability into CKD care will necessitate technological innovation, policy reform, and equitable access. Future collaborative research should employ long-term life-cycle assessments to guide sustainable, patient-centered kidney care. It should account for variability in CKD pathways and balance effectiveness, sustainability, and equitable access worldwide.

title: Using Game‐Based Experiential Learning With Scenario‐Based Assessment to Measure Climate Change Competence Among Adolescent Students in Pakistan
summary: ABSTRACT Many adolescents are unaware of how unsustainable practices reinforce climate change factors. Although game‐based learning (GBL) is acknowledged as effective, assessing climate change competence often relies on self‐report measures
content: ABSTRACT Many adolescents are unaware of how unsustainable practices reinforce climate change factors. Although game‐based learning (GBL) is acknowledged as effective, assessing climate change competence often relies on self‐report measures that may not capture actual understanding. This study addresses the limited use of GBL for climate change education and overreliance on self‐report assessments. We developed a game‐based experiential learning intervention using a board game simulating real‐world climate factors. To measure its effectiveness, we designed a scenario‐based assessment evaluating systems thinking through open‐ended responses. We compared 24 adolescents under three conditions: GBL, lecture‐based learning (LBL), and control. Findings indicated that GBL significantly improved scenario‐based performance compared with the control group. Game participants demonstrated more advanced systems thinking, identifying more causal relationships and considering more stakeholder perspectives. While self‐reported confidence showed a moderate correlation with scenario performance across the sample, within‐group analysis revealed that self‐reports failed to capture the specific competence gains produced by the game‐based intervention. Interactive board games can improve climate change competence; however, assessment must extend beyond self‐reports.

title: Global greenhouse gas emissions from wastewater treatment plants
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This record contains the data and code accompanying the article “Global greenhouse gas emissions from wastewater treatment plants” (Nature Sustainability). The study compiles a global database of 90,514 wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs),
content: This record contains the data and code accompanying the article “Global greenhouse gas emissions from wastewater treatment plants” (Nature Sustainability). The study compiles a global database of 90,514 wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), infers the treatment configuration of plants without documented process information with machine learning, and estimates their direct CH4 and N2O emissions in 2022 with Monte Carlo simulation, together with projections to 2050. Files Supplementary Data 1 (Combined configuration information.xlsx). Compiled N2O and CH4 emission factors for each treatment configuration, with sources, facility-to-bioreactor ratios, records supplemented from similar processes and IQR screening results, and the parameters of the 2050 mitigation scenarios. Supplementary Data 2 (Combined WWTP information.xlsx). Plant-level database of 90,514 WWTPs, with administrative location, coordinates, served population, reported treatment level and process, and the 26 socio-economic, settlement, land-cover and climatic predictors used for treatment-process inference. Supplementary Data 3 (Region_resolved pollutant flows and GHG emissions.xlsx). Pollutant loads and CH4 and N2O emissions for each administrative region by pathway, the projected values used in the scenario analysis, and the country-level comparison with the EPA inventory. Source Data Fig. 1 to 4 and Source Data Extended Data Fig. 1 to 3. Data underlying the main and Extended Data figures of the article. Figures_code.zip. Python code used to draw the figures. The full code is available at https://github.com/QixiangZ/Global-WWTP-GHG-accounting. Each Supplementary Data file opens with a Dictionary sheet that defines every column.

title: Iot and machine learning for multi-horizon soil moisture forecasting using leakage-free reconstructed sensor data in precision agriculture
summary: Smart agriculture has emerged as an important approach for improving crop productivity, resource efficiency, and climate resilience through continuous environmental monitoring and predictive analytics. This study presents an Internet of Thi
content: Smart agriculture has emerged as an important approach for improving crop productivity, resource efficiency, and climate resilience through continuous environmental monitoring and predictive analytics. This study presents an Internet of Things (IoT) edge computing and machine learning framework for multi-horizon soil moisture forecasting in precision Agriculture. The proposed system integrates a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device with soil moisture, temperature, relative humidity, carbon dioxide (CO $$_2$$ ), and camera sensors to continuously monitor environmental and crop conditions on a cassava farm. Sensor data were processed using an edge-computing architecture and subsequently analyzed using statistical and machine learning techniques. To address prolonged sensor outage, a leakage-free time-series reconstruction methodology was developed that preserves temporal causality by reconstructing missing observations using only historical information available before the outage. Following data preprocessing and feature engineering, four supervised machine learning models including Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), together with Persistence and ARIMA benchmark models, were evaluated for 1-day, 2-day, 5-day, and 7-day soil moisture forecasting. The nonlinear machine learning models consistently outperformed the benchmark approaches, with XGBoost and MLP achieving the highest predictive performance, reaching R2 score of up to 0.94 while substantially reducing forecasting errors. Comparative experiments further demonstrated that leakage-free reconstruction significantly improved forecasting accuracy relative to the non-reconstructed dataset. Feature importance analysis identified cyclical time-of-day information, historical soil moisture observations, and engineered temporal features as the most influential predictors. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating IoT sensing, leakage-free data reconstruction, and machine learning to provide reliable soil moisture forecasting for intelligent irrigation management and sustainable cassava production.

title: FASTMIP-CMIP7: A Coordinated Multi-Emulator Ensemble for Rapid, Spatially Resolved Climate Projections under CMIP7 Scenarios
summary: Abstract. Earth System Models (ESMs) remain the gold standard for translating socioeconomic scenarios into spatially resolved climate projections, but their computational cost limits the number of scenarios and ensemble members that can be
content: Abstract. Earth System Models (ESMs) remain the gold standard for translating socioeconomic scenarios into spatially resolved climate projections, but their computational cost limits the number of scenarios and ensemble members that can be simulated and ties projections to the evidence available when simulations are performed. Climate emulators, which are statistical and machine-learning models trained on ESM output, enable large ensembles and allow projections to be updated as new observations emerge. Here, we present FASTMIP-CMIP7, a coordinated ensemble of seven emulators providing spatially and temporally resolved projections of temperature, precipitation and climate impact indicators for four newly released scenarios from the 7th phase of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP7), spanning very low (VL) to high (H) emissions. Despite scenario ranges having narrowed in CMIP7 comapred to CMIP6, emissions pathways remain the dominant source of uncertainty in regional end-of-century temperature projections, making mitigation the strongest lever for limiting future warming. In 2100, global land temperature reaches 2.3 °C under stringent mitigation (VL), and 3.9 °C under the current-policies scenario (M), approximately 1.4 times the global mean warming. Under M, even the coolest 5 % of years in 2100 are warmer over land than 95 % of present-day years. Precipitation projections are more heterogeneous, with internal variability and regional climate responses often obscuring scenario differences. Nevertheless, robust drying emerges in northern South America and the Mediterranean, where additional drying relative to today is 2.5 to almost four times greater under current policies (M) than under stringent mitigation (VL). Structural differences between emulators and choices in training, testing and validation introduce a new layer of uncertainty to emulated ensembles. Common, streamlined validation experiments are needed to establish confidence in emulated projections and support the broader integration of climate emulators into future climate assessments.

title: Targeted Spectral Threshold Tests for Reducing Cloud Omission in the GOSAT-2 CAI-2 Cloud Mask
summary: Abstract. Cloud detection is a common problem in optical remote sensing, but its consequences vary by mission. In GOSAT-2, missed clouds matter because they can affect greenhouse gas retrievals. This research introduces a targeted omission-
content: Abstract. Cloud detection is a common problem in optical remote sensing, but its consequences vary by mission. In GOSAT-2, missed clouds matter because they can affect greenhouse gas retrievals. This research introduces a targeted omission-recovery approach for the GOSAT-2 CAI-2 Level 2 cloud mask over water. Rather than replacing the operational mask, the method identifies and corrects its errors. True-positive and false-negative cloud footprints are mapped into two-dimensional spectral feature spaces proposed from native CAI-2 L1B ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared radiances. Polynomial logistic regression was used to estimate the probability that a cloud footprint belonged to the detected-cloud group. A Kolmogorov–Smirnov test then compared false negatives at or above the weakest detected TP level with those below it, and the three feature spaces that separated these groups most clearly across granules were converted into probability-threshold tests. Finally, these tests were applied only to pixels labeled no-cloud in the original L2 mask, with additional controls such as sun-glint filtering. Among four overwater granules around Japan, the revised mask reduced cloud omission by 64–83 %, while overestimation increased by 0 to 4 percentage points. Cohen's kappa increased by 5–14 points, reaching 0.88 to 0.93. In the independent granule, the tests recovered 55.4 % of the clouds missed by the L2 mask while introducing false positives over only 2.07 % of cloud-free pixels. Also, an indicator semivariogram showed that recovering the missed clouds improves the mask most at the scales of edges and small and scattered clouds. These results show that missed clouds in CAI-2 contain recoverable spectral structure, which can be used to improve the operational CAI-2 cloud mask over the ocean.

title: Drying the Cradle of Civilization: Water, Food, and Societal Security at a Crossroads in Iraq
summary: Abstract Iraq is facing grave problems and threats regarding the future of its nation, which can be classified into water security, food security, and societal security. These challenges spring from a legacy of past conflicts, unwise admini
content: Abstract Iraq is facing grave problems and threats regarding the future of its nation, which can be classified into water security, food security, and societal security. These challenges spring from a legacy of past conflicts, unwise administrative policies, and complex geopolitical and environmental factors. Water scarcity results from a severe reduction in the abundant flows of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, unfair transboundary sharing, climate change impacts, and haphazard water management. Food insecurity is a natural consequence magnified by agricultural stagnation and population growth. This paper provides an overview of the present situation and outlines proposed solutions, though the future remains uncertain given the fragile economy and the political will required for reforms.

title: Agricultural TFP Dynamics and Ozone-Depleting Substances Panel Analysis in Latin America
summary: Abstract This study evaluates the long-term relationships between ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out policies, land surface temperature anomalies, and agricultural Total Factor Productivity (TFP) dynamics across a panel of 23 countr
content: Abstract This study evaluates the long-term relationships between ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out policies, land surface temperature anomalies, and agricultural Total Factor Productivity (TFP) dynamics across a panel of 23 countries over a 35-year period (1990–2024). Employing a two-stage analytical framework combining an input-oriented Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) Malmquist index with second-stage panel fixed-effects econometric regressions, aggregate TFP growth is decomposed into technical efficiency change and technological progress. Empirical findings reveal that regional agricultural TFP dynamics were primarily driven by shifts in the production frontier and cross-country structural variations. Second-stage econometric estimates demonstrate that historical consumption of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs_IHS) and Methyl Bromide (MB_IHS) did not exert statistically significant negative disruptions on agricultural productivity (β = 0.0160,p = 0.2744; β = 0.0218,p = 0.3691, respectively), reflecting successful technological substitution and producer adaptation during the Montreal Protocol phase-out mandates. Furthermore, annual surface temperature anomalies showed no significant aggregate impact (β = 0.0093,p = 0.9388), highlighting the limitations of macro-level climate averages. Marked cross-country heterogeneity underscores the imperative for targeted policies that bridge technical efficiency gaps and enhance agricultural resilience.

title: Long-term agricultural water conservation under straw and plastic mulching characterized with stable water isotope tracing
summary: Soil health and water resource efficiency are key aspects of sustainable agriculture, and various mulching practices can contribute towards improved soil water conservation and crop yields. A 13-year long-term experiment was conducted to co
content: Soil health and water resource efficiency are key aspects of sustainable agriculture, and various mulching practices can contribute towards improved soil water conservation and crop yields. A 13-year long-term experiment was conducted to comparatively analyze the long-term effects of straw mulching and plastic mulching on soil properties, winter wheat physiological characteristics and yields. Stable water isotope tracing was used to analyze spatio-temporal distributions of soil water fluxes and root water uptake, so that the mechanisms whereby mulching influences soil water conservation and plant water availability can be further characterized. Results showed that both mulching practices increased the proportion of macroaggregates (>0.25 mm) (31.7%-41.6%), water content at field capacity (3.5%-7.9%), saturated hydraulic conductivity (54.9%-89.1%), leaf photosynthesis, instantaneous water use efficiency (WUE 0 ) (13.7%-34.6%), and winter wheat yields (6.9%-19.2%) compared with the control. Straw mulching was more effective than plastic mulching in reducing soil bulk density, promoting organic carbon and total nitrogen accumulation. Plastic mulching led to similar long-term cumulative yields, more consistent annual yields, and less long-term soil quality improvement than straw mulching. Stable water isotope tracing indicated that winter wheat mainly used water from the shallowest 40 cm of soil, and that both mulches improved plant water availability likely by reducing subsurface drainage losses. Additionally, plastic mulching inhibited early topsoil evaporation during the critical jointing stage. Therefore, straw mulching facilitates long-term soil improvement, whereas plastic mulching stabilizes yields under acute droughts. Further research comparing mulch types across different agricultural systems and geographical regions may enhance the generalizability of these single-site findings.

title: THE REBOUND EFFECT: A BLIND SPOT IN LABORATORY EMISSION-REDUCTION EFFORTS
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Conference proceedingSF2A 2026 M. Béthermin, K. Baillié, N. Lagarde, J. Malzac, R.-M. Ouazzani, J. Richard, O. Venot, A. Siebert (eds) https://sf2a.eu/proceedings/2026/2026sf2a.conf.999H.pdf Abstract. In an effort to limit global warming, r
content: Conference proceedingSF2A 2026 M. Béthermin, K. Baillié, N. Lagarde, J. Malzac, R.-M. Ouazzani, J. Richard, O. Venot, A. Siebert (eds) https://sf2a.eu/proceedings/2026/2026sf2a.conf.999H.pdf Abstract. In an effort to limit global warming, research laboratories are more and more measuring their greenhouse-gas emissions and taking steps to reduce them. However a cheaper or faster service may be used more, and saved money or time, which then may support other activities that in turn emit greenhouse gases. These responses are called rebound effects. We explain the main types of rebound effect and discuss several examples, namely computing, artificial intelligence, teleworking, and research budgets. Studies in other sectors show that rebound can be large. While efficiency remains useful for both science and emission cuts, we argue that rebound effects is an important, possibly dominant effects, that must be accounted for in any greenhouse gas emission reduction strategy.

title: Livestock farming and soil erosion prevention ecosystem service: a RUSLE-GIS estimation in Italian alpine grassland-based dairy farms
summary: The ecosystem service of erosion prevention (ESEP) becomes increasingly important due to the increasing intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events, particularly in Italy, which records the highest soil loss rate in Europe (24.13% of
content: The ecosystem service of erosion prevention (ESEP) becomes increasingly important due to the increasing intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events, particularly in Italy, which records the highest soil loss rate in Europe (24.13% of total soil loss in EU; average 8.46 t ha−1 year−1). Knowledge on ESEP focuses mainly on farmland, orchards and forests, while grassland managed by mountain dairy farms have been less studied. This study uses a 2017 dataset from 38 grassland-based dairy farms in the Eastern Italian Alps. The aim was to identify the environmental and management factors that most influence soil erosion. The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) was applied in a GIS-based framework. Monthly variation in the C factor (representing land cover and management effects) was estimated for three plots per farm (113 plots total) using a Generalised Linear Mixed Model. Although estimated mean soil loss (9.48 t ha−1 year−1) is slightly above the Italian average, nearly half of the plots have erosion rates lower than this benchmark. The C factor shows significant correlations with mean monthly temperature, altitude and species richness in the plot, fuel used per hectare and farm area. Higher temperature lowered the C-Factor, resulting in better soil protection, and the other factors increased it, though with a lower strength. This modelling study is a first step towards understanding the relative importance of factors driving mountain soil erosion. Such study could support the assessment of soil erosion in future scenarios, involving livestock farming abandonment in a context of climate change

title: Perspective of euhydration in children: health risk during climate change
summary: Euhydration during infancy and childhood is a complex task and especially gains importance especially during climate change. Euhydration is maintained through neuroendocrine pathways, but heat stress can lead to disturbance in water homeost
content: Euhydration during infancy and childhood is a complex task and especially gains importance especially during climate change. Euhydration is maintained through neuroendocrine pathways, but heat stress can lead to disturbance in water homeostasis, with dehydration being particularly critical in children. Voluntary dehydration is common among children and inadequate water intake can lead to both short-term and long-term health issues. Discussing water excretion mechanisms, including thermoregulation and kidney function potential health impacts can be highlighted. Furthermore, individual aspects potentially impact water homeostasis of an individuum. Climate change exacerbates the risk of dehydration. Current drinking recommendations do not account for these challenges. This overview offers an inside of current research data on hydration principles and increased long-term risks for health due to climate change. It points out deficiency of data in children and is at the same time a call to action for research on climate sensitive drinking recommendations.

title: CLIMATE CONDITIONS, FORMATION FACTORS, AND HYDRO-ECO-GEOGRAPHICAL IMPORTANCE OF NORTHERN SURKHANDARYA
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Ushbu maqolada Surxondaryo viloyatining shimoliy qismi - Hisor tizmasining janubiy yon bagʻirlari va togʻ oldi vodiylari - iqlim sharoitlari, ularning shakllanish omillari hamda gidro-eko-geografik ahamiyati tahlil qilingan. Denov meteostan
content: Ushbu maqolada Surxondaryo viloyatining shimoliy qismi - Hisor tizmasining janubiy yon bagʻirlari va togʻ oldi vodiylari - iqlim sharoitlari, ularning shakllanish omillari hamda gidro-eko-geografik ahamiyati tahlil qilingan. Denov meteostansiyasining 1991–2020-yillar iqlim normalari (Jahon meteorologiya tashkiloti, NOAA arxivi) va nashr etilgan gidrometeorologik ma'lumotlar asosida hududda oʻrtacha yillik harorat 15,6–17,5 °C, yogʻin miqdori tekislik qismida 200–350 mm, togʻlarda esa 790 mm gacha ekanligi, yogʻinning taxminan 85% i qish va bahor oylariga toʻgʻri kelishi aniqlandi. Asosiy iqlim shakllantiruvchi omillar sifatida subtropik kenglik, Hisor tizmasining shimoliy sovuq havo massalaridan toʻsiq vazifasi, janub va janubi-gʻarbning tropik havo massalariga ochiqligi hamda balandlik mintaqalanishi koʻrsatildi. Surxondaryo va Sherobod daryolari oqimi qor va muzlik suvlaridan shakllanadi: Sherobod havzasida aprel–iyun oylariga oʻrtacha suvli yillarda yillik oqimning 55,1% i toʻgʻri keladi. Masofadan zondlash ma'lumotlariga koʻra, Hisor muzligi maydoni 1990–2024-yillarda 8,6 km² dan 5,1 km² gacha (40,7% ga) qisqargan. Suv resurslarini moslashuvchan boshqarish va ekotizimlarni muhofaza qilish boʻyicha takliflar ishlab chiqildi.

title: Bridging Innovation and Ecosystem Resilience: A Regional Case Study of the Seshachalam Biosphere (Tirupati-Kadapa)
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Rapid industrialization and increasing anthropogenic pressures necessitate a paradigm shift from conventional end-of-pipe remediation toward preventive, sustainable, and environmentally benign approaches.The present study explores the integ
content: Rapid industrialization and increasing anthropogenic pressures necessitate a paradigm shift from conventional end-of-pipe remediation toward preventive, sustainable, and environmentally benign approaches.The present study explores the integrated role of green research, sustainable technologies, and green chemistry in promoting regional environmental protection, with particular emphasis on the ecologically sensitive and biodiverse Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve, spanning the Tirupati and Kadapa districts of Andhra Pradesh, India.By incorporating the twelve principles of green chemistry, particularly atom economy, the use of renewable feedstocks, and the development of less hazardous synthetic pathways, the study highlights opportunities to integrate sustainable chemical practices with advanced ecological conservation strategies.These approaches offer potential pathways for protecting the region's fragile dry deciduous and scrub forest ecosystems, conserving threatened endemic species such as Pterocarpus santalinus (Red Sanders) and Cycas beddomei, and preserving its distinctive geological and geomorphological heritage.Furthermore, the study proposes a comparative assessment of the region's biophysical, physicochemical, and conservation indicators in relation to selected Indian and international biodiversity hotspots.It also examines trends in the global green chemistry market and explores the potential of closed-loop phytotechnology, green extraction methods, and phytonanotechnology as sustainable interventions for watershed management, pollution mitigation, and ecosystem restoration.Collectively, these approaches emphasize the importance of integrating green chemistry and technological innovation into regional environmental governance to strengthen biodiversity conservation, promote resource efficiency, and support long-term ecological sustainability.

title: Under-utilized wild varieties: a focus on Vigna vexillate in Africa
summary: Wild varieties can be used to improve genetic diversity in agriculture to enhance food security. Their potential to enhance genetic diversity remains unexplored. This systematic review focuses on the underutilized Vigna vexillata, a wild va
content: Wild varieties can be used to improve genetic diversity in agriculture to enhance food security. Their potential to enhance genetic diversity remains unexplored. This systematic review focuses on the underutilized Vigna vexillata, a wild variety with superior morphological and physiological traits compared to other Vigna species. The agro-ecological, nutritional, and medicinal properties of V. vexillata are discussed in relation to other Vigna species. Agro-ecological, V. vexillata possesses several advantages, including resistance to pests and diseases and adaptability to marginal climates and saline soils. The species' long non-glandular trichomes and the presence of amylase inhibitors in its seeds contribute to its resistance to pests and diseases. The high survival rate and growth capacity of the seeds with mineral concentration in the roots and shoots under saline conditions, suggest its potential for cultivation in marginal environments. Morphologically, it has larger leaves, thicker stems, and greater pod size and number. Nutritionally, grains of V. vexillata contain 25%–38% protein and 50%–60% starch, and sulphur-containing amino acids. Similarities in the reproductive and chromosomal structure of V. vexillata with other Vigna species can advantageously be used to genetically enhance the agro-ecological, morphological and nutritional traits of other Vigna species through research, policy, and advocacy.

title: Xây dựng bộ tiêu chí và chỉ số đánh giá khả năng tích lũy các-bon của cây gỗ phân tán ở cấp cá thể: cơ sở khoa học và thử nghiệm bước đầu
source: Tạp chí Khoa học và Công nghệ Lâm nghiệp
summary: Đánh giá các-bon cây gỗ phân tán tại Việt Nam chủ yếu dừng ở ước tính trữ lượng tại một thời điểm, chưa phản ánh đầy đủ khả năng tích lũy các-bon và chất lượng phép ước tính. Nghiên cứu xây dựng bộ tiêu chí và chỉ số S–Q–R đánh giá khả năng
content: Đánh giá các-bon cây gỗ phân tán tại Việt Nam chủ yếu dừng ở ước tính trữ lượng tại một thời điểm, chưa phản ánh đầy đủ khả năng tích lũy các-bon và chất lượng phép ước tính. Nghiên cứu xây dựng bộ tiêu chí và chỉ số S–Q–R đánh giá khả năng tích lũy các-bon của cây gỗ phân tán theo khung phân cấp tiêu chí – chỉ số – biến kiểm chứng, dựa trên hướng dẫn IPCC, phương trình sinh khối của Chave và cộng sự (2014) và cách tiếp cận UFORE/i-Tree. Bộ gồm ba tiêu chí với bốn chỉ số: lượng các-bon tích lũy – S (kg C/cây); tốc độ tích lũy – Q (mức thay đổi trữ lượng các-bon thuần hằng năm, ưu tiên xác định từ đo lặp, khi chưa có được mô phỏng theo kịch bản – Q_kb) và Q_rel; chất lượng dữ liệu và phương pháp ước tính – R (0–1), báo cáo độc lập. Thử nghiệm trên 44 cá thể thuộc 35 loài tại Trường Đại học Lâm nghiệp cho tổng trữ lượng 14,22 tấn C (khoảng tin cậy 95%: 11,1–18,5 tấn C), phân bố lệch mạnh (trung vị 122,33 kg C/cây; CV 159,1%). Trung vị Q_kb đạt 5,26 và 13,01 kg C/cây/năm với tốc độ tăng trưởng đường kính 0,83 - 1,98 cm/năm. R dao động 0,450–0,810: 20 cá thể ở mức cao, 23 trung bình (chủ yếu do khối lượng riêng gỗ cấp chi hoặc cây bị cắt tỉa) và 1 cá thể thấp. Bộ tiêu chí vận hành được với dữ liệu điều tra thông thường; Q_kb chỉ có ý nghĩa thử nghiệm và cần kiểm chứng trên mẫu lớn, nhiều vùng sinh thái, có đo lặp trước khi xây dựng ngưỡng đánh giá hoặc hướng dẫn kỹ thuật.

title: Can Sri Lanka Become a Regional Hub for Algal Biodiesel Production? A Critical Review of Ecological Potential, Technological Readiness, and Future Prospects
source: Journal of Environmental Professionals Sri Lanka
summary: Sri Lanka's dependence on imported fossil fuels and its abundant aquatic resources have generated increasing interest in algal biodiesel as a sustainable third-generation biofuel. This review critically evaluates the country's potential to
content: Sri Lanka's dependence on imported fossil fuels and its abundant aquatic resources have generated increasing interest in algal biodiesel as a sustainable third-generation biofuel. This review critically evaluates the country's potential to develop a commercially viable algal biodiesel sector by synthesizing evidence on ecological suitability, indigenous algal resources, technological readiness, sustainability benefits, and commercialization challenges. Sri Lanka possesses favorable climatic conditions, diverse freshwater and marine ecosystems, and several indigenous microalgal and macroalgal species with promising lipid productivity. However, comparison with international experience demonstrates that favorable natural resources alone are insufficient for commercialization because harvesting costs, downstream processing, economic viability, and policy support remain major constraints. The review identifies critical research gaps in pilot-scale cultivation, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle analysis, and strain improvement, and proposes strategic priorities including integrated biorefineries, wastewater-based cultivation, industrial CO₂ utilization, and supportive policy frameworks. These coordinated interventions are essential for positioning Sri Lanka as a competitive regional hub for sustainable algal biodiesel production.

title: Associations of Rainfall, Temperature, and Habitat Transformation with Elephant and Giraffe Abundance and Distribution in Meru National Park, Kenya (1995–2025)
source: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources
summary: The study investigated the relationships between rainfall patterns, temperature fluctuations, habitat alterations, and the distribution and abundance of elephants (Loxodonta africana) and giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis) within Meru Nation
content: The study investigated the relationships between rainfall patterns, temperature fluctuations, habitat alterations, and the distribution and abundance of elephants (Loxodonta africana) and giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis) within Meru National Park over a thirty-year period (1995–2025). Employing a combination of remote sensing data, climatic records, and wildlife census information, the research explored how environmental variables influence habitat quality and the spatial distribution of these keystone species. The findings reveal significant correlations: declining rainfall and rising temperatures are associated with habitat degradation, notably forest loss and grassland expansion, which in turn affect the movement and population dynamics of elephants and giraffes. While elephants exhibit some resilience due to their adaptive foraging and water dependence, giraffe populations are more sensitive to habitat changes driven by climatic variability. The study emphasises the necessity of integrated conservation strategies that account for climate influences to ensure the sustainability of these species and their habitats in Meru National Park.

title: Perceptions of environmental health education among medical students: opportunities for improving the training of health professionals on planetary health issues – a cross-sectional survey in a French university
summary: Abstract Background Deteriorating environmental conditions directly affects human health and healthcare organization. Although environmental health education in initial medical training appears to be a key factor to implementing attenuation
content: Abstract Background Deteriorating environmental conditions directly affects human health and healthcare organization. Although environmental health education in initial medical training appears to be a key factor to implementing attenuation and adaptation strategies, it remains insufficiently integrated into medical curricula, and the views of students receiving suchtraining are rarely documented. This study aims to identify the methods of integration and teaching deemed most relevant by medical students who completed a compulsory 31-hour module. Methods A descriptive, cross-sectional, survey study was conducted among third-year undergraduate medical students at a French university who had taken the ‘Environmental Health’ module in the 2024–2025 and 2025–2026 academic years. Students completed a 43-item questionnaire one year after the course for the 2024–2025 cohort, or immediately afterwards for the 2025–2026 cohort. Closed-ended responses were analyzed descriptively as counts and percentages; no statistical testing was performed. Open-ended questions were analyzed narratively. Results A total of 140 questionnaires were analyzed, representing a final response rate of 37.3%. Among the respondents, 94 (67.1%) considered the cross-curricular integration of the course throughout the entire program to be more relevant than a standalone module. There were 96 (69.1%) who felt that 30 hours was too long, while 102 (72.9%) believed that all students should take this type of course. Immersion in other contexts (83.6%) and hands-on learning (74.3%) far outstripped theoretical instruction (22.9%) among the tools considered useful for raising awareness, while university courses were ranked last among sources of awareness (28.6%). Finally, 114 students (81.4%) reported that their other teachers never or rarely addressed these issues. Conclusions Students who are among the most extensively trained in environmental health in France consider their course to be too long butbelieve that these issues should be taught to everyone, in a cross-disciplinary manner and through active learning formats. Training teachers in all disciplines appears to be a prerequisite for this change.

title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth's surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrien
content: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth's surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

title: Welfare impacts of climate-smart agriculture adoption among smallholder maize farmers in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
summary: Climate change continues to threaten agricultural productivity worldwide, with smallholder farmers in developing countries facing heightened vulnerability due to limited resources and adaptive capacity. This study examined the welfare impac
content: Climate change continues to threaten agricultural productivity worldwide, with smallholder farmers in developing countries facing heightened vulnerability due to limited resources and adaptive capacity. This study examined the welfare impacts of adopting Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices (CSAPs) among smallholder maize farmers in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The practices investigated included drought-tolerant maize varieties, rainwater harvesting systems, maize-legume intercropping, and crop diversification. Using cross-sectional data from 378 farmers and guided by Random Utility Theory, the study applied an Endogenous Switching Regression (ESR) model to address potential selection bias in adoption decisions. Household welfare was assessed using the Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS) and the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale (HFIAS). Results showed that 47.1% of farmers had adopted CSAPs. Adopters experienced significantly better welfare outcomes, recording lower food insecurity levels (HFIAS score of 7.67 compared to 9.73 for non-adopters) and higher dietary diversity (HDDS of 6.79 compared to 5.39). Treatment effects analysis further indicated that while adopters benefited substantially in terms of food security, non-adopters could achieve even greater improvements in dietary diversity if they adopted CSAPs. The findings underscore the importance of strengthening extension services, improving access to credit, promoting climate-resilient seed systems, and supporting diversified farming practices to enhance resilience and welfare among smallholder farming households.
