Even though our journey produced a lot more questions than answers, we eventually found the name of the elephant as well as the circumstances of this poor creature’s demise.

title: Effect of Tax Incentives on Performance of Manufacturing Companies in Rwanda. A case of Sulfo Rwanda Industries
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of tax incentives on performance of manufacturing companies of Sulfo Rwanda Industries.Specifically, the study attempted to assess the effect of capital allowance incentives on the performance of Sulfo Rwanda
content: This study examined the effect of tax incentives on performance of manufacturing companies of Sulfo Rwanda Industries.Specifically, the study attempted to assess the effect of capital allowance incentives on the performance of Sulfo Rwanda Industries Ltd.The study was guided by the Accelerator Theory of Investment and adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design using a mixed-methods approach.The target population comprised 142 employees of Sulfo Rwanda Industries Ltd, and a census approach was adopted.Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and regression analysis, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically.The findings showed that respondents agreed that capital allowance incentives encourage investment in machinery and equipment, support modernization of production facilities, reduce taxable income, improve cash flow, and facilitate accelerated depreciation.Pearson correlation analysis revealed a strong positive relationship between capital allowance incentives and company performance (r = .801,p < .01).Regression analysis further established that capital allowance incentives had a positive and statistically significant effect on company performance (β = .354,p = .000),with the model explaining 73.4% of the variation in performance (R² = .734).The study concludes that capital allowance incentives contribute significantly to the performance of Sulfo Rwanda Industries Ltd by supporting productive investment, modernization, liquidity, and operational efficiency.The study recommends that the company should strategically maximize available capital allowance incentives when planning investments in machinery, equipment, and production technologies.

title: Green Finance, Environmental Governance, and the Performance of Green Innovation
summary: ABSTRACT Green finance can support green innovation not only by financing research and development (R&D), but also by facilitating the application of green technologies. Drawing on institutional theory and the dynamic capability perspective
content: ABSTRACT Green finance can support green innovation not only by financing research and development (R&D), but also by facilitating the application of green technologies. Drawing on institutional theory and the dynamic capability perspective, this study examines how green finance relates to two stages of the green innovation value chain: green technology R&D and the conversion of technological innovation into economic and environmental outcomes. Using panel data for 284 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022, we find that green finance is positively associated with performance at both stages of the innovation value chain. The evidence is consistent with improved urban financing conditions and greener consumption, while stronger environmental governance reinforces these relationships. The association becomes stronger after identifiable thresholds in green‐finance development and extends across city boundaries through positive spatial spillovers. These effects are also more pronounced after 2016 and in eastern cities. These findings show that green finance operates not simply by expanding the supply of capital, but also by interacting with firms' resource‐acquisition, market‐sensing, and resource‐reconfiguration capabilities across a sequential innovation process.

title: Effect of Internal Control Systems on the Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Rwanda: A Case Study of SULFO Rwanda Industries Ltd
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the effect of internal control system components on the performance of manufacturing firms in Rwanda, using SULFO Rwanda Industries Ltd in Kigali as a case.It was guided by four objectives: to assess the effect of risk a
content: This study examined the effect of internal control system components on the performance of manufacturing firms in Rwanda, using SULFO Rwanda Industries Ltd in Kigali as a case.It was guided by four objectives: to assess the effect of risk assessment practices, control activities, information and communication systems, and monitoring mechanisms on firm performance.The study was anchored on Agency Theory, Control Theory, Institutional Theory, and the Resource-Based View.A descriptive and explanatory design with a quantitative, cross-sectional approach was adopted.The target population was 91 employees, and a census was used; 86 complete questionnaires were returned, a 94.5% response rate.Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression.Correlation results showed significant positive relationships between performance and risk assessment (r = 0.981), control activities (r = 0.952), information and communication (r = 0.817), and monitoring (r = 0.935), all at p = 0.000.Regression showed the components explained 96.9% of variation in performance (adjusted R² = 0.969), each having a significant positive effect.The study concluded that effective internal control systems enhance performance and recommended strengthening segregation of duties, improving monitoring, and enhancing information systems.

title: Influence of Procurement Policies on Local Content Growth in Rwanda’s Construction Industry: A Case of NPD Ltd
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study examined the influence of procurement policies on local content growth at NPD Ltd in Rwanda's construction industry.The four dimensions were procurement planning policy, supplier selection policy, contract management policy, and
content: This study examined the influence of procurement policies on local content growth at NPD Ltd in Rwanda's construction industry.The four dimensions were procurement planning policy, supplier selection policy, contract management policy, and risk management policy.Guided by the Resource-Based View, Agency Theory, Institutional Theory, and Transaction Cost Economics, the research employed descriptive and correlational designs using quantitative questionnaires and qualitative interviews.The population comprised 224 NPD Ltd employees, from whom 144 respondents were selected using Slovin's formula, stratified sampling, and simple random sampling.Of the questionnaires distributed, 129 were returned complete (89.58%).Instrument validity was supported by a content validity index of 0.862, while overall Cronbach's alpha was 0.869.Data were analyzed using SPSS version 29, Pearson correlations, and multiple regression.The four procurement-policy variables were positively associated with local content growth (r = 0.792, 0.898, 0.741, and 0.805, respectively; p < 0.001).The combined regression model explained 87.8% of variation in local content growth (R² = 0.878; F = 221.600,p < 0.001).Supplier selection policy showed the largest standardized coefficient (β = 0.486, p < 0.001), followed by procurement planning (β = 0.233, p < 0.001), contract management (β = 0.211, p < 0.001), and risk management (β = 0.126, p = 0.046).All four null hypotheses were rejected.NPD Ltd should improve local-supplier evaluation, procurement forecasting, contract monitoring, and supply-chain risk mitigation to strengthen local content growth.

title: The Analysis and Strategy in Developing National Resilience in Semiconductor Supply Chains in Indonesia
summary: Semiconductors have become essential components across diverse industries, yet their global supply chains remain highly vulnerable to public health crises and geopolitical tensions, such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the US–China rivalry. Al
content: Semiconductors have become essential components across diverse industries, yet their global supply chains remain highly vulnerable to public health crises and geopolitical tensions, such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the US–China rivalry. Although Indonesia possesses significant critical mineral resources for semiconductor components, including silica, nickel, gallium, and germanium, its semiconductor sector lags behind Southeast Asian neighbors such as Singapore, Malaysia, and Vietnam and remains deeply dependent on overseas supply, as reflected in a persistent semiconductor trade deficit since 2019. This research combined a systematic literature review, document analysis, and thematic analysis of focus group discussions and expert interviews with researchers, industry stakeholders, and government officials to evaluate Indonesia’s national capabilities in research, technological innovation, and talent development, in line with the Golden Indonesia 2045 vision. The findings show that Indonesia has a large domestic market but a limited number of semiconductor researchers, highly skilled engineers, and research facilities, with research capacity concentrated in IC design and layout. Building national resilience in the semiconductor supply chain therefore requires technological advancement, a state-directed workforce, targeted industrial policies, and integration into global value chains rather than complete self-sufficiency. Key recommendations include utilizing domestic resources through downstreaming policies, providing government incentives to attract foreign investment, and prioritizing the fabless business model as a realistic entry point to bridge the technological gap and ensure economic security. Indonesia can also complement ASEAN’s existing strengths in back-end manufacturing and research and development (R&D) to strengthen regional supply chain resilience.

title: Digital–Real Economy Integration and the Synergistic Advancement of Carbon Reduction, Pollution Abatement, Green Expansion and Economic Growth: Evidence from China
summary: In the context of China’s “dual carbon” goals, the deep integration of the digital and real economies (DRI) has emerged as a critical engine of industrial transformation, promoting resource efficiency and enabling coordinated carbon reducti
content: In the context of China’s “dual carbon” goals, the deep integration of the digital and real economies (DRI) has emerged as a critical engine of industrial transformation, promoting resource efficiency and enabling coordinated carbon reduction, pollution abatement, green expansion, and economic growth (CPGG). However, whether and how DRI exerts a synergistic promotion effect on a multi-dimensional CPGG system remains unclear, and the internal logic underlying this relationship has not been fully clarified. Using panel data covering 30 Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2023, this study measures DRI using a patent co-classification method and quantifies the CPGG synergy with a composite system synergy model. A two-way fixed-effects model is then employed to examine the effect of DRI on CPGG synergy, the underlying transmission mechanisms, and regional heterogeneity. The results show that DRI significantly enhances CPGG synergy, confirming that digital–real integration can deliver multi-dimensional environmental and economic dividends rather than creating a trade-off between the two. The mechanism analysis shows that DRI promotes CPGG synergy by stimulating green technological innovation and reducing energy intensity. Green finance positively moderates this relationship, strengthening the effect of DRI on coordinated CPGG development. The heterogeneity analysis indicates that the effect is more pronounced in central provinces, regions with less stringent environmental regulation, and provinces with more developed digital infrastructure. This study connects digital–real economy integration with multi-dimensional green coordinated development by explaining how the integration depth and boundary conditions shape the environmental and economic synergistic outcomes.

title: ENGINEERING LEGISLATIVE AND ECONOMIC POWER A Comparative Study in Political Economy, Constitutional Law, and Finance in the Multipolar World
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This monograph examines the intersection of constitutional law, political economy, and financial engineering in the contemporary multipolar world. Rejecting the post-Cold War convergence thesis, it identifies three distinct "Economic Consti
content: This monograph examines the intersection of constitutional law, political economy, and financial engineering in the contemporary multipolar world. Rejecting the post-Cold War convergence thesis, it identifies three distinct "Economic Constitutions": the US model of capital sovereignty and extraterritorial jurisdiction; the EU model of regulatory sovereignty and the Brussels Effect; and the Asian model of developmental state capitalism. Employing comparative constitutional analysis, institutional political economy, and geopolitical gameThis monograph establishes a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding the intersection of constitutional law, political economy, and financial engineering in the contemporary multipolar world. Challenging the post-Cold War narrative of convergent liberal market economies, it posits the existence of distinct "Economic Constitutions": the flexible, capital-sovereign model of the United States; the regulatory, normative-power model of the European Union; and the instrumental, developmental-state model of Asia. Employing an interdisciplinary methodology synthesizing comparative constitutional law, institutional political economy, and geopolitical game theory, the study deconstructs how law functions not as a neutral market referee but as the primary architectural tool of capital accumulation and geopolitical statecraft. Through rigorous analysis of legislative architectures, landmark jurisprudence, and financial mechanisms, it examines critical arenas of modern conflict: the governance of artificial intelligence and data, the weaponization of interdependence in semiconductor supply chains, the extraterritorial reach of financial sanctions, and the legal engineering of the green transition. The work culminates in a novel theoretical synthesis of the emerging multipolar legal order, providing policymakers, jurists, and scholars with an advanced analytical toolkit to navigate the fragmentation of global economic governance. It argues that hegemony in the twenty-first century depends not merely on capital volume but on the sophistication of legislative and juridical engineering, offering a definitive reference for understanding the new rules of global power.

title: Understanding blockchain adoption in supply chains through institutional forces, fashion waves, and leadership mediation
summary: Abstract Although blockchain has been widely promoted as a transformative technology for supply chains, its widespread adoption has not met expectations. High-profile initiatives such as TradeLens were ultimately discontinued, highlighting
content: Abstract Although blockchain has been widely promoted as a transformative technology for supply chains, its widespread adoption has not met expectations. High-profile initiatives such as TradeLens were ultimately discontinued, highlighting persistent challenges and limited industry-wide adoption. To better understand this pattern, we examine blockchain adoption through a different theoretical lens—framing it as a bandwagon process shaped by institutional forces and management fashion and exploring how top management support translates external pressures into firm-level decisions. Based on survey data from 320 U.S. managers with direct blockchain experience and strategic decision-making roles, the study offers insights from those directly involved in the adoption process. The structural equation modeling results indicate that coercive pressure, mimetic pressures, fashion setters’ influence, and perceived technological progressiveness all significantly influence adoption decisions. Top management support partially mediates coercive and fashion-driven pressures but does not mediate mimetic or normative pressures. These findings suggest that during early adoption stages, legitimacy-seeking and symbolic motivations often outweigh efficiency-driven considerations. This study contributes in two important ways. First, it is the earliest effort to integrate social contagion and management fashion perspectives to explain blockchain adoption in supply chains. Second, it reconceptualizes top management support as a mediating mechanism rather than a straightforward antecedent. Overall, the study enriches theory on technology diffusion under uncertainty and underscores the need for practitioners to carefully evaluate hype-driven pressures while leveraging leadership commitment to convert symbolic adoption into meaningful, value-creating implementation.

title: Supply Chain Agility mediates the Influence of Supply Chain Integration, Supply Chain Visibility and Digital Transformation on Supply Chain Performance
source: Dinasti International Journal of Education Management And Social Science
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of supply chain integration, supply chain visibility, and digital transformation on supply chain performance, with supply chain agility as a mediating variable in Indonesian companies and the logisti
content: This study aims to analyze the influence of supply chain integration, supply chain visibility, and digital transformation on supply chain performance, with supply chain agility as a mediating variable in Indonesian companies and the logistics industry. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed through a literature review of 60 scientific articles published between 2021 and 2026, sourced from Springer, Wiley, ProQuest, Emerald, Taylor & Francis, Sage, SINTA, Copernicus, and Google Scholar. Data analysis involved reduction, descriptive and comparative presentation, and synthesis of research findings. The results indicate that supply chain integration, visibility, and digital transformation positively influence supply chain agility and performance. Furthermore, supply chain agility contributes to improved supply chain performance. The findings also demonstrate that supply chain agility mediates the relationships between supply chain integration, visibility, digital transformation, and supply chain performance. This study highlights the importance of integrating supply chain processes, enhancing information visibility, and adopting digital technologies to strengthen organizational agility and improve supply chain performance in Indonesia's logistics sector.

title: Synchronised Exuberance or Contagion? Date-Stamping and Validating Speculative Bubbles Across Cryptocurrencies and Energy-Transition Assets
summary: This study examines whether speculative bubbles in cryptocurrency markets are transmitted to the assets that finance the energy transition, or whether both segments respond to common drivers. Using freely available weekly and daily data fro
content: This study examines whether speculative bubbles in cryptocurrency markets are transmitted to the assets that finance the energy transition, or whether both segments respond to common drivers. Using freely available weekly and daily data from January 2020 to September 2026, it applies the generalised sup ADF procedure with Monte Carlo and wild-bootstrap critical values, separates global explosiveness, exploratory local crossings and independently validated bubbles, and benchmarks the dating against ex-ante log-periodic power-law singularity (LPPLS) diagnostics and ε-drawdown target events. Synchronisation, causality and dynamic probit tests are calibrated by circular-shift, bootstrap and simulation designs and conditioned on measured common factors. Only Bitcoin’s 2020–2021 run-up survives family-wise control; validated bubbles occur in Bitcoin, Ether and clean-energy equities in 2020–2021 and in battery equities in 2025–2026. Crypto and clean-energy exuberance overlapped in a single joint episode, but the overlap is not significant after multiplicity correction, and no specification shows crypto exuberance predicting green exuberance; the 2017 crypto bubble and the 2024 crypto exuberance had no green counterpart. Detection power is limited and lead–lag orderings are not robust. The evidence rejects crypto-to-green contagion but does not identify a common driver, and is best read as a descriptive account of one shared episode.

title: PIML-Driven Spatial Optimization and Active Telemetry Control of Integrated Grey-Green Systems to Minimize Modernization Capital Investment in US Combined Sewer Systems
summary: Abstract Combined sewer overflow (CSO) mitigation requires reliable hydraulic prediction and cost-effective infrastructure planning. This study develops a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework integrating surrogate modelling, r
content: Abstract Combined sewer overflow (CSO) mitigation requires reliable hydraulic prediction and cost-effective infrastructure planning. This study develops a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework integrating surrogate modelling, real-time control (RTC), and spatial green-grey infrastructure optimization to minimize capital investment in combined sewer systems. The framework was evaluated using the 11.7-ha EPA SWMM Example 8 benchmark, NOAA Atlas 14 design storms, and 20 years of hourly rainfall data from Philadelphia. Data-driven and physics-informed surrogates were compared through one-step prediction, closed-loop rollout, and extreme-storm evaluation. Rule-based control (RBC) and model predictive control (MPC) were assessed across 15 design storms, while NSGA-II optimized infrastructure configurations and capital costs. PIML-soft achieved a CSO-flow rollout NSE of 0.87 under test conditions and 0.93 for withheld 25-100-year storms, outperforming the data-only MLP in extended prediction. RBC reduced CSO volume by 5–29% relative to passive operation and outperformed the tested MPC configurations. The selected GI-led design, comprising 38 bioretention units and 6,000 gallons of residual storage, reduced modal capital cost from $0.87 million to $0.49 million compared with grey-only storage. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrated PIML and spatial optimization for benchmark-specific, cost-effective CSO management.

title: Bankruptcy law for the space sector—Legal and geopolitical issues
summary: Abstract The SpaceX IPO (Initial Public Offering), amongst other things, brought attention to the space sector. However, there is so much more going on within the space sector outside the public markets. It is a nascent sector and has a lot
content: Abstract The SpaceX IPO (Initial Public Offering), amongst other things, brought attention to the space sector. However, there is so much more going on within the space sector outside the public markets. It is a nascent sector and has a lot of small start‐ups alongside the big space companies. In a highly innovative and growing sector like this, bankruptcy considerations are significant. This article argues that getting bankruptcy law for this industry right is an important, but often overlooked, consideration for States that are looking to facilitate the growth of New Space (private space companies) and to attract and retain innovation and talent in this area, while also addressing issues of national security and geopolitics. To that end, this article provides an analysis of the various issues at stake (taking off from where international scholars left off) and provides a set of recommendations that States and other actors might draw on and apply to their specific jurisdiction. Many of the issues dealt with in this article are new and still developing, and so this is an introductory article on the topic and an invitation for further research.

title: Will It Form a Glass? Tackling Glass Formation Using Binary Classification
source: International Journal of Applied Glass Science
summary: ABSTRACT Glass formation is one of the most important and fundamental open problems in glass science. Predicting whether a liquid will form a glass appears simple but is considerably complex. In this work, we address glass formation in inor
content: ABSTRACT Glass formation is one of the most important and fundamental open problems in glass science. Predicting whether a liquid will form a glass appears simple but is considerably complex. In this work, we address glass formation in inorganic nonmetallic liquids using binary classification to predict the probability that a given liquid will form a glass under typical laboratory conditions. Using a dataset of more than 50 000 experimental observations, we trained random forest classifiers that achieved ROC–AUC values of 0.87 and macro‐averaged PR‐AUC of 0.85 on the holdout dataset (i.e., unseen data). Model selection included hyperparameter optimization with Bayesian search and cross‐validation. Two feature representations were evaluated: raw atomic fractions and physicochemical descriptors derived from the compositions. The models are well‐calibrated, enabling users to adjust the decision threshold to balance false‐positive and false‐negative rates according to their specific application. Using SHAP values, we extracted valuable insights from the trained models that are consistent with established glass science and provide new empirical insights. For example, we identified that the weighted sum of DFT bandgap energy of the constituent elements is positively correlated with glass formation, a finding consistent with the electronic character of known network‐forming elements. This result is particularly relevant for composition screening, especially in inverse design problems. The collection of models developed in this work is free software and was named VITRIFY ( Vitrification Inference Tool for Rapid Identification of glass‐Forming abilitY ).

title: Explainability Metrics for Object Detection Models
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: Object detection models based on deep learning achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in many applications, but their predictions are difficult to interpret. Existing explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for computer vision mostl
content: Object detection models based on deep learning achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in many applications, but their predictions are difficult to interpret. Existing explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for computer vision mostly focus on image classification, and their direct extension to object detection is non-trivial, as detectors must explain both what was detected (class) and where it was detected (bounding box). In this paper, we revisit perturbation-based saliency methods for object detection, with a particular focus on D-RISE, a popular model-agnostic technique. We highlight practical limitations of D-RISE, particularly the absence of a detector-specific importance score aligned with detection performance. We then propose a novel detection-loss based explainability score that quantifies the importance of each image region through the deterioration of the detector’s loss under random masking. The proposed score jointly accounts for classification confidence and localisation quality, and it is normalised to be in [0, 1], providing an interpretable per-pixel importance measure. The proposed score is evaluated on three datasets covering industrial and general-object detection scenarios. In addition to qualitative visualization, we report object-level explainability statistics and deletion-based fidelity analysis to assess the alignment between highlighted regions and detection confidence. The results indicate that the proposed $$\varDelta $$ -based scoring method produces consistent and interpretable saliency maps that are directly linked to changes in detection loss. Overall, the proposed approach establishes a principled link between visual explanations and detection performance, and paves the way for robust, quantitative comparison of XAI methods for object detection.

title: Agency mismatches limit the realised impact of water conservation measures
summary: Abstract Water conservation is usually catalogued by technology – efficient fixtures, leak control, reuse, metering, process integration. That framing hides a stubborn fact: realised savings consistently fall short of engineering potential
content: Abstract Water conservation is usually catalogued by technology – efficient fixtures, leak control, reuse, metering, process integration. That framing hides a stubborn fact: realised savings consistently fall short of engineering potential and often fade with time. Rebound, poor maintenance and behavioural decay explain part of the gap, but not all. A further share is an agency mismatch: the actor who would benefit from a measure lacks the authority, capacity and incentive to deploy it, while the actor who holds them does not benefit. That mismatch is not a new discovery – it is well documented in energy-efficiency and institutional-resource research – but it has not been systematically mapped for water conservation. Using the Scandinavian concept of rådighet (agency), separated here into capability (authority and capacity) and incentive alignment (motivation), I code water-conservation measures against the actors holding primary and secondary agency, and against how quickly each agency-holder can actually act. Clear patterns emerge: agency is concentrated for network measures and fragmented for building-scale ones; the largest potentials sit with the weakest-agency actors; concentrated agency and short latency rarely coincide outside the utility itself; and standards, pricing and digital infrastructure act as agency bridges. Two Swedish field trials illustrate why misaligned agency undermines otherwise sound technology, and the framework sets out what an agency-first approach means for policy.

title: Rights Without Remedies: Bundled Causation and the Legislative-Branch Whistleblower Gap
summary: Employees of the Library of Congress occupy an unusual position in American employment law. They are protected against reprisal for opposing discrimination by the Congressional Accountability Act (CAA), and they are protected by statute aga
content: Employees of the Library of Congress occupy an unusual position in American employment law. They are protected against reprisal for opposing discrimination by the Congressional Accountability Act (CAA), and they are protected by statute against reprisal for reporting to the Library’s Inspector General. But only the first protection comes with a forum and a remedy. This article studies that asymmetry with formal tools and uses the recent case of Dines v. Office of Congressional Workplace Rights as a worked example. The case went through a Merits Hearing Officer, the Board of the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, which affirmed without opinion under its Rule 36. The article makes four contributions. First, it models the right–remedy structure of legislative-branch employment law as a mapping from protected acts to enforcement channels. It proves that disclosures to an Inspector General fall into a statutory remedial gap and shows that the gap removes deterrence in a Becker-type enforcement model. Second, it gives a structural-causal analysis of employer reasons stated as an undifferentiated aggregate, such as “disruptive behavior,” that contains protected and unprotected conduct together. A finding that such an aggregate reason was legitimate and genuine does not, by itself, settle whether protected activity was a but-for cause of the decision. A separate finding that the unprotected residue alone was sufficient does. Third, it shows that when employers can bundle reasons and adjudicators accept bundled reasons, the deterrent effect of anti-reprisal law falls in proportion. Fourth, it models certiorari review of an unexplained affirmance as a vehicle problem: the chance that winning the question presented changes the outcome is bounded by the product of the failure probabilities of every alternative ground, including forfeiture. Public data illustrate the institutional setting: Supreme Court filings fell from 8,857 in the 2006 Term to 3,856 in the 2024 Term; petitions in forma pauperis fell by roughly two thirds; and Rule 36 judgments account for about 41% of the Federal Circuit’s decisions in appeals from post-grant patent proceedings. The analysis supports two conclusions. Congress should adopt the whistleblower recommendation that the OCWR Board has repeated in at least seven biennial reports. Adjudicators facing aggregate reasons should require explicit disaggregation of protected and unprotected conduct.

title: Adoption, complementarity and productivity effects of modern maize inputs in Uganda
summary: Abstract The adoption of modern agricultural inputs is a sustainable approach to productivity growth in developing countries, especially amid soil fertility decline and climate challenges. Governments have therefore prioritized access to im
content: Abstract The adoption of modern agricultural inputs is a sustainable approach to productivity growth in developing countries, especially amid soil fertility decline and climate challenges. Governments have therefore prioritized access to improved seed and inorganic fertilizers to close productivity gaps. This study investigates factors influencing modern maize input adoption among smallholder farmers in Uganda and examines the effects of input choices on productivity, using data from the World Bank–funded Agriculture Cluster Development Project. A multinomial endogenous switching regression model was used to assess the drivers and impacts of input choices. Results show that adopters of only improved maize seed had access to credit and extension services, owned livestock, experienced drought, and cultivated smaller plots. Those adopting both improved seed and fertilizer were more educated, had higher incomes, cultivated larger areas, and accessed extension services. Non-adopters had the lowest education and income levels, smallest land sizes, limited access to credit, training, market information, and were mostly engaged in non-farm work. No significant factors were found for adopting only inorganic fertilizer. In terms of productivity, adoption of modern inputs significantly increased maize yields. Farmers using both improved seed and fertilizer achieved an Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) of 735 kg/ha (185.5% increase), those using only improved seed gained 698 kg/ha (138.5%), and those using only inorganic fertilizer gained 359 kg/ha (137.8%). The study highlights the importance of strengthening education, credit, and extension systems, and improving agro-input markets to enhance complementarity and reduce productivity gaps. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study is not a clinical trial.

title: Surviving thoughts of a North Briton: Hume and the “decline and fall of the British Empire”
summary: In 1776, three events converged in British intellectual history: David Hume’s death, the American Declaration of Independence, and the publication of the first volume of Edward Gibbon’s Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire. Contemporaries j
content: In 1776, three events converged in British intellectual history: David Hume’s death, the American Declaration of Independence, and the publication of the first volume of Edward Gibbon’s Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire. Contemporaries joked that Gibbon might next chronicle Britain’s downfall. The joke provides a point of departure for examining Hume’s late political reflections and their reception among contemporary and later readers. His correspondence and revisions to Essays and The History of England reveal concerns about public credit, press liberty, and barbarism. British radicals and American colonists read these works selectively. While radical writers continued to draw on Hume’s warnings about public credit, which remained in later editions, they also quoted his earlier defence of press liberty even after he had withdrawn it, putting his arguments to political purposes he did not necessarily share. For Hume, the future of English offered a different prospect. In advising Gibbon to write in English, Hume looked to the American settlements for the language’s future and suggested that it could outlast French. His fears of political and institutional decline coexisted with an expectation that Britain’s language and literary culture might endure beyond the fortunes of the state.

title: Limited Awareness Little Action: How Limited Knowledge of the Paris Agreement Undermines Devolved Climate Governance in Nakuru County, Kenya
source: African Journal of Climate Change and Resource Sustainability
summary: This study examined the extent of awareness of the Paris Agreement and Kenya's related climate obligations among the residents, county and national officials, civil society representatives and private sector actors in Nakuru County, and how
content: This study examined the extent of awareness of the Paris Agreement and Kenya's related climate obligations among the residents, county and national officials, civil society representatives and private sector actors in Nakuru County, and how that level of awareness, or the lack of it, shapes local climate governance and public participation in climate change adaptation measures. Under Article 7, state parties to the Paris Agreement are obligated to strengthen adaptive capacity, build resilience and lower vulnerability to climate change. Delivery of these expectations in a devolved system of governance, such one in Kenya, hinges on whether the sub-national institutions and communities tasked with turning national commitments into local practice actually understand what those commitments involve. Using a descriptive, single case study design, drawing on interviews, focus group discussions with 63 purposively and snowball-sampled participants spanning six stakeholder categories and document review, this study reveal a consistent split between rich, experience-based knowledge of climate change and thin formal knowledge of the Paris Agreement as a legal and policy instrument. The level of awareness of the Paris Agreement and Kenya's related climate obligations differs markedly by stakeholder group. It is moderate and patchy among technical officers, minimal among elected leaders, and close to absent among ordinary residents, who tend to understand climate change through what they have traditionally lived rather than through international policy terminology. Rather than a simple communication shortfall, this study argues that the awareness gap of the Paris Agreement and Kenya's related climate obligations reflects a structural break in the communication channel connecting national policy design and the county level. This knowledge gap limits the public participation guaranteed under Article 10 of Kenya's Constitution and negates states' gains against the country-driven adaptation process envisioned in Article 7 of the Paris Agreement. This study recommends embedding of climate change adaptation measures in communication within devolved governance structures in Nakuru County through; institutionalised local climate communication, prioritising awareness among elected leaders, funding awareness-raising as a standing County function, localising but not merely disseminating national policy content on climate change adaptation, drawing on and utilising existing community structures, and tracking levels of awareness of climate change adaptation among citizens as a standing governance indicator of National Determined Contributions (NDC).

title: Beyond access and survival: an equity-centered framework for supportive-care outcomes in childhood, adolescent, and young adult oncology
summary: Background Equity research in childhood, adolescent, and young adult (CAYA) oncology has traditionally emphasized diagnosis, treatment access, clinical-trial participation, treatment delivery, and survival. These outcomes are essential but
content: Background Equity research in childhood, adolescent, and young adult (CAYA) oncology has traditionally emphasized diagnosis, treatment access, clinical-trial participation, treatment delivery, and survival. These outcomes are essential but do not fully capture patients’ supportive-care experiences. This review evaluates supportive-care equity and proposes an equity-centered measurement framework. Methods We conducted a focused narrative review of childhood and AYA oncology literature addressing symptom and toxicity burden, financial hardship, psychosocial and palliative care, unplanned acute care, survivorship, social determinants of health, and patient-reported outcomes. Evidence was synthesized by supportive-care domain, multilevel determinants, care processes, measurement considerations, and longitudinal applicability. Results Group differences have been reported across selected supportive-care-sensitive outcomes, including toxicity-related utilization, guideline-concordant care, financial hardship, palliative-care processes, acute-care disposition, and survivorship engagement, although findings are heterogeneous and predominantly observational. Measurement itself is equity-sensitive: child, caregiver, and clinician reports are not interchangeable; language, literacy, and instrument selection influence participation and interpretation; neighborhood proxies incompletely represent household conditions; and missing patient-reported outcomes may be socially patterned. For AYAs, developmentally salient domains include fertility, financial security, education, employment, and independence. We propose an evidence-informed, hypothesis-generating framework linking structural and social context, access and care processes, supportive-care outcomes, and longitudinal outcomes, with measurement operating as a cross-cutting layer. Conclusions Supportive-care equity should be evaluated as both a clinical-outcomes and measurement problem. Future studies should use patient- and family-reported social determinants, explicit reporter and language strategies, transparent missing-data assessment, and multilevel interventions.

title: Impacto de la estrategia empresarial a través de la gestión de conocimiento en la industria automotriz: revisión sistemática de literatura
source: LATAM Revista Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales y Humanidades
summary: La industria automotriz experimenta cambios operativos y ambientales que demandan una reestructuración, donde obtener y utilizar la información de manera eficiente se convierte en un desafío para mantenerse vigente. Dando solución a esta pr
content: La industria automotriz experimenta cambios operativos y ambientales que demandan una reestructuración, donde obtener y utilizar la información de manera eficiente se convierte en un desafío para mantenerse vigente. Dando solución a esta problemática, el objetivo de este artículo es establecer de qué manera influye la gestión del conocimiento a la estrategia empresarial en la manufactura automotriz, bajo los estudios de las obras literarias científica existentes. Para lograrlo, se adelantó una exploración metodología de la literatura basada en la orientación del protocolo PRISMA, en el que se evaluaron 93 documentos encontrados en la colección Scopus. Estos datos obtenidos evidencian cómo el conocimiento orienta las elecciones estratégicas sobre dos áreas orientadas a la gestión: la implementación de modelos de manufactura sostenible y la mejora constante de la flexibilidad operativa para suplir las demandas del sector, facilitando la integración de nuevas tecnologías y herramientas. Al final se concluye que el capital intelectual se consolida como una ventaja competitiva, al dominar el conocimiento sobre estrategia corporativa.

title: Rice Protein Concentrate Ball Milling: Particle Size Reduction Kinetics, Techno‐Functional Properties, and Pepsin Hydrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Background and Objectives Rice protein is a nutritious and hypoallergenic ingredient; however, its low solubility limits functionality. Ball milling offers a chemical‐free modification strategy, although its milling kinetics and ef
content: ABSTRACT Background and Objectives Rice protein is a nutritious and hypoallergenic ingredient; however, its low solubility limits functionality. Ball milling offers a chemical‐free modification strategy, although its milling kinetics and effects on enzymatic hydrolysis remain poorly understood. This study evaluated ball‐milling particle size reduction kinetics at 600 and 900 rpm, and its effects on techno‐functional properties and pepsin hydrolysis of rice protein concentrate. Findings Ball milling at 600 rpm led to higher milling efficiency, decreasing the particle size D50 from 9 to 7 μm. The protein solubility, water retention, and oil retention index increased by up to 112.3%, 21%, and 54%, respectively. No changes were observed in color, moisture, or water activity. Ball‐milled samples showed a higher degree of hydrolysis determined by the pH‐stat method (3.54%–3.70%) compared to the control (2.35%), and similar enzymatic kinetic rate constants. Conclusions Physical modification by ball milling is an effective strategy to improve the techno‐functional properties and pepsin digestibility of rice protein concentrate, increasing its potential for food applications. Significance and Novelty This study demonstrates the potential of ball milling to improve rice protein functionality and digestibility while providing new insights into particle size reduction and enzymatic hydrolysis kinetics, supporting its broader application in food formulations.

title: Whose priorities? Media reporting and the output legitimacy of International Organizations
summary: Abstract Traditional accounts of output legitimacy emphasize that support for multipurpose international organizations (IOs) depends on their ability to deliver effective policies. We argue that legitimacy beliefs also hinge on which polici
content: Abstract Traditional accounts of output legitimacy emphasize that support for multipurpose international organizations (IOs) depends on their ability to deliver effective policies. We argue that legitimacy beliefs also hinge on which policies IOs are perceived to prioritize, and that media reporting on the policy focus of international organizations plays an important role in this process. Such reporting can shape legitimacy beliefs by influencing the extent to which citizens perceive an IO’s policy output to align with their own ideological preferences. Using the European Union as a test case, we analyze over 400,000 news articles from Austria, France, Germany, and Spain with semi-supervised machine learning to identify issue emphasis. We link this to Eurobarometer survey data capturing individual-level assessments of the EU’s output legitimacy. We find that citizens tend to evaluate the EU more positively when media coverage highlights policy areas aligned with their ideology. These findings suggest that citizens judge IOs not only by how well they perform, but also by whose priorities they are perceived to serve.

title: Purinergic Imbalance and Adenosinergic Modulation of Antibacterial Activity in Severe COVID-19 and Sepsis
summary: Abstract Sepsis and immunosuppression are major contributors to mortality in the intensive care unit. This study investigated dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly systemic adenosine alterations, in relation to biomarkers and impa
content: Abstract Sepsis and immunosuppression are major contributors to mortality in the intensive care unit. This study investigated dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly systemic adenosine alterations, in relation to biomarkers and impaired antibacterial activity in severe COVID-19 and sepsis. Peripheral blood samples from COVID-19 patients at different disease stages were analyzed. Plasma purine levels were quantified by LC-MS/MS. To assess the functional effects of patient plasma, PBMCs from healthy donors were incubated with plasma from severe COVID-19 patients, resulting in increased CD39, PD-1, and KLRG1 and reduced CD73, CD28, and CD127 expression on T cells. Antibacterial activity was assessed in vitro using healthy-donor monocytes and RAW 264.7 macrophages exposed to patient plasma and challenged with GFP-expressing Escherichia coli (OP50-GFP). At hospital admission, ATP was lower, and AMP was higher in SARS-CoV-2-negative pneumonia and non-ICU and ICU COVID-19 patients than in healthy controls, whereas adenosine was lower in both COVID-19 groups. Longitudinally, nonsurvivors showed decreased ATP and increased adenosine from T1 to T2, with higher Δadenosine and lower ΔATP than survivors. Among septic patients, adenosine was higher in nonsurvivors. In vitro, cells exposed to plasma from septic ICU patients exhibited lower antibacterial activity. Adenosine and the A1/A2A antagonists DPCPX and ZM 241385 further supported a role for adenosinergic signaling: adenosine alone or combined with DPCPX reduced antibacterial activity, whereas DPCPX alone increased it. Overall, dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly altered adenosine dynamics, may contribute to impaired antibacterial defense and immune dysfunction in severe COVID-19, with circulating plasma factors potentially increasing susceptibility to secondary infections.

title: Responsibility and Accountability in Maritime Law: Criminalisation of the Ship’s Master
summary: Responsibility Accountability Maritime Law examines the phenomenon of criminalisation which confronts the Master in their professional conduct, both in terms of Flag State and Port State rights and obligations. The fault lines of criminalis
content: Responsibility Accountability Maritime Law examines the phenomenon of criminalisation which confronts the Master in their professional conduct, both in terms of Flag State and Port State rights and obligations. The fault lines of criminalisation, which go to the heart of the question, demand an understanding of how the concept of criminal justice has evolved to impose accountability on the Master, in circumstances which had not been crimes before. Since this book was first published, the maritime world has changed dramatically, requiring a new understanding of responsibility and accountability before the Master can make rational decisions to respond to the risk of criminalisation. While the basic theory of accountability for criminalisation and the sources of law provide the foundation, this second edition presents a new introduction to summarise the necessity for changes in structure in order to define the pre-existing law with which the Master must comply, acknowledging the re-emergence of risk in the Gulf in 2026, and the foreseeable emergence of risk in the Arctic as geopolitical pressures create uncertainty as to who will assert jurisdictional control in the management of merchant shipping in this region. The Sources of Law chapter has been expanded to address risk management in the context of current geopolitical turmoil, balancing company commitments with the safety of the ship and crew. New content includes detention of Masters and crew, the International Convention on Arrest of Ships, universal jurisdiction, and relevant case studies such as the M/T Heroic Idun. The book’s format meets the needs of lawyers, academics and maritime professionals, with the aim of analysing the character of criminalisation to determine the features which characterise the phenomenon in Port and Flag State contexts; it interrogates the aim to define the nature of criminalisation and identifies the constituent problems in such criminal accountability. Each chapter relies heavily on case studies to illustrate how the laws which reflect national policy underpinning those priorities are applied in practice. This structure enables an understanding of the problems in the criminal process, with a view to offering options for solutions. The book is directly relevant to a broad range of parties which includes lawyers, academics, P & I clubs, seafarers, shipowners, managers and agents, and national and international seafaring unions. The current law and cases have been verified up to June 2026.

title: L ANALYSE DE L EFFET DES CRITERES ESG SUR LA CREATION DE LA VALEUR FINANCIERE : ETUDE ECONOMETRIQUE SUR LE MARCHE DES ACTIONS DE CASABLANCA
summary: His article examines the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria on the financial performance of companies listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange. The methodological approach is based on a cross-sectional linear regre
content: His article examines the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria on the financial performance of companies listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange. The methodological approach is based on a cross-sectional linear regression model, estimated using the ordinary least squares (OLS) method. The empirical results reveal no significant relationship between the integration of ESG criteria - whether in terms of the overall score or the individual ESG dimensions - and financial performance as measured by return on assets (ROA). By contrast, the sector of activity appears to be a determining factor in this performance, with manufacturing and services showing higher profitability. These results can be explained, on the one hand, by the fact that the effect of ESG criteria is primarily evident in the long term and, on the other hand, by the failure of stock market investors to take these dimensions into account, as they prioritise immediate financial profitability, regardless of the company’s non-financial profile.

title: A Brief Oral History of Fossil Fuel Divestment (An interview with Bill McKibben)
summary: We cannot overstate the significance of journalist and environmental activist Bill McKibben to the fight against the climate crisis.McKibben's book The End of Nature (1989), the first publicly facing book on the crisis, appeared just as cli
content: We cannot overstate the significance of journalist and environmental activist Bill McKibben to the fight against the climate crisis.McKibben's book The End of Nature (1989), the first publicly facing book on the crisis, appeared just as climate change began to emerge as an issue in US politics.Twenty subsequent books, along with influential articles in venues such as The New Yorker and Rolling Stone, have propelled climate change into the public view.He serves as the Schumann Distinguished Scholar in Environmental Studies at Middlebury College, where with his students he founded 350 .org, a climate action group that was instrumental in coordinating a global upsurge of climate protests.These included the successful civil disobedience campaign against the Keystone XL Pipeline Proj ect in the US and the New York People's Climate March (2014), which helped push for greater ambition in the Paris Agreement.His current proj ects include Third Act, a group he helped found, which organizes climate action among people over the age of sixty, and a Substack newsletter, "The Crucial Years."As we considered oil money and the sustainable acad emy for this volume, we asked him to help us think about another impor tant initiative: the fossil fuel divestment campaign, which he launched on college campuses starting in 2011.(Full disclosure: It was his visit to Dickinson College in 2012, as Rose-Walters Prize winner, that recruited one of our coeditors to climate work.)Since 2011, according to the Global Fossil Fuel Commitments Database, institutions with investments totaling $40.76 trillion have divested from fossil fuels.More than $6 trillion of that comes from educational institutions.Emily Pawley: Could you start by giving us a quick sense of what the climate movement looked like to you and your students at Middlebury, just before the divestment movement started?What prompted the turn to a divestment campaign as a strategy?

title: The Impact of Transferrable Development Rights on Rural–Urban Migration in China: Evidence From Chongqing's Land Quotas Trading Programme
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how construction land institutional reform affects the reallocation of rural labour. We study Chongqing's Land Quotas Trading (LQT) programme, a government‐guided market system for trading transferable developme
content: ABSTRACT This study examines how construction land institutional reform affects the reallocation of rural labour. We study Chongqing's Land Quotas Trading (LQT) programme, a government‐guided market system for trading transferable development rights, utilizing rural household surveys from the Chinese Household Income Project (CHIP) in 2002, 2008, 2013 and 2018, together with county‐ and city‐level data. Using a difference‐in‐differences (DID) approach, we find that the LQT programme significantly increased rural–urban migration, both extensively and intensively. We further find that the alleviation of liquidity constraints, the suppression of housing prices and the expansion of the urban economy are potential mechanisms through which these effects operate. Further analysis shows that the programme increased labour devoted to migrant and local non‐agricultural work while reducing agricultural labour, accompanied by higher household non‐agricultural income and living consumption. These findings suggest that construction land institutional reform can facilitate rural labour reallocation towards non‐agricultural activities, while its potential implications for agricultural production and rural land use warrant further attention.

title: The role of GABAergic inhibitory neurons in psychiatric disorders: insights from cellular and genomic studies
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: The excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance is fundamental for proper neural circuit function, and its disruption has emerged as a convergent mechanism across multiple psychiatric disorders. Primarily, GABAergic inhibitory neurons play essentia
content: The excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance is fundamental for proper neural circuit function, and its disruption has emerged as a convergent mechanism across multiple psychiatric disorders. Primarily, GABAergic inhibitory neurons play essential roles in regulating network dynamics, necessary for physiological, cognitive and emotional processing. This review synthesizes current evidence from genetic, epigenetic, transcriptomic, and cellular studies implicating GABAergic neuron dysfunction in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), major depressive disorder (MDD), schizophrenia (SCZ), and bipolar disorder (BD). We first define the E/I balance and its functional implications for neural circuit dynamics and define the main GABAergic subtypes: Parvalbumin (PVALB), Somatostatin (SST), Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide neurons (VIP) and Lysosomal Associated Membrane Protein Family Member 5/Paired Box 6 positive GABAergic neurons (LAMP5/PAX6+). We then examine GABAergic involvement across distinct neurodevelopmental phases, highlighting critical windows of vulnerability where perturbations can produce lasting consequences. Subsequently, we synthesize and discuss disorder-specific evidence across ASD, MDD, SCZ, and BD, which share substantial clinical overlap and converging genetic architectures. High-resolution single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approaches have fundamentally transformed our understanding, revealing that rather than a uniform global deficit, these conditions exhibit localized, cell-type-specific dysregulations that target distinct interneuron subpopulations in a region- and disorder-dependent manner. Methodological advances now enable integration of genomic risk with cell-type-specific transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles, though challenges remain in translating these findings to clinical applications. Despite promising preclinical evidence, clinical trials targeting GABAergic signaling have yielded mixed results, underscoring the complexity of inhibitory circuit dysfunction and the need for more precise, subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Leveraging these high-resolution, multi-omic insights holds significant promise for refining psychiatric nosology, discovering reliable biomarkers, and advancing targeted therapeutics and personalized medicine.

title: The Silent Leadership Algorithm: AI as a Strategic Partner for Sustained Growth
summary: The Silent Leadership Algorithm is an essential guide for executives and managers confronting the realities of AI integration in today’s fast-moving business environment. Rather than framing AI as a technical challenge alone, this book show
content: The Silent Leadership Algorithm is an essential guide for executives and managers confronting the realities of AI integration in today’s fast-moving business environment. Rather than framing AI as a technical challenge alone, this book shows leaders how to translate complex decisions into clear, human-centered strategy. Through the powerful WHO–HOW–WHAT–WHY framework, readers learn how to pair AI’s speed, scale, and predictive capabilities with the judgment, restraint, and emotional intelligence required to lead effectively across global, culturally diverse teams. Designed with both senior leaders and operational managers in mind, the book provides practical value at every level of the organization. It demonstrates how to leverage AI to enhance decision quality, identify high-potential talent, reduce bias, and strengthen cross-border coordination while maintaining trust and legitimacy with employees and stakeholders. By integrating micro-level leadership skills such as reflective listening and emotional regulation with macro-level applications such as supply chain optimization and strategic alignment, the authors provide a clear roadmap for turning AI adoption into measurable performance gains rather than organizational friction. At a time when many leaders struggle to balance technological acceleration with human expectations, The Silent Leadership Algorithm offers a distinct competitive advantage: a model for leading quietly yet decisively. It equips executives to move beyond reactive, technology-driven decisions and instead build resilient, purpose-driven organizations where AI enhances but does not replace human insight. For leaders seeking to navigate AI transformation with confidence, precision, and credibility, this book provides both the mindset and the methods to achieve sustained growth.

title: Promotion incentives for local officials and high quality urban economic development
source: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
summary: Promotion incentives influence local policy choices, but their relationship with multidimensional urban development remains insufficiently understood. Using 3,552 city-year observations for 296 Chinese cities during 2012-2023, this study co
content: Promotion incentives influence local policy choices, but their relationship with multidimensional urban development remains insufficiently understood. Using 3,552 city-year observations for 296 Chinese cities during 2012-2023, this study constructs a promotion incentive index from relative growth, fiscal surplus, and employment performance. High-quality development is measured across innovation, coordination, openness, green development, and shared development. Two-way fixed-effects estimates yield a positive coefficient of 0.0705, significant at the 1% level. This association persists under alternative outcome measures, samples, and controls. Government policy attention, firm entry, and factor allocation efficiency are positively associated with promotion incentives, consistent with the proposed channels. Positive estimates also appear across regional and temporal subsamples and all five development dimensions. City-level wild bootstrap tests support two development thresholds, with the incremental second-threshold test significant at 5%. The incentive coefficients decline from 0.0979 to 0.0676 and 0.0461 across increasing income regimes. These findings indicate that the relationship between promotion incentives and urban development quality varies with cities' economic development levels.

title: Co-developing a human wellbeing-centered, socio-economic framework for small-scale fisheries: The Bahamas’ Nassau grouper fishery as a case study
summary: Most fisheries assessments focus on stock status and economic output but say little about the lived experiences of fishing communities, the cultural value of fisheries, or the governance conditions that decide whether regulations work. Guid
content: Most fisheries assessments focus on stock status and economic output but say little about the lived experiences of fishing communities, the cultural value of fisheries, or the governance conditions that decide whether regulations work. Guidance for broader socio-economic monitoring exists, but no single set of indicators fits every fishery; it has to be worked out in context, with the people whose wellbeing is being measured. Less is known about how this is done in practice. We describe, step by step, how general monitoring guidance was adapted with stakeholders into a wellbeing-centered, socio-economic framework for The Bahamas’ domestic fisheries, using the critically endangered Nassau grouper ( Epinephelus striatus ) as a case study. Twenty-eight participants from government, non-governmental organizations, research, and the value chain took part through meetings, surveys, a hybrid workshop, and interviews. Together they defined the scope, confirmed six wellbeing domains and prioritized 6 research themes. The resulting framework (Framework V01) contains 59 indicators across 20 attributes, including indicators of readiness for a prospective national seafood labeling program. We report the criteria used to select attributes and indicators and the minimum standards set for inclusive participation. T Participation was uneven, which shaped the framework and is discussed as a limitation. Framework V01 has not yet been tested in the field. Its content is specific to The Bahamas, but the documented process, including its compromises, offers a practical reference for others adapting wellbeing monitoring to their own fisheries.

title: BIABooster-based characterization of the cell-free DNA fragmentome in healthy adult blood donors reveals stable reference profiles and pre-analytical influences
summary: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a versatile biomarker in oncology, prenatal testing, and organ transplantation. Although cfDNA concentration and genomic markers are widely used, its fragment size distribution (fragmentome) offers addit
content: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a versatile biomarker in oncology, prenatal testing, and organ transplantation. Although cfDNA concentration and genomic markers are widely used, its fragment size distribution (fragmentome) offers additional diagnostic potential. However, robust reference profiles for healthy individuals—particularly for fragments exceeding 300 bp—remain lacking. We used the BIABooster system to analyse cfDNA from 240 healthy adult blood donors, collected in two French cities of different climate at four different time points over a one-year period. cfDNA concentration and size distribution up to 1650 bp were measured and synthesised in 10 concentration and size descriptors. Potential correlations with demographic and haematological parameters were assessed. For selected samples, cfDNA was also analysed up to 10 kb, and the impact of an end-repair step was investigated. cfDNA size profiles were highly consistent across collection sites and time points and were not significantly affected by the demographic and haematological parameters investigated. In particular, the relative abundances of mono- and di-nucleosomal cfDNA fractions were remarkably stable across individuals. Analysis of longer cfDNA fragments revealed an unexpected peak around 3.2 kb that appeared to depend on pre-analytical conditions. This study establishes a detailed characterisation cfDNA fragmentation profiles in healthy adult blood donors and highlights their limited variability across geographic, temporal, demographic and common haematological parameters. It also demonstrates that pre-analytical conditions, particularly blood collection procedures, can influence specific fragmentome features and should therefore be carefully considered when developing cfDNA size profiling for clinical applications.

title: Decoupling Contamination Detection from Classification Accuracy: A Confidence-based Triage Framework with Explainable AI for Water Quality Monitoring
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Binary classification is the standard approach in machine learning-based water quality monitoring, but its false negative rates remain a practical concern-contaminated samples misclassified as safe go undetected.This study applies selective
content: Binary classification is the standard approach in machine learning-based water quality monitoring, but its false negative rates remain a practical concern-contaminated samples misclassified as safe go undetected.This study applies selective prediction to water potability screening and characterises the resulting Accuracy-Safety Decoupling, demonstrating that contamination detection can be substantially improved independently of overall classification accuracy through a confidence-based triage framework.Rather than relying on binary decision boundaries, the framework sorts predictions into safe, uncertain, and contaminated zones using dual probability thresholds, directing uncertain cases to human review instead of automatic clearance.A Random Forest classifier was trained on 46 features engineered from 15 physicochemical parameters in a synthetic water quality dataset of 2,500 samples generated under controlled conditions to isolate framework performance from dataset-specific artifacts.The model achieved 79.2% accuracy and 86.79% ROC-AUC.The triage system raised the contamination capture rate from 75.21% to 98.3%, a triage-level measure of samples not auto-cleared as safe, an improvement confirmed by McNemar's test (χ² = 26.04,p < 0.0001), A paired risk difference of 23.14 percentage points (95% CI [15.63, 30.65]), and non-overlapping bootstrap confidence intervals.SHAP and LIME analysis showed moderate-to-strong agreement (Spearman ρ = 0.608), with chloramines, turbidity, and pH emerging as the top predictive factors.The dataset was generated under a documented parametric specification with an explicit rule-based labelling function, establishing a controlled methodological baseline against which future real-world deployments can be benchmarked.

title: AGILE У ВІДНОВЛЕННІ АРХІТЕКТУРИ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ МІСТ: ГІБРИДНА МОДЕЛЬ АДАПТИВНОГО ПУБЛІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ
summary: AGILE У ВІДНОВЛЕННІ АРХІТЕКТУРИ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ МІСТ: ГІБРИДНА МОДЕЛЬ АДАПТИВНОГО ПУБЛІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ Анотація.В статті обґрунтувати можливості перенесення цінностей і практик Agile з ІТ-середовища на відновлення архітектури українських міст
content: AGILE У ВІДНОВЛЕННІ АРХІТЕКТУРИ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ МІСТ: ГІБРИДНА МОДЕЛЬ АДАПТИВНОГО ПУБЛІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ Анотація.В статті обґрунтувати можливості перенесення цінностей і практик Agile з ІТ-середовища на відновлення архітектури українських міст та запропонувати гібридну управлінську модель, придатну для органів місцевого самоврядування, служб відновлення й територіальних громад в умовах триваючої воєнної невизначеності.Застосовано системний і порівняльний аналіз, контент-аналіз програмних і аналітичних документів (RDNA5, матеріали URC 2026, посібник KSE зі відновлення, дані системи DREAM), кейс-метод (Scrum на об'єкті в Бородянці; тактичний урбанізм Києва, Львова, Харкова; проєкт TORV) та узагальнення практик адаптивного публічного управління.Визначено, що класична каскадна модель «повний проєктпотім будівництво» втрачає дієвість там, де змінюються безпекові вимоги, демографія, донорські стандарти та фізичний стан кварталів.Обґрунтовано відповідність чотирьох цінностей Agile-маніфесту логіці відбудови.Описано чотири робочі інструменти: incremental urbanism, tactical urbanism, Scrum на окремому об'єкті та гібрид Waterfall + Scrum/Kanban на рівні портфеля громади.Запропоновано каркас із чотирьох епіків відновлення та роль органу публічної влади як власника єдиного product backlog громади.Зроблено висновки про те, що Agile не скасовує стратегію «build back better», зелене відновлення й євроінтеграцію, а змінює спосіб руху до нихчерез портфель коротких інкрементів.Реалістичний горизонт 2026-2028 рр.полягає не в скасуванні нормативної каскадності, а в узаконенні гібриду: експертиза чергами, прийняття інкрементів, тимчасові споруди як офіційна стадія, участь мешканців як user research кожного спринту.

title: Trends in the intervals between and distribution of diagnostic dental visits among adults in Denmark
summary: Before 1999, the recommended dental recall interval for adults in Denmark was 6-7 months. In 1999 and in 2013-2015, two major regulations were made aiming to increase this interval. This study analyzes the use of dental examination services
content: Before 1999, the recommended dental recall interval for adults in Denmark was 6-7 months. In 1999 and in 2013-2015, two major regulations were made aiming to increase this interval. This study analyzes the use of dental examination services for adults in Denmark over the 32-yr period from 1990 to 2021 using national registry data comprising information on 6,894,773 persons (133,811,495 person-years). Overall, 24% of the adult population did not receive a subsidized dental examination during the entire follow-up period, whereas 69% (n = 4,774,716) had at least two registered dental examinations. Median examination intervals increased slightly before 2013, increasing by about 3 months in the period 2013-2015 to 11 months, whereafter they remained stable. Examination intervals increased among 20-59-yr-olds but remained stable for older ages. Lower income, lower education, and immigrant or descendant status were associated with no dental examinations or longer examination intervals. Our analyses show that dental practices compensated for the 1999 restriction on standard examination intervals by use of control examination services, and the 2013-2015 risk-based interval reform was counteracted by increasing use of preventive and supragingival scaling services. Our findings support the notion that dentists working in a fee-for-service system have and exercise market power.

title: Prioritizing the Conservation of Pondok Pesantren as Cultural and Religious Heritage
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: The conservation of Pondok Pesantren as a cultural and religious heritage considers user perception to evaluate the technical aspects. Many building studies are based on technical aspects and rarely involve user perception. Pondok Pesantren
content: The conservation of Pondok Pesantren as a cultural and religious heritage considers user perception to evaluate the technical aspects. Many building studies are based on technical aspects and rarely involve user perception. Pondok Pesantren as an Islamic religious, educational institution was developed by a social and multicultural approach. The results of this study are used to develop maintenance and conservation priorities that benefit in the development of educational institutions, cultural preservation, economic and investment improvement, the application of sustainable buildings, and the development of educational and religious tourism.This research determines the priority of conservation and maintenance efforts at Pondok Pesantren heritage. The priority is determined by analyzing the level of influence and optimisation of building performance factors by implementing green building principles. The method used is multiple linear regression and optimisation by using dynamic programming. Research data is the perception of user consisting of residents and visitors. Residents of Pondok Pesantren include teachers and students.The priority of improving the performance includes: Security protection for residents and visitors; Free from dangerous materials and devices; Function of natural lighting; Aesthetics of park, landscape, and vegetation; Ease of indoor and outdoor circulation horizontally; Performance and reliability of roof structures; Durability of dormitory buildings; Regularity in buildings arrangement; Availability of information and communication facilities for visitors; and Alternative energy from wind sources or Environmental drainage and utility systems.

title: Everyday treasures: Applying product personalities to design user–product relationships
summary: This research applies Transactional Analysis, a theory of interpersonal relationships, to identify people's relationships with emotionally attached and frequently used objects in their daily routines. Through two complementary studies, it i
content: This research applies Transactional Analysis, a theory of interpersonal relationships, to identify people's relationships with emotionally attached and frequently used objects in their daily routines. Through two complementary studies, it investigates both the nature of these attachments and their implications for design. In Study 1, thirty semi-structured interviews invited participants to present their favourite objects, explain the reasons for their attachment, and rate the objects' perceived personality attributes and the emotions they evoke. The findings reveal that attachment to everyday objects is primarily driven by functional aspects and the services they facilitate, rather than aesthetic or symbolic aspects. These “everyday treasures” were most often associated with Adult and Nurturing Parent personalities, along with positive-passive and positive-active emotions. Building on these insights, a conceptual framework was developed to guide designers in creating emotionally resonant products. Study 2 involves a focus group workshop where eight design professionals validated the applicability of the framework in the design process, as a tool for evaluating existing products, generating concepts, and testing outcomes. Together, the studies demonstrate how Transactional Analysis can inform design practice by supporting the creation of products that develop meaningful emotional connections with users. • Explores emotional attachment to frequently used everyday products. • Identifies function and facilitation as key drivers of product attachment. • Shows that users favour products associated with Adult and Nurturing Parent personalities. • Proposes a Transactional Analysis-based framework for emotional user–product relationship design. • Demonstrates the applicability of the framework within design processes.

title: Theological or pedagogic recontextualisation? The Anglican religious education curriculum in Hong Kong
